Adhesive hydrogel-mediated spatiotemporal delivery of garlic-derived nanovesicles reprograms immunometabolism to rescue periodontal bone regeneration.
abstract: The core challenge in regenerating inflammatory bone defects, such as periodontitis-related bone resorption, lies in the dysregulation of the immune-metabolic microenvironment, which required implanted materials to simultaneously possess tissue sealing properties, sustained immune modulation capacity and metabolic intervention functions. Herein, garlic-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (GaELNs), exhibiting anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activities, are embedded in an injectable, tissue-adhesive polyethylene glycol hydrogel (GaE-PEG) to meet the challenges. The hydrogel exhibited favorable tissue adhesion and sustained release of GaELN-associated protein in vitro. GaE-PEG promoted macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated periodontal ligament stem cells, GaE-PEG alleviated mitochondrial oxidative stress, restored oxidative phosphorylation, suppressed excessive glycolysis, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses linked these effects to mitochondrial metabolic regulation, while oligomycin treatment attenuated the osteogenic response, supporting a contribution of oxidative phosphorylation. In a rat model of periodontitis-related bone defects, GaE-PEG reduced local inflammation and promoted alveolar bone regeneration, with improved regenerative outcomes compared with a single local injection of free GaELNs at an equivalent dose and Bio-Gide™/Bio-Oss™ treatment. These findings support an adhesive hydrogel strategy integrating local nanovesicle delivery with immunomodulation and metabolic regulation to promote bone regeneration under inflammatory conditions.

How Human–AI Interaction Reshapes Construction Workers’ Safety Behaviors: Insights from Agent-Based Modeling
abstract: The complex nature of human–artificial intelligence (AI) interaction (HAI) introduces new challenges for worker safety. While ensuring human well-being in HAI has become a shared objective, the lack of quantifiable approaches limits our ability to capture its nuanced effects on workers. To address this gap, the present study develops an agent-based modeling framework grounded in stimulus-organism-response (SOR) theory. The model simulates workers’ interactions with AI systems and peers within a bounded two-dimensional space, tracking the resulting cognitive, emotional, and behavioral responses. It comprises three components: worker-agent design, SOR process modeling, and an interaction rule base. Experiments were conducted under three scenarios: (1) repeated simulations with balanced parameter settings, (2) batch simulations with varying parameter settings, and (3) empirical validation at a real smart construction site. Results demonstrate that workers’ safety behavior progressively deteriorates as HAI deepens, with extra-role safety behavior exhibiting the most pronounced decline. This study extends the application of SOR theory to the construction industry and deepens the understanding of HAI in the context of construction safety. Practically, it underscores the cumulative cognitive and emotional effects of HAI on workers, providing both a managerial basis for defining human–AI boundaries and a quantifiable tool for long-term safety decision-making.

title: Quantitative Evaluation and Machine Learning–Based Diagnostic Warning Method for Multilayer Heterogeneous Reservoir Development: A Case Study from Z Oilfield, Dongpu Depression, China
abstract: Rational evaluation and warning-oriented diagnosis of development performance are essential for efficient management of multilayer heterogeneous reservoirs because they support timely identification of underperforming development units. In this study, a quantitative fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method and a machine learning–based diagnostic warning framework are proposed. First, 10 evaluation indicators integrating geological, development, and economic factors were selected from 68 candidate parameters across eight key aspects. Second, the index weight set was calculated by combining the criteria importance through intercriteria correlation (CRITIC) method, coefficient of variation (COV) method, and analytic hierarchy process (AHP), and the trichotomy method was used to determine the classification boundaries of good, medium, and poor. Based on the established quantitative evaluation method, 52 development units of the Z Oilfield, a mature multilayer heterogeneous fault-block waterflooding oilfield in the Dongpu Depression, China, were quantitatively evaluated. Third, a diagnostic warning model was developed by comparing multiple regression models, including linear regression, ridge regression, random forest, gradient boosting, and back-propagation (BP) neural network. The 52 development units were divided into training and independent testing subsets at a ratio of 70:30, and fivefold cross-validation was performed within the training subset for model assessment. The results show that gradient boosting achieved the best testing performance among the tested models, with a test coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) of 0.737, root-mean square error (RMSE) of 5.940, and mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.884. Finally, the selected model was applied to 10 representative development units, and the results indicated that M82 requires particular attention, and several medium-level units should be continuously monitored. The proposed method provides a practical tool for quantitative evaluation, diagnostic warning, and refined management of multilayer heterogeneous reservoirs.

title: Mechanism Construction and Combustion Characteristics Analysis of Diesel Fuel Blended with Nano-CeO 2
abstract: The catalytic influence of CeO 2 nanoparticles on diesel combustion was investigated through detailed kinetic modeling. A diesel surrogate consisting of n - dodecane ( NC 12 H 26 ) and p-xylene ( C 8 H 10 ) was adopted to represent the major chemical characteristics of real diesel fuel. A catalytic reaction mechanism describing the redox behavior of cerium dioxide ( CeO 2 ) was incorporated into the base fuel mechanism to construct a simplified kinetic framework for CeO 2 nanofuels. Combustion simulations were performed under various initial temperatures and pressures to evaluate the influence of CeO 2 nanoparticles on ignition behavior and combustion reactivity. The results indicate that the addition of CeO 2 significantly promotes the formation of OH and H 2 O 2 radicals at relatively low temperatures, leading to shorter ignition delay and enhanced heat release rates. At higher temperatures, combustion is dominated by rapid thermal decomposition of fuel molecules, which reduces the dependence of the system on catalytic radical generation and weakens the catalytic influence of CeO 2 . Furthermore, CeO 2 nanoparticles accelerate hydrocarbon oxidation and CO conversion while also enhancing nitrogen oxides ( NO x ) reduction reactions. Reaction pathway analysis shows that the primary oxidation pathways of the base fuel remain unchanged, whereas the catalytic reactions mainly affect radical formation and intermediate oxidation processes. These findings provide insight into the catalytic combustion mechanism of CeO 2 nanofuels and their potential for improving diesel combustion performance.

title: Risk Assessment of Earth-Rock Dams: A Data-Knowledge Dual-Driven Approach Using IAHP-CRITIC and Two-Dimensional Cloud Model
abstract: This paper proposes a novel data-knowledge dual-driven risk assessment methodology, addressing the limitations of traditional approaches, such as excessive subjectivity, incomplete weighting allocation, and reliance on a single evaluation dimension. The method is based on the improved analytic hierarchy process-criteria importance through intercriteria correlation (IAHP-CRITIC) combined weighting method and two-dimensional cloud model (TDCM). It innovatively constructs a new scoring method for the factor layer of the evaluation index system by utilizing quantitative indexes such as anomaly rate, aging components, change amplitude, and development trend from monitoring data. First, risk probability and consequence are adopted as assessment dimensions to construct a risk assessment system for earth-rock dams, incorporating key monitoring elements such as environmental factors, deformation, seepage, and stress–strain. By analyzing indexes including anomaly rate, aging component, change amplitude, and development trend, the scores for each evaluation index at the factor layer for both risk probability and consequence are determined, and the corresponding cloud digital characteristics are subsequently computed. Second, the IAHP-CRITIC combined weighting method is employed to determine the weights of evaluation indexes within the TDCM framework. Finally, by integrating the risk cloud map and the proximity concept, the risk level is evaluated intuitively and precisely regarding risk probability and consequence. The method is applied to the risk assessment of a concrete-faced rockfill dam in Xinjiang, China. The results indicate strong agreement with the inspection conclusions of the project. Compared with the one-dimensional cloud model (ODCM), the proposed TDCM better captures multidimensional and random uncertainties, offering an effective and rapid tool for the quantitative assessment of dam safety risks.

title: Host and anatomical filters prevent microbiome convergence in avian scavengers.
abstract: How host-associated microbiomes assemble under intense environmental microbial exposure remains a central question in microbial ecology. Vultures represent a unique natural system because these species differ markedly in feeding ecology and carcass use. We characterized bacterial communities across four anatomical niches (facial, buccal, tracheal, and cloacal) in 155 individuals spanning all four European obligate vulture species (subfamily Gypaetinae: Gypaetus barbatus, Neophron percnopterus, and Aegypiinae: Aegypius monachus and Gyps fulvus) and the facultative scavenger Milvus milvus. Microbiome composition was jointly structured by host species and anatomical niche, with host identity explaining more variation than anatomical compartment and a significant interaction indicating that interspecific differentiation depended on body site. Each niche supported distinct bacterial assemblages and core microbiomes: Cloacal communities were enriched in anaerobic gut-associated taxa, whereas facial and tracheal communities contained more environmental and respiratory-associated bacteria. Host-specific taxonomic signatures persisted within anatomical niches despite recurrent exposure to the same carrion-associated microbial pool. Age further influenced community composition, whereas sex had little detectable effect. The facultative scavenger showed the same broad anatomical compartmentalization observed in obligate scavengers, although taxonomic signatures differed among species. Thus, sustained exposure to a shared, microbially rich resource was insufficient to produce a common scavenger microbiome. Instead, microbiome assembly reflected hierarchical filtering by host identity, anatomical environment, and ontogeny. These findings distinguish microbial exposure from microbial persistence, establishing avian scavengers as a natural model for understanding how host-associated communities remain differentiated, despite recurrent exposure to shared environmental microbial reservoirs across ecological and anatomical scales in vertebrate hosts.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Coevolution of social network structure and life history in toothed whales.
abstract: Toothed whales offer a 34 My-long natural experiment for the evolution of complex mammalian societies. However, quantitative comparative analyses of social structure in these species are lacking. Here, we draw on existing social network analyses to compare social structure across toothed whales. We consider published measures of two social network traits across all toothed whales: modularity ([Formula: see text]), which captures divisions or "cliques" in a social community, and social differentiation ([Formula: see text]), which estimates how much whales vary in their relationships-whether they associate equally with others or form special bonds with specific individuals. Combining these with a recently published database of life history traits, we applied phylogenetic multilevel models with the objective of exploring the origins of social network structure. We identified 98 measures of modularity and 89 measures of social differentiation from 23 toothed whale species. Social network structure was more similar among closely related species (showing strong phylogenetic signal), despite substantial intraspecific variability. Toothed whales with longer lifespans and larger bodies tended to form more modular social networks, as did those where males were proportionally larger than females. Similar but weaker patterns were found between life history traits and social differentiation. Results from causal coevolutionary models provide preliminary evidence that social structure has been both a leader and follower of changes in life history. Our findings reveal the correlated evolution of social network structure and life history traits in toothed whales, shedding new light on the origins of social relationships.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Hormonal Regulation and the Mechanistic Basis of a Sex-Limited Color Polymorphism.
abstract: The presence of multiple discrete color patterns within a species has captivated evolutionary biologists for more than a century, including cases in which the polymorphism is confined to one sex. The brown anole Anolis sagrei exhibits a female-limited polymorphism in dorsal patterning, which is controlled by allelic variation at the autosomal CCDC170 locus. Here, we present and test a threshold model that can explain why the polymorphism is female-limited. We hypothesize that the hormonal environment determines whether allelic variation at the morph-associated locus is phenotypically manifested, potentially through estrogen-dependent regulation of CCDC170 and its neighboring gene ESR1, which are more highly expressed in female than male embryos. By manipulating embryonic estradiol levels, we show that genetic males can be induced to express the polymorphism according to allelic variation at the CCDC170 locus, which is naturally masked in males. Inversely, treating genetic females with fadrozole, which depletes estradiol, leads to monomorphic patterns irrespective of genotype, as in natural males. Using RT-qPCR on sexual organs, we demonstrate that these effects are accompanied by changes in gene expression levels of CCDC170 and ESR1 in response to estradiol and fadrozole, lending support to the threshold model. Our results suggest that the CCDC170-ESR1-locus is part of a mechanistic link between the morph-determining and the sex differentiation systems, and provide a causal explanation for the developmental origin of a sex-limited color polymorphism.

title: EQUALITY BEFORE THE LAW IN THE SPHERE OF DIGITAL PROPERTY (THE CORRELATION BETWEEN THE CONSTITUTIONAL PRINCIPLE OF EQUALITY AND DIFFERENTIATION OF THE LEGAL REGIME OF SUBJECTS IN THE SPHERE OF DIGITAL PROPERTY)
abstract: The article is devoted to the study of the problem of the correlation between the principle of equality before the law and differentiation of the legal regime of subjects in the sphere of digital property. Based on the analysis of doctrinal approaches, new laws and judicial practice, a model of a balanced legal regime is substantiated, combining a unified basic status of digital property as an object of civil rights with targeted differentiated restrictions for certain categories of participants. Criteria for permissible differentiationare proposed, ensuring compliance with the constitutional principles of equality and proportionality.

title: The Personal Fund as a Mechanism for Family Business Succession in Russia
abstract: The article studies the impact of the personal fund structure on ensuring family business succession and transforming traditional approaches to succession planning. The conclusion is substantiated that transferring key assets to an independent legal entity enables the founder, during their lifetime, to establish a stable governance model for the family business, define the procedures for asset utilization, and secure the financial interests of family members after their death. The significance of a personal fund is examined in terms of preserving unified corporate control, preventing the fragmentation of ownership interests and shares among heirs, mitigating the risk of inheritance and corporate disputes, and maintaining the continuity of a family business. Particular attention is paid to separating the functions of business management from the receipt of economic benefits: heirs and other family members can act as beneficiaries of a personal fund without being directly involved in managing the company. The article analyzes the specific features of the legal status of beneficiaries and separately examines the property qualification of 100 million rubles established by the civil law which is required for the creation of a lifetime personal fund. The conclusion is made that the high qualification amount limits the accessibility of this structure for small and medium-sized enterprises, even though they are also exposed to the risks of inheritance disputes and business fragmentation. Proposals are formulated regarding the possible differentiation of the legal regulation of personal funds established specifically for managing family businesses. In conclusion, the need to align the articles of association and terms and conditions for personal fund management with the founder’s prenuptial agreement, divorce settlement agreement, and testamentary dispositions is emphasized.

title: The Relationship Between Types of Proceedings and Other Procedures for Case Hearings in Civil Proceedings
abstract: The article examines the relationship between a type of proceeding and other case consideration procedures in civil procedure. The author views civil procedure as a four-level system of case examination procedures, the levels of which are: type of judicial proceedings, type of proceeding, features of the examination of individual categories of cases, and the legal case. Each level represents a differentiation of the civil procedural form to varying degrees. The constructed model allows for an examination of the dynamics of case examination procedures — their emergence and transition from one level to another.

title: Explainable EEG Foundation Models for Schizophrenia Detection Across Independent Datasets
abstract: Schizophrenia is a complex psychiatric disorder associated with altered brain electrophysiology. EEG foundation models provide promising approaches for learning transferable neural representations; however, their effectiveness and interpretability for schizophrenia detection remain insufficiently investigated. Three pretrained EEG foundation models, EEGMamba, EEGPT, and BIOT, were systematically evaluated for schizophrenia classification, with Simple Mamba included as an additional comparison. Two independent resting-state EEG datasets were analyzed: ASEEG, comprising 51 individuals with schizophrenia (SZ) and 50 healthy controls (HC), and Warsaw, comprising 14 SZ and 14 HC participants. Subject-wise cross-validation was employed. Integrated Gradients (IG) and channel occlusion were used to investigate spatial importance and explanation consistency. EEGMamba achieved the strongest performance on both datasets. On ASEEG, it obtained 79.18 ± 8.00% accuracy, 82.33 ± 12.54% sensitivity, an F1-score of 0.79 ± 0.10, and ROC-AUC of 0.83 ± 0.09. On Warsaw, EEGMamba achieved 78.33 ± 24.90% accuracy and 80.00 ± 14.21% sensitivity. XAI revealed model- and dataset-dependent patterns involving frontal/frontopolar, central, temporal, and parietal regions, with recurrent importance of C3, C4, Cz, Fp1/Fp2, and P3/P4. On Warsaw, BIOT demonstrated strong agreement between IG and occlusion (ρ = 0.744, p < 0.001). EEG foundation models show potential for subject-independent schizophrenia detection, with EEGMamba providing the strongest predictive performance. Complementary XAI analyses revealed spatially distributed discriminative information and highlighted the importance of jointly evaluating predictive performance and interpretability across independent datasets.

title: In silico perturbation as an adversarial attack: combinatorial searchover cell states in single-cell foundation models
abstract: Background: Identifying which genes to perturb in order to drive a cell towards a desired state is a common problem in biology, and the answer is often a combination of genes. Single-cell foundation models can predict the effect of forcing a gene on without an experiment, but in silico perturbation has been confined to single genes or to a few hundred enumerated combinations. In token-based models, choosing which genes to force on is formally the same optimization problem as a discrete adversarial attack on a language model. We therefore investigated whether Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG), a search developed for such attacks, can be used to find combinations of genes. Results: Our results suggest that GCG is useful for finding combinations of genes. In Geneformer, the effect of a set was well below the sum of the individual effects of its members, which suggests that assembling combinations from single-gene effects is not a promising approach. GCG exceeded forward-selection greedy search at equal cost in two models (Geneformer and scGPT) and at every set size. Against published reprogramming protocols, GCG recovered the reported factors at a rate well above chance and higher than the random-pool and all-gene greedy searches at equal cost, although ranking genes by their individual effect gave a higher recovery rate. Recovery corresponded to whether a search used the embedding gradient, which suggests that the gradient is useful for narrowing the search, whereas stronger optimization of the objective did not raise recovery, which suggests that the similarity induced by the model does not fully reflect the regulatory logic of genes. Conclusions: These results are obtained within the constraints of the foundation models; nevertheless, searching for combinations of factors with foundation models extends in silico perturbation beyond single genes, reveals a property of the induced objective that single-gene evaluation does not, and points to a new direction for using and evaluating the models.

title: Enhanced rock weathering increases crop yield: a global meta-analysis
abstract: Enhanced rock weathering (ERW) is increasingly considered for CO₂ removal on agricultural land, yet its effects on crop productivity remain uncertain across crops, soils and amendment practices. This work is the first global meta-analysis of experimental evidence published between 1983 and 2026, comprising 7,236 treatment-control comparisons from 113 publications. Of these, 2,086 comparisons from 52 publications were eligible for multilevel random-effects meta-analysis with publication-clustered robust inference. ERW increased harvested yield by 29.0% (95% CI: 8.7–53.1%; 22 publications, 91 comparisons), shoot dry biomass by 16.1% (95% CI: 8.6–24.2%) and aboveground potassium uptake by 36.5% (95% CI: 26.7–47.0%). However, the publication-balanced median harvested-yield increase was 14.8% across the broader evidence base, and substantial heterogeneity produced a wide prediction interval (-43.4% to + 194.0%). Crop-specific responses varied, while exploratory moderator analyses did not establish reliable predictors of agronomic effectiveness across soil conditions, climates, rock materials or application practices. Strictly matched experimental responses revealed a positive association between potassium uptake and harvested yield (Spearman's ρ = 0.905; adjusted q = 0.008), although the limited evidence and potential mathematical coupling preclude causal interpretation. Overall, ERW can improve agricultural productivity, but the magnitude and consistency of these benefits remain context-dependent. Agronomic performance should therefore be evaluated independently of CO₂ removal, with greater emphasis on replicated field experiments and concurrent measurements of crop productivity, nutrient acquisition and soil conditions.

title: DELINEATION OF AGRICULTURAL FIELD BOUNDARIES USING MACHINE LEARNING: BASED ON THE CASE OF THE ZHETYSAI DISTRICT, KAZAKHSTAN
abstract: Accurate delineation of agricultural field boundaries is essential for agro-production monitoring, irrigation management, and sustainable land use planning. Manual digitization is labour-intensive and poorly scalable, while conventional segmentation algorithms are sensitive to spectral heterogeneity and weak inter-field contrast. The Zhetysai district of southern Kazakhstan – where approximately 45-50% of irrigated farmland exhibits salinization – exemplifies the urgent demand for automated field mapping. This study evaluates the Meta AI Segment Anything Model (SAM) with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning as a parameter-efficient, scalable approach to automated field boundary delineation. High-resolution Esri World Imagery served as the primary data source. A training dataset of 705 manually digitized field polygons was prepared in ArcGIS Pro and exported as classified tiles. SAM – pre-trained on over one billion masks – was fine-tuned via the SAMLoRA architecture, which freezes the Vision Transformer encoder and trains only lightweight adapter layers, enabling efficient domain adaptation from limited annotations. The model was trained on a CUDA GPU with early stopping, then applied district-wide to generate a pixel classification raster, which was vectorized into closed field polygons and validated through expert visual inspection. Fine-tuning achieved 91% overall pixel accuracy on the validation subset. Applied to the full study area, the model delineated 4,060 field polygons covering 809.76 km2 . Expert verification confirmed high boundary correspondence and negligible false positives. The results demonstrate that a foundation model can be effectively adapted to a new agrolandscape with minimal labelled data, yielding a reproducible and scalable geospatial workflow suitable for precision irrigation management, sown area assessment, and land resource governance across irrigated regions.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL SATISFACTION AS A MODERATOR IN THE HARNESSING OF COMMUNITY-BASED TOURISM FOR SUSTAINABLE GROWTH
abstract: Community-based tourism (CBT) has come up as a viable solution towards development of sustainable tourism. Against the conventional tourism models, CBT focuses on the active participation and empowerment of the local communities in the planning, management, and decision-making processes in tourism. Through prioritization of local ownership, cultural preservation and environmental conservation, the CBT seeks to achieve more equitable distribution of tourism benefits and minimizing negative impacts. This is more so applicable in developing areas where tourism can be used as a trigger in bringing about socio-economic development provided it is done in a responsible manner This study aims to investigate how communitybased tourism (CBT), with its three dimensions (economic, social, and environmental), affects long-term tourism growth and explores the moderating role of environmental satisfaction in the relationship between (CBT) factors and sustainable growth (SG). An online survey was conducted, involving 402 participants from the local community, representatives of the tourism sector, and visitors to the Dhofar tourism destination. A two-step quantitative approach was employed, utilizing structural equation modelling (SEM) using WarpPLS software. The findings demonstrated that the economic factor had a positive influence on sustainable growth, whereas the social factor exerted a negative influence, and the environmental factor exhibited no effect. Environmental satisfaction serves as a crucial moderator, amplifying the positive effects of social and environmental factors on tourism sustainability. CBT is a model of tourism that places local communities at the center of tourism management, development, and operation. This approach not only prioritizes environmental and cultural conservation but also enhances local livelihoods, making it a powerful tool for fostering sustainable tourism development. This study represents one of the limited investigations within the Sultanate of Oman in this context. The findings may assist the tourism industry in comprehending the potential advantages and challenges of (CBT) as well as how to employ it in their specific fields.

title: SPATIAL DISPARITIES IN CULTURAL TOURISM: A MULTIDIMENSIONAL ANALYSIS OF MUSEUM ATTENDANCE DYNAMICS IN BULGARIA
abstract: This study aims to identify and analyse spatial disparities and structural stratification of regional museum activity in Bulgaria over a 13-year period (2012-2024). The primary objective is to evaluate the stability, growth trajectory, and resilience of regional cultural supply models in response to external and macroeconomic shifts, specifically the COVID-19 pandemic. A multidimensional statistical analysis was applied to panel data from the National Statistical Institute and the Institute for Market Economics, encompassing all 28 administrative districts in Bulgaria. Quartile grouping (based on visits per 1000 inhabitants) was utilized to differentiate clusters, while long-term dynamics and crisis resilience were assessed through specific indicators: Coefficient of Variation (CV), Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR), Sensitivity Index (SI), and Recovery Index (RI). Through this approach, the districts were categorized into three distinct performance tiers: Highlevel (Leaders), Mid-level, and Low-level. The analysis reveals significant structural imbalances and high systemic volatility across all clusters, indicating a critical dependence on incidental tourist flows. A “scale paradox” was identified, whereby districts with moderate attendance volumes and a developed local product demonstrate considerably higher post-crisis adaptability compared to traditional leaders. Although all groups exhibit coefficients of variation exceeding 40%, the Mid-level segment achieves the highest annual growth (4.95%) and positive recovery (17.15%), outperforming the top-tier districts, which record slower growth (1.62%) and negative post-pandemic recovery (-12.08%). Empirical profiles highlight stable cores (Veliko Tarnovo, Gabrovo), strategic event legacies (Plovdiv), and nature-integrated recovery (Smolyan), contrasting with transitdependent declines (Vidin). The high structural volatility underscores an urgent need for a conceptual shift in regional cultural policies. Strategic management should pivot towards active audience development and integrated regional tourism products, linking public subsidies to institutional flexibility and proven post-crisis resilience rather than merely static volumes.

title: Histogram Analysis of IVIM MRI Parameters for Distinguishing Pseudo-progression and True Progression in High-Grade Gliomas.
abstract: Background Differentiating pseudoprogression (PsP) from true progression (TP) in high-grade gliomas (HGGs) is challenging, as conventional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) lacks sufficient specificity. Intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) MRI, may improve diagnostic performance by providing insights into tumor microstructure. Objective To evaluate the diagnostic performance of IVIM MRI derived parameters histogram in distinguishing PsP from TP in HGG patients. Material and Methods In a prospective study, 30 patients with WHO grade III or IV gliomas, previously treated with standard therapy, underwent IVIM MRI. Parametric maps (D, D*, f, and Apparent Diffusion Coefficient (ADC)) were normalized to contralateral white matter, and histogram features were extracted from enhancing lesions. Univariate analysis identified significant features, and multivariate logistic regression assessed their combined diagnostic performance. The model's diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, with Area Under Curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Results Histogram analysis revealed significant differences in most histogram features of the D-ratio, D*-ratio, and ADC-ratio between PsP and TP groups. The 50th percentile of the D-ratio and the 99th percentile of the D*-ratio were identified as independent predictors in the final model, with AUC values of 0.79 and 0.728, respectively. The final model achieved an AUC of 0.853, demonstrating high sensitivity (93.8%), specificity (64.3%), and overall accuracy (80%), outperforming individual parameters. Conclusion The 50v percentile of the D-ratio and the 99th percentile of the D*-ratio demonstrated significant discrimination power between PsP and TP. Their combination further enhanced diagnostic accuracy, making them valuable metrics for clinical decision-making in HGG management.

title: An IoT-enabled environmental informatics framework for real-time crop disease detection using attention-driven deep learning
abstract: Introduction Crop diseases are a major challenge in agriculture because their early and accurate identification is essential for reducing crop losses and improving productivity. The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) with deep learning provides an effective approach for automated crop disease monitoring by enabling the collection and analysis of environmental parameters such as soil moisture, temperature, and humidity. However, accurate fine-grained disease identification remains challenging because of variations in disease symptoms, environmental conditions, and visual characteristics. Methods This study proposes an IoT-enabled deep learning framework for automated crop disease detection and classification. The collected crop images are pre-processed using scaling, normalization, and data augmentation techniques to improve image quality and model generalization. For efficient disease detection, a lightweight attention-driven convolutional neural network-based object detection approach, termed YOLO10-YSTs (You Only Look Once 10-Yield Surveillance Technology), is employed. The framework integrates the real-time detection capability of YOLO10 with an attention mechanism to emphasize disease-relevant regions and a stigmergy-based encoding strategy to enhance feature representation and extraction. In addition, a novel DBGU-LSTM (Dual-Bi-Gated Recurrent Unit with Long Short-Term Memory) architecture is developed for fine-grained crop disease classification. Results The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides effective disease detection, discriminative feature representation, and fine-grained classification. The DBGU-LSTM architecture achieves improved classification performance and training stability compared with the conventional deep learning models considered in the study. Overall, the proposed approach achieves a classification accuracy of 97.99%, demonstrating its effectiveness for automated crop disease recognition. Discussion and conclusion The results indicate that combining IoT-based environmental monitoring with attention-driven deep learning and recurrent feature-learning mechanisms can provide an effective solution for intelligent crop disease detection. The proposed framework enables accurate identification of disease patterns while supporting efficient and automated agricultural monitoring. Therefore, the approach has potential to assist farmers in early disease diagnosis, reduce crop losses, and improve agricultural productivity.

title: Measurand-Aware Inter-Platform Consistency Assessment of GOES Land Surface Temperature Harmonization
abstract: Cross-platform land surface temperature (LST) harmonization is often evaluated by agreement of individual observations, although urban analyses commonly rely on spatial differences and temporal changes. We investigated whether improving agreement in urban-core and surrounding-ring LST also improves their core–ring contrast and pre-to-post-sunset transition. Using Advanced Baseline Imager observations from Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES)-16, -17, -18, and -19 over western North American cities during 2019–2026, we evaluated five cohorts using established mean-squared-error (MSE) decomposition and cross-validated model selection at each measurand. Component root-mean-squared error (RMSE) decreased by 29.3–59.7%, whereas core–ring contrast RMSE ranged from an 11.5% reduction to a 13.1% increase. Loss of residual covariance offset 94.6–114.0% of gross variance-plus-bias gains. In the post hoc 2026 temporal evaluation of the same 75 cities used for 2025 calibration, core and ring RMSE declined by 59.7% and 56.1%, but contrast RMSE reduction was −0.14% (95% crossed city–interval bootstrap interval, −6.75% to +6.48%, with cities and intervals resampled independently). The historical 2021 evaluation likewise showed only a small, uncertain contrast improvement (2.9%; 95% interval, −4.3% to +9.8%). Calibration-based selection retained raw contrasts and transitions, while a residual interval rule withheld uncertain transition direction claims. Independent three-station radiometric comparisons assessed raw satellite products at station scale rather than the complete urban workflow. These findings demonstrate why harmonization performance should be evaluated at the derived scientific quantity, with processing decisions based on its observed cross-platform consistency.

title: Managerial Innovation as a Lever for Digital Transformation Success: Toward an Integrated Organizational Value Creation Framework
abstract: The accelerating pace of digital transformation has fundamentally restructured competitive landscapes across industries, compelling organizations to reconsider not only their technological investments but, more critically, their managerial architectures and innovation capacities. While extant scholarship has extensively examined the technological dimensions of digital transformation, comparatively limited attention has been devoted to managerial innovation as a primary enabling condition for sustained digital transformation success. This article addresses that gap by developing a theoretically grounded, integrative conceptual framework—the Integrated Organizational Value Creation Framework (IOVCF)—that articulates the causal pathways through which managerial innovation drives digital transformation and ultimately generates organizational value. Anchored in four complementary theoretical perspectives—Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the Resource-Based View (RBV), Organizational Change Theory, and Socio-Technical Systems Theory—the framework models a cascading logic: managerial innovation cultivates organizational capabilities (agility, learning, adaptability, and collaborative intelligence), which in turn facilitate digital transformation success (technology adoption, process digitalization, data integration, and digital innovation), culminating in multi-dimensional organizational value creation (operational performance, resilience, stakeholder satisfaction, and sustainable competitive advantage). Twelve formal research propositions are derived and theoretically justified. Managerial implications emphasize that digital transformation leaders must invest in organizational redesign, agile management practices, digital culture formation, knowledge management systems, employee empowerment, and collaborative ecosystems alongside—and often prior to—technology deployment. A rich agenda for future empirical research is outlined, encompassing cross-national validation, SME contexts, AI-enabled transformation, and sustainability-oriented digital strategies.
journal: International Journal of Automation and Digital Transformation

title: An Integrated XAI-RL Architecture for Ethical Decision-Making in Autonomous Robots
abstract: Can a robot's ethical reasoning be transparent without slowing it down? That is the question we set out to answer. Autonomous robots now make decisions that affect people's lives, and if we cannot understand how they decide, trust becomes a serious problem. We built a unified architecture that couples Explainable AI (XAI) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) through three connected components: a Perception Layer for situational awareness, a Decision Reasoning Layer that breaks agent utility down into measurable ethical sub-rewards (safety, fairness, and well-being), and a contrastive Explainability Engine grounded in a real-time Ethical Ledger. We tested it against Black-Box RL and two post-hoc XRL baselines (LIME and SHAP) across two simulation environments and a physical robot pilot on a TurtleBot3 platform. Our system reached 92±3% ethical alignment in simulation and 89±4% on the physical platform, beating every baseline (p < 0.01 throughout). In a controlled, IRB-approved user study (N=128), participants rated it higher on trust (4.5±0.4), understandability (4.6±0.3), and perceived safety (4.4±0.5) than the alternatives. Explanations were also fast: 4.2±0.6 ms on average, versus 18.3±2.1 ms for SHAP and 12.7±1.8 ms for LIME on the same hardware—well within real-time limits. An ablation study and sensitivity analysis back up these architectural choices.
journal: International Journal of Automation and Digital Transformation

title: From Emotion to Expression: The AL–DL–CL Framework for Understanding Communication in the Age of AI and Digital Media
abstract: Rapid progress in digital media and artificial intelligence is transforming human communication, facilitating the rapid exchange of messages and minimizing the chances of reflective interpretation. Existing theories in linguistics, psychology, and cultural studies address the structural, cognitive, or social aspects of language, yet fail to explain how emotional processing, internal linguistic structuring, and culturally mediated communication function as a coherent, dynamic system. Through this model, the authors present the AL–DL–CL framework that explores how three layers are engaged in a process that results in communication, through a recursive interaction between the Automatic Layer (AL), the Deliberate Layer (DL), and the Cultural Language Layer (CL). In such a process, the affective or unconscious processes in AL are consistently reframed into structured internal representations via DL, and through CL, and translated back into culturally-expressed language serves as a feedback mechanism, with a tendency to modify cognition and emotional response. Based on a multi-method exploratory approach of sequential cultural transmission, clinical case study analysis, and group-based validation, the results indicate that language is not so much a static container for meaning as a process of reconstruction that is molded by the dynamic interaction between emotion, cognition, and culture. This model also demonstrates how digitally mediated communication can amplify AL-directed reaction and limit DL-level thinking, which increases the potential for misinterpretation, polarization, or misinformation. The AL–DL–CL framework provides guidance in a unified theoretical perspective around language emergence, responsible AI design and digital literacy and intercultural discourse based on the continuous transformation system of communication, and not on the linear encoding.

title: Multi-agent generative AI ecosystems for cyber-physical systems in Industry 5.0
abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) are increasingly being implemented in critical industrial infrastructure, where complexity and interdependence are rising, posing significant cyber and operational risks. Traditional anomaly detection algorithms can be ineffective in capturing temporal dynamics, relational dependencies, and interpretable response requirements. The present paper proposes a multi-agent generative AI system to detect CPS anomalies and provide decision support by combining temporal feature encoding, relational modeling as graphs, supervised learning, and reasoning with an LLM. The architecture consists of detection, diagnosis, planning, governance, and human-in-the-loop validation agents. The framework is tested on the SWaT benchmark data. Findings indicate that the Autoencoder, LSTM, and 1D-CNN are more effective in terms of raw detection metrics, whereas the Random Forest provides more interpretable and agent-readable evidence to support the post-detection decision. Analysis of features and sensor family suggests the relevance of relational dependencies in characterizing anomalies. The multi-agent layer converts selected anomaly predictions into context-dependent explanations and governance-filtered recommendations to aid operator review, response planning, and process resilience. Overall, the framework supports transparent and human-supervised CPS anomaly management aligned with Industry 5.0 principles.

title: XLeaf-Net: an explainable deep learning framework for mango leaf disease classification and severity assessment using Grad-CAM-based visual interpretation
abstract: Accurate mango leaf disease recognition is important for automated crop-health assessment, but reliable evaluation requires transparent data partitioning, appropriate baseline comparison, and cautious interpretation of severity and explainability outputs. This study presents XLeaf-Net, an explainable deep-learning framework for mango leaf condition classification, image-derived severity assessment, and Grad-CAM-based visual interpretation. Experiments were conducted on the balanced MangoLeafBD dataset using an image-level stratified train-validation-test protocol with file-level integrity and capture/session-group overlap checks. XLeaf-Net was trained from scratch and compared with from-scratch VGG16, ResNet50, and EfficientNetB0 models under the implemented model-specific training configurations. An auxiliary severity model used conservative, image-derived symptom-intensity proxy labels, while Grad-CAM was applied to qualitatively examine class-discriminative regions. XLeaf-Net achieved 98.67% image-level test accuracy and a 98.66% macro F1-score, outperforming the evaluated from-scratch baselines while using 2.52 million parameters. The severity model achieved 78.17% accuracy and an 80.89% macro F1-score. Grad-CAM visualizations frequently overlapped with visually symptomatic leaf regions in representative correctly classified images. These findings demonstrate strong image-level performance within the implemented protocol; however, severity labels were not expert-annotated, and the evaluation was not session-independent. XLeaf-Net should therefore be considered a compact candidate framework requiring further independent validation.

title: Development of an Integrated Web-Based Partnership Management Information System for PHRI Bekasi City
abstract: Professional associations require integrated information systems to improve administrative efficiency and support digital transformation. However, the Indonesian Hotel and Restaurant Association (PHRI) Bekasi City still manages membership administration, membership fee payments, organizational information dissemination, and hotel occupancy reporting through separate and predominantly manual processes, resulting in inefficient data management and delayed administrative services. This study aims to develop an integrated web-based Partnership Management Information System to streamline administrative processes and enhance organizational services. The project was governed using the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK) framework for initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, and closing, while the Waterfall model guided sequential software development. Laravel was employed as the web application framework, MySQL as the database management system, Bootstrap for the user interface, and the Midtrans payment gateway for digital membership fee transactions. Functional evaluation was conducted through User Acceptance Testing (UAT) with the PHRI Bekasi City management board, while technical performance was evaluated using Google PageSpeed Insights. The developed system successfully integrated membership management, digital membership cards, digital payment processing, organizational information management, and hotel occupancy reporting into a single platform. UAT results showed very good scores across functionality (93%), performance (92.5%), interface (91%), and efficiency (97%), while Performance Testing indicated strong results on desktop and good results on mobile devices. These findings demonstrate that the proposed system effectively supports the digital transformation of partnership management and provides a practical reference for implementing integrated information systems in similar professional organizations.
journal: Journal of Engineering Technology and Science Integration (JETSI)

title: EZpred: Improving Deep Learning‐Based Enzyme Function Prediction Using Unlabeled Sequence Homologs
abstract: Features extracted from sequence homologs significantly enhance the accuracy of deep learning‐based protein structure prediction. Indeed, homolog‐aware models such as AlphaFold generally produce more accurate protein structures compared to single sequence‐based methods like ESMfold. In contrast, features from sequence homologs are seldom employed for deep learning‐based prediction of the biological functions of a protein, such as Gene Ontology terms or Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers. Although a small number of models also incorporate function labels from sequence homologs, they cannot utilize features extracted from homologs that lack function labels. To address this gap, we developed EZpred, which is the first deep learning model to use sequence homologs by extracting their sequence features while ignoring any function labels. Starting with the target sequence and homologs identified by MMseqs2, EZpred extracts sequence features using the ESM‐C protein language model. These features are then fed into a deep learning model to predict the EC numbers of the target protein. For test enzymes with < 30% sequence identity to any training proteins, the F1‐score of EZpred EC number prediction is at least 34% higher than state‐of‐the‐art EC number prediction models. These results demonstrate the strong positive impact of sequence homologs in deep learning‐based enzyme function prediction.

title: The Pie Theory of Plant Breeding: A systems framework
abstract: Plant breeding has achieved remarkable success through concepts and approaches including yield‐component analysis, ideotype breeding, heterosis, genotype‐by‐environment interaction (GE), genomic selection, multi‐trait selection, and the breeder's eye. Although each illuminates an important aspect of crop improvement, these concepts are often considered separately. This article proposes the “Pie Theory of Plant Breeding” as a systems framework that integrates established and emerging breeding concepts within a common perspective of optimization, expansion, prediction, adaptation, and validation. Optimization seeks the best‐performing combination of competing traits within available biological capacity, whereas expansion shifts the biological boundary and enlarges the space of possibilities available for subsequent optimization. The two processes are interdependent: expansion creates new opportunities for optimization, while optimization realizes the value of expansion and reveals constraints that may require further expansion. Within this framework, competing traits determine how biological capacity is converted into cultivar value, whereas enabling genes, gene combinations, traits, and environmental inputs create, preserve, protect, or expand that capacity. The framework applies across pure‐line and hybrid breeding: parent selection creates possibilities through merit and complementation, while heterozygosity expands the range of selectable genetic states without necessarily guaranteeing heterosis. The breeder's eye and genomic selection are interpreted as complementary G + GE (GGE)‐based prediction systems operating on different sources of information, while formal multi‐location, multi‐year, and multi‐trait GGE integration validates whether predicted optimization and expansion have translated into adaptation and agricultural value. Plant breeding is therefore viewed as a recursive process in which biological possibilities are created, optimized, predicted, filtered, and ultimately validated through whole‐system performance.

title: Maternal mortality in the Americas, 2000-2023: an ecological study of temporal trends, socioeconomic inequalities, and progress towards 2030 targets.
abstract: Background Maternal mortality rose sharply during 2019-2021, coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic, against a backdrop of already fragile progress in maternal survival across the Americas. We assessed whether the subsequent decline restored sufficient and equitable progress towards the 2030 regional benchmark. Methods We conducted an ecological country-year observational analysis using Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group (MMEIG) estimates for 36 countries and territories, together with the regional series for the Americas, from 2000 to 2023. Temporal trends were assessed using continuous log-linear models with zero to four joinpoints. Social inequalities were quantified using the slope index of inequality (SII), relative index of inequality (RII), and health concentration index (CIx). We also estimated the annual rate of reduction required for each country and territory to reach a maternal mortality ratio (MMR) of 30 per 100,000 live births by 2030. As the principal external comparison of the pandemic-period signal, country-year MMRs officially reported to the Pan American Health Organization were compared with the corresponding MMEIG estimates. Findings Regional maternal deaths averaged 9408 annually during 2000-2019, peaked at 14,498 in 2021, and declined to 7813 in 2023. The maternal mortality ratio (MMR) decreased from 70.4 in 2000 to 58.5 in 2023, despite rising from 58.9 in 2019 to 106.8 in 2021. Joinpoints occurred in 2014, 2019, and 2021; the 2000-2023 average annual percentage change was -0.9%. Reaching an MMR of 30 by 2030 would require a 9.6% annual regional reduction. In 2023, the SII was -123.6 (95% CI -181.7 to -65.6), the RII was 9.9 (4.4-22.5), and the CIx was -39.6% (-52.4 to -15.3). These measures describe concentration of MMEIG-estimated mortality among countries at the lower end of the GDP distribution and are not interpreted as independent effects of GDP. Interpretation The post-2021 decline is consistent with recovery, but it did not restore an adequate or equitable long-term trajectory. The pandemic-period rise was also evident in many independently reported country series, although its magnitude and timing varied and causal attribution cannot be established from this ecological analysis. Reaching the 2030 benchmark requires sustained acceleration, differentiated country support based on mortality and target gaps, stronger maternal-death surveillance and response, and equitable access to high-quality care. Funding This study received no specific funding.

Mitochondrial antiviral signalling protein (MAVS) in cardiovascular diseases (CVD): a novel pharmacological target.
abstract: Mitochondrial antiviral signalling protein (MAVS), also known as interferon-β (IFN-β) promoter stimulator 1 (IPS-1), virus-induced signalling adaptor (VISA), and CARD adaptor inducing IFN-β (CARDIF), has emerged as a regulatory node linking mitochondrial stress, innate immune signalling, and cardiovascular disease (CVD) pathogenesis. In the cardiovascular system, MAVS is activated not only by viral RNA sensors such as retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I) and melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 (MDA5), but also by endogenous danger signals. This activation promotes transcription of NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) and pro-inflammatory cytokines, and facilitates NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and cytokine maturation, processes implicated in myocardial inflammation, remodelling, and dysfunction in conditions such as myocardial hypertrophy, atherosclerosis, and cardiomyopathy. Beyond inflammasome activation, MAVS intersects with multiple cell death and homeostatic pathways relevant to CVD, including apoptosis, autophagy, and, potentially, ferroptosis. Preclinical studies show that genetic ablation of MAVS, or pharmacological interventions that limit mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS), mitochondrial double-stranded RNA (mtdsRNA) release, or downstream innate immune signalling, can attenuate MAVS-associated inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic remodelling, thereby slowing disease progression in experimental cardiovascular models. MAVS, however, also performs essential protective functions, particularly in antiviral defence and maintenance of cardiac homeostasis, underscoring the need for context-specific, cell-type-restricted, or pathway-selective modulation rather than indiscriminate inhibition. Collectively, these findings position MAVS as a promising therapeutic target in CVD, warranting further investigation into MAVS-associated signalling pathways and their modulation in cardiovascular contexts.

Automatic Gravel Road Dust Monitoring Analysis Using Deep Learning Models and Small Uncrewed Aircraft Systems
abstract: Gravel, unsurfaced, or unpaved road networks account for 35% of the total roadways in the US, with some states such as Iowa having about 60% of their roadways unpaved, and regular monitoring is required to maintain and extend their service life. Among the major types of gravel road distress, dust clouds from passing traffic can cause significant environmental problems, impair visibility, and pose health risks to human respiratory systems. Popular technical manual for unsurfaced road maintenance management typically recommend assessment of dust-severity levels based on the severity of a dust cloud produced by a vehicle driving at 40 km / h ( 25 mi / h ). Because this method exposes assessors to unsafe conditions, its use is impractical for long road networks and high-dust severity conditions, so there is a need to explore automated and remote-sensing techniques for rating dust severity. Although previous studies have employed image-processing techniques to assess dust levels from images captured by vehicle-mounted cameras, dust accumulation on windshields and unstable camera attachments have reduced the reliability of such data collection. To address these limitations, this paper investigates the application of small uncrewed aircraft systems (sUAS) in rating dust clouds generated by traffic at various speeds. For this experiment, we collected dust data using sUAS from three gravel roads in Iowa and applied deep-learning models, specifically You Only Look Once version 8 large (YOLOv8l), to detect the truck driven for dust activation and residual network (ResNet) models to classify the level of dust severity in each sUAS video frame. The ResNet-152 classification model achieved the best result on the test data set with a weighted F1-score of 0.9867, highlighting a promising outcome for adoption of sUAS for dust monitoring.

title: Utilization of Copper Tailings in Structural Ceramsite: Processing Optimization, Mechanical Performance, and Sustainability Assessment
abstract: The accumulation of copper tailings (CTs) has become a serious environmental challenge, and their recycling into building materials offers a practical way to reduce waste and support sustainable construction. This study examines the preparation of ceramsite from copper tailings, fly ash, and bentonite. The work aims to produce aggregates with high strength suitable for concrete applications. A uniform experimental design was used to explore how raw material ratios, sintering temperature, and sintering time influence the properties of ceramsite, while data analysis and process optimization were supported by regression-based modeling and numerical optimization techniques. The optimized ceramsite exhibited high compressive strength and very low water absorption. It had a dense matrix, contributing to its strength and durability. Microstructural investigations using X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive spectroscopy revealed the presence of quartz, feldspars, mullite, and corundum, with mullite and corundum playing a key role in improving strength. To evaluate practical performance, concrete specimens were prepared with varying volumetric replacement ratios of ceramsite and tested for their mechanical properties. Results demonstrated that replacing ordinary crushed stone with ceramsite significantly enhanced both compressive and flexural strength. The greatest improvements appeared at moderate replacement levels, and overall performance still surpassed conventional concrete even at higher ratios. In addition, carbon emission assessments confirmed that producing ceramsite from CTs generated substantially lower emissions compared with traditional aggregates, supporting its role as a green material. Overall, this work demonstrates a promising pathway for recycling industrial waste into high-quality construction materials, providing both environmental and engineering benefits.
journal: Journal of Materials in Civil Engineering

title: Multidimensional Urban–Rural Integration Based on Factor Flows and Its Effects on Landscape Patterns: A Case Study of Nanjing, China
abstract: Urban–rural integration (URI) refers to coordinated development between cities and rural areas. While existing research addresses URI quantification, effects, and optimization, gaps remain in quantifying URI from the perspective of factor flows, analyzing its distribution across urban–fringe–rural regions, and examining URI’s impact on landscape patterns. This study analyzed Nanjing, which is a typical metropolitan city of China, using a machine learning method to identify urban, fringe, and rural areas, quantifying URI from economic, social, and spatial dimensions, and applied a Random Forest regression model combined with Shapley additive explanations analysis to examine URI’s influence on landscapes. Findings include the following: (1) Nanjing’s urban, fringe, and rural areas occupied 18.3%, 29.0%, and 52.7% in 2022, respectively. (2) Urban area had the highest URI estimations of all dimensions. Fringe area held the medium values, with lower social and spatial integration. URI in rural areas was the weakest. (3) URI showed significant effects in fringe and rural areas. In fringe zones, ecological land division was positively correlated with spatial integration, while construction land patterns were influenced by multidimensional URI dynamics. In rural zones, construction land connectivity was shaped by the synergy of spatial and social integration and service facility distribution. (4) Based on these findings, a differentiated zoning strategy was proposed to guide region-specific integration and landscape optimization. This study provides a new perspective on understanding URI, offering both theoretical and practical implications for landscape optimization.

Climate change adaptation practices in fruit-irrigated agriculture: the role of nudging in farmers’ adoption decisions
abstract: This study analyses farmers’ responses to economic incentives and behavioural nudges for promoting adoption of water and soil conservation practices, identifying which are most effective. A discrete choice experiment was conducted with irrigated fruit farmers, focusing on three climate change adaptation agricultural practices (subsurface irrigation, regulated deficit irrigation and cover crops) combined with a monetary incentive (framed as subsidy or discount) and additional services replicating the most common characteristics of nudges. Four categories of nudges are evaluated: facilitators (advisory mobile apps), confrontational (apps showcasing the negative effects of not adopting the water-saving practices), social norms (apps benchmarking individual performance against peers) and reinforcement (public recognition and certifications). The analysis incorporates preference heterogeneity based on farmers’ attitudes to nudging. Results show that both monetary incentives and nudges increase farmers’ willingness to adopt subsurface irrigation, regulated deficit irrigation and cover crops. Apps tackling behavioural biases can reduce the need for compensation. Confrontational nudges are most effective; facilitation nudges show heterogeneous response and social influence and signalling nudges generate undefined responses. Therefore, there is potential to reduce the overall cost of promoting biodiversity and water-saving technology adoption by farmers by combining economic incentives with tailored nudges. The study focuses on irrigated fruit farmers in the Region of Murcia, Spain, which may limit the generalisation of the findings to other agricultural systems and geographical contexts. Moreover, stated preferences derived from a discrete choice experiment may differ from actual adoption behaviour. Future research could test these behavioural interventions in real-world settings and examine their effectiveness across different farmer profiles, agricultural sectors and regions. Financial incentives remain important for encouraging farmers to adopt climate change adaptation practices, but behavioural interventions can complement them and potentially reduce the level of financial support required. Policymakers, irrigation associations and advisory services could use digital tools providing personalised information on the environmental consequences of farming practices. For example, irrigation-scheduling and climate-risk dashboards could provide tailored recommendations based on environmental conditions and local water availability, combining behavioural information with technical guidance according to farmer profiles. Promoting climate change adaptation practices can contribute to more sustainable water and soil management in water-scarce agricultural regions. By making the environmental consequences of farming decisions more visible, behavioural interventions may strengthen farmers’ awareness of climate-related risks and encourage more sustainable resource use. Tailoring these interventions to farmers’ environmental attitudes and risk perceptions may also improve their effectiveness and support broader collective efforts towards climate-resilient agriculture. This study explores how combining economic incentives and nudges can facilitate the adoption of climate change adaptation farming practices. The combined economic and behavioural analysis provides novel evidence to inform the design of more climate-resilient agricultural policies.

title: When AI takes control, who takes responsibility? Structural analysis of agentic AI risks in supply chains
abstract: Agentic AI systems execute procurement decisions, reroute shipments and renegotiate supplier contracts at speeds that preclude real-time human review. The existing literature offers limited analytical attention to the risks that arise when decision authority is delegated to agents. This paper develops a risk taxonomy for agentic AI in supply chains and traces the hierarchical dependencies and influence magnitudes among the identified risks. A systematic review of literature, analyzed through theories–characteristics–contexts–methods framework, produces the risk taxonomy. A hybrid modified total interpretive structural modeling and fuzzy decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory methodology is then applied to structured expert judgments to establish the causal hierarchy and quantify inter-risk influence. Three risks, namely workforce skill gap, data quality and reliability and ethical misalignment occupy the deepest level of the causal hierarchy. Lack of accountability and governance and data privacy emerge as terminal outcomes. All three analytical methods converge on a conclusion: agentic AI risks originate at the institutional layer, with technical risks acting as transmission mechanisms. The findings indicate that effective governance requires that workforce capability, data integrity and objective-function alignment are addressed before deployment. The stratified agentic AI governance framework is proposed that translates hierarchical structure into a sequenced intervention architecture, providing practitioners with governance priorities organized by risk-propagation logic. This paper contributes a systematically derived risk taxonomy and a causally weighted governance map for agentic AI risks in supply chains. Five propositions are derived from the causal structure and are advanced as a testable research agenda.

title: Commercial coconut farming as agribusiness investment in sub-Saharan Africa: empirical evidence of financial viability from Ghana’s Jomoro district
abstract: Perennial tropical cash crops in Sub-Saharan Africa attract significant policy interest yet suffer from a systematic absence of formal investment appraisal evidence. This study evaluates the financial viability and risk profile of establishing a 100-acre commercial coconut farm in Ghana’s Jomoro District, the country’s preeminent coconut-producing zone, generating replicable evidence to inform investment decisions, development finance targeting and agricultural sector policy across emerging economies. A mixed-methods investment appraisal framework integrates primary data from 23 structured key informant interviews, spanning farmers, input suppliers, equipment dealers and export agents with secondary macroeconomic data from the Ghana Statistical Service, Bank of Ghana, Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and Ghana Commodity Exchange. Five analytical techniques are applied: net present value (NPV), internal rate of return (IRR), benefit–cost ratio (BCR), simple and discounted payback period, and multi-scenario sensitivity analysis across revenue and cost perturbations of ±10% and ±20%. At a 25% discount rate, the project yields a positive NPV of GH₵5.07 million, an IRR of 38% and a profitability index (BCR) of 1.66, all substantially exceeding the cost-of-capital hurdle. The simple payback period is 5.3 years (discounted: 6.3 years). Despite cumulative pre-production losses of GH₵6.10 million during the four-year moratorium, the farm transitions to sustained profitability from Year 1, with net margins rising from 39% to 56% by Year 5. Sensitivity analysis identifies revenue volatility, not cost escalation, as the dominant risk driver. The analysis is grounded in 2025 price levels for a single agro-ecological zone. Future research should extend this framework to smallholder scales and across Ghana’s multiple coconut belts, and should incorporate climate risk modelling and longer-horizon projections that capture the full productive life of the palm. The 100-acre commercial farm model generates an estimated 31 permanent and 50 seasonal farm-level jobs, derived from the labour cost parameters in the financial model. The intercrop system further supports commodity exchange market participation. The study provides a financial foundation for designing inclusive investment models, including outgrower schemes and cooperatives that extend these benefits to smallholder households. Based on a systematic review of the perennial crop investment appraisal literature, this study addresses a critical regional evidence gap by providing the first comprehensive formal investment appraisal of commercial-scale coconut farming in West Africa. The concurrent treatment of debt service dynamics, intercrop revenue modelling, year-by-year moratorium discounting and multi-scenario sensitivity analysis under Ghanaian macroeconomic conditions constitutes a methodological contribution directly transferable to comparable perennial crop investment contexts across Sub-Saharan Africa.
