title: Who am I really talking to? Authenticity, transparency, and the case for “AI ticks” in AI-mediated communication
abstract: The growing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into everyday messaging systems is transforming the conditions under which interpersonal communication takes place. As AI-mediated communication (AI-MC) becomes increasingly seamless and context-sensitive, it blurs the boundary between human expression and algorithmic assistance. This development raises fundamental questions about potential challenges to authenticity in personal relationships and possible strategies to address them. In this regard, we make three main contributions. First, we offer a technically grounded analysis of emerging AI-MC architectures, distinguishing between external prompting, keyboard-level assistance, and fully integrated in-app co-authoring systems. Second, we develop a normative account of authenticity in AI-MC, understood as a second-person, relationship-sensitive notion, drawing on analytic theories of endorsement, relational normativity, and socially situated self-expression. On this basis, we argue that authenticity cannot be directly engineered by design, since it depends on reflective agency and context-dependent interpersonal obligations. Third, we advance a design-oriented proposal aimed at mitigating authenticity-related concerns without resorting to paternalistic restrictions: the introduction of optional and granular disclosure mechanisms (“AI ticks”) that allow users to signal the presence and degree of AI assistance in a context-sensitive manner. We argue that such forms of transparency function not as a substitute for authenticity, but as a pro-ethical condition that enables agents to negotiate authenticity-based obligations within their relationships. The analysis contributes to current debates on the ethics of AI-mediated communication and the conditions of responsible human–AI interaction.

title: A hybrid negative sampling strategy for landslide susceptibility assessment in mining area
abstract: Reliable delineation of non-landslide samples remains a challenge in data-driven landslide susceptibility assessment, particularly where landslide inventories are incomplete. This study proposes a hybrid negative sampling (HNS) strategy that integrates frequency ratio (FR)-based susceptibility pre-screening with SPY-based positive–unlabeled (PU) learning and differentiated instance weighting. Specifically, an initial pool of fuzzy negatives was derived from frequency ratio-based susceptibility indices, followed by the SPY algorithm to identify relatively high-confidence negative candidates. The integration of these two sources allows candidate negatives with different screening confidence levels to contribute to model training through distinct weights. Applied to Jiaokou County, a loess mining area in China (157 inventory-positive geological hazard records, 1,914 slope units), the methodology was evaluated using a common five-fold spatial holdout validation protocol with XGBoost and SVM, four baseline sampling strategies, and positive-to-negative ratios of 1:1 and 1:2. HNS achieved the highest mean ROC-AUC across all four classifier–ratio configurations, including 0.812 ± 0.041 for XGBoost and 0.797 ± 0.055 for SVM at 1:2, although its improvements over baseline strategies were modest and not statistically significant. Sensitivity and ablation analyses indicated that differentiated weighting primarily influenced the trade-offs among Recall, Precision, and Specificity, without consistently improving overall discrimination or area-based capture performance. Furthermore, SHAP analysis identified fractional vegetation cover (FVC), nighttime lights (NTL), and lithology as the leading contributors to model predictions rather than direct causal factors. Overall, HNS provides a structured approach to incorporating candidate negatives with different screening confidence levels, offering competitive predictive performance with application-dependent benefits and trade-offs.

GPCRAgent: an intelligent multi-agent platform integrating knowledge graphs and large language models for GPCR-targeted drug discovery.
abstract: INTRODUCTION G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are major therapeutic targets in drug discovery. However, systematic characterization of GPCR functions and ligand interactions remains constrained by the high cost and complexity of experimental approaches. Although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance in biomedical question answering, their direct application to GPCR research is limited by insufficient integration of structured domain knowledge and poor interpretability of generated inferences. OBJECTIVES This study aimed to develop an interpretable artificial intelligence framework for automated and traceable analysis of complex GPCR-related problems, and to evaluate its utility in GPCR knowledge reasoning, structural property interpretation, disease target prioritization and ligand recommendation. METHODS We developed GPCRAgent, a multi-agent artificial intelligence framework enabled by VecKG-CoReason, which integrates vector-based semantic retrieval with knowledge graph-guided collaborative reasoning. GPCRAgent was evaluated on benchmark tasks covering GPCR knowledge question answering, multiple-choice reasoning and structural property interpretation. Its practical utility was further assessed in an idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis case study, in which prioritized targets and ligand candidates were supported by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. RESULTS GPCRAgent achieved accuracies of 85 % in GPCR knowledge question answering, 90 % in multiple-choice reasoning and 83 % in structural property interpretation, outperforming general-purpose LLMs across benchmark tasks. In an idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis case study, GPCRAgent identified LPAR1 as the top candidate and prioritized potential ligands. In a separate renal fibrosis study, experimental evaluation of the optimized LPAR1 ligand in kidney organoids showed suppressed fibrosis-associated marker induction during IL-1β-induced fibrosis. These results illustrate how the platform integrates evidence for target prioritization and structure-based ligand assessment. To facilitate broader adoption, an online platform (https://cbcb.cdutcm.edu.cn/GPCRAgent/) was developed to support GPCR-related drug discovery. CONCLUSION By integrating structured knowledge retrieval with collaborative multi-agent reasoning, GPCRAgent provides an interpretable AI framework for evidence-based GPCR target prioritization, ligand recommendation, and decision support.

Altered effective connectivity during cognitive distancing in cognitive behavioral therapy nonresponders with depression
abstract: Background Approximately half of individuals with major depressive disorder (MDD) do not respond to cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT). Cognitive distancing is a reappraisal tactic central to CBT, and neural responses during reappraisal have been linked to psychotherapy outcome. We examined whether pretreatment effective connectivity during cognitive distancing was associated with CBT response in adults with MDD. Methods Seventy-seven outpatients with MDD (31 women) completed fMRI during a distancing task before 25 CBT sessions as part of the SPeED trial, which included a pre-CBT phase of exercise or waiting list. Dynamic causal modeling estimated effective connectivity within a 10-region network. Group differences were assessed with parametric empirical Bayes, and predictive utility was evaluated with leave-one-out cross-validation. Results Responders (n = 39) showed greater relative modulation along a dorsomedial-to-ventrolateral prefrontal-to-superior frontal/pre-supplementary motor area cascade during distancing, whereas nonresponders exhibited greater relative modulation of amygdala-to-ventrolateral prefrontal cortex connectivity. Nonresponders showed decreased dorsolateral prefrontal self-inhibition during negative picture processing, consistent with heightened local excitability. Distancing-related effects exceeded 99% posterior probability and predicted treatment response in cross-validation (r = .21–.31, p < .05). Conclusions Effective connectivity during distancing robustly differentiated responders from nonresponders, with nonresponders showing weaker intra-prefrontal control and stronger amygdala-to-prefrontal influence. These neural patterns contribute to insight into CBT nonresponse and suggest a mechanism associated with lowered symptom improvement through cognitive interventions. However, incremental predictive value beyond baseline clinical measures was modest. If replicated prospectively, such measures may contribute to multimodal prediction models and adjunctive treatment strategies. Clinical trials registration name Neurobiological correlates and mechanisms of the augmentation of psychotherapy with endurance exercise in mild to moderate depression – SPeED, http://apps.who.int/trialsearch/Trial2.aspx?TrialID=DRKS00008869, DRKS00008869.

title: Reservoir-Scale Heterogeneity in CO2 Geological Storage: A Review of Characterization, Mechanisms, Prediction, and Management with Future Perspectives
abstract: The large-scale deployment of CO2 geological storage imposes stringent requirements on injectivity, subsurface space utilization, and long-term safety, making reservoir-scale heterogeneity a critical constraint on engineering feasibility and storage reliability. However, existing studies have primarily focused on individual heterogeneity elements, localized storage processes, or specific spatial scales, while systematic understanding of the coupling among multiple structural types, cross-scale transfer, and their impacts throughout the storage lifecycle remains limited. Therefore, this study synthesizes experimental, modeling, field, and ML studies, distinguishing their evidence sources and validation limits, to summarize the origins, types, characterization methods, and quantitative indicators of heterogeneity and to compare approaches for geological modeling, probabilistic prediction, and engineering regulation. The reviewed literature indicates the influence of geological architecture and connectivity on preferential migration and plume distribution. Quantitative effects on pressure, capacity, and trapping remain dependent on site conditions and model assumptions. Based on the identified limitations, recommendations are proposed in eight areas: evaluation standards, multisource data integration, structural fidelity, scale correction, probabilistic prediction, dynamic updating, zonal injection, and intelligent regulation. These recommendations are aligned with the major challenges identified in this review, covering standardized evaluation, structural representation, uncertainty-aware prediction, adaptive management, and engineering regulation throughout the storage lifecycle. This study reveals the differentiated roles and dual effects of heterogeneous structures and provides a basis for reservoir screening, capacity and risk assessment, injection optimization, and long-term management.

title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
abstract: Exoplanet imaging is the main method for detailed characterization of planets orbiting beyond 1 au but it requires suppressing the bright glare of the star to see the faint planet light. As well as sophisticated instrumentation, effective image processing is necessary for starlight suppression, which continues to be a substantial limitation. Standard algorithms use reference images for starlight modelling and thus they are limited by inevitable telescope instabilities that change from reference to science observation. Addressing this challenge will increase the number of planets amenable to direct imaging and will be a notable step towards imaging exo-Earths with future observatories. Here we present a new physics-based method for starlight subtraction. Our method combines a multistep optimization with a flexible physical model to produce a starlight model, allowing modelling and compensation of instrument instabilities. We use automatic differentiation (autodiff) to optimize millions of model parameters. We demonstrate our method on observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Near-InfraRed Camera (NIRCam) coronagraph instrument. We achieve sensitivity 2-15 times superior to standard techniques, including the first detection of 51 Eridani b at 4.3 $μ$m. This is the first time, to our knowledge, that such an approach has demonstrated substantially improved sensitivity on real, on-sky coronagraphic imaging. Our framework can be extended to other current and future ground-based and space-based observatories, including the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), potentially relaxing the unprecedented stability requirements needed to make these a success.

title: Land fragmentation and agricultural commercialization: New insights from Cameroon
abstract: Land fragmentation (LF) is a salient feature of smallholder agriculture. However, its implications for agriculture and the livelihoods of smallholders remain ambiguous as studies report both negative and positive effects. In this study, we add to the literature by analyzing how LF is associated with agricultural commercialization, which has not been studied so far. This is important because commercialization is an essential facet of agricultural transformation with several implications for the livelihood of smallholders. Specifically, we hypothesize and test a potential non-linear relationship between LF and commercialization, using unique survey data from Cameroon. Estimating non-linear models, we find a robust non-linear (inverted U-shape) relationship between LF and commercialization. As LF starts increasing, it is initially associated with higher commercialization up to a threshold beyond which further increases in LF are associated with lower commercialization. We further show that the possible mechanisms through which LF operates are crop diversification and the use of modern inputs like pesticides and inorganic fertilizers, where we also find these inverted U-shape patterns. In addition to different U-shape tests that confirm these results, the results are also robust across different indicators of LF, different estimators, and are unlikely to be driven by unobserved factors. These findings suggest that LF could also have positive benefits and thus these patterns may be relevant for policy makers when designing consolidation policies. In addition, modeling the relationship between LF and other outcomes would provide more insights for targeted policies.

title: Automated Compliance Checking for BIM Models via a Large Language Model-Driven BIM-to-Text Paradigm
abstract: Automated compliance checking (ACC) for building information modeling (BIM) is a vital task in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. However, significant semantic gaps among Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) schemas, regulatory texts, and logical rules necessitate extensive manual intervention for domain-specific knowledge modeling and rule interpretation. Fully automated compliance checking for BIM models remains a challenging task. To address these issues, this study proposes an innovative BIM-to-text paradigm, which takes full advantage of the context understanding and generation capabilities of emerging large language models (LLMs). Unlike the existing mainstream methods, the original intention of our proposed method is to convert BIM semantic information into natural language descriptions, rather than converting the specification text into logical rules. First, regulatory entities and entity types are extracted from regulatory texts using LLMs with a self-correction mechanism. Second, we have designed a novel BIM parsing strategy and data storage schemes, and the LLM is used for semantic alignment between IFC entities and regulatory entities to identify BIM semantic fragments. Next, the BIM semantic fragments are converted into BIM description texts via LLM guided by the BIM-to-text motivation. Finally, the regulatory texts and the generated BIM description texts are fed into the LLM to infer the results of compliance checking. On the building BIM ACC data set and the bridge BIM ACC data set, our method achieves F1-scores of 95.70 and 96.13% in the end-to-end setting, respectively. The experimental results also indicate that the proposed framework can avoid complex ontology modeling and rule interpretation processes in the traditional semantic parsing–based BIM ACC methods, and achieves compliance checking with a higher level of automation. This work contributes a novel LLM-driven BIM-to-text paradigm for ACC.

title: Vision-Language Model-Based Demonstrators for Imitation Learning in Construction Robotic Timber Assembly
abstract: Intelligent construction robots are deemed the future of on-site construction for improved productivity and safety. To automate the construction process, imitation learning (IL) has been adopted to train construction robots in a repertoire of tasks. However, collecting demonstrations for robots to imitate from usually requires teleoperation setup and devices, such as virtual reality (VR) and gloves. To autonomously and efficiently generate demonstration data for imitation learning in construction tasks, we propose a large foundation model-based demonstration-generation framework, in which the Segment Anything Model (SAM) is used to extract geometric representations of objects of interest and a vision-language model (VLM), conditioned on mark-based visual prompting and languages, produces high-level action suggestions. As the demonstrator framework is imperfect and is computation-intensive to be fine-tuned, only successful episodes are retained automatically and structured into demonstrations for distilling a lightweight text-conditioned robot policy via behavioral cloning (BC). We evaluate the framework on a UR10 robot arm in Isaac Sim for a language-conditioned timber assembly task with frame pose randomization. The autonomous demonstrator achieves success rates ranging from 76.9% (small perturbations) to 33.7% (largest perturbations) but can be rolled out to curate balanced demonstration data sets. Policies distilled from these demonstrations attain 100% success across all three perturbation ranges and two placement scenarios, while retaining up to 70% success under modest out-of-distribution (OOD) frame poses. An ablation on the number of demonstrations shows that the distilled policies reach 100% success with only 70% of the data in low-variation settings but require about 90% of the data to achieve 100% success under larger workspace perturbations.

title: Cultural safety as clinical practice: an evidence-informed model for general practice training.
abstract: BACKGROUND Cultural safety is a core expectation of contemporary general practice and a critical component of high-quality care for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. It is defined by the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (Ahpra) as an ongoing, reflective practice that recognises power imbalances, addresses systemic racism, and is determined by the patient. Cultural safety remains difficult to operationalise within general practice education and assessment. Traditional training and assessment tools privilege observable behaviours and technical competence, offering limited capacity to evaluate reflexivity, power awareness, and relational trust. This study aimed to develop a community-informed framework and recommendations to guide the teaching, supervision, and assessment of cultural safety in general practice training. METHODS A multi-phase qualitative and consensus-development study was undertaken in Australian general practice settings. Data were drawn from interviews with general practitioners (GPs), GP registrars, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander participants; a modified nominal group technique incorporating yarning with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander participants; and a modified eDelphi process involving experts in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health, education, and community leadership. Findings from all phases were synthesised and aligned with the Ahpra definition of cultural safety to develop a consolidated framework. RESULTS The resulting framework articulates key knowledge domains, skills, and practising behaviours relevant to culturally safe general practice, while emphasising reflexivity, power awareness, and relational accountability. It identifies elements that may be meaningfully supported and assessed within training, highlights the central role of patient perspectives, and cautions against checklist-based approaches that risk undermining the relational nature of cultural safety. CONCLUSION This study presents a practical, evidence-informed framework and recommendations to support general practice training organisations, supervisors, and registrars in embedding cultural safety within clinical education and assessment. Grounded in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives and expert consensus, the framework offers guidance for moving beyond procedural approaches towards culturally safe practice as a relational, patient-determined process.

title: Perceived competitiveness as an antecedent of strategic governance: adaptive signals in Ibero-American MSMEs
abstract: This study analyzes whether current perceptions of business competitiveness are associated with the future strategic orientation of organizational governance in Ibero-American MSMEs, with an emphasis on Honduras. Unlike traditional approaches, this work inverts the analytical logic and examines perceived competitive signals (environment and internal performance) as antecedents of future corporate governance decisions. The research adopts a quantitative and explanatory-comparative approach, with data from the survey of the 2024 Ibero-American MSME Report by FAEDPYME (7,762 companies in 12 countries) (FAEDPYME 2024). The Perceived Business Competitiveness Index (PBCI), with environment and performance dimensions, and the Strategic Governance Perspective Index (SGPI), derived through (k-means) and distances to centroids, are constructed. The association is evaluated with OLS models with country fixed effects and robustness analysis with fractional models. The perception of internal performance is positively and statistically significantly associated with the future strategic orientation of governance, while the perception of the competitive environment does not present a significant association once business characteristics and country heterogeneity are controlled for. This pattern suggests that the future governance orientation (towards continuity, professionalization or succession) responds more to confidence in perceived internal capabilities than to the reading of external conditions. The Honduran subsample maintains the same direction for the performance component, although with lower statistical significance, while the environment component is also not significant in the Honduran case. The findings have differentiated implications for two audiences. For MSME managers, they suggest that governance decisions (continuity, professionalization and succession) are more linked to confidence in perceived internal performance than to the reading of the external environment, which invites strengthening internal capabilities as a basis for anticipatory strategic planning. For public policymakers and business support institutions, the results support the design of differentiated interventions according to the company's strategic profile, with special attention to MSMEs facing greater restrictions in internal capabilities. The study inverts the traditional logic by positioning perceived competitiveness as an antecedent and not as a result of the future strategic orientation of governance, opening an adaptive reading of the phenomenon. As a methodological contribution, it proposes the SGPI as a continuous indicator constructed through unsupervised learning.

title: Do financial analysts improve the quality of earnings forecasting? Evidence from Central Europe, 2014–2024
abstract: This study examines whether consensus analyst forecasts for annual earnings per share (EPS) are more accurate than a standard random walk (RW) model for companies listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange, the Prague Stock Exchange, the Budapest Stock Exchange and the Bucharest Stock Exchange during 2014–2024. Consensus analyst forecasts for annual EPS from EquityRT are compared against RW model predictions using mean arctangent absolute percentage error, mean absolute error and mean square error. Wilcoxon and permutation tests assess statistical significance. For the Warsaw Stock Exchange, which provides the largest sample, the analysis is further stratified by analyst coverage intensity, firm capitalization, industry classification, corporate governance structure, institutional ownership composition and dividend orientation. Robustness checks employ alternative error metrics across multiple dimensions. Consensus analyst forecasts for annual EPS demonstrate no statistically significant differentiation from RW predictions for Poland (excluding 2020), the Czech Republic (excluding 2020 and 2022), Hungary (excluding 2020) and Romania (excluding 2019 and 2022). This finding holds with respect to ownership structures and dividend policies. In the Polish market, for which detailed multi-dimensional analysis is provided, the absence of analyst advantages persists across annual periods, analyst coverage levels, firm sizes and industry groupings. These results challenge prior evidence of analyst superiority over statistical models in developed markets by drawing on a distinct market setting. This investigation provides the first rigorous statistical examination of analyst forecasting performance across the major Central European capital markets, offering broader empirical insights into the boundary conditions of analyst expertise. The findings challenge the universal applicability of analyst superiority documented in developed markets, demonstrating that consensus analyst judgment provides no measurable advantage over RW benchmarks for annual EPS forecasting when market conditions exhibit RW earnings behavior. These results carry immediate implications for global investment strategies and resource allocation decisions, suggesting that expenditures on equity research may be misallocated in markets where fundamental earnings unpredictability renders consensus analyst forecasts no more accurate than RW benchmarks for annual EPS.

title: Digital leapfrogging or digital divide? Internet penetration and structural transformation in Africa
abstract: This study aims to investigate whether digitalization accelerates structural transformation in African economies or reinforces existing structural inequalities. Using panel data on African countries and a rigorous fixed-effects framework, complemented by dynamic System GMM estimation, the analysis provides a direct test of the digital structural transformation hypothesis. The results show a strong and robust positive effect of internet penetration on structural transformation, even after controlling for key macroeconomic and demographic factors. Sectoral evidence reveals a clear mechanism: increased internet access reduces the share of agriculture while significantly expanding the services sector, confirming that digitalization actively reallocates economic activity across sectors. Crucially, interaction results show that the impact of internet penetration is stronger in slower-growing, less advanced economies, providing compelling evidence in favor of the digital leapfrogging hypothesis rather than the digital divide. These findings establish digital infrastructure as a central driver of modern structural change and suggest that expanding internet access can serve as a powerful policy tool for accelerating inclusive development in Africa.

title: Does agro-climatic vulnerability affect the crop insurance adoption in India?
abstract: To examine the effect of agricultural vulnerability to climate change on the adoption of crop insurance in India. The seasonal-agricultural vulnerability index (AVI) from climate change has been constructed at the district level for the entire country using satellite data, agricultural statistics and census parameters. Further household-level farmer data are obtained from the 77th Round of the Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households by NSSO to assess the effect of AVI on crop insurance adoption among the farmers cultivating paddy and wheat as one of their major crops. To address the issues of separation in the data, the firth logit model is employed for the empirical analysis. The results show that agricultural vulnerability positively influences the adoption of crop insurance among the agricultural households in India. The heterogeneity analysis reveals that households with large landholdings, higher education and awareness of the Minimum Support Price are more likely to have crop insurance. Adoption of insurance is lower among socially marginalized communities. Further, it notes that India has a significant area under agricultural climate vulnerability, and crop insurance adoption is very low at around 7%. This article presents insightful policy suggestions that policymakers should focus on promoting crop insurance in highly vulnerable regions and helping to enhance the risk mitigation capacity of farmers in India. The novelty of this article lies in its examination of how vulnerability to climate change affects the uptake of crop insurance as a means of alleviating the risks associated with climate change.

title: Climate conditions, financial uncertainty and market resilience in African equity markets: an event-driven probabilistic deep learning approach
abstract: This paper examines stock-market volatility in Egypt, Morocco, Nigeria, South Africa and Tunisia under geopolitical and financial uncertainty and physical climate conditions. African evidence rarely integrates event-time shock analysis with full-distribution forecasting while distinguishing physical climate signals from climate-related financial risk. The study develops an event-driven probabilistic framework grounded in a Climate–Market Conditioning Framework (CMCF). The study combines cumulative abnormal volatility (CAV) analysis with Mixture Density Network–Long Short-Term Memory (MDN-LSTM) volatility and return-density models. Daily market data from January 2015 to April 2025 are combined with Geopolitical Risk, Financial Stress Index and National Aeronautics and Space Administration Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources climate indicators. Forecasts use a strict chronological holdout and are compared with Generalised Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GARCH)(1,1)-Normal, GARCH(1,1)-Student-t, Exponential GARCH (EGARCH), Glosten–Jagannathan–Runkle-GARCH (GJR-GARCH), Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting. Distributional performance is additionally benchmarked against probabilistic GARCH using the weighted interval score (WIS). Shock responses are heterogeneous across markets. The four fixed global events provide descriptive economic differences but weak small-sample inference, whereas larger factor-specific event samples yield selected market-dependent effects. GARCH-family models remain stronger for point forecasts and GARCH-Normal also records lower WIS, while MDN-LSTM often produces lower-tail hit rates closer to the nominal 5% level. Distributional and Value-at-Risk diagnostics nevertheless show country-specific calibration limitations, especially in South Africa and Nigeria. The findings provide useful insights for investors, regulators, and policymakers by improving volatility monitoring, supporting tail-risk management, and informing macroprudential risk assessment in vulnerable financial markets. The evidence also supports integrating climate-sensitive volatility indicators into scenario analysis and sustainable-investment risk monitoring, while avoiding causal policy claims that are not identified by the forecasting design. The paper integrates event-based volatility analysis with probabilistic forecasting in African equity markets and develops a Climate–Market Conditioning Framework. The framework distinguishes physical climate conditions from climate-related financial risk and proposes that financial consequences are conditioned by market structure, liquidity, international integration and adaptive investor behaviour rather than being uniform or mechanically causal.

title: When sustainability backfires: Gen Z’s perceptions of greenwashing and trust in corporate campaigns
abstract: Corporate sustainability initiatives have come under growing criticism for greenwashing practices that undermine the credibility of sustainability marketing and erode consumer trust. This study aims to explore how Generation Z consumers in Vietnam differentiate between authentic sustainability claims and greenwashing signals in digital marketing communications. A qualitative research design was adopted using semi-structured interviews with 15–20 Generation Z participants aged 18–27 in Vietnam. Data were analyzed using a hybrid inductive-deductive thematic analysis approach. The findings reveal that Gen Z consumers rely strongly on evidence-based cues such as quantified environmental impact, third-party certifications and transparency signals to assess authenticity. In contrast, vague claims and aesthetic “green” imagery without supporting evidence trigger skepticism and perceptions of greenwashing. This study contributes to the literature by proposing a cue-based process model explaining how Gen Z forms green trust in digital marketing environments.

title: Phagocytosis activity is retained by JMML macrophages and increased by CD47 inhibition.
abstract: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukaemia (JMML) is a childhood myeloid malignancy driven by RAS (rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog) pathway mutations, characterized by myeloid cell accumulation and organ infiltration. We investigated how clonal macrophage polarization, phagocytic function and CD47 (cluster of differentiation 47) expression contribute to immune dysregulation. Human PTPN11 (protein tyrosine phosphatase non-receptor type 11) -mutated JMML spleens exhibited higher M1-like macrophage levels than KRAS (KRAS proto-oncogene, GTPase)-mutated cases or controls. Both human JMML macrophages and murine cells from Mx-Cre;Ptpn11D61Y/+ mice retained phagocytic activity, with M1-like cells being the most active. CD47, a 'don't eat me' signal, was upregulated in human and murine JMML cells; its blockade enhanced in vitro phagocytosis. In a patient-derived xenograft model, the CD47 inhibitor magrolimab reduced leukaemia burden in the spleen but not the bone marrow. No synergy was observed between magrolimab and azacitidine. These findings demonstrate that clonal JMML macrophages retain phagocytic activity and contribute to an inflammatory phenotype. While CD47 blockade shows limited therapeutic potential, this study clarifies the interplay between macrophage polarization, immune evasion and inflammation, providing a basis for future JMML strategies.

title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Optimize Ecological Restoration for Climate and Biodiversity
abstract: The restoration of degraded ecosystems is critical for mitigating climate change and reversing biodiversity loss. Depending on the primary objective—such as maximizing carbon sequestration or protecting threatened species—and within the boundaries of budget limitations, different spatial priorities have been identified at global and regional scales. Funding mechanisms to support such work comprise public sources, philanthropy, and the private sector, including the sale of carbon and biodiversity credits. However, effectively exploring trade‐offs among restoration objectives and estimating the price of biodiversity and carbon credits to design financially viable projects remains scientifically challenging. Here we harness the power of artificial intelligence implemented in the software CAPTAIN to identify spatial priorities for ecological restoration that maximize multiple objectives at once and to allow a robust evaluation of biodiversity and climate outcomes. We find through a series of simulations that even low‐to‐moderate consideration of biodiversity in the design of restoration projects leads to the selection of restored areas that disproportionately improve the conservation of threatened species, while the carbon captured is only slightly reduced. We propose the bundling of biodiversity and carbon credits to support restoration efforts even in areas previously excluded for economic reasons. Applying our methodology to plant diversity in the Atlantic Forest of eastern South America, one of the most biodiverse and threatened ecosystems globally, we demonstrate its potential to guide restoration and to quantify trade‐offs between multiple optimization scenarios. Our study provides a robust, scalable method to maximize the joint benefits of ecological restoration for climate and nature.

title: Protected Areas Reduce Heat Exposure in Squamates Globally
abstract: Protected areas (PAs) are central to biodiversity conservation, yet their capacity to buffer species from climate‐driven heat exposure, that is, the duration and frequency of exposure to temperatures exceeding species' critical thermal limits, remains poorly quantified at global scales. Here, we assessed whether squamate reptiles inside PAs experience lower heat exposure than conspecifics in unprotected, human‐modified landscapes, and how this buffering effect varies across latitudes, biomes, and evolutionary lineages. Using biophysical modelling of operative temperatures across 248 species, we show that PAs consistently reduced both annual hours above critical thermal maximum (CT max ) and the frequency of critical days under current and future climatic scenarios (+2°C and + 4°C). We found that under current climate, protected sites had 51 fewer hours above CT max and 3.5 fewer critical days than unprotected sites, and the proportional reduction persisted under +2°C and + 4°C warming scenarios. The buffering effect was most pronounced at low latitudes and tropical biomes, where species already operate close to their thermal limits. Deserts and xeric shrublands, together with tropical grasslands and savannas, emerged as biomes with elevated heat exposure, reinforcing growing concern for arid‐zone reptiles under climate change. Substantial phylogenetic signal in heat exposure indicated that evolutionary history shapes thermal vulnerability beyond geography and biome alone, with the magnitude of PA buffering varying considerably across squamate lineages. Our findings demonstrate that PAs can provide refugia from heat exposure, and that their conservation value under climate change depends on the retention of structurally complex habitats and thermally heterogeneous microhabitats.

title: UniHam: A Large-Scale SOC-Complete Dataset and Benchmark for Hamiltonian Learning in Materials
abstract: Accurate prediction of electronic Hamiltonians would enable broad property inference while avoiding the high computational cost of Density Functional Theory (DFT). However, progress toward general-purpose materials foundation models is limited by a data bottleneck: existing Hamiltonian datasets are typically small, lack structural diversity, and often omit essential relativistic physics such as spin--orbit coupling (SOC). We therefore construct UniHam, a large-scale Hamiltonian dataset and benchmark suite comprising 100,000+ DFT-computed complex-valued Hermitian Hamiltonians with full SOC, covering 72 elements and a wide range of crystal geometries and symmetries (spanning diverse lattice types and space-group families). Building on UniHam, we benchmark two representative state-of-the-art models under a standardized protocol and introduce complementary evaluation metrics that jointly assess three dimensions: (i) Hamiltonian reconstruction accuracy, (ii) out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization across composition/symmetry shifts, and (iii) the ability to support downstream property prediction from the predicted Hamiltonians. Experiments on UniHam demonstrate that the proposed benchmark and metrics effectively differentiate model capabilities, revealing intrinsic SOC- and element-dependent failure modes, large variations in compositional OOD robustness, and the necessity of spectral-level evaluation to assess whether Hamiltonian predictions reliably support downstream electronic-structure properties. Overall, UniHam provides a reproducible, SOC-complete benchmark that can sharpen model comparisons and accelerate the development of next-generation foundation models for quantum materials.

title: When Agents Have Faces: Deepfake Avatars, Emotion Signals, and Strategic Trust in Human–LLM Interaction
abstract: AI systems are increasingly presented through faces, voices, and emotional displays, making the interface part of the social and strategic context in which users make decisions. While anthropomorphic design is often assumed to increase trust, this assumption is less clear in mixed-motive settings where cooperation, coordination, and bargaining depend on perceived intent. We study this problem in a two-phase incentivized experiment in which participants interact with frontier LLM agents through a text-only interface, a cartoon avatar, or a photorealistic deepfake avatar. The study included 246 participants and focused on three canonical games: the Prisoner’s Dilemma, Battle of the Sexes, and the Ultimatum Game. The agents were powered by GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro, or Claude Opus 4.7, with one model fixed for each participant throughout the experiment. In the avatar conditions, agents can autonomously select emotional states that are rendered through speech and facial animation. We find that embodiment does not produce a uniform trust effect: avatar conditions are associated with different patterns of cooperation, exploitation, coordination, and bargaining behavior. Emotional expression is likewise associated with different human responses across the two avatar implementations: negative affect under the photorealistic implementation is associated with a larger reduction in human cooperation than under the cartoon implementation. These results show that avatar implementation and affective display are strategically consequential interface choices, while the present design does not isolate visual realism or emotional display as independent causal factors.

title: Differentiable Rendering for Specular Materials via Projected Specular Manifolds
abstract: Physics-based differentiable rendering computes derivatives of radiometric measures with respect to scene parameters. A key challenge lies in handling scene discontinuities from geometries, materials, and other factors. These discontinuities lead to a unique boundary integral defined on discontinuity curves. While occlusion-induced discontinuities have been well studied, those caused by materials, especially specular materials, remain largely unexplored. Specular bidirectional scattering distribution functions (BSDFs) contain Dirac delta distributions arising from the laws of perfect reflection or refraction, which constrain light path geometry and restrict the path integral to the specular manifold. The specular manifold is defined by geometric constraints and lacks explicit location, making the evaluation of discontinuity curves challenging. To address this, our key insight is that we can locate the specular manifold without explicit computation by projecting it onto a subregion of a specular object, which we call the projected specular manifold (PSM). After projection, while exact locations of discontinuity curves remain unknown, we can adopt the warped-area reparameterization to convert the boundary integral into an interior integral over the surface, avoiding the need to precisely locate these curves. The key challenge of this reparameterization is constructing an additional velocity field. For this, our key observation is that for a specular path, the distances from vertices to manifold boundaries and associated velocities are known. Therefore, we propose a simple but practical direct-interpolation-based method to construct the velocity. Furthermore, we extend the warped-area sampling to handle visibility boundaries with specular BSDFs and generalize our method to glossy materials. Our computed derivatives match references with minor additional computational cost, and can successfully drive gradient-based optimization tasks like shape and position estimation. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/Rhythm25/PSM.

title: End-to-End Motion Capture for Arbitrary Skeletons
abstract: Recent methods for arbitrary-skeleton motion capture from monocular video [Gong et al. 2026] follow a factorized pipeline, where a Video-to-Pose network predicts joint positions and an analytical inverse-kinematics (IK) stage recovers joint rotations. While effective, this design is inherently limited, since joint positions do not fully determine rotations and leave degrees of freedom such as bone-axis twist ambiguous, and meanwhile the non-differentiable IK stage prevents the system from adapting to noisy predictions or optimizing for the final animation objective. In this work, we instead present the first fully end-to-end framework, where both Video-to-Pose and Pose-to-Rotation are learnable and jointly optimized. Crucially, we observe that the ambiguity in pose-to-rotation mapping arises from missing coordinate-system information, as the same joint positions can correspond to different rotations under different rest poses and local axis conventions, and to resolve this we introduce a reference pose-rotation pair from the target asset, which together with the rest pose not only anchors the mapping but also defines the underlying rotation coordinate system. This turns rotation prediction into a well-constrained conditional problem and enables effective learning. In addition, our model predicts joint positions directly from video without relying on mesh intermediates, which improves both robustness and efficiency, and both stages share a skeleton-aware Global-Local Graph-Guided Multi-Head Attention (GL-GMHA) module for joint-level local reasoning and global coordination. Experiments on Truebones Zoo and Objaverse show that our method reduces rotation error from ~17° to ~10°, and to 6.54° on unseen skeletons, while achieving ~20× faster inference than mesh-based pipelines. Code, data, and an interactive Hugging Face demo will be available at https://animotionlab.github.io/MoCapAnythingV2/.

title: Dirichlet Splatting: Differentiable Rendering for Wave-Based Inverse Problems
abstract: We present Dirichlet Splatting , a physically grounded differentiable rendering method for inverse problems with wave-based coherent sensors. Unlike optical cameras, these sensors observe a scene in a band-limited Fourier space whose continuous point response is complex-valued and oscillatory. Our key observation is that the point spread function of a reflector in this Fourier space is the Dirichlet kernel , not a Gaussian. We instantiate each splat as a Dirichlet kernel in closed form, model each primitive as a planar surfel rendered through a surfel-aware Dirichlet splat whose complex amplitude is set by wave propagation physics, and introduce a sliding Frank-Wolfe adaptation tailored to the rugged, non-convex landscape that the Dirichlet oscillation induces. On terahertz tomography, Dirichlet Splatting recovers reflector geometry with an order of magnitude fewer parameters, faster convergence, and higher accuracy than 3D Gaussian Splatting.

title: Metalog Materials
abstract: A central aspect of modern physically based rendering is the practical yet realistic modeling of material appearance, which requires efficient and accurate representations of bidirectional reflectance distribution functions (BRDFs). In this paper, we present a unified material reflectance representation based on metalog distributions. Introducing quantile-based metalog interpolation and metalog mixture models, our representation captures a wide range of complex reflectance behaviors of both analytic models and real-world materials, while remaining interpretable and efficient. Our approach achieves competitive runtime performance and a small memory footprint, while enabling continuous interpolation between fundamentally different reflectance behaviors. Furthermore, our model is fully differentiable with respect to the coefficients defining the distributions, thus easily integrates into existing differentiable rendering pipelines. In summary, metalog materials can effectively represent real-world reflectance data, interpolate between multiple materials within a unified representation, and be acquired from real-world images via differentiable rendering.

title: Learned pi metalens for wide-field-of-view near-infrared imaging
abstract: Wide—field-of-view (FoV) near-infrared (NIR) imaging is vital for compact augmented reality and robotic systems. Conventional wide-FoV optics rely on bulky compound refractive optics, limiting miniaturization. Metalenses composed of sub-wavelength meta-atoms offer a compact alternative. However, achieving high transmission and complete 2π phase coverage simultaneously over wide angle-of-incidence (AOI) remains challenging, leading to blur and non-uniform efficiency across the field. Here, we present a learned π metalens based on an AOI-aware design framework that achieves uniform-quality 100° FoV NIR imaging. Rather than enforcing full 2π phase control, we leverage meta-atoms that maintain high-transmission across wide angular ranges, which inherently exhibit restricted phase coverage. To design such a phase-limited metalens, we introduce a differentiable phase-limited metalens representation that incorporates the AOI-aware vectorial response of meta-atoms. This effectively learns a metalens using phase-limited high-transmission meta-atoms, yielding improvements in focusing efficiency and image sharpness across a wide FoV. Our learned π metalens demonstrates a 14% improvement in modulation transfer function at the largest AOI and a 2.4x enhancement in focusing-efficiency uniformity compared to conventional quadratic 2π metalenses. Our results suggest that, when AOI-dependent responses are properly modeled, complete 2π phase coverage is not strictly required for high-performance wide-FoV metalenses, opening new opportunities for compact NIR imaging systems in robotics, human-computer interaction, and eye-tracking in extended reality systems.

title: ABACUS: Adapting Unified Foundation Model for Count Image Understanding and Generation
abstract: We present ABACUS, a unified vision-language model that jointly addresses object counting, crowd counting, referring-expression counting, and count-faithful image generation within a single 3B-parameter model. ABACUS introduces three contributions: density-aware adaptive zooming paired with an objectness map from multi-head self-attention decomposition to spatially ground count predictions; a boundary-aware count policy trained via GRPO with nested local, boundary, and global rewards to eliminate over- and undercounting at crop boundaries; and a cycle-consistent GRPO strategy in which the frozen understanding branch scores generated candidates on count-deviation and aesthetic quality, closing the understanding-generation synergy gap without any external critic or annotation. ABACUS achieves state-of-the-art results across seven benchmarks spanning object counting (FSC-147, CARPK), crowd counting (ShanghaiTech A/B), referring-expression counting (REC-8K), count-faithful generation (CoCo-Count, T2I-CompBench, GenEval), and count reasoning (CountQA), surpassing both task-specific specialists and larger generalist models. Project page is at https://mondalanindya.github.io/pages/ABACUS/.

title: Rethinking Network Foundation Models: From Bigger Models to Better Data
abstract: Network foundation models (NFMs) report high accuracy on traffic tasks, yet diagnostic studies keep finding that this accuracy rests on shortcuts: artifacts of how the training data was collected. The usual response to a weak model is a bigger one, and better evaluation and better architectures both hold the training data fixed. We argue that the lever is the data. A trace's network context is the set of factors that generated it: the application, the transport, and the network conditions. A good NFM is a minimal sufficient representation of network context: it preserves those factors and spends the least data and model capacity needed to do so. We show, in one setting, that better data helps. A semantically deduplicated pre-training set one-tenth the size of a campus corpus matches the full corpus and beats an equal-size random sample on context preservation (how much of the network context the model keeps). Obtaining better data is a search over which traces to select and which conditions to generate, where selection is generation limited to what was already collected. Composing real application, transport, and network components makes controlled generation cheap and produces the bytes and headers an NFM reads as in deployment. One context-preservation objective can then decide which data to keep and how much model capacity to retain; the search and the capacity choice remain proposals. For the factors it can specify, networking can pursue minimal sufficiency more directly than most domains, because it can generate traffic through the stack it deploys and check what a representation kept against the conditions it specified.

Terminal differentiation program of CD8 T cells guides immunotherapeutic options for CLL patients.
abstract: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) remains incurable and autologous T-cell-based therapies induce durable remissions in only a minority of patients. Although poor T-cell performance in CLL has been attributed to exhaustion, T cells from CLL patients retain cytokine production and lack key transcriptional markers of exhaustion, suggesting an alternative state of differentiation. Here, we performed an integrated phenotypic, epigenetic and functional analysis of circulating CD8⁺ T cells from treatment-naive CLL patients to define the nature and therapeutic relevance of terminal differentiation in CLL. CD8⁺ T cells from treatment-naive CLL patients were enriched for a terminally differentiated, CD27⁻CD28⁻CD57⁺KLRG1⁺ population with several senescence-associated features, including increased cell size, granularity, β-galactosidase activity, and reduced basal autophagy. However, these cells lacked key hallmarks of irreversible senescence. Instead, CLL T cells mounted robust but transient proliferative bursts and developed activation-associated γH2AX signals followed by impaired persistence and increased cell death upon repeated activation. Especially CD57⁺ T cells were vulnerable and incompatible with the experimental steps required for CAR T-cell manufacturing. The potent, acute effector function of these cells could, however, be harnessed by bispecific T-cell engagers, which induced effective cytolysis of both cell lines and primary CLL targets by these T cells. Collectively, our data support a model in which CD8+ T-cell dysfunction in CLL reflects accumulation of short-lived, terminally differentiated effector cells rather than canonical exhaustion or irreversible senescence. This state limits durable persistence required for CAR T-cell approached while preserving acute cytotoxicity relevant for bispecific antibody-based therapies in CLL.

title: Contrasting patterns of herb-layer diversity and their environmental correlates in evergreen coniferous and deciduous broadleaf forests: evidence from Mount Lao, China
abstract: Evergreen coniferous forests and deciduous broadleaf forests in the warm-temperate zone of northern China exhibit fundamentally distinct environmental and spatial correlates of understory herb-layer diversity across α- and β-diversity dimensions. Canopy cover correlates with α-diversity in coniferous forests, while soil organic matter correlates with richness in deciduous broadleaf forests. For β-diversity, compositional turnover correlates primarily with soil pH in coniferous forests but with available potassium in deciduous broadleaf forests, with geographic distance (dispersal limitation) contributing substantially in both. Understory herb layers harbor over 80% of vascular plant diversity in temperate forests and serve as early indicators of ecosystem dynamics. While evergreen coniferous forests (ECF) and deciduous broadleaf forests (DBF) differ fundamentally in microenvironmental conditions (transmitted irradiance, litter dynamics, and soil properties), few studies have systematically compared how these contrasting systems shape herb-layer diversity within homogeneous climatic regions. This study aimed to quantify whether and how the environmental and spatial correlates of α- and β-diversity in understory herb-layer communities differ between warm-temperate ECF and DBF from China, and to identify forest-type-specific management implications for biodiversity conservation. Using vegetation surveys, soil sampling, and advanced modeling (GAMM and GDM) across 69 forest plots on Mount Lao, China (36°05′–36°19′ N, 120°24′–120°42′ E), we assessed how herbaceous community assembly differs between the two forest types across multiple diversity dimensions. The two forest types harbored distinct compositions (15 species exclusive to ECF, 23 to DBF). In ECF, species richness showed a significant unimodal relationship with canopy cover (optimal at 0.6–0.7), whereas DBF richness declined with increasing soil organic matter. Overstory diversity was positively correlated with herbaceous richness in both systems. For β-diversity, soil pH was the strongest predictor of compositional turnover in ECF, while available potassium was the strongest predictor in DBF. Both forest types displayed strongest distance–decay relationships within 0–15 km, consistent with joint contributions of environmental filtering and dispersal limitation. Divergent canopy–soil interactions suggest that differentiated management approaches may be beneficial: in ECF, maintaining canopy cover within the observed optimal range (0.6–0.7) may support higher richness, whereas in DBF, management could emphasize nitrogen mitigation and soil carbon regulation through mixed-species plantations, which may help maintain species evenness. As these inferences derive from correlative analyses at a single local scale, they should be treated as hypotheses to be tested rather than general prescriptions.

title: Foresight and governance of complexity in the era of AI
abstract: Today’s challenges address a multitude of interconnected agents, resulting in complex systems whose evolution is difficult to predict. Policy makers are asking scientists to identify future scenarios and provide different solutions. The European Union has recognised in foresight a strategic process to support decisions. We show that foresight, governance and lobby are intertwined, and we assign an increased relevance to foresight when dealing with the uncertainty of the evolution of the socio-economic systems. To tackle the complexity in governance and decision processes, we describe an operational methodology named CLEVER to facilitate the problem setting and identification of the most appropriate mode of governance. It can be also adopted to analyse scenarios and their dynamics. CLEVER is based on a logical scheme, thus not dependent on the rapid evolution of tools empowering the information retrieval and future orienteering. We also reflect on the role of AI as an emergent technology, already having an impact on many of the involved processes.

title: From prediction to demographic plausibility: a critical review of machine and deep learning in longevity modeling
abstract: Longevity forecasting lies at the intersection of demography, public policy, and actuarial science, yet the recent expansion of machine and deep learning methods has been markedly uneven across these fields. This article offers a selective and critical review of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) applications to mortality and longevity modeling, with particular attention to the contrast between demographic and actuarial uses. On this basis, the paper asks whether a productive collaboration between demography and deep learning remains possible, and argues that it does—provided that applications are problem-driven, interpretable by design, uncertainty-aware, and validated against demographic criteria rather than predictive accuracy alone. The most promising path for demography lies not in the wholesale adoption of black-box predictors, but in the development of hybrid and demographically grounded models capable of combining flexibility, interpretability, and substantive relevance.

title: A Computational Brainsphere Model for the Simulation of Alzheimer's Disease
abstract: Nowadays, there are different medical imaging techniques to collect data about the progression of Alzhei\-mer's disease in a patient's brain. These data describe different phenomena which are still not understood from a biological point of view. How can these data sets be combined in a mathematical model to simulate the evolution of such a neurodegenerative disease in a computer? In this snapshot, we present one possible approach to address this task with the help of graph theory and partial differential equations.

title: Impact of built environment in mountainous aging communities on spatiotemporal behavioural differentiation among older persons: a geospatial analysis
abstract: As demographic aging deepens, the conflict between efficiency of public space resource allocation in mountainous communities and the diverse needs of older persons becomes more prominent. Understanding the adaptability between space and behaviour is crucial for identifying the built environment characteristics associated with the older persons’ outdoor activities for targeted environmental interventions. This study focuses on 42 public spaces in Chongqing, a typical mountainous city in China. From the perspectives of spatial layout and design, it establishes a connection between the public space environment and the characteristics of the older persons’ outdoor activities. Spatial clustering is used to explore the spatiotemporal aggregation of the older persons’ activities, and multiple linear regression models are employed to quantify the associations between environmental factors and the older persons’ behaviours. The results aim to match spatial environments with the activity requirements of older persons, providing evidence for optimising age-friendly built environment upgrades.
journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Urban Design and Planning

title: Climate footprint in arid Tunisia: cropping systems, crop pattern and crop water productivity
abstract: Tunisia is recognized as vulnerable to climate change impact, ranked 64th out of 187 countries in the 2022 ND-GAIN Index. With less than 150 mm mean annual rainfall, irrigation becomes essential in arid regions. Additional water supply was estimated between 2970 and 9730 m 3 /ha. Crop water productivity (CWP) was high in mulberry and pomegranate (CWP > 1.5 kg/m3), while low values were recorded in species like pistachio, olives and date palm (CWP ≤ 0.5 kg/m3). In palm groves, appropriate water management systems could save until 620 m 3 /ha by a 10% increase in CWP. For olive tree, CWP can be amplified by creation of medium- to high-density orchards, reducing tree spacing within the row. Warm temperatures during the chilling period of dormancy led to the limitation of suitable land for pome fruits’ growing and accentuating alternate bearing in some nut crops. Scion/rootstock combinations are under test for better growth and yield performances. The national strategy should focus on cultivating crops with low chill needs and reduced water consumption. Biodiversity in-situ should be enhanced to promote sustainability and resilience of fruit cropping systems in dry lands.

title: Warp-Geo: Differentiable Geometry Representation for Dynamic-Boundary Simulation and Shape Optimization
abstract: Modern inverse problems and adaptive simulations require efficient and differentiable representations of complex geometries that can be updated frequently for gradient-based optimization. Existing methods cannot simultaneously achieve both. We present Warp-Geo, a differentiable GPU-accelerated framework for reconstructing signed distance fields and evaluating surface normals from point clouds of complex 3D geometries. Warp-Geo combines uniform grids for GPU parallelism with implicit differentiation through the Poisson solve, enabling frequent geometry recomputation while maintaining full differentiability. We demonstrate Warp-Geo on forward SDF reconstruction, dynamic fluid--structure interaction with moving boundaries, and inverse shape optimization via automatic differentiation with gradient validation. GPU scalability analysis confirms practical feasibility for frequent geometry updates. The framework, implemented in Warp and JAX, enables seamless integration with differentiable physics solvers for end-to-end shape optimization.

title: Modeling and simulation methods used in the maritime industry: evolution, applications and future perspectives
abstract: Modeling and simulation (M&S) techniques have evolved from optional engineering tools to indispensable pillars of modern maritime practice. This article presents a comprehensive systematic review of the most important modeling and simulation methodologies applied to maritime industry processes, including workflows for ship design, shipyard fabrication and construction, port and terminal operations, vessel traffic management, maintenance scheduling, supply chain logistics, and risk management procedures. The study demonstrates that M&S techniques enable safer, more efficient, and more environmentally sustainable operations, validated by scientific standards. The COVID-19 pandemic served as a critical catalyst, consolidating the strategic value of M&S as a central component of maritime resilience and innovation. This research traces the evolution of M&S adoption from 2010 to 2025, identifying four dominant research directions: maritime simulators, computational fluid dynamics (CFD)/finite element analysis (FEA), digital twins, and artificial intelligence-based methods. The analysis reveals that while traditional approaches dominated the 2010-2020 period, emerging technologies—particularly digital twins and AI-based methods—have accelerated exponentially since 2020, reflecting the maritime industry's accelerated digitalization. Forward projections through 2035 indicate that AI-based methodologies will experience the highest growth rate at approximately 329%, followed by digital twins at 147%, underscoring the fundamental transformation of maritime research and practice. The integration of these advanced modeling approaches offers optimal equilibrium between physical precision and computational efficiency for addressing complex maritime challenges.

title: Staging, workup, neoadjuvant/adjuvant therapy, and treatment options for cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) is the second most common skin cancer worldwide and represents a growing source of morbidity and mortality. Incidence continues to rise globally, driven by an aging population, cumulative ultraviolet exposure, and increasing prevalence of high-risk patient populations. While most cSCCs follow an indolent course, a clinically meaningful subset can demonstrate aggressive behavior, highlighting the need for accurate risk stratification and individualized management strategies. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence regarding the clinical presentation, tumor biology, diagnostic evaluation, staging systems, and treatment paradigms for cSCC with emphasis on emerging prognostic tools shaping future care. We summarize key clinical and histopathologic features associated with adverse outcomes, including depth of invasion, differentiation, and perineural involvement, and review current imaging and nodal assessment strategies. Staging frameworks, including American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC), Brigham and Women's Hospital (BWH), and evolving stages of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) systems, are discussed alongside newer models such as risk-integrated squamous cell carcinoma staging, which aim to improve outcome discrimination. Treatment approaches encompassing surgery, radiation therapy, and systemic immunotherapy are reviewed, with particular attention to risk-adapted use of Mohs micrographic surgery, adjuvant radiation therapy (ART), and neoadjuvant or definitive programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1) blockade for advanced disease. Finally, we examine emerging molecular prognostic assays, including gene expression profiling (GEP), that offer biologic insight beyond traditional clinicopathologic factors and may refine decisions regarding surveillance and treatment escalation. As the burden of cSCC continues to expand, integrated frameworks incorporating clinical, histopathologic, and molecular data will be essential for optimizing outcomes while minimizing patient and system-level burdens, particularly for identifying tumors requiring treatment escalation.

title: DreamLander: A 6-DOF World Model based Reinforcement Learning Planetary Lander
abstract: Soft powered descent landings are becoming evermore important in the field of space exploration and scientific advancement, because of their ability to deliver mission critical payloads, both highly accurately and safely. The high efficiency restriction on planetary landings due to the severely limited fuel supply results in the need for optimal guidance trajectories and control. Model based reinforcement learning is proving to be an important tool in simplifying the highly complex process of generating optimal guidance trajectories and control. In this work, we present DreamLander, a state of the art model based reinforcement learning algorithm based on DreamerV3, to generate optimal guidance and control for a realistic 6 degree of freedom entry descent landing problem. The model based approach creates a sample efficient and highly generalizable model that can be applied to a variety of scenarios whilst maintaining a high degree of accuracy, landing within 2 meters of the designated landing zone, and with velocity norm less than 0.3 meters per second. DreamLander makes use of state sensor observations, making progress toward End-to-End solutions of the Entry Descent Landing problem.

title: Differentiable Search of Compositionally Complex Alloys
abstract: Identifying solid-solution compositions in multicomponent alloys requires exploring a highdimensional design space while accounting for competing phases. We present a differentiable search framework that uses composition gradients of a thermodynamic objective to identify promising alloy regions without exhaustive grid enumeration. In the present implementation, an alchemical machine-learning interatomic potential and ideal configurational entropy provide a differentiable free-energy approximation for random solid solutions. Gradient-based optimization is combined with metadynamics biasing to explore multiple basins, and a tangent-plane criterion screens candidates against precipitation of competing compounds. Applied to the Mg–Al–Sc–Ti–V–Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni system on fcc, bcc, and hcp lattices at 1000 and 1600 K, the search recovers compositionally complex alloy (CCA) families supported by literature. The dominant Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni candidate region expands at 1600 K to include V-containing families and six-principal-element compositions. Screened compositions show substantial departures from equimolarity, highlighting the value of continuous composition optimization. The search also identifies the less-explored Mg–Sc–Ti system, for which preliminary CALPHAD calculations suggest extended high-temperature bcc solid-solution fields under suitable pressure conditions. These results demonstrate a framework for efficient search of CCAs and illustrate how differentiable materials models can serve directly as tools for materials design.

title: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning and Gradient Boosting for Student Dropout Prediction on OULAD
abstract: Student dropout in e-learning remains a persistent problem, and the belief that deep learning outperforms conventional methods has rarely been tested on large, real data. This study compares five models: Random Forest, XGBoost, a convolutional neural network (CNN), a long short-term memory (LSTM) network, and a hybrid CNN-LSTM, for dropout prediction on the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD), covering 32,593 students with 21 aggregated features shared by all models. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) was applied within each fold of a 5-fold stratified cross-validation, and the best model was explained with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and converted into a three-tier Early Warning System (EWS). XGBoost reached the highest accuracy (86.77%) and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9442, ahead of the hybrid CNN-LSTM (accuracy 85.36%, AUC 0.9328). The gap had a large effect size (Cohen's dz = -1.06) but was not significant (p = 0.077). SHAP identified active span as the strongest predictor, and the EWS flagged 10,180 students as high-risk. External validation on an independent public dataset reproduced the ranking (XGBoost AUC 0.923; deep models mean AUC 0.879). Interpretable gradient boosting therefore matches or exceeds deep learning on tabular data.

title: Multi-crop disease classification using a Dilateformer-MobileNetV2 dual-branch fusion network
abstract: Multi-crop disease classification requires discrimination among visually similar symptoms. This study evaluates late feature fusion of Dilateformer and MobileNetV2 for 45-class image classification. The two pooled representations are concatenated before classification. The original experiment achieved 97.21% Top-1 accuracy and 96.63% macro F1 on a 59,905-image benchmark. During revision, PlantDoc-derived samples were added to the existing collection to broaden image diversity. On this expanded 68,682-sample dataset, the selected fusion checkpoint achieved 95.45% accuracy and 93.63% macro F1 on 6,550 test samples, compared with 95.48% accuracy for MobileNetV2. These results belong to distinct data and implementation versions. Dataset provenance, parameter accounting and branch-specific gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) support interpretation of the revision-stage results. The findings demonstrate useful multi-crop classification performance, while showing that simple feature concatenation does not guarantee improvement over a single branch. Independent field generalization remains to be established.

title: An exploratory classification-tree analysis of crop residue allocation trade-offs in crop-livestock systems in Malawi
abstract: Background Crop residues are a critical resource in crop-livestock systems, serving competing functions as livestock feed and soil-management inputs. However, limited residue availability often creates trade-offs between supporting livestock productivity and maintaining soil fertility, making allocation decisions a persistent challenge in integrated farming systems. Understanding the factors that influence these decisions is important for promoting sustainable intensification and improving resource-use efficiency. Therefore, this study sought to identify the behavioral, socioeconomic, and human-capital factors associated with crop-residue allocation decisions among three participant groups engaged in integrated crop-livestock systems in Malawi. Groups A and B, comprising younger highly educated students and graduates/community youth with mixed livelihood activities, respectively, participated in a structured experiential-learning intervention and served as treatment groups, while Group C, consisting predominantly of older farmers, served as the comparison group. Methods An exploratory Classification and Regression Tree (CART) analysis was conducted using nine group-year observations derived from three investor groups observed over three production cycles. Residue allocation was classified into two categories: livestock feed and land management. Candidate predictor variables included risk tolerance, group income, education level, occupation, marital status, livestock ownership, and exposure to crop-livestock systems (CLS) training. Model performance was evaluated using confusion matrices, classification accuracy, precision, recall, F1-scores, and cross-validation procedures. Results The CART model identified risk tolerance, group income, and education level as the principal factors associated with residue-allocation decisions, with risk tolerance emerging as the root node and strongest discriminator among candidate predictors. Of the nine group-year observations, 55.6% were allocated to land management and 44.4% to livestock feed. Group A allocated residue to land management during the first two production cycles before shifting to livestock feed in the third year, Group B consistently allocated residues to livestock feed across all 3 years, and Group C consistently allocated residues to land management. These patterns suggest that differences in residue-allocation behavior were associated with variation in behavioral, economic, and educational characteristics across the groups. The model achieved perfect classification of the training data and a cross-validated accuracy of 77.8%. Class-specific performance metrics indicated comparable classification performance across allocation categories, with precision, recall, and F1-scores of 0.80 for land management and 0.75 for livestock feed, and macro-average and weighted-average scores of 0.78. Occupation, marital status, livestock ownership, and CLS training were not retained in the final tree structure. Conclusion The findings suggest that residue-allocation decisions within crop-livestock systems are associated primarily with behavioral, economic, and human-capital characteristics, particularly risk tolerance, income, and education. Differences observed among Groups A, B, and C appear to reflect variation in these characteristics rather than group membership itself. However, given the small sample size and exploratory nature of the analysis, the identified decision pathways should be interpreted as indicative patterns rather than robust predictive relationships. Future research using larger datasets and direct measures of learning and behavioral change is needed to validate these findings and strengthen understanding of residue-allocation decision-making in integrated crop-livestock systems.
