title: DTW-kNN and Sentinel-2 NDVI Time Series for Field-Scale Maize Identification and Multi-Crop Classification in an African Smallholder Landscape
abstract: Mapping crops at the field scale supports agricultural planning, production monitoring and resource allocation. However, this remains difficult in smallholder landscapes, where planting dates vary among farms, ground-reference data are limited, and fields are small, fragmented and irregularly shaped. This study evaluated Sentinel-2 Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) time series combined with Dynamic Time Warping k-nearest neighbour (DTW-kNN) for maize identification and multi-crop classification in the O.R. Tambo District Municipality, South Africa.. A maize reference trajectory was first developed from known maize fields and then assessed against independent maize validation fields and candidate unknown fields. Known maize fields produced low DTW distances to the maize reference trajectory, while Days After Planting alignment showed a clear maize phenological pattern, with NDVI increasing after planting, peaking between approximately 90 and 120 DAP, and declining thereafter. For multi-crop classification, a simple mean-reference DTW baseline achieved 80.0% accuracy on independent validation fields. Retaining individual reference-field trajectories (DTW-kNN) instead of a single mean reference improved on this baseline. Training-only cross-validation selected DTW-kNN with k = 1 and a one-composite warping window; this configuration achieved 92.9% independent validation accuracy, comparable to benchmark Random Forest and Support Vector Machine classifiers (95.7%). DTW-kNN remained competitive while retaining direct temporal-similarity interpretation. When applied to 128 unlabelled fields, the selected DTW-kNN classifier predicted 106 fields as maize and 22 as soybean, with 65.6% of predictions classified with high confidence. The findings show that Sentinel-2 NDVI time series combined with DTW-kNN can support interpretable field-level crop classification in fragmented smallholder farming systems.

title: Low-Power FPGA-Based Differentiable Mesh Rendering for On-Device Dense Photometric Pose Refinement
abstract: Differentiable rasterization enables image inversion by providing gradients of image-based losses with respect to camera and scene parameters, and has become a practical foundation for inverse graphics and photometric estimation on GPUs. However, the real-time deployment of differentiable rendering in embedded perception remains challenging due to the high cost of per-pixel sampling and gradient computation. In this work, we present an nvdiffrast-inspired differentiable rasterization engine implemented on FPGA and demonstrate its use in a simplified dense photometric pose-refinement task. Our design follows the modular philosophy of nvdiffrast while specializing it for deterministic, low-latency hardware execution. We implement point-sampled triangle rasterization with hard z-buffer visibility, perspective-correct interpolation, and an analytic antialiasing stage that yields stable, non-zero gradients at silhouettes and occlusion boundaries. Unlike GPU pipelines where texturing behavior may be hardware defined, our FPGA implementation controls the texture sampler, enabling a fused rasterize–interpolate–texture operator with a matched backward pass. Beyond pixelwise gradients, we introduce an on-device accumulation scheme that directly forms Gauss–Newton normal-equation terms, enabling second-order pose updates with substantially fewer iterations than gradient descent. We validate forward rendering and derivatives against a GLSL reference implementation, and report FPGA resource utilization and runtime. The core rasterization and analytic antialiasing pipeline achieves 2.5 ms per frame, while the full textured keyframe-projection operator runs in 8 ms per frame on an AMD Kria KV260. In a dense photometric pose-refinement evaluation on synthetic and real sequences, the proposed Jacobian accumulation reduces the number of optimization iterations required for convergence, improving time-to-solution despite the added cost of texturing. Together with a post-implementation on-chip power estimate of 3.662 W and an estimated 29.3 mJ per full-resolution differentiable rendering iteration, these results provide an implementation-level estimate of the accelerator’s power envelope for real-time photometric tracking and refinement.

title: ECG-Based Arrhythmia Analysis and Short-Term Ventricular Event Prediction Using Deep Learning
abstract: Early prediction and characterization of ventricular arrhythmias are important for reducing the risk of sudden cardiac death, a leading cause of mortality worldwide. Conventional ECG analysis commonly relies on full waveform processing, which can be computationally intensive and may provide limited interpretability at the individual-beat level. In this study, we propose a lightweight Hybrid CNN framework for beat-level ECG analysis and short-term prediction of ventricular arrhythmic events. ECG signals are segmented into individual heartbeats, and eleven statistical, temporal, and morphological features, namely the mean, standard deviation, maximum, minimum, RR interval, RR ratio, QRS amplitude, QRS width, energy, skewness, and kurtosis, are extracted from each beat. At each prediction time point, a sequence containing up to 300 consecutive heartbeats is organized as the input to the proposed Hybrid CNN, with a minimum sequence length of 20 beats. The primary task is binary prediction of the occurrence of a ventricular arrhythmic event within the subsequent five-minute window, where a ventricular event is defined by a “V” annotation in the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database. To assess the reliability and reproducibility of the proposed framework, the experimental analysis includes annotation-parser validation, explicit definition of ventricular event labels, automatic R-peak detection, feature ablation analysis, quantitative explainability, and confusion-matrix-based performance evaluation. The current implementation uses offline preprocessing, and its suitability for strictly causal real-time prediction requires further investigation. Experiments conducted on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database demonstrate that the proposed Hybrid CNN achieves a sensitivity of 90.22% and a specificity of 89.55% for short-term ventricular event prediction. The ablation further evaluates the contribution and temporal robustness of the proposed beat-level representation. Overall, the proposed framework provides an integrated and lightweight solution for beat-level ECG representation, arrhythmia characterization, and short-term ventricular event prediction, with potential applicability to real-time wearable and edge-AI ECG monitoring systems.

title: MeteoFormer: The Accuracy–Faithfulness Trade-Off of Built-In Attention in Meteorological Forecasting
abstract: Built-in attention is often presented as a free explanation of what a forecasting transformer relies on, but the claim is rarely tested. We test it on MeteoFormer, a patch-based transformer with single-head variable and temporal attention that forecasts four weather variables 24 h ahead from 96 h of hourly input on the Jena and Beijing PRSA datasets. Against ten baselines trained under one protocol with five seeds, MeteoFormer has the lowest mean absolute error on Jena (3.025 against 3.107 for Crossformer, Diebold–Mariano p < 0.05 against every baseline after Holm correction) and is level with Crossformer on Beijing (4.151 against 4.138, p = 0.72), while Crossformer has the lower squared error, a difference traced to humidity. The model depends heavily on the latest observations: losing the last 16 h raises its Jena error by 73% and drops it from first to sixth place. The explanation claim fails. The fidelity of the variable attention does not differ from zero (0.012 on Jena, 0.046 on Beijing), far below SHAP on the same model; the temporal attention is almost uniform although the forecast depends mainly on the last 16 h; and the configuration selected for accuracy has the least faithful attention (0.012 against 0.181 with instance normalization, p = 0.001), but the more faithful configuration is less accurate (Jena MAE 3.195 against 3.025) and its attention remains below SHAP.

title: Design of Auxetic Metamaterials via Adaptive Body-Fitted Mesh-Based Bi-Directional Evolutionary Structural Optimization
abstract: Fixed-grid topology optimization is widely used for auxetic metamaterial design, but its discretization-dependent boundaries may require substantial refinement or post-processing, potentially altering slender ligaments and the resulting deformation mechanisms. This study develops an adaptive body-fitted bi-directional evolutionary structural optimization (BESO) framework for two-dimensional periodic auxetic metamaterials. The topology is persistently represented by an implicit field on a fixed background grid, while a geometry-conforming T6 finite-element mesh is regenerated for periodic homogenization at each iteration. Mutual-energy sensitivities are normalized by element area and transferred from the nonuniform analysis mesh back to the background design field, enabling stable evolutionary updates under repeated remeshing. The adaptive workflow reconstructs the boundary within the optimization loop, avoiding a separate post-optimization B-spline smoothing step; in the fixed-grid Q4 comparison, this smoothing reduces the magnitude of the Poisson’s ratio. The mesh-parameter study shows how the adaptive mesh-size ratio affects computational time and the optimized auxetic response. In the tested comparison, the adaptive workflow shows closer agreement between the optimized and independently verified Poisson’s ratios.

title: HiMambaMap: A Hilbert-Scanning Mamba Diffusion Network for Online Map Generation from Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: Remote sensing image-to-online map translation (RSMT) represents a critical research frontier in geographic information processing. With the rapid development of deep learning, generative models have attracted increasing attention for automatic map generation. However, existing methods incur substantial computational overhead when modeling global contextual information. Recently, Mamba has been widely adopted in remote sensing for capturing global dependencies with linear complexity. However, naively applying its sequential scanning mechanism to RSMT tends to disrupt local spatial relationships essential to map generation. In this study, we propose HiMambaMap, a Hilbert-scanning Mamba diffusion network for RSMT. Specifically, it is built upon a Brownian bridge diffusion model, where the proposed denoiser combines a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) encoder for local spatial feature extraction and a Mamba decoder for efficient global dependency modeling. To further improve the spatial consistency of the generated maps, we introduce a Multi-Scale Feature Fusion (MSFF) module into the denoiser for enhanced multi-scale feature fusion and incorporate a four-directional Hilbert scanning strategy into the Mamba decoder to better preserve spatial locality. Extensive experiments on two widely used datasets demonstrate that HiMambaMap achieves competitive generation quality and pixel-level color consistency, while maintaining the lowest parameter count and computational complexity among several state-of-the-art methods.

title: Focus, Magnify, and Detect: An Adaptive Region-Aware Detector for Remote Sensing Object Detection
abstract: Object detection in remote sensing images (RSIs) suffers severely from small-scale instances, which are inherently constrained by extremely low pixel occupancy, fragile spatial detail retention, and insufficient discriminative feature representation. Global scaling is an intuitive strategy to compensate for the spatial information loss of small targets, yet it inevitably brings significant computational complexity as convolutional networks grow quadratically with the elevation of spatial resolution. In order to alleviate this accuracy–efficiency dilemma, we propose a focus, magnify, detect network, named adaptive region-aware detector (ARADet), tailored for object detection in RSIs. In the focus stage, our region-aware attention (RAA) module generates a Gaussian-constrained attention heatmap to rapidly localize potential small-target regions from the regional attention map. In the magnify stage, we introduce a differentiable affine magnification mechanism with learnable scaling factors. For each focused region, the network adaptively predicts a scaling factor and constructs a center-aligned affine transformation matrix to achieve center-preserving regional magnification. Unlike global upsampling schemes, our module only enhances target-region features and fills them back into the original feature map, thus keeping the overall feature resolution unchanged. The final enhanced features are fed into the detection head for category classification and oriented bounding-box regression. Extensive experiments conducted on two standard aerial object detection benchmarks, including DOTA and DIOR-R, demonstrate that ARADet brings 1.18% mAP improvement over the baseline method, with merely 0.3726M additional parameters. Although the introduced feature amplification yields a moderate rise in FLOPs, ARADet achieves favorable accuracy gains with negligible parameter overhead and surpasses many state-of-the-art oriented detectors.

title: MFM-TransUNet: Multi-Scale Feature Modeling Network for Remote Sensing-Based Surface Water Extraction
abstract: Accurate extraction of surface water is of great significance for water resource management, ecological conservation, and flood disaster monitoring. However, water bodies in high-resolution remote sensing imagery are often obscured by building shadows, vegetation, complex backgrounds, or spectral confusion. Consequently, traditional semantic segmentation methods frequently struggle with global feature modeling and the preservation of boundary details. To address these challenges, this paper proposes MFM-TransUNet, a remote sensing water extraction network based on multi-scale feature modeling. The network employs an encoder–feature modeling–decoder architecture. A Ghost-SE encoder is utilized to extract multi-scale hierarchical features, while a High-Performance Sequence Modeling Module (HPSM) is introduced to aggregate local contextual information from high-level features through depthwise 1D convolutions, with a feed-forward network enhancing nonlinear feature representations along the channel dimension. During the decoding phase, a learnable weight-fusion strategy is applied to balance the contributions of features from different levels, and an Edge-enhanced Feature Attention (EFA) is incorporated to strengthen boundary-related information within the decoded features. The proposed method was evaluated in terms of segmentation accuracy, module ablation, and cross-dataset performance. Experiments on the GID dataset demonstrate that MFM-TransUNet achieves an Overall Accuracy (OA) of 96.27%, a Mean Intersection over Union (Mean IoU) of 89.24%, an F1-Score of 94.20%, and a Boundary IoU of 63.52%, showing competitive performance compared with several mainstream baseline models. Ablation studies evaluate the contributions of the key modules, while experiments on the LJ-Water and Water-CD datasets assess the model’s performance across different datasets. These results suggest that MFM-TransUNet achieves a favorable trade-off between segmentation accuracy, boundary-related performance, and computational cost, providing a potential approach for surface water extraction in complex remote sensing scenarios.

title: SSC-DETR: Real-Time End-to-End Small-Object Detection in UAV Remote Sensing Imagery via Saliency-Guided Sparse Attention and Signed Sparse Semantic Calibration
abstract: Small-object detection in UAV imagery is difficult because targets occupy only a few pixels amid cluttered backgrounds. Although high-resolution features preserve fragile spatial cues, dense contextual interaction over these features is computationally expensive, while multiscale fusion can weaken or misalign local semantic responses. We propose SSC-DETR, a real-time end-to-end detector that addresses these challenges through selective contextual interaction before fusion and selective semantic calibration afterward. Saliency-Guided Sparse Attention (SGSA) learns a spatial selection prior—a saliency map explicitly supervised by Gaussian targets derived from ground-truth bounding boxes—and uses it to select object-relevant high-resolution tokens for sparse self-attention while retaining dense local features elsewhere. Signed Sparse Semantic Calibration (SSSC) independently selects a smaller set of post-fusion positions and injects spatially aligned, bounded signed semantic residuals to reinforce useful evidence or suppress inconsistent responses. Haar-DWT downsampling and a scale-calibrated GIoU–GCD localization objective complement the two modules. Experiments on VisDrone and AI-TOD-v2 demonstrate improvements with ResNet-18 and ResNet-50. With ResNet-50, SSC-DETR increases AP from 29.6% to 35.2% on VisDrone and from 25.5% to 28.9% on AI-TOD-v2 while retaining real-time inference.

title: Transfer-Aware Anomaly Detection for Sustainable AIoT-Enabled Water Infrastructures: A Systematic Review of Graph-Based Models, Tabular Foundation Models, and Privacy-Preserving Adaptation
abstract: Early detection of leaks, bursts, process faults, and cyber-physical attacks is a direct lever for the sustainable management of water infrastructures: it reduces non-revenue water, the energy spent on treating and pumping lost water, and service interruptions (Sustainable Development Goal 6). Anomaly detectors for water distribution networks (WDNs) and wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are increasingly deployed through Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) architectures, yet a detector that performs well on one system cannot be assumed to transfer to another with a different topology, sensor layout, demand pattern, and label availability. This systematic review examines the literature through this transfer problem, with graph neural networks (GNNs) as topology-aware models, tabular foundation models (TFMs; in the retrieved evidence, the TabPFN family) as candidate local screeners, federated learning as privacy-preserving adaptation, and digital twins and explainable artificial intelligence as validation and trust layers. It follows PRISMA 2020 and is registered retrospectively in the Open Science Framework (DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/D7RXU). Peer-reviewed articles, theses, and preprints in English or Spanish were identified through modular block searches (Google Scholar, publisher sites, three Spanish repositories), author-supplied sources, and citation chasing, verified against primary records on 6–7 September 2026, screened in two stages, coded with a predefined framework, appraised with a six-item checklist, and synthesized descriptively because tasks, datasets, and metrics are not commensurable. The corpus comprises 150 unique works: 76 water-specific experimental studies, 21 benchmark or testbed studies, and 53 method, review, or contextual works. Graph-based approaches have the stronger water-specific evidence for topology-dependent tasks in WDNs, whereas TabPFN-family TFMs rest on general tabular-learning evidence and one water-adjacent prediction study, with no validated water anomaly-detection use. Only 6 of the 76 experimental studies evaluate an explicit transfer mechanism, federated evidence is limited to one water study, and no study reports an operator evaluation of explanations. The review contributes a transfer taxonomy with study counts, an evidence-class scheme, a gap map of demonstrated and proposed components on a transfer-aware AIoT layout, and an evaluation agenda based on source–target protocols, and identifies the evidence utilities need before transferable detectors can support sustainable operation at scale.
