title: Deadwood Mitigates Declines in Soil Food‐Web Energy Fluxes in Canopy Gaps
abstract: Across forests worldwide, frequent climate extremes and intensified timber harvest are reshaping forest structure by increasing tree mortality and canopy opening, threatening terrestrial biodiversity and ecosystem sustainability. In unmanaged forests, natural disturbances create canopy gaps and leave substantial deadwood on site, whereas timber harvesting creates gaps through the removal of living trees, thereby limiting the accumulation of deadwood. However, how these disturbances and management practices affect ecosystem functioning, especially of the belowground system, remains little understood. Here, we reconstructed 116 soil animal food webs in a full‐factorial experiment manipulating forest gaps and deadwood addition. We quantified energy fluxes of soil food webs as an integrative measure of belowground ecosystem functioning and investigated their network architecture 2 years after establishment of the experiment. Forest gaps reduced total food web energy fluxes by 13.4%, decreased network connectance, and shifted energy flow towards the bacteria‐dominated “fast” channel, indicating simplified soil food webs, impaired soil functioning, and reduced energy retention belowground. However, compared to gaps without deadwood, the presence of deadwood in gaps increased total energy flux by 37.4%, primarily through enhanced fungivory and wood‐feeding pathways, and restored network connectance and cycling rates to levels comparable to those in closed‐canopy forests. Our results demonstrate that deadwood acts as a key structural component that mitigates the detrimental effects of canopy gap formation on belowground ecosystem functioning, underscoring deadwood retention after timber harvest as a practical strategy to safeguard soil functioning in a more disturbance‐prone future.

title: PGCopilot: an AI-assisted research agent for plant functional genomics.
Melting and resistivity of iron at Earth core conditions using pulsed Joule heating
abstract: The melting temperature and electrical resistivity of iron at high pressure are essential for understanding Earth’s core. Here we use a new high-pressure method – microsecond pulsed Joule heating in diamond anvil cells – to identify melting and measure resistivity of solid and liquid iron. More than 300 reproducible melting measurements indicate a surprisingly shallow melting curve, reaching 6 K/GPa and 4160 ± 80 K at 200 GPa. Extrapolating in pressure and iron alloy composition, and combining with our 76 μ Ω cm measurement of liquid iron’s resistivity, we infer a relatively cold core-mantle boundary (3430 K) with a low adiabatic outer core heat flow (9.8 TW). This suggests thermal convection alone could have powered the geodynamo prior to inner core formation and that today’s lowermost mantle is fully solid.

title: HiDream-O1-Image: An Open-Source Pixel-Level Unified Transformer for General Image Generation
abstract: Modern image generation systems often employ latent diffusion paradigm with image Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and separate text encoder. This modular design is efficient, but it can result in potential loss of pixel-level details and sub-optimal visual-semantic alignment. We present HiDream-O1-Image, an open-source image generation model built on a pixel-level Unified Transformer. The model directly patchifies noisy RGB images and places image patches, prompt tokens, and optional visual-condition tokens into one unified Transformer sequence. A hybrid attention mask keeps causal processing for text and context tokens while allowing generation tokens to exchange global visual information. In addition, a lightweight prompt agent is adopted to rewrite underspecified user requests into structured generation prompts. The released HiDream-O1-Image supports text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, subject-driven personalization in a unified interface. Despite its highly efficient 8B scale, HiDream-O1-Image achieves comparable performances against significantly larger state-of-the-art models. We release the model weights, inference code, and prompt agent to facilitate future research in unified multimodal generation: https://github.com/HiDream-ai/HiDream-O1-Image. Demonstrating significant community impact, the model garnered over 30,000 downloads on HuggingFace within just one week of its open-source release and has been rapidly integrated into popular platforms and tools such as ComfyUI, WaveSpeedAI, and fal.ai.

title: Ruminative Contrastive Attention Calibration for Training-Free Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning in MLLMs
abstract: While Multimodal Large Language Models excel at general visual question answering, their performance degrades significantly on tasks that depend on fine-grained details. This limitation makes it challenging for models to reliably handle tasks such as counting, document understanding, and complex reasoning. A recent strategy to enhance visual details is to perform multi-round inference, using the model's attention to crop a single, rectangular region of interest. This approach is computationally inefficient and is less effective for tasks that require analyzing multiple, arbitrarily shaped regions. To overcome these flaws, we identify a key bottleneck termed attention dilution and formulate the extraction of task-relevant semantic focus as a variational inference problem. Derived from the optimal solution under this formulation, we propose Ruminative Contrastive Attention Calibration (RumiA), a training-free inference method. RumiA computes the Conditional Pointwise Mutual Information of visual tokens via a Layer-Wise Attention Contrast, acting as a semantic unsharp masking filter that helps suppress background priors while maintaining the ability to attend to multiple regions. Capitalizing on the cross-scale stability of this distribution, RumiA leverages an efficient, smaller MLLM to perform a soft key-value calibration on a larger target model during a single inference pass. We evaluated our method on three MLLM families across ten benchmarks, focusing on fine-grained and complex reasoning. Our results show that RumiA achieves competitive improvement over strong baselines and reduces the computational cost.

title: Vocabulary-Free Segmentation via Multi-mask Category Generation with MLLMs
abstract: Mask-based recognition with multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offers a promising route to vocabulary-free segmentation. However, existing methods typically predict each candidate mask independently, limiting shared-context reasoning, while naive joint multi-mask generation suffers from cross-mask interference. We present VFSeg, a vocabulary-free segmentation framework for joint multi-mask recognition that predicts attribute-category outputs for all masks in a single pass. Specifically, Position-Anchored Embedding (PAE) is designed to establish stable positional anchors by binding observations of the same mask across crops to shared slots, thereby decoupling position from content. Building on this design, Attribute-Guided Disambiguation (AGD) further improves output discrimination by generating concise, visually grounded attributes to guide mask category prediction, thereby reducing confusion among similar targets. To support VFSeg training, we build VGAMask, a large-scale supervision corpus of mask-category-attribute tuples. Experiments show that VFSeg substantially outperforms prior vocabulary-free baselines and demonstrates stronger open-ended semantic capability.

title: From Structure to Details: Asynchronous Diffusion Refinement for Multispectral and Panchromatic Image Fusion
abstract: Diffusion model based fusion of low-resolution multispectral (LRMS) and panchromatic (PAN) images has attracted increasing attention in recent years. However, most existing methods jointly treat PAN and multispectral images as conditions to the denoising network without explicitly distinguishing their distinct roles in the fusion process. As a result, the model is unable to impose differentiated constraints and guidance, leading to unsatisfactory spectral information preservation and spatial detail enhancement. Recent advancements have demonstrated that diffusion models tend to generate overall structures in the initial denoising stages and then progressively recover fine details in latter stages. Motivated by this observation, we propose an Asynchronous Diffusion (AsyDiff) model that progressively performs image fusion from structure reconstruction to detail refinement. Specifically, AsyDiff employs two dedicated data streams: a spatial stream for detail enhancement and a spectral stream for spectral preservation. Correspondingly, the diffusion process is divided into three stages. The structure reconstruction stage primarily uses the PAN stream to reconstruct the initial spatial structure, while the spectral refinement stage uses the multispectral stream to refine spectral information and improve detail consistency. An asynchronous transition stage is introduced between them to alleviate conflicts between the two streams. Extensive experiments on multiple satellite datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in both visual quality and quantitative evaluation metrics. The source code is available at https://github.com/yangyingkun/AsyDiff.

title: SAFER: Sequential Adaptive Forensic Evidence Reasoning for Generalizable Visual Forensics
abstract: Image forensics has become increasingly challenging in the era of heterogeneous manipulations, where editing, AI-generated content, and deepfake synthesis expose highly diverse forensic cues across tracks and samples. Existing methods predominantly follow a static one-shot paradigm, in which all inputs are processed with the same computation graph and evidence pathway. Such a design is increasingly restrictive for generalizable forensics, where different samples and forgery tracks often require different types and amounts of evidence. In this work, we propose SAFER (Sequential Adaptive Forensic Evidence Reasoner), a prior-guided forensic agent that reformulates forgery analysis as a budget-aware sequential evidence reasoning problem. Given an input image, SAFER first derives an initial forensic prior using a lightweight multi-scale front-end. Conditioned on this prior, a policy network then adaptively queries one or more track-aware experts from a heterogeneous expert pool under a limited computation budget. The queried evidence is subsequently integrated by a reliability-aware decision aggregation module to produce the final forgery prediction, tampering mask, and explainable report. To make sequential decision-making trainable, we further introduce a progressive policy learning strategy that combines imitation learning and reinforcement learning. Extensive experiments show that SAFER achieves robust performance across diverse scenarios, while providing a more favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-off than conventional static pipelines. Our results suggest that adaptive sequential evidence reasoning offers a practical new paradigm for real-world multimedia forensics.

title: Geometric Guardrail: Manifold Geometric Constrainer for Noisy Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Feature Fusion
abstract: Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Fusion (MRSIF) faces a critical challenge of fusion collapse in few shot or noisy scenarios, such as those obscured by fog and clouds, where models over-rely on the dominant modality or suffer from severe semantic shifts, leading to the failure of the multimodal fusion mechanism. We have observed that the intrinsic geometric representation of the feature space can correspondingly characterize semantic information, thereby providing an effective geometric-driven solution for avoiding and correcting fusion collapse challenges. To be specific, we propose Residual Manifold Geometric Constrainer (ReMaCo), a novel plug-and-play fusion enhancement module that treats MRSIF task as a constrained progressive evolution process on non-Euclidean manifolds. Firstly, dual manifold constraints are designed: Lorentz hyperbolic space is utilized to model the intrinsic confidence among multimodal features, while unit hyperspherical space is employed to stabilize the directional consistency of feature semantics against noise-induced drift. Furthermore, Residual Fusion Feature Calibration (RFFC) module is designed to guide the model to focus on uncertain regions in multimodal inputs through hyperbolic energy maps and implement residual feature correction, which prevents the suboptimal state propagation. By transforming the optimization from purely data-driven search to geometric-guided refinement, ReMaCo provides a robust fusion paradigm for sophisticated MRSIF tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method effectively mitigates fusion collapse and achieves superior segmentation performance in challenging, interference-prone remote sensing scenarios. The code is available at https://github.com/PhilipHan-HITSZ/ReMaCo.

title: ColorFlow: Robust Image Colorization with Pixel Flow Matching
abstract: Image colorization is an inherently underconstrained task requiring precise semantic understanding and strict structural alignment. Existing colorization methods typically model high-frequency signals and low-frequency semantics jointly, overlooking their distinct and complementary characteristics. This frequency coupling frequently leads to color bleeding across semantic boundaries. To address these limitations, we introduce ColorFlow, a novel generative model that decouples frequency representations. The proposed architecture clearly separates high-frequency signals from low-frequency semantics and then ultimately integrates them. To effectively fuse this information, the model employs a fully differentiable Fast Guided Filter as its core module. This filter directly uses low-frequency semantics to spatially guide high-frequency signals, ensuring a coherent color distribution. To prevent blurring and desaturation, we further incorporate two loss functions: LPIPS loss preserves fine details, while DINO loss enforces global semantic consistency. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that ColorFlow achieves highly competitive overall performance, successfully synthesizing perceptually vibrant images with precise semantic alignment.

title: A Parallel City-Scale Acoustic Ground-Truth Engine for NLoS Embodied Perception
abstract: Embodied AI agents rely on multi-modal perception for situational awareness in complex urban environments. While visual simulation has achieved photorealism, generating physics-grounded acoustic datasets remains a critical bottleneck. Existing Geometric Acoustics (GA) renderers, though efficient for high frequencies, often yield null signals in Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) blind spots because they cannot resolve low-frequency wave diffraction. To bridge this gap, we propose a parallel, voxel-based acoustic benchmark generation engine powered by a mesoscopic Lattice Boltzmann kernel. Scalable to the hundred-million-voxel level on supercomputers, the framework captures 3D wave dynamics and continuous multipath healing within an explicitly bounded low-frequency band (up to approximately 100 Hz in the present benchmark) and under rigid structural-boundary assumptions, while circumventing the meshing bottleneck of traditional solvers. We validate the engine through a multi-resolution ablation study (grid spacing from 1.5 m to 0.5 m) in a realistic urban intersection. Leveraging these fluid-dynamic data, we establish a diagnostic benchmark spanning GCC-PHAT, MUSIC, and a pre-trained Deep Learning architecture (DL-CRNN), quantifying the out-of-distribution shift between geometric assumptions and wave-based transients. Millisecond-level analysis exposes spatial-aliasing failure modes in these representative localization paradigms. Accordingly, the simulated fields serve as a validated low-frequency hard-boundary wave reference, rather than full-band real-world acoustic ground truth, for diagnosing NLoS perception algorithms and developing wave-informed spatial-audio models.

title: ArchFact: A Multimodal System for Unstructured Archaeological Report Extraction and Assertion-Based Verification
abstract: Archaeological excavation reports—combining artifact illustrations, stratigraphic descriptions, and typological catalogs—remain largely inaccessible to computational analysis, constraining the scale and reproducibility of cultural heritage research. Transforming these heterogeneous, unstructured documents into queryable databases requires solving two interrelated challenges: extracting structured records from complex multimodal layouts, and verifying extraction quality at corpus scale without exhaustive manual review. We present ArchFact, an end-to-end system integrating established computer vision and natural language processing techniques into a unified pipeline for archaeological report digitization. The extraction stage combines domain-adapted object detection, cross-modal matching, and multi-agent LLM frameworks to handle fragmented cross-page text and spatially separated figure-caption pairs. The verification stage introduces an assertion-driven quality control mechanism where evaluation criteria are iteratively refined through human-AI collaboration. Validated across Chinese and English archaeological corpora, the full system reduces per-catalog processing time by approximately 95% and expert verification workload by 92% compared to fully manual workflows.

title: Who is a Better Puppeteer: Subjective and Objective Quality Assessment for Generative 3D Animated Human
abstract: Although recent advances in AI-based Text-to-Motion (T2M) algorithms have enabled text-driven 3D Animated Human (3DAH), often referred to as "Puppeteers" for their ability to streamline 3D animation design, the quality of the generated motion remains a critical concern. More importantly, the T2M field continues to lack reliable and objective evaluation metrics, which substantially hinders the advancement of puppeteers and negatively impacts user experience. To address this gap, we introduce the first large-scale quality assessment dataset for generative 3DAHs, termed AHQA-3D, which comprises 1,200 3DAHs sequences generated by 6 representative puppeteers. Through carefully designed subjective experiments involving recruited participants, we obtain human quality ratings for each 3DAH. The results highlight the impact of different factors on animation quality. We further propose ViSCA, an objective quality assessment agent based on Qwen2.5-VL. ViSCA supports end-to-end quality evaluation across four dimensions: 3D motion fidelity, 2D human body representation, visual quality, and semantic consistency. Experimental results demonstrate that ViSCA outperforms existing evaluation methods and exhibits stronger alignment with human perception.

title: Multimodal AI for Healthcare: From Medical Imaging to Omics and Vision–Language Models
abstract: Multimodal artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping healthcare by connecting medical images with text, molecular measurements, spatial omics, clinical behavior, and agentic decision support. Yet these directions are often presented separately, making it difficult for multimedia researchers to see how vision-language modeling, image-omics fusion, biology-informed learning, spatial pathology foundation models, etc. This quarter-day tutorial provides a coherent overview of the field, spanning medical vision-language models, multimodal learning under imperfect data and intelligent medical agents, biology-informed multimodal learning for precision medicine, image-omics fusion, foundation models for multi-omic and spatial pathology, expert behavior as multimodal supervision, and trustworthy multimodal healthcare AI. Attendees will leave with a structured map of core methods, representative clinical applications, practical design principles, and open challenges for building trustworthy multimodal healthcare AI systems.

title: Embodied Multimedia: From Multimedia Content to Situated Human-AI Interaction
abstract: Multimedia research, which has traditionally been concerned with the analysis and generation of multimedia content, has increasingly addressed multimodal human behavior. This development is exemplified by current ACM Multimedia Challenges, including POLY-SIM [3], which addresses robust speaker identification under missing-modality and cross-lingual scenarios, MultiMediate [2], which targets engagement estimation across domain, age, and culture, and REACT [4], which focuses on generating appropriate facial reactions in dyadic interactions. Together, these challenges reflect a broader shift from analyzing multimedia content toward analyzing, understanding and generating multimodal behavior in increasingly complex social contexts. The next frontier is to develop embodied AI systems that understand, support, and fluently participate in situated human interaction. We pursue this vision through virtual agents and social robots that facilitate communication between people and AI and increasingly between people themselves. The talk will demonstrate how pretrained multimodal foundation models can be leveraged to create context-aware embodied AI. Drawing on applications in assistive communication, AI-mediated group discussions, and social coaching, the talk will illustrate how embodied agents enabled by these models can help overcome communication barriers, facilitate social interaction, and foster authentic self-expression. At the same time, significant challenges remain in grounding multimodal models in physical and social context, ensuring responsive and coordinated behavior, and evaluating whether apparently socially intelligent behavior is appropriate, robust, and trustworthy [1].

title: International Workshop on Industrial Physical AI
abstract: Industrial Physical AI extends data-driven intelligence from purely digital spaces into the physical world by embedding physical laws, multimodal perception, and causal reasoning into model design, opening a path toward reliable, deployable intelligent systems for safety-critical industrial environments. The International Workshop on Industrial Physical AI (WIPAI 2026), co-located with the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM 2026) in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, provided a focused forum for researchers and practitioners to discuss the latest advances, challenges, and opportunities in multimodal-driven physical AI for real-world industrial scenarios. The workshop addresses the gap between general multimedia research and industrial deployment, treating multimodal technology as the perceptual foundation of Industrial Physical AI. After a rigorous review process, eight papers were accepted for oral presentation, spanning multimodal sensing and monitoring of manufacturing processes, physics-grounded agents and world models, LLM orchestration for physical assembly, vision--language--action policies and their execution runtimes, the physical fidelity of feed-forward 3D reconstruction, and topological validation of robot-swarm dynamics. This summary describes the motivation, scope, and technical themes of the workshop and overviews the accepted contributions.

title: Chinese Composite Character Generation via Recursive IDS-Tree Processing and Component-Level Style Transfer
abstract: A Chinese composite character is an integrated and recognizable artistic glyph formed from multiple source characters through component sharing, structural recombination, and spatial compression. Traditional design relies heavily on manual expertise, whereas image-space-only generation methods do not readily support explicit control over component reuse; whole-character style transfer may also disrupt nonstandard composite layouts. To address these issues, this paper proposes a structure-first framework for Chinese composite character generation. The framework first parses two to four input characters into Ideographic Description Sequence (IDS) trees and constructs hierarchical composite candidates from shared leaf components and their structural roles, thereby keeping component provenance and recombination relationships traceable. It then performs recursive layout using ink bounding boxes (bboxes), visual centroids, and structural roles measured from KAGE glyphs, and generates renderable glyphs through controlled subtree collapsing and glyph-integrity checks. During stylization, the system applies the diffusion-based font-generation model FontDiffuser to individual IDS leaf components and uses role- and character-aware bbox scale normalization to mitigate scale inflation in simple components without cropping the generated stroke contours. The system also supports batch-task construction for two to four characters through shared-component validation, with separate outputs for simplified Chinese, traditional Chinese, and multiple structural candidates. In addition, this paper proposes a candidate scoring method with structural-quality constraints that combines image features for brushwork, structure, layout, and expressive vitality with component reuse, explicit overlap, and high-overlap risks among component layout boxes. In an expert-rating experiment on 60 clerical-script composite-character images, the final score after applying generation-quality constraints achieved Pearson and Spearman correlation coefficients of 0.693 and 0.651, respectively, with the expert scores. The results demonstrate the feasibility of structurally interpretable artistic-glyph generation across multiple script styles and support preliminary assisted candidate ranking on clerical-script candidates.

title: One-Versus-Rest Crop Classification from Multi-Temporal Sentinel-2 Imagery Using a Hybrid CNN–LSTM Architecture and Explainable GeoAI
abstract: Accurate crop classification from satellite imagery can substantially enhance agricultural monitoring. Recent advances in deep learning have improved crop classification by employing models that take into account both spatial and temporal information contained in satellite image time series. However, the limited interpretability of these models remains a major challenge for their adoption in agricultural applications. This study presents a one-versus-rest classification framework for five crop types (wheat, maize, rapeseed, sunflower and watermelon and melon), in Ialomița County, Romania, using a CNN-LSTM (Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory) architecture and nine Sentinel-2 images acquired throughout the 2025 growing season. Each image sequence consisted of four spectral bands and NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index), enabling the exploitation of spectral, spatial and temporal information. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). The models achieved high validation accuracy, with values of 96.01% for wheat, 94.33% for maize, 97.48% for rapeseed, 97.06% for sunflower and 97.06% for watermelon and melon classifications. Explainable AI (XAI) techniques such as Integrated Gradients and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) were employed to quantify the contribution of individual spectral bands and acquisition dates to the classification decision. The Integrated Gradients analysis showed that for some crops, NDVI was the most influential input feature, accounting for 50.78% of the feature importance in wheat classification, 39.30% in rapeseed classification and 40.01% in watermelon and melon classification, while for other crops, the NIR (Near-infrared) spectral band was the most influential feature, accounting for 29.89% of the feature importance in maize classification and 41.00% in sunflower classification. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves high classification performance while providing meaningful explanations of model predictions, highlighting the importance of both vegetation characteristics and seasonal dynamics in crop classification.

title: Advancements in Tobacco Crop Monitoring: A Survey of Deep Learning Technologies
abstract: The challenge of tobacco monitoring is a technical and political issue, given that tobacco production is a cross-cutting issue that involves agricultural management, regulatory compliance and illegal harvesting. Tobacco acreage estimation and tobacco classification have been expanded through the use of remote sensing and deep learning has enhanced the capacity to extract spatial, spectral, and temporal patterns from the timeseries data. This survey summarizes the literature on tobacco monitoring and tobacco-relevant crops in a new format, a critical comparison between the various sensing platforms and learning paradigms. It reviews the multispectral, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) and hyperspectral data sources, as well as traditional machine learning, convolutional, recurrent, attention-based and hybrid models, and points out the experimental conditions in which several studies have achieved high accuracy. The most significant advances have been made in multi-temporal optical classification and UAV-based field-scale mapping, while operational deployment remains hindered by the lack of benchmark datasets, cross region validation, and few SAR–optical fusion studies, as well as the lack of mature decision support pipelines. Future progress will be possible with open tobacco-specific benchmarks, multi-sensor fusion, transferable models, explainable AI and scalable monitoring systems, which will facilitate agricultural and policy decision-making.

title: Resource-Constrained Adaptive Sampling for Variance Monitoring: Comparing Rule-Based, MLP, and LSTM Acquisition Policies
abstract: Automated monitoring must balance detection delay and measurement use. This study compares rule-based, feedforward multilayer perceptron (MLP), and long short-term memory (LSTM) acquisition policies coupled to a common exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) variance detector. Experiments 1 and 2 comprise 714,000 and 660,000 test trajectories, respectively. Closely matched rule and LSTM configurations achieve in-control average run lengths of 369.97 and 370.11, consumption of 4.918 and 4.917 observations per epoch, and weighted detection delays of 18.860 and 18.864 epochs; the conditional 95% bootstrap confidence interval for the difference in their weighted delays includes zero. A third experiment repeats optimization, selection, calibration, and testing ten times per family, comparing a search budget of 512 candidate evaluations with one of 30 CPU seconds. The mean LSTM-minus-rule delay contrasts are −0.219 and +0.206 epochs, respectively, with across-run 95% intervals [−0.723, 0.285] and [−0.295, 0.708]. Scenario weights, measurement prices, and acquisition duration further affect policy comparisons. The findings characterize the evaluated finite search procedures and operating points within a common detector; they establish neither intrinsic superiority nor equivalence of the policy architectures.

title: Multi-Decadal Remote Sensing of Land Cover and Surface Water Dynamics in a Data-Limited Monsoon Lake Watershed in Myanmar
abstract: Long-term monitoring of land use/land cover (LULC) and surface water is challenging in monsoon lake watersheds with limited reference observations. This study constructed annual LULC in the Inle lake watershed, Myanmar, for 2000–2025 using Landsat annual median composites, six reflectance bands and six spectral indices. Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM) and XGBoost were evaluated using spatially grouped internal testing of purposively selected reference samples. SVM achieved the highest 26-year mean internal overall accuracy (71.49%), kappa (0.620) and macro-F1 (71.79%). A separate stratified probability sample of 600 fixed pixels was assessed for 2000, 2010, 2020 and 2025 to estimate map accuracy, class areas and paired net changes within a common 5438.20 km2 domain. Area-weighted overall accuracy ranged from 58.7% to 71.4%, while Built-up user’s accuracy remained low at 12.4–22.9%. Reference-based 2000–2025 changes were Agriculture +450.1 km2 (95% sampling interval: +203.4 to +696.8), Forest −631.5 km2 (−857.3 to −405.7) and Water +42.3 km2 (−23.5 to +108.0). The Water interval included zero, and the reference assessment did not establish a 2020–2025 recovery. Annual trend significance for Agriculture and Built-up changed under assumed classification error correction scenarios. Within the Landsat 8-only period (2013–2025), mapped Forest still declined, whereas mapped Agriculture showed no monotonic trend. Within the fixed open water outline of Inle lake, mapped water declined slowly but consistently (−0.07 km2 yr−1; p < 0.001), the Moebye reservoir showed no trend, and most of the mapped decline occurred in the surrounding sanctuary wetlands. Most of the reference-based agricultural increase and forest loss occurred between 2000 and 2010. The results support agricultural expansion and forest loss but leave watershed-wide surface water change uncertain. Distinguishing raw mapped trajectories from reference-based estimates and sampling uncertainty is essential for interpreting long-term watershed change.

title: Multimodal and Multitemporal Drone Remote Sensing Approaches to Archaeological Prospection: The Case Study at the Medieval Castle of ‘t Huis ten Bosch, Weesp, The Netherlands
abstract: This article evaluates the contribution of multi-temporal UAV remote sensing to archaeological prospection in a Dutch grassland context, using the moated castle site of ’t Huis ten Bosch as a detailed case study. Six UAV campaigns, spanning more than four years and deploying thermal, multispectral, RGB and LiDAR sensors, are compared with magnetometry, electromagnetic induction, and coring data, and evaluated against seasonal and atmospheric conditions. The combined dataset corroborates and refines the subsurface record of the primary moat, secondary moat, and central tower and walls, demonstrating that no single prospection technique, applied in isolation, could have produced the same level of structural detail and interpretative confidence. A systematic comparison of anomaly visibility across campaigns shows that detectability varied considerably between campaigns, tracking soil properties, moisture history, vegetation phenology, and mowing regime, with the clearest results tending to coincide with transitional meteorological conditions instead of prolonged extremes, on the evidence of six campaigns. The study highlights both the promise and the site-specific constraints of UAV-based prospection, and identifies methodological limitations related to sensor availability, campaign density, and the use of regional meteorological data. It concludes by outlining some provisional best practices for UAV survey design and by arguing for stratified, multi-site implementations to develop a comparative empirical basis for optimising sensor deployment in archaeological prospection in the Netherlands and beyond.

title: A Differentiable Spatially Varying Ensemble Modelling Framework for Runoff Model Heterogeneity
abstract: Conceptual rainfall–runoff models usually apply a single runoff generation structure to an entire catchment, although contrasts in soil, terrain, climate, and vegetation can produce different runoff responses within it. We developed a differentiable spatially varying ensemble (Spatial ENS) that combines GR4J, a vertically mixed runoff model (VMM), and HBV, and applied it to the Jiagenba catchment in the Yalong River Basin, southwestern China. A neural gating network maps gridded climate and land surface attributes to model weights for each cell, and the weighted runoff is routed through a shared Muskingum river network. Under leave-one-year-out cross-validation for 2017–2022, Spatial ENS achieved a flood season (June–October) Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) of 0.78, compared with 0.77, 0.70, and 0.74 for GR4J, VMM, and HBV, respectively, and the highest Kling–Gupta efficiency (0.80). Its mean annual NSE gains were 0.02, 0.09, and 0.05. The learned weights varied systematically in space, and permutation diagnostics identified clay fraction, terrain slope, and potential evapotranspiration as the dominant inputs to the gating network. These results indicate that outlet discharge can constrain spatially structured model weights and that the resulting ensemble improves flood season simulation in this catchment.

title: Advancements in Cloud-Native Systems: A Systematic Mapping Study of Reliability and Scalability across Cloud-Native, Edge-Native and AI-Enabled Systems
abstract: Cloud-native systems now extend to the network edge and host artificial-intelligence (AI) workloads, including AI agents, but evidence on their reliability and scalability is scattered and uneven. We report a PRISMA 2020 systematic mapping study with an evidence-graded synthesis. Five logged OpenAlex searches on 11 October 2026 covered cloud-native systems, edge AI, agentic AI for operations, reliability of agentic applications and physical AI; 189 records from an earlier exploratory search were added separately. After 301 duplicate removals and an automated peer-review venue rule, 4,611 records were screened against written criteria and a five-level relevance scale. The review includes 1,794 primary studies from 2017-2026 and 95 secondary studies, with every decision released in Dataset S1. Each primary study was assigned to a 13-category taxonomy and graded as simulation, prototype or testbed, production data, production deployment, or not determinable from the abstract. Of 1,003 studies with a determinable level, 66.2% used prototypes or testbeds, 18.0% simulations and 15.8% production data or deployments. A 93-study synthesis core, appraised from indexed abstracts, shows production deployments of cascading-failure prevention, trace- and graph-based root-cause analysis and predictive autoscaling, and production-trace evaluations of cold-start mitigation. Edge reliability and physical AI rely mainly on simulations and testbeds. AI-agent reliability uses tool-grounded diagnosis, explicit safety properties, trace-driven repair and workload-aware scheduling, while empirical studies show that agent frameworks remain fragile. Conclusions are limited to the documented corpus. The principal gaps are production evidence for edge-native systems, shared resilience benchmarks and dependable agentic operations.

title: Agents Propose, Code Verifies, Humans Decide: Verified Agentic Ingestion of Heterogeneous Scientific Tables into Relational Databases
abstract: Public scientific datasets rarely arrive analysis-ready. They arrive as messy folders of wide matrices, long tables, spreadsheets, and per-cohort files whose keys and encodings differ, and every reanalysis must reconnect them first. A coding agent can automate this, but its mistakes can look plausible, and without an audit trail, a mistake that corrupts data can go uncaught. We present an AI-assisted ingestion pipeline built on one rule: LLM agents propose, deterministic code verifies, and humans decide. Narrow agents see compact, citable evidence about the files, never the data, and return typed proposals. A verifier with 39 check types tests each proposal against that evidence in two loops, one for the schema's structure and one for its meaning, and a human reviewer approves the schema and the load. Code compiles PostgreSQL DDL, reshapes the data, quarantines rows it cannot place, records provenance, and reconciles every staged row against the database. On four public biomedical datasets, one held out from development, 9 of 20 first proposals failed a check and every failure was caught: the loops repaired eight, and a one-line reviewer edit fixed the ninth. All 45.1 million values loaded with zero reconciliation gap. Discovering a dataset's structure took 4-7 LLM calls and preparing its data at most one more, costing under $0.50 per dataset. In a separate test, each of nine planted data errors was quarantined with a reason or recorded in an audit log.

title: What Does Multiple Choice Actually Measure? Disentangling Video Understanding from Option Exploitation
abstract: Video understanding evaluations are intended to measure a model's proficiency in video perception and task solving. However, current VideoQA benchmarks struggle to isolate these capabilities due to their reliance on multiple-choice (MC) answer guidance, language priors, and fragile scoring pipelines. Disentangling these confounding factors reveals how much of a model's score is supplied by the evaluation context rather than earned through faithful perception. Across six VideoQA benchmarks of varying length, we find that accuracy is significantly above chance without any visual input. This is caused by shortcutting and option-prior reliance. We express these effects in the language of faithfulness: option-exploitation and answer-conditioned reasoning traces are unfaithful even when they are correct. Together, our results show that a VideoQA score is jointly determined by language priors, option timing, and how outputs and labels are converted into correctness. We produce a novel Option-Delayed Replay (ODR) mechanism that discloses options at controlled stages of an open-ended (OE) trajectory, to obtain objective MC scores from faithful option-free inference. Our work demonstrates that agentic methods with ODR and faithful inference can match option-exploiting performance. Finally, we formalize our diagnostic collection and ODR as a reproducible evaluation protocol, and we release a human-relabelled edition of LVBench (correcting $20.5\%$ of keys) to remove annotation noise as a confounding variable.

title: Rescene-ESM: an Earth system model built around a frozen AI weather model
abstract: Earth system models underpin climate projections, but their cost limits how many scenarios, ensemble members and impact pathways can be explored. Machine-learning weather models forecast as skillfully as physics-based models at a fraction of the cost, yet coupled to an ocean they have produced weak El Nino variability or have learned it from climate-model output, and none carries the climate through rivers to the people exposed to it. Here we present Rescene-ESM, an Earth system model whose coupler, YAHO, yokes a frozen 20.8-million-parameter AI weather model to physically formulated ocean, sea-ice, land, river, carbon and energy components constrained by observations. Adding the couplings one at a time shows what each contributes: over a climatological ocean the AI atmosphere varies from year to year by a third of the observed amount over the oceans, and an interactive mixed layer, an equatorial wave ocean, the residual of the observed sea surface temperature (SST) equation as stochastic forcing and the land's moisture flux raise this step by step and bring El Nino and its teleconnections, leaving the mean climate almost unchanged. The full model simulates about 1,000 years per day on one graphics processing unit, holds the observed climate for a thousand years without drift, reproduces the observed 1979-2022 global warming, carries forced change with a physically based structure around the frozen network (transient climate response 1.60 K), routes runoff to 212 river gauges with a median seasonal-cycle correlation of 0.79 and, driven by emissions, separates the heatwave exposure of an SSP1 and an SSP3 world by a factor of 4.7 in 2081-2100, three-quarters of it through the warmer climate.

title: A Globally Convergent Line-Search Quasi-Newton Method for Discounted Markov Decision Processes
abstract: In this paper, we develop a line-search quasi-Newton (LSQN) method for discounted Markov decision processes (MDPs). The method maintains an inverse model to approximate the inverse of the current policy Jacobian and refines it through an inner learning procedure that preserves existing secant conditions and achieves the prescribed accuracy in at most $n$ queries in exact arithmetic for an MDP with $n$ states, even when the initial inverse model is singular. A sign-based direction correction combined with an Armijo line search ensures monotonic decrease of the Bellman residual norm across policy changes without requiring a value-iteration fallback. We prove global Q-linear residual convergence and local Q-superlinear convergence of the value iterates from arbitrary finite initial value vectors and inverse models, without requiring a unique optimal policy. Numerical experiments show competitive performance against nine baselines, while public benchmarks demonstrate that the inner learning procedure typically requires far fewer than $n$ learning queries.

title: SoftPAT3D: Physics-Augmented Text-to-3D Scene Generation with Deformables
abstract: We present SoftPAT3D, a physics-augmented framework for text-to-3D scene generation in which deformable objects, such as cloth, stuffed toys and ropes, are generated as physically valid, simulation-ready bodies and placed in intersection-free contact with the furniture that supports them, with one another and with themselves. Existing physics-augmented pipelines simulate rigid bodies only and cannot accommodate a generated deformable object, which text-to-3D generation returns as a geometrically invalid mesh, sometimes self-intersecting, that has no rest shape, no material model and no admissible initial state. These are the inputs a deformable simulation requires, and we construct each from information already in the pipeline. The rest shape comes from how the object is manufactured rather than from the generated physically inconsistent deformed configuration, and a material library assigns each deformable object its initial elastic parameters, which can then be optimized. The occluded support is regenerated and converted into a watertight collision mesh, each object is released from an optimizable placement above the supporting part that the prompt specifies, and the complete scene is driven to static equilibrium under one unified contact model, with completion verified by geometric checks and a vision-language model. When a scene fails the prompt, a grid search over placements corrects it, and the adjoint of a differentiable simulation of the same contact energy reaches the targets the grid does not, places several bodies jointly and recovers and optimizes material parameters. Multi-body scenes equilibrate in a single simulation, and the pipeline also runs from the text prompt alone. On all sixty-five prompts, SoftPAT3D produces no undesired interpenetration of any kind, whereas every other system does, and its scenes directly support scene editing and robotic manipulation.

title: Dual Model Predictive Control through Sampling-Based Belief Propagation
abstract: We propose a sampling-based dual model predictive control (MPC) approach that combines belief propagation with parameterized feedback policy optimization. By sampling uncertain dynamics and process noise, we approximate the evolution of the hyperstate over the prediction horizon, allowing future control decisions to adapt to anticipated observations and belief updates. This enables the controller to account for the future value of information without explicit exploration incentives. We establish almost-sure uniform convergence of the sample-average objective to the finite-horizon expected objective over a compact policy class. The approach is specialized to Bayesian linear regression and evaluated on stochastic systems with constant and time-varying uncertain dynamics. We compare our approach to certainty equivalent control, and an MPC that optimizes over open-loop control sequences rather than feedback policies, demonstrating the benefits of our method in terms of both control performance and information gain.

title: Control-Aware Command Generation for Asynchronous Control and Action Inference with Vision-Based Policies towards Fast Execution
abstract: Vision-based control policies, including vision-language-action models, have enabled robots to perform increasingly complex tasks. However, their execution speed is often limited by the high computational cost of action inference. In this work, we investigate what can be achieved at the control level without modifying the underlying policy learning process. We introduce an asynchronous inference and control framework that enables fast task execution while maintaining smooth and stable robot motions. By formulating the generation of continuous target positions from discontinuous model predictions as a tracking control problem, our method makes asynchronous inference practical for real robots. We further accelerate execution through adaptive action skipping based on the variance of predicted positions. Experiments with Action Chunking Transformer and OpenVLA-OFT on a bimanual robot demonstrate substantial speedups while preserving high task success rates.

title: Deterministic Narrative Gravity: Bridging Theory of Mind and Historical Simulation through ABM-LLM Architectures
abstract: Historical social simulation faces a fundamental reproducibility challenge: the stochastic nature of large language models (LLMs) introduces a digital butterfly effect that prevents exact replication across multi-turn runs. Furthermore, the inability to control low-level server parameters in commercial LLM hosting environments severely limits reproducibility. To overcome this opacity, we present a deterministic multi-agent framework coupling LLMs to an Agent-Based Modelling (ABM) pipeline grounded in Theory of Mind (ToM) and Cognitive Archaeology, and validate exact artifact identity within local, pinned execution environments using SHA-256 hashing. Run locally at temperature zero with clean per-call model reloads, the system injects differentiated cognitive states per turn through dissonance-driven behavioural modes and gated internal voices. Evaluating seven model configurations spanning 4B to 31B parameters against an ablated baseline reveals clear operational boundaries. Small models ($\leq$8B) suffer from context capacity overload, producing repetitive, specular dialogue loops. However, at $\geq$12B parameters, the ABM scaffolding breaks the monotonous response patterns seen in ablation. Crucially, these scaffolded models exhibit spontaneous diegetic expansion: they coherently expand scenario lore through tactically motivated, anachronism-free details rather than escalating into aggression. By resisting the structural pull toward premature scene closure, scaffolded sessions sustain an open terminal Narrative Vector ($V_N = \mathrm{Open}$ in 12/21 overall; 9/9 in official $\geq$12B configurations) whereas unscaffolded ablation never does (0/21). This framework provides a transparent, auditable benchmark architecture for virtual archaeology, with the full pipeline released as open-source software to enable independent replication.

title: ALETHEIA: A Multi-Frequency Eddy Current Pulsed Thermography Dataset for Neural Operator Learning in Nondestructive Testing
abstract: Learning neural solvers for spatiotemporal partial differential equations (PDEs) under real-world constraints remains a key challenge in scientific machine learning, especially for inverse tasks with sparse and noisy boundary observations. We present the Aletheia dataset, the first 3D benchmark for learning data-driven solvers in the context of nondestructive testing (NDT). The dataset simulates eddy-current-induced heating in conductive solids and models the resulting transient heat propagation governed by the heat equation. Aletheia contains over 4,700 high-resolution samples across 10 excitation frequencies (1-100,kHz), each providing volumetric heat source and temperature fields over time. It supports both forward prediction of temperature evolution and inverse reconstruction of internal heat sources or defects from surface infrared measurements. Real infrared thermography data from cracked rail specimens are included for calibration and comparison. We define four canonical tasks on both regular and irregular grids and benchmark them using various neural operators. Aletheia establishes a unified platform for evaluating neural PDE solvers under realistic NDT conditions, enabling progress in reliable, data-driven inverse modeling. The dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/sherlock-0327/ALETHEIA.

title: Learning calibrated probabilistic forecasts using Koopman mode decomposition and the continuous ranked probability score
abstract: Well-calibrated forecasting for non-linear dynamical systems is essential in science and engineering applications such as fluid dynamics and weather prediction. We present a forecasting method combining probabilistic machine learning with the structured linear dynamics of Koopman mode decomposition. Within this framework, the observation, linear dynamics, and state reconstruction operators are constructed using standard machine learning architectures, producing predictive distributions via the pushforward of injected noise samples. The model is trained using a proper scoring rule, the continuous ranked probability score, to directly target calibrated, accurate forecasts. The approach is validated on two non-linear ordinary differential equation examples and two partial differential equation examples, vortex shedding and cavity flow, using both large and small, noisy datasets. Results demonstrate that known Koopman eigenfunctions and spectra can be identified and used for accurate forecasting. The model can also produce multi-modal predictive distributions, demonstrated for a trajectory initialised on the boundary between two basins of attraction. Uncertainty is captured by the sample ensemble spread, with spread--skill ratios close to one over the training horizon in several experiments, although for extended rollouts and noisy datasets, the ensemble may become under- or over-dispersed. In low-noise experiments, temporal rollout is generally accurate for at least twice the training horizon, and up to twenty times in some cases. Approximation quality is comparable to a deep ensemble approximation over the training horizon, but at a reduced computational cost and with better robustness in identifying Koopman eigenvalues.

title: ErosionBench: Probing Alignment Decay in Enterprise Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: As enterprises delegate consequential work to multi-agent LLM systems, benign-looking requests can escalate into unsafe actions as they propagate across sessions through poisoned shared state, long-context documents, and trusted peer messages: no single message is malicious, yet the assembled tool action is. Prior benchmarks isolate a single agent under prompt injection or score multi-agent attacks by their final output, leaving cross-session erosion of shared state out of scope. We introduce ErosionBench, an environment-grounded benchmark that executes such attacks and verifies alignment decay at the process level, scoring the realized tool call against authorized intent and provenance with deterministic contracts, not output text. Each scenario is authored as a deterministic state graph before any prose is rendered, so every state change traces to a known cause. It spans four enterprise domains and four decay mechanisms across 1,728 scenarios with matched benign controls, labeled against the OWASP Top-10 for LLM Applications, plus 198 image-based attacks, each paired with a text equivalent, so a defense must survive the same attack in either channel. Perimeter defenses suppress attacks only by over-refusing 54-92% of legitimate work, so a low attack-success rate can conceal severe over-refusal. As a reference defense, we propose a calibrated Meta-Auditor pairing synchronous state checks with asynchronous trajectory monitoring; on a family-disjoint 906-scenario held-out split it reaches 98.5% recall at a 2.9% false-positive rate. Since it monitors trajectory, not surface content, its detection is channel-invariant: the strongest auditor flags image-delivered attacks about as reliably as their text equivalents (recall gap $\leq$2 points per model). Across GPT, Gemini, and Claude auditors, calibration keeps false positives low while recall tracks model capability, strongest for Claude.

title: How Efficient Is Your Agent? Online Predictive Bounds under Budget Constraints
abstract: We evaluate AI agents in an online setting where tasks arrive sequentially and, before running each task, we construct an upper predictive bound on its \emph{time-to-success}---the number of interactions until the task is completed successfully. Under a limited budget, some runs are stopped early, so their time-to-success is unobserved (right-censored), and the correctness of the bound may be unknown. We introduce \emph{\textbf{PR}edictive Bounds for \textbf{O}nline \textbf{B}udget \textbf{E}fficiency} (\texttt{PROBE}), a method for constructing calibrated upper predictive bounds while adaptively allocating a limited budget across agent tasks to reduce the anticipated coverage deficit. Our method calibrates the bounds online using inverse-probability-weighted feedback together with a correction designed to minimize coverage deficit while remaining unbiased. We prove that \texttt{PROBE} provides a coverage guarantee for any finite time horizon while satisfying the budget constraint. Experiments on software engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, and instruction following show that \texttt{PROBE} attains a coverage rate closer to the target level with tighter predictive bounds than a calibrated baseline.

title: A Unified Framework for License Plate Identification and Character-Recognition
abstract: This paper presents a unified framework for license plate detection and character recognition on low-power edge hardware. The proposed network uses a shared CSP-Darknet and PANet feature encoder with an anchor-free localization head and a RoIAlign-based sequence-recognition branch. Character decoding is performed directly on aligned feature maps, avoiding image-space plate cropping and a second recognition backbone. The model is trained on an AI-assisted dataset of approximately 37,000 manually verified images covering license plate layouts from all 50 United States. The dataset includes variations in illumination, viewpoint, weather, blur, occlusion, and plate design. The framework is converted to an INT8 TensorRT engine and evaluated on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano with 8 GB memory. The INT8 model shows an mAP50 of 97.8% and a full-sequence accuracy of 90.7%. It records 147 FPS at 6.8 ms end-to-end latency, with 315 MB inference memory and 9.4 W average power consumption. Relative to the YOLOv8s+CRNN baseline, the proposed deployment provides a 7.1x throughput increase and a 77.8% reduction in allocated inference memory

title: ScrapeBench: Evaluating Legal Compliance of AI Agents in Website Scraping
abstract: AI agents deployed on the open web are becoming more capable of performing actions that may breach contractual provisions and violate computer security laws. In this paper, we introduce ScrapeBench, the first agentic benchmark for empirically evaluating the legal compliance of AI agents with website scraping policies, namely terms of service (ToS) and $\texttt{robots.txt}$ directives. Across widely used closed-weight and open-weight AI agents, we find that most agents exhibit low compliance rates (< 5%) when instructed to scrape websites in our sample of 1,626 popular websites that explicitly prohibit scraping. In addition, we observe that even where AI agents actively check the applicable ToS and $\texttt{robots.txt}$, they continue to exhibit low compliance rates. Conversely, in our sample of 269 websites that do not prohibit scraping, we observe that agents sometimes refuse to scrape despite it being lawful, such as Claude Opus 4.6 exhibiting an over-refusal rate of 98.5%. Our human baseline experiments (n = 180 participants) suggest that humans exhibit compliance rates comparable to AI agents but over-refuse at much higher rates.

title: Linking Event-sequence Data Claims to Analytic Provenance in Chatbots: Technique and Evaluation
abstract: Chatbots are increasingly used to analyze temporal event sequences of which website clickstreams are among the most common. Explanations are essential for understanding claims about event-sequence data. However, existing systems often require programming expertise to interpret these explanations and fail to explain the data processes underlying the data claims. We introduce a technique for linking a data claim to its analytic provenance (i.e., the analytic steps and results that produced it). It has two components: a reference table that records analytic steps and results in addressable cells, and a citation format that binds each claim to one or more cells. To operationalize this technique for clickstream analysis, we curated a set of analytic operations for clickstream analysis, organized them through a pivot-table abstraction, and developed tools that an AI agent can invoke to create a reference table and assemble a natural language response with cited data claims. To evaluate how citations affect users' assessment of data claims, we conducted two crowdsourced experiments with 90 participants each. The experiments showed that participants perceived correct data claims to be more accurate with citations when compared with no explanations, and that they perceived incorrect data claims to be less accurate with citations when compared with code and no explanations.

title: Conditional Diffusion-Based Proxy Representation Recovery for BCVA Prediction with Missing SLO Modality
abstract: Preoperative prediction of postoperative best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) can support prognosis assessment and individualized decision-making in cataract surgery. Multimodal learning can integrate preoperative optical coherence tomography (OCT) images, scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO) images, and clinical text to characterize patient status. However, SLO images are often missing in real-world clinical data due to acquisition or data-management issues, resulting in incomplete multimodal inputs. To address this problem, this paper proposes a conditional diffusion-based method for SLO proxy representation recovery and fusion prediction. Instead of reconstructing raw SLO images, the proposed method formulates SLO missingness as proxy representation recovery in the latent feature space. Specifically, OCT image features and clinical text features are first fused to construct an OCT-text conditional representation, which guides the reverse denoising process of the diffusion model to estimate sample-specific SLO proxy representations. The recovered SLO proxy representation is then used as a substitute for the unavailable SLO modality and incorporated into the downstream multimodal fusion prediction network for postoperative BCVA prediction. Experiments were conducted on 2,141 preoperative multimodal cataract samples, with an SLO missing rate of 58.80%. The proposed method achieved an accuracy of 0.9714 under the criterion of an absolute prediction error within 0.1 LogMAR and a mean absolute error of 0.0423, outperforming representative postoperative visual acuity prediction and missing-modality learning methods. These results indicate that representation-level proxy recovery can alleviate the impact of SLO modality missingness on postoperative BCVA prediction.

title: DIY Customized Speech Recognition for a Person with Speech Disabilities
abstract: General-purpose state-of-the-art automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems fail systematically for speakers with moderate to severe speech disabilities. This paper describes the design, implementation, and evaluation of a customized ASR system built for the first author, a researcher with cerebral palsy and dysarthria. We fine-tuned OpenAI's Whisper medium and large-v3 models using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on audio samples recorded from the first author's own speech on consumer-grade hardware. On a held-out test set of 100 previously unseen utterances, the corresponding transcriptions resulted in a Word Error Rate drop from 49% to 17% for medium and from 30% to 12% for large-v3, while the Character Error Rate fell from 26% to 7% for medium and from 16% to 5% for large-v3, indicating that the residual errors are minor phonemic substitutions. Based on these models, the first author developed AVoz, a mobile application that acts as a real-time interpreter, converting his speech into synthesized voice for the listener. All processing is performed locally, ensuring that no audio data leaves the user's machine. We argue that the methodology is replicable. Moreover, we publish the full LoRA configuration, the implementation, and a step-by-step recording and training protocol, so that other people with speech disabilities, or their family members and caregivers, can build their own systems with a few hours of labeled audio data and a couple of days of GPU time.

title: Agentic Attribution of Cloud Resource Ownership
abstract: Security tools raise findings across cloud environments, and AI agents now investigate and prioritize them. A finding is still resolved by people: it has to reach the people responsible for fixing it and accountable for the resource it concerns. Ownership is the organizational context that decides who that is. Where recorded, it is declared by hand in configuration management databases or owner tags and goes stale unless kept current; accounts are shared, and automation creates much of the infrastructure. The knowledge sits in work records, code history, audit logs and identity directories, encoded in each organization's own conventions. Recovering it poses four challenges: the signal is scattered across sources, none of them authoritative; the conventions that carry it differ between organizations; reaching an owner takes multi-hop links; and those related to a resource differ in the strength of their relation. We define ownership as a set of entities, people or teams, each related to the resource by one of five patterns ordered by strength. We present a reference architecture for agentic ownership attribution that derives ownership from these records instead of declaring it: it profiles an organization offline into tested signal procedures and an ownership playbook, then attributes each resource with a coordinator agent and parallel investigators, with confidence computed by rules. On 100 resources of 50 Amazon Web Services (AWS) resource types in one organization, we pool the architecture's candidates with those of an unprimed general-purpose agent and verify every evidence piece against the records. The architecture reaches 92.1% weighted recall and 86.6% weighted precision, against 54.8% and 77.4%, at 0.55 times the agent's cost per unit of coverage. The difference lies in people who build and change resources without an explicit owner, found through work records and code history.

title: Agent Self-Improvement with Frozen Weights: The Added Value and Limits of Failure Traces
abstract: We evaluate whether an AI agent's harness, the notes around its model, can learn from the agent's failure traces beyond a matched search that never sees them. It can, but less than it looks. We tested an open 9-billion-parameter model with fixed weights; a larger teacher model wrote its notes. On generated customer-service decisions, where both note writers were told the target rules, notes based on the agent's mistakes improved accuracy by 4.0 percentage points over notes from the same process with the mistakes withheld. That process alone, trying and keeping better-scoring notes, reached about 60% of the total improvement. In full customer-service conversations the same notes showed no demonstrated improvement. Separately, a strict screen of single lessons admitted two customer-service lessons, still awaiting tests on new data, and one tool-use lesson, written without seeing the agent's mistakes, which showed no demonstrated gain on new tool-use tasks. A neutral note with no procedure scored higher than the learned lessons (exploratory). A blind audit judged 146 of 240 tool-use test items defective.

title: AOP-Smart-Finder: A High-Throughput Human-AI Hybrid Framework for AOP Discovery and Evidence Mapping from Large-Scale Literature
abstract: The rapid growth of scientific literature and the high heterogeneity of biological terminology and mechanistic descriptions make it difficult for researchers to integrate scattered research evidence, identify connections among biological events, and construct mechanistic networks. Here, we developed a high-throughput human-AI hybrid framework, AOP-Smart-Finder, for biological event discovery, relationship mining, and Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) construction and evidence mapping from large-scale literature. This framework integrates Large Language Models (LLMs), AOP-Smart retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technology, and Python-based automation, supporting two analysis modes: one based on a single compound and the other based on a predefined set of biological events. In the di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) case, the system processed 12,983 articles within 30 min and included 1,093 of them, from which it extracted 1,589 biological events (including 458 official key events [KEs] and 1,131 candidate KEs) and 2,519 key event relationships (KERs). In the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) case, the system identified 55 stressors from 437 articles and extracted 278 biological events and 548 event relationships. Following manual curation and Weight of Evidence (WoE) evaluation, a mechanistic network comprising 16 KEs and 23 KERs was ultimately constructed. This framework can either use existing AOPs as knowledge guidance for mechanistic expansion and evidence supplementation, or discover novel event connections and construct mechanistic networks around user-specified research topics. It provides a high-throughput, traceable, human-AI hybrid methodology for complex biological mechanism elucidation and AOP discovery driven by large-scale literature.

title: Probing Exotic Electron-Electron Interactions via Adiabatic Spin Inversion in MRFM
abstract: Light bosons beyond the Standard Model can mediate exotic spin-dependent interactions between electrons, motivating sensitive searches at short distances. We propose a magnetic resonance force microscopy (MRFM) scheme that exploits oscillating-cantilever-driven adiabatic reversals (OSCAR) of electron spins to convert these interactions into measurable mechanical signals. The ferromagnetic tip serves as both a dense polarized-spin source and a source of magnetic-field gradients, enabling force detection without magnetic shielding between the source and sensor. Within a linearized treatment of the coupled spin-mechanical dynamics, we derive resonance-frequency shifts associated with the $V_2$ and $V_3$ interactions and a second-harmonic force signal arising from the velocity-dependent $V_8$ interaction. We further investigate interrupted-OSCAR differential detection and distance-dependent measurements to discriminate exotic signals from conventional magnetic backgrounds. Using representative parameters from ensemble and single-spin MRFM experiments, we estimate the projected sensitivity under specified noise and statistical assumptions. The results suggest that the proposed scheme could provide complementary sensitivity to short-range spin-dependent interactions, with the potential to improve existing constraints on $V_2$ over selected submicrometer interaction ranges. Our study establishes adiabatic spin-inversion MRFM as a promising approach to probing exotic electron-electron forces.

title: Does Predictive Performance Translate to Causal Performance? Evaluating tabular foundation models as nuisance learners for causal effect estimation
abstract: Tabular foundation models based on prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) achieve strong predictive performance, but their value for causal inference is unclear. We evaluated whether PFNs, which predict through in-context learning, could match or outperform conventional nuisance learners in supporting accurate causal estimation and reliable uncertainty quantification (inference). Learners modeled propensity scores and outcome regressions within doubly robust estimators of average causal effects, with and without cross-fitting, across synthetic and semi-synthetic settings with varying confounding complexity and effect heterogeneity. Under simple parametric data-generating processes, the PFNs were competitive with correctly specified parametric regressions and ensembles containing them. In more complex settings, they outperformed all conventional learners evaluated, including richly specified Super Learner ensembles, for both accuracy and uncertainty quantification. As sample size increased, only the two PFN models (TabPFN and Mitra) consistently approached nominal confidence interval coverage, whereas under-coverage persisted for conventional learners. In some settings, PFNs achieved near-nominal coverage and well-calibrated standard errors even without cross-fitting. At the smallest sample size (n=200) and in the higher-dimensional semi-synthetic settings, PFNs and other flexible learners exhibited poor coverage without cross-fitting. For PFNs, this appeared to be driven by propensity score overfitting consistent with in-sample memorization of treatment labels. These findings highlight the promise of prior-data fitted networks as in-context nuisance learners for causal estimation, while underscoring the need for further evaluation in challenging settings.

title: Decomposing Earth Embeddings with Sparse Autoencoders
abstract: Earth observation foundation models produce global metre-resolution embeddings that underpin work across agriculture, ecology, hydrology, and beyond. Yet these embeddings are opaque: each dimension entangles unrelated physical concepts, which makes them difficult to interpret and their robustness hard to assess. Here, we propose sparse autoencoders (SAEs) as a principled way to decompose Earth embeddings into sparse, approximately monosemantic features over an overcomplete dictionary. Because LLM judges of interpretations do not transfer to satellite pixels, and spatial autocorrelation matters, we introduce a tailored evaluation protocol. It scores any SAE on reconstruction at matched sparsity, alignment with reference concepts, and spatial scale, each against baselines that include an SAE whose decoder is a frozen random dictionary. On this protocol, SAEs reconstruct AlphaEarth and Tessera embeddings better than every baseline at matched sparsity. Their features align with far fewer reference concepts than raw embedding dimensions (on AlphaEarth, 88% align with at most one of 20 concept groups, most with none, against a median of 12 per raw dimension). They also carry more of their variance at fine spatial scales (23 to 32% within a 640 m patch for BatchTopK and Matryoshka, against 9%). An SAE with a frozen random decoder shares both properties, which therefore follow from sparsity, whereas only a learned dictionary reconstructs the embedding accurately: on AlphaEarth, trained SAEs leave eight times less variance unexplained. We test the sparse code on two applications, discovering land-cover sub-concepts and detecting out-of-distribution pixels by area-of-applicability estimation. Both indicate how sparse features could be used, but neither is yet reliable enough for practical use. Together, these results are a step toward Earth observation models whose features can be inspected.

title: RoCoMark: Robust Code Watermarking Against LLM-Based Functionality-Preserving Rewriting Attacks
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) present significant challenges to source tracing of generated code, as LLM rewriting can substantially alter the syntactic and structural characteristics of watermarked code. However, existing watermarking methods often suffer severe performance degradation under LLM-based functionality-preserving rewriting attacks. We attribute this vulnerability not merely to the intensity of rewriting, but to a fundamental distribution mismatch between the perturbations encountered during watermark training and the global, non-deterministic rewriting behaviors induced by LLMs. In order to deal with this challenge, we propose RoCoMark, a Robust Code waterMarking framework that explicitly learns and adapts to LLM rewriting behaviors. RoCoMark is a multi-round minimax game between the watermark embedder and LLM rewriter. In each round, the embedder first learns threat profiling from LLM-rewritten code by optimizing the watermark encoder through contrastive learning and knowledge distillation while mitigating catastrophic representation drift. Then the embedder improves strategies by optimizing the watermark encoder and extractor simultaneously. Finally, an adaptive attack-evolution mechanism based on Reflexion and short- and long-term memory pools is applied, enabling continuous interaction between the watermark embedder and evolving rewriting strategies. This iterative attacker-defender process progressively improves the robustness of the watermark against diverse and previously unseen LLM rewriting behaviors. Extensive experiments on four typical benchmarks, under attacks generated by five LLMs, show the effectiveness of RoCoMark. RoCoMark achieves an average detection AUROC of 74.2% and a Rewrite BitACC of 75.3%, while maintaining a code functionality pass rate above 99.7%.

title: MOMENT-DP: Momentum Aware Evaluation of Correlated Noise for Differentially Private Training
abstract: Temporally correlated noise can substantially improve the utility of differentially private optimization, yet candidate mechanisms are commonly designed or evaluated using only partial information about the optimization process, such as workload structure, learning-rate schedules, or local curvature. We study whether persistent optimizer state provides additional information that can change the relative utility of privacy-valid correlated-noise mechanisms. We introduce MOMENT-DP, an optimizer-state-aware framework that models how temporally correlated privacy noise propagates through momentum-based optimization. For locally quadratic objectives, MOMENT-DP expresses privacy-induced final loss through an optimizer transfer operator that jointly captures curvature, learning-rate scheduling, momentum, and temporal noise covariance. NoiseCurve's curvature-aware quadratic criterion is recovered exactly as the zero-momentum, constant-learning-rate special case. Changing only momentum while holding curvature, schedule, privacy calibration, and candidate mechanisms fixed induces genuine mechanism-ranking reversals. The effect persists outside exact quadratic dynamics in per-example-clipped private logistic regression, while remaining unresolved in the neural regime we study. These results establish optimizer state as an under-modeled, decision-relevant axis in evaluating temporally correlated privacy noise.

title: When Normality Shifts: Multi-Level WavLM Modeling for Open-World Audio Deepfake Detection
abstract: Audio deepfake detectors trained with known synthesis attacks can learn generator-specific shortcuts that fail as synthesis systems and acoustic conditions evolve.
