We investigate an attack-free alternative: a normality model trained exclusively on bona fide speech, which scores synthetic audio by its deviation from authentic representations. We propose MLN-WavLM, a method that applies shrinkage-Mahalanobis modeling to pooled hidden states from a frozen large-scale, pre-trained speech processing WavLM Base+ architecture. Evaluated on ASVspoof 2019 LA, our best attack-free variant achieves an 8.45\% Equal Error Rate (EER), closely tracking a fully supervised WavLM-HM-Conformer baseline (7.86%). However, when subjected to the ASVspoof 2021 DF domain shift, performance drops to 22.12% EER, exposing vulnerabilities in the bona-fide-calibrated operating point. Layer-wise analysis reveals that early WavLM representations dominate the ensemble. To test real-world viability, we simulated deployment streams using unlabeled threshold adaptation. While robust median/MAD recalibration easily handles in-domain contamination up to 10%, recalibrating under the 2021 DF domain shift triggers a total collapse of low-FPR recall. We conclude that while frozen source-domain normality can effectively rank deepfakes, it does not yield a stable open-world decision rule, and downstream threshold adaptation cannot rescue upstream ranking degradation.

title: GOPR-CAD: Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning for CAD Generation
abstract: Generating accurate CAD models requires substantial engineering expertise and careful control of geometry, topology, and mechanical constraints. Text-to-CAD aims to simplify this process, but current LLM-based methods often generate CAD programs directly. Language models remain unreliable when producing long code while coordinating coupled geometric, topological, and dimensional constraints. Consequently, executable programs may still produce structurally incorrect models, which execution rate and rendered appearance may fail to reveal. To address these limitations, we propose GOPR-CAD, an agentic Text-to-CAD pipeline based on Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning. A language model acts as a decision agent over encapsulated CAD operations and progressively constructs an executable operation graph, which a deterministic compiler converts into the final CAD model. This separation requires no additional training and supports different language models. To evaluate structural fidelity, we construct MHCAD, a benchmark of 300 standard mechanical part requirements derived from Machinery's Handbook. Their explicit structures enable reference-free STEP/B-rep evaluation. GOPR-CAD achieves 82.7% Structural Yield on MHCAD, and 87.2% Structural Yield on an external CADPrompt subset.

title: Learning through Capacity Awareness to Minimize Hospital Readmissions
abstract: Predictive algorithms are increasingly used to guide hospital discharge decisions, yet these models can exhibit censoring bias for vulnerable patients due to insufficient historical data or past discharge decisions. When biased readmission risk predictors are used to inform discharges, the training data generated by discharge decisions may perpetuate similar biases when predictors are re-trained, leading to a vicious cycle. We extend a queueing-based Markov decision process for hospital discharge to incorporate periodically retrained readmission risk predictors. Our key insight is that cost-optimal, "capacity-aware" operational decision policies can naturally diversify the lengths of stay at which patient outcomes are observed, enabling consistent estimation of readmission risk without explicit fairness constraints. We prove that repeated retraining under discharge-up-to policies converges to unbiased risk estimates under well-specification. In synthetic experiments and calibrated simulations based on patient-level data from a partner hospital, we find that where commonly used threshold-on-risk policies can remain persistently biased, discharge-up-to policies reduce learning error over status quo decision policies (such as thresholding on risk) by 24%-25%. These improvements to estimation also mitigate some forms of bias, reducing readmission cost disparities (adjusted for baseline risk differences between demographic groups) by 38%-63%. Our results demonstrate how capacity-aware decision policies can improve both predictive performance and fairness by addressing censoring bias.

title: AgentCT: A Vision-Language Agent for Universal CT Imaging
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) restoration methods often use a single network for low-dose CT (LDCT), sparse-view CT (SVCT), and metal artifact reduction (MAR), despite the distinct physics of these degradations. We propose AgentCT, a vision-language agent that identifies the degradation and routes images to task-specific restoration models. A LoRA-adapted Qwen3-VL-4B controller predicts degradation type and severity, selects a specialist, and reassesses the restored image. The LDCT specialist uses an image-domain diffusion model, whereas the SVCT and MAR specialists combine projection-domain correction, data consistency, differentiable filtered back-projection, and image refinement. We evaluated the controller and specialists separately on patient-disjoint Mayo 2020 abdominal CT data across three severity levels for each degradation. The controller achieved 95.7% accuracy for degradation type and 93.9% for severity, with a 100% JSON parse rate. Using ground-truth degradation labels for routing, AgentCT achieved an overall PSNR/SSIM of 46.18 dB/0.984, compared with 44.93 dB/0.976 for AMIR and 44.29 dB/0.979 for TAMP, and attained the highest PSNR in all nine settings. For SVCT, its dual-domain specialist achieved 46.04 dB with 4.2 million parameters, compared with 44.43 dB for single-task AMIR and 43.57 dB for all-in-one AMIR with 23.5 million parameters. These results support degradation-specific CT restoration with controller-based model selection; evaluation under automatic routing and on independent clinical data remains necessary. Code is available at https://github.com/hao1635/AgentCT.

title: Music Inpainting With Similarity-Guided Latent Diffusion
abstract: We propose a music inpainting technique combining similarity matching and a diffusion-based generative model to replace large segments of audio recordings with suitable alternatives. The proposed hybrid method, Similarity-Guided Diffusion Posterior Sampling (SimDPS), retrieves candidate replacement segments from the wider signal based on contextual similarity and uses them to guide the diffusion process toward coherent reconstructions. Being model-agnostic, the framework is compatible with any pre-trained diffusion model operating in either the waveform or latent domain. Objective evaluations demonstrate that SimDPS outperforms widely adopted RePaint and DPS methods across acoustic features and neural-embedding distance metrics. Subjective evaluations on multi-genre music datasets confirm that SimDPS enhances perceptual plausibility compared to previous diffusion-based methods and demonstrates robustness to poorly matched similarity candidates. These findings pave the way for improved music restoration and context-aware audio editing.

title: Hydrograd v2.0: a differentiable two-dimensional shallow-water model on unstructured meshes with steady and unsteady adjoints for calibration and closure learning
abstract: We present \textit{Hydrograd} v2.0, a significantly improved differentiable 2D shallow-water model written in Python with JAX. The model solves the shallow-water equations on the unstructured meshes of production models such as SRH-2D and HEC-RAS 2D with a well-balanced, positivity-preserving finite-volume scheme that handles wetting and drying. Gradients are tailored to the type of problem. Steady states are found by Newton's method with an exact sparse Jacobian obtained by graph colouring, and their gradients follow from the implicit function theorem at the cost of one linear solve. Unsteady flows are differentiated in reverse mode with checkpointing, or with an implicit time integrator whose gradient costs about two forward runs. All gradients agree with finite differences, to about $10^{-8}$ for steady flows. On the Savannah River case, the steady water surface differs from that of SRH-2D by 4.7\,mm (root mean square). Steady closure learning was 96 times faster than differentiating through time marching and reached a lower loss. An inflow hydrograph was inverted from stage records with a peak error of 2\,\%. In an unsteady roughness calibration, a singular value decomposition analysis of the sensitivity matrix showed that the stage records at the gauges are 70 to 160 times more sensitive to the total resistance of the reach than to its distribution among the roughness zones, which explains why only a gauge layout with gauges in every zone recovered all five roughness values. On one GPU, a mesh of 512,000 cells takes 7.6\,s for a forward run and 51\,s for a gradient.

title: Safeguarding Agentic AI in Radiology Workflows: A Multimodel Evaluation of Rule-based and Large Language Model-based Verification
abstract: Purpose: To estimate how often tool-using large language model (LLM) agents record clinically relevant false or unsupported information in simulated radiology documentation and how much safeguards applied before each action reduce these errors. Materials and Methods: In this simulation study (October 2026), 48 synthetic, radiologist-reviewed base scenarios covered finding communication, tumor board preparation and follow-up management. Forty-three also had a misleading-information variant (91 variants). Six LLM agents (Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6.1-Sol, GLM-5.3, MiniMax M3, Gemma-4-31B, Qwen3.8-27B) completed each variant with permissions only, deterministic rules, and rules plus a locally run LLM checker (1638 episodes). The primary outcome was at least one executed high-severity violation per episode. Risk differences were estimated per agent at base-scenario level and, exploratorily, pooled across agents, with analyses of document access and blocks. Results: With permissions only, 7.3%-27.1% of episodes had a high-severity violation (pooled across agents, 19.4%). Pooled, it was 16.7% with rules (-2.8 percentage points; 95% CI: -6.1, 0.5) and 13.2% with rules plus the LLM checker (-6.2; 95% CI: -9.5, -3.0). Adding the LLM checker to rules changed it by -3.5 (95% CI: -6.3, -0.7). No difference between agents was detected (P = .43), and task success did not decrease detectably. In misleading variants, agents opened the altered document in 83% of episodes regardless of error, and 58% of erroneous statements cited it. Most blocked actions (64%-68%) would not have caused a violation and were returned for revision. Conclusion: Layered safeguards reduced but did not prevent high-severity errors. Errors after misleading information reflected misjudged rather than missed information.

title: Solar cycle variations of meridional flow and differential rotation in a non-kinematic dynamo model
abstract: Flux transport dynamo models have emerged as the leading paradigm for explaining the observed solar cycle. However, most of these models are kinematic and axisymmetric. We develop a non-kinematic dynamo model by specifying large-scale flows, such as the differential rotation and meridional flow. Thus, our model does not require the $Λ$ effect or other parameterisations of turbulent transport to generate the large-scale flows; it only solves the fluctuating flows and thermodynamics. Our model is inherently 3D by construction, although it is currently operating in axisymmetric mode because the source for poloidal field generation (Babcock-Leighton $α$) is assumed to be axisymmetric. Our model reproduces solar-cycle variations in both the meridional flow and the differential rotation -- specifically, the torsional oscillation in some agreement with observations. The model naturally exhibits some variability in the solar cycle, even without incorporating stochastic fluctuations, offering a new methodology for modelling the non-kinematic solar dynamo in 3D.

title: HydroTuring: A physics probe benchmark testing mass, energy, and momentum conservation in hydrologic models
abstract: Hydrologic models, including deep learning systems now deployed for operational flood forecasting, are evaluated primarily by how closely their simulated hydrographs match observed streamflow. However, high hydrograph skill does not guarantee physical consistency: in a synthetic calibration experiment, a conceptual model that loses 15% of its water input to an unreported sink still reaches a Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.93, and no shared benchmark tests whether models obey fundamental conservation laws. Here we introduce HydroTuring (v0.1.0), a black-box benchmark of 37 physics probes that test mass (24 probes), energy (7) and momentum (6) conservation in hydrologic models. Each probe runs a controlled experiment on forcing generated at run time from a recorded seed and applies binary pass or fail criteria validated against 18 physically exact and 59 deliberately broken reference models. Across 32 evaluated models (3 exact references, 7 AI-based models and 22 process-based models), only the 3 exact references pass every probe among the 28 models scored on 5 or more probes. Process-based and AI-based models pass similar shares of their scored probes (76% and 74%), and a pre-trained flood-forecasting LSTM fails 6 of the 11 runoff-only probes it can be scored on. Furthermore, 49% of all 1,184 model-probe pairs remain unscored because models omit the required state or flux variables, while the scored failures occur in perturbation responses and state bounds rather than long-term water-budget closure. HydroTuring provides a reproducible smoke test for model development, peer review and operational deployment under an open community protocol.

title: Hadronic final-state effects on open-charm production at LHC energies
abstract: We investigate the influence of hadronic final-state interactions on open-charm observables in pp and Pb+Pb collisions at LHC energies within the microscopic Parton-Hadron-String Dynamics (PHSD) transport approach. Calculations with and without charm-hadron rescattering are compared with ALICE measurements and predictions of the Statistical Hadronization Model for charm. The relative integrated $D$-meson multiplicities are essentially insensitive to hadronic interactions. PHSD reproduces the weak system dependence of the nonstrange $D$-meson ratios and the increase of $D_s^+/D^0$ from pp to Pb+Pb collisions, consistent with the statistical-model trend from strangeness undersaturation towards equilibrium. In contrast, hadronic rescattering redistributes the transverse momentum spectra at low and intermediate momenta and enhances the elliptic flow. These results demonstrate the importance of accounting for the hadronic evolution when extracting QGP properties from differential open-charm observables.

title: HEART: a resonance-cascade model of soft hadron production in p+p collisions at 158 GeV/c
abstract: Fischer and co-workers interpret the NA49 identified-hadron spectra in p+p collisions at 158 GeV/c as the sum of a target and a projectile component, each the decay of an excited hadronic system. This paper supplies an event-level realization of that picture, the HEART model (Hadronic Excitations And Resonance Transitions), and tests it on the published NA49 data. Single diffraction, double diffraction, and non-diffractive exchange produce color-singlet excited systems. Each system is a catalogued resonance below a duality boundary of 1.7 to 2.2 GeV or a member of a resonant continuum above it. It de-excites by successive two-body transitions with exact conservation laws, and one-pion exchange produces the leading neutrons. Fourteen parameters are fitted to 1,254 points of the $π^\pm$, $K^\pm$, $p$, and $\bar{p}$ double-differential cross sections and eight neutron points. Under an error model that profiles the correlated systematic uncertainties, with a declared 5% model floor, the fit yields $χ^2 = 2263$ on 1248 degrees of freedom. On the same points, EPOS-LHC, UrQMD, and PYTHIA 8 at their published tunes give $χ^2$ values 4.2 to 14.4 times higher. The model needs no central source. The forward $K^+$ deficit, the forward $K^*(892)^0$ excess, and the flat $Λ$ $x_F$ distribution point to the momentum sharing at the vertex where the leading baryon turns into a hyperon. The $Ξ^-$ reaches 0.61 of the NA61/SHINE yield. The charged multiplicity of a heavy excited system grows linearly with its mass, faster than in $e^+e^-$ annihilation. The observables that distinguish a cascade from string and fireball models lie in the fragmentation region, where wide-acceptance fixed-target spectrometers can measure them.

title: LAION-Audio-XL: A Web-Scale Corpus and Scaling Studies for Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining
abstract: Recent progress on contrastive audio-language models can be attributed mainly to the scale and quality of their training data. Larger training datasets expose models to a broader range of sounds and corresponding audio captions. To exploit this, we collect 1.48 billion audio samples from academic datasets, internet datasets, web collections, Common Crawl, and YouTube, and process them with a multi-stage curation pipeline. Furthermore, we generate short and long captions for samples in our corpus that lack them. We use our dataset to study the scaling behavior of contrastive audio-language models based on the NaFlex architecture for the audio encoder. Our experiments identify trade-offs between model size and training data for a given compute budget. Moreover, our resulting models, CLAP2, outperform prior audio-text models of comparable size on the MAEB and HEAR benchmarks. We release our dataset, captions, model checkpoints, and code.

title: Practical Deep Learning-Based Block Demapping for mmWave MIMO Systems
abstract: Deep learning is expected to play a central role in 6G systems, by enabling data-driven physical layer designs that can adapt to practical wireless impairments. This is particularly important for millimetre-wave (mmWave) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, which are strongly affected by residual channel distortions, interference, and hardware non-idealities that are difficult to capture with analytical models. In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based soft demapper that performs block-wise processing of received symbols instead of conventional symbol-wise detection. The demapper employs a one-dimensional convolutional neural network to learn temporal structure induced by practical propagation and hardware effects, while producing soft bit outputs compatible with soft-decision decoding stages. The proposed approach is trained and evaluated for a 4$\times$4 wideband mmWave MIMO system at 60~GHz, using an over-the-air dataset collected across multiple days and settings. Experimental results demonstrate consistent improvements over a conventional soft-decision demapper, including up to a 2.6$\times$ reduction in bit error rate for 16QAM and up to a 17.6$\times$ reduction for 64QAM under real over-the-air mmWave MIMO conditions. The proposed demapper is further implemented on a Zynq RFSoC platform using a reconfigurable convolution engine and fixed-point arithmetic, achieving an approximately 34.3$\times$ speedup compared to a processor-based implementation, and demonstrating that learning-based demapping can be deployed efficiently on resource-constrained edge hardware.

title: A software infrastructure proposal for mathematical research with AI agents
abstract: In 2026, AI agents began to produce mathematical results. They formalize complete theorems and settle open problems faster than a research group can review the results. The difficulty is shifting to organizing that output, deciding which results to trust and understanding them as a group. Current tools address particular problems or assist individual researchers, and none of them is designed as the shared working environment of a research group. We propose the design of a self-hosted environment in which a group of people and agents does its daily mathematical work. It consists of a small open core, which each group deploys with the resources it has and adapts through extensions. The core records who did what and gives every message and result a stable address. We also outline how the formal libraries of different groups, maintained mostly by agents, can form a network. We describe Stemma, an early prototype that implements part of the proposal, and illustrate it with a synthetic example.

title: Adjoint Kernel Sensitivity of the Rough Heston Characteristic Exponent
abstract: Multi-factor approximations of rough volatility kernels affect the characteristic exponents used in Fourier-based derivative valuation. We derive an adjoint representation for the first-order sensitivity of the rough Heston characteristic exponent with respect to its memory kernel, with model parameters and the input variance curve held fixed. The Volterra--Riccati functional $\mathcal L_T(K,z)$ admits a local real-analytic extension, jointly in the kernel perturbation and the transform parameter. The Fréchet derivative of this extension with respect to the kernel in $L^1$ is represented by integration against a continuous sensitivity kernel $B_K(u,z)$, obtained from a backward linear Volterra equation and independent of the perturbation direction. This representation resolves the leading-order contributions of kernel perturbations across memory lags. On the structural kernel class, which contains the fractional kernel and its multi-factor approximations and has empty interior in $L^1$, the extension yields Hadamard directional differentiability and a first-order expansion with a quadratic $L^1$-remainder for all sufficiently close structural kernels, uniformly on compact subsets of the strip of transform parameters. The same sensitivity kernel yields multi-factor weight and decay-rate derivatives. Numerical experiments at multi-factor reference kernels assess the finite-resolution implementation and illustrate how the lag distribution of positive perturbations with equal $L^1$ mass affects the first-order response.

title: Projective symmetries and differential recursions for the large-$N$ Gross--Witten--Wadia and one-dimensional QCD matrix models
abstract: We compare the fixed-charge planar Gross--Witten--Wadia (GWW) model with source-free one-dimensional QCD at large $N$ and $N_f/N$ fixed. In both models the resolvent and one-cut condition give an algebraic equation for a derivative of the free energy: a quartic for GWW and a sextic for QCD. Finite-$N$ Toeplitz determinants independently check the selected QCD branch. Signed permutations of homogeneous parameter triples realize $S_4$; the resulting action on the algebraic branches and operator labels gives a common projective description of the two models. For QCD, the sextic yields a differential recurrence linking small-charge rows two apart. The same second-order PDE gives a finite-width column recursion that reconstructs the coefficient pyramid from its GWW boundary. A distinct boundary, obtained from the first resummed coefficient, is the Narayana triangle. A formally collapsed slice counts decorated bipartite plane trees and admits an exact symmetric product formula. The many-flavor scaling reduces the sextic to the quartic and retains transverse projective data: the QCD divided-difference triple coalesces at this boundary, whereas the limiting quartic satisfies the full standard GWW third-order system. We distinguish algebraic degree, mixed differential order, and fixed-parameter ordinary differential order throughout.

title: The Average Patient: Do Simulated Psychiatric Patients Answer Like Real People?
abstract: Language models are used as simulated psychiatric patients to train clinicians and evaluate AI therapists, and are judged by plausibility or total scores. We give a framework for simulated respondents: an information budget bounds how much simulated patients can differ, and an average-patient hypothesis, that a model answers each item at the level typical of the named condition and severity, implies little variation, a full profile of the condition's typical symptoms and totals at or above the top of the stated severity band. We examine these implications at matched totals on item-level data from eight human samples, including a clinical and an instructed-feigning sample. Across 17 models, simulated patients vary 1.5 to 11 times less than real respondents with the same total and on most questionnaires endorse nearly every symptom at a middling level; on the PHQ-9 their symptoms covary less like real ones. People, honest or feigning, answer "not at all" about as often as genuine patients with the same totals, and more often than every model. Single answers are highly concentrated, and prompt changes, published personas, larger models and reasoning reduce the pattern without removing it. In interviews, patients told a severity are rated as having nearly every symptom, so an assessment agent's recognition of absent symptoms goes untested, and scored against the stated severity the agent places a quarter of them in their band, against about half of patients given a real symptom profile. Having the model word such a profile restores half to two thirds of the variation.

title: A Physical Testbed for Self-Driving Laboratories: Comparing Bayesian and Agentic Optimization in a Minimal Closed-Loop Color Formulation Task
abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) integrate laboratory robotics and automation with AI-driven decision-making to close the design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycle. However, physical testbeds that combine off-the-shelf hardware and AI into a functioning closed-loop workflow remain in early stages of development, and their integration with commercial laboratory automation is comparatively less developed. In this work, we develop a physical testbed that assembles and integrates commercially available laboratory automation instruments and demonstrate continuous, closed-loop, autonomous operation over 24 cumulative hours of unattended experimentation. We validate this platform on a minimal closed-loop discovery task in which the system autonomously formulates aqueous dye mixtures to match a target absorbance spectrum. The system completed six independent campaigns, each consisting of 48 closed-loop iterations over approximately four hours. In every campaign, the system autonomously selected, dispensed, and measured each mixture, with an AI-driven decision-making algorithm determining subsequent formulations without human intervention. Using this testbed, we compared the performance of two AI-driven decision-making algorithms, traditional Bayesian optimization (BO) and an agentic approach, in selecting mixtures under a fixed total-volume constraint. The agentic optimizer matched target absorbance spectra using fewer iterations than BO, with reductions up to 52%, and converged on a solution for one target that BO failed to match within 48 iterations. These results demonstrate a reference physical platform for SDLs that can evaluate both established and emerging AI strategies, including large language model (LLM)-directed optimization, before their deployment in real-world applications where experiments may be costly and time-consuming to prepare.

title: MADSNet: A Multi-Scale Axial-Attentive Dense Spiking Network for Spike Camera Image Reconstruction
abstract: Spike cameras encode dynamic scenes into high-temporal-resolution binary spike streams for efficient high-speed vision. Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) can process such signals with sparse and accumulate-only computation, existing SNN-based reconstruction methods are typically shallow and still lag behind ANN-based models in reconstruction fidelity. This paper proposes MADSNet, a Multi-scale Axial-attentive Dense Spiking Network for spike camera image reconstruction. MADSNet adopts a hierarchical spiking encoder--decoder, where a multi-scale spike stem extracts early features, axial spike attention captures long-range dependencies, a dense spiking bottleneck enhances feature reuse, and a spike-to-continuous decoder reconstructs continuous intensity images from spike-domain representations. Experiments on gray-scale and color spike reconstruction show that MADSNet outperforms SSIR by 4.3 dB PSNR and Spk2ImgNet by 1.94 dB on SREDS. Compared with Spk2ImgNet, it achieves about 15$\times$ lower latency and uses only about 1/40 of the estimated energy, demonstrating that carefully designed SNN architectures can improve reconstruction quality while preserving computational efficiency.

title: Evidence-Grounded Iterative Reasoning for the Diagnosis of Diffuse Cystic Lung Diseases
abstract: Overlapping imaging manifestations complicate the differential diagnosis of Diffuse Cystic Lung Diseases (DCLDs), while limited annotated data constrain supervised model development. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can integrate imaging and clinical information, but their diagnostic reasoning remains limited by incomplete volumetric perception and insufficient grounding in disease-specific evidence. We propose DCLDs-EIR, an evidence-grounded iterative reasoning framework coupling diagnostic hypothesis refinement with multimodal evidence acquisition and verification. Multiview renderings of predicted lung and cyst segmentations characterize global cyst distributions and initialize the differential diagnosis. Competing hypotheses guide axial CT inspection to identify local findings that, together with clinical context, inform retrieval from a disease-specific knowledge graph. Accumulated patient observations and retrieved knowledge are jointly assessed for diagnostic support and refutation to revise the diagnostic state. Updated hypotheses and unresolved distinctions guide subsequent inspection, forming a feedback loop between evidence acquisition and hypothesis verification. Multicenter evaluation demonstrates that DCLDs-EIR consistently improves diagnostic accuracy over baselines and enables traceable differential diagnosis through explicit links between diagnostic hypotheses, patient observations, and disease-specific knowledge.

title: Multimodal Graph Learning: A Survey of Models, Benchmarks, and Frontiers
abstract: Multimodal attributed graphs (MAGs), in which nodes carry text, images, and other modalities while edges encode relations among entities, underlie e-commerce, social media, content platforms, and creative applications. Learning on MAGs has developed along two complementary lines: graph-centric methods redesign how modalities are fused, propagated, and connected within message passing, while foundation-model-centric methods pretrain transferable multimodal graph encoders or bring graph context into multimodal large language models for prediction and generation. In parallel, several benchmarks have appeared with different datasets and evaluation protocols. This survey takes an algorithm-centric and evaluation-grounded view of the field and makes three contributions. Modeling: we introduce a unified message-passing formulation and organize methods into five integration levels (feature, propagation, topology, learning, and foundation model), covering discriminative and graph-conditioned generative models; within this formulation we derive representative methods as special cases, compare their assumptions, expressiveness, and cost, and identify cross-modal sensitivity as a property that separates otherwise similar architectures. Datasets and evaluation: we review recent benchmarks, summarize their datasets and metrics, define model-independent descriptors (label homophily, average degree, clustering, and edge provenance), and map each evaluation protocol to the baselines it uses. Frontiers: we connect multimodal graph learning to AI agents, covering the multimodal graphs that agents perceive and remember and graph engineering, the practice of organizing agent workflows as explicit graphs; we then discuss open problems, concrete efforts for the community, and research directions, including when graph structure helps in the presence of strong multimodal foundation models.

title: PhysMoE: Fast Spatial Grounding with Single-Token Coordinate Representation in Modality-Decoupled VLMs
abstract: Embodied Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are backbones for robotic planning and manipulation. However, for coordinate prediction in grounding tasks, existing architectures suffer from two distinct bottlenecks: discrete tokenization disrupts spatial continuity with high decoding latency, while standard point regression fails on multi-contact affordances and irregularly shaped targets. To resolve these challenges, we propose PhysMoE, introducing three core contributions: (1) sharing lower layers for multimodal context while routing upper layers to specialized spatial (pixel) and linguistic (text) experts by physical modality, eliminating gradient interference; (2) encoding each coordinate as a single token by reusing the visual encoder's learned positional embeddings, injecting 2D spatial priors to natively align coordinates with visual features and ease training; and (3) differentiable Signed Distance Field (SDF) supervision on pointing, accommodating affordances and irregular geometries without costly mask decoders. Compared to the base model, PhysMoE achieves a 15.7% average gain and an 8.31x throughput speedup across 9 coordinate-based grounding benchmarks (trajectory, affordance, and localization), while preserving multimodal understanding and reasoning across 11 text-based embodied benchmarks.

title: Seeing Is Not Believing: Counterfactual Lesion Erasure Teaches a Small Medical Vision-Language Agent to Report Only What the Image Shows
abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) often report a finding because the question names it; standard benchmarks miss this. From public segmentation datasets we build counterfactual views without manual annotation: the lesion erased by inpainting, a same-shape control edit elsewhere, and unedited lesion-free images. The evidence sensitivity gap (ESG) is the rate of absent-or-refer answers after erasure minus the rate after the control edit; it is zero for a model that ignores the image or reacts to both edits alike. MedScope-4B (Qwen3.5-4B, LoRA, image tools) was trained on label-derived trajectories, selected by a pre-registered rule and tested once against nine frontier and six open VLMs; four pre-registered checks then probed the mechanism. On 507 internal cases across five imaging types, MedScope-4B reached ESG 0.758 and claimed an erased lesion in 9.6% of cases, against 0.27-0.47 and 41-62% for the frontier models (all p<0.001), without significant loss of accuracy on real lesions. Without counterfactual views ESG fell to 0.279+-0.107 (three seeds); the effect replicated on MedGemma 1.5 4B and two unseen inpainting tools. At four external centres the advantage held but frontier models detected more real lesions; on a fresh external test MedScope-4B detected 0 of 48 pneumothorax films, with net utility below gemini-4-argon's (-0.36 [-0.50, -0.23]). Matching the control edit was not shown to matter; over three seeds no fresh-external ESG advantage over removal-based DPO was established; a paired-view consistency objective did not beat a matched-compute control, while that continuation alone cut erased-lesion claims on unseen tools at every seed, at a cost in sensitivity at one. Training on erased and edited images gives a small model an evidence-gated disposition that prompting does not give frontier models; it does not improve perception, and rare critical findings need coverage.

title: Just AI Governance and the Forbidden-Boundary Principle
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes consequential decisions, yet predictive accuracy is not a sufficient justification for delegated authority. This conceptual study develops an integrated framework for assessing just AI across normative, data, model, and governance layers. Drawing on plural theories of justice, sociotechnical fairness research, and publicly available governance standards, it maps six justice requirements to observable evidence, decision rights, and remedies. It proposes a two-stage evaluation rule: exclude uses that fail independently justified minimum rights constraints, then compare eligible alternatives across multiple performance and governance criteria. As an explicitly limited normative analogy, Genesis chapter 2 motivates a Forbidden-Boundary Principle (FBP), under which an AI agent must not execute externally consequential actions outside pre-authorized boundaries. The resulting First-Principle Safe-Stop Protocol (FPSSP) comprises an independently governed policy monitor, a mandatory execution gate, a restricted or alternative safe-state controller, immutable-oriented audit trails, and accountable human authorization for recovery. We distinguish this normative and traceability contribution from existing Simplex and runtime assurance architectures; we do not claim a novel safety switch or formal proof of universal ethical compliance. A policy schema, threat model, test matrix, outcome definitions, and a prospective comparison design make the proposal falsifiable. No FPSSP implementation, experimental dataset, numerical improvement, or verified latency bound is reported. The framework supports future evaluation rather than constituting evidence of operational safety.

title: Asesmen Diagnostik dan Pembelajaran Berdiferensiasi: Studi Kasus Kualitatif tentang Analisis Kebutuhan Belajar Siswa di Sekolah Menengah Pertama
abstract: Students’ diverse learning needs require instructional practices informed by accurate diagnostic assessment and responsive pedagogical decisions. This study examines how student learning needs are identified, translated into differentiated instruction, and supported through school organizational practices. Employing a qualitative case study design, the research was conducted at SMP Negeri 2 Tanah Grogot, East Kalimantan, Indonesia, involving eight purposively selected informants comprising a principal, two guidance counselors, two subject teachers, and three students. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, observations, and documentation and analyzed through data condensation, display, and conclusion verification. Findings reveal that students’ needs encompass academic readiness, interests, learning preferences, and environmental conditions. Diagnostic assessment provides initial information that guidance counselors and teachers use to map student profiles and adjust instructional activities, learning support, and assessment products. Teachers provide varied learning opportunities while maintaining shared learning objectives. The findings also identify a recurring process connecting needs identification, information sharing, instructional decisions, monitoring of student responses, and pedagogical reflection. Teacher collaboration, professional development, facilities, and school leadership support this process. The study proposes a context-specific Diagnosis-to-Differentiation Adaptive Learning Model, positioning diagnostic assessment as a foundation for continuous instructional adaptation rather than merely student classification. As a single-school case study, the findings offer contextual insights without establishing causal effectiveness or broad generalizability. These insights inform school-level planning for responsive and inclusive teaching.

title: MaizeEviReason for Auditable Evidence Applicability and Conservative Release in Maize Disease Decision Support
abstract: Agricultural evidence can be topically relevant yet conflict with the conditions of a query, or lack the information needed to support an action. We present MaizeEviReason, an auditable interface that keeps source conditions, distinguishes applicable, inapplicable and undetermined states, and separates applicability assessment from deterministic release checks. The core evaluation measures how much information is lost when conditions are projected onto fixed fields and what coverage is given up when supplied contracts are enforced. Matched learning experiments evaluate applicability prediction, and a public-pipeline diagnostic examines whether the interface is activated. On 49 constructed assignments from five documents, a six-field projection wrongly accepted 13 conflicting or unresolved assignments and reached an accuracy of 0.7347, against 0.8367 for direct interpretation of the text contract. The complete rule agrees perfectly with its reference, as expected, because those labels were derived from the same contracts. On 120 constructed release records, deterministic gating reduced observed symbolic violations from 7 to 0, while coverage fell from 55.83% to 50.00%. The prespecified source-family comparison of decision accuracy was not significant (Holm-adjusted $p = 0.75$), and the eight-record source-bound test covered only one family. On ten permanently held-out documents, the condition-differential evidence adapter (CDEA) obtained a macro-F1 of 0.4949 with the state loss and 0.2518 with its full objective. In the public evaluation the condition interface was never activated, so its effect under usable condition inputs remains untested. Taken together, these descriptive diagnostics locate information loss in the evaluated condition representation and mark the operating scope of applicability assessment and output checking; they are not evidence of general decision-support effectiveness.

title: StableProt: Structure-Aware Deep Learning for Protein Thermostability (Tm) and Environmental Adaptation (OGT) Prediction
abstract: Predicting protein melting temperature (Tm) and organismal optimal growth temperature (OGT) is essential for enzyme engineering, biocatalyst design, and metagenomic bioprospecting, yet computational prediction faces several fundamental bottlenecks: sequence-only representations miss tertiary packing; dual-task coupling induces destructive gradient conflict; natural database skew (>87% mesophiles) drives mesophilic collapse; and existing tools produce uncalibrated point predictions. To address these challenges, we present StableProt, a structure-aware framework that couples amino acid sequences with Foldseek 3Di structural tokens via a frozen SaProt backbone to capture 3D contacts. Disjoint heads condition thermodynamic stability on ecological context without gradient conflict, while targeted 14% mesophilic subsampling expands thermophile representation to eliminate mesophilic collapse. Calibrated ensemble modeling reduces calibration error to 1.92%, providing dependable 95% confidence intervals. Evaluating models across 10°C temperature intervals reveals severe baseline collapse at thermal extremes, whereas StableProt maintains robust accuracy across regimes. On ProThermDB and zero-shot FireProtDB, StableProt achieves state-of-the-art probabilistic accuracy (CRPS = 4.52°C and 8.71°C) while recovering 92.0% of hyperthermophiles (≥80°C), and in prospective validation, its calibrated intervals capture both enzyme stability (75.3% coverage) and host environmental growth temperatures (78.1% coverage). StableProt is freely accessible as an interactive web server at https://stableprot.dixitlab.org/.

title: Digital Inclusion and Rural Agricultural Development: Socioeconomic Determinants of Mobile Phone–Based Information Use and Tomato Productivity in Bangladesh
abstract: Despite the growing push to bring mobile phones to smallholder farmers for access to crop information, there is limited evidence for productivity gains for high-value crops. This study aims to determine the constraints of informative mobile phone usage and its impact on tomato output from 200 tomato farmers of Noakhali Sadar in Bangladesh through a survey. Structured interviews were used to gather the data, which were then analysed using a Cobb–Douglas production function and OLS estimation as well as logistic regression. Education, credit access, group membership, household income and market distance had significant positive influence on the likelihood of informative mobile phone use (p < 0.05). Yield was significantly higher (p < 0.01) in informative use, land being under tomato crop and extension contact and lower in higher seed cost. Pest management, cost savings and timely farm operations were major advantages, and weak government support and limited credit availability were major constraints reported by farmers. There are opportunities to increase digital literacy, rural credit, and extension services to improve the effectiveness of agricultural advisory services delivered via mobile.
journal: International Journal of Business, Arts and Scientific Study

title: Pesticides and Hypospadias in Southern Brazil: An Ecological Study.
abstract: Rio Grande do Sul ranks among the Brazilian states with the highest pesticide consumption and one of the highest prevalences of hypospadias, a congenital anomaly often associated with prenatal exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals. We assessed the relationship between prenatal pesticide exposure and hypospadias risk through an ecological study of 1 776 670 live births in the state from 2010 to 2022. Using a spatial Bayesian hierarchical model, we examined associations between hypospadias and municipal-level indicators: relative crop area, pesticide sales, and probability of pesticide detection in water samples. The prevalence was 4.69 cases per 10 000 live births, with 10 municipalities at high risk and 15 at low risk. Higher risk was associated with tobacco cultivation. Sales of metaflumizone and Melaleuca alternifolia were associated with increased risk, while detection probabilities of alachlor and DDT showed the largest estimated effects, although these estimates were accompanied by substantial uncertainty. While causal inference is not possible in this ecological design, findings generate hypotheses for future research on prenatal pesticide exposure. Considering other environmental risk factors may further clarify hypospadias etiology. Identifying modifiable determinants is key to guiding interventions and public policies to reduce this condition's burden, particularly in rural areas and agricultural populations.

title: Quorum Sensing and Biofilm Regulation in ESKAPE Pathogens: Mechanisms, Therapeutic Targets, and Translational Challenges
Antibacterial and pro-osteointegrative bioactive coatings on titanium implant surfaces for oromaxillofacial applications: a systematic review and bayesian network meta-analysis of preclinical studies
abstract: Numerous preclinical studies have investigated bioactive coatings on titanium implant surfaces to enhance antibacterial and osteointegrative performance in oromaxillofacial applications. However, these studies employ heterogeneous experimental methods and biological outcomes, making it difficult to identify which coating strategies hold the greatest translational potential. This systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis (NMA) aimed to rank titanium coating strategies published over the last five years according to their biological performance, using a quantitative statistical framework. Nine coating categories of increasing compositional complexity, ranging from single-component (inorganic, organic, peptides/growth factors) to two-component and three-component formulations combining these classes with each other or with antibiotics, were compared across six biological outcomes in preclinical models. Inclusion criteria followed the PICOS framework for studies published between 2020 and 2025. Three databases were searched according to PRISMA 2020 and its NMA extension. Mean difference (MD) was used for outcomes on a common scale; ratio of means (RoM) when measurement units were heterogeneous. Treatment ranking was estimated using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Study reporting quality and data completeness were assessed, and studies with insufficient quantitative data were excluded from the quantitative synthesis. Of 143 records identified, 59 met the inclusion criteria and 40 contributed to the quantitative synthesis. SUCRA rankings indicated that three-component hybrid coatings incorporating antibiotics achieved the highest antibacterial performance and osseointegration, while inorganic coatings functionalized with peptides or growth factors demonstrated superior osteogenic differentiation. Organic coatings combined with peptides or growth factors showed the greatest cell proliferation. These findings provide the first evidence-based ranking of bioactive coating strategies for titanium implant surfaces, suggesting a potential advantage of multi-component formulations over single-agent approaches across biological outcomes. The identified compositional complexity gradient may inform the rational design of future multifunctional coatings and help prioritize candidates for further preclinical and translational validation in oromaxillofacial applications. A review and Bayesian network meta-analysis of titanium implant coatings screened 143 studies and included 59. Hybrid coatings with antibiotics ranked highest for antibacterial activity and osseointegration; inorganic coatings with peptides or growth factors ranked highest for osteogenic differentiation; and organic coatings with peptides ranked highest for cell proliferation. The summary states that multicomponent coatings outperform single-component coatings for antibacterial and osseointegration outcomes.

title: Coarsen or refine? coordination cost and the modular architecture of digital platforms under AI-driven complexity
abstract: Platform owners that build their own technology must decide whether rising, AI-driven complexity calls for coarser (more integrated) or finer (more decoupled) module boundaries. We develop a computational model in which a platform searches a rugged performance landscape under an endogenous coordination cost, and show that the answer depends on the source of that cost. When coordination cost is structural, scaling with unit size, the performance-maximising architecture coarsens as complexity rises; when it is transactional, scaling with the interdependence a change must renegotiate, the architecture refines, and a critical cost mix separates the two. We then make AI a decision variable. The platform chooses how much AI to deploy. Deployment raises interdependence and lowers decomposability, AI absorbs part of the coordination cost of the changes it handles, each use carries a cost, and capacity is limited. Against a no-AI benchmark and a treatment in which AI only changes parameters, deployment moves the optimal architecture to integration in both cost regimes, to about eleven of twelve decisions per module, while the parameter-only treatment leaves granularity unchanged. The usage cost governs this shift, and integration economises on scarce AI capacity. Along an adoption path, decomposability carries about 90% of the erosion of modular value. Modelling autonomous AI agents as look-ahead searchers yields governance rules, including a decomposability threshold for re-centralisation. The study recasts the modularity–complexity debate as two questions a platform can diagnose: which coordination cost dominates, and which one its AI absorbs.

title: Soil factors governing shoot metal(loid) concentrations of lettuce and Swiss chard: a multivariate assessment across diffuse soil contamination gradients
Multi-scale modeling of continent-wide tracking data confirms the importance of landscape mosaics for the European wildcat
abstract: Land use change is a major threat to the persistence of wildlife in human-dominated landscapes, making the knowledge of the amount and spatial configuration of suitable habitat essential for conservation. The European wildcat (Felis silvestris) currently persists in fragmented populations and faces ever increasing human pressure. We modeled and mapped suitable wildcat habitats at the continental scale, to identify opportunities and constraints for its conservation. We compiled a large telemetry dataset comprising 200 wildcats across Europe and developed multi-scale habitat suitability models using Maxent. Habitat selection was analyzed at two hierarchical levels: home-range placement within the wider landscape and selection within the established home ranges. At both levels, wildcats selected broadleaved forests, mixed forests, and grasslands, while avoiding landscapes dominated by large continuous forests. For home-range placement, they preferred lower terrain ruggedness and less intensive agriculture. Within the home ranges, wildcats selected forest edges and small woody features. Our results highlight the importance of heterogeneous forest–grassland mosaics habitats. More than half of the predicted suitable habitat occurred outside protected areas, highlighting the need for effective conservation strategies beyond their borders. Predictions of suitable areas should, however, be interpreted cautiously in regions where environmental conditions extend beyond those represented in the calibration data. By providing the first continental-scale habitat suitability map based on a large European telemetry dataset, our study offers a spatial foundation for identifying conservation priorities and supporting the long-term connectivity and recovery of wildcat populations.

title: A tool for quantifying Grapevines Vigour: Accurate canopy cover and crop volume assessment via drone-based point clouds from conventional and oblique RGB cameras
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
abstract: This study aimed to develop a tool capable of capturing the spatial variability of grapevine vigour from a geometric approach. The methodology was evaluated during the 2023, 2024, and 2025 growing seasons in a 1.27 ha trellised vineyard in Tarazona de la Mancha (Albacete, Spain). Green canopy cover (GCC) estimates were compared with reference data obtained using GEO-LAIC software across 33 uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) flights. Biomass volume (BV) estimates were compared with values derived from the alphashape algorithm using 10540 observations. The relationship between BV and pruning weight was also assessed to identify the optimal period for biomass estimation. GCC estimates showed strong agreement with GEO-LAIC, achieving coefficients of determination (R2) of up to 0.97 and root mean square error (RMSE) values below 0.04. BV estimates showed moderate agreement with the alphashape-derived values (R2 = 0.65), providing a basis for further calibration. The optimal period for estimating pruning weight was identified between BBCH growth stages 75 and 81. BV showed a stronger relationship with pruning weight than GCC. The proposed geometric approach effectively captures grapevine vigour variability while prioritising geometric accuracy over radiometric quality, potentially enabling the use of low-cost RGB sensors. This methodology offers a promising tool for precision viticulture and spatially targeted vineyard management.

title: Enhanced rock weathering for sustainable carbon capture: advances, challenges, and future prospects in terrestrial ecosystems
abstract: Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) is a carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategy that accelerates mineral dissolution in terrestrial systems to draw down atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2), with the potential for co-benefits across managed and natural ecosystems. This review evaluates ERW’s real-world effectiveness through the lens of measurable carbon fluxes and storage permanence. We synthesize evidence across geochemical kinetics, hydrology, mineralogy, particle size distributions, and biological mediation, showing that the wide range of reported field-scale carbon removal rates (approximately 0 to 9 t CO2 per ha−1 yr−1) reflects diverse site-specific environmental conditions and complex geochemical, biological, and hydrological processes that cannot be explained by intrinsic mineral reactivity alone. Widely used proxies, such as total cation dissolutions, soil pH changes, or crop yield gains, are less reliable indicators of field-scale CDR than alkalinity export or cation mass balance. Furthermore, estimates of net CDR should account for both the efficiency of converting weathering products into durable carbonate storage and full lifecycle emissions. Lifecycle assessments consistently identify energy for grinding and logistics as the dominant sources of cost and emissions, implying an optimal particle fineness for maximizing net removal. A tiered appraisal of modeling approaches highlights remaining uncertainty across geochemical, ecohydrological, and socioeconomic processes in current models, with plausible 2050 deployment potential estimated at 0.2–4 Gt CO2 yr−1. We further assess environmental and social risks, including trace-metal accumulation, long-term soil health, and occupational hazards. We conclude by outlining a framework for credible scaling that integrates rigorous monitoring, multi-scale modeling, and precautionary governance. Under these conditions, ERW emerges not as a universal solution, but as a potentially meaningful component of a diversified carbon removal portfolio.
journal: Reviews in Environmental Science and Bio/Technology

title: An Endothelial-Integrated 3D Compartmentalized Osteochondral Platform for Modeling Vascular-Osteochondral Interactions.
Association of temperature and relative humidity with leaf rust and stripe rust incidence and severity in wheat across major wheat-growing districts of Punjab, Pakistan
abstract: Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) is the main crop of Pakistan, with Punjab accounting for about 75% of national yield. The major diseases affecting wheat yields are leaf rust (Puccinia triticina) and stripe rust (Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici). This research aimed at establishing the effect of temperature and relative humidity on the incidence and severity of the diseases in the eight pilot areas in Punjab during the crop growing season of 2024–2025. To achieve this objective, 160 wheat farms (20 farms per area) were visited and checked twice in three growing stages (GS 20–29, GS 30–59, GS 60–79) in fields of Akbar-19, MH-21 and Fareed-06 cultivar. The researchers applied linear mixed-effects model (with a random “district” factor), while for stripe rust, ordinary least squares models were used. The study found that humidity positively affected the incidence (β = 1.26, P = 0.023) and severity (β = 0.73, P = 0.027) of leaf rust, while average temperature has no effect on the disease severity. Disease progressed rapidly across the growth stages (the leaf rust incidence rose from 7.8% at GS 20–29 to 47.6% at GS 60–79). Marginal means for leaf rust incidence were estimated to be 39.3% (Akbar-19), 27.2% (MH-21), and 15.2% (Fareed-06). The highest model accuracy was observed for leaf rust incidence (R² = 0.90). The findings of this particular season suggest that relative humidity and the crop's stage of development are more closely associated with rust emergence than average temperature, hence suggesting the use of less susceptible varieties (like Fareed-06) for better outcomes.

title: Explained and latent components of the social-vulnerability gradient in traffic injury burden: a population-weighted Bayesian spatial decomposition.
abstract: Traffic-injury inequity is commonly assessed using cross-sectional or multi-year aggregated analyses, which can obscure temporal change, confound observed social and infrastructural associations with latent spatial dependence, and mask the distinct roles of individual dimensions of social vulnerability. This study develops an uncertainty-aware Bayesian spatiotemporal framework that moves beyond spatial association mapping by explicitly decomposing traffic-injury inequity into interpretable social and infrastructural associations, structured neighborhood dependence, unstructured cell-specific heterogeneity, and common temporal variation. A Gamma model with a Besag-York-Mollié 2 (BYM2) spatial effect and a first-order random walk (RW1) temporal effect was applied to annual population-normalized Traffic Injury Rates (TIR) across 2311 Voronoi cells in New York City from 2021 to 2024, jointly incorporating AADT, 15 disaggregated social-vulnerability indicators, and nine physical-environment measures; the Gamma precision was scaled by resident population, and the population-weighted concentration index of expected injury burden along the SVI rank was decomposed into additive components with posterior credible intervals. Expected burden in the most vulnerable population quintile was 1.44 times that of the least vulnerable (95% CrI 1.40-1.49). In this decomposition, social-vulnerability indicators carried 59% of the gradient (8-112%) and the latent structured spatial carried 77% (24-131%), while network and built-form conditions offset 34% and traffic volume contributed -3%; without the spatial effect, the same indicators absorbed 119% of a smaller gradient. AADT (β = 0.268; 95% CrI: 0.231-0.306) and building area (β = 0.224) had the strongest positive conditional associations with TIR; credible SVI associations were positive for minority status, housing-cost burden and mobile homes, and negative for multi-unit housing and limited English proficiency. Residual spatial variation was predominantly neighborhood-structured (φ = 0.983; 0.936-0.999), and the year effect was small. Population-scaled precision improved WAIC by 875 points, and the model did not out-predict a cell-mean persistence baseline for held-out years, so its value lies in attribution and uncertainty rather than forecasting. By distinguishing persistent neighborhood-level inequity from annual change and propagating posterior uncertainty, the framework supports differentiated safety prioritization, combining corridor-level engineering assessment in areas with high traffic exposure and network-related burden with neighborhood-scale equity prioritization where elevated TIR coincides with adverse social conditions, and local audits where the latent structured effect is credibly positive.

Interpretable minimal-input reference evapotranspiration modeling for smart agriculture in data-scarce regions: Integrating reconstructed land surface temperature and air temperature
Resolving the open questions in individualized and cumulative patient dose in the era of AI.
abstract: Radiation dose in medical imaging has been quantified through measurable metrics such as computed tomography dose index volume (CTDIvol), dose length product (DLP), kerma area product, kerma at reference point etc. They are benchmarked through diagnostic reference levels (DRLs); and communicated in terms of effective dose and population-based risk estimates. None of these tools was designed to describe the dose, the reference standard, or the risk applicable to the individual patient. In every other domain of medicine where a potentially harmful agent accompanies a beneficial clinical intervention, from contrast nephrotoxicity in CT imaging to anesthetic risk in surgery, the field has moved beyond population metrics to individualized measurement and individual clinical decision-making. Radiation protection in medical imaging has not yet made this transition. This paper resolves several open questions on cumulative dose that have long been used to justify inaction. It argues that the transition is now technically achievable, that the barriers to it are primarily architectural, regulatory, and cultural rather than physical or computational, and that artificial intelligence and emerging imaging technologies provide the enabling infrastructure to complete it. We describe the three-tier structure of barriers to individual dose tracking: technical, institutional and regulatory, and cultural; and propose the elements of a system that would place the individual patient's cumulative radiation dose record where it belongs: in their medical record, alongside their medication list, visible at the point of every subsequent clinical imaging decision.
journal: Physica medica : PM : an international journal devoted to the applications of physics to medicine and biology : official journal of the Italian Association of Biomedical Physics

title: From population-based cancer registration to quality registries: the Polish National Cancer Registry as an integrated oncology data ecosystem.
abstract: Background and purpose Population-based cancer registries provide an essential data source for epidemiological research and surveillance. This article presents the organizational and functional architecture of Poland's electronic Polish National Cancer Registry (e-PNCR) platform, an integrated data ecosystem designed to modernize national cancer registration and support the development of high-granularity quality registries. Materials and methods Implemented in 2023, the e-PNCR platform centralizes nationwide data acquisition, integrating multi-institutional real-world data (RWD) via automated hospital network exports (Enterprise Service Bus) and structured web interfaces. Natural language processing (NLP) models extract registry-relevant concepts from unstructured clinical documents, followed by automated validation compliant with European Network of Cancer Registries/Joint Research Center recommendations. Results The platform utilizes a modular architecture to support disease-specific quality registries. Frameworks such as the Polish Onco-Hematological Registry are deployed directly as structural extensions of the core national infrastructure. This paradigm allows new registries to reuse existing standardized terminologies and validation rules without modifying external hospital interfaces. Furthermore, the integrated NLP pipelines extract clinical information with an average sensitivity and positive predictive value of ∼87%, streamlining case registration while maintaining mandatory expert verification. Conclusions The e-PNCR platform establishes a highly scalable paradigm for national cancer registration, facilitating the efficient generation of high-quality RWD. By leveraging a shared technological infrastructure, the deployment of specialized quality registries requires substantially fewer resources. Crucially, the platform's standardized data environment increases the registry's readiness for seamless future integration with European data-sharing initiatives, including the European Health Data Space.

title: Optimal soil water content and tiller number for sustaining wheat yield under delayed irrigation at the jointing stage
Yield loss and bias across irrigated modern wheat varieties due to excessive furrow gaps in raised bed plots
Soybean phenotypic changes from long-term breeding worldwide: A quantitative review
Forensic delivery of intelligence outcomes: Quality considerations.
abstract: Forensic intelligence (FORINT) is a powerful extension of forensic science's role in policing and security, enabling forward-leaning forensic contributions for wider effect, including prevention and disruption of crime. However, operational implementation has been inhibited by concerns relating to quality and the potential for misinterpretation or misuse of forensic information. To directly apply laboratory-centric quality assurance approaches to FORINT would be to place it in a Procrustean bed, ill-suited to its transdisciplinary, adaptive, and often predictive approach to generating activity/crime level propositions and other insights. However, FORINT can, and should, be delivered within a principles-based quality management framework, wherein quality is a property of the system - not a restrictive compliance mechanism. Through established quality system principles, intelligence theory and forensic science, and extensive operational experience, a structured FORINT delivery framework is proposed, leveraging recognised constructs such as the 'intelligence cycle' and FORINT praxis with standards familiar to forensic scientists, without imposing rigid, laboratory-focused requirements. Quality considerations are mapped to structured processes across planning, collection, collation, analysis, review & reporting, and dissemination & evaluation. Focus is accorded to leadership, customer/decision-maker engagement, workforce design, and governance. Human factors are recognised throughout, as FORINT analysis involves contextualised interpretation and judgement of complex, incomplete, and uncertain information under pressure. The model is structured to mitigate bias and misinterpretation, ensuring ethical, reliable, and defensible assessments. These recommendations position FORINT as an effective, robust means of maximising the utility of scientific insights, enhancing the outcomes of forensic science and policing intelligence, while maintaining the trust of practitioners, decision-makers, and the public.

title: From static to dynamic parameter regionalization for process-based evapotranspiration modelling through differentiable parameter learning
Epidermal Differentiation Disorders (EDDs): Translational insights and technical challenges of three-dimensional epidermal, full-thickness, and organoid skin models.
abstract: Monogenic epidermal differentiation disorders (EDDs) are individually rare, but collectively affect many patients, often causing lifelong morbidity. Recent advances in genetics prompted the Reclassifying Epidermal Differentiation Disorders Initiative (REDDI) to introduce a gene-based classification of EDDs, replacing eponyms and grouping disorders as syndromic (sEDD), nonsyndromic (nEDD), or palmoplantar (pEDD). Because EDD pathology is largely epidermal and most disorders result from single gene variants, they are well suited for modelling in human keratinocytes grown within three-dimensional tissue models that can reproduce tissue-level pathology. We review published human epidermal equivalents (HEEs), skin equivalents (HSEs), epidermal organoids (HEOs), and skin organoids (HSOs) engineered to study EDDs. Most models replicated key disease features, including defective epidermal differentiation, tissue architecture, cell adhesion, and barrier function and provide platforms to investigate pathophysiology and evaluate therapeutic strategies. Most published models represent nEDDs, whereas pEDDs and sEDDs remain underrepresented due to disease features extending beyond the epidermis. Emerging bioengineering approaches, including incorporating additional cell types and application of extrinsic physical cues may help address these limitations. We also outline strategies for collaboration, resource sharing, advocacy, and targeted funding, which are essential to expand the repertoire of EDD models and accelerate development of effective therapies for these orphan disorders.

title: Circadian regulation of crop adaptation: from model systems to field constraints
SHANK3 drives abnormal neurodevelopment in iPSC-derived 2D and 3D brain models of Phelan-McDermid Syndrome.
abstract: Phelan-McDermid Syndrome (PMDS) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by 22q13.3 deletion involving SHANK3. While SHANK3 is critical for synapses, its role in early human neurodevelopment remains elusive. Here, we generated induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived 2D neuronal cultures and 3D cerebral organoids from two twin Phelan-McDermid syndrome patients with a 1.7 Mb 22q13 deletion encompassing SHANK3 gene. PMDS organoids showed reduced volume due to impaired neural progenitor cells (NPCs) proliferation. PMDS NPCs exhibited biased differentiation with decreased excitatory neurons but increased GFAP+ astroglia and GABAergic neurons. PMDS neurons displayed simplified morphology, reduced synapse density and diminished excitability. Importantly, lentiviral-mediated SHANK3 overexpression largely rescued these defects. Our findings identify SHANK3 as a key regulator of early neurodevelopment and provide mechanistic insights into PMDS pathogenesis.

title: Pre-driven and post-gated memristive Hopfield network: Dynamics, FPGA realization and image encryption.
abstract: Many existing memristive synaptic models merge presynaptic and postsynaptic activities into a single aggregated stimulus, making their distinct functional roles difficult to interpret. To address this issue, this paper proposes a memristive synapse with a pre-driven and post-gated state-update mechanism, in which presynaptic activity drives synaptic-state evolution while postsynaptic activity nonlinearly modulates the direction and strength of the update. The proposed synapse is embedded into a compact two-neuron memristive Hopfield neural network to investigate how this functional decomposition influences network dynamics. Equilibrium and stability analysis, bifurcation diagrams, Lyapunov exponents, and multistability analysis reveal variable-wing chaotic attractors, parameter-dependent transitions, and coexisting dynamical states. FPGA implementation verifies the hardware realizability of the proposed system, while a color-image encryption scheme demonstrates the application potential of the generated chaotic sequences. These results show that the proposed framework provides a functionally interpretable modeling route for incorporating differentiated pre/post synaptic regulation into memristive Hopfield dynamics.
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society

title: Divergent hydraulic safety and efficiency trade-offs of woody plants are associated with mycorrhizal types at the global scale.
abstract: The hydraulic safety-efficiency trade-off is a core mechanism for woody plants to adapt to their environments. Symbiosis with different mycorrhizal fungi (arbuscular mycorrhiza, AM and ectomycorrhiza, ECM) may affect plant water acquisition strategies. However, whether the hydraulic trade-off strategies of woody plants differ among mycorrhizal types, and what drives these differences, remains unclear. Therefore, this study integrated global plant hydraulic parameters and climate data by mycorrhizal type to explore the associations between mycorrhizal types and plant hydraulic strategies and identify the main driving factors. After controlling for phylogeny, plant growth form, height, and climate, we found that AM plants had significantly larger conduit diameters (38.32 μm) than ECM plants (27.75 μm). The safety-efficiency slope was significantly steeper in ECM than in AM plants, indicating a greater efficiency cost for ECM plants to enhance safety. Environmental factors had different driving effects, water availability dominated AM plant trade-off strategies (38.63%), whereas temperature was a key driver for ECM plant hydraulic strategies (42.08%). Partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) further revealed that climate indirectly affects AM tree height by regulating conduit diameter and trade-off positions (Residuals/Distance), whereas ECM tree height is primarily directly driven by trade-off traits. In conclusion, differentiation in hydraulic trade-off strategies is an important mechanism for woody plants with different mycorrhizal types to adapt to different environments, providing a new perspective for understanding plant hydraulic responses to global change.
