title: High-resolution forest height mapping across boreal and temperate forest sites using Hongtu-1 multistatic X-band TomoSAR
The hidden dimension: Resolving the vertical gradients of solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence emissions and gross primary production in modern maize canopy
Population genomic differentiation and demographic history across an elevational gradient in an endemic bromeliad of the Atlantic Forest mountains.
abstract: Montane elevational gradients provide natural laboratories for investigating how environmental heterogeneity, geographic isolation, and historical climatic dynamics shape demographic history, population divergence, and diversification. Topographic complexity and historical climatic oscillations are major drivers of biodiversity patterns in mountain regions worldwide. The Brazilian Atlantic Forest (BAF), a Neotropical biodiversity hotspot characterized by naturally fragmented montane habitats, provides a suitable system for investigating these processes. Here, we used over a thousand SNPs from populations of Pitcairnia flammea Lindl. (Bromeliaceae) distributed across an elevational gradient to investigate patterns of genetic diversity, population structure, and demographic history. Bayesian and coalescent-based analyses revealed strong population structure, with two major genetic groups broadly contrasting higher-elevation populations with low- and mid-elevation populations, although elevation itself was not directly supported as a driver of genetic divergence. Demographic modeling supported early asymmetric gene flow between the two major genetic groups, with higher migration from Group 2 towards Group 1, followed by subsequent isolation. Divergence-time estimates and heterogeneous changes in effective population size further suggest distinct demographic trajectories during the Middle and Late Pleistocene. Together, our results reveal divergent evolutionary trajectories within a single endemic species and suggest that population differentiation across the Atlantic Forest mountains reflects the combined effects of habitat fragmentation, historical connectivity and isolation, genetic drift, and demographic changes potentially associated with Pleistocene climatic oscillations.

title: WT-DETR: A Lightweight Model for Defect Detection in Buried Sewer Pipelines Based on Frequency–Domain Feature Processing
abstract: Advancements in artificial intelligence have provided promising solutions for the detection and classification of internal defects in buried sewer pipelines. However, deep learning methods in this domain still face challenges, particularly regarding limited detection accuracy for small defects and excessively large model sizes. This study proposes a methodology that utilizes sonar images and defect frequency-domain features for the accurate identification and classification of pipeline defects. First, raw sonar data collected and processed from field scans are analyzed and filtered. Subsequently, deep learning algorithms are trained and evaluated on the extracted features to recognize and classify pipeline defects. To capture low-frequency structural details, a feature extraction module termed re‑parameterized wavelet‑convolution (RepWT) is designed. Additionally, two distinct feature processing architectures are fused to reduce the computational overhead for deployment. Finally, by integrating the proposed inner-minimum‑point‑distance IoU (MPDIoU) loss function, a neural network model named wavelet convolution-detection transformer (WT-DETR) is developed for sonar-based pipeline defect recognition. The performance of WT-DETR is compared against several state-of-the-art models. Experimental results indicate that WT-DETR achieves highly competitive performance for buried sewer pipeline defect detection, reaching a precision of 88.5%. These results align with theoretical expectations, demonstrating the effectiveness of the WT-DETR model in buried sewer pipeline defect detection.
journal: Journal of Pipeline Systems Engineering and Practice

title: Spatiotemporal Approach to Assess the Impact of Urbanization Policies on Urban Expansion and Sprawl Using Remote Sensing in Tiaret, Algeria
abstract: This study examines the spatial implications of urbanization policies on urban expansion and sprawl. While the shortcomings of urban containment policies have garnered considerable scholarly attention, policies promoting urbanization remain underexplored, with limited empirical research assessing their spatial impacts. To address this gap, we integrate key urbanization policies into a spatiotemporal analysis of 50 years, enabling a nuanced evaluation of policy interventions on urban growth and sprawl through the analysis of their rates, directions, and spatial patterns. This is accomplished using remote sensing techniques and GIS, complemented by standard deviational ellipse, multibuffer ring, landscape metrics, and other spatial indices, to quantify and analyze urban dynamics. The study focuses on Tiaret, a medium-sized Algerian city characterized by a dynamic urban governance trajectory, contributing to research on underexplored urban contexts. The findings demonstrate a significant correlation between urbanization policies and the rate, direction, and patterns of urban expansion and sprawl. Over four decades of policy-driven urbanization, the city experienced an overall average annual urban expansion rate of 28.2%, with urban sprawl dominating 99% of newly developed areas, which were marked by low density and high fragmentation. This study provides an evidence-based framework that quantifies how urbanization policies shape the extent, direction, and spatial patterns of urban growth, enabling planners to anticipate unintended consequences and design more sustainable, policy-sensitive urban strategies.
journal: Journal of Urban Planning and Development

title: Foundation Models in Radiology: Development, Applications, and Future Impact
Who verifies and who continues? Personality and physiological predictors of anomaly-responsive oversight in AI-supported navigation.
abstract: Intelligent systems increasingly place humans in oversight roles, yet users exposed to the same anomaly warning do not respond uniformly. Across two studies using an AI-supported navigation task, we examined whether warning design, focal HEXACO traits and trial-level physiology explained anomaly-specific evaluation and verification/override behaviour. Both studies used a 2 × 2 manipulation of warning salience and explanation style. Study 1 combined eye tracking and pupillometry; Study 2 used electrodermal activity. Prominent and especially explanatory warnings produced the largest behavioural and evaluative effects. Personality showed smaller effects, with behavioural increments sensitive to model specification; Conscientiousness was most consistently associated with verification, whereas Emotionality was associated with evaluative and physiological responsiveness. Repeated participant-level validation showed substantial incremental prediction from pupil features and smaller gains from electrodermal features, including under temporally restricted sensitivity analyses. The findings support a differentiated person-centred account of anomaly-responsive oversight while separating subjective trust from behavioural reliance and verification.

title: From detection to decision: molecular, genomic, and AI innovations for managing Ganoderma boninense in oil palm.
abstract: Ganoderma boninense causes basal stem rot (BSR) in oil palm, resulting in substantial economic losses, particularly for smallholders who contribute approximately 40% of global production. This review synthesizes advances in molecular diagnostic techniques (qPCR, LAMP), whole-genome sequencing of resistant Elaeis guineensis genotypes, and AI-driven remote sensing to enhance understanding of G. boninense pathobiology. Soilborne mycelia of the pathogen can persist for more than 10 y. Asymptomatic infections, which are frequently missed by conventional methods, can lead to significant disease spread within plantations over 2 y. CRISPR-based paper-strip tests have demonstrated high sensitivity (detecting < 1 pg DNA in laboratory settings), while marker-assisted selection has helped identify additional resistance QTLs. Trichoderma biofilms and biodegradable fumigants reduced soil inoculum by 50-75% in controlled studies. AI-based decision support systems have demonstrated promising accuracy for guiding interventions and potential cost savings, although further field validation across diverse conditions is needed.

title: Seeing the Gaps: Heatmaps, Metrics, and the Hidden Failures of Explainable AI in Dentomaxillofacial Radiology - A Systematic Review.
abstract: OBJECTIVES This systematic review aims to evaluate the techniques and reported patterns of heatmap-based visual explanations in deep learning (DL) systems for dental radiographic classification tasks. METHODS A literature search following PRISMA guidelines was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, IEEE Xplore Library, Oria.no and Google Scholar to retrieve studies using DL for dental classification tasks. Only articles with a visual explanation (heatmap) were selected. Risk of bias assessment was done with QUADAS-2, PROBAST-AI and CEBM. The heatmap technique, reasons for inclusion, explanations provided and patterns were analysed. RESULTS In the 136 studies reviewed, Grad-CAM was the most commonly used technique. The predominant reason for using visual explanations was to understand the decision-making process of the DL model. Some heatmaps reflect established radiographic criteria, while others exhibit unique, label-dependent patterns that sometimes emphasise irrelevant areas. Cropping to the region of interest influences visual explanations. CONCLUSIONS Visual explanations seem clinically plausible to domain experts when aligned with domain knowledge, but clinical plausibility does not equal technical faithfulness. Formal faithfulness testing was rarely performed among the included studies. Therefore, explanations should not be assumed to accurately represent the model's underlying reasoning. Limitations include the evaluation of studies not primarily designed for visual explanation assessment. No funding was received for this review. Authors declare no competing interests. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE Visual explanations, while clinically plausible when aligned with domain knowledge, remain insufficiently validated and should not be assumed to faithfully represent model reasoning. An implausible explanation does not necessarily indicate model failure. Domain/task-specific evaluation metrics for explainable AI in dentomaxillofacial radiology are needed.

title: The transcriptional regulation of specialized terpenoid biosynthesis and its regulation by jasmonic acid.
abstract: All plants produce terpenoids for their general metabolism but most, if not all, also produce terpenoids in their specialized metabolism. These specialized metabolites play an essential role in the interaction of plants with their environment, in particular with other organisms. They are also of great economic value to us as they are used as medicine, in our food and as perfumes. The regulation of terpenoid biosynthesis has received much attention as it is costly for the plants to produce even though they only contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Some terpenoids are constitutively produced but most of them are induced upon biotic stress with a key role for the phytohormone jasmonate-isoleucine (JA-Ile). It has become clear that the regulation is mostly at the level of transcription with an important role for basic-helix-loop-helix (bHLH) and MYB transcription factors in the JA-Ile inducible pathways. This review summarizes recent breakthroughs with examples of specific mono-, sesqui- and diterpenoids, describing the complex molecular network regulating their biosynthesis in certain model systems with other phytohormones involved as well. It also points out that several other avenues of regulation need more attention to understand the fine tuning of the regulation. This will help optimizing the production of these specialized metabolites in our crops.

title: Soil Microbes Mediate Contrasting Effects of Plant Diversity on Biotic Resistance and Invasional Meltdown
abstract: Biological invasions are intensifying worldwide as a major component of global change, with soil microbes increasingly recognized as key regulators of invasion outcomes. Yet how soil microbes interact with biodiversity to determine whether communities resist or facilitate invasion, particularly through their effects on plant growth and species interactions, remains unclear. Here, we conducted a two‐phase feedback experiment in which soils were conditioned across a diversity gradient of native or invasive plant communities. We characterized soil fungal communities and quantified microbial effects on plant growth and species interactions between phylogenetically paired native and invasive species. Biodiversity generated contrasting invasion outcomes depending on community origin, driven by distinct microbial pathways. In native‐conditioned soils, increasing diversity reduced invader dominance (biotic resistance), primarily mediated by microbial effects on interspecific competition that enhanced native competition strength while reducing that of invaders. In contrast, in invasive‐conditioned soils, increasing diversity facilitated invader dominance (invasional meltdown), primarily driven by enhanced invader growth and suppression of natives. These patterns were associated with shifts in key microbial groups. Putative pathogen richness increased with increasing plant diversity and was negatively associated with native growth, whereas AMF richness declined with increasing plant diversity in native communities but increased with increasing plant diversity in invasive communities, promoting invader growth and competition strength. By integrating biodiversity‐ecosystem functioning, biotic resistance, invasional meltdown, and competitive interactions within a plant–soil feedback framework, our study advances invasion ecology. It identifies soil microbes as central mediators that link biodiversity to ecosystem invasibility through distinct pathways affecting plant growth and species interactions.

title: DSC-SPFC: End-to-End Structure-Preserving Feature Coding with Dual-Stream Companding
abstract: As large foundation models are increasingly deployed in distributed settings, transmitting intermediate representations has become a bottleneck, making feature coding important for reducing communication and storage overheads. However, intermediate representations from large models often exhibit significant heterogeneity and peaky, heavy-tailed distributions, posing challenges for end-to-end optimization and effective entropy modeling. Existing methods typically rely on handcrafted preprocessing pipelines for feature compression, which limits generalizability and may introduce structural and semantic distortions. Although recent studies introduce learned distribution transformations to mitigate feature heterogeneity, their decoupled design does not support end-to-end joint optimization. To address these issues, we propose Dual-Stream Companding for Structure-Preserving Feature Coding (DSC-SPFC), an end-to-end framework that operates directly on tensor structures. DSC-SPFC decomposes features into a bounded main stream and a complementary residual stream, and maps both into a stable latent space via differentiable companding for joint entropy coding. This design improves robustness to outliers while preserving reversibility and end-to-end learnability. Experiments on LLaMA3, DINOv2, and SD3 across common sense reasoning, semantic segmentation, and text-to-image synthesis show that DSC-SPFC provides improved rate--task trade-offs under the BPFP metric over packing baselines and recent decoupled distribution-transformation methods.
journal: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia

title: AECIL: Automatic Environment Construction and Invariant Learning Towards Robust Visual Question Answering
abstract: Visual Question Answering (VQA) models often suffer from severe generalization degradation under distribution shifts, as they excessively rely on statistical shortcuts while ignoring genuine causal evidence. Existing debiasing methods face two major limitations. First, in feature modeling, they frequently overlook the complex spatial topological dependencies between cross-modal entities. Second, regarding intervention mechanisms, they predominantly rely on manually predefined heuristic strategies, lacking the capability to automatically construct diverse interventional environments in an end-to-end manner. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel framework termed Automatic Environment Construction and Invariant Learning (AECIL). Specifically, we design a Dynamic Causal Masking (DCM) mechanism that first captures the geometric and semantic correlations of multimodal entities via a structured graph network. It then employs differentiable discrete sampling to adaptively decouple features into causal features and spurious features, thereby automatically generating virtual interventional environments reflecting diverse distribution shifts. Building upon this, we further introduce a Joint Invariant Optimization (JIO) strategy, which integrates Counterfactual Consistency (CFC) and Invariant Risk Minimization (IRM) to compel the model to converge toward a robust cross-distribution causal mapping across varying interventional environments. Extensive experiments on mainstream datasets, including VQA-CP v2 and VQA v2, demonstrate that AECIL not only successfully overcomes the inherent in-distribution (ID) performance degradation bottleneck, but also achieves superior out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization performance compared to the benchmark debiasing models.

title: Adaptive Sparse Structural Evolution for Continual Learning in Spiking Neural Networks
abstract: Lifelong learning enables intelligent systems to acquire knowledge incrementally while preserving previously learned information—a hallmark of human cognition. However, most Spiking Neural Network (SNN) models lack the critical biological mechanisms that support this capacity, particularly sparse circuit reconfiguration and context-aware gating observed in the brain. Inspired by neuroscientific insights into synaptic rewiring and task-differentiated cortical modulation, we propose a novel framework for sparse structural continual learning in SNNs. Our approach integrates two core innovations: (1) a context-aware gating mechanism based on logistic regression that detects task-specific representations from spatio-temporal spike activity, and (2) an iterative sparse structure learning module that dynamically prunes and regrows task-specific connections in a biologically plausible manner. Together, these components facilitate efficient representation segregation, reduce catastrophic forgetting, and improve parameter efficiency. Experimental results on class-incremental CIFAR-100 benchmarks show significant gains in both continual learning performance and computational efficiency over state-of-the-art SNN baselines, which use only half the number of parameters, with up to 1.11% improvement in average accuracy and up to 2.67% increase in last accuracy. This work offers a biologically grounded pathway to scalable and adaptive lifelong learning in neuromorphic AI systems.

title: SLD-Flow: Statistical Label Dependency for Incomplete Multi-View Multi-Label Classification
abstract: Multi-view multi-label classification (MvMLC) is fundamental to multimedia applications yet suffers from missing views and incomplete annotations that undermine semantic correlation modeling. Existing methods tackle these issues through label completion, either by learning label correlations or imputing missing labels with pseudo-labels. However, both rely on heuristic metrics like cosine similarity that conflate genuine semantic relationships with random co-occurrences, severely limiting generalization under sparse supervision. To address this limitation, we propose SLD-Flow, a statistically grounded framework that reformulates label correlation learning as a problem of significance-aware dependency inference. At its core lies Statistical Label Dependency (SLD), which models label co-occurrence via the hypergeometric distribution, employing expectation to establish a baseline for random co-occurrence and variance to quantify its fluctuation. This formulation enables principled differentiation between meaningful dependencies and random noise, yielding a robust label relation graph. Building upon SLD, we further construct a label-structure-guided learning paradigm that integrates two key components: (i) manifold-based label completion guided by statistically significant dependencies to mitigate noise propagation, and (ii) distribution consistency regularization that injects SLD priors into representation learning to enforce structural alignment between feature and label spaces. Through the synergy of completion and regularization, this unified design effectively bridges label space structure with feature space learning, substantially enhancing robustness against missing views and label sparsity. Extensive experiments show that SLD-Flow consistently outperforms SOTA methods.
journal: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia

title: CDR-GS: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Cross-Device Rendering
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting has achieved remarkable progress in real-time scene rendering, yet existing methods are predominantly tailored to a single camera model, typically the pinhole camera, which limits their applicability to images captured by heterogeneous devices. In this paper, we introduce CDR-GS, the unified 3DGS framework explicitly designed for cross-device rendering. Our key insight is to leverage 360° images as a universal intermediate representation that inherently encompasses the full field of view (FoV) of diverse camera models, thereby eliminating the need for error-prone block-wise rendering and mapping. A differentiable cross-device mapping then transforms the intermediate 360° images into target camera domains, forming a unified rendering pipeline supervised directly by original cross-device images. To mitigate the excessive GPU memory overhead of activating nearly all Gaussians during 360° rendering, we propose a Gaussian selection strategy that exploits prior Gaussians and target FoV to retain only high-contribution Gaussians. We further design an adaptive-FoV mapping method that substantially reduces textureless regions when projecting cross-device images into pinhole images for prior Gaussians generation. To facilitate future research, we establish CDR-Bench, a benchmark comprising three datasets and adapted baselines. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CDR-GS achieves state-of-the-art rendering quality and efficiency across diverse camera models.

title: Evolving, Not Training: Training-Free Reasoning Segmentation via Evolutionary Prompting
abstract: Reasoning Segmentation requires models to interpret complex, context-dependent linguistic queries to achieve pixel-level localization. Current dominant approaches rely heavily on Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) or Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, SFT suffers from catastrophic forgetting and domain dependency, while RL is often hindered by training instability and rigid reliance on predefined reward functions. To break the bottleneck of static inference paradigms, we propose EVOL-SAM3, a zero-shot framework that reformulates reasoning segmentation as a dynamic inference-time optimization problem. A fundamental challenge in this formulation is the non-differentiable modal gap between discrete semantic reasoning and continuous pixel-level execution. EVOL-SAM3 iteratively refines prompt populations via a Generate-Evaluate-Evolve loop, employing a Visual Arena for tournament-based fitness assessment and Semantic Mutation for error correction. A Heterogeneous Arena integrates geometric and semantic priors to ensure robust selection. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EVOL-SAM3 not only outperforms baselines in terms of primary metrics and token consumption, but also surpasses fully supervised state-of-the-art methods on the ReasonSeg benchmark in a zero-shot setting.
journal: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia

title: FoveaUI: Foveated On-demand Visual Evidence Acquisition for GUI Grounding
abstract: GUI grounding requires precise identification of interface elements from high-resolution screenshots, but processing dense visual inputs with large vision–language models incurs substantial computational overhead. Existing visual token compression methods typically allocate a fixed budget, ignoring the large variability of visual redundancy across different GUI layouts. We show that a fixed visual budget is suboptimal, as the necessity of high-resolution visual evidence varies substantially across interface contexts. We propose FoveaUI, a dynamic high-resolution budget allocation framework for GUI grounding. The agent first reasons over a low-resolution global view and selectively requests high-resolution crops only when fine-grained evidence is required. FoveaUI introduces three coordinated components that progressively address when to seek high-resolution detail, where to acquire it, and how to leverage it effectively: a balanced training strategy for on-demand resolution allocation, a mix-tool strategy paired with a smooth process-level reward for region and granularity selection, and locality-prioritized attention masking for efficient utilization of acquired high-resolution information. Experiments on GUI grounding benchmarks show that our method maintains strong grounding performance while substantially reducing high-resolution visual token costs.
journal: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia

title: Decoupling Regime and Mechanistic Heterogeneity via Hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts for Global Carbon Flux Prediction
abstract: The integration of physical laws and machine learning has emerged as a compelling paradigm for modeling complex real-world systems. Compared to traditional numerical solvers, this approach significantly improves computational efficiency while preserving physical consistency. However, the source--sink dynamics of global carbon fluxes are driven by a complex coupling of diverse physical and biogeochemical mechanisms, resulting in pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Existing physics-informed methods typically embed governing equations directly into model architectures or loss functions. Inherently, this imposes strong assumptions of regime uniformity and mechanistic homogeneity, neglecting the intricate interactions across different regimes and physical processes. Consequently, while these methods excel on idealized partial differential equations (PDEs), they often exhibit limited generalizability when applied to complex real-world systems. To bridge this gap, we propose a hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework, termed Regime and Mechanism Decoupled Mixture-of-Experts (REM-MoE), that explicitly encodes regimes and evolutionary mechanisms as two independent inductive biases during prediction. The core innovation lies in structurally decoupling complex systems: first-level experts model regime-specific heterogeneity, while second-level experts capture the diversity of underlying mechanisms. By dynamically combining these two levels, REM-MoE adaptively represents evolutionary dynamics under varying ''regime--mechanism'' conditions, thereby modeling state-dependent changes in regime--mechanism interactions. We validate our approach on a global carbon flux prediction task, where observational signals are jointly driven by multiple mechanisms across diverse regimes. Experimental results show that the proposed method consistently outperforms strong baselines in prediction accuracy while learning regime-dependent mechanism representations that are aligned with physical reference patterns. Furthermore, REM-MoE maintains strong performance over longer forecasting horizons and yields physically interpretable routing patterns. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/Son4ta/REM-MoE.
journal: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia

title: RemoPhysEmo: A Multimodal Emotion Dataset with Remotely Sensed Physiological Signals via Video and Radar
abstract: Emotion recognition is a fundamental task in affective computing, and most current works consider multimodal fusion to integrate comprehensive information for better performance. Among the modalities, physiological signals present a specialty, as on the one side, they are hard to alter, providing more objective evidence for emotion understanding; on the other side, they require delicate equipment to be attached to the body, which is inconvenient and interfering for the monitored persons. Existing multimodal emotion research concerns more of non-physiological modalities, such as video, audio, and text, whereas physiological signals remain insufficiently explored. To bridge this gap, we introduce a new multimodal emotion dataset with remotely sensed physiological signals by millimeter-wave radar and facial videos. The new dataset is targeted to facilitate two research fields: 1) multimodal remote physiological signal measurement, and 2) physiological-behavioral fusion for emotion recognition with only remote sensors. Furthermore, beyond clip-level emotion annotations, we also provide fine-grained intensity labels, enabling more detailed temporal emotion analysis. Extensive benchmarks were established on the new dataset, including uni- and multimodal approaches for remote physiological signal measurement and emotion recognition. It is expected that the dataset and benchmarks provide a new testbed and open up new possibilities for future research. The dataset is available at: https://github.com/helloworld-YY/RemoPhysEmo.
journal: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia

title: Towards Richer Referring Multi-Object Tracking in Satellite Videos: A Large-Scale Dataset and Baseline
abstract: Referring Multi-Object Tracking in satellite videos (RMOT-SV) aims to track multiple targets in remote sensing imagery using natural language descriptions. Existing benchmarks remain limited in scale and annotation diversity, with short and simple expressions that provide insufficient support for complex scenarios involving multiple tiny objects. To address these limitations, we present SatRMOT, the largest and most diverse benchmark for referring multi-object tracking in satellite videos. SatRMOT is characterized by three key properties: (i) larger scale, with 523 videos, 138k frames, and 19k referring expressions, substantially exceeding existing RMOT-SV benchmarks; (ii) richer expressions, where each video is annotated with diverse natural language descriptions involving motion patterns, spatial relations, and contextual cues; and (iii) multi-object referring for tiny targets, where expressions frequently describe multiple small objects, particularly cars, in dense and complex satellite scenes. A multi-agent collaborative framework is developed to enable scalable and high-quality annotation with reduced human labor and time costs. Building upon this dataset, we propose Dual Refinement Track (DRTrack), a strong baseline for RMOT-SV that performs joint visual-linguistic refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate the challenging nature of our dataset and the effectiveness of our method. The dataset will be released at https://satrmot.github.io/.
journal: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia

title: GreenMM: Efficient Systems and AI for the Planet
abstract: GreenMM: Efficient Systems and AI for the Planet is a half-day workshop held in conjunction with ACM Multimedia 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The workshop brings together two views of sustainability in multimedia AI. The first, Green in AI, asks how multimedia systems can use less computation, energy, memory, data, and adaptation effort. The second, Green by AI, considers how images, video, audio, remote sensing, and other multimodal data can support environmental and planetary applications. GreenMM received 13 submissions and accepted 9 papers for presentation, with four selected for oral presentation and five for posters. The accepted programme spans visual-token reduction for vision-language and biodiversity applications, parameter- and data-efficient adaptation, energy-aware 3D Gaussian Splatting, and environmental monitoring under geographic and spectral shift. The programme also includes two invited keynotes and an open panel discussion. This paper summarizes the motivation and scope of GreenMM, the review and selection process, the technical programme, and several questions that emerged across the accepted contributions.
journal: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia

title: Seventy years of parasocial research: a bibliometric analysis and science mapping, 1956–2025
abstract: Research using the term ‘parasocial’ has appeared since 1956 in media studies and psychology and, more recently, in influencer marketing. This study maps the development, intellectual structure and recent thematic direction of the 2174 journal works published from 1956 to 2025 that use the term ‘parasocial’ in its media sense. Using records from OpenAlex, it combines performance analysis with co-citation, bibliographic coupling, keyword mapping and topic analysis and tests the robustness of the main mapping results across alternative corpora, periods and network settings. Output increased from one article in 1956 to 521 works in 2025, and, by authors’ affiliations, the USA, Indonesia and China had the most works. Horton and Wohl’s 1956 article is cited by 63.1% of the works with a reference list. Under the main network settings, the most frequently cited references form two co-citation communities, which we interpret as a media-psychology foundation and an influencer-marketing stream; they differ in topic and in the age of their references, and the share of co-citation link weight between them increased across the three periods from 2014–2019 to 2023–2025. The keyword ‘Influencer marketing’ appears in 28.7% of the works published in 2023–2025; in that period the topic ‘Digital Marketing and Social Media’ exceeded ‘Media Influence and Health’, whereas across 2020–2025 the two were nearly equal (397 and 405 works). OpenAlex topic labels identify AI-related topics in 3.0% of the works from 2023–2025. A separate language-model-assisted classification of titles and stored abstracts classified 71 of these works (6.3%) as studying a parasocial bond with an artificial partner; the author examined every such case individually. Together, the widely shared cited reference, the rising co-citation between the two communities and the application of the concept to influencers and artificial agents offer a frame for comparing which conditions of a parasocial bond studies keep and which they change; how studies define or measure the phenomenon, and whether the concept applies to artificial agents, are questions that future content analyses and experiments could examine.

title: HeartGuard: An IoT-Enabled Cardiovascular Health Monitoring and Risk Prediction System
abstract: HeartGuard is a prototype system that uses Internet of Things (IoT) technology to monitor cardiovascular health and predict risks. It combines physiological sensing, ECG data capture, wireless communication, database storage, and patient medical profiles within one integrated platform. The hardware centers on an ESP32 microcontroller and includes sensors for heart rate, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), temperature, and ECG. The system displays data locally on an OLED screen and also sends it to a web application, allowing remote data viewing. The software integrates real-time sensor readings with patient details such as age, sex, blood pressure, cholesterol, chest-pain type, exercise-induced angina, ST depression, and resting ECG results. For risk prediction, HeartGuard uses a Random Forest machine learning model, while ECG arrhythmia classification relies on a convolutional neural network (CNN). Currently, these models are developed using publicly available data from Kaggle. In the future, HeartGuard aims to train models directly on data collected by the deployed sensors. The prototype presents cardiovascular risk as a percentage calculated at the application level, but future versions plan to use calibrated probabilities directly from the Random Forest output. The system includes interactive interfaces for risk visualization, ECG analysis, patient records management, and generates clinical-style PDF reports.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Advances and Paradigms in Modern Plant Bioinformatics: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Plant bioinformatics has undergone a paradigm shift from simple gene discovery and sequence alignment to AI-driven multi-omics integration, graph pangenomics, and precision molecular breeding. The intrinsic hyper-complexity of plant genomes—characterized by high polyploidy, extensive heterozygosity, massive repetitive element burdens, and dynamic structural variations—has mandated the invention of specialized assembly algorithms, statistically robust annotation pipelines, and high-dimensional deep learning architectures. This comprehensive review synthesizes core computational methodologies across de novo polyploid sequence assembly (Overlap-Layout-Consensus vs. De Bruijn Graphs), structural and evidence-based functional annotation, epigenomic landscape mapping (WGBS, ATAC-Seq), graph-based pangenomics, single-cell multi-omics resolution, and transcriptomic network modeling. Furthermore, we evaluate state-of-the-art transformer-based Genomic Language Models (GLMs), structural biology integrations (AlphaFold3/ESMFold), and specialized plant databases. Finally, key computational bottlenecks, infrastructure scaling considerations, and actionable computational frameworks for accelerating climate-resilient crop breeding are critically evaluated.
journal: Research Journal of Life Sciences, Bioinformatics, Pharmaceutical and Chemical Sciences

title: Spectrogram-Based CNN Autoencoder for One-Class Anomaly Detection in Machining Vibration Signals
abstract: This work presents a one-class anomaly detection framework for vibration-based condition monitoring in machining processes using a convolutional neural network autoencoder. Three-axis vibration signals acquired during industrial broaching are transformed into time--frequency spectrograms and combined into a compact three-channel representation, enabling convolutional feature learning on multivariate time-series data. The autoencoder is trained exclusively on normal process data and detects anomalous strokes based on reconstruction errors. Labeled validation data are used for threshold calibration and an independent test set is reserved for final performance evaluation. To improve sensitivity to short-lived process instabilities such as chatter, a localized residual-based metric termed Segmented Vertical Error (SVE) is introduced. Experimental results on approximately 10{,}000 broaching strokes show a clear separation between normal and anomalous process conditions under strong class imbalance. The processing pipeline is additionally evaluated on an external public turning dataset as a proof of concept, indicating preliminary applicability beyond the original broaching setup. The results suggest that spectrogram-based autoencoder models can provide a practical and scalable basis for one-class anomaly detection in industrial vibration monitoring.

title: NeuralProphet for Ordinal Time Series Forecasting: A Two-Stage Approach with Threshold Optimization
abstract: Air quality indices, energy load levels, and similar series are recorded as ordered categories, yet standard forecasting methods produce continuous predictions. We propose a two-stage approach using NeuralProphet, which decomposes a series into trend, seasonality, and autoregressive components. In the first stage, NeuralProphet is fit to the ordinal labels treated as continuous, yielding a decomposition and a continuous forecast. In the second, ordered thresholds mapping it to categories are optimized on a validation segment, replacing naive rounding. We evaluate the method on simulations and on two hourly series, Beijing air quality and electricity load in a Ball State University building, with U.S. Drought Monitor categories as a third series. In simulation the method recovers the latent ordering and generating components, and threshold optimization improves the quadratic weighted kappa over rounding in every condition, especially when the first stage is miscalibrated but order-preserving, as under trend shifts or evolving seasonality. On the hourly series it outperforms logistic and ordered-logit baselines at every horizon, and threshold optimization improves on rounding at all but the shortest Beijing horizon and at every drought horizon. The approach is an effective, interpretable route to ordinal forecasting without a specialized ordinal model.

title: Wavelet-Constrained Prior-Guided Flow Matching for Remote Sensing Spatiotemporal Fusion
abstract: Spatiotemporal fusion techniques can generate remote sensing imagery with both high spatial and temporal resolutions, thereby supporting a wide range of Earth observation applications. Although recent diffusion-based STF methods have shown promising reconstruction performance, generation from Gaussian noise typically requires many iterative sampling steps, resulting in considerable inference cost. To enable efficient few-step reconstruction, we propose WPFM-STF, a wavelet-constrained prior-guided Flow Matching framework for remote sensing spatiotemporal fusion, specifically adapting Flow Matching to the characteristics of STF by formulating reconstruction as a continuous transport process from a learned spatiotemporal prior to the target fine-resolution image. Specifically, a learnable prior generator integrates multi-temporal and multi-resolution observations to produce an initial estimate that already captures scene structure and temporal variation, thereby shortening the effective transport path compared with noise-based generation. Conditional Flow Matching is then employed to learn the prior-to-target velocity field, providing a more flexible and progressive refinement process than one-shot regression while enabling accurate reconstruction with only a few ordinary differential equation evaluations. To further preserve fine spatial structures during few-step transport, a wavelet detail constraint is imposed on the high-frequency components of a residual-induced auxiliary reconstruction derived from the predicted velocity field. Extensive experiments on the CIA, LGC, and Daxing datasets demonstrate that WPFM-STF achieves competitive or superior reconstruction performance with only a few ODE evaluations; ablation studies validate the effectiveness of the learned spatiotemporal prior, prior-guided flow refinement, and wavelet detail constraint; and efficiency analyses further confirm its substantial advantage over iterative diffusion-based STF methods.

title: Ancestral knowledge in the artisanal sector and its socioeconomic benefits in the state of Tabasco
abstract: This article examines the relationship between ancestral knowledge, artisanal production, and socioeconomic benefits in Tabasco through an integrative review of academic literature and official documents. The corpus covers embroidered strips, plant fibers, wood carving, drum making, and workshop organization, together with cultural statistics, legislation, and public programs. Findings show that craft knowledge functions as a territorial asset: it preserves memory and identity, mobilizes local materials and family networks, creates self-employment and supplementary income, and strengthens women's economic agency. Evidence from Nacajuca documents family-based value chains, intergenerational transmission, and high female participation. Yet the sector faces informality, intermediation, weak cost accounting, a digital divide, industrial imitation, input scarcity, and insufficient protection of collective designs. A socioeconomic benefit model is proposed that links community-led safeguarding, business capabilities, authenticity, marketing, and governance. The article concludes that sustainable profitability requires recognizing communities as knowledge holders and distributing value fairly without separating products from the cultural and ecological processes that make them possible.

title: The Power of Behavioral Antecedents in Predicting Supply Chain Performance of Crop Seed Enterprises
abstract: This study examined whether opportunistic behavior, supply chain collaboration, social bonds (supply chain socialization) and human resource practices predict supply chain performance, measured as quality, response time, productivity and financial/cost performance, in crop seed enterprises in Kenya. Guided by social exchange and systems theories, a quantitative survey was conducted of 143 crop seed enterprises registered in Kenya as of 2024. Data were collected from supply chain heads, operations officers or their equivalents in public and private seed companies and analyzed using structural equation modeling, with each driver tested in a separate prediction model. Each hypothesis was partially supported, with one performance dimension significantly related to each driver. Opportunistic behavior significantly lowered quality (b = ?0.40, p = .036). Supply chain collaboration (b = 0.225, p = .040) and human resource practices (b = 0.225, p = .033) were positively associated with productivity, while social bonds were associated with shorter response times (b = ?1.024, p = .034). No driver significantly predicted financial/cost performance at the .05 level. Crop seed enterprises should curb opportunism through clear contracts and quality verification, invest in collaboration and human resource practices to raise productivity, and build partner socialization to improve speed, with support from seed associations like Seed Trade Association of Kenya (STAK) and regulators like Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Service (KEPHIS). The study contributes to behavioral prediction models of multidimensional supply chain performance in an under-researched agricultural input sector. Received: 09 September 2026 / Accepted: 29 October 2026 / Published: November 2026

title: Food Security in the Sultanate of Oman, 1975–2025: Fisheries, Falaj Agriculture and the Rise of Diversified Self-Sufficiency
abstract: Oman differs from its Gulf neighbours in several respects relevant to food security: a long Arabian Sea coastline with productive fisheries, a monsoon-influenced southern region (Dhofar), an ancient irrigation tradition based on the falaj system, and major ports at Sohar, Duqm and Salalah that lie outside, or at the mouth of, the Strait of Hormuz. Since the start of the modern state in 1970, its population has grown from well under one million to over five million, and food demand has risen accordingly. This review traces Oman's food-security trajectory over five decades, drawing on National Centre for Statistics and Information data, ministry production statistics reported in the national press, the Global Food Security Index and the scholarly literature. Over the period, coastal agriculture on the Al Batinah plain suffered severe groundwater salinisation, which undermined date and lime cultivation. Since about 2010, however, deliberate investment in fisheries, aquaculture, dairy, poultry, eggs and protected vegetables has raised overall food self-sufficiency to about 65.8% in 2024, with sector ratios of 144.5% for fish, 87.3% for animal production, 66.4% for food and beverage industries and 49.4% for agricultural crop products. At commodity level, the latest reported self-sufficiency is about 146–162% for fish, 97–99% for dates, 92–97% for milk and 92–95% for eggs, while poultry stood at 55–60% and red meat at 46% in 2023. Oman scored 71.2 in the 2022 GFSI (35th of 113), and its gain of 13.8 points since 2012 was the largest improvement of any country. The review concludes that Oman's combination of marine resources, targeted investment and port diversification offers a model for arid states, while water quality, climate risk and feed dependence remain the principal constraints.

title: Mining Fossil Water: A Review of Groundwater Depletion, Recharge and Sustainable Management of the Nubian Sandstone Aquifer System
abstract: The Nubian Sandstone Aquifer System (NSAS), shared by Egypt, Libya, Sudan and Chad, is the largest fossil groundwater system on Earth, underlying about two million square kilometres of the eastern Sahara. Most of its water was recharged during humid periods of the Pleistocene and early Holocene and is effectively non-renewable on human timescales. Expanding abstraction for desert reclamation in Egypt's Western Desert and for Libya's Great Man-Made River has lowered water levels, dried artesian springs and raised pumping costs at major centres. This review synthesises hydrogeological, isotopic, numerical-modelling and satellite-gravimetry (GRACE) studies to assess the state of the aquifer. The literature agrees that large-scale transboundary drawdown is likely to be limited, but that local drawdown at pumping centres co-located with oases will become excessive, threatening oasis ecosystems, traditional agriculture and the economic viability of reclamation schemes. GRACE-based studies estimate depletion of about 4.4 km³ per year in the Dakhla sub-basin and show that modern recharge is episodic and limited to the southern and eastern margins during exceptionally wet years or high stands of Lake Nasser. The review discusses the economics of mining fossil water for low-value crops, the environmental impacts on oases, and the institutional arrangements of the Joint Authority for the Study and Development of the Nubian Aquifer, and proposes a framework for planned, transparent depletion management.

title: Extreme Heat in the Middle East and North Africa: Observed Trends, Future Projections and Impacts on Health, Labour, Water and Food Security
abstract: The Middle East and North Africa (MENA) is one of the world's climate-change hotspots. Observations show that the Eastern Mediterranean and Middle East has warmed by about 0.45 °C per decade since 1981, almost twice the global rate, and that the number of very hot days has roughly doubled since 1970. This review synthesises observational and modelling studies of extreme heat in MENA and its consequences. Under a scenario in which global emissions decline after 2040, the number of extremely hot days per year is projected to rise from about 16 in 1986–2005 to about 80 by mid-century and 118 by the end of the century; under business-as-usual emissions, about 200 unusually hot days per year are projected, and the maximum temperature of the hottest days may approach 50 °C. Regional models project the emergence of super- and ultra-extreme heatwaves of unprecedented intensity and duration, while studies of wet-bulb temperature show that the humid coasts of the Gulf and Red Sea could experience conditions approaching the limits of human tolerance. The consequences include heat-related illness and mortality, reduced outdoor labour productivity, higher electricity and water demand, crop and livestock stress and threats to urban liveability. The review evaluates adaptation measures, including heat-health early warning systems, occupational heat standards, urban greening and cool materials, building-energy efficiency and climate-resilient agriculture, and identifies research priorities for the region.

title: Multi-Task Deep Learning for Simultaneous Prediction of Agricultural Biological Traits
abstract: Agricultural traits are interdependent, yet prediction pipelines often fit each phenotype independently and discard information carried by correlated traits. This study evaluated whether multi-task deep learning improved simultaneous prediction of maize grain yield, plant height, anthesis date, silking date, and grain moisture by learning a shared genomic-environmental representation while retaining trait-specific output functions. We conducted an empirical analysis using Genomes to Fields records, integrating genotype principal components with target-independent early-season weather, soil, and management covariates. The analytical cohort comprised 16,728 plot records from 1,102 hybrids across 41 location-year environments; 2014-2016 formed the development period, and 2017 remained isolated for temporal confirmation. We compared a task-balanced hard-sharing network with elastic net, random forest, XGBoost, multi-trait GBLUP, matched single-task neural networks, and a cross-stitch multi-task comparator. Validation included nested environment-grouped testing, genotype-ID transfer, kinship-cluster holdout, joint unseen-genotype × unseen-environment stress testing, temporal confirmation, and an independent protocol-replication benchmark using the European DROPS maize panel. The multi-task model retained the lowest standardized error across the principal G2F regimes, with the strongest gains for anthesis and silking; the advantage narrowed but remained positive under kinship-controlled transfer and independent protocol replication. Environment-level leave-one-out sensitivity and exact sign-based inference supported the temporal ranking without treating bootstrap resamples as new biological replicates. The findings indicate that multi-task learning is most defensible when task covariance is biologically justified, predictor timing is target-independent, genetic relatedness is controlled explicitly, and validation matches deployment conditions. The framework provides a rigorous basis for simultaneous prediction of agricultural traits under multiple forms of distribution shift.

title: AI-Based Smart Agriculture: An Integrated Machine Learning Framework for Crop Recommendation, Fertilizer Recommendation and Crop Yield Prediction
abstract: Agricultural productivity in India is strongly affected by weather variability, soil degradation and the over- or under-use of fertilizers. Farmers still tend to rely on personal experience when choosing a crop, estimating its yield and deciding how much fertilizer to apply. This paper presents an integrated, web-based decision-support system that performs three tasks within a single framework: crop recommendation, fertilizer recommendation and crop yield prediction. The system takes soil nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium), temperature, humidity, soil pH, rainfall, soil moisture, soil type and crop type as inputs. The pipeline consists of data acquisition from public repositories, cleaning and normalisation, correlation-based feature selection, and model training using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Random Forest (RF). Model performance is evaluated with cross-validation using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score and correlation-based measures. In the reported experiments, the ANN model for yield prediction reached an accuracy of 94.70% and the Random Forest model for fertilizer recommendation reached 93.94%, and the crop recommendation model [insert accuracy] was the best performer for its task. The models are packaged in a Java (JSP/Servlet, Weka, MySQL) web application that lets farmers obtain all three recommendations from one input form..
