title: Differentiable Agent-Based Modeling for Multi-Echelon Supply Chains: Gradient-Based Optimization of Heterogeneous Policies at Scale
abstract: Global supply chains rely on the interactions of thousands of heterogeneous agents, posing significant challenges for optimization. While traditional optimization often assumes homogeneity to ensure tractability, Reinforcement Learning struggles with sample inefficiency when scaling to high-dimensional state spaces. We propose a Differentiable Agent-Based Model for multi-echelon inventory management. By implementing stochastic dynamics via differentiable tensor operations, we enable direct gradient propagation through the simulation. We validate the framework by recovering theoretical Newsvendor optima without supervision. Crucially, we demonstrate ``Mass Personalization'' by optimizing 10,000 distinct agent policies simultaneously in seconds, achieving a 53% cost reduction compared to scalar baselines. Furthermore, we utilize gradient sensitivity analysis to generate causal heatmaps, accurately recovering inherent lead-time delays from the computation graph. This approach bridges the gap between simulation and optimization, enabling the efficient training of self-correcting Digital Twins.

title: Where Should Models Run? A Collaborative Inference Framework for Embodied Intelligence in 6G
abstract: Embodied intelligence systems rely on fast and reliable inference to enable real-time perception, reasoning, and control. Recent advances in large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) models, including Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, have significantly enhanced the capabilities of embodied agents in complex environments. However, deploying these models remains challenging due to the limited computational resources and energy budgets of robotic platforms. A fundamental question is where inference should be executed. Collaborative inference, which partitions models across end devices, edge servers, and the cloud, has emerged as a promising solution. Yet determining the optimal partitioning point remains an open problem, as it depends on wireless network conditions, model structure, and privacy requirements. This article reviews the state of the art in collaborative inference for embodied intelligence and proposes an edge-centric framework in which the edge coordinates model partitioning and execution. Through both simulation and real-world experiments over WiFi and 5G networks, we demonstrate that the optimal partitioning strategy varies with network conditions and model structure. We further identify latency-minimizing partition points for ResNet-101, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and OpenVLA-7B in collaborative inference between NVIDIA Jetson Nano or AGX Xavier devices and an AGX Thor edge server under varying wireless conditions. Finally, we discuss the future directions for collaborative inference in 6G-empowered embodied intelligence systems.

title: Physics2Weight: Direct Neural Network Architecture and Weight Generation from Physical Laws Using Large Language Models
abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled weight-space programming (WSP), which directly generates neural network weights without gradient-based optimization. However, extending WSP to physical problems remains challenging, particularly in achieving both solution accuracy and physical consistency. In this paper, we propose Physics2Weight (PtW), a framework that extends WSP to solving partial differential equations by directly generating neural network weights and editing architectures based on governing equations and initial and boundary conditions. PtW introduces physics-constrained prompting and physics-guided architecture editing, combined with iterative weight refinement from WSP, to improve solution accuracy and physical consistency without gradient-based optimization. Experiments on four PDEs, namely the heat, advection, Burgers', and Allen--Cahn equations, demonstrate lower solution errors than conventional physics-informed neural networks, while revealing limitations in satisfying the governing equations for nonlinear PDEs.

title: Predictive Surprise as Self-Grounding Concept Bottleneck for Interpretable Time Series
abstract: Time-series classifiers deployed in risk-sensitive domains must be (1) accurate, (2) interpretable, and (3) able to abstain when evidence is weak. Existing methods do not deliver all 3 at once, and the obstacle is structural, rather than logistical. Meaningful temporal patterns cannot be defined without knowing segment boundaries, yet meaningful boundaries cannot be placed without knowing which patterns to expect. Existing approaches break this circularity by using fixed windows or expert-annotated vocabularies, thereby sacrificing at least one of the 3 properties. We introduce ConceptTime, which closes the loop through a single self-supervised signal. A frozen probabilistic forecaster predicts a distribution over the next observation at every timestep of the sequence. We call the mismatch between its prediction and the realized signal the predictive surprise. This signal both locates segment boundaries and characterizes each resulting segment through the forecaster. Segments are thus grounded by how they behaved relative to expectation, not by what they look like. These summaries cluster into a vocabulary of dynamical regimes that we call concepts. A lightweight head classifies from the concept sequence, and the distance to the nearest concept yields reliability by design. Across 17 public benchmarks, ConceptTime is competitive with state-of-the-art black-box accuracy, beats every interpretable baseline, and retains near-98% accuracy on Epilepsy with 1% of labels. It further remains competitive with softmax, prototype-distance, and SHAP/TimeX/TimeX++ on OOD detection and deletion faithfulness, without a single annotation, language model call, or domain expert. Code is available at: https://github.com/Sachithx/ConceptTime.git.

title: Embodied Science Agents: Making Embodied Experimental Design Learnable
abstract: Recent advances in large models have accelerated AI for Science toward agentic science, where AI agents autonomously conduct scientific discovery. Realising this vision requires closing the loop between computational reasoning and physical experimentation, positioning self-driving laboratories (SDLs) as critical enablers. However, existing SDLs exhibit a fundamental paradox: foundation model integration has increased linguistic sophistication while severing physical grounding. By treating models as disembodied planners that output symbolic workflows for separate robotic systems, current architectures inherently block the development of embodied experimental intuition. We argue that overcoming this paradox requires embedding \emph{learnability} along three interdependent axes: cognitive learnability (learning what to investigate), experimental learnability (learning where to search), and embodied learnability (learning how to act). Building on this view, we introduce the Embodied Science Agent (ESA), which unifies digital intelligence with physical embodiment through three synergistic components: a Digital Agent that provides cognitive and experimental learnability via memory-based reasoning and Bayesian optimisation, an Embodied Agent that provides embodied learnability via generalisable instrument control, and an Embodied Unified Interface for seamless coordination. We validated ESA in autonomous wastewater treatment experiments, navigating over 200 million possible conditions. Through 15 continuous rounds, ESA raised the final solution transmittance from 82\% to 99.7\%, corresponding to a 98.5\% reduction in residual dye concentration and near-complete decolourisation, while its learned visuomotor policies generalised across varying instrument placements, a promising step toward next-generation SDLs for autonomous scientific discovery.

title: AI-Based Pest Detection and Classification for Multi-Crop Farms Using Enhanced YOLOv8: A Review and Proposed Framework
journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Engineering and Management

title: Pemetaan Wilayah di Kota Palembang untuk Memprioritaskan Penyaluran Bantuan Sosial Menggunakan Algoritma K-Means Clustering
abstract: Poverty remains a multidimensional social issue in Palembang City, where the poor population reached 10.22% in 2023. The distribution of social assistance often faces challenges such as data inaccuracies, uneven distribution, and subjective decision-making processes. This study aims to apply the K-Means Clustering algorithm to map 18 sub-districts in Palembang City into priority zones for social assistance distribution based on seven socio-economic indicators. The dataset includes poor population, unemployment rate, average income, population density, public facility access score, number of social assistance recipient households, and the Human Development Index (HDI). Data preprocessing was performed using Min-Max Normalization, followed by the calculation of the Composite Vulnerability Index (CVI). Model evaluation using the Elbow Method, Silhouette Score (0.45–0.55), and Davies–Bouldin Index confirmed K=3 as the optimal number of clusters. The resulting clusters categorize the sub-districts into high priority (emergency, e.g., Kertapati, Gandus, and Seberang Ulu I), medium priority (alert, e.g., Plaju, Sukarami, and Sako), and low priority (independent, e.g., Ilir Timur I, Bukit Kecil, and Alang-Alang Lebar). In addition, a Decision Support System (DSS) simulator was implemented based on the clustering and CVI results to provide data-driven budget and quota allocation recommendations.

title: Implementation of Latent Dirichlet Allocation for the Analysis of Election Logistics Distribution Reports at Bawaslu RI
abstract: Purpose – This study aims to implement Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) for analyzing election logistics distribution monitoring reports at Bawaslu RI and to develop an interactive dashboard to support topic exploration. The study addresses the difficulty of manually interpreting large collections of institutional reports containing operational, administrative, geographical, procurement, and legal information related to election logistics distribution. Design/methods/approach – This research applied a quantitative text mining approach. A total of 254 valid PDF-based monitoring reports were extracted, validated, cleaned, and transformed into an analyzable corpus. Text preprocessing involved case folding, text cleaning, tokenization, and stopword removal using Indonesian and domain-specific stopword lists. The cleaned corpus was represented using Bag of Words and modeled using LDA with the Gensim library. Topic configurations from 2 to 15 were evaluated using the C_V coherence score, and the results were integrated into a web-based dashboard using Streamlit and PyLDAvis. Findings – The optimal model produced ten topics with a C_V coherence score of 0.4040. The generated topics represented themes such as regional supervision, logistics completeness, administrative procedures, island distribution, procurement, archipelago distribution, and post-election legal processes. The dashboard enabled interactive exploration of topics, coherence evaluation, topic interpretation, and visualization of intertopic relationships. Research implications/limitations – The study demonstrates the value of topic modeling for improving the analysis of government monitoring reports, although expert validation with Bawaslu officers remains necessary. Originality/value – This study contributes by applying LDA to official election logistics reports and integrating the results into an accessible analytical dashboard for election supervision stakeholders.
journal: Journal of Embedded Systems, Security and Intelligent Systems

title: TRANSMISSION LINE ICE ACCRETION PROBABILITY PREDICTION AND DE-ICING THRESHOLD OPTIMIZATION BASED ON BAYESIAN EXTREME VALUE THEORY AND MONTE CARLO SIMULATION
abstract: Transmission line icing is a rare and severe hazard; therefore, a fixed de-icing threshold cannot account for forecast uncertainty, accumulated long-term risk, and the economic trade-off between de-icing costs and tower collapse losses. Based on 30 years of annual maximum ice-thickness data, real-time weather forecasts and operating cost parameters, this paper builds a probabilistic prediction and de-icing decision model. A generalised extreme value distribution is used to obtain the prior via maximum likelihood estimation, Bayesian updating and Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling generate the posterior distribution, a homogeneous Poisson process determines the long-term event frequency, and finally, Bayesian expected loss yields a dynamic de-icing threshold. The fitted GEV parameters are μ=11.95, σ=3.08, ξ=-0.19, and the 50-year and 100-year return levels are 21.5 and 23.9 mm, respectively. Under the given severe-weather condition, the posterior mean is 15.6 mm, and the probability of exceeding 15 mm is 0.84. The probabilities of at least one event within 10, 20, 30 and 50 years are 0.9030, 0.9906, 0.9991 and 0.9999, respectively. The optimal de-icing threshold ranges from 14.2 to 18.6 mm, reducing the expected total cost by about 18.7% compared with a fixed-threshold policy. This report provides verifiable statistical decision support for the construction of a high-probability warning system and proactive de-icing measures for transmission lines.

title: Economic Evaluation of Sustainable Agricultural Production Systems for Improving Farm Productivity, Resource Efficiency and Rural Livelihood Development
abstract: The growing challenges of agricultural resource depletion, escalating production costs, environmental degradation, and rural economic vulnerability have emphasized the importance of transitioning toward economically viable and sustainable agricultural production systems. This study develops an integrated economic evaluation framework to assess the contributions of sustainable agricultural practices toward enhancing farm productivity, resource-use efficiency, profitability, and rural livelihood development in Pakistan. The research examines a farm-level dataset comprising 2,400 agricultural households distributed across 12 agricultural districts during 2020–2025, incorporating 86 socioeconomic, environmental, and production-related variables. Agricultural production systems are categorized into conventional farming (960 farms), integrated resource management (720 farms), and climate-smart sustainable agriculture (720 farms). The analytical framework integrates Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA), Stochastic Frontier Analysis (SFA), cost–benefit analysis, and multivariate regression modelling to evaluate technical efficiency, resource allocation, economic returns, and household welfare outcomes. The reported findings indicate that sustainable agricultural production systems improve average crop productivity by 24.6%, increase irrigation water-use efficiency by 31.8%, enhance fertilizer-use efficiency by 27.4%, and reduce agricultural energy consumption by 19.7% compared with conventional farming. Economic assessment reveals that average annual net farm income increases from PKR 485,000 under conventional farming to PKR 672,000 under sustainable agricultural management, representing a 38.6% improvement. Furthermore, the benefit–cost ratio increases from 1.42 to 1.89, while mean technical efficiency rises from 0.71 to 0.89. Multivariate regression analysis identifies statistically significant positive associations between sustainable agricultural adoption, farm productivity, resource efficiency, and household income (*p* < .01). Additional findings demonstrate a 22.3% improvement in rural livelihood performance and a 17.6% reduction in agricultural production costs. The study establishes an integrated economic assessment perspective demonstrating the potential of sustainable agricultural systems to strengthen agricultural competitiveness, optimize resource utilization, and enhance rural socioeconomic resilience. These findings offer policy-relevant insights for promoting sustainable agricultural investment, resource-efficient farming technologies, inclusive rural development, and long-term agricultural sustainability in developing economies. title: Controlled Evaluation of Gated Multimodal Fusion for Lie Detection Using Facial Motion and Speech Cues
abstract: Automatic lie detection from video requires combining weak behavioral cues under clip-level supervision. In gated multimodal models, the effects of modality-prior initialization and continuing regularization are difficult to distinguish without matched controls. This study evaluates a three-stream DOLOS pipeline combining static face crops, short-term optical flow, Wav2Vec2-base speech representations, and face-validity masks. Three gated logit-fusion conditions are compared: uniform initialization without regularization, directed initialization without regularization, and directed initialization with Prior-KL. Each condition is evaluated across three predefined splits and three random seeds. The directed-initialized Prior-KL model achieves 64.16 ± 4.56% AUC, 58.96 ± 4.16% balanced accuracy at the validation-selected threshold, 56.74 ± 10.67% lie-class F1, and 57.45 ± 5.15% macro-F1. Relative to the uniform-initialized control, the combined initialization-plus-KL configuration gains 2.26 percentage points in AUC and 2.29 points in macro-F1. With directed initialization held constant, adding KL yields higher lie-class F1 but no improvement in AUC or balanced accuracy. A matched seed-42 ablation finds that static facial appearance alone achieves higher AUC and balanced accuracy than the fused model, while fusion yields higher lie-class F1. These findings associate the observed mean AUC gain with directed initialization and show a class-specific trade-off from regularization. They also motivate identity-disjoint evaluation to assess the role of appearance-related shortcuts.

title: Laborguard Blockchain-Enabled Agricultural Labor Verification and Anti-Human-Trafficking Compliance Device
abstract: The LaborGuard Blockchain-Enabled Agricultural Labor Verification and Anti-Human-Trafficking Compliance Device is a proposed portable, ruggedized data-processing platform intended to strengthen agricultural workforce accountability, crop-production documentation, regulatory compliance and ethical supply-chain transparency. The underlying external design is registered with the United Kingdom Intellectual Property Office under Design No. 6548985, with a registration date of 25 August 2026 and a grant date of 8 September 2026. Classified under International Design Classification 14-02, the registered subject matter is the visible configuration of data-processing equipment. LaborGuard extends this hardware concept into a proposed integrated operational platform for agricultural enterprises, cooperatives, extension services, certification bodies, labor inspectors and other authorized stakeholders. The technical concept links authenticated workforce participation with agronomic operations across economically important crops such as soybean, corn, wheat, rice, cotton, sugarcane, potatoes, tomatoes, lettuce, strawberries, grapes, apples, citrus, almonds and cassava. In the intended implementation, the device records worker identities and employment agreements alongside field assignments, planting, fertilizer management, irrigation, pesticide applications, weed and disease control, harvesting, storage, transportation and post-harvest handling. Each validated operation would be assigned appropriate crop, plot, operator, time and authorization metadata, generating a connected evidence trail for labor oversight and crop-production traceability. The proposed hardware embodiment incorporates a protective angular enclosure, a raised carrying handle, a display, an identification module, sensor connections, grouped control keys, a grille, status indicators and recessed side openings. Electronic subsystems would include secure processing, encrypted local record storage, geographic positioning, communications hardware and, where lawfully justified, biometric-assisted worker authentication. A permissioned blockchain would hold transaction commitments and verifiable audit metadata while sensitive personal records remain under controlled off-chain storage. Offline data capture and subsequent synchronization would support farm operations in locations with intermittent connectivity. LaborGuard also envisages a combined rule-based and analytical compliance layer. Employment-record comparisons and calibrated anomaly-detection models could highlight unexplained wage deductions, mismatches between identities and assignments, excessive recorded working hours, recruitment-fee discrepancies and other indicators associated with labor exploitation. These findings would support structured review and timely referral; they would not independently establish trafficking, child labor or coercion. A worker- centered governance model, human review, grievance channels, consent or another lawful basis for data processing and protection against retaliation remain necessary. The intended contribution is the coordinated documentation of who performed an authorized agricultural activity, where and when the activity was undertaken, how its production parameters were recorded, and which compliance checks were performed. This structure could support farm certification, responsible sourcing, sustainability reporting, food-safety documentation and transparent production management. The UK design certificate establishes the appearance shown in its registered illustrations; the proposed ruggedized configuration and functional system described in this report require detailed engineering, experimental testing and any appropriate additional intellectual property filings.

title: Global Proposal for the TNM Staging System for Poorly Differentiated Thyroid Cancer.
abstract: Key Points Question Can a dedicated TNM staging system be developed for poorly differentiated thyroid cancer (PDTC)? Findings In this cohort study of 1010 patients with PDTC, level VII lymph node metastasis was associated with significantly worse survival than level VI or lateral neck metastases, prompting its upgrading as a new N1c category and the establishment of a dedicated PDTC staging system with clear prognostic discrimination, which was externally validated by the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database. Meaning A PDTC-specific TNM staging system is proposed to inform future staging revisions.

title: From Generative Molecular Design to Agentic Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery.
abstract: Over the past decade, artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly influenced the early stages of drug discovery, which focus primarily on target evaluation and the design or identification of new active small molecules or biologics. Deep neural networks adapted from areas such as natural language processing and computer vision have provided novel opportunities for generative modeling and human-machine interactions. State-of-the-art AI models for generative molecular design have emerged, but remain only little understood so far. Furthermore, new computational systems are being devised rapidly that are expected to significantly transform the drug discovery landscape in the near future. These developments pose challenges to computer-aided drug discovery in various ways. In the following, we discuss these opportunities and challenges, with a focus on molecular design.

title: Restoring Predictability: A Variance Risk Premium Modified for Overnight Returns
abstract: Recent literature documents that the variance risk premium (VRP) loses its predictive power for market returns during the pandemic. We show that this failure is largely attributable to the standard measurement of realized variance, which equally weights overnight squared returns and intraday realized variance. Simulations demonstrate that the predictive performance of the conventional VRP deteriorates as overnight volatility and jump activity increase. To address this issue, we propose a new linear forecasting model for expected variance that separately captures the dynamics of daytime and overnight variance. Empirically, our model‐based VRP restores significant in‐sample predictability. In out‐of‐sample exercises, it achieves the best performance among competing predictors and generates substantial economic gains for a mean‐variance investor over short and medium horizons.

title: Mitochondrial Transplantation Preserves Regenerative Capacity of Denervated Skeletal Muscle by Disrupting a Ca2+ Overload-Mitophagy-Ferroptosis Circuit.
abstract: BACKGROUND Denervation-induced muscle atrophy progresses during the interval between nerve injury and reinnervation, and depletion of muscle satellite cells (MuSCs) contributes to impaired functional recovery. Although mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired quality control are implicated in muscle wasting, whether excessive mitochondrial turnover drives MuSC failure after denervation remains unclear. This study aimed to identify the pathogenic mechanisms underlying MuSC depletion and determine whether mitochondrial transplantation therapy (MTT) preserves regenerative capacity. METHODS A sciatic nerve transection model was established in mice to induce denervation-associated muscle atrophy. Mitochondria isolated from differentiated MuSCs were transplanted into denervated gastrocnemius muscles beginning 6 h after injury and repeated every 3 days for 6 weeks. RNA sequencing, calcium imaging, mitochondrial ultrastructural analysis, mito-mKeima-based mitophagic flux assessment, flow cytometry and molecular analyses were performed to investigate disease mechanisms and therapeutic effects. In vitro calcium overload models combined with Mdivi-1 treatment and Pink1 knockdown were used to define the regulatory pathway linking calcium stress, mitophagy and ferroptosis. RESULTS Denervated muscle exhibited early calcium dyshomeostasis (Fluo-4 AM fluorescence increased 6.7-fold vs. Sham, p < 0.0001) and mitochondrial dysfunction within 3 days, followed by iron accumulation (nonheme iron increased 1.5-fold, p = 0.0046) and ferroptotic changes by 2 weeks. Mechanistically, sustained calcium overload activated the Ampk-Tsc2-mTorc1 pathway in MuSCs, inducing Pink1-dependent excessive mitophagic flux. Mito-mKeima flow cytometry confirmed increased mitophagic flux after denervation, with approximately tenfold elevation at Day 3 and persistent activation at 2 weeks. Excessive mitophagy promoted Fth1 degradation (reduced by 47.5%, p = 0.0181) and increased Tfr1 expression (1.9-fold, p = 0.0035), thereby enhancing ferroptotic susceptibility. Inhibition of mitochondrial fission or Pink1 knockdown reduced iron accumulation (Fe2+ fluorescence reduced by 58.3% and 69.2%, respectively, both p < 0.01) and protected MuSCs from ferroptosis. MTT restored mitochondrial homeostasis by reducing calcium overload (73.7% decrease vs. A23187, p < 0.0001), increasing ATP production (36.9%, p < 0.01), suppressing excessive mitophagic flux, normalizing iron metabolism (39.9% reduction, p = 0.0015) and preserving MuSCs (30.0% increase vs. DN_PBS, p = 0.0196). Consequently, MTT attenuated denervation-induced muscle fibre atrophy and improved functional recovery following delayed nerve repair. CONCLUSIONS This study identifies an early pathogenic cascade linking calcium overload, excessive mitophagic flux and ferroptotic susceptibility as a critical driver of MuSC dysfunction during denervation-induced muscle wasting. MTT preserves regenerative capacity by interrupting this degenerative circuit and restoring mitochondrial quality control, providing a potential therapeutic strategy for denervation-associated muscle atrophy and other muscle wasting disorders.

title: Temporal Dynamics of Soil Organic Carbon Contents in Long‐Term Monitored Arable Sites in Lower Saxony, Germany
abstract: Temporal changes in soil organic carbon (SOC) contents in agricultural soils are variable, and underlying drivers are not sufficiently understood. The objectives were to describe the long‐term dynamics of SOC contents at 41 sites in Lower Saxony, Germany, and to analyze the relationships between estimated long‐term changes of SOC contents and climate, soil, and agricultural management data. Mixed‐effects regression models with observation weights were calculated for each site to estimate long‐term SOC changes (ΔSOC), and the long‐term ΔSOC values were then described using climate, soil, and agricultural management variables. The fitted regression lines for the temporal trajectories of SOC dynamics fell within the 95% confidence intervals of the annual mean SOC values in 96% of the observations, consistent with the expected coverage under a well‐fitting model. Multiple linear regression modeling for the estimated long‐term ΔSOC values explained the estimated ΔSOC variation satisfactorily (coefficient of determination R 2 = 0.77) and identified four variables with significant contributions: the initial SOC content with a negative regression coefficient and the initial pH, initial proportion of years with catch crops, and the clay content with positive regression coefficients. The results suggest that initial soil properties (SOC content and pH) and agricultural management, as well as the clay content may explain temporal changes in SOC contents to a large extent.

title: Knowledge‐Based Process Assurance: A Stakeholder‐Driven Framework for Internal Control
abstract: UK corporate governance remains on a largely “comply or explain” basis, despite continuing control failures. This paper proposes a Self‐Assurance (SA) paradigm—a decentralised, stakeholder‐centred, knowledge‐management process that embeds control ownership and testing within business operations. Using a conceptual governance lens, a portable SA framework is posited based on role identification within processes and key routines. This is developed through designing process maps and controls that identify risk and align control design with stakeholder needs and their risk ‘appetite’. Drawing on field applications when implementing a Financial Self Assurance process (FSA), observations are made on implementation challenges (culture, capability, systems, reporting) and practical countermeasures (explicit ownership, authority delegation, process mapping, targeted training, and dashboards). This leads to the view that FSA may be characterised as a knowledge‐led business‐friendly route to stronger internal control. The paper's contribution lies in the development of a pragmatic, scalable methodology for organisations to generate defensible control assurance while improving process performance and KM.

Verification of Security Properties of Cryptographic Protocols
abstract: Developing cryptographic protocols that are free from vulnerabilities is very challenging, as evidenced by numerous design flaws and implementation bugs in widely used protocols. Recent work has leveraged model checking to generate negative test cases, that is test cases that include the behavior of Dolev-Yao attacker. In this paper, we address the problem of analyzing execution traces produced by testing protocol implementations with such negative test cases. We propose a method for detecting violations of security properties by model-checking execution traces. Our approach employs a model checker based on DLTL, a Linear Temporal Logic with freeze operators, and supports automation of the testing process through pre- and post-processing steps. These steps, respectively, bridge the gap between different levels of abstraction and synthesize the results produced by the model checker.We present experimental results as a proof of concept for the feasibility of the proposed method.

Ulnar styloid osteolysis following distal radius fracture without ulnar fracture: frequency and associated factors.
abstract: OBJECTIVES To determine the frequency and characteristics of ulnar styloid osteolysis after distal radius fracture without concomitant ulnar fracture. Secondary objectives were to assess associated risk factors and surgical outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS A retrospective observational, single-center, radiographic cohort of adult patients diagnosed with distal radius fracture between July 1, 2018, and June 30, 2020, was reviewed. Ulnar styloid osteolysis was documented using wrist radiographs at diagnosis and follow-up. Patients with ulnar fractures or erosive arthropathy were excluded. Time to detection, size, morphology, location, and evolution of ulnar styloid osteolysis were recorded. Associations with patient and fracture characteristics were evaluated using Cox models. RESULTS 143 patients (104 female, mean age 55.8 ± 17.6 years) were included. Ulnar styloid osteolysis was identified in 16.8% of patients (n = 24), with a median detection time of 56 days (range 24-386). Osteolysis was more likely in fractures with: comminution (83.3% vs. 59.7%, HR = 3.457 [1.145-9.845], p = 0.027), diastasis (33.3% vs. 10.1%, HR = 3.905 [1.646-9.266], p = 0.002), dorsal angulation (79.2% vs. 24.4%, HR 4.766 [1.619-14.035], p < 0.001), impaction (66.7% vs. 17.6%, HR = 5.823 [2.486-15.647], p < 0.001) and active smoking (35.5% vs. 16.5%, HR = 2.650 [1.054-6.665], p = 0.038). Osteolysis was more frequently observed in patients who underwent surgery (50.0% vs. 20.2%, HR 2.541 [1.119-5.770], p = 0.026). No significant association with age, sex, osteoporosis, scapholunate dissociation, step-off deformity, or intra-articular extension. CONCLUSION Ulnar styloid osteolysis was observed in approximately one in six patients with distal radius fractures in this cohort; this finding was associated with multiple markers of fracture severity. KEY POINTS Question How often does ulnar styloid osteolysis occur after a distal radius fracture without ulnar involvement, and what clinical factors are associated with its development? Findings Ulnar styloid osteolysis develops in up to 16.8% of patients with radial fractures not associated with ulnar fracture in our population. Clinical relevance Ulnar styloid osteolysis after radial fracture occurs more frequently in patients with greater fracture comminution, dorsal angulation, diastasis, and impaction, as well as smokers. It must be differentiated from inflammatory arthropathies to avoid unnecessary investigations.

High-frequency monitoring and model-assisted analysis of N2O emission pulses after cattle slurry application under contrasting soil management systems
abstract: Nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions from fertilised agricultural soils are often dominated by short-lived emission pulses, but their regulation under contrasting tillage systems remains uncertain. This study combined high-frequency automated chamber measurements, process-based estimates of mineral nitrogen availability and Random Forest analysis to investigate N2O emission dynamics after cattle slurry application under conventional tillage, minimum tillage and no-tillage. The experiment was conducted during a maize–barley sequence in northern Italy. Daily N2O fluxes, soil temperature, water-filled pore space, carbon dioxide fluxes and mineral nitrogen dynamics were analysed to identify the main controls of post-fertilisation emission pulses. Most crop-period N2O emissions occurred within the first 40 days after slurry application, accounting for 91–97% of total emissions during maize and 78–89% during barley. In absolute terms, cumulative N2O–N emissions averaged 4.68 ± 0.74 kg N ha-1 during maize and 2.04 ± 0.74 kg N ha-1 during barley. This difference was not explained by water-filled pore space alone, which was broadly comparable between crop periods, but by the interaction among soil temperature, slurry-derived ammonium and nitrate availability, microbial activity and tillage-related soil physical conditions. Random Forest models showed crop- and system-specific driver importance, with soil temperature dominant during barley and stronger roles of water-filled pore space and mineral nitrogen during maize. No-tillage reduced area-scaled emissions but caused a strong yield penalty during maize, whereas it showed a more favourable agro-environmental balance during barley. These findings highlight the need to evaluate slurry and tillage management through both emission intensity and crop productivity.

title: AI Sapience and Responsible Reasoning
abstract: Large language models are increasingly taken to be capable of semantic practices. Debate about what to make of this has largely been conducted as a dispute about understanding. I argue that these standard framings, whichever side one takes, leave out an essential component of discursive reasoning: responsibility. To assert something is to make oneself answerable for what is claimed, to stand ready to defend it, and to give up a previously-asserted claim that cannot be defended. What settles whether a system is a participant in discursive practice is therefore not merely whether it understands, nor merely how well it performs, but whether it can be held to what it has claimed. Drawing on Brandom’s inferentialism, I develop five criteria for responsible reasoning, each of which admits of degrees. What they track is not independence from a community, since no speaker’s discursive capacities are independent of the community that institutes the norms she is answerable to, but the degree to which an agent does its own deontic scorekeeping. The central thesis I defend is accordingly agent-neutral: an agent whose performances fail these criteria is not, to that extent, reasoning responsibly.

title: Sustainable crop production under future climates: national mapping of cover-crop rotations and soil organic carbon–N2O trade-offs
abstract: Sustainable crop production requires management that maintains yields while limiting nitrogen losses and greenhouse gas emissions. Yet national assessments rarely compare cover-crop rotations with prevailing systems across future climates while jointly evaluating productivity, nitrogen leaching, soil organic carbon (SOC), and nitrous oxide (N2O). This limits the identification of regional trade-offs and the design of locally appropriate rotations. To address this gap, we used DSSAT to compare diversified 4-year rotations with legume and non-legume cover crops against business-as-usual rotations across German agro-ecological zones under six climate models and RCP4.5 and RCP8.5. We evaluated grain-unit production, nitrogen use efficiency, nitrogen leaching, SOC change, and net greenhouse gas balance. Direct and indirect N2O emissions were estimated with a nitrogen input- and leaching-dependent IPCC Tier 2 approach; net soil CO2 exchange was inferred from simulated SOC change. Cover-crop rotations increased grain-unit production and nitrogen use efficiency and reduced nitrogen leaching across scenarios and zones. Legume cover crops produced the strongest productivity gains, with cereal yield increases of approximately 16–33% depending on zone and scenario, while nitrogen leaching declined by approximately 40%. SOC increased, but gains slowed over time. N2O responses depended on zone, climate, and nitrogen management. Together, SOC change and N2O emissions yielded approximately 35–45% lower net field-level greenhouse gas balance than business-as-usual rotations by century’s end. The study’s novel contribution is a Germany-wide, baseline-relative assessment that jointly maps productivity, nitrogen losses, and SOC–N2O trade-offs for contrasting cover-crop rotations under future climates. These model-based comparisons of field-level fluxes are more robust in terms of relative differences and spatial patterns than in terms of absolute magnitudes.

title: Gamma knife thalamotomy for essential tremor: can machine learning predict tremor improvement on the day of treatment?
Stability and Pluripotency Status of Human Embryonic Stem Cell Lines Following Long-Term Cryopreservation.
abstract: BACKGROUND Human embryonic stem cell (hESC) lines preserved in biobanks represent valuable resources for developmental biology and regenerative medicine. However, the long-term effects of cryopreservation on genomic stability, differentiation capacity, and pluripotency state remain poorly characterized. The recent emergence of stem cell-based embryo models (SCBEMs) has further increased interest in identifying hESC lines exhibiting naïve pluripotency characteristics. METHODS Four SNUhES lines (SNUhES35, SNUhES42, SNUhES43, and SNUhES49) cryopreserved for 2,443-4,242 days were recovered and evaluated for chromosomal integrity by G-banding karyotyping, pluripotency marker expression (Oct4, SSEA-4, and Tra-1-61), and tri-lineage differentiation capacity through embryoid body formation. Directed cardiomyocyte differentiation was assessed by cardiac lineage marker expression and multi-electrode array (MEA) analysis. Quantitative RT-PCR was performed to characterize pluripotency states using naïve-associated markers (TFCP2L1, KLF2, KLF4, and PRDM14) and DNMT3L. RESULT All four hESC lines were successfully recovered following 6-13 years of cryopreservation and maintained normal karyotypes after thawing and expansion. Robust expression of pluripotency markers and preserved tri-lineage differentiation capacity were observed in all cell lines. Despite long-term storage under identical conditions, the lines exhibited distinct lineage-specific differentiation tendencies. Cardiomyocyte differentiation generated spontaneously beating clusters in all lines, with SNUhES43 showing the highest cardiac marker expression and electrophysiological activity as confirmed by MEA recordings. Pluripotency profiling revealed that SNUhES35 and SNUhES49 exhibited a naïve-like pluripotent state, whereas SNUhES42 and SNUhES43 displayed characteristics of primed pluripotency. CONCLUSION Human ESC lines cryopreserved for up to 13 years retain genomic stability, pluripotency, and the capacity for functional differentiation, including the generation of electrophysiologically active cardiomyocytes. Importantly, archived hESC collections contain biologically distinct cell lines with different pluripotency states and lineage-specific differentiation propensities. The identification of naïve-like SNUhES lines highlights the value of systematic re-evaluation of long-term cryopreserved hESC biobanks and supports their application in stem cell-based embryo models, blastoid generation, and studies of early human development.

title: Diverse Regulatory Cell Populations in Antibody Mediated Rejection
abstract: Antibody-mediated rejection (ABMR) is a leading cause of late graft loss, and current therapies act almost exclusively on the effector arm of the alloimmune response. This review examines three classes of regulatory cell from innate and adaptive lineages and the stages of the ABMR response at which each acts, in order to assess their potential as therapeutic targets. CD4⁺ Tregs constrain alloimmune priming through CTLA4 dependent costimulatory blockade, cytokine-mediated suppression, and competition for IL-2. CXCR5⁺CD8⁺ antibody-suppressor cells directly eliminate donor-reactive IgG⁺ B cells in murine models. T follicular regulatory (Tfr) cells restrain germinal center reactions and alloantibody generation, and their loss produces enhanced, more pathogenic donor-specific antibody (DSA). Notably, Tfr regulation is initiated early in T-B interactions, Tfr expansion physiologically lags that of Tfh cells, and Tfr numbers are reduced in chronic ABMR. Regulatory B cells and myeloid-derived suppressor cells remain comparatively unexplored in ABMR, and the latter carry a risk of profibrotic differentiation under chronic inflammatory conditions. Regulatory cell populations act predominantly during the early phases of the alloimmune response. Their therapeutic utility in ABMR is therefore likely to be constrained by timing, and to lie in the prevention of de novo DSA rather than the reversal of established rejection.

title: Presumption of guilt? AI chatbots and the role of affirmation vivas in assessing academic integrity
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the proliferation of conversational agents have brought transformative changes in education but pose challenges in ensuring the academic integrity of assessments. This article proposes ‘affirmation vivas’ as a potent response to reasonable doubts about the authorship of assessed student work. It draws on a case-study of the first affirmation viva conducted at the University of Glasgow, conducted after ChatGPT “confessed” to generating part of a student dissertation. During the viva, while acknowledging experimenting with AI chatbots, the student successfully demonstrated understanding and ownership of their work. The article reviews practical and ethical issues involved in responding to suspected AI misuse and develops a principled framework for affirmation vivas. We conceptualise these vivas as a means of affirming student understanding rather than detecting AI misuse or presuming misconduct. We derive five principles for their fair and proportionate implementation, including a high threshold for convening them, a presumption of innocence throughout the process and for marking to take place only after the viva, avoiding biases that derive from assuming a student’s guilt.

title: AI companions, human concerns: a pragmatic perspective
abstract: The rise of agentic AI and so-called AI companions introduces a shift in the modes of interactions between humans and machines. The exact contours of this shift remain unclear, but early signs of social, affective, and even romantic engagements demonstrate areas of potential benefit and potent harms to individuals and to the broader social fabric. A full appreciation of these benefits and harms demands a multi-perspectival account not only of technological innovation and emerging modalities of human-machine interaction, but also of the historical, socio-cultural, psychological, and ethical aspects of companionship. This essay provides such as account through a pragmatist perspective that considers the material, institutional, and psycho-social conditions behind the rise of AI. From this perspective, the essay broadens the notion of “alignment” as one between means and ends rather than the commonly accepted formulation between design goals and outputs. We argue that AI companionship blurs the boundaries between tools and social actors—a dynamic that emerges from the interplay of technical architectures, intentional design practices, user psychology, and political-economic forces. Given that interplay, a set of interrelated questions arise, which we address in three clusters (supply, demand, mediation), highlighting the emerging social and ethical dilemmas, and suggesting pragmatic interventions to inform public discourse and policymaking. In so doing, we hope to curtail the tremendous fallouts that have become evident in other domains such as social media only in retrospect, and to contribute to the creation of an environment conducive to social cohesion and individual wellbeing.

title: Early growth performance and structural stability of eight introduced Hevea brasiliensis (Willd. ex A.Juss.) Müll. Arg. clones in Tepi, Southwest Ethiopia
abstract: Rubber tree (Hevea brasiliensis (Willd. ex A.Juss.) Müll.Arg.) is a key industrial crop for expanding Ethiopia’s latex production. Early growth performance and structural stability of eight introduced clones (IRCA230, PB217, RRIC100, RRIC121, IRCA41, PB86, RRIC101, and RRIM623) were evaluated at the Tepi Agricultural Research Station. A randomized complete block design with three replicates was employed. The survival (%), height (m), and diameter (cm) were measured annually for five years (2019–2023). The slenderness coefficient was calculated as the annual ratio of the mean height (cm) to the mean diameter (cm) for each clone to assess structural stability. A bias-reduced (Firth) logistic regression analysis revealed significant effects of clone and year on survival probability over the study period (Likelihood ratio χ² = 177.89, df = 13, p < 0.001). Survival increased significantly after the establishment year (p < 0.001), averaged across clones and blocks, exceeding 97% from Year 2 (2020) onward and approaching complete stand stabilization by Year 5 (2023). Linear mixed-effects models (individual tree random intercepts) showed that clone and year strongly influenced height and diameter (all χ²s significant, p < 0.001). Significant Clone × Year interactions for both height and diameter indicate that growth trajectories over time differed among clones (height χ² = 426.22; diameter χ² = 1285.73; p < 0.001). By the end of the trial, the RRIM623 was the tallest (11.7 ± 0.7 m), and the RRIC121 had the largest diameter (11.5 ± 1.4 cm). The slenderness value decreased from 140 to approximately 100 after the third year. PB86 had the lowest average slenderness ratio (80), while RRIM623 retained a higher slenderness, suggesting potential structural instability. RRIC121 and RRIC100 combined high early growth and stability, indicating that they are prime candidates for large-scale H. brasiliensis cultivation in similar agroecology. Further studies on latex yield are recommended.

title: Simulating ionic liquid fragmentation in electrospray thrusters with foundation models
abstract: Predicting the products of ionic-liquid impacts on extractor surfaces is important for electrospray-thruster lifetime analysis, yet available atomistic methods require a compromise between chemical fidelity and computational cost. Reactive force fields enable high-throughput sampling but do not explicitly resolve electronic charge redistribution and may miss relevant reaction pathways during impact, whereas mixed quantum--classical density-functional-theory molecular dynamics (DFT/MD) can capture charge redistribution and neutral-product formation at substantially higher computational cost. Pretrained atomistic foundation models have recently emerged as a potential route toward DFT-like chemical fidelity at considerably lower cost. Here, we benchmark two pretrained machine-learning interatomic potentials, MACE-MP-0 (medium) and MACE-POLAR-1, against DFT/MD and ReaxFF for geometry optimization of 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate (EMI-BF$_4$) and for 10-100 eV impacts on a model Au extractor surface. The models reproduce several collision outcomes observed in DFT/MD, including ionic dissociation, high-energy covalent fragmentation, and, in particular, HF formation through neutralization-like chemistry that is not captured in the ReaxFF simulations. In the computational-performance benchmark, MACE-POLAR-1 and MACE-MP-0 (medium) completed each 2~ps trajectory in 5.12 and 2.54~min, respectively, corresponding to wall times approximately four orders of magnitude shorter than the DFT/MD reference under the reported benchmark conditions. These results support pretrained machine-learning potentials as a practical intermediate-cost approach for chemically resolved electrospray-impact simulations and motivate targeted fine-tuning with DFT data for broader applications in electrospray-thruster and electric-propulsion modeling.

S100A7 promotes orthodontic tooth movement by enhancing osteoclastogenesis via the receptor for advanced glycation end products.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Orthodontic tooth movement (OTM) requires coordinated remodeling of the periodontal ligament (PDL) and alveolar bone, but clinically relevant molecular regulators remain incompletely defined. We investigated damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) in human PDL and the mechanism by which a candidate DAMP regulates OTM. METHODS PDL from premolars exposed or not exposed to 7 days of orthodontic force underwent tandem mass tag-based proteomics. Candidate expression was validated by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction, and immunohistochemistry. Wild-type and mS100a7a15-knockout mouse OTM models, local mS100a7a15 administration, and primary murine osteoclast assays were used to assess function and mechanism. RESULTS S100A7 was upregulated in force-loaded human PDL and peaked at day 7; its murine homolog, mS100a7a15, showed a similar pattern and was enriched on the compression side. mS100a7a15 deficiency reduced osteoclastogenesis, alveolar bone resorption, and OTM. Recombinant mS100a7a15 enhanced receptor activator of nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) ligand-induced osteoclast differentiation, ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2 N (UBE2N) expression, tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 6 (TRAF6) ubiquitination, and NF-κB activation. Receptor for advanced glycation end products antagonism attenuated NF-κB activation and osteoclastogenesis, whereas Ube2n knockdown reduced TRAF6 ubiquitination and osteoclast differentiation. Local mS100a7a15 administration accelerated OTM without further reducing distal alveolar bone height in the 7-day model. CONCLUSIONS S100A7 promotes osteoclast-mediated OTM through the receptor for advanced glycation end products, UBE2N, TRAF6, and NF-κB axis. This pathway may provide a target for modulating orthodontic treatment rate, although long-term periodontal and root safety requires evaluation.

How to rewrite the stars: Mapping your orchard over time through constellations of fruits
abstract: Following crop growth through the vegetative cycle allows farmers to predict fruit setting and yield in early stages, but it is a laborious and non-scalable task if performed by a human who has to manually measure fruit sizes with a caliper or dendrometers. In recent years, computer vision has been used to automate several tasks in precision agriculture, such as detecting and counting fruits, and estimating their size. However, the fundamental problem of matching the exact same fruits from one video, collected on a given date, to the fruits visible in another video, collected on a later date, which is needed to track fruits'growth through time, remains to be solved. Few attempts were made, but they either assume that the camera always starts from the same known position and that there are sufficiently distinct features to match, or they used other sources of data like GPS. Here we propose a new paradigm to tackle this problem, based on constellations of 3D centroids, and introduce a descriptor for very sparse 3D point clouds that can be used to match fruits across videos. Matching constellations instead of individual fruits is key to deal with non-rigidity, occlusions and challenging imagery with few distinct visual features to track. The results show that the proposed method can be successfully used to match fruits across videos and through time, and also to build an orchard map and later use it to locate the camera pose in 6DoF, thus providing a method for autonomous navigation of robots in the orchard and for selective fruit picking, for example.

title: Harvesting sequence planning for strawberries in clusters using Large Language and Vision–Language Models
Machine-readable operator manuals over the ISO 11783 network for offline, multilingual LLM assistance
abstract: If agricultural machinery is to support intelligent, offline assistance, then the system must access technical documentation dynamically. In this paper, the Semantic Synchronization of operator manuals over ISO 11783-based CAN buses is analyzed, defined as the process that brings the local knowledge base of a tractor-side assistant into agreement with the operator manual of the connected implement. Data transfer performance was benchmarked using Markdown, JSON, and XML; various open-weight Large Language Models (LLMs) were also evaluated in cross-lingual query tasks. The automatic evaluation of the answers was validated against four human raters. A complete manual was transferred over a physical ISO 11783 network in 31 to 89 s, depending on format and transport settings, which is comparable to the object pool upload that operators already wait for at the first coupling of an implement. Markdown produced the smallest files, while the question-answering performance was comparable across the three formats for most models. With retrieval-augmented generation, locally run models answered most questions on the English manual correctly, with no advantage of the largest model over 7B and 8B models, but performed worse on the five other language editions. Keyword retrieval failed across languages, whereas semantic retrieval provided the cross-lingual capability. The exchange requires only a new parameter group that uses the existing request and transport mechanisms of ISO 11783, which makes it a candidate for standardization. The study is a proof of concept with inference on PC-grade hardware; deployment on embedded agricultural hardware remains future work.

title: Real-time edge intelligence for wheat disease management: integrating lightweight severity grading with LLM-driven cognitive reasoning
Autonomous apple fruitlet sizing and growth rate tracking using computer vision
abstract: In this paper, we present a computer vision-based approach to measure the sizes and growth rates of apple fruitlets. Measuring the growth rates of apple fruitlets is important because it allows apple growers to determine when to apply chemical thinners to their crops in order to optimize yield. The current practice of obtaining growth rates involves using calipers to record sizes of fruitlets across multiple days. Due to the number of fruitlets needed to be sized, this method is laborious, time-consuming, and prone to human error. With images collected by a hand-held stereo camera, our system, segments, clusters, and fits ellipses to fruitlets to measure their diameters. The growth rates are then calculated by temporally associating clustered fruitlets across days. We provide quantitative results on data collected in an apple orchard, and demonstrate that our system is able to predict abscise rates within 3.5% of the current method with a 6 times improvement in speed, while requiring significantly less manual effort. Moreover, we provide results on images captured by a robotic system in the field, and discuss the next steps required to make the process fully autonomous.

Surrogate Quality Score: A Novel Composite Performance Metric for Model Selection
abstract: The growing reliance on high-fidelity, state-of-the-art machine learning based models for engineering decision-making necessitates robust and systematic approaches for model selection. While high predictive accuracy at untrained points is a necessary trait in the final model, other attributes such as model complexity, forecastability, explainability, scalability, and physics-awareness may be equally important or relevant criteria depending on application context and user requirements. In this work, we propose a novel composite performance metric, Surrogate Quality Score (SQS) for model selection based on predictive accuracy and model complexity simultaneously. SQS heuristically integrates these two attributes through a weighted product of normalized measures, yielding a unified score to reflect overall model quality. A user-specified parameter in SQS enables explicit control over the accuracy-complexity trade-off, thereby incorporating human judgement and preference in the model selection process. We extensively discuss and justify the formulation of SQS and demonstrate its utility through an illustrative example. By combining predictive accuracy and model complexity, SQS offers a systematic and objective approach for model selection based on both attributes.

title: Seasonal variations and influencing factors of daytime mercury oxidation in the urban atmosphere.
abstract: Atmospheric mercury oxidation is crucial to global mercury cycling but remains poorly understood, particularly in the complex urban atmosphere. Here we identified the seasonal variations and influencing factors of daytime mercury oxidation in the urban atmosphere using one-year of dual-channel observations, machine learning and chemical box modelling. We found that the daytime increase in GOM/TGM ratio was most pronounced in summer (11.5 ± 5.5%) and weakest in winter (6.8 ± 3.8%). This seasonal variation in mercury oxidation intensity is regulated by distinct factors: oxidation-related species in summer, meteorological conditions in spring and autumn, and particle-related processes in winter. By analyzing the seasonal influence of oxidation-related species, we find that ozone primarily enhances mercury oxidation by promoting the formation of oxidizing radicals, and this promoting effect exhibits clear seasonal variability, leading to the strongest effect in summer and the weakest in winter. In contrast, based on box model results in differentiated scenarios, the NO2 inhibits mercury oxidation mainly by reducing the availability of oxidizing radicals, and this inhibitory effect shows little seasonal variation. Incorporating the roles of O3 and NO2 on mercury oxidation through their seasonally varying regulation of radical availability can provide a more comprehensive understanding of atmospheric mercury oxidation and its cycling patterns.

title: Acoustic Correlates of Endoscopically Identified Vocal Fold Lesions in a Large Clinical Cohort: Perceptual Associations and Screening Performance.
abstract: Benign vocal fold lesions are among the most common causes of dysphonia, yet large cohort studies integrating endoscopic, perceptual, and acoustic domains remain scarce. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and distribution of vocal fold lesions in a large clinical cohort and to determine acoustic characteristics linked to endoscopically detected vocal fold lesions and able to differentiate them from structurally normal vocal folds, corroborated by perceptual severity ratings. METHODS In this cross-sectional cohort study, 782 patients with dysphonia underwent videolaryngostroboscopy, standardized acoustic recording, and auditory-perceptual evaluation using the Consensus Auditory-Perceptual Evaluation of Voice (CAPE-V) and GRBAS scales. Acoustic parameters (jitter, shimmer, harmonics-to-noise ratio [HNR], and smoothed cepstral peak prominence [CPPS]) were compared across lesion categories and entered into multivariable logistic regression models. RESULTS Vocal fold polyps were the most prevalent lesion (32.1%), followed by nodules (24.0%), Reinke's edema (16.0%), cysts (13.9%), and granuloma (7.9%). All acoustic parameters differed significantly across categories (P < .001), with polyps showing the greatest deviation from normal values. CPPS was the strongest independent predictor of lesion presence (adjusted OR 1.62 per 1-dB decrease, P < .001) and correlated most strongly with CAPE-V overall severity (r = -.71, P < .001). The combined acoustic model discriminated lesion from non-lesion voices with excellent accuracy (AUC = 0.91). CONCLUSIONS Acoustic changes, such as decreased CPPS and HNR and increased jitter and shimmer, were related to vocal fold lesions identified by endoscopy. CPPS had the greatest separation between patients with a lesion, identified endoscopically, and structurally normal patients. These acoustic measures should be viewed as a screening/triage marker of vocal fold abnormality and not as a marker of benignity or lesion-specific etiology, however, because the study excluded malignant, neurological, and other major voice pathologies. Acoustic assessment is thus a useful non-invasive complement to laryngeal endoscopic assessment, but should not replace it.
journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation

Survival benefit of prophylactic central neck dissection in T3b differentiated thyroid carcinoma.
abstract: OBJECTIVE To assess whether prophylactic central neck dissection (pCND) is associated with disease-specific survival (DSS) in clinically node-negative patients with T3b differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC). DESIGN A population-based retrospective study. METHODS We analyzed 3274 clinically node-negative T3b DTC patients from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database (2004-2022) who underwent surgery with pCND (n = 1511) or without pCND (n = 1763). Random Survival Forest (RSF) models with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantified variable importance and effects. Dependence and partial dependence plots derived from the RSF model were used to reveal the relationships between the variables and predicted survival probability. Traditional Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing risk models provided complementary validation. RESULTS Central neck dissection emerged as the third most important prognostic factor (17% relative importance), followed by age (30%) and tumor size (27%). In partial dependence analysis, the adjusted 10-year DSS was 1.2 percentage points higher with pCND (98.4% versus 97.2%, p < 0.001). Patients without pCND had a higher hazard of disease-specific mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.82, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.28-2.59, p < 0.001), and the absolute difference in DSS increased from 0.5% at 5 years to 1.3% at 10 years and 2.4% at 15 years. CONCLUSIONS pCND was independently associated with better DSS in clinically node-negative T3b DTC, most of which was papillary thyroid carcinoma. Because node negativity was confirmed pathologically only in the pCND group, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation before they inform guideline recommendations.

title: How to develop organizational resilience using digital technologies

An AI-Driven System for Travel Vaccination Guidance using Agentic Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG).
abstract: BACKGROUND Travel vaccination information is distributed across national health authorities. We developed a system combining conversational and structured access to destination-specific information. METHODS A multi-agent chatbot and dashboard integrated information from Viaggiare Sicuri, TravelHealthPro, and CDC Travelers' Health. One physician formulated and scored ten Italian-language queries, evaluating the complete user-visible interaction. Dashboard extraction was assessed across twenty countries, ten purposively selected and ten randomly selected, against a reference combining entries from the same sources. Information-retrieval times were compared within countries for one clinician using paired analyses. RESULTS Mean chatbot scores were 4.9/5 for accuracy and completeness and 4.8/5 for clarity. The dashboard identified 286 of 295 harmonized reference entries, with 97.40% mean country-level recall, 96.95% pooled recall, 100% precision, and 98.56% mean country-level F1-score. Mean retrieval times were 80.9 seconds for manual consultation and 19.7 seconds for the dashboard. The mean paired saving was 61.3 seconds (95% CI: 54.1-68.4; p < 0.001), corresponding to a relative reduction of 75.7% (95% CI: 73.0-78.3%). CONCLUSIONS The findings support technical feasibility and preliminary extraction performance. Independent assessment of delivered answers and validation in clinical workflows are needed to establish clinical utility.

title: AAV-mediated expression of a SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibody in monocyte-derived dendritic cells and human airway epithelial cells.
abstract: Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) offer potential for treating pulmonary infections but typically require high-dose intravenous delivery due to poor diffusion from the bloodstream to the respiratory epithelium. Here we evaluated adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors to enable full mAb expression in human respiratory cell subsets. In A549 human lung carcinoma cells, which model alveolar type II (ATII) pneumocytes, the engineered AAV6.2FF vector demonstrated superior transduction efficiency compared to the parental AAV6. A single AAV6.2FF vector encoding both the immunoglobulin heavy and light chains linked by a P2A self-cleaving peptide (HC-P2A-LC) produced higher IgG1 levels than co-transduction with separate heavy and light chain vectors (HC + LC). In human monocyte-derived dendritic cells (moDCs), AAV6.2FF-HC-P2A-LC driven by the SFFV promoter induced sustained expression of a SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing IgG1. Efficient transduction and high-level mAb expression were also observed in primary human ATII organoids and lung fibroblasts. In contrast, air-liquid interface (ALI) cultures of differentiated airway epithelial cells showed lower, but stable, IgG1 expression that reduced SARS-CoV-2 propagation. These findings qualify AAV6.2FF as a promising platform for localized mAb expression in the human respiratory tract.
journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy

title: NeuroD1-induced fate conversion partially restores GABAergic neuronal identity in Huntington's disease.
abstract: NeuroD1 is a master transcription factor governing neuronal differentiation and subtype specification, yet its potential to restore striatal identity in Huntington's disease (HD) remains unresolved. In HD, striosomal D2 striatal projection neurons (SPNs) represent the earliest and most selectively vulnerable population, leading to early collapse of striatal compartmental organization. Here, we show that astrocyte-targeted expression of NeuroD1, via AAV9-mediated delivery of NeuroD1 under the GFAP promoter in a transgenic murine model of HD, reinstates hallmarks of inhibitory neuronal maturation, synaptic proteins, and chloride homeostasis in the striatum. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing further revealed selective recovery of striosomal D2 transcriptional programs and compartment-specific molecular signatures. NeuroD1 treatment promoted the partial reorganization of striosome-matrix compartmental distinctions, including the restoration of MOR1-defined striosomal domains. These cellular and circuit-level restorations were accompanied by significant amelioration of functional deficits in motor coordination and clasping behaviors. Together, these findings establish astroglial NeuroD1-mediated identity reinforcement as a potential strategy to counter subtype- and compartment-specific circuit disintegration in HD.
journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy

title: QUESNAY AND TURGOT ON THE CONDITIONS OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
abstract: This essay examines the physiocrats’ vision of economic development in eighteenth-century France, emphasizing their belief in agriculture as the foundation of prosperity. Quesnay and Turgot advocated trade liberalization and legal despotism to raise agricultural productivity and stabilize the economy. However, entrenched social structures and elite consumption diverted wealth from rural investment, undermining these goals. The physiocrats’ reliance on price incentives ignored competitive pressures that drive reinvestment in modern economies. Quesnay’s idealization of China as a model of state-enforced natural order revealed both his recognition of these limits and the theoretical contradictions within physiocratic thought on growth and governance.
journal: Journal of the History of Economic Thought

title: Organically raised meat chicken performance and carcass traits in an integrated crop-livestock system (ICLS) are not affected by cover crop management
abstract: Pasture-raised poultry integrated into cover crop systems offers a promising avenue for small-scale organic producers. However, how cover crop management affects broiler performance and product quality in chicken-based integrated crop-livestock systems (ICLS) remains poorly characterized. A two-year experiment was conducted on certified organic land at the Purdue University Meigs Horticulture Research Farm (Lafayette, Indiana, USA) to evaluate how cover crop management affects growth performance, feed efficiency, carcass characteristics, and meat color of slow-growing broilers in an organic ICLS. Treatments were chicken integration with access to high forage (ICLS-HF) or low forage (ICLS-LF), arranged in a randomized complete block design with four blocks. Cover crops were an oat/pea/turnip mixture in 2024 and a cereal rye/pea mixture in 2025. Freedom Ranger broilers were used in 2024 and Red Sasso broilers in 2025, with approximately 46–50 birds per treatment integrated for 42–46 days per season. Data were analyzed with linear mixed-effects models, with treatment, year, and their interactions as fixed effects and block within year as a random effect. Cover crop mowing reduced forage availability (P 0.05). Production year was the dominant source of variation: Freedom Rangers in 2024 achieved higher live weights (2.78 vs. 2.04 kg, P 0.05), suggesting that outdoor rearing supports leg muscle development independent of forage management. These findings indicate that cover crops can serve as a viable pasture component in organic chicken-based ICLS without compromising animal performance.

title: Physics‐Informed Neural Networks as Differentiable Surrogates for 4D‐Variational Data Assimilation
abstract: Biogeochemical forecasting requires state estimation methods that accommodate sparse observations, nonlinear dynamics, and discontinuous ecological processes. Four‐dimensional variational data assimilation addresses this challenge but depends on tangent‐linear and adjoint models that are costly to derive and maintain alongside evolving forward codes, and that are not defined where biogeochemical formulations are non‐differentiable. We propose a framework in which a physics‐informed neural network (PINN) replaces the traditional numerical model and its linearizations, remaining differentiable through automatic differentiation while embedding simplified governing equations as structural guardrails and computing the forward, tangent‐linear, and adjoint operators simultaneously from a single computational graph. Applied to nitrate‐phytoplankton‐zooplankton dynamics as a controlled testbed, our approach achieves an approximately six‐fold speedup over traditional numerical models in twin experiments while maintaining comparable state estimation accuracy across observation sampling scenarios. Jacobian analysis shows that the learned sensitivities are consistent with the embedded ecological relationships where these agree with the data, while departing where simplified formulations prove inadequate. This framework demonstrates that PINN‐based surrogates can maintain dynamical consistency in variational data assimilation while reducing implementation burden, offering a path toward more flexible and maintainable forecasting systems for increasingly complex biogeochemical models.
