title: Everyday Instagram behavior maps distinct facets of loneliness in young adults
abstract: Loneliness is a major health risk and is often hard to detect. It is multidimensional and can involve social, emotional, and structural facets with different causes and behavioral consequences. An open question is whether these facets can be differentiated in everyday Instagram behavior. We analyzed consented Instagram data exports from 415 US college students and modeled five validated measures related to loneliness using activity patterns, language, and images. Multimodal traces distinguished subjective loneliness but were less informative for structural isolation. Model explanation analyses revealed dissociable signatures: social loneliness was linked to low interpersonal engagement (fewer likes and comments), whereas emotional loneliness was linked to negative affect (negative language and sad/angry facial expressions) and late-night activity. Together, these results provide a cross-measure behavioral “construct map” of loneliness, suggesting that multimodal digital traces can separate markers of dissatisfaction with social connections from markers of emotional isolation, moving beyond generic prediction toward construct-sensitive characterization. Because the sample was of college age, predominantly female, and largely Asian or White, an important next step is to test whether these signatures generalize to more diverse populations.

title: A thermosensitive bovine placenta decellularized extracellular matrix/Pluronic F127 composite hydrogel supports lineage specification and glia-associated development in hiPSC-derived human spinal cord organoids.
abstract: Human spinal cord organoids (hSCOs) provide valuable platforms for modeling spinal cord development, disease, and injury-related processes, but their maturation and cellular complexity remain strongly influenced by the culture matrix. Here, we developed a thermosensitive bovine placenta decellularized extracellular matrix/Pluronic F127 composite hydrogel (BP-dECM/PF127CH) as a cost-effective, ECM-rich three-dimensional matrix for the generation of hiPSC-derived hSCOs. The composite hydrogel exhibited a thermosensitive sol-gel transition at physiological temperature, an interconnected porous microarchitecture, and favorable cytocompatibility with hiPSCs, with levels of apoptosis, viability, and proliferation comparable to those observed with Matrigel. Under identical RA/SHH-based caudal-ventral induction conditions, BP-dECM/PF127CH-cultured hSCOs demonstrated significantly enhanced folding morphogenesis and, by Day 22, yielded 4.82-fold more NKX6.1+ ventral progenitors and 3.28-fold more PAX6+ cells comparable to Matrigel. This matrix-driven developmental reshaping resulted in 2.74-fold more HB9+ motor neurons, 2.19-fold more GFAP+ astrocytes, 1.29-fold more TMEM119+ microglia together with coordinated upregulation of VGLUT1 and GAD67 (1.55-fold each), indicating enhanced regional progenitor patterning, motor neuron differentiation, glial lineage diversification and balanced excitatory/inhibitory synaptic specification, while preserving global neuronal differentiation (Tuj1, MAP2) and myelination (MBP). With 99.62% DNA removal and retention of laminin and fibronectin, BP-dECM/PF127CH combines native ECM instructiveness with practical thermosensitive handling at 20-30-fold lower cost than Matrigel. This composite hydrogel establishes a versatile and scalable platform for engineering advanced organoid models with enhanced structural and cellular fidelity.

title: Modeling Unsafe Behaviors within Construction Crews: A Safety-Based Cognitive Perspective
abstract: Unsafe behaviors among workers are one of the root causes of accidents. Construction crews’ behavioral decision-making is closely correlated with factors such as safety cognition, interpersonal interactions, and environmental conditions. Building upon a comprehensive consideration of the multidimensional factors influencing individual safety cognition and behavioral decisions, this study aims to explore the safety cognitive process for behavioral decision-making and subject interaction within construction crews. An agent-based modeling (ABM) model was developed for the experimental simulation. The model quantitatively assessed the impacts of individual psychological characteristics, supervisors’ management measures, and work situational factors on the emergence and evolution of unsafe behaviors. The results reveal that (1) enhancing workers’ self-efficacy and supervisor identification can benefit safety management within the crew; (2) supervisors’ intensified safety coaching and safety control can reduce the occurrence of unsafe behaviors; and (3) implementing strategies to reduce safety behavior cost for workers can effectively improve safety performance. Unsafe behaviors are more likely to proliferate in low-risk environments, while managers in high-risk environments need to take strong measures to reduce workers’ safety behavior cost and prevent the occurrence of large-scale unsafe behaviors. The research provides a mechanistic explanation for safety decision-making, quantifies the nonlinear effects of psychological characteristics, supervisory interventions and situational factors, and proposes a differentiated safety management strategy based on computational experiments. This study expands the application of safety cognition models and ABM methods in enhancing safety performance.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: Influence of Soil Particle Size, Shape, and Mineralogy on Microbially Induced Calcite Precipitation
abstract: Microbially induced calcite precipitation (MICP) has gained increasing attention as a potential sustainable ground improvement technique. This study investigates the influence of soil particle size, shape, and mineralogy on the MICP process and on the evolution of shear-wave velocity (Vs) in biocemented soil columns. MICP experimental soil column tests were conducted using three silica sands (Ottawa 20/30, F-75, and F-110), a naturally carbonate-rich silty sand (Blessington soil), and artificially graded carbonate–silica sand mixtures (75% silica sand and 25% Iceland spar). Vs and chemical measurements were performed during MICP experiments, and biocemented samples were preserved for scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analyses. Results showed that the amount of precipitated calcite in carbonate-rich Blessington soil columns was up to twice that observed in the silica sand columns, highlighting the strong influence of soil mineralogy on the MICP process. The Vs profiles showed an overall trend of decreasing Vs with an increase in median particle size tested, which indicated the dominant effect of the number of particle contacts on the evolution of Vs with cementation. Furthermore, carbonate–sand mixtures exhibited increased calcite precipitation, but reduced Vs compared to their pure silica sand counterpart columns, demonstrating the combined effects of soil mineralogy and particle shape on both calcite precipitation and stiffness development. SEM observations revealed a distinct change in the morphology of precipitated calcite on the surfaces of carbonate soil particles (Blessington and Iceland spar) forming closely packed, uniform calcite crystals resembling the growth of a preexisting carbonate phase, which suggested that carbonate soil particles offered a lower energy barrier that facilitated a more extensive calcite precipitation compared to silica sands. Furthermore, the nature of cementation bonds evolved from contact cementation to cementation matrix and ultimately to pore filling as the median particle size of the tested soils decreased, implying that the formation, morphology, and extent of cementation bonds are governed by the specific surface area of soil. Based on these insights, a new model is proposed that relates Vs to normalized calcite content, which effectively captures the variation of Vs with cementation across different soil types tested in the present study, as well as within a broader dataset compiled from the literature.
journal: Journal of Geotechnical and Geoenvironmental Engineering

title: Suitability of Suction Stress–Based Rainfall Intensity–Duration Paradigm for Predicting Tropical Storm–Induced Multiple Slope Failures
abstract: A case study analyzing three landslides in Pohang, South Korea, during tropical storm Typhoon Hinnamnor in September 2022 is conducted to assess the suitability of the recently developed suction stress–based rainfall intensity–duration (SS-ID) paradigm for predicting multiple slope instabilities. Postfailure field investigation and laboratory testing were carried out to determine field hydrologic and geotechnical settings and soil properties. This information was used to determine these slopes’ critical suction stress profiles where the effective stress reaches the failure state or the local factor of safety reaches unity. Hydromechanical numerical modeling was then conducted under various rainfall intensities to identify the slopes’ corresponding durations for slope failure and thus the rainfall intensity–duration (ID) threshold curves of the slopes. The precipitation records during and before Typhoon Hinnamnor at Pohang were used to determine rainfall episodes and slopes’ rainfall intensity–duration data. The determined rainfall intensity–duration data at the three sites for Typhoon Hinnamnor were all above the corresponding predetermined ID threshold curves, correctly and novelly predicting the occurrence of the observed landslides. Further independent physical simulations of transient two-dimensional hydromechanical processes at the three failed slopes were conducted for independent confirmation. Excellent matches in predictions of the slope failure locations and timings are demonstrated, further physically validating the suitability and effectiveness of the SS-ID paradigm for multiple slope instability prediction. Because the suction stress–based ID curves are characteristic of a given region and they can be determined a priori, the SS-ID paradigm provides a practical way to use live rainfall data to forecast multiple slope instability in a region.
journal: Journal of Geotechnical and Geoenvironmental Engineering

title: A Coupled Hydromechanical Model for Bed-Separation Water Inrush at Longfeng Coal Mine in China
abstract: Bed-separation water inrush refers to the sudden water inflow into mine workings from mining-induced roof bed-separation cavities when a hydraulic connection is created, and it is a common and hazardous water disaster in deep coal mines. Previous studies predicting water inrush were based mainly on pure mechanical or seepage models, and ignored the hydromechanical coupling processes. However, pore-pressure changes redistribute effective stress and reshape flow paths and the flow field. Therefore, these models fail to dynamically predict water inrush. In this study, a coupled hydromechanical model incorporating the Mohr–Coulomb model, Biot’s equation, and seepage equations was applied to simulate stress redistribution and water inflow for a karst aquifer in Longfeng Coal Mine in Guizhou Province, China. Compared with the classical mechanical model, the coupled hydromechanical model captures stronger tensile stress variation and sharper vertical displacement discontinuities. The tensile-unloading transition occurs earlier, and the separation belt becomes more continuous in the coupled hydromechanical model. When the working face advanced to 100 m, the stress curve from the coupled hydromechanical model reached about 14.3–14.8 MPa at 90–110 m, whereas it was lower and the peak value occurred later using the classical mechanical model. The predictive performance of the coupled model was validated quantitatively against field observations. The RMS error (RMSE) was 45.94 m 3 / h , the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) was 12.35%, the coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) was 0.916, and the index of agreement ( d ) was 0.979. When the working face advanced to 500 m, the predicted cumulative inflow reached 2,300 m 3 . This case study demonstrates the potential engineering usefulness of the coupled hydromechanical model and provides a scientific basis for risk evaluation and hazard prevention in complex geological conditions.

title: Operational Interface Governance, Digital Capability, and Resilience Support in Cross-Border Critical Infrastructure: A Capability-Pathway Perspective
abstract: Cross-border critical infrastructure operations depend on aligned information, authorization, and coordination interfaces across organizations and jurisdictions. This study examines operational interface governance scenario (OIGS) as an upstream condition associated with digital capability and its translation into resistance and recovery support. Resilience support denotes the focal operating organization’s perceived support role rather than overall system resilience. Drawing on the dynamic capabilities perspective, a between-subjects scenario-based survey of 371 practitioners was analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) and bias-corrected bootstrapping. Enhanced OIGS was positively associated with digital capability, which was positively associated with strategic sensing, timely decision-making, and change implementation capabilities. Direct paths from digital capability to both resilience-support dimensions were supported; timely decision-making had the strongest supported direct path to recovery support. Change implementation capability was not supported as a direct predictor of recovery support because its 95% bias-corrected bootstrap confidence interval included zero, whereas the OIGS–digital capability–change implementation capability–recovery support chain pathway was supported. The findings characterize cross-border infrastructure resilience support as a governance and capability process and support pairing interface governance with digital investment.

title: Maize genetic diversity is largely unstructured by human ethnolinguistic diversity in its center of origin.
abstract: Population structure and environmental features often capture major axes of genetic variation in many species. Yet the impacts of human activity often remain unquantified. For domesticated species that rely on human activity for survival and dispersal, human movements and cultural differences may play key roles patterning genetic diversity. Maize is a staple crop of enormous cultural importance to indigenous peoples of the Americas, but cannot survive or disperse without farmers. Using publicly available genotyping and passport data from approximately 2,000 traditional maize varieties, more than 500 whole genome sequences of humans from Mexico, and indigenous linguistic maps, we quantify anthropogenic effects on maize genetic diversity in the Americas. Maize shows very little overall structure, highlighting the effectiveness of indigenous farmers in moving and mixing maize populations. While principal components of maize diversity show meaningful correlations to human genetic diversity, our linear modeling suggests little additional impact of human population structure beyond shared geography. Though differences in maize diversity are often patterned by language locally, we find only weak genome-wide effects at larger spatial scales. Despite the relatively weak global signal of anthropogenic effects, linguistic Genome-wide association, outlier [Formula: see text] analyses, and selection scans identified loci associated with specific languages. Leveraging landscape-level sequencing data, we highlight how anthropogenic factors have shaped patterns of maize genetic diversity across Mesoamerica.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Evaluation of Soil-Water-Atmosphere-Plant (SWAP) model in vertisol under various tillage and nitrogen application rates using wheat as a test crop
Comparative cytotoxic and stress-associated effects of three triazine herbicides in PC12 cells.
abstract: BACKGROUND Atrazine, simazine, and cyanazine are structurally related triazine herbicides, but their cellular responses have not been compared extensively under the same experimental conditions. We compared cytotoxic and stress-associated responses to the three compounds in undifferentiated PC12 neuronal-like cells. METHODS Cells were exposed to atrazine, simazine, or cyanazine at 20 or 200 μM for 12, 24, or 48 h. Relative metabolic viability, DCFH-DA fluorescence, supernatant nitrite, apoptosis-related transcripts, and protein-associated signals were assessed. RESULTS All three herbicides reduced metabolic viability and increased DCFH-DA fluorescence and supernatant nitrite under the tested conditions. Cycs, Trp53, Bcl2, Casp9, and the corresponding protein-associated signals also changed after exposure, consistent with altered apoptosis-related signaling. Response magnitude and time course varied among compounds and exposure conditions. CONCLUSION Atrazine, simazine, and cyanazine produced cytotoxic and stress-associated responses in undifferentiated PC12 cells, accompanied by changes in apoptosis-related molecular markers. The study was not designed to establish a relative potency order, and direct cell-death assays are required to determine whether these molecular changes progress to apoptosis. Studies in differentiated or primary neuronal models will be needed to assess their neuronal relevance.
journal: Journal of environmental science and health. Part. B, Pesticides, food contaminants, and agricultural wastes

title: Forecasting Culex pipiens/restuans abundance in Ontario, Canada using surveillance and weather data.
abstract: Reliable short-term forecasting of vector abundance is critical for guiding localized mosquito control, yet week-ahead prediction at the Public Health Unit (PHU) scale remains challenging. We developed and evaluated a week-ahead forecasting framework for Culex pipiens/restuans abundance using 22 years of routine surveillance and meteorological data from 34 PHUs across Ontario, Canada. Based on a subset of predictors selected through feature-selection techniques, models integrating recent mosquito abundance and lagged weather variables were evaluated with multiple regression-based approaches, including linear, neural network, and random-forest regression, under random, temporal, and spatial validation schemes. Under cross-validation, top-performing models explained approximately 69% of the variance in weekly mosquito abundance. In independent testing on 2022 to 2023 data, the best-performing model achieved a 14.4% reduction in RMSE and an absolute increase in R2 of 0.124 relative to the persistence baseline. Across validation schemes, predictive performance was driven primarily by recent mosquito abundance history, whereas recent weather conditions provided additional gains, with contributions attenuating at longer lags. Increasing predictor complexity yielded diminishing returns for week-ahead forecasting. Consistent performance across validation schemes indicates model robustness. Overall, these results demonstrate a parsimonious approach for routine short-term forecasting at the PHU scale, with potential applications in surveillance, resource allocation, and targeted mosquito control.

title: TAS1R3 biases bone marrow stromal cell fate toward adipogenesis through PLCβ4-p38 signaling.
abstract: How mesenchymal lineage allocation is regulated by nutrients remains poorly understood. Here, we identify TAS1R3, which has been recognized as a component of taste receptors in the taste buds, as being expressed in bone marrow stromal cells (BMSCs) and as a regulator of BMSC fate. Genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of TAS1R3 impaired adipogenic differentiation in primary BMSCs, whereas TAS1R3 overexpression enhanced adipogenesis in a BMSC-derived cell line. Consistent results were observed in a human MSC model, in which TAS1R3 promoted adipogenic differentiation and suppressed osteogenic differentiation. Transcriptomic, pharmacological, and knockdown analyses showed that TAS1R3 promotes adipogenesis through phospholipase C beta 4 (PLCβ4)-dependent p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) activation. In contrast, under osteogenic conditions, TAS1R3 attenuated p38 phosphorylation, reduced alkaline phosphatase activity, and restrained osteogenic differentiation. Together, these findings identify TAS1R3 as a context-dependent regulator of p38 signaling and show that extraoral TAS1R3 signaling directs mesenchymal lineage allocation toward adipogenesis at the expense of osteogenesis.

title: A role for SUMO activating enzyme-2 in human cancer transformation models reveals regulation of self-renewal and induced differentiation.
abstract: Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are a rare subset of tumor cells that initiate and sustain tumor regrowth and are associated with chemotherapy resistance leading to patient relapse. The molecular processes that endow CSCs with these unique behavioral characteristics are not fully understood. Post-translational modifications (PTMs), such as Small Ubiquitin-like Modifier (SUMO)-ylation, have emerged as one of several shared mechanisms across cancer subtypes also implicated in human CSC biology. Here, we investigated the role of SUMOylation by studying the E1-activating enzyme subunit, SUMO activating enzyme-2 (SAE2), in human models of CSCs and leukemia. Using loss- and gain-of-function strategies, we demonstrate that SAE2 is required and sufficient to sustain CSC self-renewal while its loss promotes differentiation. SAE2 overexpression enhances SUMOylation and stabilizes the central CSC mediator, OCT4 in the transformed-human pluripotent stem cell (t-hPSC) model, potentially by maintaining SAE2/OCT4/β-catenin axis. Knockdown of SAE2 in non-CSC lines such as OCI-AML3 leukemia cells activates AKT/ERK-mediated differentiation signaling leading to suppressed cell proliferation and reduced leukemic engraftment upon xenotransplantation. Our results indicate SAE2 as an important regulator of CSC biology in vitro and in vivo, with dissimilar roles in non-transformed human stem cells. These detailed observations suggest that targeting SAE2 and SUMOylated proteins may offer an attractive line of investigation into CSC regulation and understanding human cancer.

title: Dose-Response Effects of Seed-Applied Fluopyram and Pydiflumetofen on Soybean Cyst Nematode and Yield: A Component Network Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Fluopyram and pydiflumetofen are increasingly used in multicomponent seed treatments for soybean cyst nematode (SCN) management, yet their dose-response effects on yield and SCN population dynamics under field conditions remain poorly characterized. A central obstacle is that field trials rarely evaluate identical formulations, so the contribution of any single active ingredient cannot be compared or combined across trials. This study applied component network meta-analysis (CNMA), which decomposes multicomponent treatments into the contributions of their shared active ingredients, across 21 Ohio field trials (2022-2025; 787 plots; 97 treatment entries). Within-trial treatment means were estimated using spatial mixed models with tensor-product P-splines and synthesized by mixed-effects meta-regression. Pydiflumetofen exhibited a positive dose-dependent yield response that increased with SCN egg density at planting (P = 0.025); whereas the corresponding response of fluopyram was smaller (P = 0.057). At the labeled 1× rate, predicted pydiflumetofen yield gains rose from 33.6 kg/ha at low SCN pressure (500 eggs/100 cm³) to 150.4 kg/ha at high pressure (10,000 eggs/100 cm³). Effects on final SCN population density were small and inconsistent: fluopyram produced dose-responsive reductions of 4.0%, 7.8%, and 12.7% at the 1×, 2×, and 3.33× rates (all P > 0.05), whereas pydiflumetofen effects were negligible (≤1.2%). Yield responses therefore increased with SCN pressure without corresponding reductions in final SCN density. To our knowledge, this is the first application of CNMA in plant pathology, offering a framework for evaluating dose-response effects in multicomponent crop protection products under field conditions.

title: Artificial intelligence in dialysis.
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in dialysis have matured beyond the initial phase of algorithm development. Recent work has shifted toward clinical implementation, evaluation, and governance. During the past year, the first randomized trial of AI-guided dosing in maintenance hemodialysis has been published, a meta-analysis of technology-guided dry-weight adjustment has appeared, and the first professional society framework for the responsible use of AI in kidney care has been released. RECENT FINDINGS The Anemia Control Model is now supported by hospitalization outcomes and cost-effectiveness analyses. A randomized trial demonstrated that AI-guided erythropoiesis-stimulating agent dosing achieved outcomes comparable to physician-directed dosing. Technology-guided dry-weight adjustment is supported by a meta-analysis of 21 randomized trials. Machine learning for vascular access is evolving toward preoperative clinical decision support, while peritoneal dialysis is beginning to receive greater attention from the machine learning community. Large language models are entering nephrology along two complementary paths: open generative systems for education and clinical support, and deterministic, protocol-driven frameworks designed for safety-critical bedside applications. At the same time, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has released comprehensive lifecycle guidance for AI-enabled medical devices. SUMMARY The major challenge for AI in dialysis is no longer developing accurate prediction models. Instead, success will depend on effective workflow integration, validation across diverse patient populations, ongoing postdeployment monitoring, and demonstrating meaningful improvements in patient outcomes.
journal: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

title: Diagnosis of personality disorders in youth.
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW Diagnosis of personality disorders (PDs) in children and adolescents remains clinically controversial, despite revisions in DSM-5-TR Alternative Model for Personality Disorders (AMPD) and ICD-11 removing formal age-limits for PD diagnosis. This review synthesizes recent 12-18-month evidence on conceptual debates, diagnostic frameworks, assessment instruments, cross-cultural considerations, diagnostic risks (over-diagnosis versus under-diagnosis), and clinical-ethical implications for personality pathology among young people. RECENT FINDINGS Dimensional severity-centred systems (AMPD Criterion-A/ICD-11 personality-functioning severity) have gained empirical ground for youth populations, yet categorical and dimensional approaches show partial nonoverlap in clinical adolescent cohorts. Validated brief self-report screening tools (LPFS-BF 2.0, BPFSC-11, LoPF-Q 12-18 screener) cannot replace semi-structured clinical interviews (STiP-5.1, CI-BPD). Youth PD presentations vary substantially across cultural contexts; identity-disturbance may be less prominent in nonwestern samples. Longitudinal data confirm substantial plasticity of personality-functioning in adolescence, while sub-threshold personality pathology predicts later psychosocial impairment. Ethical scholarship favours staged-care over stepped-care models, arguing that appropriate early diagnosis reduces rather than amplifies stigma. SUMMARY Contemporary youth-PD diagnosis requires hybrid categorical-dimensional, multiinformant assessment. Clinicians must differentiate normative adolescent developmental turmoil from enduring personality-related functional impairment. Gaps persist in youth-specific cut-offs for dimensional tools, cross-cultural measurement invariance, and longitudinal real-world clinical outcome research.

title: Bacterial protein function prediction via multimodal deep learning
abstract: Bacterial proteins are specialized with extensive functional diversity for survival in diverse and stressful environments. A significant portion of these proteins remains functionally uncharacterized, limiting our understanding of bacterial survival mechanisms. Hence, we develop Deep Expression STructure (DeepEST), a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts protein function in bacteria by assigning Gene Ontology (GO) terms. DeepEST comprises two modules: a multi-layer perceptron that uses gene expression and gene location, and a protein structure-based module that uses predicted structures and amino acid sequences. Within DeepEST, we integrate these modules through a learnable weighted linear combination and introduce a novel masked loss function to fine-tune the structure-based predictor for bacterial species. These choices are well suited for bacteria, in which functionally related genes frequently colocalize and are cotranscribed within operons, allowing transcription dynamics to serve as informative, condition-dependent signals. We show that DeepEST outperforms existing protein function prediction methods on a 25-species benchmark, relying solely on amino acid sequence or protein structure. Averaged over the 25 species, DeepEST reaches a protein-centric F max of 0.689 and a term-centric micro-AUPRC of 0.756, a relative improvement of 4.4% and 11.6% over the second-best method, the structure-based predictor DeepFRI. Moreover, DeepEST predicts GO terms for unclassified hypothetical proteins across 25 human bacterial pathogens, supporting their experimental characterization. DeepEST bridges organism-specific data integration and structure-based transfer learning, providing a method tailored for bacterial protein function prediction in settings with structural and multi-condition expression data.

title: Innovative but unreachable: sustainable revenue models for agri-tech in emerging markets
abstract: This case aims to facilitate discussion and learning around the following teaching objectives: to enable students to evaluate alternative business models for commercialising AI-based solutions; to help students apply stakeholder analysis to assess the feasibility and impact of implementing selected business models in AI-driven sustainability initiatives; to enable students to assess the financial viability and long-term sustainability of proposed revenue models for AI-enabled solutions; and to encourage students to develop strategic frameworks for monetising AI-enabled innovations. The case narrates the entrepreneurial journey of Nitin, an AI enthusiast striving to introduce a groundbreaking solution to a community (farmers) that needs help but has yet to recognize its value and contribution. As the founder of AiProff, Nitin has developed AI-driven technology to address the urgent issue of wildlife encroaching on farmland and damaging crops. His innovation, PashuTham, is an AI-powered system designed to detect and deter crop-raiding animals without causing any harm. This modern and novel approach to mitigating human-wildlife conflict safeguards crops from wildlife raids, ensuring better yields and sustaining agricultural productivity. Although PashuTham is technically sound and has received positive reviews during testing, AiProff struggles to market the product due to the target segment – farmers – lacking the financial means to afford the solution. This case highlights the critical challenges regarding the economic viability of technological innovations in the agricultural sector. This teaching note uses the i5 Playbook framework, particularly the methods to make learning more meaningful and designing for iteration, to enhance class engagement by creating interactive, reflective and student-centred learning experiences. This case is designed for Postgraduate-level course – MBA in Entrepreneurship. It is best positioned in modules exploring revenue model designs, where students must grapple with the tension of the commercial viability of innovations. It is equally suited for courses in Executive Education focused on emerging market challenges and marketing of AI innovations. CSS 3: Entrepreneurship.

title: When evaluating ideas exposes the evaluator: leader impostor thoughts and the obstruction of employee creativity
abstract: Leaders’ evaluation and development of employee ideas shape employee creativity. Yet how leaders respond to employee ideas when they perceive others to evaluate their professional competence more favorably than they evaluate it themselves, and how these responses are subsequently associated with employee creativity, remain largely underexplored. Grounded in self-presentation theory, this study examines how leader impostor thoughts are associated with different responses to employee ideas, identifies employee creative reputation as a boundary condition, and provides theoretical support and practical guidance for organizational idea management practices. The hypothesized model was tested across two complementary studies: a three-wave multisource field study with 176 matched supervisor-employee dyads, and a 2 × 2 between-subjects scenario experiment involving 248 managers. Consistent results were observed across both studies. Leader impostor thoughts were positively associated with leader idea rejection when employee creative reputation was low, but negatively associated with creative-idea developmental feedback when employee creative reputation was high. The field study further showed that both conditional pathways are linked to lower employee creativity, forming two distinct obstructive patterns: selection-based obstruction and development-based obstruction. From a self-presentational perspective, this study develops a bidirectional account of leader idea gatekeeping by bringing the evaluator’s own professional image into explanations of gatekeeping and explaining why leader impostor thoughts may be associated with differentiated rather than uniform responses to employee ideas. It also extends the creative reputation literature by identifying creative reputation as a social-evaluative cue that structures the meaning of leaders’ gatekeeping responses. Furthermore, by distinguishing the selection function of idea rejection from the developmental function of creative-idea developmental feedback, it offers implications for organizational idea management and leadership development.

title: Mapping innovative culture: a validated multidimensional scale for China's water engineering sector
abstract: This study develops and validates a multidimensional, theory-driven scale for assessing innovative culture in China's water engineering sector, differentiating motivational, capability-related, environmental and behavioral conditions surrounding innovative work. Drawing on the componential theory of creativity, self-determination theory and organizational support for innovation theory, a 20-item scale was developed and tested with 222 mid- and senior-level managers in Chinese water engineering organizations. Content validation and pilot testing were followed by exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and measurement-invariance testing across experience groups. The benefit dependency network (BDN) was used only as a conceptual framework for positioning the validated dimensions within broader benefit-realization logic; its relationships were not statistically tested. Results support four dimensions: intrinsic motivation, domain-relevant skills, work environment and creativity-relevant processes. The dimensions demonstrated satisfactory reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity and model fit, supporting a multidimensional rather than undifferentiated representation of innovative culture in the sampled organizations. The validated scale provides organizations with a diagnostic tool for evaluating innovation-related cultural attributes. It enables the identification of strengths and gaps in innovation capacity, guiding the design of targeted development programs, leadership practices and cultural transformation strategies. The study provides a theoretically integrated and psychometrically supported measure of innovative culture in the comparatively underexamined context of Chinese water engineering. It extends performance-management research beyond innovation outcomes toward differentiated cultural conditions and provides a foundation for future research linking these dimensions to performance outcomes. The BDN is retained as a conceptual, not empirically validated, benefit-realization lens.
journal: International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management

title: Evaluation of a Multi-Link Machine Learning Approach for Rainfall Detection Using Satellite Microwave Links
abstract: The impacts of climate change have increased the need for reliable real-time rainfall monitoring systems. This study investigates rainfall detection using a network of opportunistic sensors based on satellite microwave links (SMLs) combined with machine learning (ML) classifiers. Two models, a random forest (RF) and a convolutional neural network (CNN), were trained on aggregated SML data, including information from neighboring links. The results demonstrate that leveraging information from multiple links substantially enhances the detection of both wet and dry periods compared to single-link approaches. Moreover, the RF model consistently provides a more stable and reliable trade-off than CNN, improving rainfall detection and reducing misclassifications overall, with particularly strong performance during harsh weather conditions. The study spanned up to 32 rainy days between 2021 and 2024.

title: Ask to Land: Learning a Mask-Conditioned Open-Vocabulary Landing Policy via Differentiable Physics
abstract: Existing drone landing systems, whether model-based or learning-based, typically rely on predefined visual markers (e.g., ArUco tags) or are trained for specific platform categories, and often assume structured target motion. Recent open-vocabulary studies enable text-prompted target selection, but integrating this capability with learned closed-loop landing control remains underexplored. To this end, we present Ask to Land, a mask-conditioned framework that enables a quadrotor to land on various platforms described by a user in natural language, including randomly moving platforms. The core of our approach is the integration of a frozen state-of-the-art open-vocabulary perception frontend (YOLO-World with MobileSAM) and a control policy learned by differentiable physics. By providing real-time, task-agnostic semantic segmentation masks as policy inputs, our framework enables the drone to land on prompt-selected targets without target-specific fine-tuning while continuously tracking dynamic target motion during descent. The frozen frontend processes the prompt, while the policy receives the mask without text embeddings or category labels. To efficiently optimize the control policy, we leverage differentiable physics learning via Backpropagation-Through-Time (BPTT), and employ a carefully designed reward that enforces visual alignment with the landing target and altitude-adaptive descent speed, together with stable control. Real-world deployments validate that our approach achieves landings on diverse user-specified objects, including static and moving platforms.

title: Computational and machine learning models for optimising germination under cold stress conditions of common bean with titania ( TiO 2 ) nanoparticles
abstract: Common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris ) is an important edible legume that is sensitive to cold stress, especially at the germination and the seedling stage, leading to low germination and seedling vigour. Application of external stimulants can help to alleviate cold stress in plants at early stages. Titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) is one of the nanoparticles that can be used for this purpose. In this study, different concentrations of TiO 2 (0, 50, and 100 mg/L) were added to the Murashige and Skoog medium. Surface‐sterilised seeds were cultured on the TiO 2 ‐enriched medium and transferred to 0 and 4°C for 120 and 240 h, then transferred to the growth room, automated at 24°C. The germination data were recorded daily and analysed using the GerminaR package in R. Seven different germination variables named germination percentage (GRP), mean germination time (MGT), mean germination rate (MGR), germination speed, uncertainty (UNC), synchronisation (SYN), coefficient of variation in germination time, seedling vigour, and coefficient of velocity of germination (CVG) were analysed by Taguchi design (TD) and response surface regression analysis (RSRA). Results of the TD revealed temperature, time, and TiO 2 as the most important factors based on the largest signal‐to‐noise ratio. RSRA revealed the impact of TiO 2 , temperature, and TiO 2 × time on GRP. TiO 2 × time was found to be important for MGT and CVG. The UNC factor was also regulated by temp., time, and temp. × times. The multi‐output Random Forest model produced a mean cross‐validated R 2 of 0.718 across the germination metrics, with the highest values recorded for MGT ( R 2 = 0.872) and MGR ( R 2 = 0.755), while comparatively low R 2 scores were recorded for SYN and CVG. This study allows us to understand the germination pattern for common beans under cold stress conditions and can be used for testing other crops.

title: Microbial Life‐History Strategies Shape Biocrusts Soil Multifunctionality Responses to Multi‐Year Snow‐Cover Change
abstract: Winter snowfall is a critical water source sustaining the survival and ecological functioning of biocrusts in desert ecosystems, yet how different biocrust types respond to altered snow‐depth conditions and maintain soil multifunctionality (SMF) through microbial community adjustments and life‐history strategies remains poorly understood. Based on a field snow‐manipulation experiment, we compared SMF responses in cyanobacterial and lichen crusts under snow removal, ambient snow, and double‐snow treatments across different treatment‐duration categories and further explored the underlying microbial regulatory mechanisms. Cyanobacterial and lichen crusts exhibited contrasting SMF responses to altered snow conditions. SMF significantly increased in cyanobacterial crusts in the short‐term treatment plots (1 year), whereas lichen crusts showed a significant decline only under short‐term snow removal. In the medium‐ and long‐term treatment plots (8 and 11 years), differences in SMF between altered‐snow and ambient‐snow conditions were reduced for both biocrust types. Lichen crusts mainly showed increases in bacterial and total microbial diversity under snow manipulation, whereas significant diversity responses in cyanobacterial crusts were primarily associated with fungi. Microbial life‐history strategies showed clear but biocrust‐type‐specific associations with SMF. Random forest and structural equation modeling (SEM) analyses indicated that SMF in cyanobacterial crusts was strongly constrained by the S strategy, while Y‐related metabolic pathways were positively associated with SMF; in contrast, SMF in lichen crusts was positively associated with the A strategy but negatively associated with the S strategy. Soil physicochemical properties also played an important role in regulating SMF, but their effects and interactions with microbial attributes differed between the two biocrust types. Overall, this study demonstrates that altered snow conditions regulate biocrust SMF through the coupling of soil environmental changes and microbial functional responses, with the underlying regulatory pathways strongly dependent on biocrust type.

title: Climate Warming Reduces Seed Mass in European Beech Through Altered Resource Dynamics and Drought
abstract: Seed mass is a key life‐history trait that influences dispersal, seedling establishment, and plant fitness, yet its long‐term response to climate change remains poorly understood. We used two long‐term datasets of European beech ( Fagus sylvatica ) from the United Kingdom (1989–2024) and the Netherlands (1976–2024) to test whether seed mass has changed over time and whether any decline can be attributed to changing climate or altered resource dynamics. Seed mass declined by 13% over the study period, with a non‐linear decrease starting in the mid‐2000s. Models of year‐to‐year variation showed that seeds were smaller in years with lower reconstructed stored resources and in years that early summer was dry. Temporal contribution analysis indicated that the long‐term decline in seed mass was driven primarily by declining resource availability, with increasing drought making an additional contribution. Climate warming affects seed size in beech by direct effects of drought on seed development, and indirectly by altering reproductive dynamics and shortening the intervals available for resource recovery between reproductive events. Because seed mass influences dispersal and survival of seeds and seedlings, declines in seed mass are likely to reduce regeneration potential. Our findings identify an indirect pathway by which climate change may weaken forest regeneration.

title: Clinical Services Provided by Pharmacists in Primary Health Care in Latin America: A Scoping Review.
abstract: OBJECTIVE To map and characterise evidence on pharmacist-provided clinical services in primary health care in Latin America, including service types, practice settings, study designs, team integration, populations, outcomes, and equity-related dimensions. METHODS This scoping review followed JBI methodological guidance and PRISMA-ScR. Bibliographic databases and grey literature sources were searched without language or publication date restrictions according to a prospectively registered protocol. Two reviewers independently screened records and charted data. Multiple classifications per study were permitted when applicable. Findings were synthesised descriptively and narratively. RESULTS We included 134 studies from six countries, 107 of which were conducted in Brazil. Among 140 study-design classifications, randomised controlled trials (n = 26), cross-sectional studies (n = 23), mixed-methods studies (n = 21), and qualitative studies (n = 20) predominated. Among 137 study-setting classifications, primary health care units (n = 80) and community pharmacies linked to primary care (n = 29) were most frequent. The 168 study-service entries most commonly represented pharmacotherapeutic follow-up (n = 54), health education (n = 35), medication review (n = 20), and clinically oriented dispensing (n = 19); seven could not be clearly classified. Service, process, or management indicators accounted for 87 of 182 study-outcome classifications. Among 136 team-integration entries, referral-based (n = 54) and isolated (n = 35) models predominated. Only 26 studies reported an equity-related variable. CONCLUSIONS Most of the mapped studies were conducted in Brazilian primary health care settings, with comparatively few studies from other Latin American countries. Future research should examine service integration, equity, economic outcomes, and sustainability across diverse health-system contexts in the region.

title: Trajectories of self-regulated learning patterns across medical students' transition to clerkships: A longitudinal Q-method study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Medical education transitions are dynamic developmental processes in which learners shift between different roles and environments. The transition to clinical clerkship is a period of heightened vulnerability. While self-regulated learning (SRL) supports learning in such complex contexts, it remains unclear how students mobilise its different processes during this transition and how individual patterns emerge and change in its early phase. This study aims to capture the heterogeneity and temporal dynamics of SRL patterns by exploring how individual agency interacts with the clinical environment. METHODS This study employed a longitudinal Q-methodology approach. The Q-set was developed based on interviews with senior medical students and expert consensus. Then, Q-sorting was conducted with 23 medical students at two time points: 1 week (T1) and 1 month (T2) after starting their clerkships. The Q-sorting data were analysed separately at each time point using factor analysis. Factor arrays and post-sorting interviews at both time points were integrated to identify SRL patterns. Participants' transitions between patterns across the two time points were tracked to map SRL trajectories. RESULTS The Q-set comprised 44 statements. A total of 45 Q-sortings were collected (23 at T1 and 22 at T2), leading to the identification of four SRL patterns at T1 (Goal Orientation, Environmental Sensitivity, Feedback Dependence, Structural Misalignment) and four at T2 (Role-model Orientation, Structural Conflict, Proactive Challenge-Seeking, Relational Sensitivity), respectively. By tracking participants' longitudinal transitions between patterns, a Sankey diagram was used to visualise the cohort-level flows, revealing six distinct trajectories of SRL development during the clerkship transition. CONCLUSION This study highlights the heterogeneity and temporal dynamics of SRL during the transition to clerkship, which are shaped by the continuous interaction among learners' demands, multiple stakeholders and clinical environment. Educators should prioritise students' differentiated needs and support clinical transitions through fostering a socially shared regulation of learning.

title: The CitRWP-CsWUS regulatory axis governs citrus plant regeneration in association with chromatin remodeling.
abstract: Plant regeneration underpins crop genetic improvement, yet its regulatory mechanism remains poorly characterized in woody fruit trees. The RWP-RK domain-containing (RKD) transcription factor CitRWP acts as a pleiotropic regulator of nucellar polyembryony and somatic embryogenesis (SE) in citrus, but its downstream molecular network remains elusive. We demonstrate that CsWUS, a core stem cell regulator, is a direct downstream target of CitRWP. CitRWP binds to the CsWUS promoter to activate its transcription. Additionally, CitRWP interacts with the SWItch/Sucrose Non-Fermentable (SWI/SNF) chromatin-remodeling ATPase SPLAYED (SYD), synergistically enhancing CsWUS activation, while chromatin accessibility at the CsWUS locus is enhanced upon CitRWP overexpression. We further uncover that CsWUS negatively regulates CitRWP expression via a feedback loop. CsWUS overexpression promotes SE in recalcitrant citrus callus, but causes abnormal meristem proliferation and impairs shoot organogenesis from epicotyl segments. CsWUS greatly enhanced in planta transformation efficiency in the model citrus. This study establishes the CitRWP-CsWUS regulatory axis as a central module that coordinates multiple developmental fate transitions in association with chromatin remodeling, providing novel insights into the mechanisms of cellular totipotency and plant regeneration.

title: Identification of a specialized lipid barrier for Drosophila metamorphosis
abstract: Many terrestrial insects transition from humid to dry environments at metamorphosis, yet how they avoid dehydration is unclear. In Drosophila melanogaster , we identify a lipid barrier to water loss in the pupa that is anatomically distinct from that of the adult. It comprises unisex hydrocarbons that are longer and less volatile than their sex-specific adult counterparts. These hyperlong hydrocarbons are produced by larval oenocytes and stored in the fat body for subsequent transport to the cuticle at pupariation. A fatty acid elongase, EloHL, is required for hyperlong hydrocarbon biosynthesis and for a functional barrier to dehydration during early metamorphosis. Hyperlong barrier hydrocarbons are widespread across the Drosophila genus and typically transition to shorter sex-specific versions during adult maturation. In the desert species D. mojavensis , however, adults retain hyperlong hydrocarbons. This study reveals how insect lipid barriers are tuned to environmental variations in aridity and temperature during development and evolution.

title: Brainstem enkephalinergic neural circuit underlying cold-induced pain relief in mice
abstract: Application of cold or cold-mimicking chemicals to injury has long been recognized as an effective means of pain relief. However, underlying neural mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identified a cold-responsive neuronal subset within the lateral parabrachial nucleus (lPBN), the thermosensory relay region in the hindbrain, that mediates cold-induced analgesia in mice. Activation of these neurons and their projection to ventrolateral periaqueductal gray (vlPAG) increased the nociceptive threshold, while ablation of these neurons attenuated analgesia induced by cold-mimicking chemicals. We further identified that these neurons express precursor gene of enkephalin ( Penk ), which is necessary for TRPM8 (transient receptor potential melastatin 8)–mediated pain relief. Mechanistically, cold-responsive lPBN neurons frequency-dependently released enkephalin peptide into vlPAG to activate the descending pain modulation circuitry via disinhibition. Activation of cold-responsive neurons reduced spinal cord responses to noxious stimuli, suggesting the involvement of a top-down pain modulation pathway. These findings propose a central mechanism underlying cold-induced pain relief, which could be a novel therapeutic target.

title: Pink noise in dyads’ semantic similarity trajectories predicts conversation enjoyment
abstract: Conversation is a core component of human social life. Many influential theories treat conversation as a linear system, i.e., the sum of its parts. However, linear accounts of semantic entrainment lose explanatory power at their upper limits: Discussing perfectly aligned opinions becomes boring. We propose an alternate account that considers the multiscale organization of semantic similarity over the course of a conversation, as indexed by pink noise. Here, we test whether pink noise can be found in interlocutors’ conavigated trajectories through semantic space. Not only is pink noise present, but its strength predicts positive conversation outcomes like enjoyment and connection, increases with practice, and is reflected in a large language model’s representation of conversation quality. These results demonstrate an important role for scale-free dynamics in characterizing successful conversation.

title: Mevalonate pathway regulates double-negative regulatory T cell stability in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease
abstract: Lipid metabolism dysfunction and immune imbalance are critical pathogenic drivers of metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Double-negative regulatory T cells (DNTreg) are important immune regulatory cells that maintain liver immune homeostasis. However, their survival and function are compromised in MASLD. Herein, we found that mevalonate pathway and its rate-limiting enzyme HMG-CoA reductase (HMGCR) were significantly down-regulated in DNTreg from both mice and patients with MASLD, correlating with impaired DNTreg viability and immunosuppressive function. Arachidonic acid is enriched in MASLD liver and inhibits DNTreg HMGCR expression. Geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP), a downstream product of HMGCR, mediates RAC1 geranylgeranylation, which facilitates its interaction with mitochondrial CLPX protease, thereby enhancing mitochondrial function and immunoregulatory activity of DNTreg. Adoptive transfer of Pggt1b +/− DNTreg into MASLD mice demonstrated significantly diminished therapeutic efficacy compared with wild-type DNTreg. In conclusion, mevalonate metabolism–mediated geranylgeranylation is essential for the suppressive activity and immune homeostasis of DNTreg in MASLD.

title: Temporal dynamics of antigen-specific T cell expansion in primary SARS-CoV-2 infection
abstract: Quantifying T cell response during primary infection in humans is crucial for understanding adaptive immunity. Leveraging a controlled human challenge to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, we characterized antigen-specific T cell responses within and across individuals. Notably, individual clones reached similar maximum frequencies despite differences in the timing of their peak expansion. Mathematical modeling within a coarse-grained framework suggested that variability in precursor frequency between different T cell clones could be one mechanism to explain this relationship. Single-cell profiling revealed distinct temporal programs for CD4 + and CD8 + T cells, with CD4 + cells expanding earlier but contracting to a lower frequency. Clones with similar receptors, likely recognizing the same antigen, expanded at similar times. Together, these findings highlight how clone-intrinsic properties such as precursor frequency and CD4/CD8 subset status shape T cell clonal kinetics. These insights provide a quantitative framework for understanding T cell response in humans, with implications for vaccine design.

title: Humid periods over western Sahara during the Middle Miocene Climate Transition and their implications on the carbon cycle
abstract: The Middle Miocene expansion of the Antarctic Ice Sheet coincides with major sedimentological changes in Malta. This interval also saw reorganisations in ocean circulation linked to closure of the Mesopotamian Seaway (MSR-events) and perturbations in the carbon cycle (CM events). The final CM event (CM-6), slightly lags the main glacial phase and remains difficult to interpret due to competing mechanisms and conflicting p CO 2 reconstructions. To explore links between cryosphere, circulation, hydroclimate, and the carbon cycle, we present new geochemical records from Malta. Our records show that cryospheric expansion was followed by large, precessionally paced variations in sea-surface salinity and a marked regional increase in biological productivity. The results indicate a shift toward stronger monsoonal influence, delivering enhanced freshwater and nutrient fluxes to the region. This enhanced local biological carbon pump may have acted as a positive feedback to a global CO 2 drawdown. However, any contribution to global CO 2 drawdown remains tentative and cannot be confirmed without contemporaneous high-resolution open-ocean records.

title: Revisiting the additionality and durability of carbon uptake in large-scale ocean iron fertilization
abstract: Climate stabilization pathways limiting global warming to 1.5° to 2°C require rapid emission reductions alongside additional carbon dioxide removal (CDR) of ∼2 to 3 PgC year −1 . Our simulations show that sustained century-scale ocean iron fertilization (OIF) in the southern sector of the Southern Ocean (SSO) provides a contribution of ∼30 PgC, equivalent to ∼0.3 PgC year −1 . This uptake nearly matches the additional carbon uptake from global fertilization. In other iron-limited regions, fertilization-induced uptake is largely offset (70 to 100%) by anomalous outgassing in nonfertilized regions. After terminating OIF following 30 years of fertilization, the ocean retains ∼50% of the additional carbon in the SSO, whereas retention is negligible elsewhere. These results identify the SSO as the most favorable region for durable carbon removal through large-scale OIF, particularly in terms of additionality and durability, although its carbon uptake is smaller than earlier estimates. OIF-induced CDR is constrained by local and remote nutrient depletion, carbon reentrainment, incomplete macronutrient drawdown, and reduced phytoplankton carbon-to-phosphorus ratios. Incomplete macronutrient drawdown reflects the uptake controls by light, top-down controls, and rates of macronutrient resupply. Further insight into OIF potential will be enabled by standardized multimodel comparisons and targeted analysis of nutrient drawdown controls.

title: A transcriptional and cellular exploration of obesity and type II diabetes in human adipose tissues
abstract: Obesity is tightly linked to metabolic disorders such as type II diabetes mellitus (T2D), although a subpopulation of individuals with obesity do not present with these morbidities. The biological factors conferring T2D vulnerability remain incompletely understood. We recruited 58 individuals with obesity with or without a clinical diagnosis of T2D (Ob + T2D and Ob). We profiled paired samples of omental and subcutaneous adipose by single-cell RNA sequencing ( n = 10), flow cytometry under basal and stimulated conditions ( n = 42), and histology ( n = 17). Flow cytometry and chemokine quantification were also performed in paired whole blood. We identified reprogramming of the omental stromal compartment, centered on mesothelial and endothelial cells, alongside contrasting innate T cell and macrophage phenotypes across depots. Mesothelial and IGFBP2 + cells exhibited a fibrotic, epithelial-mesenchymal transition–like phenotype, while omental endothelial cells exhibited a lipid-overload, inflammatory, antigen presentation profile in T2D. Omental and subcutaneous adipose innate T cells exhibited divergent inflammatory profiles between tissues. These findings reveal previously unidentified insights into the pathophysiology of T2D in adipose tissue and identify compensatory networks within the tissues that could be exploited by targeted therapeutics.

title: Comprehensive degron mapping in human transcription factors
abstract: Gene expression is regulated by the targeted degradation of transcription factors through the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Transcription factors destined for degradation are recognized by E3 ubiquitin-protein ligases through motifs termed degrons, embedded within the sequence. In this study, we systematically map degrons in all 1626 human transcription factors. We find thousands of both known and previously unidentified degrons and characterize their sequence properties. Active degrons placed within exposed and intrinsically disordered regions contribute to modulating the abundance of the transcription factors, while the most common somatic mutations that are linked to skin cutaneous melanoma lead to unfolding and exposure of a latent degron buried in the zinc finger structure. We present examples of compartment-specific degrons and demonstrate that variant effects in transcription factors correlate with degron potency. Last, we show that while >60% of all predicted transcriptional activation domains overlap with strong degrons, acidic residues within the remaining transactivating regions counter the degron potency, showing how degrons can shape the transcription factor sequence landscape.

title: Shape-memory scaffold targets inflammation and fibrosis to restore endometrium and fertility in intrauterine adhesions
abstract: Intrauterine adhesion (IUA) is a major cause of infertility, yet current treatments remain limited in preventing fibrosis and restoring functional endometrium. We report a bi-drug, bifunctional, biodegradable shape-memory regenerative (BiSMR) scaffold enabling minimally invasive implantation, sequential drug release, and barrier protection. Proteomic profiling of chemical, mechanical, and combined injury models revealed inflammatory activation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and impaired regenerative programs, providing a molecular rationale for combining epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) with 17β-estradiol (E 2 ). BiSMR couples an E 2 -loaded PLTG [poly( l -lactide)- co -trimethylene carbonate- co -glycolic acid] backbone with a PDA-EGCG@HAMA coating, enabling rapid EGCG release followed by sustained E 2 delivery. In vitro, BiSMR promoted cell proliferation, migration, angiogenesis, and M2 polarization while suppressing myofibroblast transition. In rat IUA models, BiSMR restored endometrial structure and vascularization, reduced fibrosis, and improved implantation and live birth rates. Proteomics revealed down-regulation of fibrosis- and inflammation-related effectors and restoration of protein biosynthesis and regenerative pathways. BiSMR offers a promising strategy for IUA therapy and fertility restoration.

title: Ultrafast Meissner-levitated microrotor
abstract: Levitated mechanical systems offer a powerful and flexible platform for the realization of ultralow-noise sensors and tests of fundamental physics. Here, we report the demonstration of a levitated microrotor, consisting of a magnetic microsphere levitated by the Meissner effect at 4.2 kelvin. The rotor reaches rotation frequencies above 2.3 megahertz (138 million revolutions per minute) while exhibiting an exceptionally low damping rate of 4.75 × 10 −7 hertz. Exploiting the linear dependence of friction on the gas density, we demonstrate high-accuracy absolute pressure sensing over a wide range at cryogenic temperature. Last, we detect the thermal torque noise at intermediate pressure by operating the rotor in synchronized mode, resulting in a first preliminary narrowband search for axion-like dark matter. More broadly, the combination of high rotational speed, low temperature, and low thermal torque noise establishes a previously unidentified regime for precision measurements, with direct implications for the detection of extremely weak forces and fields.

title: Electron competition in azobenzene programs infection-adaptive antibacterial therapy
abstract: Conventional stimulus-responsive antibacterial systems generally operate through binary trigger–activation mechanisms, making them poorly suited to evolving infection microenvironments and thereby contributing to persistent infection and resistance development. Here, we establish an azobenzene-based kinetic regulatory system in which oxygen gradients commonly present in infected tissues continuously program reaction kinetics through electron competition. Oxygen acts as a competing electron acceptor within the reductive reaction network, partitioning electron transfer between azo reduction and oxygen consumption. Substituent electronic structures further reshape reduction propensity, encoding distinct kinetic behaviors. These electronically programmed kinetics translated into adaptive nanoscale dissociation and drug-release profiles: Electron-rich azobenzenes rapidly disassembled under severe hypoxia, whereas electron-withdrawing structures sustained release under mild hypoxia, generating infection state–adaptive antibacterial outputs. Moreover, the same electronic features governing reduction kinetics also reduced the reactivity and toxicity of reductive metabolites. This work establishes electron competition as a strategy for converting environmental gradients into continuous kinetic outputs for adaptive antibacterial therapy.

title: Explainable AI identifies recombination and chromatin environment as key predictors of subgenome evolution in maize and Brassica
abstract: Polyploidy, or whole genome duplication, reshapes genomes through biased gene loss and regulatory rewiring, yet the drivers of biased fractionation among subgenomes remain unclear. Using maize and Brassica rapa as model allopolyploids, we compiled 60 genomic and epigenomic features in maize and 45 in B. rapa and constructed supervised machine learning models to classify genes by subgenome identity. In both species, eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) approaches identified recombination rate as the most influential and highly interconnected feature despite nonsignificant mean differences between subgenome groups. Chromosome location, transposon density, and chromatin-associated features, including the proximity of accessible chromatin regions to genes and active histone marks such as H3K9ac and H3K27ac, consistently ranked among the top contributors to subgenome classification. XAI-derived covariation and interaction networks further revealed recombination rate as the central node connecting significant features. Together, these results highlight recombination and chromatin environment as major predictors of subgenome divergence in polyploid genomes.

title: The (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide is a microbe-derived NAD + precursor that drives gut stem cell renewal
abstract: Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD) is a critical cellular coenzyme whose decline associates with various chronic and inflammatory diseases. Improved NAD restoration may reduce disease risks and extend healthy lifespan. We report here that certain commensal bacteria including specific probiotic species produce (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide (N-MNA), which is a structural isomer of methylnicotinamide, a nicotinamide degradative metabolite. Patients with gut dysbiosis and inflammation show reduced stool N-MNA. Stable isotope tracing revealed that N-MNA can be rapidly taken up and incorporated into NAD redox reactions by intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) and non-IECs of fruit fly, mouse, and human. Genetic and pharmacological analyses suggest that N-MNA is converted to NAD + via the Preiss-Handler pathway, independent of the salvage pathway. Cell-type-specific ablation or overexpression of SIRT1, an NAD-consuming enzyme, in Drosophila , along with intestinal stem cell (ISC) lineage tracing in mice revealed that systemic N-MNA supplementation promotes ISC regeneration and gut epithelial repair. Compared to known NAD precursors, N-MNA brings a methyl group into host cells, representing a class of microbe-derived NAD precursor that stimulates the tissue regenerative power.

title: Combating drug-resistant Aeromonas veronii : Multiomics revealed the antibacterial mechanism of resveratrol
abstract: Aeromonas , widely distributed in aquatic ecosystems, is a prevalent fish pathogen and can cause human infections via contaminated aquatic products, polluted water contact, or tainted food consumption. Escalating antibiotic resistance in Aeromonas strains highlights an urgent need for alternative natural antimicrobial agents. This study investigated resveratrol’s antibacterial mechanisms against Aeromonas veronii and evaluated its protective efficacy in hybrid sturgeon. Resveratrol exhibited strong activity [minimum inhibitory concentration: 128 microgram per milliliter (μg/ml), minimum bactericidal concentration: 256 μg/ml], disrupting cell wall/membrane integrity, inducing reactive oxygen species accumulation, inhibiting adenosine 5′-triphosphate synthesis, and down-regulating key metabolic pathways via transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. In the sturgeon infection model, resveratrol-nanoemulsion notably improved survival, reduced tissue bacterial loads, mitigated oxidative stress and inflammation, and restored intestinal barrier function. These findings confirm resveratrol as a promising antibiotic alternative against A. veronii , with nanoemulsion formulation enhancing its therapeutic efficacy.

title: A robust spin-coupled tetraradical via nonalternant design
abstract: Polyradicals in open-shell polycyclic hydrocarbons (PHs) offer access to multiple spin states and hold great promise for spintronics and quantum technologies. Here we report a nonalternant, air-stable tetraradical featuring two fused 7-5-7 rings and a strongly correlated singlet ground state. This molecule displays an exceptional tetraradical character ( y 0 = 1.00, y 1 = 0.89) and exhibits long ambient stability ( t 1/2 = 33 days). Comprehensive electronic structure and magnetic response analyses reveal that the spin topology is governed by both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions, with robust electron correlation ( J 1 = +321 K, J 2 = −44 K, and J 3 = −29 K). The unique nonalternant design suppresses hyperfine and vibrational decoherence, giving rise to long spin relaxation and coherence time. These findings demonstrate that embedding nonalternant motifs into PH polyradicals provides a powerful strategy to simultaneously promote molecular stability, spin-exchange coupling, and spin robustness—key features for materials in the rising field of quantum information science.

title: Prebiotic magnetite enables chirality-magnetic surface feedback
abstract: The emergence of biomolecular homochirality requires both an initial symmetry-breaking event and a mechanism to amplify and preserve a chiral imbalance. Magnetic minerals have been shown to function as chiral agents through the chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect and may have enabled homochirality on early Earth, yet the magnetic properties of magnetite formed under realistic prebiotic conditions remain unexplored. Here, we show that magnetite synthesized through two geochemically plausible pathways—UV-driven photo-oxidation and nitrite-mediated oxidation of Fe(II)—produces particles dominated by single-vortex and multivortex magnetic domain states. Magnetic measurements and electron microscopy confirm that these populations differ markedly from the nano-fabricated thin-film substrates conventionally used in previous CISS experiments. Using three-dimensional micromagnetic simulations, we demonstrate that single-domain and vortex-state grains undergo irreversible, exchange-driven remagnetization when interacting with spin-polarized homochiral compounds. This magnetic irreversibility provides a robust mechanism for storing and reinforcing weak chiral bias, suggesting that prebiotic magnetite could have contributed to the emergence and stabilization of persistent chiral bias on early Earth.

title: Spatial proteomics reveals lipid droplet reorganization in symbiotic Paramecium bursaria cells
abstract: Endosymbiosis is an important adaptive mechanism allowing organisms to exploit previously inaccessible niches. The flexible relationship between the ciliate Paramecium bursaria and green algae represents a model system for studying early endosymbiosis evolution. However, the mechanisms underlying how P. bursaria cells maintain this endosymbiotic relationship remain unclear. Here, we use mass spectrometry–based proteomics to generate a spatial proteomic atlas of the host P. bursaria cells with and without endosymbionts. This atlas defines the protein composition of the endosymbiont-containing compartment (perialgal vacuole) and reveals pronounced remodeling of host lipid droplets upon symbiosis. Imaging analyses confirm that lipid droplets change in size, morphology, and positioning, accumulating near intracellular algae. Perturbing symbiotic cells with chemical inhibitors of lipid metabolism reduces endosymbiotic algal numbers, revealing a role for lipid droplets in the host-endosymbiont interaction. Our data provide a comprehensive resource for protein localization in P. bursaria cells and elucidate how those cells remodel an existing cellular compartment to maintain endosymbiosis.

title: Spatial control of enzyme orientation at the lipid droplet interface enables regio- and chemoselective metabolic flux
abstract: Precise spatial control over multienzyme cascade reactions is increasingly recognized as a design lever in synthetic biology for enhancing catalytic performance and directing metabolic flux. By emulating principles of cellular compartmentalization, synthetic scaffolds and engineered interfaces have emerged as powerful platforms to modulate intermediate channeling and reaction efficiency in complex biocatalytic systems. However, robust and spatially defined immobilization of multienzyme assemblies within physicochemically optimal compartments remains challenging because of the dynamic intracellular environment. Here, we reprogram the amphiphilic interface of yeast lipid droplets (LDs) as a programmable scaffold system to support regio- and chemoselective localization of enzymes. Guided by molecular dynamics simulations, we designed LD-anchoring motifs to direct the enzyme orientation at the LD monolayer interface, yielding cytosol-facing or LD inner-facing configurations. Using this designed LD-anchoring motif, we spatially reorganize a trienzyme cascade for prodeoxyviolacein (PDV) biosynthesis across the cytosol-LD interface, facilitating directional conversion of hydrophilic substrates into hydrophobic products. This spatial reorganization substantially improved PDV production by 1300%, achieving 46.25 milligrams per liter. Our approach offers a modular and tunable platform for engineering spatially organized and readily deployable enzyme cascades, opening avenues for biosynthetic catalysis at organellar interfaces.

title: Visualizing nanoscopic acoustic mode competition in a van der Waals ferroelectric
abstract: Understanding how low-dimensional ferroelectrics respond to ultrafast excitation at nanoscales is essential for controlling energy flow and mechanical functionality in next-generation polar devices, yet the nanoscopic structural response to ultrafast depolarization remains unresolved, obscuring the microscopic pathways of acoustic decoherence and energy dissipation. Here, we spatiotemporally resolve lattice motion in the van der Waals ferroelectric NbOI 2 using combined ultrafast electron microscopy and diffraction, revealing three acoustic phonons: two transverse shear modes and one longitudinal breathing mode. The transverse mode that shears the layers perpendicular to the in-plane polar axis dominates over that along the polar axis, reflecting anisotropic polarization-strain coupling. Real-space mapping uncovers spatially correlated heterogeneity in mode amplitudes and lifetimes. Regions dominated by a single shear mode exhibit significantly longer acoustic lifetimes than multimode regions, suggesting acoustic phonon–phonon scattering as a major source of decoherence. Our results provide a microscopic understanding of ultrafast depolarization-driven acoustic dynamics and spatially heterogeneous energy dissipation in van der Waals ferroelectrics.

title: Scaling up chemical recycling: High-yield polyolefin pyrolysis to liquid hydrocarbons using iron single atom catalysts
abstract: The chemical recycling of polyolefins (PO) via pyrolysis offers a circular pathway for plastic waste management, yet industrial implementation remains hindered by high energy demands and poor product selectivity. Here, we report an Fe-catalyzed pyrolysis process that achieves 97% PO conversion and a 94% yield of C6 to C35 liquid hydrocarbons. By using a zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF)–derived, N-doped porous carbon-supported iron single-atom catalyst (Fe 1 @NC) in combination with a strategic temperature gradient control, we overcome traditional thermolysis limitations. The process was further demonstrated on a kilogram scale, supporting the practical scalability of this catalytic system. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the rate-determining step is an acid base–promoted dehydrogenation of the polymer backbone. Specifically, electronic synergy between the single iron centers and the carbon support stabilizes reactive carbocation intermediates, facilitating their rapid decomposition into high-value olefins and alkanes. These findings provide a scalable and highly efficient catalytic framework for the upcycling of plastic waste into liquid hydrocarbon fractions and chemical feedstocks.
