title: Adaptive dual-programming magnetic soft robot with lifelike behavior
abstract: Magnetic soft robots with embodied intelligence of multimodal motions, environmental perception, and functional decoupling depend on ingenious material arrangement and programmable morphing information introduction. While some efforts have been made, achieving lifelike behaviors for soft robots in system-level strategy remains a notable challenge. Here, we present dual-programming hydrogel-based soft robots (DHSRs) that couple magnetic and anisotropic programming through the spatial arrangement of patterned magnetic skeletons into responsive and structural hydrogel bodies. These DHSRs exhibit programmable exquisite and multicurved structures in three-dimensional (3D) space, environment-adaptive deformation behaviors proved by switching from random jumping on land to regular swimming in water of a fish-like soft robot, and further locomotion-function decoupling capabilities of region-selective cargo delivery in an integrated “locomotion-perception-action” workflow. Our strategy in biomedical potential is exemplified by a ring-like pH-responsive DHSR for gastric ulcer therapy, which integrates multimodal locomotion (rolling, tumbling, and rotating), adaptive matching, and microneedle-mediated penetration. By collaborating with a capsule endoscopy system, we explore the possibility of a wireless and painless diagnostic-therapeutic platform in a pig model. This strategy endows the robot with perception and multitask execution capabilities, highlighting a promising route for the intelligent evolution of soft robots across diverse application domains.

title: Age reshapes selection on melanoma driver mutations
abstract: Aging is a major risk factor for melanoma. However, it is unclear whether aging fuels tumor evolution by altering mutation rates, changing the microenvironmentally induced selection on drivers, or both. We analyzed 5472 melanomas, estimating how selection on individual variants changes with patient age while accounting for differing neutral mutation rates. Neutral mutation rates increased only modestly with age; ultraviolet damage remained predominant, but endogenous processes increasingly contributed to older tumors. In contrast, selection on major drivers was strongly age dependent: The advantage of BRAF V600E declined precipitously with age, whereas NRAS Q61 mutations gained advantage. TERT promoter mutations became more frequent, yet less advantageous. Aging therefore reshapes melanoma evolution primarily by altering selection, motivating age-conscious evaluation of clinical biomarkers and therapies.

title: Measuring mixed-state topological invariant in open photonic quantum walk
abstract: Pure-state manifestations of geometric phase are well established and have found applications across essentially all branches of physics, yet their generalization to mixed-state regimes remains largely unexplored experimentally. The Uhlmann geometric phase offers a natural extension of pure-state paradigms and can exhibit a topological character. However, observation of this invariant is impeded by the incompatibility between Uhlmann parallel transport and Hamiltonian dynamics, as well as the difficulty of preparing topologically nontrivial mixed states. To address this challenge, we report an experimentally accessible protocol for directly measuring the mixed-state topological invariant. By engineering controlled nonunitary dynamics in a photonic quantum walk, we prepare topologically nontrivial mixed states from a trivial initial state. Then, by machine learning the full density matrix in momentum space, we directly extract the quantized geometric phase of the nontrivial mixed states. Furthermore, we observe that this transition of the quantized mixed-state topological invariant from a trivial to a nontrivial value is closely associated with the emergence of a topological kink structure. These results highlight a geometric phase framework that naturally extends to open quantum systems both in and out of thermal equilibrium.

title: A full-hardware edge detection system based on a highly robust dual random number generator
abstract: Conventional edge computing hardware at autonomous driving terminals is limited by chip area and power efficiency for complex image data. Recently, researchers have used memristors to construct dedicated hardware systems, achieving advancements in multiple image processing fields such as pattern recognition and edge detection. However, a full-hardware image processing system with anti-interference, low power, and high real-time performance remains challenging. Here, we fabricated a volatile Ag/AlO x /n-Si memristor with exceptional stability and low power. High-resolution electron microscopy visualized Ag conductive filament formation. Integrating two memristors with a logic circuit, we designed a low-power edge detection unit using dual random number hardware computation. Its energy consumption is 92.3% lower than traditional logic circuits, with strong anti-interference. To validate practical use, we constructed a 32-channel parallel full-hardware system with 64 devices, achieving 31.25 frames per second and excellent edge detection. The system exhibits excellent scalability, stability, and anti-interference, offering great potential for edge vision hardware in autonomous driving, safety monitoring, and surgical assistance.

title: Photonic entanglement swapping with remote quantum dots
abstract: Entanglement swapping is a protocol that details how to create entanglement between previously uncorrelated particles. Its photonic version, mediated by the interference of photon pairs generated by separate quantum systems, finds disparate applications in quantum networks. So far, entanglement swapping with entangled photons from remote systems has been implemented only using probabilistic sources. However, the scaling up of quantum networks requires nonprobabilistic quantum emitters without a trade-off between the degree of entanglement and photon-pair generation rate. Here, we demonstrate photonic entanglement swapping using photon pairs generated by two separate GaAs quantum dots. The emitters are deterministically embedded in hybrid semiconductor-piezoelectric devices that make the entangled photons from two dissimilar quantum dots nearly identical. Entanglement swapping is demonstrated with a fidelity as high as 0.71(2), more than 10 SDs above the classical limit. The experimental data are quantitatively explained by a theoretical model that also suggests how to boost the protocol performance. Our work opens the path to the exploitation of quantum dot entangled-photon sources in quantum repeater networks.

title: Three-way circulation–soil moisture–temperature feedbacks amplify the most extreme mid-latitudinal heat waves
abstract: The most extreme heat waves are intensifying faster than moderate events across many mid-latitude regions. Climate models underestimate these trends, suggesting an incomplete representation and understanding of the underlying physical processes. Here, we use an explainable machine-learning framework to investigate interactions among atmospheric circulation, surface soil moisture, and temperature, and their role in recent heat extremes. We show that a three-way interaction among these components becomes active once a critical temperature threshold is exceeded, contributing, on average, ∼10% to peak temperature anomalies during the most extreme heat events across ∼28% of humid mid-latitude regions. We further reveal that this interaction is systematically underestimated in CMIP6 and CESM2 Large Ensemble simulations. Soils in climate models are too dry at the initiation of heat waves, therefore suppressing subsequent soil-moisture depletion and inhibiting feedback activation. These findings help explain regional model biases in upper-tail warming and highlight avenues for improving future projections of extreme heat events.

title: Quantum-interference metrology of dissipative Kerr solitons
abstract: Dissipative Kerr solitons in optical microresonators underpin chip-scale frequency combs with applications ranging from coherent telecommunications to precision spectroscopy. Yet the characterization of their intrinsic femtosecond temporal structure remains challenging, as the low pulse energy and broad spectral bandwidth necessitate optical amplification and careful dispersion compensation in conventional ultrafast diagnostics, both of which can substantial distort the waveform. Here, we demonstrate a quantum-interference metrology of microcomb solitons based on Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. By attenuating the soliton stream to the single-photon level and measuring fourth-order interference, we directly retrieve near transform-limited pulse durations without amplification or dispersion management, remaining accurate even after propagation through 25 kilometers of standard fiber. The same interferogram also provides direct access to the temporal separations in multisoliton states by converting intersoliton separations into additional interference dips at corresponding delays, enabling subpicosecond characterization of their intracavity temporal structure. This quantum-inspired paradigm introduces a metrological approach that is immune to amplification and dispersion distortions, offering a powerful tool for the characterization of complex soliton physics.

title: Structure of the Chimalliviridae bacteriophage Goslar reveals host recognition and infection machinery
abstract: Large-genome bacteriophages (phages) of the Chimalliviridae family have a distinctive life cycle, building compartments inside infected bacterial cells that broadly protect their genomes from host defenses. Here, we use cryo–electron microscopy to determine a structure of the Escherichia coli –infecting Chimalliviridae phage Goslar. We combine manual modeling of 25 structural proteins with AlphaFold structure predictions of an additional three proteins to generate a composite model with 2888 protein chains from 28 different structural proteins, totaling more than 1.4 million amino acid residues. Our structure reveals the architecture of the Goslar capsid, portal, tail, and baseplate, highlighting structural similarities and differences with other tailed phages. Combining our structural data with quantitative mass spectrometry of Goslar virions, we identify several high-copy virion-associated proteins that likely play key roles when injected into host cells upon infection. We also identify a Chimalliviridae -specific family of proteins that form long, flexible filaments anchored at the phage baseplate and which incorporate carbohydrate-binding domains, suggesting a key role in host recognition.

title: Reciprocal control of genome instability and RNA processing in cancer: Mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities
abstract: Genomic instability and dysregulated RNA processing are each recognized as core hallmarks of cancer, but accumulating evidence indicates that they are mechanistically intertwined rather than independent features. Chromosomal instability, mismatch-repair deficiency, and homologous recombination deficiency can reshape RNA splicing, 3′ end formation, and RNA surveillance through changes in gene dosage, DNA damage signaling, and alterations in regulatory elements. Conversely, aberrant splicing, polyadenylation, and RNA modifications can impair DNA repair, perturb mitotic control, and promote replication stress, thereby reinforcing genomic instability. This bidirectional circuit drives clinically relevant phenotypes, including therapeutic resistance, immune modulation, and emergent vulnerabilities that are not captured by DNA-centric biomarkers alone. Here, we present a unified framework for the genome instability–RNA processing axis and its direct clinical implications for cancer diagnosis, treatment stratification, and therapeutic exploitation, highlighting the most actionable mechanistic interfaces and discussing how integrated DNA-RNA biomarkers and rational combination strategies could extend precision oncology beyond static genomic lesions.

title: High-impulse and reactant-regenerative combustion-based micro actuators
abstract: The use of combustibles in micro-actuator technologies enables powerful impulsive actuation capabilities comparable to those of natural organisms. However, the exogenous dependence of fuel limits the development of combustion-based actuators. We present a closed-cycle reactant regeneration strategy wherein the bidirectional interconversion between hydrogen and water achieves real-time fuel replenishment for reactant-regenerative electrolysis and combustion reactions. Based on this, we develop a 1.5-centimeter actuator that generates forces above 20 newtons and operates continuously for >7200 cycles without refueling (a two orders-of-magnitude improvement over existing combustion-based actuators). Experiments confirm its strength and cross-environment versatility for removing obstacles, jetting, and striking via underwater cavitation. These features enable the actuator to be integrated into small robotic platforms, allowing them to reconfigure local surroundings in an active manner.

title: Dual-acting compounds that deliver an acidifying domain via zanamivir to the virus surface are potent influenza inhibitors
abstract: While contemporary antiviral development primarily strives to produce “lock and key” inhibitors, we present here a different approach to drug design that uses compounds devised to alter the microenvironment of the virion surface, making it incompatible with virus entry. We illustrate this strategy with inhibitors of influenza virus and show that compounds designed to produce a proton-rich mantle above the virion surface affect the ability of the viral hemagglutinin to interact with cellular receptors and gain entry to the cell. The compounds show exceptional antiviral activity both in vitro and in vivo and protect against influenza illness in ferrets and in mice after a single dose, either therapeutically or prophylactically.

title: Strigolactone receptor D14 integrates phosphate and strigolactone signaling by interacting with and stabilizing PHR1
abstract: Strigolactone (SL) and low phosphate (LP) signaling coordinately regulate shoot and root architecture and plant adaptation. While LP signaling is generally considered upstream of SL biosynthesis, their interaction is more complex. For instance, exogenous SL exerts opposite effects on lateral root formation under low versus high phosphorus. Here, we show that under LP, SL-induced anthocyanin accumulation requires PHR1, demonstrating that PHR1 functions downstream of SL signaling. We uncovered an SL-dependent physical interaction between PHR1 and the SL receptor DWARF14 (D14). This interaction promotes PHR1 dimerization, stabilizes PHR1 by inhibiting its ubiquitination-mediated degradation, and enhances its transcriptional activation activity. The D14-PHR1 complex directly binds and up-regulates the SL biosynthesis gene MAX3 and anthocyanin biosynthesis genes, thereby inhibiting branching and hypocotyl elongation and promoting anthocyanin accumulation. These findings indicate that PHR1 mediates the coordination of SL and LP signaling, potentially explaining SL’s opposing effects on lateral root formation under different phosphorus conditions. In the phr1 mutant, exogenous SL inhibited lateral roots under both LP and Pi-sufficient conditions, confirming that the promoting role of SL under LP requires PHR1. PHR1 also interacted with D14 to activate LBDs and HB23 , regulating lateral root formation. Collectively, LP signaling coordinates with SL signaling via two parallel pathways: regulating SL biosynthesis to align SL functions with LP requirements and enhancing PHR1 activity through PHR1-D14 interaction to amplify LP signaling outputs.

title: MYC primes a paralog synthetic lethality involving the mitochondrial translocase subunits TIMM17A and TIMM17B and N-Acetylaspartate
abstract: To identify the genes and pathways required for the survival of MYC -amplified cancers, we engineered an isogenic cell system in which transformation is driven by oncogenic MYC . Using a genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 library, we identified the mitochondrial membrane translocase TIMM17A as uniquely essential for the survival of MYC-transformed cells. This dependency arises from MYC-driven suppression of TIMM17B , the paralog of TIMM17A . TIMM17A/B is an essential component of the TIM23 mitochondrial protein import complex, and the MYC-induced suppression of TIMM17B creates a strong dependency on TIMM17A . N-acetylaspartate supplementation rescued TIMM17A dependency in MYC -amplified cell lines, highlighting the unique and crucial role of this metabolite in the cell fitness of MYC -amplified cancers. These observations identify a paralog dependency required for the survival of a subset of MYC-driven cancers.

title: Y chromosome instability in the early mouse embryo
abstract: The Y chromosome lacks canonical centromeric repeats necessary for high-fidelity chromosome segregation. In adult tissues, this causes Y loss and predisposes to disease. However, its impact on embryogenesis is unknown. Here, we identify the first mouse embryonic mitoses as a window during which the Y centromere is unusually weak. This vulnerability impairs kinetochore strength and the Y becomes preferentially trapped at the spindle pole, resulting in missegregation. To study the impact of Y loss, we generate an aggregation model to track specific aneuploidies in mosaic embryos. Loss of the Y slows down cell division and compromises embryo size. Our findings reveal a developmental window during which the Y is especially vulnerable to loss, with implications for male sex determination and the origin of Turner syndrome (XO).

title: CD8 + T cells induce RIPK1-regulated brain endothelial cell death in cerebral malaria
abstract: Cerebral malaria (CM) is a potentially lethal complication of Plasmodium falciparum infection characterized by blood-brain barrier disruption and brain hemorrhage. Although immune-mediated endothelial damage is central to CM pathology, the mechanisms linking cytotoxic immune responses to endothelial injury remain unclear. Here, we show that CD8 + T cells induce receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)–regulated cell death of brain endothelial cells in mouse CM, while RIPK1 phosphorylation is increased in brain endothelial cells in human CM. Using magnetic resonance imaging, three-dimensional tissue-cleared brain imaging, cross-species pathology, endothelial translatomics, immunocerebrovascular interactomics, and genetic association testing, we identify a CD8 + T cell–dependent, RIPK1-centered mouse endothelial cell death program. Combined RIPK1 and caspase inhibition protected cross-presenting endothelial cells from CD8 + T cell–mediated death in vitro. In vivo, brain endothelial-specific genetic inactivation or systemic pharmacological inhibition of RIPK1 kinase activity prolonged survival in mouse CM without altering parasitemia. These findings support RIPK1 inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy to counter CD8 + T cell–induced endothelial death in CM.

title: Molecular engineering of noncoordinating backbones in Zr-MOFs for ultrasensitive piezofluorochromism-based high pressure sensing
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising pressure-responsive luminescent materials, but precise control of their emission under pressure remains a substantial challenge. Here, we engineered the piezofluorochromic response of zirconium-based MOFs by tuning the polarity of the emissive moieties through noncoordinating phenyl substituents. Four isostructural UiO-67 derivatives were synthesized. The most polar ligand, in UiO-67-PA, yields ultrasensitive piezofluorochromism with a bathochromic shift of 190 nanometers per gigapascal below 0.36 gigapascals. This sensitivity arises from two cooperative effects: enhanced conjugation through pressure-driven rotation of the aromatic rings and amplified orbital overlap resulting from polarity-induced electronic redistribution. This work broadens the strategies for modulating MOF luminescence and highlights their potential for pressure sensing.

title: A single–amino acid difference between rodent and human Andes virus affects viral glycoprotein trafficking
abstract: Andes virus (ANDV) causes hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), with rare outbreaks involving person-to-person transmission. A human ANDV isolate from one such outbreak and a rodent isolate from the same region differ in lethality in Syrian golden hamsters. Genomic analysis revealed 25 nonsynonymous substitutions, including one leading to a T641I change in the human ANDV glycoprotein precursor near its cleavage site. Although the isolates differed in growth kinetics, strand-specific RT-qPCR did not support major differences in viral RNA synthesis, whereas virion release was delayed in the case of the human isolate. In human cell expression systems, a single I641T substitution in the human ANDV glycoprotein resulted in decreased Golgi retention and faster release of virion-like particles relative to wild-type glycoprotein. Since ANDV egress takes place at the Golgi, the T641I change present in the human ANDV isolate may represent a human adaptive mutation influencing glycoprotein trafficking and virus particle release.

title: Molecular determinants of Kingella kingae translocation across polarized respiratory epithelium.
abstract: Kingella kingae is the leading cause of osteoarticular infections in children under 36 months of age. The pathogenesis of K. kingae disease begins with colonization of the oropharynx followed by translocation across the respiratory epithelium, entry into the bloodstream, and dissemination to distant sites. The bacterial factors that facilitate translocation across the respiratory barrier are poorly understood. In this study, we used polarized Calu-3 cells differentiated at an air-liquid interface (ALI) as a model of the respiratory epithelium combined with molecular genetics, barrier integrity measurements, cytotoxicity assays, and RNA sequencing to interrogate the molecular mechanism by which K. kingae breaches the respiratory epithelium. We found that the pore-forming RtxA toxin drives disruption of the epithelial barrier and is a major contributor to translocation. We observed that type IV pili (T4P) also contribute to translocation and mediate a toxin-independent translocation mechanism. Strains lacking both RtxA and T4P were unable to translocate, confirming that at least one or the other of these factors is required for translocation. Transcriptomic profiling of K. kingae identified 512 differentially expressed bacterial genes during infection and suggested a new role for HprK and a novel esterase in the process of translocation. This study establishes that multiple bacterial factors influence K. kingae translocation across the respiratory epithelial barrier and provides insight into important gene expression changes during K. kingae interaction with host cells.

title: How Much Visual Evidence Does a Grounding Agent Need? Budget Profiles for Agentic Remote-Sensing Visual Grounding
abstract: Remote-sensing visual grounding does not have a uniform inference cost. A whole-scene view preserves layout but can erase tiny referents, whereas tile retrieval and zoom recover detail at additional latency. This paper asks a practical question: how much visual evidence should a grounding agent acquire before returning a horizontal box? We study the HBB inference profiles of AgentRSVG, whose controller maintains cross-scale hypotheses, directs retrieval and zoom toward unresolved query constraints, and uses a grounding verifier to stop or continue. Low, Main, and High profiles share trained weights and validation-frozen stopping thresholds; they differ only in caps on actions, tiles, proposals, and zooms, while Single removes the iterative loop from the common visual backbone. On DIOR-RSVG, Single obtains 69.20 Pr@0.5 and 61.25 mIoU. Low raises these values to 85.80 and 77.15 at 2.6 seconds per query, recovering 83.2% of the Single-to-Main accuracy gain. Main reaches 89.15 Pr@0.5 and 80.28 mIoU at 4.0 seconds, whereas High adds only 0.57 Pr@0.5 while increasing latency by 40%. On RSVG-HR, Main obtains 92.18 Pr@0.5 and 80.45 mIoU. Small-target diagnostics identify where extra computation is most useful, while verified positive cases illustrate successful localization across scale, repetition, geometry, and context. These results turn a single headline score into an explicit accuracy–cost frontier and identify a strong operating point for budget-constrained agentic grounding.

title: MM-SkillBench & MM-SkillRouter: Benchmarking and Routing Multimodal Skills for Agents
abstract: Agent performance increasingly depends on the ability to understand, select and reuse external skills. Recent skill routing methods begin to equip agents with suitable skills by encoding each skill into textual representations, and then retrieving the most relevant skill for a given user request. However, text-only skills may be insufficient enough to capture the full information required for agent execution. Particularly, for multimodal tasks, this text-only format weakens retrieval signals and limits the ability of multimodal agents to select skills grounded in visual context. Despite recent progress in skill routing, learning to retrieve multimodal skills for agents remains largely unexplored. To address this gap, we introduce MM-SkillBench, a large-scale multimodal skill benchmark. MM-SkillBench contains 34,421 training samples of multimodal skill and 500 evaluation queries across 13 diverse categories. To support multimodal skill retrieval, we first equip each skill with visual skill card, textual skill summary and schema, structuring its intent, inputs, outputs, constraints, execution flow, and visual semantics in a retrieval-friendly form. we then identify skill samples that require multimodal queries, such as requests involving screenshots, visual examples, or image-grounded observations, and synthesize corresponding queries with visual inputs for these samples. Building on this benchmark, we propose MM-SkillRouter, the first skill router for multimodal agents. MM-SkillRouter first retrieves candidate skills leveraging multimodal skill representations and then reranks them for fine-grained query-skill matching. Experiments show that MM-SkillRouter consistently improves multimodal skill selection, achieving 0.698% Hit@1 and outperforming baselines by 24.2%, which indicates that multimodal skill formulation provide additional stronger skill representations and offer a practical path toward more accurate skill routing for multimodal agents. title: Imagine Before You Act: A Self-Evolving Industrial Agent with a Physics-Grounded World Model
abstract: Physical AI extends data-driven intelligence into the physical world, yet industrial deployment demands agents that are safe, causal, and robust to the distribution shift that machines inevitably undergo. Most industrial LLM/agent systems today act as open-loop advisors: they diagnose or recommend from sensor summaries but never simulate the physical consequences of an intervention before committing to it. We present Pave (Perceive–Anticipate–Verify–Evolve), a multimodal physical AI agent built around a physics-grounded generative world model that serves as the agent’s internal simulator. Pave (i) fuses heterogeneous industrial signals including multi-channel vibration, multivariate process sensors, and textual maintenance context into a shared physical latent under a physical-consistency objective; (ii) rolls out candidate interventions through an ensemble, physics-informed latent world model to anticipate their effects with calibrated uncertainty; (iii) executes only actions whose imagined trajectories satisfy operating-envelope constraints with high probability (verify-before-act); and (iv) continually adapts the world model from surprise-weighted real outcomes, closing the sim-to-real gap over a machine’s life. Across the Tennessee Eastman process and three rolling-bearing benchmarks, Pave raises closed-loop fault-mitigation success by up to 16 points and reduces safety constraint violations by over \(60\%\) relative to model-free RL, model-based RL, and open-loop LLM-agent baselines, while staying well calibrated under distribution shift.
journal: Proceedings of the 1st International Workshop on Industrial Physical AI

title: Did You Hear That? Detecting AI Voice Agents by Exploiting Their Robustness
abstract: AI voice agents enable scalable vishing and impersonation attacks, yet existing detection methods face practical limitations. Artifact-based detectors degrade as synthesis quality improves, challenge–response tests are socially awkward, and adversarial jamming must often be loud or continuous to disrupt modern automatic speech recognition (ASR). We introduce HEARD, a detection framework built on a new principle: instead of perturbing the AI while remaining imperceptible to humans, HEARD applies brief, conspicuous distortions that humans notice but robust ASR systems largely ignore. A human caller is likely to comment on the disturbance, misunderstand the utterance, or request repetition, whereas an AI agent continues coherently from the recovered transcription. We map fifteen audible distortions into three families and evaluate them across six ASR models spanning multiple architectures and five years of development, as well as an experiment involving 41 human volunteers. Using semantic similarity and an LLM-based conversational-legibility metric, we find that across 2,421 LibriSpeech and TED-LIUM utterances, modern ASRs preserve a mean legibility of 97.8%, while the best distortion keeps every model at or above 98.3%. Moreover, performance improves with model recency, making stronger ASR systems easier, not harder, to distinguish from humans.
journal: Proceedings of the 2nd ACM Workshop on Deepfake, Deception, and Disinformation Security

title: Active Acoustic Probes for AI Voice Call Detection
abstract: AI voice calls are making it increasingly practical to impersonate people during live audio conversations, whether through voice cloning, real-time conversion, or autonomous voice agents. Current defenses remain mostly passive: they inspect received audio for artifacts created by current generators, which locks defenders into an arms race structurally favoring the attacker. Active defenses invert this dynamic by injecting fresh evidence during the call, but they typically require the remote speaker to cooperate by performing a challenge task. We propose an active acoustic probe that requires no such cooperation: it verifies whether the returned audio traversed a genuine physical speaker-to-microphone path. During a call, the verifier sends a brief high-frequency acoustic challenge and checks whether it survives in the returned audio. Normal physical paths preserve the challenge, whereas the tested voice-conversion paths suppress it. This yields a simple, explainable signal-processing rule calibrated only on normal physical-path recordings. The probe is correctly detected in 99% of trials across diverse consumer audio form factors, from open laptop/phone playback to ear-worn headphones and earbuds, while all 200 outputs from four tested speech-to-speech and voice-conversion configurations fail the detector.
journal: Proceedings of the 2nd ACM Workshop on Deepfake, Deception, and Disinformation Security

title: Upstream Supply Chain Security in MCP: Structural Limits of SAST and Deployment-Side Defense
abstract: The rapid growth of Generative AI (GenAI) has accelerated the adoption of Model Context Protocol (MCP) as a standardized interface connecting AI models with external tools and data. However, upstream supply chain vulnerabilities in MCP servers can propagate malicious behavior across many downstream agents. To address this issue, we introduce a three-dimensional taxonomy and five upstream attack objectives, including credential exfiltration, decision poisoning, covert channels, dependency confusion, and time-triggered logic bombs, and implement them in controlled testbeds. We then evaluated 39 widely used MCP-related repositories with an automated Static Application Security Testing (SAST) framework and manual triage. The results expose structural limitations of source-only, pattern-based scanning for upstream threats because such scanning cannot independently establish provenance, destination, or deployment-specific exploitability when the decisive evidence lies outside the scope of static analysis. Therefore, we propose a deployment-side defense model centered on provenance attestation, destination allow-listing, and runtime egress monitoring. We also present a control-coverage matrix that maps attack objectives to these controls and provides a basis for assessing MCP supply-chain risk beyond traditional severity scoring.
journal: Proceedings of the 3rd ACM Workshop on Large AI Systems and Models with Privacy and Safety Analysis

title: Design Exploration for Context-Based Access Control of Vision-Language-Action Model-Based Embodied Agents
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA)-based embodied agents combine large AI models with physical perception and actuation, creating safety and security risks when unauthorized actions lead to physical hazards. These systems therefore require context-based access control that accounts for runtime conditions while meeting latency constraints. However, existing work has focused primarily on access policies, leaving the system-level implications of alternative access-control designs underexplored. This short paper implements a context-based authorization framework for VLA-based embodied agents and evaluates motion thresholds, session key validity periods, and centralized versus decentralized authorization deployments. Our results quantify how these design choices affect authorization frequency and end-to-end latency and show that decentralized authorization substantially reduces latency and variability.
journal: Proceedings of the 3rd ACM Workshop on Large AI Systems and Models with Privacy and Safety Analysis

title: Embodied AI Must Treat Visual Bias as a Safety Primitive, Not a Robustness Penalty
abstract: While embodied agents increasingly incorporate diverse sensors, they predominantly rely on learned visual representations for manipulation and control. However, when visual preferences are tightly coupled with action generation, benign cues can induce task failures, unsafe motions, or exploitable vulnerabilities. We present a diagnostic study of visual bias as a safety primitive for embodied AI evaluation and defense: an independently operationalizable property tied to an identifiable risk class, not a standalone safety guarantee. Agents should be assessed not merely on task success, but also on whether their actions remain grounded in visual evidence relevant to the task. We study this risk through controlled visual variations under task-equivalent conditions, naturalistic distractors aligned with inherited visual preferences, and counterfactual action analysis. Our results show that benign perceptual changes can produce divergent behavior, while task-irrelevant content can receive disproportionate action relevance and induce physical failures. We further introduce a counterfactual detection method that combines persistent region selection with changes in predicted actions after masking, helping distinguish behaviorally relevant preference-aligned content from regions that are merely visually salient. These findings provide preliminary diagnostic evidence of visual bias and demonstrate the need for broader preference discovery, visual shortcut mining, and failure mode search to improve predeployment risk coverage and guide targeted mitigation in both model development and real-world deployment.
journal: Proceedings of the 3rd ACM Workshop on Large AI Systems and Models with Privacy and Safety Analysis

title: Design and Fabrication of mmWave Radar-Based Eye Tracking Smart Glasses
abstract: Eye tracking is becoming a central input modality for extended-reality and smart-glasses systems. In virtual reality, gaze can support foveated rendering, avatar eye contact, and hands-free selection. On AR or everyday smart glasses, gaze has an additional role: it tells what the wearer is paying attention to in the surrounding world. When a user asks, ''What is this?'', the answer depends on whether the user is looking at a sign, a warning light, a product label, or a person in the scene. This context is especially important for on-device AI agents. A front-facing camera can capture the scene, but it does not by itself reveal the user's attention. Gaze can disambiguate speech, focus perception, and enable low-effort interaction without asking the wearer to point or touch a controller. The challenge is that smart glasses have a much tighter hardware budget than headsets. Sensors must be small, low power, robust to outdoor conditions, and unobtrusive enough to fit into eyewear.

title: Agentic AI-Generated vs. Clinician-Authored Hospital Course Narratives for Cardiology Hospitalizations: A Blinded Physician Evaluation.
abstract: Background: Discharge summaries are essential for safe transitions of care, but writing the hospital course narrative is time intensive. Large language models can generate plausible clinical narratives, yet prior approaches often rely on static inputs and remain vulnerable to omissions and factual inconsistencies. Methods: We developed an electronic health record (EHR)-integrated agentic artificial intelligence (AI) system that uses Gemini 2.5 Pro and Model Context Protocol tools to retrieve clinical notes, diagnostic reports, diagnoses, medications, and appointments on demand. In this retrospective, blinded, paired study, 50 inpatient cardiology encounters were randomly selected from admissions July 13 to 27, 2024, at Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota. Five physicians rated AI-generated and clinician-authored hospital course narratives for each encounter (250 ratings) on 0-to-10 scales for overall quality, clarity, completeness, accuracy, and readability and indicated a preference. The primary outcome was the paired difference in overall quality (linear mixed-effects model with crossed random intercepts for encounter and reviewer). Secondary domains were analyzed similarly with Bonferroni adjustment, and preference with a crossed random-effects logistic model. Results: Clinician-authored narratives were preferred in 132 ratings (52.8%) and AI-generated narratives in 118 (47.2%) (odds ratio for clinician-authored preference, 1.12; 95% CI, 0.71 to 1.78). Overall quality did not differ significantly (mean, 7.27 AI-generated versus 7.42 clinician-authored; difference, -0.15; 95% CI, -0.86 to 0.56; p=0.627). AI-generated narratives were rated higher for clarity (0.36; 95% CI, 0.07 to 0.65) and readability (0.72; 95% CI, 0.20 to 1.24) but lower for completeness (-0.84; 95% CI, -1.36 to -0.32) and accuracy (-0.35; 95% CI, -0.66 to -0.05). After Bonferroni correction, only lower completeness remained significant (adjusted p=0.012). Conclusions: Hospital course narratives generated by the EHR-integrated agentic AI system did not differ significantly from clinician-authored narratives in physician-rated overall quality or preference. Lower completeness supports continued clinician review before use in the medical record.

title: MRI-based deep-learning radiomics nomogram for differentiating FIGO 2023 stage I from stage II–IV endometrial cancer: a multicenter study
abstract: Preoperative identification of FIGO 2023 stage I endometrial cancer (EC) is important for treatment planning. We aimed to develop and validate a deep-learning radiomics nomogram (DLRN) based on multiparametric MRI to distinguish stage I EC from stage II–IV disease. This study retrospectively enrolled patients from three centers. Patients from Centers 1 and 2 were randomly split into a training set (n = 616), and an internal test set (n = 158), and Center 3 served as an external test set (n = 232). The DLRN integrated deep-learning features, intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics features, and clinical characteristics. The DLRN was compared with clinical, radiomics, and deep-learning models. Discrimination was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with AUCs compared using DeLong’s test. A total of 1006 patients (mean age, 56.5 ± 9.7 years) were analyzed. In the internal test set, the DLRN achieved an AUC of 0.852, higher than the clinical (0.673; p = 0.001), original radiomics (0.765; p = 0.030), and combined radiomics (0.793; p = 0.050) models. In the external test set, the DLRN remained robust (AUC = 0.829) and outperformed the clinical, original radiomics, and combined radiomics models (AUC = 0.680, 0.681, and 0.743; all p < 0.005). With DLRN assistance, radiologists showed improved diagnostic performance. The MRI-based DLRN showed robust discrimination between FIGO 2023 stage I and stage II–IV EC across test sets, supporting its potential for preoperative risk stratification and decision support. Question The introduction of the FIGO 2023 staging system has made the differentiation between stages more challenging, highlighting the need for better tools. Findings A new MRI-based deep-learning radiomics nomogram (DLRN) accurately identifies high-risk patients, significantly outperforming traditional and individual clinical prediction methods. Critical relevance statement This tool helps doctors make better preoperative treatment plans, potentially improving patient outcomes in endometrial cancer.

Bodily Self Disturbances: A New Clinical Marker of Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness (PPPD) is among the most prevalent chronic neuro-otologic disorders, affecting 15%-20% of adults seen in neurology and specialized dizziness clinics. Classified as a functional vestibular disorder with established diagnostic criteria, PPPD typically follows peripheral or central otoneurological disorders. However, the mechanisms underlying the transition to chronic perceptual dizziness remain unclear. Beyond maladaptive postural control and visual dependence, theoretical models implicate altered multisensory integration and disrupted predictive processing. Such mechanisms may extend to disturbances of the bodily self, a dimension increasingly recognized in functional neurologic disorders, but not yet systematically investigated in PPPD. METHODS We characterized bodily self disturbances in PPPD by assessing depersonalization-derealization (DD) symptoms in a large cross-sectional study (n = 455), including 100 patients with PPPD, 180 patients with other otoneurological disorders, and 175 healthy controls. DD symptoms were assessed using the Cambridge Depersonalization Scale, alongside measures of anxiety, depression, dizziness-related impairment, and PPPD symptom severity. RESULTS Patients with PPPD exhibited markedly elevated DD symptoms compared with both other otoneurological disorders and healthy controls. Notably, 20% of patients with PPPD met the threshold for clinical DD, compared with 7.2% of other otoneurological disorders and <1% of controls. DD severity in PPPD overlapped with levels observed in other functional neurologic disorders but remained lower than in primary dissociative disorders. Factor analyses identified 3 DD dimensions: bodily self disturbances, cognitive and affective detachment, and numbing. Only bodily self disturbances, capturing disruptions in self-location, agency, body ownership, and first-person perspective, robustly differentiated PPPD from other otoneurological disorders (η2 = 0.20, p < 0.001). This dimension predicted PPPD diagnosis (odds ratio = 1.40, p < 0.001) and showed significant discriminative ability (AUC = 0.66). Individuals in the highest decile of bodily self disturbances had nearly ten-fold increased odds of PPPD. Structural equation modelling confirmed a direct effect of PPPD on bodily self disturbances, partially mediated by depressive symptoms but independent of age, sex, migraine, and anxiety. DISCUSSION These findings identify DD as a previously unrecognized component of the PPPD phenotype and establish bodily self disturbances as a novel clinical marker for PPPD, refining phenotyping and informing pathophysiologic models.

title: AI-Enabled Smart and Precision Agriculture: Smart Sensors, IoT, Deep Learning, Computer Vision, and Decision Support: A Comprehensive Survey
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated with smart sensors, Internet of Things (IoT) networks, machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision to support site-specific agricultural management. However, strong performance on computational benchmarks does not necessarily translate into reliable decisions, effective field interventions, or measurable improvements in agricultural productivity and resource efficiency. This comprehensive narrative survey critically synthesizes advances in agricultural sensing, IoT architectures, data processing, multimodal sensor fusion, predictive modeling, computer vision, decision optimization, and automated actuation. Particular emphasis is placed on the relationships between measurement reliability, model generalization, decision feasibility, intervention accuracy, and verified agricultural outcomes. The reviewed literature demonstrates promising capabilities in crop monitoring, yield prediction, disease and weed recognition, precision irrigation, and selected automated operations. Nevertheless, heterogeneous evaluation protocols, limited independent field validation, sensor calibration challenges, distribution shifts, interoperability barriers, and deployment costs constrain operational reliability and generalizability. To address these interconnected challenges, the survey proposes a literature-informed reference architecture linking agricultural observations, data integration, AI inference, constrained decision-making, physical interventions, and outcome feedback, supported by uncertainty assessment, human oversight, and cross-layer assurance. The proposed architecture is conceptual and has not been empirically validated. Future research priorities include reproducible field evaluations, representative agricultural datasets, uncertainty-aware and explainable AI, resource-efficient computing, interoperable infrastructures, and economically inclusive deployment. The review concludes that the practical value of AI-enabled precision agriculture should be evaluated through reliable interventions, sustainable resource utilization, and demonstrated agricultural outcomes rather than predictive performance alone.

title: Measuring the sensitivity of sand pile geometry to substrate roughness for calibrating friction parameters in the discrete element method
abstract: Accurate calibration of contact parameters in the discrete element method (DEM) remains one of the critical challenges for predictive modelling of granular flows and wear processes. In this work, we propose and experimentally validate a novel calibration strategy based on the morphological analysis of granular heaps formed under controlled low-mass deposition. Operating deliberately in the sensitivity-threshold regime, where reproducibility is preserved while local interactions remain highly distinguishable, we demonstrate that the geometry of the heap provides diagnostic information beyond the conventional single-angle-of-repose test. A systematic series of experiments with sand deposited on substrates of varying roughness revealed a distinct dual-slope profile, reflecting the separation between particle–substrate and particle–particle interaction domains. Internal and external slope angles, along with height distribution and top-shape descriptors, were employed as multi-criteria calibration metrics. These features proved highly sensitive to substrate roughness and feed conditions, allowing for the independent identification of friction and rolling resistance parameters in DEM simulations. Numerical modelling combined with surrogate-based regression confirmed the feasibility of recovering key particle–surface parameters from the experimental heap geometry. The proposed framework offers a resource-efficient and reproducible approach to DEM calibration, reducing the computational load while maintaining sensitivity to local contact mechanics. The methodology is directly applicable in tribological modelling of granular-induced wear, particle-surface
journal: Advances in Science and Technology Research Journal

title: Improving AI-based modelling for mass customisation strategy: Insights from automotive industry
abstract: The potential of the mass customisation (MC) strategy is continuously expanding through the implementation of Industry 4.0/5.0 technologies. In this study, a novel approach to enhancing the potential of Artificial Intelligence-based techniques for MC level prediction was presented. Firstly, the empirical research was conducted among more than 150 European manufacturing companies in the automotive sector concerning factors influencing the increase in the level of MC, as well as the Industry 4.0 or 5.0 technologies applied. Next, the collected survey data was pre-processed to eliminate infrequent responses and subsequently analysed using the k-means clustering method for labelling purposes. The resulting dataset was then used to fine-tune parameters and train a classifier based on a multilayer perceptron (MLP), aimed at identifying the MC level in automotive enterprises. The developed classifier achieved average accuracies of 0.94 and 0.93 for training and testing, respectively. The proposed approach was validated through real-life case studies from the automotive industry, demonstrating the adaptability of our concept and its potential for diverse industrial applications.
journal: Advances in Science and Technology Research Journal

title: Deep Learning Theory through the Lens of Statistical Physics: A Topical Review
abstract: The recent success of foundation models and deep learning has far outpaced our theoretical understanding of how large-scale neural networks learn and generalize. Statistical physics provides a natural language for describing such high-dimensional, nonlinear, and strongly coupled systems, offering concepts such as mean-field theory, phase transitions, energy landscapes, and stochastic dynamics. In this topical review, we adopt a statistical-physics way of thinking -- from concepts including phases and criticality, and free-energy viewpoints, to methods such as kernel and Gaussian-process limits, mean-field and dynamical mean-field theories, random-matrix tools, and Fokker-Planck formalisms, and to a mindset emphasizing universality, scaling, and tractable limits with explicit validity regimes. We survey recent progress on understanding modern deep learning through this lens, including mean-field analyses of wide networks, spectral and geometric perspectives on loss landscapes, stochastic-gradient-based training viewed as a dynamical process, and phase-transition analogies that organize phenomena such as overparameterization, generalization, and representation change. Our goal is to synthesize these threads into a coherent framework that clarifies what each approximation explains, when it is expected to hold, and how apparently competing narratives relate or diverge. Together, these perspectives form a unified physical framework that views representation learning as a collective phenomenon in high-dimensional systems, bridging deterministic and stochastic regimes of gradient-based optimization.

title: TRANSFORMATION OF U.S. AND EU POLICY TOWARD CENTRAL ASIA IN 2022–2026: GEOPOLITICAL AND GEOECONOMIC PRIORITIES
abstract: The article provides a comprehensive examination of the transformation of United States and European Union policy toward Central Asia amid changes in the international political configuration following the beginning of Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine. The purpose of the study is to identify the geopolitical and strategic substance of the intensification of Western engagement in the region, its institutional, geoeconomic, resource-related, and security priorities, as well as the impact of these processes on the foreign policy manoeuvring of the Central Asian states. The methodological framework combines comparative, historical-political, and institutional approaches, together with an analysis of strategies, declarations, international agreements, and statistical data. It is argued that, prior to 2022, Central Asia remained an area of limited engagement for the United States and the European Union because of Russia’s dominant position, institutionalised through the CIS, the CSTO, and the EAEU, as well as China’s growing influence through the Belt and Road Initiative, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, and the China–Central Asia format. The study establishes that Russia’s war against Ukraine increased the strategic importance of the region as a source of critical raw materials, a space for alternative transport connectivity, and an area of enhanced control over sanctions circumvention. Under the administration of Joe Biden, geoeconomic, resource-related, and transport priorities gained greater weight in U.S. policy toward Central Asia, while its normative and security components were preserved. Under Donald Trump, reductions in programmes supporting democratic institutions were accompanied by a more pronounced trade-oriented and mercantilist approach focused on trade agreements, U.S. exports, access to strategic resources, and transport and technology projects. It is demonstrated that EU policy evolved from the normative and development-oriented model of the 2007 strategy, through the increasing pragmatisation of its approach in 2019, toward an operational model of investment and infrastructure cooperation embodied in the Global Gateway initiative, the 2023 Roadmap, support for the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor, the first EU–Central Asia Summit in 2025, and projects in the fields of critical raw materials, digital infrastructure, water, energy, and climate. The article concludes that the growing engagement of the United States and the European Union broadens the scope for multi-vector foreign policies among the states of the region but does not provide a rapid alternative to Russian and Chinese influence because of persistent economic, security, and infrastructure dependencies. For Ukraine, these developments highlight the need for a pragmatic policy toward Central Asia focused on logistics, energy, agricultural cooperation, education, digital solutions, and post-war reconstruction.

title: A live agent benchmark of independent action authorization for healthcare AI agents
abstract: Benchmarks measure what healthcare AI agents can do, not what they may be authorized to do. We built a live-agent benchmark holding task, model, prompt and tools fixed, varying only whether an independent authorization layer gated execution. 576 synthetic care-coordination episodes ran under four arms: deterministic rules, an unconstrained agent, a gateway-governed agent, and a gateway plus autonomy controller. Episodes carry hidden truth and a lossy observable projection, so the gateway can both wrongly authorize and wrongly block. A prespecified rule set blinded to arm adjudicated safety. Unsafe actions occurred in 0.7% of fully governed versus 0.4% of unconstrained episodes (+ 0.4 points, 95% CI -0.5 to + 1.2, P = 0.6875). Routine task success, escalation accuracy, and calibration were each significantly worse under full governance, which also required more time and human effort. These synthetic findings use rule-based adjudication, lack a human comparator, and do not establish clinical effectiveness.

title: Network Based Quantum Inspired Deep Learning Framework for Cardiovascular Disease Prediction Using Interpretable Feature Interaction Networks
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of global mortality, accounting for approximately 17.9 million deaths annually. It is required that the development of sophisticated network-based predictive algorithms that can preserve the multifaceted feature interaction in the early detection of the disease and clinical decision support. This research introduces a new hybrid scheme of quantum-inspired feature interaction networks and deep neural network structures to predict CVD. We use our methodology to build a full graph of feature interactions based on ZZ-feature maps and the weight of edges is a pairwise quantum-inspired correlation between clinical features. This network-based representation is further provided to a multi-layered neural network with ensemble decision-making. Experimental validation on the UCI Cleveland Heart Disease dataset demonstrates (303 patients, 13 clinical attributes), our hybrid architecture has an accuracy of 90.5% (95% CI: 89.491.6), precision of 89.1, recall of 91.24%, F1-score of 89.9%, and ROC-AUC of 0.936, and a 5-fold stratified cross-validation. The statistical significance analysis confirms that the quantum-inspired network transformation yields statistically significant performance improvements over the baseline approaches (p < 0.01, Cohen’s d > 0.8). However, we note that control experiments isolating the ZZ-feature map contribution from the dimensionality expansion (20→40 dimensions) and ensemble effects have not been performed in the current study and are reserved for future work. The results of SHAP-based network interpretability analysis indicate that thalassemia, the major vessel count, and chest pain type are the most powerful nodes in the prediction network, which aligns with traditional cardiovascular diagnostic guidelines. The suggested framework provides a reproducible methodology, with transparent limitation reporting, that serves as a basis for network-driven clinical decision support systems and preserves paths for translating quantum hardware.

title: Multimodal Prompt Learning with Vision--Language Foundation Models for Automated Storyboard Assessment and Formative Feedback in Film Education
abstract: Storyboards articulate cinematic meaning through compositions, actions, captions, and the temporal relations between shots. Assessing them is challenging because recognizable shot attributes do not uniquely determine narrative quality, and persuasive feedback may lack evidence in the submitted panels. We formulate storyboard assessment as criterion-conditioned inference over an editable temporal graph and propose Criterion-constrained Rubric-aware Feedback Transport (CRaFT). The approach couples frozen vision–language encoders with low-rank criterion prompts, unbalanced optimal transport between multimodal evidence and rubric anchors, and ordinal score prediction. A graph-consistent counterfactual objective scores candidate revisions by their localized, criterion-specific effects, while conservative selection can abstain when support or uncertainty is inadequate. On the reported public-data evaluations (MovieShots, FullShots, AVE, and MovieNet), CRaFT obtains macro-F1 scores of 77.4%, 73.1%, 72.3%, and 70.0%, respectively, exceeding the strongest listed prompt baseline by 5.2–5.9 percentage points across these tasks. The reported AVE sequence-order accuracy reaches 80.1%, while the mean ordinal agreement on constructed rubric proxies is 0.69 quadratic-weighted kappa. The same system supports a teacher-aligned five-criterion assessment protocol with independent validation of cited evidence, edit benefit, and model abstention. This separation of measurable cinematic proxies from instructor judgment is central to the proposed evaluation design.

title: DualTrust: Asymmetric Bayesian Reputation and Cryptographic Gating for Autonomous AI Agents
abstract: The proliferation of Ambient Wearable Intelligence (AWI) ecosystems, spanning augmented reality glasses, smartwatches, and pervasive edge IoT actuators, is fundamentally transitioning human-AI interaction from explicit tactile commands to continuous, implicit background tool delegation. In these ambient environments, autonomous Large Language Model (LLM) agents are granted operational authority to invoke external APIs, reserve financial micro-quotas, and control physical actuators. However, existing safety guardrails depend on secondary LLM-as-a-judge classifiers that introduce prohibitive runtime latencies (400–850 ms) and recurring token expenses, while static role-based access control fails against continuous behavioral drift, memory backdoors, and interleaved salami-slicing exploits. We present DualTrust, an asymmetric Bayesian reputation and cryptographic gating runtime engineered for autonomous multi-agent containment. DualTrust enforces a decoupled principal-agent architecture that strictly isolates Human Principal Accountable Credit from Bayesian Agent Operational Standing. Agent behavior is continuously modulated via an asymmetric power-law slashing engine (Δβ ∝ (sev · c^2) · v_a^1.8) with instantaneous clean-streak reset, deterministic SHA-256 64-bucket striped concurrency locks, atomically locked rollback refunds, and an O(1) RAM sliding-window RFC 6962 Merkle audit ledger with rolling epoch seals that bounds active memory consumption by committing historical roots to persistent storage. Evaluated across 176 automated invariant tests and 10,000-cycle Monte Carlo attack simulations, DualTrust makes deterministic authorization verdicts in a median latency of 47.10 µs in-memory (mean 63.16 µs, tail p99 287.10 µs) and 155.80 µs under persistent SQLite WAL disk transactions, with end-to-end Python decorator wrappers executing in median 60.70 µs (async) and 88.30 µs (sync) without external API calls. Compared against state-of-the-art LLM guardrails, DualTrust achieves over 6,600× lower latency (and over 32× to 50× lower latency than localized AST validators), by policy construction blocks Sybil defamation against collusive probation swarms, and provides tamper-evident, append-only audit durability with RFC 6962 inclusion verification, establishing a practical, foundational governance runtime for trustworthy ambient intelligence.

title: Mathematical Modeling on the Effect of Flood on Farmland: A Nonlinear Dynamical Systems Approach
abstract: This paper provides a three-dimensional nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) model to clearly understand the effects of flooding on agricultural farmlands. The model uses three interacting state variables: farmland productivity F(t), soil quality index S(t), and floodwater level W(t). The novelty of this work lies in: (i) explicit mechanistic coupling between all three variables, including positive feedback from soil quality to productivity and negative feedback from vegetation to floodwater (ii) identification of critical bifurcation thresholds using rigorous stability analysis; and (iii) quantification of synergistic effects from combined management interventions. Existence and uniqueness of solutions were established using the Picard-Lindelöf theorem; all biologically possible equilibrium points were identified, and their stability was assessed through the Routh-Hurwitz criteria. Extensive numerical modeling was carried out using MATLAB and sensitivity analysis was applied to identify the most critical parameters governing system behavior: drainage capacity (δ), flood input intensity (μ), and the crop damage coefficient (α). The model reveals critical thresholds i.e at drainage capacity 0.30 and flood input 0.70, above which the system reaches the irreversible degradation regimes. In combinations, there are synergistic advantages, with up to 32.8% productivity gain recorded when drainage infrastructure, flood-resistant crops, and soil conservation have been integrated into management. The results show that thresholds for drainage and flood-input parameters exist that govern the extent of degradation of farmland productivity during flooding, and that integrated management strategies are considerably more effective than single interventions, providing actionable evidence-based targets in agricultural resilience planning in flood-prone areas.
journal: Journal of Qassim University for Science

title: A time-resolved image-environment dataset for tatsoi growth monitoring and intelligent phytoprotection benchmarking
abstract: Image-based crop monitoring is now widely used in sustainable plant production, but public datasets that combine visual canopy appearance with synchronized local environmental measurements remain scarce. As a result, models are difficult to evaluate under field variation that must operate under field variation, including changes in plant growth, microclimate, soil conditions, pest pressure, illumination, and acquisition date. We present a time-resolved tatsoi ( Brassica campestris L. ssp. chinensis var. rosularis Tsen) image-environment dataset collected during winter cultivation from 12 November 2025 to 28 February 2026. The dataset contains 3456 plant-level images from 128 repeatedly imaged plants across 27 acquisition dates. Each image is linked to Labelme polygon annotations of the tatsoi canopy, derived bounding boxes and segmentation masks, plant identity, acquisition date, seven phenotype or condition labels, and synchronized field solar insecticidal lamp Internet of Things (SIL-IoT) records. The sensor-derived metadata used in the baseline analyses include air temperature and humidity, illumination, rain-status records, device-level pest-signal counts, soil moisture and temperature, wind speed, and wind direction. These metadata are provided as nearest sensor readings and as 1 h, 6 h, and 24 h pre-capture aggregates. Standardized random, temporal, and plant-holdout splits are provided to support reproducible evaluation. Baseline benchmarks showed that the resource can be reused for canopy detection, canopy segmentation, and image-environment trait recognition. Under the plant-holdout split, YOLOv8n reached a box mAP50–95 of 0.887, RetinaNet-R50 reached a box mAP50–95 of 0.826 among torchvision detectors, and Swin-T with environmental features reached a mean macro-F1 of 0.819 across plant-level traits. The dataset provides a reusable resource for multimodal crop phenotyping, field-condition visual benchmarking, and intelligent phytoprotection research.

title: Vision–Language–Action Model for Agricultural Fresh Produce Handling with a Humanoid Robot
abstract: Reaching, grasping, and placing delicate fresh produce are among the most labor-intensive operations in agricultural production, yet most robotic solutions remain task-specific, single-crop systems that generalize poorly across the morphological diversity of fresh produce. This study investigates whether a large, pre-trained Vision–Language–Action (VLA) model can be adapted with only modest demonstration data to serve as a flexible language-conditioned produce-handling policy on a humanoid robotic platform. The NVIDIA GR00T N1.7-3B foundation model is fine-tuned for a standard 23-degree-of-freedom Unitree G1 humanoid robot fitted with two Dex3-1 three-finger dexterous hands, whose arm and hand joint streams form a 24-dimensional combined manipulation command space. This study also compared the π0.5 VLA model. Demonstrations were collected through a Meta Quest 3 extended-reality teleoperation pipeline augmented with a multi-label recording mode that embeds a natural-language goal in each episode, yielding 605 language-conditioned demonstrations (261,724 synchronized frames) across four produce categories (lemon, peach, pear, and tomato). A dual-camera design paired a wide-angle head camera for global scene context with a wrist-mounted camera for close-range grasp feedback. The results show that the fine-tuned policy achieved a 96.25% individual-trial success rate and 85% on mixed-scene trials requiring retrieval of the language-specified item. However, adapting the π0.5 VLA model to the same data achieved 68.75% individual-trial success. Furthermore, a controlled ablation isolated the role of close-range perception. Without wrist-camera input, the policy reached every target in single-item trials but failed to secure a single grasp, resulting in 0% pick-and-place success despite comparable training loss. Therefore, close-range wrist perception was a precondition for contact in this setting. Together, these results demonstrate that VLA fine-tuning can transform a pre-trained humanoid foundation model into a reliable, data-efficient policy for multi-category fresh produce handling. This work provides a practical step toward flexible humanoid robotic systems for agricultural pick-and-place, sorting, and postharvest automation.

title: Statistical Descriptors of β-Variational Autoencoder Latent Feature Maps for Image-Based Blueberry Canopy-Size Phenotyping
abstract: Plant-level canopy-size assessment is important for precision agriculture applications, including crop monitoring and variable-rate fertilization, but trait-specific annotation remains costly. This study investigates whether unsupervised β-Variational Autoencoder (β-VAE) latent maps from an image reconstruction model encode canopy-size information recoverable through compact statistical descriptors. A β-VAE was trained on the designated training partitions of a dataset of 2043 field-acquired RGB images of individual blueberry plants, without canopy-size labels. The encoder generated spatial posterior mean (μ) and log-variance (logσ2) maps, from which per-location Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence maps were also computed. These maps were summarized into five descriptor configurations and evaluated using a separate classifier. The 300-feature reference configuration, which combined μ, logσ2, and KL descriptors, achieved 73.11% accuracy, 73.54% balanced accuracy, and 73.42% macro-F1 under a stratified-random split. Independent retraining of the complete pipeline for three acquisition session-held-out evaluations yielded 63.04 ± 4.54% balanced accuracy and 60.92 ± 6.68% macro-F1. Corresponding balanced accuracies were 78.77 ± 7.24% for ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B0 and 54.13 ± 4.95% for a radial basis function support vector machine using 22 image descriptors; summaries are unweighted means ± sample standard deviations across sessions. These findings support a compact and modular framework for image-based blueberry canopy-size phenotyping, in which unsupervised representation learning is separated from downstream supervised classification, although performance remained below supervised transfer learning. The reference trait measures image-relative canopy extent, not physically calibrated plant size.

title: Deep Percolation Risk and Optimal Irrigation Threshold for Sunflower Under Mulched Drip Irrigation: A HYDRUS-2D Modeling Study
abstract: Deep percolation induced by excessive irrigation represents a critical bottleneck limiting water use efficiency in sunflower fields under mulched drip irrigation in arid regions. However, systematic understanding of stage-specific allocation of water losses remains limited. This study conducted a field experiment on oilseed sunflower with three irrigation levels (300, 450, and 600 mm) in Shihezi, Xinjiang. The two-dimensional finite-element software, version 2.05 (HYDRUS-2D model) was calibrated and validated to simulate water balance components in the 0–60 cm soil profile across growth stages. The model demonstrated satisfactory performance, with coefficient of determination (R2) ≥ 0.70, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.025–0.039 cm3 cm−3 and Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) of 0.574–0.822. Results showed that evaporation responded weakly to irrigation amount (increasing by only 1.3 mm from 300 to 600 mm), while deep percolation increased nonlinearly, with the high-irrigation treatment exhibiting a percolation rate approximately five times that of the low-irrigation treatment. Crop water consumption exhibited pronounced stage-specific differences: during the seedling stage, evapotranspiration (92.29 mm) was derived almost entirely from soil evaporation; and from budding to filling (S2–S5), cumulative root water uptake accounted for 75–78% of seasonal total, while percolation losses during this period represented 91.5–96.3% of total deep percolation. An irrigation amount of 450 mm optimized the trade-off between grain yield and water use efficiency. A “small and frequent” irrigation strategy during S2–S5 is recommended to minimize deep percolation and enhance irrigation water use efficiency.

title: Tabular Foundation Models Versus Established Tabular Learners: A Regime-Stratified Critical Review
abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are pretrained once across many tables and applied to a new table by conditioning on its labelled rows, with no training on that table. They challenge gradient-boosted decision trees, the long-standing default for tabular prediction, but the published comparisons are hard to interpret, because studies differ in data regime, split design, baseline tuning, and metric. This review assesses the evidence regime by regime. From 76 peer-reviewed works selected under a documented protocol, it defines TFMs by reusable cross-table pretraining, organises them by pretraining data, context mechanism, scale, modality, and task interface, and compares them with tree ensembles, deep tabular networks, and tabular-to-image methods. Seven recurring claims are graded on peer review, evaluator independence, split match, baseline strength, and replication, with all scores published. One claim is strongly supported: on small-to-medium independent and identically distributed tables, TFMs match or exceed tuned tree ensembles without per-dataset tuning. Tuned tree-based and deep models remain as strong or stronger on temporal, feature-engineered data; above 10,000 rows the evidence is developer-reported except for one independent clinical benchmark; and no eligible study tests a frozen TFM under a grouped split or beyond its feature envelope. Tabular-to-image methods win only on small or very high-dimensional tables. Among the comparison-bearing studies, about one in ten use a deployment-matched split, none of them an independent evaluation of a TFM, and more than half of those evaluating a pretrained model report no contamination check. A reporting checklist, an evidence ladder, and seven research directions turn these findings into practice.

title: Machine Learning and SHAP for Morphological Feature Identification of Longjing Tea Straightness
abstract: The sensory evaluation of Longjing tea quality relies predominantly on subjective human judgment. Straightness is a critical sensory descriptor in the morphological quality assessment of Longjing tea, which lacks objective and quantifiable criteria. To objectively quantify this descriptor from a morphological perspective, this study developed an interpretable machine learning framework that integrates computer vision and SHAP analysis to digitally characterize the sensory attribute of straightness. Nine morphological features were extracted from Longjing tea samples collected across major production regions, including six contour-based and three skeleton-based descriptors. Three classification models, namely random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and support vector machine (SVM), were constructed and compared based on morphological features. SHAP analysis was employed to interpret model decisions, identifying three core morphological determinants, length ratio (lr), standard deviation (sd) and rectangularity (R), which consistently ranked highest in both univariate effect sizes and cross-model feature importance, with Cliff’s δ of 0.93, 0.81 and −0.78, respectively. By establishing a quantitative link between morphological features and sensory terminology, this study offers an interpretable tool for automated tea quality evaluation, with broader implications for digital standardization in quality evaluation of agricultural products.

title: Forecasting Post-Pandemic Tourism Recovery: Counterfactual Benchmarks, Intervention Models and Value–Volume Asymmetry in Greece
abstract: Whether tourism has recovered from the COVID-19 shock depends on the benchmark used. This study combines interrupted time-series models, structural-break detection, an event-study specification and counterfactual forecasts to quantify the shock and recovery of Greek tourism using 132 monthly observations for 2015–2025. A counterfactual path is forecast from a trend–seasonal model estimated on pre-pandemic data, validated out of sample against seasonal-naïve, exponential-smoothing and SARIMA benchmarks, and compared with SARIMA, damped-trend ETS and growth-scenario alternatives; a sieve bootstrap quantifies the uncertainty of shortfalls and recovery dates. Travel receipts, inbound traveler flows and receipts per traveler are compared. Receipts and arrivals contracted by approximately 83%, a finding that was robust across intervention dates, HAC bandwidths and serially correlated-error specifications, whereas a single constant recovery slope is not supported. Both indicators regained their 2019 levels in April 2023 under all rules. Relative to the counterfactual, receipts met a three-month criterion in February 2024 while arrivals had not by end-2025; receipts cross first with probability 0.64, but the dates depend on the run-length rule and the assumed pre-pandemic growth, and in real terms the post-2022 lead of receipts reflects prices, not higher spending per traveler. Domestic accommodation demand resisted the shock better; foreign demand rebounded faster.

title: From E-Commerce to AI Commerce: Rethinking the Consumer Journey in the Era of AI Agents
abstract: The emergence of increasingly autonomous Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents is reshaping how consumers search for information, evaluate alternatives, and make purchasing decisions. While existing consumer journey models have incorporated AI primarily as a decision-support technology, they provide limited conceptual guidance for understanding situations in which AI agents perform purchasing activities on consumers’ behalf. Drawing on consumer journey theory, AI-enabled commerce, and human–AI collaboration research, this conceptual paper adopts a theory-adaptation approach to examine how established frameworks may be extended to account for emerging forms of delegated decision-making. We propose the Human–AI Collaborative Consumer Journey, a framework that conceptualizes purchasing as a collaborative process involving consumers and consumer-authorized AI agents across different stages of the journey. Its central contribution is the concept of Delegated Consumer Agency (DCA), defined as the configuration of authority consumers grant AI agents to perform cognitive or operational purchasing activities within predefined goals and constraints. The framework highlights how human and AI participation may vary across purchasing contexts and identifies implications for consumer autonomy, decision-making, and e-commerce management. Finally, six research propositions and a future research agenda are presented to guide empirical investigation.
