title: Analysis of Supply Information, Code Bidding, and Efficiency in Repetitive Simultaneous Ascending Online Auctions: A Study of India's eNAM Digital Agricultural Market
abstract: This paper analyzes a Repetitive Simultaneous Ascending Auction (RSAA) mechanism employed in India's eNAM digital agricultural market. RSAA is characterized by full seasonal supply transparency and a strategic seller option to reject equilibrium bids. We develop a model of the RSAA game with inter-round strategic dependence and endogenous seller entry, and we find conditions for collusion formation. Using transaction-level data, we empirically validate the emergence of code bidding, a tacit collusive strategy sustained by low bidder concentration and shared supply information. The results show that demand-side coordination systematically reduces price competition. Moreover, the coexistence of supply transparency and strategic rejection introduces significant allocative inefficiencies despite the ascending-price format. These findings offer novel insights for auctions and market design, particularly concerning collusion vulnerability and efficiency in agricultural and digital commodity markets.

title: Noise-Regularized Training for Learned Image Compression
abstract: Learned image compression (LIC) is trained almost exclusively on clean images: the only stochastic perturbation in the loop is an additive uniform proxy injected in the latent domain to keep the entropy model differentiable. Outside compression, by contrast, a long line of work---from Tikhonov regularization and contractive autoencoders through denoising score matching and modern diffusion models---has established that Gaussian noise at the input of a network with a clean target acts as a structured probe of the data manifold rather than as data augmentation. Building on this view, we introduce noise-regularized training for LIC: at every training step we add Gaussian noise to the encoder input while keeping the distortion target, the latent uniform proxy, the hyperprior, and the entropy coding pipeline unchanged. The recipe is architecture-agnostic and adds essentially no training or inference overhead. Across backbones and operating regimes it yields consistent BD-Rate gains: -2.60% on a reproduced ELIC and -0.85% / -1.05% / -2.38% on the Base/Medium/Large scales of a variable-rate DMCI codec, with DMCI-Large reaching -22.02% against VTM-22.0. A second-order expansion of the noisy RD loss accounts for these gains: because the noise enters upstream of the analysis transform, it converts the clean RD objective into a structured $O(σ^{2})$ regularizer comprising an information-weighted encoder-Jacobian penalty (rate side) and a Frobenius contractive penalty on the end-to-end reconstruction map (distortion side). A finite-difference Lipschitz analysis shows corresponding sensitivity reductions of ~12% for the encoder and ~8% for the end-to-end codec, while an exact-JVP test further shows preferential contraction of high-information directions. Code and trained models are available at https://github.com/Googolxx/NoiseRegu-LIC.

title: DMAJOR: A JWST Legacy Survey of Protoplanetary Disks
abstract: We propose an infrared imaging survey of resolved protoplanetary disks spanning a range of galactic environments, directly mapping the 3D structure of planet-forming disks across the IR. DMAJOR (Disk Motions and Architectures JWST Observational Reference survey), our legacy survey, will deliver a benchmark sample to reveal structure and connection to environment. The exquisite stability of JWST allows us to probe for variability with a time-scheduled revisit strategy, while its sensitivity and resolution open a window on disks unobservable from the ground. A uniform sample will reveal how small grains and ice are distributed in protoplanetary disks, how scattered light structures relate to large-scale environmental features, and identify new companions. To achieve this, DMAJOR takes advantage of model-based data analysis using telemetry and mutual calibration to enhance processed data products while minimizing telescope overheads.

title: WorldMind: Test-Time Scaling for Visual Spatial Reasoning through Latent World Simulation
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have continuous deficiency in spatial reasoning tasks that require \emph{mental spatial transformation}, such as reasoning under hypothetical changes in viewpoint or position, known as perspective-taking tasks. Existing approaches either scale linguistic reasoning or augment VLMs with static geometric representations, but neither directly enables active transformation of the represented scene. World models offer this capability, yet existing systems typically communicate through synthesized RGB images, introducing a latent-to-pixel-to-latent bottleneck. We introduce \emph{WorldMind}, a framework for test-time scaling of spatial reasoning through latent world simulation. Given a query and observation, the VLM selects useful spatial transformations, while a world model executes them and exposes aligned intermediate latent features directly to the VLM. The resulting latent evidence is incorporated into subsequent reasoning steps, enabling iterative spatial simulation without repeatedly decoding imagined states into pixels. To optimize this interaction, WorldMind further employs process-verifiable reinforcement learning that rewards reasoning progress only when the associated action and latent transition are valid. WorldMind thus scales spatial reasoning by allocating additional inference-time computation to active world simulation rather than generating more language or pixels. Across VSI-Bench, MMSI-Bench, and MindCube-Tiny, WorldMind achieves an average improvement of 16.0% over the base VLM and 8.3% over the strongest RGB-based world simulation.

title: DeepResearch RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models for Deep Research Report
abstract: Empowered by Large Language Models (LLMs), deep research systems integrate online information into research reports through multi-step web searching and information synthesis. Evaluating these reports presents a significant challenge due to their long context, high information density, and domain specificity, necessitating the use of AI evaluation as a substitute for prohibitively expensive human assessment. However, few studies have examined the effectiveness of existing reward models or LLMs in understanding and evaluating such research reports. To bridge this gap, we introduce DeepResearch RewardBench, the first benchmark dedicated to evaluating reward modeling for research reports. We collect diverse report candidates from multiple agents or tool-augmented LLMs. These candidates are scored using query-specific golden rubrics, and we ensure data quality and difficulty through a combination of multi-round filtering and human verification. Our benchmark comprises preference datasets formatted as pairs, triplets, and quadruplets to test ranking capabilities across varying levels of difficulty. Extensive experiments demonstrate that while current reward models handle general coherence effectively, their performance significantly degrades when evaluating research reports. Generative LLMs acting as judges demonstrate comprehensive superiority in this domain, with comparative evaluation proving more effective than direct scoring methods. We anticipate that this benchmark will serve as a vital testbed for the evaluation and advancement of research agents.

title: Generative Active Learning for Label-Efficient Pan-Organ Ultrasound Diagnosis
abstract: Medical ultrasound (US) enables real-time, non-invasive diagnosis, yet building US-based AI systems is limited by data scarcity, costly expert annotation, and limited cross-center generalizability. Privacy constraints and instance-level reporting hinder the collection of diverse abnormal cases and frame-level labels, while repeated retraining for new centers increases computational cost. We introduce EvoDiff, a generative active learning framework that integrates diffusion modelling with information-theoretic objectives, evolutionary search, and curriculum-based sampling to select informative samples across heterogeneous US datasets. EvoDiff formulates sample selection as a generate-to-retrieve process, in which diffusion-based optimization in feature space guided by information gain produces synthetic probes, and only the real unlabeled samples retrieved by these probes are annotated and used for downstream training. Across six benchmarks covering fifteen datasets and 16,696 images, we evaluate EvoDiff on convolutional network and transformer-based foundation model. EvoDiff approaches fully supervised performance with substantially fewer labels, outperforms active learning baselines, and improves foundation model generalization under cross-domain external validation on unseen cohorts. A reader study with six radiologists indicates the potential to support clinical annotation workflows, with a model-based estimated 24% to 84% reduction in annotation workload at matched downstream performance.

title: Physics-Based Differentiable Beamforming for Deep Learning-Based Contrast Enhanced Ultrasound Super-Resolution Imaging
abstract: Ultrasound is widely used for vascular imaging because it is non-invasive, real-time, and cost-effective. However, its spatial resolution remains limited by diffraction to an order of the acoustic wavelength. This limitation is particularly restrictive for imaging of the microvasculature and high-resolution vector-flow-imaging. In this work, we present a multi-channel physics-based deep learning approach to super-resolve monodisperse microbubbles directly from multi-channel radio-frequency (RF) data. We also present a novel image-based metric for model evaluation. The proposed pipeline combines a learnable deconvolution network with a differentiable beamforming layer, enabling a direct deconvolution of the microbubble (MB) signature prior to image formation. By operating on multi-channel RF data, the method aims to improve localization robustness in the presence of dense microbubble populations and deconvolve the lateral direction in a relatively low-frequency regime (1.7 MHz) where MBs exhibit nonlinear behavior. The model is trained and evaluated on simulated data using monodisperse lipid-coated MBs over a broad range of acoustic pressures and microbubble densities. The proposed method improves the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) compared to the single-channel approach. It achieves sub-wavelength axial and lateral resolution while slightly improving robustness to dense microbubble populations outside the training domain. It also demonstrates generalizability across transmit configurations without requiring explicit training on each transmit configuration.

title: Semiprime Factorization with Discrete Diffusion and Beam Search: Scaling Laws
abstract: We demonstrate that transformer architectures trained with discrete denoising diffusion and decoded via guided test-time beam search can learn to recover the prime factors of semiprime integers directly from data. Our approach establishes a new frontier for learning-based semiprime factorization, successfully factoring 68-bit integers-a substantial advance over the prior 56-bit state of the art. While computationally less efficient than classical factoring algorithms, our model requires no domain-specific number-theoretic priors and learns purely from training examples. In practice, the diffusion model acts as a generative prior, identifying promising factor candidates where exact verification or lattice-based post-processing can complete the factorization. Furthermore, we derive empirical scaling laws relating approximation quality to training data volume, model size, and test-time computation. In contrast to language, problem size is the key driver of scaling behavior. Achieving a fixed accuracy on a held-out test set requires compute that scales exponentially with bit length. Consequently, our findings pose no threat to security, as the projected compute cost required to factorize cryptographically relevant integers remains prohibitive.

title: Reaching separated flow states by release and recapture with learned latent feedback
abstract: Targeting a prescribed flow configuration rather than an aerodynamic coefficient is challenging because the desired state may lie outside the natural attractor. We demonstrate cluster-based control in a learned vorticity representation for two-dimensional flow over a NACA0015 airfoil at $Re=500$ and $α=15^\circ$, using a localized streamwise momentum source near the leading edge. An actuation-enriched ensemble is compressed with a variational autoencoder and partitioned into macrostates. We optimize a continuous feedback law interpolating macrostate-dependent amplitudes without an explicit latent dynamical model. For an attached target, the optimized law approaches constant forcing, arrests vortex shedding and maintains the attached state. For a strongly separated target, the law instead establishes attachment, withdraws actuation so that the natural separation transient carries the flow through the target, and restores forcing to recapture attachment. Over the evaluation horizon, the closed-loop trajectory revisits the target approximately every three shedding periods. Companion open-loop calculations isolate the arrest, release and recapture processes.

title: Jais 3: Introducing Arabic-centric Agentic AI
abstract: We present Jais 3, a fleet of six open, Arabic-centric agentic language models ranging from 0.9B to 375B parameters. Jais 3 is built to complete tasks for Arabic speakers, not only to answer questions in plain text: it is trained to plan multi-step tasks, call tools and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, operate a terminal, search the web, and read, edit, and produce PDF, spreadsheet, and presentation files, while communicating with the user in Arabic. Instead of pretraining from scratch, we adapt each model of the fully open K2 Horizon fleet to Arabic through continual pretraining, followed by supervised fine-tuning (SFT), final token preference optimization (FTPO), and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). We combine natural Arabic text with translated, transliterated, and synthetic Arabic, and replay the base model's own training data to keep its reasoning, agentic, and English abilities. Jais 3 covers Modern Standard Arabic and the major regional dialects, follows instructions with Arabic-specific constraints, and inherits the 512K-token context window of K2 Horizon (all models except the 0.9B). To our knowledge, its 375B model is the largest open Arabic-centric language model to date. For evaluation, we revisit how Arabic models are assessed, moving to fully generative evaluation on audited Arabic benchmarks. Across model sizes, Jais 3 matches or outperforms open-weight models of comparable size on Arabic and agentic benchmarks, with particularly strong agentic capabilities and Arabic instruction following, and far fewer hallucinations. We release the weights and the checkpoints from every training stage of all six models, together with samples of the training data, the data recipes and training configurations, the training logs, the audited benchmarks, and the evaluation code.

authors.name: Sheikh Khalid bin Khalifa Al Nahyan

title: FAIR Universe Weak Lensing ML Uncertainty Challenge: Dataset and Cosmological Inference Competition
abstract: Weak gravitational lensing is a powerful cosmological probe that enables direct mapping of the matter distribution and precise constraints on the fundamental parameters governing structure formation in the universe. In recent years, machine learning has shown strong potential for extracting cosmological information from weak-lensing data beyond traditional summary statistics. However, progress has been limited by the lack of standardized benchmarks that capture the complexity of the dataset, simulator imperfections, and various systematic biases encountered in realistic analyses. To address this gap, we present the FAIR Universe Weak Lensing Machine Learning Uncertainty Challenge, one of the NeurIPS 2025 competitions, as a benchmark dataset and evaluation study. Our dataset reflects realistic weak-lensing observations, incorporating multiple systematic biases, and thereby providing a controlled testbed for robust cosmological inference under uncertainties. We summarize the main methodological advances developed by the winners of our challenge, including data augmentation with conditional optimal transport, an AI-agent-driven approach for parameter inference, ensemble learning, Vision Transformer-based architectures, and physics-informed feature integration. By unifying the benchmark dataset and the winning solutions, this work provides a community resource for developing and evaluating machine learning methods for weak lensing cosmology and, more broadly, for scientific inference under systematic uncertainties.

title: The microstructure of information through mean field learning interaction
abstract: We study how knowledge about partially observable model parameters is being created and propagated in large scale systems. Information is generated from observational signals whose dynamics depend endogenously on the learning history, the learning duration, the decisions and the related costs encountered by a continuum of decision makers. Such characteristics give rise to a new class of sequential testing problems in which there is continuous endogenous feedback. Adopting the classical approach of Shiryaev, we relate the problem to an optimal stopping one for the representative belief process, whose generator now depends on the evolving interactions. Considering a fixed point for the latter, we introduce a notion of mean field game and prove the existence of an equilibrium. Our arguments, which are based on a combination of pde and probabilistic techniques, involve a detailed analysis of the underlying variational inequality and the geometry, stability and continuity of the free boundaries.

title: Dynamical Light-Matter Coupling with Protected Superconducting Oscillators
abstract: Superconducting circuits hosting long-lived bosonic modes are an excellent platform for emulating the dynamics of light and matter and exploiting them for quantum information processing. The space of accessible dynamics is greatly extended by introducing the frequency tunability of artificial atoms, whereby the interactions with the light field of a microwave cavity can be modified on demand. However, using external flux bias to control the frequency of transmons introduces significant losses to coupled cavities, reducing their single-photon lifetimes to a few tens of $μ$s. These imperfections compromise the usefulness of the bosonic mode, which loses its ability to store and manipulate the quantum information of many-photon states. This thesis investigates the issue and demonstrates how to enhance the flux control of microwave cavities without compromising protection. Several hardware solutions were explored, including off-plane remote flux sources routed by a magnetic hose, and lithographically printed on-chip lines equipped with multiple stages of filtering. These developments equip the systems with broadband flux control and photon lifetimes of several hundred $μ$s. They enable the real-time manipulation of the two central parameters of the Rabi model: detuning and coupling strength. This flexibility translates into operational primitives of interest, such as the calibration of nonlinearities to different interaction regimes, the activation of parametric resonances with adjustable coupling strengths, and the use of number-selective transmon-cavity transitions for qudit state preparation and control. These results lay the groundwork for exploring richer synthetic light-matter systems, controlling cavities with more complex nonlinear circuits, and engineering driven-dissipative systems with applications in quantum computation and sensing.

title: Sample complexity and scalability of adaptive-sampling trust-region methods for zeroth-order stochastic optimization --- Part I: common random numbers meet supermartingales
abstract: We analyze adaptive sampling stochastic model-based trust-region methods that build their models in random subspaces and use common random numbers (CRN) within an iteration, and obtain, within a STORM-type analysis, the first $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ bound on the number of function evaluations needed to reach $\varepsilon$-stationarity, both almost surely and in expectation. The subspace model reduces the per-iteration computational cost, which allows scalability. The analysis relies on a general framework for the complexity of adaptive stochastic processes that carries the almost-sure analysis of ASTRO-DF into the STORM setting and adds expected bounds by a direct counting argument, without the renewal-reward argument of Blanchet et al. (2019). The bounds are obtained for two variants of a stochastic model-based trust-region method that differ in how the function evaluations used to measure progress are generated. The first algorithm, ASTRA-F, proceeds in a STORM-like manner: the trial point and the incumbent are re-evaluated on an independent set of replications, so that the estimates entering the acceptance test are independent of the model, as every existing STORM-type analysis requires their accuracy to be assessed conditionally on the model. The second, ASTRA-R, allows a practical approach: the trial point is evaluated on the replications already drawn to build the model, which avoids re-evaluating the incumbent, needs one adaptive sample size per iteration instead of two, and reduces the randomness entering the iteration. To our knowledge, no STORM-type analysis has been able to accommodate the latter approach as the accuracy of an estimate at a point chosen from the samples cannot be assessed conditionally on the model; we overcome this with a probabilistic chaining argument.

title: SIRIS: Can LLMs Tell When Simulation Errors Matter in AI-Driven Systems Research
abstract: LLM agents increasingly drive systems research and rely on simulators to evaluate candidate designs at scale. Simulators are imperfect by design: their modeling limitations can distort predictions yet leave the recommended design correct, or change which design should be selected. We introduce Siris to test whether LLMs can tell these cases apart, judging from their systems understanding when a limitation invalidates the simulator's recommendation. By perturbing a simulator, Siris constructs workload pairs with the same candidates, limitation, and simulator recommendation. The perturbation changes predictions on both workloads, yet a reference simulator supports the recommendation on only one. Evaluating thirteen frontier LLMs on LLM serving design problems, we find that identifying a limitation does not ensure a correct choice, and even the strongest models sometimes abandon valid recommendations. Self-correction through a review turn helps these models restore valid choices but introduces new errors in several others. These findings motivate evaluating systems understanding through design decisions under imperfect simulators.

title: URL-Sim: Unified and Regulated LiDAR Simulation for High-Fidelity Reconstruction of Dynamic Driving Scenes
abstract: Reconstructing high-fidelity LiDAR simulation scenes from real-world driving logs is essential for cost-effective safety validation of autonomous driving systems. While simulators based on Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) achieve realistic scene reconstruction, their large-scale adoption is limited by slow rendering speeds. Recent 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) approaches have improved rendering efficiency through explicit primitive representation and differentiable rasterization. However, existing 3DGS-based methods remain largely restricted to rigid vehicles and produce redundant primitives through unconstrained densification. To address these limitations, we propose URL-Sim, a unified and regulated dynamic LiDAR simulation framework. URL-Sim constructs a dynamic Gaussian scene graph that decouples the modeling of traffic participants, including vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists, enabling accurate reconstruction of heterogeneous dynamic objects within a single framework. It further introduces a regulated Gaussian densification strategy that ranks primitives with multi-dimensional importance scores and allocates Gaussians to the most critical regions while keeping the total primitive count bounded. Experiments on the Waymo and KITTI-360 datasets demonstrate that URL-Sim achieves higher quantitative accuracy and visual quality than existing baselines under comparable primitive budgets, and accurately recovers the geometry and poses of diverse dynamic traffic participants.

title: NAVE: A Normalized, Adaptive Conformer for Antarctic Whale Vocalization Detection
abstract: Antarctic whale vocalization detection requires temporally localizing call boundaries in long underwater recordings and classifying them into predefined call types. Training reliable machine learning models for this task is difficult due to the variability and sparsity of whale calls in passive acoustic monitoring datasets. These difficulties are further amplified by time-varying noise that can mask whale calls and by site-specific ambient sound characteristics to which a trained model may not generalize. In this work, we present NAVE, a Conformer-based detector that improves whale-call detection via three components. First, its input representation combines per-bin complex mean subtraction, which suppresses constant site-specific ambient sound characteristics, with an additional per-channel energy normalization (PCEN) channel that adapts to temporal variations in the noise floor. Second, a frequency-dynamic stem processes these noise-aware representations with convolutions that adapt across the characteristic frequency bands of the target call types. Third, we use a Conformer backbone with a convolution kernel matched to the duration of the target calls that adds an inductive bias and improves temporal localization. We evaluate NAVE on BioDCASE 2026 Task 2 using leave-one-site-out cross-validation across the validation sites, which approximates deployment on unseen recording sites. A single NAVE model with a tuned per-class threshold exceeds the stronger WhaleVAD-BPN baseline, using no boundary-proposal network and no search over post-processing parameters. A controlled ablation study shows that the normalized front-end and a duration-matched convolutional kernel each contribute substantially to recovering the D downsweep, the hardest class for previous detectors, with the wide kernel giving the largest aggregate gain.

title: Beyond Access: A Learning-Centered Model of Digital Inclusion among Agricultural Women in Rural Pakistan
abstract: Digital inclusion among rural agricultural women cannot be described based on availability of devices and connectivity alone. This study examines the learning-related factors with Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Accessibility (IA) and meaningful utilization (MU) among rural agricultural women in Faisalabad District. Quantitative data from 384 participants were statistically analyzed followed by three focus group discussions in Faisalabad District by an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design. Formal Education (FE), Learning-Related and Contextual Constraints (LRCC), and Daily ICT Time (DIT) were examined in relation to ICT Accessibility (IA) and Meaningful Utilization (MU). In Model I, FE was neither significantly associated with nor an independent predictor of IA, whereas LRCC was positively associated with and significantly predicted IA. In Model II, FE was positively associated with and significantly predicted MU (β = 0.534), whereas LRCC had a small, non-significant bivariate association with MU but a small negative conditional coefficient. DIT was positively associated with FE and MU but negatively associated with IA and LRCC. In Model III, FE positively predicted DIT, whereas LRCC negatively predicted DIT. Qualitative data identified four interconnected domains: Literacy, Language Competence, and Digital Skills; Awareness of Digital Opportunities; Informal Learning and Support; and Contextual Conditions shaping learning opportunities. Integration indicates that IA represents an opportunity rather than an endpoint. FE, learning capabilities, social support, and contextual conditions help explain how women convert digital opportunities into purposeful use, while DIT represents intensity rather than meaningful utilization. Therefore, the study develops a Learning-Centered Model of Digital Inclusion that distinguishes access, exposure, and meaningful use.
journal: Journal of Qualitative Research in Education

title: Effect of Land use Types on Soil Properties within Federal College of Education Kontagora, Niger State, Nigeria
abstract: The impact of land use on soil properties was investigated for five (5) land use types (old orchard, sole beans farm, sole maize farm, soya beans farm and uncultivated land). From each of the identified land use types, samples of soil were collected from depths of 0–15 cm and 15–30 cm, prepared and analyzed in the laboratory for soil properties. The upper layer of the soils (that is, 0–15 cm) had relatively higher organic carbon content than the 15–30 cm depth, although not significantly different between the land use types as well as with depths. The results also revealed that there were no significant differences between the land use types in the contents of NO3-N, NH4-N, Fe, texture, pH, Ca and Na whereas soil properties such as total-N, available phosphorus, Mg and K were significantly different in the soils of the different land use types. The soils were all loamy sand by textural classification. Hence, it was recommended that that conventional tillage operation should be discontinued on the lands that are used for cultivation of crops to avert the risks of erosion because of the loose nature of the soils. Also, the adoption of appropriate management practices such as manure application can help to improve the soil texture and enhance the soils’ retentive capacities.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF AGRICULTURE AND EARTH SCIENCE

title: Digital Divide in Agricultural Extension: Exploring ICT Accessibility and Its Influence on Rural Farming Communities
abstract: This study explores the digital divide in agricultural extension by examining ICT accessibility and its impact on rural farming communities. Given the increasing role of technology in agriculture, understanding how ICT accessibility influences agricultural productivity, the effectiveness of extension services, and digital inclusion strategies is crucial. Using a combination of descriptive and correlation analyses, the research investigates the current state of ICT infrastructure in rural areas and its implications for farming practices. The findings reveal significant disparities in ICT accessibility among rural communities, with improved access correlating strongly with enhanced agricultural productivity (r = 0.65, p < 0.01) and more effective agricultural extension services (r = 0.72, p < 0.01). Furthermore, the study highlights the critical role of digital inclusion strategies in bridging the digital divide, with a strong correlation observed between effective strategies and higher ICT access (r = 0.78, p < 0.01). These results underscore the need for targeted investments in ICT infrastructure, the integration of technology into extension services, and the implementation of comprehensive digital inclusion strategies. Addressing these areas can significantly enhance the effectiveness of agricultural support services, improve productivity, and foster overall development in rural farming communities.

title: Relevance of Technological Development To Economic Growth in Africa: A Position Paper
abstract: Technological development is increasingly pivotal to Africa's aspirations for productivity, growth, structural transformation, and global competitiveness. This position paper argues that technology should be viewed as an essential component of Africa's economic-growth strategy. Technology can enhance productivity, slash transaction costs, expand market accessibility, back up financial inclusion and create novel economic opportunities. However, its merits depend on complementary investments in human capital, digital infrastructure, energy, research and development, finance and effective institutions. Recent evidence shows that digital infrastructure promotes innovation in Africa, particularly when supported by human capital (Osei, 2024), while technological innovation and human capital jointly contribute to industrial productivity and competitiveness (Awode & Oduola, 2024). The paper examines the major technological opportunities and impediments shaping Africa's development, including digitalisation, artificial intelligence, automation, fintech, smart agriculture, digital health and emerging mobility. It further highlights continuous challenges such as insufficient infrastructure, unreliable energy, limited digital skills, weak research capacity, financing constraints and institutional gaps. The paper argues that addressing these constraints needs coordinated policies that join technological development with education, industrialisation, entrepreneurship and inclusive economic transformation. Africa must therefore move beyond technology consumption towards technology adaptation, production and innovation. Empowering local technological capabilities and regional cooperation is necessary for ensuring that technological progress result in sustainable, inclusive and broad-based economic growth across the continent.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT

title: Computer Vision by YOLOs for Detection of Major Diseases in Vietnamese Custard Apple Using Fruit Imagery
abstract: Amid Vietnam rapid digital transformation in agriculture, the integration of artificial intelligence technologies for identifying, monitoring, and predicting crop pests and diseases has emerged as an inevitable trend.

title: Integrating Digital Information Retrieval Systems and E-Resources for Sustainable Development in Nigeria
abstract: This paper examines how digital information retrieval systems and electronic resources can help advance sustainable development in Nigeria. As the country works towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), having easy access to organized information is increasingly important in education, healthcare, agriculture, and governance. The study reviews current digitization efforts at Nigeria's National Library, Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) digital platforms for beneficiary institutions, including the National Repository of Nigeria and the Online Public Access Catalogue, as well as initiatives like the Raw Materials Research and Development Council (RMRDC) Digital Archive and E-Library System. The article discusses how structured information management, based on linked data principles and open access knowledge platforms like Wikidata and Wikibase, can improve discoverability, preservation, and use of Nigerian intellectual and cultural resources. A mixed-methods approach, using document analysis and case studies, shows that while progress has been made in building digital infrastructure, challenges remain. These include a lack of digitization equipment and internet connectivity, inconsistent metadata standards, and gaps in digital literacy. The findings indicate that integrated information systems can significantly enhance research efficiency, support evidence-based policymaking, and preserve indigenous knowledge for future generations. The article ends with suggestions for aligning policies, investing in infrastructure, building capacity, and encouraging public-private partnerships to enhance the role of digital information systems in Nigeria's sustainable development efforts.

title: Epidemiological Modeling of Seasonal Influenza Through Periodic Mean-Reverting Stochastic Processes
abstract: Seasonal influenza follows annual cycles, but variation in epidemic magnitude and timing complicates preparedness. We applied periodic mean reverting stochastic differential equations (SDEs) to seven seasons of weekly Texas influenza surveillance data. Missing observations were imputed using MissForest and compared with four alternative methods. Stochastic variability was modeled using {sigma}X(t) dW(t), with p = 1/2,2/3,5/6, and 1, representing square root, intermediate sublinear, and multiplicative diffusion. Each specification was evaluated for direct influenza modeling and within a susceptible, exposed, infectious , and recovered model incorporating waning immunity, where the SDE governed transmission. Parameters were estimated using least squares and approximate maximum likelihood for direct models and sample-proportion weighted least squares for stochastic SEIR models. Model-based parametric bootstrap assessed direct-model parameter uncertainty. For direct modeling, p = 1/2 achieved the lowest RMSE (712.8) and AIC (5383.0), with similar AIC for p = 2/3 (5383.2). For stochastic SEIR modeling, p = 1 achieved the lowest RMSE (0.02926), compared with 0.03506 for p = 1/2. The deterministic SEIR model yielded R = 1.158. Transmission peaked approximately 10 weeks before infectious prevalence, while stochastic transmission generated variation in epidemic peak timing. Bootstrap analysis identified dependence between mean-reversion and diffusion parameters. Overall, the appropriate diffusion structure depended on the epidemiological quantity modeled, supporting flexible characterization of seasonal transmission variability while requiring prospective validation before operational forecasting.

title: EIN-RECAP: Evidence-Grounded Multi-Agent Summarization and Retrieval of Infectious-Disease Expert Discussions
abstract: Infectious disease experts exchange practical knowledge through clinical discussions, but identifying relevant information across years of conversations is difficult. These discussions often contain differing opinions and emerging observations that are not yet reflected in published evidence. We present EIN-RECAP, an AI-assisted platform developed with Emerging Infections Network (EIN) experts and deployed in beta to summarize and search historical discussions. The system combines retrieval-grounded summarization, citation validation, and hybrid search while distinguishing published evidence from community experience. We evaluated summarization methods across 3,185 threads and conducted blinded expert review on a recent subset. Although a multi-agent workflow achieved stronger automated scores, experts favored a simpler generation pipeline and identified repetition, inaccuracies, and overconfident recommendations in the more complex system. This feedback motivated an ensemble that improved discussion coverage and key clinical points on nine high-disagreement threads, although retrieval relevance remained a limitation. Our findings demonstrate the importance of expert involvement in clinical AI development and show why automated evaluation alone is insufficient to guide system selection.

title: Bridging the Digital Divide: The Efficacy of Mentor Ship-based Coaching in Enhancing AI Competencies for Agri-business Owners in West Region of Cameroon
abstract: This study investigated the efficacy of mentorship-based coaching in enhancing artificial intelligence (AI) competencies among agri-business owners in the West Region of Cameroon. Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to 384 agripreneurs who had participated in mentorship programs. A quantitative research design was adopted, and hypotheses were tested using multiple regression analysis with Ordinary Least Squares estimation. The findings reveal that mentorship programs have a positive and statistically significant influence on AI competency development (β = 0.413, p < 0.01), explaining approximately 30% of the variance (R² = 0.3012), while structured coaching plans exhibit a positive but insignificant influence (β = 0.128, p = 0.078). The study concludes that mentorship-based coaching serves as an effective mechanism for bridging the digital divide and enhancing AI competencies among agri-business owners. The study recommends that agricultural organizations implement structured mentorship programs incorporating practical AI training and specifically target women agripreneurs who show greater responsiveness to such interventions.
journal: JALINGO JOURNAL OF SOCIAL AND MANAGEMENT SCIENCES

title: Green Finance and Sustainable Investment Strategies for Climate-Resilient Economies
abstract: Climate shocks are making economic fragility more costly, and green finance is becoming more important for financing investments that mitigate it. This paper explores the relationship between green finance intensity and the nature of sustainable investment strategies with respect to climate resilience, covering 96 economies categorized into four groups (advanced, emerging Asian, other emerging, and low-income economies). Six of these instruments were merged with a green finance intensity index, a climate resilience index, and carbon-intensity reduction to create the portfolio shares across the instruments. The sharply different financing models revealed in the results are evident: green bonds occupy 30.7 percent of portfolios in the advanced economies, but only 6.2 percent in the low-income economies, while resilient and adaptation infrastructure have the highest share in the latter (29.9 percent). There is a strong association between Green Finance intensity and Resilience (r = 0.86), with decreasing marginal returns beyond higher levels of intensity; while controlling for income and intensity, there is still explanatory power for adaptation spending (R² = 0.81). The results validate a differentiated approach: scale and diversify capital investments in places where there is low intensity, and focus investments in places where resilience needs are highest, in terms of adaptation.

title: AI-Enabled Decision Support Systems for Improving Public Administration Effectiveness
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming one of the sources for transforming public administration through introducing new techniques in information processing, policy analysis, service provision, resource management, and decision-making. Public organizations work in an information-intensive environment in which administrators have to analyze large amounts of structured and unstructured data, taking into account changes in the socio-economic, environmental, and technological environment. Traditional decision-making techniques can be restricted by fragmented information systems, manual information processing, limited analytic capacity, time delays in information processing, and difficulties in finding complex interrelations in large datasets. Integration of artificial intelligence techniques with databases, analytic models, visualization techniques, and current e-governance technologies in AI-enabled Decision Support Systems (DSS) creates an opportunity to overcome these limitations and provide administrators with information, predictions, recommendations, and scenarios for decision-making based on evidence. This paper analyzes the role of AI-enabled DSS in enhancing the efficiency of public administration through a conceptual and literature review approach. The study will focus on the evolution of DSS, application of AI in public administration, decision-making theories, technological, organizational, and governance issues. Conceptual framework is generated through the integration of decision-support concepts into the Technology–Organization–Environment framework. The use cases under discussion include applications in the development of policies, delivery of services to citizens, resource allocation, fraud detection, urban planning, healthcare, education, social services, and disaster response. Challenges associated with data accuracy, privacy issues, cybersecurity, biases of algorithms, explainability of decisions, legal aspects, digital divide, skills of personnel, and organizational barriers are discussed as well. The analysis shows that the utilization of AI technologies within decision support systems may increase the effectiveness, analytical capabilities, timeliness, forecasting abilities, monitoring and resource planning if there is relevant data and proper organizational and governance mechanisms. Nonetheless, the application of AI needs to be limited to a decision-support tool rather than a substitute for the human decision-making in public organizations.
journal: International Academic Journal of Social Sciences

title: An Intelligent Bookkeeping and Tax Filing Model for Farming Households Based on AI and Accounting Rules
abstract: With the advancement of digital village construction, farm households are increasingly operating online but commonly face practical difficulties such as disordered bookkeeping and cumbersome tax filing. Conventional enterprise-level fiscal and tax software, however, cannot accommodate the scenarios of farm households. To address this gap, this study integrates accounting principles, agriculture-related tax policies, and AI technologies such as optical character recognition (OCR) and natural language processing (NLP) to construct a lightweight, highly compliant prototype for intelligent bookkeeping and tax filing by farm households, and implements it on a WeChat mini-program platform. Retrospective simulation tests using historical operating data from 217 farm households show that the prototype significantly improves bookkeeping standardization rates and tax filing accuracy while effectively reducing fiscal and tax compliance risks. The standardized operating data it generates also provide a foundation for building a digital credit system for farm households. This study offers a reference for digital village construction and agriculture-related inclusive fiscal and tax services.

title: Osmotic stress tolerance at the juvenile developmental stage of wheat
abstract: Aim. To evaluate the level of tolerance of ten winter soft wheat varieties bred by the SGI-NCNS to osmotic stress simulated by a 12% PEG 6000 solution, to identify adaptive juvenile genotypes. Methods. Laboratory rapid screening method for breeding material for water deficit, morphometric analysis of vegetative organs, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), and calculation of the integrated tolerance index (ITₓ). Results. Under control conditions, differences among varieties were non-significant (p < 0.05). Osmotic stress caused significant differentiation of genotypes by morphometric parameters (p < 0.05). The highest adaptability was demonstrated by the line Erythrospermum 2437/16 (ITₓ = 0.81) and the cultivar Velychava (ITₓ = 0.78), maintaining the stability of organ growth processes under moisture deficit conditions. The cultivar Nasnaha proved to be the most sensitive to stress (ITₓ = 0.57) due to a significant slowdown in the development of underground and aboveground organs. Conclusions. Modeling stress with 12% PEG 6000 and evaluating integrated tolerance index effectively screens juvenile plant water deficit tolerance. Identified tolerant genotypes offer valuable source material for breeding. The results of the analysis of variance (p < 0.05) confirmed the reliability of the obtained data, while the clear differentiation of genotypes by the integrated tolerance index (ITx) demonstrated the effectiveness of approach.

title: Immune-metabolic crop management through phase-timed anti-stress interventions
abstract: Aim. To develop a phase–time management (PTM) framework linking the efficiency of stress-protective interventions to plant physiological state, and to define phase-specific protocols with verifiable field predictions. Methods. System analysis of plant molecular physiology literature, conceptual modelling of the SA–JA/ET–ABA–TOR multistable signalling network, comparative evaluation of stress modulators across plant states, and formulation of experimentally testable hypotheses for field validation. Results. The PTM concept is based on immune-metabolic multistability with five attractor states (S₁–S₅), hysteresis of signalling transitions, and defined sensitivity windows (PSW, RSW, BSW). Three phase-specific protocols are proposed: (A) cytokinin application during post-ABA recovery phase resulting in + 15% grain yield; (B) glycine betaine applied 72 h before stress preserving ≥ 40% cell wall invertase activity; (C) melatonin + nitrate applied after herbicide stress reducing SnRK1-dominant state duration by 2–3 days. Field diagnostic markers include Fv/Fm, leaf water potential, stomatal conductance, and leaf temperature. Conclusions. PTM represents a novel systems-level agronomic framework integrating plant physiological state into the timing and selection of stress-protective interventions. Proper alignment of compound, dose, and sensitivity window improves ROI to 9:1–15:1 compared to reactive management.

title: Weather and Agrometeorological Indices in Relation to Phenology, Growth and Yield of Rainfed Pearl Millet under Different Growing Environments
abstract: Agrometeorological assessment of crop phenology and productivity helps to understand crop–weather relationships and the effects of thermal and radiation resources on crop performance. In rainfed areas, where crop development is strongly influenced by prevailing weather conditions, thermal indices are useful for assessing phenological development, resource-use efficiency and yield. A field experiment was conducted during the Kharif season of 2022 at the Research Farm Area, Department of Agricultural Meteorology, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar, to study the effect of sowing dates and varieties on phenology, thermal indices, heat use efficiency and yield of rainfed pearl millet under semi-arid conditions. The experiment was laid out in a factorial randomised block design with three sowing dates (24th June, 18th July and 10th August) and three varieties (GHB 558, HHB 67 Improved and HHB 197), with four replications. Growing degree days, heliothermal units, photothermal units and heat use efficiency were calculated to assess the thermal and radiation conditions during crop growth. Heavy rainfall of 190.8 mm during Standard Meteorological Weeks 38th–39th caused prolonged waterlogging in the 10th August sown crop, severely damaging it before physiological maturity. The 24th June sown crop recorded greater accumulation of growing degree days, heliothermal units and photothermal units, a longer crop duration and a higher grain yield (3974.5 kg ha⁻¹) than the 18th July sowing (2976.3 kg ha⁻¹). It also recorded higher heat use efficiency (2.49 kg ha⁻¹ °Cday⁻¹) than the 18th July sowing (2.06 kg ha⁻¹ °Cday⁻¹). Among varieties, GHB 558 recorded the highest grain yield (4026.0 kg ha⁻¹), 1000-grain weight (9.98 g), biological yield (14531.3 kg ha⁻¹) and heat use efficiency (2.58 kg ha⁻¹ °Cday⁻¹). Delayed sowing reduced the accumulation of thermal indices and shortened the crop growing period. Grain yield showed significant positive relationships with growing degree days (r = 0.72**), heliothermal units (r = 0.73**) and photothermal units (r = 0.71**), while bright sunshine hours showed a strong positive relationship (r = 0.96**) and evening relative humidity showed a negative relationship (r = −0.84*). Regression analysis showed strong relationships between thermal indices and phenological development (R² = 0.97–0.99), whereas the combined model incorporating growing degree days, heliothermal units and photothermal units explained 54.2 per cent of the variation in grain yield (R² = 0.542, p = 0.001). The study indicated that timely sowing during late June, particularly with GHB 558, resulted in better utilisation of thermal resources and higher productivity of rainfed pearl millet, while delayed sowing increased the risk of yield reduction due to unfavourable weather conditions.
journal: International Journal of Plant & Soil Science

title: Hydraulic Audit and Techno-economic Comparison of Photovoltaic and Diesel Pumping for Drip Irrigation in the Maradi Valley, Niger
abstract: Aims: To audit an analytically sized, battery-backed photovoltaic (PV) drip-irrigation design for 1 ha in relation to borehole hydraulics and documented costs, and to compare it with direct-coupled PV and diesel pumping. Study Design: A design audit and numerical simulation study without field measurements. Place and Duration of Study: Djirataoua irrigation perimeter, Maradi, Niger (13.41° N, 7.14° E); reference design of January 2026, analysed in 2026. Methodology: An hourly model coupled FAO-56 crop water demand, PV output, a variable-speed submersible pump and tank and battery balances. Options were compared by the levelised cost of water (LCOW) and volumetric coverage, with Monte Carlo, Sobol and multi-objective analyses. The model was checked against the original PVsyst outputs but not validated with field data. Results: The main error was hydraulic: the design flow (23 m³ h⁻¹) was more than three times the borehole yield (7 m³ h⁻¹), the head was underestimated (20 instead of 25.4 m) and pump power was overestimated nearly threefold. A direct-coupled 3 kWp array with a 50 m³ tank met about 98 % of the seasonal demand; the January–February shortfall was set by the borehole, not by irradiation. At datasheet-based prices, direct PV, battery-backed PV and diesel cost 194, 201 and 190 FCFA m⁻³ (West African CFA franc): the battery did not reduce costs in the tested configurations, and solar was cheaper than diesel in about half of the Monte Carlo runs, depending mainly on the pump-set price. The reported internal rate of return (6.15) was an annuity factor. Conclusion: Such systems should be sized from a pumping test and the peak-day demand. The solar–diesel choice depends more on local pump-set prices than on sunshine, and groundwater sustainability must be assessed before any extension.

title: Contribution of Market Gardening to Household Food Security in DOUM-DOUM Commune, Lake Province, Chad
abstract: Objectives: Off-season market gardening is regarded as a means of diversifying diets and generating income. This study aimed to analyse the contribution of market gardening to household food security in DOUM-DOUM Commune, Lake Province. Study Design: Cross-sectional quantitative survey. Place and Duration of Study: DOUM-DOUM Commune, Lake Province, Chad, from November 2024 to April 2025. Methodology: A quantitative survey was conducted among 60 market-gardening households, with 59 usable questionnaires, randomly selected from three purposively selected villages. A structured questionnaire collected sociodemographic, agricultural, and economic data. A multiple linear regression model identified the determinants of annual income from market gardening. Household Dietary Diversity Scores (HDDS) and Food Consumption Scores (FCS) were calculated. Results: Households were predominantly male-headed (94.9%), aged 31- 40 years (40.7%), and had primary education only (76.3%). Onion (27.1%) and tomato (22.0%) were the main crops. Market gardening was the primary source of income for 30.5% of households. Mean annual income from market gardening was 548,200 FCFA. The regression model was globally significant (F 14, 44) = 12.57; P < 0.001; adjusted R² = 0.74) and showed that cultivated area (β = 0.814; P < 0.001), fertilization (β = 0.128; P = 0.025), and irrigation investment (β = 0.141; P = 0.011) significantly increased income. Access to credit had a positive but only marginally significant effect (β = 0.118; P = 0.056). High-income market-gardening households had an HDDS of 9.2 versus 6.4 for low-income households and a reduced lean season of 1.8 months versus 4.2 months. Conclusion: Market gardening effectively contributes to food security through daily self-consumption and monetary access to food. Improving access to land, fertilization and irrigation is a priority, while credit remains a secondary factor. These results argue for prioritizing interventions to sustainably strengthen food security in the Sahelo-lacustrine zone.

title: From Farm-level Tools to State-level Assessment: A Scoping Review of Dairy Sustainability Indicators
abstract: Dairy production is expected to deliver nutritious food, rural livelihoods and export earnings while reducing greenhouse gas emissions, nutrient losses and pressures on land, water, biodiversity and animal welfare. Indicators are the principal means by which these expectations are translated into measurable performance, yet they are developed for different purposes and at different scales, from on-farm diagnostic tools to sector inventories and jurisdiction-wide composite indices. This critical narrative review, conducted with a scoping purpose, maps how dairy sustainability indicators are constructed, applied and aggregated across the farm, supply-chain, regional and state or national levels, and evaluates whether information generated at one level can legitimately inform decisions at another. Peer-reviewed studies, methodological reviews and authoritative institutional sources were identified through multidisciplinary, agricultural, economic and regional scholarly indexes, supplemented by citation tracking, and were appraised qualitatively for relevance, transparency, representativeness and robustness. The synthesis shows that farm-level tools differ widely in normative framing, indicator logic, scoring and aggregation, so that tools applied to the same farms can produce divergent judgements. Environmental indicators are the most mature, but carbon footprints remain sensitive to allocation rules, emission-factor tiers and functional units, and intensity metrics often move in the opposite direction to absolute emissions that matter for state targets. Economic indicators are comparatively well supported by accountancy data, whereas social and animal-welfare indicators remain under-specified and are frequently lost or distorted during aggregation. State-level assessments follow four broad routes: weighting representative farm samples, top-down inventories, modelled regional typologies and composite indices built from administrative statistics. Each route carries characteristic risks, including unrepresentative sampling, spatial misallocation, leakage through imported feed and weighting choices that can reorder jurisdictions. Smallholder and mixed crop–livestock systems, which dominate milk supply in several countries, are poorly served by tools designed for specialised temperate farms. A nested indicator architecture, built on a verifiable core of farm data, explicit scaling rules and paired intensity and absolute metrics, is proposed as a defensible direction. Its validity remains to be demonstrated through longitudinal and cross-jurisdictional testing.
journal: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports

title: Digital Finance for Agriculture: Mobile Money, FinTech, Credit Access and Smallholder Investment
abstract: Digital finance promises to lower the costs of financial transactions, expand rural savings and credit, and improve the timing of agricultural investment. Yet access to an account is not equivalent to access to suitable finance, and the movement from digital transactions to farm productivity is neither automatic nor uniform. This critical narrative review examines peer-reviewed evidence on mobile money, digital savings, algorithmic credit, payment digitisation, and their relationships with smallholder investment, risk management and livelihoods. Evidence from randomised trials, panel studies, observational farm surveys, qualitative research and recent reviews is compared with attention to causal identification, agricultural seasonality, inclusion and consumer protection. The strongest findings concern reduced transfer frictions and improved opportunities for remittance-based consumption smoothing. More conditional evidence links mobile payments and savings to specific productive inputs; incentives and the timing of liquidity often determine whether financial access changes investment. Recent experimental work on agricultural digital credit shows greater input spending without reliably demonstrated improvements in harvest output or profits. Consumer risks, including data misuse, opaque pricing and adverse credit reporting, complicate welfare assessments. The review argues that agricultural digital finance should be appraised as an interconnected system of payments, liquidity, insurance, market relationships and safeguards rather than as an isolated application or financial inclusion metric. Research priorities include seasonally timed randomised evaluations, long-term farm profitability, distributional effects, interoperable value-chain payments and transparent risk-adjusted consumer outcomes. Digital finance may relax consequential frictions, but durable agricultural benefits depend on product design, institutions and the broader production environment.

title: Automatic Lesion Morphometrics Reliably Predict Sensorimotor Recovery After Spinal Cord Injury: A Longitudinal, Multicenter Neuroimaging Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE To evaluate automatic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived lesion morphometrics against manual measurements and their prognostic value for characterizing distinct acute to chronic neurological recovery trajectories after spinal cord injury (SCI). METHODS We studied a retrospective, multicenter cohort of cervical and thoracolumbar SCI patients who underwent routine clinical MRI at 3-4 weeks post-SCI and neurological examinations over 6 months. Lesion severity was quantified using both established manual measurements and a novel automatic approach. We assessed the between-method agreement of MRI-derived lesion morphometrics, including lesion length, lesion width, and tissue bridge width, and their ability to stratify patients according to 6-month motor and sensory outcomes. Data-driven prediction models were used to identify clinically meaningful lesion measures and their respective thresholds, differentiating subgroups of specific recovery profiles. RESULTS Eighty-three patients from eight sites were included. Automatically derived lesion morphometrics showed moderate to strong agreement with established manual measures (Spearman's ρ: 0.540-0.821, p < 0.001), capturing inter-individual differences in lesion severity and demonstrating comparable prognostic value. Lesion width represented the strongest predictor of 6-month neurological outcomes, splitting patients into recovery-specific subgroups. Patients with a smaller lesion width (threshold: 5.88-6.41 mm) demonstrated higher 6-month sensorimotor scores and superior recovery trajectories, while tissue bridges (threshold: 0.17 mm) further refined motor prediction-based stratification of more severely affected patients. INTERPRETATION Automatic MRI measures of lesion severity hold promise as scalable, time-efficient in vivo biomarkers of SCI prognosis, with potential for clinical adoption to guide treatment decisions and multicenter trial planning.
journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology

title: High-Entropy Complementary d-Band Decoupling of Redox Kinetics for Bidirectional Catalysis in Lithium-Sulfur Batteries.
abstract: The reversible conversion of sulfur and Li2S in lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries is limited by the bidirectional redox kinetics. A single-component catalyst is difficult to simultaneously meet the differentiated adsorption and catalytic requirements in the multi-step conversion of polysulfides. We propose a high-entropy complementary d-band center model, extending the classical d-band center theory to multi-metal systems. The complementary d-band centers of multiple metals align the HOMO and LUMO of sulfur species, coordinating the electron transfer balance and accelerating the redox kinetics. The multi-metal sites collaboratively construct a "highly efficient capture → cascade conversion → rapid desorption" closed-loop pathway, with the d-p hybridization network regulating the adsorption energy and effectively suppressing the shuttle effect. Based on this design, the high-entropy selenide catalyst with a customized electronic structure and strong synergy effect has achieved excellent cycle stability and rate performance in Li-S batteries.

title: UAV‐Based Canopy Equivalent Water Thickness for Variable‐Rate Drip Irrigation in Winter Wheat
abstract: Canopy equivalent water thickness (EWT) is a quantitative indicator of canopy water status. However, its application in variable‐rate drip irrigation remains insufficiently investigated. A two‐year lysimeter experiment was conducted in the North China Plain (NCP) using two winter wheat cultivars and four irrigation treatments: FI0, FI60, FI90 and variable‐rate irrigation (VRI). Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) multispectral imagery was used to estimate plot‐averaged canopy EWT at jointing, booting, flowering and grain filling. Twelve vegetation indices and four machine‐learning models were evaluated for EWT inversion. LightGBM performed best in 2025 (coefficient of determination [ R 2 ] = 0.716, root mean square error [RMSE] = 0.043 g cm −2 , relative prediction deviation [RPD] = 1.91), whereas the decision tree performed best in 2026 ( R 2 = 0.791, RMSE = 0.033 g cm −2 , RPD = 2.32). Plot‐averaged EWT increased from jointing to flowering and declined during grain filling, while red‐edge indices maintained relatively stable relationships with EWT. Compared with FI90, VRI reduced crop evapotranspiration by approximately 40% while maintaining grain yield close to FI60. The EWT‐based VRI achieved a favourable balance between grain yield and water input, demonstrating its potential for precision drip irrigation.

title: Value of Intratumoral and Peritumoral Ultrasound Radiomics Nomogram for Differential Diagnosis of C-TIRADS 4 Thyroid Nodules.
abstract: OBJECTIVE The Chinese Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (C-TIRADS) 4 thyroid nodules (TNs) have intricate sonographic features that potentially lead to overdiagnosis or misdiagnosis. This study aimed to improve the precision of differentiating C-TIRADS 4 TNs using radiomic nomograms that include both intratumoral and peritumoral features. METHODS A total of 337 patients with C-TIRADS 4 thyroid nodules confirmed by pathology or FNAB were retrospectively enrolled and randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 269) and a validation cohort (n = 68) at a ratio of 8:2. Radiomics features were extracted from intratumoral and peritumoral (1-3 mm) regions on B-mode ultrasound images. Feature stability was assessed using intraclass and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Key features were selected through a sequential process involving the Mann-Whitney U test, recursive feature elimination (RFE), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, followed by calculation of the radiomics score (Rad-score). Independent predictors were identified by univariate and multivariate logistic regression. Three models were constructed: a clinical and ultrasound model (Model 1), a radiomics model (Model 2), and a combined nomogram integrating both (Model 3). Model performance and clinical utility were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS Multivariate analysis showed that age, margin, echogenic foci, and the intratumoral and peritumoral 1 mm Rad-score were independent predictors for the benign or malignant nature of C-TIRADS 4 nodules (p 0.05), and DCA indicated that it provided the greatest clinical net benefit. CONCLUSION The nomogram integrating clinical characteristics, ultrasound characteristics, and intratumoral and peritumoral 1 mm Rad-score can distinguish benign from malignant C-TIRADS 4 TNs, with superior diagnostic performance compared to single-modality models. It may serve as a non-invasive and reliable tool to reduce unnecessary FNAB rates.

title: New Insight to Morphogenetic Movements Underlying Gastrulation in the Freshwater Gastropod Lymnaea stagnalis (Mollusca: Heterobranchia).
abstract: Gastropod molluscs, inhabiting marine, freshwater, and terrestrial environments, are a unique group to uncover the evolution of developmental pathways shaped by adaptation to novel environments. However, the detailed comparative data are available for a few marine gastropods only. We present here the first comprehensive, stage-by-stage description of early embryogenesis in a representative of freshwater gastropod molluscs. We visualized and characterized the cellular basis of morphogenetic movements in the pond snail Lymnaea stagnalis, from cleavage to late gastrula, using state-of-the-art microscopy. We traced dpMAPK localization during 3D organizer differentiation and endomesoderm segregation. For the first time, rhythmic embryonic pulsations, potentially regulating development through biomechanical forces, were demonstrated for Spiralia. We revealed a continuous network of long filopodia connecting all embryonic cells throughout development, and speculate that they may function as cytonemes. This finding suggests a putative structural basis for cell-cell communication in Lymnaea. We also provide novel insights into the morphogenetic movements of gastropod gastrulation demonstrating that in Lymnaea the segregation and internalization of the two germ layers-mesoderm and endoderm-are separated in time. Gastrulation initiates at the 25-cell stage and proceeds through three distinct phases: primary mesoderm formation; invagination of the vegetal plate composed of bottle-shaped endodermal cells; shaping and zippering of the blastopore. Cellular mechanisms underlying the endoderm segregation contribute to the elongation of the embryo, the displacement of the mouth Anlage toward the ventral side, and the approximation of the animal and vegetal poles. Our data provides new material for establishing Lymnaea as a valuable model for cutting-edge investigations in Evo-Devo.

title: Elective Neck Dissection in cT1-4 N0M0 Submandibular Gland Cancer.
abstract: OBJECTIVE To investigate occult nodal metastasis (ONM) and overall survival (OS) in patients undergoing elective neck dissection (END) for clinically node-negative submandibular gland cancer (SMGC). METHODS The 2006 to 2018 National Cancer Database was retrospectively reviewed for patients with cT1-4 N0M0 SMGC undergoing surgical resection. Linear, binary logistic, Kaplan-Meier, and Cox proportional hazards regression models were implemented. RESULTS A high proportion of patients were female (N = 710, 54.6%) and White (N = 1059, 82.5%) with adenoid cystic carcinoma histology (N = 567, 43.6%) classified as cT1 (N = 545, 41.9%). A minority of patients (N = 255, 19.6%) underwent END. Academic/research reporting facility, high grade, cT3, and cT4 classification were associated with higher odds of undergoing END; Medicare insurance was associated with lower odds (p < 0.05). ONM was identified in 63 (24.7%) patients undergoing END. The rate of ONM increased with cT classification (13.2% in cT1, 27.9% in cT2, 22.0% in cT3, and 50.0% in cT4) and grade (6.5% in well-differentiated, 9.5% in moderately differentiated, and 40.3% in poorly differentiated). END was not associated with OS (hazard ratio [HR] 1.11, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.84-1.46, p = 0.461). However, ONM was associated with worse OS (HR 3.69, 95% CI, 2.25-6.05, p < 0.001); 5-year OS for patients without and with ONM was 83% and 50%, respectively (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION END is performed frequently in SMGC but is not associated with OS. Although the rate of ONM approaches 25%, these findings suggest that END should not be routinely performed for prognostic purposes alone, especially in the absence of adverse features. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: 4

title: Autonomous Agricultural Robot Framework featuring Temporal Dynamic Graph Neural Network based Semantic Segmentation coupled with Novel Navigation Line Extraction for efficient field operation and intelligent decision making.
abstract: BACKGROUND Autonomous agricultural robots support precision farming and improve operational efficiency; however, reliable navigation in complex field environments remains challenging because of inconsistent lighting, variable soil textures, irregular crop growth patterns, and visual occlusions. These conditions hinder accurate crop row detection, semantic segmentation, and navigation line extraction. This study proposes an Autonomous Agricultural Robot Framework Featuring Temporal Dynamic Graph Neural Network Based Semantic Segmentation Coupled with Novel Navigation Line Extraction (AAR-TDGNN-SS-NLE) to improve navigable path identification and autonomous field operation. RESULTS RGB images of corn crop rows from the Crop Row Detection Dataset are annotated with ground-truth masks to distinguish traversable and non-traversable regions. Image preprocessing using the Inverse Unscented Kalman Filter (IUKF) includes noise reduction, normalization, resizing, and contrast enhancement. Geometric transformations and color adjustments are applied to increase dataset diversity and improve model generalization. Efficient Net-B7 performs pixel-level semantic segmentation, while the Human Evolutionary Optimization Algorithm (HEOA) optimizes model parameters. The Temporal Dynamic Graph Neural Network (TDGNN) subsequently extracts stable navigation lines by capturing temporal relationships, path curvature, and orientation. Performance is evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and intersection over union (IoU). The proposed AAR-TDGNN-SS-NLE framework achieves an overall accuracy of 98.01% and outperforms the existing DLSS-NNLE-AAR, SS-EID-FRNLE, and UDA-SS-AR frameworks according to the reported experimental results. CONCLUSION The proposed framework integrates semantic segmentation, evolutionary optimization, and temporal graph-based navigation line extraction to support accurate path identification and autonomous agricultural navigation. It offers potential for improving the efficiency of agricultural field operations and supporting intelligent decision-making in complex farming environments. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: 6-Shogaol Promotes Fatty Acid Oxidation and Osteogenic Differentiation in Aged Bone Marrow Mesenchymal Stem Cells Through Allosteric Regulation of Carnitine Palmitoyltransferase 1A.
abstract: Age-related osteoporosis is heavily driven by the senescent decline of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), characterized by impaired osteogenic differentiation and excessive lipid accumulation. Defective fatty acid oxidation (FAO) is a critical metabolic hallmark of this pathogenic shift. This study aimed to investigate whether 6-Shogaol (6S), a bioactive dietary compound, could rescue the osteogenic potential of senescent BMSCs by remodeling lipid metabolism. The effects of 6S were evaluated in vitro using replicative and D-galactose-induced senescent BMSC models, and in vivo using 18-month-old naturally aged mice. Underlying mechanisms were elucidated through transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses, oxygen consumption rate (OCR) measurements, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assays. 6S treatment effectively alleviated the senescence phenotype, reduced lipid droplet accumulation, and restored osteogenic differentiation in aged BMSCs. In vivo administration of 6S significantly attenuated bone loss and improved trabecular microarchitecture in aged mice. Mechanistically, multi-omics and metabolic flux analyses revealed that 6S promoted FAO by enhancing the enzymatic activity of CPT1A via direct binding to the GLN30 residue. This binding allosterically increases the spatial distance between GLN30 and GLU3, thereby antagonizing the physiological inhibition of CPT1A by Malonyl-CoA (MCoA). Mutation of the GLN30 residue (Q30A) abolished the 6S-mediated restoration of FAO and osteogenic capacity. 6-Shogaol acts as a novel allosteric modulator of CPT1A. By specifically targeting the GLN30 residue to relieve Malonyl-CoA inhibition, 6S restores FAO homeostasis in senescent BMSCs and promotes osteogenesis, highlighting a promising metabolic intervention strategy for age-related osteoporosis.

title: Staying with the pack: connectivity constraints in an isolated wolf subpopulation
abstract: European gray wolf (Canis lupus) populations experienced severe range fragmentation due to human persecution, habitat loss, and prey depletion. In Portugal, the Iberian wolf (C. l. signatus) subpopulation south of Douro River faces a high extinction risk driven by long-term demographic decline and limited gene flow. This study aimed to identify the main factors limiting functional connectivity within this endangered subpopulation. We tested two hypotheses: isolation by distance (IBD), where genetic differentiation is primarily driven by geographic distance; and isolation by resistance (IBR), which posits that genetic differentiation is influenced by landscape and ecological factors that impede movement. Resistance surfaces were derived from habitat suitability models incorporating trade-offs between ecological resources and human disturbance. To ensure robust inference, we assessed wolf-dog admixture using Bayesian clustering and assignment to parental and hybrid classes. We identified 30 of the 39 wolves estimated to occur in the region, and conducted an individual-based landscape genetics analysis, relating pairwise genetic distances to geographic and resistance distances (i.e., least-cost distances) using multiple regression. Both hypotheses significantly explained genetic distances between individuals. However, after accounting for population structuring, their contributions decreased substantially, likely reflecting the influence of social structure and kinship. We suggest much of the remaining variance is largely shaped by high human-induced mortality, which limits long-distance dispersal. Improving connectivity in this wolf subpopulation requires addressing social and demographic barriers alongside landscape-level constraints. Mitigating human-wolf conflict and reducing mortality rates is essential for enhancing functional connectivity and ensuring the long-term viability of this endangered subpopulation.
