Capability-Opportunity-Motivation-Behavior (COM-B) Correlates of Physical Activity in People with Multiple Sclerosis Who Have Analogue Generalized Anxiety Disorder.
abstract: BACKGROUND Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) is prevalent, yet poorly managed among people with multiple sclerosis (MS). Physical activity (PA) may be a potential lifestyle, behavioral approach for managing GAD in MS. As a foundational step in developing PA behavior change interventions, this study applied the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation-Behavior (COM-B) model for explaining PA behavior in people with MS who have analogue GAD (AGAD). METHODS Participants (N = 320) prescreened for AGAD completed online surveys regarding PA (Godin Leisure Time Exercise Questionnaire (GLTEQ), Physical Activity Staging Questionnaire (PASQ)) and COM-B constructs. Participants were categorized into current PA groups based on GLTEQ scores, and long-term PA groups based on PASQ scores. Multivariate analysis of variance and discriminant function analysis (DFA) identified COM-B constructs that differentiated PA groups. RESULTS All COM-B constructs significantly differed among current and long-term PA groups. DFA identified Action Control, Intention, Self-efficacies (Action, Maintenance, Recovery), Action and Coping Planning, and Goal Setting as primary constructs differentiating PA groups. CONCLUSION This study identified factors within the Capability and Motivation domains of the COM-B model as primary correlates of PA in persons with MS and AGAD. Such results might guide the development of behavior change interventions for increasing PA and perhaps treating GAD in MS.

Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of farmers towards sustainable agriculture in the Barind Tract of Bangladesh
abstract: The global imperative to transition towards sustainable agriculture is particularly acute in vulnerable, resource-scarce regions such as the Barind Tract of Bangladesh, an area characterized by a semi-arid climate, low soil fertility, and acute water scarcity. Understanding the drivers of and barriers to adoption is critical, and the Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice (KAP) framework provides a useful analytical lens. This study assessed farmers’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices concerning sustainable agriculture and examined the socio-economic and institutional factors associated with each of the three KAP domains. Data were collected through structured, face-to-face interviews with 273 smallholder farmers selected via a multi-stage random sampling procedure in the Rajshahi district. Composite KAP scores were computed by summing item scores, and respondents were categorized on the basis of their obtained composite scores. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and three separate multiple linear regression models. The findings reveal a notable paradox: although farmers possess moderate to high levels of knowledge (mean = 19.27 out of 30) and largely favorable attitudes (mean = 56.34 out of 70), their actual adoption of sustainable practices remains moderate (mean = 18.42 out of a possible 38), exposing a persistent knowledge–practice gap. Annual farm income emerged as the strongest and most consistent positive correlate across all three KAP domains, underscoring economic capacity as a fundamental enabler of engagement with sustainable agriculture. Farming experience was positively associated with knowledge and attitude, cosmopoliteness with knowledge, and age negatively with knowledge, whereas formal education, training, and agricultural extension contact showed no statistically significant associations. The results suggest that adoption in this context is constrained less by cognitive limitations than by structural and economic barriers. Policy should therefore complement information campaigns with financial de-risking instruments, stronger market linkages for sustainably produced crops, and facilitative, farmer-centric extension approaches to help bridge the intention–action divide.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of land surface temperature and vegetation cover in Thanjavur district Tamil Nadu India using remote sensing and GIS
abstract: Land Surface Temperature (LST) and vegetation dynamics are widely recognized as reliable indicators of environmental change, urbanization, and climate variability. Understanding their spatial and temporal interactions is essential for sustainable environmental planning, particularly in agriculturally intensive regions experiencing rapid land-use transformation. This study investigates the spatio-temporal variations of LST and the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) in Thanjavur District, Tamil Nadu, India, using multi-temporal Landsat imagery acquired during 2011 and 2021. Satellite images were processed using standard remote sensing techniques to derive LST and NDVI, while Geographic Information System (GIS)-based spatial analysis was employed to evaluate block-level variations. A simple linear trend analysis was employed to project potential environmental conditions for 2031 based on observed temporal changes. The results indicate considerable spatial heterogeneity in both thermal conditions and vegetation cover across the district. During 2011, the highest LST (46 °C) was recorded in Ammapettai Block, whereas Thiruvonam exhibited the highest NDVI (0.7128), reflecting dense vegetation supported by the Cauvery Delta irrigation system. In 2021, Thanjavur Block emerged as the principal thermal hotspot (43 °C), while vegetation cover declined in several urban and peri-urban areas. The projected 2031 scenario suggests a continued increase in thermal intensity in rapidly developing regions together with a gradual reduction in vegetation density. Regression analysis showed a weak and statistically insignificant relationship between LST and NDVI (R² = 0.043; p = 0.477), indicating that surface temperature is influenced not only by vegetation but also by urban expansion, irrigation practices, land-use characteristics, and local environmental conditions. The study demonstrates the usefulness of integrating remote sensing and GIS techniques for long-term environmental monitoring and provides baseline information for sustainable land-use planning, urban greening, climate adaptation, and environmental management in the Cauvery Delta region.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and coupling coordination between urban expansion and carbon storage in the chengdu-chongqing urban agglomeration
abstract: Urban expansion, a prominent feature of global land-use change, profoundly influences terrestrial carbon dynamics and regional ecological security. Under the framework of green and low-carbon development, understanding the multiscale spatiotemporal coupling between urban expansion and carbon storage is vital for informing sustainable urbanization strategies. Taking the Chengdu-Chongqing urban agglomeration in western China as a representative case of rapid urbanization, this study integrates multitemporal remote-sensing data from 2000 to 2020 to investigate the dynamic patterns and interactions between urban growth and carbon storage. Carbon storage was quantified by integrating the InVEST model with the biomass expansion factor (BEF) method, which replaces the uniform class-mean carbon densities used in conventional InVEST applications with stock-volume-derived, province-specific forest biomass densities. The results indicate that: (1) built-up area increased from 3,140.3 km² in 2000 to 15,550.5 km² in 2020. After a slight slowdown during 2005–2010, absolute expansion accelerated markedly and reached its highest rate during 2015–2020, while the spatial pattern remained dominated by Chengdu and Chongqing; (2) regional carbon storage showed an overall increasing trend with significant spatial heterogeneity, with high-value zones primarily located in the northeastern and southwestern parts of the study area; (3) the coupling coordination degree (CCD) between urban expansion and carbon storage exhibited scale-dependent trajectories: the city-scale mean increased slightly from 0.368 in 2000 to 0.394 in 2020, whereas the county-scale mean decreased continuously from 0.557 to 0.490, with high-CCD counties concentrated in the forest-dominated periphery and low-CCD counties in the urbanized cores. These results provide an empirical basis for balancing urban development and ecological conservation in rapidly urbanizing regions.

title: Economic analysis of agricultural information systems (AIS) adoption in Jordan: determinants, productivity effects, and farm-level evidence
abstract: This study examines the economic dimensions of using Agricultural Information Systems (AIS) in the Jordanian agricultural sector. Using a mixed-methods approach, this study analyzes the determinants and productivity effects of adoption based on farm-level survey data from 842 agricultural holdings in 12 governorates, supplemented by retrospective data covering 2015–2024. Uses binary logistic regression with governorate fixed effects and heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors to account for the small number of clusters (12 governorates). The results show that digital infrastructure (β = 0.156, p < 0.001), farm income (β = 0.847, p < 0.001), and operator education (β = 0.423, p < 0.001) significantly increase the likelihood of adoption with Nagelkerke R² = 0.412. Distance from urban centers reduces the probability of adoption (β = −0.089, p = 0.001). Productivity associations are estimated using OLS regression. AIS-enabled farms exhibited 104.2% yield improvement and 51.5% higher water use efficiency compared to non-adopters. Production costs decreased by 28.5%, with an average payback period of 1.8–2.7 years. The model explains 81.4% of the variance (adjusted R² = 0.814) with AIS investment intensity and implementation quality as primary drivers. The study identify significant regional differences, with adoption rates ranging from 36.5% (Ma’an) to 58.6% (Amman). Financial barriers (72.8%), limited digital skills (67.4%) and lack of infrastructure (64.7%) are the biggest obstacles to adoption. The findings confirm that AIS adoption acts as a productivity-enhancing investment in water-scarce agricultural economies, although self-selection biases suggest that the observed associations may exaggerate causal effects. Policy implications emphasize targeted infrastructure investment and human capital development in peripheral areas to bridge the digital divide.

Phenethyl alcohol-assisted high-pressure homogenization enhances EPA preservation and facilitates lipid release from Nannochloropsis oceanica biomass during in vitro digestion.
abstract: Microalgal biomass is a sustainable and vegan source of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), but the rigid cell wall of Nannochloropsis sp. limits lipid release and its effective utilization in food and feed applications. This study investigated the effects of high-pressure homogenization (HPH), alone and in combination with phenethyl alcohol (PEA), a food-grade membrane-permeabilizing agent, on the disruption of Nannochloropsis oceanica cells. The impact of these treatments on lipid release and eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) retention was further evaluated using a standardized in vitro digestion model. Marked cell damage in N. oceanica was observed at the fourth pass during HPH. In contrast, PEA-assisted HPH induced substantial cell disruption as early as the second pass. These observations were confirmed by microscopy and trypan blue based membrane permeability assessment. Relative EPA content decreased by 2.56% points after HPH, while PEA+HPH limited the reduction to 1.70% points by reducing the number of required processing cycles. The combined PEA+HPH approach reduced cell aggregation and increased lipid release during in vitro digestion, from 13.02 ± 3.81% in untreated biomass to a maximum of 53.06 ± 2.55% in PEA+HPH treated biomass. Overall, these findings highlight the potential of PEA-assisted HPH processing to enhance the nutritional value of N. oceanica biomass.

title: Regulatory fragmentation in the EU insect-based food sector and potential implications for the development of an emerging food chain.
abstract: Insect-based foods (IBFs) are regulated in the European Union (EU) as Novel Foods through a centralized authorization procedure. However, the absence of specific hygiene requirements for establishments operating along the IBF supply chain in Annex III of Regulation (EC) No 853/2004, together with the possibility for Member States (MSs) to require their approval, may result in divergent approaches to their regulatory classification across the EU. Against this background, this study systematically examined national legal databases and the institutional websites of competent authorities (CAs) across the 27 MSs to assess how establishments producing, processing or marketing IBFs are classified and to discuss the potential implications for food business operators (FBOs) and CAs. Relevant national sources were retrieved for 16 MSs, whereas no specific information was identified for 11 MSs. Three models were identified: 1) a registration-based approach (12/16 MSs), 2) a conditional approval approach (3/16 MSs), and 3) a multi-tier hybrid approach including authorization (1/16 MSs). Further heterogeneity was observed in the delimitation between primary production and post-primary stages, as well as in the application of the identification mark in MSs requiring approval. These differences may affect legal certainty and potentially create non-uniform regulatory conditions for FBOs, while also complicating the work of CAs. These findings highlight the need for clarification at EU level regarding the regulatory classification of establishments operating along the IBF supply chain. Such clarification could enhance regulatory predictability, harmonize official controls and reduce internal market disparities.

title: Contrasting stage-associated succession and ecological assembly of bacterial and fungal communities during industrial sauce-flavor Baijiu heap fermentation.
abstract: Whether stage-associated community differentiation corresponds to inferred assembly processes and profile dissimilarities remains unclear in industrial sauce-flavor Baijiu heap fermentation. Pre-turn and post-turn samples from rounds R3-R7 of two consecutive production cycles were examined by integrating bacterial and fungal community profiles, βNTI-RCbray assembly assignments, PICRUSt2-predicted MetaCyc profiles, FUNGuild annotations, physicochemical measurements, GC-MS volatile profiles, and matched local temperatures. Exploratory pair-aligned models related each pair's assembly-process family (ProcessFamily) to annotation-profile or measured volatile-profile dissimilarity calculated from the same samples. After adjustment for Round and Position, Stage accounted for 1.85-2.01% of bacterial and 12.69-14.24% of fungal Bray-Curtis variation, while Round had the largest conditional share. Fungal Stage shares remained larger after temperature adjustment and across corresponding leave-one-round-out comparisons, without a greater prevalence of selection-related assignments. Adding round-specific time trends reduced Stage shares to 0.18-0.56% for bacteria and 0.62-1.44% for fungi, indicating substantial sensitivity to fermentation progression. In Cycle II, ProcessFamily associations with bacterial MetaCyc and fungal guild-profile dissimilarities had partial R2 values of 2.30% and 5.97%, respectively, with little change after physicochemical adjustment. Neither cross-cycle reproducibility nor a general correspondence with measured volatile-profile dissimilarity was established. These findings distinguish compositional differentiation from inferred assembly structure and ecological-annotation correspondence from measured chemical relationships. They identify fungal composition and pair-level annotation associations as candidates for further validation, without establishing an independent turning effect.

CasHyper: Modeling multi-factor interactions and asymmetric influence in cascade prediction via hypercomplex algebra
abstract: Cascade prediction aims to forecast the future evolution of information diffusion and is an important task in social network analysis. Most existing methods represent users and cascades in real-valued Euclidean spaces, which may offer limited capacity to model multi-factor interactions and asymmetric influence in complex diffusion processes. To address these challenges, we propose CasHyper, a hypercomplex-based cascade prediction framework that integrates hypercomplex algebra with graph neural networks and Transformers. CasHyper organizes user and cascade embeddings into multiple hypercomplex components, with each component encoding distinct latent factors, and uses structured algebraic operations to model cross-component interactions. The non-commutative hypercomplex product further yields order-dependent interaction representations, enabling the model to learn asymmetric influence among users. In the network encoding stage, a static heterogeneous graph channel captures user-user and user-cascade relations, while a Neural ODE-based dynamic channel models the continuous evolution of node states and edge weights. A hypercomplex Transformer with norm-preserving rotary transformations is then introduced to incorporate relative positional information into cascade sequence modeling. Finally, an interaction-aware module and a linear projection module are combined to estimate the probability of each candidate user participating next. Experiments on four real-world datasets show that CasHyper achieves competitive or better performance than the compared methods under the evaluated settings, including relative improvements of up to $43.24\%$ on Android and $18.43\%$ on Christianity in Hits@50.

Incentive-compatible risk preferences and sustainable land management adoption under climate risk: Evidence from semi-arid Kenya.
abstract: Sustainable land management (SLM) practices are widely promoted as an effective pathway for mitigating climate-induced production risks and enhancing agricultural sustainability. However, their uptake has remained low across Sub-Saharan Africa despite the associated benefits. Existing studies have primarily evaluated socio-economic and institutional determinants, with limited evidence on incentivized risk preference and loss aversion, particularly for multiple practice adoption. This gap is especially consequential in arid and semi-arid regions, where production uncertainty is high and adoption decisions are inherently risky. In South Eastern Kenya (SEK), recurrent droughts and extreme climate events have contributed to widespread food insecurity, crop losses, and livestock deaths, making adoption important for agricultural sustainability and climate resilience. Using data from 867 farm households selected through multistage sampling in semi-arid SEK, this study examines how risk preference and loss aversion are associated with SLM adoption breadth. An incentivized field experiment was employed to elicit both measures while adoption behaviour was assessed using a generalized Poisson regression model. Risk-loving farmers show greater adoption breadth than risk-averse farmers, while higher loss aversion is associated with lower adoption breadth. Locus of control, aspiration, wealth, shock exposure and crop diversity are positively associated with adoption breadth. Perceived climate-resilience benefits show a modest positive association, whereas perceived productivity and environmental-quality benefits are negatively associated. These findings highlight the relevance of behavioural heterogeneity for strategies to broaden SLM adoption in climate-vulnerable semi-arid areas.

abstract: Recreating bone remodeling remains challenging in bone organoids. In this issue of Cell Stem Cell, Pinho et al.1 develop bone organoids within liquefied microcapsules that support osteoblast, osteocyte, and osteoclast differentiation without exogenous differentiation inducers. This model supports matrix deposition and resorption, enabling investigation of cellular interactions underlying bone remodeling.

title: Investigating predictors of pertussis vaccination in pregnancy across England: cross sectional studies of maternity staff and mothers.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Pertussis vaccination is recommended for all pregnant women in England. Uptake remains suboptimal, with regional and demographic variability, leaving neonates at risk. This persists despite expansion of vaccine provision across maternity services since 2017. This study aimed to identify determinants of inequity and opportunities for intervention. METHODS Cross-sectional online surveys of: ii) 551 maternity healthcare professionals (HCPs), comparing those working in trusts within the highest- and lowest-vaccinating regions of England. i) 377 mothers of young babies from lowest-vaccinating regions, comparing women vaccinated versus unvaccinated against pertussis in their recent pregnancy; and Questionnaires were informed by the COM-B framework. Logistic regression modelling assessed factors associated with vaccination, alongside content analysis of free-text responses. RESULTS i) HCP survey: Area-level deprivation was strongly associated with low-vaccinating regions. Controlling for this, low-vaccinating regions were associated with HCPs' lower confidence in vaccine discussions and more perceiving these as burdensome, greater desire for training, and increased perceived responsibility for vaccination. Free-text responses described midwifery culture of providing vaccination information neutrally, avoiding direct recommendations in favour of supporting women's choice. ii) Mothers' survey: Most mothers (90%) rated HCPs as influential in their vaccination decision. Non-vaccination (20% of sample) was most strongly associated with lack of awareness that pertussis vaccination was recommended and lack of conviction that their midwife supported vaccination. Main reasons for vaccination were safety for the baby and HCP recommendation. Clear midwife recommendation was associated with satisfactory perceptions of vaccine communication across groups. The importance of access was commonly recognised but did not differentiate between groups in either study. CONCLUSIONS Midwives need support to avoid a neutral stance and provide clear, confident recommendations, including infant safety reassurance. Funding models should account for deprivation, not solely service size, to help reduce vaccination inequity.

title: High-dose parecoxib induces stress-associated pathological remodeling in C2C12 myotubes.
abstract: Parecoxib is a selective COX-2 inhibitor widely used for postoperative analgesia. Although NSAIDs can influence cellular metabolism and stress responses, whether parecoxib alters skeletal muscle cell homeostasis has not been systematically examined. Here, differentiated C2C12 myotubes were used as an in vitro model to investigate parecoxib-induced stress remodeling. Parecoxib caused limited changes in myotube morphology at 1 and 4 μM, whereas significant structural changes were observed at 10, 50, and 100 μM compared with control. Protein-normalized ATP content was reduced, whereas LDH release was not increased across the tested concentration range. Parecoxib also reduced Akt and FoxO3a phosphorylation, increased atrogin-1 and Bax expression, and increased AMPK phosphorylation. RNA sequencing identified changes in Gadd45a, Hmox1, Tnfaip3, Depp1, Tfrc, and Abra. Functional enrichment analyses highlighted pathways related to PI3K-Akt, FoxO, MAPK, cytoskeletal organization, muscle differentiation, and myofibril assembly. Parecoxib exposure during differentiation produced limited changes at 1 and 4 μM, whereas significant impairment was observed at 10, 50, and 100 μM compared with control. Together the results show structural and stress-related changes in C2C12 myotubes at higher parecoxib concentrations. They do not establish skeletal muscle toxicity under clinical exposure conditions.

title: Global Potential of No-Tillage in Enhancing Soil Carbon and Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions While Sustaining Crop Yields
abstract: Pursuing the balance between environmental sustainability and agricultural productivity remains a critical challenge for achieving global sustainable development goals. No-tillage (NT), as a key measure of sustainable conservation and climate-smart agriculture, offers a promising approach to addressing this challenge. However, its comprehensive effects on soil carbon accumulation, greenhouse gas emissions, and crop yields remain unquantified at the global scale, limiting our ability to optimize both environmental and agronomic outcomes. Here, we conducted such a global synthesis by combining a meta-analysis of 8,303 paired observations from 1,371 studies with a random forest model to assess the influence of site conditions and management on NT effects. Our meta-analysis demonstrates integrated benefits of NT in enhancing soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks in 0–30 cm layer by 11.0% and mitigating greenhouse gas (the sum of CO2, CH4, and N2O in CO2-equivalent) emissions by 13.5%, without a significant impact on crop yields (−0.6% ± 1.5%). The integrated benefits are stronger in drier climates and coarser-textured soils, and they exhibit significant time-dependent patterns. Our prediction identifies 44% of global croplands as being optimal for NT’s integrated benefits, mainly in Africa, South Asia, and North America. Adopting NT in these areas would result in a 4.8% increase in major food-crop yields, a 15.2% increase in 0–30 cm SOC stocks, and a 6.4% reduction in global cropland emissions, respectively. These findings underscore the relevance of implementing NT in suitable regions by adopting it into Good Agricultural Practice Guidelines.

title: Cold Atmospheric Plasma-Enabled SiOx Nanocoatings for Surface Energy Modulation and Enhanced Seed Germination.
abstract: Modern agricultural systems demand higher and more reliable yields under increasing constraints on land, water, and fertilizer inputs. Rapid and uniform seed germination is therefore critical for improving crop establishment and overall yield performance. Although existing strategies, such as ionizing gas treatments, polymer coatings, and nanoparticle-based seed treatments, can enhance water uptake and early vigor, they often suffer from limited stability, processing complexity, or potential seed damage. Here, we introduce a dry, cold atmospheric plasma (CAP)-assisted deposition platform for the conformal SiOx nanocoating of seeds, enabling a hydrophilic, storage-stable surface modification under ambient conditions. The deposition process was systematically optimized to achieve rapid, uniform coating formation directly on the seed surface. As a model system, corn seeds (Zea mays L.) were coated with SiOx nanofilms under optimized conditions. Wettability analysis revealed a ∼4-fold reduction in the static water contact angle for SiOx-coated seeds relative to pristine controls, compared with a ∼2.9-fold reduction for plasma-treated seeds without precursor introduction. Importantly, the SiOx-induced hydrophilicity exhibited superior stability, showing less than 3° contact angle recovery after 21 days of storage, whereas plasma-treated seeds alone displayed ∼50° recovery within 120 h. This stable and enhanced surface hydrophilicity translated into accelerated germination and improved early seedling vigor, resulting in SiOx-coated seeds exhibiting improved total seedling growth immediately after treatment and maintaining an approximately 38% increase compared with pristine controls after storage, demonstrating consistent storage stability. In comparison, the early-germination and seedling-growth advantages of plasma-treated seeds diminished substantially after storage, indicating that CAP-deposited SiOx provides a more persistent and storage-stable functional modification. Collectively, these results establish CAP-deposited SiOx nanocoatings as a scalable, solvent-free nanotechnology platform for stabilizing seed hydrophilicity, accelerating germination, and promoting early seedling growth under agronomically relevant conditions.

title: The dual-level dynamics of moral incongruence: A multilevel analysis of problematic pornography use.
abstract: Research regarding compulsive sexual behavior disorder has expanded rapidly, yet controversy remains concerning the role of moral evaluations in shaping perceptions of behavioral addiction. This study evaluated the longitudinal relationships between moral disapproval of pornography, pornography use frequency, and problematic pornography use (PPU) at both between-person and within-person levels. Data were collected over five waves (2 years) from a large community sample of American adults (N = 4,363); analyses were restricted to those who contributed at least one active-use wave (N = 7,512 person-waves from 2,903 individuals). Using a multilevel modeling approach, results at the between-person level indicated that moral disapproval was negatively associated with use frequency but positively associated with PPU and that the interaction of disapproval and frequency was a significant predictor of PPU. At the within-person level, we did not find evidence for a purely within-person effect of moral incongruence (e.g., state pornography-viewing frequency and disapproval did not interact to predict PPU), but we did find clear evidence for a cross-level interaction. Trait moral disapproval interacts with within-person, within-time point deviations in pornography use frequency to predict greater levels of PPU. Collectively, these findings suggest that while moral disapproval may serve as a population-level barrier to pornography use, it functions as a specific risk factor for self-reported feelings of addiction among individuals who use pornography, particularly during periods when they experience relatively higher levels of use. Our results also underscore that behavioral frequency is an insufficient metric for assessing sexual dysregulation and must be interpreted within the context of an individual's moral evaluations. Clinically, these findings emphasize the necessity of diagnostic precision to differentiate moral incongruence from genuine behavioral dysregulation in the assessment and treatment of compulsive sexual behavior disorder and PPU.
