title: Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome Protein Is Required for Glucocorticoid-Dependent Eosinopoiesis and Eosinophil-Rich Inflammation in Murine Models.
abstract: Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome Protein (WASP) is a pleiotropic cytoskeletal regulator expressed in haematopoietic tissues that plays essential roles in immune cell function, including leukocyte migration and signalling. By contrast, WASP's roles in leukocyte production remain insufficiently explored. Recent observations of the regulation of murine eosinophil production by distinct signalling pathways, respectively involving glucocorticoids (GCs) and cysteinyl leukotrienes (CysLTs), prompted us to investigate their dependence on WASP. To explore the contribution of WASP to eosinophil development and its relationship to GC- and CysLT-dependent regulatory pathways in vivo and ex vivo. We used wild-type (WT) and WASP-deficient mice in models of thioglycolate-induced peritonitis, allergic asthma and surgical stress to assess eosinophil recruitment and production. We used ex vivo cultures, co-culture systems and pharmacological interventions (dexamethasone, hydrocortisone, indomethacin, leukotriene receptor agonist and antagonist) to evaluate eosinophil differentiation and regulation of the eosinopoietic microenvironment. WASP-deficient mice displayed reduced eosinophil accumulation at extramedullary inflammatory sites and failed to mount a GC-induced eosinopoietic response. This defect was associated with the adherent stromal-enriched compartment, as GC responsiveness was restored when WASP-deficient progenitors were co-cultured with WT adherent bone marrow cells. Conversely, CysLT-driven eosinopoiesis remained intact in WASP-deficient mice. Our findings indicate that GC-mediated induction of eosinopoiesis depends on a WASP-sensitive, heterogeneous adherent bone marrow compartment. In contrast, the CysLT pathway remains functional in the absence of WASP. These results suggest that WASP contributes to eosinophil production through effects associated with the adherent haematopoietic microenvironment, while the precise cellular subset responsible remains to be defined.

title: From Static Choices to Navigating Clinical Trajectories: Reframing Therapeutic Reasoning in Medical Education.
abstract: PROBLEM Therapeutic reasoning is central to clinical practice and informed by established frameworks such as evidence-based medicine and shared decision-making. In educational settings, however, therapeutic decision-making is frequently taught and assessed as a discrete choice among predefined treatment options. This static framing - commonly structured through decision trees and guideline algorithms- emphasizes treatment selection under uncertainty but may insufficiently reflect the temporally evolving and regulatory nature of patient care. CONCEPTUAL SHIFT We propose that therapeutic reasoning can be more fully understood as the navigation of clinical trajectories rather than the selection of isolated choices. Drawing on complex adaptive systems theory, we conceptualize disease, resilience, and health as dynamically interacting functions evolving through feedback loops and shifting stability. Therapeutic reasoning is the anticipatory and interpretive process that guides the adaptive regulation of evolving clinical trajectories across coupled systems of organism and pathology. This perspective complements established decision-making models by making the temporal and systemic dimensions of therapeutic practice explicit. FRAMEWORK We operationalize this reframing through a phase-based model distinguishing disease-dominant decline, therapy-dominant modulation, and resilience-dominant recovery. Using severe pneumonia as an illustrative case, we demonstrate how inflection points and destabilizing events reveal the dynamic cognitive work underlying therapeutic practice and provide a conceptual scaffold for structuring therapeutic thinking. IMPLICATIONS Reframing therapeutic reasoning as trajectory navigation enriches the teaching of therapeutic decision making by providing a conceptual scaffold for curriculum design, clinical supervision, and assessment.
journal: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice

title: Hovering in turbulent rock-array microhabitats: Multidimensional kinematic responses of Schizothorax grahami.
abstract: The interaction between flow and riverbed structures creates spatially heterogeneous turbulent microhabitats that influence fish station-holding strategies and energy allocation. This study investigated the hovering behaviour of Schizothorax grahami in complex turbulent microhabitats formed by rock arrays of different scales using flume experiments. Video analysis and data storage tag (DST) tilt sensors were combined to quantify five multidimensional kinematic indicators: ground swimming speed ( V g ), angular velocity of swimming direction ( ω α ), tail-beat angular velocity ( ω β ), pitch angular velocity ( ω θ ) and roll angular velocity ( ω φ ). As rock-element size increased, fish hovering positions shifted from dispersed distributions to regions with local velocity gradients around rock elements, with clear positional overlap observed under some large-rock-array conditions. Increasing discharge generally increased the mean values and standardized within-condition variances of most kinematic indicators. Trial-level Spearman correlation analysis showed that V g had the strongest positive correlation with ω α . Generalized linear mixed models further revealed functional differentiation among kinematic responses: V g and ω α were mainly driven by flow velocity ( U mag ) and turbulent kinetic energy, whereas ω β , ω θ and ω φ showed weaker hydrodynamic responses. These findings suggest that fish hovering is an active multidimensional regulation process in which position maintenance, directional correction, propulsion and postural stabilization show partially differentiated response patterns. These findings provide new insights into the locomotor and postural strategies that enable benthic fish to maintain stability in heterogeneous turbulent environments and improve our understanding of fish behavioural adaptation to complex flows.

title: Application of computer algorithms in fault prediction of urban rail transit vehicles
abstract: Focusing on the large-scale multi-source monitoring data generated during the operation of urban rail transit vehicles, a computer algorithm computing framework for fault prediction tasks is constructed. The algorithm is based on the operation data of key vehicle components and uses multi-sensor data synchronization processing and time series feature extraction mechanisms to perform high-dimensional feature encoding on the vehicle state sequence. It also combines graph structure modeling methods to depict the interrelationships between different components. At the model level, a multiscale time series feature fusion strategy is introduced. Through the joint modeling of deep time series networks and graph convolution computing units, potential fault patterns under complex operating conditions can be identified. At the same time, parallel computing and model optimization mechanisms are designed to control the computational complexity and inference efficiency during the training stage, enabling the prediction model to maintain stable convergence in large-scale data environments. Experimental results show that on the constructed track vehicle operation data set, the proposed algorithm outperforms traditional time series prediction models in terms of prediction accuracy and model stability. The overall prediction accuracy reaches 93.8%, and the average inference time is controlled within 20ms, verifying the effectiveness of this computing framework in modeling complex vehicle operation data.
journal: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)

title: Big data-driven complex temporal behavior prediction and intelligent recommendation algorithms
abstract: A unified framework integrating Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) with adaptive attention and Graph Neural Networks (GNN)-based collaborative filtering is presented for e-commerce product sales forecasting and intelligent recommendation. The TCN module models local and long-range temporal dependencies in transaction sales data by combining causal convolutions and dilated convolutions. The adaptive attention mechanism can achieve dynamic prioritization to reflect significant demand changes and promotion-driven anomalies. GNN overcomes data sparsity thru deep feature embedding and effectively captures the multi-relational patterns between different consumer behaviors and product attributes, creating a unique user-item interaction graph. A large number of experiments conducted on real large scale e-commerce datasets have shown that in a volatile market environment, the ensemble framework consistently achieves lower sales prediction errors compared to traditional ARIMA and LSTM baselines. The collaborative filtering module, thru the improvement of demand-aware node features, provides better ranking and recommendation accuracy for cold-start users and frequent users. Quantitative results demonstrate significant operational improvements, such as enhanced inventory management, timely inventory adjustments, and improved targeting in marketing campaigns. The structure of the system ensures its scalability and adaptability, making it a powerful data-driven solution in the complex and ever-changing e-commerce ecosystem.
journal: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)

title: Optimization of crop planting strategies under uncertain environments based on genetic algorithm and NSGA-II
abstract: Optimizing how resources are allocated under tight constraints and deep uncertainty remains one of the more formidable challenges in complex system planning. This paper introduces a unified modeling and algorithmic framework designed to tackle optimization problems marked by multidimensional uncertainty and strict physical limitations. To begin, a single objective optimization model is constructed with the goal of maximizing total returns while navigating intricate spatial and temporal constraints. Within this stage, a genetic algorithm (GA) is employed to efficiently explore the vast discrete solution space in search of a strong baseline strategy. Given the volatility inherent in external variables such as market prices and yield rates, the study then turns to scenario generation. A low-discrepancy Sobol sequence is used to produce high-dimensional random scenarios that are uniformly distributed, offering a robust way to quantify environmental uncertainty. Building on this foundation, a mean variance multi-objective robust optimization model is developed. To navigate the trade-off between maximizing expected returns and minimizing risk, the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) with an elite retention strategy is applied. The result is a well-defined set of Pareto optimal solutions. Experimental results and sensitivity analyses confirm that this hybrid algorithmic framework holds up remarkably well even under severe and simultaneous fluctuations. It offers a reliable quantitative tool for decision making in complex and uncertain environments, supporting planners with strategies that are not just theoretically sound but practically resilient.
journal: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)

title: TP-EG: a hybrid machine learning framework for Olympic medal prediction and competitive effect analysis
abstract: Olympic medal prediction is a challenging task due to the complex relationships among national participation structures, event characteristics, and historical performance trends. To address this problem, this study proposes a TP-EG hybrid prediction framework integrating a two-stage Random Forest model with an EVE-GMM event distribution model. First, seven feature indicators are constructed from historical Olympic participation data to characterize national competitive strength, resource allocation patterns, and host-country effects. A two-stage Random Forest architecture is then designed to perform medal-winning classification and medal-count regression separately, improving prediction stability for sparse samples. To further capture latent event-level distribution characteristics, an EVE-GMM model based on Gaussian Mixture Modeling and Expectation-Maximization optimization is introduced. Subsequently, a nonlinear regression ensemble strategy is employed to fuse the outputs of the two models, enhancing prediction robustness and accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior performance in prediction accuracy and error metrics compared with conventional baseline models. Based on the proposed framework, the medal table for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games is predicted, and the probabilities of national improvement and first-time medal-winning are quantitatively evaluated. In addition, an EEIA model based on the squared CUSUM test is established to identify and quantify the “Great Coach Effect” through structural change detection in event-level performance sequences.
journal: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)

title: Prediction and analysis of application software operation based on improved LightGBM
abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning have made model refinement increasingly important for efficient software operation. Continuous user-platform interactions generate substantial behavioral traces that can support data driven prediction. This study develops a modified LightGBM model for intelligent application operation. The loss function incorporates L2 regularization to constrain complexity, while training samples are reweighted according to quantified user value and behavioral periodicity. Historical YouTube interactions - views, likes, comments, and follows - are used to construct the experimental dataset. Performance is assessed with accuracy, recall, precision, and F1-score. All four metrics approach 1, and the trained classifier identifies likely online periods and potential followed bloggers for July 22, 2024. These outputs can guide personalized recommendation schedules. Under noisy conditions, the modified model exhibits less overfitting and stronger robustness than the comparison methods while improving recognition of behaviorally unstable samples.
journal: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)

title: Image recognition of Amur tiger based on ResNet50 and transfer learning
abstract: Accurate recognition of Amur tiger images is crucial for population conservation and habitat ecosystem monitoring. To address the inefficiency and high misjudgment rate of manual screening in processing massive infrared camera images, this study proposes an optimized Amur tiger image recognition model based on ResNet50 and transfer learning. Leveraging the PyTorch framework, the model adopts a transfer learning strategy: it freezes the convolutional and pooling layers of the pre-trained ResNet50 (retaining general visual feature extraction capabilities learned from ImageNet) and replaces the original fully connected layer with a 2-class output layer to adapt to the binary classification task. Targeted data augmentation (random rotation, translation, horizontal flipping) is applied to the training set to enhance generalization, while the test set undergoes standardized preprocessing (size adjustment, center cropping, normalization) to ensure evaluation stability. Experimental results show that the model achieves a validation accuracy of over 99.8% and maintains low loss (below 0.005) on the test set, effectively distinguishing Amur tigers from confusing animals (lions, leopards, etc.) and habitat backgrounds. This work realizes efficient and accurate automated processing of wild infrared camera data, providing a reliable technical tool for Amur tiger conservation and ecological monitoring.
journal: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)

title: PCA-FNN: classification and prediction of new energy vehicle prices
abstract: To address the issues of computational complexity and insufficient generalization caused by high-dimensional features in the classification of new-energy vehicle segments, this paper proposes a classification method that combines Principal Component Analysis (PCA) with a Fully Connected Neural Network (PCA-FNN). First, the raw data undergoes preprocessing, including missing value imputation, outlier handling, and standardization. Second, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is used to reduce the original 20-dimensional features to 18 dimensions, accounting for 96.31% of the total variance. Then, a single-hidden-layer Fully Connected Neural Network (18-1-4) is constructed for modeling, and the Softmax function is employed to output the probability distributions for the four price tiers. Ablation experiments show that the model achieves an accuracy of 97.00% with PCA-based dimensionality reduction, compared to 96.67% without PCA, representing an improvement of 0.33 percentage points. In comparative experiments, the PCA-FNN's accuracy (97.00%) and macro-average F1 score (0.9692) both outperformed those of LSTM (75.00%, 0.6805), Bi-LSTM (76.67%, 0.7025), entropy-weighted FNN (96.33%, 0.9623), and traditional FNN (96.67%, 0.9659). The experimental results indicate that the PCA-FNN can effectively eliminate feature redundancy, improve classification performance and training efficiency, and possess good generalization ability and engineering application value.
journal: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)

title: Selective prediction in medical image classification with provable selective risk control
abstract: Deep learning models deployed in clinical settings risk silently producing high-confidence misdiagnoses on ambiguous cases. Selective prediction mitigates this by allowing the system to abstain when uncertain, but existing empirical threshold methods offer no formal guarantee that the error rate among accepted predictions stays within a tolerable level. We propose a selective prediction framework that combines split conformal prediction with Hoeffding’s inequality to construct a finite sample, high-probability upper bound on the selective risk. Given a user-specified risk tolerance 𝛼 and failure probability 𝛿, the method selects the largest entropy threshold on an independent calibration set for which the Hoeffding upper bound remains below 𝛼, thereby maximizing coverage while provably controlling the conditional misclassification rate. Experiments on the COVID-19 chest x-ray (4-class) and ISIC 2019 Skin Lesion (8-class) datasets show that empirical baselines violate the risk constraint in up to 59% of random data splits, whereas our method achieves a 0% violation rate across 100 splits on both datasets, at the cost of only a 7-percentage point reduction in coverage. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides reliable, distribution-free risk control suitable for safety-critical medical image classification.
journal: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)

title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
abstract: The pseudogap stands out in the phase diagram of the cuprate high-temperature superconductors because its origin and relationship to superconductivity remain elusive. The origin of the pseudogap has been debated, with competing hypotheses attributing it to preformed electron pairs or local order, such as charge density waves. We present unambiguous evidence supporting the pairing scenario, using local shot-noise spectroscopy measurements in Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ . Our data demonstrate that the pseudogap energy coincides with the onset of electron pairing and is spatially heterogeneous with values reaching up to 70 milli–electron volts. Our results exclude a pure local order origin of the pseudogap, link the pseudogap to Cooper pair formation, and suggest that the limiting factor for higher critical temperature in cuprates is phase coherence.

title: Discovering molecular modulators with nanoswitch screening
abstract: Molecules that modulate protein-protein interactions, including through ternary complex formation, have been established as key therapeutics. Yet they can be challenging to discover, as standard screening approaches often lack throughput or fail to directly assay multibody interactions. We addressed this by combining DNA nanoswitch–based selection of nucleotide-encoded libraries with next-generation sequencing to create FIND (Functional Interaction–based Nanoswitch Discovery), which enables ultrahigh-throughput discovery of compounds that induce or increase protein-protein interactions. We demonstrate FIND by discovering nanobodies that stabilize the interaction between angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 and the receptor-binding domain of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 and by discovering agonists of peroxisome proliferator–activated receptor gamma from a DNA-barcoded small-molecule library. By enabling rapid discovery of molecular modulators, FIND could lead to new therapeutics across many conditions.

title: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat
abstract: Anthropogenic noise is a rapidly expanding global pollutant, but its effects across biological levels from individuals to ecosystems remain unquantified. We conducted phylogenetically controlled meta-analyses of 214 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species with ranges that span six continents. Noise altered at least one physiological, developmental, or behavioral trait in 80% of species studied, with declines in fitness and abundance and disruptions of predator-prey interactions. Effects occurred in every habitat, although response mechanisms varied for some traits and species, creating winners and losers. Only multispecies analyses can reveal such species- and ecosystem-level impacts of anthropogenic stressors. Our results establish noise as a novel selection pressure reshaping ecosystem dynamics and as a pervasive stressor requiring soundscape protection alongside habitat conservation.

title: Quantum gas microscopy of three-flavor Hubbard systems
abstract: Hubbard systems are paradigmatic realizations of strongly correlated many-body systems. Introducing additional species breaks the SU(2) symmetry of the Hubbard model and leads to a wide variety of new exotic quantum phases. Here, we extended quantum gas microscopy to three-flavor Fermi lattice gases in the Hubbard regime. Relying on site- and flavor-resolved detection, we studied the phase diagram of the three-flavor Hubbard model and found signatures of flavor-selective localization and selective pairing at temperatures down to the tunneling energy scale. Our measurements were then compared with numerical linked-cluster expansion calculations. Further increase of phase space density may enable the observation of a distinct pair Mott phase at half filling and shows a path toward the study of color superfluidity and other aspects of quantum chromodynamics.

title: Tumor metastasis co-opts liver hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression
abstract: Cancer-associated hematopoietic abnormalities contribute to systemic immunosuppression. However, whether tumors can initiate localized extramedullary hematopoiesis to suppress antitumor immunity remains unclear. In this study, we identify a distinct form of hepatic hematopoiesis driven by liver metastasis–associated hematopoietic stem cells (LM-HSCs). Liver metastases establish ectopic periportal hematopoietic niches that recruit bone marrow HSCs through Kupffer cell–dependent C-C motif chemokine receptor 1 (CCR1) signaling. Although LM-HSCs retain self-renewal and multipotency, cAMP response element–binding protein (CREB) activation skews their differentiation toward the myeloid lineage, particularly annexin A1–positive (ANXA1 + ) immature neutrophils. These neutrophils produce glucocorticoids, which activate glucocorticoid receptor signaling in a paracrine manner and induce immune checkpoint receptor expression and functional anergy in CD8 + T and natural killer cells. Collectively, these findings suggest that liver metastases reprograms hepatic hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression.

title: Quantum gases below 10 picokelvin in space
abstract: Ultracold atom platforms enable low temperatures and long free evolution times, which are crucial for fundamental physics tests and atom interferometry. The lowest equivalent temperature reported in such a system is 38 pK with a free expansion time of 2 s, achieved in atom-chip-based magnetic traps in microgravity. Optical dipole trap (ODT) systems offer better optical access and the flexibility to condense both magnetic and non-magnetic atoms, but have not been used to prepare quantum degenerate gases under microgravity conditions. Here we report an ODT-based Bose-Einstein condensate created aboard the China Space Station, containing 2.0 × 10 4 atoms, reaching an equivalent temperature of 9.7 − 2.7 + 3.2 pK with a free expansion time of 7.0 s. This record-low temperature could stimulate a new generation of ODT-based experiments in quantum simulation and precision measurements in space.

title: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply
abstract: Dansgaard-Oeschger (DO) events during the last ice age are thought to reflect rapid shifts in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC). Greenland ice cores suggest warming transitions within only a few decades—or even just over 10 years. Using precisely dated speleothem oxygen-isotope records from the Asian monsoon region, we have shown that the same DO warmings unfolded over more than a century. Isotope modeling revealed that Greenland records primarily capture a rapid atmospheric reorganization triggered by the initial sea-ice retreat in the northeastern North Atlantic, whereas the parallel AMOC recovery and hemispheric thermal adjustment proceeded much more slowly. These findings reveal that natural AMOC transitions evolved more slowly than the rapid North Greenland oxygen-isotope shifts would imply, thereby refining our understanding of “abruptness” during DO events.

title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients’ plasma. Mechanistically, dietary fiber increased the abundance of Bacteroides xylanisolven s, which converts androstenedione into a nonandrogenic secondary hormone metabolite we named coproandrosterone, which is further metabolized by gut microbiota into dihydro-coproandrosterone. This metabolic pathway was validated in a mouse model. These findings highlight the potential of dietary fiber to alleviate PMOS by modulating androgen homeostasis through gut microbiota, offering insights for prebiotic and probiotic therapies.

title: When fat adapts: From physiological remodeling to disease
abstract: Adipose tissue undergoes extensive remodeling to adapt to changing physiological demands. This plasticity encompasses changes in adipocyte metabolism and number, extracellular matrix organization, vascularization, immune composition, and innervation. When coordinated, these processes preserve energy buffering, thermogenesis, endocrine function, and local tissue support. Pathological adipose tissue remodeling drives obesity-related complications and contributes to many diseases involving organ-associated adipose depots throughout the body. In cancer, tumor-associated fat can develop a metabolic and fibroinflammatory niche that promotes tumor growth and invasion, and remodeling of other depots can directly disrupt neighboring tissues. Recent studies have identified mesenchymal, immune, vascular, and adipocyte states that govern adaptive or pathological outcomes. These findings broaden therapeutic goals beyond reducing fat mass toward restoring adipogenesis, substrate turnover, thermogenic capacity, and tissue-niche function.

title: Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago
abstract: Cannabis is the world’s most-used illicit psychoactive plant, yet direct prehistoric evidence for its consumption is rare. In this study, we present the earliest direct evidence of cannabis use: offerings of plant parts and chemical compounds in ancient human hair recovered from a monumental tomb in Siberia. The findings suggest that the plant was used for its psychoactive qualities across Eurasia, where specific wild populations might have had naturally higher active compound levels. We show that the practice of cannabis consumption dates back at least 2800 years, anchoring debates around contemporary usage and informing discussions on cannabis in medicine, public health, law, and industry.

title: Seafloor geodesy delineates fast megathrust relocking after the giant 2011 Tohoku earthquake
abstract: How and when the subduction megathrust recovers its locking state after a great earthquake is important to understanding earthquake-cycle physics and future hazards. Here we report the delineation of the relocking process after the 2011 magnitude 9 Tohoku earthquake with 14 years of postseismic seafloor geodetic observations. These data, combined with onshore geodetic observations, analyses of repeating earthquakes, and numerical modeling, reveal how the recovery of locking is interrupted by afterslip on the megathrust and accompanied by stress relaxation in the viscoelastic upper mantle. The results indicate that the megathrust has already arrived at a locking state today similar to that before the earthquake despite the ongoing stress relaxation. The acquired knowledge aids understanding of megathrust earthquake cycles at other subduction zones.

title: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling
abstract: Elastocaloric cooling (eC) uses shape memory alloys (SMAs) as energy-efficient, eco-friendly refrigerants. However, cost-effectively fabricating SMAs into fatigue-resistant, heat transfer–enhanced structures remains a key obstacle to commercialization of the eC technology. We introduce a “stamping and stacking” (S-S) method for producing porous, fatigue-resistant SMA structures. Honeycomb-like chips are stamped from nitinol (NiTi) thin sheets and then stacked into a layered tubular structure to increase heat exchange surface and at the same time avoid buckling and splitting failures encountered in existing SMA structures. The stacked structure endures >10 8 compression cycles and can deliver high specific cooling power of 3850 watts per kilogram. Our S-S method reduces fabrication costs by one order of magnitude compared with existing approaches, enabling mass production of eC refrigerant structures for commercial deployment.

title: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children’s everyday speech
abstract: Children learn to understand and speak from the speech around them, yet how that everyday input shapes learning remains unresolved. Large language models show that language is learnable from data, but their scale and training conditions differ sharply from a child’s natural experience. We trained cognitively feasible, child-specific models on longitudinal home recordings from eight children across their first 1000 days of life. Each model learned incrementally from a single child’s ordered speech input without prior linguistic knowledge, developing phoneme-like and word-form representations that tracked each child’s learning pace. Learning was dependent on dense daily sampling and replay of recent input, indicating that both experience- and memory-related processes are necessary. These findings show that everyday experience contains sufficient structure for language learning and establish child-specific modeling for testing developmental theories.

title: Obesity management medications: The way forward
abstract: Obesity is now widely recognized as a chronic progressive condition. The altered biological mechanisms that cause obesity frequently require long-term treatment, including pharmacotherapies or bariatric surgery. In recent decades, the pathophysiology of obesity has been understood to an extent that obesity management medication (OMM) discovery could be rationally pursued. Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

title: Denoising the US Census: Succinct block hierarchical regression
abstract: The 2020 United States Census adopted differential privacy to protect individual confidentiality, adding calibrated noise to summary demographic measurements that are then reconciled into population tables. We developed BlueDown, a postprocessing algorithm that combines techniques from linear regression and constrained optimization while exploiting measurement structure for efficiency. On 2020 Census data, BlueDown reduced the error of groupings by race at the county level by 21 to 36% and of all county-level groupings by 9 to 58%; at the tract level, it reduced error of groupings by housing type by 38 to 61%. These gains came at no cost to confidentiality or computational efficiency and would improve the validity of research relying on this definitive dataset and analyses used to guide the distribution of more than $1.5 trillion in annual federal spending.

title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer’s disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)–based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

title: Can artificial intelligence align with Indigenous science?
abstract: As the use of generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) increases, alarms are being raised about how the technology could replace human contribution, override human supervision, ignore ethical and technical guardrails, and cause increasingly irreparable harm to the environment. This creates potentially destructive outcomes for life on Earth. From a traditional Indigenous science perspective, such possibilities in themselves would be enough to immediately stop presently configured AI releases. In a Lakota context, science must ensure as little harm as possible is done to life. Therefore, AI as presently configured simply would not qualify to advance further from an ethical and scientific standpoint. Indigenous science asks something fundamentally different than what AI presently seeks to, or can, answer. But that does not mean that future forms of AI can never align with Indigenous science.
