title: PSGAgent: Enhancing MLLMs'Dynamic Visual Perception for Panoptic Scene Graph Generation via Agentic Reasoning
abstract: Panoptic Scene Graph generation (PSG) requires holistic yet fine-grained reasoning over complex relations among objects. However, current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) applied to PSG suffer from a perception bottleneck: they function as static observers limited by fixed-resolution views. As a result, models often overlook critical relations involving small or peripheral objects and struggle to differentiate ambiguous predicates in complex scenes. To address these limitations, we propose PSGAgent, an agentic framework that enhances visual perception for PSG through a think-act-observe loop. PSGAgent allows MLLMs to dynamically refine their visual perception using two tools: a Region Zoom-In Tool for local exploration of small or boundary relations and a Visual Highlight Tool for relation-focused segmentation that filters out irrelevant contextual noise. To optimize decision-making, we construct a two-stage training pipeline. First, we create a high-quality, error-aware Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (M-CoT) dataset that provides robust supervision for cold-start learning. Then, we design a novel hierarchical reward mechanism integrated with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) to enable strategic and adaptive tool usage. Extensive experiments on the PSG benchmark show that PSGAgent achieves SOTA performance, demonstrating strong capability in both holistic and fine-grained scene understanding.
journal: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia

title: When Should Forecasting Models Listen to Text? Counterfactual Utility Routing for Multimodal Time Series Forecasting

authors.name: Yusen Liu
authors.affiliation: University of Technology Sydney, Sydney, Australia

authors.name: Xiufeng Liu
authors.affiliation: Technical University of Denmark, Lyngby, Denmark

authors.name: Xu Cheng
authors.affiliation: Tianjin University of Technology, Tianjin, China

authors.name: Huan Huo
authors.affiliation: University of Technology Sydney, Sydney, Australia

journal: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia
abstract: Time-series forecasting supports decisions in domains such as finance and healthcare, where forecasts may depend on events not fully represented in numerical histories. Multimodal forecasting can supply this context through text, but the additional information is useful only when it remains relevant to the target and forecast horizon. Existing methods commonly fuse text at every prediction step, even when it is stale, weakly related to the target, or informative only for certain horizons. We therefore frame text use as a horizon-wise decision and introduce CUTS, a Counterfactual Utility Routing framework for selective fusion. For each forecast step, CUTS retrieves horizon-specific evidence and produces matched text-conditioned and no-text forecasts. A utility estimator predicts the benefit of the retrieved evidence, while its uncertainty moderates the final interpolation between the two forecasts. On Time-MMD, CUTS achieves the best nine-domain normalized MSE and MAE among the evaluated methods. It records the lowest MSE in five of nine domains. On FNSPID, it achieves the lowest average MSE and MAE and obtains the lowest MSE at the 3-day and 5-day horizons. Ablations identify horizon-specific evidence selection and staged training as key contributors. Corruption and routing analyses further show that uncertainty-aware routing helps CUTS limit its reliance on unreliable text.

title: HINT-RAG: Hypothesis-Contrastive Differentiable Retrieval Augmented Generation for Medical Image Report Generation

authors.name: Yiming Cao
authors.affiliation: Jinan-NTU Green Technology Research Institute (GreenTRI), Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, Singapore

authors.name: Yanyu Xu
authors.affiliation: Joint SDU-NTU Centre for Artificial Intelligence Research (C-FAIR), Shandong University, Jinan, China

authors.name: Zhiqi Shen
authors.affiliation: Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, Singapore

journal: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia
abstract: Translating medical images into accurate natural language descriptions is a critical challenge in cross-modal understanding. However, existing RAG-based methods typically retrieve references according to visual similarity, where visually similar images may correspond to different clinical findings and report semantics. Visually matched but semantically mismatched samples can introduce misleading multimodal evidence, thereby reducing the accuracy of generated reports. To address this challenge, we propose a hypothesis-contrastive differentiable retrieval augmented generation (HINT-RAG) framework, a perceive-query-disambiguate cross-modal learning paradigm for ambiguity-aware medical report generation. Specifically, the perceive module formulates uncertainty-aware hypotheses to capture plausible clinical semantics from the input image. The query module leverages these hypotheses to perform contrastive differentiable retrieval, aiming to identify discriminative evidence from clinically confusable candidates rather than merely visually similar samples. The disambiguate module adaptively fuses visual features and retrieved evidence to resolve cross-modal ambiguity before report decoding. Extensive experiments on public datasets show that HINT-RAG achieves leading performance in both natural language generation and clinical efficacy metrics.

title: Remote Sensing Image-Text Retrieval via Hierarchical and Targeting Semantic Alignment
abstract: Remote sensing image-text retrieval (RSITR) can facilitate visual language mining in spatial scenarios, which holds significant importance for aviation and aerospace applications. Existing RSITR methods often lack joint coarse-grained and fine-grained alignment, or their unified learning strategies are inefficient. Additionally, there is no analysis of remote sensing characteristics in these fine-grained feature learning. To address these issues, this paper proposes Hierarchical and Targeting Semantic Alignment (HTSA) for remote sensing image-text retrieval, which simultaneously considers the construction of global and local features. In coarse-grained semantic alignment, cross-modal classification learning and inter-modal matching learning are combined. For fine-grained semantic learning, targeted semantic alignment is introduced to highlight essential objects, which are overlooked by current RSITR methods, but crucial for remote sensing scenarios. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of the proposed framework, while different ablation studies discuss the functions of specific components.
journal: Proceedings of the 35th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management

title: Learning Video-Derived Behavioral and Physiological Representations for Automated Deception Detection
abstract: Deception detection in video conferencing is increasingly important with the rise of remote interviews, online judicial hearings, and telemedicine consultations. Existing approaches either rely on observable behavioral cues (e.g., micro-expressions and head movements) or depend on specialized equipment for physiological sensing (e.g., thermal cameras or wearable devices). The former benefits from the ubiquity and non-intrusive nature of commodity RGB cameras but often suffers from limited accuracy, while the latter provides more reliable and discriminative signals at the cost of additional hardware, hindering scalability in real-world deployment. In this work, we bridge the gap between behavioral cue-based and physiological signal-based approaches and introduce DeceptSense, a video-derived multimodal framework for contactless deception detection using only RGB video. The key insight is that complementary signals, including motion dynamics, facial temperature variations, and cardiac activity, can be jointly recovered from RGB video. DeceptSense extracts these modalities using an iDT descriptor for motion dynamics, an RGB-to-thermal pipeline for temperature variation modeling, and an rPPG module for cardiac signal extraction. It then employs a cross-modal attention mechanism to align the three temporally asynchronous modalities. Extensive experiments show that DeceptSense achieves an AUC of 89.6% on the challenging Real-Life Trial dataset and AUCs of 64.5% and 65.1% on the BOL and MU3D datasets, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed video-derived multimodal framework for automated deception detection.
journal: Proceedings of the 35th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management

title: AquaNord-SE: A Large-Scale Longitudinal Multimodal Benchmark for Swedish Inland Water Quality
abstract: Predicting inland water quality reliably requires integrating water quality observations, satellite remote sensing, meteorological reanalysis, and catchment descriptors, yet no benchmark provides these modalities jointly under reproducible evaluation protocols for optically complex, seasonally ice-affected inland waters. We introduce AquaNord-SE, a longitudinal multimodal benchmark of 883,325 samples from 18,743 Swedish lake and river monitoring stations over 2000-2025, integrating 38 water quality parameters from SLU Miljödata MVM with observations from five satellite sensor streams, ERA5-Land and MESAN meteorological reanalysis, 64 HydroATLAS catchment attributes, and 13 derived water quality indices. The dataset is structured as station-aligned multimodal feature sets and spatial-temporal archives, accompanied by a five-tier modality ablation design and three orthogonal generalization splits across spatial, temporal, and latitudinal axes. Benchmarking across tabular, spatial-temporal, and multimodal baselines under split conformal prediction and quantile regression reveals that static catchment attributes alone (R2 = 0.303 Chlorophyll-a, R2 = 0.642 Secchi) consistently outperform all non-tabular models, while total phosphorus proves intractable across all families (best R2 = 0.118). Conformal calibration error increases from 0.062 to 0.225 across the oligotrophic-hypereutrophic gradient, co-locating with the eutrophic regime where atmospheric correction (AC) failure exceeds 65% of optical retrievals. We additionally release a gridded water quality index (WQI) NetCDF at 5 km resolution over 2000-2025, supporting Water Framework Directive (WFD) compliance and long-term trend analysis. The dataset and evaluation protocols are publicly available to support reproducible research in environmental knowledge management and data-driven water quality assessment and monitoring.
journal: Proceedings of the 35th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management

title: MIKU: Material Invariance and Knowledge Unification for PBR Generation
abstract: High-quality material generation for physically based rendering (PBR) remains challenging because datasets and synthesis pipelines lack standardized representations. Differences in material definitions, rendering conventions, and parameterizations lead to unstable and physically implausible results. We propose MIKU, a unified framework for standardized PBR asset representation and physically consistent material generation across diverse 3D content domains. Its core is a unified processing pipeline that standardizes the workflow from data preprocessing to final texture synthesis, maintaining consistent geometry and texture representations. A normalization scheme harmonizes heterogeneous material parameterizations in a common representation space, enabling robust cross-dataset training and inference. Building on this formulation, we train a novel physically aware diffusion model for PBR texture generation within a two-stage multi-view synthesis framework. First, geometry-aware albedo generation synthesizes multi-view albedo maps under explicit geometric guidance to ensure cross-view appearance consistency. Second, metallic-roughness generation uses the diffusion model to predict physically plausible roughness and metallic maps conditioned on the generated albedo and unified representation. Trained end-to-end on standardized data, the model learns to generate materials that respect category-level material priors and semantic part boundaries. By decoupling representation standardization from appearance synthesis, MIKU substantially improves material generation stability and physical consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art texture quality and semantic consistency across object parts, advancing automated material generation for 3D content creation.

title: If an Agent Can Write Your Code, What Is Left for You to Learn? Asking, Reviewing, and Owning AI-Assisted Programming
abstract: When a coding agent can produce a program, its tests, and an explanation, the submission says little about what the student understands. My dissertation investigates how computing students can use AI while retaining the reasoning needed to learn programming. I take part in examining three practices: asking for tutoring that requires students to reason, reviewing generated code against expectations formed before seeing it, and owning the work by explaining AI assistance and their own decisions. In two prompting studies, including a randomized trial with 979 CS1 students, students’ tutoring prompts improved after instruction. In CodeCue, predicting program behaviour before seeing an agent’s changes made students feel better prepared, but did not measurably change how they reviewed. Our study on AI attribution found that what students think should be disclosed differs from what they would disclose themselves. The next phase connects these practices, beginning with a randomized attribution study and extending to repeated tasks with gradually reduced support. I will examine how students learn to direct coding agents, evaluate their work, and retain programming understanding that they can apply independently.
journal: Proceedings of the 26th Koli Calling International Conference on Computing Education Research

title: Scaffolding Novice Programming in the LLM Era: Balancing Learning and Automation
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are reshaping programming, creating a dual challenge for computing education. While LLMs can help novices by translating natural language to code, there is a significant risk of over-reliance where learners get solutions without understanding the underlying concepts. This is compounded when AI tools "over-repair" student mistakes, hiding crucial learning opportunities. My PhD research addresses this challenge by designing and evaluating pedagogical frameworks that shift the focus from syntax-heavy coding to critical thinking and effective collaboration with AI. My work is guided by three research questions focusing on the design of LLM-powered educational tools, the analysis of student interaction patterns, and the evaluation of new pedagogical frameworks. My initial study evaluated NLPG-Exercise, a novel activity where novices arrange natural-language fragments to construct programs. This work established the importance of instruction fidelity—the principle that an educational tool must faithfully translate a learner’s logic, including mistakes, rather than silently correcting them. The study (N=170) demonstrated the feasibility of this approach but also revealed low but significant rates of fidelity errors, where the LLM either repaired incorrect logic or introduced new errors. Building on these findings, my future work will formalize these ideas into new pedagogical frameworks. This includes developing LLM Code Audit Problems, where students critique and refine flawed AI-generated code, and Agentic Prompt Problems, where they learn to solve complex tasks by collaborating with an LLM teammate. The ultimate goal is to develop and validate a cohesive pedagogical sequence that effectively teaches both programming and AI literacy, providing empirical evidence to guide curriculum design in the LLM era.
journal: Proceedings of the 26th Koli Calling International Conference on Computing Education Research

title: Teaching Human–AI Programming: A Scoping Literature Review
abstract: After the initial hype surrounding Generative AI (GenAI), we are beginning to see a “normalization” of its use in computing education. With the emergence of agentic AI systems, the community seems to start developing pedagogical approaches and tools incorporating human-AI collaboration as a skill. However, a recent overview of key trends in how related human-AI collaboration skills are taught is lacking. It is the goal of this work to address this gap through a scoping literature review within the ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, and Scopus. Through search terms, we identified 163 papers that were preprocessed and screened. Exclusion and inclusion criteria led to the final set of 10 papers, which were qualitatively analyzed w.r.t. the educational context, pedagogical approach, and tool use. The analysis yielded an overview of recent research trends and examples of how computing educators are incorporating human-AI collaboration. These findings help inform educators in designing pedagogical interventions and instruction, as well as tool developers and researchers interested in implementing and evaluating new agentic AI systems for teaching computing.
journal: Proceedings of the 26th Koli Calling International Conference on Computing Education Research

title: From Rewards to Consequences Through Designing AI
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) can be introduced to K–12 learners through accessible examples of agents learning from rewards and interaction. However, such examples may leave deeper questions of AI design and critical AI literacy unexplored. This demo presents Reward Machine, a browser-based, GDPR-compliant, no-code classroom activity for learners aged 13–15 that introduces RL through game creation. Learners design their own story to be implemented in grid-world environments, define agents, goals, and reward structures, and compete to train agents in peer-created scenarios. These experiences support critical reflection on the human choices, values, and unintended consequences involved in real-world AI design.
journal: Proceedings of the 26th Koli Calling International Conference on Computing Education Research

title: A muzzle-based self-enhancing cow recognition method using YOLO and LLM
abstract: In the modern era, using the technology of image processing, people are beingfacilitated in many sectors. Therefore, we have decided to do research on cowrecognition using the methods of image processing. Because cows are prettyessential for human beings, and people from the entire world are being facilitatedby cows. Because of that reason, many technologies have been invented till nowfor the cow. Here we have presented an approach to identify the cow. Like thefingerprint of a human, the cow muzzle is also unique. Due to this reason, wecan recognize the cow based on the muzzle. To recognize muzzles, we have usedYolo and the Structural Similarity Index (SSI). Image processing is a sector ofArtificial Intelligence and data is quite important to train models. Moreover, totrain a model for image processing, it is needed to manage a high-configurationcomputer. But there are many regions in the world where people hardly get suchpowerful machines. To mitigate this issue, we have introduced a unique methodwhere we do not need a large amount of data for the image processing task. Toeliminate the necessity of collecting a huge amount of data, we included a self-enhancing feature, which helps the model to predict accurately and also helpsto improve performance by increasing the amount of data. However, withouta large amount of data, it will be possible to predict appropriately because ofthe presence of self-enhancing features. This certain program helps the modelto improve its capability for delivering faster responses. LLM is responsible toadd the self-enhancing feature. On the other hand, to find out the most suitableYolo model for our research, we have trained data with three different versionsof Yolo: Yolo v7, v8, and v9. We evaluated the performances of these threeversions in terms of Precision, Recall, mAP50, and mAP50-95 and found Yolov9 to be the best among them. It excels with a precision of 0.391, a recall of0.916, a mAP50 of 0.559, and a mAP50-95 of 0.307.
journal: International Journal of Informatics and Communication Technology (IJ-ICT)

title: CPU-optimized regularized convolutional neural network architecture for multimedia-based breast cancer metastasis detection
abstract: The histopathological diagnosis of breast cancer metastases, a subjective and lengthy process, benefits from advances in artificial intelligence for its automation. This study proposes an automatic classification method based on a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture with progressive regularization (Batch normalization and adaptive dropout), trained on the PatchCamelyon (PCam) dataset. Our approach integrates a data augmentation strategy specific to medical images and advanced optimization for CPU environments, allowing us to balance performance, robustness, and computational accessibility. The architecture comprises only 94,000 parameters, 223 times fewer than leading models. Multi-criteria evaluation shows competitive results: area under the curve (AUC) of 92.92%, F1-score of 82.39%, accuracy of 88.74%, and specificity of 90.61%. A bootstrap robustness analysis provides 95% confidence intervals (AUC: [89.56% 92.91%]), and an ablation study quantifies the reduction in overfitting through progressive dropout (33.6%). This research validates that a well regulated and CPU-optimized CNN architecture can achieve clinically relevant performance while remaining accessible on standard environments, thus opening up concrete prospects for the development of practical AI tools in digital pathology.
journal: International Journal of Informatics and Communication Technology (IJ-ICT)

title: Advanced IoT and ML-driven personal safety technology for women
abstract: This article introduces VigilNet, a personal safety system powered by internet of things (IoT) and machine learning (ML) that identifies environmental irregularities instantaneously through intelligent wearable gadgets. In contrast to solutions dependent on extensive datasets and reactive alert systems VigilNet employs a few-shot learning (FSL) strategy utilizing siamese neural networks (SNNs) to achieve precise anomaly recognition, with limited training data. In the information and communication technology (ICT) realm, VigilNet is a smart IoT sensing and communication network with interconnected wearable sensor nodes continuously collecting physiological and environmental data for real-time processing. The SNNs based FSL module then fuses these multiple modal streams of sensor information and extracts the similarity-based threat assessment, which in turn drives an intelligent decision support system to alarm the operator to take timely action for any abnormal situations. VigilNet, thus, combines IoT connectivity, real-time data analytics, and machine-learning-driven decision support into a single personal safety system. The framework was tested on an IoT wearable dataset encompassing heart rate, body temperature, ambient noise and proximity data. Experimental results demonstrate that VigilNet achieves a threat detection rate (TDR) of 0.85, false alarm rate (FAR) of 0.10, and a response time (RT) of 3.5 seconds, outperforming conventional IoT–ML safety models. These findings validate the feasibility, efficiency, and robustness of the proposed architecture and confirm the potential of FSL-based techniques for next-generation women’s safety technologies.
journal: International Journal of Informatics and Communication Technology (IJ-ICT)

title: Toward Sex-Specific Host Modulation Therapy for Periodontitis.
abstract: Periodontitis, a leading cause of tooth loss worldwide, arises from a dysregulated host immune response, and males consistently show higher prevalence and more severe disease than females. This disparity historically has been attributed to behavioral/environmental factors, but growing evidence indicates that biological sex, acting through hormonal signaling and sex chromosome-linked genetic mechanisms, independently shapes periodontal immune responses and subsequent bone resorption. In this review, we examine preclinical and clinical evidence on the impact of biological sex on host modulation therapies to prevent periodontitis. The IL-1β/inflammasome pathway and osteoclast differentiation via receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand (RANKL)/osteoprotegerin (OPG) signaling both show clear sex-dependent regulation in experimental periodontitis, illustrating the biological complexity that single-target therapies must address in this heterogeneous condition. In a mouse model, inflammasome-mediated IL-1β signaling drives alveolar bone loss selectively in males, while females progress to comparable bone loss through IL-1β-independent mechanisms. IL-17 plays a dual role, driving inflammatory bone resorption while also supporting antimicrobial defense, and evidence points to this balance being sex dependent, with more severe effects observed in females when IL-17 signaling is disrupted. IL-6 is an established driver of periodontal bone loss, and although sex-specific data within periodontitis remain limited, sex-dependent anti-IL-6 receptor treatment responses have been observed in other inflammatory diseases that warrant further investigation. Complement-mediated immunity shows biological sex differences in humans and animal models, though whether these discrepancies directly influence periodontal disease progression needs to be determined. Resolvins and cyclooxygenase inhibitors also show sex-dependent effects outside the periodontal field. Collectively, this evidence positions biological sex as a tractable, currently underappreciated variable to improve host modulation strategies. Incorporating sex as a biological variable into preclinical and clinical periodontal research and ensuring sex-disaggregated data reporting offer a clear opportunity to develop precise, sex-informed nonsurgical therapeutics that better serve both male and female patients.

title: Animal models to organoids for PK/PD studies of nanomedicines using advanced biomaterials for pancreatic cancer: A review.
abstract: Nanomedicines built on advanced biomaterials are emerging as promising solutions for cancer therapy due to their potential for faster clinical translation. Selecting appropriate animal or in vitro models is critical to accelerating this translation while improving affordability and accessibility. This scoping review examines the preclinical model landscape for Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC), a malignancy projected to become the second leading cause of cancer-related death by 2030. Early diagnosis and timely treatment substantially reduce reliance on surgical intervention and improve survival, underscoring the need for models that support development of early-diagnostic tools and less invasive nanomedicine-based therapies. This review classifies preclinical models ranging from immunocompromised to non-immunocompromised rodents (mice, rats, hamsters) and porcine systems according to their suitability for studying pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) of nanomedicines, and for analyzing mutagenesis, tumor growth, engraftment, metastasis, and tumor heterogeneity. Chemotherapeutic agents and nanodrug delivery systems are compared across these models, with chemically induced rat models identified as particularly robust for PK/PD evaluation. We further assess emerging in vitro organoid models derived from cell lines, primary human tissue, xenografts, and organoid-rodent hybrid systems for their capacity to accelerate drug and nanomedicine screening. Our analysis indicates that in vitro organoid models combined with rat models offer the most efficient platform for demonstrating nanomedicine efficacy, safety, and ability to overcome therapeutic resistance in PDAC. It also highlight opportunities to integrate organoid systems with Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning ( AI/ML) approaches to further accelerate translational timelines, offering a roadmap for aligning model selection with specific clinical endpoints in future nanomedicine development.

title: Cyber-pirates: the perils of agentic AI for the protection of healthcare data.
abstract: The recent unauthorised access by AI agents of Australian Medicare Statistics is alarming. This unauthorised access attack, or "hack," has occurred in the context of similar hacks on Hugging Face and RubyGems by swarms of AI agents acting together. AI agentic hacks represent a substantial cyber security threat, both for large and small organisations, and for sensitive data, such as in healthcare records. We provide a succinct update on these events and basic advice on defending healthcare data against hacks by AI agents.
journal: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

title: Modelling the spatial dynamics of flood inundation in Bayelsa State, Nigeria, using remote sensing and machine learning techniques
abstract: Flooding is a persistent environmental challenge in Bayelsa State, Nigeria, driven by low-lying terrain, high rainfall, and inadequate drainage systems. This study evaluates flood susceptibility in the Lower Niger Basin using a geospatial modelling approach. Ten flood-conditioning factors; rainfall, drainage density, slope, elevation, soil texture, land use/land cover (LULC), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and proximity to rivers were integrated within a Random Forest (RF) framework. Spatial datasets were processed using ArcGIS and Google Earth Engine, and the model was trained with historical flood and non-flood locations to produce a high-resolution susceptibility map. Results indicate that areas receiving 2500 to 3199 mm of annual rainfall, particularly Southern Ijaw, Ekeremor, and Brass, exhibit the highest flood susceptibility. Over 82% of the region is characterized by low slopes (0 to 3°) and elevations ranging from 16 to 41 m, increasing flood vulnerability. High drainage density zones (up to 0.677 km/km²) contribute to flash flooding, while clay and sandy clay loam soils (covering > 60% of the area) reduce infiltration and enhance runoff. Built-up areas and regions with NDVI < 0.1 are also associated with higher flood risk. The RF model achieved an accuracy of 91%, with high-risk zones predominantly located within 1 km of major rivers. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of integrating machine learning with geospatial analysis for flood susceptibility mapping in data-scarce, low-lying environments. The resulting map provides a reliable decision-support tool for flood risk management, land-use planning, and targeted mitigation strategies in Bayelsa State.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven precision immunogenetics for cancer stem cell-targeted CAR immunotherapy
abstract: Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are a major contributor to therapeutic resistance, tumour recurrence, and disease progression because of their self-renewal capacity, phenotypic plasticity, immune evasion, and ability to persist after treatment. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-based immunotherapy has transformed the treatment of several hematological malignancies, but effective targeting of CSC-driven disease, especially solid tumour, remains challenging. Antigen heterogeneity and loss, CSC plasticity, CAR-cell dysfunction, metabolic constraints, and an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment (TME) can limit long-term therapeutic responses. CSC-associated antigens such as CD133, CD44, EpCAM, HER2, CSPG4, ALDH, and EGFRvIII have been investigated as CAR targets, although their heterogeneous and context-dependent expression raises important concerns regarding CSC specificity and on-target/off-tumour toxicity. Artificial intelligence (AI) and computational approaches provide opportunities to integrate genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, spatial, and clinical data for CSC-associated antigen discovery, biomarker identification, CAR design, patient stratification, and toxicity prediction. However, the evidence supporting these applications varies considerably, ranging from computational and preclinical studies to retrospective clinical modelling, while prospective clinical validation of AI-guided CSC-targeted CAR therapy remains limited. Similarly, next-generation platforms, including CAR-natural killer (CAR-NK) cells, CAR-macrophages (CAR-M), gamma-delta CAR-T cells, and CAR-invariant natural killer T (CAR-iNKT) cells, remain at different stages of translational development. This review critically examines CSC biology, mechanisms of resistance to CAR-based therapy, emerging CAR platforms, and the potential role of AI in precision immunogenetics. Particular emphasis is placed on differentiating CSC-intrinsic, CAR-cell-intrinsic, and TME-mediated resistance and on defining the evidence maturity of AI applications. Finally, current challenges in data availability, tumour heterogeneity, model bias, external validation, interpretability, safety, and prospective clinical translation are discussed, together with priorities for developing clinically validated AI-enabled CSC-targeted CAR therapies.
journal: Journal of the Egyptian National Cancer Institute

title: PD-1 deficiency impairs Treg differentiation in Trichinella-infected mice via inhibition of fatty acid oxidation.
abstract: Helminth infections establish long-term host persistence by inducing regulatory immune responses that limit pathology while promoting parasite survival. Programmed death 1 (PD-1), an inhibitory receptor expressed on activated T cells, plays an essential role in maintaining immune homeostasis during chronic infections. Regulatory T cells (Tregs) expand during helminth infection and are critical for controlling excessive inflammation; however, the metabolic mechanisms linking PD-1 signaling to Treg differentiation during helminth infection remain poorly defined. Here, we investigated the role of PD-1 in regulating Treg differentiation during Trichinella spiralis infection, focusing on metabolic reprogramming in CD4⁺ T cells. Using a murine infection model, we compared wild-type and PD-1-deficient (PD-1⁻/⁻) mice and evaluated Treg differentiation in vivo and in a bone marrow-derived dendritic cell (BMDC)-CD4⁺ T-cell co-culture system stimulated with muscle larval excretory-secretory products (MES). PD-1 deficiency significantly reduced splenic FoxP3⁺ Treg frequencies following infection and impaired MES-induced Treg differentiation and Treg-associated cytokine production in vitro. Metabolic profiling revealed that CD4⁺ T cells from infected PD-1⁻/⁻ mice exhibited markedly reduced fatty acid oxidation (FAO), accompanied by decreased expression of Carnitine Palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A), a key rate-limiting enzyme in FAO. PD-1 deficiency was associated with enhanced PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling and suppressed AMPK activation. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of PI3K partially restored FAO activity and rescued Treg differentiation in PD-1⁻/⁻ CD4⁺ T cells. These findings suggest that PD-1 supports Treg development during T. spiralis infection, at least in part, through a CPT1A-associated FAO pathway, highlighting a PD-1-associated metabolic pathway that may contribute to helminth-induced immune regulation.

title: Concurrent Multi-Level Policy Implementation and the Technology Transfer Performance of Chinese Universities
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the effects of concurrent multi-level policy implementation on university technology transfer performance. It clarifies the moderating roles of government financial support and regional research and development (R&D) conditions. It further examines heterogeneous policy effects across university disciplinary characteristics, geographical locations, regional technology intermediary density, and industrial structure. The findings offer a refined empirical perspective for evaluating multi-level policy effectiveness and optimizing university technology transfer practices. They also provide guidance for strengthening basic research capacity and better integrating of basic and applied research in universities. Design/methodology/approach Panel data from 61 universities directly under the Ministry of Education spanning 2011–2019 were analyzed. We employed the Difference-in-Differences (DID) method to empirically test the specific impact of the concurrent implementation of local and university-level policies on university technology transfer. Additionally, moderating effect models and grouped regression are adopted to explore the underlying mechanisms. Findings The empirical results show that the concurrent implementation of local and university-level policies exerts a significantly positive impact on university technology transfer. Second, government financial support and the regional R&D environment play positive moderating roles in the relationship between the joint-treatment indicator and university technology transfer. Third, the positive effect is more salient in specific subsamples, including science and engineering universities, comprehensive universities, universities located in the eastern region, and universities situated in areas with a high density of science and technology intermediaries and a high proportion of the tertiary industry. Research limitations This study has two major limitations. First, due to data accessibility, the research observation window is limited to 2011–2019. Although this period covers the critical pre- and post-revision stage of the Law on the Promotion of the Transformation of Scientific and Technological Achievements and enables the capture of short- and medium-term policy effects, the long-term evolutionary impacts of relevant policies remain to be further explored. Second, to ensure data integrity and sample representativeness, the research sample only covers universities directly affiliated with the Ministry of Education. Future studies can expand the sample scope to incorporate diverse types of higher education institutions to further generalize the existing empirical conclusions. Practical implications This study indicates that the effects of concurrent policy implementation exhibit significant regional and institutional heterogeneity, and that government financial support as well as the regional R&D environment positively moderate these effects. Based on this, in the future construction of multi-level policy systems and the optimization of the innovation ecosystem, it is necessary to balance the rigidity and flexibility of institutional design, improve policy efficiency, and facilitate the transformation of scientific and technological achievements in universities. Originality/Value This study contributes to the extant literature on policy-driven university technology transfer by systematically examining the mechanisms and pathways of the concurrent implementation of local and university-level policies. Unlike prior studies that focus on single-dimensional policy analysis, this paper differentiates between individual policy effects and concurrent policy implementation. It further introduces government financial support and regional R&D conditions as moderating variables to clarify the contingent mechanisms of policy implementation. Combined with heterogeneity analysis of universities’ disciplinary attributes and regional environmental characteristics, this study reveals the differentiated operational logic of concurrent policy implementation across diverse scenarios. The extended research framework enriches the theoretical boundary of policy effectiveness research in university technology transfer, providing empirical evidence for optimizing technology innovation and transformation governance systems.
journal: Journal of Data and Information Science

title: Conservation of Nuclear Receptor DAF-12 with Evidence for Ligand Diversification in Plant-Parasitic Nematodes.
abstract: Plant-parasitic nematodes cause extensive crop losses that threaten global food security and create substantial economic hardship, yet strategies for their control remain limited. Although plant-parasitic nematodes have life cycles that mirror those of their free-living and animal-parasitic relatives, comparatively little is known about the signals that drive life-cycle progression. Dafachronic acids (DAs) are steroid hormones that control life cycle by activating DAF-12 nuclear receptors in Caenorhabditis elegans and animal-parasitic nematodes. To define whether an analogous pathway exists in plant-parasitic nematodes, we investigated the responsiveness of DAF-12 orthologs from six plant-parasitic nematode species to Δ7-DA, an endogenous DAF-12 ligand in C. elegans and several animal-parasitic nematodes. We find that whereas some plant-parasitic nematode receptors are activated by Δ7-DA, others are not. Structural modeling of all six ligand-binding domains, together with docking of Δ7-DA into each model, indicates that responsiveness is governed by a combinatorial ligand-recognition network surrounding the ligand carboxylate rather than by any single contact residue. We further demonstrate that egg and second-stage juvenile extracts from the soybean cyst nematode, Heterodera glycines, lack detectable DA but contain distinct lipophilic fractions that activate its DAF-12 ortholog. Together, these findings suggest that some plant-parasitic nematodes may utilize endogenous DAF-12 ligands that are structurally distinct from DA. Uncovering modulators of this pathway could lead to new strategies to combat nematode-driven crop loss.

title: Digital Empowerment in Rural America: Internet-Capable Technology Use Among Somali Bantu Refugee Families in Western Pennsylvania
abstract: This study examines how Somali Bantu refugee families living in rural Mercer County, Western Pennsylvania, use internet-capable technologies (ICTs) to empower everyday life in the rural United States. Drawing on Mäkinen’s conceptualization of digital empowerment, this study frames empowerment as a process through which refugees use ICTs to cope with challenges and gain control over daily life. Using an ethnographic case study approach, the study focuses on three multigenerational Somali Bantu families (n = 17) residing in a rural farming community between November 2025 and May 2026. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and participant observation across homes, farms, and mosque gatherings, and were analyzed using thematic analysis. Findings suggest ICTs play a significant role in participants’ religious, agricultural, community, and emotional empowerment. Participants used smartphones and social media platforms for online religious communication, halal farming coordination, agricultural learning, maintaining social ties, and coping with emotional stress and isolation. ICTs also supported community belonging, transnational communication, and rural adaptation. The study contributes to community informatics scholarship by demonstrating how a refugee-background farming community appropriates everyday technologies to sustain faith, livelihood, and community in a geographically isolated rural setting. Findings aim to inform policymakers, refugee resettlement agencies, and organizations serving refugee communities about the role ICTs play in rural adaptation and empowerment in the United States.

title: From Governance Principles to Architectural Primitives: Designing and Evaluating a Microservices-Based Smart Governance Platform for a Wellness Tourism Ecosystem
abstract: The growing importance of Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) in tourism underscores the need for governance models that integrate strategic processes with technological infrastructures. Although digital platforms are widely credited with operationalizing governance principles such as transparency, accountability and participation, the mechanisms through which architectural decisions enact those principles remain largely unspecified. This article presents the design and evaluation of a smart governance platform for a wellness tourism ecosystem[1], developed through a hybrid methodology combining Design Science Research with the Waterfall model and Scrum. The study makes three contributions. First, it proposes an explicit mapping between six governance principles and the architectural primitives that enact them — bounded contexts with private data stores, asynchronous event propagation, role-based access control, and a consolidated analytical store — together with the observable evidence each primitive produces. Second, it documents the resulting microservices-based artifact as a reference decomposition, stating the alternatives rejected and the trade-offs accepted. Third, it reports an evaluation combining architectural analysis with functional and load testing, identifying sensitivity points and residual risks alongside confirmed strengths in scalability and reliability. The findings show that governance principles are not satisfied by digital platforms in general, but by specific and traceable architectural choices — notably the reconciliation of transparency and autonomy through the propagation mechanism rather than through access-control policy.

title: Imputation Sensitivity and Robustness of Student Clustering in Higher Education Data
abstract: This paper investigates how different approaches to handling missing data shape the outcomes of unsupervised clustering in educational datasets. Three commonly used imputation algorithms – mean substitution, Random Forest and Multiple Imputation with Chain Equations (MICE) – were applied to student records from a Croatian higher education institution. The analysis included 461 students, with 46 (9.98%) missing values for study duration. Each dataset was analyzed individually using three clustering algorithms: K-means, Ward’s hierarchical clustering and Gaussian mixture model (GMM). The three imputation methods and three clustering algorithms produced nine algorithm-dataset combinations. Solutions containing between two and ten clusters were evaluated using the silhouette coefficient. It was also examined whether the different datasets produced numerically and substantively similar student clusters. The results show that different imputation choices have a pronounced impact on Ward’s hierarchical clustering, which selected ten clusters for MICE, six for Random Forest and four for Mean Replacement. On the other hand, K-means and GMM showed a high degree of robustness, consistently identifying the same number of clusters in all completed datasets – eight clusters for K-means and two for GMM. The analysis showed that when imputation was done with the mean value, all missing study durations were replaced with the same value. In contrast, Random Forest and Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE) estimated different study durations for each student, which preserved larger differences among the imputed values. Despite these methodological differences, several interpretable student profiles emerged repeatedly, including high-achieving students, long-studying older students, low-achieving early-leavers and students with moderate academic success. These results show that the effect of missing data processing on student grouping is algorithm-specific. Solutions based on centroids and mixtures were comparatively robust in this data set, while Ward’s hierarchical clustering produced different results since the imputation methods changed the calculated similarities between students. These results may benefit researchers working with unsupervised machine learning and incomplete educational data sets. Therefore, educational clustering analyses should examine whether different imputation methods produce the same number of clusters, and whether the resulting clusters represent similar groups of students.

title: Automatic keyphrase extraction and annotation: modern theoretical approaches and practical solutions for text and speech
abstract: The exponential growth of textual and audiovisual information has made the task of automatic keyphrase extraction (KE) increasingly significant. This article provides a comprehensive analysis of contemporary theoretical approaches and practical solutions for KE across both text and speech modalities. The primary contribution of this work is its systematic synthesis of these often-disparate research strands into a unified analytical framework, highlighting the evolution of the field from statistical methods towards large language models (LLMs) and end-to-end speech processing. We examine the stages of KE, the characteristics of keyphrases in written and spoken language, and terminological nuances. Various methods for automatic KE are discussed and analyzed in detail: statistical, hybrid, machine learning-based, and structural. The review dedicates substantial attention to emerging paradigms, including keyphrase generation using LLMs, and provides a detailed overview of methodologies and challenges in automatic corpus annotation. Furthermore, we specifically analyze current directions and inherent difficulties in KE for spoken language, comparing transcript based and end-to-end acoustic approaches. This synthesis leads us to conclude that the field is moving towards a more integrated, context-aware paradigm. Future progress will depend on addressing key challenges such as data scarcity for low-resource languages, effective multimodal fusion, and the nuanced evaluation of generative KE systems.

title: An Evaluation of Zero-Shot Classification of Multimodal Foundation Models for Point Clouds
abstract: Modelling the existing building stock for maintenance, renovation, and decommissioning relies on point clouds from laser scanning or photogrammetry, whose objects must be segmented and classified, traditionally with computer vision models that require task-specific training. To avoid this training, this paper proposes to use the zero-shot classification capabilities of multimodal foundation models (MMFMs) for the pre-classification of segmented point clouds. Our approach renders one to four isometric views of each object and classifies them with MMFMs. Weevaluate it on the public datasets ModelNet40 and S3DIS Area 5 across several MMFMs. OnModelNet40, the best configuration, Gemini-3.6-Flash with four views, achieves 55.4% accuracy and a Macro-F1 of 47.7%, and all six MMFMs evaluated with one to four views improve as the number of views increases. On S3DIS, adding textual dimensions derived from an axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) to the RGB views improves the accuracy of all four evaluated models; for Gemini-3.6-Flash, accuracy increases from 42.1% to 60.5% with a Macro-F1 of 59.7%. While MMFMs remain below specialised trained classifiers, they show that MMFMs can support the zero-shot pre-classification of segmented point clouds and could support bootstrapping the annotation of training data. The evaluation framework is publicly available on GitHub.

title: Reliable Retinal Screening with Foundation Models under Distribution Shift
abstract: Reliable deployment of deep learning classifiers for retinal disease screening requires accurate in-distribution classification, effective out-of-distribution (OOD) detection, and well-calibrated predictions under distribution shift. This study investigates the open-world reliability of the EyeCLIP foundation model and evaluates whether calibration-oriented fine-tuning improves performance under external-domain shift. A three-class fundus classification task comprising diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and normal images was constructed using APTOS2019, G1020, and ORIGA, with ORIGA held out entirely for external evaluation. Standard balanced fine-tuning was compared with calibration-oriented fine-tuning and a frozen-feature linear probe. Five OOD scoring methods were evaluated alongside post-hoc temperature scaling and accept–reject analysis. Performance was assessed using classification, OOD detection, and calibration metrics. Standard balanced fine-tuning out-performed calibration-oriented fine-tuning in in-distribution accuracy (0.928 vs. 0.781), k-nearest-neighbor OOD detection (AUROC 0.938 vs. 0.878), and post-hoc OOD calibration (ECE 0.081 vs. 0.450). The calibration-oriented model misclassified 69% of normal ORIGA images as glaucoma. At 25% overall rejection, standard balanced fine-tuning rejected 50.9% of OOD samples while falsely rejecting 1.6% of in-distribution samples. Standard balanced fine-tuning combined with post-hoc calibration and feature-space k-nearest-neighbor abstention provides a simple and effective strategy for improving the reliability of open-world retinal screening.

title: Conditional Scenario Forecasting of Children’s Health Indexes under Social Infrastructure Development: A Four-Outcome System and the Effect of Statistical Registration in the Regions of Uzbekistan
abstract: Purpose of research . Conditional scenario forecast is typically constructed for a single index of health usually infant mortality and cannot reveal the heterogeneous, sometimes opposite, response of different child-health indexes to social infrastructure development. This paper creates a multi-outcome conditional forecast of four child-health indexes under alternative infrastructure trajectories and assesses how far recorded indexes are fit for monitoring the results of such policy . Materials and methods. A balanced panel of fourteen regions of Uzbekistan over 2012–2024 (one hundred and eighty-two observations) is used. Four outcomes infant mortality, proportion of underweight children, incidence of bacterial dysentery and acute respiratory infections are modelled jointly by a system of externally unrelated regressions with regional fixed effects and logarithmic dependent variables. Infrastructure is presented by three composite indexes medical, utility, and educational. Scenario trajectories are specified as index increments calibrated to historical rates, and forecast uncertainty is estimated using the Monte Carlo simulation method. Results. A unified infrastructure-driven acceleration shifts the four indexes in different directions. By 2030, under the forced scenario, infant mortality decreases by 4.2 percent, the proportion of underweight children by 13.3 percent and dysentery incidence by 9.6 percent, while the reported incidence of acute respiratory infections does not decrease, but increases by 1.4 percent. The cause is the positive association of the medical index with the recorded respiratory morbidity, reflecting fuller ascertainment and offsetting the weak protective effect of educational infrastructure . Conclusion. A single-outcome forecast yields a falsely homogeneous picture of improvement. A multi-outcome forecast shows that some child-health indexes are structurally unresponsive to infrastructure development in recorded terms, calling for caution in using reported morbidity as a measure of progress and for well-targeted regional policy.

title: Gaussian Process Modelling for Precision Olive Irrigation-Fertilization Management: Continuous Prediction and Uncertainty Quantification of Olive Oil Quality
abstract: Introduction Olive oil quality is influenced by irrigation, fertilization, and seasonal climate variability. This study aimed to predict quality at unobserved water-fertilizer combinations while quantifying predictive uncertainty for risk-informed management. Methods A two-year (2023-2024) split-plot 3×3 factorial trial at INRA Meknès, Morocco, generated 54 biological olive-oil samples of Olea europaea L. cv. Picholine Marocaine across nine water-fertilizer combinations (50-100% ETc × 50-100% NPK), yielding 324 FTIR-ATR acquisitions. Matérn-5/2 Gaussian Process models with Automatic Relevance Determination were trained on 18 treatment-year means. Performance was assessed using Spearman ρ 2 under leave-one-treatment-out and leave-one-year-out cross-validation. Uncertainty was partitioned into aleatoric, temporal, and epistemic components, and Pareto optimisation identified resource-efficient regimes. Results LOTO-CV ρ 2 ranged from 0.408 (TFC) to 0.750 (carotenoids), with DPPH at 0.633 and TPC at 0.427. LOYO ρ 2 reached 0.790 for carotenoids and 0.494 for TPC. Temporal uncertainty accounted for ~58% of total uncertainty, versus 36% aleatoric and 6% epistemic. TPC was more sensitive to irrigation than fertilization (W/F = 0.22). The Pareto-optimal regime (≈50% ETc × ≈56% NPK) achieved 91% of maximum composite quality with 28% lower fertilisation cost. Discussion Seasonal variability was the dominant uncertainty source, highlighting the importance of multi-year data. Carotenoid and TPC patterns transferred across seasons, whereas DPPH required seasonal recalibration. Conclusion FTIR-GP modelling with Pareto optimisation offers a promising framework for uncertainty-aware olive management, but broader validation across seasons, sites, and cultivars is needed.

title: Differentiable programming for ocean model design and calibration
abstract: Differentiable programming gives numerical models access to the exact gradients of their solution with respect to their inputs, and turns the calibration of model parameters and the training of hybrid machine-learning components into gradient-based optimization problems. Here we use a differentiable version of the ocean model Veros to examine what this capability brings to ocean model design and calibration. The model is written in JAX and computes sensitivities with forward- and reverse-mode automatic differentiation, with no change to its forward numerical behavior. We consider three applications. In the first, two physical parameters, lateral viscosity and bottom friction, are calibrated from satellite-like observables over a two-day control window; the calibrated model restores the simulated circulation over a long term, multi-year evaluation. In the second, a subgrid parameterization representing the backscatter of energy toward resolved scales is trained online and improves the kinetic energy and shear of a long term simulation. In the third, a neural correction is trained online to compensate a biased vertical mixing closure. The simulation is fitted over a two-day control window, and similarly to the previous applications, the correction remains stable and effective over a multi-year free-running simulation. Across the three applications, quantities optimized over windows of about one hundred solver steps yield skill that persists over integration times that are orders of magnitude longer, which indicates that solving online learning problems using differentiable programming is a practical tool for ocean model design and calibration.

title: Polymer Informatics in the Era of Foundation Models: From Representation to Autonomous Design
abstract: Foundation models, pretrained on broad datasets and adapted to multiple tasks, offer a way to reuse chemical knowledge across polymer property prediction and inverse design. Realizing this opportunity requires connecting learned representations to materials whose properties also depend on molecular populations, formulation, processing, and measurement conditions. Here, we review advances in polymer foundation models and the data, representations, and experimental workflows that support their use in materials design. We organize these developments around the polymer material state, a description linking chemical identity to molecular distributions, architecture, morphology, and preparation history relevant to a target property. This perspective relates the material described by a model or simulation to the specimen prepared and measured experimentally. We examine what polymer models learn during pretraining and adaptation, how polymer representations retain relevant material information, and how predictions can guide experimental choices. The discussion follows candidate polymers through synthesis, processing, and prospective experimental validation to consider how experimental feedback can improve both models and the preparation of materials for specific applications. We also discuss how foundation models could help connect candidate selection with automated experiments, and the practical requirements for reliable and more autonomous polymer design. Our aim is to clarify how progress in foundation models can meet the practical needs of polymer research and support closer connections between computational polymer design and experimental discovery.
