title: Economic and mathematical modelling of innovative development of the agricultural sector.
abstract: Purpose: To develop an economic and mathematical model of innovation development in the agricultural sector to quantitatively assess the impact of capital investment, human capital, and energy efficiency on agricultural value added in Ukraine, accounting for energy efficiency factors. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study combined a systematic review of scientific literature with economic-statistical and economic-mathematical modelling. The analysis was based on official data from the State Statistics Service of Ukraine and Eurostat for 2014–2024 to evaluate relationships between investment, human capital, energy efficiency, and agricultural performance. Linear and log-linear regression models were estimated by ordinary least squares (11 annual observations for 2014–2024), with multicollinearity testing (VIF) and residual diagnostics; EU-27 trends were analysed using descriptive and correlation analysis. Research Limitations: The analysis relies on macro-level data and does not examine enterprise-level differences. Future research should incorporate firm-level indicators and institutional factors. Findings: Capital investment promotes technological modernisation and production efficiency, while qualified human capital enhances labour productivity and innovation capacity. Energy-efficient technologies reduce resource consumption, optimise production costs, and strengthen sustainability. Hybrid and digital analytical models improve forecasting accuracy and support management under market and environmental uncertainty. The findings confirm that investment, technology transfer, human capital, and energy efficiency significantly contribute to agricultural competitiveness and sustainable growth in Ukraine and the European Union. Practical Implication: The results support evidence-based policies promoting investment, workforce development, and energy-efficient technologies. Social Implication: Innovation strengthens rural development, environmental sustainability, and food security. Originality/Value: The study provides an integrated quantitative framework linking investment, human capital, and energy efficiency to agricultural value creation. The novelty lies in including energy consumption as an explicit factor alongside capital investment and human capital indicators (employment, personnel costs and wages) in a single value-added model for Ukraine, complemented by an EU-27 analysis of energy productivity and labour dynamics, whereas existing approaches assess these factors separately (Table 1).

title: TOWARD SUSTAINABLE AGRITOURISM: HOW SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY SHAPES TOURIST CITIZENSHIP BEHAVIOR
abstract: Agritourism has increasingly emerged as an important form of sustainable tourism due to its economic, social, cultural, and environmental contributions to rural communities. Despite the growing attention to sustainable tourism, limited research has examined how destination social responsibility encourages tourists to engage in voluntary behaviors that support destinations, particularly in agritourism settings. In addition, previous studies have provided limited understanding of the psychological and contextual mechanisms through which destination social responsibility influences responsible tourist behavior. To address these gaps, the study develops and tests an integrated framework based on the stimulus–organism– response framework and signaling theory to explain the psychological and social mechanisms through which destination social responsibility influences responsible tourist behavior. Using partial least squares structural equation modeling on a sample of 424 tourists at agritourism destinations in Vietnam, we find that perceived destination social responsibility stron gly and positively predicts tourist citizenship behavior. Meanwhile, tourist-destination congruence and place attachment serve as partial mediators. Furthermore, destination reputation positively moderates the relationship between perceived destination social responsibility and tourist citizenship behavior. This study contributes to the sustainable tourism literature by clarifying the cognitive, emotional, and signaling processes underlying responsible tourist behavior in agritourism settings. The findin gs also provide practical implications for destination managers seeking to develop culturally aligned and reputation-enhancing strategies to foster sustainable agritourism development.

title: Understanding socio-ecological crises through agri-food systems
abstract: This forum examines how socio-ecological crises are reshaping labor–nature relations in contemporary agri-food systems. These transformations are examined through five ethnographic cases that focus on: the cheapening of labor in the Mexican avocado industry; the migrant labor paradox in Austrian greenhouses; the novel labor surveillance dynamics in digitalized South African agriculture; the entanglement of human and non-human labor in French conservation agriculture; and the re-valuation of tortilla production in Mexico. The contributions are united by a common understanding of labor processes as mediators of the nature–society relationship and seek to broaden current debates in the study of the work-environment nexus. The forum opens up questions about sustained pressure on laborers and the combined exhaustion of soils, bodies, and climates.

title: “Forcing a standard that is unachievable”
abstract: South Africa is a major Southern Hemisphere exporter of fresh fruit, the largest share of which is destined for counter-seasonal, high-value European markets. Remote and proximal sensing technologies, such as satellites, drones, and field cameras, are among the cluster of digital agricultural technologies, also known as “agritech,” promising optimization of yields, the lowering of input costs, and compliance with standards set by overseas agri-food governance actors in the horticultural production network. Reflecting on the labor-environment nexus in the transition to the digital-industrial fruit farm, the following contribution explores data-driven technologies employed at the orchard level. I draw on ethnographic material collected between 2024 and 2025 in the Western Cape, South Africa's most economically productive and labor-intensive fruit growing region, focusing on the strategies of farm managers, agritech employees, and local fruit export actors. This article puts forward two main observations: (1) digital intervention should be examined in light of commercial pressures placed on producers in the form of a double bind of sustainability standards and quality specifications, as stipulated by supermarket retailers; and (2) well-known trends of labor restructuring in the post-deregulation period from the mid-1990s onward are being accelerated by the deployment of digital technologies and are further compounded by the labor redistribution accompanying the introduction of new categories of highly skilled technical workers.

title: Quantifying "Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus"-like Brain Morphometry patterns in an Alzheimer's Disease Cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) is largely underdiagnosed. It is a potentially treatable contributor to cognitive decline, and cognitive improvement may occur even with comorbid Alzheimer's disease. However, iNPH-related imaging features can overlap with age-related and neurodegenerative atrophy, making differentiation difficult. Automated morphometric profiling of NPH-like patterns in biomarker-defined Alzheimer's disease cohorts has not been systematically explored. This pilot study aimed to quantify iNPH-like brain morphometry in an Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort using deep-learning-based morphometry and automated callosal angle measurement. MATERIALS AND METHODS We included N=30 amyloid-negative reference iNPH patients and N=1003 ADNI participants with structural T1-weighted MRI and CSF biomarkers. Age- and sex-adjusted volumetric z-scores were obtained using a deep-learning-based morphometry algorithm. We derived an iNPH morphometric profile using principal component analysis and Gaussian modeling of the reference iNPH cohort and applied it to the ADNI participants to compute individual iNPH similarity scores. We also automated callosal angle measurement for further clinical representation. We compared scores across cognitive stages and biological Alzheimer's disease groups and evaluated against expert Radscale review. RESULTS iNPH-like morphometry increased with cognitive impairment, with mean differences of 0.03 between cognitively normal and mild cognitive impairment (p=0.06), 0.06 between mild cognitive impairment and dementia (p<0.001), and 0.09 between cognitively normal and dementia groups (p<0.001). Among cognitively impaired participants, scores were higher in biologically-defined Alzheimer's disease patients than biologically-defined non-Alzheimer's disease patients (mean difference=0.08, p<0.001). The iNPH similarity score correlated most strongly with ventricular enlargement features. Automated callosal angle measurements showed high agreement with expert ratings (Gwet's AC1 = 0.939) and angles below 90° occurred in 1.5% of ADNI participants. CONCLUSIONS Automated normative morphometric profiling and callosal angle quantification identified heterogeneous iNPH-like structural patterns in the ADNI cohort. These tools provide a scalable approach for characterizing iNPH-like imaging features in dementia cohorts where identifying a potentially treatable contributor to cognitive impairment remains relevant. Further clinical validation remains necessary.

title: The concept of adaptive management of the process of launching innovative medicines to the pharmaceutical markets of BRICS countries (review)
abstract: The article substantiates the need for the BRICS countries to transition from static to adaptive models of regulatory governance for the process of launching innovative medicines, primarily advanced therapy medicinal products (ATMPs), to the market. Based on a system-oriented analysis of scientific publications and official regulatory documents, trends in the development of biotechnological medicines and the transformation of regulatory systems are identified. It is demonstrated that China, India, Brazil, South Africa, Russia, and the EAEU states are implementing various configurations of adaptive regulation, including accelerated and prioritized procedures, conditional approvals, reliance approaches, Early Access Programs (EAPs), digitalization of dossiers (CTDs), and the integration of realworld evidence. A concept of adaptive management is proposed, including interrelated notions as follows: adaptive drug lifecycle management, adaptive regulation, adaptive pathways and adaptive design of clinical trials. This model is shown to allow for reducing delays in providing access to vital innovative medicines along with strengthening the scientific and methodological basis for regulatory decisions. Priority areas for the formation of a common adaptive regulatory space for BRICS countries are identified, including the development of joint scientific consulting centers, the harmonization of procedures, the expansion of mutual recognition practices, and the integration of digital technologies.

title: A physics-guided uncertainty calibration framework for reliable probabilistic rainfall forecasting under heavy and extreme rainfall conditions
abstract: Reliable rainfall forecasting requires not only accurate point predictions but also well-calibrated estimates of predictive uncertainty, particularly during heavy and extreme events where forecast errors carry the greatest operational consequence. Deterministic machine learning models provide point forecasts without quantifying uncertainty, while existing probabilistic methods generally derive uncertainty from statistical relationships in the available data without explicitly conditioning it on the physical state of the atmosphere. This study presents a physics-guided uncertainty calibration framework for probabilistic rainfall forecasting. A two-stage architecture employs gradient-boosted regression to estimate the conditional mean and a separate heteroscedastic model trained on out-of-fold residuals to estimate the predictive variance. An interpretable Atmospheric Instability Score, constructed from moisture, thermodynamic, synoptic, and dynamic indicators weighted by variance-model feature importance, then scales the predictive variance on a per-sample basis. The framework is evaluated on the WeatherAUS dataset (145,460 daily observations, 49 stations) for next-day rainfall using rolling-origin validation across five expanding windows. Physics-guided calibration is found not to improve average probabilistic skill, as the Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) achieves its best overall value without calibration. It does, however, yield statistically significant improvements in the regimes of greatest operational importance, reducing CRPS by 0.76% for heavy rainfall (20–50 mm, n = 1,632; p 50 mm, n = 362, p < 10 –11 ), improving 70.5% and 76.2% of days respectively. The optimal calibration strength increases monotonically with rainfall intensity. The framework therefore trades average sharpness for tail reliability, at a computational cost an order of magnitude below comparable probabilistic baselines.

title: Single-Class and Three-Class Detection of Foxtail Species Using YOLOv8, YOLO11, and YOLO26 Architectures
abstract: Automatic weed detection represents a tool of interest for precision agriculture and crop monitoring. In this work, the performance of YOLOv8, YOLO11, and YOLO26 was evaluated for the detection of the Foxtail species Cenchrus setaceus and Cenchrus alopecuroides (grouped into a single class), Cortaderia jubata, and Digitaria insularis, due to their presence in Colombia and the large number of images available for their training and evaluation. Images obtained from iNaturalist, Wikimedia Commons, Pl@ntNet and the authors’ own collection were used to construct a dataset of 3156 images. The models were evaluated based on the metrics of Precision, Recall, F1-score, mAP@50, mAP@50-95, and inference speed. The results showed the YOLO26 family remained competitive in each experiment, with the YOLO26s model standing out for both configurations. In addition, the quality and consistency of the dataset labels have a great influence on training efficiency. The results obtained demonstrated the potential of YOLO architectures for the automatic identification of Foxtail species.

title: Four-Year Continuous Rhizobium–Legume Green Manure Synergy Improves Reclaimed Mine Soil Fertility by Regulating the Soil Biochemical Processes
abstract: Reclaimed mine soils in northern China suffer from extreme nutrient deficiency, low organic matter content, and impaired microbial activity, which severely challenge ecological restoration. Leguminous green manures inoculated with high-efficiency rhizobia offer a promising bioremediation strategy. However, long-term field evidence and understandings of microbial mechanisms remain insufficient. A 4-year consecutive field experiment was conducted with three legumes (Vicia villosa Roth, Vicia sativa L. and Glycine max (L.) Merr.) inoculated with host-specific rhizobia. Plant traits, soil properties, enzyme activities, and microbial communities were analysed using redundancy analysis (RDA), co-occurrence network analysis, and structural equation modelling (SEM). Compared with the corresponding non-inoculated green manure controls, rhizobium inoculation increased dry matter yield by 96.61–185.40% and improved soil nutrient contents and enzyme activities (p < 0.05) across legume species. The rhizobium–legume green manure treatments markedly reshaped the soil bacterial and fungal community structure relative to the bare-soil control, enriching putatively beneficial genera and suppressing a pathogenic genus (p < 0.05); because the non-inoculated green manure plots were not sequenced, these shifts cannot be attributed to inoculation alone. RDA identified soil organic matter and invertases as core drivers of bacterial communities, whereas total nitrogen dominated fungal community structuring. Co-occurrence networks of inoculated treatments displayed markedly higher complexity and tighter connectivity, with soil organic matter, bacterial Shannon diversity, and urease identified as core regulatory hubs. SEM revealed a robust positive cascading pathway, whereby rhizobium inoculation promoted green manure growth, enhancing soil fertility, which in turn stimulated soil enzyme activities. The standardised effect of inoculation on green manure growth was 0.885, and its indirect effects transmitted through growth reached 0.614 on soil fertility and 0.276 on soil enzyme activity. Planting green manure per se also exerted a strong effect on soil fertility (β = 0.470, p < 0.001), with an indirect effect of 0.208 on soil enzyme activity, indicating that crop establishment accounted for a substantial part of the observed improvement. Rhizobium inoculation enhanced remediation efficiency mainly by amplifying this plant-growth-mediated cascade rather than by directly altering soil biochemical properties. The Vicia villosa Roth + Rhizobium leguminosarum M16 system was optimal, improving soil fertility via a microbial enzyme-mediated positive cascade. This study provides a promising model for mine soil restoration.

title: Soil Health Assessment for Crop-Specific Production: Linking Soil Microbiomes, Pathogen Risk, and Crop Nutritional and Phytochemical Quality
abstract: Soil degradation is one of the greatest threats to sustainable agriculture, yet current soil health assessment frameworks largely rely on physicochemical indicators and may insufficiently account for crop-specific biological requirements and microbiome functions. Increasing evidence indicates that different crops require distinct combinations of physical, chemical, and biological soil properties and recruit differentially enriched rhizosphere microbial assemblages that regulate nutrient cycling, disease suppression, plant performance, and nutritional quality. This review critically examines current concepts of soil quality and soil health and highlights the need to shift from generalized toward crop-specific soil health assessment. We synthesize the principal physical, chemical, and biological indicators of soil health, with emphasis on soil microbiomes, beneficial microorganisms, soil-borne pathogens, molecular diagnostic approaches, and representative sampling strategies. Using publicly available FAOSTAT and EPPO datasets as an exploratory European case study, we describe continental crop production patterns and the geographical occurrence of major plant pathogens to illustrate how regional crop production and pathogen records can provide context for crop-specific soil health assessment. We further assess evidence linking soil properties and plant-associated microbiomes with crop nutrient composition and bioactive phytochemical accumulation. Collectively, this review proposes a crop-specific conceptual framework that integrates ecological, biological, and agronomic processes to support the interpretation of soil health measurements and provides a basis for future empirical validation.

title: Full Bayesian Analysis of Seasonal Vector Autoregressive Models: An Application to Solar Radiation in Najran, Saudi Arabia
abstract: Modelling multiple seasonal time series is a pervasive challenge across diverse domains, including energy, transportation, and financial markets. Existing Bayesian methods for seasonal vector autoregressive (SeVAR) models treat lag-order identification, coefficient estimation, and multi-step forecasting as separate tasks, lacking a unified framework. To address this limitation, we develop a comprehensive Gibbs sampling scheme capable of executing all three tasks simultaneously for SeVAR processes. We embed the SeVAR model in a hierarchical Bayes mixture framework in the spirit of group (block) stochastic search variable selection (Block-SSVS). Rather than assigning inclusion indicators to individual coefficients, a single Bernoulli-distributed binary indicator is attached to each lag matrix, ensuring that all entries within a block are either jointly retained or jointly shrunk toward zero. Following the free-parameter approximation standard in the literature, the cross (regular×seasonal) lag blocks are treated as unrestricted free parameters rather than as the exact products implied by the multiplicative operator, so the fitted model is a seasonally structured subset VAR over the candidate lag set generated by that operator. A block-structured spike-and-slab matrix normal prior governs the stacked coefficient matrix conditional on these block indicators and the innovation precision matrix, and a Wishart prior completes the precision-matrix specification. Within this hierarchical structure, we establish the closed-form full conditional posteriors for all model parameters. Specifically, we derive that the coefficient matrix follows a matrix normal distribution, the precision matrix yields a Wishart posterior, and each block indicator follows a Bernoulli posterior governed by the joint, matrix-variate evidence of its block. Furthermore, the one-step and multi-step conditional predictive distributions are established as a multivariate normal structure. Leveraging these results, we construct a stochastic simulation-based recursion to produce multi-step forecasts. The resulting posterior block-inclusion probabilities furnish an automatic best-subset SeVAR model at no additional computational cost beyond the Gibbs sampler itself. A controlled Monte Carlo study confirms the accuracy of the procedure for identification, estimation, and prediction. In addition, an application to hourly solar radiation in Najran, Saudi Arabia, demonstrates the framework’s identification capacity on genuinely bivariate stochastic data, with forecast accuracy reported at the data’s own predictability floor.

title: Effects of Fertilisation Practices on Nutrient Cycling Through the Regulation of Soil’s Physicochemical Properties and Microbial Communities
abstract: Continuous cultivation and fertiliser inputs restructure the spatial distribution of soil nutrient pools and drive the evolution of the underlying soil microenvironment. To elucidate the effects of long-term agricultural interventions on nutrient dynamics and crop productivity in farmland, this study systematically evaluated the long-term ecological effects of fertilisation strategies based on a 46-year long-term wheat–soybean rotation experiment. Twelve fertilisation treatments, including an unfertilised control, straw return, organic manure, and different chemical fertiliser rates alone or in combination with organic amendments, were established. The physicochemical properties of non-rhizosphere soil were systematically determined, and metagenomic sequencing was used to characterise the bacterial community’s diversity and structure. Long-term excessive dependence on chemical fertilisers severely disrupted the soil chemical balance, as indicated by the excessive accumulation of available phosphorus, different available potassium levels among treatments, and decline in pH, increasing the environmental risks associated with agricultural production. The manure-only and manure plus low-rate mineral treatments had more available potassium and showed soil surface features of unverified composition in SEM images. Redundancy analysis revealed that the soil pH, available phosphorus, and available potassium were the principal physicochemical environmental factors associated with differences in non-rhizosphere bacterial communities. Structural equation modelling indicated that although high-rate chemical fertilisation directly promoted wheat yields by increasing available phosphorus, it indirectly suppressed non-rhizosphere microbial diversity by decreasing the soil pH, potentially threatening the long-term sustainability of agricultural productivity. Overall, optimising the fertiliser composition and adopting combined organic and mineral fertilisation are important for balancing soil nutrients, maintaining microbial ecological stability, and achieving sustainable agricultural development.

title: Beyond Nitrogen Status: Predicting Crop Response to Additional Nitrogen in Intensive Vegetable Production Systems
abstract: Crop response to nitrogen (N) fertilizer varies across space and time due to complex interactions among soil properties, weather, water availability, crop characteristics, and management practices, making the response to additional N difficult to predict. This variability presents a major challenge for N management because measurements of soil or crop N status do not necessarily indicate whether additional N will increase crop yield or quality. In intensive vegetable systems, short production cycles, frequent irrigation or fertigation, relatively shallow rooting in some crops, and high-value crops create narrow margins between insufficient and excessive N supply. The objectives of this critical review were to (i) examine how N supply, transformations and losses, water dynamics, root acquisition, and dynamic crop N demand generate variation in N response within genotype (crop) × environment × management (G × E × M) interactions; (ii) evaluate the capacity and limitations of soil and plant diagnostics, remote sensing, process-based models, and data-driven approaches to predict N response; (iii) identify factors limiting the transferability of N-response predictions; and (iv) define research priorities for predicting the marginal crop response to additional N and its uncertainty. This review identifies interactions among indigenous N supply, N transformations, soil water, root acquisition, and dynamic crop demand as major sources of variation in fertilizer response. Although soil and plant diagnostics, remote sensing, process-based models, and data-driven approaches provide valuable information about N status and crop performance, their capacity to predict the marginal yield or quality response to additional N remains constrained by incomplete process representation and limited counterfactual evidence. Prediction transferability is further limited by variation in G × E × M conditions, highlighting the need for response-generating experiments, improved representation of soil–plant–water interactions, explicit quantification of uncertainty, and independent validation across environments.

title: Genotypic Adaptation of Durum Wheat to Contrasting Water Regimes: Linking Phenology, Chlorophyll Status, Yield Components, and Grain Yield
abstract: Water scarcity is a recurrent constraint to durum wheat production in semi-arid Mediterranean-type environments, yet genotype performance can change sharply with the timing and severity of seasonal drought. This study quantified phenological, chlorophyll-related, yield-component, and grain-yield responses of 45 durum wheat genotypes grown during 2021–2022 and 2022–2023 under rainfed and supplementary-irrigated field conditions in Diyarbakır, southeastern Türkiye. The experiment comprised equal-sized plots with four replications under each water regime. Supplementary irrigation was delivered by drip irrigation in five applications beginning at stem elongation. Precipitation from sowing to heading was 187.0 mm in 2021–2022 and 285.5 mm in 2022–2023, and April was warmer in the first season (17.9 °C versus 14.7 °C). Grain yield was significantly affected by growing season, water regime, genotype, and all two- and three-way interactions (p < 0.01), although diagnostic tests indicated heterogeneous residual variance among environments and the combined fixed-effect ANOVA is therefore interpreted cautiously. Mean grain yield under rainfed conditions was 466.5 and 3254.3 kg ha−1 in the first and second seasons, respectively, compared with 4208.1 and 5560.9 kg ha−1 under supplementary irrigation. The exceptionally low first-season rainfed yield represents a near-crop-failure environment; stand-count data were not available to separate establishment losses from subsequent drought effects. Pooled drought indices descriptively ranked Fırat-93 highest for STI (0.638) and GMP (3901.4 kg ha−1), whereas Şahinbey had the highest pooled YSI (0.518); these index differences were not subjected to inferential significance testing and should not be interpreted as statistically distinct tolerance classes. Grain yield was associated with SPAD and yield components in pooled genotype means, but these associations were environment dependent. The results characterize genotype responses across four site-year × water-regime combinations and provide hypotheses for validation in broader multi-location and multi-year trials.

title: Residual Diagnosis-Guided Abundance Correction for Blind Hyperspectral Image Unmixing
abstract: Recent blind hyperspectral image unmixing methods have achieved effective spectral–spatial representation, yet the reliability of estimated abundances remains difficult to assess because errors in jointly estimated endmembers and abundances can compensate for each other. To address this issue, we propose Residual Diagnosis-Guided Abundance Correction (RDAC), a post-correction framework that preserves the initial abundance estimate as an anchor and characterizes its mismatch using structured reconstruction residuals. Abundance candidates are then combined with structured residual information, while only 1% reference abundances are used to learn the correction. RDAC was evaluated on the Jasper Ridge, Samson, and Urban datasets. With UNMamba as the primary blind-unmixing backbone, RDAC achieved A-RMSEs of 0.0229, 0.0175, and 0.0359, reducing the initial errors by 55.05%, 70.80%, and 59.63%, respectively. It also achieved the lowest mean A-RMSE among the compared methods on Jasper Ridge and Samson while remaining competitive on Urban. Further experiments showed that reconstruction error alone does not reliably indicate abundance accuracy. When applied to NMF, RDAC reduced A-RMSE by 80.45%, 89.25%, and 77.61% on the three datasets. The results indicate that structured residual diagnosis can support abundance correction under limited supervision, and the NMF experiment shows that the same correction framework can also be used with an alternative blind-unmixing backbone.

title: A Machine Learning Approach for XCH4 Retrieval over China Based on TROPOMI Spectral Features
abstract: Methane is a major greenhouse gas that plays a critical role in climate change. Accurate monitoring of methane at the regional scale is essential for understanding its spatiotemporal dynamics and underlying processes. Here, a machine learning-based framework is developed to retrieve column-averaged methane (XCH4) by integrating shortwave infrared spectral information from TROPOMI. Spectral channels are first analyzed through machine learning-based feature importance analysis, and normalized spectral features are subsequently constructed. These features are then combined with auxiliary variables, including meteorological conditions, observation geometry, and surface environmental factors, to develop an XCH4 retrieval model. The GOSAT L2 XCH4 product is introduced as a high-accuracy reference observation for correcting the retrieved XCH4 results, and independent validation is conducted using observations from the TCCON site. Among the evaluated models, XGBoost demonstrates the best performance, achieving an R2 of 0.91 and an RMSE of 9.28 ppb under five-fold cross-validation. The model also maintains relatively better predictive performance compared with other models under both temporal and spatial extrapolation scenarios. Compared with the TROPOMI L2 product, the retrieved XCH4 shows improved agreement with TCCON observations, with a higher correlation (R = 0.84) and reduced errors. Based on this approach, a daily, spatially continuous XCH4 dataset over China for 2021 is generated. Analysis of the retrieved dataset reveals pronounced spatiotemporal patterns, characterized by higher XCH4 concentrations in eastern China and lower values in the western regions, as well as a distinct seasonal cycle.

title: Remote Sensing Bathymetry of Nearshore Island Reefs via an Enhanced Dual-Stream Mixture Density Network
abstract: High-resolution bathymetry is critical for nearshore reefs, navigation, and island engineering. This paper proposes an Enhanced Mixture Density Network (EMDN) using dual-stream feature disentanglement and mixed total variance regularization to improve both accuracy and reliability of satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB). Validated with ICESat-2 and Sentinel-2 data over island reefs in the South China Sea and Hawaii, EMDN achieves RMSEs of 1.20 m, 1.24 m, and 3.71 m at Ganquan, Guangjin, and West Molokai, with the lowest mean uncertainties (0.76 m, 0.75 m, 2.46 m). Comparisons with the evaluated baselines demonstrate improved bathymetric accuracy and lower CRPS values, together with sharper prediction intervals and competitive calibration, highlighting the potential of EMDN for nearshore reef bathymetric mapping.

title: A Multiscale Remote-Sensing Assessment of Root-Zone Soil Moisture, Evapotranspiration and Canopy Moisture Stress Across Uruguay During the 2020–2023 Drought
abstract: Drought affects meteorological forcing, root-zone water availability and land-surface functioning at different spatial and temporal supports. We evaluated Uruguay’s 2020–2023 drought using an observational 2016–2024 panel of 1423 SMAP parent cells. Monthly SPEI-3, SPEI-6 and SPEI-12 represented short, intermediate and persistent climatic water-balance deficits. SMAP root-zone soil moisture (RZSM) was retained at 9 km support, whereas actual evapotranspiration (ETa) and the moisture stress index (MSI) were summarized from approximately 500 m pixels using annual MapBiomas fractions for grassland, cropland and silviculture within each parent cell. For each cell and 8-day composite position, responses were expressed relative to the corresponding 2016–2019 mean. An interval was classified as locally dry when its overlap-day-weighted SPEI-12 was below −1. During 2020–2023, RZSM responses ranged from −13.09% to −16.63% among dominant landscape domains. Fraction-weighted ETa responses were −8.69% for grassland, −6.75% for cropland and −7.39% for silviculture, while oriented MSI responses were −6.62%, −3.32% and −11.20%, respectively. At lag zero, monthly RZSM correlated the most strongly with SPEI-3 (r = 0.81), followed by SPEI-6 (r = 0.64) and SPEI-12 (r = 0.51). At native 8-day support, RZSM was positively aligned with ETa (r = 0.42–0.57) and the oriented MSI (r = 0.31–0.59), although prewhitening weakened some associations. Overall, the 2020–2023 drought was consistently expressed across meteorological, root-zone and land-surface indicators. The strong association between SPEI-3 and RZSM, together with consistent land-surface departures and product-dependent ETa variation among components, highlights the value of multiscale monitoring for characterizing drought intensity and ecosystem responses across Uruguay.

title: Can Digital Inclusive Finance Reduce Agricultural Pollution Emission Intensity?
abstract: As an important component of rural revitalization and the green transformation of agriculture, the effectiveness of agricultural pollution control depends on the efficient mobilization and use of rural financial resources. Using a balanced panel of 31 Chinese provinces over 2011–2024, this study employs a two-way fixed effects model, a shift-share instrumental variable strategy, a mediation analysis and a panel threshold model to examine how digital inclusive finance affects agricultural pollution emission intensity. Three findings stand out. First, digital inclusive finance significantly reduces pollution emission intensity, with a 1% increase in the digital inclusive finance index lowering emission intensity by about 0.286%. Second, the effect operates partly through an indirect channel: digital inclusive finance fosters new quality agricultural productive forces, which in turn curb pollution, and the indirect effect is estimated with bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals. Third, the relationship is non-linear and follows a double-threshold pattern of increasing marginal returns. Agricultural economic scale, cropping structure and livestock structure are positively associated with pollution, as are environmental regulation and production conditions, whereas a more capable agricultural workforce and a larger stock of agricultural business entities reduce pollution. The study’s novelty lies in formally introducing agricultural new quality productive forces as a mediating mechanism linking digital inclusive finance to agricultural pollution control and in documenting its threshold-shaped, increasingly pronounced effect.

title: Eksplorasi Model Smart Halal Business Incubator Berbasis Artificial Intelligence untuk Mendukung Transformasi Digital UMKM Halal di Kabupaten Deli Serdang
abstract: The global halal industry has experienced rapid growth, prompting the Indonesian government to strengthen the halal MSME ecosystem through certification, mentoring, and digitalisation programmes. However, halal MSMEs in developing regions such as Deli Serdang Regency still face constraints, including limited mentor availability, restricted market access, slow halal certification processes, and the low utilisation of artificial intelligence (AI) in business incubation. This study aims to explore an AI-based Smart Halal Business Incubator model that can support the digital transformation of halal MSMEs in Deli Serdang Regency. The study employs an exploratory qualitative approach using the systematic grounded theory strategy of Strauss and Corbin, involving halal MSME actors, academics, local government, halal process assistants, business incubator managers, investors, and halal certification bodies as purposively selected informants until data saturation was reached. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, FGDs, observation, and documentation, and were analysed through open, axial, and selective coding. The findings yield a new conceptual framework, the AI-Driven Smart Halal Business Incubation Framework (ASHBI Framework).

title: Chatbot Workflow Automation Using n8n as an Innovation in Digital Academic Services in Higher Education
abstract: Improving the quality of digital academic services in higher education requires systems that are fast, responsive, structured, and accountable. While chatbots are commonly used as digital service tools, their implementation often focuses on conversation rather than effective management of service processes. This study develops workflow automation using n8n, a node automation tool, to support academic service tasks. Employing the Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, the research includes problem identification, solution design, artifact development, and system evaluation. The result is a modular, reusable, node-based workflow automation model that manages academic service processes. Evaluation across four different service scenarios demonstrated that the workflows operated as intended, enhancing service accessibility, process clarity, and consistency in service delivery. This model offers a practical framework for higher education institutions to adopt and implement efficient digital academic services.
journal: Jurnal JTIK (Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Komunikasi)

title: Directional Robustness Asymmetry in Indonesian Sarcasm Detection: A Cross-Platform Evaluation of IndoRoBERTa on X and Reddit
abstract: Sarcasm can reverse sentence polarity, making it one of the hardest problems in natural language processing and a persistent obstacle to reliable sentiment analysis on social media, where models are often deployed on platforms they were not trained on. Research on Indonesian sarcasm has largely stayed within a single domain or tested transfer in only one direction, leaving the cross-domain robustness of the IndoRoBERTa family on the IdSarcasm benchmark unclear. This study measures and compares the cross-domain robustness of IndoRoBERTa-small and IndoRoBERTa-base, with IndoBERT as a baseline, across X (Twitter) and Reddit, using the F1 gap (ΔF1) after cleaning anonymization artifacts, adding a data-size control, and running Stratified 5-Fold cross-validation. The results reveal a one-sided asymmetry: X → Reddit transfer is far more fragile (ΔF1 0.345–0.400) than Reddit → X (0.135–0.240), failing by missing sarcasm (false negatives) rather than over-flagging it (false positives). Practically, training on the context-rich domain (Reddit) and choosing IndoRoBERTa-base give the most reliable cross-platform sarcasm detection, with direction-specific mitigation recommended for robust deployment.
journal: Jurnal JTIK (Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Komunikasi)

title: Architecture of the management system for the efficiency of business processes of agricultural enterprises
abstract: The article substantiates the architecture of a system for managing business process efficiency in agricultural enterprises as an integrated structural and functional model that connects strategic objectives, process activities, resources, information and analytical support, digital technologies, performance evaluation, and managerial decision-making. The research aims to develop a conceptual and structural-functional approach to organizing the management of business process efficiency in agricultural enterprises, taking into account the specific conditions of agricultural production. The study applies a systems approach, analysis and synthesis, structural-functional modeling, process-oriented analysis, and conceptual generalization. The proposed architecture integrates strategic, process, managerial, information-analytical, digital, and development contours and establishes their functional relationships with the external environment, resources, stakeholders, and management results. A closed management cycle is established, which includes goal setting, formation of key performance indicators, process monitoring, performance evaluation, diagnosis of deviations and their causes, managerial decision-making, implementation of managerial influence, and subsequent process improvement. The results demonstrate that performance evaluation should not be treated as the final stage of management, but as an information basis for the next managerial intervention and a new management cycle. The scientific novelty lies in the conceptual integration of three interrelated components: the architecture defines the composition and relationships of the management system; the management cycle determines the sequence and logic of its functioning; and process maturity characterizes the enterprise’s capability to apply, integrate, and continuously develop the respective management mechanisms. This paper proposes a five-level process maturity model comprising initial, basic, managed, integrated, and developing levels. The model reflects the transition from predominantly reactive and functionally fragmented management to data-based, integrated, proactive, and continuously improving management of interconnected business processes. The practical significance of the research consists in the possibility of using the proposed architecture as a conceptual basis for designing and improving management systems, coordinating business processes, organizing performance monitoring, integrating digital and analytical tools, and supporting managerial decisions in agricultural enterprises. Further research should focus on developing a scientific and methodological toolkit to quantitatively assess the actual maturity and efficiency of business process management, identify strengths and weaknesses, and substantiate priority areas for improvement at the enterprise level. Keywords: architecture; business processes; efficiency management; agricultural enterprises; process maturity; management cycle.
journal: Actual problems of innovative economy and law

title: Methodological approaches to assessing the levels and effectiveness of innovative development in the agricultural complex
abstract: The article provides a theoretical and methodological substantiation and systematization of a comprehensive framework of analytical approaches for assessing the levels and multidimensional efficiency of innovative development in the agricultural sector under digital transformation, climate instability, and macroeconomic shock conditions. The study proves the necessity of conceptual differentiation and subsequent synthesis among “innovative potential”, “innovative activity”, and “innovative receptivity”. The study establishes a three-dimensional indicator matrix across these core functional blocks, along with a minimax normalization algorithm to derive an integrated index of innovative development level. The paper highlights the limitations of strictly financial metrics when evaluating agricultural innovations and proposes an integrated “economy — ecology — society” framework. The paper formalizes an optimization model to calculate the economic effect of local technological innovations (drones, precision farming), accounting for saved crop areas and reduced agrochemical use. The paper introduces a modified Net Present Value criterion (cap N cap P cap V sub cap A. g r i. ) that incorporates probabilistic parameters for catastrophic agroclimatic events, severe yield fluctuations, and military risks. The study also validates non-parametric Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) combined with the Malmquist Productivity Index (MPI) to decompose total factor productivity into managerial efficiency gains and technological frontier shifts. The study identifies strategic directions for adapting the European framework of Agricultural Knowledge and Innovation Systems (AKIS), the composite AKIS Index, and ADI EU metrics to Ukrainian practice. This alignment harmonizes national diagnostics with the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP 2023–2027) and the European Green Deal. The study recommends establishing a digital innovation monitoring hub to reduce technology-adoption lags and integrating ecological capital valuation into state support mechanisms. Keywords: agricultural sector, innovative development, innovative potential, innovative receptivity, multidimensional efficiency, precision agriculture, AKIS, DEA, Malmquist index.
journal: Actual problems of innovative economy and law

title: Farmers’ Digital Participation in Agriculture: A Global Bibliometric Study and Implications for Agri-Marketing
abstract: As a major driver of economic growth in recent years, e-commerce has spurred farmers’ interest in participating in digital market-oriented agricultural systems more than ever, resulting in a profound impact on societal and economic development. Under this context, the inclusion of farmers in contemporary e-commerce practice deserves investigation. For this reason, this study attempts to provide up-to-date insights into farmers’ digital participation in agricultural practices. For this purpose, a bibliometric analysis was conducted using CiteSpace. The data were extracted from Web of Science between 2005 and 2025, and 499 publications were ultimately included in the analysis of co-citation networks, keyword co-occurrence, and burst detection. The results identified influential authors and their corresponding works, six major clusters, and four stages of farmers’ digital participation. The findings further show a clear shift from a technology-oriented focus to a greater emphasis on market engagement, platform ecosystems, and institutional governance. In particular, recent research shows the growing importance of digital skills, social capital, and policy support in directing farmers’ participation in digital markets. Based on the results, this study has important implications for agri-marketing strategies and policy development, suggesting that improving farmers’ digital capabilities, enhancing platform accessibility, and strengthening institutional support are necessary to promote broader digital participation. This study benefits not only academicians but also business practitioners and policy-makers.
publisher: Nan Yang Academy of Sciences Pte Ltd

title: A Deep Learning-Driven Approach for Musical Instrument Sound Synthesis and Acoustic Optimization.
abstract: This structured narrative review examines deep‑learning‑driven musical instrument timbre synthesis, covering playing‑condition control, acoustic defect diagnosis, structural inverse design, and subjective‑objective quality evaluation. Adopting a structured narrative review method, this work follows the main themes of technical paradigms, application closed loops, supporting resources, evaluation evidence, and industrial constraints. Relevant methods are organized as direct fitting of waveforms or spectrograms to hybrid modeling embedded with physical priors, and further toward interpretable end‑to‑end systems built upon differentiable digital signal processing (DDSP) and differentiable physical modeling. A closed‑loop research framework of "multimodal evidence‑physical constraint‑perceptual evaluation‑human‑in‑the‑loop" is proposed in this paper. The major findings are as follows: pure data‑driven models possess strong representation capability yet suffer from data bias and uncontrolled extrapolation; physical priors can boost sample efficiency and parameter interpretability, whereas their benefits depend on the accuracy of priors and optimization stability; differentiable acoustics provides a unified interface for synthesis, inversion, and design, but still encounters challenges including high‑frequency gradient pathology, multi‑physics coupling, real‑time computation and incomplete perceptual objectives. Future research directions include cross‑cultural musical‑instrument datasets, digital twins with uncertainty estimation, auditable auditory preference models, low‑latency edge‑end deployment, and governance of copyright and performer rights. This study provides a unified conceptual framework and reusable evaluation pathways for music‑acoustics researchers, algorithm developers, and lutherie engineers.

title: Neurocognitive Processing of Visual Design in Digital Learning: Roles of Dynamic Color and Visual Texture in Learning Engagement.
abstract: Dynamic color and visual texture are pervasive features of digital learning materials, yet their neurocognitive effects during learning remain insufficiently characterized. The authors investigated 26 university students using a 3 × 2 within-subject design comprising three dynamic color trajectories and two visual texture conditions (Smooth and Rough), while 64-channel EEG and condition-specific learning engagement were recorded. ERP and time-frequency analyses yielded temporally differentiated findings. Visual texture was associated with early P50 and theta activity, whereas an exploratory delta-band sensitivity analysis did not identify a reliable texture difference. Lightness was associated with N100 and early theta-to-low-beta activity, and saturation was associated with P300, beta/low-gamma activity, and inter-trial coherence. Learning engagement differed significantly across dynamic color trajectories, F(2, 50) = 18.74, p < 0.001, partial η2 = 0.429, and texture conditions, F(1, 25) = 62.32, p < 0.001, partial η2 = 0.714, with higher engagement under Smooth than Rough. Mean P300 amplitude was positively associated with engagement in a linear mixed-effects model, β = 0.43, 95% CI [0.28, 0.58], p < 0.001. These findings suggest distinct relationships among perceptual processing, subsequent task-related neural responses, and subjective engagement.

title: The Development of the SONICC Learning Model Assisted by Augmented Reality Media in Elementary Science Education
abstract: This study developed, validated, tested the practicality, and examined the effectiveness of the SONICC learning model assisted by augmented reality media in elementary science education for students in an Elementary School Teacher Education Study Program. The study used a research and development design based on the Borg and Gall model. The development process produced a SONICC learning model with six syntax stages: Setting Goals, Organization, New Idea, Innovation, Critical and Creative Thinking, and Communication. It also produced five supporting products: a learning model book, teaching material book, lecturer guidebook, student guidebook, and augmented reality media guidebook. Data were collected using validation sheets, practicality questionnaires, documentation, and learning outcome tests. The validation results reached an average score of 92.30% with a validity value of 3.69, indicating a very valid category. The practicality results reached 94.27% with a practicality value of 3.66, indicating a very practical category. The effectiveness test showed an N-Gain score of 78.78%, which was categorized as effective. These findings show that the SONICC learning model assisted by augmented reality media is valid, practical, and effective for improving elementary science learning in higher education.
journal: International Journal of Technology in Education and Science

title: Webinar-Based Capacity Building for Integrated STEM: Pre-Service Teachers' Engineering Design Process (EDP) Oriented Lessons
abstract: The Philippine Department of Education emphasizes the engineering design process (EDP) as a pedagogical approach for developing problem solvers and innovators, yet Filipino learners remain among the lowest performers in science internationally. Engineering design is widely regarded as the central integrator of integrated STEM instruction, yet its integration is hardest in the life sciences, where abstract, submicroscopic phenomena and dependence on technologies unavailable in ordinary classrooms constrain what teachers can design. This study examined a webinar-based capacity building intervention preparing pre-service science teachers to develop EDP-oriented lesson plans and activities for Cell and Molecular Biology. Delivered as a one-month, three-session synchronous webinar series with digital scaffolds such as editable lesson templates, annotated exemplars, and shared resources, the intervention was evaluated using a mixed-method design with 24 third-year pre-service science teachers. Lesson plan evaluations improved from "Moderately Evident" (M = 4.01) to "Highly Evident" (M = 4.68), a statistically significant difference (p < 0.05). EDP-oriented activities were rated "Highly Evident" (M = 4.33) and demonstration teaching "Satisfactory" (M = 87.36). Four themes emerged: Value of EDP in STEM Education, Impact of the Webinar Series, Challenges in Implementing EDP, and Novel Experiences and Insights. Notably, participants' most persistent constraint was technological: access to affordable, accessible materials for rendering cellular processes designable. Findings indicate that technology-mediated capacity building can prepare pre-service teachers for integrated STEM in the life sciences, but that teacher education must also equip them with low-cost tools for visualizing and modelling submicroscopic phenomena.
journal: International Journal of Technology in Education and Science

title: A Survey of IoT-Driven Smart Agricultural Storage Systems for Fruits and Vegetables Preservation
abstract: Post-harvest preservation of fruits and vegetables is a major challenge because quality changes rapidly when temperature, relative humidity, ventilation and ripening gases are not managed appropriately. Conventional storage often relies on periodic manual inspection, which can miss short-term environmental changes and delay corrective action. This survey reviews IoT-enabled monitoring and intelligent storage approaches for fresh produce, with emphasis on low-cost embedded systems suitable for small farms, shops and local storage facilities. The reviewed literature covers wireless monitoring of ambient parameters, cloud-connected cold-storage notification, machine-learning-based freshness classification, and fruit-specific temperature and humidity monitoring. Their sensing strategies, communication methods, control capabilities and validation limitations are compared. The review identifies gaps in crop-specific thresholds, sensor calibration, automatic control, power reliability, connectivity resilience and long-duration field validation. Based on these findings, a proposed ENTC project architecture is outlined using an ESP32, temperature-humidity sensing, a gas sensor, a display, a cloud dashboard and relay-driven ventilation or cooling. The paper presents a practical evaluation plan; it does not claim experimental results for the proposed prototype.

title: Green AI for Sustainable Agriculture: An Explainable-AI (XAI) Perspective on Energy-Efficient Crop Intelligence
abstract: In modern agriculture precision forecast crop yields, diagnose plant disease and schedule irrigation systems rely on machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL). Cost of training and deploying these models is weighed their accuracy. Two research threads have far developed largely in parallel. Green AI, which treats computational and energy efficiency as a first-class evaluation criterion alongside accuracy and Explainable AI(XAI) uses technology like Shapley additive explanations(SHAP), LIME and Grad-CAM to open the “black box” models so that farmers , and policymakers can act on their predictions.This paper synthesises recent literature (2017–2026) at the intersection of these threads as they apply to agriculture, covering crop-yield prediction, plant-disease detection, and soil- and irrigation-modelling studies that report either energy-efficiency measures or explainability analyses, or both. The synthesis identifies a specific and consistent gap: while explainability is now common in high-performing agricultural ML studies, almost none of them report the energy or carbon cost of training the underlying models, and the one purpose-built Green-AI agriculture framework identified in the review explicitly leaves explainability as future work rather than integrating it. Building on this synthesis, the paper proposes a unified Green-XAI methodological framework for agricultural ML that couples resource-appropriate model families – tree-based ensembles such as Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM, alongside a compact CNN architecture for imagery – with SHAP-based interpretability and continuous energy/carbon instrumentation across the training and inference lifecycle. The paper details the proposed dataset scope, the governing model equations, the SHAP computation, and an accuracy-versus-energy evaluation protocol, and positions the framework against a comparative synthesis of the performance figures reported by prior studies

title: Self-interacting $p$-forms and the shear-free anisotropic cosmological model
abstract: The cosmological principle may require more than observations demand: what is needed is isotropic expansion without vorticity. Extended Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker (eFLRW) cosmologies realise this with a non-vanishing anisotropic spatial curvature that is balanced by an anisotropic stress while the shear vanishes. Thorsrud and others investigated such scenarios for free differential $p$-forms. Here we extend the analysis to non-Abelian $p$-forms ($p=0,\dots,4$) with self interactions. The balance requires the anisotropic stress to decay as $a^{-2}$, $a$ being the cosmological scale factor, which we combine with the gauge-field continuity equation. The general results indicate that, in the presence of a potential, fine-tuning of the same is needed in order to balance the curvature. Notably, this is not the case for a $3$-form field $\underline{H}^a$ with a potential term $V(\underline{H}^2)=A+B\,\underline{H}^2$, where $A$ and $B$ are constants: in Bianchi class A, an uncharged 3-form balances the curvature with this potential without any tuning, and a charged one does so for a suitably chosen connection. This is the only candidate we have found where the potential does not require tuning. It is also an interesting candidate as it can be interpreted as a cosmological constant in combination with a dark-matter sector mimicking curvature.
