Temporal trends and changing epidemiology of non-tuberculous mycobacteria over four decades: a retrospective laboratory-based study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES The incidence of non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) isolations has increased worldwide, although the relative contribution of demographic changes, increasing patient complexity, environmental factors, and advances in diagnostic techniques remains unclear. We aimed to describe long-term trends in NTM isolations and epidemiological changes. METHODS We performed a retrospective study of NTM-positive clinical samples processed at a tertiary referral hospital in Barcelona between 1986 and 2021. Individual demographic and microbiological data were available until 2021, whereas only aggregate data on total samples processed and NTM-positive cultures were available for 2022-2023 and were used exclusively for temporal trend analyses. Trends were analysed using logistic regression, generalized additive models, and a one-breakpoint segmented logistic regression; evidence for a change in slope was formally assessed using the Davies test. Demographic characteristics, specimen type, and species distribution were compared between two periods (1998-2005 and 2014-2021). RESULTS A total of 5,848 NTM-positive samples were identified. Among samples with available demographic data, 3,918 (66.9%) corresponded to male patients. Respiratory specimens accounted for 4,147 (70.9%) samples, whereas 426 (7.3%) were non-respiratory. Temporal trends showed a non-linear pattern. The segmented model estimated a change-point at 2017.5 (95% CI 2016.9-2018.2), with a marked increase thereafter (annual percent change 21.7%, 95% CI 18.6-24.8); the Davies test provided strong evidence of a change in slope (p<0.001). Species distribution changed significantly over time, partly reflecting improvements in microbiological identification. The Mycobacterium avium complex remained the most frequently isolated group, whereas M. kansasii and M. xenopi declined substantially. Compared with 1998-2005, patients in 2014-2021 were older (mean age 60 vs. 56 years, p<0.001) and more frequently female (41.9% vs. 28.3%, p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS Two distinct periods of increased NTM isolation were observed over the study period, with the most recent acceleration occurring around 2017-2018. This increase occurred alongside important changes in species distribution and patient demographics. These findings highlight the evolving epidemiology of NTM and support the need for enhanced surveillance systems and improved differentiation between colonization and active disease.

title: Detection of Melon Leaf Diseases Based on an Improved YOLOv8n Model
abstract: Under field conditions, melon leaf diseases suffer from irregular lesion morphology, missed detection of small lesions, insufficient localization accuracy, and considerable difficulty in edge device deployment. Using YOLOv8n as the baseline, this paper performs scenario-adaptive modifications of existing fundamental modules for melon disease detection and proposes the YOLOv8n-melon model. Specifically, an Inner-ShapeIoU loss function is constructed by combining the inner-bounding-box mechanism of Inner-IoU with the shape-aware constraint of Shape-IoU, with the hyperparameters determined via grid search, to improve the regression of irregular lesions. The EMA attention module is appended to the output of each C2f block in the neck, forming C2f-EMA units that suppress complex background interference and strengthen multi-scale lesion feature extraction. A LightHead lightweight decoupled detection head, built with SimAM and depthwise separable convolution (DWConv), is adopted to reduce computational cost. Ablation and comparative experiments are conducted on a melon leaf disease dataset integrated from multiple public sources. The proposed model contains only 2.38 M parameters and 5.9 GFLOPs, achieves an mAP@0.5 of 91.87% with a 2.17-percentage-point improvement over the baseline YOLOv8n (89.70%), and provides a favorable accuracy-complexity trade-off for edge-oriented disease detection compared with mainstream models such as YOLOv3-tiny, YOLOv5n, YOLOv8s, YOLO11n, and RT-DETR‑L. On the Raspberry Pi 4B platform, an inference speed of 10.52 FPS is achieved on static test-set images, verifying the feasibility of edge inference and providing a reference for lightweight crop disease detection.

title: Using Multispectral Imaging and Artificial Intelligence to Detect Crop Diseases and Pests Early
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
abstract: Crop disease and pest infestation is important for improving agricultural production and for the reduction of chemical use. Nevertheless, traditional RGB-based vision systems can still lack sensitivity for early detection of subtle physiological changes before symptomatic manifestations. This work presents a hybrid multisensor fusion framework that relies on CNN-Attention for multispectral and thermal automated crop-health evaluation. The anticipated model employs 10,800 multisensor observations divided into five categories of crop health: healthy, fungal disease, bacterial disease, viral disease, and pest infestation. Stratified sampling was utilized on the dataset which was split into 70% for training (7560), 15% for validation (1622) and 15% for testing (1618). The framework combines attention-based feature fusion, hybrid feature extraction, and multiclass prediction with multispectral and thermal branches based on two parallel CNNs. In an experimental evaluation against Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, RGB-CNN, multispectral CNN, thermal CNN, and CNN fusion models, the proposed scheme is showing top performance with 96.48% accuracy, 96.21% precision, 96.05% recall, 96.13% F1 score and 0.98 AUC. According to the results of the ablation analysis, we observe the contribution of each of the different models. The models of multispectral-only, multisensor fusion, attention-enhanced, and complete fusion resulted in a performance of 92.18%, 94.12%, 95.61%, and 96.48% respectively. The performance evaluation under different illumination conditions, early disease incidence, low disease severity, and at different growth stages is above 94.27%. The proposed system is expected to deliver an accurate, interpretable and scalable AI for precision agriculture. This would be achieved by fusing spectral, spatial, and physiological crop information for the early management of diseases and pests.

title: The landscape of computer vision datasets in smart agriculture: trends, taxonomies, challenges, and future directions
abstract: Modern agriculture is increasingly driven by data-centric and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled approaches to improve productivity, resource efficiency, and precision in decision-making. In this context, computer vision datasets have emerged as critical resources for enabling automated agricultural analysis. This study presents a large-scale, data-centric review of agricultural computer vision datasets using a PRISMA-guided systematic review methodology. A systematic search of the peer-reviewed data journals Scientific Data and Data in Brief, conducted through 31 January 2026, identified 2,308 records, from which 253 eligible dataset publications were retained after duplicate removal and eligibility screening based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. We systematically analyze the dataset landscape across multiple dimensions, including vision tasks, annotation strategies, acquisition environments, sensing modalities, and geographic distribution. Furthermore, we propose a unified multi-dimensional taxonomy that organizes datasets based on task orientation, semantic content, and design characteristics, enabling structured comparison and informed dataset selection. Our analysis identifies key limitations, including sampling bias, underrepresentation of crops and regions, inconsistent annotation practices, and limited interoperability, which collectively hinder reproducibility and model generalization. Additionally, challenges in dataset accessibility and the absence of standardized benchmarking frameworks restrict effective knowledge transfer. Finally, we outline critical directions for future research, emphasizing standardized dataset design, scalable annotation frameworks, and robust evaluation protocols to support the development of reliable and generalizable agricultural AI systems.

title: A semantic framework for resilience analytics and AI-assisted decision support in growing and changing socio-technical systems
abstract: Socio-technical systems are becoming increasingly interconnected, heterogeneous, and dynamic while continuously evolving through new technologies, infrastructures, policies, resources, and operational practices. At the same time, critical infrastructure operators, businesses, and public authorities face growing challenges arising from climate change, cyber threats, geopolitical instability, supply-chain disruptions, and evolving regulatory frameworks. Supporting resilience and sustainability under these conditions requires analytical capabilities that extend beyond static digital twins, application-specific simulation models, and fixed system representations. This paper presents FRAMESS (Framework for Systemic Risk Analysis and Exploring Sustainable Solutions), a semantic and extensible framework for resilience analytics, sustainability assessment, and AI-assisted decision support in growing and changing socio-technical systems. FRAMESS enables the continuous development, integration, simulation, and evaluation of evolving system models despite distributed modelling expertise, changing system architectures, emerging hazards, and large combinatorial design spaces. The framework combines semantic system modelling, flexible system models (FSMs), multi-agent simulation, scenario and disruption management, integrated assessment methods, and AI-assisted exploration within a unified analytical environment. A central contribution is the semantic representation of agents, resources, dependencies, subprocesses, hazards, and adaptation measures, enabling interdisciplinary model integration while preserving extensibility, interoperability, and analytical consistency. The framework further supports resilience quantification and benchmarking by enabling systematic comparison of alternative system configurations under multiple hazard conditions. The capabilities of FRAMESS are demonstrated through a resilience-oriented planning application for allocating strategic reserves in a food supply chain under climate change-induced drought scenarios. The demonstrator illustrates how the framework supports resilience assessment, evaluation of adaptation strategies, and AI-assisted exploration of alternative system configurations. The paper argues that future resilience management requires semantic and extensible analytical environments that integrate evolving digital twins, resilience analytics, and AI-assisted exploration to support resilient and sustainable transformation pathways under uncertainty.

Modelling-Based Assessment of Managed Aquifer Recharge: Impacts on Groundwater Quantity and Quality in the Upper Friuli Plain (Italy)
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
abstract: In the Friuli Venezia Giulia (FVG) region of northeastern Italy, declining groundwater levels and changing precipitation patterns have raised concerns about the long-term sustainability of groundwater resources. This study evaluates the potential of Managed Aquifer Recharge (MAR) in the upper Friuli Plain, with a focus on the Sammardenchia site. Surface water and groundwater quality in the study area were characterized through the analysis of inorganic and organic compounds, as well as microbiological indicators. A three-dimensional groundwater flow model was developed to simulate the regional and local site-specific hydrogeological conditions. MAR performance was assessed under different recharge scenarios, including an infiltration pond, a recharge well, and a combined pond-well recharge, based on the existing recharge structures at the site. In addition, solute transport simulations were conducted to analyze the behaviour of faecal indicator bacteria (E. coli), detected in the surface water to be used for MAR. The simulation results show that recharge through both the infiltration pond and the well increased the groundwater levels near the MAR site, with the combined recharge scenario producing the highest simulated rise in groundwater levels (~ 2.68 m) and storage. Microbial transport simulations showed substantial attenuation of E. coli during subsurface transport, particularly under the pond-recharge scenario (> 4 log) due to longer residence times. Overall, the modelling results indicate that MAR can effectively contribute to groundwater storage enhancement and attenuation of microbial contamination in the study area. Combined pond−well recharge shows the greatest potential to increase groundwater storage. Longer travel times help reduce simulated E. coli concentrations in groundwater. Different recharge configurations offer distinct benefits, depending on groundwater management objectives.

title: A scientometric and bibliometric analysis of three decades of global robotics and Internet of Things research trends and intellectual structure
abstract: The convergence of robotics and the Internet of Things (IoT) has transformed multiple sectors through autonomous, interconnected systems. Despite significant scholarly output, the knowledge structure of Robotics-IoT research remains fragmented. This study provides an integrated scientometric and bibliometric mapping of global Robotics–IoT/IoRT research, combining performance analysis, collaboration-network mapping, thematic mapping, and LDA-based topic modelling to reveal the field’s intellectual structure, collaboration architecture, dominant clusters, emerging themes, and future research frontiers. A scientometric analysis was conducted on 21,733 unique documents retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science after screening and deduplication of 23,377 initial records, covering 1993–2025 across 2,284 sources and over 44,000 indexed author-name records/clusters, cleaned via the PRISMA protocol. Biblioshiny and VOSviewer were employed for publication trends, citation structures, and collaborative networks, while LDA was applied for topic modelling. Robotics-IoT research shows rapid growth post-2016. Using all-author affiliation-country document-level full counting, India, China, and the USA lead publication output. Among the ten most productive countries, Australia shows the highest average citations per document, followed by Canada, the USA, and the United Kingdom. Collaboration networks reflect extensive global partnerships, with emerging economies demonstrating substantial international participation. Thematic analysis identifies major research streams related to industrial digitalization, IoT–robotic systems, energy-efficient networking, machine-learning-based analytics, robotics and sensing, cybersecurity, and edge/cloud computing, alongside specialized applications in agriculture and healthcare. Observed distributions show varying degrees of descriptive alignment with classical scientometric laws (Lotka’s, Bradford’s, Price’s, Zipf’s, Matthew Effect, and Pareto Principle). The originality of this study lies in the domain-specific application and empirical synthesis of these approaches to the global Robotics–IoT/IoRT research landscape. Specifically, the study provides a longitudinal analysis covering 1993–2025, examines the intellectual, social, publication and thematic structures of the Robotics–IoT/IoRT domain, evaluates a comparatively broad set of classical scientometric regularities, and complements keyword-based analysis with abstract-based LDA topic modelling. The study consequently contributes new empirical evidence concerning the evolution, concentration, collaboration, intellectual structure and thematic development of Robotics–IoT/IoRT research.

title: Context Attentive Dual Stream Emotion Aware Swin Transformer for Academic Emotion Recognition
abstract: Enhancing academic engagement and adaptive learning systems requires an understanding of students’ emotions in the classroom. Conventional facial expression recognition techniques frequently fall short in educational environments because of issues such inadequate lighting, occlusion, changing head positions, and the requirement to record contextual data outside of the face. With three significant innovations, this study suggests a unique framework for robust academic emotion recognition called Context Attentive Cascaded Preprocessing with Dual Stream Emotion Aware Swin Transformer (CADE-Swin) to overcome these constraints. To preserve both fine-grained facial expressions and broader behavioral context, a Context Attentive Multi-Task Cascaded Convolutional Neural Network (CA-MTCNN) preprocessing is first constructed to jointly extract aligned face crops and face-context regions. Second, by combining emotion-aware attention heads, the Dual Stream Emotion Aware Swin Transformer (DE-Swin) architecture prioritizes salient facial and action unit regions while processing face-only and context crops simultaneously. Third, sequence-level reasoning for continuous engagement analysis is made possible by the extension of the DE-Swin model with cross-frame temporal attention. The DAiSEE KAGGLE dataset’s 6000 video segments were used to extract the original images that capture contextual and face signals. Six augmentation techniques are applied to 12,000 original classroom images of DAiSEE dataset to create an augmented dataset of 84,000 images, which guarantees data diversity and generalization. After that, the data is manually annotated into six academic emotion classes: frustrated, bored, engaged, confused, sleepy, and yawning. The proposed CADE-Swin system outperforms current state-of-the-art algorithms in academic emotion recognition with an impressive 96.13% classification accuracy when applied to annotated images. These findings show that combining dual-stream fusion, context-aware preprocessing, and temporal emotion attention yields a very successful technique to simulate complicated student actions in authentic classroom settings, opening the door for intelligent learning analytics.
journal: International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems

title: Coupling relationships among natural resources, socioeconomic activity, and spatial morphology at the grid scale: a case study of Shanghai
abstract: This study investigates how natural-resource value, socioeconomic activity, and spatial morphology interact at the grid scale in Shanghai, with particular attention to functional differentiation, non-linear transitions, and spatial heterogeneity. Multi-source data were harmonised to a 400 m grid, and composite indicators were constructed through factor analysis and aggregation of normalised indicators. Natural-break classification, unsupervised machine-learning clustering, and Lee’s L analysis identified spatial patterns, whilst bidirectional XGBoost models interpreted with SHAP examined relationships between natural-resource value and socioeconomic activity. Aggregate activity and ground coverage show the strongest negative associations with natural-resource value, but technology and public services remain positively associated with natural-resource value, with parallel tendencies for culture, tourism, and finance. The associations of young-worker concentration and building height with natural-resource value are U-shaped. Gas and hydrological regulation shift from positive to negative associations with socioeconomic activity as provision intensifies, distinguishing ecological landscapes embedded in the built-up area from regional ecological service systems. The three-way coupling is asymmetric, non-linear, and spatially differentiated. Its planning significance lies in distinguishing land-intensive growth from knowledge- and service-oriented renewal, and urban ecological landscapes from regional ecological service systems. Super-large and mega cities should therefore coordinate load and land-occupation control, functional and vertical renewal, and the distinct urban and regional roles of ecological resources.
journal: Frontiers of Urban and Rural Planning

title: DRSQ-Net: underwater object detection algorithm using differentiable physical restoration and dynamic sparse query
abstract: To address detection challenges caused by color distortion, multi-scale objects, and occlusion in underwater images, this paper proposes DRSQ-Net, an improved You Only Look Once v11 (YOLOv11)-based network to enhance detection accuracy and generalization. DRSQ-Net integrates three distinctive innovations: 1) a Retinex-based differentiable physical restoration module that decomposes and optimizes underwater images to boost input feature quality; 2) a local–global collaborative Transformer enhancement network using dynamic convolution and an improved visual state-space model to capture fine details and long-range dependencies; and 3) a dynamic sparse query detection head that decouples classification and regression via task-aware routing for more robust object detection. Experiments on RUOD, URPC2020, and UTDAC2020 show that DRSQ-Net achieves 92.1% mAP@0.5 with only 4.2 M parameters, 5.5% higher than YOLOv11. This lightweight model is well-suited for resource-constrained underwater embedded platforms, offering good practical value.

title: Boosting Functional Dental Pulp Regeneration by a Biomimetic Self-assembling Hydrogel through Remodeling the Stem Cell Niche.
abstract: Cell-free strategies for dental pulp regeneration rely on the recruitment of endogenous stem cells, but cell entry alone is not sufficient. The stem cells require staged niche cues that support early mechanical adaptation and later coordinate odontogenic, angiogenic, and neural supportive responses. Here, we report RQK (RADA16/QP5/KLT), an injectable self-assembling peptide hydrogel designed to integrate extracellular matrix-like architecture with instructive bioactive cues for functional pulp regeneration. RQK combines the RADA16 (RAD) nanofibrous backbone with the amelogenin-derived odontogenic motif QP5 and the vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-mimetic angiogenic motif KLT. The hydrogel formed at 37°C, showed injectability and recovery, and could adapt to the irregular root canal space. In three-dimensional culture, RQK guided human dental pulp stem cells through a staged regenerative response. RQK first maintained stemness and mechanosensitive signaling, then promoted adhesion remodeling, odontogenic differentiation, enhanced angiogenic activity, and neural supportive effects. Transcriptomic analysis further linked this staged response to extracellular matrix interaction, cell adhesion, mechanosensitive signaling, and developmental programs. Molecular dynamics simulations and ultrastructural analyses suggested that interactions between RQK and collagen created a matrix environment favorable for odontogenic differentiation. Furthermore, evaluations across different stages in an infected immature beagle tooth model revealed that RQK promoted periapical healing and continued root development. Newly formed pulp-like tissue was more functional and showed odontoblast-like cell arrangement, vascular ingrowth, and neural tissue formation. These findings demonstrate that biomimetic niche reconstruction can guide endogenous stem cell behavior and improve cell-free dental pulp regeneration in vivo, providing a biomimetic framework for enhancing in situ tissue regeneration. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: This research developed RQK, an injectable self-assembling peptide hydrogel for cell-free dental pulp regeneration. Unlike conventional scaffold designs, RQK combines a nanofibrous matrix that mimics the extracellular matrix with odontogenic and angiogenic bioactive motifs. The hydrogel forms at 37°C, adapts to the irregular root canal space, and guides endogenous stem cell behavior through staged niche cues. It supports early mechanical adaptation, later odontogenic differentiation, angiogenic activity, and neural supportive effects. In an infected immature beagle tooth model, RQK promoted periapical healing, continued root development, and organized pulp-like tissue formation, providing a biomimetic strategy for enhancing in situ tissue regeneration.

Intermittent fasting enhances muscle regeneration via an EDA2R-NIK-myomixer axis.
abstract: Skeletal muscle exhibits a remarkable regenerative capacity that relies on adult stem cells known as satellite cells (SCs), which differentiate into myogenic progenitors to drive muscle repair. How varying energy availability alters myogenesis, however, remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that intermittent fasting (IF) in mice upregulates a myogenic gene program, including Myomixer, a muscle-specific fusogen that facilitates the merging of progenitor cells into myofibers. IF enhances the regeneration of injured muscles by expanding the SC population and promoting the proliferation and fusion of myogenic progenitors. These effects are absent in an SC-depletion model. We show that fasting-induced EDA2R-NIK signaling increases Myomixer expression and fusion in myoblasts. Notably, mice lacking EDA2R or NIK fail to respond to the myogenic effects of IF. Furthermore, our data suggest that mice with Duchenne muscular dystrophy also benefit from an IF regimen. Therefore, IF-induced regeneration holds potential for aiding recovery from muscle damage.

title: A hierarchical regulatory cascade programs chlamydospore formation in the nematode-trapping fungus Arthrobotrys flagrans.
abstract: Chlamydospores provide durable stress tolerance for fungal survival and enable shelf-stable biocontrol agents, yet their genetic regulation in fungi remains poorly understood. Here, using the nematode-trapping fungus Arthrobotrys flagrans as a model, we define a hierarchical regulatory cascade for chlamydospore formation. LaeA mediates H3K9 monomethylation to license this developmental program. Furthermore, we identify VeA and Ste12 as LaeA partners, and the importin KapA as a nuclear gatekeeper. This upstream module activates VosA/VelB, which induces AbaA/StuA to control the effectors ChsG, McdD, and McdD-modified glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored proteins for chlamydospore cell wall biogenesis. The expression levels of regulators within this regulatory cascade (LaeA/VeA/Ste12-VosA/VelB-StuA/AbaA-ChsG and McdD) determine chlamydospore yield and convert environmental cues into differentiation. This framework guides strain engineering for high-yield chlamydospore production and suggests a regulatory paradigm potentially conserved across fungi.

title: The YAP/TAZ-Tgfbr2-stiffness feedback loop governs divergent cell fates of muscle-resident mesenchymal progenitors.
abstract: Mesenchymal progenitors are essential for muscle regeneration, but also contribute to fat accumulation and fibrosis. Several extrinsic and intrinsic factors regulating adipogenic or fibrogenic differentiation of mesenchymal progenitors have been identified. However, it remains unclear how different cues are integrated to determine cell fate. Here, we demonstrate that interstitial stiffness and the mechanosensitive hippo pathway regulate mesenchymal progenitor cell fate. Fat accumulation model reduced interstitial stiffness and nuclear YAP/TAZ-positive mesenchymal progenitors compared with a regeneration model, whereas YAP/TAZ deficiency in mesenchymal progenitors enhanced fat deposition. Mechanistically, YAP/TAZ induced expression of the anti-adipogenic genes Aldh1a2 and Wnt5a, and the pro-fibrogenic gene Tgfbr2, which mediates TGF-β binding. Loss of Tgfbr2 in mesenchymal progenitors reduced transient collagen deposition, decreased stiffness, and increased fat accumulation during regeneration. We propose a stiffness-YAP/TAZ-Tgfbr2-collagen regulatory loop governing mesenchymal progenitor cell fate and highlight its importance for optimal muscle regeneration.

title: Pedestrian detection in occluded maize harvesting environments based on thermal infrared imaging

Risks of counter-stereotypical AI when it replaces human contact.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are often designed with stereotype-consistent social cues-such as feminized voice assistants in service roles or masculine security robots-to increase acceptance and interaction fluency. Yet these same design choices may reinforce the stereotypes they draw on. Recent work, however, proposes a more optimistic possibility: counter-stereotypical AI-for example, a female-coded technical chatbot or male-coded care robot-may reduce prejudice by functioning as synthetic intergroup contact, repeatedly exposing users to agents that serve as proxy members of social groups and challenge familiar stereotypes. We build on this account but argue that its implications depend critically on whether AI supplements or replaces human interaction. When counter-stereotypical AI adds exposure to underrepresented groups, it may challenge stereotypes by broadening the range of people users associate with particular traits or domains. When it substitutes for humans, however, its effects become more ambivalent. We identify three risks of counter-stereotypical AI as replacement: non-integration, when users treat the agent as a designed persona rather than revising beliefs about people; substitution, when synthetic contact displaces the reciprocal and agentic qualities of human contact; and illusion of inclusion, when visible AI representation is mistaken for institutional inclusion. We position replacement by counter-stereotypical AI as a critical boundary condition for theories of synthetic contact and representational AI, and as a key context for future research on prejudice, technology, and social change.

Learning safety through the observation of others: A proof-of-principle study on vicarious extinction of fear responses to respiratory threat.
abstract: Interoceptive fear-conditioning paradigms model the development and treatment of disorders involving fear of somatic sensations. While direct extinction can attenuate acquired fear, associations involving interoceptive sensations may be particularly resistant. Vicarious extinction, where individuals observe a model's safety experience, mirrors techniques used in exposure therapy. This proof-of-principle study aimed to characterize conditioned fear responses to interoceptive threat during and following a vicarious extinction procedure. Twenty participants completed a three-day differential extero-interoceptive within-subjects paradigm. On day one, participants were presented with geometrical shapes serving as conditioned stimuli (CSs), with a CS+ paired with an inspiratory resistive load (unconditioned stimulus), and a CS- left unpaired. On day two, participants observed a model responding calmly to the CSs, without exhibiting signs of dyspnea. On day three, extinction retention was assessed. Startle eyeblink response, skin conductance response (SCR), heart period, and US-expectancy were assessed. Differential learning was evident in US-expectancy ratings, as indicated by higher ratings for the CS+ than the CS- by the end of the acquisition phase. In SCR however, evidence for acquisition was not fully conclusive, as CS-differentiation emerged only at the beginning of the vicarious extinction phase. CS-differentiation was absent in startle response, and bradycardia emerged to both stimuli. During vicarious extinction, SCR decreased, while US-expectancy ratings decreased but remained elevated for the CS+. Spontaneous recovery and reinstatement of differential fear responses were observed in US-expectancy, but not SCR. Our results indicate that vicarious extinction may attenuate the subjective expectancy of threat. Thereby, this study suggests the feasiblity of vicarious extinction of fear of interoceptive threat and offers a starting point for future research on observational safety learning in the domain of fear of bodily sensations.

title: AI Identifies Clinically Relevant Asystole Among False Loop Recorder Alerts: From Data Overload to Diagnosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND Implantable loop recorders (ILRs) are often implanted to investigate unexplained syncopal episodes. However, ILRs may produce false alerts due to undersensing or artifacts, thus requiring careful review of numerous device recordings, which makes it challenging to identify clinically significant events. CASE SUMMARY We report a case of a 77-year-old woman with recurrent syncopal episodes, in whom a 7-second pause was detected by an ILR. Device interrogations showed multiple pause alerts that were identified as false events because of poor R sensing. However, the artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced remote monitoring identified a true pause with blocked P waves, leading the patient to receive a pacemaker implantation. DISCUSSION This case highlights the clinical value of AI-assisted remote monitoring in identifying clinically relevant arrhythmias among numerous device alerts. Improved automated filtering of ILR data may reduce diagnostic delays and help clinicians prioritize clinically significant events. TAKE-HOME MESSAGES ILRs may generate numerous false alerts because of sensing abnormalities, complicating the identification of clinically relevant events in routine practice. AI-enhanced remote monitoring may improve diagnostic efficiency by identifying true arrhythmic events within large volumes of device-generated data and guiding timely management.

title: The metabolic reprogramming of T cells controls airway remodeling in severe asthma.
abstract: BACKGROUND Mixed granulocytic asthma (MGA) is a severe Th2-low endotype, characterized by high Th17/neutrophilic burden and exacerbated airway remodeling. Both features confer resistance to inhaled corticosteroids and typical asthma treatments. OBJECTIVE We aimed to address gaps in knowledge, including how Th17 cells induce pathological tissue remodeling and how Th17 differentiation occurs in response to allergens. METHODS We generated a Th2-low murine model of asthma on the Il4rα-/- background that mimics the decrease in type 2 response seen in corticosteroid-resistant patients. We monitored major features of human disease including heightened airway reactivity to methacholine, Th17/neutrophilic inflammation, airway remodeling, and resistance to corticosteroid treatment. Comparative transfer of Th2 versus Th17 cells were analyzed. We further investigated how the mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) pathway modulates pathogenic Th17 cell reprogramming by in vitro T cell cultures and in vivo therapeutic blockades. RESULTS LIGHT (aka TNFSF14) and the OXPHOS pathway are enriched in human MGA and likewise upregulated in this mouse model. We show OXPHOS promotes the metabolic reprograming of Th17 cells, to sustain their survival despite steroid treatment and produce LIGHT that controls airway remodeling. Mechanistically, OXPHOS regulates RORγt expression and the subsequent transcriptional network to program differentiation of Th17 cells, whereas LIGHT drives airway remodeling by activating the MMP9-dependent TGFβ pathway. Additionally, OXPHOS+Th17 cells promote the expression of osteopontin necessary for fibroblast activation. LIGHT antagonistic blockade reduces airway remodeling, whereas OXPHOS inhibition kills Th17 cells and subsequent neutrophilia. Importantly, the dual blockade of LIGHT and OXPHOS reverses all features of MGA back to baseline and reciprocally increases the numbers of Treg cells. CONCLUSIONS The dual blockade of LIGHT and OXPHOS constitutes a promising target for clinical interventions in human MGA, possibly extending to other Th17-driven fibrotic diseases.
journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology

title: The fading palette: physiological, pathological, and clinical landscapes of hair greying.
abstract: Hair greying encompasses diverse clinical phenotypes whose persistence and reversibility reflect changes in both pigment production and regenerative capacity. Differentiated melanocytes within the anagen hair follicle pigmentary unit (HFPU) generate hair pigmentation, while melanocyte stem cells (McSCs) and their niche support pigmentary regeneration. Here, we integrate human follicular evidence with mechanistic findings from mouse models to examine how McSC-niche disturbances relate to aging-related, premature, autoimmune-associated, stress-associated, and radiation-induced greying. We organize regenerative dysfunction into three overlapping patterns: impaired self-renewal and pool maintenance, aberrant differentiation, and cell death. Niche disturbances influence each pattern and may also suppress pigment production within the active HFPU. McSC mobility and reversible state transitions further explain why regenerative failure can occur despite cell persistence. This framework links clinical phenotypes to candidate cellular disturbances and their implications for repigmentation: functional recovery when melanocytes survive, regenerative recruitment when competent progenitors remain, and restricted endogenous recovery after extensive cellular loss. By distinguishing established mechanisms from proposed human correlates, we identify phenotype-specific priorities for restoring pigmentation, preserving the melanocyte reservoir, and repairing its supporting environment. This perspective connects McSC fate biology with clinical reversibility and guides the development of strategies for sustained pigmentary recovery.

Diet-independent pregravid obesity drives premature but functionally dysregulated fetal immune maturation across multiple immune compartments in rhesus macaques.
abstract: Pregravid obesity is associated with long-term immune alterations in offspring, but the mechanisms linking maternal metabolic state to fetal immune development remain poorly defined. To address this gap, we used a rhesus macaque model of spontaneous, diet-independent pregravid obesity to examine impact of pregravid obesity on fetal immune maturation and function. We profiled immune cell frequency, function, transcriptional programs, and inferred intercellular communication in umbilical cord blood, fetal spleen, and fetal lung using spectral flow cytometry, multiplex cytokine profiling, functional stimulation assays, and single-cell RNA sequencing. Pregravid obesity was associated with altered fetal organ growth, elevated inflammatory mediators, altered immune cell frequencies, and hyperresponsive splenic leukocyte responses to in vitro stimulation. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses revealed a conserved program of innate immune reprogramming across all three compartments, characterized by heightened inflammatory, migratory, and metabolic signatures together with reduced antigen-presentation potential. We also observed impaired T cell maturation with premature effector differentiation and evidence of B cell dysfunction. Computationally inferred cell-cell communication predicted loss of tolerogenic signaling and enhanced proinflammatory pathways across splenic and lung myeloid cells. Together, these findings indicate that diet-independent pregravid obesity drives premature but functionally dysregulated maturation of fetal circulating and tissue-resident immune cells, providing a candidate mechanism for the increased susceptibility to infection, respiratory disease, and immune dysregulation reported in offspring of mothers with obesity. This connection should be tested directly in postnatal studies.

Perivascular macrophages restrict CXCR4-dependent accumulation of stem-like CD8+ T cells in tumors and limit chemotherapy efficacy.
abstract: The perivascular (Pv) niche coordinates immune-stromal interactions that facilitate cancer progression. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic inactivation of the enzyme heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) in LYVE-1+ Pv tumor-associated macrophages (PvTAMs) synergizes with cytotoxic chemotherapy (CCT) to achieve immunological tumor control in murine breast cancer models. We investigated the tumor microenvironment (TME) during the transition to immunological control and identified an increase in stem-like TCF1+PD-1+CD8+ T cells and enrichment of tumor-selective effector T cells. Stem-like CD8+ T cells were clonally diverse and rapidly acquired a TCF1- differentiated phenotype in the TME. Their tumor accumulation depended on CXCR4 and was associated with a treatment-induced expansion of proliferating CXCL12+CD34+ Pv cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). In human breast cancer, greater abundance of the stem-like CD8+ T cell program was associated with improved outcomes following CCT. These findings identify PvTAM HO-1 activity as a regulator of a stromal-stem-like T cell axis that limits chemotherapy efficacy and anti-tumor immunity.

title: Neither elevating nor degrading? Technology, job characteristics, and workers' role in manufacturing production
Embodied intelligence for crop production.
abstract: Global agriculture faces growing food demand, labor shortages, and climate uncertainty. Although automation has improved agricultural operations, adapting to variable crop states and unstructured environments remains challenging. Embodied intelligence integrates multimodal perception, contextual reasoning, and adaptive action through continuous interaction with crops and their environment. This review examines advances in embodied perception, decision-making, and execution for crop production. We discuss how multimodal sensing, crop growth models, and adaptive control connect individual operations with management objectives across the crop growth cycle. We further identify priorities for system integration, long-term validation, and practical deployment to support precise, sustainable, and resilient food production.

title: Protocol for generating nociceptor-enriched peripheral sensory neurons from human induced pluripotent stem cells.
abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) are a valuable system for studying human development, modeling disease-associated cellular phenotypes, and generating difficult-to-access cell types, such as sensory neurons (SNs). Here, we present a stepwise differentiation protocol for generating peripheral SNs from hiPSCs under defined culture conditions. We describe steps for expansion of hiPSCs, induction of neural crest cells (NCCs), dissociation and replating of NCCs, and maturation into SNs. This protocol yields nociceptor-enriched SN cultures.

title: Immunomodulatory and Antioxidant Biomimetic Hydrogel Coloaded with Glycyrrhizic Acid and Copper Gallate for Synergistic Cartilage Regeneration.
abstract: Articular cartilage lesions are persistently restrained by three interwoven pathological drivers: chronic inflammatory response, sustained oxidative stress, and progressive extracellular matrix (ECM) catabolism. Coupled with the inherently weak self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions for such injuries remain an unmet clinical demand owing to the inherently poor self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions remain an unmet clinical demand. Herein, we engineered a biomimetic composite hydrogel designated ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA, which integrates decellularized cartilage extracellular matrix, methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAMA), glycyrrhizic acid (GA), and copper gallate (Cu-GA). This integrated hydrogel platform simultaneously endows biomimetic mechanical support, potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidative bioactivities, as well as robust chondrogenic induction capacity. In vitro cellular evaluations verified the outstanding biocompatibility of the composite hydrogel. The biomaterial efficiently polarizes macrophages toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, suppresses the secretion of pro-inflammatory mediators and matrix-degrading proteases, and facilitates the migration and chondrogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Transcriptomic profiling suggested that its underlying molecular mechanisms may involve activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling cascade and blockade of the NF-κB-mediated inflammatory pathway. In vivo assessments using rat articular cartilage defect models demonstrated that the ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA hydrogel achieves satisfactory synchronous regeneration of hyaline cartilage and subchondral bone at 4 and 8 weeks post-implantation, with superior regenerative performance relative to all control groups. Collectively, this multifunctional hydrogel enables comprehensive remodeling of the pathological joint microenvironment with favorable biosafety profiles, representing a translatable candidate strategy for clinical management of cartilage degenerative disorders.

title: T-cell immunity in anti-tumor battle.
abstract: The clinical success of T-cell-based immunotherapies has transformed oncology, yet tumor immune evasion remains a formidable barrier. In this review, we delineate the developmental and molecular landscapes that shape antitumor T-cell immunity. Following a brief overview of CD4+ helper T-cell contributions, we focus primarily on CD8+ cytotoxic lineages. Rather than a passive loss of effector function, CD8+ T-cell exhaustion is increasingly recognized as functional attrition and profound oligoclonality. In the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), unremitting antigenic pressure drives an iterative selection process that` narrows a highly diverse T-cell pool into a constricted, oligoclonal population, a phenomenon termed "clonal contraction". We expand the conceptual scale of T-cell clonal selection during the immune response, tracing this clonal evolution from early thymic selection and primary antigen priming to exhaustive terminal differentiation. We further propose a structural model demonstrating how the biophysical constraints of a fixed T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire create a profound imbalance against rapidly diversifying tumor antigens. Within this framework, we highlight tissue-resident memory (Trm) as a crucial spatial reservoir that safeguards the host against the depletion of functional clones. Finally, we contextualize the therapeutic paradigm of immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) and note that, under some circumstances, durable clinical efficacy can be driven by systemic "clonal replacement". Ultimately, we argue that next-generation T-cell-based immunotherapies may shift `from attempting only to reverse functional exhaustion to actively engineering continuous clonal selection and preserving TCR repertoire diversity.

title: Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity.
abstract: Glioblastoma is incurable and resistant to therapy despite genomic stability under treatment1-8, suggesting that non-genetic cellular plasticity is a central driver of progression. Whether such plasticity reflects stochastic state switching or is governed by predictable gene regulation has remained unclear9-13. Here we introduce scDORI (single-cell deep multi-omic regulatory inference)-a deep-learning framework that infers enhancer-driven gene-regulatory networks at single-cell resolution-and apply it to single-nucleus multiome profiles of more than one million cells from primary glioblastomas. Integrating computational inference with systematic perturbation screens across patient-derived models, we show that a structured regulatory program with an asymmetric interplay of activators and repressors governs cellular plasticity in glioblastoma. The resulting transition landscape is hierarchical and predictable, but permits cross-lineage trajectories that are absent from normal neurodevelopment. Within this landscape, low-plasticity states such as the neuronal-like state are not stable differentiation end points but actively maintained configurations, stabilized by a network of safeguard repressors that silence alternative fates. We identify MYT1L as the dominant member of this network, and show that it binds to and represses master regulators of every alternative state to consolidate neuronal-like identity. MYT1L restricted plasticity even under standard-of-care therapy and suppressed tumour growth and invasion in vivo. Conversely, loss of MYT1L reactivated plasticity and accelerated malignant features, indicating that low-plasticity identity requires continuous repression. These findings reframe malignant cell state stability as a balance between activation and continuous repression, and nominate safeguard repressors as candidate therapeutic targets that are distinct from differentiation-inducing activators, with potential relevance across cancers in which phenotypic switching drives therapy resistance.

title: Computational models of complex systems meet AI agents
abstract: Complex systems have structural properties that make them a promising domain for scientific workflows driven by AI agents— systems that combine large language models with tool use and iterative execution. However, most complex systems simulators and libraries do not expose their control points and outputs in a form that text-based AI agents can readily use. Realizing the potential of agent-driven workflows requires equipping complex systems models with agent-friendly interfaces.

title: Electronic origin of the preferential NH3 response of N-substituted SnS2 monolayers: a first-principles study with machine learning force field-assisted assessment of structural stability.
abstract: Spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) was employed to investigate the adsorption and electronic responses of pristine and N-substituted SnS2 monolayers toward CO, CO2, and NH3. In parallel, a machine learning force field (MLFF) was developed and evaluated against DFT reference data to assess the structural and dynamical stability of the pristine and N-substituted substrates. The MLFF was not employed to predict gas adsorption or sensing properties, which were investigated exclusively using first-principles calculations. Among the three investigated gases, NH3 exhibits the strongest interaction with N-substituted SnS2, with an adsorption energy of -0.55 eV, an adsorption height of 1.712 Å, a Bader charge transfer of -0.22e, and a work-function change of -0.80 eV. Projected density of states and charge-density analyses reveal pronounced interfacial electronic redistribution for NH3, consistent with a stronger perturbation of the N-centered electronic states. This molecular differentiation is further reflected in the calculated relative conductivity-change metric at the Fermi level, which reaches 97.5% for NH3, compared with 44.8% for CO and 13.8% for CO2. MLFF calculations, phonon analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations further support the structural and dynamical stability of the modeled lattices. Collectively, these results establish a consistent relationship between substitutional nitrogen, spin-polarized electronic states, and the preferential electronic response toward NH3, providing a mechanistic basis for engineering N-substituted SnS2 for gas-sensing applications.

title: The upper main sequence in h and ̧hi Persei
abstract: Binary interactions play a crucial role in the evolution and eventual outcomes of massive stars. Rich young open clusters provide large co-eval populations that can be used to constrain the effects of binary evolution. The Double Cluster, h and ̧hi Persei, with a turn-off mass well above the threshold for core-collapse supernovae, is an excellent test bed for these processes. We used the observed stellar populations of h and ̧hi Persei, together with the results of a similar study of NGC 663, to constrain the evolutionary pathways of massive stars and, in particular, the role of binary interaction. We present optical spectroscopy of around 80 stars, covering the entire upper main sequence of NGC 869 and most of the brightest B-type stars in NGC 884, and used it to obtain spectral types and derive stellar parameters. We combined this dataset with Gaia astrometry to evaluate their evolutionary status and possible evolutionary paths. We find that 40% of the stars along the photometric sequence of NGC 869 have parallaxes consistent with the cluster mean but proper motions inconsistent at the 2σ level, suggesting some sort of dynamical perturbation in this field. We derived atmospheric parameters for almost 60 stars in the upper main sequence (B2,V and earlier) and found broad agreement between two independent fully automated procedures. We identified the cluster turn-offs between B1,V and B1.5,--,2,IV and differentiated this feature from the vicinity of the terminal main sequence (TAMS), where we found a population of giants between B1 and B1.5 with a high fraction of Be stars. Three luminous supergiants (HD 14134, HD 14143, HD 13854) are clearly detached from the rest of the population in all our diagrams. The bulk of the population in all of the massive clusters studied in the Perseus arm is consistent with single-star evolutionary models at a given age, but some B-type supergiants are much more luminous than any other cluster star. Their typical cluster kinematics and stellar parameters suggest a merger origin. Other lower-luminosity B-type supergiants seem consistent with the rest of the population. Kinematic analysis has indicated that most Be stars have not been dynamically perturbed by a supernova explosion. Those below the turn-off are likely to have been formed via case A mass transfer. The more massive Be stars above the turn-off do not display any other characteristic indicating a distinct evolutionary population.

title: Declining Cost-Effectiveness of Gastric Cancer Screening Over a Decade: A Cohort Modelling Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND & AIM The cost-utility of a mature cancer screening programme can shift as disease incidence, costs, and population risk change. We examined how these changes affected Korea's National Cancer Screening Program (NCSP) for gastric cancer by comparing two hypothetical cohorts parameterized with 2012 and 2022 conditions. METHODS Two structurally identical state-transition models simulated biennial endoscopic screening versus no organised screening in adults aged 40-79 years over a lifetime horizon, incorporating period-specific screen-detected health-state distributions, effective screening sensitivity, NCSP participation, and treatment costs. Incremental cost-utility ratios (ICURs) per quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) were calculated in period-specific prices. For cross-period comparison, incremental costs were converted to 2025 KRW, and net monetary benefit (NMB) was calculated at a willingness-to-pay threshold of KRW 50 million/QALY(USD 40,000). RESULTS The ICUR increased from KRW 9.62 million/QALY(USD 7,694) in the 2012 model to KRW 48.62 million/QALY(USD 38,895) in the 2022 model, and NMB in 2025 KRW decreased from KRW 1.73 million to KRW -0.05 million per person. In 2022, the ICUR was KRW 28.20 million/QALY(USD 22,558) for men and KRW 84.37 million/QALY(USD 67,497) for women. The increase was driven mainly by a shift in the screen-detected histologic composition of neoplasia toward lower-risk non-adenomatous findings and by higher costs. CONCLUSIONS The cost-effectiveness of uniform biennial endoscopic screening in Korea declined substantially between 2012 and 2022 and the 2022 results were markedly less favourable for women than for men. These findings support periodic reassessment of mature screening programmes and further evaluation of differentiated screening approaches.

title: Relationship between Mesoscopic Vehicle Group Dynamics and Microscopic Driver Behavior: A Driving Style Perspective
abstract: This study investigates the coupling relationship between mesoscopic vehicle group dynamics and microscopic driving behavior complexity under heterogeneous driving styles, aiming to reveal how local traffic environments are associated with differential volatile behaviors across driving styles. Based on high-precision vehicle trajectory data from the Highway Drone (highD) dataset, local vehicle groups are first identified using a spatiotemporal similarity-based clustering method, and drivers are classified into aggressive, moderate, and conservative groups through spectral clustering. Sample entropy is then extracted from vehicle acceleration, intervehicle distance, and time headway sequences to characterize behavioral complexity and uncertainty in driver’s microscopic maneuvers, based on which a comprehensive behavioral entropy (CBE) index is further constructed using principal component analysis. To identify high-complexity driving behaviors across different driving styles, a random forest model is developed using mesoscopic vehicle group features, including group density, average speed, and speed and distance differences between the neighboring lanes. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) is further employed to quantify the predictive contributions of key features and to identify underlying association patterns related to behavioral complexity. Results show that different driving styles exhibit significantly different responses to the same traffic environment. Aggressive drivers are more sensitive to vehicle group density and average speed, and interlane speed differences exhibit a strong association with their unstable behavior. In contrast, moderate and conservative drivers show pronounced nonlinear responses to intralane speed differences and spatial compression from adjacent lanes. These findings indicate that the mesoscopic traffic environment has differentiated effects on driving stability and decision-making fluctuations among different driving styles, providing empirical evidence for precise and proactive interventions targeting heterogeneous driving populations.
journal: Journal of Transportation Engineering, Part A: Systems

title: Radiographic manifestations of pneumatosis intestinalis and construction of an AI-assisted diagnostic system.
abstract: Pneumatosis intestinalis (PI) has a wide range of etiologies, and the imaging differentiation between benign and ischemic PI is difficult, leading to a high risk of missed diagnosis. This study systematically summarizes the CT (Computed Tomography) imaging manifestations of PI and constructs an AI (Artificial Intelligence)-assisted diagnostic model that integrates multidimensional features. This study retrospectively collected CT and x-ray data from 612 patients with PI (398 benign and 214 ischemic cases) from three tertiary hospitals, and included an external validation set of 106 cases. Imaging analysis established a five-level PI-CT severity scoring system based on gas morphology, distribution, portal venous gas (PVG), intestinal wall enhancement, mesenteric edema, and ascites. The AI system adopted a two-level architecture: The first level used EfficientNet-B3 for rapid screening on x-ray films; the second level used 3D nnU-Net (No-new-Net) to segment intestinal wall gas, and then fused the data through a three-branch network (gas morphology, accompanying signs, and clinical metadata) via cross-attention to output the probability of ischemic PI. In the internal test set, the model achieved an AUC (Area Under the Curve) of 0.947 for ischemic PI (sensitivity 91.3%, specificity 93.6%), significantly outperforming senior radiologists (AUC = 0.876); the AUC on the external validation set was 0.931. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis showed that PVG and blood lactate were the most important predictors. This two-tiered AI system can significantly improve the early identification of the causes of critical PI, providing a reliable method for intelligent diagnosis of emergency imaging.

title: CD8+ regulatory T cells limit immunopathology but impair viral clearance in Hantaan virus infection.
abstract: In hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) caused by Hantaan virus (HTNV), virus-specific CD8+ T cells mediate both viral clearance and immunopathology. Here, we characterized a CD8+ regulatory T cell (Treg) subset restricted by HLA-E (and its murine ortholog Qa-1) in HFRS patients and in a murine HTNV infection model. CD8+ Tregs (CD122+Eomes+CD49dloKIR+), a subset substantially enriched for HLA-E-restricted T cells, were significantly reduced in peripheral blood of HFRS patients and displayed a terminally differentiated profile with elevated expression of KLRG-1, NKG2A, CTLA-4, and Fas-L, correlating with disease severity. Two HTNV glycoprotein-derived nonapeptides that bound Qa-1 were identified. Following immunization with the identified HTNV peptides and subsequent HTNV challenge, wild-type (WT) mice showed attenuated renal immunopathology, whereas D227K knock-in mice (with disrupted Qa-1-CD8/TCR interaction) showed enhanced viral clearance in the spleen and kidney but exacerbated renal immunopathology. Mechanistically, Qa-1-restricted CD8+ Tregs from WT mice suppressed effector CD8+ T cell proliferation in a peptide-specific, CD8/TCR-dependent manner via enhanced TGF-β secretion. Strikingly, D227K mutation dichotomously reshaped Treg phenotype: bulk polyclonal CD8+ Tregs displayed compensatory upregulation of inhibitory receptors (NKG2A, CTLA-4, PD-1) and TGF-β, whereas epitope-specific CD8+ Tregs showed impaired antigen-specific suppressive function and attenuated TGF-β production. Collectively, these findings indicate that HLA-E/Qa-1-restricted CD8+ Tregs can restrain immunopathology during HTNV infection, potentially at the cost of delayed viral elimination. Modulation of this axis may provide insights for therapeutic strategies in HFRS and related viral hemorrhagic fevers.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Lifetime stressor exposure is associated with altered trust formation and social learning in dynamic interactions.
abstract: Although trust is fundamental to social interactions, how lifetime stressor exposure relates to the cognitive processes underlying trust remains poorly understood. Using the Stress and Adversity Inventory (STRAIN) to assess cumulative lifetime stressor exposure, combined with an adaptation of the repeated trust game and computational modeling (Hierarchical Gaussian Filtering), we investigated how stressors experienced over the life course relate to three core aspects of trust dynamics-initial trust formation, learning about others' intentions, and adaptation to changes in trustworthiness-in 168 adults. Greater lifetime stress was associated with stronger negativity biases, lower initial trust, and heightened uncertainty about others' intentions, increases that were general rather than specific to partner type. These more pessimistic priors were not accompanied by poorer reading of partners: Higher lifetime stress was associated with greater differentiation between prosocial and selfish trustees, driven by reduced investment in the selfish trustee alone. Computational analyses further indicated greater belief volatility, consistent with faster model-implied updating of perceived trustworthiness. These findings provide novel evidence that lifetime stress is associated with a profile consistent with recalibration, rather than a degradation, of the cognitive mechanisms underlying trust, with potential consequences for relationship formation and social functioning. They also provide a computationally grounded framework for understanding associations between adversity and social cognition and generate testable predictions for future experimental work.
