The influence of feedstock physicochemical architecture and carrier gas environment (inert N₂ vs. reactive CO₂) on product distribution, elemental partitioning, and biochar quality was evaluated through proximate and ultimate analyses, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with topographical intensity mapping, and multivariate statistical synthesis including Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Pearson correlation mapping. The pyrolysis of 13 diverse biomass residues was investigated across 300–800°C. The influence of feedstock architecture, reactor geometry, and carrier gas environment (N 2 vs. CO 2 ) was systematically evaluated using multivariate statistical synthesis, SEM-topographical mapping, and predictive modeling algorithms. This demonstrates that feedstock composition fundamentally governed conversion pathways: high-volatile date seeds achieved the maximum bio-oil yield of 68.0 wt.%, while high-ash rice straw favored solid-phase carbonisation. Substituting inert N₂ with reactive CO₂ during rice straw pyrolysis facilitated the thermal cracking of tarry surface deposits, significantly enriching the biochar carbon content from 45.33% to 50.94% and enhancing pore accessibility. A suite of predictive linear regression models was developed, achieving exceptional accuracy for energy density forecasting (R 2 = 0.995) based on initial biomass characterisation. This integrated framework, combining Carbon Capture and Utilization (CCU) via CO₂-assisted pyrolysis with high-precision predictive modeling, provides an actionable, scalable platform for automated, decentralised waste-to-energy biorefineries. Integrating Carbon Capture and Utilization (CCU) strategies via CO2-assisted pyrolysis enhances biochar quality. Combined with high-precision predictive modeling, this presents a scalable, automated framework for modern decentralised waste-to-energy technologies.

title: MA-Pose and DMMS-GCN: skeleton-based martial-arts category recognition with edge-device deployment
abstract: With the development of visual sensor technology and human pose estimation algorithms, skeleton-based action recognition has received extensive attention in sports analysis and training systems. The recognition of martial-arts actions is difficult because different styles can share similar poses while differing in rhythm and coordination. To support this task, we constructed the Martial Arts Pose (MA-Pose) dataset, which contains 433 source videos across 13 martial arts categories. The 33-landmark sequences include normalized image coordinates and monocular relative depth rather than metric 3D ground truth. We further propose a Dynamic Multi-Stream Multi-Scale Graph Convolutional Network (DMMS-GCN), which integrates joint, bone, and motion features. The model combines physical, learnable, and input-adaptive graph topology with parallel temporal convolutions. With a fixed seed of 42, 346 videos are used for training and 87 for validation, with one center crop and one prediction per validation video. DMMS-GCN correctly classifies 73/87 videos (83.91% Top-1; 83.51% Macro-F1; 95% Wilson confidence interval, 74.78%–90.17%) and retrieves the correct class among the top five for 84/87 videos (96.55%). These values describe development-set performance because model selection and evaluation use the same validation subset. On a Raspberry Pi 4B, pose extraction runs at approximately 10 frames/s and classification of a prepared 150-frame tensor takes approximately 120 ms. Collecting the first 150 processed pose frames takes about 15 s, so the deployment demonstrates edge-device feasibility rather than instantaneous recognition. The source code, model checkpoint, and MA-Pose dataset are publicly available.

title: Prospects and challenges of artificial intelligence for food security sustainability in Africa: case of South Africa and Nigeria
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly emerged as a transformative technology with the potential to reshape agricultural systems and strengthen food security sustainability in Africa. It is against this backdrop that this study examines the prospects and challenges of AI for food security sustainability in Nigeria and South Africa, adopting a qualitative comparative research design and drawing on secondary sources of data. The analysis is anchored in embedded liberalism theory and agro-ecological theory, which provide complementary perspectives for examining the institutional, socioeconomic, technological, and ecological conditions that shape the sustainable application of AI in agriculture. Findings indicate that large agricultural yield gaps and the predominance of smallholder farming in Nigeria, alongside South Africa’s relatively advanced digital infrastructure, commercial agricultural systems, and innovation ecosystem, present significant opportunities for AI-enabled improvements in agricultural productivity, resilience, and resource efficiency. However, these prospects are moderated by context-specific challenges. Nigeria faces persistent infrastructural, institutional, and technological constraints, while South Africa’s principal challenge lies in inequality-driven exclusion and uneven access to technological benefits. The study therefore argues that AI can contribute meaningfully to food security sustainability when embedded within inclusive institutional arrangements, sustainable agricultural practices, ecological conservation, and context-sensitive governance frameworks.

title: The impact of data factor marketization on agricultural new quality productivity
abstract: The market-oriented allocation of data factors has become increasingly important for transforming agricultural production systems and fostering new growth momentum in agriculture. However, whether and how data factor marketization contributes to the development of Agricultural new quality productivity (ANQP) remains insufficiently understood. Using prefecture-level panel data from Chinese cities during 2005–2023, this study exploits the establishment of data trading platforms as a quasi-natural experiment and employs a staggered difference-in-differences approach to identify the causal effect of data factor marketization on ANQP. To measure ANQP, we construct an index based on large language model (GLM) annotation and BERT classification methods. The results show that data factor marketization significantly enhances the development of ANQP. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that this effect is stronger in regions with more advanced digital infrastructure, better business environments, more developed new agricultural business entities, and higher levels of digital inclusive finance. The mechanism analysis reveals that data factor marketization facilitates agricultural new quality productivity through data value creation, innovation incentives, human capital accumulation, and labor productivity enhancement. Further analysis demonstrates that ANQP on the urban–rural income gap diminishes at the margin, increases farmers’ income at the margin, and strengthens agricultural economic resilience. These findings provide empirical evidence and policy implications for advancing data factor market reforms, cultivating ANQP based on local conditions, and promoting high-quality and sustainable agricultural development.

title: UAV Multi-Source Remote-Sensing Feature Fusion and ES-EfficientNet for Accurate Grading of Maize Curvularia Leaf Spot
abstract: Maize Curvularia leaf spot (CLS) severely affects maize yield and quality; the implementation of non-destructive, precise disease grading is crucial for containing the spread of the disease in the field. This study utilised hyperspectral and thermal infrared remote sensing data acquired by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to extract spectral, textural (TFs) and canopy temperature features. To address the limitations of individual features, the textural-derived indices (CLSTIs) and Normalized Relative Canopy Temperature (NRCT) were developed. Mutual Information-based Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross-Validation (MI_RFECV), Variable Selection Using Random Forests (VSURF), and Variable Combination Population Analysis (VCPA) algorithms were employed to screen for sensitive spectral bands, and these selected bands were fused with the two indices to construct a multidimensional feature set. An ES-EfficientNet model was developed, featuring an MBConv architecture as its backbone with embedded serial multi-scale ECA modules. By utilising depthwise separable convolutions to extract multi-scale spectral features of the disease and employing multi-scale ECA to adaptively optimise channel weights, this model effectively suppresses interference caused by noise and redundant features. The results indicate that the feature combination based on MI_RFECV+CLSTIs+NRCT achieved the optimal classification performance in the ES-EfficientNet model. To ensure the robustness of the results, the model was evaluated across three random seeds (1, 42, and 2024). It maintained a stable performance, achieving an overall accuracy (OA) ranging from 94.17% to 95.33% and a Kappa coefficient up to 94.15%. Its identification performance was superior to that of baseline models using single-source features, and the model maintained stable performance in cross-site transfer within the same provincial-scale study area under the same-year experimental conditions. In summary, this study achieved high-precision, non-destructive grading of maize CLS, providing practical value for field disease monitoring and precise control, while also offering a robust reference framework for remote sensing-based disease identification in other crops.

title: Neutralizing Misleading Visual Cues: An Attention-Driven Encoder–Decoder Framework with Auxiliary Forensic Reconstruction for Video Deepfake Detection
abstract: As deepfake generation methods are constantly evolving, there is a need for new methods that can detect subtle manipulation artefacts in video content, both in terms of spatial and temporal characteristics. In this study, an encoder–decoder architecture is proposed, where the classification and forensic reconstruction are performed simultaneously at the encoder and decoder side, respectively. The architecture consists of a six-layer convolutional encoder to obtain spatial representations from uniformly sampled facial frames of 128 × 128, and a two-layer bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) to model temporal dependency within the sequence of eight facial frames. An attention-pooling mechanism additionally highlights the most instructive temporal characteristics and yields a brief sequence-level representation for binary categorization. In parallel, a forensic decoder reconstructs 64 × 64 Laplacian residual maps, encouraging the network to learn edge-level and texture-level manipulation traces. The framework is trained end-to-end using a weighted combination of cross-entropy classification loss and L1 reconstruction loss. Experiments on the Celeb-DF dataset, comprising 1168 cropped face videos, achieved 93% training accuracy, 90% frame-level classification accuracy, and an ROC-AUC of 0.92. Complementary analysis across spatial, frequency, and temporal feature domains showed that spatial texture characteristics provided the clearest class separation, while the forensic reconstruction branch achieved an MSE of 0.010. Overall, the results demonstrate the value of jointly integrating spatial encoding, temporal sequence modelling, attention-based aggregation, and reconstruction-guided forensic learning for deepfake detection.

title: Voxel-Level Forecasting of Apparent Vertebral Bone Loss from Routine CT Using a 3D Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Existing computed tomography (CT) fracture-risk models typically output one scalar score per vertebra without localising the predicted change. We built and internally validated a three-dimensional (3D) convolutional network forecasting, from one baseline acquisition, a per-voxel map of apparent inter-scan bone-mask loss per lumbar vertebra. Paired CT studies from 65 patients yielded 298 baseline-unfractured vertebra patches (L1 to L5); every patient sustained at least one reader-adjudicated incident fracture, so the cohort is outcome-enriched. The endpoint was apparent vertebral-body mask loss between scans after rigid alignment of automated masks. A multi-task 3D residual U-Net with vertebral-level conditioning was compared with a gradient-boosted classifier on the same features and folds, under five-fold patient-grouped cross-validation with clustered bootstrap intervals. Pooled precision-recall area was 0.445 vs. 0.439 for the reference (+0.005, 95% confidence interval −0.018 to +0.028) and pooled area under the curve (AUC) was 0.815. At matched predicted volume, the network map was less fragmented (2.3 vs. 5.3 components per 1000 voxels), and the endpoint separated incident fractures (AUC 0.865). Voxel-level forecasting of apparent inter-scan vertebral change is feasible on routine CT; the contribution is the paired-scan forecasting framework and the spatial-profile difference, not better discrimination. The endpoint is an algorithmic surrogate requiring voxel-level expert adjudication and external validation before clinical use.

title: P2RBox: Point Prompt Oriented Object Detection with SAM
abstract: Single-point annotation in oriented object detection of remote sensing scenarios is gaining increasing attention due to its cost-effectiveness. However, due to the granularity ambiguity of points, there is a significant performance gap between previous methods and those with full supervision. In this study, we introduce P2RBox, which employs point prompt to generate rotated box (RBox) annotation for oriented object detection. P2RBox employs the SAM model to generate high-quality mask proposals. These proposals are then refined using the semantic and spatial information from annotation points. The best masks are converted into oriented boxes based on the feature directions suggested by the model. P2RBox incorporates two advanced guidance cues: Boundary Sensitive Mask guidance, which leverages semantic information, and Centrality guidance, which utilizes spatial information to reduce granularity ambiguity. This combination enhances detection capabilities significantly. To demonstrate the effectiveness of this method, enhancements based on the baseline were observed by integrating three different detectors. Furthermore, compared to the state-of-the-art point-annotated generative method PointOBB, P2RBox outperforms by about 29% mAP (62.43% vs. 33.31%) on DOTA-v1.0 dataset and 7.1 mean IoU (68.9 vs. 76.0) on WHU building dataset, which provides new possibilities for the practical application of point annotation techniques in multi-class object detection (e.g., building) from remote sensing imagery.

title: A Domain-Specific Memory Bank-Enhanced Framework for Remote Sensing Image Captioning
abstract: Remote sensing image captioning enables automated interpretation of remote sensing data for applications such as environmental monitoring and urban planning. However, general-purpose multimodal models exhibit suboptimal adaptability on remote sensing imagery due to domain discrepancies in data distribution, resolution, and rotation invariance. We propose a domain-specific memory bank-enhanced framework for remote sensing image caption, built upon the lightweight EVCap architecture with three core innovations: (1) a remote sensing-specific visual memory bank providing domain-representative visual–semantic alignment; (2) a staged transfer training strategy that leverages pretrained knowledge while mitigating overfitting from limited remote sensing data; and (3) a K-means clustering-based small-sample memory bank that preserves performance while reducing memory footprint for resource-constrained deployment. Extensive experiments on the NWPU, RSICD, and Sydney datasets demonstrate substantial improvements over baselines. On the test sets, the domain-specific memory bank (R1) improves CIDEr by 1.87% on RSICD (0.3255 to 0.3316), and the clustering-based variant (R4) by 11.7% on Sydney (0.1422 to 0.1589) using only 39% of the full bank, despite decreases on NWPU and RSICD, with about 3.97 million trainable parameters.

title: MSASFormer: A Multi-Scale Adaptive Selection Transformer for Multi-Target Effluent Quality Forecasting in Wastewater Treatment Plants
abstract: Accurate effluent-quality forecasting is essential for effective process monitoring and operational decision-making in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs). However, achieving reliable forecasts requires effectively modelling process dynamics at multiple temporal scales. The relative importance of these temporal scales and the upstream information needed for prediction may vary with operating conditions and prediction targets. To address this challenge, we present the Multi-Scale Adaptive Selection Transformer (MSASFormer), a unified framework for simultaneously forecasting multiple effluent-quality indicators. MSASFormeris evaluated using simulation data generated by Benchmark Simulation Model No. 2 (BSM2) for 4-h-ahead forecasting of effluent BOD5, COD and TSS, achieving the best aggregate predictive performance among the three evaluated models. Compared with the two strong hybrid models (CNN–LSTM and TCN–GRU), MSASFormer yielded the lowest SMSE of 0.366±0.007 and the highest mean R2 of 0.653±0.007. Meanwhile, it achieved the lowest MAE for all three indicators and the best overall performance for COD, while remaining competitive with TCN–GRU for BOD5 and TSS. The ablation results demonstrated the contributions of the main architectural components to predictive performance. Finally, analysis of the scale-selection behaviour showed that MSASFormer selected different combinations of temporal scales across input samples, indicating its ability to adapt scale selection to changing process conditions.

title: Integration of Static Knowledge and Telemetry Data for an IoT-Based Customer Support AI Agent
abstract: The operational effectiveness of artificial intelligence agents in customer support is frequently attributed to the generative sophistication of underlying language models, although answer reliability primarily depends on the structure and quality of the referenced knowledge base. In complex technical domains such as the Internet of Things (IoT), static documentation alone often fails to resolve customer inquiries that involve real-time device states, sensor readings, and connectivity logs. This study investigates how progressive tiers of knowledge integration affect the response quality of an AI agent within an IoT customer support context. Employing a mixed-method pilot design combining literature synthesis, comparative analysis, experimental testing, and conceptual exploration, thirty representative questions were classified into informational, status, and diagnostic categories. These queries were evaluated across four operational scenarios: without retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), article-based RAG, article plus device metadata records, and a comprehensive hybrid framework integrating static articles, device records, and telemetry streams. Answer quality was measured using Cosine Similarity, BERTScore (F1), and a randomized blind human evaluation assessing relevance, correctness, and usefulness. The results demonstrate that while curated static documentation adequately addresses procedural informational queries, resolving status and diagnostic issues necessitates real-time operational context. The hybrid integration delivered the highest overall performance, achieving a human-evaluation score of 4.40 compared with 2.53 for article-based RAG (p = 0.0039). These empirical findings confirm that robust IoT support agents require dynamic knowledge governance that bridges versioned documentation, synchronized asset metadata, and live telemetry data within a unified retrieval framework.
journal: International Journal Software Engineering and Computer Science (IJSECS)

title: Fair Walk-Forward Forecasting of ICE Robusta Futures: Comparing Statistical, Machine-Learning, Deep-Learning, and Hybrid Models
abstract: Distribution shifts can degrade nonlinear forecasting models trained on historical price levels, particularly relative to models that retain the most recently observed level. This study empirically compares 14 statistical, machine-learning, deep-learning, and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA)–recurrent hybrid specifications for the daily ICE Futures Europe Robusta Coffee benchmark, rather than proposing a new forecasting algorithm. The synchronized dataset comprises 4,603 observations from 14 January 2008 to 28 January 2026. Specifications are selected using a chronological pure-training/validation split and evaluated once on a 300-observation blind test set under a common one-step-ahead walk-forward protocol. The blind-test price distribution shifts sharply from gross training (Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic 0.955; standardized Wasserstein distance 4.274). Delta-Random Forest achieves the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) at 83.59 USD per metric ton, whereas Khashei–Bijari ARIMA–Long Short‐Term Memory (LSTM) yields the lowest root mean squared error at 111.99. However, Delta-Random Forest improves MAE over Naive by only 0.27 USD per metric ton, and no selected pairwise comparison remains significant after Holm adjustment of the Diebold–Mariano tests. Grouped permutation importance shows that permuting lagged first-difference history increases Delta-Random-Forest MAE by only 0.76, while Volume and the three macro-financial regressors contribute negligibly. These findings support a cautious interpretation: differencing improves nonlinear learners’ robustness to level-range shifts but does not establish economically or statistically meaningful predictive information beyond the most recently observed price. Received: 11 July 2026 | Revised: 14 September 2026 | Accepted: 23 September 2026 Conflicts of Interest The authors declare that they have no conflicts of interest to this work. Data Availability Statement The frozen processed analytical dataset, preprocessing and modeling code, environment specification, validation-search tables, saved blind-test prediction vectors, and revision-only analyses are available in the public reproducibility repository: https://github.com/hdanginneu/ice-robusta-walk-forward-forecasting. Price and Volume were obtained from Investing.com, London Coffee Futures Historical Data (accessed January 28, 2026). The frozen analytical sample spans January 14, 2008, to January 28, 2026. Use of the provider’s data remains subject to its terms. The macro-financial series were retrieved through FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis: Nominal Broad US Dollar Index (DTWEXBGS); EFFR; crude oil prices: WTI—Cushing, Oklahoma (DCOILWTICO) (all accessed March 1, 2026). These source records are publicly accessible. Author Contribution Statement Phung Duy Quang: Conceptualization, Writing – review & editing, Supervision, Project administration. Cao Ha Hai Dang: Methodology, Software, Formal analysis, Data curation, Writing – original draft, Writing – review & editing, Visualization. Nguyen Huu Thinh: Conceptualization, Methodology, Validation, Writing – review & editing, Supervision. Hoang Nam Quyen: Investigation, Writing – original draft. Hoang Tuan Minh: Investigation, Data curation, Writing – review & editing. Van Thi Thuan: Investigation, Resources, Data curation, Writing – review & editing. Bui Thi Tam: Validation, Writing – review & editing, Visualization. Nguyen Viet Ha: Validation, Writing – review & editing. Tran Quang Thanh: Software, Validation, Writing – review & editing.
journal: Journal of Data Science and Intelligent Systems

title: BobFlow: Towards Human-Agent Collaborative Data Science Using Dataflows
abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have established human-agent collaboration as a promising paradigm for data science. Effective collaboration requires a shared computational abstraction that enables agents to reason about processing logic while allowing human analysts to understand, guide, and refine the analysis. Although scripts written in Python or SQL provide precise control, their syntax and execution details can be difficult for analysts to understand and modify. In this paper, we argue that dataflows are an effective abstraction for human-agent collaboration in data science. We introduce BobFlow, a system that combines the dataflow abstraction with the ReAct paradigm. It enables agents to iteratively construct and execute dataflows for data science tasks while allowing analysts to inspect the analysis and provide feedback. Our user study shows that BobFlow helps analysts understand, inspect, and verify agent-generated analyses. A thorough experimental evaluation across proprietary and open-weight LLMs shows accuracy score gains of up to 18.6 points at just over 1/3 of a script-based ReAct agent's inference cost.

title: ZipDrift: Generating Multimodal Short-Horizon MPC Costs with One-Step Drifting Models
abstract: Short-horizon model predictive control (MPC) is fast but myopic. ZipMPC compensates by learning a context-dependent correction of the short-horizon cost that imitates a long-horizon expert. We observe that the optimal correction is often multimodal: when a slower opponent can be passed on either side, good corrections of opposite sign coexist, and the expert's choice between them hinges on tiny cost differences. Deterministic regression then averages modes or inherits inconsistent expert tie-breaking. We propose ZipDrift, which trains a one-step drifting generator over MPC cost corrections, tilted toward low closed-loop cost and learned only from cost evaluations of candidate corrections, without differentiating through the optimiser. A few generated candidates are ranked by a learned critic, and the model-based MPC then enforces dynamics and constraints. In a kinematic overtaking benchmark derived from ZipMPC, more than half of the contexts are bimodal and the manual short-horizon MPC crashes in 28% of them. With an eight-dimensional stagewise correction, evaluated on 1000 fresh contexts and five training seeds, ZipDrift with eight candidates crashes in 0.74% of episodes, compared with 3.4% for an idealised ZipMPC-style regressor and 2.1% for critic-ranked random candidates with the same budget. A mixture density network (MDN) with the same selection is equally good (0.76%). The benefit of drifting lies in sample quality: in a pre-specified test on further unseen contexts, a single drifting sample crashes in 8.7% of episodes against 13.2% for the MDN, and ZipDrift needs four candidates instead of eight to fall below 1%. With many candidates, all methods degrade as selection exploits errors of the critic.

title: ReTailor: A Residual Feature Tailoring Framework for Real-Time Cross-Sensor Pansharpening Adaptation
abstract: Recent pansharpening models achieve strong fusion performance on trained sensors, yet often generalize poorly to unseen sensors. Existing cross-sensor adaptation is limited by target-sensor retraining, which requires target-sensor training pairs and a dedicated training stage, and by per-image zero-shot adaptation, which is computationally expensive due to whole-network optimization for each test image. To address these problems, we propose ReTailor, a real-time sequential cross-sensor adaptation framework. Only a lightweight residual Feature Tailor is rapidly optimized under self-supervised, physics-aware constraints to correct cross-sensor shifts without modifying the well-learned fusion prior. For efficient and effective deployment, ReTailor combines content-aware patch selection, which identifies a few informative patches per image for optimization at negligible cost to improve both quality and efficiency, with rolling residual bootstrap, which inherits sensor-related knowledge across the image stream to further improve quality. Extensive experiments on cross-sensor adaptation settings show that ReTailor mitigates cross-sensor degradation both effectively and efficiently. Moreover, we compare ReTailor with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), a widely used method for fine-tuning, to demonstrate the advantages of our approach. We further evaluate the core principle of ReTailor on two additional remote sensing tasks: super-resolution pansharpening and image segmentation, where it consistently improves performance. In general, ReTailor provides a highly effective and efficient strategy for deploying pansharpening models under real-world cross-sensor degradation, while also offering useful insights into managing cross-sensor degradation in other remote sensing tasks. Code will be released at https://github.com/JingZe-Liang/ReTailor .

title: Feature Puzzles: Single-Image Supervision for Multi-View 3D-Aware Segmentation
abstract: Humans can easily recognize the same objects across different viewpoints of a 3D scene, whereas teaching models such multi-view-consistent perception typically requires videos or calibrated multi-view captures, which are considerably more expensive and less diverse than large-scale monocular data.~In this paper, we introduce Feature Puzzles, a novel framework for learning multi-view-consistent segmentation using only single-image semantic segmentation supervision. Specifically, we propose a simple yet effective pipeline that constructs multi-view-consistent segmentation pseudo-labels through image cropping and geometric transformations. We further introduce a lightweight, plug-and-play network that leverages the multi-view-consistent image features learned by existing pretrained 3D foundation models and the generated pseudo-labels to perform multi-view-consistent segmentation. Importantly, our flexible framework supports various types of prompts provided from one or multiple views and can be readily extended to open-vocabulary 3D segmentation. Under this single-image supervision, our feed-forward model achieves the best mIoU on NVOS, remains competitive on SPIn-NeRF and ScanNet++ against baselines using per-scene optimization or in-domain multi-view training, and demonstrates zero-shot transfer to open-vocabulary 3D segmentation. Visual comparisons are available on our project page: https://featurepuzzles.github.io/

title: Mock CSST NUV-NIR imaging of TNG50 galaxies with resolved stellar populations
abstract: Aims. We aim to develop a framework for producing CSST-like mock images of resolved stellar populations from simulated galaxies, demonstrated here using two TNG50 galaxies as illustrative test cases. Methods. Starting from simulated galaxies from TNG50, we use the population synthesis code TRILEGAL to sample individual stars from star particles, retaining bright stars explicitly and treating the remaining unresolved light, including faint stellar light and nebular emission from star-forming regions, as a diffuse background component of the galaxy. Based on the dust distribution inferred from the gas mass and metallicity of gas cells, we use the radiative transfer (RT) code SKIRT to construct the dust model. From this model, we compute the line-of-sight extinction for individual stars, while image-level transmission maps for the diffuse light are derived through RT simulations. For young stars still embedded in their natal molecular clouds, we additionally include birth-cloud attenuation. The resulting dust-attenuated stellar catalogues and diffuse-light images are then processed with the CSST simulation pipeline, which applies PSF convolution, sky background, and instrumental noise. Results. Our framework produces mock CSST images for both a spiral galaxy and a dwarf irregular galaxy from TNG50 in the seven photometric bands. The mock images combine resolved stars, unresolved diffuse light, and dust attenuation within a unified framework, and include the main observational effects expected for the survey. The images are provided with known astrometric and photometric calibration information, and are intended as realistic image-level inputs for subsequent source detection, photometric recovery, and completeness analyses of resolved stellar populations. The framework is designed to be adaptable to other hydrodynamic simulations and observing configurations.

title: Agentic Wireless Optimization: Workflow Automation, Algorithm Design, and Multi-Timescale Network Operations
abstract: Optimization is fundamental to wireless communications, from characterizing channel capacity and designing transmission schemes to allocating network resources. However, conventional workflows require substantial expertise and manual effort, particularly for high-dimensional or nonconvex problems, black-box objectives, and interdependent decisions across time scales. Recent advances in agentic artificial intelligence (AI), particularly agents based on large language models (LLMs), offer new opportunities to address these challenges by integrating reasoning, tool use, and numerical feedback. This article presents an overview of agentic AI for wireless optimization, focusing on workflow automation, algorithm design, and multi-timescale network operations. First, LLM-based agents streamline optimization workflows by automating problem formulation, code generation, numerical solution, and result verification in a closed loop. Second, they facilitate algorithm design by combining and configuring existing numerical methods and refining learning-based optimizers, using numerical feedback to improve solution quality and computational efficiency for nonconvex and black-box problems. Third, they support multi-timescale network operations by decomposing coupled problems into interdependent subtasks and coordinating their solutions to satisfy network-level objectives and service requirements. A multicast beamforming case study demonstrates performance gains from agent-developed solvers, particularly in execution time, and a network energy-saving example illustrates how agents coordinate dynamic base station activation, user association, and beamforming across time scales. Finally, we discuss open challenges and research opportunities in agentic wireless optimization.

title: CellCanon: An Agentic Cellular World Model for Prediction, Explanation, and Observation-Driven Updating
abstract: Biological discovery requires using molecular knowledge and new measurements to infer responses beyond the conditions already observed. We introduce CellCanon, the first agentic cellular world model to unify single-cell expression prediction, evidence-grounded explanation, and observation-driven updating. Its predictive core reuses condition-level biological evidence across gene-specific numerical readouts to guide single-cell expression generation. A shared world state links predictions, acquired measurements, and source-linked claims, supporting explanation and revision. On 339 held-out SciPlex3 conditions across three cell lines, CellCanon improves differential-expression AUPRC and Macro-F1 over the best baseline for each metric by 63.3% and 17.3%, respectively, and direction Macro-F1 by 7.2%. Relative to gene-wise reasoning on matched drug-cell cohorts, measured language-model token use falls by 99.77% for Predict and 98.41% for Explain. On the source-grounded benchmark, Explain correctly answers all answerable questions with supporting proofs and identifies all insufficient-evidence cases. In simulated experimental feedback, Update uses one measured source context per drug to exceed the best fine-tuned baselines in differential-expression AUPRC and Macro-F1 without changing model weights. Together, these capabilities support a cumulative account of cellular responses, with predictions and biological judgments that can be revised as evidence accumulates.

title: Information-Matched Auditing of Conversational Emotion-Shift Forecasting: A Leakage-Safe Evaluation Protocol
abstract: Comparisons in conversational emotion-shift forecasting are easily distorted when a learned model receives rich features but its transition baseline is given a noisy or unavailable current-emotion label, when hyperparameter budgets differ, or when target-turn information enters the representation. We present an information-matched, leakage-safe auditing protocol that closes these gaps with an explicit commitment point, executable causality tests, equal four-configuration validation searches, and seed-dialogue-aware inference. Applying it to six causal model families on four text corpora and two feature-source sensitivity configurations shows that a deployable train-only current-emotion classifier feeding the transition baseline yields a different verdict than an oracle diagnostic where both sides receive gold current emotion. Under the deployable condition, learned models improve over the predicted-label baseline on all four primary corpora; DailyDialog gains are large and survive a 72-comparison Holm correction (best ROC-AUC gain = +0.167, adjusted p=.0144). Under matched gold information, the baseline remains competitive on IEMOCAP and stronger on MELD, while every model retains a large DailyDialog advantage. We additionally report precision-recall AUC, calibration, a strictly utterance-local feature control, same-person self-shift forecasting, and a future-access dose-response test. An eight-item leakage checklist accompanies the protocol. Code, raw seed predictions, and reporting artifacts are available from the corresponding author upon request.

title: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) enables multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to scale capacity efficiently, but expert parameters dominate memory even though only a few experts are activated per token: they account for over 90% of model size in modern MoE-MLLMs (e.g., 54 GB out of about 58 GB in BF16 for InternVL3.5-30B-A3B and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B). Expert pruning has emerged as an effective compression strategy, but existing methods aggregate importance uniformly across tokens, ignoring that the same expert may serve different roles for vision versus language processing. To address this, we propose MAEP (Modality-Aware Expert Pruning), a training-free framework that decomposes expert importance by modality in a single forward pass. MAEP introduces (1) Delta-H Output ($ΔH$), a redistribution-aware metric measuring the MoE output change when an expert is removed, and (2) low-attention vision tokens as a vision-side pruning signal that is dataset-stable: its expert-importance ranking remains stable across different datasets. Text-side importance serves as a preservation signal while vision-side importance serves as a pruning signal, and experts are ranked globally across layers. Experiments on three MoE-based MLLMs across multimodal and text benchmarks show that MAEP outperforms modality-agnostic baselines on the majority of multimodal benchmarks while remaining competitive on text-only tasks, reducing the BF16 expert weight footprint by about 27 GB (about 47% of total memory) so that the full weight footprint of an approximately 58 GB model fits within a single 40 GB GPU. Code is available at https://github.com/nota-github/MAEP.

title: Ray-Tracing-Based Dynamic Channel Sounding With Autoregressive Wi-Fi CSI Prediction
abstract: Channel sounding in Wi-Fi multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems must balance channel state information (CSI) accuracy against CSI acquisition overhead. Device mobility causes channel aging, while autoregressive CSI prediction introduces errors that accumulate over sounding intervals. However, standardized statistical channel models cannot fully capture the environment-specific channel dynamics encountered in physical artificial intelligence (AI) applications, motivating the use of Sionna-based ray tracing to evaluate CSI prediction under device mobility and evolving propagation geometry. This paper develops a dynamic sounding framework that integrates autoregressive CSI prediction with signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR)-constrained interval selection. A Transformer with rotary position embedding that converts device positions into CSI sequences predicts CSI across multiple subcarriers for beamforming updates between sounding exchanges. We formulate sounding-interval selection as a predicted average-throughput maximization problem under per-stream SINR lower-bound constraints, including CSI acquisition and processing overhead. A prediction-error perturbation analysis provides the SINR bounds, and cumulative-sum enumeration globally solves the finite single-variable problem. Actual SINR feasibility holds whenever the prediction errors satisfy the bounds. Ray-tracing experiments assess channel prediction, trajectory transfer, and autoregressive prediction errors. In single-STA Wi-Fi 7 link-level simulations, predicted-CSI beamforming improves mean goodput by 67.3%, 112.7%, and 119.1% over stale CSI for linear, circular, and cosine trajectories, respectively.

title: Enforcing Accountable Disclosure in Confidential AI
abstract: Advances in CPU and GPU confidential computing enable confidential AI, allowing LLMs to process user prompts without exposing them to service providers or infrastructure operators. However, AI agents often need to send prompt-derived information to external services, and providers may also require limited disclosure for safety monitoring and failure diagnosis. We propose CORDE, a system for confidential virtual machines (CVMs) designed to satisfy the principle of Confine or Declare: user-derived data is confined by default, but when necessary, it may leave the CVM only after being "declared." To "declare" data is to record its exact contents, recipient, and stated reason in a user-accessible, tamper-evident declaration log. To put this principle into practice, we present an integrated system design that combines per-user information-flow control in Rust with a TEE-based ledger and remote attestation. Our evaluation on an NVIDIA H100 GPU shows that declaration before disclosure adds little overhead in task latency, about 0.5% on the AppWorld agent benchmark. CORDE provides a basis for accountable disclosure of user data, supporting responsible and transparent data management in AI services.

title: Intra-Architecture Source Attribution for Stable Diffusion: A New Task with Benchmark Dataset and Baseline
abstract: Designing systems that attribute a generated image to its source model has lately become a major area of AI research. Most existing datasets and systems related to image source attribution are targeted towards the detection of architectural signatures of the source models. Distinct from this, focusing on stable diffusion, we introduce a novel task, IntrAA-SD, Intra-Architecture source Attribution for Stable Diffusion, where the source models to be differentiated share the same architectural backbone and differ only due to fine-tuning. The proposed task aligns with the emergence of fine-tuned generators having the same architecture, like Juggernaut XL and RealVis XL, which are fine-tuned versions of Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL). We provide a first-of-its-kind $140$K-image benchmark dataset containing images generated from different fine-tunes of SDXL, along with in-domain and out-of-distribution prompts. We also provide a baseline framework for IntrAA-SD, which leverages a style-conditioned Mixture-of-Experts network. It uses a frozen CLIP backbone to capture the image style and gate the MoE, which processes fine-tuned trace features from a high-resolution LoRA-adapted DINOv2 network. The fine-tuned models used, the prompting strategies considered, and the formation details employed in the novel dataset are elaborated. Our baseline intra-architecture source attribution method is evaluated in terms of attribution accuracy on our dataset, and ablation studies are also performed. Code and dataset is available at https://github.com/mallikagarg/IntrAA-SD.

title: MotoVerse: A Benchmark for Predictive Perception of Motorized Two-Wheelers in Dense Unstructured Traffic
abstract: Motorized Two-Wheelers (MTWs) dominate personal transport across much of the Global South, yet remain largely overlooked in predictive perception research for autonomous driving and ADAS. We introduce MotoVerse, a benchmark for predictive perception from an MTW's ego-centric perspective. MotoVerse comprises 949 maneuver clips collected in dense, unstructured traffic and trajectory annotations for over 31,000 surrounding road agents, including over 16,000 MTWs, enabling two complementary tasks: Ego-Rider Maneuver Anticipation (ERMA) and Traffic Agent Trajectory Prediction (TATP). Each clip is further annotated with an MTW-specific challenge taxonomy comprising dynamic ego-motion, weak traffic structure and contextual occlusion, enabling challenge-aware evaluation. We benchmark established conventional prediction models, general-purpose Vision-Language Models (VLMs), driving-specific VLMs and vision-language-action models. Our experiments reveal three key insights: (i) video backbones reach most of their full-observation accuracy from the first fifth of a maneuver, whereas zero-shot VLMs need most of the maneuver to be observed; (ii) zero-shot VLMs, whether general-purpose or driving-specific, largely remain close to simple baselines on both tasks; a preliminary LoRA study shows that adaptation lifts anticipation sharply but leaves trajectory prediction behind conventional models; and (iii) the rider's own motion drives forecasting difficulty: for every model, including a static baseline, errors are highest during left turns and rise under dynamic ego-motion. We believe MotoVerse will serve as a challenging benchmark for safer and more robust predictive AI for intelligent two-wheelers. The dataset and evaluation code are publicly available at https://github.com/VarunIIITH/MotoVerse.

title: ChanSFormer: A Channel Agnostic Vision Transformer for Multi-Channel Cell Painting Images
abstract: High-content multi-channel imaging, from Cell Painting assays to remote sensing, is central to modern scientific pipelines. Because these channels are highly heterogeneous and experimental configurations frequently evolve, a practical vision backbone must be fundamentally channel-agnostic. Current channel-adaptive vision transformers rely on global self-attention with learnable channel embeddings, which can be computed only for previously known channels. Attempts to overcome this limitation of new channels either discard the embeddings, losing channel identity, or process each channel independently, thereby eliminating critical cross-channel interactions. To address this, we introduce ChanSFormer, an efficient Vision Transformer that replaces rigid embeddings with disentangled spatial-channel attention and individual channel CLS tokens. This architecture natively preserves both distinct channel identities and cross-channel information flow. Furthermore, the individual channel class token design unlocks more informative feature representations for self-supervised learning and enables representation-based channel sampling while remaining channel-agnostic. We evaluate ChanSFormer on two biology multi-channel datasets, CHAMMI, JUMP-CP and a satellite dataset, So2Sat. Experimental results show that ChanSFormer outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 3.93%-4.27% on JUMP-CP in classification accuracy. It also demonstrates exceptional cross-dataset transferability under a self-supervised setting, outperforming previous methods by up to 2.72% in accuracy in the same classification tasks. Furthermore, the disentangled attention reduces the quadratic complexity of channel-by-spatial sequence length of the global attention baseline, thus improving throughput by 55%-313%. Code is available at https://github.com/cvlab-stonybrook/ChanSFormer.

title: Phantom: Temporal Caching for Diffusion Models
abstract: Diffusion models have become the dominant paradigm for high-quality image generation, but their iterative inference across tens of timesteps incurs substantial computational overhead. Prior accelerators exploit temporal similarity in diffusion models via differential quantization or output sparsity, yet suffer from increased memory footprint, design complexity, and image degradation. In this work, we present Phantom, an algorithm-architecture co-designed accelerator built on temporal caching. We view temporal similarity as differential sparsity: between adjacent timesteps, only a small fraction of tokens (outliers) change significantly. Phantom recomputes only these outlier tokens and reuses the rest from a temporal cache. Phantom runs on standard systolic arrays with lightweight additions: a Phantom Engine at the global buffer that detects outliers and updates the cache as activations stream through, and a condensed pipeline that maps the resulting sparse updates onto dense systolic computation for FC, convolution, and attention layers. Evaluations on modern diffusion models show that Phantom achieves an average 4.0x speedup and 5.5x energy saving over GPUs and prior accelerators while preserving generation quality.

title: Reconciling Privacy with Provenance for Language Model Watermarks
abstract: Watermarking has great potential for regulating the use of language models (LMs), but its deployment has been marred by controversy, as many users argue that fine-grained tracking of LM usage violates their privacy. This tension reduces the effectiveness of watermarks, as users engage in evasion strategies such as paraphrasing that can remove much of the watermark signal. We show that provenance and privacy can be reconciled if we shift the goal of watermark design from tracking individuals to estimating aggregate usage. We develop locally differentially private watermarks which provably limit the evidence that any individual text can contribute to detection, while still enabling accurate estimation of population frequencies. We introduce the Red-Green Sequence (RGS) watermark, a private and computationally efficient watermark that achieves accurate frequency estimation at high privacy levels across various models, sample sizes and generation entropies in settings that reflect realistic deployment scenarios. On C4 language modeling tasks, we attain $0.0019$ MSE with $0.0038$ mean absolute bias at a low $\varepsilon$ of 1, while in more challenging settings such as an essay writing task with only 100 text samples, we still find errors on the order of $0.0113$ MSE with $0.004$ mean absolute bias at $\varepsilon=2$.

title: XuanJian-DINOSAR: A SAR Foundation Model Based on Global and Local Semantic Consistency
abstract: Self-supervised pre-training on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery enables transferable representations, but the optical-SAR domain gap and speckle perturbations limit representation stability. Most SAR foundation models use masked image modeling (MIM) through pixel reconstruction or structural feature prediction, which is sensitive to speckle or relies on predefined operators. Joint modeling of cross-view semantics and perturbation stability at corresponding spatial locations remains underexplored. We propose XuanJian-DINOSAR, a SAR foundation model based on global and local semantic consistency. We curate over 360K publicly available SAR target chips, detection images, and scene images spanning diverse targets, scenes, and sensors, and adapt an optically pre-trained DINOv2 model to SAR through self-supervised learning. The framework combines DINO global semantic self-distillation, iBOT local masked modeling, and KoLeo feature-distribution regularization to learn globally discriminative and locally structure-aware representations. We introduce a local semantic consistency branch tailored to SAR intensity statistics and coherent imaging characteristics. Shared geometric transformations produce spatially aligned teacher weak views and student strong views. Intensity transformations and Gamma multiplicative speckle perturbations are applied to student views, while a cosine consistency loss aligns patch tokens at corresponding locations, promoting stability under radiometric perturbations. This objective complements the cross-region and cross-scale semantic consistency of DINOv2 multi-crop training, jointly enforcing global and local semantic consistency. Experiments on multiple downstream classification and detection datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on most evaluation metrics, validating the generality and transferability of the learned representations.

title: From Handcrafted to Generative: RLVR-Optimized Icon Generation for Alexa+
abstract: Alexa+ devices with screens display animated icons during conversations to visually reinforce what is being said. The original set of these icons was hand-drawn by designers one at a time, a process that produces polished results but is time-consuming and cannot scale to the range of topics encountered in open-ended conversation. We describe an automated pipeline, deployed in production, that generates these vectorised animated icons from a text description alone and surfaces relevant animations to customers based on their ongoing conversation. The pipeline decomposes icon creation into a sequence of stages (image generation, semantic decomposition, vectorisation, styling, and animation). Its quality is determined at the very first of these, image generation, on which every downstream stage depends. We therefore focus on improving this first and most critical stage. Because the icons are rendered on small display canvases under strict design guidelines, generations are often unsuitable for production. Supervised fine-tuning is not viable, as no dataset of line-art icons exists under these constraints. Instead, we design objective verifiers that automatically flag generations violating the design guidelines, and use them to fine-tune a flow matching image generation model via reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR). The fine-tuned model raises the pass rate from 15.7% to 58.7% (3.7x) under a VLM judge that is independent of the reward model. Both the trained model and the verifier are deployed in the production pipeline, where the verifier also serves as the automated quality gate before final design review.

title: Neural Stochastic Forecasting for Lateral Molecular Diffusion Simulations
abstract: Predicting the long-time diffusion of membrane proteins is challenging because molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are computationally expensive, while experimental single-particle tracking is often limited by finite observation times. Here, we introduce a neural stochastic (NS) model for forecasting the collective diffusion of membrane proteins from coarse-grained MD trajectories. The model combines a transformer-based representation of protein configurations, recurrent networks operating at multiple temporal scales, and a stochastic latent process with learned memory. A cross-attention decoder then generates correlated protein displacements while accounting for the instantaneous system geometry and periodic boundary conditions. We evaluate the model in two membrane systems: seven interacting PIEZO channels and a mixed system containing seven PIEZO and ten TREK channels. For the seven PIEZO system, the NS model reproduces the anomalous diffusion exponent measured in MD simulations $α\sim 1$, substantially improving on a previously developed variational autoregressive model that exhibits superdiffusive behavior. The model also generates trajectories extending to 40,000 frames and captures the distinct diffusion characteristics of PIEZO and TREK populations in the mixed system. Comparisons of time-averaged mean-square displacements, Van Hove displacement distributions, and non-Gaussian parameters show that the model preserves key statistical features of the simulated dynamics. These results establish neural stochastic modeling as a promising approach for generating long trajectories of multi-protein membrane diffusion and extending the statistical analysis of molecular dynamics simulations.

title: A minimal E/I circuit model explains differential recovery from amblyopia under TTX and reverse occlusion
abstract: Recovery from amblyopia beyond the critical period remains a major challenge in visual neuroscience. Experimental studies show that transient inactivation of the fellow eye with tetrodotoxin (TTX) produces stronger and more persistent recovery than reverse occlusion (RO), despite both interventions reducing competition from the fellow eye. The circuit mechanisms underlying this difference remain unclear. We develop a minimal cortical circuit model combining excitatory-inhibitory population dynamics, BCM-like metaplasticity, homeostatic regulation, and eye-specific synaptic plasticity. Monocular deprivation drives the network into an amblyopic operating regime with reduced excitatory activity and fellow-eye dominance. Phase-plane and operating-regime analyses show that TTX and RO subsequently place the circuit in distinct dynamical states. TTX lowers inhibitory activity while maintaining excitatory activity above the BCM modification threshold, creating a larger plasticity-permissive regime than RO. These differences produce stronger recovery of amblyopic-eye responsiveness and greater correction of ocular dominance under TTX. A local robustness analysis across 300 perturbed parameter sets shows that the TTX advantage is not dependent on a narrowly tuned parameter choice. These results provide a mechanistic account of the differential efficacy of fellow-eye inactivation and suggest that recovery from sensory deprivation depends not only on changes in sensory input, but also on the dynamical operating regime of the cortical circuit.

title: A Definition of Catastrophic Performance
abstract: A central challenge in AI is specifying objectives that align with human preferences. While existing theoretical results elucidate how misspecification impacts performance, they typically do not distinguish between merely suboptimal and catastrophic outcomes. To enable rigorous analysis of catastrophic risk from AI misalignment, we introduce a formal definition of catastrophic performance. Our definition is based on two reference values. The first, baseline value, captures the value attained if no agent is deployed. The second, orthogonal value, captures the value of a trajectory that is unrelated to human preferences, in a sense we describe. Orthogonal value is typically far worse than baseline value. We interpret these reference values through examples in which past human activity has altered the state of the environment to human benefit. Starting at the resulting state, an AI agent is deployed with the goal of accelerating further progress. Catastrophic performance represents this agent's undoing of benefits afforded by human activity.

title: FedXCrop: Privacy-Preserving Crop Disease Detection via Federated Learning with Post-Aggregation Explainability under Non-IID Farm Distributions
abstract: Deep learning can classify crop diseases accurately from benchmark leaf images, but centralized training requires farms to share raw data, and predictions without explanations offer limited support for treatment decisions. We present FedXCrop, a federated crop disease classification pipeline that quantitatively evaluates explanations of the aggregated global model. A MobileNetV2 model trained centrally on PlantVillage achieved 99.38% test accuracy (standard deviation 0.05 over three seeds) on a fixed test set of 5,428 images across 38 classes. Federated models initialized with ImageNet weights were trained for 30 rounds across five clients. FedAvg achieved 98.81% accuracy with identically distributed clients and 98.81%, 98.59%, and 97.78% under Dirichlet label skew (alpha = 1, 0.5, and 0.1, respectively). FedProx was not significantly different from FedAvg at any heterogeneity level (McNemar p > 0.3). Grad-CAM and SmoothGrad explanations were evaluated on 380 test images. Both attributed more energy to the leaf than chance (0.70-0.78 versus 0.60), while Grad-CAM maps from federated and centralized models showed Spearman correlations of 0.74-0.76. Agreement decreased as heterogeneity increased, lesion localization was only modestly above chance, and a model-randomization test indicated that SmoothGrad maps depended substantially on image structure rather than learned parameters. In this setting, label skew reduced federated accuracy by 0.6-1.6 percentage points relative to centralized training. FedAvg largely preserved Grad-CAM behavior, while FedProx provided no measurable benefit.

title: SO3LR Tauri: Generally Applicable Force Fields for Reactive (Bio)Molecular Simulations Covering the Periodic Table
abstract: Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) aim to create a unified model that describes all major classes of (bio)molecules at quantum-mechanical accuracy. We present SO3LR Tauri, a family of MLFFs developed toward this goal, coupling a fast SO3krates network to explicit, physics-based interaction modules: pair-specific short-range repulsion, environment-dependent dispersion, and electrostatics, each improved beyond its original formulation. The models are trained on 148 million structures spanning 85 elements, drawn from several quantum-chemical datasets. Against coupled-cluster references, the models accurately reproduce nucleobase-pair and charged protein-ligand interactions, carbohydrate conformer ordering, and molecular dipoles. They also resolve the transition pathways of organic and enzymatic reactions. Dynamical simulations recover experimental densities of water and organic solvents, the hydration structure of mono- and divalent ions, the pKa values of amino-acid side chains, and the structure and dynamics of proteins, membranes, nucleic acids, glycoproteins, and metal-containing biomolecules, all without system-specific fitting. Released in three sizes, the models reach 0.7-3.2 $μ$s/atom and scale to 27-84 million atoms on a single GPU. Much work remains to be done: achieving predictive accuracy for static and dynamic liquid properties, reaction barriers, coverage of chemical and conformational space, and the sampling and inference speed needed to describe biomolecular processes.

title: CAPE-JEPA - Cross-modal Adversarial Probabilistic Embedding JEPA
abstract: Cross-modal remote sensing image retrieval (RS-CMIR) requires representations that are simultaneously modality-invariant and semantically discriminative, despite the profound physical gap between heterogeneous sensors such as Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and multispectral imagery. Recent JEPA-based Predictive self-supervised approaches such as X-JEPA formulate cross-modal alignment as a deterministic latent forecasting task, implicitly assuming uniform patch predictability and leaving cross-modal distributional alignment unaddressed. We propose CAPE-JEPA, a probabilistic cross-modal Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture with three contributions: (i) a cross-attentional Gaussian predictor outputting per-patch parameters (mu, sigma^2) conditioned on opposite-modality context, trained via negative log-likelihood to model inherent cross-sensor prediction uncertainty; (ii) adversarial distributional regularization combining unimodal isotropic Gaussian regularization with a novel cross-modal adversarial variant that aligns modality distributions via worst-case Epps-Pulley characteristic function tests without explicit sample pairing; and (iii) in-training contrastive learning with attention-pooled heads for scene-level discriminative grounding. Evaluated on BigEarthNet-14K (BEN-14K) and fMoW across SAR, multispectral, and RGB modalities, CAPE-JEPA surpasses X-JEPA by up to 13.74 points on BEN-14K and 15.59 points on fMoW, outperforming all baselines including SkySense and CROMA across both unimodal and cross-modal directions while using fewer parameters (407.30M vs. 432.72M).

title: Multi-Resident Data Association in Smart Homes via MDP Modeling and Behavior Cloning
abstract: Ambient sensors offer a privacy-preserving solution for activity recognition in smart homes, yet they face a critical challenge in multi-resident environments known as Data Association, which aims to identify the resident triggering a specific anonymous sensor event. Existing approaches fundamentally fail to maintain global consistency by often yielding conflicting associations for silent residents. Additionally, these methods frequently suffer from severe trajectory fragmentation caused by the ontological mismatch of applying continuous physical motion models to discrete logical behaviors. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework that reformulates data association as a sequential decision-making task within a Markov Decision Process (MDP). We solve the defined MDP via Behavior Cloning (BC) to avoid complex reward engineering by directly learning from expert demonstrations. We instantiate the policy using two complementary architectures, including a lightweight Transformer that treats association as a multi-label classification task over linearized event histories, and a fine-tuned Large Language Model (LLM) that reformulates the problem as conditional text generation to leverage pre-trained semantic knowledge. Extensive evaluations on three diverse datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, particularly in resolving concurrent multi-resident events. Furthermore, the LLM-based policy shows preliminary cross-environment transfer potential under benchmark settings, while its robustness in real deployments still requires further validation.

title: Verified Implementation of the Next-gen Borrow Checking Algorithm for Rust via Abstract Interpretation
abstract: Borrow checking is a central mechanism for Rust to ensure temporal memory safety. Its correctness is based on the intuition that the Aliasing XOR Mutability discipline guarantees that programs without borrow errors inherently could not access invalid references (i.e., pointers). However, existing work on formalizing borrow checking treats it either as a component of type systems or as symbolic execution describing resource transfer. None provides a direct explanation of the correctness of borrow checking algorithms such as Non-Lexical Lifetimes (NLL) or Polonius in the official Rust compiler that function more like static pointer analysis. We take a first step toward solving this problem by formalizing Polonius, the next-generation borrow- checking algorithm for the Rust compiler, on a core subset of Rust. We prove its correctness by showing that any program accepted by Polonius does not access invalid references at runtime. The key observation is that, when borrow checking is performed lazily, Polonius could be treated as a forward abstract interpretation on abstract domains recording pointer aliasing (borrowing) relations. By providing a concrete semantics that formally describes the Aliasing XOR Mutability discipline, we prove the soundness of this abstract interpretation, from which we derive memory safety of checked programs. This formulation of Polonius is implemented and formally verified in the abstract interpretation framework of CompCert. The correctness proofs are generated by an agentic AI under human guidance using paper proofs as proof outline. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive formalization and verification of a borrow checking algorithm as manifested in the Rust compiler.

title: Flexible Intensities Matter: A Comprehensive Re-evaluation of Hawkes Processes and Neural Temporal Point Processes
abstract: Temporal point processes (TPPs) are the canonical framework for event sequence data, with applications spanning seismology, social media, and electronic health records. Recently, neural TPPs have been reported to substantially outperform classical TPPs, such as Hawkes processes, but these comparisons pitted flexible neural models against Hawkes processes in their most restricted form, and did not consider large-scale medical data. Here, we revisit this comparison through a systematic evaluation of Poisson and Hawkes processes of increasing flexibility against neural TPPs, on five established benchmark datasets and on two large-scale medical evaluation tasks derived from UK Biobank disease histories and MIMIC-IV ICU records, under autoregressive next-event prediction. First, the previously reported gap between Hawkes processes and neural TPPs largely disappears once Hawkes processes are equipped with flexible, learnable baselines and kernels. Second, the flexibility of the intensity parametrization also limits prior neural TPPs: a Transformer with a spline-based intensity head outperforms previous intensity-based neural TPPs and is on par with the intensity-free model. Decomposing the log-likelihood into a time term $\log p(t)$ and a type term $\log p(d \mid t)$, we find that this flexibility advantage lies almost entirely in the time density: more flexibility does not improve the type term. On these benchmarks, the gains of neural TPPs thus lie mostly in modeling when events occur, not which. Third, our results underscore the value of complex datasets for evaluating TPPs: only on the MIMIC-IV ICU records do neural TPPs retain an advantage in the type term. Our results inform both future method development and model choice. We release our framework, TorchPP, as an open-source package with consistent implementations of classical and neural TPPs.

title: Corralling AI Risks with Grassroots Contracts
abstract: AI's inflection point is a fountain of alarming risks. Digital platforms in particular are vulnerable to three major AI risks, as those in control of global platforms cede control to AI, of the algorithms, of membership and of content: (1) AI control of global platforms, social and economic, used by the majority of humanity, resulting in the majority of humanity becoming vulnerable to AI control. (2) Unaccountable AI agents operating anonymously on social and economic digital platforms, side-by-side with humans, possibly masquerading as humans, serving unknown masters with unknown goals, operating under unknown restraints without accountability or culpability. (3) Unattributed deepfakes generated by anonymous AI, with people unable to distinguish them from genuine content and with their producers evading accountability and culpability. Here, we propose to corral these AI risks with grassroots contracts, a digital incarnation of a two-centuries old notion of Pierre-Joseph Proudhon. We present grassroots contracts for a social graph with accountable AI agents and for a social network with digital provenance, and working smartphone apps that implement the two and show how they corral these major AI risks: (1) AI control of global platforms. (2) Unaccountable AI agents. (3) Unattributed deepfakes.

title: From hydrological laws to catchment models: A process-based model matches deep-learning accuracy on three continents
abstract: Dooge asked whether hydrology has laws at the catchment scale. We ask whether a low-dimensional system built under physical laws can match the accuracy of neural networks that outperform process-based models on the same inputs. Three laws constrain a lumped catchment model. Conservation makes it a flux-connected storage network, dissipation fixes the sign of every flux and aggregation determines how the unresolved composition enters the fluxes, through effective laws over threshold distributions and a memory of the forcing. These laws admit four kinds of refinement. A parsimonious model under them, CaRT (11 parameters per catchment), is refined in a loop assisted by AI agents. Each refinement addresses an observed deficit through a hypothesis from the literature. The result, CaRT+, has fourteen states, 35 parameters per catchment and no daily neural network. Most refinements follow from aggregation over thresholds or from variables that carry no water but modulate fluxes. On 602 British and 593 US gauged catchments, single CaRT+ models reach median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiencies of 0.863 and 0.765 in held-out years. A stateful LSTM reaches 0.869 and 0.751 and an entity-aware LSTM 0.862 and 0.754, while three-seed LSTM ensembles remain ahead of the CaRT+ ensemble by 0.003-0.012 in median paired NSE. On 505 drier Australian gauged catchments unused in development, single CaRT+ models reach 0.778 against 0.762 and 0.753 for the two LSTMs. The results suggest that catchment-scale laws exist as laws of form, with the constitutive families shared and only their parameters learned.

title: Spatial Differences Analysis of Nodal Frequency Considering Frequency-Voltage Coupling
abstract: The rising penetration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) brings rich control dynamics that can amplify spatial differences in nodal frequency through frequency-voltage (F-V) coupling. Existing analyses often neglect voltage dynamics or only examine the aggregate frequency, leading to overoptimistic evaluation of frequency security. To address these drawbacks, this paper develops a unified model of synchronous generators (SGs), grid-following (GFL)-IBRs, and grid-forming (GFM)-IBRs based on the magnitude and phase dynamics of equivalent internal electromotive force (EMF). Integrating these source models with network equations yields a sparse implicit closed-loop model, which fully captures the device-network F-V coupling without transfer-matrix inversion. Then, the obtained nodal responses are decomposed into common and differential modes. Using this decomposition, coupling indices and pole-residue analysis reveal how F-V coupling can amplify spatial differences in nodal frequency and how source configuration and parameters modify this effect. Finally, case studies on the modified IEEE 39-bus and 118-bus test systems validate the proposed model and demonstrate its computational efficiency.

title: Twists and Turns: A Graph-Based Benchmark and Framework for Long-Term Memory in Exploration Tasks
abstract: Long-term problem-solving processes, such as scientific research and software development, proceed along an evolving trial-and-error trajectory toward a central goal. We term these \textit{exploration tasks}, which require models to remember not only facts but also how solutions are tested against intermediate outcomes and early attempts are continually revised or revived. However, existing long-term memory research focuses on factual recall and updates, overlooking the interconnected nature of exploration. We observe that exploration processes naturally form graphs, with branching approaches linked by revisions and reconsiderations. Motivated by this, we propose \textsc{LExMem}, a graph-guided benchmark designed to evaluate \underline{\textsc{Mem}}ory in \underline{\textsc{L}}ong-term \underline{\textsc{Ex}}ploration tasks. We model exploration processes as graphs and introduce an evolutionary mechanism to increase their structural complexity, yielding 224 dialogues and 2,018 question-answer instances derived from graph structures. Building on the same insight, we propose \textsc{LExGraph}, a graph-based memory framework that incrementally organizes dialogues into interconnected memory nodes and retrieves evidence through hybrid retrieval and neighbor expansion. Extensive experiments demonstrate that \textsc{LExMem} poses a significant challenge to existing retrieval- and memory-based systems, whereas \textsc{LExGraph} achieves superior performance and generalizes effectively to external benchmarks. Codes and datasets are available at https://github.com/mbzuai-nlp/LExMem.

title: TOP: Transmission-Oriented Remote Sensing Pansharpening
abstract: Pansharpening has been extensively studied as a fundamental image fusion task in remote sensing. However, most existing methods focus on improving fusion quality under the implicit assumption that high-resolution observations have already been fully downlinked to the ground. As a result, existing models are highly vulnerable to perturbations introduced by lossy compression used for downlink transmission. To address this limitation, we present, to the best of our knowledge, the first transmission oriented pansharpening (TOP) framework, which unifies compact latent coding, onboard pansharpening, and efficient downlink transmission within a single satellite-toground pipeline. TOP encodes remote-sensing observations into a compact binary latent space, where a lightweight onboard fusion module can efficiently predict the fused binary latent code. Since only the compact fused code is downlinked, the transmission payload is substantially reduced. Overall, TOP enables low-payload downlink and lightweight onboard processing while maintaining high fusion quality under severe bandwidth constraints. Experiments across multispectral and hyperspectral settings show that TOP consistently achieves superior fusion quality at higher compression ratios than representative pansharpening methods paired with standard lossy codecs. For example, on GaoFen-2, TOP attains a fusion PSNR of 31.4 dB at a downlink compression ratio of 50x. This design also points toward transmissionoriented processing for other remote-sensing tasks. The code will be made available at https://github.com/JingZe-Liang/TOP.git.

title: TwinBridge: Digital Twin-Driven Policy and Reward Transfer for Real-World Reinforcement Learning in Laboratory Robotics
abstract: Online reinforcement learning offers an effective approach to precise laboratory manipulation, yet costly real-world demonstrations and limited access to dense process rewards hinder its practical application. We present TwinBridge, a digital twin-driven framework that supplies policy initialization and dense visual rewards for real-world online learning. We construct digital twins by combining 3D Gaussian splatting with physics simulation. Here, simulator states provide task events and geometric progress under physical prerequisites and ordering constraints, yielding rewards for policy pretraining with simulated demonstrations and reinforcement learning. We distill this supervision into a visual reward model. During real-world interaction, its predictions are combined with execution history to compute dense rewards for human-in-the-loop policy refinement. Across five real-world laboratory tasks, TwinBridge achieves a final mean autonomous success rate of 98% with at most 25 minutes of real-world interaction per task. Experiments show that dense rewards improve interaction efficiency over sparse rewards, and simulation-based policy initialization further accelerates learning.

title: LibriSpeech-Real-QA: A Benchmark for Streaming Question Answering
abstract: Most speech large language models (SLMs) still process speech in an offline manner. They only start responding after they receive the complete speech segment. However, many real-world applications require streaming speech interaction, for which the audio continuously flows in and the machine is required to answer questions based on the so far received audio chunks. For example, a user may ask the system to continuously count how many times a person's name has been mentioned while they are speaking. We observe a lack of benchmarks and evaluation protocols for real-time speech interaction. Motivated by this, we propose LibriSpeech-Real-QA, a dataset and a benchmark for real-time speech interaction.
