title: CoRTeC: A Differentially Private Release for Synthetic Tabular Data, Decodable by Any Generator
abstract: The records that could train the most useful models, such as a hospital's patient files, are often the ones an institution cannot share. We propose CoRTeC, a method that releases synthetic versions of such records under differential privacy. Differential privacy places a proven limit on what the synthetic data can reveal about any person, and in particular on membership inference. CoRTeC spends the privacy budget once, on a small file of noisy counts designed for training a classifier. For each group of records, the file gives the group's size, its balance of outcomes, a histogram of every column for each outcome and the outcome rate in each of several non-overlapping cells. A reviewer can check every number before the file leaves the institution. Anyone can then turn the counts into synthetic rows, as often as they like and at no further privacy cost. A maximum-entropy decoder can do this without any language model, and so can each of the five frozen language models we tested. None of them ever sees a real record. A selection step then matches the rows to the released counts. Decoded without a language model, the automatically configured release at $\varepsilon = 2$ trains classifiers to within 0.02 AUC of a real sample of the same size on the Adult dataset, across three data splits. On NHANES and bank marketing, without the selection step, it stays within 0.05 AUC. On Adult, with a fixed cohort rule, the release carries the outcome rates a deployment names more closely than a real sample does, at some cost in accuracy on pairs of columns. Four controls show that most of the utility comes from the release and the selection step, and that a language model adds what it knows from the column names. No private row ever reaches a model, and no row CoRTeC generates copies a real one. The strongest membership attack stays far below the bound the budget allows.

title: Teachers’ self-reported AI literacy across educational levels in Greece: Awareness without conceptual depth?
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) literacy is increasingly recognized as an essential teacher competence, yet evidence concerning its dimensional structure and variation across educational sectors remains limited. This study investigated self-reported AI literacy among 1,173 in-service teachers in primary, secondary, and higher education in Greece, examining its empirical structure, overall levels, and associations with prior AI-related training and teaching level, while accounting for academic qualifications. Data were collected through a researcher-developed questionnaire and analyzed using exploratory factor analysis, descriptive statistics, and general linear models. Two dimensions emerged: Conceptual–Technical AI Literacy and Critical–Ethical AI Literacy, while Practical AI Use was retained as a separate indicator. Overall self-reported AI literacy was relatively low, with substantially higher scores on critical–ethical indicators than on conceptual–technical indicators, suggesting a profile of perceived awareness without corresponding conceptual depth. Prior AI-related training was positively associated with all AI-literacy outcomes across educational sectors. However, significant teaching-level × training interactions revealed particularly strong associations in higher education, especially for Conceptual–Technical AI Literacy. These findings highlight the multidimensional and context-sensitive nature of teachers’ self-reported AI literacy and the importance of distinguishing perceived confidence from demonstrated competence. They underscore the need for differentiated, pedagogically grounded professional development that integrates conceptual understanding, practical AI applications, critical evaluation, and ethical judgment across educational sectors.
journal: International Journal of Research Studies in Education

title: Agricultural Diversification, Nutrition and Health Outcomes in Nigeria
abstract: This study examines long-run and short-run relationships between agricultural diversification, nutrition and health outcomes in Nigeria using annual time-series data covering 1990–2024. Agricultural diversification is represented by a composite index incorporating crop, land-use and agricultural value-added diversity, while nutrition and health outcomes are measured using composite deprivation indices. The study employs the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) unit root test, Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) bounds testing and error-correction modelling. The ARDL bounds tests indicate long-run relationships in nutrition and health models, with F-statistics of 4.933 and 14.327, respectively, exceeding their reported 5% upper critical bounds. The long-run estimates reveal a positive but statistically insignificant association between agricultural diversification and nutrition deprivation (β = 0.116, p = 0.896). Conversely, agricultural diversification exhibits a negative and statistically significant association with health deprivation (β = −1.287, p < 0.001). The short-run relationship with health deprivation is also negative and statistically significant (β = −2.974, p < 0.001). The error-correction coefficients of −0.662 and −1.156 for the nutrition and health models, respectively, indicate adjustment towards long-run equilibrium, with evidence of overshooting in the health model. However, residual serial correlation, borderline functional-form diagnostics and unresolved integration-order concerns necessitate cautious interpretation. The findings provide stronger statistical evidence of an association between agricultural diversification and health deprivation than between diversification and nutrition deprivation within the estimated models. The study recommends integrating agricultural diversification initiatives with policies that improve dietary quality, food accessibility, sanitation, healthcare delivery and household purchasing power to support sustainable improvements in nutritional and population-health outcomes.
journal: African Journal of Agricultural Science and Food Research

title: Design and Implementation of a Secure Online Agriculture Marketplace for Farmers and Buyers (Role Based Access and Security)
abstract: - As agricultural trade in Nigeria increasingly moves onto digital platforms, these systems inherit not only the promise of disintermediating exploitative middlemen but also the cybersecurity exposure that comes with handling the personal data, payments, and multi-role interactions of a large and heterogeneous user base. Prior research has warned that the integration of digital platforms into agriculture introduces new failure modes capable of disrupting food supply chains when security is treated as an afterthought rather than a design principle, yet comparatively few published agricultural marketplace prototypes report concrete security architectures or empirical vulnerability assessments. This paper presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of the role-based access control (RBAC) and security-by-design subsystem of AgriTrade, a secure online agriculture marketplace connecting verified Nigerian farmers with buyers. Three user roles - Buyer, Farmer, and Administrator - are enforced through a centralized authentication service issuing JSON Web Tokens (JWT), with Bcrypt-hashed password storage, mandatory input validation and escaping to prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), token-based protection against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF), and parameterized data access to prevent SQL Injection. The implemented system was subjected to static source-code analysis to identify latent vulnerabilities and to manual denial-of-service (DoS) testing intended to verify that availability-protection mechanisms remained active under attempted disruption. The evaluation confirmed that role-based restrictions were correctly enforced at every tested boundary, including the specific case of an unverified farmer account being denied product-listing privileges, and that the security controls examined performed as designed under the applied tests. These findings demonstrate that a conventional, layered security-by-design approach, rather than an elaborate or costly bespoke security infrastructure, is sufficient to establish a credible security posture for a multi-role agricultural e-commerce platform operating in a resource-constrained development context

title: Consequence and further analysis of the minor role of daylength in the floral initiation of sorghum crops
abstract: • Background and Aims Flowering time is assumed to be primarily controlled by daylength, but field observations disagree. For instance, mid-early sorghum varieties sown at the same time at tropical and temperate latitudes have similar flowering dates. We previously proposed an alternative framework integrating daily changes in sunrise and sunset times (dSR and dSS). • Methods Variety trials of mid-late varieties from the Northern Hemisphere were carried out in Madagascar and in Argentina. Series of monthly sowings of 28 varieties were carried out in Mali between 2000 and 2009. Heading date and, in Mali, panicle initiation (PI) were recorded. • Key Results In Madagascar and in Argentina mid-late varieties headed late or very late when sown in November and December, consistent with the higher dSR/dSS values of the southern hemisphere summer. In Mali, the high interannual variability in PI time in sowings between November and February revealed that up to four photoperiodic responses — two quantitative and two qualitative — may coexist within a single late photoperiod sensitive variety. Additionally, the qualitative responses may be triggered by an internal dSR/dSS phasic coincidence, which is set at the onset of the photoperiod-sensitive phase. These hypotheses were used to design a research model that incorporated only dSR and dSS cues. The model fitted the dataset well when two sets of parameters were calibrated for the first quantitative response, which covered two periods of over and under twelve hours per year. After daylength was added to the first qualitative response, the model also accurately predicted the duration to PI observed in three varieties sown at tropical and temperate latitudes. • Conclusions The flowering time of sorghum crops mainly relies on dSR and dSS cues, while daylength plays a minor role. Two new hypotheses now require confirmation through further evidence, which is likely to come from genetic analyses.

title: Where single-cell foundation models help: a benchmark of annotation, perturbation and regulatory inference against simple baselines
abstract: Single-cell foundation models (FMs) are proposed as general tools for cell-type annotation, in silico perturbation and gene-regulatory-network (GRN) inference. To identify where they add value, we benchmarked five FMs (scGPT, Geneformer V1 and V2, Nicheformer, scFoundation), CellOracle, supervised perturbation models including STATE, and task-matched simple baselines on the same data, from K562 Perturb-seq screens and primary cells to healthy-donor and isogenic leukodystrophy brain organoids, a public organoid CRISPR screen and lung cancer biopsies. FMs were most useful when labels had to be transferred across species: from human to mouse lung, Nicheformer reached 0.98 accuracy and Geneformer V2 and scFoundation about 0.90, against 0.68 for the best baseline. Zero-shot in silico perturbations captured the direction of real responses in K562, with up to 75% of perturbations shifted in the expected direction (scFoundation, p < 1e-8), and Geneformer V2 networks recovered patient-level tumour differential expression better than co-expression (fold enrichment 2.9 versus 2.0). Within a species, FM embeddings annotated cells as accurately as principal components. In organoids, predicted knockout effects were largely explained by where the target is expressed, and an expression-matched control test isolated the gene-specific part, 12 to 35% of the effects. Isogenic Canavan and Krabbe organoids and 4H patient organoids, with one library per line and time point, did not yet separate methods from differences between clones and donors, which defines the replication needed for future validation. Fine-tuning changed classification accuracy but not knockout rankings. We release the benchmark, baselines, pipeline checks and the isogenic reference task as the fmaudit package, so that new models can be evaluated on the tasks where FMs already help. Key Points Five single-cell foundation models, a GRN-based simulator, supervised perturbation models including STATE, and non-foundation baselines were compared on annotation, perturbation and GRN inference across cell lines, isogenic disease organoids, a public organoid CRISPR screen and human tumour biopsies. Foundation models were most useful for transferring cell-type labels across species. From human to mouse, Nicheformer, Geneformer V2 and scFoundation clearly exceeded principal-component and CellTypist baselines, while within a species all methods performed similarly. Zero-shot in silico perturbations captured the direction of real K562 responses for several models, but not their magnitude. In organoids predicted knockout effects largely followed target expression, and an expression-matched control test isolates the gene-specific part. With patient-level ground truth, Geneformer V2 networks recovered tumour differential expression better than co-expression. Isogenic Canavan and Krabbe organoids and 4H patient organoids, with one library per line and time point, could not yet separate methods from differences between clones and donors, which defines the replication needed for future validation. Benchmarks of single-cell foundation models should include task-matched simple baselines, verified sample identities, replicate-level ground truth and negative contrasts. We release these checks, baselines and the isogenic reference task as the fmaudit package.

title: Autonomous generalizability auditing of scientific foundation models
abstract: Determining where scientific foundation models generalize beyond their development data is essential for reliable use, but aggregate benchmarks obscure performance limits and rigorous audits are difficult to conduct routinely. Here, we introduce AutoSPECTRA, a coding-agent protocol for systematic generalizability auditing. To inform its design, we reviewed 38 studies across five biological domains and evaluated coding agents, which generated hypotheses and empirical analyses but applied inconsistent standards for judging evidence. We then structured AutoSPECTRA around measurable generalization axes, prespecified analyses, controlled comparisons and independent confirmation. Across four biological foundation models, audits linked performance to protein sequence composition and relatedness to pretraining data (ESMFold2), representation of perturbations in training (STATE), effective spatial resolution (CONCH), and residue-level genomic, evolutionary and structural context (AlphaMissense). Agents also evaluated alternative explanations and rejected unsupported hypotheses. AutoSPECTRA provides a systematic approach to discovering and testing the limits of scientific foundation models.

title: Cross-cancer knowledge transfer for lymph node metastasis prediction: Applicability of an axillary lymph node-based deep learning model
abstract: Evaluation of lymph node (LN) metastasis is critical for cancer staging and treatment planning. Since radiologic hallmarks of metastatic LNs are shared across primary cancers, a computed tomography (CT)-based deep learning (DL) classifier developed from one anatomy may transfer to others. This study built a DenseNet-121 ensemble model using clinical-implication-applied preprocessing and evaluated its cross-anatomical generalizability to LNs from diverse primary cancers. A DenseNet-121 ensemble model combining fixed-size cropping (FSC) and adjustable square cropping (ASC) was trained from ImageNet initialization on an axillary lymph node (ALN) dataset (n = 1,128 from 523 breast cancer patients). The model utilized clinical-implication-applied perinodal cropping with bicubic filtering and standardized resizing. To test cross-anatomical generalizability, an external dataset of 256 CT images across four anatomical regions was evaluated: cervical, mediastinal, upper-abdominal, and lower-abdominal LNs. Perinodal free margins were systematically varied from 10% to 40% to optimize the balance between context preservation and surround interference. Bicubic filtering and standardized resizing yielded the highest internal performance on the original ALN dataset (FSC-ASC ensemble area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC] 0.958, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.920–0.987 at 40% margin). The model demonstrated site-dependent, above-chance generalizability across all external regions. Cervical LNs achieved the highest performance at a 40% margin (AUROC 0.939, 95% CI 0.875–0.989). Mediastinal LNs peaked at a 10% margin (AUROC 0.796, 95% CI 0.672–0.903), with wider margins degrading performance due to adjacent structural interference. Upper-abdominal and lower-abdominal LNs reached optimal performance at a 30% margin (AUROC 0.814 for upper; AUROC 0.917 for lower). A single ALN-trained DL model can accurately predict LN metastasis across cervical, mediastinal, and abdominal stations through site-specific perinodal margin tuning. These findings support the feasibility of cross-cancer knowledge transfer and the clinical utility of generalizable backbones for pan-cancer nodal assessment.

title: Estimating bone marrow adiposity from head MRI and identifying its genetic architecture.
abstract: Bone marrow (BM) adiposity changes radically through the lifespan, but this phenomenon is poorly characterized and understood in humans. Large datasets of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans of the head have been collected to study the human brain, but also contain unexploited information about other organs. We developed an artificial neural network that localizes calvarial BM in T1-weighted MRI head scans, enabling us to study its composition in several large MRI datasets, and to model sex-dimorphic age trajectories, including the effect of menopause. We revealed high heritability in single-nucleotide polymorphism and twin data, and identified 41 genetic loci significantly associated with the trait, including six sex-specific loci. Integrating mapped genes with existing BM single-cell RNA-sequencing data revealed patterns of adipogenic lineage differentiation and lipid loading. Finally, we identified significant genetic correlations with several human traits, including cognitive ability and Parkinson's disease, which is intriguing in light of the recently discovered channels that link calvarial BM to the meninges.

title: Smart Contracts in Agribusiness: Transforming Transactions, Procurement and Value-Chain Governance
abstract: Smart contracts, understood as computer programs that execute pre-agreed terms when specified conditions are recorded on a shared ledger, are frequently presented as a means of reducing delay, opportunism and intermediation costs in agribusiness. The claim is attractive because agricultural exchange is shaped by seasonal production, perishable and heterogeneous products, weather risk, delayed payment and weak contract enforcement, particularly where smallholders supply larger buyers. This critical narrative review examines how far the available evidence supports the use of smart contracts in three areas of agribusiness: transactions, including payment, settlement, finance and insurance; procurement, including contract farming, public food procurement and certification-linked sourcing; and value-chain governance. Peer-reviewed literature published between 2015 and 2026 was identified through multidisciplinary and discipline-specific scholarly databases, citation chasing and authoritative institutional sources, and was appraised for design, evidential strength and relevance to agricultural contracting. The synthesis indicates that the evidence base is large but shallow. Most studies are design prototypes, test-network deployments, simulation or game-theoretic models and expert-ranking exercises, whereas independent field evaluations, cost data and outcome measures for farmers are scarce. Smart contracts appear most defensible where contractual contingencies are digitally observable, low in ambiguity and settled in digital money, as in automated payment against verified delivery events or index-triggered insurance. They are weakest where value depends on contestable quality judgements, physical delivery, renegotiation after shocks or relational trust, conditions that dominate much of agribusiness. The oracle problem, uncertain legal status, code rigidity, interoperability limits, digital exclusion and the concentration of design authority among lead firms constrain transformative claims. Smart contracts therefore complement, rather than replace, contractual and relational governance, and their distributional effects depend on who writes, controls and audits the code. Priority research needs include field trials with credible comparison groups, transaction-cost accounting, studies of dispute resolution and renegotiation, inclusion-sensitive designs for smallholders and comparative legal analysis. A measured conclusion is that smart contracts can automate well-specified fragments of agribusiness exchange, but the transformation of procurement and value-chain governance remains a hypothesis rather than an established outcome.

title: Medicinal Plant-Derived Biostimulants for Crop Improvement: Phytochemistry, Mechanisms, Agronomic Evidence, and Future Prospects
abstract: Medicinal and aromatic plants represent a phytochemically rich yet underexplored source of botanical biostimulants. Most research and commercial products focus on macroalgal extracts, humic substances, protein hydrolysates, and microbial inoculants; medicinal plant extracts remain comparatively under-validated mechanistically and agronomically. This review examines 37 experimental studies published up to July 2026, covering cereals, legumes, vegetables, and horticultural crops. It explores the phytochemical composition of medicinal plant extracts, their physiological and molecular effects, extraction and formulation technologies, and regulatory challenges. Extracts of Moringa oleifera, Aloe vera, and Glycyrrhiza glabra, containing diverse phenolics, flavonoids, terpenoids, alkaloids, and saponins, have shown potential to improve seed germination, seedling vigour, crop yield, and tolerance to drought, salinity, and heavy-metal stress. Although plant species differ considerably in phytochemical composition, their extracts may produce similar physiological responses in plants. This suggests that chemically distinct extracts can influence growth through common regulatory pathways. These effects may involve reactive oxygen species (ROS) signalling, enhanced antioxidant defence, and direct free radical scavenging by phenolic compounds. However, responses vary among species, and some metabolite-rich medicinal plant extracts show no measurable benefits. Phytochemical variability, non-standardised extraction, formulation instability, and fragmented regulatory frameworks continue to constrain translation into agricultural practice. Future research should prioritise green extraction technologies, nano-enabled delivery systems, multi-omics integration, and predictive modelling to strengthen mechanistic understanding and identify promising candidates. Standardised extraction and multi-location field trials are essential to ensure consistent efficacy and establish medicinal and aromatic plants as a reliable source of biostimulants.
journal: Journal of Advances in Biology & Biotechnology

title: Breaking the Vicious Cycle for Diabetic Wound Healing: A Dynamic-Static Dual-Mode Nanofiber Platform for NETs Degradation, Inflammation Resolution, and Scar Prevention.
abstract: Chronic diabetic wounds are trapped in a self-perpetuating vicious cycle-persistent infection, oxidative stress, and NET-driven inflammation-that severely impairs healing. Here, we engineer a piezoelectric nanofiber membrane (DMTP) that breaks this cycle via a dynamic-static dual-mode strategy. DMTP integrates a Mn-Ti bimetallic MOF with sustained DNase I release, enabling four coordinated functions: (i) piezodynamic ROS generation for on-demand antibacterial action; (ii) an electric field to guide fibroblast migration; (iii) sustained DNase I release to degrade pathological NETs; and (iv) intrinsic POD/SOD enzyme-mimetic activity for continuous ROS scavenging. Mechanistically, we show that NETs drive fibroblast differentiation into α-SMA+ myofibroblasts, a key fibrotic driver, and DMTP effectively suppresses this pro-fibrotic process. In diabetic mice, DMTP achieves 94.32% wound closure with orderly collagen deposition and modulated inflammation (TNF-α↓, TGF-β↑). In a rabbit ear hypertrophic scar model, DMTP significantly reduces scar formation by inhibiting α-SMA expression. This work offers a transformative strategy to achieve diabetic wound healing with diminished scarring by directly dismantling the infection-oxidative stress-NETs-fibrosis axis.

title: Multi‐Location Temporal Forecasting of Near‐Surface Temperature and Relative Humidity Across Diverse Climatic Regions of India Using a Stacked Ensemble Framework
abstract: Accurate short‐term forecasting of near‐surface air temperature and relative humidity is important for climate monitoring, urban planning, energy management, agriculture and other weather‐sensitive socio‐economic activities. However, the strong climatic variability across India presents challenges for developing forecasting frameworks capable of generalising across multiple geographic regions while maintaining predictive accuracy. This study proposes a multi‐location temporal forecasting framework based on a stacked ensemble machine learning approach for predicting near‐surface temperature and relative humidity across multiple Indian cities representing diverse climatic conditions. The proposed forecasting architecture integrates Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and CatBoost as base learners. Predictions generated by these models were combined using Ridge regression as a meta‐learner within a stacked ensemble framework. The framework was implemented within a multi‐output regression structure to enable simultaneous prediction of temperature and relative humidity. Model performance was evaluated using the coefficient of determination ( R 2 ), root mean squared error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) under chronological held‐out testing and time‐series‐aware validation. On the pooled evaluation of 8742 held‐out observations, the stacked ensemble achieved R 2 values of 0.933 for temperature and 0.787 for relative humidity, with MAE values of 0.802°C and 6.320°C percentage points, respectively. Per‐city persistence achieved a comparable temperature R 2 of 0.933 and a lower temperature MAE of 0.783°C, while ARIMA achieved a higher humidity R 2 of 0.797 and a lower humidity MAE of 5.699 percentage points. Five‐fold walk‐forward validation yielded mean R 2 values of 0.935 ± 0.018 for temperature and 0.898 ± 0.024 for humidity. Leave‐one‐city‐out validation assessed performance at unseen locations. Recursive multi‐step forecasting at 6‐, 24‐, 48‐ and 96‐h horizons showed progressive forecast degradation with increasing lead time, particularly beyond 24 h. SHAP‐based interpretability analysis identified lagged temperature as an influential predictor, highlighting the importance of temporal persistence in short‐term meteorological forecasting. Overall, the results show that the stacked ensemble provides useful short‐term predictive skill, while the walk‐forward, persistence, LOCO and multi‐step evaluations place clear limits on claims of temporal and cross‐location generalisation.

title: Agrobiodiversity dynamics in traditional socioecological systems: An agent‐based model approach on the role of kinship systems and variety transmission
abstract: Context : Agrobiodiversity depends on multiple interconnected socioecological processes. The loss of crop diversity represents a critical challenge for global food security and for the resilience and adaptation of small‐scale farming communities to climate change. However, the role of kinship and the transmission of variety in the formation of agrobiodiversity have not been systematically addressed. Objectives : Our objective was to examine how kinship and transmission of varieties influence the dynamics of the diversity of cassava ( Manihot esculenta) in traditional socioecological systems. Methods : We employed an agent‐based model to simulate the vertical diffusion of cassava varieties by considering different postmarital residence norms, variety of transmission rules and two marriage norms (Endogamy and Dual Organization). Results : The model successfully captured the expected loss of diversity over time, while also demonstrating that social norms slow down this process. We further showed that the interaction between postmarital residence rules and variety transmission consistently impacts diversity patterns between groups and clans. Conclusions : By showing how the transmission of varieties' dynamics shapes ecological outcomes, this work underscores the central role of human social institutions in sustaining agrobiodiversity. Moreover, our study highlights the importance of exploring, both ethnographically and theoretically, the complementarities between horizontal and vertical transmission. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

title: Leaf morpho-anatomical traits as bottom-up modulators of plant-arthropod interactions: a meta-analytic synthesis.
abstract: BACKGROUND Morpho-anatomical leaf traits play a central role in the bottom-up modulation of plant-arthropod interactions, influencing herbivore preference, feeding, and overall performance. Yet, inconsistent findings across studies prevent broader generalizations regarding the contribution of these traits to plant resistance. Here, following the PRISMA guidelines, we conducted a systematic and meta-analytic synthesis of nearly nine decades of publications retrieved from the Web of Science and Scopus databases. RESULTS Successive screening steps yielded 123 articles for qualitative evaluation and 43 articles for quantitative synthesis. Taxonomic, experimental, and performance-related variables were extracted, and effect sizes (Hedges' g) were estimated using random-effects models. Meta-analyses indicated that internal anatomical traits, particularly epidermal and palisade tissue thickness, significantly reduce herbivore preference and feeding. Meta-regressions further showed that increased expression of these traits prolongs development and reduces survival. For surface structures such as trichomes, consistent patterns emerged in meta-regressions, revealing reductions in feeding and reproduction. Increased cuticular roughness reduced host plant preference, whereas leaf shape and size exhibited no detectable effects on arthropod performance. CONCLUSION Collectively, these results highlight leaf structural traits as effective physical modulators in trophic interactions. Although current evidence is biased toward external features, the identified relationships point to promising targets for breeding insect-resistant crops, particularly increased tissue thickness and surface roughness. These findings also support ecological pest management strategies that promote plant phenotypes that reduce herbivore performance and thereby lower reliance on chemical control. © 2026 The Author(s). Neural Stem Cell Therapies for Central Nervous System Regeneration: Advances, Challenges, and Integrative Technologies.
abstract: Neural stem cells (NSCs) are promising candidates for central nervous system (CNS) regeneration because they self-renew and differentiate into neural lineages. Advances in genome engineering, extracellular vesicles (EVs), biomaterials, organoids, single-cell technologies, and precision medicine have expanded approaches for characterizing, engineering, delivering, and evaluating NSC-based therapies for neurological disorders. CRISPR/Cas9 and related platforms may enable more precise modification of NSC function, while NSC-derived EVs offer potential cell-free strategies. Engineered hydrogels and three-dimensional scaffolds may improve cell survival, engraftment, migration, and integration. Organoids and single-cell omics provide increasingly detailed models of cellular heterogeneity and lineage specification. However, clinical translation remains limited by immune compatibility, tumorigenic risk, manufacturing standardization, graft survival and integration, and regulatory requirements. Rigorous preclinical validation, standardized manufacturing, appropriately designed clinical trials, long-term safety monitoring, and harmonized regulatory frameworks are required before routine clinical application.

title: Conversational AIs and Mnemonic Distortion
abstract: Conversational AI agents designed to simulate interactions with deceased persons—referred to here as Interactive Personality Constructs of the Dead (IPCDs)—offer a novel and potentially highly valuable way to memorialise the deceased. But IPCDs could also undermine the goal of remembrance. This paper argues that IPCDs put users at risk of mnemonic distortion—an epistemic harm in which generated misrepresentations of the deceased become incorporated into our memory of the deceased, such that some of what subsequently shapes our conception of the deceased person originates in the IPCD rather than the deceased—reshaping or, at worst, replacing our memories of the person we hoped to remember. Such distortions are importantly distinct from imaginative engagement with the deceased or the testimony of others, which may also alter our memories of the deceased. The risk of mnemonic distortion is not inherent to IPCDs but rather contingent on design; the paper concludes by considering how this concern could inform recommendations for the design of IPCDs.

title: Assessing future climate risks to date palm production in Saudi Arabia: scenario-based projections and adaptation priorities from machine learning evidence
Quantifying snowmelt contribution to streamflow using ensemble machine learning and remote sensing
abstract: Snowmelt plays a vital role in sustaining river flows and regulating water resources in mountain ecosystems, particularly under changing climatic conditions. This study aims to quantify the contribution of snowmelt to streamflow by estimating snow cover and snow water equivalent (SWE) in the Greater Caucasus Basin of Azerbaijan. MODIS snow-cover and FLDAS land-surface products were analyzed using Random Forest, with data processed on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform to support computationally efficient and consistent snow-data processing. On the held-out product-derived test data, the RF models reproduced the dominant variability in SCA and SWE, with RMSE values of 16.3 km² and 2.3 kg m⁻², respectively; these metrics represent product-based agreement rather than an independent improvement in absolute accuracy over MODIS or FLDAS. MODIS and FLDAS products indicated peak snow cover in December 2023 (1,310 km²) and maximum SWE in February 2023 (23 kg m⁻²). During 2013–2023, mean March–June net SWE depletion was 20.48 kg m⁻², equivalent to 0.168 kg m⁻² d⁻¹. Model-attributed snowmelt runoff represented 35.70% of total discharge (SMC_total) and 45.11% of rainfall- and snowmelt-associated runoff (SMC_direct), with SMC_total reaching 71.20% in winter. These findings demonstrate pronounced seasonal and interannual variability in snow storage and its model-attributed contribution to streamflow during the common 2013–2023 analysis period. The study demonstrates the value of machine learning for snowpack monitoring and highlights the need for long-term simulations and expanded ground-based networks to improve prediction of peak flow events in mountain basins.

Hydroclimatic trends in Southeastern Türkiye from multi-source earth observation data
abstract: Southeastern Türkiye, located in the upper Tigris–Euphrates basin, is increasingly exposed to hydroclimatic stress under semi-arid conditions. This study integrates multi-source remote sensing and reanalysis datasets, including ERA5-Land, CHIRPS, MODIS NDVI, GRACE MASCON, and JRC Global Surface Water, within a Google Earth Engine–QGIS workflow to assess regional hydroclimatic trends during 2000–2020, with GRACE/GRACE-FO terrestrial water storage evaluated over 2002–2020. Spatial trend analysis was complemented by Mann–Kendall significance testing and Sen’s slope estimation to strengthen statistical interpretation. Results indicate warming, vegetation greening, and declining terrestrial water storage over the study period, based on non-parametric trend analysis of annual aggregated observations. Because hydroclimatic time series may exhibit residual temporal autocorrelation, statistical significance should be interpreted cautiously and primarily as exploratory regional trend evidence rather than definitive inferential proof. The coexistence of vegetation greening and declining terrestrial water storage indicates contrasting regional environmental trends between vegetation dynamics and integrated water storage. However, the present analysis does not directly quantify irrigation withdrawals, groundwater abstraction, or other anthropogenic drivers; therefore, the causes of these contrasting trends cannot be determined from the current datasets alone. These findings should therefore be interpreted as exploratory regional evidence rather than as attribution of specific climatic or anthropogenic drivers. Persistent warming and declining terrestrial water storage highlight the importance of continued monitoring of regional water-resource conditions. These findings provide a reproducible framework for multi-variable regional hydroclimatic trend assessment.

title: Co-application of biochar and poultry manure improves plant water availability and drought tolerance of Ananas comosus in a clayey Ferralsol
abstract: Enhancing soil water availability is critical for improving crop drought resilience in highly weathered tropical soils. This study evaluated the synergistic effects of industrial charcoal fines (a biochar byproduct) and poultry litter on the water status of pineapple (Ananas comosus (L.) Merr.). We compared a process-based, flux-based model (FBM) against the traditional FAO-56 method to provide a mechanistic assessment. A greenhouse experiment was conducted using a completely randomized factorial design with nine treatments (four replications). Treatments consisted of biochar and poultry litter applied alone or in combination at rates of 5% and 10% (v/v). Irrigation was managed via tensiometry. Plant available water and drought stress were modeled by integrating soil hydraulic properties, root distribution, and plant transpiration. Results indicated that the combined application of biochar and poultry litter significantly increased both Total Available Water (TAW) and Readily Available Water (RAW). In contrast, the sole application of biochar was detrimental to plant water availability, reducing RAW by up to 16.5%. Modeling revealed that the modification of soil hydraulic properties, rather than increased root growth, was the primary driver of these improvements. Regarding plant performance, the combined application maximized agronomic traits, yielding increases of up to 417% in aboveground biomass and 464% in water use efficiency (WUE) compared to the control. These gains occurred without significant alterations to root length density, reflecting pineapple’s specific resource allocation strategy under prolonged optimal hydration. Furthermore, RAW calculated via the FBM emerged as a highly sensitive predictor of plant performance, accurately linking the improved soil mesoporosity to extended periods of optimal relative transpiration, relationships that traditional metrics failed to capture. We conclude that co-application with an organic source is a prerequisite for effectively utilizing biochar from industrial charcoal fines, overcoming their physical limitations to mitigate crop drought stress. Ultimately, this management strategy enhances key plant parameters such as aboveground biomass, WUE, and transpiration maintenance. Future research should validate these integrated amendments in long-term field trials to assess their ultimate impacts on fruit yield and the C3-CAM metabolic transition under varying seasonal climates.

title: Multi-stress environmental drivers of archaeological deterioration in Al-Fustat, Historic Cairo: integration of hydrochemistry, remote sensing, and urban analysis
abstract: This study investigates the main environmental factors causing deterioration in Al-Fustat archaeological area in Historic Cairo. A multidisciplinary approach was applied, combining field observations, hydrochemical analysis, remote sensing, and GIS techniques. Water samples were collected and analyzed to evaluate groundwater quality, while land use/land cover (LULC) and land surface temperature (LST) changes between 1996 and 2022 were assessed using Landsat data. LULC mapping was based on historical land-use maps, Google Earth Pro imagery, and field observations, while LST was derived from Landsat data using the USGS Collection 2 Level-2 Surface Temperature product. The results show the formation of waterlogged zones affecting archaeological remains. Hydrochemical analysis in 2026 indicates very high salinity levels, dominated by sodium and chloride, with significant nitrate contamination, which may be associated with anthropogenic sources such as wastewater leakage. Total dissolved solids (TDS) ranged from 22,950 to 82,880 mg/L, while nitrate concentrations reached up to 6100 mg/L in the shallow groundwater samples. Remote sensing analysis reveals an increase of 38.5% in urban land accompanied by a reduction of approximately 80% in green areas during the period from 1996 to 2022. The mean LST (μ) values increased from 32 °C in 1996 to about 38.54 °C in 2022, with a noticeable increase in urban heat island (UHI) intensity. The study identifies groundwater salinity, elevated temperature, and urban activities as important environmental factors associated with archaeological deterioration. These conditions may promote moisture movement and salt crystallization within building materials, potentially accelerating structural damage. The findings highlight the need for improved drainage, regular monitoring of groundwater levels and quality, and the use of conservation materials compatible with saline and damp conditions to protect archaeological remains.

Cornus officinalis-derived exosome-like nanovesicles alleviate osteoporosis by attenuating oxidative stress and improving bone homeostasis.
abstract: Osteoporosis is a prevalent metabolic bone disorder characterized by impaired bone formation, excessive bone resorption, and progressive microarchitectural deterioration. Oxidative stress and its associated mitochondrial dysfunction are important contributors to osteoblast apoptosis and osteoclast activation. Therefore, developing safe strategies that attenuate oxidative stress and restore bone remodeling balance is of great significance. Cornus officinalis is a traditional herbal medicine with antioxidant and bone-protective potential, providing a promising natural source for osteoporosis intervention. In this study, Cornus officinalis-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (CONVs) were isolated and characterized, and their anti-osteoporotic effects were systematically evaluated. In vitro, CONVs were efficiently internalized by MC3T3-E1 and RAW264.7 cells, showed favorable cytocompatibility, promoted osteogenic differentiation and mineralization, and inhibited osteoclast formation. Under oxidative stress conditions, CONVs reduced reactive oxygen species accumulation, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, and attenuated apoptosis in MC3T3-E1 cells. Transcriptomic analysis and molecular validation further suggested that the protective effects of CONVs were associated with restoration of NRF2/HO-1-related antioxidant signaling. In an ovariectomized rat model, oral administration of CONVs improved bone mineral density, trabecular microarchitecture, biomechanical strength, and bone remodeling balance, while showing favorable biosafety. These findings suggest that CONVs may serve as natural nanovesicle-based biomaterials for osteoporosis intervention.

title: FGFR1-driven brachyury promotes endothelial-like differentiation of glioblastoma stem cells via SOX2/ZEB1/YAP1 signaling pathways.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by intensive vascular proliferation that is essential for tumor growth. Recent studies indicate the existence of tumor-derived endothelial-like cells can arise from the differentiation of GBM stem cells (GSCs). The transcription factor brachyury plays a critical role in promoting stem cell identity and vasculogenesis during normal embryonic development. However, its involvement in endothelial-like differentiation of GSCs remains unknown. By integrating clinical bioinformatics from GBM databases with preclinical in vitro and in vivo models, including patient-derived GSC cell lines and xenografts, we found that brachyury is highly expressed in GBM tissues and correlates with angiogenesis genes. Our study demonstrated that brachyury is activated by fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 (FGFR1), which subsequently promotes GSC differentiation into endothelial-like cells via SOX2/ZEB1/YAP1 signaling. GSCs with high brachyury expression display great sensitivity to selective FGFR inhibitors in vascular tube formation assays. In vivo pharmacological targeting of FGFR1 with inhibitor E7090 or brachyury gene editing using Cas9/gRNA suppresses GBM neovascularization and tumor growth. Furthermore, gene signature analysis of GBM patients further demonstrated that a lower FGFR1/brachyury/SOX2/ZEB1/YAP1 signature score significantly correlates with favorable overall survival outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of FGFR1-driven brachyury activation in GSC-derived neovascularization and suggest that targeting the FGFR1-directed brachyury/SOX2/ZEB1/YAP1 signaling represents a promising therapeutic strategy for GBM.

title: Driving effects of landscape patterns on land desertification in the agro-pastoral ecotone of northern China.
abstract: The agro-pastoral ecotone of northern China is an ecologically fragile zone sensitive to global change, and a typical region for studying the coupling between landscape patterns and ecological processes. Existing studies have explored the spatiotemporal patterns of landscape and desertification in this region, but the spatiotemporal variations in the strength and direction of their associations remain unclear. In particular, whether the same landscape index can exhibit opposite associations under different spatial and temporal contexts has received limited attention. To address these limitations, this study integrated multi-source datasets, including Moderate-resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) and land cover data, to investigate the spatiotemporal characteristics of landscape patterns and land desertification in the agro-pastoral ecotone of northern China from 2000 to 2020. Land desertification was identified using a C5.0 decision tree based on MSAVI, Albedo, and BSI as remote sensing proxies of vegetation and surface conditions rather than direct measurements of soil degradation. A geographically and temporally weighted regression (GTWR) model was further employed to quantify their spatiotemporal associations and reveal the heterogeneous relationships between landscape patterns and land desertification. The results showed that: (1) landscape patterns exhibited pronounced spatiotemporal changes during 2000-2020, characterized by increased grassland aggregation, pronounced changes in cropland fragmentation, an increase in the total number of patches, and enhanced connectivity and heterogeneity; (2) land desertification was alleviated overall, with the area of non-desertified land increasing by 79.3% relative to 2000, showing a pattern of "overall improvement with local fluctuations"; (3) except for AI_gl, all other landscape pattern indices exhibited statistically supported positive and negative local associations with land desertification across different spatiotemporal units. The GTWR coefficient ranges varied substantially among landscape pattern indices, with PLAND_cl exhibiting the widest coefficient range, from -0.643 to 0.492, revealing pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity in the relationships between landscape patterns and desertification. GTWR outperformed OLS and GWR (R2 = 0.657), while coefficient sign agreement across spatial scales ranged from 77.9% to 83.8%, indicating some scale sensitivity in local estimates. This study clarifies the spatiotemporal differentiation patterns and heterogeneous associations between landscape patterns and desertification in the agro-pastoral ecotone, provides new empirical evidence for understanding pattern-process interactions in ecotonal regions, and supports differentiated desertification control and adaptive ecosystem management according to local environmental conditions.

title: An empirical study of self-admitted technical debt in AI agents
Reelin-enhanced neural stem cell therapy promotes neuroangiogenesis, remyelination, and functional recovery after subcortical capsular ischemic stroke.
abstract: AIMS This study established a reproducible mouse model of posterior limb of the internal capsule (PLIC) ischemia to investigate whether Reelin potentiates neural stem cell (NSC)-mediated functional and structural recovery, addressing the limited regenerative strategies for subcortical stroke. MATERIALS AND METHODS A deep photothrombotic PLIC stroke model was induced in mice using a fiber-optic laser system. Embryonic NSCs were isolated from E14 embryos and characterized by flow cytometry, showing >85% Nestin positivity. Reelin effects on NSC viability were evaluated by MTT assay. Seven days after stroke, mice received intracortical PBS, NSCs, Reelin, or NSCs plus Reelin. Recovery was assessed by modified Neurological Severity Score. Histological, immunofluorescence, immunohistochemical, ELISA, flow cytometric, and ultrastructural analyses examined inflammation, endogenous and grafted NSC responses, neurogenesis, angiogenesis, axonal repair, myelin preservation, and diaschisis. KEY FINDINGS The optimized model produced consistent focal PLIC infarcts with marked motor deficits. Reelin increased NSC viability in vitro in a dose-dependent manner up to 200 nM. In vivo, combined NSC + Reelin treatment reduced TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, while increasing IL-10 and TGF-β. It also promoted M2 microglial polarization, enhanced proliferation and neuronal differentiation of endogenous and transplanted NSCs, increased GAP-43-positive axonal regeneration and vWF-positive angiogenesis, preserved myelin integrity, and attenuated retrograde degeneration/diaschisis. These effects were accompanied by increased internal capsule volume and improved neurological function, together with histological and ultrastructural evidence of enhanced axonal integrity and myelin preservation. SIGNIFICANCE The combined strategy promotes recovery by coordinating neuroinflammatory resolution, extracellular matrix remodeling, neurogenesis, angiogenesis, axonal regeneration, and remyelination. These findings support Reelin-assisted NSC therapy as a promising combinatorial regenerative approach for subcortical ischemic stroke.

title: A haplotype-resolved lychee pangenome uncovers structural and haplotype variations associated with flowering time divergence and fruit sugar composition.
abstract: Lychee is a representative tropical-subtropical fruit species of southern China and is widely appreciated for its unique and characteristic flavor. Pangenome provides a powerful framework for capturing genetic variation and elucidating the genomic basis of phenotypic diversity in economically important crops. Here, we polished the lychee reference genome by reassembling with advanced sequencing technologies and manually curating gene models with transcriptomic support. We confirmed the hybrid origin of the elite lychee cultivar 'Feizixiao', and found that recombination has contributed to its superior fruit quality and robust environmental adaptability. We also generated haplotype-resolved genomes for 12 representative lychee accessions and constructed the first lychee pangenome, revealing extensive structural variations (SVs) and widespread gene copy number variations across the species that affect a substantial proportion of genes. Leveraging the pangenome together with resequencing data from 314 lychee accessions, we uncovered genomic variants underlying key agronomic traits in lychee. A ∼10 kb structural variant located in the promoter region of LcFT3 that affects transcriptional regulation of the CO-NF complex, providing a mechanistic explanation for flowering time divergence within the population. In addition, SVs at the LcSAI locus, like SNPs, are significantly associated with fruit sugar content. We characterized both coding and cis-regulatory variants of LcSAI, revealing their combined effects on allelic enzyme activity and gene expression that together shape fruit sugar composition. Collectively, this study establishes a comprehensive genomic resource for lychee and demonstrates that structural and haplotype-level variations captured by a pangenome underlie key developmental and metabolic traits in perennial fruit crops.

Whole-tumor dual-layer spectral detector CT quantification for preoperative identification of poorly differentiated cervical squamous cell carcinoma: An interpretable prediction model.
abstract: OBJECTIVES To develop an interpretable dual-layer spectral detector CT (DLCT) model for preoperative identification of poorly differentiated cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC), and to compare two-dimensional region-of-interest (2D ROI) with whole-tumor three-dimensional volume-of-interest (3D VOI) parameter-extraction strategies. METHODS This retrospective study included 205 surgically treated patients with CSCC who underwent contrast-enhanced DLCT before surgery. Patients were assigned to training (n = 113), internal validation (n = 47), and temporal validation (n = 45) cohorts. Parameters were extracted using 2D ROI- and 3D VOI-based analyses. Clinical, 2D DLCT, 3D DLCT, and DLCT-clinical fusion models were developed using multivariable logistic regression and evaluated by discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS 3D VOI-based analysis showed higher interobserver reproducibility than 2D ROI-based analysis (mean intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.950 vs. 0.875; P < 0.001). The 3D DLCT model included arterial-phase 70-keV virtual monoenergetic attenuation (CT70keV-AP), arterial-phase normalized effective atomic number (NZeffAP), and venous-phase normalized iodine density (NIDVP). Its areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.897, 0.895, and 0.885 in the training, internal validation, and temporal validation cohorts, respectively. The 2D DLCT and 3D DLCT models did not differ significantly in AUCs after multiple-comparison correction. The fusion model achieved AUCs of 0.900, 0.916, and 0.881, respectively, outperforming the clinical model without significantly improving on the 3D DLCT model. CONCLUSIONS 3D DLCT quantification provides an interpretable and noninvasive imaging biomarker for preoperative identification of poorly differentiated CSCC and may support individualized risk stratification. External validation in larger multicenter cohorts is needed to confirm generalizability.

title: LSTM and DeepONet Surrogate Models for Particle Trajectory and Bed Segregation Prediction in Magnetically Fluidized Beds
abstract: Particle-resolved prediction in magnetically fluidized beds (MFBs) is needed to link local particle motion with bed-scale segregation, yet repeated CFD-DEM simulations remain computationally expensive. This study develops and benchmarks two complementary deep-learning surrogates for Lagrangian trajectory prediction in a magnetic-last MFB: a particle-wise long short-term memory (LSTM) network and a deep operator network (DeepONet). Both models are trained on a common CFD-DEM data set of 9240 binary particles under a magnetic-field gradient increasing from 0 to 0.30 T m–1. The source code developed in this study is openly available to facilitate reproducibility and future research. In particle-wise forecasting, both architectures achieve R2 > 0.99 and recover the segregation-index evolution from predicted positions; DeepONet yields narrower ensemble error bounds, whereas LSTM incurs lower training cost. A shared DeepONet further generalizes across particle identities (R2 = 0.9991, 0.9984, and 0.9975 in X, Y, and Z) while preserving principal collective structures. Applied without retraining to an unseen inlet gas velocity, the DeepONet retains an R2 above 0.99 in all three directions (pooled R2 of 0.998) and the LSTM retains a pooled R2 of 0.991, and trained-surrogate inference reproduces the full 14 s trajectory of all particles roughly an order of magnitude faster in wall-clock time than the reference CFD-DEM simulation while using eight times fewer cores. The results establish complementary sequence- and operator-learning routes for accelerated analysis of MFB dynamics with demonstrated transfer to an unseen operating condition.

title: Analog Rules, Digital Reality: Implementing Rules as Code for Pesticide and Crop Biotechnology Safety Assessments
abstract: Agricultural and digital innovations are advancing rapidly, creating new opportunities to explore how regulatory review processes can become more efficient, transparent, and scalable while maintaining rigorous oversight. This perspective introduces Rules-as-Code (RaC), the practice of translating regulatory requirements into machine-executable logic as a mechanism to realize this transition. Two case studies illustrate how RaC can support automated compliance checks in pesticide and crop biotechnology risk assessments. By providing a standardized digital representation of regulatory requirements, RaC offers a framework to enhance consistency, efficiency, and regulatory preparedness in an increasingly data-rich scientific landscape.
journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

title: Specialized SWOT SSH Data Assimilation Improves the Representation of Multiscale Variability in the Ocean Model
abstract: The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission provides wide‐swath sea surface height (SSH) observations at scales poorly sampled by conventional altimetry. Assimilating SWOT data remains challenging because part of the short‐wavelength variance may not be dynamically representable by a given model configuration. We therefore develop a two‐step multiscale 4DVAR framework to assimilate real SWOT SSH observations. The first step constrains broad‐scale SSH mismatches, whereas the second assimilates the remaining SWOT information using a shorter decorrelation scale and the first‐step analysis as background. In the northern South China Sea, the multiscale framework reduces SWOT SSH residuals, yields more organized scale‐dependent increments, and improves the representation and forecast persistence of model‐resolved multiscale SSH variability. Independent SST, Argo, and drifter observations further indicate reduced upper‐ocean thermal biases, mainly within the mixed layer. These results demonstrate that scale‐dependent assimilation can make more effective use of SWOT's multiscale information within a finite‐resolution regional model.

title: Spatial spillovers and causal configurations of the digital economy driving green manufacturing transformation in China
abstract: The digital economy has emerged as a critical engine for high-quality economic development, yet its specific mechanisms and configurational pathways in empowering green manufacturing transformation remain under-explored. Based on panel data from 31 provinces in China (2012–2023), this study constructs a dual-methodological framework integrating the Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution, transmission mechanisms, and causal recipes of this relationship. The empirical results reveal four key findings. First, green manufacturing transformation exhibits a steady upward trend but follows a distinct “East-High, West-Low” spatial gradient. Second, the digital economy exerts a significant positive impact on local green transformation and generates positive spatial spillovers to neighboring regions, though the spillover effect is weaker than the direct effect due to administrative barriers; technological innovation and environmental regulation are identified as two pivotal transmission channels. Third, a “Northeast Paradox” is observed: while the digital economy promotes green growth in most regions, it shows a significant negative interaction effect in the Northeast, attributed to the “lock-in effect” of rigid industrial structures. Fourth, fsQCA identifies four sufficient pathways leading to high green efficiency: “Digital-Talent Driven,” “Digital-Innovation Driven”, “Internal-Capability Driven”, and “Comprehensive Synergy”. Notably, a substitution effect exists between talent support and R&D intensity, offering flexible transformation strategies for resource-constrained regions. By moving beyond linear effect analysis, this study provides a multidimensional analytical roadmap to support the design of differentiated, context-sensitive green transformation policies.

title: Personality expression and perception in large language models and humans
abstract: Growing numbers of people frequently turn to Large Language Models (LLMs) for concerns from various areas of life. Because its content has become ubiquitous, examining user perceptions of LLM-produced text and its distinguishability from human writing is crucial. This study investigated how seven LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-3.5, Llama 3, Gemma, Gemini, Phi-3, Orca-2) describe themselves when compared to humans. LLM-generated outputs and human responses were collected using psychological questionnaires (Big Five, self-esteem, narcissism) and tailored prompts to elicit short self-descriptive texts. Six LLM and ten human judges then evaluated personality traits and text origin based on these self-descriptions (140 total, half LLM-generated). Results show that current LLM outputs can convey personality-consistent cues in questionnaires and texts. The perception of such significantly differed from that of humans. Both LLM and human judges accurately inferred personality from short self-descriptions and correctly differentiated between LLM-generated and human text. Linguistic analysis and participant feedback revealed textual cues distinguishing LLM-produced from human language and offered insights into how LLM versus human judgment and decisionmaking differ.

A Model Coupled with Fractional-Derivative and Peridynamic Theory for Water Migration in Unsaturated Expansive Clay
abstract: Expansive clay exhibits multiple fissures and undergoes deterioration due to fluctuations in moisture levels. To guarantee the stability of earth structures built on expansive clay in semiarid regions, significant emphasis has been placed on studying the effects of water migration. This paper introduces an innovative method that utilizes a nonlocal model and peridynamic theory as substitutes for the temporal and spatial derivative terms. Based on spatial integration, the peridynamic formulation effectively captures the path dependency of water transport in unsaturated expansive clay, enabling an accurate representation of the diffusion process. Furthermore, the use of a fractional derivative accurately characterizes subdiffusion phenomena arising from the fractal nature of heterogeneous media. The accuracy of the model was further confirmed by analyzing the measured data collected from migration experiments conducted in a closed system, where different temperatures and water potential gradients were applied. The findings indicate that the proposed model effectively captures the process of water migration in unsaturated clay, offering valuable insights into understanding the patterns governing water movement in expansive clay under unsaturated conditions.

title: Melatonin ameliorates renal fibrosis by disrupting the DANCR/QK-mediated stabilization of MALAT1 and inhibiting Galectin-3-dependent macrophage polarization.
abstract: BACKGROUND Renal fibrosis drives kidney dysfunction in chronic kidney disease via inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibroblast activation. Deciphering its mechanisms is vital for antifibrotic therapy. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS A mouse model of renal fibrosis was established via unilateral ureteral obstruction, with melatonin treatment administered. Exosomes from human kidney 2 (HK-2) cells were characterized and co-cultured with phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-induced M0 macrophages. Macrophage polarization was analyzed via flow cytometry. Gene‑interaction studies were performed, including ribonucleic acid (RNA) immunoprecipitation, pull-down, and luciferase reporter assays. RESULTS Melatonin treatment decreased metastasis-associated lung adenocarcinoma transcript 1 (MALAT1) expression in TGF‑β1‑treated HK‑2 cells, alleviated collagen deposition, and improved renal function in vivo. Mechanistically, melatonin disrupted the interaction between differentiation antagonizing non-protein coding RNA (DANCR) and the RNA‑binding protein quaking (QK), thereby destabilizing MALAT1 to downregulate Galectin‑3, which in turn inhibited both M1/M2 macrophage polarization. HK‑2‑derived exosomal MALAT1 was transferred to macrophages, promoting polarization, and administration of MALAT1‑overexpressing exosomes abolished melatonin's protective effects in vivo. CONCLUSION Melatonin destabilizes MALAT1 by suppressing DANCR-associated QK, thereby reducing Galectin-3 to restrain macrophage polarization and mitigate renal fibrosis. Several limitations exist: a single acute animal model, lack of macrophage-specific MALAT1 knockout mice, and absence of clinical validation.

title: Transfer of tropane alkaloids from maize silage contaminated with Datura stramonium to milk of dairy cows.
abstract: Datura stramonium, a poisonous plant producing toxic tropane alkaloids (L-hyoscyamine and scopolamine), is increasingly spreading on agricultural crop land used for feed production. To examine the transfer of tropane alkaloids (TAs) from feed to milk, four high yielding dairy cows received a total mixed ration containing maize silage naturally contaminated with Datura stramonium for ten days with a daily mean TA dosage of 0.12 mg/kg body weight. TA content of individual cow composite milk was measured at each milking using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. L-hyoscyamine was detected in milk with a mean of 0.90 µg/kg, corresponding to a steady-state transfer rate of 0.039% ±0.007%. D-hyoscyamine was detected in neither silage nor in milk, indicating no evidence for natural racemisation. Scopolamine remained below the limit of detection in milk. Health parameters of the experimental cows were monitored by clinical investigation and using a digital sensor system monitoring rumination. No clinical signs of intoxication were observed. Feed naturally contaminated with Datura stramonium can lead to TA occurrence in milk, which may contribute to consumer exposure. In the contaminated maize silage, Datura seeds and remaining plant parts were analysed separately to determine their contribution to total TA content. Total TAs in maize silage originated mainly from the Datura plant parts. Therefore, maximum levels based on the total TA content of animal feed instead of Datura seed weight may be more appropriate to protect animal and human health alike.
