title: Prediction of Global Mesoscale Eddy Trajectories Using a Temporal Convolutional Network
abstract: Mesoscale eddies are ubiquitous throughout the global ocean, and their propagation and evolution exert important influences on oceanic energy transport and salt exchange. Accurate prediction of short-term mesoscale eddy propagation is therefore crucial for advancing understanding of mesoscale dynamics and improving marine forecasting skill. To address the limited ability of traditional statistical approaches to represent complex nonlinear propagation, a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) is developed for future eddy position prediction. The results show that the TCN, when constrained by multi-source background information including surface winds, sea surface currents and bathymetry, can effectively capture the nonlinear short-term propagation behavior of mesoscale eddies. For 7-day lead time prediction on a global scale, the model yields a median distance error of 19.85 km, outperforming widely used baselines including LSTM, MLP and maximum likelihood estimation. However, discrepancies remain under low-latitude, strong background-flow, and high-speed propagation conditions, suggesting that stronger physical constraints should be incorporated in future work to improve generalization and physical consistency.

title: MAPPING RICE CROPS IN CLOUD-COVERED MOUNTAINOUS AREAS USING SENTINEL-1 RADAR AND RANDOM FOREST ALGORITHM: A CASE STUDY IN LAO CAI, VIETNAM
abstract: Rice mapping in mountainous regions remains challenging because persistent monsoon cloud cover severely limits the availability of optical satellite imagery. In Lao Cai Province, northwestern Vietnam, rice monitoring is further complicated by steep terrain, fragmented agricultural fields, and heterogeneous cultivation systems dominated by smallholder terraced rice. This study developed a Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar time-series framework within the Google Earth Engine platform to identify the most effective variables for operational rice mapping under cloudprone and topographically complex conditions. A total of 22 candidate variables, including temporal backscatter features, phenology-based growth indicators, polarimetric indices, and topographic variables, were evaluated using a Random Forest classifier trained with 1,639 reference samples. The classification achieved an Overall Accuracy of 91.4% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.83. The estimated rice area was 30,752 ha, corresponding to a relative error of 6.8% compared with official agricultural statistics. Notably, temporal Vertical-Horizontal (VH) backscatter dynamics during the tillering and harvest stages provided the strongest discriminative capability for rice detection, substantially outperforming conventional polarimetric indices. Furthermore, temporal Synthetic Aperture Radar phenology is highly effective for detecting fragmented rice fields in mountainous environments where optical remote sensing is frequently obstructed by clouds.

title: Visual search as a cognitive marker to discriminate progressive supranuclear palsy from Parkinson’s disease
abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy is a high priority for both patients and clinicians. Nearly half of individuals with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy are initially given an alternative diagnosis—most commonly Parkinson’s disease—and the correct diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy is delayed by an average of three years compared with Parkinson’s disease. Problems with cognition arise early in the progression of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, including profoundly disturbed visual search. This search deficit is likely caused by a combination of oculomotor, visuospatial, attentional and executive dysfunction, which is not observed in Parkinson’s. Since assessment of visual search is not routinely included in clinical testing for Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, it may represent a promising method for differentiating these movement disorders. However, few studies have systematically compared visual search in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy and Parkinson’s disease, so the extent to which search deficits can reliably differentiate the two diseases is unknown. To address this issue, patients with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (N = 28), Parkinson’s disease (N=28) and age matched controls (N=27) completed four tests of visuospatial attention: an easy feature search task, a difficult feature search task, a conjunction search task and a paper-and-pencil cancellation task (the Bells test). We measured perceptual sensitivity (d prime), search time and detection accuracy. Search efficiency in the Bells test was also modelled using Quality of Search score. In addition, patients completed tests of oculomotor system integrity, the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and the National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire 25. As predicted, Progressive Supranuclear Palsy was associated with a profound search deficit: search was slow and highly disorganised on all tests. Furthermore, reflexive orienting along the vertical axis was impaired on the easy feature search. Critically, Receiver Operator Characteristic analyses revealed that the Quality of Search score derived from the Bells test classified Progressive Supranuclear Palsy with a sensitivity of 82%, a specificity of 96%, and Area under the Curve of .90. Given the Bells test is fast to administer (∼5 mins), free, relatively simple to score and already widely used in neuropsychology assessment, it has the potential to be a highly effective addition to the battery of tests used in the differential diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy

title: Evolving view on phylogenetic networks
abstract: Reticulate processes such as hybridization, introgression, and horizontal gene transfer cannot be fully represented by a bifurcating tree. Enter phylogenetic networks: first as split graphs to visualize tree discordance, then as explicit probabilistic models that capture biological phenomena. Here, we describe the broad taxonomy of network representations, distinguishing the principal classes of explicit networks, their biological interpretability and our ability to accurately estimate them from empirical data. We also trace the evolution of the main network inferential methods from hybrid detection tests, distance- and subgraph-based amalgamation methods, probabilistic approaches under the multispecies network coalescent, composite-likelihood and divide-and-conquer frameworks, while highlighting the selective pressures of statistical identifiability and computational scalability that have shaped this evolution. As we move towards a network thinking paradigm, previously isolated methodological lineages from population genetics, phylogenomics, and mathematical network theory are now introgressing, uniting diverse network models into a shared framework that can integrate sequence- and species-level reticulate processes, increase robustness to systematic errors, and refine algorithms for genome-scale data, expanding the tree of life into a richer, more entangled yet clearer picture of evolution.

title: Cooperation and privacy-protection strategies for cross platform targeted advertising in competitive markets
abstract: In practice, platform partnerships may be unstable, and privacy protection strategies may vary across platforms. This study examines optimal cooperation and privacy protection strategies for third-party platforms implementing cross-platform targeted advertising in competitive markets. We develop a game-theoretic model involving two competing third-party platforms, one e-commerce platform, consumers, and advertisers. Equilibrium outcomes are derived using backward induction. The model captures platforms' decisions regarding cross-platform cooperation and privacy protection strategies. In cross-platform targeted advertising, cross-platform cooperation does not necessarily confer a competitive advantage on cooperating third-party platforms. Both symmetric and asymmetric cooperation can arise in equilibrium, depending on competition in the consumer and advertiser markets. Privacy protection does not necessarily increase platform profits, and its effects depend on the relative strength of competition along the content and privacy protection dimensions. Third-party platforms do not always choose high levels of privacy protection. Their choices depend on consumer privacy concerns and rivals' strategies, while asymmetric protection can provide a basis for differentiation. This study examines competing third-party platforms' decisions on cooperation with an e-commerce platform and privacy protection in cross-platform targeted advertising. It extends platform coopetition research by explaining how vertical data cooperation reshapes horizontal competition and advances privacy strategy research by examining the relative strength of competition along the content and privacy protection dimensions. The findings help third-party platforms assess when cooperation increases profits and which privacy protection strategy is preferable.
journal: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics

title: Spatial and vertical price transmission in potato markets in India
abstract: This paper has examined the dynamics of price transmission and co-movement across geographically dispersed markets and in the wholesale–retail supply chains for a perishable crop (potato) in eight major Indian cities, evaluating the interconnection among the wholesale and retail prices and market arrivals of the crop. It has applied various unit-root tests, a standard vector autoregressive model, the Granger causality test and a correlation method to monthly potato prices and market arrivals data from January 2010 to December 2022. It has offered evidence for spatial and vertical integration of potato markets. The wholesale prices were transmitted across the cities involved in potato trading. The prices were transmitted between wholesale and retail markets in most cases. While market arrivals have influenced the prices and marketing margins, these factors in turn have some effects on market arrivals in some cities. There exists evidence of significant co-movement of prices in the spatial and vertical markets. In the markets with significant cross-market price transmission, the effects and incentives of any policy are likely to be transmitted to all the markets without requiring much intervention. The policies to reduce price variability and enhance market integration should focus on facilitating trade, improving infrastructure and reducing restrictions on the movement of the commodity across markets. It has applied an alternative methodology to long-range monthly data for a set of objectively selected potato markets representing different locations and market characteristics throughout the country, and conducted market integration analysis, taking into account the effects of market arrivals on the prices.
journal: Journal of Agribusiness in Developing and Emerging Economies

title: Strategic integration of business intelligence tools to enhance business management efficiency
abstract: This study examines how data and business intelligence (BI) systems support procurement decisions and strategic execution. It aims to improve the efficiency of business management. A five-stage implementation framework is proposed for integrating BI into strategic business execution. The methodology includes technical validation and a case study that assesses the impact of digital transformation and BI adoption on tracking strategic execution and key performance indicators (KPIs). We frame BI adoption within the broader digital transformation (DT) agenda, aligning data, processes and governance to strategic objectives. Research shows that aligning digital transformation initiatives with an organization’s specific operational needs is the most cost-effective path to achieving efficiency. Analysis suggests that a successful digital transformation must be closely linked to the management requirements. Selecting appropriate BI tools is critical to delivering substantial business value. The proposed framework offers managers a structured approach to implementing BI systems aligned with strategic goals. The case study provides actionable insights for professionals aiming to improve operational and management performance through data-driven strategies and digital transformation. The research contributes to the literature on digital transformation by presenting a structured, stage-gated framework for integrating BI tools into strategic management. It offers practical guidance for organizations seeking to enhance performance through data-informed decision-making, differentiating itself through a detailed implementation model developed and illustrated in a procurement context.

title: Islamic corporate social responsibility as a governance-embedded system: evidence from Islamic banks in Malaysia and Indonesia
abstract: Although there has been a rapid rate of expansion observed in the domain of Islamic banking, there remains an inconsistent degree of institutionalisation of Islamic corporate social responsibility (ICSR). The reason is that a higher priority level has been placed on contractual and financial compliance by existing CSR and Shariah governance models, rather than broader socio-economic aspects. The purpose of this study was to develop an ICSR framework to assess the capacity of existing Islamic banking institutions to institutionalise ICSR through relevant governance mechanisms and Islamic social finance instruments, while examining their relationships with socio-economic outcomes. In this investigation, a qualitative multiple-case study design, which involved both Maybank Islamic (Malaysia) and Bank Syariah Indonesia (Indonesia), was employed. Specifically, semi-structured interviews were conducted with a total of 20 purposively selected senior informants, with 10 from each of the two institutions, who were directly involved in the process of ICSR governance and implementation. The interviews, which ranged between 60 and 120 min, were triangulated with corresponding institutional and sustainability documents. After collecting the data, a thematic content analysis was performed through the NVivo software, which incorporated iterative coding, intercoder verification, participant validation and cross-case comparison to identify relevant patterns of ICSR institutionalisation and socio-economic value creation. The findings revealed a clear hierarchy of ICSR institutionalisation, wherein zakat represented the most formally embedded instrument, supported by Shariah oversight, structured procedures, auditing and reporting. Meanwhile, voluntary instruments, including sadaqah and infaq, and developmental instruments, such as qard al-hasan and waqf, exhibited weaker and more fragmented degrees of organisational integration. Four differentiated socio-economic outcome clusters were associated with the above instruments, namely, immediate relief and redistribution (zakat), community trust and relational legitimacy (sadaqah or infaq), economic empowerment (qard al-hasan) and long-term or intergenerational welfare (waqf). Importantly, the interview results demonstrated an institutionalisation–impact paradox, in which instruments associated with greater long-term developmental potential were not equivalent to those most strongly embedded within existing structures of governance. A policy-relevant framework was provided for existing Islamic banking institutions, regulators and Shariah boards to strengthen the governance, coordination, measurement and reporting aspects of relevant ICSR instruments that were often under-institutionalised. The proposed framework could also inform the development of Shariah-specific social responsibility indicators that were aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which could enable more substantive and comparable assessment of ICSR beyond conventional CSR reporting processes. Islamic ethical underpinnings, Shariah governance structures, Islamic social finance tools and various socio-economic outcomes were incorporated in this study into a consolidated and empirically grounded framework. Particularly, it was demonstrated that there were varying levels of institutionalisation and socio-economic value observed in existing ICSR instruments, which highlighted the existence of an institutionalisation–impact paradox. As such, there was a deeper understanding of how Islamic obligations are converted from religious teachings into actual organisational practice and developmental value.

title: What does green mean? Modelling herbivore foodscapes and resource tracking in forested environments.
abstract: The forage maturation hypothesis predicts that herbivores should select plants at intermediate growth stages because they strike a balance between biomass and nutritional quality. Methods for identifying this key stage of plant phenology commonly rely on satellite-based greenness indices and their derivatives. By combining such indices with fine-scale movement data, ecologists have uncovered many novel behaviours and life-history strategies, including 'green-wave surfing' by herbivores. Yet, few studies have evaluated the degree to which greenness indices accurately reflect variation in forage characteristics or their selection by herbivores in forested habitats. We studied relationships among remotely sensed greenness indices, on-the-ground measures of forage biomass and quality and resource selection by white-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus), elk (Cervus canadensis) and moose (Alces alces) in the coniferous forests of northern Idaho, USA. We hypothesized that remote-sensing methods for measuring the green wave (i.e. the phenological progression of understory food plants) are not useful in coniferous forests because variation in greenness is driven mainly by conifers. We also hypothesized that patterns of forage selection by large herbivores are not detectable in the forest using greenness indices. We tested predictions derived from these hypotheses using on-the-ground measures of forage biomass and quality and more than 10 years of movement data from GPS collars. Remotely sensed greenness indices explained <2.5% of variation in forage biomass (adjusted R2 < 0.024), which was more readily predicted by variation in tree canopy cover, topography and climate (total biomass: adjusted R2 = 0.313; high-quality biomass: adjusted R2 = 0.174). Moreover, with only one exception (elk selected pixels where the instantaneous rate of green-up was near its peak), greenness indices were among the least useful predictors of selection by large herbivores. Indeed, although all three species selected forage biomass, elk and moose simultaneously avoided greener pixels. Our results indicate that greenness indices are of limited value for predicting variation in forage resources or their selection by large herbivores in forested environments. Despite their intuitive appeal and ease of accessibility, such indices cannot always be substituted for on-the-ground measurements of plant traits that directly influence nutrient intake by herbivores.

title: Abundance Redistribution Increases Predator‐Prey Interaction Potentials Among North American Birds
abstract: Species are shifting their geographical ranges, yet the consequences of these spatial redistributions for species interactions have not been examined at broad spatial and temporal scales. Here, we characterize shifts in the potential for predator‐prey interactions among North American birds over the past 50 years. We first predict potential predator‐prey interactions based on existing data, then construct a novel, abundance‐weighted metric of interaction potential for each pair of predator and prey species in local communities. We found nearly universal increases in predator‐prey interaction potentials across North America that are mostly driven by increases in predator abundances. The spatial redistributions of predators and prey lead to turnover of interactions within local communities that are less associated with changes in climate than with human‐induced land use changes. Our results highlight the importance of considering traits, abundances, and species interactions—including known and potential interactions—when studying the ecological consequences of range shifts.

title: Divergent Patterns of Interactions Between Dissolved Organic Matter and Microbial Communities in Mangroves and Salt Marshes
abstract: Mangroves and salt marshes are major blue carbon reservoirs, where dissolved organic matter (DOM) dynamics are co‐regulated by primary production, microbial transformation, and environmental conditions. Understanding whether these two coastal wetlands exhibit fundamentally different DOM–microbe interaction patterns is critical for assessing blue carbon functioning. However, such interactions and their environmental determinants remain unclear. Here, we conduct a continental‐scale comparison between mangroves and salt marshes spanning ~5000 km of China's coastline to elucidate the linkages between DOM molecules and microbial communities. DOM and bacterial β‐diversity are positively correlated in both wetlands, but their respective distance–decay relationships are significant only in salt marshes. DOM–microbe co‐occurrence networks are bacteria‐dominated in both wetlands, but are more complex and positively linked in mangroves, whereas negatively linked in salt marshes. DOM‐gene networks show that carbon fixation and methanogenesis genes are primarily associated with recalcitrant DOM in mangroves, but with labile DOM in salt marshes. Soil pH, together with mean annual temperature, dissolved organic carbon, soil organic carbon, total nitrogen, and amorphous calcium, collectively influence the divergences in DOM composition, microbial community structure, and carbon metabolic functions. These findings offer key insights into DOM–microbe interaction mechanisms and their divergent patterns across “blue carbon” ecosystems.

title: Chemical cues and cognitive models: Integrating metabolomics and AI for plant stress resilience.
abstract: Plants make thousands of different chemicals that reveal how they cope with changing climates. This view explains how evolving artificial intelligence approaches can combine these chemical fingerprints with genetics and environment to build a digital twin of a plant, helping breeders predict performance and develop climate-resilient crops much faster.

title: Plant Phenotyping in Plant Factories: Progress, Challenges and Prospects.
abstract: Plant factories with artificial lighting (PFALs) are enclosed vertical cultivation systems equipped with customisable LED spectral regulation, whose stacked spatial structure and controlled light environments substantially differ from open fields and conventional greenhouses, bringing unique and specialised challenges to precise plant phenotyping. Driven by high-throughput sensing technologies and artificial intelligence (AI), plant phenotyping in PFALs has achieved considerable advances. This review comprehensively summarises progress in PFALs plant phenotyping, covering sensing techniques including RGB imaging, multispectral imaging, hyperspectral imaging, and 3D point cloud reconstruction, as well as advanced analytical models integrating machine learning, deep learning, large language models, and AI agents for phenotypic data mining. We further highlight the important bottlenecks restricting the industrial application of PFALs phenotyping: commercial phenotyping devices are generally bulky, costly, and incompatible with compact vertical cultivation layouts, while the shortage of PFALs-specific phenotypic datasets and scenario-adaptive optimisation models hinders large-scale industrial translation. To clarify the differentiated technical characteristics of PFALs phenotyping, we systematically compare the discrepancies in phenotyping strategies, technical demands, and application scenarios between PFALs and traditional greenhouses. On this basis, we propose targeted solutions and prospective development directions for PFALs phenotyping, focusing on miniaturised and integrated phenotyping equipment, optimised AI-driven analytical frameworks, and multi-omics intelligent breeding. Distinct from previous general phenotyping reviews, this paper specifically targets the vertical, controlled PFALs cultivation scenario, systematically sorting out its exclusive technical challenges and corresponding coping strategies, and providing actionable insights for the future intelligent upgrading and industrialisation of PFALs / vertical farm plant phenotyping technology.

title: Phosphoprotein Phosphatases (PPP), Important Molecular Switchers in Plant Cell and Environment Responses.
abstract: Protein phosphatases, the executors of protein dephosphorylation, play indispensable roles in plant growth, development, and stress adaptation. This review summarizes the classification and biological functions of plant protein phosphatases, with a specific focus on the phosphoprotein phosphatase (PPP) family. By forming dynamic holoenzyme complexes with diverse regulatory subunits, PPP precisely controls vital cellular processes such as hormone signalling pathways, cell division, and light responses. Recent studies highlight the critical involvement of PPP in immune defence and abiotic stress adaptation, including drought and salt tolerance. Although PP1 and PP2A are extensively studied in non-plant systems, functionally dissecting PPP in plants remains an essential frontier, particularly in elucidating isoform-specific functions, mapping regulatory subunit-substrate-kinase networks, and decoding post-translational modifications. Looking forward, integrating phosphoproteomics with advanced toolkits, such as TurboID proximity labelling, AP-MS, substrate-trapping mutants, as well as single-cell and spatial omics, alongside bioinformatics, will be pivotal in overcoming these challenges. Ultimately, engineering regulatory subunit-PPP-substrate modules for crop improvement. Given that protein phosphatases are emerging as a pivotal regulatory hub for balancing the growth-defence trade-off, unravelling their multifaceted roles will simultaneously advance fundamental plant biology and drive innovations in precision breeding.

title: Invisible Threads Weaving a New Fabric: How Digitalization Is Reshaping Work and Life in Undeveloped Areas
abstract: While digitalization is reshaping work and life globally, its micro‐level impacts on individual behavior in undeveloped areas remain insufficiently understood. This study examines how rural digitalization influences time allocation across paid work, housework, and leisure using data from 8774 individuals in the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), matched with county‐level metrics from the Index of Digital Rural County. Employing an instrumental variable two‐stage least squares (IV‐2SLS) approach to address endogeneity, we find that a one‐standard‐deviation increase in rural digitalization reduces weekly work hours by 2.03 h and housework by 1.92 h, while increasing leisure by 0.81 h. These effects are associated with increased off‐farm productivity, agricultural outsourcing, farmland transfer, and online shopping. However, women experience larger reductions in work time, while men benefit more from reduced housework. Productivity and wage gains are concentrated among higher‐income individuals, suggesting that digitalization may exacerbate existing inequalities. Our findings demonstrate how rural digitalization reshapes market and nonmarket time use and highlight the need for complementary policies that promote labor‐saving outsourcing services and rural e‐commerce while addressing gender disparities and unequal access to the benefits of digital transformation.

title: Dynamic task planning methods for air-sea cross-domain unmanned swarms mimicking wolf-pack hunting mechanisms
abstract: To address the challenges of task allocation and cooperative planning for cross-domain air-sea unmanned swarms operating in complex, dynamic environments, this paper proposes a dynamic task planning method inspired by wolf pack hunting mechanisms. By analyzing the role differentiation, cooperative pursuit, and encirclement strategies observed in wolf pack hunting, a task allocation model for multi-role heterogeneous swarms was constructed, and an autonomous, trigger-based dynamic task replanning mechanism—driven by environmental situational awareness—was designed. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a task completion efficiency of 93.5%, representing improvements of 15.3 and 8.7 percentage points over traditional centralized planning methods and the generic Contract Net Protocol, respectively. The method also exhibits significant advantages in resource utilization and dynamic adaptability, with an average planning response time of only 0.87 seconds. Even with large-scale swarms (20 nodes), the completion rate remained at 91.2% with a replanning trigger latency of less than 0.5 seconds, thereby validating the method's scalability and dynamic adaptability. This approach offers an effective solution to the task planning challenges faced by heterogeneous air-sea swarms operating under conditions of communication constraints and environmental uncertainty.
journal: International Conference on Wireless, Optical Communication, and Information Engineering (WOCIE 2026)

journal: Proceedings of the 35th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
abstract: Retail procurement decisions are made by forecasting future demand and then optimizing procurement plans under time-varying unit procurement costs and operational constraints. In this predict-then-optimize pipeline, even the same magnitude of prediction error can induce different downstream procurement costs because prices vary over time, and operational constraints can make forecasted demand infeasible when used directly as a procurement plan. As a result, minimizing standard prediction losses, even with weighting schemes, does not necessarily minimize downstream procurement cost. This motivates Decision-Focused Learning (DFL), which trains predictors with respect to downstream decision objectives. Applying DFL to large numbers of consumers requires demand aggregation to smooth noisy individual demand, stabilize forecasts, and prevent downstream optimization from yielding noise-driven decisions while preserving heterogeneity relevant to procurement decisions. We propose a DFL framework with differentiable micro-demand aggregation that jointly trains consumer clustering, aggregate demand forecasting, and downstream procurement optimization in an end-to-end pipeline. In numerical experiments on demand forecasting and electricity retail procurement optimization, the proposed method reduced procurement regret, defined as the cost gap between prediction-based decisions and the full-information optimum, by 25.6% versus a k-means-based prediction-focused baseline and by 3.3% versus its DFL counterpart. Furthermore, this approach exhibits robustness to the number of clusters.

journal: Proceedings of the 35th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
abstract: In recent cases of multivariate time series forecasting, models are facing challenges that are due to complex interactions between multiple variables, rapid regime shifts and extreme events that cause problems, especially in the domain of electricity markets like the Australian National Electricity Market (NEM). In our research, we tried to improve the existing singular value decomposition autoencoder (SVD-AE) by introducing a spectral aspect to the anomaly scoring and coming up with a regularisation framework aimed at increasing the accuracy of the time series foundation model (TSFM). We used 5-minute resolution NEM data to evaluate our framework; specifically, the anomaly detection part was done on multiple variables influencing the Regional Reference Price (RRP), such as demand, generation, interconnector, temporal and weather, but the zero-shot forecasting and fine-tuning of the forecasting part were done solely on raw and regularised RRP against the same original ground truth. The forecasting outputs from our Hybrid-Scored SVD-AE (HS-SVD-AE) are then compared to the existing baseline SVD-AE. The experiments showed that in the fine-tuned scenario of TSFM, our proposed framework outperforms the existing SVD-AE regularisation by a good margin, but in the zero-shot scenario, SVD-AE performs better by a slight difference. Our findings in this research show that explicitly scored spectral information structure can complement multivariate anomaly detection, which produces more robust foundation model forecasting.

title: Forecasting Functions, Not Points: Time Series Forecasting via Polynomial-Fourier Coefficient Prediction

journal: Proceedings of the 35th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
abstract: Environmental sensor signals, including meteorological, air-quality, and eco-hydrological measurements, are highly characterized by a slowly varying trend and a small number of low-frequency periodic components. In long-term forecasting benchmarks for these signals, the models that explicitly capture trend and seasonality have consistently achieved strong performance. However, in practical deployments, the dominant periods of environmental signals vary between regimes, which heavily forces a deployed forecaster to operate over a wide range of varying prediction horizons H. Standard point forecasting models, such as DLinear, PatchTST, and TimeMixer, tie the output projection weights directly to H. Consequently, any change in the horizon severely increases the decoder parameter count and requires complete, expensive retraining. To the best of our knowledge, no prior studies have proposed a flexible forecasting framework that eliminates this horizon-dependent structural rigidity. Therefore, we propose a novel functional forecasting framework called CoefNet (Coefficient-prediction Network), which approaches long-term time-series forecasting by predicting the coefficients of a continuous function ƒ(t) composed of polynomial and Fourier terms. The decomposition into trend and seasonality is explicitly encoded in the structure of ƒ(t) itself, allowing the same trained coefficients to be evaluated on any arbitrary target grid without additional parameters or retraining. Since a pure polynomial-Fourier basis captures global trend and periodicity but may not capture the detailed local variations of signals, we further propose a per-sub-window low-rank modulation scheme. This adaptable scheme captures localized fluctuations by perturbing the shared coefficients at a minimal 4% parameter overhead. As a result, CoefNet successfully achieves the coarse-to-fine prediction property without requiring post-hoc interpolation. Extensive experimental results on four datasets of real-world environmental sensors demonstrate that the proposed approach is robust against varying horizons, attaining state-of-the-art performance in 13 of 16 settings against nine baselines for standard point forecasting.

title: Does Trust Spill Over?: Exploring Asymmetric Trust Dynamics Between Teammate AI and Guide AI in Cooperative Games
abstract: Cooperative games increasingly feature multiple AI agents serving distinct roles, yet how players form and transfer trust across such agents remains unclear. We investigated trust spillover between a task-executing Teammate AI and an advisory Guide AI in a web-based cooperative cooking game (within-subjects, N = 23). Teammate AI ability (high vs. low) and Guide AI accuracy (high vs. low/absent) were experimentally manipulated. Results revealed a directional asymmetry in trust spillover. Teammate AI ability significantly influenced trust in the Guide AI ( \(\eta _p^2 =.220\) ), whereas Guide AI accuracy and presence had no effect on trust in the Teammate AI ( \(\eta _p^2 =.002\) ). This suggests that, under cognitive constraints, trust propagates from high-salience task agents to lower-salience advisory agents, but not vice versa. Additionally, the presence of the Guide AI improved performance and perceived control independent of advice accuracy, suggesting an attentional cueing effect. Finally, congruent agent quality levels enhanced perceived relatedness, highlighting the importance of system-level coherence. These findings demonstrate asymmetric trust spillover in cooperative games with role-differentiated AI, where execution-focused agents anchor system-wide trust formation, with implications for multi-agent AI systems in which agents serve distinct functional roles.
journal: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Role of Geospatial Surveying in Enhancing Crop Quality Through Land Assessment and Resource Optimization: A Case Study of Smallholder Farmers in Guduru District
abstract: Agriculture is the cornerstone of Ethiopia’s economy, yet its productivity is constrained by soil degradation, inefficient land management, and uniform application of inputs. These challenges are acute in Guduru District of the Horro Guduru Wallaga Zone, where smallholder farmers depend on traditional methods that do not account for spatial variability in soils, topography, and vegetation. This study investigates the role of geospatial surveying in enhancing crop quality and optimizing resource use through precision agriculture. A mixed-methods geospatial approach was employed, integrating field-based GPS data, Sentinel-2 remote sensing imagery, soil sampling, and GIS-based spatial analysis. Five representative kebeles were selected by stratified sampling to capture variability in elevation, soil type, and land use. Digital Elevation Model (DEM) and slope analyses were combined with soil data and Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) classification to generate land suitability maps, and ordinary kriging was applied to estimate unsampled soil properties and vegetation indices. Findings revealed significant spatial heterogeneity: Nitisols and Vertisols showed high potential for cereal and legume production under targeted management, whereas Leptosols were highly erosion-prone and unsuitable without conservation measures. NDVI analysis indicated that vegetation vigor varied substantially within and across kebeles, highlighting inefficiencies in uniform input application. Weighted overlay analysis classified 41% of farmland as highly suitable (S1), 36% as moderately suitable (S2), 15% as marginally suitable (S3), and 8% as unsuitable (N). These results show the potential of geospatial surveying to provide actionable insights for precision input management, soil conservation, and crop diversification. For policymakers, integrating geospatial frameworks into agricultural extension systems offers a pathway toward sustainable land use and improved food security. The findings provide a replicable model for similar highland contexts across Ethiopia and sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Dental Research: Innovation versus Integrity?
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models and agentic pipelines, is reshaping dental research. This article examines the opportunities and risks of AI in knowledge production in oral health research. On one hand, AI accelerates literature synthesis, data analysis, and manuscript drafting; on the other, it introduces new risks, including fabricated findings and citations, overconfident inference, and homogenization of research focus. These shifts challenge the mechanisms that maintain scientific credibility such as peer review, reproducibility, and human judgment, especially in fields like dentistry, where small datasets and limited editorial capacity may amplify vulnerabilities. We here identify 3 structural asymmetries: 1) the growing gap between the rapid pace of AI-assisted production and slow human validation, 2) the divergence between AI-generated linguistic fluency and the true robustness of the generated evidence, and 3) unequal institutional capacity to govern AI and the incentives set by the research system for (mis)using AI for research. We conclude with a call for proportional and enforceable governance frameworks, including mandatory AI disclosure standards, provenance tracking, structured adversarial testing of research tools, and interdisciplinary oversight. Moreover, we suggest institutional reform, including revising incentive structures, fostering AI literacy, and enforcing auditability to safeguard research integrity. In the age of machine-assisted content, credibility becomes a scarce resource. Dental science must not merely adopt AI but actively govern it to ensure that its accelerated outputs remain trustworthy, equitable, and clinically meaningful.

title: miR-8485 by Targeting ITGAM Expression Alleviates Cognitive Impairment Induced by Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: ObjectivePost-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a major complication of ischemic stroke (IS). This study aims to explore the role of miR-8485 in PSCI and its underlying molecular mechanism.Methods84 PSCI patients and 90 post-stroke cognitively normal (PSCN) patients were included. Serum miR-8485 and ITGAM expression were examined via reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. The diagnostic efficacy of miR-8485 was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. Risk factors of PSCI were determined via logistic regression analysis. An in vitro PSCI cell model was constructed through oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Cell viability, apoptosis and inflammatory factor levels were determined by Cell Counting Kit-8 assay, flow cytometry and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The oxidative stress was evaluated by measuring superoxide dismutase (SOD), malondialdehyde (MDA) and catalase (CAT) levels. The interaction between miR-8485 and ITGAM was verified by dual-luciferase reporter assay.ResultsmiR-8485 was downregulated in PSCI patients, and ROC analysis showed that it could differentiate PSCI patients from PSCN patients. Downregulated miR-8485 expression was associated with PSCI disease severity. In OGD/R-treated human microglial cells (HMC3), upregulation of miR-8485 increased cell viability, suppressed inflammatory responses and oxidative stress, and inhibited apoptosis. ITGAM was the target of miR-8485. Overexpression of ITGAM partially reversed the protective effect of miR-8485 upregulation in OGD/R-induced HMC3 cells.ConclusionmiR-8485 alleviates OGD/R-induced inflammatoty responses and oxidative stress via targeted inhibition of ITGAM expression. The miR-8485/ITGAM axis may serve as a key regulatory pathway and a potential therapeutic candidate for further investigation in PSCI.
journal: Journal of geriatric psychiatry and neurology

title: Artificial Intelligence for Cardiovascular Health Behavior Change: A Narrative Review of Patient-Facing Tools.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in the United States and disproportionately affects racial/ethnic minoritized populations, low-income communities, older adults, and rural residents. Behavioral interventions can reduce cardiovascular risk, yet traditional programs face scalability barriers, including high costs and limited reach. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the efficacy and equity of patient-directed AI tools that support health education and behavior change for cardiovascular health. Using PRISMA-ScR elements, we searched 10 databases (January 2010 to December 2025), yielding 19 empirical studies evaluating Generation 2.0 AI systems aligned with the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) framework. Of these, five were randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and 14 were nonrandomized (quasi-experimental, observational, or early-stage) studies. AI-enabled interventions such as conversational agents, machine-learning models, and reinforcement-learning systems addressed hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, and related conditions. Among the RCTs, one demonstrated superiority of an AI-powered program over usual care (AI-delivered Diabetes Prevention Program), whereas the remaining four reported outcomes equivalent or non-inferior to standard behavioral care. Effects were most apparent in high-intensity interventions that paired machine learning-based personalization with structured behavioral curricula, although the multi-component nature of these programs limits inference about AI-specific contributions. Across nonrandomized studies, greater engagement intensity was consistently associated with improved cardiometabolic outcomes, although causal attribution to AI-specific mechanisms remains limited. Most studies had small samples, short follow-up, and limited reporting on safety and equity. Technology-intensive interventions were concentrated in higher-resourced settings, and populations with limited health literacy showed reduced engagement. Overall, evidence supports cautious optimism that AI can meaningfully scale personalized cardiovascular prevention; however, realizing that equitable and clinically meaningful impact will require rigorous trials with longer follow-up, explicit behavioral science integration, safety-conscious governance, and equity-centered strategies addressing digital determinants of health.
journal: Health education & behavior : the official publication of the Society for Public Health Education

title: Translational Strategies in Smart Drug Delivery Systems for Controlled and Personalized Pharmacokinetics.
abstract: Advancements in drug delivery systems (DDSs) have developed pharmacotherapy by enabling precise control over drug pharmacokinetics (PKs), enhancing therapeutic efficacy, minimizing toxicity, and improving patient compliance. This review comprehensively examines emerging DDS strategies designed to optimize absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) of therapeutic agents. Key innovations include nanotechnology-based carriers (liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, and dendrimers), stimuli-responsive and smart delivery systems, site-specific and tissue-targeted DDS, and prodrug DDS hybrid approaches. Integration of PK modeling, artificial intelligence (AI), and omics data has facilitated personalized and patient-specific therapy, while advanced computational tools allow predictive simulation of drug behavior. Translational challenges such as scale-up, regulatory approval, interpatient variability, long-term safety, and clinical trial design are discussed, alongside strategies to overcome these barriers. Future perspectives emphasize AI-assisted optimization, multimodal DDS combining therapeutic and diagnostic functionalities, biodegradable and sustainable materials, and regenerative and cellular delivery platforms. Collectively, these developments highlight a paradigm shift toward adaptive, precise, and personalized pharmacotherapy, bridging preclinical innovation with clinical application. This review provides a comprehensive framework for understanding the current landscape and future directions of DDS in controlling PKs, ultimately supporting safer and more effective patient-centric therapies.

title: In Situ Resource Utilization for Agriculture on Mars: Quantifying the Effects of Black Soldier Fly Frass Amendment on Pea Growth in Martian Regolith Simulant
abstract: Future long-duration missions to Mars will require in situ food production systems to reduce dependence on resupply missions and enhance crew autonomy. This study evaluated the growth performance of peas, Pisum sativum, cultivated in Martian regolith simulant (MMS-1) ameliorated with black soldier fly, Hermetia illucens , (BSF) frass at inclusion levels of 0%, 10%, 25%, and 50% by volume. Pea plant fitness was then assessed over the course of two, 8-week greenhouse trials by measuring germination rate, plant height, leaf chlorophyll content, and final dry biomass. These were compared against peas grown in a control substrate consisting of commercially available gardening soil treated with the same frass-inclusion percentages (0%, 10%, 25%, or 50% by volume). Germination and height responses were statistically similar between regolith and soil, suggesting that properly amended regolith may be able to sustain in situ crop growth on Mars. Notably, peas grown in regolith simulant (without perchlorates) + frass exhibited slightly higher chlorophyll content than the controls, while biomass productivity was lower than commercial potting mix + frass when comparing across the same frass-inclusion percentage. These findings represent the first experimental evidence that BSF frass can enhance crop cultivation in a Martian soil analog, highlighting its potential role in bioregenerative life support systems and in situ resource utilization strategies. In addition, fitting quadratic regression models to the data indicated an optimal frass inclusion between approximately 5% and 32% (depending on which metric was to be maximized), beyond which fitness declined. Beyond space applications, these findings build on prior studies by further supporting the value of insect-derived amendments for improving nutrient-poor or degraded soils.

title: Strategic Feasibility Study for a National Telecommunications Satellite in Peru
abstract: The global context shaped by the COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the critical importance of connectivity, transforming it from a perceived privilege into a fundamental necessity for social, educational, and economic activities. In countries with complex geographies such as Peru, ensuring equitable access to telecommunications services remains a significant challenge. While national initiatives—such as the deployment of a fiber-optic backbone network—have improved connectivity across many regions, important gaps persist in remote and hard-to-reach areas due to geographic, climatic, and investment constraints. In this context, satellite telecommunications emerge as a strategic solution to extend coverage and complement existing terrestrial infrastructure. This paper presents a feasibility study for the development or acquisition of a national telecommunications satellite in Peru, aimed at expanding connectivity to underserved populations and supporting key sectors such as education, remote work, agriculture, and rural development. This work analyses an explicit geopolitical and financing comparison of precedent cases in the region, a corrected and internally consistent bandwidth-demand model, a multi-reference cost benchmark drawing on five comparable satellite systems, and a financial decision-making model that weighs a dedicated national satellite against co-owned regional capacity and emerging low-Earth-orbit (LEO) alternatives. The study evaluates technical and operational requirements, including coverage analysis, power budgets, bandwidth estimation, and service demand projections, and considers the integration of the satellite system with existing ground infrastructure across different implementation scenarios. The analysis indicates that a national or regionally shared satellite system is a technically credible way to address elements of the digital divide, but that its economic and strategic advantage over co-owned capacity or LEO-based alternatives depends strongly on financing structure, full life-cycle costing, and the degree of operational sovereignty sought, rather than on payload capacity alone.

title: Deep learning framework for the assessment of odontoid fractures on cervical CT: optimization of sensitivity and specificity
abstract: Odontoid fractures are injuries that may be overlooked on cervical CT and can lead to serious clinical consequences. In this study, four deep learning models were evaluated independently for the assessment of odontoid fractures on selected 2D CT slices, with particular attention to false-negative and false-positive predictions. A balanced dataset was used (training: 1208 images; test: 604 images; 302 fracture and 302 healthy images in the test set). Fracture cases were annotated with bounding boxes. YOLOv10s was used for detection, ResNet18 for classification, and nnU-Net v2 2D and SwinUNETR 2D for weakly supervised segmentation. Each model was evaluated independently. SwinUNETR’s image-level threshold analysis was exploratory. ResNet18 classification using reference-box crops for fracture-positive images and central crops for healthy images achieved accuracy of 98%, sensitivity of 99.3%, specificity of 96.7%, and F1 of 98%. YOLOv10s-derived image-level decisions yielded specificity of 97.4%, precision of 97.1%, sensitivity of 90.1%, and F1 of 93.5%. SwinUNETR 2D mask-derived decisions yielded sensitivity of 99.3%, specificity of 40.4%, accuracy of 69.9%, and F1 of 76.7%. Corresponding nnU-Net v2 2D values were 70.9%, 88.4%, 79.6%, and 77.7%. These image-level metrics describe task-specific outputs and decision rules. The findings support preliminary technical feasibility within a single-center, selected-slice evaluation. The proposed alarm–confirmation strategy was not tested as a combined system. External validation on complete CT examinations and comparison with radiologists are needed to establish clinical effectiveness.

title: Identifying the determinants of soccer coach turnover by competing risks models: a case study on Italian League Serie A
abstract: This paper investigates the determinants of head coach turnover in the Italian Serie A over the period 2010-2019 by explicitly accounting for multiple exit mechanisms within a competing risks framework. Four mutually exclusive exit types are considered: end of contract, mutual consent, resignation, and sacking. To identify robust predictors of turnover, we combine classical cause-specific Cox models with a variable selection procedure based on forward selection, LASSO regression, and Random Survival Forests. The results show that performance-related variables are the primary drivers of coach turnover, while personal characteristics play a limited role once performance is controlled for. Short-term performance indicators, such as points per match until turnover, strongly influence the risk of dismissal. Conversely, cumulative poor performance substantially increases dismissal risk: a higher proportion of losses over a coach's tenure raises the hazard of sacking by more than four times. Season timing also plays a crucial role, as sackings and mutual-consent terminations are significantly more likely to occur during the season, whereas contract expirations concentrate at the end of the season. Overall, the findings highlight that clubs differentiate between short-term performance shocks and longer-term performance trajectories when deciding how and when to replace a head coach. By distinguishing among exit mechanisms and adopting a conservative variable selection strategy, the study provides a robust and nuanced assessment of managerial turnover dynamics in the most important Italian professional football league.

title: Exploring the role of soil amendments and agronomic practices in enhancing Gossypium hirsutum L. resilience to climate change: a path forward for sustainable cotton farming
abstract: Cotton (Gossypium hirsutum L.) is an important fiber crop, but its yield and overall fiber quality are constrained by biotic and abiotic factors. Under certain conditions, moderate rises in temperature and elevated atmospheric CO₂ levels may enhance cotton growth and productivity. However, these benefits are often constrained by heat and water stress. This review critically synthesizes the research on the contribution of soil amendments and agronomic practices to improving soil structure, nutrient retention, rhizosphere functionality, and plant stress resilience in cotton systems. Organic, mineral, and microbial amendments, including biochar formulations, can improve soil properties and microbial activity, especially under arid and saline conditions. Nevertheless, their effectiveness is highly context-dependent. Cotton exhibits physiological plasticity through changes in rooting patterns, osmotic adjustment, and antioxidant defense mechanisms, but its reproductive system is highly sensitive to heat stress. Phenological evidence suggests that warming accelerates crop development and increases the risk of heat and water stress during sensitive growth stages. Based on this synthesis, we propose the Climate-resilient cotton production model (CR-CPM), which conceptualizes cotton resilience as a threshold-based outcome emerging from interactions among soil, microbial, physiological, phenological, and management processes, where physiological thresholds determine the transition from effective management to system-level stress under extreme conditions. This framework emphasizes the need for integrated, site-specific strategies to sustain cotton productivity and soil health under increasing climatic stress.

title: Understanding gender-based constraints among potato farmers for benefiting from quality seeds
abstract: Potatoes constitute a major crop in Kenya and are cultivated by approximately 800,000 smallholder farmers. However, yields remain low because of limited access to certified seeds. Formal seed system interventions lack gender responsiveness, leaving female farmers at a disadvantage and reliant on recycling saved seeds. This study is based on an assessment of a seed distribution intervention by Kisima Farm, a private seed company. This study aims to assess gender-specific differences in potato production, resource access, and decision-making. It also examines socioeconomic, institutional, and cultural factors that influence women’s and men’s access to and adoption of quality potato seeds from certified sources. This study is a secondary gender analysis of data collected from potato farmers in central Kenya. The study employs a multivariate probit model to examine gender differences in certified seed adoption and use. It also uses the exogenous switching treatment effects regression (ESTER) model to assess the causal effect of plot manager gender on productivity. Female farmers have lower access to quality seeds than male farmers. The ESTER model shows lower potato productivity for female plot managers. Factors such as the need to replace seeds every three seasons, limited access to land, household food insecurity, and price constraints contribute to a 71% gender gap in potato productivity. Commercialised potato seed systems are male-oriented and are inadequate in addressing the needs of female smallholder farmers. The study recommends gender-responsive seed system interventions grounded in targeted needs and capacities of women towards fostering more inclusive and diverse potato production systems. Not applicable.

title: Genotypic variation and root traits associated with hypoxia tolerance in quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.)
abstract: Waterlogging-induced hypoxia is becoming an increasingly important constraint to crop production under climate change. Although quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) is recognized for its tolerance to drought and salinity, its response to hypoxia remains poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of hypoxia on growth, root development, biomass accumulation, and individual seed yield in 28 quinoa genotypes. Hypoxia reduced plant height by 31%, leaf area by 47%, root length by 39%, and shoot dry weight by 37% (mean hypoxia tolerance index 0.69, 0.53, 0.61, and 0.63); shoot dry weight remained 44% lower after recovery, whereas root diameter increased by 28% under hypoxia. Correlation analysis revealed that root length and root surface area were positively associated with individual seed yield, whereas root diameter was negatively related to several growth traits, highlighting the importance of maintaining root development under hypoxia. Permutational multivariate analysis of variance across 19 traits attributed 37.1% of overall phenotypic variation to genotype, 30.0% to oxygen regime, and 18.8% to their interaction (each p = 0.001), and hierarchical clustering on hypoxia tolerance indices resolved three genotype groups with contrasting trait profiles. Under hypoxia, Amachuha and Isluga produced the highest individual yields, followed by EDK4 and Chadmo. Under genotype-level validation (leave-one-genotype-out, leave-one-cluster-out, and highland-versus-lowland cross-ecotype splits), no model predicted the individual yield of genotypes excluded from training better than the mean yield of the training genotypes under the same oxygen regime, so trait-based yield prediction does not transfer to unseen quinoa genotypes. These findings provide valuable insights into the mechanisms of hypoxia tolerance and identify promising genetic resources for breeding quinoa cultivars adapted to waterlogging-prone environments.

title: Organic floriculture for sustainable production: Advances in soil health, eco-friendly inputs and crop management
abstract: Organic floriculture is gaining importance as a sustainable production system that addresses the environmental concerns associated with conventional flower cultivation, particularly the excessive use of synthetic fertilisers and pesticides. These inputs contribute to soil degradation, ecological imbalance and reduced sustainability of ornamental crop production. This review presents recent advancements in sustainable organic practices in floriculture, emphasising the role of organic nutrient sources, biofertilisers, biostimulants, eco-friendly growing substrates and integrated pest and disease management strategies. Studies on organic production systems in major ornamental crops have reported improvements in plant growth, flowering attributes, flower quality, essential oil content and post-harvest performance. An integration of biological inputs, microbial inoculants, botanical-based pest management and environmentally safe cultivation practices offers promising alternatives for reducing chemical dependency. Sustainable resource management approaches, including water conservation techniques, protected cultivation, precision farming and improved post-harvest handling, further enhance the efficiency and resilience of organic floriculture systems. Additionally, organic certification standards, including International Federation of Organic Agriculture Movements (IFOAM), European Union (EU) organic and United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) organic, promote sustainable floriculture by restricting synthetic chemicals and encouraging environmentally responsible production practices. However, limitations related to nutrient availability, effective pest and disease management, production consistency and certification constraints continue to restrict widespread adoption. Future research should focus on developing efficient organic input formulations, innovative cultivation technologies and region-specific sustainable production models to enhance productivity, sustainability and adoption among farmers. This review highlights the potential of organic floriculture as a viable approach for achieving environmentally sustainable, economically viable and high-quality ornamental crop production.

title: A dual-stream multitask deep learning model for supply chain demand forecasting with statistically derived early-warning signals
abstract: Accurate demand forecasting is crucial in supply chain management (SCM) as global supply networks become increasingly complex and exposed to disruptions. Traditional models that rely mainly on historical sales may miss demand shifts driven by heterogeneous auxiliary signals and often do not provide explicit early warning of abnormal events. This study proposes a dual-stream multitask deep-learning model that integrates demand forecasting and statistically derived earlywarning signal estimation within a unified framework. The model adopts a dual-input architecture: (i) an LSTM branch that captures temporal dynamics from historical sales sequences and (ii) a Transformer encoder branch that models supplementary auxiliary features and statistically derived anomaly signals computed from that same sales series, including STL residual–based indicators, change-point flags, and calendar variables. The fused representation is jointly optimized to predict both the demand two days ahead of the input window and the probability of a statistically defined anomaly event on that day. Experiments are conducted on the public Kaggle Store Item Demand Forecasting dataset (10 stores, 50 items, daily sales from 2013 to 2017), using the most recent 90 days in each series for validation and synthetic anomaly labels derived from statistical residual analysis. Compared with a unimodal LSTM baseline, the proposed model reduces RMSE by approximately 7.23% and MAE by approximately 6.86%, and the bootstrap confidence intervals of both gaps exclude zero. Under an identical evaluation protocol the model also outperforms a naive forecast, a seasonal naive model and AutoARIMA, whereas a global gradient-boosted tree baseline attains a slightly lower point error (RMSE 0.5574 versus 0.5798). Because ground-truth incident labels are unavailable for this dataset, the classification task is supervised by weak labels derived from the residuals of the same series; the resulting discrimination is limited (ROC–AUC between 0.578 and 0.589 and PR–AUC between 0.126 and 0.141 against a positive rate of 0.100), and the anomaly head is therefore presented as a calibrated, cost-aware screening signal rather than as a validated anomaly detector. Under a 5:1 false-negative-to-false-positive cost ratio the proposed model attains the lowest expected cost among the configurations compared, and temperature scaling yields well-calibrated alert probabilities, so that a single multitask model can support both replenishment decisions and screening-level early warning.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COMPUTERS COMMUNICATIONS & CONTROL

title: Wild Edible Plants as Underutilized Agro-Biodiversity in Albania: Traditional Knowledge, Use, Among the Adolescents
abstract: Wild edible plants (WEPs) are an important but underutilized component of agro-biodiversity, providing nutrient-dense food, raw materials, and cultural value, yet across the Mediterranean and the Balkans the traditional knowledge that underpins their use is eroding as rural lifeways change. This study documented WEP knowledge, use practices, and the channels through which such knowledge is transmitted among adolescents in Albania, and assessed the relative nutritional value of the most commonly used species. We combined a cross-sectional questionnaire completed by 520 respondents with an ethnobotanical literature review and a synthesis of nutritional data for 15 widely used species. Most participants (78.8%) were aware of wild plants in general terms, but fewer than half used them personally (40.4%) and only about a third could identify species in their local environment (34.6%). Knowledge transmission had shifted from family tradition to digital media (50.0% versus 38.5%), and household use (63.5%) greatly exceeded personal use, indicating that practical skills are being lost between generations. The reviewed species showed high relative nutritional value, with several, such as stinging nettle, exceeding common cultivated greens in key micronutrients. The findings depict a generation that remains culturally aware of its wild-food heritage but is increasingly disconnected from the practices that sustain it. We argue that conserving WEP-related agro-biodiversity in Albania requires integrating traditional food-plant knowledge into agricultural extension, education, and community initiatives before it is lost.

title: Masked Self-Supervised Temporal Modeling of Agricultural Prices: A Case Study of Wheat MSP in Rajasthan Region
abstract: Support Price (MSP) forecasting under sparse and irregular agricultural time-series conditions. Method: District-level wheat production and price data from all districts of Rajasthan Region, for 2016–2025 were pre-processed and segmented into temporal windows. In this work, we propose a Masked Self-Supervised Temporal learning framework for MSP forecasting that emphasizes representation learning rather than direct label dependence using masked reconstructive temporal learning. Performance was compared with ARIMA and supervised LSTM using mean squared error (MSE) on log-transformed prices. Findings: ARIMA produced the MAE (164.97), while supervised long short-term memory (LSTM) achieved 60.58. The proposed Masked Self-Supervised Temporal Learning (MSSTL) framework achieved a MAE of 32.67 and showed stable convergence and improved data efficiency. MSSTL learned temporal representations capturing seasonal patterns, production–irrigation interactions, and longer-term market memory without relying exclusively on labeled price observations. The results indicate that Masked Self-Supervised Temporal learning can provide a useful balance between forecasting performance and robustness when agricultural datasets are limited. The future-trend analysis emphasizes directional stability rather than exact long-horizon price values. Novelty: The study applies two-stage Masked Self-Supervised Temporal representation learning to wheat MSP forecasting in a data-scarce district-level agricultural setting, reducing dependence on labeled price data. Keywords: Crop Price, Minimum Support Price, Deep Learning, Masked Self-Supervised Learning, Temporal Learning
journal: Indian Journal Of Science And Technology

title: Drift No More: Spectral Locking for Long-Horizon Open-Weight Multi-Agent AI
abstract: Long-horizon multi-agent systems suffer from three tightly coupled failures: task drift, role drift, and state staleness. We test the hypothesis that these share a common representational cause: agent hidden states move away from the directions encoding the active task, assigned role, and current shared state. A pilot study over 14,832 annotated turns supports this: drifted turns collapse near-uniformly across all three anchor subspaces (pairwise r = 0.72-0.78). Existing methods address these failures separately, operating at the surface-text level or treating control directions independently. We introduce ATLAS (Algebraic Task-role Locking with Adaptive Spectral Memory), a training-free intervention acting on hidden states before a token is generated. ATLAS builds a positive-semidefinite anchor kernel over task, role, and state subspaces and steers hidden states toward their shared high-coherence eigendirections; a low-rank Gram decomposition keeps this tractable. Across long-horizon memory, state maintenance, tool use, least-privilege coordination, and embodied stress tests, ATLAS outperforms prompting, retrieval, memory, and activation-steering baselines. Against A-MEM it improves memory macro-average accuracy by up to 5.7 points and reduces write/read failures by up to 31.7%/24.8%; against MemoryArena-Agent it gains up to 4.8 points. It gains 10.7-12.1 points under perturbation, reaches 93.5% role consistency, and transfers to a 72B backbone (macro-average 61.0 vs. 56.2). Ablating the joint task-role-state span costs 7.2 points against 0.8 for a matched-rank random span, indicating these directions are functionally implicated, not incidental; supplying them by prompt or retrieval recovers 4.3 points less. ATLAS is therefore a representation-level controller for open-weight multi-agent systems, complementary to output-level protocols for black-box agents.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: Deep Convolutional Learning for Automated Multi-Class Quality Grading and Defect Recognition of Fruits and Crop Leaves
abstract: Grading harvested produce by eye is slow, depends heavily on the inspector, and yields inconsistent results from one batch to the next, which contributes to post-harvest loss and unfair pricing. This paper presents an automated grading framework based on a convolutional neural network (CNN) that goes beyond identifying which crop is in an image and instead judges its condition. Images of fruits and leaves are assigned to one of five quality grades—healthy, ripe, unripe, pest-damaged, and rotten—so that maturity stage and common defects are recognized within a single model. The pipeline combines image normalization and enhancement, extensive data augmentation, hierarchical feature learning, and a softmax classifier trained with cross-entropy loss and the Adam optimizer. On a held-out test set the model reaches 94.9% accuracy and a macro-averaged F1-score of 94.8%, surpassing a support vector machine trained on hand-crafted features by 8.4 percentage points while needing only about 21 ms per image. These results indicate that the approach is accurate and fast enough to support real-time sorting and supply-chain decisions in precision agriculture.

title: Integrating Remote Sensing, Management Information, and Satellite Embeddings for Machine-Learning Prediction of Field-Level Maize Yield in Kenyan Smallholder Systems
abstract: Field-level crop yield prediction is an important application of precision agriculture, but it remains challenging in African smallholder systems because plots are small, management is heterogeneous, and satellite pixels can mix multiple land covers. This study evaluated machine-learning approaches for predicting maize yield from 6,016 field-year observations in Kenya during 2017–2020 using Sentinel-2 remote-sensing variables, climate, soil, terrain and location attributes, survey-based management information, and 64-dimensional satellite embeddings. Eleven candidate algorithms were compared using cross-validation, followed by XGBoost predictor-group and SHAP analyses. XGBoost achieved the strongest pooled performance (R² = 0.383; RMSE = 1,334 kg ha⁻¹; MAE = 1,013 kg ha⁻¹). Conventional remote sensing alone achieved R² = 0.196; adding climate, soil, terrain, and location increased R² to 0.250, while adding management information increased it to 0.386. Management accounted for 32.4% of grouped SHAP importance, with plant density as the most influential individual predictor. Satellite embeddings matched the predictive performance of conventional remote-sensing predictors while reducing satellite predictor dimensionality by approximately 77%. The results show that remote sensing and machine learning can support field-level yield monitoring in heterogeneous smallholder systems, but plot-level management information remains critical for improving prediction.

title: Silent methodological failures in AI-assisted science: benchmarking large language model agents for virtual gene knockout analysis
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in computational biology, yet their reliability in executing complex scientific workflows remains poorly characterized. Here, we benchmarked five LLM agents (DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM 5.1, HY3 Preview, Kimi K2.6, and Minimax M2.7) on virtual gene knockout analyses using four computational frameworks across two single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets. All agents successfully completed the assigned workflows, but their quantitative outputs varied substantially: execution times spanned a 31fold range (61 − 1,920 s), while cross-model coefficients of variation reached 142.1%. Notably, four of five agents (80%) exhibited “silent methodological failures,” generating computationally valid, error-free code that produced biologically implausible results. Among the evaluated agents, GLM 5.1 showed the most balanced performance across computational efficiency and biological plausibility. These findings demonstrate that successful code execution alone does not ensure scientific validity and highlight cross-model concordance and biological validation as important quality-control strategies for Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted computational biology workflows.

title: From Execution to Discovery : Physical Verification as the Key Gap in AI Agents for Science
abstract: Why can AI agents operate reliably in digital environments such as software development yet still struggle to achieve autonomous scientific discovery? We argue that this gap reflects not only limitations in model capability but also differences in how agent capabilities are externalized and how reliably environments can verify the consequences of agent actions. In this survey, we trace the technical evolution of AI agents and propose a three-stage framework of capability externalization: reasoning externalization makes knowledge, memory, and intermediate inferences inspectable; execution externalization makes tool use and long-horizon workflows governable; and world-interaction externalization integrates environmental evidence into hypothesis revision and action selection. Materials discovery provides a demanding testbed for all three stages, spanning literature-grounded hypothesis generation, computational design, automated experimentation, and iterative knowledge updating. Although agents can increasingly complete predefined research workflows, workflow automation alone does not constitute scientific discovery. Sustained autonomy requires agents to assess whether new observations support or challenge a hypothesis and to select subsequent experiments accordingly. We therefore identify environmental verifiability as a central systems constraint on agent autonomy: the extent to which an environment can translate actions into timely, attributable, reproducible, and affordable evidence. This perspective positions physical verification capacity as a key scaling dimension for autonomous scientific discovery.
