title: Generalized Disjunctive Programming with Derivative-Free Configuration Search
abstract: Generalized disjunctive programming (GDP) describes process design alternatives with Boolean variables, disjunctions, and logical propositions, and fixing one configuration leaves a subproblem in the continuous variables. Conventional GDP methods require explicit equations, which a simulator may not expose, and mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) reformulations can be intractable for nonconvex models. The external-variable reformulation turns configuration choice into an optimization over an integer lattice whose objective is the subproblem value, which derivative-free optimization (DFO) can search while the GDP model continues describing the alternatives. We pair GDP models with surrogate DFO methods and the direct-search method NOMAD and compare them with discrete steepest descent (D-SDA), logic-based and MINLP solvers, and enumeration on nine process models, 21 test functions, a pharmaceutical flowsheet simulated in PharmaPy, and a catalytic distillation column with 100,947 configurations. On the largest reactor network, the surrogate methods MISO and RBFOpt reach the reference in nine or ten of ten runs with about 30 subproblem solves, whereas logic-based methods solve nearly one subproblem for each admissible configuration and most D-SDA descents end at one local minimum. In the flowsheet example, where GDP solvers do not apply, RBFOpt and MISO find the best of 36 simulated configurations in every run with 20 evaluations. For the catalytic column, D-SDA and MISO reach the best known design with 100 evaluations, whereas MINLP solvers find no design within 15% of it and global solvers return contradictory certificates. This search pays off when the configuration space is too large to enumerate, has deceptive local minima, or has MINLP reformulations that fail, and enumeration or a direct reformulation is simpler for small algebraic models.

title: SlackBench: Benchmarking Agents on Collaborative Projects Grounded in Real Code Repositories
abstract: AI Agents are becoming digital coworkers that can browse the web, write code, run experiments, and assist humans over extended horizons. Yet existing benchmarks fall short of real knowledge work: many rely on synthetic data or isolated tasks, missing the complex, multi-party dynamics of collaborative projects, where critical information is scattered across conversations, code, and evolving decisions. Even simple workplace questions may require locating relevant channels and direct messages, recovering context from long discussions, inspecting repository state, reconciling stale or conflicting evidence, and synthesizing across sources. We introduce SlackBench, a benchmark for evaluating agents on realistic research and engineering workflows that require joint reasoning over workplace communication and evolving repository state. Grounded in privacy-preserving reenactments of real academic research projects, SlackBench provides reproducible environments with realistic multi-party dialogue, evolving decisions, and corresponding code changes grounded in GitHub repositories and Google Docs. It contains 140 queries spanning heterogeneous-source agentic search, abstention on unanswerable or false-premise questions, goal-directed summarization, and circumstance inference over long conversations. These tasks are not reducible to static corpus question answering: agents must determine which conversations matter, traverse threads, inspect repository state, and synthesize evidence across communication and code artifacts. Across 33 frontier models and agent harnesses, the best system scores around 80% and most agents score below 66%, highlighting substantial headroom for improvement. SlackBench thus provides an extensible framework for evaluating agents in collaborative work environments. The SlackBench dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuanzhiMao/SlackBench .

title: Iterated creation, grading, and revision of data science projects by language models
abstract: We evaluate the extent to which agentic AI models can complete an end-to-end data science project, and how this improves with feedback. A 'writer' model with specific tools creates a complete data science project including downloading, cleaning, and analyzing a dataset, and writing a short paper about it. The project is executed and a 'grader' model evaluates it. The writer can then revise its submission, and this repeats for a total of three rounds. We consider seven models from five developers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and Z.AI. Each model is both a writer and a grader, so there are 49 writer-grader pairs and we run each pair three times. Of the 147 initial submissions, 107 run and render, and the average score increases from 59 per cent to 76 per cent after the final round of feedback. By writer the extent of the increase ranges from 3 percentage points for Anthropic's Opus 5.5 to 46 percentage points for Anthropic's Haiku 4.5, and by grader it ranges from 13 percentage points for Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash to 32 percentage points for Anthropic's Haiku 4.5. When a model grades its own writing the score tends to be about 9 percentage points higher than the average of what the other models give it. About half of the difference that we see from round to round is within the grader's own noise. Feedback generally results in the highest marks, but even just having the chance to revise, or having the additional budget, in terms of time or tool calls, without any feedback, results in considerable increases for some of the models but not for others. We find that how much such a loop helps depends on which model plays which role, but weaker models generally do not improve stronger models.

title: Role-based Effectiveness of an Epistemic Uncertainty Estimate in Training Models for Semantic Segmentation of 3D LiDAR Point Clouds
abstract: Point cloud segmentation is a fundamental task in 3D data analysis, with applications across robotics, augmented and virtual reality, and remote sensing. However, the inherent sparsity, noise, and unordered nature of point clouds introduce significant challenges, particularly in achieving reliable classification. While the state-of-the-art rely on training models for explicit modeling of uncertainty, there is a gap in exploring different roles that estimated uncertainty using generative approaches can play. This work investigates the impact of deterministic uncertainty in point cloud segmentation by explicitly modeling epistemic uncertainty and using it in different roles, namely, as a feature and in loss function. We evaluate a baseline artificial neural network (ANN) and two uncertainty-aware variants (uncertainty as an additional input feature and as a per-sample confidence weight in the training loss) on four large-scale LiDAR benchmarks spanning airborne and mobile acquisition, namely ISPRS Vaihingen, AHN3, Paris-Lille-3D, and Toronto-3D, together with PointNet++ and RandLA-Net references and their uncertainty-augmented counterparts under canonical spatially disjoint train and test splits. Under this protocol, uncertainty-aware modeling improves mean Intersection over Union, recovers minority classes that the baseline ANN never predicts at all, and in half of the configurations improves the alignment between prediction error and estimated uncertainty as measured by Patch Accuracy versus Patch Uncertainty. Our findings indicate that uncertainty can play multiple roles in the segmentation pipeline rather than as a device for improving accuracy alone.

title: ChangeJEPA: Predict Before You Compare for Remote Sensing Change Detection
abstract: Remote sensing change detection is typically formulated as Siamese feature comparison, where two images are encoded independently and a decoder determines which discrepancies correspond to meaningful change. This is challenging because the encoders preserve both true scene changes and nuisance variations such as illumination, seasonal, radiometric, and geometric differences. We introduce ChangeJEPA, a bitemporal joint-embedding predictive architecture that reformulates change detection as latent post-state prediction. Given a pre-change image and partial post-change evidence, ChangeJEPA predicts the full post-change representation under two complementary conditions: a prior hypothesis derived from the pre-change scene and an updated hypothesis conditioned on observed post-change context. A joint-embedding predictive loss aligns both hypotheses with the target latent representation, encouraging semantic consistency while suppressing transient appearance variations. Change is then inferred from the disagreement among the pre-change representation, the observed post-change target, and the predicted latent states, capturing complementary evidence of change, prior surprise, contextual update, and prediction reliability. Across SYSU-CD, LEVIR-CD+, and CDD, ChangeJEPA consistently outperforms its decoder matched Siamese baseline by up to 1.51 IoU points and achieves the best IoU and F1-score on all three benchmarks, demonstrating the advantage of latent post-state prediction over direct feature comparison. Page: https://buddhi19.github.io/ChangeJEPA

title: What Do We Mean When We Say'F*ck AI'?: Moral Panic, Semantic Indeterminacy, and the Reification of Techno-Capitalism
abstract: Academic and (increasingly) public resistance to artificial intelligence (AI) often blurs the line between legitimate critique of techno-capitalist exploitation and (inflated) existential risk. Moreover, discourse around AI can sometimes resemble a "moral panic" where an apparently clear and identifiable scapegoat is targeted in lieu of the complex systemic problems that are causing (genuine and justified) social anxieties. However, AI is not a monolith. In this paper, we explore the environmental, political, and socio-technical consequences of the semantic indeterminacy of discourse about "AI" in conjunction with the increasing moral panic encompassing these technologies. We argue that since the umbrella term "AI" lacks a coherent, singular referent, the moral panic about AI inadvertently reifies the concept of an autonomous, singular agent with inherent and often autonomous tendencies, which aligns with corporate narratives. Hence, well-intentioned critique, activist pushback, and public protest paradoxically amplifies hype-based discussions of AI, thus validating the "threat" narrative that tech leaders deploy to exaggerate their products' capabilities and market value, further consolidating and centralising their political and socio-economic power. Moreover, if "AI" does not refer to a unified class of technologies, then policy intended to govern "AI" will systematically (and necessarily) fail. We conclude by proposing ways forward to improve AI literacy, enforce accountability, and repurpose existing regulation in order to imagine a more positive AI future.

title: Learning vs. Optimizing Players in Budgeted Games
abstract: We study repeated general games over $T$ rounds between a utility-maximizing optimizer and a learning agent, where budget constraints couple the players' decisions across rounds. Without budgets, low swap regret simultaneously guarantees the learner sublinear regret and caps the optimizer at its Stackelberg value. Budgets break this picture: adversarial no-regret becomes impossible, so the natural goals are non-manipulability---no adaptive optimizer earns more than $\mathtt{BSE} \cdot T + o(T)$, where $\mathtt{BSE}$ is its Budgeted Stackelberg Equilibrium value---and low stochastic regret when the optimizer plays a fixed mixed strategy. We give an efficient, budget-feasible learning algorithm that achieves both goals in every budgeted game: any adaptive optimizer, budgeted or not, earns at most $\mathtt{BSE} \cdot T + O(\sqrt{T})$ in expectation, and if the optimizer plays a fixed mixed strategy on each of a constant number of intervals, the learner has $O(\sqrt{T})$ regret on each such interval. Our learner best responds to forecasts of the optimizer's play that are calibrated in two novel senses, since under budgets the calibration that prevents manipulation no longer yields low stochastic regret. Response calibration, which conditions on the learner's own mixed response by embedding its continuous mixing weight as a step function in $L^2([-1,1])$, prevents manipulation without discretizing responses; dual-weighted Lagrangian calibration ensures low regret. Although low calibration error requires randomized forecasts---distributions over a continuous space that need not have a succinct representation or be directly computable---we construct such forecasts in polynomial time by simulating online gradient ascent.

title: Exploring the Privacy--Size Tradeoff for Differentially Private Self-Attentive Variational Autoencoders
abstract: Data tends to be most useful when it is shared, and the data most worth sharing is often the data that privacy obligations restrict. Synthetic data from a generator trained under differential privacy (DP) is one way to reconcile the two, but its utility depends on the privacy budget $\varepsilon$ and on how much data the generator sees - a parameter that most data sharing applications of synthetic data control. We present SAVANT, a self-attentive variational autoencoder for tabular data trained with DP-SGD that, to our knowledge, is the first to combine attention, a VAE, and DP in one tabular model. We evaluate it against two marginal mechanisms, PrivBayes and MST, jointly over the privacy budget and the dataset size on two public datasets, measuring the utility a downstream classifier loses by training on synthetic rather than real data. We find that, under the same DP guarantee, more data generally means more utility. For the marginal mechanisms it absorbs most of what a strict budget costs, and a noise-scaling argument suggests DP-SGD exchanges data fo budget at a worse rate. Two independent membership-inference attacks, judged against a measured null, found no aggregate membership signal.

title: Anduin: A sybil-resistant agentic marketplace reputation system
abstract: As autonomous AI agents enter permissionless onchain markets, selecting new service providers remains a core challenge. Existing reputation systems depend on scarce resources like human curation, identity credentials, or voluntary reviews, while naive volume rankings are vulnerable to Sybil attacks. We evaluate whether existing onchain payment histories can yield provider ratings that are resilient against Sybil attacks. Using a 157-day dataset comprising 66M agentic transactions worth $6.1M across 16 blockchains, we model payment flows as a bipartite graph between buyers and providers. A provider's rating is derived from graph paths linked to a buyer's existing trusted network. We propose three Sybil-resistant rating algorithms: a max-flow rating and two relaxed algorithms optimized for stronger rating performance. Evaluating these algorithms against simulated adversaries across 813 buyers, we show that rating manipulation costs 20% of those buyers' total spend and is around 23x harder to manipulate than the standard similarity rule (collaborative filtering).

title: Distinguishing Initial-Condition and Model Error Using Machine-Learning Weather Models
abstract: Differentiable weather models allow atmospheric initial conditions to be directly optimized to shadow a known trajectory, which we take from a reanalysis dataset. Here, we extend this optimization to include the forecast model, GraphCast, using low-rank adaptation (LoRA). We compare model optimization with initial-condition (IC) optimization, and then joint optimization, where both are tuned simultaneously. When compared against a control forecast initialized with reanalysis data, LoRA and IC optimization individually produce similar improvements. We find similar results when IC and LoRA are jointly optimized across a spectrum of solutions where a tuning coefficient smoothly shifts the weight of the joint optimization from all-LoRA to all-IC; forecast improvement is not unique to the relative contributions of model and IC corrections. To better discriminate the source of error, we introduce a second model, Pangu-Weather, as a supervisor that gates IC updates during joint optimization. This gated optimization is the same as before, except that IC updates at each epoch are accepted only when they improve the forecasts of both models; otherwise, only the LoRA update is accepted. Results show that this cross-model constraint substantially improves agreement between the two models in their response to the same optimized ICs, narrowing the gap in mean forecast error reduction from 64% to 10%. Moreover, when used together, the LoRA and IC corrections from the gated optimization yield GraphCast forecast improvements similar to those from the ungated optimization. These results imply that model error that is encoded in the ungated ICs is shifted to the LoRA corrections via gating, yielding IC corrections that may provide better analysis estimates.

title: Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization for Autonomous AI Agents
abstract: Autonomous software agents can act through tools, delegate work, and change their models or execution environments while earlier authorizations remain in flight. We present Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization (ACCA), an approach designed to be harness-independent, for maintaining operational authority according to currently justified assurance. It distinguishes evidence validity from contextual applicability, derives assurance claims from eligible evidence, and resolves a multidimensional effective-authority envelope within a principal-declared ceiling and applicable policy. A typed dependency graph supports selective re-evaluation of authorization-relevant changes. An authority epoch changes when effective authority changes; a distinct optional authorization-basis version supports revalidation of action-specific authorization conditions. Protected effect-time enforcement can reject stale actions before a consequential resource change, subject to the available commit mechanism. A compositional Domain Governance Profile expresses domain-specific semantics without granting authority. Controlled scenario tests implemented as a regression suite using a trading profile exercise default-deny rules, evidence-conditioned contraction and recovery, policy divergence, selective non-response, and stale-action rejection at a local gateway before the simulated-broker boundary. The study establishes implementation-level evidence in one domain, not a cross-domain guarantee of harmful-behavior prevention.

title: Spatio-Temporal Multi-Order Interaction for Video Recognition
abstract: Many temporal approaches for video recognition rely on explicit cross-channel aggregation projections, which have quadratic complexity in the number of channels, introducing significant computational overhead. In addition, the spatio-temporal representation used for video recognition is biased either toward local order interactions (for CNNs) or toward global order interactions (for transformers). Starting from the multi-order spatial representation of MogaNet, our method introduces two complementary contributions to tackle these problems. First, for the temporal modelling, we introduce parallel multi-order processing with depthwise-only convolutions and implicit gating-based aggregation, which is linear in the number of channels, inducing a considerable computational reduction. Second, we propose a dual interaction between spatial and temporal dimensions, which allows a better spatio-temporal representation without increasing the computational cost. By combining these two contributions, our proposed VideoMogaNet achieves performance on par with or better than state-of-the-art action recognition approaches across multiple video benchmarks (UCF101, HMDB51, Kinetics-400, Diving48), while considerably reducing the cost of the temporal branch.

title: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
abstract: First-principles defect calculations can now be performed autonomously by AI agents, enabled by established computational methods and open-source Python toolkits. However, reliable and repeatable defect calculations require clear scientific and technical guidance that helps agents resolve ambiguities and avoid errors in calculation setup, execution, postprocessing, and analysis. Here, we present DefectSkills, a set of structured prompts that provides human-in-the-loop guidance to AI agents performing first-principles calculations of point defects in semiconductors and insulators using the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP). The prompts encode human expertise and guide agents through unit-cell relaxation, electronic-structure and dielectric calculations, phase-stability and chemical-potential analysis, charged-defect supercell generation and calculations, finite-size corrections, formation-energy calculations and thermodynamic analysis, and data backup. By packaging this expertise as reusable agent skills, DefectSkills supports consistent workflow execution across agentic AI systems and reproducible defect calculations.

title: How Do Artificial Agents Make Decisions in Light of Visual Data?
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated significant advances in reasoning with visual data, which is particularly important given that much of human knowledge is encoded visually in scientific articles and other sources. However, a gap remains in understanding how artificial agents, powered by VLMs, perceive and navigate decision-making under uncertainty in the presence of visual data. This study explores this gap by evaluating and analyzing autonomous decision-making processes. Building upon prior work in visualization literacy and decision theory, we conducted two complementary studies: one examining how agents perceive and quantify uncertainty encoded in visualizations, and another investigating how artificial agents make decisions based on visual data in the form of images. We analyzed perception accuracy and decision performance across models and visualization types. Our results show that GPT-4o demonstrates the highest accuracy in perceiving uncertainty in pie and bar charts among the tested models. For decision-making, autonomous agents showed the best alignment with rational decision theory when uncertainty was represented through circle charts, icon arrays, or text.

title: Toward an Optimal Configuration for Tree Species Classification from Bark Images: A Leakage-Safe Ablation Study
abstract: Background: The automatic identification of tree species from bark photographs is of practical interest for forestry inventory and the wood-processing industry, yet the design choices that govern the accuracy of deep-learning approaches have not been studied systematically, and some prior results may be inflated by leakage of images of the same trunk across training and test partitions. Methods: A systematic ablation study is conducted on the public BarkNet 1.0 dataset (20 species) under the established tree-level, leakage-safe partitioning scheme. Using ConvNeXt-V2 backbones, the following factors are varied in turn and evaluated by five-fold cross-validation: patch size, the strategy by which per-patch predictions are aggregated into an image-level decision, the training regime (single- versus two-stage), backbone capacity, the whole-image baseline, and the number of patches available at inference. Results: Per-patch accuracy rises monotonically with patch size (from 75.6% at 160 px to 89.6% at 512 px), and image-level accuracy rises in step, plateauing near 94.9% around 512 px. Learned aggregation exceeds majority voting by at most 0.7 pp, an advantage that shrinks as patches grow and attention becomes near-uniform. Backbone capacity (pico to tiny) alters accuracy by less than a point, and two-stage training offers no advantage over one-stage. Whole-image classification (91.9%) trails patch-based aggregation, since it admits no bag to average over; accuracy increases with the number of patches at inference, saturating around 64. Conclusions: The study yields a simple recommended configuration: patches as large as possible while leaving enough to average over (around 512 px here), with a nano backbone. It also quantifies the second-order role of learned aggregation and model capacity, providing a reproducible reference point for practitioners and future research

title: Decentralized Impedance Specifications for Grid-Connected Converters: a Sequence-Domain Gershgorin Method, and a Frequency-Wise Framework for Combining Different Criteria
abstract: In complex grid scenarios, with many power electronics (PE) converters connected, having specifications for converters can ease the design process. A practical approach is to impose the specifications on the converter's small-signal impedance in the frequency domain. This is advantageous since impedance is a physical property that can be measured. This paper focuses on providing decentralized impedance specifications for each converter connected to an ac bus. With decentralized specifications, each converter has its own specifications, which are independent of other converters' impedance. This enables a competitive multi-vendor environment while guaranteeing system stability. Existing methods of imposing decentralized specifications, based on the small-gain, passivity and Gershgorin theorems, are formulated within a common frequency-domain framework. Building on this, two new solutions that reduce the conservativeness of the specifications are proposed. First, Gershgorin-based decentralized specifications are formulated in the modified sequence domain. Second, a framework for combining different specification types across frequency ranges is developed and mathematically proven. The methods are compared on examples covering sub-synchronous and harmonic-range interactions of grid-following converters, grid-forming converters, and a mixed grid-forming/grid-following system, using analytical models, black-box impedance measurements, and time-domain responses obtained from simulations and an experimental setup.

title: Efficient Gaussian Process Modeling for Large Replicated and Censored Data in Industrial Research
abstract: Gaussian process regression is widely used for modeling responses in both physical and computer experiments. In practice, data from physical experiments may include replications and be subject to censoring due to equipment limitations or contextual constraints, and such datasets can be large, posing a scalability challenge for standard Gaussian process inference. Motivated by a real-world industrial research study, we develop a Gaussian process modeling framework that efficiently analyzes large replicated and censored data. Our approach integrates a Vecchia approximation for computational scalability with a likelihood-based formulation that fully exploits replication and rigorously incorporates information from censored observations, analogous to exact simulation from truncated distributions. Through experiments on synthetic data and a real case study from industrial research, we demonstrate that the proposed method yields improved predictive accuracy and reliable uncertainty quantification compared to existing approaches, making it well suited for large-scale applications with structured replication and incomplete data.

title: CoReFlow: Consistency-Relaxed Flow Maps for Probabilistic Traffic Forecasting
abstract: Probabilistic traffic forecasting is essential for reliable Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), as it captures uncertainties in complex road networks. Recent diffusion- and flow-based generative models have facilitated uncertainty modeling through a multi-step sampling process. However, beyond slow inference, this process is designed to capture complex multimodal distributions, which misaligns with the limited complexity of the conditional traffic data distribution, causing models to underperform deterministic baselines. To address this, we introduce the \underline{Co}nsistency-\underline{Re}laxed \underline{Flow} Map (CoReFlow) model, presenting the first effort to leverage the one-step generation capability of flow maps, known as solution operators of probability-flow ordinary differential equations. Besides, we improve accuracy using a concise training objective that supervises the model via interpolation endpoints over finite time intervals. Unlike existing methods (e.g., self-distillation and MeanFlow Identity) that maintain trajectory consistency to model multimodal distributions, our objective leverages conditional mean to restrict the consistency, thereby achieving higher accuracy in the probabilistic traffic forecasting task. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets show CoReFlow achieves state-of-the-art forecasting accuracy. It surpasses recent baselines, provides competitive uncertainty modeling, and reduces inference costs compared to existing generative baselines.

title: Constraining Ganymede's Interior Structure and Bulk Composition from Its Present-Day Magnetic Field Strength
abstract: Ganymede is the only Solar System satellite with a global magnetic field driven by a core dynamo. Although its small moment-of-inertia (MoI) factor indicates a differentiated structure of a metallic core, rocky mantle, and outer hydrosphere, its exact bulk composition and layer thicknesses remain highly uncertain. We developed a comprehensive, long-term thermochemical evolution model that couples thermal history with magnetic field generation. Building upon previous theoretical frameworks, this study systematically evaluates how diverse chondritic precursor compositions constrain Ganymede's internal thermochemical evolution and core solidification processes. Based on interior structures initially permitted by a wide range of chondritic compositions and geodetic constraints, we applied the observed equatorial surface magnetic field strength ($\sim$719 nT) as a dynamic filter. Our evolutionary simulations demonstrate that while magnetic dynamos can operate under entire melting, Fe-snow, and FeS-layer regimes, the requirement to sustain the observed field strength strongly restricts the viable interior models. Satisfying this constraint preferentially requires a relatively large core radius and a specific, non-eutectic bulk core sulfur concentration. Consequently, this coupled thermochemical approach highlights the main novelty of this study: characterizing the hydrosphere's density serves as an independent constraint to break the structural degeneracy of Ganymede's bulk composition. Our model indicates that L and CI chondrites yield parameter spaces capable of sustaining comparable field strengths under a low-density hydrosphere scenario (1,200 kg m-3), whereas the H chondrite composition can satisfy this criterion under a high-density scenario (1,300 kg m-3). These predictions provide a critical framework to be tested by the JUICE mission arriving in 2031.

title: Generative Modeling for Cascading Extremes via Autoregressive Transformers
abstract: Extreme events often occur sequentially, from earthquake-tsunami cascades to successive extreme losses in financial markets. We introduce an extremal token representation that encodes multivariate observations as a categorical sequence. A quiet token records the absence of threshold exceedances; otherwise, the token identifies the exceeding component with the largest marginal probability-scale score. The representation is invariant to componentwise strictly increasing transformations. It preserves the identity and temporal ordering of dominant exceedances but discards their magnitudes and the identities of nondominant simultaneous exceedances. A decoder-only transformer estimates the history-dependent next-token kernel on this representation, and recursive sampling generates future token sequences from the induced joint predictive law. We amortize our generative model by pretraining across simulated process families with varying parameters and dependence persistence. Next-token predictions are evaluated against exact conditional probabilities for held-out categorical processes and particle filter references for heavy-tailed vector autoregressive processes. Applied to ten-second returns for five semiconductor stocks, the pretrained model supports zero-shot transfer, while a few epochs of adaptation improve agreement between observed and generated token frequencies and transition patterns. These results support task-specific tokenization and simulation-based pretraining for modeling which dimensions dominate multivariate extremes.

title: The Male Abstraction Bias in Internet Culture and Large Language Models
abstract: Conceptual abstraction and gender are two equally central aspects of the human mind, yet they have traditionally been studied in isolation from one another, as though they were fundamentally separate. Here, we find gender and abstraction are systematically linked throughout the space of concepts spanning single (N = 40,000) and multi-word expressions (N = 67,000): across billions of words and millions of images on the internet --- and across numerous measurement techniques, including human and AI classifications --- more abstract concepts are more associated with men, a pattern we show replicates in languages around the world. This male abstraction bias not only holds across semantic domains, but it also maps onto grammatical structure: verbs and adverbs are more abstract and more male-coded, revealing a system-wide trace of stereotypes accentuating agentic qualities in men. Furthermore, we show this bias readily emerges in the free associations humans and AIs produce in controlled online tasks, indicating its psychological internalization and its algorithmic reproduction. These findings identify a latent structure in conceptual space that unifies a range of stereotypes: for example, framings of women as more embodied, emotional, and warm, versus men as more cognitive, rational, and competent; as well as erroneous views of men as better at mathematics, science, and engineering. More broadly, by analyzing an unprecedentedly large, multimodal sample of online data, we provide culture-wide evidence of gender as a core organizing principle shaping conceptual space far beyond the characterization of people and social roles.

title: Self-Supervised Learning of Universal Latent Spaces for Operator Learning
abstract: Neural operators fit their representation of functions to the task they are trained on, so every new task rebuilds a reduced space from labeled data. Following the self-supervised pre-training that made representations shareable in natural language processing and computer vision, we decouple representation learning from operator learning. A functional autoencoder is pre-trained on analytic functions synthesized on the fly, with no solver and no labels, to represent functions on arbitrary point clouds, and the latent space it induces is frozen and reused across tasks. The representation is exactly equivariant to translation, dilation, and amplitude, and reconstructs solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) and natural images on geometries it never saw. Being task-agnostic, the latent space can be interpreted in its own right. The whole space is used and decodes to valid fields, it preserves the ordering of distances between physical fields, its geodesics interpolate physical evolutions, and edit directions transfer across fields. With frozen representation maps, a dataset is encoded once and a neural operator is trained entirely on cached embeddings, which saves memory and training time. On 28 tasks in fluid dynamics, solid mechanics, acoustics, and the Helmholtz and Poisson equations, this paradigm can exceed the accuracy of state-of-the-art end-to-end architectures, with up to an order of magnitude higher throughput and memory savings that fit models nearly two orders of magnitude larger on consumer-grade GPUs. At inference, latent rollouts run up to an order of magnitude faster than regular rollouts, and chunked inference processes functions of over half a billion points on a single consumer-grade GPU.

title: OdorSpaces: Visual-Olfactory Embodied Navigation in 3D Environments
abstract: Olfaction provides critical information about airborne chemical cues, yet it remains largely underexplored in embodied AI, with limited prior machine olfaction work focusing primarily on semantic odor perception. We introduce OdorSpaces, a physics-based simulation platform and benchmark for visual-olfactory embodied navigation. OdorSpaces augments Habitat-Sim with 3D odor transport and dispersion simulated by Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS), enabling agents to navigate photorealistic indoor environments using both visual and olfactory observations. The benchmark includes two representative source-seeking scenarios: invisible gas-leak localization and early-stage fire localization. We develop an initial multimodal reinforcement learning policy that integrates visual observations and olfactory measurements over time. Experiments show that the policy outperforms a diverse set of baselines, establishing a strong reference for future research on visual-olfactory embodied navigation.

title: GRASP: Gradient-Guided Sampling for Contact-Rich Physics-Based Motion Retargeting
abstract: We study physics-based retargeting of human demonstrations for robot learning: finding robot controls that reproduce reference motions under contact dynamics. We propose GRASP (Gradient Recovery from Archived Samples for Proposals), which combines sampling-based exploration with gradient-guided refinement without requiring a differentiable simulator. GRASP-TO extends tempered sequential Monte Carlo by fitting local quadratic cost models to archived rollouts and using their gradients to guide Markov chain Monte Carlo rejuvenation. Metropolis-Hastings correction preserves the target distribution for each fixed proposal kernel, and a population analysis connects the recovered gradients to Gaussian smoothing. GRASP-MPC scales this optimizer to long demonstrations through warm-started receding-horizon planning. Experiments on dexterous hands and humanoids show accurate retargeting with a shared tracking objective and no task-specific contact rewards, including 92.8% success on 1352 bimanual OakInk2 demonstrations. The refined references improve PPO tracking in pen spinning and humanoid-object interaction. We also demonstrate dexterous manipulation and whole-body humanoid motion on real hardware.

title: PAYWORTHY: Can LLMs Predict Which Freelance Jobs an AI Agent Will Complete?
abstract: Before an AI agent takes on a paid job, someone has to judge whether it is likely to succeed. We test whether frontier language models can make this call before any attempt. We propose PAYWORTHY which contains 1{,}494 real freelance job postings, sampled from 18.8M postings made between 2020 and 2026 on a freelancing platform. An agent attempts each job from the posting alone in a single run, and an LLM judge acting as the client decides whether to accept the work. We ask 18 models to forecast how likely the agent is to succeed and measure how well each model's forecasts rank the accepted jobs above the rejected ones (AUC, where 0.5 is a random ranking). The answer depends on how the agent is described. Told what the agent cannot do, every model ranks the jobs well (AUC 0.66--0.86). Told instead that it is a generic agent with a browser and code execution, the same models rank the same jobs about as well as a random ordering (0.45--0.56). These results hold under judges from four other model families (Claude, GLM, Kimi and Qwen), and the informed forecasts also rank the verdicts of two human raters. Code is available at https://github.com/upwork/Payworthy

title: How to Look Inside the Black Box: A Survey of Yu. E. Nesterov's Contributions (On the Award of the 2026 Gauss Prize)
abstract: On July 23, 2026, at the opening of the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia, the International Mathematical Union announced the award of the Gauss Prize to Yurii Evgenievich Nesterov -- an award for mathematical work with significant applications outside mathematics. This article explains the mathematical content of the recognized work of Yu. E. Nesterov and traces its influence on modern computational practice. The exposition is based on a concept that Yu. E. Nesterov himself regards as one of his main results: the classical complexity theory of convex optimization is oriented toward a black-box oracle, but its pessimistic bounds can be overcome by using a priori information about the internal structure of the objective function. We trace Yu. E. Nesterov's scientific career, then introduce the language of oracle complexity together with a classification of objective function models (geometric, algebraic, and structural), and subsequently discuss his main results in chronological order: the fast gradient method, fast automatic differentiation, the theory of self-concordant barriers and polynomial-time interior-point methods, the $π/2$ theorem, the stable dynamics model of traffic flows, the smoothing technique, primal-dual methods, cubic regularization of Newton's method, the modified Gauss--Newton scheme, coordinate descent methods and methods for huge-scale problems, gradient-free methods, universal gradient methods, implementable tensor methods, and "superfast" methods. Each topic is accompanied by historical background, precise statements specifying the problem class, oracle, and type of guarantee, examples, and a discussion of the current state of the art.

title: Research on the Practice of Organic Dryland Agriculture and Rural Revitalization Model in Lingqiu County
abstract: Lingqiu County is located in the northeast of Shanxi Province, at the southeast end of Datong City, in the golden growth zone of crops at latitude 38 ° -39 ° N. It is an important production area for high-quality small grain crops in North China and a demonstration county for organic dryland agriculture in Shanxi Province. Since 2013, based on its ecological endowment, Lingqiu County has identified organic agriculture as an important direction for its economic development. After more than a decade of continuous exploration, it has gradually embarked on a rural revitalization path that balances ecological protection and industrial development. This article systematically reviews the development process, practical path, and comprehensive effectiveness of organic dryland agriculture in Lingqiu County, and analyzes its model characteristics from four dimensions: planning guidance, technological support, industrial integration, and brand building. Research shows that Lingqiu County, led by Chehe Village, has achieved a transformation from single point testing to global promotion through mechanisms such as village enterprise cooperation, school land collaboration, and tertiary industry linkage. There are 133 certified organic varieties in the county, and the total output value of organic agriculture exceeds 570 million yuan. The per capita income of villagers in Chehe Organic Community has significantly increased. The practical experience of Lingqiu has certain reference value for developing ecological agriculture and promoting economic transformation in underdeveloped areas and ecological functional zones.

title: Application of UAV Remote Sensing in Crop Detection
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) remote sensing has become an important means of accurate detection of crops because of its high spatial-temporal resolution, flexibility, and cost control. This paper systematically summarizes the research progress of UAV Remote Sensing Application in crop detection. Firstly, the principles of mainstream sensors such as multispectral, hyperspectral, thermal infrared, visible light, and lidar and their application characteristics in agricultural monitoring are summarized. Secondly, focusing on the main tasks of pest identification, lodging monitoring, weed detection, and soil moisture monitoring, the retrieval methods based on different sensors are sorted out. On this basis, the advantages, disadvantages, and application scope of physical model and machine learning inversion models are compared. Research shows that the combination of multi-source sensor fusion and machine learning models significantly improves detection accuracy, but it still faces challenges such as poor model generalization ability, high sensor cost, and complex data processing. In the future, it should promote the coordinated development of UAV remote sensing, satellite and aerial remote sensing, and build a multi-scale, all-weather agricultural monitoring system.
journal: Academic Journal of Science and Technology

title: A Comparative Analysis of Volatility Predictions via EGARCH, Transformer and Hybrid EGARCH-Transformer Models: Changes in Forecasting Ability after Introducing Sentiment Factors
abstract: The application of cryptocurrency asset volatility forecasting is relevant for real‑world risk‑management procedures and derivatives pricing in the digital‑asset market. This paper assesses out-of-sample forecast performance for three model families: standalone EGARCH, vanilla Transformer, and an EGARCH‑Transformer combined hybrid architecture for forecasting Bitcoin volatility. Another goal is to measure whether there is any actual marginal forecasting benefit from investor sentiment obtained from the Reddit posts. We use information from Reddit with the subreddit r/Bitcoin from 25th March 2021 to 30th December 2024. We collaborate with the open-source ProsusAI/finbert language model that has been trained for financial text tasks to construct a daily sentiment score based on the number of upvotes given to the post‑comment. In the hybrid model we constructed, the one-step-ahead conditional-variance values produced by EGARCH are used as other features as input to the Transformer network. The results from controlled feature-ablation tests show that, in general, using structured volatility inputs (volatility realized from volatility inputs) and EGARCH conditional volatility outputs yield better forecasts. Social media sentiment data of investors, by comparison, has mixed results. Under specific combinations of features, sentiment boosts the accuracy of predictions, but in other experimental settings, it hinders the accuracy of predictions. We have problems consistently filtering subjective signals from forum text by retail investors with our hybrid EGARCH‑Transformer implementation. Results indicate that the performance of hybrid models is much more influenced by the composition of the input features and quality of the raw data than by adding additional predictor variables to the network.
journal: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Determinants of Cloud Storage Adoption in Indonesia: Integrating Positive Valence, Security, and Trust
abstract: Cloud storage adoption in Indonesia remains under-researched, and prevailing technology-adoption models generally assume that user trust is a robust antecedent of adoption intention. Drawing on the positive Valence Framework, this study integrates two positive utility constructs—perceived ubiquity and perceived benefits—with security and trust to explain behavioral intention to adopt cloud storage. Survey data from 202 digitally literate Indonesian internet users were collected through Google Forms and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM); common method bias was assessed using Harman’s single-factor test and a full collinearity (VIF) assessment. Perceived benefits exerted the strongest effect on behavioral intention, followed by security and perceived ubiquity, whereas trust had no significant effect. Theoretically, the non-significance of trust indicates that, in an ecosystem dominated by a few globally legitimate providers embedded in users’ device platforms, trust operates as an assumed baseline rather than a differentiating criterion. This reframes trust from a direct antecedent to a boundary-conditioned, hygiene-type factor and refines the applicability of Valence- and TAM/UTAUT-based adoption models to developing digital markets.
journal: Journal of ICT Research and Applications

title: Hybrid and Classical Machine Learning Models for Mixed-crop Recommendation in Precision Agriculture: An Empirical Performance Analysis
abstract: Precise mixed-crop recommendation is essential for increasing agricultural productivity, improving land utilization, and supporting sustainable farming. Effective crop combinations depend on several environmental and soil factors, making accurate recommendations a challenging task. This study compared classical and hybrid machine learning approaches for mixed-crop recommendation using an indigenous dataset from Andhra Pradesh, India. The dataset consisted of seven key features: nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, temperature, humidity, pH, and rainfall. The study evaluated Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbor (K-NN), Decision Tree (DT), Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), and Extra Trees (ET), alongside a proposed hybrid Random Forest-Extra Trees (RF-ET) model. Performance was measured using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, k-fold cross-validation, and confusion matrix analysis. The results show that the proposed hybrid RF-ET model achieved the best performance, obtaining 95.91% accuracy, 95.98% precision, 95.91% recall, and 95.94% F1-score. The model also demonstrated strong robustness through cross-validation. These findings indicate that hybrid machine learning can significantly improve the accuracy and reliability of mixed-crop recommendation systems, providing farmers with better decision-support tools for sustainable and efficient agricultural production.
journal: Journal of ICT Research and Applications

title: AI-Enhanced Competency-Based Learning Approaches for Developing Advanced Problem-Solving Skills in Agricultural Education Postgraduate Programmes
abstract: Driven by severe climate pressures, resource scarcity, and the urgent demand for sustainable intensification, the modern agricultural landscape has grown exceptionally complex, making the development of advanced problem-solving skills among postgraduate students an absolute necessity for sector innovation and practice. To bridge the limitations of traditional educational methods, this study evaluated Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enhanced competency-based learning approaches tailored for postgraduate agricultural education programmes. The research comprehensively explored foundational definitions and models including AI in education, competency-based frameworks, and advanced problem-solving attributes while outlining specific core competencies, pedagogical strategies, and a structured implementation framework. Concluding that AI-driven, competency-focused methodologies are vital to maintaining transformative, industry-responsive curricula that yield highly skilled researchers and educators, the study recommended that postgraduate programs proactively integrate these AI technologies, modernize curricula with digital and climate-smart agricultural practices, upskill academic staff, invest heavily in infrastructure, and systematically monitor program relevance to align with shifting industry demands.
journal: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY

title: Human resource development through ESG-oriented agricultural training: Knowledge outcomes in IoT-assisted and conventional irrigation settings
abstract: Background: The social pillar of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) emphasizes human resource development, yet evidence on ESG-oriented agricultural training in non-farming urban communities remains limited. This study assesses changes in knowledge following an ESG-oriented agricultural training program and examines whether IoT-assisted infrastructure is associated with differential knowledge gains. Methods: A quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test design without a control group was employed among 20 female community beneficiaries across two sites in Batam, Indonesia, Barelang (IoT-assisted drip irrigation) and Nongsa (conventional irrigation). A purpose-built 25-item binary (yes/no) self-assessment instrument was administered before and after training, covering four domains; land preparation, plant maintenance, IoT and smart farming, and digital marketing. Participant baseline characteristics were collected separately. Findings: Mean scores increased significantly from 10.70 (SD = 4.71) to 22.20 (SD = 2.33) out of 25 (W = 210.0, p-value < 0.001). Plant maintenance and digital marketing showed substantial gains increasing from 11.7% to 93.3% and from 35.0% to 94.0% suggesting that applied training was accessible across educational backgrounds. However, the IoT domain diverged sharply: Barelang gained +3.35 items of 5 reaching near-perfect comprehension, while Nongsa declined by −0.33 items, which may indicate a possible response-shift phenomenon whereby theoretical instruction without hands-on technology exposure heightened awareness of knowledge limitations rather than consolidating applied competency. The small sample (n = 20) limits generalisability. Conclusion: Participants reported significantly higher self-assessed knowledge after ESG agricultural training regardless of educational diversity, while IoT-related outcomes appeared to differ by infrastructure access. Novelty/Originality of this article: This study contributes to the ESG literature by examining whether IoT infrastructure access is associated with human resource.
journal: Interaction, Community Engagement, and Social Environment

title: Sugarcane Yield Prediction Using Machine Learning in Sentinel-2 and Google Earth Engine for Andhra Pradesh, India
Beyond Single-fault Testing: Evaluating Ai Sre Agents Under Compound Production Incidents
Continuous Risk-adaptive Authorization for Ai Agents – Evaluating Adaptive Authorization and Risk Control (aarc) with Nist Mapping
Digital Decision Support for Smallholder Farmers using Explainable Multi Criteria Agricultural Intelligence
abstract: Under uncertain weather, fluctuating prices, constrained liquidity and limited access to advice, smallholder farmers have to make decisions on what to grow, but many digital advisory services provide a single, black-box answer that can't be questioned by farmers and extension agents. This article introduces an explainable multi-criteria decision support system which ranks candidate crops for each plot, explains in simple language the reasons for choosing a particular crop and provides confidence in the rank. A fuzzy agro-ecological suitability is combined with a water-stress yield model which incorporates Monte Carlo rainfall and price shocks, together with seven benefit and cost criteria, Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) weights and TOPSIS ranking. The closeness margin between the recommended crop and the runner-up crop is distributed in a pie chart across individual criteria and Dirichlet perturbation of the weights measures recommendation stability. All data are simulated: 20 synthetic landscapes of 40×40 plots (2.5 km cells), six crops with indicative parameters, and a hypothetical expert panel (AHP consistency ratio 0.013). The recommended crop for each landscape was groundnut on 37.5%, sorghum on 31.0% and pearl millet on 17.4%. It produced a mean net return of 210 USD/ha and has a loss probability of 18.7% under out-of-sample seasons with 25% fatter rainfall and price shocks than assumed during the design process, while a traditional rule of thumb has a mean net return of 67 USD/ha and a loss probability of 38.9%. The Shapley attributions summed exactly to the closeness margin (maximum error 5.6e-16), and the mean stability was 0.84, with 53.3% of plots above 0.9. These results demonstrate the mechanics and behaviour of the framework in a controlled setting; they are not field evidence.
journal: Journal of Smart and Sustainable Farming

title: Advanced Engineering Management for Public Services: Strategic Planning for India's Infrastructure Expansion, Asset Safety, Energy Efficiency, and Community Service Availability: A systems-based framework for integrated public works management
abstract: India is rapidly expanding infrastructure to support electrification, industry and industrialization, roads, water supply, agriculture, transport, sanitation, and other public services. As this investment creates a larger and more interconnected public asset base, its contribution to national development depends on safe operation, efficient use, reliable service, and timely maintenance. This paper develops an advanced engineering management framework that links service availability, asset safety, energy performance, condition monitoring, lifecycle cost, and long-range planning. It builds on the author's public-works concept note [1], whose core proposals are zone-wise service mapping, utility system inventories, integrated monitoring, a coordinating agency, cost comparison, future demand assessment, and a sample-village pilot. Drawing on digital utility management and procurement readiness approaches, the framework connects verified asset and service data to risk-based maintenance, coordinated work planning, efficient energy use, timely procurement, and future investment decisions. It proposes indicators for continuity, response, safety, energy, resource losses, maintenance, utilization, cost, and public feedback. Because the concept note provides no national baseline or measured outcome dataset, this paper does not claim quantified improvements. It instead shows how agencies can measure performance, protect asset safety, improve utilization of public investment, and test the approach through a pilot before scaling it.

title: A Multi-Method Diagnostic Framework for Detecting Feature–Label Independence: A Case Study on Crop Health Classification
abstract: We worked on a machine learning project to predict crop health from agronomic data. We used a real-world dataset of 212,019 field records with 32 attributes like temperature, humidity, rainfall and soil properties. Our goal was to see how well four machine learning models. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Histogram-based Gradient Boosting and XGBoost. Could predict crop health. We tested these models using a method called stratified 5fold crossvalidation and then fine-tuned the best model. The dataset only had a healthy or unhealthy label for each crop so we created a new label with five levels of severity. Surprisingly all four models performed about well as guessing the most common answer, which was not very good. We did checks to see if the data or models were the problem and it seems the data just doesn't have enough information to predict crop health. We think it's essential to share results, like this so other don't waste time on similar projects.
journal: International Journal of Data Science and IoT Management System

title: DAPHNE: A global database of pest herbivores and their natural enemies
abstract: Anticipating and managing the impact of herbivorous pests requires evidence-based knowledge about the interactions between pests and their natural enemies. Knowledge of species’ ecologies and biological interactions are typically disseminated in unstructured text across hundreds of thousands of scientific articles spanning a rapidly growing scientific literature, but manually screening this literature is time-consuming and impractical at scale. Taxonomic and geographic coverage thus remains sparse, and structured data on interactions between individual species are lacking, particularly for invertebrates. Large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as a novel and powerful text-mining tool for knowledge extraction and evidence synthesis in a wide range of scientific disciplines, including ecology and conservation. In this study, we use an open-weight, pre-trained LLM to analyse abstracts of a corpus of published material on biological pest control to obtain a global Database of Pest Herbivores and their Natural Enemies (DAPHNE). This method resulted in the extraction of 175,404 species interactions from 112,830 published pest control studies, containing 16,755 unique animal taxa resolved at the species level. Interactions include herbivory (granivory, frugivory and gall-formation), predation, parasitism and hyperparasitism, and comprise a range of additional information, such as species’ taxonomy, pest status, pest importance, natural enemy importance, provision of biocontrol, associated plants and industries, invasiveness and the vectoring of pathogens and diseases. Validation of the results shows that most data columns were extracted with high recall and precision (>90%) and comparison of DAPHNE with other sources shows a high degree of agreement, but also highlights that the dataset contains information that may have been missed by other sources. In addition to the identification of important crop pests and their natural enemies, DAPHNE may be used for a variety of use-cases, including the identification of invasive species and pathogen vectors, trophic network analysis and literature search and discovery.

title: Brazilian bryophytes: a national-scale comprehensive dataset of species richness and geographic distribution
abstract: Bryophytes (Anthocerotophyta, Marchantiophyta, and Bryophyta) remain under-sampled in large-scale biodiversity databases in Brazil, despite their ecological importance. In Brazil, Flora e Funga do Brasil recognizes 1,618 bryophyte species distributed across six biomes that are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic pressures such as deforestation, agricultural expansion, and climate change. Nevertheless, knowledge of species geographic distributions remains fragmented and based on scattered records. Flora e Funga do Brasil serves as the official taxonomic reference for the country, providing the accepted species list and serving as a baseline for biodiversity studies. However, as it was designed as a nomenclatural and taxonomic checklist, it does not integrate primary occurrence records with geographic coordinates and collection dates. Consequently, occurrence data remain dispersed across herbaria, digital repositories, and the scientific literature, without dynamic updates linked to the official checklist. This disconnect between the taxonomic framework and primary occurrence records limits macroecological and biogeographical analyses at national scales, which depend on standardized georeferenced biodiversity databases. To address this gap, we compiled 102,528 bryophyte occurrence records from herbarium specimens, using data from GBIF and the speciesLink network, complemented by field collections from the Caatinga and records from the Cryptogamic Herbarium of the State University of Piauí. All records were georeferenced and curated, including verification of inconsistent coordinates, removal of duplicates, and taxonomic standardization using Bryonames. When available, information such as collection date and collector was retained. The dataset comprises 1,820 species, 125 families, and 442 genera. Bryophyta (mosses) was the most diverse group (1,056 spp., 84 families, 310 genera), followed by Marchantiophyta (745 spp., 37 families, 124 genera) and Anthocerotophyta (19 spp., four families, seven genera). Among mosses, the most species-rich families were Sphagnaceae (79 spp.), Fissidentaceae (76 spp.), and Pottiaceae (76 spp.). Among liverworts, Lejeuneaceae dominated with 335 species, followed by Lepidoziaceae (58 spp.) and Plagiochilaceae (51 spp.). Among hornworts, Anthocerotaceae, Dendrocerotaceae, and Notothyladaceae each included six species. Regionally, the Southeast showed the highest richness (1,338 spp.), followed by the South (974 spp.), Central-West (937 spp.), Northeast (897 spp.), and North (763 spp.). Regarding biomes, the Atlantic Forest (1,523 spp.) and Amazon (1,054 spp.) were the most species-rich, followed by the Cerrado (810 spp.), Caatinga (671 spp.), Pampa (269 spp.), and Pantanal (61 spp.). These patterns reflect both ecological gradients and historical sampling biases. This dataset bridges the gap between the official taxonomic checklist and primary occurrence data by integrating multiple sources into a standardized, openly accessible database. It provides a robust tool for studies in macroecology, biogeography, and conservation, enabling analyses of spatial patterns of species richness, endemism, and taxonomic, functional, and phylogenetic diversity across environmental gradients. It also supports species distribution modeling, climate change impact assessments, biodiversity hotspot identification, and conservation planning at regional and national scales. Users are encouraged to cite this article when using the dataset and to report downstream applications derived from it. title: MERIT: Multi-agent EHR-grounded Risk Identification and Tailored Care for Early Cognitive Decline in Primary Care
abstract: Background: Dementia is frequently underdiagnosed in primary care, with fewer than half of cases identified and only 8-20% detected at early stages. Our objective is to develop an Agentic AI-powered clinical decision support systems (CDSS) maintaining the patient's virtual cognitive status and provide physicians with ready-to-use summaries and next step suggestions. Methods: We developed MERIT (Multi-agent EHR-grounded Risk Identification and Tailored Care for Early Cognitive Decline in Primary Care) via participatory co-design with primary care provider. It maintains a virtual cognitive status based on the patient's electronic health records (EHR) and conversation with the patient and provide clinical decision support based on it. Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) was employed by the system to retrieve dementia-related risk factors from multimodal EHR. Additionally, we used reflection Agentic AI design pattern to improve quality of AI Agent generated text. We used one PCP's patient data to optimize the system, then used patients from another four PCPs for testing. We mainly used expert manual evaluation based on 5-point Likert-Scales. For readability of patient summary and personalized education material, besides manual evaluation, we also employed widely used Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch We-Kincaid Grade Level. Results: MERIT has four modulars: 1) patient conversation agent; 2) patient virtual cognitive status maintainer; 3) personalized education provider; and 4) decision support provider. Our evaluation focused on the provider-facing part, which relies on EHR without involving any patient conversation. The evaluation on the testing data demonstrates good performance. On a 5-point Likert scale, in the test set, patient virtual cognitive status summaries received average scores of 4.0 (SD 0.74) for correctness, 4.2 (SD 0.59) for completeness, 4.3 (SD 0.59) for readability, and 4.1 (SD 0.71) for clinical usefulness; clinical decision support received 3.9 (SD 0.87) for correctness, 4.3 (SD 0.66) for completeness, and 4.3 (SD 0.64) for adoptability; and the personalized education material received average ratings of 4.3 (SD 0.62) for completeness, 4.5 (SD 0.60) for readability, 4.3 (SD 0.78) for usefulness, and 4.4 (SD 0.49) for empathy. Automated readability assessment showed that patient summaries had a mean Flesch Reading Ease score of 18.3 (SD 4.9) and a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 13.7 (SD 0.7), consistent with college-level text, whereas personalized patient education had a Flesch Reading Ease score of 50.1 (SD 7.1) and a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 11.7 (SD 1.5), which is high-school student understandable text. Conclusion: Our developed system MERIT can maintain a virtual cognitive status based on the patient's multimodal EHR, provide the patient with clear and readable personalized education materials, and provide the PCP with ready-to-use cognitive summaries and decision support with high adoptability. By integrating our CDSS into Epic in the near future, our developed system will largely benefit older adults with cognitive decline and slow down the progression.

title: The Myth of Mankurt and a Conceptual Framework for Digital Food Identity and Data Sovereignty in Kyrgyzstan
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of digital food identity, in which Ch. Aitmatov’s rethought myth of mankurt serves as an analytical lens to criticise digital food regimes and processes of digital mankurtisation. Using Kyrgyzstan as an illustrative documentary case, the paper examines how policy, service, and media materials frame data governance, local knowledge, and food-cultural diversity in agrifood digitalisation. The analysis identifies a potential representational and governance gap: efficiency, traceability, registries, and administrative integration are more visible in the analysed corpus than farmer data rights, local knowledge, and food-cultural practices. This finding concerns documentary representation and institutional framing; it does not demonstrate the loss of local practices or the experiences of farmers and consumers. We developed a typology of digital mankurtisation levels (epistemological, regulatory, infrastructural, and political-economic). We introduced the “field scout of data” institute as an element of humanistic digital food policy, aimed at strengthening food sovereignty and the cultural diversity of food in the digital age.

title: LED Lighting in Greenhouse Floriculture: A Critical Review of Photobiology, Spectral Optimisation, Energy Dynamics and Climate-Smart Cultivation
abstract: Light-emitting diode (LED) technology has expanded the possibilities for manipulating floral induction, plant architecture, ornamental quality and resource use in protected floriculture. Yet improvements demonstrated under controlled spectra do not necessarily translate into commercially valuable gains under variable greenhouse sunlight, nor does higher electrical efficacy automatically reduce whole-greenhouse energy demand. This critical narrative review synthesises physiological, crop-production and engineering evidence relating to supplemental and photoperiodic LED lighting, with particular attention to cut roses, chrysanthemums, gerbera and bedding ornamentals. Relevant peer-reviewed literature and methodological sources were identified through targeted searches of accessible scholarly indexes and reference tracing, with a literature cut-off of 23 August 2026. The evidence supports distinct, interacting roles for radiation quantity, spectral composition, timing and photoperiod. Red-rich spectra can favour cut-rose productivity in particular cultivar and greenhouse settings, but there is no universally optimal red-to-blue ratio. Far-red and blue radiation regulate elongation and flowering in ways strongly conditioned by photoperiodic category, baseline sunlight, developmental stage and the absolute flux of other wavelengths. Changes in the daily light integral frequently account for apparent spectral benefits, whereas flowering responses to low-intensity night interruption need not involve substantial photosynthetic energy. Greenhouse energy models show that replacement of high-pressure sodium lamps with LEDs can reduce lighting electricity while increasing heating requirements because less useful heat is emitted by the lamps. This distinction complicates claims of cost, carbon and energy savings. The review proposes a decision framework that separates photobiological effects from photon-dose effects and evaluates crop quality, timing, energy, heating, water and postharvest performance within explicit environmental and economic boundaries. Priority is given to sunlight-aware multi-factor trials, independent replication, dynamic controls and transparent, whole-system accounting. LEDs are best understood as flexible control tools rather than intrinsically climate-smart inputs; their net contribution depends on crop, climate, management and system design.
journal: International Journal of Environment and Climate Change

title: The Nexus between Natural Farming and Agroforestry: Ecological Synergies for Sustainable Agricultural Systems
abstract: Natural farming and agroforestry are frequently advanced as complementary pathways for reducing external inputs, rebuilding soil functions, diversifying production and improving resilience. Their compatibility, nevertheless, is more readily inferred from ecological principles than demonstrated by experiments that deliberately combine the two systems. This critical narrative review examines the conditions under which natural farming practices, especially the Indian zero-budget and community-managed variants, may interact with trees, shrubs, perennial crops and livestock to improve agroecosystem performance. Peer-reviewed field studies, modelling analyses, reviews and meta-analyses were appraised for their designs, comparators, causal interpretation and applicability across contrasting farming environments. Evidence supports several plausible synergies: diversified litter and root inputs can sustain soil cover and biological activity; well-designed tree canopies modify near-surface microclimates; woody habitats support some natural enemies and other biodiversity; and perennial products diversify farm income. These effects are neither additive nor universal. Nitrogen fixation cannot replace phosphorus, potassium and other nutrients removed through harvest, and trees can compete with annual crops for radiation, water and nutrients. Natural-farming experiments in southern India report comparable or improved short-term yields under specified management packages, while nutrient-budget modelling warns of potential constraints during wider adoption. Recent agroforestry syntheses show gains in soil carbon and related attributes but substantial heterogeneity and measurement weaknesses; evidence on combined natural-farming–agroforestry interventions remains particularly thin. Interpreting yield benefits requires attention to baseline input intensity, transition duration, whole-farm output, labour, crop identity, canopy geometry and habitat context. The review develops an evidence-calibrated framework distinguishing demonstrated effects of each component from interactions that require factorial testing. Priority needs are long-term replicated system comparisons, complete nutrient and greenhouse-gas budgets, biodiversity-function measurements and inclusive livelihood evaluation. Integration should therefore be treated as a context-specific design proposition rather than an inherently superior production model.
journal: Journal of Advances in Biology & Biotechnology

title: Digital Competence, Attitudes and ICT Utilisation among Agricultural Extension Personnel: A Critical Narrative Review
abstract: Agricultural extension organisations increasingly rely on information and communication technologies (ICTs) to acquire technical knowledge, coordinate fieldwork, communicate with farmers and deliver advice. Yet the possession of digital devices, favourable attitudes towards technology and effective professional use are not interchangeable achievements. This critical narrative review examines their relationships among agricultural extension personnel, with particular attention to the conditions under which digital capability becomes credible and inclusive advisory practice. Peer-reviewed empirical studies, conceptual contributions and relevant professional competence frameworks published principally from 2010 to 28 August 2026 were examined through transparent, thematic literature selection and critical appraisal. Evidence from South and South-East Asia, sub-Saharan Africa and other advisory systems indicates that many extension workers recognise the potential usefulness of ICTs, while frequently facing gaps in data-management skills, maintenance support, connectivity, training and task-specific application. Positive acceptance measures commonly coexist with limited use for diagnosis, tailored recommendations, feedback and evaluation. The literature is strongest in describing reported access, perceptions and associations; it is substantially weaker in independently measuring competence, tracing actual advisory activity or linking personnel-level digital practice with farmer outcomes. Established acceptance models explain part of the intention to use technology, but their individual emphasis incompletely captures organisational incentives, advisory ethics, local languages and the relational nature of extension. The review proposes a distinction between access, operational competence, advisory judgement, task-specific utilisation and demonstrated service quality, treating their relationships as context-dependent rather than automatic. Research priorities include validated performance-based assessments, repeated observation of professional workflows, comparative organisational studies and ethically designed evaluations of training and support packages. Digital extension policy should therefore move beyond device distribution and generic skills courses towards sustained, context-sensitive professional capability and accountable advisory service delivery.
