title: Supply Chain Analysis of Mustard in Sri Ganganagar District of Rajasthan, India: Marketing Channels, Price Spread, Efficiency and an ARIMA Forecast of Production and Productivity
abstract: Background: Mustard is an important oilseed crop in irrigated north-western Rajasthan, where marketing arrangements influence the prices received by growers. Aims: To map the mustard supply chain of Sri Ganganagar district, estimate channel-wise price spread and marketing efficiency, forecast production and productivity, and prioritise grower constraints. Study Design: Cross-sectional field survey using a linked farmer–intermediary schedule, combined with univariate time-series analysis of published secondary data. Place and Duration of Study: Sri Ganganagar district, Rajasthan, India, during the rabi mustard marketing season 2025-26. Methodology: One hundred and twenty growers (multistage sampling, six blocks) and 40 intermediaries (ten per channel, selected using purposive and snowball sampling) were interviewed. Price spread, marketing cost, margin, producer’s share and marketing efficiency were computed following Acharya’s framework; constraints were ranked by the Garrett Ranking Technique and cross-checked by the Rank-Based Quotient (RBQ). An ARIMA model was fitted to the 2000-01 to 2024-25 Rajasthan and all-India series and validated on a five-year hold-out sample. Results: Four channels were identified. The regulated market was the most-used route (36.67%), but the village-trader and commission-agent routes together accounted for 50.83% of growers, while the direct farmer–processor route was used by only 12.50%. Price spread narrowed from Rs 743/q in Channel I to Rs 388/q in Channel IV, the producer’s share rose from 89.1% to 94.2%, and marketing efficiency from 8.17 to 14.21. ARIMA (0, 1, 1) with drift was adequate for all series (Ljung–Box P = .55 and P = .80; hold-out MAPE 14.5% and 7.0%) and projects state productivity to reach 1,766 kg/ha by 2029-30. Garrett and RBQ gave an identical ranking: price volatility first (64.25; RBQ 90.00), lack of storage second (54.90; 75.00). Conclusion: Production is robust and projected to grow, yet about half the growers market through the least efficient channels for reasons of convenience and liquidity. Raising grower income depends less on further yield gains than on price stabilisation, warehouse-receipt-linked storage, and aggregation that opens the shorter channels to small growers.

Small-Pore Chitosan Microcarriers Support Surface-Adherent Growth of Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Neural Stem Cells and Improve Intranasal Therapy of Murine Anosmia.
abstract: Intranasal delivery of neural stem cells offers a non-invasive strategy for central nervous system repair, yet its efficacy is limited by rapid mucociliary clearance and poor cellular retention. Although chitosan-based carriers have been explored, the architectural principles governing neural stem cell behavior in the intranasal microenvironment remain poorly defined. We compared chitosan microcarriers (CSMs) with three pore architectures (mean surface pore sizes 4.7 ± 1.7, 15.9 ± 3.2, and 20.5 ± 0.7 µm), fabricated via freezing-controlled phase separation, using induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neural stem cells (iPSC-NSCs). Cellular responses did not vary linearly with pore size: the smallest-pore formulation, CSM-196, supported surface-adhesion-dominant growth, whereas both larger-pore formulations supported infiltration-dominant growth. CSM-196 was also associated with increased proliferative activity, spontaneous neuronal differentiation, and elevated neurotrophic factor secretion without exogenous induction factors. In a methimazole-induced anosmia model, the CSM-196-iPSC-NSC formulation produced greater improvements in olfactory behavioral recovery, olfactory epithelial thickness, neuronal marker expression, and epithelial proliferation than cell-only delivery administered by the same route and schedule. This chitosan-based platform provides a surface-adhesion-oriented cell-delivery strategy that warrants further evaluation for intranasal neural regenerative therapy.

title: Reln mRNA Delivery Drives Neurogenic Bone Regeneration by Orchestrating Schwann Cell-Mediated Exosomal Trafficking.
abstract: Neurogenic bone regeneration is essential for the effective restoration of bone tissue functionality, while the mechanisms and new strategies underlying neurogenic bone regeneration remain to be further explored. Here, single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed enhanced mesenchymal-Schwann cell crosstalk during bone regeneration. Functionally, we verify that Schwann cells are indispensable for bone regeneration via paracrine exosome-mediated crosstalk with MSCs, a process promoted by Reelin. Mechanistically, Reelin enhances Schwann cell-derived exosome internalization by MSCs via regulating exosomal proteins, especially UBE2K, which promotes MSC osteogenic differentiation through the ERK pathway, associated with Lys63-linked polyubiquitination. For effective neurogenic bone regeneration, we engineered mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as a CRISPRa delivery system for local Reln gene activation at the defect area. This mRNA delivery system could promote bone regeneration in both calvarial defect and tibial fracture models by constructing a pro-osteogenic neurogenic microenvironment. Collectively, our findings uncover a Reelin-Schwann cell exosomes-ERK regulatory axis in bone regeneration with translational potential, highlighting the therapeutic value of targeting neural-osteogenic crosstalk in bone regeneration.

title: Additive main effect and multiplicative interaction analysis of N and K fertilizations to perennial ryegrass turf
abstract: Additive main effect and multiplicative interaction (AMMI) analysis has been shown to be more effective than the conventional two‐way fixed effects model when targeting the interaction. Field studies accumulate noise in the interaction, and this reduces predictive accuracy. Statistics from the multivariate component of AMMI are useful for interpreting the multiplicative interaction compared to the additive model, the basis of analysis of variance (ANOVA). Previously published field studies (RCB with four replicates) were reanalyzed using AMMI. AMMI was used to investigate clipping yield, soil K and leaf tissue K responses to 15 fertilizers (F, various N and K combinations) repeated over 5 years (Y) in perennial ryegrass ( Lolium perenne L.) maintained as turfgrass. Noise in the F × Y interaction with 56 degrees of freedom (df) ranged from 22.2 (clipping yield) to 44.0% (leaf tissue K) of F × Y sum of squares before AMMI partitioning of 39 df as noise. AMMI‐1 statistical gain using 4 reps was equal to as many as 8.8 reps using AMMI‐F (full or cell means model). AMMI‐F raw means exhibited twice the crossovers of AMMI‐1 means. AMMI‐1 interaction scores (IAS‐1) for fertilizer and year correlated with soil pH and offered plausible interpretation of F × Y interactions in AMMI‐1 biplots. AMMI reduction of noise is underutilized in data analysis, especially in field studies where simple two‐way interactions are common and the interaction becomes quickly buried by noise when repeated in years.

title: Fake Review Detection from Classical to Transformers: Gains and Limits
abstract: Reported fake review detection performance is hard to interpret when model families are evaluated under different data splits and development procedures. This study compares six traditional machine learning systems, five deep learning models, seven pretrained Transformer encoders, and seven sentiment‐augmented Transformer variants on the Amazon‐based fake reviews dataset (FRD) under one leakage‐controlled protocol: a duplicate‐safe 70/10/20 partition; validation‐only selection of checkpoints, thresholds, models, and ensembles; and a test set reserved for final evaluation and paired inference. Accuracy rises from 94.32% (TF‐IDF + SVM) and 95.00% (Word2Vec + LSTM) to 98.23% with the validation‐selected plain Transformer (ModernBERT), the largest stage‐level gain. A validation‐selected soft‐voting ensemble adds a small but significant improvement, to 98.75% (ROC‐AUC 0.9991). Sentiment augmentation, an explicit sentiment profile added through a dedicated fusion head, did not improve accuracy consistently: Over five training runs per backbone, its effect changed sign for all seven encoders, including the three with a significant first‐run effect. Zero‐shot evaluation on AiGen‐FoodReview, which replaces Amazon/GPT‐2 with Yelp/GPT‐4‐Turbo reviews, shows that the in‐domain operating performance does not carry over: Every transferred Transformer‐based system labels nearly all machine‐generated reviews as authentic, and the final ensemble ranks the two classes in reverse (ROC‐AUC 0.4357). No configuration ranks generated reviews above authentic ones in all five runs; plain BERT reaches a ROC‐AUC of 0.9055 in one run but only 0.30–0.77 in the others. Controlled in‐domain gains and external validity must be established separately.

title: Amygdala Oligodendrocyte MDH1 Dysregulation and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in High Urea-Induced Anxiety-Like Behavior.
abstract: The high incidence and mortality rates of anxiety disorders in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) have drawn attention. Prior studies identified urea as an independent risk factor for mental disorders in CKD. While urea accumulation is known to impair synaptic plasticity, its effects on glial cells remain unclear. How urea influences oligodendrocyte lineage differentiation may represent a critical node in neuron-glia interactions. Previous studies have shown that OL-lineage cells may be underrepresented in scRNA-seq datasets. We selected amygdala tissue from wild-type and high-urea (UT-B-/-) mice and performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), behavioral tests, and cellular experiments to delineate the impact of urea on oligodendrocyte lineage dynamics. In UT-B-/- mice, the relative abundance of oligodendrocyte subpopulations enriched for mitochondrial transcripts decreased, suggesting vulnerability to urea toxicity. Dlat and MDH1, genes associated with TCA cycle-related metabolism, were downregulated alongside alterations in mitochondrial and oxidative phosphorylation-related transcriptional programs. Urea dose-dependently decreased MDH1 expression, mitochondrial membrane potential, and intracellular ATP content in MO3.13 cells. Regulatory analyses linked MDH1 to energy metabolism and neurodegenerative pathways. Trajectory reconstruction suggested altered differentiation- and myelination-related transcriptional programs in mitochondria-related oligodendrocytes (MitOLs). The cytoplasmic concentration and fate of oxaloacetic acid (OAA) are regulated by the reversible catalysis of MDH1. OAA supplementation partially restored amygdalar MDH1 expression and alleviated anxiety-like behaviors in UT-B-/- mice, while improving mitochondrial bioenergetics in urea-exposed MO3.13 cells. These findings support a candidate metabolic-glial model linking elevated urea, MDH1 dysregulation, oligodendrocyte bioenergetic dysfunction, and anxiety-like behavior, with potential relevance to CKD-associated anxiety.

title: An Innovative Indirect Measure of Socioeconomic Status (SES)-Related Intergroup Differentiation Among Adolescents.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Adolescence is a critical period for understanding social class, forming class-related attitudes, and shaping future social engagement. However, the global educational segregation trend may hinder this learning by separating adolescents into socioeconomic status (SES)-based school settings, thereby fostering intergroup misunderstandings, prejudice, and weakening social cohesion. Before implementing interventions to reduce these divides, a reliable, valid, and age-appropriate measure of SES-related attitudes is needed. To address socially desirable responding in explicit measures, this study developed and evaluated the Intergroup Indirect Attitude-relevant Differentiation Measure (IIAM) for assessing adolescents' SES-related attitude-relevant differentiation. METHODS A total of 328 Year 7-9 students from relatively advantaged secondary school contexts (higher-SES) (Mage = 13.06, including both female and male students) in Mainland China and Hong Kong participated. The IIAM was developed using the Error-Choice technique, with items informed by a literature review and expert panel input. Face and content validity were examined through cognitive interviews, construct validity was assessed through exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha. RESULTS Findings indicated that the IIAM showed good face validity and strong internal consistency, with Cronbach's alpha values in the 0.80s. Both EFA and CFA supported a unidimensional, seven-item structure with satisfactory model fit. CONCLUSION The IIAM appears to be a feasible indirect measure of SES-related attitude-relevant intergroup differentiation, with preliminary evidence supporting its internal consistency and dimensional structure among higher-SES adolescents. Further research is encouraged to confirm the internal consistency, construct validity of the measure in socioeconomically heterogeneous samples, including adolescents from lower-SES backgrounds.

title: Super-Resolution Ultrasound for Lymph Node Evaluation: Diagnostic Value of Static Time-Point Parameters Versus Dynamic Temporal Changes.
abstract: OBJECTIVES To evaluate quantitative super-resolution ultrasound (SRUS) parameters (static central-to-peripheral ratios and dynamic temporal changes) for differentiating benign and metastatic lymph nodes, and to compare the performance of corresponding predictive models. METHODS A prospective study included 172 pathologically confirmed lymph nodes (100 benign, 72 metastatic). SRUS was performed to derive density and velocity parameters, with central-to-peripheral ratios and temporal changes calculated. Static and dynamic models were constructed using univariate analysis, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by cross-validation, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, decision curve analysis, and clinical impact curve. RESULTS Metastatic lymph nodes showed significantly lower central-to-peripheral ratios of density and velocity parameters but higher relative temporal changes in density SD and velocity SD compared with benign nodes (all P < .05). The static time-point model retained 2 SRUS variables (Mean.Density_C_P_T2, Max.Density_C_P_T3), yielding a full-sample AUC of 0.8607. The temporal change model included 2 dynamic parameters (Velocity SD change from T1 to T2, Mean density change from T2 to T3) and achieved a higher AUC of 0.8715, with better accuracy, specificity, and model fit. Both models showed favorable calibration and clinical net benefit. CONCLUSION Quantitative SRUS parameters effectively reflect pathological angiogenesis in metastatic lymph nodes. The temporal change model provides superior diagnostic performance over the static time-point model and may serve as a reliable noninvasive tool for distinguishing benign from metastatic lymph nodes.
journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine

title: In vitro phenotyping and genomics: a conceptual framework linking plant tissue culture with GWAS, QTL mapping, and multi-omics
Critical Validation of Deep Learning-Based Cervical Vertebral Fracture Detection on Computed Tomography Localizer Radiographs.
abstract: Localizer radiographs are low-resolution two-dimensional overview images acquired prior to computed tomography (CT) scans. Their automated analysis could support the early detection of cervical vertebral fractures in trauma patients and thus enable immediate adjustment of imaging protocols. This study investigated to what extent deep learning-based methods can reliably detect such fractures on localizer radiographs, with a focus on critically validating model behavior beyond standard performance metrics. On a custom-annotated dataset of 346 trauma patients, two approaches were compared: a full-image binary classification and a two-step pipeline that first localizes the cervical spine and then classifies the cropped region. Model validity was assessed through a permutation test, occlusion testing, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, an analysis of potential confounders, and a subgroup analysis by anatomical fracture location. The full-image classifier formally achieved the highest test-set performance with a precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) of 0.477, compared with 0.349 for the cervical-spine-level classifier. Our validity analysis indicates that the full-image classifier does not primarily rely on the fracture region itself, rendering it unsuitable for clinical use. This work therefore presents a case study of shortcut learning and illustrates validation methods that may be of value for comparable studies on small datasets with visually subtle targets.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

title: Comparison of models for dynamical structures of solar plasma
abstract: Possible mechanisms of generation of dynamical plasma structures are associated with the Schwarzschild criterion for convective instability and with excess energy (heat, magnetic): due to the superadiabatic temperature gradient, the overheated plasma starts to rise. In the framework of Navier-Stokes MHD equations, the complete system of equations for the full axisymmetric plasma model includes equations for the stream function, the azimuthal velocity component, the density change, the flow function of poloidal magnetic field, and the azimuthal component of the magnetic field. Within the framework of ideal hydrodynamics, the simplest plasma model is applicable to the initial stage of generation of plasma structures. In this case, rigorous analytical solutions are constructed from blocks. Within the framework of ideal hydrodynamics, some intermediate model - the refined model considers rotating plasma at the growth stage. In this case, some unidirectional differential rotation occurs. The full model studies the development of structures as rotating plasma from the very beginning to the highest development stage. The velocity field is adjusted to boundary conditions. Velocity components change in a coordinated manner. The stationary axisymmetric ambient magnetic field and its gradients have little effect on the plasma structure and velocity field. The movement structures for all models are similar. Radial flows converge towards the axis at the bottom, and there is an outflow to the periphery near the top of the plasma structure. The maximum vertical velocity component is reached at the center of the axis. Applications of these models to solar structures, including jets, are discussed.

title: Restricted and Repetitive Behavior Subtypes Show Distinct Associations with Adaptive Functioning in Autistic Children.
abstract: Restricted and repetitive behaviors (RRBs) are a core feature of autism spectrum disorder, yet their distinct impacts on adaptive functioning remain unclear. Adaptive functioning, including communication, socialization, and daily living skills, is critical for quality of life in autistic children. Here we performed exploratory factor analysis of the Repetitive Behavior Scale-Revised in 167 autistic children aged 3-12 years, identifying three RRB subtypes: sameness/ritualistic/restricted behaviors, stereotypic/self-injurious behaviors, and compulsive behaviors. In primary models adjusting for age and sex, sameness/ritualistic/restricted behaviors predicted lower socialization, whereas stereotypic/self-injurious behaviors predicted lower communication and daily living skills. In a sensitivity analysis additionally adjusting for IQ, in the subset of children with available cognitive data, only sameness/ritualistic/restricted behaviors remained a significant predictor across all three domains. These findings suggest that not all RRB subtypes are equally associated with adaptive functioning, underscoring the need to differentiate RRBs when designing interventions. Understanding subtype-specific associations may guide strategies that address behaviors hindering adaptive outcomes while considering those with potential regulatory functions.

title: Digital technologies for crop water stress detection, prediction and water-management decision-making in smallholder rainfed systems: a review
abstract: Drought remains the single largest climatic threat to crop production in rainfed and smallholder farming systems, where irrigation infrastructure is limited and crop failure translates directly into food insecurity. Over the past decade, a rapid expansion of digital technologies has transformed our capacity to detect and anticipate crop water stress. This review examines how these technologies are being connected, or fail to be connected, to water-management decisions and agronomic interventions that improve outcomes for farmers. We reviewed relevant evidence across five dimensions: (i) sensing and prediction technologies; (ii) water-stress indicators; (iii) digital decision-support and advisory systems; (iv) intervention and adoption pathways in smallholder contexts; and (v) measured effects on yield, water-use efficiency (WUE) and drought resilience. Key findings include: detection accuracy has outpaced decision integration, with machine-learning models routinely achieving R² of 0.75–0.90 under controlled conditions but rarely feeding operational decisions; a marked lab-to-field transfer gap, with accuracies falling by up to ~ 22% points in farmer fields; a systematic WUE-yield trade-off under deficit irrigation; and consistent evidence that frugal tools outperform sophisticated systems in smallholder cost-benefit terms. Digital tools deliver their largest gains when they amplify proven agronomy (deficit and supplemental irrigation, rainwater harvesting, drought-tolerant cultivars) and when they are institutionally embedded in extension and water-governance systems. This evidence was integrated into a framework that identifies the “missing middle” between sensing and action as the field’s critical bottleneck, and derive research priorities for transferable, decision-centred, smallholder-appropriate digital water management.

title: Xianfang Huoming Decoction ameliorates hidradenitis suppurativa-like pathology by restoring NCSTN/Notch signaling homeostasis in NcstnΔKC mice and NCSTN-knockdown HaCaT cells
Opening the Black Box: How Agentic AI-Assisted Modeling Lets Pharmacometricians See Inside NONMEM.
EEG emotion recognition based on masked generative adversarial networks and neural architecture search
abstract: EEG signals face challenges such as a scarcity of training data, significant individual variability, and difficulties in designing neural network architectures, which severely limit the performance and generalization capabilities of emotion recognition models. This paper proposes a method for EEG-based emotion recognition that integrates masked generative adversarial data augmentation with personalized neural architecture search: First, we design a data augmentation strategy based on a random electrode mask generative adversarial network using frequency-domain features, which effectively expands the training dataset and alleviates the problem of overfitting during within-subject training; second, we construct a neural architecture search space suitable for EEG signals and use a differentiable architecture search method to automatically discover the optimal network topology. Finally, a personalized architecture search strategy is employed to independently search for the classification network best suited to each subject’s EEG signal characteristics. Experimental validation on the public EEG emotion dataset DEAP achieved a classification accuracy of 98.64% on the Arousal dimension and 98.59% on the Valence dimension, outperforming traditional machine learning methods and deep learning models with fixed architectures.

A meta-analysis of artificial intelligence and the customer brand relationship in tourism and hospitality
abstract: This meta-analysis pools 23 independent samples (N = 9,875) on the association between customer-facing artificial intelligence (AI) and the customer-brand relationship in tourism and hospitality. Earlier reviews of this question are narrative or stop at technology acceptance; this one quantifies the relational link and extends it into the generative-AI period. Each effect size is a zero-order, construct-level correlation taken from the primary study’s correlation matrix, and no standardised path coefficients were pooled. A random-effects model (restricted maximum likelihood with the Knapp-Hartung adjustment) gives a pooled correlation of r = 0.62, 95% CI [0.54, 0.68], with a 95% prediction interval of [0.18, 0.85]. The analyses found no statistically reliable differences by technology (service robots, chatbots, generative AI, general AI tools; Q-between = 4.1, p = 0.25), by anthropomorphism (Q-between = 1.6, p = 0.21), by type of AI predictor (Q-between = 1.8, p = 0.42), by outcome family (Q-between = 6.4, p = 0.17), by sub-sector, or by region, although several subgroups hold only a few samples and the tests have limited power. Heterogeneity is considerable (I-squared = 96.4%) and is not accounted for by the coded moderators, the correlation source, or publication year. There is no sign of a small-study effect (Egger p = 0.99; trim-and-fill adjusted r = 0.59). The certainty of evidence is low (GRADE), and because every correlation comes from a single-source survey, the pooled estimate is best read as an upper bound. Interpreted within a stimulus-organism-response framework, the evidence shows a positive association that the coded artefact-level categories do not differentiate, but the large between-study variation and the cross-sectional, self-report designs mean the average should not be treated as a universal value.

title: Natural deep eutectic solvents as active systems rather than inert solvents
abstract: Natural deep eutectic solvents (NADES) have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional pharmaceutical solvents and excipients. This review critically evaluates whether NADES can be accurately described as inert media within existing drug delivery paradigms. Current pharmaceutical frameworks assume linearity, additivity, and functional independence, yet growing experimental and computational evidence demonstrates that NADES exhibit non-ideal, supramolecular behavior governed by cooperative hydrogen bonding, dynamic microheterogeneity, and composition-dependent interactions. Apparent solubility enhancement in NADES has been experimentally shown to arise from kinetically stabilized supersaturation rather than equilibrium solubility, as time-dependent crystallization studies demonstrate delayed nucleation and prolonged metastable states rather than a shift in thermodynamic equilibrium, challenging equilibrium-based solubility models. Furthermore, small compositional variations, particularly in water content, produce disproportionate changes in physicochemical behavior, undermining reproducibility and predictability. Observed biological effects are frequently confounded by intrinsic component activity and lack clear differentiation between controlled modulation and nonspecific toxicity. To address these limitations, the “Active System Hypothesis” is proposed, positioning NADES as supramolecular systems that regulate local physicochemical environments. This work highlights the need for integrated, mechanism-driven frameworks that link composition, structure, and biological response. Ultimately, redefining NADES as complex, multicomponent systems is essential for developing predictive models, ensuring reproducibility, and enabling their rational translation into pharmaceutical applications.

title: Artificial intelligence and synthetic biology for integrated crop improvement
abstract: Conventional crop breeding has delivered substantial yield and quality gains but faces persistent constraints from long breeding cycles, limited genetic diversity, and increasing climate volatility. Artificial intelligence (AI) and synthetic biology (SynBio) are emerging as complementary technologies that can accelerate allele discovery, trait design, and deployment across major staples and under-researched crops. Machine learning, computer vision, and robotics support high-throughput phenotyping from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery and mobile devices, while genomic prediction models that integrate multi-omics and climate data can improve selection accuracy for traits such as yield stability and stress tolerance. SynBio platforms enable precise genome editing, synthetic circuits, and metabolic pathway engineering, with applications ranging from biofortified rice to multiplex editing in maize and pangenome-informed breeding in orphan crops such as chickpea and pearl millet. Their convergence, often described as “Breeding 5.0,” supports AI-guided design–build–test–learn (DBTL) cycles that optimize ideotypes for resource efficiency, resilience, and nutrition while reducing reliance on agrochemical inputs. This narrative review outlines the evolution from classical to molecular breeding, synthesizes current AI–SynBio pipelines with illustrative case studies, and highlights persistent challenges in data quality, transformation efficiency, biosafety, regulatory harmonization, and equitable access. We conclude with priorities for inclusive innovation to ensure that climate-smart, nutritious crops benefit diverse agroecosystems responsibly.

title: Sustainable soil practices for improving soil health, greenhouse gas mitigation and climate resilience of rice cropping systems
abstract: Climate change is threatening rice yields more and more, which undermines global food security. Traditional agricultural practices further endanger the ecosystem by causing carbon emissions, soil degradation and wasteful water usage. Despite some progress in this area, local adaptation, soil quality improvement and mitigation remain insufficient. This review emphasises the importance of sustainable soil management in enhancing the climate resilience of ecosystems. Conservation tillage can reduce carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions by 25–40% and production costs by 20–35%. Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) and the System of Rice Intensification (SRI) reduce methane emissions by 40–70% whilst increasing water retention capacity by 25–65%. Organic amendments can increase soil organic matter content by 25–40%, while the use of biochar can increase drought resilience by 15% and grain yield by 10% in stressful conditions. Integrated practices can reduce total greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 30–50%. This study also suggests the development of climate-resilient rice varieties that can cope with climate change, and new soil amendments, such as biofertilisers that have been enhanced by nanotechnology and designer biochars. Moreover, digital agriculture such as using artificial intelligence to monitor soil health and precision application technologies. This review highlights the urgent need to make these practices mainstream in order to ensure long-term productivity and ecological stability.

title: Automatic Ultrasound Habitat Radiomics for Differentiating Henoch-Schonlein Purpura Nephritis from IgA Nephropathy in Children: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES To assess a noninvasive ultrasound habitat radiomics approach with automatic kidney segmentation for distinguishing pediatric Henoch-Schonlein purpura nephritis (HSPN) from immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN). MATERIALS AND METHODS This retrospective multicenter study included 592 biopsy-confirmed pediatric patients from three centers (HSPN, n = 338; IgAN, n = 254). The development cohort (n = 453) was split into training (n = 362) and internal validation (n = 91) cohorts, and an independent external validation cohort (n = 139) was used for final testing. Kidney regions of interest were automatically segmented using nnU-Net. K-means clustering defined three echogenic habitat subregions, and 408 radiomics features were extracted from the whole-kidney region and habitat subregions. Feature selection was performed in the training cohort, and three machine-learning classifiers were evaluated. The selected radiomics model was compared with clinical and combined models. RESULTS nnU-Net achieved high kidney segmentation performance, with a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.957 and a mean intersection over union of 0.918 in the independent healthy-child test set. Fifteen radiomics features were retained, including six whole-kidney features and nine habitat-derived features. Logistic regression showed stable performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.806 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.715-0.897) internally and 0.825 (95% CI, 0.758-0.892) externally. The combined model outperformed the clinical model in AUC in both cohorts (0.846 vs 0.717; 0.805 vs 0.733). CONCLUSION This deep-learning-assisted ultrasound habitat radiomics approach enabled automatic kidney delineation and showed encouraging performance as a reproducible imaging adjunct for differentiating pediatric HSPN from IgAN.

Contrastive Adapter Training and Consensus Knowledge Distillation for Multi-Source-Free Domain Adaptation in Skin Cancer Diagnosis
abstract: Skin cancer diagnosis, particularly differentiating melanoma from benign nevi, is challenging due to the visual similarity between lesions. Although convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs) have shown promising performance, their effectiveness often deteriorates on data from heterogeneous clinical sources. Conventional domain adaptation methods address domain shift but require access to source data during adaptation, which is often infeasible due to privacy regulations. Multi-source-free unsupervised domain adaptation (MSFDA) addresses this limitation by leveraging multiple labeled source domains to generalize to an unlabeled target domain without requiring access to source data. However, existing MSFDA methods rely on full backbone fine-tuning, leading to catastrophic forgetting and overfitting on small clinical datasets, and address domain shift at the aggregation stage without establishing a shared domain-invariant feature space. Furthermore, their reliance on hard pseudo-labels or confidence-weighted aggregation introduces noisy supervision signals under domain shift. To address these limitations, we propose CAT-CKD, consisting of two components: (1) contrastive adapter training (CAT), which trains lightweight ConvPass adapters within a frozen ViT backbone using supervised contrastive learning (SCL) to establish a shared domain-invariant feature space before source-specific model training, and (2) consensus knowledge distillation (CKD), which aggregates logits from multiple source models into a consensus supervisory signal and adapts a student model on unlabeled target data using KL divergence. Experiments on five publicly available skin lesion datasets show that CAT-CKD achieves an average AUROC of 86.1%, outperforming existing MSFDA methods while requiring only 4.3M trainable parameters. The code is available at https://github.com/A-Abedi/CAT_CKD.

Cell-Cycle Regulatory Responses in Retinal Degeneration: From Post-Mitotic Homeostasis to Cell-State Transitions and Fate Decisions.
abstract: Cell-cycle regulatory perturbations are increasingly implicated in retinal degeneration, yet their biological significance varies fundamentally across retinal cell types because proliferative competence differs between terminally differentiated neurons and proliferation-capable retinal populations. While retinal neurons normally maintain permanent cell-cycle exit, Müller glia, microglia, retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells, endothelial cells, and pericytes retain varying capacities for quiescence, proliferation, and injury-induced reactivation. Consequently, alterations in cyclins, cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs), RB-E2F signaling, DNA replication machinery, or checkpoint regulators may represent distinct biological states depending on cellular context. In this review, we examine cell-cycle perturbations across inherited retinal diseases (IRDs), age-related macular degeneration (AMD), diabetic retinopathy (DR), retinal gliosis and inflammation, and retinal organoid models. We critically assess current evidence for neuronal cell-cycle re-entry and propose a practical evidence hierarchy that distinguishes pathway activation, neuronal localization, progression through cell-cycle phases, cell-type-specific causality, and longitudinal cellular fate. We argue that many reported findings reflect incomplete or ambiguous evidence and should not be equated with bona fide neuronal cell-cycle re-entry. We further propose a fate-bifurcation model in which cellular outcomes are determined by the depth and duration of cell-cycle engagement together with cell identity, checkpoint integrity, CDK inhibitor activity, DNA damage burden, metabolic state, and microenvironment cues. Under this framework, limited or checkpoint-restrained engagement may support transient neuronal adaptation or survival, whereas sustained activation may promote senescence-like states, and deeper progression under inadequate checkpoint control may contribute to neuronal dysfunction and death. In proliferation-competent retinal compartments, related pathways may instead drive gliosis, immune expansion, epithelial remodeling, angiogenesis, or senescence. By integrating evidence across retinal diseases and cell types, this state-based framework provides a unified interpretation of apparently conflicting observations and offers a conceptual foundation for developing cell-type- and state-specific therapeutic strategies for retinal degeneration.

title: Early Increases in GDF-15 Are Associated With Declines in Cardiac Function With Breast Cancer Therapy.
abstract: BACKGROUND Growth differentiation factor (GDF)-15 is a stress-responsive cytokine induced by mitochondrial dysfunction and genotoxic stress, mechanisms central to anthracycline cardiotoxicity. Whether early changes in GDF-15 following cancer therapy relate to subsequent cardiac dysfunction is not established. OBJECTIVES We evaluated the longitudinal trajectory of GDF-15 and its associations with changes in cardiac function and structure following cardiotoxic cancer therapy in women with breast cancer. METHODS In 366 women receiving anthracyclines and/or trastuzumab from the Penn Cardiotoxicity of Cancer Therapy prospective cohort study, associations between baseline, early-peak (maximum 0-6-month change), and longitudinal GDF-15 concentrations with quantitative echocardiographic measures of systolic, diastolic, and structural function over 36 months were evaluated using multivariable linear mixed-effects models. RESULTS GDF-15 rose from a median baseline of 662 to an early-peak of 1,412 pg/mL, with trajectories differing across regimens (P = 0.004). Each doubling of the early-peak-to-baseline GDF-15 ratio was associated with a subsequent 1.5 percentage point decline in left ventricular ejection fraction (β -1.5%; 95% CI: -2.5 to -0.6; P = 0.002) and a 0.9-unit worsening in longitudinal strain (β 0.9; 95% CI: 0.4-1.4; P = 0.001). GDF-15 was not associated with diastolic outcomes, incident diastolic dysfunction, or incident cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction. CONCLUSIONS In women receiving anthracycline- and/or trastuzumab-based breast cancer therapy, early increases in GDF-15 were associated with modest declines in left ventricular ejection fraction and worsening of longitudinal strain, without associations with diastolic measures. These findings support mechanistic investigation of GDF-15 in anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity. (Cardiotoxicity of Cancer Therapy [CCT]; NCT01173341).

title: Whose startup does the AI back? An algorithm audit of reputation and demographic signals in LLM-assisted crowdfunding
abstract: Large language model (LLM) assistants increasingly advise backers on which crowdfunding campaigns to support. LLMs have known race and gender problems, and it is unsettled whether they reproduce, erase, or reverse the discrimination documented in entrepreneurial finance. We ask when, and through which decision process, LLM assistants use founders' gender and ethnicity. In a pre-specified choice-based conjoint experiment, seven LLMs chose among five synthetic campaigns with independently randomized quality signals and founder names, under three backer personas and a persona-free control (40,248 responses). By default, founder names barely matter: under budget-conscious and delivery-focused personas, gender and Black-name effects are statistically equivalent to zero. When the backer wants to support underrepresented creators, the models favor Black-signaled (+8.1 percentage points; positive in all seven models) and female-signaled (+5.1) founders. They do so most strongly among near-tied campaigns and for the founder who alone carries the signal, and they almost never name gender or ethnicity in their reasons. The results fit an agency account of algorithmic discrimination: an aligned assistant takes its demographic preferences from its user rather than from its training data.

title: Aggregate-scale reorganization of multitrophic soil micro-food webs under fertilization and earthworm activity shapes soil-plant nutrient coupling.
abstract: Fertilization is widely used to enhance crop productivity and nutrient cycling, whereas earthworms reorganize soil aggregates, creating heterogeneous microhabitats for soil micro-food webs. However, how earthworms modify fertilization effects on aggregate-associated multitrophic communities and soil-plant nutrient transfer remains unclear. We conducted an outdoor mesocosm experiment in a Sichuan pepper-faba bean agroforestry system with NPK fertilization (NPK; 15-15-15, 6.67 g kg-1 dry soil), earthworm addition (EW; Eisenia fetida, 60 g m-2), their combination (NPK + EW), and a control across microaggregates (MIA; <0.25 mm), small macroaggregates (SMA; 0.25-2 mm), and large macroaggregates (LMA; 2-8 mm). Compared with NPK treatment, EW treatment significantly increased bacterial and protistan Shannon diversity from 724.24 to 803.42 (10.93%) and from 120.54 to 163.39 (35.55%), respectively (p < 0.05). Fungal Shannon diversity was primarily structured by aggregate size and was significantly higher in MIA (122.42) than in SMA (91.06) and LMA (107.16, p < 0.05). NPK + EW treatment non-additively reorganized co-occurrence network toward greater fungal representation and modularity. MIA supported the most complex co-occurrence networks and showed the strongest associations between microbial attributes and soil-plant nutrient variables. Beyond the positive effects of NPK fertilization and earthworm addition, structural equation modeling revealed that protistan diversity positively affected both soil nutrient supply and plant nutrient uptake (path coefficients = 0.29 and 0.32), whereas network complexity was negatively related to soil nutrient acquisition (-0.70) and supply (-0.47). These findings indicate that multitrophic coupling is an important mechanism through which fertilization and earthworm enhance nutrient transfer from soil to plants across aggregate-scale microhabitats.

title: Hybridization reshapes maize phenotypic plasticity through coordinated changes in environmental responses and genetic architecture.
abstract: Phenotypic plasticity is central to crop adaptation under climate variability, yet how hybridization reshapes it remains unclear. Here, we integrate multi-environment phenotypes, environmental variables, and genomic data from 456 maize inbred lines and 912 corresponding hybrids evaluated across 11 environments to dissect the environmental and genetic bases of plasticity for flowering time, plant height, and ear weight. Reaction-norm analyses reveal two- to three-fold greater plasticity variation in inbreds than hybrids, indicating more uniform plastic responses in hybrids. Environmental association analyses demonstrate that inbreds and hybrids respond to the same environmental factors with different magnitudes or even opposite directions (e.g., correlations between diurnal temperature range and flowering time ranged from -0.73 to -0.14 in inbreds but 0.22 to 0.46 in hybrids). Genome-wide association analyses identify distinct parental loci for plasticity, with more loci and larger effects in hybrids. Functional validation shows that ZmBAF60_13, a chromatin-remodeling gene found only in the inbred panel, negatively regulates flowering-time plasticity. Integrating multiple environmental indices improves phenotype prediction accuracy by up to 16% over single-index models. Together, this study reveals that hybrids exhibit reduced plasticity variation and differ from inbreds in environmental responses and genetic associations, providing a framework for predicting crop performance under climate variability.

title: P2Y6R is associated with adipose inflammation and muscle wasting in pancreatic cancer cachexia.
abstract: BACKGROUND Pancreatic cancer has one of the highest incidences of cancer-associated cachexia, a multi-organ wasting syndrome driven by complex tumor-host interactions. Although adipose tissue functions as an active endocrine organ contributing to systemic inflammation, the mechanisms linking adipose inflammation to skeletal muscle wasting remain incompletely understood. METHODS An orthotopic pancreatic tumor mouse model was combined with pharmacological P2Y6R inhibition using MRS2578. Cachexia-associated targets were identified by transcriptomic analysis of mouse datasets, and P2Y6R function was examined in vitro cancer-associated adipocyte (CAA) and C2C12 myotube models. RESULTS Transcriptomic analysis identified P2Y6R as a cachexia-associated gene, with expression selectively upregulated in visceral adipose tissue and CAAs under pancreatic cancer conditions. In contrast, P2Y6R expression was minimal in skeletal muscle and comparatively low in tumor tissue. In the orthotopic model, pharmacological inhibition of P2Y6R with MRS2578, initiated before overt weight loss, attenuated body weight loss. This was accompanied by reduced serum IL-6 and IL-1β levels (IL-1β at 3 mg/kg only) and decreased expression of the atrogenes mRNA expression in skeletal muscle. In vitro, conditioned medium from CAAs suppressed myotube differentiation, whereas P2ry6 knockdown in adipocytes attenuated this effect. Mechanistically, the P2Y6R-dependent secretome of cancer-associated adipocytes was associated with increased atrogene expression and altered FOXO3 phosphorylation in myotubes. CONCLUSIONS Our findings indicate that P2Y6R is associated with adipose inflammation and muscle wasting in pancreatic cancer cachexia, and that pharmacological P2Y6R inhibition attenuates cachexia progression in a preventive setting. These results suggest a potential contribution of adipocyte P2Y6R to adipose-muscle crosstalk and highlight P2Y6R as a candidate therapeutic target for cancer-associated muscle loss.

title: State-Dependent EEG Markers of Excitation/Inhibition and Hemodynamic State Are Associated with Random Noise Stimulation Effects.
abstract: BACKGROUND Non-invasive brain stimulation effects vary substantially across individuals, yet the physiological factors associated with this variability remain unclear. OBJECTIVE We tested whether baseline and task-related EEG markers of excitation/inhibition (E/I) and hemodynamic state are associated with the effects of transcranial random noise stimulation (tRNS) on learning. METHODS Participants completed a mathematical learning task during active or sham tRNS. We indexed E/I-related population dynamics using the EEG aperiodic exponent, for which lower values have been linked to relatively greater excitation than inhibition, and assessed hemodynamic state using fNIRS-derived oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO). Behavioral learning was modeled using generalized linear mixed-effects models. RESULTS tRNS accelerated learning relative to sham stimulation but did not reliably induce pre-post changes in resting-state aperiodic exponent or HbO. Instead, stimulation effects were state-dependent. Higher resting-state aperiodic exponent and lower resting-state HbO were associated with greater behavioral gains under tRNS, while task-related aperiodic exponent was associated with stimulation-related differences in learning. Task-evoked HbO was associated with learning rate but did not significantly differentiate stimulation effects. Across modalities, the findings identify complementary electrophysiological and hemodynamic correlates of variability in learning under stimulation. However, statistical support for the EEG moderation effects was attenuated in models including participant-specific learning slopes, indicating sensitivity to random-effects specification and the need for replication. CONCLUSIONS The findings argue against a simple tonic-shift account of tRNS and support a state-dependent framework in which stimulation effects depend on ongoing electrophysiological and hemodynamic context. EEG and fNIRS provided complementary information about variability in learning and stimulation response, supporting multimodal approaches to understanding and individualizing neuromodulation.

title: Advancing remote sensing of carbon fractions in coastal waters: retrieval algorithms and optical proxies for Sentinel-2 MSI and Sentinel-3 OLCI
Performance Evaluation of CO2 Huff-n-Puff in Shale Oil Reservoirs: Multiwell Huff-n-Puff and Parameter Optimization
abstract: CO2 huff-n-puff (HnP) is an established enhanced oil recovery (EOR) method for shale oil reservoirs. However, its field-scale implementation in multiwell fractured systems remains challenging because fracture-controlled interwell connectivity can cause operational interference and inefficient CO2 allocation. A field-scale numerical model of the HH shale oil reservoir, incorporating complex natural and hydraulic fracture networks, was constructed and history-matched against field production data, followed by a structured sequential one-factor-at-a-time analysis and descriptive Spearman rank-correlation screening of the associations between operational parameters and performance indicators. Results indicate that, for the calibrated HH reservoir realization, the intragroup synchronized and intergroup asynchronous strategy achieved the highest cumulative incremental oil production among the investigated strategies (9.59 × 104 t), together with a CO2 utilization efficiency of 0.266 t oil/t CO2. This performance was associated with the cross-group pressure contrast observed under the asynchronous operation of the two well groups. Rank-correlation screening indicated that cycle number and cyclic CO2 injection mass showed the strongest associations with oil recovery and CO2 utilization efficiency, respectively, within the investigated cases. Within the investigated ranges and under the experimentally constrained diffusion setting of the calibrated HH reservoir model, 45 days and 450 t/d were identified as the preferred soaking time and injection rate, respectively. Extending the soaking time from 45 to 55 days yielded only marginal improvements, whereas increasing the injection rate from 450 to 600 t/d slightly reduced both incremental oil production and CO2 utilization efficiency. Furthermore, compared with the uniform injection scheme, the differentiated injection scheme maintained a comparable OOIP-based recovery factor (15.97% versus 15.84%) while reducing the cumulative gross CO2 injection mass from 36.0 × 104 to 33.1 × 104 t, corresponding to an 8.1% reduction. The EOR-oriented CO2 utilization efficiency consequently increased from 0.274 to 0.305 t oil/t CO2. Therefore, its principal benefit was the more efficient use of the injected CO2 rather than a substantial increase in ultimate oil recovery. This work provides a field-scale numerical workflow for designing and evaluating coordinated multiwell CO2 HnP operations in fractured shale oil reservoirs.

title: Fanconi anemia pathway protects neuron–glial lineage integrity by resolving differentiation-induced endogenous DNA damage
abstract: Fanconi anemia (FA) is a congenital DNA repair disorder classically characterized by bone-marrow failure, yet emerging neurodevelopmental manifestations encompassing both congenital malformations and progressive neurodegeneration in FA patients remain mechanistically unexplained. Here we show that loss of the FA pathway selectively compromises neuroectodermal lineage progression in human cellular models, leading to impaired neuronal morphology, defective expression of neuronal and oligodendroglial markers, mitochondrial dysfunction, and defective electrophysiology. Mechanistically, transcriptional reprogramming during neural differentiation triggers a metabolic surge of endogenous formaldehyde, resulting in the accumulation of DNA-protein crosslinks (DPCs) and subsequent cell apoptosis in FANCL –/– cells. These defects are effectively rescued by restoring either FANCL or the formaldehyde-detoxifying enzyme ADH5. Moreover, conditioned media from FANCL –/– neural culture induces a reactive astrogliosis-like response in recipient cells, supporting a non-cell autonomous pro-inflammatory component. Together, our findings establish the FA pathway as a critical safeguard of neurodevelopment, coordinating both intrinsic lineage maturation and extrinsic paracrine homeostasis.

title: Techno-economic and environmental assessment of next-generation battery-powered farming robots
abstract: Decarbonizing agriculture without compromising productivity is a major challenge under rising input costs and labor scarcity. Autonomous battery-powered agricultural robots (ABARs) could help by reducing dependence on conventional machinery and enabling more precise application of inputs, but their system-level economic and environmental performance remains unclear. Here, we integrate total cost of ownership and life cycle assessment to evaluate a small ABAR for cradle-to-farm-gate crop production of strawberries, onions, lettuce, and peanuts under organic and non-organic management. Across modeled scenarios, benchmarked costs range from 76% below to 17% above literature-based reference ranges, while greenhouse-gas emissions fall within or below reported ranges. Variable inputs dominate both outcomes, contributing 72–90% of costs and 72–95% of global-warming impacts, with seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation water as main drivers. These results suggest that ABAR value depends less on the platform than on the ability of autonomous operation to reduce input use and labor demand. This study compares a small autonomous battery-powered farming robot with conventional farming and finds competitive costs and low greenhouse-gas emissions, driven mainly by reductions in labor and input use.

title: Integrating landscape ecological risk and ecosystem service value for ecological zoning in railway corridors: the Hefei–Hangzhou high-speed railway case
abstract: The rapid development of high-speed railways (HSR) has reshaped land use and impacted corridor ecosystems, often reducing ecosystem service value (ESV) and increasing landscape ecological risk (LER). Ecological zoning is thus essential for diagnosing and planning ecosystems along HSR lines. Using the Hefei–Hangzhou HSR corridor as a case study, this research examines the spatiotemporal dynamics of ESV and LER from 2010 to 2020 by applying the value equivalence factor method and the landscape ecological risk index. Based on ESV-LER integration, differentiated ecological zones were established, and future scenarios (2025–2035) were simulated using the PLUS model. Key findings include: (1) Built-up areas expanded notably (+ 157.84 km2), while farmland experienced the largest decline (− 130.24 km2) during 2010–2020. (2) LER structure shifted from high- and medium–high-risk dominance toward medium-risk categories, with overall risk declining, whereas total ESV showed an initial rise followed by a net reduction of 286.59 million CNY (− 2.46%). (3) Ecological conservation and control zones formed the mainstay of zoning; the ecological protection zone decreased most significantly (− 10.98%), while the ecological improvement zone grew the fastest (+ 16.50%). (4) The ecological spatial distribution in the study area remains largely consistent with 2020 across 2025, 2030, and 2035, still dominated by ecological control zones—which show a slight decrease (− 9.54%)—and stable ecological conservation zones. By integrating LER and ESV, this study proposes a novel zoning framework to support ecological management in HSR corridors.

title: Research on the application framework of multi-agent technology-driven failure analysis for industrial products
abstract: Accurate failure analysis in intelligent supercharging stations is critical for operational safety and efficiency. However, traditional methods suffer from poor cross-condition adaptability, limited few-shot learning capability, and insufficient cross-model generalization. This paper proposes a Multi-Agent Failure Analysis Execution System (FAES), which synergistically integrates a Multimodal Workbench, an Intelligence Hub, and a modular agent cluster. The Multimodal Workbench fuses heterogeneous sensor data (voltage, current, temperature, acoustic) through a progressive three-level fusion strategy with cross-modal attention and Dempster-Shafer evidence theory. The Intelligence Hub formulates task allocation as a constrained optimization problem, which is relaxed to a differentiable softmax routing mechanism. This enables real-time, load-aware scheduling. A fine-tuned large language model (Qwen3-Omni) provides domain-adaptive diagnostic reasoning through closed-loop reinforcement learning from human feedback. Extensive experiments on real-world charging station data demonstrate that FAES achieves 83.2% diagnostic accuracy under few-shot cross-dataset transfer-a 15.8 percentage point improvement over training from scratch and reduces average response time by 42.9% (from 4.2 s to 2.4 s) via dynamic multi-agent scheduling. Ablation studies quantify the contribution of each component, while hallucination analysis confirms a low rate of just 0.4%. These results establish FAES as an explainable, generalizable solution for industrial fault diagnosis, filling a critical gap in the application of LLM-based multi-agent collaboration to charging station maintenance.

title: Farm practice typologies as a strategy for management-relevant land use and land cover mapping in the Great Lakes Region
abstract: The Great Lakes region (GLR) is dominated by agricultural land use, characterized by diverse land use and land cover (LULC), land management practices (LMPs), and, in turn, diverse land processes. Conventional LULC classification systems often rely on coarse categorizations, summarized into spatial units that are either unmeaningful to management or lack the fidelity to capture human-driven heterogeneity relevant to environmental outcomes. Furthermore, most LULC systems are temporal snapshots, agnostic to the spatial dependencies of temporal land-use transitions and fail to provide an inventory of the diversity of land use and management within regions. Hence, we developed a multi-year integrated typology framework by combining LULC class transitions (2008–2023) with trends in LMPs, to characterize these differences in the landscape, using inductively developed, threshold-based classification rules at the farm-parcel level.​ Our multi-year integrated typology combined LULC and LMP classes to yield a total of 135 unique land types for the GLR, capturing sufficient variation in agricultural management and landscape heterogeneity that is not reflected in conventional LULC products. Staple Crop Rotation – Tile Drained (StRot-TD) and Staple Crop Rotation – Conventional (StRot-Con) emerged as the dominant multi-year integrated typologies across the GLR. Across three threshold scenarios in sensitivity analysis, 84.27%, 99.01% and 83.43% of parcels retained LULC transition, LMPs trend and multi-year integrated typology classes respectively. The diversity of annual integrated typology increased over time due to the complexity of land use and management practices, even though it decreased for conventional LULC. To demonstrate the practicality of our approach, we used linear mixed-effects models, which compare the performance of our annual integrated typology relative to conventional LULC classifications in predicting water-quality parameters (phosphorus, nitrite, and Kjeldahl nitrogen) in streams draining agricultural watersheds. The annual integrated typology models achieved lower RMSE and higher R 2 than conventional LULC models in the validation for phosphorus, nitrite, and Kjeldahl nitrogen, supporting the predictive value of combining the management attributes in the case study. The framework offers a flexible, interpretable tool for landscape characterization, agricultural planning, conservation implementation, and informed decision-making, and is replicable across regions.

title: Sensing and reversible capture of methylamine, methanethiol, and formic acid on Ti2C-based MXene monolayers: a DFT study.
abstract: Surface termination governs adsorption and electronic response in Ti2C MXene monolayers, but how O, F, and OH terminations shape sensing and reversible capture across distinct functional groups remains unresolved. Using dispersion-corrected first-principles DFT, we evaluated Ti2CO2, Ti2CF2, and Ti2C(OH)2 for the adsorption of methylamine (CH3NH2), methanethiol (CH3SH), and formic acid (HCOOH), selected to represent amine, thiol, and carboxyl groups, respectively. The adsorption energies ranged from -0.663 to -0.231 eV, and overall adsorption strength followed Ti2C(OH)2 > Ti2CO2 > Ti2CF2. Ti2CO2 and Ti2CF2 preferentially adsorbed CH3SH, whereas Ti2C(OH)2 preferred CH3NH2 and formed the strongest adsorption complex overall. Adsorption-energy-based molecular residence-time estimates ranged from 8.10 × 10-8 to 1.40 × 10-1 s, indicating preliminary desorption trends rather than established regeneration kinetics. Ti2CO2 remained semiconducting, with model-dependent band-gap-based electronic response estimates of 22.6-33.5% and work function shifts of -0.62 to +0.13 eV, supporting its potential for semiconductor sensing within the assumed conductivity model. Ti2C(OH)2 exhibited the strongest adsorption, particularly for CH3NH2; its subsecond residence-time estimates do not independently establish reversible capture performance. Its small, similar work function shifts of -0.05 to -0.03 eV indicated limited molecular differentiation through work function alone. Ti2CF2 exhibited the weakest adsorption and shortest residence-time estimates, while molecule-dependent work function shifts of -0.54 to +0.14 eV supported its potential for work-function-based sensing. These findings demonstrate that the strongest adsorption does not necessarily produce the most distinctive electronic response and establish distinct adsorption, preliminary desorption, and electronic-response profiles for the three Ti2C monolayers.

title: An osteophilic and fibrophobic nanocomposite hydrogel for alveolar bone defect repair.
abstract: Uncontrolled soft-tissue invasion remains a major challenge in alveolar bone defect repair and is conventionally managed using guided bone regeneration membranes. However, membrane-based approaches mainly depend on passive physical exclusion and lack active tissue selectivity. Herein, we report an osteophilic and fibrophobic nanocomposite hydrogel, termed BHP-gel, composed of crosslinked gelatin and Ca(OH)2-activated bioactive hollow particles. BHP-gel is designed to provide structural support while actively regulating early cellular competition between osteogenic and fibroblastic cells within bone defects. In vitro, BHP-gel selectively promoted the viability, migration and osteogenic differentiation of MC3T3-E1 pre-osteoblasts, accompanied by increased calcium-associated staining, while suppressing the viability and migration of L929 fibroblasts and gingival fibroblasts. Transcriptomic analysis suggested that fibroblastic inhibition was associated with downregulated migration-related genes and altered apoptosis-related transcriptional responses, whereas BHP-treated MC3T3-E1 cells showed upregulated genes related to migration, calcium signaling, and Wnt-associated osteogenic regulation. In a rat alveolar bone defect model, BHP-gel improved micro-CT-derived indices of mineralized tissue formation and trabecular microarchitecture compared with the control, HP-gel, and Bio-Oss® groups. These findings suggest that BHP-gel supports bone repair and exhibits cell-type-dependent regulation of osteogenic and fibroblastic cells in vitro, providing a materials-based strategy that may reduce reliance on exogenous barrier membranes for alveolar bone defect repair.

title: Mental distress and healthcare utilisation among sami and non-sami adults: a prospective registry-linked cohort study utilising data from the SAMINOR 2 questionnaire survey and the Norwegian control and payment of health reimbursements database (2012-2022).
abstract: Mental distress is associated increased healthcare utilisation, but little is known about whether the relationship between mental distress and use of health care services differs between Sami and non-Sami populations in Norway. The aim of this study was to investigate whether level of mental distress was associated with a different pattern of use of primary and specialised healthcare services among Sami and non-Sami populations. Data from the SAMINOR 2 Questionnaire Survey were linked to data from the Norwegian Control and Payout of Health Refunds Database and Statistics Norway. Level of mental distress based on the 10 items Hopkins Symptom Checklist was the primary exposure variable. Participants were categorised as Sami or non-Sami and stratified by sex. Primary and specialist healthcare utilisation, and the interaction between mental distress and ethnicity, were assessed by estimating incidence rates and incidence rate ratios from Negative binomial generalised linear models with a log link. The primary model was adjusted for age, years of education, and chronic conditions. Mental distress was associated with increased utilisation of both primary and specialist healthcare services across all ethnic and sex groups. Only minor differences in use of health care were observed between the two ethnic groups. Ethnicity did not significantly modify the associations between mental distress and use of health care. The association between mental distress and healthcare use was largely similar across ethnic groups after adjustment for covariates. Comparable utilisation rates should not be interpreted as evidence of identical healthcare-seeking processes, as cultural, contextual, and structural factors may influence how individuals engage with healthcare services. Further research should explore pathways to healthcare among Sami and non-Sami populations.

title: PlantVirDisConDB: an integrated resource linking plant virus sequence records with hosts, phenotypes, targets, antiviral evidence, and AI-assisted prioritization.
abstract: Research on plant viruses depends on taxonomy, nucleic acid sequences, host and disease records, molecular targets, and antiviral assays. These data are distributed across separate resources, making integrated retrieval and comparison difficult. PlantVirDisConDB (https://dpai.ccnu.edu.cn/PVDCDB) is freely accessible without login or registration and links these data through curated plant virus records. At the July 2026 reporting date, it comprised, in round numbers, 5000 virus and subviral agent records and 38 000 sequence accessions. It also included approximately1900 hosts, 9000 virus-host associations, 4800 disease names, 5000 structure records, and 25 000 small molecules. Direct assay records for plant viruses are distinguished from general antiviral background data; experimental and predicted structures, and measured activities and model outputs, are also labelled separately. Linked record pages support retrieval across these data types, access to individual sequence records, target searches, and molecular similarity searches. An activity prediction module ranks candidate molecule-virus pairs with applicability warnings and does not imply experimental or field efficacy. PlantVirDisConDB links viral nucleic acid entities to hosts, phenotypes, targets, and antiviral information and is updated through continuing curation and user feedback.
