title: Sociocultural Appearance-Related Attitudes and Psychological Resources and Their Associations With Moderate-Intensity Exercise, Body Size Perception, and Screen Time Among Female University Students: Cross-Sectional Latent Profile Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND Female university students encounter appearance ideals, comparison cues, and appearance-related pressure across traditional and digital media environments. These sociocultural influences may coexist with psychological resources such as body appreciation and weight-control self-efficacy. However, variable-centered analyses may obscure heterogeneity in how these characteristics are combined within individuals. The measures used in this study assessed broader sociocultural appearance-related attitudes rather than platform-specific digital exposure. OBJECTIVE This study aimed to identify latent profiles characterized by ideal-body internalization, appearance comparison, perceived media pressure, body appreciation, and weight-control self-efficacy among female university students and to examine whether these profiles differed in moderate-intensity exercise duration, self-perceived body size, and screen-based sedentary behavior. METHODS A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between May and June 2025 among 2034 female students recruited by convenience sampling from 1 comprehensive university in China. Latent profile analysis compared 1- through 6-profile solutions. Model selection considered information criteria, likelihood-ratio tests, entropy, profile size, parsimony, and substantive interpretability. Distal outcomes were compared using the Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars (BCH) procedure for continuous outcomes and the distal categorical outcome (DCAT) procedure for categorical outcomes. Sensitivity analyses examined alternative exercise definitions, transformations, extreme-value handling, sociodemographic adjustment, and self-reported BMI. Conventionally calculated weekly moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) outcomes were examined among 1056 participants with complete activity data. The primary analysis preserved classification uncertainty, and supplementary models assessed the robustness of associations without treating most-likely profile membership as error-free. No population-prevalence inference was intended. RESULTS A 4-profile solution was retained (entropy=0.874): very low sociocultural attitudes-higher body appreciation (137/2034, 6.74%), average sociocultural attitudes (1081/2034, 53.15%), lower sociocultural attitudes (452/2034, 22.22%), and higher sociocultural attitudes (364/2034, 17.9%). Solutions with 5 and 6 profiles each contained a very small class of approximately 1.7% (35/2034), and the adjusted Lo-Mendell-Rubin test comparing 6 vs 5 profiles was nonsignificant (P=.47). The profiles were differentiated primarily by a low-to-high gradient in appearance comparison, ideal-body internalization, and perceived media pressure. Moderate-intensity exercise duration differed across profiles in the primary analysis (BCH Wald χ23=15.3; P=.002), but complete-case weekly MVPA did not (P=.52). Body-size perception differed in the unadjusted analysis (DCAT χ29=20.4; P=.02), although the overall association was not independent of sociodemographic characteristics and self-reported BMI. Weekly screen-use categories did not differ significantly across profiles (DCAT χ212=16.7; P=.16). CONCLUSIONS The retained profiles were sample-specific statistical configurations that largely represented a sociocultural low-to-high gradient rather than 4 clearly discrete psychological types. Associations with exercise and body-size perception were modest and sensitive to outcome definition or covariate adjustment. The cross-sectional findings do not establish causal direction or digital media mechanisms. Longitudinal, multisite studies incorporating direct measures of digital exposure, exercise motivation, objectively assessed activity, and measured anthropometry are needed.

title: Sustainable postharvest management of fruits: Bridging biology, technology and policy
abstract: Postharvest loss remains a major barrier to agricultural productivity, yet proven technologies and interventions exist to reduce it. Globally, an estimated 14% of food is lost between harvest and retail (FAO, 2019), while a further 19% of the food available to consumers is wasted in retail, food service, and households (UNEP, 2024). Fruits and vegetables are among the most perishable agricultural commodities, and their high-water content, fragile tissues, and vulnerability to mechanical injury and decay lead to value-chain losses of 20% - 50%, depending on the crop and region (Khan et al., 2024). Where fruit is lost depends on where it is grown. In developing regions, losses occur early, on farms and during handling, because cold storage facility is scarce and produce passes through thousands of unconnected smallholders. In developed economies, losses occur later, at retail and household levels, driven by overproduction, strict cosmetic standards and consumer behavior (Khan et al., 2024). Globally, these losses cost hundreds of billions of dollars annually. Due to this, growers earn less, consumers pay more, and the land, water and energy used to produce the fruit gets wasted. Although logistics plays pivotal role in post-harvest loss reduction, however, it explains only part of the problem. Understanding quick fruit deterioration needs looking at biology. Physiological and biochemical processes going on within fruit are important in fruit spoilage. Senescence is not a simple decay, but a firmly regulated process in which ethylene plays a central role. In climacteric fruits, ethylene biosynthesis and signalling trigger a burst of respiration that drives ripening, while non-climacteric species follow quieter, ethylene-independent cues feeding into much the same genetic machinery (Tipu and Sherif, 2024). As senescence proceeds, reactive oxygen species accumulate faster than the fruit's antioxidant enzymes can neutralise them, causing lipid peroxidation and membrane damage. Simultaneously, enzymes such as polygalacturonase and cellulase break down the pectin and hemicellulose that give tissue its structure, explaining why ripe fruit softens. Chlorophyll degrades, other pigments accumulate, water is lost through transpiration, and starch converts into sugar, rewriting colour, texture, and flavour within days. Ethylene and abscisic acid pathways, alongside carbohydrate and ROS metabolism, remain the principal molecular drivers of this decline across both fruit classes (Storch et al., 2025). Every serious postharvest intervention such as cold chain, packaging, coating, or biocontrol agent, works by interrupting one of these triggers rather than masking its effects. Conventional refrigeration is the obvious starting point, but it is energy intensive, still largely dependent on hydrofluorocarbons, and out of reach for smallholders without reliable grid access. Low carbon alternatives are beginning to close this gap. Solar photovoltaic cold storage, paired with cold thermal energy storage using ice, chilled water, or phase change materials, keeps cooling running through cloudy days and after dark, making it more dependable in weak-grid settings and considerably lower carbon than diesel backed refrigeration over its lifetime (Mehtab et al., 2026). Passive evaporative systems achieve much the same result with no electricity at all such as charcoal coolers, clay pot devices, and cooling blankets exploit evaporative cooling to lower produce temperature by 3–10°C and raise relative humidity to 70–100%, buying several extra days of shelf life (Defraeye et al., 2023). Field trials in tropical value chains report postharvest loss reduction of up to 45% from these passive systems, rivalling far costlier mechanical options. Where cold chains manage the environment fruit sits in, modified and controlled atmosphere packaging (MAP/CAP) manages the microclimate around each piece, adjusting oxygen, carbon dioxide, and nitrogen levels to slow respiration, delay ripening, and hold microbial growth in check. It is among the most commercially proven postharvest tools, yet its dependence on petroleum based films has pushed research toward starch, chitosan, and cellulose based alternatives that now match synthetic films for barrier performance while breaking down naturally once discarded. Edible coatings extend this idea further, forming a semipermeable layer directly on the fruit's surface that regulates respiration, water loss, and gas exchange while carrying active compounds where they are needed. Chitosan, alginate, and gum arabic dominate this space for their antimicrobial properties, film forming stability, and compatibility with plant derived actives such as essential oils, which additionally slowdown enzymatic browning and limit lipid peroxidation restraining senescence on several fronts at once. Because these materials are renewable, non-toxic and compostable, they align with both circular economy goals and clean label consumer preferences. Non-thermal physical treatments offer a chemical free complement to these methods without sacrificing sensory quality or nutrition. Cold plasma, produced by ionising gas at room temperature, generates reactive oxygen and nitrogen species, UV photons, and charged particles that eliminate surface pathogens while pushing the fruit's own metabolism. Reported microbial log reductions of 2.0–5.0 across fruit types match or exceed conventional sanitisers without heat damage (Shill and Sit, 2025), while also stimulating antioxidant enzyme activity that helps preserve phenolic and flavonoid content. Pulsed light, UV-C, ozone, and electrolysed water work through related mechanisms, suppressing spoilage organisms with little effect on firmness, colour, or vitamin content, a natural complement to cold chains and packaging rather than a replacement. A different, biological line of defence targets pathogens directly. Botrytis cinerea, Penicillium, and Alternaria species collectively account for 35–50% of postharvest fruit losses each year, historically controlled with synthetic fungicides whose long-term overuse has bred resistance and raised consumer health concerns (Godana et al., 2026). Biocontrol agents such as antagonistic yeasts, bacteria, and filamentous fungi, offer a genuinely sustainable alternative, competing for nutrients and space, producing antifungal metabolites, forming protective biofilms, and activating the fruit's own defences. Research is moving past single-strain products toward compatible microbial consortia, including yeast-bacteria combinations from naturally fermented foods, which cast a wider antagonistic net and hold up better under commercial variability than any single organism. None of these interventions work well unless growers know precisely when and where to apply them, and digital, AI-enabled tools are turning postharvest management from reactive inspection into predictive, data-driven decision-making. In developing regions, where losses from rotting, mechanical damage, and inconsistent grading can reach 40–80% in the worst cases, AI-augmented sensing is beginning to address these inefficiencies directly (El-Beltagi et al., 2025). Non-destructive imaging i.e., RGB, hyperspectral, near-infrared and X-ray methods, combined with deep learning models such as convolutional neural networks can now assess soluble solids, firmness, internal defects, and ripeness stage quickly and objectively, replacing subjective sampling. Connecting these systems to Internet-of-Things sensor networks enables continuous, real-time monitoring across the supply chain, catching problems before quality slips (El-Beltagi et al., 2025). Paired with robotic sorting and grading, this is already improving throughput, consistency, and traceability from farm to retail shelf. Even with better cooling, packaging, sanitation, biocontrol and monitoring in place, some fruit will always be rejected and this is where circular-economy thinking earns its keep, treating discarded pomace, peels, and cosmetically rejected fruit as an underused source of valuable biomolecules rather than waste. Of the roughly 1.3 billion tonnes of edible food lost or wasted globally each year, much of this material still contains vitamins, fibre, polyphenols and prebiotic compounds, sometimes at higher concentrations than in fruit that reached market (Worku et al., 2026). Green extraction methods such as ultrasound-assisted extraction, supercritical fluid extraction and deep eutectic solvent systems recover these bioactives efficiently and with a light environmental footprint, feeding into nutraceuticals, functional foods, and biodegradable packaging while opening new revenue streams for growers. Integrated biorefineries take this further by turning fruit waste into energy, biofertiliser and microbial growth media. This eases pressure on food supplies, cuts landfill methane, and supports SDG 12's goal of halving food waste. Technology alone, though, will not end postharvest loss. In smallholder economies, 15-50% loss persist not because solutions are missing, but due to financial limitations, poor coordination of institutions, implementation is irregular, and extension services are under considerable pressure due to resource constraints. Closing the gap requires farmer training, locally adapted technologies, wider credit access, stronger policies, and integration of postharvest practices into climate-smart value chains from the outset. Postharvest management is a core component of food security and climate policy, reducing losses, improving efficiency, and strengthening resilience while advancing SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production). From senescence physiology to low‑carbon cooling, sustainable packaging, non‑thermal decontamination, microbiome‑based biocontrol, AI monitoring, and waste recovery, these approaches demonstrate that no single technology can address postharvest challenges in isolatio

title: QuickLeaf-LWA high-throughput software: automated digital image analysis for accurate measurement of leaf shape and size
abstract: Aim: Leaf size and shape are key character for assessing photosynthesis, growth, genetic diversity, and plant health. Manual measurement is labor-intensive, time-consuming, and error-prone, particularly in large-scale phenotyping studies. This study aimed to develop QuickLeaf-LWA, a software tool for rapid, precise, and automated estimation of leaf size (length and width) and shape (aspect ratio) from digital images. Methodology: QuickLeaf-LWA integrates high-throughput automation (HTA) with comprehensive trait management and morphological analysis workflows. The software employs a robust image-processing pipeline using adaptive threshold for accurate leaf segmentation from complex backgrounds, followed by morphological operations to reduce noise. Leaf dimensions and aspect ratio are calculated using a rectangular-bounded, radially rotated image approach. Results: Accuracy assessment showed low mean error rates (0.584–3.283%) and high accuracy (96.717–99.416%). Root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) values were low (0.150–0.564 and 0.082–0.476, respectively), with strong correlations to manual measurements (R2 ≥ 0.96). Interpretation: QuickLeaf-LWA enables rapid analysis of hundreds of leaves within minutes offers an intuitive interface with batch-processing capability, making it a practical tool for plant physiology, genetics, agriculture, horticulture, and leaf phenotyping research. Key words: Aspect ratio, Digital image analysis, Leaf phenotyping, QuickLeaf-(LWA)

title: Fusarium sugarcane pathosystem: Etiology, diversity, host-pathogen interactions, epidemiology, diagnosis and management of Pokkah Boeng disease of sugarcane
abstract: Pokkah Boeng is an emerging and economically significant disease of sugarcane (Saccharum spp.), causing yield losses of 10-15% in India and posing an increasing threat to sustainable cane production worldwide. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of current knowledge on the Fusarium Sugarcane Pathosystem, encompassing disease etiology, pathogen diversity, host-pathogen interactions, epidemiology, diagnostics and integrated management strategies. Particular emphasis is laid on the taxonomic complexity, phylogenetic relationships and pathogenic variability of the Fusarium species complex associated with Pokkah Boeng disease of sugarcane. The review further explores the influence of climatic drivers, crop production practices, inoculum dynamics and pathogen dissemination mechanisms in shaping disease outbreaks, with particular relevance to Indian agro-ecosystems. Recent advances in understanding molecular interactions between Fusarium and sugarcane are discussed including fungal effectors, virulence-associated factors, host defence responses and emerging biotechnological approaches. Current disease management practices, including resistant cultivar deployment, cultural measures, biological control, fungicide application and RNA based technologies are critically evaluated. Finally, key knowledge gaps and future research priorities are highlighted, emphasising the integration of precision diagnostics, genomics-assisted resistance breeding, climate based disease forecasting and sustainable agro-ecological approaches for durable management of Pokkah Boeng disease of sugarcane. Key words: Epidemiology, Fusarium spp., Host Pathogen interaction, Pokkah Boeng, Sugarcane

title: STRATEGIC OPTIMIZATION OF PROVINCIAL-AUTHORITY IRRIGATION NETWORKS IN WEST JAVA: A MULTI- OBJECTIVE PROGRAMMING FRAMEWORK FOR PERFORMANCE-BASED BUDGETING
abstract: Provincial irrigation agencies in West Java must allocate limited operation, maintenance, and rehabilitation budgets across ageing networks in uneven condition. This study develops a Multi-Objective Programming (MOP) framework for the 99 provincial-authority irrigation areas that integrates the six-aspect Irrigation System Performance Index (IKSI) of Ministerial Regulation No. 12/PRT/M/2015 directly into the optimization model, and links it to physical-condition assessment, budget scenarios, a five-year simulation, and qualitative policy interpretation. The model minimizes public expenditure while maximizing IKSI-weighted performance and the share of crop-water requirements met, subject to water, hydraulic, regulatory, and fiscal constraints. Evidence comes from a field survey of 99 canal segments and planning and budget documents. Of the 99 surveyed segments, 38 (38.4%) were in good, 41 (41.4%) in moderate, and 20 (20.2%) in damaged condition. Under the realistic budget scenario, the good-condition share is projected to reach 45.4–48.4% by 2029, an increase of 7–10 percentage points; this is a scenario projection, not a Pareto-optimal solution. The framework reframes irrigation budgeting as a strategic portfolio-allocation problem.

title: Realization and analysis of Artificial Intelligence appearance in Agricultural system
abstract: Agriculture is increasingly expected to produce more food while minimizing the usage of water, chemical-based fertilizers, energy, chemicals, and labor. Agricultural decision-making is further complicated by climate unpredictability, soil degradation, shortages of water, crop illnesses, pests, weeds, and yield uncertainties. An IEEE-style review and implementation methodology for AI in agriculture is presented in this research. Examined are a number of important applications, including as crop recommendations, crop-yield estimation, disease and pest recognition, weed identification, soil and nutrient administration, smart irrigating, weather forecasting, livestock monitoring, agricultural robots, and post-harvest management. A multilayer AI-enabled farming system is proposed in which a conventional sensor, image processing, and historical information are acquired through IoT, UAV, satellites, and field devices; processed information is provided to machine-learning(ML)/deep-learning models; and the ensuing decisions are transmitted to farmers or automated actuators. Conventional models such as Decision Tree(DT), Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbor(KNN), Support Vector Machine(SVM), and Artificial Neural Network(ANN) are contrasted conceptually with CNN, LSTM, and Transformer-based techniques.Substantial research gaps in dataset variety, model generalization and explanation, efficiency of computation, cybersecurity, field validation,, and cost for small-scale farmers are also identified in the report. For sustainable intelligent agriculture, a future research path based on explainable AI, edge intelligence, hybrid AI, and multimodal data fusion is suggested.
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Growth-State Consistency Learning for Temporal Plant Growth-Stage and Leaf-Count Estimation
abstract: Purpose: This study addresses temporally inconsistent plant growth-stage predictions and visible leaf-count estimates from image sequences. Design/Methodology/Approach: Growth-State Consistency Learning (GSCL) combines an ImageNet-pretrained ConvNeXt-Tiny encoder, spatial self-attention, a two-layer temporal Transformer, growth-stage classification, visible leaf-count regression, and one-sided prediction-level monotonicity regularizers. PhenoLeaf-TS was partitioned by plant into 222 training, 48 validation, and 48 held-out test plants. Four-frame windows were used. Research Limitation: Since the stage labels are defined by visible leaf count thresholds, the two prediction tasks are statistically and conceptually coupled. In the setting where true leaf loss or senescence occurs, the prior may not be valid. Findings: The average predictions for 2514 unique test images resulted in an accuracy of 93.20% with 92.70% balanced accuracy and 92.90% macro-F1 score. The mean absolute error for leaf count was 0.69 leaves. The complementary window-conditioned evaluation showed 93.00% accuracy with 92.40% balanced accuracy and 92.60% macro-F1 score and a mean absolute error of 0.70 leaves. Practical Implication: The approach makes repeated-image monitoring more stable. Social Implication: More stable plant image monitoring could promote data-informed crop and plant research. Originality/Value: GSCL integrates temporal multi-task prediction with soft consistency regularisation on predicted outputs, reporting both unique-frame and overlapping-window evaluations.

title: Pengaruh Topografi Lahan terhadap Produktivitas Pemanen di Perkebunan Kelapa Sawit
abstract: This study examines the effect of land topography on the productivity of oil palm harvesters at PT Salim Ivomas Pratama. The method used in this study is a quantitative comparative approach, to compare productivity across different topographies. This study analyzes the performance of 90 harvesters divided into two types of topography (flat and hilly) using purposive sampling. Other variables such as the age of the harvesters, work experience, crop variety, and harvesting infrastructure were included in the regression model as control variables to avoid estimation bias and ensure that the effect of topography on productivity could be analyzed more accurately. Data analysis was conducted using the chi-square test to determine differences in productivity between the two topographies and multiple linear regression to identify the determinants of harvest yield. The results of the study demonstrate that hilly terrain significantly reduces harvester productivity due to the difficult and physically demanding terrain. In addition to topographic factors, productivity also decreases with the increasing age of harvesters, plant age, and tree height. Conversely, the use of high-yielding plant varieties and the availability of good harvesting infrastructure were found to increase harvester productivity. Meanwhile, work experience does not have a significant effect on productivity.

title: CORPORATE STRATEGY TO HUMAN CAPITAL: THE ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND GOVERNANCE TRANSITION IN HOSPITALITY WITH A BIBLIOMETRIC APPROACH
abstract: Within The Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework has become a defining paradigm in the transformation of the hospitality industry, shifting the focus from profit-oriented models to integrated sustainability and accountability systems. In this context, understanding how ESG research evolves and what dimensions dominate the discourse becomes increasingly important. The aim of this study is to analyse the development of ESG-related research in hospitality between 2009 and 2025, with particular attention to the transition from financial governance to human capital-oriented approaches. Despite the expansion of the field, the literature remains fragmented, characterised by conceptual ambiguity with Corporate Social Responsibility, inconsistent measurement practices, and limited integration of ESG dimensions within servicebased industries. The research is based on a bibliometric analysis of 987 publications indexed in the Web of Science database. The methodological approach combines performance analysis with science mapping techniques in order to identify publication trends, intellectual structures, and conceptual developments within the field. The results indicate a significant increase in research activity after 2019, accompanied by a shift in thematic focus. Earlier studies primarily emphasised financial performance, environmental efficiency, and external stakeholder perceptions. In contrast, recent research highlights the growing importance of employees as key drivers of ESG value creation. This reflects a redefinition of the Social dimension, which increasingly functions as an internal governance mechanism centred on employee engagement, well-being, and organisational behaviour. At the same time, the Environmental and Governance dimensions remain strongly interconnected through performance metrics and regulatory requirements, resulting in an imbalanced ESG structure. The internal social dimension is less standardised and insufficiently integrated into strategic decision-making processes. The study concludes that this imbalance limits the effectiveness of ESG implementation in the hospitality sector. The findings suggest that future development depends on the systematic integration of human capital considerations into governance frameworks, particularly in response to emerging European sustainability regulations. The contribution of the paper lies in identifying the internal social dimension as a key frontier of ESG research and in providing a structured overview of the field’s evolution, offering both theoretical clarification and practical relevance for sustainability-oriented management in hospitality.

title: A Machine Learning Framework for Precision Soil Quality Characterization for Crop-Specific Fertilizer Recommendation in Heterogeneous Agro-Ecosystems
abstract: Accurate fertilizer recommendation is fundamental to precision agriculture, yet many machine learning models rely on static soil nutrient measurements without adequately incorporating environmental factors that influence nutrient availability. This study proposes a hybrid machine learning framework that integrates soil chemical, physical, and climatic variables into a Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-derived Soil Quality Index (SQI) for crop-specific fertilizer recommendation. The framework combines PCA-based feature extraction with Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) classifiers. Experiments were conducted on an 8,000-record dataset comprising 11 crop types, five soil classes, and seven fertilizer categories. Model development included standardized preprocessing, stratified train-test partitioning, and exhaustive hyperparameter optimization. Despite this rigorous framework, all models achieved only 12.4–14.0% test accuracy, equivalent to the 14.29% random baseline for a seven-class classification problem. Statistical auditing revealed that fertilizer labels were not significantly associated with soil or crop types (Chi-square, p = 0.584 and p = 0.100, respectively), while mutual information between continuous predictors and fertilizer labels was negligible. Learning-curve analysis further showed that the models have excellent training performance but no improvement in validation accuracy, indicating poor predictor-label dependency rather than inadequate model capacity. These findings demonstrate that dataset quality, rather than algorithm selection, constrained predictive performance. The primary contribution of this work is a robust and reusable machine learning pipeline complemented by a systematic predictor-label dependency auditing protocol. This framework provides a practical methodology for validating agricultural datasets before model deployment, thereby improving the reliability, reproducibility, and trustworthiness of precision agriculture and digital soil mapping applications.

title: Cultivated area and yield dynamics of maize and soybean in South Africa: a pre- and post-GM introduction analysis (1987-2025)
abstract: South Africa has cultivated genetically modified (GM) maize and soybean commercially for more than two decades, yet long-term evidence on how cultivated area and yield evolved across the periods before and after GM introduction remains limited. Using a pre- and post-GM introduction framework, this study examines national cultivated-area and yield dynamics for maize (1987-2025) and soybean (1988-2025), using 1998 and 2001 as the predefined commercial GM introduction breakpoints, respectively. The pre-GM period refers to the historical years before commercial GM introduction, while the post-GM period covers the years from commercial introduction onward. Annual commercial crop data from the Crop Estimates Committee were analysed using descriptive comparisons, Chow structural-break tests and autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) bounds testing. Mean maize cultivated area declined from approximately 3.55 million ha in the pre-GM period to 2.65 million ha in the post-GM period (−25.4%), while mean yield increased from 2.28 to 4.42 t/ha (+94.1%). Mean soybean cultivated area increased from approximately 74,561 ha to 515,198 ha (+591.0%), while mean yield increased from 1.45 to 1.81 t/ha (+24.8%). The Chow test identified a significant structural break in the maize cultivated area-yield relationship at 1998 [F(2,35)=6.234, p=0.0048], but not for soybean at 2001 [F(2,34)=0.791, p=0.4615]. ARDL bounds testing supported a long-run relationship between cultivated area and yield for soybean (F=9.250, p<0.001), whereas cointegration was not supported for maize (F=3.203, p=0.226), whose selected ARDL model also showed diagnostic weaknesses. The findings reveal different patterns for the two crops. Maize yields increased despite a decline in cultivated area, while soybean experienced increases in both cultivated area and yield. However, these changes cannot be attributed solely to GM technology, as other factors, including climate, market conditions, agricultural policies and technological developments, may also have influenced the observed trends.

title: Glutamate-centered metabolic and signaling networks in skeletal homeostasis and diseases
abstract: Glutamate (Glu) occupies an unusual position in skeletal biology, functioning as both a local signaling molecule and a central intermediate of cellular metabolism. Although these roles are often discussed separately, they converge on processes that determine bone and cartilage homeostasis. This review integrates glutamatergic signaling with the intracellular glutamine (Gln)-Glu-α-ketoglutarate (α-KG)-glutathione (GSH) pathway and examines how Glu availability is translated into cell-specific responses. Across osteoblasts (OBs), osteoclasts (OCLs), bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), and chondrocytes, Glu receptors and transporters modulate Ca 2 ⁺, cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP), and kinase signaling, whereas Gln-derived Glu supports tricarboxylic acid (TCA)-cycle metabolism, biosynthesis, epigenetic regulation, and antioxidant defense. The balance between these signaling and metabolic functions varies with cell type, differentiation stage, nutrient supply, mechanical loading, and inflammation. This context dependence may explain why Glu-associated pathways can support bone formation in one setting but favor resorption or cartilage damage in another. Evidence from osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, intervertebral disc degeneration, and multiple myeloma-associated bone disease highlights how disturbed nutrient availability and local Glu handling can impair tissue homeostasis. However, most mechanistic evidence remains preclinical, and Glu-related concentrations, spatial gradients, and metabolic fluxes in human skeletal tissues are poorly defined. Stable-isotope tracing, spatial metabolomics, cell-specific genetic models, and targeted delivery strategies will be essential for translating this Glu-centered network into skeletal therapies.

title: Epithelial inflammatory memory in ulcerative colitis: molecular mechanisms and translational implications
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) can relapse after clinical and endoscopic remission, raising the question of whether previously inflamed epithelium retains altered responsiveness. Patient-derived colonic organoids and lineage-resolved colitis models show that inflammation-associated chromatin accessibility can persist after removal of the original environment and influence subsequent epithelial behavior. Basal inflammatory transcription, however, can return toward normal during organoid expansion. These observations distinguish ongoing inflammatory output from latent regulatory competence; transcriptomic normalization alone neither establishes nor excludes functional memory. Differences between paired colonic regions and persistence across molecular layers support spatial and molecular heterogeneity. Exposure history, treatment, and patient characteristics are plausible modifiers whose independent contributions remain unresolved. This Review focuses on the evidence for epithelial inflammatory memory in UC and its implications for regeneration and mucosal healing. We examine how stem and regenerative lineages could retain prior experience, with emphasis on enhancer accessibility and the supporting evidence for histone, DNA-methylation, and metabolic mechanisms. Persistent epithelial states are distinguished from continued niche stimulation, reversible adaptation, fixed injury, and somatic clonal selection. Altered recall can accelerate repair while coexisting with deficient differentiation, barrier function, or regenerative reserve, making functional recovery more informative than inflammatory output alone. Translational opportunities include targeted biopsy assays linked to organoid recall, longitudinal sampling during remission, and interventions that restore mature epithelial function. Stepwise assay validation and treatment testing could connect these mechanisms to clinical outcomes, although no epithelial memory assay or memory-directed therapy is currently validated for routine UC care.

title: Monocyte regulatory phenotypes and systemic proteomic signatures in helminth-tuberculosis coinfection
abstract: Chronic helminth infection is associated with altered anti-mycobacterial immunity, including impaired Th1 responses and expansion of regulatory immune populations. However, how helminth infection reshapes coordinated innate and adaptive immune pathways during active tuberculosis remains poorly understood. We therefore investigated systemic and cellular immune signatures associated with helminth infection, tuberculosis (TB), and helminth-TB coinfection. Plasma and peripheral blood mononuclear cells were obtained from healthy Swedish controls, endemic Peruvian controls, individuals with helminth infection, active tuberculosis, and helminth-TB coinfection. Plasma proteins were quantified using high-throughput Olink proteomics, while circulating monocytes and CD4 + T-cell compartments were characterized via flow cytometry. Protein abundance, monocyte phenotypes, and CD4 + T-cell differentiation and activation marker expression were compared between study groups. Proteomic profiling revealed broad differences associated with active TB, whereas helminth infection alone was associated with relatively few differentially abundant proteins compared with endemic controls. Participants with helminth-TB coinfection exhibited 65 differentially abundant proteins compared with endemic controls, including 33 that met the significance threshold only in this comparison. These proteins were associated with immune regulation, leukocyte trafficking, vascular activation, and myeloid responses. Flow cytometric analysis revealed increased PD-L1 expression on intermediate monocytes in helminth-infected participants compared to endemic controls, while plasma CD274 abundance was highest in helminth-TB coinfection. Coinfected individuals also displayed increased IL-4 receptor expression on classical and intermediate monocytes compared to the endemic control group. Within the CD4 + T-cell compartment, helminth infection was associated with broad upregulation of PD-1 across naïve, central memory, effector memory, and effector subsets, whereas TB was associated with altered T-cell differentiation and increased TIM-3 expression. Helminth-TB coinfection combined these features and was further characterized by increased frequencies of CTLA-4 + , CD40L + , and CD28 + CD4 + T-cell populations. Plasma proteomic and cellular profiling identified distinct immune signatures associated with TB, helminth infection, and their co-occurrence. Helminth-TB coinfection was associated with additional changes in immune regulation and cell-communication pathways, alongside concurrent activation-associated and inhibitory features across monocyte and CD4 + T-cell compartments. Together, these findings support an exploratory model in which active TB is associated with broad systemic inflammatory remodeling, while helminth exposure is associated with an additional regulatory overlay during coinfection.

title: A metabolic flux efficiency model reveals mitochondrial triage: H2S reallocates carbon skeletons to match cysteine under cyanide stress in rice
abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) achieves comparable growth recovery to cysteine (Cys) in rice under cyanide (CN - ) stress, despite Cys being the direct substrate for CN - detoxification and driving a substantially higher assimilation rate via β-cyanoalanine synthase (β-CAS). This paradox implies a fundamental trade-off between immediate detoxification and long-term resilience. Here, we profiled tissue-resolved metabolomics of the TCA cycle intermediates oxaloacetate (OAA) and α-ketoglutarate (α-KG), and their cognate aspartate (Asp)- and glutamate (Glu)-family amino acids, the branches most intimately linked to CN - assimilation, together with transcriptional analysis of their biosynthetic genes. We then developed a Metabolic Flux Efficiency ( MFE ) model, a proof-of-concept framework that integrates these data to estimate relative flux efficiency within the TCA–amino acid (AA) cycle. H 2 S is proposed to execute a mitochondrial triage strategy, depleting root nitrogen reserves (Asn and Gln reduced by 92% and 67%) to liberate carbon skeletons, while boosting root α-KG (+93%) to sustain anaplerotic TCA cycle flux. The calibrated MFE model (Asp family: α = 0.39, β = 1.52; Glu family: α = 0.37, β = 1.64) suggests that metabolic conversion dominates over transcription in governing flux under CN - stress, and predicts that H 2 S redirects flow away from primary nitrogen assimilation (Glu→Gln) toward energy-generating cycles (Orn→Cit). This pattern is consistent with recovery being governed not by nitrogen abundance but by dynamic reallocation of carbon skeletons from storage to biosynthetic and anaplerotic routes. By redefining the mitochondrion as a metabolic regulatory hub that prioritizes reconstruction over mere survival, our work provides a quantitative framework for interpreting metabolic trade-offs and a conceptual basis for engineering stress-resilient crops.

title: Interpretable YOLO and mask-guided pooling for maize leaf disease classification in complex field backgrounds
abstract: Accurate identification of maize leaf diseases is essential for intelligent agricultural field management and targeted pesticide application. However, most current deep learning recognition research is limited to uniform laboratory backgrounds, presenting a significant domain gap with real-world farmland environments. Existing end-to-end classification models are prone to “Shortcut Learning” when facing complex field backgrounds containing soil, weeds, and varying illumination. They tend to fit environmental noise rather than true pathological characteristics, leading to poor generalization and the risk of illusory high performance. To fundamentally address this overfitting paradox, this paper proposes an innovative mask-guided pooling classification model requiring zero additional parameters (Mgp-YOLO11n). Specifically, we constructed a dataset of 3,092 real-world field images with complex backgrounds covering five maize health categories: Healthy, Gray Leaf Spot (GLS), Northern Leaf Blight (NLB), Northern Leaf Spot (NLS), and Curvularia Leaf Spot (CLS). We utilized a YOLO11-seg model embedded with a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to achieve high-quality instance segmentation of disease spots. Subsequently, the traditional Global Average Pooling (GAP) layer is replaced in the downstream classification network. The prior mask serves as spatial hard attention weights, and a dynamic effective area normalization mechanism (MGP operator) is introduced during feature aggregation to achieve physical isolation at the feature space level. Classic large models were introduced as benchmarks for a “background retention” versus “black background” cross-validation, alongside deep interpretability analysis via Grad-CAM. Experimental results indicate that while the baseline YOLO11n-cls model achieves an initial accuracy of 92.30% in complex backgrounds, it decreases sharply to 77.30% in the black background test (in which pixels outside the annotated leaf mask are set to black while the leaf region and image dimensions remain unchanged—this masks rather than crops the background, eliminating background cues without forcing the model to attend specifically to lesions), confirming the defect of relying on background induced spurious correlations. In contrast, Mgp-YOLO11n improves accuracy in complex backgrounds to 93.24%, and its accuracy in black background tests increases to 95.94% with zero additional learnable parameters and negligible impact on real-time inference speed. Grad-CAM heatmaps conclusively demonstrate that the MGP mechanism successfully eliminates background shortcuts, overcomes the receptive field’s edge penetration issue, and forces the network to focus entirely on intrinsic pathological characteristics. This study reconstructs the feature extraction paradigm of the classification head, mitigates the accuracy-centric pitfall in agricultural vision, and provides a robust framework for deploying agricultural edge-intelligent terminals, such as plant protection drones, in highly complex farmland environments.

title: Conserved and species-specific guard cell transcriptional responses and drought physiology in Arabidopsis and tomato
abstract: Crop productivity is severely threatened by climate change-related stresses, including drought stress. During drought, physiological and transcriptional changes occur in guard cells to regulate stomatal closure and minimize excess water loss. Tomato is an important crop species in temperate regions, with a high water requirement. To further understand the drought response in tomato, we performed RNA-seq on guard cell-enriched samples of plants subjected to severe drought stress. We investigated drought-responsive changes in gene expression and alternative splicing, including the role of ABA signaling genes. Comparing this data to previous work on the model species Arabidopsis thaliana , we highlighted an increased level of transcriptional reprogramming in tomato. These differences translated to the physiological level, where we observed earlier stomatal closure during progressive drought in tomato compared to A. thaliana using thermal imaging. Overall, this study sheds new light on tomato GCs during drought, and emphasizes the importance of translational studies on crop species.

title: Crop-adapted arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi in maize: from symbiotic function to field reliability
abstract: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) can improve nutrient acquisition and stress responses in maize, yet inoculation benefits remain inconsistent across fields. Root colonization alone does not establish effective nutrient transfer or net crop benefit. This critical narrative review examines maize-associated AMF diversity, arbuscule-mediated exchange, host genotype effects, phosphorus availability, stress responses, rhizosphere and hyphosphere interactions, inoculant quality, and field evidence. We define crop-adapted AMF by demonstrated function in a specified maize–soil–management context, rather than fungal origin or colonization percentage alone. Drawing on mechanistic research and contrasting field outcomes, we propose a six-stage Maize–Soil–AMF Fit Framework linking native resource mapping, functional screening, compatibility tests, formulation quality, field integration, and ecological monitoring. The framework distinguishes practical agronomic evidence from advanced mechanistic measurements and permits three decisions: inoculate with a validated product, manage an effective native AMF network, or avoid intervention. It is a conceptual decision aid, not a validated predictive model. Reliable application requires replicated, genotype-aware field tests with appropriate native-AMF controls, prespecified crop outcomes, and transparent assessment of uncertainty and economic value.

title: Temporal and gender heterogeneity in the association between physical exercise and subjective wellbeing in China: an age–period–cohort analysis
abstract: Although the positive association between physical exercise (PE) and subjective wellbeing (SWB) is well documented, little is known about whether its magnitude varies across the life course, birth cohorts, survey periods, and gender groups. This study analyzed pooled repeated cross-sectional data from five waves of the China General Social Survey (2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, and 2023), comprising 30,247 adults aged 18–97 years. A Hierarchical Age–Period–Cohort Cross-Classified Random Effects Model (HAPC-CCREM) was used to examine age-, period-, cohort-, and gender-related heterogeneity. Robustness was assessed using 5-year cohorts and the original five-category PE measure. Exercisers consistently exhibited higher predicted SWB than non-exercisers across the age range. The PE-related advantage followed a nonlinear age pattern, being pronounced in young adulthood, attenuating through middle adulthood, and strengthening again in later life. The cohort-level PE random-slope variance was statistically significant, whereas no statistically significant period-level variation in the PE slope was detected under the current model specification. Cohort-specific estimates descriptively indicated that the PE-related advantage was relatively large among earlier-born cohorts, narrowed across successive cohorts, reached a comparatively low level among those born during 1990–1999, and recovered modestly among those born in 2000 or later. Gender-related interaction terms were jointly significant. The PE–SWB association was stronger among men at the mean age, and the gender difference varied with age. The main findings remained stable across the sensitivity analyses. The positive association between PE and SWB varies across age, birth cohorts, and gender. These findings highlight the importance of considering life-course position, generational experience, and gendered circumstances when examining heterogeneity in this association. Because the data are repeated cross-sectional and the proposed mechanisms were not directly measured, the results should not be interpreted causally. Differentiated PE and wellbeing promotion strategies may therefore be appropriate for different population groups.

title: Coarse-to-fine-grained insulator defect detection using two-stage deep learning framework
abstract: In power transmission and power distribution systems, insulators are the fundamental components which provide mechanical support and electrical isolation between conductors and supporting towers. However, these insulators are continuously exposed to extreme weather conditions, mechanical stress, pollution and dust, which can lead to surface damage and abnormal operation. Conventionally, manual on-site inspection is performed to identify faulty insulators. However, this method is labor intensive, risky, and reactive. With the advancement in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology and deep learning method, automatic visual inspection has replaced the conventional methods. However, automatic visual inspection from UAV images is challenging task due to complex background and small size of the insulators. To address these challenges, we proposed a framework that consists of two stages. In the first stage, you only look once (YOLO)-based is used for extracting candidate region of insulator to get coarse class prediction. During the second stage, the candidate regions are then cropped from the image into image patches and fed to a lightweight patch-level classifier. In order to enhance inter-class separability, hard-pair contrastive classification loss is proposed by adding hard-pair contrastive term to the cross-entropy loss in the embedding space. The proposed technique is evaluated using an open-source insulator defect image dataset. The experiment results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed framework compared with the YOLO variants and representative two-stage detectors.

title: Analysis of the spatiotemporal evolution of agricultural production efficiency and its determinants in China
abstract: China faces regional disparities in agricultural development. Understanding the spatiotemporal evolution of agricultural production efficiency and its driving factors is essential for advancing sustainable agricultural development. Using panel data from China’s 31 provinces from 2013 to 2023, we constructed an input–output indicator system and applied the super-efficiency slacks-based measure (SBM) model to evaluate agricultural production efficiency. The results indicate that the evolution of agricultural production efficiency went through three stages. The period from 2013 to 2016 was characterized by fluctuations; the period from 2016 to 2021 was characterized by an overall upward trend; the period from 2021 to 2023 was characterized by a downward trend. The number of provinces with an agricultural production efficiency score of ≥1 increased from 8 to 11. Temporal kernel density analysis revealed that polarization between high- and low-efficiency provinces weakened from 2013 to 2022 but intensified in 2023. Spatial kernel density analysis showed a decline in the spatial clustering of agricultural production efficiency, with high-density zones gradually expanding from coastal areas to inland regions. Geographic detector analysis identifies socioeconomic factors (per capita education expenditure, farmer income, agricultural development level) and agricultural structure (pesticide input, planting structure) as key determinants, with rankings showing moderate sensitivity to temporal aggregation and discretization method but substantive policy priorities remaining consistent. Region-specific issues, including the low comparative returns from agriculture in the eastern region and low production efficiency in the central grain-producing region, underscore the need for countermeasures tailored to regional patterns of agricultural production efficiency across different regions. Such measures could include increased investment in human capital and optimization of crop structures. These findings provide empirical support for region-specific strategies aimed at improving agricultural production efficiency and promoting sustainable agricultural development.

title: Environmental suitability and climate-informed spatial prioritization of Opuntia ficus-indica (L.) MILL. in India using MaxEnt and the analytic hierarchy process
abstract: Climate-informed diversification of water-limited farming systems requires identifying environmentally suitable areas that remain favorable under future climate conditions. This study assessed the current and future environmental suitability of cactus pear ( Opuntia ficus-indica ) across India and developed a spatial prioritization framework for dryland agricultural planning. MaxEnt models using 138 spatially thinned occurrence records and climatic, soil, and land-use/land-cover predictors were projected to the 2050s and 2070s under four RCP scenarios using the BCC-CSM1-1 global climate model. MaxEnt-derived suitability was integrated with selected soil and land-surface criteria through the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). Future suitability persistence was quantified using the Climate Persistence Index (CPI) and combined with current integrated suitability to derive the Climate-smart Opuntia Priority Index (COPI). Current Moderate-to-Optimum integrated suitability covered approximately 1.085 million km 2 , of which 73.41% (796,315 km 2 ) retained at least Moderate suitability across five or more of eight future scenarios. COPI identified 549,070 km 2 (16.80% of the analyzed area) as High or Very-high priority, primarily in western India, with additional opportunities in peninsular regions. Five independently reported Indian experimental locations corresponded spatially with High or Very-high COPI classes; however, observed differences in survival and productivity demonstrated that model-derived suitability does not directly predict crop performance. The principal limitations include reliance on a single climate model, predefined MaxEnt regularization and AHP weights, static soil and land-use assumptions, and limited field correspondence. Thus, COPI provides a preliminary biophysical decision-support framework for prioritizing genotype evaluation, agronomic trials, and climate-smart dryland diversification rather than direct evidence of cultivation success or agricultural resilience.

title: Minute-Level Identification of Session-Conditioned Continuous News Decay via Differentiable Half-Life Learning
abstract: Financial-news studies commonly aggregate articles by day or use broad event windows, obscuring the elapsed time between publication and a tradable market response. We ask whether timestamped news and minute-level prices can identify how information persistence varies by release session and volatility. We propose Differentiable Session-Aware Rapid Attention Decay (DiffSARAD), which jointly learns a continuous global half-life, session- and volatility-conditioned adjustments to it, and a three-class post-publication abnormal-return classifier. The representation combines conditional exponential weights with both weighted FinBERT sentiment composition and decayed news intensity, preserving half-life identifiability for single-news histories. Using 23,294 analyst-rating items for 23 equities from 2 January 2018 to 30 June 2020, executable 30-, 60-, and 120-min labels, and 18 expanding purged folds with strictly separated validation, the estimated base half-life is 17.4–23.0 h. Intraday coefficients are positive and post-market coefficients negative in all 18 folds at every horizon, indicating slower intraday and faster post-market decay, and the pattern recurs under a second processing version. Synthetic recovery experiments on the archived event-history design confirm that these parameters are recoverable and that near-zero coefficients are returned under a zero-effect generating process. News and decay features lower daily log loss versus price-and-market features under serial-dependence-robust inference, and verified nested ablations attribute small but significant loss reductions to each conditioning component. The news-count baseline remains the strongest classifier, and a two-basis-point cost stress turns net returns negative.

title: Resilient Emergency Crop Harvesting Systems Under Extreme Weather: From Risk Sensing to Machinery Control and Coordinated Scheduling
abstract: Extreme rainfall, flooding, typhoons, heat and drought, early frost, and compound hazards are reshaping fundamental constraints for crop harvesting. When such hazards strike close to crop maturity, agricultural losses stem not merely from reduced field yield but propagate along a risk chain featuring degraded crop status, deteriorated field trafficability, degraded harvester performance, transport-drying congestion, and progressive grain quality deterioration. Existing investigations mostly address weather warning, remote sensing, combine-harvester manipulation, machinery scheduling, and postharvest management in isolation. Such fragmented research fails to resolve core system-level challenges for emergency harvesting, including the determination of field harvesting priority, the estimation of safe harvest duration, adaptive adjustment of machine configurations under varying crop–soil conditions, and the coordinated deployment of limited harvester fleets, transportation vehicles, and drying infrastructures. This review constructs an integrated technical chain for emergency crop harvesting. Disaster scenarios and risk formation mechanisms are analyzed; the capabilities of satellites, unmanned aerial vehicles, ground-based sensors, and crop models for retrieving maturity, lodging status, moisture content, and field operability are assessed. Adaptive chassis, headers and threshing-cleaning systems, alongside online monitoring and multi-parameter control targeting loss rate, grain breakage, impurity content, feed rate, and machine faults are comprehensively reviewed and summarized. Further analysis expands from single-machine control to field-level priority ranking, harvester-vehicle collaboration, inter-regional machinery scheduling, and the coordination spanning harvesting, drying and storage. A resilience evaluation framework oriented toward loss mitigation, operational efficiency, economic benefit, and recovery capability is proposed. Although abundant sensing, prediction, control, and optimization modules have been documented in published literature, these components are deficient in shared state variables, empirically validated risk thresholds, and closed-loop decision-making mechanisms coping with real-time perturbations. Future studies are recommended to integrate multi-source data assimilation with hybrid mechanistic-data-driven models, so as to build interpretable predictions for remaining safe harvest time, crop–soil–machine digital twins, and rolling inter-regional scheduling platforms. These technical progresses are expected to transform emergency crop harvesting from experience-driven mobilization into a quantifiable, verifiable, and restorable resilient operation system.

title: Automated Organ Segmentation of Sunflower Plants from 3D Point Clouds Using an Improved Region-Growing Algorithm
abstract: Accurate segmentation of plant organs is a key foundation for the automatic extraction of three-dimensional phenotypic traits of crops and the intelligent monitoring of growth status, and it plays an important supporting role in the screening of superior traits and precision cultivation management. However, for crops with complex plant architecture, the complex spatial relationships among organs and significant morphological differences still make 3D point cloud segmentation face considerable challenges. Taking sunflower as an example, its stems, leaves, and flower discs are interwoven with one another in 3D space, and the leaf morphology is irregular. Existing plant organ segmentation methods are prone to problems such as confusion between flower discs and stems, fragmentation of stem point clouds, and leaf oversegmentation. To address these issues, this study proposes an improved region-growing algorithm for organ segmentation of sunflower plants. The proposed method first performs denoising and downsampling preprocessing on the original point cloud data to remove noise and redundant points. Using the plant base as the initial seed point, the main-stem skeleton is iteratively extracted by incorporating local neighborhood compactness, representative candidate points selection, growth direction continuity, and local linearity constraints. Subsequently, a buffer-based reconstruction strategy is employed to recover the complete stem point cloud, while the remaining point clouds are processed through density-based clustering and organ classification. Experiments were conducted on point cloud datasets of 30 tall single-head sunflower plants (5 plants for parameter tuning, 25 plants for quantitative evaluation). The proposed method achieved segmentation precision values of 93.22%, 99.00%, and 91.86% for sunflower stems, leaves, and flower, respectively. The corresponding recall values were 98.11%, 97.38%, and 98.77%, while the F1-scores reached 95.55%, 97.81%, and 94.20%, respectively. Comparative experiments with the traditional region-growing method and the skeleton extraction method on four representative plants showed that the proposed method achieved the highest F1-scores for all three organs, improving the average F1-score by 48.28 and 12.35 percentage points, respectively. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately segment individual sunflower organs from single-plant point clouds, providing reliable technical support for efficient extraction of key phenotypic traits.

title: Remote Sensing-Based Mapping of Paddy Rice Cultivation Areas: Progress and Prospects in the Era of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Accurate and timely mapping of paddy rice cultivation areas underpins food security assessment, agricultural resource management, and climate change adaptation. Because remote sensing provides repeated, large-scale observations, it has become indispensable for monitoring rice cultivation. This review synthesizes studies published since 2000, emphasizing methodological and technological advances since 2016, and critically evaluates the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in rice mapping. We examine the observational characteristics and inherent limitations of optical imagery, synthetic aperture radar (SAR), hyperspectral data, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) observations, and multi-source data fusion for rice identification. We then trace the evolution of mapping methods, from threshold-based classification and phenology-driven time-series analysis to machine learning, deep learning, and cloud-computing frameworks, comparing their accuracy, scalability, computational efficiency, transferability, and interpretability. Applications at global, regional, and field scales, each characterized by distinct objectives and spatial requirements, are reviewed alongside prevailing validation strategies and sources of uncertainty. Persistent challenges include cloud contamination, spectral and phenological confusion among crop types, ambiguous target definitions, limited cross-regional generalizability, difficulty in distinguishing multiple cropping cycles, insufficient evidence of model transferability, and geographical concentration of the existing evidence base. Priority directions include adaptive multi-source data fusion, self-supervised and physics-guided learning, Earth observation foundation models, explainable and uncertainty-aware AI, parcel-level product generation, and operational monitoring systems coupled with crop growth models.

title: Differentiated Neurocognitive Profiles in Problematic Social Media Use: Evidence of Left Frontal Alpha Power, Parietal Activity, and Neural Flexibility in an Adapted Go/NoGo Paradigm
abstract: There is growing evidence to suggest that problematic social media use reflects a variety of neurocognitive profiles. This study examined differences in absolute alpha and beta spectral power using electroencephalography across three usage profiles: Compulsive Use Profile (CUP), Distress-Associated Profile (DAP) and Functional Profile (FP), derived from a prior cluster analysis. Activity was recorded during three experimental phases: baseline rest, an adapted Go/NoGo task with social media stimuli, and recovery. A 32-channel EEG was recorded from 42 young adults (x¯ = 19.62 years) during the 3 phases mentioned. Absolute spectral power (Welch method) was calculated for the alpha and beta bands in frontal and parietal regions. Mixed ANOVAs, Mann–Whitney U pairwise comparisons and Friedman tests were performed to assess neural modulation. A cluster effect approaching, but not reaching, conventional significance was found for left frontal alpha power (p = 0.057); a direct test of the Profile × Phase interaction for this variable was not significant (p = 0.837), indicating this trend was not specific to any one experimental phase. Pairwise comparisons revealed that the CUP showed significantly lower left frontal alpha power than the FP during the task phase (p = 0.012), with no differences at rest or during recovery. The DAP group showed lower left parietal alpha power during the task (p = 0.036) and lower right parietal alpha power at rest (p = 0.034) compared with the FP group. Only the FP group exhibited significant modulation of alpha power (neural flexibility) across phases (p = 0.035). Problematic social media use is not a uniform phenomenon. The CUP and DAP show distinct neural patterns in the frontal cortex for compulsivity and in the parietal cortex for emotional vulnerability, supporting the use of differentiated neurocognitive models and the need for tailored clinical interventions.

title: Deep Learning-Based Classification of Mandibular Growth-Rotation Phenotypes from Lateral Cephalometric Radiographs: A Comparative Evaluation of Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Background/Objectives: The cross-sectional classification of mandibular growth-rotation morphology is relevant to orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning, but conventional structural assessment is observer-dependent. This study developed and internally evaluated deep learning models for classifying existing clockwise and counterclockwise mandibular growth-rotation phenotypes on lateral cephalometric radiographs; it did not forecast future longitudinal growth. Methods: Eight hundred untreated radiographs from individuals aged 9–20 years were labelled by consensus using Björk and Skieller morphological indicators (clockwise, n = 376; counterclockwise, n = 424). A stratified 80:20 training–validation split was used. ResNet50, InceptionV3, and VGG16 were fine-tuned after Gaussian noise reduction, min–max normalisation, and limited geometric augmentation. Results: VGG16 showed the most favourable validation accuracy–loss profile. The archived aggregate confusion matrix (n = 800) yielded an apparent accuracy of 81.13% (95% CI, 78.38–83.75) and balanced accuracy of 81.32% (95% CI, 78.62–83.96); recall was 84.57% for clockwise and 78.07% for counterclockwise phenotypes. Because the matrix included the complete labelled cohort, these values are descriptive apparent performance and not an independent test estimate. Conclusions: VGG16 can classify cross-sectional mandibular growth-rotation phenotypes with promising apparent performance. External, longitudinal, and observer-benchmark validation is required before clinical use.

title: TimesFM-Based Photovoltaic Power Forecasting with Few-Shot Residual Adaptation Under Data Scarcity
abstract: Accurate photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is becoming increasingly important for the secure and economical operation of renewable-rich power systems. However, conventional data-driven forecasting methods generally rely on sufficient site-specific historical observations, limiting their applicability to newly commissioned PV stations with severe data scarcity; meanwhile, forecasting performance is still predominantly evaluated using statistical error metrics, which cannot fully reflect its practical value in power system operation. To address these issues, this study develops a PV forecasting framework based on the pretrained time-series foundation model TimesFM, which exploits transferable temporal representations to enable zero-shot forecasting with limited target-site data. A lightweight residual quantile few-shot adaptation scheme is further introduced to learn station-specific forecasting deviations from limited historical observations while keeping the pretrained forecasting backbone fixed, thereby improving target-site adaptation and forecasting capability. In addition, a multi-dimensional power-system-operation-oriented evaluation framework is established to assess forecasting performance from economic, flexibility, regulation, and network-operation perspectives, together with different PV integration locations and installed capacities. Experimental results demonstrate that for the investigated CYT Station 1 case, the proposed method improves deterministic and probabilistic forecasting performance relative to zero-shot TimesFM and achieves substantial adaptation gains using limited target-site observations. The improved forecasts also reduce forecasting-induced operating costs and reserve requirements and yield system responses closer to those obtained with actual PV generation, confirming that forecasting improvements can be translated into measurable operational benefits.

title: A Hybrid LSTM–Weibull Framework for Estimating Phenolic Joint Seal Replacement Needs in the Generating Units of the Santo Antônio Hydropower Plant
abstract: Long maintenance outages require advance planning. This article presents a sequential hybrid framework for the paired phenolic joint seals of 50 generating units at the Santo Antônio Hydropower Plant, Brazil. A unit-specific long short-term memory (LSTM) model estimates the time to recorded replacement and supplies the horizon for Monte Carlo propagation using length-indexed Weibull wear models. An empirical hazard yields seal-specific outputs. Their maximum provides a signaling index based on the logical OR rule, under which either seal can trigger a signal, rather than an exact calibrated joint probability. The main historical configuration uses seven inputs, including gross head, on a 10-day grid. The corresponding archive contains 8858 forecasts across 89 of 100 selected cycles, with a pooled timing mean absolute error (MAE) of 33.58 days and disjoint network-training and validation records. Replacing arithmetic averaging with the maximum raises the mean index from 90.526% to 94.230%. A known-horizon check and a latent-wear sensitivity analysis are reported separately. A chronological calendar experiment uses fitted models held fixed during evaluation, separate development data, and a later test period containing 29 replacements. At the 90% cutoff, false-positive rates are 48.57% and 47.43% for descriptive action windows of 100 and 200 days. Precision is 8.84% and 16.89%. Higher cutoffs reduce false positives but can reduce event-warning coverage. A supervised joint-event probability extension improves Brier loss relative to a constant-risk reference while overestimating mean event risk. The results demonstrate a coupling of temporal prediction and stochastic condition projection, but do not establish an optimal cutoff, satisfactory probability calibration, or prospective operational effectiveness.

title: Breaking the Transformation Bottleneck in CRISPR/Cas-Based Crop Improvement: From Genotype-Dependent Regeneration to DNA-Free and In Planta Delivery Systems
abstract: CRISPR/Cas genome editing offers new opportunities for crop improvement, but its wider application remains limited more by the difficulty of delivering editing tools into plant cells and regenerating whole plants than by the editing chemistry itself. Many elite cereal, legume, and vegetatively propagated crops remain difficult to transform and regenerate, restricting genome editing to a limited range of amenable genotypes and often requiring additional breeding to introduce desired traits into elite varieties. This review examines how these interconnected barriers influence the recovery of fertile, heritably edited plants and evaluates emerging strategies to overcome them. We discuss developmental regulators such as BBM, WUS2, and GRF-GIF fusions, approaches that induce new meristems, and alternative delivery systems involving nanoparticles, viral vectors, pollen tubes, and DNA-free Cas ribonucleoproteins or guide RNAs. We distinguish the major steps from delivery and editing to plant regeneration, recovery of fertile plants, and transmission of the desired edits to progeny, highlighting that improvements in one step do not necessarily overcome the entire process. We compare these approaches in terms of their applicability across species and genotypes, reported efficiencies, heritability, and practical limitations. Persistent challenges include mosaicism, unintended off-target changes, and limited applicability to non-model and polyploid crops. Finally, we discuss how improved regeneration systems, base and prime editing, machine-learning-guided design, and evolving precision-breeding frameworks in the European Union, United States, Japan, and India may contribute to broader applications of genome editing in crop improvement.
journal: Journal of Genome Biotechnology and Genetics

title: Efficient VNIR Hyperspectral Models for Estimating Pigment and Fluorescence Traits in Vertically Farmed Lettuce
abstract: Nondestructive estimation of pigment content and chlorophyll fluorescence traits is valuable for vertical farming. However, hyperspectral models for fluorescence traits have rarely been tested on vertically farmed crops. This study evaluated a VNIR hyperspectral lettuce dataset with a fully auditable workflow-based on white-normalized and leaf-masked reflectance cubes acquired between 400 and 1000 nm. The final analysis used 113 matched leaf samples from 57 plants grown in nutrient film technique and aeroponic systems. Model evaluation was performed with five-fold grouped cross-validation by plant, so that leaves from the same plant were never split between training and test folds. Models were selected only within the training folds, and the whole procedure was repeated ten times. A growing system holdout was used as a robustness check. The study focuses on four targets selected by the agronomical team as the main variables of interest: chlorophyll, anthocyanins, PItotal (overall photosynthetic performance), and ET0/RC (electron transport flux per reaction center). The main scientific claim is based on spectral-only models, while spectral plus metadata models are reported separately as operational extensions. The most consistent result was obtained for ET0/RC with an interval partial least squares model built on leaf core reflectance in the 580–620 nm region, reaching grouped out-of-fold R2 = 0.76 and between growing system R2 = 0.46 and 0.59. Anthocyanins showed a promising within-dataset result, although transfer between growing systems was limited, with the best spectral-only model obtained from a core-only leaf summary (R2 = 0.55). Chlorophyll and PItotal were only moderately predictable (R2 = 0.38 and 0.41, respectively) and are presented as supporting results rather than headline findings. For all four targets, spectral models performed better than models using only cultivation data. These results suggest that careful preprocessing, plant-grouped validation, and compact latent variable models can recover useful VNIR signals for selected lettuce traits, although predictive performance remains strongly target dependent and should be confirmed on other cultivars and growing systems.

title: A Second-Order Spatial Guided Sampling Method for Outlier Removal in UAV Remote Sensing Image Registration
abstract: Image registration is fundamental to UAV remote sensing data processing, but repetitive textures, viewpoint and scale variations, terrain relief, and local deformation can introduce numerous outliers into tentative correspondences. The existing random-sampling and spatial-consistency methods commonly rely on pointwise confidence or isolated pairwise relations and therefore cannot reliably determine whether a locally compatible relation receives stable group-level structural support. To address this limitation, we propose SPGSC++, a second-order spatial guided sampling method for outlier removal. SPGSC++ first uses PCA to reduce the dimensionality of tentative correspondences, thereby reducing the computational burden of subsequent spatial relation construction. It then derives second-order structural quality from the common-neighbor support of directly compatible edges and uses this quality for initial data subset selection and residual-informed data subset refinement to generate and optimize a homography. Comparative experiments show that, on the five datasets CIAP, SUIRD, UAV, ZHANGZHOU, and PAN, the proposed method achieves mean Precision, Recall, F-Score, Runtime, and mean reprojection error values of 0.9627, 0.9797, 0.9702, 0.3724 s, and 1.6454, respectively. Relative to the original SPGSC, SPGSC++ increases the mean F-Score by 0.0391 and reduces Runtime and mean reprojection error by 32.39% and 58.12%, respectively. Overall, the innovation of SPGSC++ lies in using second-order common-neighbor structural quality to guide initial subset selection and residual-informed refinement for robust estimation in UAV remote sensing image registration.
