title: Three-Dimensional Mapping of Soil Textural Fractions on the Grounds of IFTO, Pedro Afonso Campus, Tocantins, Brazil
abstract: Soil texture, determined by the proportions of sand, silt and clay, is a fundamental indicator of soil physical quality and an important attribute for soil classification. This study mapped the three-dimensional distribution of soil texture in a pasture area at the Instituto Federal do Tocantins (IFTO), Pedro Afonso Campus, Tocantins, Brazil. Forty soil samples were collected at three depth intervals (0–20, 20–40 and 40–60 cm). Spatial modelling combined Ordinary Kriging and the Random Forest machine learning algorithm using environmental covariates derived from a digital elevation model and drone imagery. Clay content increased with depth, from 14% in the surface layer to 22% at 40–60 cm, whereas sand content declined from 71% to 58%, indicating greater textural differentiation in the subsurface. Model performance was generally modest, with R² values ranging from -0.04 to 0.21. Ordinary Kriging achieved the highest predictive performance at 40–60 cm (R² = 0.21, RMSE = 5.58% and MSE = 4.86%), slightly outperforming Random Forest (R² = 0.18, RMSE = 5.72% and MSE = 4.93%). These results indicate that the spatial dependence of the data had a stronger influence on soil texture prediction than the environmental covariates incorporated into the machine learning model. Although predictive accuracy was limited, the integration of geostatistical and geospatial techniques successfully characterised the spatial variability of soil texture. The resulting three-dimensional maps provide valuable information for sustainable soil management, land-use planning and future precision agriculture applications, while establishing a robust baseline for further investigations of soil spatial variability.
journal: International Journal of Advanced Multidisciplinary Research and Studies

title: The Implementation of MSME Upgrades and Its Stages in Pajajar Village, Majalengka Regency
abstract: Background. Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are the backbone of Indonesia's economy, absorbing around 119 million workers and contributing more than 60% of the national Gross Domestic Product (GDP), but the structure of MSMEs is still very unequal because micro enterprises dominate up to 99.70% of the total business units (UKMINDONESIA.ID, 2026). This inequality makes the agenda of "upgrading"—increasing business capacity from micro to small and medium—a policy priority of the Ministry of Cooperatives and SMEs. Objectives. This research is part of a series of literature reviews on Pajajar Village, Rajagaluh District, Majalengka Regency, which has previously discussed waste bank institutions, the application of waste management technology, and food security at the household level; this study expands the study to the realm of strengthening the local economy through upgrading MSMEs and its stages of implementation. Methods. The method used was a descriptive-qualitative literature review by examining the MSME policy framework for upgrading classes, cluster models and MSME assistance, the concept of One Village One Product (OVOP), as well as national scientific journal articles on marketing digitalization (marketplace and QRIS) and business legality (NIB, halal certification, and PIRT). The results of the study formulated a four-stage model of MSMEs upgrading for Pajajar Village—pioneering and legality, digitalization and marketing, standardization and certification, and upgrading and expansion—which were synthesized from the Go Legal-Go Digital-Go Bankable-Go Global framework. Results. This study also synthesizes the relationship of MSMEs upgrading with the results of the previous three literature reviews, showing that compost, compost, and yard crops can be processed into value-added MSME products which are then marketed digitally, forming a circular waste-food-MSME economic value chain at the village level. Conclusion. This study recommends that the Pajajar Village Government start the pilot stage of business legality collectively through cooperatives/BUMDes, while still considering the potential of circular economy educational tourism as an added value for village MSMEs.

title: Diffusion modeling for characterizing neuropathology in psychotic disorders: a Machine Learning study
abstract: Psychotic spectrum disorders exhibit overlapping symptoms and heterogeneous neuropathology, complicating subtype differentiation. Conventional diffusion MRI models may conflate concurrent microstructural alterations. This study investigated whether integrating complementary diffusion compartments improves discrimination within the psychosis spectrum. A framework combining Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI), Diffusion Kurtosis Imaging (DKI), Free Water Imaging (FWI), and Intravoxel Incoherent Motion (IVIM) was evaluated using multi-shell diffusion MRI data from 1,267 Human Connectome Project participants (1,094 healthy controls; 173 patients). Parameter recovery was assessed through simulations, while regional diffusion features were analyzed using neural networks with nested, site-stratified five-fold cross-validation, ablation, scanner harmonization, and confound controls. The integrated framework distinguished patients from controls with a pooled out-of-fold AUC-ROC of 0.968 (95% CI: 0.952–0.981), compared with 0.896–0.929 for reduced models. Conventional DTI and DKI models showed near-chance discrimination between schizophrenia-spectrum and non-schizophrenia psychosis (AUC-ROC = 0.543–0.564), whereas the integrated framework achieved 0.716 (95% CI: 0.635–0.792), significantly outperforming DTI and DTI+DKI (paired bootstrap p = 0.011 and 0.007, respectively). Ablation demonstrated complementary contributions from extracellular free-water and perfusion metrics beyond conventional diffusion measurements. Same-cohort matched analysis retained strong patient-control discrimination (AUC-ROC = 0.958), although acquisition confounding remains a limitation. These findings establish the incremental predictive value of multi-compartment diffusion integration for distinguishing psychotic subtypes, providing a foundation for microstructural profiling and patient stratification, pending independent validation.

title: Micro-Catchment Typology for Integrated Catchment Management
abstract: Catchment management plans in data-scarce regions usually treat erosion, flooding, runoff and water harvesting separately, so interventions are prioritised hazard by hazard rather than by the combined condition of each land unit. This study developed a multivariate typology of 163 micro-catchments in the 1,641.7 km 2 Idah Catchment, north-central Nigeria. Nine indicators derived from a 12.5 m digital elevation model and open global datasets were reduced with principal component analysis and grouped with k-means clustering. The first component (57.6% of variance) described a gradient from wooded plateau units to cultivated, flood-prone lowland units. Four management zones were identified: wooded plateau headwaters (50.1% of the area), steep, flashy plateau margins (21.7%), cultivated erosion– runoff hotspots (10.4%) and flood-prone floodplain (17.8%). The zones agreed with Ward clustering (adjusted Rand index 0.69), were reproduced by a random forest with 92% out-of-bag accuracy and were spatially coherent (65% of neighbouring units shared a zone, against 32% expected by chance). The hotspot and floodplain zones occupied 28.2% of the area but generated 54.9% of the soil loss and 58.3% of the 25-year runoff, contained 26 of the 28 significant soil-loss hotspots and had the highest groundwater recharge potential. Scenario analysis indicated that conservation agriculture with contour bunds on cropland in these two zones would reduce soil loss by 31.8%, whereas clearing 20% of headwater tree cover would increase it by 89.6%. Check dams outside the floodplain could retain up to 18.7% of the 25-year runoff. Annual rainfall declined significantly in the lowland zones. The typology concentrates management effort where hazards coincide and offers a transferable framework for integrated planning in ungauged

title: Effects of AI-Empowered Digital Inclusive Finance on the Income Growth of County-Level Farmers in Yunnan Province: An Empirical Test Based on County-Level Panel Data
abstract: {'en': "Using panel data of 119 counties (cities, districts) in Yunnan Province from 2015 to 2022, this paper constructs an AI-empowered digital inclusive finance index and examines its effect on county-level farmer income growth and the underlying channels with a two-way fixed-effects model. The results show that AI-empowered digital inclusive finance significantly promotes farmer income growth: a one-unit increase in the index raises rural residents' per capita disposable income by about 0.12% on average, and this conclusion remains robust after instrumental-variable estimation, replacement of the dependent variable, winsorization, and system GMM estimation. Mechanism tests indicate that AI-empowered digital inclusive finance mainly works through three channels—easing credit constraints, popularizing digital payment, and expanding e-commerce channels for agricultural products—whose combined mediation contribution exceeds one half. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the income effect is more pronounced for farmers in poverty-stricken and mountainous counties, and mainly manifests as growth in operating and wage income. Accordingly, policy recommendations are proposed, including deepening county-level intelligent risk control, improving rural digital infrastructure, developing e-commerce for plateau-featured agricultural products, and strengthening county-level financial risk monitoring."}

title: Environment-Aware DNA Language Model for Stress-Responsive Genomic Prioritization in Maize
abstract: Abiotic stresses such as heat and drought severely reduce the productivity of major crops including maize, with adverse implications for agricultural sustainability. Despite progress in characterizing stress resilience, identifying genomic regions associated with stress response remains challenging due to complex genotype-by-environment interactions. Genomic Foundation Models (GFMs), inspired by advances in Large Language Models (LLMs), leverage large-scale self-supervised pre-training on DNA sequences to capture regulatory patterns; however, their adaptation to plant stress-response analysis remains underexplored. In this work, we propose an environment-aware DNA-LLM framework that incorporates stress-specific prompt tokens into AgroNT, a transformer-based plant GFM, using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT). The model learns stress-conditioned genomic representations that exhibit distinct structures across environmental contexts. We further formulate a prioritization method that uses stress-induced shifts in these representations relative to the control condition together with stress-token-associated transformer attention patterns to identify putative stress-responsive genomic regions. The framework was evaluated on the Genomes-to-Fields (G2F) dataset, comprising over 4,000 maize hybrids grown across 38 locations over 8 years, using grain yield under heat, drought, and combined heat-drought stress. Flowering traits were used to assess generalizability of the stress-conditioned representations across phenotypes. The prioritized regions were assessed using spatiotemporal differential gene-expression profiles, stress-associated quantitative trait loci, and transcription-factor characterization. Regulatory motif analysis further revealed stress-associated motifs enriched within the prioritized sequences as well as model-emphasized high-attention regions. Functional annotation of genes proximal to prioritized regions highlighted roles in transcriptional regulation, signaling, and metabolic pathways relevant to abiotic stress adaptation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of stress-conditioned transformer-based sequence modeling for environment-aware genome-to-phenome analysis in crop improvement.

title: ECG foundation models share an age-related performance disparity that originates in the data, not the models
abstract: Background Electrocardiogram (ECG) foundation models are proposed for clinical use and promoted as fair, yet such claims are rarely tested with subgroup-stratified evaluation. We measured demographic disparities across four ECG foundation models, tested whether mitigation removes them, and asked whether the dominant disparity originates in the models or in the data and the clinical task. Methods We probed frozen embeddings of four architecturally distinct ECG foundation models (ECGFounder, xECG, ECG-FM, DeepECG-SSL) in thirteen cohorts on four continents (5.4 million analysed ECGs, 31 endpoints, six held-out cohorts), stratified by age, sex and race. We examined embedding geometry, tested post-hoc correction, larger labelled training sets, comorbidity exclusion and low-rank fine-tuning, and compared each network with an untrained copy of itself and with logistic regression on classical ECG measurements. Findings Disparities concentrated on age, not sex or race (median worst-group AUROC gap 0.028 vs 0.004 and 0.016; age exceeded sex in 97% of results) and replicated externally (ED-BWH 30-day MACE AUROC 0.81–0.90 under 40 years, 0.64–0.71 at ≥75). Age formed a smooth gradient in the embeddings, whereas sex, though most decodable, carried no gap. No remedy closed it (low-rank adaptation: −0.007 to −0.004). Untrained copies (r=0.81, 102 pairs) and classical measurements ( ρ =0.90) reproduced the endpoint-specific gaps, and pretraining raised AUROC (+0.067) without changing them. The largest race effect, higher potassium error in Black patients, vanished at matched true potassium. Interpretation ECG foundation models carry an age-structured disparity that replicates externally and survives mitigation. Because untrained networks and a classical model reproduce it, the results indicate that it is inherited from the age structure of the ECG and its labels rather than created by the models, so switching or adapting models will not remove it. Age-stratified reporting, untrained and classical baselines, and age-specific thresholds and recalibration are therefore needed. Funding Austrian Research Promotion Agency (FFG; CARDISENSE project, grant FO999922422). Graphical abstract Research in context Evidence before this study We searched PubMed, Google Scholar, and arXiv from database inception to October, 2026, using combinations of the terms “ECG” or “electrocardiogram”, “foundation model” or “self-supervised”, and “fairness”, “bias”, “equity”, “subgroup”, or “demographic”, with no language restriction. Open-weight ECG foundation models have proliferated and are increasingly proposed for clinical use, and benchmarks compare them on aggregate accuracy without stratifying by subgroup. The fairness literature documents demographic performance gaps in task-specific ECG classifiers, most often for sex or race on single tasks in single cohorts, and the remedies it proposes act on the model (reweighting, adversarial debiasing, group-robust training, fine-tuning). The one subgroup analysis of ECG foundation models we found covered two models of one family on their own endpoints, stratified by age and sex only. To our knowledge, no study has evaluated several architecturally distinct ECG foundation models along age, sex and race across endpoint families and continents, and none has tested whether a disparity found in a foundation model is also present without any pretraining or without deep learning. Added value of this study Evaluating four architecturally distinct ECG foundation models across thirteen cohorts on four continents, including six held-out external cohorts, we show that strong average and external discrimination coexists with a disparity that concentrates on age, not sex or race, and that replicates externally. The pattern has a consistent substrate: age is encoded as a smooth gradient in the embeddings, while sex and race, both decodable, carry no comparable gap. The gap is shared across every architecture and pretraining objective, and neither post-hoc correction, larger labelled training sets, exclusion of comorbid ECGs nor low-rank fine-tuning closes it. Two controls explain why: untrained copies of the same networks and a logistic regression on classical ECG measurements reproduce the endpoint-specific age gaps, which indicates that the gap is inherited from the data and the clinical task rather than learned in pretraining. Implications of all the available evidence Fairness evaluation of ECG foundation models should prioritise age and report age-stratified performance as a primary result, because a threshold fixed on the pooled population operates at a worse point for older patients than the headline metric implies. Because the gap persists across architectures, vendors, fine-tuning and even untrained networks, switching models will not resolve it. Evaluations should include an untrained and a classical baseline before attributing a gap to a model, and services deploying these models should use age-specific thresholds and recalibration, or at minimum report and monitor performance by age band.

title: Using refuge plants to manage resistance evolution and crop yield in agricultural fields
abstract: The evolution of pesticide resistance in herbivores poses a significant challenge in agriculture. A refuge strategy, where farmers plant non-toxin-treated plants to promote growth of susceptible herbivore individuals near treated plants and facilitate gene exchange between susceptible and resistant individuals, has been used in resistance management. However, we know very little about the effect of spatiotemporal fluctuations in selection pressure on resistance management. Furthermore, pests show oviposition preference and assortative mating behaviours, both of which have rarely been considered by researchers when designing resistance management strategies. Using a stochastic eco-evolutionary plant-herbivore model, we show that over a wide range of population parameters, directional changes in toxicity level and refuge frequency that reduce selection pressure for the resistance allele in the initial pest generations are much more effective for resistance management than exposing pests to a constant toxicity level and refuge frequency across pest generations. However, the exact magnitude of the effect of changing toxicity and refuge frequency relative to keeping them constant across pest generations is sensitive to underlying population parameter values. Our results show that the refuge strategy is most effective when niche choice can evolve, but assortative mating shows both negative and positive effects in resistance management. Thus, our results reveal a potential mechanism underlying the refuge strategy’s successes in the field. We show how resistance allele dominance and resistance costs influence our observations, and discuss our results in the context of partial protection from directional selection and field resistance management.

title: Controversies in Zero-Shot Forecasting with Time Series Foundation Models and a Three-Layer Framework for Trustworthy Evaluation
abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) aim to forecast new datasets without target-specific parameter updates. Assessing this capability requires scrutiny of how evaluation evidence is generated and interpreted. We present a semi-systematic review of 80 core papers on the evaluation of TSFMs and large language model (LLM)-based forecasting methods. The review comprises 68 papers from the initial search and 12 from a targeted supplementary search within the same January 2022 to August 2026 publication window. We organize the evidence around benchmark integrity, ranking robustness, and domain transferability. In the reviewed literature, empirical audits of overlap between TSFM pretraining corpora and test benchmarks remain limited. Protocol choices, including normalization, forecast horizons, information availability, and metric aggregation, can alter model comparisons. Domain studies report both competitive performance and limitations, depending on task formulation, the relevance of pretraining data, sampling granularity, and data quality. These findings warrant conditional interpretations of zero-shot results rather than general claims of success or failure. We propose a five-part checklist for trustworthy evaluation and identify research priorities in corpus auditing, statistical comparison, domain-specific calibration, broader empirical coverage, and model selection. Reliable deployment requires evidence relevant to the intended task and operating conditions.

title: APPLICATION OF LIFE TABLE IN MODELLING LIFE OF CITRUS TREES
abstract: Citrus trees are long-lived perennial crops whose survival and productive longevity are influenced by age, disease, environmental conditions, cultivar, rootstock, soil properties and orchard management. Reliable estimation of citrus tree life expectancy is important for orchard planning, replacement decisions, production forecasting and sustainable citrus management. This study develops a life-table framework for estimating citrus tree survival and remaining life expectancy. A synthetic cohort of 300 citrus trees was generated to demonstrate the statistical methodology. The cohort was followed over age intervals of three years, and the numbers surviving and dying within each age interval were used to construct an abridged life table. The results obtained from the analysis using the life table (survival analysis) clearly indicates that the life expectancy range get to the optimum at 21-24 yrs interval and decline accordingly to 0 at age interval 48-51.
journal: International Journal of Pure and Applied Science

title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Disease and Pest Management in Cauliflower: A Review
abstract: Cauliflower (Brassica oleracea var. botrytis L.) is a nutritionally important cole vegetable and a high-value component of intensive vegetable production. Its yield and market quality are frequently reduced by bacterial, fungal and oomycete diseases and by insect pests that cause direct feeding injury or facilitate secondary infections. Conventional disease and pest surveillance is largely dependent on visual scouting, expert diagnosis and periodic field observations. These approaches remain indispensable, but they can be labour-intensive, subjective and difficult to scale over large production areas. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, image segmentation, object detection, remote sensing and predictive analytics, offers a complementary approach for rapid and repeatable crop-health assessment. This review examines the potential role of AI in cauliflower disease and pest management, covering image acquisition, disease classification, lesion localisation, severity estimation, insect identification, automated counting, forecasting, smartphone applications, UAV-based surveillance and AI-enabled integrated pest management. Cauliflower-specific research has demonstrated promising performance of deep-learning models. The Cauli-Det modified YOLOv8 system reported precision of 93.2%, recall of 82.6% and mean average precision of 91.1% for bacterial soft rot, downy mildew and black rot in its experimental dataset (Uddin et al., 2024). Another recent cauliflower study reported 99.85% classification accuracy using EfficientNet-B3 under its experimental conditions (Malik et al., 2025). Broader plant-disease research also demonstrates strong potential for CNNs and transfer learning (Mohanty et al., 2016; Ferentinos, 2018), while pest-detection research supports automated insect recognition and monitoring (Thenmozhi & Reddy, 2019; Chakrabarty et al., 2026). However, field variability, limited crop-specific datasets, class imbalance, symptom similarity, model explainability, computational requirements and inadequate independent validation remain major constraints. Future research should integrate AI predictions with weather, crop stage, pest abundance, disease severity and economic thresholds so that the technology supports practical, affordable and environmentally responsible IPM in cauliflower.
journal: International Journal of Plant & Soil Science

title: E-Commerce in Agribusiness: Transforming Agricultural Input and Food Markets in Emerging Economies
abstract: E-commerce is altering the organisation of agricultural input distribution, farm-output marketing and urban food procurement across emerging economies. Yet the proposition that digital platforms necessarily reduce intermediation, raise farm incomes and improve food-system efficiency is not established by the evidence as a whole. This critical narrative review examines transaction-based digital marketplaces, electronic agricultural auctions, input e-stores, digitally mediated procurement and consumer-facing food platforms, with attention to China, India and sub-Saharan Africa. Peer-reviewed empirical studies, reviews and selected methodological sources were purposively assessed for identification strategy, outcome validity, external relevance and conflicting results. The literature indicates that electronic commerce can broaden market reach, enable comparison of input offers, reorganise procurement and support sales continuity during disruptions. The magnitude and distribution of these benefits depend on logistics, verification of goods, intermediary services, buyer competition, digital capabilities and platform rules. A randomised expansion study in rural China found limited producer-income effects, whereas several observational and quasi-experimental studies report gains for selected participants; recent evidence also indicates diminishing returns, unequal benefits and adverse spillovers on offline farmers. Indian electronic agricultural markets demonstrate that price transparency does not guarantee effective cross-market competition, while African evidence documents both opportunities for input dealers and persistent fulfilment and trust constraints. Consumer-facing platforms complicate food-safety oversight and create new informational and nutritional concerns alongside possible improvements in monitoring. The synthesis advances an institutional transaction-chain framework that distinguishes online discovery from fulfilled, contestable and equitable trade. Policy evaluation should prioritise net margins, realised transactions, quality, distributional spillovers and durable market access rather than registrations or platform sales alone. Longer-term, independently evaluated comparisons across crop types and regions remain necessary before broad transformation claims are warranted.
journal: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports

title: Integrating genetic improvement, precision agriculture, and sustainable intensification for climate‐resilient horticulture in Ethiopia: A systematic review
abstract: Climate change poses significant challenges to horticultural production in Ethiopia through increasing temperatures, erratic rainfall, drought, pest outbreaks, and soil degradation. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on the roles of genetic improvement, precision agriculture, and sustainable intensification in enhancing climate‐resilient horticulture in Ethiopia. A total of 46 studies published between 2012 and 2026 were reviewed from major scientific databases and institutional reports. The findings indicate that most studies have focused on genetic diversity assessment, germplasm characterization, and quantitative genetic analyses, which provide a strong foundation for breeding climate‐resilient horticultural crops. In contrast, evidence on advanced genomic technologies, such as genome‐wide association studies, genomic selection, gene editing, and multi‐omics, remains limited within Ethiopian horticultural research. Precision agriculture technologies improve resource‐use efficiency through data‐driven irrigation, nutrient, and pest management. Sustainable intensification practices enhance productivity, soil health, and adaptive capacity. Integrating these three approaches provides a promising framework for developing climate resilient horticultural systems in Ethiopia, although greater investment in modern breeding technologies, digital infrastructure, and interdisciplinary research is required to realize this potential. However, infrastructure limitations, financial constraints, weak extension services, and limited interdisciplinary research remain major barriers requiring strategic policy and investment interventions.

title: Landmark-Based Anatomical Dissection and Real-Time Functional Assessment of the Mouse Eustachian Tube.
abstract: Objective Eustachian tube dysfunction (ETD) contributes to middle ear diseases, but practical methods for functional assessment in mice remain limited. We aimed to develop a landmark-guided mouse Eustachian tube (ET) dissection protocol and a real-time pressure-based system for ET functional evaluation. Methods A detachable portable device was developed for real-time measurement of intraluminal pressure changes in the mouse middle ear-ET complex. The ET was isolated using the cochlea, auditory bulla, and styliform process as landmarks while preserving the mucosa and adjacent tissues. Acute ET inflammation was induced by intratympanic injection of lipopolysaccharide, heat-inactivated Streptococcus pneumoniae, or Staphylococcus aureus; PBS served as a control. ET function was assessed using active clearance of negative pressure (ACNP), passive opening pressure (POP), and passive closing pressure (PCP), followed by histologic validation. Results The pressure system recorded real-time pressure changes and enabled repeated ACNP and POP measurements under the tested conditions. Compared with controls, ACNP was significantly reduced in all pathogen-treated groups (all p < 0.05), with the greatest reduction in the S. aureus group. ACNP differed among pathogen-treated groups, mainly driven by the S. aureus group (p = 0.0078; η 2 = 0.802). POP increased significantly after inflammatory challenge but did not differ among pathogen-treated groups (p = 0.3132; η 2 = 0.282). Histology showed epithelial injury, ciliary loss, mucus retention, and mucosal thickening in treated groups, most prominently after S. aureus challenge. Conclusion We developed a portable pressure-based system and a landmark-guided dissection workflow for structural and functional evaluation of the mouse ET. These methods provide a practical methodological approach for studies using mouse models of acute inflammation-associated ETD. Level of Evidence N/A.

title: Integrated GWAS and RNA-Seq analyses identify candidate genes for drought tolerance in spring wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) from the cold and arid region of China
Water Markets for Climate Change Adaptation: Trade, Storage, and Investment Under Stochastic Water Supply
abstract: It is widely accepted that water markets can support adaptation to climate change. However, quantifying this adaptive capacity is difficult as it requires models that represent both stochastic water supplies and forward-looking behaviour by market participants. We develop a stochastic dynamic model of the Murray-Darling Basin water market in which irrigators form rational expectations over future water prices, and make monthly water use, annual crop planting, and long-run investment decisions. The model is solved using reinforcement learning methods to approximate expectations, combined with mathematical programming to estimate market equilibrium. We validate the model against observed prices and irrigation activity from 2008 to 09 to 2021–22 and apply it to an ensemble of 37 CMIP6 climate projections for the southern Basin. Under drier future climates, water markets support adaptation through increased inter-regional trade flows into the downstream Murray, and larger storage reserves through more conservative crop planting. However, under the driest projections, inter-regional trade constraints bind, price differences widen across zones, and long-run irrigation development contracts by up to 16 per cent. The results highlight both the value and the limits of market-based adaptation, with implications for the design of water market institutions under a non-stationary climate.

title: An integrated water quality index and GIS-based assessment of the irrigation suitability of geothermal waters in the Sahara Desert
Circ_0018814 promotes the osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells in ankylosing spondylitis by regulating the miR-944/KLF4 axis.
abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory disease primarily affecting the spine and sacroiliac joints. This study investigated the impact of circ_0018814 on the osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in AS through the regulation of the miR-944/KLF4 axis and to evaluate its potential role in the progression of AS. GSE203155 was used as an exploratory screening dataset to identify candidate circRNAs associated with osteogenic differentiation in AS-MSCs. Circ_0018814 expression was further evaluated in bone marrow samples and primary MSCs. The effects of circ_0018814 on osteogenic differentiation markers (ALP, RUNX2, COL1A1) in MSCs from AS patients were assessed using western blot, ALP assay, and alizarin red S staining. The targeting relationship between circ_0018814, KLF4, and miR-944 was confirmed through luciferase reporter and RNA immunoprecipitation assays. Fluorescence in situ hybridization was used for cellular localization. Further experiments in a murine AS model evaluated the impact of circ_0018814 on AS lesions and MSC differentiation. The results showed that overexpression of circ_0018814 significantly enhanced the expression of osteogenic markers ALP, RUNX2, and COL1A1, and promoted the osteogenic differentiation of MSCs. Additionally, circ_0018814 regulated KLF4 expression by targeting miR-944. Inhibition of miR-944 upregulated KLF4 expression and promoted osteogenic differentiation. In the AS mouse model, downregulation of circ_0018814 significantly alleviated spinal lesions, restored normal expression levels of miR-944 and KLF4, and reduced disease-related osteogenic changes. This study demonstrates that circ_0018814 plays an important role in the pathological progression of AS by regulating the miR-944/KLF4 axis. circ_0018814 may serve as a novel potential therapeutic target for AS, providing new insights for future treatment strategies. However, the in vivo findings should be interpreted cautiously because tail vein delivery of lentiviral constructs is not MSC-specific.

Joint developmental trajectories of body surveillance and body satisfaction across late adolescence.
abstract: Body image development during adolescence involves multiple theoretically related but conceptually distinct processes, yet little is known about whether these processes unfold together in similar ways across individuals. Using six-wave longitudinal data from 585 Chinese vocational high school students (40.5% female), we identified joint trajectories of body surveillance and body satisfaction across T2-T5 and examined their associations with T1 adversity, social support, and gender and with T6 life satisfaction. Parallel-process latent class growth modeling identified three pathways: vulnerable (8.89%; high surveillance and low satisfaction), normative (51.45%; moderate surveillance and increasing satisfaction), and adaptive (39.66%; low surveillance and high, increasing satisfaction). Although body surveillance and body satisfaction showed contrasting relative levels across pathways, body satisfaction increased in the normative and adaptive pathways without corresponding declines in body surveillance. Physical abuse and female gender were associated with vulnerable-pathway membership, whereas classmate support was associated with adaptive-pathway membership. Life satisfaction was highest in the adaptive pathway, intermediate in the normative pathway, and lowest in the vulnerable pathway. These findings add a developmental perspective to objectification theory by distinguishing between differences in relative levels and patterns of change and suggest that adolescent body image development may involve increasing differentiation among partially related body image processes across late adolescence.
