title: Co-design of adaptive-hysteresis solar MPPT and energy-neutral duty scheduling for ultracapacitor-powered wireless sensor nodes
abstract: Solar-powered wireless sensor nodes are constrained by both harvesting-stage losses and temporal mismatch between harvested energy and node service demand. This paper develops a co-designed harvesting and energy-management framework that addresses these limitations jointly. A closed-form expression for the polarization efficiency of a hysteretic maximum power point tracking stage is derived for an ideal single-diode photovoltaic model, accounting simultaneously for ripple loss and set-point error. The formulation converges to the conventional second-order Taylor approximation in the narrow-band limit and remains within 0.09% points of a full single-diode model, including series and shunt resistances over 50–1000 W/m2. A loss-aware hysteresis band is obtained by minimizing ripple, switching, and resonant-conduction losses, while the tracking set point is determined analytically using a Lambert-W-based fractional open-circuit-voltage relation. A predictive scheduler allocates only stored energy exceeding a forecast-based reserve, for which conditional energy neutrality is established under a stated forecast-conservatism assumption. For a 25 mW PV module, 30 F ultracapacitor, and 3.3 V mote, seven-day mixed-weather simulations yield 0.933 mean efficiency vs 0.898 for a fixed-band reference, double the service events, and eliminate service interruptions. Ablation analysis further distinguishes harvesting-stage improvements from system-level recovery of otherwise curtailed energy.
journal: Journal of Renewable and Sustainable Energy

title: Origami state machine with time-varying magnetic fields.
abstract: Achieving reliable, remote control over multiple stable states in modular systems remains a challenge due to the coupling between modules and history-dependent transitions. Here, we present magnetic origami state machines that enable deterministic navigation from any unknown initial state to any target state under magnetic actuation. By assuming mutually distinct energy barriers in modular Kresling origami assemblies, we realize fully accessible transition graphs with scalable state spaces. Guided by the graph associated to the state machine, a rotating magnetic field induces a universal reset that autonomously drives the system to a known equilibrium state from arbitrary states without sensing or feedback, while pulsed magnetic inputs further enable programmable transitions to any target state via prescribed actuation sequences. A reduced-order Lagrangian mechanics model predicts snap-through dynamics across reset, stepwise programming (between graph nodes), and shortcuts (by adapting pulse magnitude and orientation) where inertia triggers simultaneous multicell transitions with a single pulse. These results establish a general framework for programmable magneto-mechanical state machines with autonomous state reset and full state-space control.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Characterization of Ovarian Small Round Cells Reveals Distinct Molecular and Cellular Features Under Spermatogonial Stem Cell-Supportive Conditions.
abstract: The mammalian ovary contains diverse cell populations with distinct molecular and functional characteristics. Rare ovarian-derived cell populations remain incompletely characterized. Spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) provide a well-established model for studying cellular features associated with pluripotency, niche interaction, and germline-associated programs. Here, we investigated whether ovarian-derived cells exhibit selected characteristics associated with these features under defined culture conditions. Using mouse ovarian tissue, we isolated and characterized ovarian-derived small round cells (OSRCs) following culture under SSC-supportive conditions. Using Oct4-GFP transgenic mice, we identified two ovarian-derived populations: ovarian epithelial-like cells (OELCs) and OSRCs. These populations were compared using morphology, alkaline phosphatase activity, marker expression analysis, molecular comparison with SSC populations, and transplantation into an SSC-supportive testicular environment. OELCs showed characteristics of ovarian somatic cells, whereas OSRCs exhibited increased expression of selected pluripotency-associated markers and variable expression of germline-associated markers. OSRCs differed from undifferentiated SSCs, showing reduced or heterogeneous expression of markers such as Ddx4 and Dazl. Following transplantation, OSRCs localized within seminiferous tubules but showed no evidence of germline differentiation. OSRCs represent a distinct ovarian-derived cell population with partial overlap with pluripotency-associated and germline-associated molecular features. These findings provide a basis for further investigation of ovarian cellular heterogeneity.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

title: Isolation and characterization of Metapseudomonas agri sp. nov. and Metapseudomonas agrisoli sp. nov. isolated from the rhizosphere soil of agricultural fields.
abstract: Two novel strains MAHUQ-55T and MAHUQ-62T were isolated from the rhizosphere soils of rice and pumpkin, respectively. Both strains were Gram-negative, catalase- and oxidase-positive, motile and rod-shaped. Strains MAHUQ-55T and MAHUQ-62T grew at 10-45 °C and 10-40 °C and pH 5.5-10.0 and 5.0-10.0 and tolerated 0-3.0% and 0-4.0% (wt/v) NaCl, respectively. Both strains hydrolysed l-tyrosine, Tween 20 and Tween 80. Phylogenetic analysis based on 16S rRNA gene sequences indicated that strains MAHUQ-55T and MAHUQ-62T belong to the genus Metapseudomonas, showing the highest sequence similarities to Metapseudomonas furukawaii KF707T (98.9%) and Metapseudomonas lalkuanensis PE08T (99.4%), respectively. The genome sizes of strains MAHUQ-55T and MAHUQ-62T were 6,415,999 and 6,038,011 bp, respectively, with DNA G+C contents of 65.1 and 63.0 mol%. The average nucleotide identity (ANI) and digital DNA-DNA hybridization (dDDH) values between the two strains and their closest relatives were below the species delineation thresholds (ANI: 95-96%; dDDH: 70%). Both strains exhibited ubiquinone 9 as the predominant respiratory quinone and C12 : 0, C16 : 0, summed feature 3 (C16 : 1 ω7c and/or C16 : 1 ω6c) and summed feature 8 (C18 : 1 ω7c and/or C18 : 1 ω6c) as major fatty acids. Based on dDDH, ANI value, genotypic analysis and chemotaxonomic and physiological data, strains MAHUQ-55T and MAHUQ-62T represent two novel species within the genus Metapseudomonas. Therefore, the names Metapseudomonas agri sp. nov. (type strain MAHUQ-55T=KACC 22002T=CGMCC 1.18516T) and Metapseudomonas agrisoli sp. nov. (type strain MAHUQ-62T=KACC 22243T=CGMCC 1.18999T) are proposed.
journal: International journal of systematic and evolutionary microbiology

title: Multiphase Flow Regime Identification in Pipelines Using FBG Dynamic Strain and Machine Learning
abstract: Fiber Bragg grating (FBG) sensors provide an effective approach for monitoring flow-induced dynamic strain (DS) in pipelines, where the measured DS signatures reflect the underlying multiphase flow behavior. In this work, DS responses were recorded from four representative three-phase flow regimes in a controlled pipeline flow loop using two externally mounted FBG sensors operating at a 5 kHz sampling rate and exposed to mixtures of CO2, water, and diesel oil. The acquired signals were pre-processed and transformed into the frequency domain using the fast Fourier transform (FFT), and principal component analysis (PCA) was used to guide binary slug/non-slug grouping. Cross-FBG slug/non-slug classification was then evaluated by training the models on one FBG channel and testing them on the other. The CNN achieved accuracies of 90.78% for FBG1-to-FBG2 and 85.83% for FBG2-to-FBG1 testing, while the RF baseline achieved 83.37% and 84.70%, respectively, using 17 handcrafted time- and frequency-domain features. These results indicate that FBG-based DS sensing combined with frequency-domain machine learning can support nonintrusive slug/non-slug discrimination in controlled three-phase pipeline flow.

title: Physically Aware Generative Design for Spatial Mechanism Synthesis: A Differentiable Diffusion-Refinement Framework
abstract: Spatial mechanism synthesis requires joint reasoning over discrete topology and continuous geometry under strict loop-closure constraints. Existing search-based methods are often tied to predefined topology spaces, while purely data-driven generators can produce topologically plausible but kinematically infeasible mechanisms. This paper proposes GenRefMechSyn, a physics-aware generative framework that integrates Mimic, a Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based topology–geometry sketch generator, Refiner, a differentiable kinematic refiner, and Judge, a refinement-aware value model. Mimic proposes candidate mechanism sketches, Refiner optimizes continuous geometry under fixed topology and projects candidates toward the kinematic-feasibility region, and Judge uses refinement feedback to guide diffusion sampling toward candidates with higher downstream refinability. Under a 1000-trial acceptance protocol, GenRefMechSyn achieves 81.6% two-translational-DOF (2T) kinematic validity; controlled baselines obtain 6.6% for DiT+Refiner without Judge guidance/feedback augmentation, 84.3% for genetic algorithm (GA)+Refiner with a favorable fixed topology, and 12.2% for multi-topology GA+Refiner. The generated mechanisms reach loop-closure residuals and task errors on the order of $10^{-3}$ and $10^{-4}$, respectively. The same architecture and seed set are also used in an independently trained two-rotational-DOF (2R) feedback run, showing applicability to a separately trained rotational task.

title: GSP-Guided Soft-Gated Descriptor Learning for Robust Point Cloud Registration in Locally Ambiguous Geometry
abstract: Learning-based point cloud registration commonly trains local descriptors by pulling matched points together and pushing negatives apart. This is effective when negatives correspond to genuinely different local structures. However, many points in 3D scenes lie in low-distinctiveness regions, including table surfaces, walls, floors, object faces, and repeated structures. Treating such locally similar points as negatives forces the network to separate descriptors that should remain similar, thereby creating non-repeatable pseudo-salient features that do not generalize across scans. Existing methods improve correspondence quality through transformers, overlap prediction, coarse-to-fine matching, or outlier pruning, but descriptor supervision still largely relies on generic metric learning and does not determine where strong discrimination is geometrically reliable. This letter proposes a local-ambiguity-aware point cloud registration framework centered on graph-signal-processing (GSP) guided supervision allocation. The framework uses a KPConv backbone, computes a geometry reliability gate from local surface variation and normal-boundary response, models dense descriptors as graph signals, and obtains a low-pass reconstruction through superpoint coarsening based on farthest point sampling (FPS). The GSP residual and geometry gate redistribute descriptor variation: low-response regions receive weaker discriminative amplification, whereas middle- and high-response regions carry stronger circle-inspired metric supervision. Training concentrates discriminative learning on regions where high-quality, repeatable descriptors are more likely to form rather than manufacturing isolated feature peaks on ambiguous surfaces. A weighted variance regularizer prevents feature collapse. Experiments on 3DMatch and 3DLoMatch demonstrate improved indoor registration recall, while KITTI evaluation shows competitive outdoor performance with a lightweight KPConv-based architecture.

title: Integral Reinforcement Learning for Latent Human Capability Inference in Human–Robot Interaction
abstract: Human–robot interaction (HRI) requires awareness of a human agent’s latent capability to enable safe, personalized, and effective assistance. A central challenge is that capability is not directly measurable during interaction, although it strongly influences appropriate engagement and resistance settings. This article proposes an artificial intelligence (AI) framework based on off-policy integral reinforcement learning (IRL) for latent capability inference from delayed input–output interaction histories. The framework uses an actor–critic architecture: the critic quantifies how interaction-dynamics variations influence the IRL target policy, and the actor maps policy-derived attributes to capability classes for engagement and resistance selection. Statistical analysis and case studies show that the policy coefficient $\beta$ is the most consistent and interpretable signature, with strong monotonic correlation to stiffness and damping variations and robust behavior across trajectories and effort patterns, while task completion time provides complementary damping-sensitive information. In this simulation-based study, task completion time is treated as a completed-path metric. Comparative simulations against model-based baselines further support the proposed data-driven, model-light AI inference strategy under noise, nonlinearities, and abrupt dynamics changes. A downstream extended Kalman filter (EKF)-based classification study further shows greater feature overlap and interclass confusion than the proposed IRL-based representation, even under a simplified noiseless setting. Within the evaluated simulation setting, the results support completed-path and fragment-level latent capability inference, while continuous online deployment for AI-enabled adaptive assistance in contact-rich HRI tasks remains future work.

title: TextDestroyer: A Training-Free and Annotation-Free Diffusion Method to Destroying Anomalous Text From Images
abstract: In this article, we propose TextDestroyer, the first training- and annotation-free method for scene text destruction using pretrained diffusion models. Unlike existing scene text removal approaches that require extensive annotation and retraining, our method leverages the inherent capabilities of pretrained diffusion models to achieve complete text obliteration while preserving background integrity. TextDestroyer employs a three-stage hierarchical process for precise text localization: Introductory text capturing through cross-attention aggregation, continuous text adjustment via cropped subimage processing, and meticulous text delineation using clustering analysis. For text destruction, we replace identified text regions with Gaussian noise in the latent space before reconstruction. During the diffusion denoising process, we introduce a novel background restoration mechanism that combines self-attention key-value guidance with strategic latent code replacement to ensure seamless background recovery. The key advantages of TextDestroyer include: 1) reducing the need for labor-intensive annotation and resource-intensive training requirements; 2) effective suppression of recognizable textual traces through a destroy-then-reconstruct paradigm; and 3) strong extensibility for rapid iteration and integration with other image editing methods.

title: Secure Hardware Accelerator for Resilience Against Adversarial Attacks in ViTs
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have demonstrated exceptional performance across various computer vision tasks. However, their susceptibility to adversarial white-box attacks poses a significant risk, especially in safety-critical applications. These attacks, with full model access, pose severe threat by drastically reducing accuracy. In response, we propose SAMURAI, a lightweight, preprocessing-based defense pipeline that mitigates adversarial perturbations without requiring model retraining or architectural changes. SAMURAI defends against adversarial inputs by applying a fixed sequence of four transformations: JPEG compression, resizing and center cropping, Gaussian smoothing, and normalization. This process disrupts adversarial attacks while preserving the semantic integrity of the image. Unlike computationally expensive defenses, SAMURAI introduces minimal overhead (e.g., 0.001x for ViT-Large), making it extremely lightweight for real-time deployment. Furthermore, our method generalizes effectively to other vision architectures, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), demonstrating strong transferability. To support efficient deployment in resource-constrained environments, we also design a custom hardware accelerator for the SAMURAI pipeline that enables in-situ preprocessing within accelerators, effectively mitigating adversarial attacks. Experimental results show that SAMURAI achieves robust accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art while requiring only 0.009x the computational cost.

title: A Gaussian Reinforcement Aggregation Network for Multimodal Classification
abstract: To address the heterogeneity in the distribution of discriminative features in remote sensing land-cover classification, we propose a Gaussian reinforcement aggregation network (GRAN). First, we design a sample spatial-spectral score decoupling (S3D) strategy based on category-specific characteristics. The S3D dynamically partitions the original dataset into multiple expert training subsets according to the spectral and spatial complexity of different categories, thereby enabling each expert to focus on modeling the discriminative boundaries of specific category groups. Second, a physics-inspired Gaussian derivative expert network (GDE-Net) is introduced and independently trained on each subset. The GDE-Net constrains the gradients in the spectral and spatial dimensions through low-frequency spectral derivative enhancement (LSDE) and high-frequency spatial derivative awareness (HSDA) modules, implicitly injecting physical prior information from the imaging process into the network, thus effectively extracting deep, fine-grained features highly correlated with the category. Finally, to mitigate the fragmentation caused by independently trained expert models and to achieve globally optimal classification performance, we propose an adaptive coupling factor aggregation network (ACFA-Net). The ACFA-Net adaptively integrates the complementary knowledge of multiple expert models. As a result, the final model exhibits strong global discriminative capability while maintaining high sensitivity to tail categories. Extensive comparative experiments conducted on multiple remote sensing datasets demonstrate that the proposed GRAN framework achieves superior classification performance. Our code is available at the following URL:https://github.com/ChenC1027/GRAN
journal: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology

title: Sequential Differentiable Alignment-Based 2D–3D Optimal Gaussian Distribution Registration for Monocular Endoscopic Video AR Guidance
abstract: Registration between preoperative 3D data and intraoperative 2D endoscopic videos is crucial for advancing Augmented Reality (AR) guidance in surgery. However, due to the complexity of intraoperative scene, it is difficult to achieve accurate real-time 2D–3D registration without prior camera poses or anatomical landmarks. To overcome these challenges, a novel 2D–3D gaussian mixture splatting registration architecture is proposed, which integrates optimal gaussian distribution registration with sequential differentiable alignment. First, to achieve consistent feature representations across 2D and 3D data, the gaussian mixture model feature distributions are constructed through the gaussian splatting pipeline from the preoperative 3D data and the intraoperative 2D endoscopic images, respectively. Secondly, freeing from prior pose or landmarks, a novel optimal gaussian distribution registration module is designed to establish the global coarse registration by minimizing the feature divergence of gaussian mixture models. Finally, a sequential differentiable fine alignment module is employed to achieve real-time local alignment between the rasterized 3D data and the intraoperative endoscopic video. The evaluation is carried out on the public Scared endoscopic dataset, the Clinical Endoscopic Kidney and Liver dataset from the local hospital. The experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in quantitative and qualitative comparisons.
journal: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology

title: TRAG-DPO: Enhancing Visual Question Answering in Tomato Disease Diagnosis via Hybrid Retrieval and DPO-Based Preference Alignment
abstract: Advances in intelligent vision systems have advanced tomato disease diagnosis from manual inspection to automated image-based analysis. Most prior deep learning approaches formulate tomato disease diagnosis as closed-set image classification, producing only coarse disease labels without interpretability or interactive reasoning. These limitations motivate visual question answering based on vision-language models, which provide question-driven explanations and guidance. However, existing models often struggle to perceive small and subtle lesion regions, suffer from cross-modal mismatch when retrieving external agronomic knowledge, and generate responses that are not well aligned with diagnostic intent. To overcome these challenges, we propose TRAG-DPO, a unified retrieval-augmented vision-language framework for tomato disease visual question answering that formulates diagnosis as a knowledge-guided interactive reasoning process. The framework comprises three modules: 1) A fine-grained lesion-aware visual encoding (FG-ViT) that enhances sensitivity to localized lesion regions while preserving global structural context. 2) A coarse-to-fine hybrid retrieval mechanism that narrows the semantic search space through image-text category matching and then selects question-relevant passages to provide evidence-based context. 3) A preference alignment mechanism that employs Direct Preference Optimization to transform retrieved agronomic knowledge into concise and intent-aligned responses. We further construct a composite resource integrating a tomato-specific visual instruction dataset, a disease knowledge base, and a preference fine-tuning dataset with expert-validated comparisons. Extensive experiments on both closed-ended and open-ended tomato VQA benchmarks demonstrate that TRAG-DPO consistently outperforms both general-purpose and agriculture-specific vision-language models. In addition, cross-crop experiments on corn and rice disease VQA further verify the transferability and scalability of the proposed framework. Data and code are available at: https://github.com/SaaSttt/TRAG-DPO
journal: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology

title: JPEG Compression Simulation Invertible Neural Network for Robust Image Steganography
abstract: JPEG compression, a ubiquitous operation on social media platforms, disrupts the embedding distribution of stego images, impairs the extraction of secret information, and increases their detectability. Existing robust image steganographic methods typically approximate JPEG compression using differentiable noise layers, which enable gradient propagation but model compression mainly as a one-way perturbation. To address these issues, we propose a JPEG Compression Simulation Invertible Neural Network (JCS-INN). JCS-INN employs invertible encoding layers to simulate JPEG compression and transforms the lost high-frequency information into auxiliary latent variables constrained by an isotropic Gaussian distribution, thereby enabling high-quality reconstruction through invertible decoding. Based on JCS-INN, we design a dual-domain security-enhanced steganographic network (DDSESNet) that integrates both spatial-domain and JPEG-domain steganalyzers. Through joint adversarial training, the generator achieves end-to-end compression-aware optimization and learns to produce compression-resistant stego images. Furthermore, JCS-INN can serve as a plug-and-play module to replace the noise layers in other steganographic frameworks, improving both their robustness against JPEG compression and training efficiency. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art approaches in both security and the quality of extracted secret images under compressed transmission environments.
journal: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology

title: JLSDNet: Jointly Learning Structured Light and Depth Estimation for Active Stereo
abstract: Active stereo systems based on structured light have emerged as a promising solution for high-accuracy 3D perception. By projecting specially designed patterns onto object surfaces, these systems provide reliable correspondence cues that facilitate dense depth reconstruction. However, existing approaches typically employ pre-defined projection patterns that are decoupled from the scene content, device characteristics, and depth estimation algorithms, which severely limits the overall performance of active stereo systems. In this work, we present a novel end-to-end framework, termed JLSDNet, that jointly learns structured light patterns and depth estimation for active stereo. Specifically, 1) we propose an Adaptive Structured-light Generation Network (ASGNet) that produces optimized projection patterns tailored to each scene. 2) We introduce a hybrid differentiable imaging model that integrates hardware in the forward pass and an optical simulation model in the backward pass, enabling efficient and accurate gradient propagation through active stereo systems. 3) We design a novel Disparity-Attention Depth Estimation Network (DANet) that fuses structured light and RGB information to build a more efficient cost volume, which suppresses redundant information and enhances depth estimation accuracy. Experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in challenging scenes.
journal: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology

title: AGSM: Anchor-Guided Spatial–Semantic Modeling for Remote Sensing Image Captioning
abstract: Remote sensing image captioning (RSIC) aims to generate natural language descriptions for complex remote sensing imagery through effective cross-modal alignment between visual content and textual semantics. Due to densely distributed objects and complex spatial layouts, remote sensing scenes exhibit strong dependencies between local object details and global semantic context, posing significant challenges for discriminative visual representation learning. Existing methods struggle to capture such global–local dependencies and conduct targeted enhancement for key local regions, leading to fragmented global–local representations and limited semantic discriminability in generated captions. To address this issue, the Anchor-Guided Spatial-Semantic Modeling (AGSM) is proposed for RSIC. AGSM uses global–local semantic dependencies from CLIP-extracted CLS and patch tokens to guide feature enhancement and interaction. Specifically, a Visual Anchor Feature Diffusion (VAFD) module strengthens representative local features through anchor-based aggregation and diffusion. A Bi-Mamba Spatial Infusion (BMSI) module injects spatial dependencies into global semantic representations via bidirectional sequence modeling. Furthermore, a Spatially Gated FiLM-Mamba (SGFM) module, where FiLM denotes Feature-wise Linear Modulation, enables adaptive and cooperative global–local interaction through spatially adaptive modulation. The fused representations are finally decoded by a Mamba-based language decoder to generate accurate and coherent captions. Experimental results on four public benchmark datasets, including Sydney-Captions, UCM-Captions, RSICD, and NWPU-Captions, demonstrate the effectiveness and competitive performance of the proposed method.
journal: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology

title: HSDNet: A High-Order Structure Distillation Network via Multi-Type Hypergraph for Traffic Prediction
abstract: Traffic forecasting, a core task in intelligent transportation systems, has recently benefited from advances in graph neural networks (GNNs) and hypergraph neural networks (HGNNs). However, existing methods face three limitations: fixed-topology modeling struggles with dynamic states, purely data-driven relations may ignore structural priors, and heterogeneous traffic attributes are insufficiently exploited. Motivated by the fact that traffic dependence is jointly governed by stable road topology, time-varying latent correlations, and attribute-driven regional heterogeneity, we propose a High-order Structure Distillation Network (HSDNet) to unify global and local structural views. In the teacher network, a static hypergraph encodes persistent spatial priors, while an adaptive hypergraph captures state-dependent correlations; their fusion yields high-order global representations. In the student network, adaptive sub-hypergraphs built within attribute-similar clusters emphasize localized behaviors. A self-distillation mechanism transfers teacher structural knowledge to the student to jointly optimize global topology and local patterns. Experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that HSDNet achieves superior predictive accuracy and strong adaptability across diverse traffic scenarios.
journal: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems

title: An Adaptive Event-Driven Task Migration Strategy for Collaborative Mobile Edge Computing
abstract: Collaboration among edge nodes via task migration is a promising solution for mobile edge computing (MEC) to efficiently meet time-varying and spatially unbalanced computing demands with limited resources. However, existing task migration strategies are primarily confined to a discrete-time paradigm, which suffers from modeling inaccuracy and control dilatoriness. To address this issue, this paper proposes an online stochastic learning-based adaptive task migration strategy operating in a continuous-time event-driven framework. Aiming to ensure satisfactory MEC performance for differentiated services with minimum energy consumption, the policy optimization of task migration jointly with resource allocation and transmission scheduling is formulated as event-driven continuous-time Markov control processes, accurately capturing the stochastic dynamics of task arrival, migration and processing. By leveraging gradient estimation and stochastic approximation, an online stochastic learning algorithm is developed to address the constrained policy optimization. It is computationally efficient and environment-adaptive, capable of real-time computing and online optimization in various unknown environments. Numerical simulations are conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed strategy, and comparative results confirm its effectiveness.

title: Hybrid-Action MADRL-Based Scheduling for Task Offloading and Trajectory Planning in Multi-UAV Systems With Latency Minimization
abstract: Considering the limitations of a single uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) in capacity and coverage, cooperative UAVs assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) architecture has been popular for large-scale mobile terminals (MTs). However, the high mobility of MTs and the limited resources of UAVs lead to challenges such as imbalanced resource allocation and high task latency. Therefore, this paper proposes a hybrid-action MADRL-based scheduling framework for task offloading and trajectory planning in multi-UAV systems. Specifically, considering the predictable mobility of MTs and the limited computing resources of UAVs, a cooperative offloading framework is proposed through alternative MEC based on UAV tracking. To minimize the long-term total delay through the joint optimization of UAV trajectory control, computing resource allocation, and task migration decisions, a non-convex and high-dimensional coupled problem is formulated with constraints on the resources of UAVs and service requirements. To solve this problem, we propose an enhanced hybrid-action multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (HA-MADDPG) algorithm, built upon centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE) paradigm. The developed algorithm incorporates the Gumbel-Softmax mechanism for differentiable discrete action modeling and adopts soft policy updating for convergence stability. Simulation results demonstrate that the HA-MADDPG algorithm based on multi-UAV cooperative MEC system significantly reduces system task delay, improves edge resource utilization and enhances training convergence compared to several mainstream benchmark schemes.

title: LLM-Enhanced MARL for Multi-Hop UAV Networking: An Edge-Cloud Protocol Aware Framework
abstract: With the development of the integration of aerial, terrestrial, and satellite networks, Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) serve as a new type of aerial communication platform, playing a key role in Internet of Things (IoT) scenarios. However, multi-hop UAV networks still suffer from energy limits, bandwidth scarcity, dynamic topology, and unstable links. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an edge-cloud communication protocol framework (EC-LLM-MARL) based on Large Language Models (LLMs) and MARL. In this framework, the cloud side constructs a chain-of-thought to guide LLM reasoning, and distilled expert strategies are transferred to UAVs through knowledge distillation and fine-tuning, improving training efficiency and reducing communication overhead. Additionally, a Graph Attention Network (GAT) is employed to extract deep features of observation targets, while Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) is combined with a self-attention mechanism at the UAV end to enhance credit assignment and convergence efficiency in dynamic environments. Furthermore, the framework designs a differentiated reward mechanism for task load balancing among multiple UAVs, improving the scalability of the algorithm in large-scale network scenarios. Extensive simulations show that EC-LLM-MARL significantly accelerates training convergence and substantially outperforms existing methods, achieving a 77% increase in throughput, a 13% rise in coverage, and the highest remaining energy levels.

title: Generative AI Model Assisted Multimodal Semantic Vehicular Edge Computing for Collaborative Perception
abstract: Vehicular edge computing (VEC) plays a pivotal role in enabling cooperative perception for connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs), providing comprehensive environmental awareness for safe vehicle control and road safety. However, collaborative perception in VEC faces significant challenges arising from stringent bandwidth constraints, communication latency, and high computational demands. In this paper, we propose a novel multimodal semantic vehicular edge computing (SVEC) architecture for cooperative perception to address these challenges. In the proposed SVEC framework, multimodal sensor data is intelligently selected for task-oriented sharing, and data modalities are adaptively transformed in response to dynamic communication and computing resource constraints. The selected information is then transmitted using advanced semantic encoding and decoding techniques, significantly reducing bandwidth consumption. To compensate for potential information loss introduced by semantic compression, we design a generative AI–based enhancement mechanism to preserve high perception fidelity. We further formulate a joint optimization problem to maximize the vehicles’ quality of experience (QoE) for cooperative perception. To solve this problem, we develop a diffusion-based multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm that improves exploration efficiency and jointly optimizes vehicle policies in high-dimensional and complex state spaces. Extensive simulation results show that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms the benchmarks, reducing the average system latency by about 28%, decreasing the average system cost by about 19%, and lowering the semantic perception error by up to 40%, while achieving the highest average rewards and average QoE.

title: Enhancing Autonomous Driving With Physics-Informed and Human-Guided Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Achieving safe, efficient, and human-like autonomous driving (AD) in complex real-world environments remains a critical challenge. To address the limitations of conventional AD learning paradigms that struggle with imperfect human demonstrations and insufficient safety guarantees, this article proposes a novel physics-informed and human-guided reinforcement learning (PI-HGRL) for AD, combining the dual advantages of human-like behavior from demonstrations with the safety assurances of physical models. PI-HGRL employs a dynamic, risk-aware task delegation mechanism that adapts to complex driving contexts by prioritizing human guidance in low-risk scenarios and relying more on physical models in high-risk situations, enhancing data quality and ensuring reliable, efficient human–AI collaboration. Moreover, a progressive fading intervention mechanism (PFIM), inspired by scaffolding theory in human education, is first introduced to systematically reduce reliance on hybrid enhanced guidance (HEG) and facilitate the agent’s transition from imitation learning to surpassing learning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PI-HGRL outperforms baseline methods in driving safety, data efficiency, and generalization capability. Ablation studies further validate the contributions of the physical model and PFIM to the overall strategy. These results suggest that PI-HGRL offers a promising direction for building trustworthy and adaptive human–AI collaborative driving systems.
journal: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics: Systems

title: Estuarine Biofilm Communities Adapt to Changing Conditions While Retaining Crucial Pollutant-Combatting Functions.
Repurposing Regulatory Rodent Toxicology Safety Archives to Identify Candidate Hormetic Longevity Agents Highlights Emergent Mitochondrial Mechanisms
abstract: Efforts to extend longevity and healthspan have benefited from the use of in vitro systems, short‐lived model organisms and computational approaches, but translation to humans depends on demonstrating efficacy and safety in mammalian in vivo models. However, rigorously controlled rodent lifespan studies are slow, costly and low‐throughput. Hormesis, the induction of adaptive stress response pathways by low‐level toxic or metabolic challenges, provides a mechanistic means for improved resilience, but testing hormetic dose–response relationships in mammals is logistically challenging. Regulatory long‐term toxicity studies, mandated for chemical authorisation, routinely generate lifespan and chronic toxicity data from large cohorts across multiple dose groups and therefore represent an underused resource for detecting unexpected survival benefits. We mined a random subset of the German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment (BfR) electronic archive for long‐term rodent pesticide studies in ≥ 50 animals per dose and sex. From qualifying studies with 154 substances, we identified 27 substances (18% of entries) that significantly increased survival at study termination (≥ 10%, p < 0.05). Fifteen publicly disclosable substances were examined further; roughly half perturbed mitochondrial oxygen consumption rates in mammalian cells, and bromoxynil acted as a mitochondrial uncoupler. Back‐translation to Caenorhabditis elegans showed bromoxynil improved multiple healthspan indicators without compromising organismal health. Regulatory toxicity archives can thus be repurposed to identify candidate compounds, targets and mechanisms for mammalian healthy ageing research, complement conventional screening pipelines, align with 3Rs by maximising existing data, and supply high‐quality datasets for AI‐driven prioritisation of interventions for rigorous preclinical follow‐up.

title: Pantethine Restores Epidermal Homeostasis and Modulates Vesicle-Associated Proteins in Psoriasis.
abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by disrupted epidermal homeostasis driven by interconnected immuno-inflammatory, metabolic, and redox signalling networks. Vesicle-associated intercellular communication has emerged as an important contributor to inflammatory amplification and tissue remodelling within the epidermal microenvironment. Pantethine, a stable vitamin B5 derivative with lipid-modulatory and anti-inflammatory properties, has been implicated in regulation of cellular stress responses and membrane-associated signalling pathways, suggesting potential therapeutic relevance in psoriasis. Here, we investigated the effects of pantethine using a full-thickness 3D human psoriatic skin model following keratinocyte safety assessment. Integrated histopathological, immunohistochemical, quantitative RT-PCR, and proteomic analyses were employed to interrogate inflammatory, oxidative, proliferative, apoptotic, differentiation-associated and vesicle-related responses. Pantethine significantly reduced epidermal thickening and normalized multiple psoriasis-associated molecular signatures. Proteomic profiling revealed coordinated modulation of vesicle-associated, cytoskeletal and extracellular matrix-related proteins, accompanied by reduced expression of exosome-associated markers CD63 and CD9. Pantethine suppressed pro-inflammatory signalling involving IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-17, S100 family members, and hyperproliferative keratin-associated pathways while reducing caspase-3-associated apoptotic activity. Concurrently, pantethine enhanced antioxidative and immunoregulatory responses through activation of Nrf-2 and TGF-β, restored differentiation and barrier-related markers including filaggrin, caspase-14, and involucrin, and reduced hypoxia- and tissue-remodelling-associated mediators including HIF-1α, VEGF, COL6A3, and COL1A2. Network-based proteomic analyses further identified computationally inferred associations with SLIT/ROBO-related pathways, although these associations require further functional validation. Collectively, these findings support pantethine as a promising candidate that modulates vesicle-associated proteins together with inflammatory and tissue-remodelling responses involved in epidermal homeostasis.

title: Temperature Carryover Effect Revealed for Marine Fishes Using Spatio‐Temporal Distributed Lag Models
abstract: Understanding the impact of changing temperature on population densities is necessary to predict the likely impact of climate anomalies (e.g., marine heatwaves) or forecast distribution shifts under future climate scenarios. Population densities are often analyzed using spatio‐temporal models (STMs), which typically predict densities based on local habitat conditions while also estimating latent spatial and spatio‐temporal variation. Recent research extends STMs by also estimating density responses to habitat conditions at nearby locations using a “spatially distributed lag” (SDL) that averages habitat conditions in the vicinity of samples. Here, we extend the SDL by incorporating insights from diffusion‐enhanced STMs to simultaneously estimate spatially distributed and time‐lagged responses to nearby and past habitat conditions (a “spatio‐temporal distributed lag” STDL). We then use summer bottom trawl survey data from the eastern Bering Sea (1982–2024) to measure whether spatial and/or temporal lags are parsimonious when predicting population density from temperature anomalies for six ecologically important fishes. Results show that time‐lagged responses are parsimonious, positive, and substantial (correlation of 0.20–0.83 per year) for five species, and that density responses to temperature anomalies also diffuse outward over time for four species at 30–53 km per year. A self‐ and cross‐test simulation experiment shows that model selection can identify the appropriate model and that parameter estimates are approximately unbiased. We therefore conclude that temperature carryover effects arise in marine fishes and implement the method in the R package sdmTMB so that future studies can estimate nonlocal and time‐lagged responses when measuring density responses to habitat.

title: Co-Designing a Website With Young People to Enable the Uptake of Online, Self-Help Single Session Interventions for Mental Health: A Participatory Approach.
abstract: BACKGROUND Evidence-based self-help digital interventions are a promising approach to low-barrier mental health and well-being support. They could be particularly impactful at the early stages of help-seeking and could reach young people who may not otherwise access any help at all. To capitalise on these interventions, they need to be offered in ways that are engaging and easily navigated by the end-user and promote trust and credibility. Co-designing the implementation of these interventions could enable this. METHODS We aimed to co-design a website to host self-help digital interventions aimed at young people in the United Kingdom. We used the Design, Develop, Build and Test model to guide our development process. Over 8 months, we ran a series of participatory virtual co-design workshops with young people as contributors (N = 29, 13-18 years). RESULTS By iteratively moving between the design-development-build phases, we co-created our website, including branding, look and feel, structure, content and functionality. All design decisions were led by what young people told us was most important to them. CONCLUSIONS Young people's input shaped every aspect of the co-designed unlockwellbeing.org.uk website, from branding to functionality, ensuring relevance, credibility and accessibility. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION This descriptive paper presents a practical, experience-informed illustration of how to meaningfully involve young people in the co-design of digital mental health resources. Grounded in both the literature and our own participatory co-design work, we describe the iterative development of a website hosting evidence-based self-help interventions for young people with symptoms of depression. Using the Design, Develop, Build and Test model, we engaged 29 young people aged 13-18 in a series of virtual workshops over 8 months, ensuring that every design decision, from branding to functionality, was led by their input.
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

title: Crop‐System Variation in Methyl‐Eugenol‐Responsive Male Bactrocera Assemblages Covaries With Geographic and Landscape Context
abstract: Methyl eugenol trapping is widely used to monitor male Bactrocera , but capture patterns can reflect crop context, geography, elevation and surrounding landscape as well as species biology. We analysed a harmonised dataset from nine apple, nine guava and nine citrus orchards in East Java, Indonesia, using nine traps per orchard in two sampling periods (486 trap‐period observations). Among 16,185 males, Bactrocera carambolae Drew & Hancock represented 57.6% of apple captures, whereas Bactrocera dorsalis (Hendel) represented 71.9% of guava and 94.8% of citrus captures. Repeated‐measures negative‐binomial models showed markedly higher B. carambolae captures in apple than in guava or citrus, while absolute B. dorsalis captures did not differ among crop systems and sampling period had no overall effect. Crop system explained substantial variation in elevation ( R 2 = 0.742), plant age and latitude. Accordingly, the crop association detected by simple PERMANOVA ( R 2 = 0.269, p = 0.0012) weakened after conditioning on broad geography ( p = 0.0618) or elevation ( p = 0.0682). A pre‐specified AICc candidate set identified crop‐only as the highest‐ranked model for B. carambolae , whereas landscape‐configuration models ranked slightly above crop‐only for B. dorsalis and total captures; these rankings were not robust to leave‐one‐orchard‐out and spatial‐covariance sensitivity analyses. Bactrocera umbrosa (Fabricius) occurred in eight of nine guava orchards but was absent from citrus. These results support context‐aware trap surveillance while showing that lure‐based crop associations should not be interpreted as confirmed host use, infestation or crop damage.

title: Risk-Oriented Differentiated Governance for Ambiguous Information.
abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence has led to an exponential increase in false information, especially ambiguous information. Hampered by resource constraints, conventional governance approaches fall short of enabling efficient and precise risk management. In response, this paper innovatively proposes a risk-oriented tiered governance framework tailored to ambiguous information. Specifically, we quantify epistemic uncertainty via multi-level semantic features, combine it with network propagation features to determine latent influence scores, and construct a risk function capturing their synergy. Critical and acceptable boundaries are introduced to categorize ambiguous information into discrete risk levels, tier-specific governance strategies are devised, and a propagation throttling (limiting each user's successful forwards per ambiguous information) strategy is innovatively proposed for medium-risk information. Finally, we simulate differentiated governance strategies across risk levels of ambiguous information, systematically assess governance effectiveness, and offer a comparative discussion grounded in fairness and ethics. This study offers an operational analytical framework for refined risk governance of ambiguous information, contributes methodological innovations in risk quantification modeling and tiered governance strategies, and provides theoretical support and practical guidance for risk management authorities in designing differentiated measures.
journal: Risk analysis : an official publication of the Society for Risk Analysis

title: Holographic study of the scalar meson $K_0^*(1430)$ with dynamical longitudinal confinement
abstract: Within the framework of light-front holographic QCD, where transverse confinement is inherently realized through holography, the structure and mass spectrum of the light scalar meson $K_0^{*}(1430)$ are investigated by employing the invariant mass ansatz and enhancing the model with a longitudinal confinement potential (specifically, the 't Hooft equation and the analytically solvable LMZV potential). The combined transverse and longitudinal confinement dynamics lead to more reliable calculations of key observables, including decay constants, parton distribution function, $ξ$-moments, and twist-$2$ and twist-$3$ distribution amplitudes. Transition form factors for the semileptonic decay $B \rightarrow K_0^{*} \ell^+ \ell^-$ are computed from these amplitudes, yielding predictions for differential branching ratios and longitudinal lepton polarization asymmetries as functions of $q^2$. The results are compared with other theoretical models, offering valuable insights into the non-perturbative dynamics of QCD. The predicted observables provide theoretically motivated benchmarks for future experimental investigations of $B\rightarrow K_0^*(1430)\ell^+\ell^-$ decays at LHCb and Belle II.

title: Programming by Teaching: Authoring Agent Workflows through Voice Conversation
abstract: Agent workflow automation is increasingly accessible to users without programming experience, but much of the knowledge needed to author workflows is implicit. Programming by Demonstration captures what users do on screen but not the rules behind their actions. We propose Programming by Teaching, where users teach a task to an AI through real-time voice conversation while navigating the application, as they would teach a colleague. The AI listens, takes notes, and generates an agent workflow. We implemented both modes in the same Chrome extension and compared them in a within-subjects study with 28 participants, primarily non-programmers. Teaching passed held-out edge-case tests at 87.2% compared to 46.7% for demonstration (p =.002). Teaching reduced cognitive load (p =.04), scored higher on both pragmatic and hedonic quality (p ≤.001), and made it easier to incorporate rules not visible in the UI (p =.003). The hardest part of demonstration was not building the workflow but editing it afterward; teaching sidesteps this by front-loading specification into conversation.
journal: Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Neighborhood: Dynamic Spatial Alignment for Traversable Telepresence Across Remote Spaces
abstract: We propose Neighborhood, a mixed reality (MR) telepresence system that allows users to experience an illusion of walking between local and remote spaces as if they are physically connected. Prior studies transmit either the avatar or the space alone to the remote space. Works that transmit both limit either remote space’s visibility or traversability to specific areas. Our work builds upon prior works by transmitting both the avatar and the space, while also supporting full visibility and traversability of local and remote spaces with user’s activities grounded with their real furniture and objects, distinct from VR traversal. Our system begins with users moving to the specific area they wish to connect. Using the chosen spaces, the optimization function aligns them to initiate Walking In Mode, visualizing a traversable area with remote spaces augmented. If users wish to move to a different area, the system transits to Panning Mode. Here, the moving user’s avatar appears stationary while the background shifts from the observing user’s perspective. We quantitatively measure metrics including the size of the neighborhood and ablate each term to evaluate the optimization function across diverse spatial configurations. We also conducted an exploratory user study with 21 participants, showing that traversing within Neighborhood evokes a compelling sense of real spatial adjoin.
journal: Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: iRing: Rich Interaction on Smart Ring with Multi-point Capacitive Touch Screen
abstract: Rising interest in smart rings reflects a growing demand for immediate, lightweight interaction. However, prior designs have largely treated rings as input-only interfaces, or devices with limited on-device visualization, fall short in supporting for tightly coupled, direct, and expressive co-located interaction. To bridge this gap, we present iRing, a lightweight (6.4 g), low-cost ($46.43), open-source, and reproducible smart ring platform centered on a capacitive multi-touch display. We design a compact, multi-touch interface using accessible components that fit the ring’s tight form factor. It further integrates a flexible OLED display, BLE micro-controller, IMU, and PPG sensor, supporting both local and remote interaction. To bridge hardware touch sensing and interaction events, we introduce nano interactions—a compact vocabulary that adapts familiar touch primitives for direct, co-located input and visual output on ultra-small, curved surfaces. Nano interactions allow interaction within a single glance–touch cycle, supporting one-handed, low-attention use under motion. We implement a set of applications to explore the design space enabled by multi-touch on a ring. A user study with 12 participants demonstrates reliable touch interaction and provides positive short-term assessments of usability, comfort, and social acceptability, highlighting opportunities for compact interaction surfaces supporting glanceable and on-the-go interaction.
journal: Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: PrejSense: Non-intrusive Gaze-Informed Prediction of Implicit Prejudice Against Machine for Proactive Interface Adaptation
abstract: Implicit prejudice against machine can critically undermine the effectiveness of human-AI collaboration by limiting trust, cooperation, and system acceptance. Despite its significance, such prejudice is rarely addressed in real world usage and is often assessed retrospectively through self-report measures or implicit association test, lacking automated and adaptive interface essential for responsive system design. Drawn from dual process theory, we propose and test PrejSense, a proof-of-concept adaptive interface loop that uses non-intrusive gaze signals to predict users’ prejudice states and adapt interface support accordingly. First, we develop interpretable deep learning models to predict prejudice from gaze features. Second, we develop adaptive interface using LLM agents to dynamically respond to estimated prejudice states, with expert-informed refinement. Third, we build a full-stack system for automated prejudice prediction and adaptive interaction, enabling non-intrusive integration into collaborative AI systems. We conduct a user testing experiment to evaluate the effectiveness of PrejSense. Compared with baseline, PrejSense significantly enhanced emotional trust and showed marginal positive effects on cognitive trust and WOA. These results provide preliminary evidence for state-contingent prejudice-aware adaptation in a low-risk decision-support task. By combining gaze-informed prejudice prediction with adaptive interaction design, this work opens a design space for prejudice-aware adaptive interfaces while highlighting the need for larger-scale validation.
journal: Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Priors of U: Dynamic Preference Learning for Embodied Interaction
abstract: People have their own habits; from how they organize their workspace, over which mug they reach for in the morning, to how they prepare for cooking. Such preferences are context-dependent, dynamic, and often difficult to articulate. As embodied AI agents, such as robots, enter personal spaces, effective interaction requires understanding these implicit and evolving preferences; otherwise, such systems risk being more hindering than helpful. We propose an architecture that learns user preferences from real-world behavioral observation without requiring explicit instruction or feedback. We introduce a factor-graph-based user model that captures preferences across spatial arrangement, tool selection, and workflow, and continuously adapts as tasks and contexts change. The model expands with new observations, enabling open-ended, in situ learning of user-specific preference patterns. Our evaluation shows accurate, calibrated predictions across domains and robust adaptation over time. We demonstrate personalized robot assistance scenarios illustrating seamless and context-aware human–agent interaction.
journal: Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: CARVid: Content-Aware Retargeting of Videos with On-Screen Graphics
abstract: Video editors routinely reframe landscape videos containing on-screen graphics, such as lower thirds or scoreboards, to portrait aspect ratios for sharing on social media. Existing methods often crop, shrink, or distort these graphics, reducing readability and disrupting their original design. Manual redesign is also slow and frustrating due to the difficulty of dealing with layered compositions or flattened videos with graphics that lack editable layers. We present CARVid, a content-aware retargeting tool for adapting on-screen graphics in videos to new aspect ratios while preserving readability and original design intent. CARVid leverages recent advances in foundation vision and segmentation models, together with a novel graphics-processing algorithm guided by a VLM critic, to detect graphical overlays, extract them from their underlying videos, and apply content-aware retargeting operations to adapt them to new aspect ratios. Our human-in-the-loop approach combines text-aware scaling, layout-aware horizontal and vertical segmentation, and content-aware space removal to support both automatic and user-directed retargeting of on-screen graphics. We conducted a technical evaluation using a custom dataset of 60 in-the-wild videos from popular internet sources that contain on-screen graphics. Results provide evidence of CARVid’s technical feasibility across a wide range of videos.
journal: Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: BrewSense: A Mobile Water Quality Monitoring Platform using Laser Reflection near Brewster Angle
abstract: BrewSense is a mobile water-quality monitoring platform for realtime, large-scale detection of inland water pollution beyond the reach of grab sampling and remote sensing, whose alternatives are invasive, expensive, or limited to narrow classes of solutes and controlled environments. BrewSense leverages laser reflection near Brewster's angle to remotely infer the refractive index of surface water, which varies approximately linearly with the concentration of both ionic and organic solutes. It combines a beam-splitter and orthogonal-polarizer front-end that strongly suppresses ambient light, synchronized electrodynamic indexers with magnetic angle sensing, and hierarchical angular sampling, Gaussian spot filtering, and derivative-based Brewster-angle fitting that stabilize measurements under platform motion, waves, turbidity, and temperature variations. Implemented on a UAV, BrewSense operates at meter-scale standoff distances and achieves sub-10-4 refractive-index resolution under controlled conditions. Controlled and real-lake-water tank experiments evaluate inorganic salts (NaCl, NH4Cl) and organic solutes (glucose, urea), and a UAV deployment validates end-to-end operation in a NaCl-dominated field setting. BrewSense achieves up to 3.2× lower error than prior UWB and vibration-based systems and an approximately 8% mean relative concentration-estimation error across 20 UAV field sites.
journal: Proceedings of the Twenty-seventh International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Poster: When Safer AI Makes the System Less Safe: Inference Reuse and Systemic Risk in Networked Autonomy
abstract: Network-assisted inference can improve the decisions of autonomous agents, while reusing inference results can avoid repeated computation. However, when multiple agents reuse the same inference result, their failures become more coupled. We show that beyond a simple threshold, simultaneous failure can become more likely even though every agent is individually more accurate. We then characterize when the resource savings from reuse justify this added shared-failure risk.
journal: Proceedings of the Twenty-seventh International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Ripple: Coordination-Free Message Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows at the IoT Edge
abstract: Distributed intelligence in IoT and edge systems increasingly runs as agentic AI: production large language model (LLM) applications execute as workflows—directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) of agents and tools that exchange prompts, retrieved context, and tool outputs across end devices, edge servers, and the cloud. When many such workflows share a capacity-limited link, such as an edge gateway uplink or a regional aggregation point, that link rather than the GPU gates the communication phase, and a message that unblocks an idle agent may wait behind an unrelated bulk transfer. A dependency-aware link scheduler can mitigate this, but a scheduler that ranks messages by whole-workflow remaining work and downstream critical path requires a global, continuously updated view of every concurrent workflow, that is, a central coordinator that heterogeneous and dynamic IoT edge deployments typically lack. This paper presents Ripple, a coordination-free link scheduler in which each agent ranks only its own outgoing messages, using a local rule that prioritizes downstream criticality per unit transmission cost and applies an age credit to curb long waits. The required downstream-criticality signal is a bounded scalar initialized with the source's task descriptor, so no runtime node maintains the global graph. In an event-driven, flow-level evaluation on a shared 100 Mbps link with heavy-tailed messages (median 419 KB, 99th-percentile about 30 MB) and four DAG shapes, network waiting accounts for 46% of the mean workflow completion time (WCT) under fair sharing at offered load ρ=0.88. Ripple reduces mean and 99th-percentile WCT by 24% and 38% relative to fair sharing, and attains 9% lower mean and 27% lower tail WCT than a global-view reference heuristic while using no global state. A knowledge-horizon analysis shows that performance saturates at a one-hop view, and an ablation finds that message size and age drive most of the aggregate gain. The results use an idealized flow-level priority model; a DSCP/eBPF realization that needs no coordinator and no change to the LLM runtime is proposed but not yet evaluated.
journal: Proceedings of the Twenty-seventh International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: An Agentic AI Architecture for Zero-Touch IoT Device Onboarding and Interoperability
abstract: The heterogeneity of Internet of Things (IoT) devices remains a major barrier to scalable deployment, automated onboarding, and cross-platform interoperability. Device-specific protocols, software dependencies, telemetry formats, and runtime constraints often require manual configuration and ad-hoc integration logic. This paper proposes an agentic AI architecture for zero-touch IoT device onboarding, where a large language model is used as an autonomous configuration agent capable of generating device-side software, installing dependencies, validating runtime behavior, and recursively correcting failures until convergence is achieved. The proposed architecture introduces a closed-loop workflow that combines device inspection, AI-based runtime generation, remote deployment, telemetry validation, and self-correction. Interoperability is addressed through a normalized telemetry contract that abstracts device-specific behavior into a common telemetry representation. We evaluate the approach on a real IoT device by benchmarking multiple AI models under clean installation conditions in two campaigns: the original pipeline and a second pipeline assisted by a locally trained semantic context optimizer. The comparison covers convergence time, correction cycles, recursive iterations, and prompt tokens. The optimizer-assisted campaign reduced prompt redundancy and recursive recovery effort while preserving successful onboarding across all tested models. Overall, the results show that agentic AI can support zero-touch onboarding while exposing measurable differences among models in reliability, efficiency, and runtime convergence.
journal: Proceedings of the Twenty-seventh International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Air pollution in the context of building structure and density in selected Polish cities
abstract: The aim of the study was to determine the differentiation of mean annual concentrations of particulate matter PM2.5 and PM10, benzo(a)pyrene (BaP), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), and benzene (C₆H₆) in 2018–2024 in the context of the structure and intensity of development in Gdańsk, Kraków, and Łódź. The analysis also account - ed for reported pollutant emissions and mean annual wind speed. Data from GIOŚ, KOBiZE, and IMGW-PIB, as well as building data from BDOT10k were used. The highest mean annual concentrations of all analysed pollutants were recorded in Kraków, where the share of built-up area was 49%, and the lowest in Gdańsk, where this share was 30%. After accounting for differences between cities, significant positive correlations between reported emissions and concentration were found for BaP (ρ = 0.90), NO₂ (ρ = 0.60), and PM10 ( ρ = 0.55). However, in the models accounting for the city effect, reported emissions were not significantly associated with the concentration of any of the analysed pollutants. The mean annual wind speed was highest in Gdańsk (3.98 m/s) and lowest in Kraków (3.08 m/s). The height structure of buildings differed between cities, but did not directly correspond to the observed differences in concentrations. The results indicate that the differentiation of mean annual air pollutant concentrations between cities co-occurs with differences in building intensity and wind speed. Due to the limited number of cities analysed, these relationships should not be interpreted as causal.

title: Reactive dyes adsorption by chestnut shells coated with nanoparticles of zinc oxide: Characterization, isotherm and kinetic studies
abstract: This investigation employed a new adsorbent composed of chestnut shell powder and covered with ZnO nanoparticles. Coated chestnut shell (CCS) was examined to assess the adsorption of Reactive Blue-19 Dye and Red Reac - tive-2 from a water-based mixture. Considerable increases in the capability of adsorption of the chestnut shell were recognized following the coating of the powder particles with ZnO nanoparticles. The adsorbent was analyzed using surface area analysis, FTIR, SEM, and XRD to verify its structural and morphological properties. Batch adsorption Research was done to ascertain the optimum Situations, including the solution pH, adsorbent dosage, contact period, speed of shaking, and initial dye concentration, all conducted at room temperature, which is 25 °C. Both the Freundlich and Langmuir isotherm models were used to describe the equilibrium information on adsorption. As a result revealed that the process of adsorption followed Langmuir’s isotherm model, using correlation values (R²) of 0.9886 for Reactive Red-2 and 0.9955 for Reactive Blue-19, demonstrating monolayer adsorption onto a uniform surface. The greatest CCS adsorption capacity was observed for Reactive Blue-19 (172.413 mg/g), followed by Reactive Red-2 (114.942 mg/g). Kinetic information was correlated using both pseudo-first-order and pseudo-second-order models. The findings demonstrated that the model of pseudo-second order gave greater results compared to the pseudo-first order model, considering correlation coefficients (R²) of 0.9951 for Reactive Red-2 and 0.9975for Reactive Blue-19, demonstrating that the process of chemisorption step that limits the rate of adsorption mechanism. Thus, these results show that CCS is among the best and most efficient adsorbents for getting rid of wastewater tainted with reactive dye residues.

title: Digital Transformation in South American Soybean Production: A Systematic Review of Drivers and Barriers to Agricultural Technology Adoption
journal: Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção

title: When Actors Stop Participating: Delegated Participation and Representative-Centered Organizing
abstract: Organizational theories usually treat participation as actor-bound: the actors whose interests are at stake are expected to occupy the interactions through which outcomes are produced. Agentic artificial intelligence and other autonomous representatives weaken that correspondence. This conceptual article develops a theory of delegated participation, defined as the authorized transfer of communicative, evaluative, coordinative, or exchange-related participation from a principal to a representative. The argument moves beyond treating participation delegation as merely another agency relationship. When representatives operate on multiple sides of an exchange, they form an interaction system that can persist without direct principal participation, reshape the alternatives reaching principals, and separate participation from accountability. The model identifies activity conditions, capability–structure alignment, and authorization as antecedents; bilateral representation and interaction displacement as mechanisms; and symbolic concentration and representative-centered organizing as organizational consequences. The framework contributes by challenging the actor-bound conception of participation, identifying bilateral representation as a discontinuity in organizing, and explaining why declining principal participation may coexist with persistent principal accountability and increasingly consequential symbolic appearances. The article concludes with managerial implications and an empirical research agenda focused on recruitment, procurement, customer service, and AI-mediated negotiation.

title: Towards Fine-grained and Robust Detection of Human-AI Co-authorship
abstract: The widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) is reshaping how textual content is produced, complicating text provenance, and raising concerns for misinformation, plagiarism, and intellectual property. While prior work on AI-generated text detection has progressed, one-dimensional human-AI co-authorship scores lack signals directly relevant to ``AI involvement''. It remains unclear how adversarial paraphrasing distorts detection signals. In this work, we formulate a discrete-class text provenance detection framework. This framework allows an abstraction of realistic co-authorship scenarios into distinct degrees of AI involvement, differentiating the AI polishing on the surface level from the AI updating the discourse structures. This framework reveals the mechanisms of how adversarial paraphrasing blurs the decision boundaries for co-authorship detectors. To improve robustness of the detectors, we augment training data with adversarial paraphrases generated by the state-of-the-art paraphrasing attack model, exposing detectors to challenging meaning-preserving rewrites. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and generation models demonstrate that adversarial paraphrasing substantially degrades detectors trained only on benign data, while adversarial data augmentation leads to consistent robustness gains and good cross-generator transferability. Overall, our findings highlight the value of discrete-class formulation and principled data augmentation for building reliable detectors of human-AI co-authorship.

title: PIPNet EA for Robust and Explainable Crop Weed Classification Using Enhanced Prototype Evidence Aggregation
abstract: Deep learning models can achieve high accuracy on clean crop–weed images but often lose performance when field images are affected by noise, blur, poor illumination, motion, or compression. This study presents PIPNet-EA, an enhanced prototype-based interpretable prediction framework that combines top-κ spatial evidence aggregation with confidence-weighted prototype reasoning. Five deep learning architectures—ResNet50, ResNet101, ViT-B/16, PIPNet-R50, and PIPNet-R101—were evaluated on two crop–weed image datasets under seven common image corruptions at three severity levels: mild, moderate, and severe. The evaluation generated 210 model–corruption–severity accuracy measurements, while the accuracy retention rate (ARR) was used to quantify the proportion of clean-image performance preserved under degradation. PIPNet-R50 showed the strongest overall robustness. On the challenging field dataset, its mean accuracy was 0.641, 0.568, and 0.437 under mild, moderate, and severe corruption, respectively, compared with 0.594, 0.525, and 0.391 for ResNet50. It retained 98.9%, 87.7%, and 67.5% of its clean performance across the three severity levels, exceeding the corresponding retention of ResNet50. Prototype activation maps remained focused on meaningful plant structures, including leaf tips, midribs, and petiole regions, even under moderate degradation. By combining evidence from multiple spatial locations rather than relying on a single dominant activation, PIPNet-EA reduces the effect of local image corruption while maintaining interpretable predictions. These findings support prototype-based evidence aggregation as a practical approach for developing robust and explainable crop–weed classification systems for precision agriculture.
