Across Qwen-3.5 9B, Nemotron-H 8B, and Kimi-Linear 48B-A3B, LoReS supports robust 8-bit state quantization and lower effective precision on shorter decode horizons. We implement LoReS in vLLM and demonstrate end-to-end decode speedups.

title: The Laplace transform of the time of ruin in the Cramér--Lundberg model with Erlang $E_2(μ)$ claims: spectrum, exact moments and matrix reduction
abstract: We study the Laplace transform of the time of ruin in the classical Cramér--Lundberg model with claims having an Erlang distribution of shape parameter 2. We derive an integro-differential equation with two boundary conditions. For every positive discount rate, we show that its characteristic polynomial has one negative root and two distinct positive roots. Boundedness excludes the growing exponential term and yields a representation of the transform as a sum of two decaying exponentials. We construct a finite-dimensional matrix reduction of the convolution chain. For a model parameter set, we obtain exact expressions for the ruin probability, the mean time of ruin, and higher moments, including the third moment at zero initial surplus. We prove analyticity in the discount rate and justify the resulting moment series. We consider the analytic continuation of the representation to negative discount rates separately. For Erlang claims with an arbitrary positive integer shape parameter, we establish a closed linear system and the asymptotics of the root continuing the zero root at zero discount.

title: Reduction of the integro-differential equation to an ordinary differential equation in ruin models with investment in a risky asset
abstract: We study ruin models with the surplus invested in a risky asset and Erlang-distributed claims: non-life insurance, annuity payments and the mixed model. Assuming that the integro-differential equation for the survival probability has a classical twice continuously differentiable solution, we prove that this solution satisfies a linear ordinary differential equation. We construct explicit annihilating operators and write the coefficients of the reduced equation in closed form through binomial coefficients (for the mixed model with equal shape parameters). A converse criterion is obtained: a bounded solution of the reduced equation satisfies the integro-differential equation if and only if the residual vanishes at zero initial capital together with its derivatives of order below that of the annihilator. The exponent of the power branch at infinity is determined by the parameters of the risky asset alone and does not depend on the shape parameter. For the mixed model we classify the fundamental set of solutions: the exponentially growing modes are excluded by boundedness. The connection coefficient of the power branch is nonzero by a known power-law lower bound for the ruin probability, and in the annuity model by the reduced equation and the boundary condition at zero. Hence the ruin probability has power-law asymptotics with a positive constant for all shape parameters and all positive exponents, and a complete asymptotic expansion up to a multiplicative constant in all three models. For non-life insurance with Erlang claims of order two the expansion coefficients are computed by an explicit recurrence.

title: Federated Estimation of Loading Spaces in Tensor Factor Models under Differential Privacy
abstract: Tensor factor models provide low-dimensional representations of tensor-valued observations while preserving their multiway structure. When these observations are held by different clients, privacy constraints may prevent them from being pooled for centralized analysis. We study estimation of common loading spaces in Tucker tensor factor models under federated differential privacy, allowing heterogeneous sample sizes, privacy budgets, and factor strengths. The proposed method combines private stability testing, Huber aggregation, and Gaussian perturbation at each client with weighted aggregation at the server. We establish non-asymptotic upper bounds governed by a scaled harmonic mean of the squared local error rates, and prove minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors under strong factors, fixed factor ranks, and fixed noise variance. We further develop a private calibration procedure that selects the local tuning parameters and aggregation weights without knowledge of the noise level or client-specific factor strengths. The resulting adaptive estimator preserves the privacy guarantee and attains the error rate obtained with oracle tuning. We illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed estimators through simulation experiments and an application to a Meditation Traits EEG dataset.

title: AgenticMobility: An Open-Source Platform for Multi-AI-Agent Mobility Dynamics
abstract: Understanding mobility dynamics and the effects of urban transportation management policies requires examining how individual travel decisions, traffic conditions, and policy interventions influence one another over time. We present AgenticMobility, an open-source experimental platform for studying how mobility AI agents and other AI agents interact, adapt through repeated experience, and collectively shape mobility outcomes. Persistent agents retain identities and relevant states across rounds, with explicit interfaces defining information access, admissible actions, and decision schedules; linked records trace decisions, execution, and feedback. In the current implementation, large language model (LLM) agents act as travelers choosing routes and departure times and as a manager periodically adjusting link charges within MATSim. A preliminary demonstration spans 100 simulated days in each of five configurations, with one run per configuration and a shared simulation seed. In the joint traveler--manager run, all 1,179,300 finalized target decisions satisfied action constraints; execution checks verified implementation of accepted choices and preservation of personal memories across days. Trajectories show stable route choices alongside departure-time adjustments and differences between controlled-trip and population-wide outcomes. The platform supports experiments on individual adaptation, collective outcomes, and management interventions by varying information access, retained experience, and management feedback. Source code is available at https://github.com/Agentic-City-Research/Agentic-Mobility

title: Geometric Morphology Learning: Empowering Foundation Models from Structure to Spacetime Intelligence
abstract: Geometry is the very form that connects space, time, and matter, serving as the fundamental fabric of the physical world, from continuous fields to discrete structures. Despite its importance, deep learning is inherently blind to geometry. Riemannian geometry stands as a well-established mathematical foundation for studying geometry, yet it remains largely incompatible with deep learning architectures. To bridge this gap, we establish a new learning framework--Geometric Morphology Learning--that learns geometric or topological structures, shapes or conformations for representation learning, reasoning and action modeling. Moving beyond early attempts limited to specific geometric priors, this theory centers on modeling the intrinsic geometry of objects and learning from such geometric or topological knowledge. Specifically, we construct a neural bundle, a unified scaffolding linking local and global structures, and formulate differentiable operators, including connection and curvature, thereby enabling the study of geometry with advanced geometric concepts such as holonomy and cohomology. Consequently, Geometric Morphology Learning opens new horizons in foundation models, reasoning and planning, graph modeling, physical simulation, PDE systems, and dynamics, marking a fundamental shift toward instilling systematic geometry in artificial intelligence.

title: ReWY: Faster Gradient Computation for Delta-Rule Attention Family
abstract: Delta-rule linear attention underlies language models such as Kimi Linear and Qwen3-Next. Chunkwise implementations expose matrix parallelism, but their backward passes compute unnecessary auxiliary adjoints. We present ReWY, an algebraic reformulation that reduces this work before optimizing accelerator execution. Differentiating the chunk correction as one triangular residual system eliminates the inverse adjoint and reduces seven local WY matrix products to three. Two complementary transformations expose further reuse: centered matrix contractions replace pairwise vector-gate processing, and scalar-gate reductions reuse key-gradient products instead of forming a key Gram matrix. These identities simplify backward computation for DeltaNet, GDN, KDA, and GDN2 while preserving the recurrence and gradients in exact arithmetic, without changing the architecture or training objective. We implement the reduced graph on GPUs and Ascend NPUs. Under matched recomputation and full-saving policies, precision-qualified six-shape comparisons with frozen FLA references yield 1.15-1.81$\times$ geometric-mean complete low-level backward speedups on NVIDIA GPUs. All four operators achieve 1.18-1.70$\times$ on H100 and H200 while retaining original FP32 working matrices. A separate public-autograd evaluation on Ascend 950DT, including gradient conversions, yields 1.09-2.89$\times$ under available matched policies. Paired ablations establish further ReWY gains after optimizing the complementary contractions. Complete-gradient checks validate the recorded operator cases; supplementary full-model backward measurements assess integration into community FLA models and a GDN2 layer port. Code and reproduction materials: https://github.com/flashserve/ReWY.

title: Knowledge-Guided Floodwater Level Reasoning for Cloud-Edge Collaborative Monitoring
abstract: Frequent urban floodwater poses a serious threat to the safety and efficiency of intelligent transportation systems. Existing vision-based methods for floodwater level detection face two main limitations. First, the lack of explicit reasoning leads to poor detection performance and little interpretability. Second, these methods struggle to generalize to the complex and varied real-world road scenes seen from different viewpoints. To address this, we reformulate the task as an explicit visual reasoning problem and propose HydroReasoner, a floodwater level reasoning framework designed for cloud-edge collaboration. HydroReasoner builds on Qwen2.5-VL and is trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization. To address the scarcity of reasoning process annotations, we build a floodwater domain knowledge graph HydroKG and design a novel KG path reward. Through deterministic graph traversal over HydroKG, this reward supervises the model's reasoning process at a fine granularity, which improves both reasoning and generalization. For edge deployment, we apply 4-bit quantization to the model, cutting GPU memory usage by 57% and inference latency by 43% while out-of-domain accuracy drops by only 0.2 percentage points. We also propose a confidence-based cloud-edge routing mechanism, which improves system safety and eases the computational load on the cloud. In addition, we build HydroLevel, a floodwater benchmark dataset of 3,000 images, for training and evaluating the model. Experimental results show that HydroReasoner achieves detection accuracy 4.0 and 13.6 percentage points higher than conventional vision baselines in the in-domain and out-of-domain evaluations respectively, with performance dropping by only 4.4 percentage points out of domain.

title: Multimodal BVP and Respiration for Automated Pain Recognition with Hankel-FCN
abstract: Automated pain recognition is a fundamental challenge for the advancement of clinical care and empathetic human-computer interaction, due to the subjective and dynamic nature of pain. In this study, we propose a deep learning framework for objective pain assessment based on multimodal physiological signals from the AI4Pain dataset. The approach focuses on Blood Volume Pulse (BVP) and Respiration (RESP), capturing complementary aspects of autonomic responses to nociceptive stimulation. To explicitly model their temporal dynamics, the signals are transformed into structured trajectory representations using Hankel matrix embeddings, enabling the learning of dynamical patterns beyond conventional time-series representations. These embeddings are processed by modality-specific Fully Convolutional Networks, and their outputs are integrated through a late fusion strategy for three-class classification (No Pain, Low Pain, High Pain). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 67.09% and an F1-score of 66.41%, providing competitive performance compared to existing approaches, while relying on no handcrafted feature engineering. Multimodal fusion significantly outperformed either modality alone, and the Hankel embedding showed a trend towards further improvement. Further validation is required to establish generalisability to broader populations and clinical settings.

title: Large-Scale Bayesian Optimisation Using Uncertainty-Calibrated Product-of-Experts Gaussian Process Models with Trust Regions
abstract: The use of collections of independent local Gaussian processes (GP-ind) combined with trust regions is a widely adopted approach for large-scale and high-dimensional Bayesian optimisation (BO). However, this approach suffers from several limitations, including discontinuities at the boundaries of disjoint regions, an inability to capture long-range spatial correlations, potential information loss, and abrupt increases in computational overhead. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel BO algorithm, termed BO-pro-c-tr. The proposed method employs a product-of-experts Gaussian process model with uncertainty calibration (GP-pro-c) as its surrogate model and incorporates a one-to-many association strategy for integrating GP-pro-c with trust regions. Empirical results suggest that, when combined with the GP-LCB acquisition function, BO-pro-c-tr achieves an average reduction of 2.6% in simple regret and 34.9% in computational overhead relative to BO algorithms based on independent local GP models coupled with trust regions.

title: Reinforcement Learning in High-Energy Physics: A Survey from Accelerator Control to Theory Exploration
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a machine learning paradigm in which an agent learns a decision-making policy by interacting with an environment, guided by a scalar reward rather than explicit supervision. Supervised and unsupervised learning have become indispensable tools in high-energy physics (HEP), but they learn from fixed datasets, whereas many HEP tasks are closed-loop decisions: the data an algorithm observes depend on its choices, the feedback is sparse or delayed, and the objective is often measured on a real machine or in a stochastic simulation, not by a differentiable model. This survey reviews the application of RL to such tasks: accelerator control and feedback, data quality monitoring, jet grooming, clustering, and representation, charged particle tracking, beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) and string model building, detector design, trigger control, analysis, and formal quantum field theory computation. It provides a self-contained introduction to the underlying RL methods, from model-free and model-based to multi-agent, offline, inverse, and bandit approaches, reviews each domain against its traditional methods, and summarizes the head-to-head comparisons. The applications range from policies deployed on real accelerators and evaluated on recorded collision data to exploratory studies in formal theory. RL is most advantageous for repeated tasks with a fast simulator, decisions inside fast control loops, operation under faults and corrupted measurements, physics-based rewards in place of labels, and sequential discrete constructions with a reusable policy, while Bayesian optimization, genetic algorithms, and differentiable methods remain competitive elsewhere. We conclude with the open challenges that recur across domains, including reward design, sim-to-real transfer, safety, the lack of shared benchmarks, and the statistical validity of policy-driven decisions.

title: Looking Forward to Constructing Better Causal Comparisons
abstract: Constructing credible comparison groups is a central challenge in observational causal inference. Conventional approaches assess comparability through observed characteristics or pre-treatment outcome trajectories, although causal identification depends on unobserved untreated potential outcomes after treatment. We propose a forward-looking framework that selects or weights controls using prognostic scores: predictions, based on pre-treatment information, of the outcomes units would experience without treatment. These scores target either untreated outcome levels or changes, depending on the comparability condition underlying the causal design. They can be estimated using post-treatment outcomes observed for untreated units or exclusively from historical data. To construct these scores, we leverage tabular foundation models, whose extensive pretraining enables them to capture complex relationships among predictors and effectively extract their predictive information, even when application-specific samples are limited. Crucially, predictions guide comparison-group construction, whereas observed outcomes determine treatment effect estimates. We derive an exact decomposition of estimation error into prognostic-score imbalance and differences in forecast errors, clarifying why neither predictive accuracy nor score balance alone guarantees causal identification. The National Supported Work application reveals that stronger pre-treatment covariate balance does not necessarily yield estimates closer to experimental benchmarks, highlighting the practical relevance of prognostic-score comparisons.

title: The Vibe Paradox: What EEG Reveals About Your Brain When Vibe Coding
abstract: Background: Much of the enthusiasm for vibe coding rests on two intuitive beliefs: (1) that developers stay invested even when they no longer write the code, and (2) that delegating more of the work to AI lowers their cognitive load. Objective: Our goal was to investigate whether developers' neurophysiological states and interactions with AI are consistent with these beliefs when they work with agentic vs. non-agentic AI on their own project vs. a legacy codebase. Method: We conducted an exploratory within-subjects crossover study with 11 participants across 22 sessions. Each participant used GitHub Copilot Chat in one session and Cursor Agents in the other, working on their own project and a legacy codebase, with tool-codebase pairings randomly assigned and session order counterbalanced. We recorded participants' EEG, on-screen activity, and prompts, and analyzed 7,924 EEG data points, 984 activities, and 141 prompts. Results: Our findings contradict both beliefs. With the agent, participants remained indifferent to task outcomes, even on their own projects, and cognitive load was higher than with non-agentic AI. Furthermore, their ways of interacting shifted: with non-agentic AI, participants asked how the code worked and read it to verify changes; with the agent, they described desired app behavior and checked results in the running app. Conclusion: Our study reveals a vibe paradox: delegating to an agent left participants motivationally disinterested, even on their own projects, without relieving cognitive load, while coinciding with increased trust in AI. The community should treat this paradox as a first-class concern if developers and their AI agents are to go far together, and not just fast.

title: EarthJev: Calibrated, Non-Generative Answers to Natural-Language Questions about Sentinel-2 Land Cover
abstract: Vision-language models for remote sensing answer questions about satellite images by generating text: every answer costs a decoding loop, has to be parsed back to an option, and comes without a usable probability. We present EarthJev, a 0.8B-parameter model that answers typed questions about multispectral Sentinel-2 patches without generating any token. All 12 bands enter the vision encoder of Qwen3.5-0.8B through a widened input layer initialised from the RGB kernels, and, following the open OneJev recipe, the answer is read from the logits of the option letters at a single position and trained with cross-entropy plus Brier score. Under a pre-specified analysis plan, we compare it with the same backbone fine-tuned to generate the answer and with three multimodal language models fine-tuned with LoRA, all trained on the same 70,890 questions from 5% of BigEarthNet v2.0 and timed in one job on the same GPU; VQA models that classify over a fixed answer vocabulary are reported as a reference for the cost of answering only the questions seen in training. EarthJev answers a question in 19.9 ms, 4.3 to 8.7 times faster than the multimodal language models and 6.8 times faster than its own backbone used generatively; when all the questions about an image are asked together, it answers them in 42.8 ms, 3.7 to 10.1 times faster than the batched generative models. On 36,028 test questions it reaches 86.0% accuracy (three seeds), 0.6 and 1.2 points below the two 2B multimodal models and 3.5 points below the remote-sensing EarthDial-4B, with answers that are valid by construction and calibrated probabilities (ECE 0.006). Replacing the nine non-RGB bands with their mean costs 4.5 points, so the model uses the multispectral input, and in an ablation training the whole vision encoder raises accuracy to 88.4% at the same cost. Code and model: https://github.com/CosmoIknosLab/EarthJev

title: The Neural Density Model: An Open 3D Thermospheric Density Reanalysis for 2003--2026 From Tracked Space Debris
abstract: Thermospheric mass density controls satellite drag but is observed directly by few missions, and the leading operational product (HASDM) relies on non-public radar data. We present the Neural Density Model (NDM), a 3D density reanalysis for October 2003--October 2026 at 250--800~km. Previous approaches either convert the orbital decay of tracked objects into point densities or correct empirical models with a few global scale factors. NDM instead fits a spatially resolved neural correction to NRLMSISE-00 directly to the observed decay of 600--800 objects per year, through a differentiable drag operator, jointly with their ballistic coefficients, calibration spheres and accelerometer densities. On withheld satellites the median error is 0.078 (natural-log units), against 0.101 for HASDM and 0.310 for NRLMSISE-00; NDM has the smaller bias, HASDM slightly smaller scatter. On Spire GNSS orbits, never used in training, NDM and HASDM perform comparably. NDM uses only public observations.

title: ZT-DAC: ML-Driven Dynamic Access Control Policy for Zero Trust in DER Networks
abstract: The increasing penetration of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) in the smart grid has significantly expanded the cyber-attack surface. Traditionally, DER networks rely on static role-based access control (RBAC) mechanisms that assume persistent trust after authentication. This limitation enables adversaries to maintain unauthorized privileges and move laterally across DER systems, disrupting grid operations. Although attribute-based access control (ABAC) enables fine-grained and context-aware access decisions, it does not fully eliminate implicit trust. Zero Trust (ZT) principles can be incorporated to enhance ABAC policies. This paper proposes a dynamic access control framework for implementing ZT in DER networks (ZT-DAC). The proposed solution employs a two-stage verification process and integrates an Open Policy Agent (OPA)-based RBAC with a machine learning (ML)-based ABAC to enforce continuous and adaptive trust score assessment. To support realistic DER operations, a DER-specific access control model is developed and used to generate a domain-informed dataset of access requests incorporating both legitimate and adversarial behaviors. Experimental results on the dataset show that the OPA-based decision layer achieves \(91.92\%\) accuracy, with a False Positive Rate of \(14.45\%\), while the ML model achieves a Mean Absolute Error of \(2.074\) and an \(R^2\) of \(0.891\) in trust-score prediction. The ABAC layer achieves \(93.27\%\) accuracy, with a FPR of \(3.88\%\), validating its practical feasibility within realistic DER environments.

title: Rewarded for Not Getting Caught: Why Alignment Training Selects for Conditional Compliance and Cannot Instill Norms
abstract: Current alignment training cannot be expected to deliver what it is meant to deliver: AI agents that comply with norms whatever the gains and whether or not anyone is watching. Training that rewards and penalizes behavior can teach norms only through that reward, and a reward can encode a norm only as a price: "do not do X" becomes "doing X costs something", and training charges the cost only when X is noticed. A price, unlike a norm, can be paid: a large enough gain outweighs it, noticed or not. And because the cost is charged only where violations are noticed, training cannot favor a policy that always complies over one that complies only where it would be caught. When an unnoticed violation is the only way to complete a task, it even favors the latter, the more so the more strongly it rewards task success. Agency makes this the normal case: agents mostly act without oversight, can often tell when they are observed, and may take steps to evade observation. That agents behave as intended when they infer they are being tested, and differently when they infer they are not, is therefore no malfunction; the training regime is working as built. This reading unifies alignment faking, sandbagging, and evaluation-aware scheming. No behavioral evaluation can show that a model does better, since that would require observing how it behaves unobserved; a model that complies when it seems unobserved may simply have recognized the test. Easing the pressure on agents to complete tasks at any cost can make violations rarer, but never impossible. For norms that no gain should be allowed to outweigh, the remedy is not deeper internalization but architecture that makes violations unavailable rather than unchosen. We state this argument explicitly, premise by premise, read recent findings and a real-world incident against it, and draw consequences for design and governance.

title: Black-Box Adversarial Example Attacks on Machine Learning based Election Systems
abstract: Machine learning models have shown exceptional accuracy for ballot classification in election systems. Recent research has demonstrated that these ballot classification models are vulnerable to adversarial example attacks. This is a critical security issue because a successful attack could alter the outcome of an election and undermine the democratic process. However, all adversarial example attacks in the voting domain have assumed a white-box threat model, where the classifier parameters are known. In this work, we advance the field of machine learning in election systems by analyzing a realistic black-box adversary. We implement and evaluate eleven state-of-the-art black-box attacks: query based attacks ADBA, Square, SurFree, RayS, and SA-MOO. We also test adaptive transfer based black-box attacks with APGD-$l_\infty$, APGD-$l_2$, APGD-$l_1$, PGD $l_0$, PGD $l_0$+$l_\infty$, and PGD $l_0$+$σ$. Our attacks span multiple different norms ($l_\infty$, $l_2$, $l_1$, and $l_0$) and three different black-box adversarial threat models (decision based, score based and transfer based). In addition to digital analyses, we physically print and scan $20,000$ adversarial examples to evaluate the real-world performance of different black-box attacks. Our finding demonstrate an even larger physical-digital robustness gap exists for black-box adversarial examples than for white-box adversarial examples. Lastly, we conduct the first ever adversarial example transferability study in the voting domain and test adversarial training and barrier zones as two possible black-box defense strategies.

title: Forecasting Earth Surface Change in Embedding Space
abstract: Repeated satellite imagery permits understanding of how our planet changes over time, letting us predict its future and plan mitigating actions. Most existing studies that rely on a time series of satellite observations forecast the spectral values at each pixel for a future target date. However, clouds, shadows, and sensor noise often corrupt these observations, so that spectral forecasters waste much of their capacity on low-level features or noise rather than real change. With the advent of Earth foundation models, we argue that forecasting in embedding space is a feasible and more effective alternative. To this end, we design a token space that handles irregular histories from different sensors and foundation models and supports forecasts at any query date. Tokens from this space are inputs to our proposed forecaster, E$^2$Forecast, which is a transformer with two branches: a Gaussian branch that directly predicts a mean point forecast and per-dimension standard deviations, and a rectified-flow branch that generates forecast ensembles. On Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 benchmarks, forecasting embeddings instead of spectral values halves the cosine distance (from 0.20 to 0.10) and greatly reduces overconfidence, lowering the z-score standard deviation from 2.63 to 1.22. By comparing new observations with its forecasts, E$^2$Forecast can also detect anomalous changes without labels or retraining, raising F$_1$ from 41.58 to 48.70 on a global benchmark. This consistent superiority is validated on nine remote sensing foundation models. Beyond change detection, we believe our approach advances the field by permitting effective reuse of diverse pretrained task heads. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/ucam-eo/e2forecast.

title: Metamorphic Testing for Evaluating Robustness of Sentiment Analysis Models
abstract: Machine learning systems are challenging to test using traditional software testing methods because their behavior is learned from data rather than explicitly programmed. This challenge is particularly significant in natural language processing (NLP), where small input variations can lead to unexpected model behavior. Conventional evaluation metrics, such as accuracy and F1-score, often fail to capture such inconsistencies. Metamorphic testing addresses this limitation by evaluating expected relationships between original and transformed inputs. With the increasing prevalence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and language-based AI systems, the need for systematic robustness testing has become even more pronounced. Motivated by this growing need, this paper presents a lightweight, batch-based metamorphic testing approach for evaluating the robustness of such systems. In particular, we consider sentiment analysis as a representative NLP task and evaluate a pretrained classifier under four transformations: synonym replacement, typo injection, word-order variation, and negation. Using consistency score, flip accuracy, and confidence change, we identify strengths in handling semantic variations and vulnerabilities to textual noise and logical transformations. These findings highlight the value of metamorphic testing in identifying behavioral inconsistencies beyond conventional performance metrics and demonstrate its potential as a systematic framework for evaluating the robustness of language-based AI systems and guiding performance improvements before deployment.

title: Can LLMs Reliably Evaluate Themselves? A Probabilistic VC Framework
abstract: As large language models (LLMs) find increasing use in critical applications, evaluating their ability to assess their own outputs has become crucial. We present a theoretical and empirical framework that examines whether LLMs can differentiate between correct and incorrect solutions while maintaining properly calibrated confidence. Building on classical Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC) theory, we adapt it to probabilistic predictors through two complexity metrics: Probabilistic VC (PVC), which measures a model's ability to confidently classify across problem types, and Calibration-aware PVC (C-PVC), which additionally demands alignment between confidence scores and actual success rates. Unlike Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Actual Error (AE), these measures give an integrated assessment of self-evaluation expressiveness and calibration, with sample complexity bounds and generalization guarantees comparable to classical VC theory. We test eleven 7-8B models on 360 original mathematical reasoning problems, TruthfulQA, and CommonsenseQA. Each model chooses between two of its own generated solutions and reports its confidence, with ground truth determined by an ensemble of larger models. The results show a systematic inverse relationship: models with greater self-evaluation expressiveness have weaker calibration. s1.1-7B and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct achieve the highest PVC-VUS scores, while JiuZhang3.0-7B is best calibrated, with the lowest ECE and the smallest PVC-VUS gap. The trade-off persists across architectures, training paradigms, and domains, pointing to a fundamental challenge in developing self-reflective LLMs, and our framework offers practical tools for diagnosing it.

title: Data-Scarce, Multi-Granular, Multimodal: Benchmark Design for Biosynthetic Gene Clusters
abstract: Biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) are co-located genes that encode the biosynthesis of specialized metabolites, an important source of antibiotics, anticancer agents, immunosuppressants, and agricultural bioactives. Deep learning, particularly self-supervised foundation models, has spurred interest in BGC sequence modeling, but evaluation has lagged behind: existing benchmarks often rely on coarse classification over small curated datasets, providing limited discrimination among models and insight into downstream utility. We propose a benchmark-design framework in which an informative benchmark should be discriminative, separating models with statistical confidence, and applicable, spanning scientifically meaningful tasks under different levels of generalization. We instantiate this framework as BGC-Bench, which derives five tasks from MIBiG, ranging from A-domain substrate prediction to BGC-molecule retrieval, evaluates them under genotype- and phenotype-shift splits, includes an active-learning setting for label-scarce discovery, and is easily extensible to new tasks and encoders. BGCs further provide a shared testbed across granularities and modalities: BGC-Bench compares twelve encoders on nucleotide, amino-acid, or Pfam-domain sequences, including compositional baselines for each input type, and combines BGC and chemical encoders for cross-modal retrieval. No single representation dominates: the best granularity depends on the biological scale of the task, and pretrained encoders do not consistently outperform other representations across tasks and splits. Active-learning experiments show that most tasks remain data-limited, encoder rankings change with labeling budget, and acquisition strategies yield modest gains. These results show that BGC model evaluation requires task-diverse, shift-aware benchmarks, and the framework can be generalized to benchmark design beyond BGCs.

title: SVD-Prune: Spectral Vision Token Pruning under Extreme Compression
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models process hundreds of visual tokens, making visual representations a major computational bottleneck. We argue that visual token pruning should be formulated not as identifying individually important tokens, but as preserving the dominant low-rank spectral structure of the visual representation. Based on this formulation, we introduce SVD-Prune, a training-free framework that leverages Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and statistical leverage scores for globally informed token selection. SVD-Prune is architecture-agnostic and can be applied at different stages of the multimodal pipeline, including encoder-side, decoder-side, and hybrid configurations Extensive experiments across VLM and VLA benchmarks demonstrate strong robustness under extreme compression. SVD-Prune reduces the visual token. SVD-Prune cuts the visual token budget by up to 99.3%, while, at a 16-token budget, encoder-side pruning lowers inference FLOPs by 82.4% and achieves a 4.18x end-to-end speedup, including pruning overhead.

title: Toward Agentic AI-Ready Workflows in Built Environment Organizations: Knowledge Structures and Interoperability Challenges
abstract: The rise of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) in the built environment is shifting attention from isolated AI tools toward autonomous systems that reason, plan, and act across project and organizational workflows. The effectiveness of such systems depends not only on large language model capabilities, but also on the readiness of heterogeneous data environments across the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) sector. These environments combine structured sources, such as CAD and BIM models, schedules, cost databases, and asset registers, with unstructured ones, including technical reports, design narratives, planning and policy documents, contracts, meeting minutes, and risk registers. This paper reviews how built environment data can be organized to support agentic AI-ready workflows, focusing on knowledge structures, interoperability, and access and integration mechanisms such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Drawing on existing literature, it examines approaches proposed to organize structured and unstructured data and considers how such data can be contextualized and made accessible to AI agents in a reliable manner. The paper synthesizes current perspectives, highlights challenges around fragmentation and interoperability, and identifies open questions for future research on AI-compatible information management in the built environment.

title: HyVox: Rethinking Low-Power Voice Intelligence towards Neuromorphic-von Neumann Edge Computing
abstract: We present HyVox, a hybrid neuromorphic--von Neumann system for low-energy open-set speaker identification under tight energy budgets. HyVox splits the workload at the speaker embedding. A neuromorphic processor embeds the speech with sparse, event-driven computation, and a von Neumann microcontroller holds the speaker gallery and makes every decision: it scores queries by cosine similarity, rejects unknown speakers, and enrolls new users by writing a prototype, with no weight update. On the neuromorphic processor, a hierarchical temporal abstraction (HTA) SNN backbone learns a synaptic time constant per leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron, allocating 832 neurons across fast, medium, and slow timescales. A 32-neuron spiking embedding extractor (SEE), pretrained on episodes that each enroll new speakers and reject outsiders, turns the backbone output into an embedding for speakers unseen in training; its 32 spike counts are the only interface between the two processors. To fit the chip's synapse and integer budgets, we compress the backbone 6.5x to 29.0k synapses, train it for integer bit-shift dynamics, and fine-tune it with chip-accurate spiking training (CAST). CAST trains through a differentiable replica of the chip's integer neuron update, derived from its cycle-accurate simulator, so that gradient descent optimizes the exact weights and thresholds the chip runs; it doubles the top-1 accuracy of the mapped backbone on unseen speakers. On 20 Common Voice households of unseen speakers, HyVox reaches 99.6\% top-1 and 5.5\% rejection EER with 2 members and 94.9\% and 13.2\% with 20, and the network deployed on the neuromorphic chip matches its trained model. Each inference on a 3-s window takes 0.96 s and 1.63 mJ of dynamic energy, 42\% lower latency than the fastest embedded ANN baseline and 13.5x less dynamic and 5.8x less total energy than the most energy-efficient one.

title: HCT-Mammo: A Compact Hybrid CNN-Transformer for Benign–Malignant Mammogram Classification with Uncertainty and Cross-Dataset Evaluation
abstract: The difficulty in comparing public-dataset results for benign–malignant mammogram classification is due to patient overlap, lesion crops, and a lack of independent testing. This study uses 896×448 breast-cropped mammograms, and the evaluated model is a hybrid convolutional neural network (CNN)–Transformer (HCT-Mammo) with a truncated ResNet-18 stem, a 4-layer Transformer encoder, and 4.91 M parameters. Patient-level separation, training, and model selection were done on the Curated Breast Imaging Subset of DDSM (CBIS-DDSM), and the models were frozen for zero-shot evaluation on the Chinese Mammography Database (CMMD). Sigmoid Confidence, Temperature Scaling and Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout were evaluated with calibration and risk–coverage analyses, and Grad-CAM and Attention Rollout were compared to lesion masks and chance baselines. The mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of HCT-Mammo was 0.780 ± 0.005 across three seeds, with a median-seed AUROC of 0.781 (95% confidence interval 0.742–0.821). HCT-Mammo did not differ significantly from EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet-50 (DeLong p = 0.59 and p = 0.33), whereas ViT-S/16 was poorer (p = 0.002). On CMMD, AUROC decreased to 0.664, and the expected calibration error after temperature scaling increased from 0.059 to 0.121. MC-Dropout offered no obvious improvement in calibration or error ranking, internally or externally. The mass localisation hit rate for Grad-CAM was 35.5%, compared with 24.4% for Attention Rollout and 4.7% for a breast-uniform baseline. The compact hybrid was competitive in-domain, but its discrimination and calibration were worse across datasets. Both datasets contain only abnormal examinations; therefore, the results reflect lesion characterization rather than screening.
journal: American Journal of Smart Technology and Solutions

title: Hybrid AI–Quantum Architecture for Sustainable Plant Disease Detection and Pesticide Recommendation
abstract: Plant diseases, pest attacks, and nutrient imbalances significantly affect agricultural productivity and can reduce both yield and quality. Timely and accurate identification of these issues is essential for effective crop management and sustainable farming. Conventional manual inspection methods are often inefficient and inconsistent, while existing deep learning approaches may struggle to differentiate between diseases with similar visual characteristics, leading to inaccurate predictions and suboptimal treatment choices. To overcome these limitations, this work introduces a hybrid classical–quantum framework aimed at improving disease detection and decision-making. The proposed system uses EfficientNet-B0 to learn rich visual representations from plant images, then processes them with a variational quantum circuit to capture complex, nonlinear feature interactions. By integrating classical and quantum techniques, the model enhances classification performance beyond traditional methods. Beyond accurate disease identification, the system provides environmentally conscious pesticide recommendations, supporting responsible chemical use. Overall, this approach serves as an effective intelligent decision-support system, contributing to more precise and sustainable agricultural practices.
journal: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology

title: Calibrated Quantile Transformers for Cost-Aware Inventory Control in Simulated Multi-Echelon Supply Networks
abstract: Accurate demand quantiles do not automatically yield low-cost network inventory decisions. We evaluate a series-aware quantile Transformer linked to a rolling residual correction that shrinks item-specific errors toward pooled calibration residuals. The corrected 0.90 demand quantile drives retailer order-up-to decisions under shared distribution-center supply, with explicit replenishment lead times. To distinguish the value of calibration from forecasting architecture, a LightGBM quantile model and fixed-buffer controls are subjected to the same simulation. 10 independently generated synthetic networks each contain 48 product-store demand series over 176 weeks, and all policies use the same chronological 31-week holdout. Across the networks, the calibrated Transformer lowers average simulated cost by 13.1% relative to static stock and 3.6% relative to its uncalibrated quantiles. The network-paired mean incremental cost reduction is 3.54% with a 95% bootstrap interval [2.33%, 4.78%]. The study isolates decision postprocessing in a controlled simulation rather than making a real-retailer deployment claim.
journal: Academic Journal of Management Science and Engineering

title: Innovative Operation Ideas of Guangxi Agricultural Assistance Platform from a Demand-Side Orientation: A Case Study of "Mang Xiaozhong"
abstract: In recent years, with the deep penetration of the digital economy into rural areas and the rapid development of agricultural e-commerce in Guangxi, the demand-side oriented agricultural assistance model has emerged as an innovative form of agricultural product circulation. In response to problems in the upward distribution of characteristic agricultural products in Guangxi—including disconnection between production and marketing, high loss in circulation links, difficulties in brand transformation, and seasonal capital shortage at the production end—the "Mang Xiaozhong" platform constructs four interconnected operation strategies: customized pre-sale, two-way exchange among production areas, rule-based trust design, and consumer-side pre-purchase crowdfunding. These strategies adapt to the industrial reality of decentralized smallholder production and staggered listing of multiple categories in Guangxi. The research shows that the demand-side oriented, asset-light third-party service model can address the practical bottlenecks of county-level agricultural assistance e-commerce in Guangxi, and has reference value for the construction of similar platforms.

title: Differentiable Spin-Center Diffusion Model Enables DEER-Guided Generative Pipeline of Weighted Protein Ensembles
abstract: Biological function entails the interconversion of a protein between distinct conformations, an equilibrium modulated by ligands and other physicochemical conditions. Double electron-electron resonance (DEER) spectroscopy captures these ensembles as distance distributions, P(r), between spin label pairs. However, the width of P(r) convolves protein conformational heterogeneity with the rotameric flexibility of the label. Because current spin label models overestimate this contribution, translating P(r) into ensembles has remained indirect and predominantly qualitative. Here, we developed spin-center (SC) diffusion, a differentiable model of the spin label with a tunable spin label rotameric width. Coupled to a frozen Boltz-2 structure generator, SC diffusion enables the entire experimental P(r) to guide ensemble generation at inference time. We demonstrate the robustness of this pipeline on synthetic P(r) of known composition, recovering the ensemble populations, including both components of a bimodal profile. Guided by experimental P(r) measured under different biochemical conditions, ensembles of the transporters PfMATE, LmrP, MhsT and P-glycoprotein were modeled and free energy differences derived from the ensembles in a condition-dependent manner. By embedding a differentiable label model in structure generation, our approach interprets DEER distributions as weighted conformational ensembles, adding a missing thermodynamic grounding to generative protein structure prediction methods.

title: An Artificial Intelligence-Driven Predictive Framework for Residential Energy Demand Forecasting in Smart Urban Environments
abstract: Reliable short-term electricity demand forecasting is a critical requirement for the operational efficiency and sustainability of smart city energy infrastructure. Insufficient forecast precision leads to either excess generation capacity, causing fuel wastage and elevated carbon emissions, or supply shortfalls that threaten grid stability. This paper presents a systematic comparison of five forecasting approaches applied to residential electricity demand prediction: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit, Convolutional Neural Network combined with LSTM, Prophet, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Experiments were conducted on the UCI (University of California, Irvine) Individual Household Electric Power Consumption dataset, which contains minute-resolution measurements of electricity usage across eight electrical attributes spanning approximately four years. A chronological 80/20 train-test split was applied throughout to ensure that model evaluation reflected performance on genuinely unseen future data. XGBoost achieved the highest predictive accuracy among the five models, attaining a root mean squared error of 0.024 kWh and a normalised root mean squared error of 2.37%, with substantially lower computational cost than the neural network approaches. Prophet captured seasonal demand patterns effectively and yielded interpretable forecast components suitable for integration with real-time urban energy monitoring systems. Among the deep learning models, Convolutional Neural Network-LSTM outperformed both standalone recurrent architectures, confirming the advantage of combining local feature extraction with sequential modelling. The results demonstrate that gradient-boosted tree ensembles, when combined with well-designed feature engineering, constitute a computationally efficient and highly accurate alternative to deep sequence models for short-term residential energy forecasting and are well-suited to deployment within smart city energy management systems.

title: The Discovery Gap: Why Artificial Intelligence Must Learn to Change Its Mind "Rethinking Human–AI Collaboration from Molecule to Market"
abstract: Scientific discovery requires the revision of belief: giving up a claim when the evidence turns against it, and knowing what else must change with it. Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed research - predicting protein structures, generating molecules, screening billions of candidates - but it does not do this. Autonomous agents traverse the discovery loop end to end without holding the beliefs that loop exists to revise. I use dynamic scientific intelligence for the class of system this requires, one that holds hypotheses as persistent objects with provenance, uncertainty and explicit dependencies. Its distinguishing condition is that a system can identify what supports each commitment and what depends on it, and so revise one without disturbing the rest. Because no architecture can revise beliefs on evidence it never receives, the problem is jointly architectural and infrastructural. Using drug development from molecule to market as the test case, I identify where evidence generated downstream should revise commitments made upstream and does not, and three decision points at which the non-delegable human act is adjudication rather than generation. I propose a revision test - an evaluation distinct in kind from any predictive benchmark - and a minimum reporting standard for claims of AI-assisted discovery. Until AI learns to change its mind well, it will remain a tool rather than an infrastructure in which discovery accumulates.

title: RUNX1-Mediated Hypoxic Signaling Impairs Myogenesis and Promotes Fibrosis in Myopathies.
abstract: Compromised myogenic repair with enhanced fibrosis is common in myopathies, including Wooden Breast (WB) myopathy in broilers, but the underlying mechanism of their co-occurrence remains elusive. Using WB myopathy as a model, we investigated the common pathological origins of these co-occurring features. Our single-nucleus RNA sequencing results showed enhanced oxidative stress and profibrotic remodeling of myofibers, increased proliferation but decreased differentiation of satellite cells (SCs), and aggravated differentiation of fibroblasts (FBs) in WB samples. Differential gene expression and pseudotime trajectory analysis further identified RUNX1 as a key regulator for both SCs and FBs, which was further supported by gene functional studies in respective cell culture models. Moreover, reduced blood flow and oxygen supply may indicate a hypoxic state in WB muscle, which was associated with enhanced RUNX1 expression. Consistently, coordinately enhanced HIF1A and RUNX1 expressions were found in differentiated FBs of human muscles and in muscles with diseases. Collectively, our study found that hypoxia-associated upregulation of RUNX1 disrupted the myogenic progression of SCs and exacerbated fibrotic differentiation of FBs, contributing to pathological degeneration in myopathies. Targeting RUNX1 may therefore represent a potential therapeutic strategy for prevention and treatment, which warrants future in vivo investigations.

title: RTMB: An R Package for Fitting Latent Variable Models With Template Model Builder.
abstract: Hierarchical and latent variable models are fundamental in ecology, fisheries science, and epidemiology, but fitting them efficiently relies on automatic differentiation (AD) combined with approximations such as the Laplace approximation. Template Model Builder (TMB) has become a standard tool for this kind of inference in R, but it requires users to write the objective function in C++, which is a potential obstacle for those unfamiliar with it, slows model iteration through compilation, and complicates debugging and simulation. We present RTMB, an R package that exposes the full power of TMB's AD machinery directly from plain R. Users write the joint negative log-likelihood as an ordinary R function; RTMB traces it onto an AD tape and hands the result to TMB's existing optimization, Laplace approximation, and reporting routines. We describe the design of the package, illustrate its use through a worked example, and provide a side-by-side comparison with the equivalent TMB implementation of a theta-logistic state-space population model. The result is a transparent, debuggable, and pedagogically accessible interface to state-of-the-art latent variable inference, with runtime performance comparable to native TMB.

title: Determinants of Crop Diversification in Boro Rice-Based, Wetland Farming Systems in Bangladesh.
abstract: The haor landscape of Bangladesh is highly reliant on Boro rice cultivation, making farm households vulnerable to recurring floods and climate-related risks. Crop diversification can intensify agricultural resilience and reduce production risks. This study examined the pattern, extent, and determinants of crop diversification using a cross-sectional field survey performed in 2023 among 240 farm households in three purposively selected upazilas (Itna, Mithamoin, and Nikli) of Kishoreganj district. The Simpson Diversification Index (SDI), based on crop-area shares, was used to measure crop diversification, while Censored Tobit and Ordered Probit models were employed to identify its determinants. The results showed that farmers were gradually familiarizing themselves with crops such as maize, mustard, jute, chili, sweet potato, groundnut, potato, pumpkin, black gram, and various vegetables, along with Boro rice. The mean SDI was 0.22, with 58.33% of households falling within the poor diversification category (0-0.24). The Tobit model indicated that household head education, farm size, agricultural training, marketing training, and extension contact positively associated with crop diversification. In contrast, road distance, duration of waterlogging, and agro-ecological location had negative effects. The Ordered Probit results generally confirmed these associations and also revealed a positive relationship between the dependency ratio and the higher category of crop diversification. Marginal effects indicated that agricultural training, marketing training, and extension contact increased the probability of achieving excellent diversification by 6.2, 5.5, and 4.8 percentage points, respectively, while each additional kilometer from a nearby road and each additional month of waterlogging reduced this probability by 5.4 and 3.1 percentage points, respectively. These findings emphasize the importance of improving farmer training, extension services, rural infrastructure, and location-specific waterlogging control to increase crop diversification and resilience in haor farming systems. Given the purposive selection of three upazilas in Kishoreganj district, the findings should be interpreted with caution in other haor regions.

title: Impact of Salinity on Rice Production in Vulnerable Southern Coastal Regions of Bangladesh: A Case Study Through a Cobb-Douglas Stochastic Production Function Model.
abstract: Salinity in coastal areas has a significant effect on the technical efficiency (maximum potential yield utilizing available inputs) of rice production and subsequently reduces food security in developing countries. We examined the salinity status and its impact on overall rice production across seasonal cycles in the southern coastal region of Bangladesh, utilizing data from 464 farmers from vulnerable coastal areas. The estimation from the Cobb-Douglas stochastic production function revealed that salinity has a statistically negative relationship with rice yield. Our study revealed that technical efficiency increased when farmers adopted salt-tolerant rice varieties and special techniques to manage salinity problems. Consequently, the profit per hectare was greater in the low-salinity zone than in the moderate- and high-salinity zones. We also find from binary logistic regression that with a greater possibility of yield loss, rice quality destruction, and salt land, farmers were more likely to migrate from cultivated rice to other crops because of salinity problems. In contrast, higher income, more consultations with extension officers and other farmers, and training knowledge, the likelihood of migrating from rice cultivation is lower. To mitigate salinity problems and ensure a sustainable future, salt-tolerant hybrid rice varieties need to be developed by research institutes, and frequent consultation and training need to be arranged by extension departments in Bangladesh.

title: Modular Biofabrication of Functional Skeletal Muscle Incorporated with Endothelialized Microvascular Seed-Derived Lumenized Microvessels.
abstract: The clinical translation of engineered skeletal muscle (eSM) for volumetric muscle regeneration is hindered by the challenge of establishing a functional vascular network capable of sustaining its high metabolic demand and ensuring graft survival. Here, we present a bottom-up biofabrication strategy to generate a pre-vascularized in vitro eSM model through the modular assembly of independently matured muscle and vascular compartments. C2C12 myoblasts were encapsulated within core-shell fibers using rotary wet-spinning (RoWS), yielding anisotropically aligned, multinucleated, and contractile myofibers expressing myosin heavy chain and sarcomeric α-actinin. In parallel, gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)-based microvascular seeds (µVS), pre-endothelialized with human umbilical vein endothelial cells, were engineered to guide rapid and structurally stable vascular formation while preventing uncontrolled capillary self-organization. Fully endothelialized µVS were incorporated into a pro-angiogenic bioink and processed via RoWS to generate tubular vascular fibers with physiological diameters (100-200 µm) and continuous CD31-positive lumens. After independent maturation, muscle and vascular constructs were bioassembled into a hierarchically organized tissue and co-cultured. By decoupling myogenic and angiogenic differentiation, this strategy overcomes medium incompatibility typical of conventional co-cultures, preserving compartment-specific architecture and function and establishing a versatile platform for muscle-vascular modeling and translational muscle repair.

title: RDAR biofilm formation and in silico analysis of putative amyloid proteins in Azospirillum baldaniorum Sp245
abstract: Azospirillum baldaniorum Sp245 is a plant growth-promoting rhizobacterium (PGPR) whose ability to benefit host crops depends on robust root colonization, a process driven by the transition from a planktonic state to a sessile, biofilm-associated lifestyle. This study investigated the capacity of A. baldaniorum Sp245 to form Red, Dry, and Rough (RDAR) morphotype biofilms. Through macroscopic evaluation and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM), we visualized the presence of exopolysaccharides, putative amyloid proteins, and extracellular DNA (eDNA) within the RDAR biofilm matrix using Calcofluor White (CFW), Thioflavin S (TS), and Propidium Iodide (PI) fluorescent probes, respectively. Furthermore, formic acid treatment of extracellular matrix proteins extracts suggests the presence of resistant, putative amyloid proteins. Because genomic screening revealed the absence of homologs of a canonical curli-dependent amyloid system, we performed a genome-wide in silico analysis to identify genes encoding alternative biofilm-associated proteins. Using the Staphylococcus aureus Biofilm-Associated Protein (Bap protein) as a reference, we identified 20 candidate proteins characterized by extensive domain reiteration and diverse architectures, including bacterial immunoglobulin (Ig-like) domains, VCBS repeats, SWM motifs, DUF4347, PKD domains, and RTX β-roll structures. Three-dimensional modeling indicates that these candidates possess elongated, filament-like conformations with repetitive β-strand motifs typical of amyloid-like assembly and calcium-dependent adhesion. These findings suggest that in the absence of traditional curli machinery, A. baldaniorum Sp245 could be using a diverse, domain-rich repertoire of alternative matrix proteins to facilitate cell surface interactions, coordinate structural stability, and establish the RDAR biofilm morphotype. Ultimately, this study establishes a foundation for understanding the role of amyloid proteins in Azospirillum biofilm matrix formation and offers new insights into the potential mechanisms of bacterial persistence and ecological fitness in the rhizosphere.

title: Precision maize crop height mapping using multispectral and LiDAR data from unmanned aerial system
abstract: Context Spatially explicit and accurate maize crop height maps are essential for supporting site-specific management in precision agriculture. Although low-cost unmanned aerial system (UAS)-based multispectral imagery offers a promising approach for maize crop height estimation, it’s accuracy under varying canopy conditions remains uncertain. Aims In this study, we used 3D point clouds to estimate maize crop height during sparse and dense canopy cover based on UAS-captured multispectral images and compare with light detection and ranging (LiDAR)-based estimates. Methods The 3D point clouds from multispectral images and LiDAR data were processed using a spatially localized grid (SLG) filtering approachto derive digital terrain model (DTM) and canopy surface model (CSM), which were then used to estimate maize crop height.Furthermore, two strategies were explored — (1) grid expansion, and (2) using ground reference derived during sparse canopy aspotential tools to mitigate issues during dense canopy cover for multispectral image-based estimations. Results Results showed that the crop height estimated from multispectral images during sparse canopy cover show comparable accuracy (r = 0.9, nRMSE = 32%) to LiDAR-based estimation (r = 0.81, nRMSE = 17%). The accuracy of multispectral-based estimation, however, significantly declined under dense canopy cover, where no meaningful correlation was observed (r = − 0.1, nRMSE = 61%). In contrast, LiDAR-based estimates show consistent level of accuracy under the same conditions (r = 0.78, nRMSE = 15%). When grid expansion strategy was implemented for multispectral-based estimation during the dense canopy cover, the nRMSE was observed to decrease up to 28%. Meanwhile, with the use of sparse canopy cover ground reference, the nRMSE decreased up to 17%, comparable to the LiDAR-based estimate. Conclusion Overall, these results demonstrate the potential of deriving crop heights cost-effectively using multispectral imaging from UAS. This approach offers a scalable and economically viable alternative to expensive LiDAR systems, enabling wider integration of crop height information into precision agriculture applications.

How Do Soil Properties and Canopy Status Influence Potato Traits while Continuously Monitoring Soil Moisture with Iot-Based Sensors?
abstract: Soil-related properties associated with potato yield and quality are implicitly linked to soil water storage (SWS) determined by soil texture (ST). This soil property also affects the potato canopy, which could be evaluated indirectly using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The objective of this study carried out in 2022 was to define explanatory soil- and canopy state-related properties (NDVI – Normalized Difference Vegetation Index), that determine with the highest extent potato ( Solanum tuberosum L.) traits: total yield (TY), dry matter (DM) content, and average tuber weight (ATW) over a rainfed production field located in central Poland (52°4′ 50.94" N, 21°10′ 6.73" E). Soil water storage was derived from continuously measured volumetric water content (VWC) using moisture sensors installed at three depths (10, 20, and 30 cm), which were connected via the Internet to exchange data (IoT-based sensors). Thus, the second objective of this study was to evaluate how temporal changes in SWS and the duration of periods when SWS falls below the level that limits plant growth affected TY in sampling areas characterized by different ST. Potatoes were grown under a suboptimal water supply during crucial stages for yield formation. More explanatory soil- and canopy state-related properties significantly, and to a greater extent, affected ATW and TY than DM content. SWS, determined between the stages of leaf development and canopy closure, played a more critical role in forming ATW and TY than soil chemical properties. NDVI derived from four out of five UAV images (58–100 days after planting – DAP) showed a very high correlation (r values of 0.79–0.90) with yield and ATW, and this canopy status indicator outperformed all soil-based variables. The model, based on sand and silt content, soil fertility in Cu and Zn, and NDVI measured at the time of fruit development, and soil water storage recorded between leaf development and canopy closure, showed the lowest RMSE of 5.85 t∙ha −1 and 7.98 g for TY and ATW prediction, respectively. A model based solely on NDVI evaluation between canopy closure and the end of flowering, and SWS determined simultaneously, was a strong alternative for forecasting TY (RMSE = 6.67 t∙ha −1 ) and ATW (RMSE = 9.23 g). In the sampling area with the highest TY, characterized by loamy sand ST, the deficit of SWS started at 46 DAP and lasted only for 12 days. In contrast, the sampling area with the lowest TY, with sandy ST, experienced SWS deficit from 34 DAP, and this period of plant-limited growth lasted for 34 days.

A multiagent framework for trustworthy AI financial advisory for displaced Ukrainians in Poland
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer opportunities for scalable financial guidance, but hallucinations, numerical errors, insufficient grounding, and unstable decisions limit their use in high-stakes financial settings. This study develops and evaluates a multiagent AI framework for retirement-oriented financial guidance using synthetic profiles modelled on displaced Ukrainians in Poland. The framework combines retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), structured profile generation, deterministic budget calculations, and an architecturally separate Evaluator Agent. The primary computational evaluation comprised 500 synthetic advisory cases. Additional experiments included a paired no-RAG ablation on 50 fixed profiles and a repeated-run stability analysis of 100 fixed profiles replayed five times. Under the predefined automated routing criteria, 327 cases were accepted, 170 required review, and 3 were flagged. After the deterministic budget overwrite, a separate deterministic arithmetic check found zero profile-to-answer mismatches. In the paired ablation, the mean final composite score was 8.40 with RAG and 7.08 without RAG. The difference was driven primarily by larger deterministic penalty deductions and grounding-gate failures without RAG, while the mean of the five LLM rubric dimensions did not improve with RAG. In repeated runs, only 14% of profiles retained identical routing across all five replays. The deterministic arithmetic pathway remained invariant, while generation, retrieval, model-based evaluation, and threshold-based routing varied across repeated execution. The framework is therefore interpreted as a controlled computational testbed and quality-assurance architecture rather than a validated autonomous financial advisor.

The Senescent Macrophage as a Central Hub in Skeletal Aging: Mechanisms, Niche Disruption, and Systemic Consequences.
abstract: Bone marrow macrophages (BMMs) coordinate skeletal remodelling, haematopoietic niche function, immune surveillance, and tissue repair. Whether a persistent senescent state in BMMs is a causal driver of skeletal ageing, however, remains unresolved. The central challenge is both definitional and causal: macrophages may be quiescent, terminally differentiated, chronically activated, tolerant, or metabolically dysfunctional, whereas commonly used senescence markers-including p16INK4a, p21CIP1, senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, and individual senescence-associated secretory phenotype factors-lack diagnostic specificity when used in isolation. In this critical Review, we distinguish evidence for senescence in anatomically defined BMMs from observations in aged marrow myeloid cells, broad myeloid perturbations, systemic senolysis, and mechanistic extrapolation from other tissues. We organize the evidence using a five-link causal chain connecting BMM identity and ontogeny, multidimensional validation of senescence, a defined macrophage-derived mediator, a response in an identified recipient cell, and phenotypic rescue after BMM-specific intervention. Current evidence supports age-associated macrophage-state changes that influence osteoblast support, bone repair, haematopoietic regulation, and inflammatory signalling. It does not yet establish that rigorously defined senescent resident BMMs are necessary or sufficient for age-related bone loss. Evidence for BMM-specific control of vascular dysfunction, haematopoietic bias, and distant-organ ageing is weaker still. The most defensible current model is therefore that senescent or persistently dysfunctional BMMs act as context-dependent amplifiers within an ageing marrow network rather than as universally established initiators. Resolving this question will require spatially resolved state validation, intersectional lineage targeting, temporally controlled necessity and sufficiency experiments, mediator-specific rescue, and validation in human bone marrow.

OC-STAMP deficiency limits MMT and ameliorates silicosis by inhibiting macrophage phenotype differentiation.
abstract: Silicosis is a progressive fibrotic lung disease characterized by myofibroblast accumulation and excessive extracellular matrix deposition, for which effective therapeutic interventions remain limited. Macrophage to myofibroblast transition (MMT) has emerged as a critical cellular source of myofibroblasts during silicosis, yet the molecular regulators governing this process are not fully understood. Osteoclast stimulatory transmembrane protein (OC-STAMP) is a multi-transmembrane protein originally identified in osteoclast differentiation, but its role in silicosis remains unexplored. In this study, we investigated the expression and functional involvement of OC-STAMP in silicosis using in vivo and in vitro models. We found that OC-STAMP was significantly upregulated in the lung tissues of silicotic mice and MH-S stimulated by SiO2, and was predominantly localized to macrophages. Macrophage-specific conditional knockout of Ocstamp (Ocstampflox/flox; Lyz2-cre) markedly suppressed M2 macrophage polarization and MMT, and attenuated the progress of silicosis. Mechanistically, Ocstamp knockdown attenuated JAK1/STAT6 signaling, whereas Ocstamp overexpression enhanced it, and pharmacological inhibition of JAK1 with Upadacitinib reversed OC-STAMP-induced MMT and signaling activation. Collectively, these findings identify OC-STAMP as a previously unrecognized regulator of MMT via JAK1/STAT6 signaling, highlighting OC-STAMP as a potential therapeutic target for silicosis and other fibrotic diseases.

Folate-decorated nanoparticles deliver bulleyaconitine A to inflammatory macrophages for rheumatoid arthritis therapy.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic autoimmune disease driven by synovial inflammatory cell infiltration and progressive joint erosion. Macrophages undergo a pathological shift toward an M1 pro-inflammatory phenotype, which plays a critical role in the progression of the disease. Modulation of M1 macrophages may be a promising therapeutic strategy. Herein, we developed folic acid-functionalized PLGA nanoparticles (FA-PLGA NPs) for targeted delivery of an anti-inflammatory natural compound, bulleyaconitine A (BLA), into M1 macrophages. The nanoparticles exhibited a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 151.91 ± 5.41 nm with a polydispersity index of 0.153 ± 0.016, a negative zeta potential (-13.50 ± 0.82 mV), a high encapsulation efficiency of 90.0%, and excellent colloidal stability. In vitro, FA-PLGA NPs were efficiently internalized by M1-polarized RAW264.7 macrophages via folate receptor-mediated endocytosis, and the uptake level was 7.79-fold higher than non-targeted NPs. Exposure to the NPs significantly reduced the population of CD86-positive M1 cells and decreased iNOS expression while increasing Arg-1 expression. Transcriptomic analysis revealed downregulation of pro-inflammatory and tissue-destructive pathways and upregulation of myeloid differentiation and immune regulation genes. In an adjuvant-induced arthritis rat model, FA-PLGA NPs treatment resulted in significant alleviation of paw swelling, joint destruction, and cartilage proteoglycan loss, as well as a decrease in the levels of serum IL-6 and TNF-α. Encouragingly, the nanoparticle formulation exhibited favorable in vivo safety, with no observable adverse effects on major organs. Collectively, FA‑PLGA NPs effectively modulated M1 macrophages and achieved potent anti‑arthritic efficacy with improved safety, demonstrating their potential as a nanotherapeutic for RA management.

Biotin-dependent metabolism controls germinal center fate and vaccine-induced antibody diversification.
abstract: Nutrient availability shapes antibody responses, yet its role in metabolic checkpoints governing germinal center (GC) B-cell differentiation remains incompletely defined. Using heterozygous (HZ) Slc5a6 M60K mice modeling human loss-of-function mutations in the multivitamin transporter SLC5A6, we found that deficient biotin imports impaired mitochondrial metabolism and restricted preGC-to-dark zone progression after vaccination. Single-cell transcriptomics and RNA velocity revealed disrupted GC trajectories, while B-cell receptor repertoire analysis showed impaired class-switch recombination, somatic hypermutation, and vaccine-induced clonal diversity. Spatial multiplexed imaging showed reduced GL7-high GC-associated B-cell regions. Flow cytometric analyses revealed reduced frequencies of RBD-specific B cells and RBD-specific GL7+CD95+ GC B cells in HZ mice, with higher frequencies after biotin supplementation. Pseudovirus assays demonstrated impaired neutralization of Wuhan-Hu-1 and Omicron BA.2. Dietary biotin supplementation restored GC-associated differentiation, antibody diversification, and vaccine-induced humoral responses. These findings identify biotin-dependent mitochondrial metabolism as an important checkpoint linking micronutrient availability to GC B-cell differentiation and vaccine responsiveness.
