title: The stimulative effect of Cordyceps sinensis functionalized selenium nanoparticles on bone development in growing mice: involvement of the gut microbiota-bone axis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Achieving optimal peak bone mass (PBM) during adolescence through adequate intake of trace element such as selenium is crucial for reducing osteoporosis risk in later life. We previously developed novel functionalized selenium nanoparticles (Cs4-SeNPs) utilizing polysaccharide-protein complex isolated from Cordyceps sinensis for prevention of osteoporosis. The gut microbiota, functioning as the "second gene pool", plays a crucial role in maintaining bone homeostasis. However, how Cs4-SeNPs regulate bone metabolism via the gut microbiota-bone axis remains unclear. OBJECTIVES To elucidate how the gut microbiota and microbial metabolites mediate the bone-promoting effect of Cs4-SeNPs. METHODS Growing mice model was used to assess the effect of Cs4-SeNPs on bone development. Metagenomics, metabolomics, and proteomics analyses were conducted to uncover the mechanism of action of Cs4-SeNPs. In vitro osteoblast and osteoclast models were employed to validate the effects of key gut microbial metabolites regulated by Cs4-SeNPs on osteogenesis and osteoclastogenesis. Pseudo-germ-free mice model treated with antibiotics was employed to determine the role of gut microbiota in bone-promoting effects of Cs4-SeNPs. RESULTS We found that Cs4-SeNPs significantly enhanced bone mass in growing mice, as evidenced by improved bone microarchitecture and increased expression of bone extracellular matrix-related markers. Notably, antibiotic treatment-induced microbial depletion abolished the effects of Cs4-SeNPs on bone development in growing mice. Increased abundance of beneficial gut bacterial genera, notably Adlercreutzia and Parvibacter, were observed following Cs4-SeNPs administration. Proteomics analysis and subsequent verification experiments demonstrated that Cs4-SeNPs inhibited the TNF-R1/TAB2/NF-κB inflammatory pathway and upregulated the expression of antioxidant proteins including SERPINA3K, GPX1, and SOD in the bone tissue. Metabolomic analysis revealed that Cs4-SeNPs treatment significantly elevated fecal and serum levels of two key metabolites: kynurenic acid and trehalose. Further in vitro studies confirmed that kynurenic acid and trehalose could reproduce the effects of Cs4-SeNPs on osteoblastic and osteoclastic differentiation. CONCLUSIONS Our findings suggest that Cs4-SeNPs optimize PBM and promote bone development in growing mice by improving the osteoblast/osteoclast balance via the modulation of the inflammatory TNF-R1/TAB2/NF-κB axis and the enhancement of antioxidant activity through the elevated levels of gut microbial metabolites kynurenic acid and trehalose in a gut microbiota-dependent manner.

title: Family Risk and Resilience Patterns Differentiate Early Childhood Vulnerability to Intergenerational Transmission of Abdominal Pain.
abstract: Children are at increased risk of developing chronic abdominal pain if a parent has an abdominal pain-related disorder of brain-gut interaction such as irritable bowel syndrome, suggesting family mechanisms of intergenerational pain transmission. However, patterns of family risk and resilience factors that predict children's vulnerability for developing chronic abdominal pain remain unknown. In a sample of parents with an abdominal pain-related disorder of brain-gut interaction and their young child without chronic pain, this cross-sectional study identified subgroups representing different constellations of family risk and resilience factors. It also tested subgroup differences on two vulnerability markers for children's future development of chronic abdominal pain: child emotional functioning and parental protective behavior. Baseline data from 212 parents and their 4-7-year-old child, participating in a randomized controlled trial testing a preventative intervention were included. Latent mixture modeling indicated a 3-group solution: (1) "High Socioeconomic Status, High Functioning" (55%) characterized by lower anxiety and depression and higher family resilience, (2) "Low Socioeconomic Status, High Pain Burden" (13%) characterized by higher pain catastrophizing and gastrointestinal symptoms, and (3) "High Socioeconomic Status, High Distress" (32%) characterized by higher parenting stress. Two of the three groups ("Low Socioeconomic Status, High Pain Burden" and "High Socioeconomic Status, High Distress" groups) showed lower child emotional functioning, and the "Low Socioeconomic Status, High Pain Burden" group also showed higher parental protective behavior, than the "High Socioeconomic Status, High Functioning" group. Results contribute to theoretical models of intergenerational pain transmission and help identify families who could benefit from preventative interventions. PERSPECTIVE: Among families of parents with chronic abdominal pain, low family resilience, low socioeconomic status, high parent pain burden, and high parent psychological distress may make young children more vulnerable to developing chronic abdominal pain in the future. These findings inform targeted interventions to prevent intergenerational transmission of abdominal pain.

Differentiated obesity treatment: Pharmacological CRF2 agonism drives fat loss, skeletal muscle hypertrophy and improved glucose metabolism in preclinical obesity.
abstract: OBJECTIVE Loss of lean mass during weight reduction may compromise metabolic health and physical function. Urocortin 2 (UCN2) activates corticotropin-releasing factor receptor 2 (CRF2) and has been linked to beneficial effects on skeletal muscle and glucose metabolism. We evaluated an acylated UCN2 analogue (acyUCN2), alone or combined with an acylated GLP-1 analogue (acyGLP-1), in preclinical obesity models. METHODS Diet-induced obese (DIO) Sprague Dawley rats and DIO Göttingen Minipigs were treated with vehicle or acyUCN2 (rats, pigs) or acyGLP-1 or combination therapy (rats only). Food intake, body weight (BW), body composition, glucose tolerance and energy expenditure (rats only) were assessed. Histology and RNA-sequencing were used to characterize muscle remodelling and transcriptional responses. RESULTS In rats, acyUCN2 reduced food intake and fat mass, increased lean mass and muscle weight, and improved glucose tolerance despite limited effects on BW. Energy expenditure was not affected. Histology demonstrated hypertrophy across fibre types and a shift from type 2A to type 2X/B fibres. Transcriptomic analyses supported muscle growth and fibre type switch, relative reduced vasculature, regulation of neuromuscular junction-associated genes, and overlap to human acute exercise-response signatures. In obese minipigs, acyUCN2 increased lean mass and improved insulin sensitivity, with modest effects on BW and fat mass, alongside regulation of genes linked to muscle biology and metabolism. CONCLUSIONS Pharmacological CRF2 agonism promotes favourable body composition, muscle hypertrophy, and improved glucose metabolism despite limited weight loss, supporting clinical development of UCN2 analogues as a differentiated obesity treatment, particularly in combination with appetite-regulating therapies and in settings where preservation of functional muscle mass is critical.

title: Integrating GWAS, transcriptomics, and machine learning enables genomic prediction of grain cadmium content in malting barley.
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) contamination in arable land poses a serious threat to the production of malting barley, a cornerstone crop for the brewing industry. Excessive Cd in grains undermines malting quality by disrupting germination evenness and reducing enzymatic activity during mashing. Despite this challenge, effective predictive tools for grain Cd levels are scarce, and the genetic architecture controlling this trait remains largely elusive. Here, we employed an integrated strategy combining genome-wide association study (GWAS), RNA-seq, and machine learning across a panel of 100 barley accessions. We benchmarked five genomic prediction algorithms, performed cis-eQTL mapping, and applied multi-omics integration to nominate high-confidence candidate genes. Our GWAS uncovered 3902 Cd-associated SNPs, and the XGBoost model, trained on merely 1000 markers, achieved the highest overall predictive performance (r = 0.86). Through systematic prioritization, we identified 67 candidate metal transporter genes. Among these, HvACA8a emerged as a likely negative modulator of grain Cd loading, whereas HvAHA9 and HvYSL15 were implicated as positive regulators. Collectively, our findings establish a robust genomic prediction framework for early Cd risk evaluation in malting barley. The identified markers and candidate genes offer tangible targets for breeding low-Cd cultivars, thereby helping to safeguard the quality of raw materials destined for the malting and brewing sectors.

title: Protocol for a phase I/II, open-label, single-arm trial of autologous chemically induced liver progenitor (CLiP) cell transplantation in patients with decompensated cirrhosis.
abstract: Introduction Decompensated cirrhosis is associated with a poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options for patients who are not candidates for liver transplantation. Although various cell-based regenerative therapies have been investigated, their clinical benefits are limited. Autologous chemically-induced liver progenitor cells (CLiPs) are expandable progenitor-like cells generated from mature hepatocytes using small-molecule reprogramming and have demonstrated regenerative potential in multiple preclinical models. Because CLiPs are bipotent and can differentiate toward both hepatocytic and biliary epithelial lineages, their lineage fate after transplantation may be influenced by the recipient liver microenvironment, and whether transplanted CLiPs undergo hepatocytic maturation in the human decompensated cirrhotic liver to the extent observed in animal models remains unknown. We describe the rationale and design of the first-in-human clinical trial evaluating autologous CLiP transplantation for decompensated cirrhosis. Setting Autologous CLiP cells (CLP-001) are manufactured from liver tissue obtained by laparoscopic partial hepatectomy and expanded in a certified Cell Processing Center under controlled conditions. Quality and safety assessment includes histopathological examination of the harvested liver tissue, sterility, endotoxin and mycoplasma testing, viable cell count, cell viability, cell-surface marker characterization, copy-number variation (CNV) analysis, and targeted cancer-related gene-panel testing (Table 1). The study is conducted under the Japanese Act on the Safety of Regenerative Medicine and has been approved by a Certified Special Committee for Regenerative Medicine. Methods This is a first-in-human, single-center, open-label, single-arm phase I/II study. Three adults with Child-Pugh class B decompensated cirrhosis who are not candidates for liver transplantation will be enrolled. Approximately 30 g of liver tissue will be harvested laparoscopically and used for CLiP manufacturing over a 12-16 week period. Following successful quality and safety testing, CLP-001 will be administered into the portal venous system through surgical cannulation of the ileocolic vein. The primary endpoint is safety, defined as adverse events and product-related deficiencies from tissue procurement through 1 month after transplantation. Secondary and exploratory endpoints include safety through 12 months and descriptive changes in liver function, fibrosis-related biomarkers, liver stiffness, and clinical manifestations of cirrhosis. Conclusion This is, to our knowledge, the first clinical evaluation of autologous CLiP transplantation in patients with decompensated cirrhosis. The trial is designed to establish the safety and procedural feasibility of the entire therapeutic workflow, including tissue procurement, cell manufacturing, quality assurance, and portal venous administration. Efficacy-related observations are exploratory, and the lineage fate of transplanted CLiPs cannot be directly established in this study. The findings are expected to provide the first clinical evidence regarding the safety and feasibility of autologous CLiP transplantation and support the future development of CLiP-based regenerative therapy for advanced chronic liver disease. At the time of submission, patient enrollment has commenced, and no participant has yet undergone CLiP transplantation.

Scaffold-based and calcium-silicate biomaterials in vital pulp therapy: a systematic review of current evidence and translational perspectives
abstract: To critically synthesise and appraise the current evidence on scaffold-based regenerative biomaterials and calcium-silicate biomaterials used in vital pulp therapy (VPT), with particular emphasis on the translational challenges associated with achieving biological regeneration of the dentine–pulp complex. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Electronic searches of MEDLINE (via PubMed), Scopus and Web of Science were performed from database inception to March 2025. Studies evaluating scaffold-based regenerative biomaterials or calcium-silicate biomaterials in VPT were included. Human clinical investigations and in vivo animal studies were considered to capture evidence across different stages of translational research. Methodological quality was assessed using study-design-appropriate risk-of-bias tools. Owing to substantial heterogeneity in study design, interventions and outcome measures, findings were synthesised narratively. Eleven studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising six clinical investigations evaluating calcium-silicate biomaterials and five preclinical animal studies investigating scaffold-based regenerative approaches. Clinical evidence consistently demonstrated favourable outcomes for calcium-silicate biomaterials in preserving pulpal vitality and promoting reparative dentine formation. Scaffold-based systems demonstrated promising regenerative characteristics, including enhanced angiogenesis, odontogenic differentiation and formation of organised pulp-like tissue under experimental conditions. However, scaffold evidence was limited to preclinical models, and no included study directly compared scaffold-based and calcium-silicate biomaterials within the same experimental or clinical framework. Current evidence supports calcium-silicate biomaterials as the clinical standard for VPT, whereas scaffold-based regenerative biomaterials remain a promising area of translational research. Although experimental findings suggest considerable regenerative potential, the absence of direct comparative clinical evidence precludes conclusions regarding comparative effectiveness. Future well-designed clinical studies are required to determine whether scaffold-based approaches can successfully translate into predictable clinical regeneration of the dentine–pulp complex.

title: Integrating Augmented Reality Sandbox Technology to Enhance Hydrology Education in Civil Engineering: A Pilot Study
abstract: Augmented reality (AR) tools may support hydrology instruction by turning abstract watershed concepts into visible and manipulable processes. This pilot study reports the construction and classroom implementation of an AR sandbox to support basin and watershed understanding in an undergraduate civil engineering hydrology course in Bolivia. The system combines a depth sensor and projector with open-source software to overlay real-time elevation, contour lines, and simulated water on a physical sand surface. The AR sandbox was integrated into one laboratory session within a 20-week course, following a socio-constructivist approach in which students worked in small groups to iteratively model landforms and test hypotheses. The activity was organized around four learning objectives: (1) delineating watershed divides from terrain form; (2) identifying drainage direction and flow accumulation; (3) distinguishing endorheic basins, where water ponds internally, from exorheic basins, where water exits through an outlet; and (4) connecting topographic changes with runoff pathways through simulated rainfall. Student perceptions were collected through a brief postsession questionnaire and complemented by instructor observations. Self-reported responses indicated high engagement and perceived support for understanding key ideas such as watershed boundaries, drainage direction, basin outlets, and the contrast between closed and open hydrologic systems. From an instructional standpoint, instructor observations suggested that the hands-on visualization helped address common misconceptions and supported the transition to subsequent numerical and geographic information system (GIS)–based tasks. While the evidence is preliminary and based on short-term perception measures, the findings suggest that AR sandbox activities may serve as a practical and adaptable supplement to hydrology education, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Future implementations will incorporate performance-based assessment, including pre- and postactivity questions, rubric-based watershed-delineation tasks, and comparisons of student performance on drainage-network and GIS-based exercises.

title: Data-Driven Micromechanical Characterization and Mapping of Shale Rocks Using High-Speed Nanoindentation
abstract: This study investigates the potential of high-speed nanoindentation in collaboration with data analytics and phase volume fractions to achieve micromechanical characterization of heterogeneous rocks. Although micromechanical characterization can be performed using mechanical testing alone, integrating chemical analysis—such as elemental mapping techniques—provides essential phase identification. This enables more accurate interpretation of phase-specific mechanical properties. However, incorporating chemical analysis increases the complexity of the process. Hence, this study proposes data-driven micromechanical characterization and mapping of heterogeneous rocks based primarily on mechanical data and limited dependence on chemical analysis. In this study, Mancos shale rock is analyzed using high-speed nanoindentation with high spatial resolution to determine the mechanical properties at the microscale. Subsequently, a suite of unsupervised statistical learning techniques, such as uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) with k -means clustering, Gaussian mixture model (GMM), Dirichlet process mixture model (DPMM), and density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN), are applied to the nanoindentation data. Additionally, an automated image processing and segmentation technique was developed and tested. The results from each technique have been systematically compared against the conventional chemomechanical approach using two metrics: weighted error, which evaluates how well cluster sizes match actual phase sizes, and spatial error, which quantifies the accuracy of mineral phase assignment at each indentation point. Based on the results, UMAP with k -means clustering is the most appropriate technique (with relatively low weighted and spatial errors of 13.40% and 30.40% for Test 2 grid and 26.74% and 49.20% for Test 3 grid) for micromechanical characterization and mapping of heterogeneous rocks, whereas DBSCAN, DPMM, and image segmentation techniques are more suitable as secondary approaches for cross-checking results from UMAP with k -means. Moreover, a comparison of the application of scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) image volume fractions and chemomechanical grid volume fractions for the phase volume fractions has been performed to derive the influence of chemical analysis on the results. This study demonstrates the capability of high-speed nanoindentation combined with machine learning techniques for micromechanical characterization with reduced analytical complexity and improved workflow efficiency.

title: Design Method for Axially Compressed Members Reinforced with Sleeves
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive investigation into a novel prefabricated sleeved retrofit technique for enhancing the global stability of steel compression members in grid structures that are interconnected through joints, such as space grids, latticed shells, and trusses. The research systematically examines the effects of key parameters, including material constitutive laws, yield strengths, outer sleeve geometries (diameter, wall thickness, and moment of inertia), and initial geometric imperfections, on the buckling behavior of reinforced members. A simplified yet accurate finite element modeling strategy, validated against experimental tests, was employed for parametric analysis. The results demonstrate that the retrofit significantly improves the buckling factor, with enhancement governed primarily by the outer sleeve’s moment of inertia rather than its material strength. Notably, the yield strength of the inner tube has a negligible effect, while the amplitude of initial imperfections significantly influences the postretrofit performance. Based on these findings, a modified column curve is proposed. For welded sleeves, the curve aligns closely with the standard column curve a, enabling straightforward design. Further, a practical and efficient design methodology is established, which determines the required sleeve dimensions by first calculating the target moment of inertia based on load demands, thereby streamlining the engineering design process. This work provides theoretical insight and a practical design framework for the application of this efficient retrofit technique.

title: Placental small-RNA sequencing reveals a distinct microRNA signature and its functional relevance in a preeclampsia rat model.
abstract: OBJECTIVE Despite extensive investigations over the last few decades, molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of preeclampsia remain incompletely understood. Emerging evidence suggests that microRNAs (miRNAs) regulate key pathological processes in preeclampsia including endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and oxidative stress. However, a comprehensive profiling of miRNA expression has not been previously carried out. Thus, using reduced uterine perfusion pressure (RUPP) model of preeclampsia, we performed placental miRNA sequencing to identify functional relevance of abnormally expressed miRNAs. METHODS Blood pressure was measured via carotid catheterization on gestational day (GD)19. Placental small-RNA sequencing was performed using Illumina NextSeq2000 sequencer. RESULTS Our analysis identified 142 differentially regulated miRNAs (40 up- and 102 down-regulated) in placenta from RUPP rats. The top upregulated miRNAs included miR-211-3p, miR-628, miR-6324, miR-363-5p, and miR-6329, while miR-3587, miR-29b-3p, miR-3556a, miR-29a-3p, and miR-21-3p were the most downregulated. Functional annotation revealed associations with immune response (miR-363, miR-21, miR-29), B-cell differentiation (miR-628), T-cell activation (miR-21), adipogenesis, and lipid metabolism (miR-211, miR-29, miR-21), and angiogenesis (miR-363, miR-21). Further, gene ontology analysis revealed significant enrichment in biological processes; regulation of transport, cell-cell signaling, and calcium-dependent exocytosis, cellular components; synaptic vesicles, perinuclear cytoplasm, and clathrin-coated vesicles, and molecular functions; glycoprotein binding, protein dimerization, and myosin binding. CONCLUSION These findings suggest that robust miRNA dysregulation in RUPP rats may underlie disease pathogenesis.

title: Blackberry Leaf Blotch Virus, a Novel Emaravirus Infecting Cultivated and Wild Blackberry Plants in Europe.
abstract: A novel emaravirus provisionally named blackberry leaf blotch virus (BLBV), was identified from cultivated and wild blackberry plants (Rubus sp.) exhibiting leaf blotch and vein banding/feathering symptoms. BLBV has been detected in Belgium, France, the Netherlands and Slovenia. The virus is most closely related to raspberry leaf blotch virus (RLBV, Emaravirus idaeobati) infecting raspberry (Rubus idaeus) in Europe, and is distant from blackberry leaf mottle-associated virus (BLMaV, Emaravirus rubi), infecting blackberry in the USA. Up to eight RNA segments were identified in BLBV isolates, including the four core RNA segments present in all emaraviruses and up to four additional non-core RNA segments. Spherical virus-like particles (70-90 nm), morphologically similar to emaravirus virions, were observed in sap from symptomatic blackberry tissue by transmission electron microscopy. The proteins encoded by the core RNA segments were all more than 20% divergent from their closest known emaravirus homologues, supporting the classification of BLBV as a new species. Genetic diversity was found among isolates even at the country level, with some additional RNA segments only detected for some isolates. Eriophyoid mites, known vectors of emaraviruses, were found on several infected plants and molecular barcoding identified the them as Epitrimerus gibbosus, an eriophyoid species previously reported on Rubus spp. in Europe. Transmission bioassays performed with these mites in a greenhouse supported E. gibbosus as a putative vector of BLBV. This discovery raises questions about the impact of BLBV on blackberry crops and the need for virus surveillance in plant propagation material.

title: Icariin Ameliorates Postmenopausal Osteoporosis by Modulating Phosphodiesterase 5A-Mediated RANKL/OPG Signaling.
abstract: To investigate the effects of icariin on postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) and its underlying molecular mechanisms. A PMOP rat model was established by ovariectomy and treated with icariin alone or combined with estrogen. Bone mineral density (BMD), serum estradiol (E2), osteocalcin (OCN), and CTX-I were measured. Bone histomorphology was assessed using HE staining and immunohistochemistry. In vivo safety was evaluated by body weight, organ indices, serum ALT, AST, BUN, CREA, and liver/kidney HE staining. In vitro, a co-culture system of MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts and RAW264.7 osteoclasts was constructed to evaluate icariin's effects on osteogenesis and osteoclastogenesis, with CCK-8 and lactate dehydrogenase assays for safety. Mechanisms were further explored via ALP/ARS staining, molecular docking, RT-qPCR, Western blot, dual-luciferase assays, and PDE5A knockdown/overexpression. Icariin significantly increased BMD, elevated serum E2 and OCN, reduced CTX-I, and improved trabecular microarchitecture in PMOP rats. Icariin promoted osteoblastic differentiation/mineralization while suppressing osteoclast activity in vitro. PDE5A was highly expressed in PMOP; icariin downregulated PDE5A, inhibited RANKL, and upregulated OPG, thereby blocking NF-κB activation, enhancing Runx2 and OCN expression, and reducing cathepsin K and NFATc1. PDE5A overexpression partially reversed icariin's effects. Icariin at high doses showed no hepatorenal or osteoblast toxicity in vivo or in vitro, as per serum, histopathology, and LDH. Icariin promotes osteogenesis and inhibits osteoclastogenesis by downregulating PDE5A and modulating RANKL/OPG signaling, thereby restoring bone metabolic balance and exerting osteoprotective effects against PMOP, with a synergistic action when combined with estrogen and a favorable safety profile both in vivo and in vitro.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging
abstract: This letter presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG-based sleep staging. To efficiently execute long temporal convolutions, a serpentine dataflow propagates activations between neighboring processing elements, reducing memory accesses by 6.2 times and 2.25 times compared with output- and weight-stationary dataflows, respectively. A hybrid quantization scheme applies runtime dynamic quantization to the LSTM and MLP layers and assigns mixed precision on a layer-by-layer basis, reducing model size by 4.16 times. Combined with a bit-flexible MAC architecture and channel-grouped memory scheduling, the accelerator supports INT2/4/8/16 inference. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, the accelerator consumes 0.40 mW and achieves a 258 times speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor. Evaluated across all 62 subjects in the public MASS-SS3 dataset using 31-fold leave-two-subject-out cross-validation, the mixed-precision approach with hybrid quantization maintains 5-class accuracy within 0.15% of the floating-point baseline when optimized for general sleep staging and N3 sensitivity within 0.51% when optimized for deep-sleep detection. The developed techniques are broadly applicable to EEG-based DL workloads.

title: FPGA Acceleration of CNN-BiLSTM for EEG-Based Sleep Staging Featuring FFT-Based Non-Unit Stride Fast Convolution
abstract: Deep learning (DL) models for real-time wearable sleep staging often rely on long-kernel temporal convolutions, a requirement that current accelerators struggle to support efficiently. To overcome this, we present an FPGA-based CNN-BiLSTM accelerator that incorporates several algorithm-hardware co-design techniques to enable efficient edge inference. Central to this design is an FFT-based non-unit stride fast convolution, which performs accumulation in the frequency domain to enable a single IFFT per block, reducing post-processing complexity to $O(N\log N)$. On the target long-kernel convolution layer, this yields a 20.5$\times$ reduction in arithmetic operations. Power-of-two quantization is applied across the pipeline, including FFT-based convolution and BiLSTM activations, with an average accuracy degradation of only 0.11% relative to the floating-point baseline across all subjects on the public MASS-SS3 dataset. Additional optimizations, including block convolution, depth-first execution, and hardware engine reuse minimize memory access and enhance resource utilization. The accelerator, implemented on a Xilinx Zynq-7000 FPGA, operates at 10 MHz and consumes 11 mW of dynamic power including data handling and configuration overhead from a microcontroller. The design achieves a DSP power efficiency of 0.91 GOPS/W/DSP using only 4 DSPs, demonstrating scalable and energy-efficient DL acceleration for sleep staging that can be extended to other wearable applications.

title: The social origins of identity and bias: Language models, accumulated meaning and positioning.
abstract: This paper develops a social psychological interpretation of distributional language models, algorithmically learned representations of natural language. Within these models, words are positioned according to patterns of usage, and the resulting embeddings can be interpreted as maps of cultural associations available for learning. This cultural-learning account explains how patterned meanings become available to individual cognition but leaves open how those meanings are socially produced. Drawing on social identity theory, discursive psychology and a stigmergic-dialogical model of communication, the paper argues that identity and bias emerge through social interaction and the accumulation of linguistic traces. As people take positions, respond to others and circulate formulations, they produce patterns of meaning that locate actors relationally and make alignments and differences recognizable. Bias emerges when this accumulation is uneven, making associations, evaluations and distinctions differentially available across communities. From this perspective, embeddings map patterns accumulated through social activity. Their geometry captures relations through which identities become recognizable and groups distinguishable. The paper extends this approach with speaker landscapes, which locate speakers by their language use and show how groups become differentiated. The result is a framework for studying how meaning, identity, bias and group differentiation are socially produced at scale.
journal: The British journal of social psychology

title: Compliance by Design: Governing AI-Augmented Quantitative Analysis in Clinical and Translational Research.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from promise to routine practice in clinical and translational research, and large language models (LLMs) are now used to scope analyses, draft and debug code, and accelerate the quantitative work that supports clinical and translational decisions. This adoption is outpacing the operational safeguards that keep such work reproducible and auditable, and the central risk is not only erroneous code but the quieter erosion of the analytical discipline on which trustworthy bench-to-bedside decisions depend. In this position paper, we argue that AI can be integrated into regulated quantitative workflows without sacrificing reproducibility, provided it operates inside a compliance-by-design architecture built on two principles: analytical intent must be formally encoded and locked before execution, and the analysis itself must run outside the LLM as specification-verified code in a validated environment. We describe three failure modes that ordinary quality control does not detect, namely context drift, the displacement effect, and implementation drift, and we link each to documented model behavior. For open-ended investigation, these principles are operationalized as a four-step execution firewall; for recurring development studies such as assay validations and animal safety studies, they are operationalized through a governed library of documented, validated agents, supported by fit-for-purpose validation, a clear separation of human and machine roles, and post-deployment monitoring. Both approaches can be implemented with components available today. Used this way, AI enhances rather than replaces quantitative expertise, which now resides less in the code a model produces than in the constraints a scientist defines before it runs.

title: Unified Learning Ensemble for Robust Leaf Disease Detection: Integrating Improved Laplacian of Gaussian (ILoG) and Unified Learning Ensemble Approach
abstract: The world's population mostly obtains its food from plants. Plant diseases, which may be prevented with continuous observation, are a contributing factor in productivity loss. Monitoring plant diseases manually is time-consuming and prone to mistakes. To overcome this problem, this research endeavours to develop an advanced tomato leaf disease detection system, aiming to address the pressing challenge of crop health deterioration. The methodology involves a comprehensive approach, starting with a robust pre-processing pipeline utilizing Non-Local Means (NLM) for image cleaning, standardizing image sizes, and normalizing pixel values to enhance model convergence. A novel Improved Laplacian of Gaussian (ILoG) segmentation algorithm is proposed for precise leaf region extraction, while advanced texture analysis methods such as Gamma Correlation-based Local Phase Quantization (GC-LPQ) and Local Directional Patterns (LDP) are explored for feature extraction. Additionally, colour-based features, including colour moments, and geometric features like leaf area, perimeter, and shape descriptors, are extracted. The research delves into effective feature selection using the Hybrid FoxWheel Optimization Algorithm (HFWOA), a combination of Binary Waterwheel Plant Optimization Algorithm (BWPOA) and FOX-Inspired Optimization Algorithm (FIOA). The Unified Learning Ensemble (ULE) approach integrates Decision Trees, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Neural Networks with weighted voting for accurate leaf disease classification. The methodology's efficacy is evaluated through cross-validation, achieving an accuracy of 99.29% with an 80:20 training-testing split. The implementation is publicly available in a GitHub repository https://github.com/psaranyadevi27-ui/UNIFIED-LEARNING-ENSEMBLE-FORROBUST-LEAF-DISEASE-DETECTION
journal: Journal of Circuits, Systems and Computers

title: Multifunctional composite magnetic particles combined with static magnetic field for treating infectious bone defects via SLC2A1-mediated HIF-1 and PI3K/AKT pathways
abstract: Infectious bone defects are a major challenge in orthopedics and stomatology, requiring strategies that eliminate bacteria and promote osteogenesis. Here, we developed a multifunctional composite magnetic particle system (F-Fe3O4) and demonstrate its synergistic combination with a static magnetic field (SMF) for treating infectious bone defects. In vitro, F-Fe3O4 demonstrated good biocompatibility with human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hBMSCs) and facilitated their proliferation, migration, and osteogenic differentiation, while inhibiting the growth of Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Enterococcus faecalis. With the application with SMF, the aforementioned effects are further enhanced. The in vivo studies in the rat model further revealed that F-Fe3O4 combined with SMF can reduce early infection, alleviate inflammation, and accelerate new bone formation. Mechanistically, RNA sequencing and verification experiments revealed that the combination therapy upregulated SLC2A1-mediated glucose uptake and activated HIF-1 and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways, thereby enhancing the osteogenic differentiation of hBMSCs. In conclusion, this study developed an efficient treatment approach for infectious bone defects by integrating F-Fe3O4 and SMF.

title: Structural inequality in higher education performance: unsupervised profiling of 452,020 Colombian Saber Pro students using UMAP and K-means
abstract: This study applies a large-scale unsupervised learning pipeline to Saber Pro microdata from 452,020 Colombian higher education students (2021 to 2023), integrating academic performance across five modules with socioeconomic, financing, labor, digital-asset, and educational-background variables. K-means, Gaussian Mixture Models, DBSCAN, and HDBSCAN were evaluated on UMAP-reduced representations across 128 configurations, using a two-phase design: hyperparameter search on a validated 200,000-record stratified sample, followed by retraining on the full dataset. An ablation study confirmed UMAP’s necessity (4.5× higher Silhouette than the original 32-dimensional space). The selected K-means K = 8 configuration showed internal validity indices (Silhouette = 0.428, Davies-Bouldin = 0.74) indistinguishable from those obtained on permuted null data, and moderate stability under the most conservative replication protocol (mean ARI = 0.506, SD = 0.085, across 15 reruns varying both UMAP seed and fitting subsample); the profiles’ structural meaningfulness is instead supported by their convergence with independently documented regional inequality patterns (geographic external validation). Eight structurally differentiated profiles emerged, ranging from severe digital exclusion in frontier territories (mean score 136.30) to high-performing students (205.28), with intermediate profiles defined by financing dependence, parental education asymmetries, and working-hour constraints. The contrast between DBSCAN’s highest Silhouette (0.828, with 98.8% of observations classified as noise) and the selected solution illustrates the importance of distinguishing statistical optimization from institutional usability. Profile alignment with known regional inequalities, without geographic variables in clustering, provides external validity. Findings support three differentiated intervention tiers: structural equity interventions, preventive academic supports, and enrichment pathways.

title: An In-depth Bibliometric Study of Complex General Surgical Oncology (CGSO) Fellowship Graduates Within the First 5-year Period of Independent Practice.
abstract: INTRODUCTION The objective of the study is to create a bibliometric profile for recent graduates of complex general surgical oncology (CGSO) fellows to understand their very early career trajectory and inform the current training paradigm. METHODS Bibliometric profiling of applicants to our CGSO fellowship program from 2017 to 2021 who completed an accredited program were included. Impact factors were adjusted for authorship position and type of publication. RESULTS Among 232 CGSO graduates, 106 (45.7%) were female, 118 (50.9%) practice at a university-based flagship hospital (UBFH), 57 (43.2%) published, on average, more than 2 manuscripts per year after at least 2 years in independent practice. The median years in independent practice were 3 years (range 1-5 years). As they progressed in their training and career, the proportions of graduates who published, their level of involvement, the type, and quality of their publications evolved. Only 24 (10.3%) graduates published in basic science or translational research studies after fellowship. In a linear regression model, institution type (estimated means UBFH 7.1 vs. non-UBFH 2.8, p < 0.001), publications before fellowship (β coefficient 14, p < 0.001), publications during fellowship (β coefficient 0.33, p < 0.001), and years since graduating fellowship (β coefficient 2.52, p < 0.001) were associated with more publications during independent practice. CONCLUSION Majority of CGSO graduates do not consistently publish after fellowship. a minority of them engage in basic science or translational research despite great emphasis during fellowship application. A dual-track model to differentiate clinical and research-oriented fellows is needed.

title: Innovation and Competition on a Rugged Technological Landscape
abstract: We integrate innovation into Hotelling's classic model of spatial competition. Potential entrants arrive sequentially and choose whether and where to innovate. They can innovate beyond the frontier, expanding the boundary of the market, or within a niche between incumbent products. Product quality is learned only after introduction, and uncertainty increases with novelty. Innovation on a rugged technological landscape is irregular, with frequent changes in direction and cycles between frontier and niche innovation. The ruggedness of the technological landscape itself deters innovation, generating fewer entrants, less product differentiation, narrower markets, and more intense competition than under certainty. (JEL D11, D21, D83, L11, L25, O31)

title: Depth-adaptive suppression of subject-dependent interference for robust cross-subject EEG emotion recognition
abstract: Objectives Cross-subject electroencephalography (EEG) emotion recognition is limited by inter-subject variability, which embeds subject-specific nuisance information in learned representations and reduces generalization to unseen individuals. Methods We propose a two-stage layer-adaptive subject-interference suppression framework built on EEG Conformer. In the search stage, differentiable gates and adversarial subject classifiers are attached to hierarchical representations from the patch embedding layer and Transformer blocks to estimate where subject information is most strongly encoded. The top-ranked layers are then fixed and the model is retrained for final emotion classification. A subject-aware supervised contrastive regularizer is further used to improve label-consistent cross-subject representation learning. Results Experiments on SEED under strict leave-one-subject-out evaluation show improved performance over representative machine-learning, domain-adaptation, and deep-learning baselines. Auxiliary experiments on SEED-IV indicate adaptability under a more challenging label setting. Layer-wise probing shows that subject-specific information remains decodable across depths but is relatively stronger in shallow and early intermediate representations. Conclusions Selective depth-aware suppression provides a practical and interpretable strategy for robust EEG-based affective brain–computer interfaces.

title: Cross-regional Crop Recommendation under Distributional Shift: Ood Quantification and Agronomic Correspondence Assessment in Kurukshetra, Haryana
abstract: Background: Cross-regional deployment of crop recommendation models is challenging because differences in soil and climatic conditions can cause distributional shifts between training and deployment domains. This study assessed the cross-regional behaviour of Random Forest (RF), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and TabNet under deployment in Kurukshetra, Haryana. Methods: Three classifiers were evaluated on a 3,000-sample Kurukshetra deployment dataset constructed from field-survey soil measurements and NASA POWER meteorological records, with controlled Gaussian perturbation of meteorological features used to expand the dataset, using a 33,000-sample, 33-crop benchmark dataset. A feature-level OOD percentage (OOD%) metric quantified domain mismatch. Top-K (K=5) ranking retained the five most probable crop candidates per sample, followed by weighted consensus. Model confidence, inter-model agreement, season-wise recommendations and correspondence with Haryana agricultural sources were assessed. Result: RF achieved the highest benchmark performance (CV F1=96.55%, Test F1=96.93%, AUC=0.9995), followed by MLP (95.31% Test F1) and TabNet (95.07%). Severe mismatch occurred for nitrogen (48.3%) and potassium (38.6%), whereas temperature and humidity remained within the benchmark range. MLP and TabNet showed higher mean top-1 confidence (0.974 and 0.955) than RF (0.346), while agreement among all three models was 13.9%. Weighted consensus ranked sugarcane, chillies, maize, wheat, cabbage and sunflower highest; five of six consensus recommendations showed manual agronomic correspondence with published regional agricultural evidence (83.3%). Season-wise analysis identified violations associated with the absence of seasonal constraints in the training data, supporting explicit OOD assessment and multi-model consensus for cautious, region-specific crop recommendation under distributional shift.
journal: Agricultural Science Digest - A Research Journal

title: Integrating Machine Learning, Deep Learning and Robotics for Intelligent Information Management and Decision Support
abstract: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Robotics are revolutionizing the landscape of intelligent information management and decision support, connecting data processing, predictive analysis, and autonomous action. This review discusses the conceptual background, technological architectures, and application areas of integrated intelligent systems. It brings together the latest advances in machine learning, deep learning, robotic perception, autonomous control, reinforcement learning, digital twins, edge AI, federated learning and human-in-the-loop decision support. The review also compares the machine learning, deep learning, robotics, and integrated approaches in terms of accuracy, scalability, adaptability, computational efficiency, explainability, and real-time decision making. These technologies are increasingly becoming relevant in the healthcare sector, in manufacturing, in supply chains, in the finance sector, in cybersecurity, in smart cities, in agriculture, and in environmental monitoring. While significant strides have been made, there are still numerous challenges to address, such as data quality, privacy, security, interoperability, computational complexity, transparency, and trust. Multimodal intelligence, foundation models, Distributed learning, and Self-learning robotics are expected to become increasingly common in future intelligent systems. In summary, learning, reasoning, and robotic execution, when integrated, provide a strong basis for trustworthy, adaptive, explainable and human-centric decision support in real-world complex environments and retain the effectiveness of human involvement in the decision process and the responsibility of system governance.
journal: Computer and Decision Making: An International Journal

title: Real-Time Production Forecasting Using GSS-Optimized Holt DES: An Empirical Comparison with ARIMA
abstract: Kurnia Plastic Factory depended on manual documentation of transactions and production scheduling, leading to postponed reporting, erroneous completion projections, and inadequate decision-making. This research created an online point-of-sale system featuring automated predictions for production duration and assessed its forecasting precision and computational efficacy in comparison to a statistical standard. The system was constructed utilizing the Extreme Programming style, the Laravel framework, PHP, and MySQL. Holt Double Exponential Smoothing technique was refined through the application of the golden section search algorithm. Functional testing verified that all 19 features functioned as intended, whereas user acceptance testing attained a success percentage of 94.74%. The assessment of forecasting efficacy was conducted by rolling one-step-ahead projections utilizing 255 observations of production duration documented from 2023 to 2025. The autoregressive integrated moving average model with parameters of one, one, and one surpassed the optimum smoothing technique in all accuracy measures, recording a mean squared error of 1.69, a mean absolute error of 1.05, and a mean absolute percentage error of 34.99%. The refined smoothing technique necessitated an average processing duration of 2.36 milliseconds, in contrast to 35.77 milliseconds for the fixed-order statistical model. The prediction endpoint yielded a response time of about 154.20 milliseconds. The smoothing technique was preserved due to its automatic parameter adjustments for each request, resulting in reduced processing expenses, even though it exhibited diminished forecasting precision. These results revealed a compromise between predictive precision and computational efficacy in production scheduling.
journal: Jurnal Teknoif Teknik Informatika Institut Teknologi Padang

title: Standard Curves of Productivity, Tree Row Volume, and Yield Efficiency by Tree Age of Commercial Sweet Orange Groves in the São Paulo Citrus Belt, Brazil
abstract: Brazil is the world’s largest producer and exporter of orange juice, with most production concentrated in São Paulo and southwestern Minas Gerais (the São Paulo citrus belt). Information on the agronomic performance of orange trees throughout the grove lifespan, including productivity and tree size, is essential for reliable assessments of production costs, revenue, and profitability. This study aimed to develop standard curves for productivity, tree row volume (TRV), and yield efficiency as a function of tree age and stratified by cultivar, region, and planting density. The analysis used data collected by the Orange Crop Forecast conducted by Fundecitrus in commercial sweet orange groves over nine consecutive seasons, from 2016–17 to 2024–25. Grove productivity increased up to ∼14 years of age and declined thereafter, with estimated yields of 25.0, 41.0, 45.1, and 37.1 t/ha for groves aged 5, 10, 15, and 20 years, respectively. ‘Hamlin’ cultivar, southwestern region, and groves planted at high density showed the highest productivity. TRV increased with grove age, reaching 14.1, 26.9, 34.8, and 37.8 thousand m³/ha at the reference ages noted above, with the highest volumes observed for ‘Hamlin’, northern and northwestern regions, and high-density groves. Yield efficiency declined with age, with 16.6, 13.3, 10.8, and 9.2 fruits/m³ at 5, 10, 15, and 20 years, respectively. ‘Natal’, southwestern region, and high-density groves were the strata that had the highest yield efficiency. These results provide a robust reference for evaluating grove performance over time and support economic feasibility analysis, management planning, and strategic decision-making in the citrus industry.

title: ECONOMIC MODELING OF COMMERCIAL VEHICLE FLEET UTILIZATION AND REVENUE OPTIMIZATION IN SAUDI ARABIA: A STRATEGIC FRAMEWORK FOR VISION 2030
abstract: Commercial fleets are the glue that holds the entire transport system together, connecting production to ports, industrial clusters and the final market. The economic value of a vehicle is far less to do with its registered capacity than with its actual productive deployment. This is a critical integrative review of the interplay between fleet utilisation, pricing, empty running, demand uncertainty and asset ownership in the context of the transformation of transport in Saudi Arabia. It draws on a range of research published between 2020 and 2025 in the areas of freight forecasting, dynamic routing, carrier collaboration, vehicle economics and Saudi transport policy. It proposes a revenue-utilisation framework which distinguishes between vehicle availability, productive time, payload use and realised yield and then links these to route level contribution and fleet investment decisions. It identifies four key mechanisms: better forecasting protects dispatch capacity; network collaboration recovers movements that would otherwise be unproductive; pricing should be based on constrained vehicle-hours rather than distance; and alternative propulsion should be evaluated in terms of duty cycle feasibility and opportunity cost. A simple illustrative calculation is provided to show how changes in utilisation and backhaul recovery can impact on contribution, without in any way implying that these are the outcomes observed in the Saudi fleet. The review concludes with a research agenda for testing these mechanisms using anonymised dispatch, telematics and financial data. The central proposition is that alignment with Vision 2030 will only be achieved through sustainable productivity gains underpinned by tangible constraints on safety, service and the environment rather than through maximising fleet size or the volume of vehicles in movement.

title: AI-Enabled Sustainable Precision Farming Using Raspberry Pi and Coral Edge TPU with Cloud-Based Model Training
abstract: Precision Agriculture requires intelligent, adaptable and efficient technology that is capable of making decisions in agriculture at the right time, based on the condition of the plants and the environment. This paper proposes the development of an AI-based sustainable precision farming system based on computer vision, cloud based model training, Raspberry Pi, Coral Edge TPU and the Internet of Things (IoT) sensing. The proposed architecture's sensing layer, edge processing layer, cloud intelligence layer, and application layer enables a complete data processing pipeline from the field to real time decision support. Crop photos are collected for AI condition classification and agricultural conditions such as soil moisture, temperature, humidity and light intensity are collected by built-in sensors. After the above preprocessing, normalisation, image resizing and augmentation, the dataset is divided into training, validation and test sets. The trained deep learning models in a cloud environment are then quantized and converted to be optimized for the edge, following this step. Following this step, the trained deep learning models are quantized and converted for optimization on edge. The optimized model achieves an exemplary accuracy of 94.82%, precision of 94.47%, recall of 94.05% and F1-score of 94.26%. Deploying with the Coral Edge TPU reduces inference latency to approximately 38ms compared to Raspberry Pi-only processing, increases processing throughput to 26.3 pictures per second and reduces CPU usage. The edge-assisted architecture reduces the need for constant connection to the cloud, giving local decision making a leg up. Illustrative sustainability study estimates that condition based monitoring can save 22% of the irrigation water used every day. The findings indicated that the introduction of the edge AI and cloud intelligence in precision agricultural systems that are responsive, scalable, and resource-efficient is technically possible.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Agentic AI Systems: A Review of Multi-Agent Reasoning, Trust, Orchestration, and Autonomous Data Science
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) — systems of autonomous, goal-directed software agents that plan, act, and coordinate with reduced human oversight — is moving from research prototypes toward applied data-science, perception, and decision-support pipelines. Yet the literature remains fragmented across largely disconnected strands: trust-aware orchestration of multimodal agents for visual classification, human adoption of autonomous AI agents, automated machine-learning (AutoML) pipelines for tabular data, and fully autonomous multi-agent systems for end-to-end data engineering. This review synthesizes four recent studies spanning these strands, together with the broader literature on multi-agent orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), large-language-model (LLM)-based knowledge-graph construction, and explainable AI, to build a unified picture of agentic AI as applied to intelligent data science. We propose a four-part taxonomy — perception-level trust orchestration, human adoption of agentic systems, automated feature/model pipelines, and autonomous data-engineering agents — and compare the reviewed studies on automation level, reasoning mechanism, knowledge representation, retrieval use, trust treatment, and evaluation methodology. The synthesis shows that individual components of an agentic data-science stack (confidence calibration, retrieval-grounded re-evaluation, automated feature synthesis, autonomous pipeline repair) have each demonstrated measurable gains in isolation, but no reviewed system couples them with a persistent, multimodal knowledge-graph layer, and adoption research indicates that user trust is not the dominant driver of usage intention — a finding with direct design implications. We identify recurring gaps in provenance, explainability, benchmark standardization, and graph-grounded reasoning, and outline an integrated conceptual framework for the reviewed research landscape, positioning closer integration of agentic data science with knowledge-graph representation as an open research trajectory rather than a solved problem.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: A Web-Based Farmer-Buyer Partnership System for Direct Agricultural Market Connectivity
abstract: Agriculture plays a vital role in the Indian economy and provides livelihood opportunities for a large rural population. However, farmers often face difficulties in finding suitable buyers, accessing market information, communicating product availability, and managing agricultural sales. Traditional agricultural marketing systems may involve multiple intermediaries, resulting in limited direct interaction between farmers and buyers. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Farmer– Buyer Partnership System, a web-based platform that provides a digital connection between farmers and buyers. The proposed system enables farmers to register, create profiles, list agricultural products, specify available quantities and expected prices, and manage buyer requests. Buyers can register, search and view available agricultural products, access relevant farmer and product information, and submit partnership requests. An administrator manages users, products, and partnership activities through a centralized system. The proposed application is developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend, Python Flask for the backend, and MySQL for database management. The system follows a structured approach to improve product visibility, communication, request tracking, and information accessibility. The proposed platform provides a foundation for direct farmer– buyer interaction and can be extended in the future with online payments, real-time market prices, logistics management, notifications, and intelligent farmer–buyer matching.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: VAANIX: A Real-Time Voice AI Agent Platform with Action-Enabled Agents, Automated Appointment Booking and a Business Workspace
abstract: Telephone support is still the main way many small businesses talk to their customers, yet it is also the channel they are least able to staff around the clock. Traditional IVR menus frustrate callers, and most of the newer AI voice products are closed, priced per minute and difficult to adapt to a specific business. This paper presents VAANIX, a self-hostable voice agent platform that connects ordinary phone calls to a streaming pipeline of speech recognition, a large language model and speech synthesis, so that a caller can simply talk and be understood. The first version of the platform focused on that conversational pipeline and a developer console. In this paper we describe a second, larger iteration. A single Agent Studio now holds everything about an agent: its prompt, voice, knowledge base, API settings, call logs, single calls and bulk calling. Agents can also be given actions at creation time. The most important of these is appointment booking, in which the agent checks availability while the caller is still on the line, books the slot, and confirms it by voice. Confirmed bookings appear immediately on a Business Workspace home screen that shows a calendar of the client's own appointments instead of generic call statistics. We explain the architecture, the action mechanism, the way double bookings are prevented, and the security design built on row level isolation. Manual testing across all modules showed that callers receive a spoken reply typically within one to two seconds and that booked slots are reflected on the calendar within moments, without the per-minute platform fees charged by managed voice agent services.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: AgriEase: One Click Solution for Farmers
abstract: Farmers often face difficulties in finding and purchasing essential farming equipment and agricultural products such as seeds, fertilizers, tractors, pesticides, and tractor accessories. They may have to visit multiple shops to compare prices, check product availability, and find suitable equipment. This process takes time, increases transportation costs, and makes it difficult for farmers to find affordable and quality products. The proposed project aims to develop an online platform that helps farmers easily search, compare, and purchase agricultural products and equipment in one place. It will provide product details, prices, availability, and easy access to Essen The methodology of the AgriEase project involves designing and developing a user-friendly web-based platform that provides farmers with easy access to agricultural products and useful farming information. The project follows a systematic approach, including requirement analysis, system design, website development, database management, and testing. AgriEase aims to provide a convenient digital platform that connects farmers with essential agricultural products and information, helping reduce the effort required to access farming resources
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: CLARITAS: Digitizing Educational Feedback Collection Through AI-Driven Sentiment Analysis and Agentic Orchestration
abstract: Traditional feedback collection in educational institutions is often paper-based, resulting in delayed analysis and limited utilization of student insights. This paper presents CLARITAS, an AI-powered educational feedback analytics platform designed to digitize and automate feedback collection and analysis for classrooms and training sessions. Featuring a role-based architecture for administrators, teachers, and students, the system analyses feedback using locally deployed DistilBERT for sentiment classification, Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) for keyword extraction, and word-frequency analysis. A self-built, restricted Agentic AI layer coordinates these components to generate structured summaries without relying on external LLMs or third-party APIs. A fully local analytical workflow supports data privacy, institutional governance, and traceability. The proposed approach provides a privacy-conscious and scalable alternative to conventional manual feedback analysis.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: An Agentic AI Framework for Master Data Synchronization, Validation and Self-Healing Across Integrated Healthcare Information Systems
abstract: Background. Large healthcare organizations run many specialty applications, such as prescribing and dispensing, warehouse and inventory, laboratory, blood bank and billing, that depend on shared master data, chiefly the patient identifier (MRN) and the product identifier with its description. Standards such as HL7 v2 and FHIR can propagate a new or changed record from an origin system, but propagation failures (rejections, unmapped codes, missing mandatory fields, duplicates and timing dependencies) still rely on manual diagnosis and repair. The resulting gaps surface as held or failed transactions at the point of care and supply. Failures also arise without any interface error, when a record exists but its local build or configuration (for example location, charge or dispensing parameters) is incomplete. Objective. To specify a human-governed, closed-loop framework in which AI agents act as integration architect, builder, verifier and support engineer: designing field mappings, configuring receiving systems against an approved build standard, verifying cross-system data validity and local build completeness, and diagnosing and remediating propagation errors. Methods. The study followed a design-science approach. The synchronization gap is formalized, a seven-class failure taxonomy is derived, and a four-layer architecture (sense, reason, act, govern) is specified with tiered autonomy grounded in the Parasuraman-Sheridan-Wickens model of types and levels of automation. An explicit tier-decision rule and tool contracts are defined, verification checks are mapped to established electronic health record data quality frameworks, the closed loop is illustrated with a synthetic worked example, and a staged evaluation protocol with quantified safety gates is specified. Results. The framework specifies agent roles and tool contracts; a proactive build-completeness check for local configuration; a default and maximum autonomy tier for each of seven failure classes; a decision rule in which the permitted tier is the minimum of a policy tier, a confidence tier and a criticality cap; safeguards (patient identity actions reserved for humans, grounding in versioned build standards, deterministic pre-execution validation, and treatment of message content as untrusted data) mapped to a threat model; and evaluation metrics (time to consistency, held-transaction rate, false-fix rate, harmful-action rate) with the sample sizes needed to demonstrate safety bounds, for example 149 consecutive correct fixes to show with 95% confidence that the false-fix rate is below 2%. This is a conceptual and design paper; no empirical results are reported. The tier-decision rule was checked exhaustively against ten stated properties over 11,440 input combinations, with no violations, and six deliberately seeded faults were each detected (Section IV-I). Conclusions. The framework proposes that an AI agent layer can be added over existing integrated systems without replacing them, turning error queues from passive backlogs into a supervised remediation loop. Whether it achieves this is untested. The paper supplies testable hypotheses, pre-specified safety gates and a staged path from shadow mode to limited autonomy for future empirical validation.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: ATLAS - Where Travel Meets AI: An AI-Powered Travel Planning and Decision-Support Platform with Live Data Grounding
abstract: Travel planning is a fragmented, multi-domain decision process: a traveller must separately research destinations, transport, accommodation, food, activities and weather before assembling a feasible schedule. This paper presents ATLAS (“Where Travel Meets AI”), an implemented AI-powered travel planning and decision-support platform that pairs a large language model (LLM) planner with deterministic grounding against live geospatial and environmental data. Given a destination, an inclusive date range, a boarding location, a budget and traveller preferences, ATLAS generates a day-by-day itinerary with the open-weight gpt-oss-120b model served through Groq, while route, weather, food and accommodation agents run concurrently and record the provenance of each data source. Model output is validated rather than trusted: a schema enforces exactly one itinerary day per requested calendar date, generated place names are resolved through OpenStreetMap’s Nominatim geocoder, and road distances and travel times are computed with OSRM from the traveller’s real boarding location, with unknown legs reported as unavailable instead of zero. The system is implemented as a React and TypeScript single-page application backed by FastAPI and PostgreSQL, and includes a live weather outlook, real restaurant and attraction listings, a simulated booking flow that issues a PDF e-ticket by e-mail, and a community Lost & Found module. We describe the architecture and grounding method, report a verification suite of 477 automated tests and preliminary functional observations, and state the system’s current limitations explicitly
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: AI-Based College Transportation Management
abstract: Colleges that run their own buses usually plan transport using fixed routes and estimated student counts. In practice, the number of students who actually travel changes from day to day, so some buses run with many empty seats while others are overcrowded. This paper presents the design of the AI-Based College Transportation Decision Support System, a full-stack web application that collects daily travel confirmations from students and uses rule-based software agents to analyse route-wise demand, check route compatibility, recommend bus allocation, and suggest seat optimization within capacity limits. Every recommendation is accompanied by a plain-language explanation, and no change becomes final until the administrator approves it. The previous allocation stays in force until a replacement plan is approved. The system is built with React.js, Node.js, Express.js and MongoDB, with JWT-based authentication and role-based access control. It uses predefined rules and calculations only; it does not use machine learning, GPS tracking, or external generative AI services. This paper describes the problem, the system architecture, the database design, the rule-based algorithms, and an illustrative worked example. Experimental evaluation on real college data is identified as future work.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: CampusWatch X: Autonomous Multi-Agent Campus Management System
abstract: Campus services often span separate processes for room reservations, faculty consultations, incident reporting, and institutional information access. This paper presents CampusWatch X, an AI-assisted campus service framework that brings these tasks behind a common conversational interface. A Supervisor agent routes requests to specialist agents for resource booking, faculty appointment scheduling, incident management, and college-information assistance. The design combines language-model interpretation with API-mediated tools and persistent application records; the College Guide is intended to ground answers in content collected from the official institutional website. This paper describes the architecture, workflow safeguards, implementation approach, and an evaluation plan. Rather than claiming unmeasured improvements, it identifies testable measures for routing correctness, scheduling conflict prevention, incident confirmation, and answer grounding. The contribution is an integration-oriented design for campus workflows that retains explicit validation and authorization boundaries.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: AgriChain: A Farmer-to-Market Intelligence Platform Integrating Satellite Imagery, Deep Learning, and Market Analytics for Precision Agriculture
abstract: Smallholder farmers in developing agricultural economies continue to face significant losses arising from delayed detection of crop stress, undiagnosed plant diseases, and volatile, opaque market pricing. This paper presents AgriChain, an endto-end farmer-to-market intelligence platform that unifies remote-sensing analytics, deep-learning-based disease diagnosis, and data-driven market forecasting within a single accessible interface. The system ingests multispectral Sentinel-2 imagery through the Google Earth Engine API to compute the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) for continuous crop-health monitoring, while a convolutional neural network trained on annotated leaf-image datasets performs on-demand disease classification from farmer-submitted photographs. A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network forecasts short-term commodity prices from historical mandi (market) records, and a rule-augmented recommendation engine fuses the outputs of these three subsystems to generate actionable, field-specific guidance covering irrigation scheduling, treatment recommendations, and optimal selling windows. The platform is implemented using a React.js frontend, a Node.js/Express backend, and a PostgreSQL/PostGIS spatial database. Experimental evaluation on a held-out test set of 4,120 leaf images across six disease categories yields a classification accuracy of 94.6%, while the price-forecasting module achieves a mean absolute percentage error of 6.8% over a seven-day horizon. Comparative analysis against three existing approaches demonstrates measurable improvements in detection accuracy and decision latency. The results indicate that tightly coupling satellite-derived agronomic indicators with deep learning and market intelligence can meaningfully narrow the information gap between farm-level decisions and market outcomes.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: PhytoSense AR: Augmented-Reality Plant Disease Diagnosis Using a Field-Adapted Vision Transformer and Colour-Based Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Plant diseases cause substantial crop losses, and smallholder farmers often lack timely access to expert diagnosis. Deep-learning classifiers trained on the PlantVillage dataset report near-perfect accuracy, yet they degrade sharply on photographs captured in the field. This paper presents PhytoSense AR, a free, browser-based diagnosis system that overlays disease information directly on the live camera view. The systemcombinesa colourspaceleafandlesionsegmentationstage,basedonHSV thresholdsandtheExcess-Green index, witha VisionTransformer(ViTB/16) classifier covering 38 classes across 14 crops. To narrow the gap between laboratory and field imagery, the classifier was fine-tuned on a mixture of PlantVillage and the PlantDoc field dataset with augmentation that simulates changes in zoom, orientation, illumination and focus, and was then exported to an 8-bit quantised ONNX model of 87 MB that runs on a CPU without PyTorch. On the PlantDoc test set of 236 unseen field images, top-1 accuracy rose from 37.7 % for the originalPlantVillage-onlymodelto76.7%forthedeployedquantisedmodel,whileaccuracyon760held-out PlantVillage images remained at 99.9 %. End-to-end processing, including segmentation and classification, takes about 200 ms per image on a laptop CPU. The system also estimates an infected-area severity and a health score, provides treatment guidance from a curated knowledge base, and offers a multilingual assistant. The results show that domain-adaptive fine-tuning on a modest field dataset, combined with lightweight deployment, makes AR-assisted plant diagnosis practical on commodity hardware
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Multimodal Framework for Agriculture Analysis using AI
abstract: Agriculture plays a vital role in ensuring food security and economic development, but traditional farming practices often face challenges such as crop diseases, unpredictable weather conditions, soil degradation, and inefficient resource utilization. Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have enabled the development of intelligent systems that assist farmers in making timely and data-driven decisions. This research proposes a Multimodal AI Framework for Agriculture Analysis that integrates multiple data sources, including crop images, soil parameters, weather information, and sensor data, to provide comprehensive agricultural insights. The framework employs deep learning models for crop disease detection, machine learning algorithms for yield prediction, and data fusion techniques to combine information from different modalities for accurate decision-making. The proposed system aims to recommend suitable fertilizers, irrigation schedules, and disease management strategies while improving crop productivity and resource efficiency. Performance evaluation is carried out using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and processing time. The experimental analysis demonstrates that the multimodal approach provides higher prediction accuracy and better decision support than single-data-source models.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Identification and Prediction System of Tomato Leaf Diseases Based on YOLO and Random Forest
abstract: Tomato crop failure in Indonesia caused by leaf disease can reach 78%, and manual visual monitoring by farmers is often delayed and subjective. This study designs and evaluates a portable, IoT-based diagnostic and prediction system for tomato leaf disease that can operate independently in the field. The system integrates a Raspberry Pi 4 single-board computer with a Raspberry Pi Camera V2, a DHT22 air temperature/humidity sensor, and a capacitive soil-moisture sensor. Two computational models run on-device: a YOLOv5 convolutional neural network that classifies leaf images into healthy, early blight, late blight, and septoria leaf spot; and a Random Forest classifier that predicts disease potential from air temperature, air humidity, and soil moisture. Results are transmitted via a 4G module to a Firebase cloud database and displayed on a real-time dashboard. Functional and field tests validated camera resolution, sensor accuracy, model accuracy, processing latency, and transmission delay. The YOLOv5-small model classified leaf images with 85.4% accuracy, while the Random Forest model predicted disease potential with 97% accuracy. On-device dual-model inference averaged 7.26 seconds and cloud transmission delay averaged 8.8 seconds, both within the 10-second design target.
