title: Who Publishes During Residency? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Peer-Reviewed Publication Among Residents in the United States
AI-Based Crop Monitoring System: Cotton Disease Detection Using CNN
abstract: Agricultural production depends on the diseases that affect plants and pests; early recognition is essential to crop management. Traditional visual analysis is labor-intensive and subjective because it might depend on the expertise of an analyst; this paper presents an AI-driven cotton disease identification system using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). This model is supported by a web dashboard and a mobile app. The model was trained using 9,495 images of cotton leaves from nine categories: Alternaria Leaf Spot, Aphids, Army Worm, Bacterial Blight, Fusarium Wilt, Healthy, Powdery Mildew, Target Spot, and Verticillium Wilt. All images were, in other words, scaled to 224 × 224 pixels and normalized to zero-to-one in the real-life scenario. Augmentation such as rotation, shifting, zooming, horizontal flipping, and shearing is implemented during the training process. What I mean to say is that the dataset was split into 7,594 training images, 947 validation images, and 954 test images. Custom CNN reached the accuracy of 95.18%, with the macro F1-score of 93.49% and the weighted F1-score of 95.15%.Flask-based backend supports the application, while the web dashboard provides the information and the model's analytics. Further evaluation using images collected under the mixed real-field conditions is needed to establish concrete reliability and generalization.
journal: International Journal for Rapid Research in Engineering Technology & Applied Science

title: Abstract Compendium: Harnessing Climate Action, Food Systems and Human Capital Development
abstract: This compendium presents contributions from the Bells–DIaDeRC International Conference 2026, examining connections among climate action, sustainable food systems and human capital development for well-being in Africa. Organised into five thematic parts, it covers resilient infrastructure; agricultural transformation; health and social inclusion; education and digital innovation; and governance, finance and sustainable enterprise. The contributions comprise empirical studies, reviews, conceptual frameworks and research proposals. They underscore how environmental pressures, institutional conditions and human capabilities shape development opportunities. The collection provides a multidisciplinary foundation for research, policy engagement and collaboration, emphasising locally grounded approaches aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

title: Markaziy Osiyo olimalari ilmiy hamkorlik yo‘lida
abstract: The article examines the role of women scientists in Central Asia in strengthening regional scientific cooperation, advancing the Sustainable Development Goals and developing science diplomacy. Drawing on evidence from Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan, as well as the disciplinary profile of women scientists from Karakalpakstan, it identifies cooperation opportunities in ecology and water resources, agriculture, biotechnology, health, digital transformation and the humanities. UNESCO, United Nations and TWAS data are used to assess women’s participation in research and the importance of regional scientific platforms. The article concludes with practical proposals for joint research consortia, grants for early-career women researchers, academic mobility and an interdisciplinary Aral Sea regional research platform.
journal: Partner conferences of the International Scientific Journal Research Focus

title: Основные направления развития рынка сельскохозяйственной продукции в Республике Узбекистан
abstract: This article examines the main features and development prospects of the agricultural products market in the Republic of Uzbekistan. Particular attention is paid to improving market infrastructure, strengthening economic relations between agricultural producers and consumers, developing storage, processing and logistics systems, and introducing digital technologies. An efficient agricultural products market is important for ensuring food security, increasing producers’ income and providing consumers with high-quality products. The article considers the development of competitive markets, modern agricultural technologies, processing industries, logistics, digitalization and export opportunities as important directions for improving the agricultural products market.
journal: Partner conferences of the International Scientific Journal Research Focus

title: Open Budgets and Cocoa Value Chain Allocations in South-West Nigeria (2021–2024)
abstract: Cocoa remains one of Nigeria’s leading non-oil export commodities, with Ondo, Oyo and Ogun States playing important roles in national production. Sustaining the cocoa value chain depends on public investment, yet Nigeria’s fiscal transparency has fluctuated, with its Open Budget Survey score declining from 45 in 2021 to 31 in 2023. This study examines the openness, allocation and implementation of cocoa-related public spending across the three states. Adopting a qualitative, desk- and library-based design, the study analyses publicly available budget documents for 2021–2024 retrieved from the Nigeria Governors’ Forum digital repository and state government portals, supplemented by civil society and academic literature. An openness assessment and allocation-mapping exercise were used to identify agriculture and cocoa-specific budget lines and, where available, compare approved allocations with actual expenditure. Findings show that agriculture’s share of total state spending remains below the Maputo/Malabo 10% target, ranging from 2.04% in Ondo to 4.31% in Oyo. Cocoa-specific institutional allocations, including Ondo’s Cocoa Revolution Office and Oyo’s Tree Crops Development Unit, constitute a small fraction of agriculture budgets, while most capital spending targets broader agribusiness and rural infrastructure. Cocoa-related investment in Ondo also depends substantially on external and development-partner financing rather than domestic recurrent revenue. Where performance data are available, implementation varies markedly: by September 2021, Oyo’s agriculture sector had spent about 52% of its revised budget, compared with approximately 12% in Ogun. The study concludes that although published budget documents are reasonably open, they reveal persistent underfunding, limited commodity-specific allocations and uneven implementation. It recommends consistent publication of expenditure-actuals data, separate reporting of development-partner disbursements, and further investigation of divergent execution rates.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF PUBLIC RELATIONS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES

title: From Static LMS to Autonomous Agents: Reimagining Moodle-Based Open and Distance e-Learning Delivery for the Agentic AI Era in Kenya
Identification of long non-coding RNAs under nitrogen stress in maize (Zea mays L.)
abstract: Nitrogen (N) is an essential nutrient for plant growth; however, a substantial proportion of the nitrogen applied to crops such as maize (Zea mays L.) remains unused, contributing to environmental pollution and inefficient resource use. Consequently, improving nitrogen use efficiency is a major objective of sustainable agriculture. Although the genetic and molecular mechanisms underlying nitrogen uptake and assimilation are relatively well characterized, the role of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) in regulating nitrogen responses in maize remains largely unexplored. In this study, we investigated the involvement of lncRNAs in maize responses to low-nitrogen stress. Two inbred maize lines with contrasting nitrogen stress tolerance—DMI 56 (tolerant) and DMI 81 (susceptible)—were grown hydroponically under nitrogen-sufficient and nitrogendeficient conditions. Root and leaf tissues were analyzed for lncRNA expression, revealing a large number of differentially expressed lncRNAs, ranging from 226 to more than 1,025 across six experimental comparisons. The Gene Ontology (GO) classification and enrichment analysis helped to annotate the function of 155 lncRNAs in total. Notably, a greater number of lncRNAs were upregulated than downregulated in response to nitrogen stress, and several lncRNAs exhibited consistent expression patterns in root tissues of both genotypes. These observations suggest that certain lncRNAs may constitute a core regulatory network involved in plant adaptation to nitrogen-limited environments. Overall, this study provides new insights into the molecular responses of maize to nitrogen stress and highlights the potential of lncRNAs as targets for improving nitrogen utilization. Further functional characterization of these lncRNAs may facilitate the development of maize genotypes with enhanced performance under low-nitrogen conditions, contributing to more sustainable and efficient agricultural systems.

title: Structure of Clinical Manifestations of Burnout Syndrome in Functional Diagnostic Physicians: Analysis of Somatic, Affective, Cognitive, and Behavioral Components
abstract: The subject of the study is the clinical manifestations of emotional burnout syndrome in functional diagnosticians, examined from the perspective of somatic, affective, cognitive, and behavioral components. The paper analyzes the specific features of the professional activities of this group: working in darkened rooms, prolonged static posture, high patient throughput, and the lack of feedback on diagnostic results. The article substantiates the insufficient adequacy of K. Maslach’s three‑component model for this group of specialists. The following specialized areas of the professional profile are identified: emotional and sensory exhaustion; musculoskeletal distress; technical dehumanization; reduction of achievements, which transforms into professional fatalism; cognitive impairments. The study of the structure of clinical symptoms and their relationship with the psychopathological component is reflected, as well as a comparison of the results with the studies conducted by therapists. The work substantiates the need to change the existing diagnostic scheme and to develop specialized preventive measures based on the results of the study. The empirical study was conducted on a sample of 228 functional diagnostics doctors and 80 general practitioners. A set of psychodiagnostic methods was used: MBI, TAS-20, the EmIn emotional intelligence questionnaire, the Lazarus coping strategies questionnaire, and the author’s questionnaire on somatic symptoms. Methods of descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, factor analysis, and multiple regression analysis were applied. The scientific novelty of the study lies in the empirical verification of the five‑factor structure of burnout syndrome in functional diagnostics physicians, which is not reducible to the classical triad. For the first time, new constructs have been introduced and operationalized — “professional fatalism” (the belief that one’s own diagnostic work has no impact on the outcome of the disease) and “technical dehumanization” (the transfer of an indifferent or cynical attitude from the patient to the technical aspect of the diagnostic process). The use of these terms is justified by the fact that the classical concepts of depersonalization and reduction of achievements do not fully reflect the specifics of the work of FD doctors; the terms were proposed by the authors of this study and are being introduced for the first time. It has been established that the clinical picture of burnout in this group of specialists is characterized by the dominance of reduction of personal achievements (49.1% at a high level), which has been transformed into professional fatalism, as well as by pronounced sensory and musculoskeletal distress, which is not detected by standard questionnaires. A clinical and psychological model has been developed that integrates professional and environmental, clinical, and psychological factors, and the directions for prevention have been substantiated, taking into account the professional specifics of functional diagnostics physicians.

title: Digital Connectivity, Institutional Quality, and Agricultural Outcomes in West Africa: Evidence from a Panel Analysis, 2004–2023
abstract: Agriculture remains an important source of employment in West Africa, where cereal yields are substantially lower than in China. This study estimates associations between national digital connectivity and agricultural outcomes in 12 West African economies during 2004–2023, using China only as a descriptive comparator. World Development Indicators on yields, sectoral value added, labour productivity, employment and connectivity are combined with Country Policy and Institutional Assessment (CPIA) scores. Two-way fixed-effects regressions with country and year effects employ country-clustered standard errors, with Driscoll–Kraay estimates reported as a sensitivity check. The baseline digital infrastructure index (DFI) coefficient for log cereal yield is 0.128 (SE = 0.068, p = .087; N = 240). A separate CPIA interaction model gives a positive moderation coefficient (0.106, SE = 0.036, p = .014; N = 224), which becomes less precisely estimated when rural electrification is included simultaneously (0.088, SE = 0.046, p = .081; N = 205). Estimates for aggregate agricultural value added per worker and agricultural employment share are statistically imprecise. Different estimation samples, 12 country clusters, residual cross-country dependence and unobserved time-varying determinants of yields limit inference. The findings are consistent with, but do not establish, institutional complementarity or causal gains from digital connectivity.
journal: Asian Journal of Agricultural Extension, Economics & Sociology

title: Long non-coding RNAs as Emerging Regulators of Agronomic Traits: Molecular Mechanisms, Functional Landscape and Prospects for Crop Improvement
abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are transcripts longer than 200 nucleotides with little or no protein-coding capacity. Once dismissed as transcriptional noise, they are now recognised as versatile regulators of gene expression that act through chromatin remodelling, transcriptional interference, microRNA target mimicry, modulation of alternative splicing and the formation of RNA–DNA hybrids. In plants, lncRNAs have been linked to many traits of agronomic value, including flowering time and vernalisation response, photoperiod-sensitive male sterility used in two-line hybrid rice, grain yield, fruit ripening, and tolerance to drought, salinity, cold, heat and pathogens. Genome-wide surveys in rice, maize, wheat, tomato and Arabidopsis have catalogued thousands of lncRNAs, and dedicated databases now support their annotation. This review summarises the classification and modes of action of plant lncRNAs, discusses well-characterised examples that bear directly on crop performance, and examines how lncRNAs can be exploited as molecular markers, engineering targets and regulatory tools in breeding programmes. Current limitations, including low sequence conservation, poor functional annotation and the difficulty of editing non-coding loci, are discussed together with future directions for translating lncRNA biology into improved crop varieties.
journal: Journal of Advances in Biology & Biotechnology

title: An Analysis of Farmers’ Profile in the Context of Digital Empowerment in Selected Districts of Rajasthan, India
abstract: Digital empowerment has become an important aspect of agricultural development, as it enables farmers to access agricultural information, government services, digital financial facilities and other development opportunities through digital technologies. In India, the Digital India Mission aims to improve access to digital services, while Common Service Centres (CSCs) serve as an important link between rural communities and digital service delivery. The socio-personal, socio-economic and communication characteristics of farmers may influence their ability to access and use these digital services. Therefore, the present study was conducted to analyse the profile of farmers in the context of digital empowerment in selected districts of Rajasthan. The study was carried out in Kota, Jaipur and Jhunjhunu districts, with a total sample of 300 farmers selected through proportionate random sampling. Data were collected through personal interviews using a pre-tested semi-structured interview schedule. The data were analysed using frequencies, percentages, means and standard deviations. The findings revealed that 60.00 per cent of respondents were in the adult age group, while 73.00 per cent were male. Other major characteristics included membership in the Other Backward Classes (54.00%), middle-level education (21.66%), medium annual income (46.33%), medium mass media exposure (52.00%) and medium innovativeness (56.33%). Furthermore, 47.34 per cent of the respondents had a medium level of extension contact, and 49.00 per cent had a medium level of achievement motivation. The findings highlight the need to strengthen agricultural extension services, improve access to agricultural information, and provide needs-based farmer training to address farmers’ existing informational and extension-related needs.

title: Economic Viability and Capital Payback of IoT-Automated Drip Irrigation Coupled with Biostimulant Application in Tomato
abstract: Background & Aims: Commercial tomato production in semi-arid regions requires irrigation strategies that conserve water without undermining farm returns. This study evaluated the financial performance of Internet of Things (IoT)-automated drip irrigation combined with foliar biostimulants, using both annualised agricultural costing and seasonal cash-flow accounting. Methods: A split-plot experiment with three replications was conducted over the 2024–25 and 2025–26 late Rabi seasons in Andhra Pradesh, India. Conventional calendar-based drip irrigation was compared with sensor-controlled irrigation triggered at 25% and 50% depletion of available soil moisture. Four foliar treatments comprised a water-spray control, seaweed extract, humic and fulvic acids, and amino acids with peptides. Capital payback, monetary water productivity and sensitivity to price and yield changes were assessed. Results: Initial capital expenditure was ₹ 1,71,884 ha⁻¹ for conventional drip infrastructure and ₹ 4,69,484 ha⁻¹ for the IoT-automated installation. Under CACP costing, automated drip at 25% DASM with foliar amino acids (I2B4) recorded the highest pooled net returns (₹ 6,54,493 ha⁻¹) and benefit-cost ratio (2.53), yielding ₹ 11,14,801 ha⁻¹ in net returns (B:C 3.60) in Year 2. Under cash-flow accounting, complete capital recovery occurred in 1.18 crop seasons (14.2 calendar months) for the total IoT setup and 1.24 crop seasons (14.9 calendar months) for the incremental automation retrofit. Scheduling irrigation at 25% DASM saved 17.12% applied water (88.71 mm) and lifted gross economic water productivity from ₹ 57.48 to ₹ 279.79 m⁻³. Sensitivity modelling confirmed farm solvency (B:C 1.76) even under concurrent -20% market price and -20% yield reductions. Conclusion: Sensor-automated drip irrigation scheduled at 25% DASM combined with foliar amino acid application delivered maximum net farm earnings, amortised capital equipment within two seasons and conserved substantial irrigation water. Extending operational state micro-irrigation subsidies (APMIP G.O.Rt.No.1004) to include sensor hardware shortens chronological payback to 1.12 seasons, establishing clear financial justification for commercial smallholder adoption.
journal: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports

title: Large language models in spirometry interpretation: impact of guideline-based prompting.
Living evidence map of the global climate and health literature.
abstract: OBJECTIVES This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (flexible). The objectives are as follows: The objectives of this living evidence map are to: systematically map the breadth, scope, and characteristics of the global literature on the relationship of climate change, climate variability, weather, climate-forcing agents, and fossil fuels with human health and well-being; enable ongoing, up-to-date access to the evolving evidence base through a living approach (encompassing content currency and adjustment of methods); enable identification of clusters of well-researched areas and evidence gaps; enable flexible, accelerated identification, visualization, selection, analysis, and export of records according to the needs of a diverse group of interest holders via an interactive interface and filtering via a dedicated taxonomy; enable the continuous monitoring of a specific topic of interest; and evaluate the rigor, legitimacy, and utility of an AI-supported living evidence mapping approach. Specifically, we envision the map to enable: researchers to identify, collate, and select existing evidence and diverse study designs, explore clusters and gaps, and produce evidence syntheses in a more efficient way; policymakers and international and intergovernmental organizations (such as the World Health Organization or the Sustainable Development Goals Synthesis Coalition) to understand the scope, scale, and distribution of the evidence; research funding bodies to take a more evidence-based approach to funding decisions and identify and fund priority topics, where evidence is most needed and duplication of efforts is avoided; science assessment bodies such as the IPCC or the Lancet Countdown on Climate Change and Health to obtain a comprehensive overview of the research landscape and obtain easy access to relevant lines of evidence for their assessment; health professionals and health systems decision-makers to monitor emerging evidence and evidence syntheses in specific areas that can inform clinical and public health practice and guidelines; and patients and communities directly affected by climate change to gain an overview of the literature relevant to the health risks they face and support the development of evidence-based preparedness and resilience strategies.
journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

title: Targeting Mitochondrial Redox Signaling Promotes Neuroregeneration and Functional Recovery in a Multiple Sclerosis Model.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases, including multiple sclerosis (MS), are characterized by progressive neuronal loss and limited regenerative capacity. To stimulate in vivo neurogenesis and oligodendrogenesis by harnessing the untapped regenerative potential of endogenous neural progenitor cells (NPCs) that are upregulated in the CNS under disease conditions, we developed a novel compound that targets Notch signaling, a pathway known to suppress neuronal differentiation of NPCs. Furapyrrodole, which was identified by screening a natural product-like synthetic chemical library, binds to and activates the mitochondrial reductase CYB5R3, which naturally downregulates Notch signaling downstream of γ-secretase. The in vivo efficacy of furapyrrodole was evaluated in mice with experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), a mouse model of MS. Furapyrrodole treatment after the peak of EAE disease significantly improved motor function and promoted recovery of motor neurons and myelination by stimulating endogenous NPC-derived neurogenesis and oligodendrogenesis. In addition, furapyrrodole supresses neuroinflammation in the CNS. Collectively, these findings indicate furapyrrodole is a promising therapeutic candidate for MS by harnessing endogenously upregulated NPCs and inducing anti-inflammation. Our study demonstrates for the first time that modulation of mitochondrial redox signaling promotes neuroregeneration and remyelination without causing severe adverse effects.

title: Modernizing data reporting in agricultural science: A framework for transparent, reproducible, and artificial intelligence‐ready research
abstract: Inadequate data reporting in agricultural journals constrains reproducibility, transparent interpretation, cross‐study data reuse, synthesis, and artificial intelligence (AI)‐driven discovery. This study aimed to (1) review current data and results reporting requirements across agricultural sciences journals and (2) propose a comprehensive, standardized framework for reporting sampling methods, datasets, metadata, statistical analyses, and research findings. Sixty journals were categorized into four groups according to their publishing organizations and editorial governance: American, International, American Geophysical Union (AGU)/American Economic Association (AEA), and Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute (MDPI) journals. Substantial differences in data and results reporting requirements were found among the groups. Mandatory public access to raw data varied considerably by publisher group: AGU/AEA (100%), International (21%), American (15%), and MDPI (0%). Explicit guidelines requiring the reporting of variability metrics were present in only 42% of International and 36% of American journals, and were absent from AGU/AEA and MDPI guidelines. Overall, standardized reporting protocols are essential to connect agricultural research with machine‐driven synthesis. At a minimum, manuscripts must consistently report sample sizes, central tendencies, and variability metrics, while raw data and metadata should be deposited in public repositories. This work provides an actionable framework for agricultural journals to strengthen editorial policies and ensure research remains transparent, reproducible, and verifiable.

title: A multi-task deep learning-based approach to identify and assess dry root rot disease in chickpea.
abstract: Premise Dry root rot (DRR), an emerging global disease exacerbated by drought, affects a wide range of crops. The disease symptoms are manually scored for large-scale germplasm screening to identify disease-resistant varieties and test transgenic lines and other varieties. Despite its use in the past, manual disease identification is not only cumbersome but also often incapable of distinguishing between similar stress phenotypes. Manual disease scoring is tedious, time-consuming, and often error-prone, especially when screening large numbers of plants. To overcome this limitation, we developed a machine learning model that employs a learning-based approach using convolutional neural networks for automated feature extraction and image-based identification and severity assessment of DRR. Methods Our models were trained, tested, and validated using an in-house dataset of 10,800 unique RGB images. A total of 51 deep learning models, including single-task and multi-task models, were developed using the Xception and Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures with standard image augmentations, and then validated on stratified independent test sets to demonstrate robustness across camera, scanner, and microscope modalities. Results The best multi-task ViT model, capable of scoring across combined datasets, achieved 94% accuracy in distinguishing DRR from the control and had a root mean square error of 1 in predicting DRR severity score. Discussion This model's metrics, including confusion matrix performance, underscore its potential as an efficient and accessible tool for large-scale germplasm screening for DRR, overcoming the challenges of manual scoring.

title: Forecasting and Explaining Environmental Fiscal Capacity: How Informality and FinTech Shape Environmental and Biodiversity Finance
abstract: This study examines the impact of the shadow economy (SE) on environmental fiscal capacity (environmental tax revenue, public environmental expenditure, and biodiversity expenditure) and the moderating role of financial technology (FinTech) across OECD countries over 2004–2022. Using second‐generation econometric techniques, with robustness assessed through the CCEMG estimator, Driscoll–Kraay fixed effects, and one‐step GMM, and complemented by machine‐learning forecasting (tensor double machine learning and a graph‐inspired machine learning model) compared using the Diebold–Mariano test. The analysis yields three main findings. First, the SE significantly reduces environmental tax revenue and public environmental and biodiversity expenditures, consistent with the hypothesis that informality constrains the fiscal capacity required for environmental protection. Second, FinTech adoption directly enhances environmental revenue and mitigates the adverse effect of the SE on environmental revenue through a transaction‐formalization channel that expands the observable tax base, although its direct association with biodiversity expenditure is negative, reflecting a countervailing frontier‐expansion effect. Third, the forecasting evidence reinforces this structural account: Environmental tax revenue is strongly forecastable and public environmental expenditure moderately so, whereas biodiversity expenditure resists accurate prediction across both models. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of digital financial innovation as a complementary instrument for reducing informality, strengthening environmental governance, and advancing biodiversity conservation in OECD economies.

title: The Rise of Agentic AI and Self-Driving Laboratories: Reshaping Drug Discovery, Development, and Precision Medicine.
abstract: The pharmaceutical sector is undergoing considerable transformation as a result of the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), automation, robotics, and advanced computing technologies. Traditional pharmaceutical discovery and development processes can be lengthy, costly, and associated with high failure rates, thereby necessitating more efficient approaches. Agentic artificial intelligence (Agentic AI) combines autonomous decision-making, goal-oriented reasoning, adaptive learning, and multi-step task execution. These capabilities may increase the autonomy and coordination of pharmaceutical research workflows. At the same time, self-driving or autonomous laboratories that utilize robotics, machine learning, laboratory automation, and real-time data analytics to conduct experiments with minimal or no human intervention have emerged as an alternative approach. Agentic AI can provide a higher-level orchestration layer for autonomous laboratories, while established approaches such as Bayesian optimization, active learning, machine learning, and robotic experimentation provide many of the underlying capabilities required for closed-loop experimentation. These technologies can be applied to drug discovery, lead optimization, formulation development, process optimization, and personalized medicine. Several challenges related to data quality, transparency, regulation, cybersecurity, ethical considerations, and infrastructure must be addressed before these systems can be widely adopted. In addition, current evidence is dominated by computational studies, research-scale proof-of-concept platforms, and early industrial implementations. Substantial uncertainty remains regarding their reproducibility, scalability, and effects on overall drug development timelines. Rather than representing an established replacement for conventional pharmaceutical research, the convergence of Agentic AI and autonomous laboratories should currently be regarded as an emerging systems-level architecture that builds upon established approaches such as Bayesian optimization, active learning, robotic experimentation, and closed-loop optimization. Its potential value lies in extending autonomy from individual computational or experimental tasks toward coordinated research workflows, although the extent of this added value remains to be established through prospective and end-to-end validation. Accordingly, fully autonomous pharmaceutical research should be regarded as a long-term research objective rather than an established technological capability, with its realization dependent on further advances in scientific reasoning, experimental validation, regulatory governance, cybersecurity, and human-AI collaboration.

Prowess of Meta-heuristics to Distinguish Potatoes
abstract: In general, the collaboration between technology and agriculture is getting stronger. Agriculture covers many crops, including vegetables and fruit types which are grown under diverse conditions. Climate and soil type are major factors during the growing process of potato. Another factor, the tuber itself, also plays a crucial role in determining characteristics of potato growth. It is therefore beneficial to distinguish different types of tubers, especially in the supply chain. Closer inspection of tubers could serve as an effective method for analyzing the elements and minerals within the potato once tubers have been correctly separated. Using machine learning in this field significantly contributes to obtaining more advanced conclusions. The Visual Geometry Group made the VGG-19 model, which was used to sort different cultivars of potatoes. Transfer learning was used by stopping the last layer of the neural network. Going further, five types of meta-heuristic methods (GA, PSO, ABC, ALO, and GWO) were used to get the best hyperparameters that yielded better results than without using meta-heuristics. Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) surpasses the other methods as well as the standard approach by reaching 90% accuracy, which was better than the standard by 23% for six cultivars of potatoes on the test set while acquiring the best values.

title: Deep gradient explainable framework with ensemble adaptive multi-scale feature fusion for plant disease detection
abstract: Accurate detection of crop disease is essential to improve crop productivity and produce healthy products. Convolution based approach has proven excellent accuracy for plant disease detection. Existing methods depend on backbone architecture and lack interpretability, limiting their robustness and practical applicability. Capturing both fine-grained texture patterns and multi-scale contextual information is a challenging task for visually similar disease classes. To address these challenges, proposed study introduces novel deep ensemble learning framework that integrates residual and multi-scale feature extraction with explainable artificial intelligence. Features extracted with a deep hierarchical and multi-scale learning network are fused using an adaptive attention-based feature-level fusion strategy. Based on fused features, the proposed Deep Gradient eXplainer (DGX) generates proper visual explanations and disease-relevant regions. The proposed framework is evaluated on benchmark PlantVillage and custom plant disease datasets and achieves a classification accuracy of 99.31%. Extensive analysis demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed feature fusion technique with DGX. This improves classification accuracy with interpretability. The proposed DGX validates that the model focuses on biologically meaningful regions, which helps to identify the correct disease.

title: Spatial distribution, clustering and locational correlates of aquaculture enterprises in Nyeri County, Kenya
abstract: Spatially explicit information is necessary for aquaculture support, management and environmental planning. This descriptive GIS-based spatial study examined the distribution of registered aquaculture farmers and production units, assessed spatial patterns, and examined locational correlates of aquaculture enterprises across the eight sub-counties of Nyeri County, Kenya. Available dated aquaculture farmers administrative workbook records span 9 November 2021 to 7 January 2024; 1 of 1,151 aquaculture farmers records contained a malformed date entry, while undated records from the broader county register were also retained where relevant. We analysed 1,203 registered farmer records, including 1,176 valid georeferenced locations for point-pattern analysis and a previously prepared GIS water-proximity classification containing 1,191 records. Distribution was assessed using farmer counts, pond counts and pond area; spatial concentration was evaluated using kernel density and nearest-neighbour analysis; and farm locations were overlaid with agro-ecological zones, rivers, dams and roads. Registered farmer counts showed limited inequality among the eight administrative units (Gini = 0.047), whereas pond counts (Gini = 0.110) and pond area (Gini = 0.301) were more unequal; these administrative summaries do not demonstrate equitable programme reach. Kieni East and Mathira East each had the largest number of registered farmers (167), Kieni East had the most ponds (250), and Mathira West had the largest pond area (73,520 m²). Farmer count was positively but not significantly correlated with pond count (r = 0.668, p = 0.070) and was not significantly correlated with pond area (r = -0.472, p = 0.238). Analysis of the 1,176 valid GPS points in WGS 84 / UTM zone 37 S showed strong county-wide clustering: the observed mean nearest-neighbour distance was 0.353 km compared with an expected distance of 0.708 km, giving an index of 0.498 (z = -32.921, p < 0.001). Existing GIS output classified 846 records (71.03%) within 1 km of a mapped river or dam; because no land-availability baseline was available, this percentage is interpreted descriptively rather than as evidence of preference for water corridors. In the complete-case logistic analysis (n = 1,138; 752 events), Mathira West and Tetu had higher odds of the short nearest-neighbour distance category and log-transformed pond area had lower odds; Kieni West, pond count and stocking status were not significant. Residual spatial autocorrelation remained, and a 5-km spatial-block sensitivity model retained Mathira West and log pond area as the most robust associations. The findings show that registered participation, spatial concentration and production-unit capacity have distinct geographies. An updated georeferenced registry would support differentiated extension, water management, pond rehabilitation, biosecurity, input delivery and market aggregation.

title: SERS ratiometric strategy leveraging carbon allocation trade-off enables Tremella fuciformis metabolic phenotyping and traceability.
abstract: BACKGROUND Accurate metabolic phenotyping and geographical traceability of gelatinous fungi are critical for uncovering fungal physiological adaptation mechanisms and advancing edible fungus quality supervision. However, high phenotypic similarity and subtle metabolic differences in homologous fungal samples pose formidable challenges to conventional physicochemical assays. Especially, relying on chemical fingerprinting without biological phenotypic implications, conventional surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) analysis is unable to discern delicate metabolic discrepancies in fungal samples. RESULTS Herein, we propose a metabolic characteristic peak ratio-based SERS strategy using Tremella fuciformis (T. fuciformis) as the model. By extracting intrinsic metabolic signatures represented by the carbon allocation trade-off between stress-resistant functional polysaccharides and storage-type carbohydrates, it delivers metabolic specificity and detection stability/reproducibility that are not possible with traditional fingerprint-based SERS fungal analysis. Integrated with machine learning, this method accurately differentiates six T. fuciformis samples, including specimens with distinct metabolic phenotypes as well as geographically differentiated samples with highly similar phenotypic features, achieving a superior accuracy of 99.2% and an AUC of 1.0. Combined with a custom-built portable Raman device we constructed, the entire detection procedure can be completed within 15 min, enabling efficient on-site analysis. SIGNIFICANCE AND NOVELTY This study establishes a bio-signature-oriented SERS paradigm that upgrades chemical fingerprint identification to fungal metabolic phenotyping, providing a versatile technical platform for exploring fungal metabolic variation and phenotypic differentiation.

WGCNA and single-cell analysis identify FLG, DSG3 and DSG1 as melanoma-associated hub genes and their modulation by Dinaciclib.
abstract: Melanoma is one of the most aggressive skin cancers, and its molecular heterogeneity continues to present challenges for diagnosis and treatment. Identification of molecular alterations associated with melanoma progression may provide clinically relevant biomarkers and therapeutic insights. In this study, differential expression analysis, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were integrated across melanoma transcriptomic datasets to identify disease-associated gene modules and hub genes. Protein-protein interaction analysis and prognostic modelling were subsequently used to characterize candidate desmosomal genes. WGCNA identified melanoma-associated modules enriched in keratinization, epidermal differentiation, and desmosome-related processes, with FLG, DSG1, and DSG3 emerging as prominent hub genes. Their prognostic relevance was evaluated in the TCGA-SKCM cohort using LASSO-Cox and multivariable survival analysis, while single-cell RNA sequencing was used to investigate their cellular distribution. The analysis revealed distinct cellular expression patterns, with DSG3 showing expression within melanoma cells, whereas FLG and DSG1 were predominantly associated with keratinocyte populations. Pharmacological validation using Dinaciclib in A375 and SK-MEL-28 melanoma cells demonstrated reduced cell viability and increased accumulation of cells in the G2/M phase, accompanied by reduced expression of FLG, DSG1, and DSG3. Molecular docking further predicted potential interactions of Dinaciclib with FLG and DSG3. Collectively, these findings identify a melanoma-associated desmosomal gene program with prognostic relevance and demonstrate that Dinaciclib treatment modulates the expression of these genes in melanoma cells.

Green-Synthesized Nanoparticles for Sensing: From Molecular Mechanisms to Next-Generation Sensing Platforms.
abstract: Green synthesis has emerged as a sustainable and mechanistically versatile strategy for fabricating nanomaterials with tunable physicochemical and interfacial properties for advanced sensing applications. Unlike conventional synthesis routes that depend on toxic chemicals, harsh reaction conditions, and post-synthetic functionalization, green synthesis integrates nanoparticle formation, stabilization, defect generation, and surface engineering within a biomolecule-rich environment. Biological entities such as plant extracts, microorganisms, proteins, polysaccharides, flavonoids, and polyphenols act as reducing and capping agents, producing intrinsically functionalized nanostructures with enhanced biocompatibility and sensing performance. Recent studies demonstrate that biomolecule-mediated synthesis strongly influences nucleation kinetics, morphology evolution, defect chemistry, electronic structure, plasmonic behaviour, and interfacial charge transfer, which collectively govern sensitivity, selectivity, and signal amplification in sensing systems. This Review critically discusses the mechanistic foundations of green nanoparticle synthesis and their use in electrochemical, fluorescence, colorimetric, SERS, and photoelectrochemical sensing platforms. Emphasis is placed on morphology engineering, defect-mediated electronic modulation, biomolecular corona formation, heterojunction design, and nano-bio interface engineering. Current challenges related to reproducibility, scalability, and mechanistic understanding are also highlighted, alongside future opportunities involving AI-assisted synthesis optimization and sustainable next-generation sensing architectures.

title: Development and multicenter validation of a cfDNA methylation-based PCR assay (myESCAP) with machine-learning prediction for non-invasive detection of esophageal cancer.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Esophageal cancer (EC) remains a significant public health burden in China. Current diagnostics modalities such as endoscopy and imaging are invasive, poorly accessible, or insensitive for early-stage cases. DNA methylation alterations in circulating free DNA (cfDNA) are promising for non-invasive cancer detection. OBJECTIVES We aimed to develop and validate a methylation PCR-based assay for EC detection using EC-specific DNA methylation targets. Here, we report myESCAP, a PCR-based assay that amplifies and quantifies levels of EC-specific methylation in cfDNA METHODS: We conducted a multi-center, retrospective case-control study with 489 EC cases and 555 non-malignant controls (benign esophageal/gastric diseases or asymptomatic) to develop myESCAP, a methylation-specific PCR assay containing 11 EC-specific methylation markers from our previous genome-wide methylation screening, selected for strong discriminative performance and PCR compatibility. cfDNA was collected, bisulfite-converted, and tested by myESCAP, and results were analyzed by six modeling strategies (generalized linear model, k-nearest neighbors, C5.0 decision tree, gradient boosting machine, random forest, support vector machine) to train EC-prediction models using 347 EC cases and 349 non-malignant controls, and validated in 142 EC cases and 206 controls. RESULTS All myESCAP markers demonstrated significant differential methylation between ECs and non-malignant controls, with adjusted p values between 5.8×10⁻3 and 3.1×10⁻88. The six models showed robust performance in the training cohort (average AUC = 0.835, average sensitivity = 76.13%, average specificity = 90.88%). They maintained performance in the validation cohort (average AUC = 0.823, average sensitivity = 75.59%, average specificity = 89%). Specifically, for stage I cases, myESCAP had an average sensitivity of 47.2%, highlighting the challenge of early detection with limited circulating tumor DNA and the need for further optimization. CONCLUSION myESCAP accurately differentiated EC from non-malignant controls. The six models collectively confirm myESCAP's robustness and clinical potential as a cost-effective, non-invasive diagnostic tool for EC.

title: Cerebrospinal fluid proteome reveals novel biomarkers for differentiating central NPSLE from central nervous system infection.
abstract: BACKGROUND Central neuropsychiatric systemic lupus erythematosus (cNPSLE) is a major cause of mortality in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Distinguishing cNPSLE from central nervous system (CNS) infections remains a critical clinical challenge due to overlapping clinical manifestations, often leading to diagnostic delays and inappropriate therapeutic interventions. We aimed to identify and validate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers to resolve this diagnostic dilemma. METHODS We conducted the largest cNPSLE CSF proteomic investigation to date using high-throughput data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (DIA-MS) in a discovery cohort comprising 20 patients with cNPSLE, 8 with CNS infection (cNIC), and 11 non-diseased controls (NDC). Differentially expressed proteins were analyzed for pathway enrichment. Candidate biomarkers were subsequently validated using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in two independent cohorts: an internal validation cohort (46 cNPSLE vs. 29 cNIC) and an external validation cohort (40 cNPSLE vs. 13 cNIC). Robustness of discovery-stage protein selection was assessed by stratified bootstrap resampling and leave-one-out analysis. The diagnostic panel was fitted and locked in the internal cohort, and applied to the external cohort without refitting. RESULTS Our proteomic profiling quantified 2175 CSF proteins, revealing enrichment in immune and metabolic pathways. We identified three proteins, matrilin-3 (MATN3), tyrosine-protein kinase Mer (MERTK), and V-set and immunoglobulin domain-containing 4 (VSIG4), that were consistently upregulated in cNPSLE compared with both cNIC and NDC groups. In the internal and external validation cohorts, MATN3 demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.875 and 0.868, respectively), followed by MERTK (AUC = 0.801 and 0.775) and VSIG4 (AUC = 0.724 and 0.752). Notably, a composite three-protein panel achieved discriminatory performance, yielding AUCs of 0.921 in the internal cohort and 0.892 in the external cohort, when the locked model trained in the internal cohort was applied without refitting. CONCLUSION We identified and validated a three-protein CSF panel (MATN3, MERTK, and VSIG4) that differentiates cNPSLE from CNS infections across multi-center cohorts. This diagnostic signature holds potential for clinical translation to facilitate early diagnosis and precise management of NPSLE.

title: Maternal Milk 3'-Sialyllactose Promotes Neonatal Intestinal Maturation and Prevents Hyperbilirubinemia through an HNF4α-Associated Pathway.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS Proper development of the neonatal small intestine is critical for nutrient absorption, barrier function, and bilirubin clearance. Maternal milk contains bioactive oligosaccharides such as 3'-sialyllactose (3'SL), while the sialyltransferase St3gal4 regulates endogenous glycosylation. Their contributions to intestinal development and neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, however, remain poorly understood. METHODS We employed the humanized UGT1 (hUGT1) mouse model, which spontaneously develops neonatal hyperbilirubinemia due to delayed induction of liver and intestinal UGT1A1. By combining this jaundiced background with maternal milk lacking 3'SL, we examined the roles of maternal milk 3'SL and the pup St3gal4 gene in neonatal intestinal development, bilirubin metabolism, and long-term gut function. RESULTS Neonates deprived of maternal milk 3'SL exhibited reduced survival, growth retardation, shortened intestinal length, and aggravated hyperbilirubinemia, associated with markedly decreased intestinal UGT1A1 expression. Transcriptomic analyses revealed downregulation of intestinal maturation markers and secretory lineage genes, accompanied by upregulation of fetal and pancreatic gene programs. RT-qPCR, immunohistochemistry, and Western blot confirmed reduced expression of goblet cell (Muc2), Paneth cell (Lyz1, Defa5), and UGT1A1 proteins in 3'SL-deficient pups. Mechanistically, St3gal4 deficiency was associated with aberrant activation of pancreatic gene programs, while 3'SL deficiency correlated with reduced HNF4α signaling, together implicating disrupted intestinal epithelial identity. Remarkably, these developmental defects were associated with long-term consequences: St3gal4-deficient mice exhibited heightened susceptibility to DSS-induced colonic injury in adulthood, with greater weight loss and reduced survival. CONCLUSIONS Collectively, these findings indicate that maternal milk-derived 3'SL and the St3gal4 gene are essential for establishing neonatal intestinal identity, promoting secretory lineage differentiation, and sustaining intestinal UGT1A1 expression. These findings reveal complementary roles of maternal milk-derived 3'SL and St3gal4-dependent sialylation in safeguarding neonatal survival and shaping long-term intestinal resilience.

Mechanism study on CSF3-Induced M2 polarization of tumor-associated macrophages and CCL9 secretion in promoting tumor progression in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) accounts for ∼85% of head and neck cancers and is the sixth most common malignancy worldwide. Standard surgery plus chemoradiotherapy has limited success due to high recurrence. Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in the tumor microenvironment (TME) promote tumor growth, invasion and angiogenesis. Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor 3 (CSF3) regulates neutrophil function and may influence monocyte differentiation into M2 macrophages in breast and bladder cancers. This study aims to investigate CSF3's role in promoting TAM-M2 polarization in HNSCC and explore the mechanisms using in vitro and in vivo approaches. Bioinformatic methods analyzed CSF3's clinicopathological significance and association with M2 infiltration. CSF3 expression was evaluated in paired tumor/normal tissues by RT-qPCR and IHC, and serum levels by ELISA. CSF3-modulated cell lines were co-cultured with TAMs; polarization was assessed via marker expression by RT-qPCR and flow cytometry. CSF3-overexpressing mouse models examined tumor growth and CD206 expression by IHC. Functional assays on MOC2 cells used TAM-conditioned supernatant. RNA-seq and CCL9 secretion were analyzed. CSF3 correlated with poor prognosis and increased M2 infiltration. Elevated CSF3 mRNA/protein were detected in tumor tissues and serum. CSF3 overexpression promoted M2 polarization, CD206 expression, and tumor growth. Conditioned medium from TAMs co-cultured with CSF3-knockdown tumor cells attenuated MOC2 proliferation, migration and invasion. Tumor-derived CSF3 upregulated TAM-derived CCL9, and exogenous CCL9 restored pro-tumor effects. Elevated CSF3 in HNSCC promotes TAM-M2 polarization and induces CCL9 production in polarized TAMs, creating a pro-tumor microenvironment that facilitates HNSCC progression.

title: Prevalence and farm risk factors for Campylobacter and fluoroquinolone resistant (FQR) Campylobacter from broiler flocks in the United Kingdom.
abstract: The increasing occurrence of fluoroquinolone resistant Campylobacter (FQRC) in broiler flocks represents a significant One Health concern. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of FQRC within UK broiler flocks and to investigate farm-level risk factors for Campylobacter and FQRC. Farms from four major broiler companies were recruited into the study. Four boot swab samples were collected pre-thinning on participating farms for microbiological culture targeting Campylobacter and FQRC. Laboratory results were analysed in conjunction with questionnaire data on farm characteristics, management, and antibiotic usage. Multivariable analyses, using a forwards stepwise logistic regression model, was conducted at farm-level. A total of 121 broiler farms were sampled. The prevalence of Campylobacter and FQRC on farms was 28% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 20.0% - 36.0%) and 21% (95% CI: 13.7% - 28.3%), respectively. Rodent presence inside empty buildings (Odds Ratio [OR]=37.2, 95% CI: 3.81 - 363.8), mechanical ventilation with roof chimney extraction (OR= 4.67, 95% CI: 1.24 - 17.6), and beetle spray use (OR= 12.9, 95% CI: 2.47-67.4) were positively associated with Campylobacter. Farms obtaining chicks from fewer hatcheries per crop were significantly less likely to test positive for Campylobacter (1-2 hatcheries per crop OR=0.19, 95% CI: 0.06 - 0.64). Rodent presence inside broiler building anterooms increased the likelihood of FQRC (OR=3.75, 95% CI: 1.07-13.1). Use of mechanical ventilation with a roof chimney (OR=15.60, 95% CI: 3.99-61.3), and rodent presence in empty buildings (OR=23.40, 95% CI: 2.81-195.0) were positively associated with FQRC (which agreed with the Campylobacter model). The study estimated the prevalence of FQRC on UK broiler farms and risk factors significantly associated with increased risk of Campylobacter and FQRC. These findings will provide evidence to guide optimisation of biosecurity for controlling these pathogens in broiler production.

title: Oral nicotine pouch extracts disrupt osteogenic differentiation in human embryonic stem cells.
abstract: Oral nicotine pouch (ONP) use has increased in recent years due to the perception that these products are a safer alternative to combustible tobacco products. However, little is known about the potential developmental toxicity of ONPs, particularly during bone formation. In this study, we evaluated the effects of ONP extracts from multiple ZYN flavors and nicotine concentrations on osteogenic differentiation using a human embryonic stem cell (hESC) model. H9 hESCs were differentiated toward the osteogenic lineage and continuously exposed to ONP extracts throughout differentiation. Cellular metabolic activity was assessed using the MTT assay, while ATP content, total protein content, alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, glutathione peroxidase (GPx) activity, and calcium deposition were evaluated using biochemical assays and Alizarin Red S staining. Gene expression was assessed using RT-qPCR and single-cell RNA sequencing, followed by pseudotime trajectory and transcriptomic point of departure (tPOD) analyses. ONP exposure caused concentration-dependent reductions in MTT activity, ATP content, total protein content, ALP activity, GPx activity, and calcium deposition. Expression of the osteogenic marker RUNX2 was generally decreased following ONP exposure, while TWIST1, SOX10, and TBX5 expression were increased in several treatment groups. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis demonstrated significant alterations in cell cluster distribution and pseudotime trajectory following ONP exposure, suggesting disrupted osteogenic lineage progression. Transcriptomic analysis further identified widespread perturbation of bone development-related genes across treatments. Wintergreen 6 mg had among the greatest transcriptomic potency metrics. Together, these findings reveal that ONP extracts disrupt osteogenic differentiation in hESCs and alter developmental lineage progression. This study provides mechanistic evidence that oral nicotine pouch extracts perturb early osteogenic differentiation in a human stem cell model and supports further evaluation of their developmental toxicity.

title: Beating the crowd: The interplay of firm experience and industry dynamics in radical innovation
Scallops as an emerging platform toward functional reproductive endocrinology.
abstract: Scallops have become one of the few molluscan systems in which reproductive endocrinology can be examined beyond descriptive molecular surveys. This review summarizes a series of studies that have progressively positioned scallops as an emerging experimental platform for advancing functional approaches in comparative reproductive endocrinology. Early work identified GnRH/CRZ-superfamily peptides and their receptors in scallops, showing that these ancient neuropeptide-GPCR modules are present in bivalves and may have multifunctional roles, but should not be interpreted as direct counterparts of the vertebrate hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis. Molecular analyses of sterol-related and nuclear-receptor-related pathways, together with sex-identification markers, further suggest that scallops provide a useful system for examining candidate mechanisms associated with gametogenesis, sex differentiation, and the stable maintenance of sexual phenotypes, without assuming vertebrate-type sex steroid regulation. At the cellular level, studies of germ cells and gonadal somatic cells have revealed the importance of the gonadal niche, whereas scallop hemocytes have emerged as experimentally accessible primary cells for cellular-level functional assays, rather than as established reproductive endocrine target cells. A major technical breakthrough has been the discovery and application of a strong OsHV-1 promoter, which has enabled transient transgene expression in scallop cells. Combined with primary hemocyte culture, this system has supported subcellular localization assays, recombinant protein production, and functional assessment of genes of interest, thereby providing a complementary route to gene function analysis in bivalves where individual-based functional genetics remains difficult. Despite current limitations, including low transfection efficiency, interindividual variability, and the limited extrapolation of hemocyte-based phenotypes to gonadal or organism-level reproductive physiology, scallop cell-based platforms provide a promising foundation for hypothesis-driven comparative endocrinology. These advances illustrate how non-model molluscs can be developed from observational subjects into experimentally testable systems, offering new perspectives on endocrine evolution, reproductive regulation, and physiological integration in marine invertebrates.

title: Artemisinin derived from Artemisia annua L. promotes thrombopoiesis via targeting FLT3: a novel strategy for thrombocytopenia management.
abstract: Artemisia annua L. (A. annua) has long been documented in traditional Chinese medicine for managing hemorrhagic conditions, attributed to its cooling and hemostatic properties. These historical applications suggest a potential role of A. annua in platelet-related disorders, although its hematopoietic mechanisms remain unclear. To investigate the thrombopoietic activity of A. annua, identify its bioactive constituent, and elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying its effects on thrombopoiesis. Chemical profiling identified major compounds in A. annua. MK differentiation was assessed in K562, Meg-01 cells, and primary murine haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). A murine radiation-induced thrombocytopenia (RIT) model was used to evaluate in vivo efficacy. Molecular docking, drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), and signaling assays were conducted to explore molecular mechanisms. A. annua promoted MK differentiation, upregulating CD41/CD42b and enhancing polyploidization. Artemisinin was identified as the principal active compound. It promoted MK maturation in vitro and restored platelet counts, MK numbers, and HSPC populations in RIT mice without inducing systemic toxicity. Artemisinin also reduced bone marrow (BM) apoptosis and DNA damage while restoring platelet function. Mechanistically, artemisinin directly bound to FLT3 and activated the FLT3/MAPK pathway, leading to increased phosphorylation of MEK/ERK and upregulation of NF-E2 and TAL1. FLT3 and ERK inhibition abrogated these effects. Artemisinin is a potent thrombopoietic agent that acts via direct activation of FLT3 and its downstream MAPK signaling cascade. The findings identify FLT3 as a novel therapeutic target for thrombocytopenia and support the potential clinical application of artemisinin in radiation-related hematological disorders.

title: Profit efficiency of conventional and conservation agricultural practices among smallholder maize farmers in Zambia
abstract: Conservation agriculture (CA), based on minimum soil disturbance, crop residue retention, and crop diversification, is promoted as a climate-smart approach to improve smallholder farmers’ resilience amid increasing climate change-related shocks and soil degradation in sub-Saharan Africa. However, CA adoption remains low, and literature on CA profit efficiency is scanty. This study assesses the profitability and profit efficiency of conventional tillage-based agriculture (CT) and CA practices in Zambia. Using a three-wave annual panel dataset of 1,938 household-level observations across contrasting farmer typologies, we apply panel stochastic frontier analysis and a panel tobit model to analyze profit efficiency and identify determinants of efficiency levels. Results show that CA practices, especially minimum tillage with crop rotation, had higher gross margins but lower profit efficiency, with inefficiencies of up to 27.78% for minimum tillage with crop rotation compared to 18.70% for CT. Principal component analysis identified three farmer typologies: asset- and income-poor, asset- and income-rich, and asset- and income-moderate. Notably, asset- and income-rich farmers achieved the highest profit efficiency under CT and full CA (minimum tillage with crop rotation and mulching), while asset- and income-poor farmers achieved the highest efficiency under minimum tillage, minimum tillage with crop rotation, and minimum tillage with mulching. Input costs (notably fertilizer and labor), maize prices, and farmer characteristics such as education, household size, and cooperative membership significantly influenced profit efficiency. The findings underscore the need for context-specific CA promotion, tailored to farmer typologies.

title: Experimental study on buckling behavior of corrugated steel arch support under tunnel surrounding rock pressure
abstract: Steel arch supports are widely used in tunnel construction, but their thin-walled nature makes them susceptible to buckling prior to strength failure. To investigate the evolution of buckling behavior and the spatial characteristics of deformation, physical model tests were conducted on steel arches. Two models were considered: flat steel arches and corrugated steel arches, along with two surrounding rock conditions: with or without sand filling. By analyzing the buckling deformations, strain and critical loads, the results demonstrated that the corrugation shape dramatically enhances structural stability, increasing the critical buckling load by approximately 20 times under identical sand-filled conditions, while reducing vault settlement by approximately 80% compared with flat steel arches. Lateral pressure from the surrounding rock further improves stability, with a lateral pressure coefficient of 0.7 yielding a 145.6% increase in the critical buckling load relative to the no-lateral-pressure condition. The results further revealed that the buckling evolution of the steel arch undergoes three stages: the elastic stage, the nonlinear plastic stage and the instability stage, where the plastic stage is dominated by tangential strain, with magnitude 1.5 to 3 times that of the longitudinal strain. Spatial differentiation of buckling deformation is identified: at the wave-peak, the vault flattens under compression, while at the wave trough, the haunch bulges outward. This study has revealed the evolutionary stages and spatial distribution of buckling in steel arches, and has identified critical early-warning indicators. The results provide practical references for both construction-stage stability control and long-term in-service safety monitoring.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and future scenario simulation of farmland carbon sources and sinks patterns in the Guanzhong region, China
abstract: Farmland ecosystems play a vital role in regional carbon cycling and are strongly influenced by climate variability and agricultural management.The Guanzhong region, a major agricultural area in northwestern China, is characterized by an intensive winter wheat–summer maize rotation and widespread irrigation.A refined assessment of cropland net ecosystem productivity(NEP) and its driving factors is therefore important for understanding the spatial heterogeneity of carbon sink capacity and for formulating carbon sequestration strategies.Accordingly, this study integrated multi-source datasets with an improved CASA model and a soil heterotrophic respiration model to estimate farmland NEP from 2000 to 2023.Trend, stability, and Pearson correlation analysis were used to investigate the spatiotemporal variation and management-related associations of NEP, while CMIP6 climate projections were used to simulate future NEP under the SSP126,SSP245,and SSP585 scenarios for 2030,2045,and 2060.The results showed that farmland NEP exhibited a fluctuating upward trend during 2000–2023,with a spatial pattern characterized by higher values in the west and lower values in the east.Human-related factors, including straw returning area, fertilizer application rate, and agricultural machinery power, generally enhanced farmland NEP, whereas excessive multiple cropping and improper irrigation exerted negative effects on NEP in certain areas; under future warming and wetting conditions, farmland NEP in the Guanzhong region is projected to decline overall, and the extent of carbon sink conservation areas is expected to decrease relative to the historical period.The findings provide scientific support for optimizing agricultural management, enhancing farmland carbon sequestration, and promoting sustainable agricultural development in the Guanzhong region.

title: Sensitive detection of in vivo traumatic brain injury foci using magnetic particle imaging.
abstract: Diagnosing traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a major clinical challenge, particularly for mild to moderate cases, due to the limited sensitivity of conventional imaging modalities like magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) in detecting subtle cerebrovascular damage early after injury occurs. Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) is a novel modality that offers high sensitivity, linear quantification, and unambiguous detection of superparamagnetic tracers such as iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs). This study evaluates the capacity of MPI to detect and visualize cerebral bleeding resulting from TBI. A controlled cortical impact (CCI) closed-head TBI model was implemented using a calibrated electromagnetic impactor to induce moderate brain injury in C57BL/6 mice. IONPs were administered intravenously after impact, to mimic potential clinical use. CT-registered MPI images revealed strong, localized signals in the impact region of injured animals at early time points, while sham animals showed no residual signal in the brain. This localized signal decayed over time and eventually approached noise levels after 7 days post-injury. A direct comparison between MPI and -weighted MRI demonstrated that only MPI reliably differentiates the early injury foci at 24 hours. These results highlight the sensitivity and specificity of MPI as a potential diagnostic tool for detecting vascular disruption in TBI, offering a promising minimally invasive approach for early injury assessment. Additionally, these results demonstrate nanoparticle accumulation in sites of moderate TBI, highlighting potential theranostic applications of MPI to develop drug carriers suitable for treatment of TBI.
