title: C:H:N:O:P stoichiometry and oxygen demand of marine organic matter are driven by phytoplankton ecophysiology
abstract: Although the hydrogen and oxygen content of marine phytoplankton plays a critical role in determining oceanic O 2 consumption rates, shaping habitat for anaerobic metabolism, they are often assumed to be constant in biogeochemical studies, resulting in biased estimates of respiration rates. Here, by simulating phytoplankton allocation in a general circulation model, we predict latitudinal variations in phytoplankton C:H:N:O:P composition and corresponding O 2 demand. These patterns are driven by physiological adaptation to environmental conditions and are consistent with observations. Subtropical phytoplankton have more C─O bonds and lower O 2 demand, as they contain more carbohydrates than higher-latitude populations. We test the sensitivity of O 2 inventory and regenerated C via the biological pump (C soft ) to plausible bounds of cellular allocation and find that the global O 2 inventory and C soft decrease by ∼11 and 14%, respectively, when a cell shifts from carbohydrate-rich to protein-rich biomass. Our findings demonstrate that biochemical remodeling of phytoplankton composition mediates large-scale patterns and oceanic budgets of O 2 and C.

title: Cryo-EM structure of a protein nanopore reveals lipid acyl chains as integral components
abstract: Nanopore-based technologies are revolutionizing nucleic acid sequencing and molecular sensing, yet the structural basis by which pore-forming proteins interact with lipid membranes remains poorly defined. The mycobacterial porin MspA is a benchmark biological nanopore owing to its exceptional stability and uniquely narrow constriction, but accurate structural information is limited to protein-only models. Here, we present a 2.5-angstrom resolution cryo–electron microscopy structure of the M2 mutant of MspA embedded in a phospholipid nanodisc, providing a high-resolution experimental observation of MspA in a lipid environment. The structure reveals an annular arrangement of extended lipid acyl chains surrounding the MspA oligomer and contacting the transmembrane barrel. Their resolved densities indicate a substantially more ordered annular lipid environment than would be expected from a largely heterogeneous and nonspecific protein-lipid interface. The structure also demonstrates how specific M2 MspA mutations modulate pore polarity, influencing ion selectivity and transport. By determining the membrane-embedded structure of MspA and revealing an ordered arrangement of acyl chains forming extensive hydrophobic interactions with the protein, this study demonstrates the importance of the surrounding lipid environment in the design of protein nanopores.

title: A-site cation–pseudohalide co-design for tin halide perovskite transistors
abstract: Tin halide perovskites are promising lead-free semiconductors for next-generation electronics; however, their implementation is constrained by a fragile crystal framework, facile Sn 2+ oxidation, and rapid crystallization kinetics. Here, we establish a molecular design principle for non-metallic thiocyanate (SCN − ) additives that stabilizes the formamidinium tin iodide (FASnI 3 ) lattice and enables high-performance, stable p-channel thin-film transistors (TFTs). Density functional theory calculations reveal that the Sn–X–Sn bond strength in the lattice and the halide migration barriers can be tuned by the size of the A-site cation and its hydrogen-bonding capability with SCN − and I − . In particular, we find that both the Sn–SCN–Sn bonding interaction and the iodine migration barrier are maximized when guanidinium thiocyanate (GuaSCN) is employed. Consistently, GuaSCN enhances the crystallinity and grain size of tens-of-nanometer-thick FASnI 3 films, prolongs carrier lifetimes, and suppresses Sn 4+ formation, without altering the intrinsic bandgap. TFTs incorporating GuaSCN achieve a field-effect mobility above 88 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , an I on/off ratio exceeding 4 × 10 9 , negligible hysteresis, and superior operational and shelf stability across hundreds of devices.

title: Electric field–controlled spin transport in a topological insulator interfaced with a ferroelectric antiferromagnet
abstract: Topological insulators have been explored extensively for spin-charge interconversion via magnetic interfaces, yet the true response of their spin-charge conversion, particularly in the absence of an external magnetic field, remains to be studied. Here, we report electric field control of spin-charge conversion in the topological insulator Bi 2 Te 3 with the antiferromagnetic multiferroic BiFeO 3 , using a nonlocal spin transport device. A systematic thickness dependence of the spin transport across the interface between Bi 2 Te 3 and BiFeO 3 reveals a signature of topological surface-state–dominated spin transport in the bilayer system. The spin-charge conversion remains robust for thicknesses above 10 nanometers but falls rapidly with reducing thickness and vanishes at 5 nanometers. This is consistent with hybridization-induced emergence of a trivial insulating phase, which is supported by the coherency factor estimated from the magnetoconductance of Bi 2 Te 3 . These results establish that spin-momentum–locked surface states dominate interfacial spin transport in the decoupled regime. Beyond presenting efficient spin-charge interconversion at an entirely insulating magnetic interface, this work also highlights sputter-deposited Bi 2 Te 3 as a high-quality and scalable platform for integrating quantum materials onto the devices. The nonlocal spin transport approach presented here provides a simple and unprecedented direct evidence of spin-charge conversion and opens an efficient and practical pathway toward designing energy-efficient spin-based devices.

title: Rashba-induced intersubband interference in high-harmonic generation
abstract: High-harmonic spectroscopy is exquisitely sensitive to the electronic structure and dynamics of quantum materials, yet quantum interference between spin-orbit-split bands has remained experimentally elusive. We observe this interference between Rashba-split bands in bismuth tellurium iodide (BiTeI) driven by strong mid-infrared laser fields. The sixth harmonic exhibits intensity-scaling kinks and an M-shaped ellipticity dependence. Theoretical simulations attribute these features to spin-orbit–mediated multichannel quantum interference, which arises from Landau-Zener-Stückelberg–type intersubband tunneling between Rashba-split bands. The suppression of harmonic yield under linearly polarized pulses arises from destructive interference among electron-hole recombination pathways, whereas increasing ellipticity modifies their relative phase and induces a distinct spectral redshift. These results establish high-harmonic spectroscopy as a probe of spin-textured band dynamics and ultrafast spin-polarized currents.

title: Mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming by a glutamine antagonist radioenhancer conjugate drives pyroptosis and antitumor immunity
abstract: Aberrant glutamine metabolism undermines the efficacy of cancer radiotherapy (RT) by promoting DNA repair, increasing oxygen consumption, and imposing metabolic stress that compromises the viability and function of cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs). Here, we report a mitochondria-enriched, metabolism-regulating monolayered metal-organic framework (MOF) nanoplatform, Hf-Ir/DON, constructed by incorporating the glutamine antagonist 6-diazo-5-oxo- l -norleucine (DON) into a radiosensitizing hafnium-iridium (Hf-Ir) MOF to inhibit glutaminolysis. This design markedly sensitizes tumor cells to RT and, upon x-ray irradiation, enables mitochondria-targeted RT-radiodynamic therapy with substantially enhanced reactive oxygen species accumulation. The resulting oxidative stress induces extensive DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, and immunogenic tumor cell pyroptosis. Concurrently, Hf-Ir/DON alleviates metabolic constraints on activated T cells, preserving CTL viability while sustaining effector and memory functions. In a murine colon cancer model, low-dose RT combined with Hf-Ir/DON achieved >95% tumor growth inhibition. Further combination with anti–PD-L1 therapy induced regression of bilateral triple-negative breast tumors and prevented lung metastasis. These results establish a radiometabolic MOF nanoplatform that potentiates RT while promoting durable antitumor immunity.

title: Metazoan diversification characterized by elevated rates of evolution during the middle Ediacaran to earliest Cambrian
abstract: To test causal hypotheses for the emergence of animal body plans, we analyze rates of molecular and phenotypic evolution across Opisthokonta, focusing on divergences within the Tonian-Ordovician interval. Both molecular and phenotypic rates increase through the Ediacaran, peaking in an Ediacaran and earliest Cambrian interval before declining thereafter. Partitioning phenotypic characters into categories relating to development, feeding, fossilization potential, locomotion, and nervous systems reveals distinct temporal patterns, with developmental traits contributing disproportionately to elevated rates in the metazoan stem lineage. Rate patterns show a temporal lag between the ecological changes integral to hypotheses of developmental evolution and the Cambrian agronomic, substrate, and information revolutions and earlier peaks in the evolution of the associated phenotypic characters. These patterns are largely independent of the timescale used. Overall, our results indicate that the primary phase of elevated evolutionary novelty occurred during the Ediacaran and culminated in the late Ediacaran-earliest Cambrian, providing the foundation for later ecological and taxonomic innovation.

title: A dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle delivery system for precision phage therapy against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria
abstract: The escalating crisis of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among Gram-negative bacteria, demands innovative therapeutic strategies. Here, we present a dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle-chimeric phage (AbLCP) system engineered to combat multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria. Our design integrates a genetically modified M13 phage displaying anti–lipopolysaccharide (LPS) antibodies with polymyxin B conjugation, which is further encapsulated within anti-LPS antibody–functionalized lipid nanoparticles. This system overcomes the fundamental limitations of conventional phage therapy, enabling efficient cellular internalization, endosomal escape, and potent intracellular bactericidal activity. In murine models of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, AbLCP achieved superior bacterial clearance and up to 10 3 -fold reduction in bacterial burden at a 10 3 -fold lower effective dose than free polymyxin B, with 67-fold selective accumulation at infection sites, and attenuated systemic inflammation and preservation of gut microbiota. Mechanistically, AbLCP neutralized LPS to suppress inflammation and induced a lethal bacterial stress response. This work establishes a transformative nanophage platform that merges synthetic biology with nanomedicine, offering a promising strategy against MDR bacterial infections.

title: Monolithic and scalable capacitive electrodes leveraging parasitic capacitance for full-body pressure mapping
abstract: Scaling capacitive pressure sensor arrays to large areas remains challenging due to electrode alignment errors, fabrication complexity, and limited dynamic range inherent in conventional parallel-plate architectures. Here, we present a scalable capacitive pressure sensor array based on a monolithic electrode architecture, where transmitter and receiver electrodes are co-integrated into a single substrate. A deformable dielectric and a floating ground (GND) layer are positioned above, eliminating alignment errors and reducing the layer-stacking process by 20%. The parasitic capacitance between the electrodes and GND layer is intentionally incorporated into the sensing mechanism, enabling stable pressure detection with effective electromagnetic interference shielding. The resulting 2911-cell array (1.7 m by 1.0 m) achieves 30 Hz full-body pressure mapping with high linearity (R 2 = 0.994). Demonstrations in sleep posture classification, pressure injury prevention, and exercise monitoring validate the platform’s versatility for healthcare and human-machine interfaces.

title: A skin-like, all-in-one hydrogel engineered via a supramolecular entangled network reinforced with hydrogen-bond–associated nanodomains
abstract: Hydrogels hold substantial promise for artificial skin in bionic robotics and biomedical devices. However, few hydrogels have a combination of properties comparable to natural human skin. Here, we report a skin-like, all-in-one hydrogel based on a supramolecular entangled network reinforced with hydrogen-bond–associated nanodomains. Within this architecture, hydrogen-bond–associated self-assembled nanodomains, polymer-chain entanglement, dynamic electrostatic interactions, and reversible metal-ligand coordination operate cooperatively to endow the network with mechanical robustness and dynamic adaptability. Consequently, the hydrogel reconciles the intrinsic trade-offs among mechanical properties, multiple functions, and multimodal perception. Its integrated performance compares favorably with that of other advanced hydrogels and even biological skin. To demonstrate its potential applications, we constructed an artificial skin using our hydrogel, which facilitates interaction with the surrounding environment, including monitoring respiration, detecting motion, and manipulating robotic grippers. These results pave the way for versatile hydrogels that replicate the unparalleled combinatory properties of natural skin more precisely for diverse intelligent applications.

title: Alleviating the stability-energy density dilemma via electron-donor-mediated orbital symmetry regulation in sodium phosphate cathodes
abstract: Manganese-based sodium super ionic conductor-type cathode materials, leveraging the multielectron redox activity of manganese, represent a promising pathway toward high-energy-density sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, the unavoidable generation of Mn 3+ (3d 4 ) species during charge-discharge processes, characterized by asymmetric e g orbital occupancy, triggers octahedral symmetry breaking. This inherent electronic structural instability creates a fundamental contradiction between achieving high energy density and ensuring long cycle life that remains inherently difficult to reconcile. Here, we report an electron-donor–mediated (EDM) mechanism that suppresses Mn 3+ -induced octahedral distortion while preserving high-spin functionality. As electron-donating Fe 3+ and V 3+ are incorporated, Mn 3+ 3d electrons undergo partial delocalization. This electronic redistribution promotes orbital interactions between neighboring transition metal sites through the transition metal-oxygen framework, driving the e g orbitals toward a more symmetric occupation and suppressing octahedral distortion. The EDM-modified cathode demonstrates a high energy density of 492.06 Wh kg −1 . It delivers 178.8 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and retains 80.2% of its capacity over 2000 cycles at 10 C, paving a novel pathway toward next-generation high-performance SIBs cathode materials.

title: GPR183 senses 7α,25-OHC to drive T reg differentiation and tumor immune evasion via AXL-JAK2-STAT5 signaling
abstract: Regulatory T cell (T reg ) accumulation within the tumor microenvironment is a major contributor to immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance. However, the metabolic signals orchestrating T reg lineage commitment remain poorly defined. We identify that the oxysterol 7α,25-dihydroxycholesterol (7α,25-OHC), produced by Vimentin + stromal cells, acts through GPR183 to promote T reg differentiation and suppressive identity. In patients with gastric cancer (GC), GPR183 + T reg infiltration correlates with advanced disease and poor survival. In syngeneic tumor models, conditional GPR183 deletion, specifically in CD4 + T cells or T reg cells, demonstrates its cell-intrinsic requirement for high-cholesterol-diet–induced T reg expansion and tumor growth, thereby abrogating immune evasion and restoring CD8 + T cell effector function. Mechanistically, 7α,25-OHC–GPR183 signaling activates the AXL-JAK2-STAT5 pathway to reinforce Foxp3 expression. Last, GPR183 antagonism modestly enhances anti-PD-1 efficacy in a model-dependent manner and prevents therapy-induced T reg expansion. These findings identify the 7α,25-OHC–GPR183–AXL axis as a potential metabolic checkpoint linking cholesterol metabolism to immune suppression, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy to enhance antitumor immunity.

title: Integrative discovery and functional dependency mapping uncover essential chimeric RNAs in the active transcriptome
abstract: Chimeric RNAs are a class of molecules defined as RNA transcripts containing genetic information for multiple genes. While their expression patterns across tissue types and disease states have been well documented, the biological function of these transcripts remains poorly understood. In this study, we developed an integrative prediction pipeline to establish an atlas of 569,640 chimeric RNAs across 1019 cancer cell lines. Leveraging this resource, we performed a systematic functional dependency screen by integrating our predictions with perturbation datasets from The Cancer Dependency Map project. This approach moves beyond prediction to identifying high-confidence functional chimeric RNAs essential for cellular processes, including a subset of recurrent chimeric transcripts generated by cis - splicing of adjacent genes. We demonstrate that depletion of selected candidate chimeras disrupts cell cycle progression and cellular fitness and that these transcripts are frequently dysregulated in primary breast tumors. Together, these results demonstrate that chimeric RNAs constitute a previously underappreciated layer of gene expression, expanding the functional genome beyond conventional genetics.

title: Competing charge and spin instabilities and giant magnetoelastic coupling in CrSb
abstract: Electronic, magnetic, and lattice degrees of freedom are often strongly intertwined in quantum materials, giving rise to competing ordered states and emergent collective phenomena. Understanding how these interactions evolve across symmetry-breaking transitions is essential for identifying new mechanisms of electronic ordering. Here, we show that the antiferromagnet chromium antimonide provides an ideal platform to investigate this interplay and uncover short-range charge-order fluctuations at the M point of the Brillouin zone, q * = ( 1 2 0 ) , persisting well above the Néel temperature, T N . These fluctuations collapse upon entering the magnetically ordered phase, revealing a direct competition between charge and spin order parameters. At T N , the phonon dispersion at q * develops a pronounced Kohn-like anomaly, signaling strong electron-phonon coupling in the vicinity of the magnetic transition. Below T N , exchange striction markedly renormalizes the associated soft phonon mode by ∼6 milli–electron volts, corresponding to the largest spin-phonon coupling reported to date. First-principles calculations show that the relevant phonon branch is unstable at the harmonic level only in the absence of magnetic order, highlighting the remarkable sensitivity of the lattice to magnetic symmetry breaking. The suppression of charge correlations upon magnetic ordering, together with the abrupt reconstruction of the phonon spectrum at T N , demonstrates an exceptional coupling between charge, spin, and lattice degrees of freedom in chromium antimonide. With its chemically simple structure and symmetry-protected altermagnetic state, chromium antimonide emerges as a model system for exploring giant spin-phonon coupling, competing electronic instabilities, and emergent broken symmetries in altermagnetic materials.

title: Extracellular vesicle-mediated restraint of hepatic CD74–NF-κB repairs diabetic neuropathy
abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) affects up to half of people with diabetes and lacks disease-modifying therapy. Here, we profiled MSC-EV biodistribution and multiomic programs across diabetic models, with key nerve repair established in db/db mice and corroborated in high-fat diet/streptozotocin- and methionine-choline–deficient mice. Systemically administered EVs predominantly accumulated in the liver and improved peripheral nerve structure and function, with benefits supported by glycemia-controlled or glycemia-adjusted analyses rather than being fully explained by systemic glycemic changes. EV treatment was associated with reduced circulating injury markers, attenuated spinal inflammatory responses, and improved endothelial junction integrity. Mechanistically, EV-encapsulated miR-24-3p repressed hepatic CD74, coinciding with reduced MHC II/NF-κB activity in macrophages. Hepatic CD74 overexpression promoted systemic inflammation and peripheral nerve injury, whereas pharmacologic NF-κB inhibition recapitulated EV-associated benefits. Together, these data define a liver-to-nerve causal axis and support EV-mediated restraint of hepatic CD74–NF-κB signaling as a cross-organ strategy for DPN repair.

title: The true scale of global wildlife trade is obscured by data gaps
abstract: Overexploitation of wildlife is one of the greatest global drivers of biodiversity loss. Yet, despite this well-established risk, data on extraction and trade are both incomplete and highly fragmented. The IPBES Global analysis estimated 50,000 species to be in trade, yet our review of wildlife trade monitoring programs found at least double that, at 107,356 species in use and trade globally. This included up to 47,685 animal species, covering 42% of all described vertebrate species. Most countries lack any systematic data on trade for species not listed in Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), with the exception of the US-specific dataset Law Enforcement Management Information System, which frequently had higher diversity of species in trade than global databases. This highlights the importance of national monitoring efforts and the need for standardized collation of wildlife trade data beyond CITES-listed species. Without these changes, global indicators on trade meant to guide sustainability and conservation will continue to focus on less than 2% of traded species.

title: ANME-2a perform methane oxidation in brackish coastal sediments via multiple pathways
abstract: Methane is a powerful greenhouse gas. Typically, a large fraction of methane formed in coastal sediments is removed via anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM). Here, we demonstrate the potential for a range of AOM pathways in brackish coastal sediments by ANME-2a archaea. At our study site, geochemical profiles indicate that AOM is primarily restricted to a shallow, metal oxide–rich sulfate-methane transition zone (SMTZ). ANME-2a were the sole methanotrophs detected, and metatranscriptomics showed the highest expression levels of the ANME-2a genes in the SMTZ. AOM activity was observed in sediment incubations with various electron acceptors, including sulfate, metal oxides, and the organic matter analog graphene oxide. Highest potential rates were observed in sediments from below the SMTZ, pointing toward fast stimulation of the deeper methanotrophic community when alleviating the electron acceptor limitation. The variety of AOM pathways and persistence of methanotrophs below the SMTZ likely contribute to the resilience of the microbial methane filter in brackish coastal sediments.

title: Fluid-driven robotic micromanipulation for assembloid fabrication
abstract: The assembly of cellular spheroids into spatially organized assembloids represents a transformative paradigm for modeling complex biological systems. However, the lack of standardized fabrication strategies fundamentally limits the precision and reproducibility of these models, hindering their widespread application. Here, we present a robotic micromanipulation platform—Fluid-Driven Tweezer with Visual Servo Control (FDT-VSC). By integrating multidimensional visual perception with microfluidic control, our system enables the gentle and programmable assembly of diverse cellular spheroids. Leveraging this platform, we achieve the bottom-up construction of structurally defined, heterogeneous multicellular tissues, and the programmed orchestration of multilineage models that recapitulate the complex microenvironments of early organogenesis. Crucially, the system improves consistency during the scalable fabrication of tumor-stroma assembloids, supporting reliable drug screening. These results demonstrate that FDT-VSC advances assembloid-based applications across modular tissue engineering, developmental biology, and drug discovery.

title: Crystalline three-dimensional membranes enable chromatography-free purification of natural products
abstract: Chromatographic purification of natural products is solvent intensive and energy-demanding and remains a major bottleneck in the sustainable production of pharmaceutical compounds. Here, we show that crystalline three-dimensional membranes enable chromatography-free purification of complex natural product mixtures by organic solvent nanofiltration. The rigid, nanomechanically robust channels of the membrane sustain continuous 6-day operation with commercial Taxus crude extracts, achieving ∼96% retention and fourfold enrichment of paclitaxel while allowing valuable precursors to permeate. The membranes exhibit high solvent permeance with negligible swelling, enabling stable molecular sieving in methanol across extended operation. Scalable fabrication via nanosphere-assembled interfacial polymerization produces continuous crystalline membranes over large areas. Life cycle assessment reveals nearly an order-of-magnitude reduction in carbon emissions compared with liquid chromatography. These results demonstrate a membrane platform that can replace chromatographic steps in natural product drug purification, offering a sustainable route for active pharmaceutical ingredient production.

title: Elevated CO 2 mitigated warming-enhanced carbon loss from northern peatland
abstract: Peatlands store one-third of the global soil carbon (C) on only ∼3% of Earth’s land surface but risk becoming C sources to accelerate climate change due to warming-induced C loss. Elevated CO 2 (eCO 2 ) may mitigate this loss by boosting plant C uptake. However, how eCO 2 and climate warming interact to influence peatland C dynamics remains unclear. Here, we investigated peatland C fate at five warming levels (+0°, +2.25°, +4.5°, +6.75°, and + 9°C), each under ambient CO 2 (aCO 2 ) and eCO 2 (+500 parts per million), by model-guided synthesis of 18 measured variables for each of the 10 treatments from an experiment. Our results showed that the peatland C loss increased with warming at a rate of 62.6 g C m −2 year −1 °C −1 , reaching 476.5 ± 104.7 g C m −2 year −1 at +9°C under aCO 2 , primarily because of increased Sphagnum mortality and accelerated decomposition. eCO 2 reduced the loss rate to 17.3 g C m −2 year −1 °C −1 , nearly halving the C loss at +9°C (269.4 ± 80.5 g C m −2 year −1 ), mainly due to enhanced tree and shrub growth. Methane emissions increased with warming, similarly under aCO 2 and eCO 2 . Our findings suggest that northern peatlands likely become major C sources under climate warming, although rising atmospheric CO 2 concentration may partially slow down the C loss. Climate-driven shifts in plant community structure, rather than peat decomposition alone, play a critical role in regulating peatland C fate and may threaten the stability of peatland ecosystem functions and services in the future.

title: Super-resolution mapping of nuclear stress signaling by probiotic-derived extracellular vesicles in UV-induced skin photodamage
abstract: Ultraviolet (UV)-induced photodamage drives oxidative stress, DNA damage, and chronic inflammation, leading to progressive cellular ultrastructure and skin function degeneration. Despite the potential of probiotics as anti-photodamage agents, their nanoscale action mechanism remains unexplored. Here, we utilize super-resolution fluorescence microscopy to investigate the cellular and molecular basis of Lactobacillus plantarum -derived extracellular vesicles ( L. plantarum EVs) in mitigating photodamage. We showed that UV irradiation triggered extensive organellar remodeling along with elevated reactive oxygen species production, DNA damage signaling, and inflammatory activation. Remarkably, pre- and posttreatment with L. plantarum EVs preserved organelle integrity and restored native nanoscale architecture. Additionally, EV treatment delayed UV-induced PARP-1 activation and nuclear condensate clustering, while suppressing NF-κB translocation and downstream inflammatory cytokine expression. These findings establish probiotic-derived EVs as modulators of stress-responsive signaling and structural homeostasis during UV-induced photodamage. By providing a super-resolution mechanistic framework for understanding probiotic EV-mediated modulation of cellular photodamage responses, this study provides a basis for future investigation of EV-based strategies for skin protection.

title: Coarse climate model grids underestimate coastal humid-heat extremes
abstract: Humid-heat extremes reach intensities close to the limit of human survivability around the Arabian Peninsula. Here, we analyze fully coupled kilometer-scale Icosahedral Nonhydrostatic (ICON) and Integrated Forecasting System–FinitevolumE Sea ice-Ocean Model (IFS-FESOM) simulations from the nextGEMS project, with original resolutions of around 9 kilometers, and compare them with station observations, ERA5, and CMIP6 projections. IFS-FESOM reproduces well the observed upper-tail wet-bulb temperature (TW) and lies near the high end of the CMIP6 distribution over coastal regions, while ICON simulates weaker extremes. Spatial smoothing suppresses localized coastal maxima, reducing daily-maximum TW extremes by up to 8°C and lowering exceedance frequencies across multiple thresholds. Native resolution fields also show stronger mid-century increases in exposure under SSP3-7.0 than their coarse-gridded counterparts. These results suggest that conventional coarse resolution projections may underestimate localized coastal humid-heat risk, although the magnitude of this effect remains model dependent.

TADA: Technology Aware DNN Accelerator Performance and Energy Estimator
abstract: Deep neural network (DNN) accelerators for edge inference must meet tight energy, latency, and area (EDP) constraints, and their optimal hardware architecture and dataflow configuration is typically identified through design space exploration (DSE). However, on-chip memory technology including cell type, bank organization, and process node, is rarely treated as a first-class citizen in DSE. For example, increasing memory capacity can reduce memory accesses through greater data reuse, but at the cost of higher area and access energy, thereby limiting the compute units budget. Consequently, memory technology can fundamentally shift the optimal accelerator architecture for a given area and EDP budget. Existing machine learning (ML)-based DSE methods require repeating simulation, data generation, and model training for each new memory technology. We present TADA, a memory technology-aware DNN accelerator performance and energy estimator that predicts system latency and energy for a given workload, hardware configuration, and memory technology. TADA is trained on a synthetic dataset that generalizes across memory technologies. The dataset spans current and future technology trends while enforcing physics-based guardrails to preserve realistic area-energy trade-offs. Each memory technology is represented by a technology signature, a vector of read energy, write energy, and storage capacity across a range of areas, provided as input alongside the workload and hardware configuration. Across 21 unseen technology curves spanning SRAM, STTRAM, ReRAM, PCM, FeFET, eDRAM, and CTT, TADA predicts system energy and latency with 1.5-4.4% and 0.7-1.2% mean absolute percentage error, respectively. In three pairwise case studies, it matches the simulator-selected memory technology at 98.7-100% of area budgets, with a mean EDP loss of at most 0.21%, while achieving over 10^4x higher evaluation throughput.

title: Genotype by environment interaction under two production systems utilizing a random regression model for milk production traits in multiparous South African Holstein dairy cattle
abstract: Dairy cattle in South Africa (SA) have to produce in varying environments which can roughly be separated as total mixed ration (TMR) and pasture (PAST) production systems according to the level of rainfall in the herd area. Previous studies aimed to determine a possible genotype × environment interaction (GxE) using 305-day lactation records, finding no interaction, but different heritabilities. An alternative random regression (aRR) model was developed using SA Holstein test-day records of herds with known production system used (TMR or PAST, analysed independently). The aRR model separates the animal genetic (additive) effect into a general production level and a linear persistency effect and shows clear differences in the genetic variances and heritability estimates over the lactation between TMR and PAST. The aim of this study was to further investigate the existence of a possible GxE interaction, using comparable data, methods and RR model to differentiate each trait (milk, fat and protein production for the first 3 lactations) separately for the two production systems (TMR or PAST). The possible reranking of sires on resulting estimated breeding values from the analysis between TMR and PAST were also investigated. Genetic correlations (0.83 to 0.93) of the genetic general production level effect between TMR and PAST were strong, while corresponding correlations of the genetic linear persistency effect were moderate (0.40 to 0.60) for all traits. Significant reranking of sires between TMR and PAST are predicted for genetic linear persistency, as well as genetic total production. Genetic correlations show a significant genotype by environment interaction for the genetic linear persistency effect between the two production systems in SA Holsteins. Genetic evaluations should analyse production traits in the different systems as genetically different traits, utilizing an applicable random regression model that can effectively dissociate genetic general production level from genetic linear persistency. Estimating separate breeding values for persistency for each production system is justified.

title: Strain and cell type dependent induction of tunnelling nanotube-like projections by African swine fever virus
abstract: African swine fever (ASF) is a devastating viral disease of pigs, causing mortality rates of up to 100%. The causative agent, African swine fever virus (ASFV), preferentially targets cells of the mononuclear phagocytic system (MPS). Despite its severe economic and animal health impact, effective antiviral treatments remain unavailable in Europe. We previously showed that ASFV strain Belgium 2018/01 induces tunnelling nanotube (TNT)-like projections in monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs), enabling physical connections between distant cells. Here, we investigated the broader relevance of this phenomenon across porcine myeloid cell populations and ASFV strains. We assessed TNT-like projection formation in monocytes, pulmonary alveolar macrophages (PAMs), splenic macrophages, polarized and non-polarized MDMs and Vero cells following ASFV infection. We further compared 20 ASFV strains representing diverse genotypes and virulence levels. Interestingly, luminal monocytes and PAMs did not develop ASFV-induced projections, whereas projection formation increased during monocyte differentiation into MDMs. Splenic macrophages also formed projections, suggesting that interstitial tissue macrophages acquire the ability to induce protrusions. Polarized MDMs exhibited reduced projection formation compared with non-polarized MDMs. Similar structures were induced in Ba71V-infected Vero cells, providing a standardized model for mechanistic studies. Importantly, all 20 ASFV strains induced TNT-like projections in MDMs, although the extent varied substantially and was independent of viral genotype or virulence. Our findings demonstrate that ASFV-induced TNT-like projection formation is a conserved, cell-state-dependent phenotype across diverse ASFV strains. These findings provide a foundation for identifying the cellular and viral determinants of TNT formation and defining its potential contribution to ASFV dissemination and pathogenesis.

title: Advances In Agrochemical Strategies for Pest and Disease Management in Horticultural and Field Crops
abstract: Global agriculture faces a critical challenge: meeting a projected 60% increase in food demand by 2050 while mitigating the ecological footprint of crop protection technologies. Plant pests and diseases cause annual losses exceeding 40% of global food crops, with economic damages surpassing USD 220 billion, yet conventional agrochemical reliance has generated a self-reinforcing "pesticide treadmill" of chemical dependency, resistance evolution, and climate change feedback. This review synthesises advances in agrochemical strategies for pest and disease management across horticultural and field crop systems, examining the historical trajectory from botanical extracts to synthetic chemistries and the contemporary shift toward sustainable alternatives. We analyse four transformative technology platforms: nanotechnology-enabled delivery systems achieving targeted, stimuli-responsive release with dosage reductions of 46.6–83.4% in cost per unit efficacy; biopesticides and biocontrol agents demonstrating 30–96% larval reduction in field trials, with policy initiatives targeting 7.5 lakh hectares in India and 50% synthetic pesticide reduction in the European Union by 2030; RNA interference-based approaches offering species-specific gene silencing; and precision application technologies integrating UAV-deep learning detection with variable-rate spraying, reducing pesticide usage by 30–50% and off-target drift by over 30%. Critical analysis reveals persistent bottlenecks in perception system degradation under environmental disturbances, formulation adaptability to very-low-volume regimes, and regulatory fragmentation impeding commercialisation. The review identifies emerging frontiers in CRISPR-integrated pest management, microbiome engineering, and digital twin predictive modelling, arguing that the future of crop protection lies not in standalone technological fixes but in the judicious integration of agrochemical tools within diversified, ecologically informed Integrated Pest Management frameworks tailored to the specific economic, agronomic, and ecological contexts of different production systems.

title: Effect of Different Agronomic Practices on Soil Physicochemical Properties, Nutrient Availability and Productivity of Field Crops
abstract: Soil health and crop productivity are strongly influenced by agronomic practices that regulate soil structure, nutrient availability, water dynamics, biological activity, organic carbon storage, and the overall resilience of agricultural systems. This review examines the major interactions between agronomic management and soil fertility, with emphasis on soil physicochemical properties, nutrient cycling, tillage systems, organic and inorganic fertilization, irrigation management, conservation agriculture, biofertilizers, weed management, precision agriculture, and crop-specific responses. Soil properties such as texture, structure, bulk density, porosity, water-holding capacity, pH, electrical conductivity, soil organic carbon, cation-exchange capacity, and aggregate stability determine the ability of soils to supply nutrients and support crop growth. Sustainable tillage, residue retention, organic amendments, balanced fertilization, diversified crop rotations, efficient irrigation, and microbial-based inputs can improve soil structure, nutrient-use efficiency, microbial activity, and water conservation. In contrast, excessive tillage, imbalanced fertilizer application, residue removal, inefficient irrigation, and continuous nutrient extraction may accelerate soil degradation, nutrient depletion, acidification, salinization, and greenhouse gas emissions. Conservation agriculture and integrated nutrient management provide important opportunities to improve soil organic carbon sequestration and long-term productivity, while precision agriculture, variable-rate nutrient application, remote sensing, drones, Internet of Things-based sensors, and artificial intelligence are creating new possibilities for site-specific agronomic management. The review also highlights the importance of managing acidic, saline, sodic, compacted, nutrient-deficient, and eroded soils through targeted reclamation and amendment strategies. Long-term field experiments remain essential for understanding changes in soil carbon stocks, nutrient balances, biological properties, and yield sustainability. Future research should integrate regenerative agriculture, climate-resilient cropping systems, nano-enabled and controlled-release fertilizers, microbiome-based soil management, digital decision-support systems, and long-term soil-health monitoring. Overall, sustainable agronomic management requires an integrated, site-specific approach that combines physical, chemical, biological, technological, and socioeconomic considerations to maintain soil fertility, improve resource-use efficiency, enhance crop productivity, and strengthen agricultural resilience under changing climatic conditions.

title: Polarimetric interferometric synthetic aperture radar and machine learning for rice canopy height estimation
abstract: Accurate and timely estimation of rice canopy height is crucial for crop monitoring, yield forecasting, lodging assessment and precision agriculture. Optical remote sensing is frequently constrained by cloud cover during the monsoon-aligned rice cultivation period. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and Polarimetric SAR Interferometry (Pol-InSAR) offer a physically grounded route to canopy structure by using the polarimetric scattering mechanisms, traditionally formalised through the random volume over ground (RVoG) model approach. This review synthesises the basic principles of the Pol-InSAR approach for vegetation height measurements and the effects of unique rice scattering mechanisms caused by the existence of a water layer under the canopy, which impose on the classical assumptions of the RVoG approach. Recent machine learning (ML) approaches provide an overview of applications, including random forest and support vector regression, in conjunction with Pol-InSAR and PolSAR data. Key persistent challenges include temporal decorrelation, water-layer phase centre ambiguity and limited cross-site applicability of the models, including physics-informed hybrid ML models, multisensors/multiband fusion and operational monitoring approaches. This review argues that combining the use of the combination of Pol-InSAR physical foundation and ML modelling is the most promising path forward.

title: Digitalization of ecosystem methods of social management and formation of economic security policy in agribusiness
abstract: The object of research is the system of economic security of agricultural and agro-industrial enterprises in the context of digitalization and ecosystem management methods. The problem addressed in the research was the fragmentation of scientific approaches to economic security, digitalization and ecosystem management, since existing models of economic security mostly do not take into account digital and ecological variables together. The methodology used is based on comparative and systematizing analysis, morphological assessment and development of an integral indicator called economic security, which combines the economic parameters of agricultural companies within the framework of a reference system for the level of digitalization, trade in agricultural products and conditions for the functioning of ecosystems. It was found that digitalization contributes to increasing the efficiency of land use through better allocation of resources, the spread of technologies and reducing the negative impact on the environment, with the greatest impact on large agribusinesses that use less qualified labor. Agroecological methods create an additional impact on the functioning of ecosystems. Calculations showed that the share of corn in the total volume of grain exports from Ukraine in 2022/23 was 58.8% (27.12 million tons) compared to 37.3% (17.22 million tons) of wheat cargo. Supplementing the base index (Sbase = 0.718) with two components – digital readiness and environmental security (total weight from 0.10 to 0.40), which increases the resulting value of 0.729–0.761 and contributes to the transition of one company from the “Vulnerable” category to the “Safe” category, at least in one of the six analyzed cases. The research results are proposed to be used to improve the system for monitoring economic security, management decisions and state policy regarding the digital and environmental transformation of agribusiness.

title: Machine Learning, Foundation Models, Skills, and Agents in the Energy Industry: A Systematic, Evidence-Graded Survey
abstract: Artificial intelligence in energy is reported far more often than it is deployed, and the evidence that would let an operator tell the difference is scattered across literatures that do not cite each other. This survey assembles it. We grade 678 claims drawn from 883 evidence cards over 455 sources across four pillars (classical and deep machine learning, foundation models, capability packaging and agents) and the whole value chain, applying one deployment ladder (demo, pilot, field trial and production) to every system. Three findings recur. First, the subfields differ in evaluation regime, not in any measured model capability: the earliest petroleum large-language-model benchmarks found date from 2026, the power sector’s from 2024, and none of them reports a human-expert baseline, so none of their scores can be read as expertlevel. Second, in this corpus, two places differ: in drilling automation and artificial lift, software writes setpoints to field equipment with no human approving each action, yet the artificial-lift system with the broadest such authority contains no machine learning, and every reinforcement-learning system here that actuates does so in a simulator, not on a well. Third, the sources in this corpus rarely measure the field’s own adoption: no Tier A source found reports an adoption rate, a pilot-to-production conversion ratio, a total cost of ownership, or a post-mortem of a cancelled programme, and 63 claims here are formally evidenced absences. The survey reports its own failures, among them a retracted absence claim, a measured skew in its own corpus and seven source caches holding the wrong document.

title: Domain Knowledge Plus AI Fluency: The New Nonnegotiable Competency for the Health Workforce in the AI Era.
abstract: In the ongoing AI boom-now supercharged by large language models and generative AI tools-the rapid integration of AI into health care and public health has created an urgent need for professionals who combine deep domain expertise (clinical, epidemiological, ethical, and contextual expertise in health and public health) with AI fluency (the ability to understand, critically evaluate, use, and oversee AI systems effectively). Without domain guidance, AI risks producing biased, unsafe, or contextually irrelevant outputs that compromise patient safety and exacerbate disparities. Conversely, domain experts lacking AI fluency may underuse or misuse these technologies, missing opportunities to improve care quality, operational efficiency, and population health. A foundational understanding of the modern AI system stack-comprising energy, accelerators, infrastructure, models, and applications-empowers health professionals to make informed decisions on adoption, evaluation, governance, and ethical use without needing to code or build models themselves. This stack framework highlights critical interdependencies and health care-specific challenges, including regulatory compliance, data privacy, sustainability, and resource constraints, particularly in low- and middle-income settings. This paper argues that cultivating domain-AI bilingualism is essential for safe, effective, and equitable AI integration worldwide. It outlines the 5-layer AI system stack applied to health care, key reasons for hybrid expertise, and a practical 4-step pathway: awakening (recognizing AI's transformative role), intrepidity (courageously engaging foundational AI concepts), bilingualism (translating between clinical needs and AI capabilities), and visionary leadership (driving organizational and policy readiness). It outlines major barriers, targeted strategies, and recommendations for educators, institutions, and policymakers. By bridging domain knowledge with AI fluency, health professionals can direct-rather than be directed by-AI technologies, including emerging agentic systems, toward more precise, sustainable, and human-centered outcomes while mitigating risks. This hybrid capability represents a nonnegotiable competency for the health workforce for thriving in the post-2026 AI era.

title: Rethinking Health Care Regulatory Sandboxes Under the European Union AI Act.
abstract: Unlabelled AI models have enabled substantial advances in health care. Since the entry into force of the European Union (EU) AI Act in 2024, these systems have become subject to a common regulatory framework in the EU intended to harmonize AI governance across all member states. One of the act's distinctive features is that it accommodates existing economic, technological, and regulatory differences among European countries by leaving certain implementation responsibilities to national authorities. This is evident in regulatory sandboxes, supervised environments for developing, testing, and validating AI systems before deployment. In this viewpoint, we provide a policy-oriented analysis of health care regulatory sandboxes under the EU AI Act and propose recommendations for their design. These recommendations address the need to document model compression techniques that may affect the classification of large high-risk systems above the 1025 floating point operations per second threshold, incorporate explainability into AI systems from the design stage, identify and document biases in health care datasets, clarify the treatment of federated learning parameter updates under the General Data Protection Regulation, and strengthen the oversight of AI agents in clinical environments. The implementation timeline makes this discussion particularly timely given the approaching deadline of August 2, 2027, by which all member states must have established at least one national regulatory sandbox.

title: Generative sampling with physics-informed kernels
abstract: We construct a generative network for Monte-Carlo sampling in lattice field theories and beyond, for which the layerwise propagation is computed and optimised independently on each layer. The architecture uses physics-informed renormalisation group flows that provide access to the layerwise propagation step from one layer to the next in terms of a simple first order partial differential equation for the respective renormalisation group kernel through a given layer. Thus, it transforms the generative task into that of solving once the set of independent and linear differential equations for the kernels of the transformation. As these equations are analytically known, the kernels can be refined iteratively. This allows us to structurally tackle out-of-domain problems generally encountered in generative models and opens the path to further optimisation. We illustrate the practical feasibility of the architecture within simulations in scalar field theories.

title: Collaborative Governance in Achieving Sustainable Food Security: A Study in Pandeglang Regency
abstract: Food security is a strategic concern that requires stakeholder collaboration through a Collaborative Governance approach. Although Pandeglang Regency has significant potential to serve as Banten Province’s food hub, it faces several obstacles, including agricultural land conversion, climate change, inadequate irrigation, weak farmer institutions, and limited intersectoral coordination. This study examines the application of Collaborative Governance to achieve sustainable food security and proposes a model to strengthen collaboration. Using a qualitative conceptual approach, the research combines a Narrative Literature Review with Document Analysis. Data are examined through content and thematic analyses based on Ansell and Gash’s five dimensions of Collaborative Governance. The findings suggest that sustainable food security depends on effective collaboration among government institutions, farmer groups, Bulog, BUMDes, private enterprises, academics, and local communities. Accordingly, the study proposes a collaborative strengthening model centered on establishing permanent coordination forums, enhancing facilitative leadership, integrating food information systems, promoting agricultural digitalization, and implementing Smart Food Governance. These strategies are expected to improve coordination, strengthen institutional capacity, and support regional food system sustainability. However, the proposed model remains conceptual and requires empirical validation, while its applicability to other regions depends on their specific contexts.

title: Using Remote Sensing Techniques to Monitor the Changes in AL-Habbaniya Lake, West of Iraq
abstract: Lakes and other water bodies change over time and are influenced by natural and anthropogenic processes during the hydrological cycle. One method for monitoring those factors is remote sensing, which collects digital information about objects or regions remotely and is useful for a wide range of tasks. It is a powerful reminder that data is focused on changes in the Earth’s surface, rather than being opposed to the traditional methods. Al-Habbaniya Lake, a vital reservoir west of Baghdad, mainly serves three functions: flood control, supplying ecosystem services, and irrigation. Recently, the lake’s surface area has significantly fallen due to drought, slow water flow in the Euphrates River, and delayed maintenance, influencing its agricultural, recreational, and natural functions. The focal point of this study is to monitor changes in Al-Habbaniya Lake in western Iraq using remote sensing techniques over approximately 34 years, 1988, 2002, and 2022, using Landsat satellite images. The methods employed are atmospheric correction, image masking, maximum-likelihood supervised classification, and identification of land cover change using ENVI 5.3. The strengths of this study are: (i) multi-temporal analysis through the use of Landsat images, (ii) atmospheric correction, which reduces the uncertainty of the data due to atmospheric effects, (iii) binary masking, which maximizes the accuracy of the lake area, and (iv) maximum likelihood classification, which maximizes the analysis of the pixels. Results showed that the water category decreased from 362.94 km2 (95.02%) in 1988 to the lowest point in 2002 at 103.03 km2 (26.97%), and then rose to 189.20 km2 (49.53%) in 2022. The soil class rose from 0.58 km2 (0.15%) in 1988 to 201.63 km2 (52.79%) in 2002, then decreased from 2002 to 2022 to 98.48km2 (25.78%). In the case of vegetation, the area grew from 18.45 km2 (4.83%) in 1988 to 77.31 km2 (20.24%) in 2002, and finally expanded to 94.30 km2 (24.69%) in 2022. Results of the change detection showed that in 1988-2002, 48.71% of the study area was changing from water to land. Conversely, 2002-2022 showed some recovery in ecology, with 11.51% of the study area recovering to water, from bare soil. Generally, the work showed that between 1988 and 2002, water loss was enormous, and only partially recovered in the following decades, providing valuable information for water management of a critical ecosystem.

title: Agricultural Input Subsidy Programmes and Household Welfare in Ghana: An Empirical Assessment
abstract: Purpose: This study evaluates smallholder farmers’ participation in Agricultural Input Subsidy Programmes (AISP) and examines the effects of participation on their wellbeing and farm productivity in Ghana. It also assesses whether AISP participation improves livelihood outcomes, particularly income, food security, consumption, and household assets. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study employed a sequential explanatory mixed-methods research design and a multi-stage sampling technique. The study collected quantitative data from 1,099 smallholder farmers in five regions of Ghana. The study collected data through structured, interviewer-administered questionnaires and qualitative interviews using an interview guide. The study used descriptive statistics, Probit regression, and Endogenous Switching Regression (ESR) to analyse participation and welfare outcomes while accounting for selection and endogeneity. Research Limitation: The cross-sectional design limits the ability to observe long-term changes at the household level, and the findings are conditioned by the assumptions underlying the econometric models and the quality of self-reported farm and welfare data. Findings: The findings indicate that AISP participation is significantly associated with demographic, farm, institutional, and environmental factors. Beneficiary farmers experienced improved livelihood outcomes, including higher income, food security, consumption, and asset accumulation compared with non-beneficiaries. AISP participation also enhanced farm productivity, particularly among farmers producing maize and rice. Qualitative evidence further indicates that timely access to subsidised fertiliser and improved seed is important for realising the programme’s productivity and welfare benefits. Practical Implication: The Ministry of Food and Agriculture should expand programme coverage and strengthen targeting and distribution through a digital database of smallholder farmers. This would improve beneficiary identification, transparency, and the effectiveness of input delivery. Social Limitation: The benefits of the programme may differ across farmers because of differences in gender, education, farm size, access to extension, market conditions, and agro-ecological circumstances. Originality/Value: The study contributes by integrating AISP participation, farm productivity, and household welfare within a sequential explanatory mixed-methods framework. It further addresses selection and endogeneity in programme participation through ESR and an instrumental-variable diagnostic, providing a more context-sensitive assessment of welfare effects.

title: CONCEPTUAL MODEL FOR COMPREHENSIVE DEVELOPMENT OF RURAL TERRITORIES BASED ON DIVERSIFICATION OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS’ ACTIVITIES
abstract: The article is devoted to the development of a conceptual model for comprehensive development of rural territories based on diversification of agricultural producers’ activities. The relevance of research is determined by the need to combine economic sustainability of agribusiness with increased employment and improved quality of life for rural population, as well as the development of infrastructure and non-agricultural economic activities. The study aims to provide a theoretical foundation for and structure a model that integrates government regulation, regional planning, scientific and educational support, and initiatives from enterprises within agro-industrial complex. The research employs a systems approach, statistical and comparative analysis, scenario modeling and an assessment of multiplicative effects. Based on data from implementation of state program “Comprehensive Development of Rural Territories” for 2020-2024 and proceedings of Novgorod region, the following key directions for diversification are identified: processing, service maintenance, rural tourism, logistics and development of local value chains. A four-stage implementation model is proposed: analysis and typology of territories, modeling of development scenarios, coordination of programs and contractual terms, implementation through infrastructure, financial and educational instruments. Projected direct, indirect and induced effects have been estimated based on scenario assumptions for agritourism cluster in Novgorod region – including the potential contribution to the gross regional product, employment, budget revenues and investment activity. The scientific novelty lies in the integration of diversification of agricultural producers’ activities and a multiplicative assessment of territorial development. The practical significance of results is associated with the possibility to apply this model in the preparation of regional programs and projects for comprehensive development of rural areas.
journal: Vestnik of Kazan State Agrarian University

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) FOR ACCOUNTING AND ANALYTICAL SUPPORT IN THE MANAGEMENT OF CROP PRODUCTION AND EXPORTS
abstract: The article examines the possibilities of using artificial intelligence in the system of accounting and analytical support for managing crop production and export operations. The relevance of the study is associated with the growing amount of accounting, production, logistics and foreign economic information that agribusiness enterprises need to process, particularly under the unstable conditions of the Ukrainian economy. The study identifies the main areas of AI application for automating accounting procedures, analyzing production costs, inventories and revenues, forecasting production indicators, detecting deviations, and supporting management decisions. Particular attention is paid to linking accounting data with information on crop yields, resource consumption, inventories, logistics, export contracts, settlements with counterparties and foreign currency transactions. Such integration provides a more complete basis for assessing production efficiency, determining the causes of changes in costs and financial results, and responding to deviations in a timely manner. An approach to integrating AI tools into the accounting and analytical system of agribusiness enterprises is proposed, taking into account the specific conditions of agricultural production and export activity in Ukraine. The study also considers the use of AI for processing primary and export documents, identifying inconsistencies between accounting and operational data, forecasting production costs and yields, and assessing the possible impact of logistics changes on export results. The main benefits and risks of AI use are outlined, including dependence on data quality, protection of confidential information, possible algorithmic errors, and excessive reliance on automated recommendations. It is emphasized that AI should complement rather than replace accounting procedures and professional judgement. The proposed approach can be used as a basis for further improvement of digital accounting and analytical systems in Ukrainian agribusiness enterprises and for strengthening information support for production and export management.
journal: Eastern Europe: Economy, Business and Management

title: Identification of climatic factors and growth stages in the prediction of fibre yield and fibre quality traits in rain-grown cotton
abstract: Understanding how and when environmental conditions influence overall crop performance is crucial for optimising the development of genotypes to a specific breeding target environment. We focused on economically important traits of Australian rain-grown cotton including fibre yield and quality traits, which have not been investigated comprehensively. The aim of the study was to identify relevant environmental factors, and the timing and extent of their impact on rain-grown cotton production. We used a data driven approach to analyse the relationship between ten climate related environmental factors across various plant growth stages and eight fibre yield and quality traits, using a large-scale field dataset of 9,283 records collected over 23 years at 4 locations, with 53 unique year-location combinations. We applied eight complementary statistical models including stepwise, penalised and Bayesian linear regression, regression-tree based ensemble methods and deep learning frameworks to (1) select the most essential environmental covariates affecting rain-grown cotton production, and (2) evaluate the predictive performance of these models. Results suggested that the environmental impacts on rain-grown cotton production were trait and growth-stage specific. Number of rainy days and solar radiation were identified as the most influential environmental factors for fibre yield traits, vapour pressure deficit at maximum daily temperature was the most influential factor for majority of fibre quality traits. However, each analysed trait was influenced by multiple environmental factors across multiple growth stages (rather than a single factor or a single growth stage). These influential covariates explained a wide range of variation in the traits, accounting for 5.8% to 68.2%. Using the best-fit random forest model, our findings revealed non-linear relationships between key environmental covariates and the traits. These results will be crucial for future genetic evaluations and analyses of genotype-by-environment interaction effects in rain-grown cotton, which must account for the influence of the environment on plant performance. Furthermore, these methods can be applied to other species to identify critical growth stages and environmental factors which most influence crop performance.

title: A MobileNet-enhanced diagnostic framework for accurate tomato leaf disease identification in smart farming
abstract: Plant diseases pose a major threat to global food security, causing up to 40% annual crop losses. Tomatoes are particularly vulnerable to fungal, bacterial, and viral infections that significantly reduce yield and quality. Deep learning has emerged as a powerful tool for automated plant disease diagnosis; however, many high-performing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) remain computationally expensive and unsuitable for mobile deployment. This work presents a comprehensive investigation of tomato leaf disease classification using a MobileNet-based transfer learning approach optimized for lightweight, real-time applications. The model was trained on the tomato subset of the PlantVillage dataset, comprising 18,345 images distributed across ten distinct classes. Extensive data augmentation, fine-tuning, and hyperparameter optimization were applied to enhance generalization. The proposed MobileNet model achieved a test accuracy of 95.76%, with macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1-scores exceeding 95%. ROC and Precision-Recall analyses yielded macro AUC values of 0.982 and 0.961, respectively, demonstrating strong discriminative capability. Comparative experiments showed that MobileNet provides the best trade-off between accuracy, parameter count, and inference speed when compared with MobileNetV2, MobileNetV3, ShuffleNet, and EfficientNet-B0. These results confirm that the proposed MobileNet model is a robust and efficient solution for tomato disease detection and is well-suited for real-world agricultural applications, particularly in resource-limited environments where mobile-based diagnostic tools can significantly support early intervention and reduce crop losses.

title: PEOS-Net: a Prototype-Energy Open-Set Network for robust tomato leaf disease recognition beyond the closed-world assumption
abstract: Deep convolutional networks now reach high accuracy on curated plant disease benchmarks such as PlantVillage, but nearly all reported systems assume a closed world in which every test image belongs to a known class. In the field, a diagnostic system will meet symptoms, crops, backgrounds or damage types absent from its training taxonomy, and a closed-set classifier will confidently mislabel them, undermining trust in automated crop-advisory tools. We introduce the Prototype-Energy Open-Set Network (PEOS-Net), built on a frozen EfficientNet-B0 backbone with a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) and two parameter-distinct heads that share this representation: an exponential moving average (EMA) prototype memory that drives classification, and a classifier-head branch that yields a free-energy out-of-distribution score. The two scores are fused into one hybrid open-set score; the normalization ranges, fusion weight and rejection threshold are selected on a held-out calibration split and never on the final test partition. We evaluated on an eight-class tomato subset of PlantVillage with two disease classes held out as unknowns, and compared against maximum softmax probability (MSP), out-of-distribution detector for neural networks (ODIN) and OpenMax baselines sharing the same backbone. PEOS-Net reached 93.87% closed-set accuracy (weighted F1 0.9392). Over five random seeds it achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.8695 ± 0.0202, an area under the precision-recall curve (AUPR) of 0.8723 ± 0.0192, an open-set classification rate (OSCR) of 0.8363 ± 0.0142 and a false-positive rate at 95% true-positive rate (FPR@95%TPR) of 0.4853 ± 0.0645 (mean ± SD). It outperformed all three baselines on every open-set metric, although the baselines had higher closed-set accuracy (96.5%). In a same-model ablation the hybrid score (AUROC 0.8610) exceeded the distance-only (0.7208) and energy-only (0.8413) scores; a paired bootstrap gave a gain over energy-only of +0.0198 (95% CI 0.0134–0.0262). Weak correlation between the two scores (|r| < 0.06) and low overlap of their errors indicate that they carry complementary information. Because the unknown classes come from the same PlantVillage source, the results support a controlled open-set study rather than validated field deployment.

title: Contact and Weight-Based Yield Monitoring Technologies for Major Root and Tuber Crops in Korea
abstract: Root and tuber vegetables, including potatoes, radishes, sweet potatoes, and carrots, are important components of Korean upland agriculture, yet harvesting and yield determination remain less mechanized and digitally integrated than cereal production. This review integrated contact- and weight-based yield measurement technologies applicable to Korean root and tuber crop harvesting, with emphasis on load-cell systems, conveyor weighing, hopper/bin weighing, impact-force sensing, and integrated multi-sensor approaches. Korean and international studies were checked in relation to sensing principles, harvester integration, calibration, dynamic measurement, spatial yield mapping, and field applicability. The literature shows that direct load-cell-based measurement provides the most physically interpretable basis for harvested mass estimation, while conveyor systems are particularly suitable for continuously conveyed crops such as potatoes and radishes. Hopper and cart weighing provide practical alternatives for semi-mechanized operations, including sweet potato harvesting, whereas impact sensing offers compact measurement but is more sensitive to crop trajectory, vibration, inclination, and mechanical damage. Korean studies have demonstrated promising sensor-level performance for potatoes and radishes; however, field-scale implementation remains constrained by vibration, slope, soil and debris contamination, tare drift, crop transport delay, limited standardization, and differences in harvester architecture. Integration of direct mass sensing with GNSS, IMU, belt-speed sensing, machine-state information, and machine vision provides a promising pathway toward reliable yield mapping. The synthesis indicates crop-specific pathways: continuous conveyor weighing after soil separation for potatoes; dynamically compensated event/impact sensing for radishes; low-impact hopper, cart, or batch weighing for sweet potatoes; and post-cleaning weighing for carrots. The main remaining gap is integrated field validation under realistic throughput, vibration, slope, headland transitions, and field-scale conditions. Future studies should report accuracy together with throughput, calibration burden, spatial-lag error, contamination effects, cost, and field repeatability.

title: TDTimexer: A Carbon Price Forecasting Model Integrating Time–Frequency Enhancement and Cross-Variable Dependency Modeling
abstract: Carbon price series exhibit nonlinear fluctuations, multi-scale temporal patterns, and complex dependencies among influencing variables, making accurate forecasting challenging. To tackle these challenges, we introduce CPO-TDTimexer as a framework for forecasting carbon prices. First, the maximal information coefficient (MIC) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are combined to identify informative input variables. Next, a Temporal Enhancement and Spectral Adaptation (TESA) module is developed to adjust frequency responses through learnable spectral weights, extract trend and seasonal components, and preserve original sequence information through residual fusion. Differential cross-attention (DCA) is then introduced into Timexer to strengthen cross-variable dependency modeling and reduce the interference of redundant information. Finally, key model hyperparameters are tuned with the crested porcupine optimizer (CPO). The framework’s effectiveness is demonstrated through experiments in the carbon markets of Guangdong, Hubei, and Shanghai. Compared with the original Timexer, CPO-TDTimexer yields average reductions of 24.48% in MAE, 22.35% in RMSE, and 25.02% in MAPE. Ablation studies further confirm the complementary contributions of TESA, DCA, and CPO. Diebold–Mariano tests support the statistical significance of the forecasting improvements achieved by CPO-TDTimexer over the benchmark models.

title: Data-Driven Multi-Objective Optimization of Low-Carbon Heating Systems in Cold Regions of China: A Case Study of Harbin
abstract: The transition to clean heating in cold regions faces challenges from extreme weather and high emissions. This study develops a dynamic modeling and surrogate-based multi-objective optimization framework for a solar-ammonia hybrid heating system. A lumped-parameter model simulates energy flows, and year-long Harbin meteorological data produce a physically consistent dataset via lumped-parameter simulation. A feedforward neural network with a residual autoregressive structure predicts temperature increments, preserving thermal inertia; it achieves RMSEs of 0.16 °C (indoor) and 0.61 °C (tank) over 168 h, including 48-h blind forecasting. This fast surrogate is embedded in NSGA-II to minimize carbon, cost, and discomfort via a climate-compensated curve and hysteresis dead-bands. Pareto analysis yields trade-offs: the carbon–comfort optimum attains 80.62 kg CO2/week and 104.85 °C·h discomfort; the cost–comfort optimum costs ~60 CNY/week. Three-dimensional optimization confirms aligned carbon and cost. TOPSIS selects a final strategy that, versus constant setpoints, reduces carbon by 30.3% and cost by 45.3% over 168 h by leveraging thermal mass and reducing boiler starts. Annual ammonia co-firing lowers CO2 from ~560 to 510 kg. The proposed integration of physics-informed simulation, residual autoregressive neural surrogates, and multi-objective evolutionary optimization provides an effective methodology for intelligent control of renewable hybrid heating systems in cold climates, contributing to deep decarbonization and energy savings.

title: Predictive Information in Reported Forced Outages for Short-Term Power Generation Forecasting: A Surrogate-Controlled Spatio-Temporal Forecasting Study
abstract: Reported forced outages may provide forecast-relevant information for short-term power generation forecasting. This study examines whether their predictive contribution in spatio-temporal Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) can be distinguished from the generic effect of adding an input channel. Hourly ENTSO-E data for Poland were evaluated over 12 quarters of 2022–2024 using a rolling-origin design, eight random seeds per quarter, and four architectures. A surrogate-controlled design decomposed the conventional ablation contrast into an information component and a channel component. The pooled information component was 0.77 MW (95% confidence interval [−0.60, 2.15]), while the channel component was −1.52 MW (95% confidence interval [−3.16, 0.11]); both varied substantially across quarters. Under matched information and equal tuning, no graph architecture differed significantly from the non-graph Temporal Fusion Transformer. However, because the original publication times of outage messages could not be reconstructed, the results do not establish that outage information was available at the corresponding forecast origins or that it provides predictive value in real time. The study evaluates forecast accuracy only; operational effects are not assessed.
