title: Forecasting Gold–Brent–U.S. Dollar Return Connectedness: Persistence Versus Macro-Financial Information
abstract: This study investigates whether U.S. macro-financial indicators improve one-step-ahead forecasts of return connectedness among gold, Brent crude oil, and the U.S. Dollar Index beyond autoregressive persistence. We estimate a time-varying Total Connectedness Index (TCI) using a TVP-VAR model with a 10-step generalized forecast-error variance decomposition and historically calibrated initialization. The U.S. Consumer Price Inflation is in line with the scheduled release dates, while predictors without historical data are not considered for the main analysis. Six forecasting models are evaluated using chronological validation and expanding-window estimation over 374 out-of-sample observations (8 May 2024–10 March 2026). The AR(2) benchmark achieves the lowest root mean squared error (RMSE=0.4898, out-of-sample R2=0.9768), compared with 0.4908 for macro-financially augmented linear regression and 0.5313 for XGBoost combining autoregressive and external predictors. The augmented XGBoost model produces 17.65% higher mean squared forecast loss than AR(2) (Holm-adjusted Diebold–Mariano p=2.10×10−5). Rolling-origin SHAP analysis attributes 94.91% of aggregate mean absolute feature attribution to the two lagged TCI predictors, indicating that historical connectedness dominates the attribution structure of the fitted nonlinear forecasting model. Exploratory inflation-regime comparisons do not provide robust evidence of a discrete 3% threshold. Within the evaluated three-market connectedness target, selected macro-financial predictors, one-step forecasting horizon, and 374-observation test period, none of the alternative models improved upon the AR(2) benchmark. These findings highlight the importance of historically consistent target construction, information availability, and persistence-aware forecasting benchmarks. They do not establish that macro-financial information generally lacks predictive value or that nonlinear forecasting models are inherently inferior.

title: Heavy Metal Transfer Dynamics and Human Health Risk Assessment in Vegetables Grown on Sewage Sludge-Amended Soils in Nyeri County, Kenya
abstract: Sewage sludge is increasingly used as an organic fertilizer in Kenyan peri-urban agriculture, yet concerns persist regarding heavy metal transfer to edible crops and associated health risks. This study evaluated the magnitude of cadmium (Cd), chromium (Cr), and lead (Pb) transfer from sewage sludge-amended soil to kale (Brassica oleracea) leaves and assessed non-carcinogenic health risks to consumers in Nyeri County, Kenya. A Repeated Measures Longitudinal Design was employed with paired soil and kale sampling from 50 plots across wet and dry seasons. Each plot served as its own control, and linear mixed models with random intercepts for plot were used to quantify metal-specific transfer efficiencies. Results showed that soil concentrations significantly exceeded leaf concentrations for all metals in both seasons (p < 0.001). The Linear Mixed Model (LMM) revealed a significant Soil × Metal interaction (χ2 (2) = 14.8, p < 0.001), with estimated soil-to-leaf transfer slopes of 0.183 (Pb), 0.235 (Cr), and 0.271 (Cd). Mean Target Hazard Quotient values were highest for Cr, followed by Cd, and lowest for Pb. Hazard Index values were significantly higher in the dry season (0.00568 ± 0.00422) than in the wet season (0.00383 ± 0.00285; p < 0.001) yet remained substantially below the regulatory threshold of 1.0. These findings indicate negligible non-carcinogenic health risk from the consumption of kale grown on sewage sludge-amended soils under the assessed exposure scenario. However, the elevated transfer efficiency of Cd warrants continued monitoring. This study underscores the need for Kenya to develop national guidelines for the safe agricultural use of sewage sludge, drawing on international benchmarks to ensure consumer safety while supporting sustainable soil amendment practices.

title: Whittle–Matérn Roughness Covariance for C-Band SAR Inversion over Bare Agricultural Soil
abstract: This study evaluates whether the Whittle–Matérn (WM) covariance representation improves pixel-wise SAR inversion over bare agricultural soil which can exhibit scale-dependent roughness. WM includes a smoothness parameter that controls covariance and roughness spectrum shape and has a Gaussian–Gamma scale-mixture interpretation. It was compared with exponential, Gaussian, and powered exponential (PE) covariance models within the same modified extended advanced integral equation model. Co-registered RADARSAT-2 and Sentinel-1 observations provided five channels for inversion. All experiments used identical observations, ancillary inputs, parameter bounds, objective function, and multi-start optimization settings. The analysis focused on the three co-polarized channels, for which covariance structure enters the scattering model directly. At a co-polarized residual tolerance of 2dB, WM produced model-consistent solutions for 425 of 439 retained pixels, compared with 384, 387, and 423 pixels for the exponential, Gaussian, and PE models, respectively. Its blind point ratio was 3.19%, versus 12.53%, 11.85%, and 3.64%, respectively. On the 342 pixels retrievable by all four models, WM gave the lowest mean absolute error for all channels except Sentinel-1 VH. The largest improvement was obtained for Sentinel-1 VV, where WM reduced RMSE to 0.501dB, compared with 0.820dB, 0.786dB, and 0.606dB for the exponential, Gaussian, and PE models. WM also yielded the most complete retrieval maps and scene mean soil moisture estimates closest to the available SMAP and station reference means. These results show that covariance representation is a material source of structural difference in unregularized multi-sensor SAR inversion.

title: Month-Aware Optical and SAR Temporal Fusion for Growing Season Crop Classification
abstract: Growing season crop classification supports agricultural monitoring, yet cloud-affected optical observations, fragmented fields, and uncertainty in mapped labels complicate reliable evaluation. Public crop maps also differ in class definitions and spatial detail, so agreement with one map does not establish independent ground accuracy. This study presents MAOSTFNet, a month-aware temporal fusion network that combines Sentinel-2 optical data and Sentinel-1 SAR data from June through September 2019 in Jilin Province. Twelve optical features and four SAR features are embedded separately, mixed by a spatial gate, and aggregated with calendar month embeddings and temporal attention. Dense decoding predicts four crop classes, while an auxiliary crop-class boundary head adds a spatial structure objective. The fixed evaluation uses corrected SAR features, grid-grouped subsets, seed 42, one checkpoint rule, a shared test mask, and one metric implementation. MAOSTFNet achieved 0.947 OA, 0.933 AA, 0.912 Kappa, 0.937 Macro F1, and 0.882 mIoU, with margins of 0.016, 0.019, 0.025, 0.014, and 0.024 over the strongest comparator. Removing August reduced Macro F1 by 0.050, and masking optical input reduced it by 0.080. Across test-support crop-coverage thresholds from 0 to 20 percent, Macro F1 ranged from 0.920 to 0.944 and remained highest among five evaluated implementations. These scores describe fixed-seed agreement with mapped labels in Jilin Province in 2019. The main support is crop-enriched, adjacent subsets have no exclusion buffer, and the results do not establish independent ground accuracy or geographically separated generalization.

title: River Freeze-Up and Breakup Prediction Using Multi-Station Adaptive Echo-State Temperature Forecasting and Reach-Specific Criteria
abstract: Freeze-up and breakup dates in cold-region rivers strongly influence winter navigation closure, spring navigation resumption, and navigation safety during ice runs. However, river-ice transitions are reach-specific and cannot be reliably determined from instantaneous air-temperature thresholds alone, while recursive multi-step forecasting is vulnerable to error accumulation. To address these challenges, this study develops the SAG-AL-ESN-HRCLRC framework for multi-station air-temperature forecasting and reach-specific freeze-up and breakup date determination in the Harbin, Heihe, and Raohe reaches. The framework extracts inter-station dependence from lagged correlations of temperature increments and combines correlation-based spatial weighting with annual, semiannual, and diurnal periodic encodings. It further employs an echo state network with an adaptive leaking rate and introduces horizon- and regime-conditioned closed-loop residual correction to reduce recursive error accumulation in both target- and auxiliary-station forecasts. Across the three scenarios, the 10-run evaluation yields an average MAE of 1.980 ± 0.193 °C, an RMSE of 2.544 ± 0.218 °C, and an R2 of 0.9761 ± 0.0030. The corresponding Step-1 and Step-56 MAEs are 1.195 ± 0.167 °C and 2.040 ± 0.230 °C, respectively. The corresponding freeze-up and breakup date prediction errors across the three ice seasons from 2023–2024 to 2025–2026 are 1.33 and 1.22 days, respectively. These results indicate that, under the data conditions and reach-specific criteria considered in this study, the proposed framework can provide useful temperature-based information for river-ice monitoring, navigation management, and ice-season safety decisions.

title: The Impact of Village Leadership Integration on Rural Residents’ Satisfaction: Evidence from China’s “Yijiantiao” Policy Reform
abstract: How grassroots governance structures shape residents’ evaluations is central to understanding the effectiveness of rural governance reform. Effective and participatory grassroots institutions provide an important foundation for the sustainable rural development. Using two waves of panel data from the China Rural Revitalization Survey (CRRS), conducted in 2020 and 2022, this study applies fixed-effects models to examine how the “yijiantiao” policy, under which the village Party secretary concurrently serves as villagers’ committee chair, affects rural residents’ satisfaction with the work of their villagers’ committees, as well as its potential channels and boundary conditions. The results show that, first, the “yijiantiao” policy significantly increases residents’ satisfaction with villagers’ committee performance. This finding is robust to alternative estimation models and outcome measures, propensity score matching, accounting for concurrent policies, and excluding early-adopter villages. Second, the mechanism analysis supports collective economic development and public service provision as two potential pathways. Leadership integration increases collective net assets, sanitation staffing, and expenditure on agricultural production services, whereas its effect on road construction and maintenance expenditure is not statistically significant. Third, the positive effect is stronger in villages led by younger Party secretaries. Prior employment within the public-sector also shows some evidence of strengthening the effect, whereas differences across groups defined by education and economic elite backgrounds are not statistically significant. Fourth, the moderation analysis indicates that formal democratic participation, including residents’ assemblies, strengthens the positive effect, whereas informal authorities, such as clans, weaken it. These findings suggest that the governance benefits of leadership integration are closely related to organizational capacity and the conditions for resident participation. This study highlights the importance of assessing leadership arrangements and provides valuable references for sustainable rural development policies.

title: Operations research model for inventory optimization through statistical demand analysis and linear programming
abstract: Efficient inventory management requires integrating demand uncertainty, costs, and replenishment decisions within a quantitative framework. This research develops an Operations Research model for inventory optimization by integrating statistical analysis, demand forecasting, ABC classification, Economic Order Quantity [EOQ], Safety Stock [SS], Reorder Point [ROP], and Mixed-Integer Linear Programming [MILP]. The procedure uses historical data to estimate demand parameters and establish differentiated replenishment policies. These parameters are subsequently incorporated into the mathematical model to determine order quantities and periods while minimizing relevant inventory costs. The results reveal a significant economic concentration among priority items and an approximate 46% reduction in relevant inventory costs compared with the baseline policy. Sensitivity analysis confirms the stability of the proposed model under the evaluated variations in demand, holding costs, and safety stock. Overall, the integrated framework provides a reproducible quantitative approach for connecting predictive analysis with prescriptive optimization and supporting cost-efficient inventory and logistical decision-making.

title: MECHANISMS OF FORMATION OF GRADIENT ZONES IN STRENGTHENING COATINGS
abstract: The working components of soil-tilling machinery operate under extreme conditions involving impact-abrasive and corrosive wear, which underscores the critical need for developing multilayer composite coatings with a gradient of properties. This study analyzes the kinetics of interphase diffusion and the mechanisms of thermal decomposition within the "L53 steel – Sormite – platinum buffer sublayer – titanium nitride" system during vacuum annealing (at 500 °C, with holding times ranging from 0 to 300 minutes). The research methodology relies on the combined use of scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Rutherford backscattering spectrometry (RBS), which allow for both detailed visualization of cross-sectional morphology and high-precision quantitative determination of elemental depth profiles. Iterative modeling of the experimental spectra using the SIMNRA software package enabled the reconstruction of the structural parameters of the multilayer system. It was determined that a platinum sublayer with a thickness of 50–100 nm functions as an effective diffusion barrier only during the first 60 minutes of thermal exposure. Extending the holding time beyond this point triggers irreversible degradation of the barrier layer, accompanied by the formation of extensive diffusion zones 10–20 μm in width. The activation of an intergranular mass-transport mechanism leads to a fivefold increase in the effective diffusion coefficient. Processes involving the uncontrolled doping of titanium nitride with chromium and iron–leading to the formation of multicomponent solid solutions (Ti, Cr, Fe)N – as well as the Ostwald ripening of the carbide phase and the development of vacancy pores via the Kirkendall mechanism, have been identified. The established quantitative relationships governing the thermal evolution of interphase boundaries provide a scientific and methodological foundation for optimizing vacuum heat-treatment parameters, predicting the durability of protective coatings, and extending the service life of agricultural machinery.

title: USE OF UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLES IN AGRICULTURAL TECHNOLOGIES OF THE KURSK REGION
abstract: The introduction of unmanned aerial vehicles into agricultural technologies of the Kursk Region in 2021–2026 was analysed. The relevance of the study is determined by the extensive cropped area, the high concentration of crop production and the need to perform technological operations within limited agrotechnical periods. The materials included regional digital transformation documents, federal strategies and experimental legal-regime documents, publicly available information on operator training, agricultural production data and a published case of winter-crop treatment by an agricultural drone. Content analysis, comparative assessment, chronological systematisation and performance modelling were applied. It was found that separate elements of technological and personnel readiness have been formed in the region: there is experience in ultra-low-volume spraying of winter barley, operator competencies are being developed, and agricultural drones are included in the regional digitalagriculture agenda. At the same time, practical diffusion is constrained by the airspace-use regime, the absence of the Kursk Region from the territories covered by the experimental legal regime for agricultural unmanned aircraft systems, and the need for special flight approvals. For a design mode with a speed of 18 km/h, a working width of 8.5 m, a time-utilisation factor of 0.55 and a 12-hour shift, the estimated output was about 101 ha per shift. Treating 10% of the regional cropped area within 30 days would require approximately 50 simultaneously operating aircraft of this capacity. In the short term, crop monitoring, mapping and research-and-production trials are the most realistic applications, whereas large-scale aerial chemical operations require a dedicated safe operating regime.

title: CMIP6-Informed Climate Change Projections and Their Implications for Agricultural Sustainability in Hisar District, Haryana
abstract: Climate change poses increasing risks to agricultural systems in semi-arid regions through rising temperatures, changing rainfall variability, increasing crop-water requirements and growing pressure on groundwater resources. This study assesses potential future climate-related risks to agricultural sustainability in Hisar district, Haryana, using a scenario-based framework that combines the historical climatic context of 1990– 2025 with published CMIP6-informed scenario information under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. We consider representative future periods to examine how climate-related agricultural risks progress. We translate scenario-based temperature changes into indicative crop-productivity responses using previously established Hisar-specific crop-temperature elasticities for wheat, mustard, cotton, and bajra. The assessment further examines the potential implications of warming and rainfall variability for agricultural water requirements and groundwater stress. Results indicate that wheat exhibits the greatest temperature-related sensitivity among the crops considered, followed by mustard, while cotton and bajra show comparatively lower direct temperature sensitivity. The findings also indicate that rising temperatures may increase evapotranspiration and irrigation needs, potentially intensifying groundwater extraction pressure in areas already experiencing groundwater stress. The study highlights the interconnected nature of climate, crop productivity, and agricultural water security in Hisar. It emphasises the need for heat-resilient crop planning, efficient irrigation, groundwater conservation, and integrated climate–water management. The study provides a district-level scenariobased assessment that can support future climate-resilient agricultural planning and more detailed modelling using highresolution climate, crop-water and groundwater datasets.
journal: International Journal of Engineering and Advanced Technology

title: Application of Transformer Model in Predicting Housing Price in Selected Vietnamese Provinces
abstract: This paper selects an appropriate machine learning model to forecast real estate and apartment prices across several major provinces and cities in Vietnam. While we primarily deploy the Transformer, we also experimented with other machine learning algorithms, such as Linear Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest, to demonstrate the Transformers superior performance. We automatically collected raw data from Vietnams largest real estate website and then preprocessed, analysed, and evaluated it. The analysis revealed that building a prediction model on a single dataset yields fewer effective results than splitting the data into two distinct sets, one for landed properties and the other for apartments, and developing separate models for each product category. Building two independent prediction models allows effective use of each product types unique characteristics, improving the accuracy and efficiency of machine learning for real estate price prediction.
journal: International Journal of Innovative Technology and Exploring Engineering

title: Visión artificial para la detección de plagas en cultivos de tomate: revisión sistemática de la literatura
abstract: Phytosanitary monitoring is an essential activity for reducing production losses caused by pests in tomato crops grown under protected agriculture conditions. In recent years, computer vision and deep learning methods have gained relevance as tools capable of automating agricultural image detection and analysis processes. Despite these advances, there is still a need to determine which techniques have been used, under what conditions they have been evaluated, and what performance they have reported, particularly in protected agriculture and small-scale production contexts. This study aims to examine research published on these technologies and assess their potential incorporation into participatory agricultural monitoring schemes. To this end, a systematic review of scientific literature published between 2020 and 2026 was conducted following the methodological guidelines proposed by Kitchenham. The review was developed through the stages of planning, study search and selection, and information synthesis, considering previously established inclusion and exclusion criteria. As a result, fifty studies related to image processing, artificial intelligence, and phytosanitary monitoring were selected and analyzed. Among the main findings of the review, several studies reported high-performance levels for deep learning models in tasks involving the automatic identification of symptoms associated with pests and other crop-related conditions. The synthesis identified the main techniques, data, application contexts, and reported performance levels, providing reference elements for assessing their potential incorporation into participatory agricultural monitoring schemes.
journal: Revista de Investigación en Tecnologías de la Información

title: Antinutritional Factors in Edible Plants and Their Effects on Nutrient Bioavailability: Molecular Mechanisms, Evidence Gaps, and Nutritional Implications
abstract: Antinutritional compounds are naturally occurring constituents of edible plants that can influence the digestion, bioaccessibility, and bioavailability of essential nutrients. Their nutritional effects depend on their chemical properties, concentration, food matrix, processing conditions, dietary composition, and host physiology. This critical review examines how major antinutritional factors, including phytate, oxalates, tannins and other polyphenols, protease inhibitors, lectins, and selected additional compounds, interact with nutrients in plant-based foods. The principal mechanisms include mineral chelation, complex formation and precipitation, protein–polyphenol interactions, inhibition of digestive enzymes, and modifications in nutrient solubility and intestinal transport. These interactions can reduce the availability of minerals such as iron, zinc, and calcium or interfere with protein digestion, although their magnitude varies among foods and dietary contexts. Food-processing techniques, including soaking, cooking, dehulling, milling, germination, and fermentation, can modify antinutrient concentrations and improve selected nutritional properties. Nevertheless, these interventions may also cause nutrient losses or alter other beneficial food constituents. Plant breeding, biofortification, and the development of low phytate varieties offer additional opportunities to improve nutrient availability, but potential trade-offs involving seed performance and agronomic characteristics require consideration. A critical synthesis of the evidence highlights an important distinction between nutrient content, bioaccessibility, and actual absorption. Chemical assays and simulated digestion models provide valuable mechanistic insights but cannot independently establish improvements in human nutritional status. Major research gaps include inconsistent analytical methods, limited representation of underutilised edible plants and traditional mixed diets, and insufficient integration of laboratory findings with human absorption studies. Future research should prioritise standardised analytical procedures, validated digestion models, transparent reporting of dietary and processing conditions, and appropriately designed human studies. Integrating these approaches can support evidence-based food processing, crop improvement, and dietary recommendations while preserving the overall nutritional value of edible plants.

title: A Protocol for Dissection, Immunostaining and Mounting of the Drosophila Visual System.
abstract: The Drosophila visual system is a powerful model for exploring how neuronal diversity is generated and integrated into functional neural circuits - a central question in developmental neuroscience. It comprises the retina and four distinct neuropils: the lamina, medulla, lobula, and lobula plate, which together form a highly organized structure that processes visual input from the retina and relays it to the higher centers of the brain. During development, the visual system undergoes significant remodeling. During larval development, neuroblasts are progressively generated from the neuroepithelium and divide asymmetrically to produce diverse neuronal subtypes by integrating spatial and temporal patterning programs. These neurons then differentiate and form precise synaptic connections that build the functional circuits of the adult visual system. These dynamic processes can be reliably studied using immunostaining across larval, pupal, and adult stages. Herein, we provide a detailed, reproducible protocol for dissecting and immunostaining the developing and adult Drosophila visual system. We primarily focus on representative imaging of larval neuroblasts to highlight spatiotemporal patterning and neuronal specification, and to visualize adult neuropil morphology. This provides a robust framework for visualizing the developing Drosophila visual system.

title: WNT5A-Associated Osteogenic Enhancement Contributes to the Protective Effects of OPG-Fc in Glucocorticoid-Associated Femoral Head Osteonecrosis.
abstract: Steroid-induced osteonecrosis of the femoral head (SONFH) is a progressive orthopedic disorder characterized by an imbalance between bone resorption and bone formation. Although receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa-B ligand (RANKL) blockers are known to suppress osteoclast activity, whether they also promote osteogenesis and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated whether osteoprotegerin-Fc (OPG-Fc) exerts osteoprotective effects in SONFH and whether wingless-type MMTV integration site family, member 5A (WNT5A) signaling is involved. A rat SONFH model was established using lipopolysaccharide (LPS) combined with methylprednisolone sodium succinate (MPS), and bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) were cultured under glucocorticoid-containing conditions. OPG-Fc, the WNT5A antagonist box5, and Wnt5a knockdown were used, and analyses included micro-computed tomography (micro-CT), histological staining, transcriptome sequencing, quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), and western blotting. Our results demonstrated that OPG-Fc significantly improved bone trabecular microarchitecture, reduced empty lacunae and tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP)-positive cells, and increased cartilage thickness in vivo. In vitro, OPG-Fc promoted osteogenic differentiation while inhibiting adipogenic differentiation of BMSCs. Transcriptome and protein analyses revealed significantly higher WNT5A expression following OPG-Fc treatment. Importantly, pharmacological blockade of WNT5A with box5 and Wnt5a knockdown partially attenuated OPG-Fc-associated pro-osteogenic effects, whereas box5 had limited effects on anti-resorptive marker changes. These findings suggest that OPG-Fc exerts dual protective actions in SONFH by suppressing bone resorption and enhancing osteogenic differentiation in association with WNT5A-related signaling. This study provides new mechanistic insights into RANKL blockade therapy and offers a potential molecular target for early intervention in SONFH.

title: Mesenchymal Stem Cell Therapy for Multiple Sclerosis: Harnessing Immunological Properties.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease triggered by damage to the central nervous system (CNS). This CNS damage is caused by the attack of autoreactive T cells against the myelin sheath. Genetic and environmental factors contribute to the development of MS, and the condition causes serious disabilities and exerts substantial health burdens. Although various disease-modifying agents have been developed, they have critical limitations; hence, effective interventions are required. In this context, cell transplantation therapy using mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), hematopoietic stem cells, neural precursors, neural stem cells, and induced pluripotent stem cells is considered a feasible alternative therapeutic approach. MSCs are adult stem cells that differentiate into multiple lineages and exert immunomodulatory, neuroprotective, and neuroregenerative effects. Therefore, MSCs are considered a promising treatment option for MS owing to their ease of isolation and low immunogenicity. This review summarizes the potential therapeutic benefits of the latest MSC-based approaches for MS treatment in animal models and humans. Furthermore, the review discusses the immunological role of MSCs and future directions for their applications.

title: AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery.
abstract: Animal behavior is a critical endpoint in preclinical pharmacology, toxicology, and therapeutic discovery, yet conventional behavioral scoring remains labor-intensive, low-dimensional, and difficult to reproduce across laboratories. Artificial intelligence (AI) can now quantify behavior from video with greater spatial, temporal, and phenotypic resolution. This review summarizes how object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents are reshaping behavioral phenotyping. General-purpose object detectors rapidly localize and track animals, whereas open-source pose-estimation tools extend measurement beyond centroid tracking to body-part trajectories and fine motor patterns; paired with supervised classifiers, they have matched human scoring and exceeded some commercial systems. Technical accuracy alone does not establish behavioral construct validity or pharmacological validity. Unsupervised methods such as Motion Sequencing represent drug responses and disease-model phenotypes as structured changes in behavioral states rather than only as predefined endpoints, providing high-dimensional fingerprints of pharmacological action. Segmentation and tracking foundation models may reduce annotation burden but require validation across species, strain, sex, apparatus, and paradigm. AI agents may assist with literature review, code generation, analysis auditing, and figure production but must remain within transparent, human-supervised workflows. In behavioral pharmacology, pose estimation is established as a measurement method and emerging as a drug-effect endpoint, supervised classification and unsupervised segmentation are emerging, and foundation models and agents remain prospective. AI-enabled behavioral analysis can become a reproducible phenotyping layer for drug discovery and toxicology if researchers adopt open pipelines, rigorous validation, and reporting standards, rather than replacing one opaque measurement system with another.

title: Adenine Promotes Osteogenic Differentiation and Suppresses Osteoclastogenesis.
abstract: Estrogen deficiency disrupts the balance between osteoblast-mediated bone formation and osteoclast-mediated bone resorption, resulting in progressive bone loss. Although AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) regulates the differentiation and activity of both skeletal cell lineages, the role of endogenous purine metabolites in this process remains poorly understood. We investigated adenine responses and AMPK-associated signaling in skeletal-cell models and assessed histological and protein changes in ovariectomized (OVX) mice. In C2C12 cells and primary bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells, adenine increased AMPK and cAMP response element-binding protein phosphorylation; upregulated runt-related transcription factor 2, alkaline phosphatase, collagen I, and osteopontin; and enhanced alkaline phosphatase staining and matrix mineralization. In C2C12 cells, Compound C and AMPKα knockdown attenuated these osteogenic responses. In receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand-stimulated RAW264.7 cells and bone marrow-derived macrophages, adenine increased AMPK phosphorylation and reduced osteoclastogenic signaling, tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase staining, and cathepsin K expression. Responses to adenine remained detectable after AMPKα knockdown in RAW264.7 cells. In OVX mice, dietary supplementation with 0.02% adenine for 10 weeks was associated with increased histology-derived trabecular thickness and bone area fraction and changes in bone-associated protein expression. No significant differences were detected in the assessed renal and hepatic indices. These findings support further preclinical investigation of adenine in estrogen-deficiency bone loss.

title: Artificial intelligence-powered solutions for environmental sustainability in medical imaging: a scoping review.
abstract: PURPOSE Growing evidence shows that medical imaging has a substantial environmental impact. With the increasing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in clinical settings, it is important to explore how this technology may support environmental sustainability. METHODS Literature searches were performed across eight databases (PubMed, Wiley Online Library, Embase, Web of Science platform, the Cochrane Library, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature Ultimate, Google Scholar, and MedRxiv) for the period January 2020-June 2026. Full-text sources in the English language were eligible for inclusion. The Joanna Briggs Institute checklists were employed for risk of bias assessment. All data were analyzed using a textual narrative synthesis. RESULTS In total, 23 studies were deemed eligible for inclusion. The literature proposed that AI tools in medical imaging could be used to minimize energy consumption by optimizing patient scheduling, decreasing scanner idle times and workstation use, reducing computed tomography over-scanning, contrast agent usage, and radiation dose, harnessing low-field magnetic resonance imaging, and curtailing low-value imaging. However, AI technologies may also impact the environment in harmful ways. CONCLUSION Although AI-powered solutions hold promise for improving sustainability in medical imaging, the true environmental impact remains largely unexplored. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE The findings of this work further strengthen the dual role of AI adoption in medical imaging related to environmental sustainability.

title: Critical Issues in Building Information Modeling (BIM) Workflows: A Multi-Case Study Review
abstract: Building Information Modeling (BIM) is increasingly used in structural and infrastructure engineering as a digital environment supporting design, construction, and asset management processes. However, the application of BIM to complex infrastructures still presents several critical issues, particularly when dealing with non-standard geometries, existing structures, and heterogeneous information flows. This paper presents a technical synthesis based on six case studies developed by the authors through BIM-based approaches applied to different structural and infrastructural fields, including bridges, road infrastructures, underground utility networks, and complex structural systems. The study analyzes the main issues encountered during the modeling, coordination, and data exchange phases, highlighting the strategies adopted to address them. The identified challenges mainly concern the geometric modeling of irregular or existing structures, interoperability issues between BIM software and structural analysis software, the management of point clouds and survey-derived data, as well as the definition of appropriate Levels of Development and Information. The paper provides a technical overview of recurring issues and offers useful indications for improving BIM workflows applied to structural and infrastructure engineering.
journal: International Journal on Engineering, Science and Technology

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY IN NIGERIAN SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES: A MIXED-METHOD REVIEW
abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) form the backbone of Nigeria's economy, comprising over 80% of registered businesses and contributing approximately 48% of national GDP. Yet, despite this strategic importance, artificial intelligence (AI) adoption for environmental sustainability among Nigerian SMEs remains limited, with scarce empirical evidence of outcomes. This study examines the pathways through which AI tools influence green practices in Nigerian SMEs, identifies structural and contextual barriers to adoption, and proposes policy and institutional interventions to accelerate environmentally beneficial AI uptake. Using a concurrent mixed-methods design, quantitative data were gathered from 144 SMEs across Nigeria's six geopolitical zones, complemented by qualitative case studies of three agri-tech firms: AirSmat Inc. (Lagos), Green Eden (Plateau State), and Anatsor (Plateau State). Analysis was grounded in the Socio-Technical-Environmental (STE) model. Five key AI-enabled sustainability pathways were identified: resource optimisation, climate adaptation planning, demand forecasting for waste reduction, real-time anomaly detection, and automated ESG reporting. SMEs applying AI in precision agriculture recorded eco-metric gains of 22–35%. Overall adoption stands at just 32.6%, constrained by high technology costs (81%), inadequate digital skills (71%), unreliable infrastructure (69–77%), and insufficient regulatory incentives (67%). Access to external partnerships emerged as the strongest predictor of positive AI-sustainability outcomes. Edge computing shows promise in low-connectivity contexts. Policy recommendations include stable energy infrastructure, targeted AI financing, and capacity-building programmes. This study offers the first systematic empirical assessment of AI's ecological impact within Nigerian SMEs, with implications for business owners, policymakers, financial institutions, and development organisations.
journal: International Journal of Advanced Academic Research

title: Waters adds AI agents to analytical testing
Smart Agricultural Marketplace: A Mobile-First Digital Platform for Direct Farmer-ro-Buyer Trade with Real-Time Pricing and UPI-Based Payments
abstract: Many farmers in India find it hard to sell their crops at a good price. They often depend on middlemen. They do not always know the prices in other markets. Payments can also come late. In this paper we describe the Smart Agricultural Marketplace. It is a mobile app that lets farmers and buyers deal with each other directly. Farmers list their crops. Buyers search the list and send requests or bids. The app also shows market prices and supports UPI payment. We plan to build the app with Flutter, and to use Firebase and Node.js for the backend. The app will work in more than one language, including Kannada and English. So far we have built a web prototype. It shows the seller and buyer screens: listing a crop, searching crops and tracking requests. Payment, live market prices and testing with real farmers are still to be done. We hope the app will help farmers find buyers, compare prices and sell with more confidence
