title: Interacting scalar-fermion two-component dark matter in a gauged $\boldsymbol{U(1)_{B-L}}$ model
abstract: We propose an interacting two-component dark matter model based on a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ extension of the Standard Model, which also accommodates neutrino masses through the type-I seesaw mechanism. The dark sector consists of a Dirac fermion $χ$ and a complex scalar $S$, which can both be stable without imposing an additional discrete symmetry and are directly coupled by a gauge-invariant Yukawa interaction. The resulting conversion, semi-conversion, and semi-annihilation processes lead to a genuinely coupled freeze-out. After imposing collider and dark matter constraints, we identify viable solutions away from the $Z'$ resonance for both mass hierarchies, $m_S > m_χ$ and $m_S < m_χ$. Despite the strong direct-detection constraints, part of the surviving parameter space remains within the reach of next-generation experiments.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks and their classical surrogates on long-range strongly correlated models
abstract: We benchmark quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs) and their classical surrogates for phase differentiation in one-dimensional strongly correlated systems with beyond-nearest-neighbour terms. Using an anisotropic Heisenberg spin chain and an extended $t$-$t'$ Fermi-Hubbard model as representative spin and fermionic testbeds, we train QCNN classifiers on labelled ground-state datasets and map out finite-size phase diagrams. In hybrid setups, we employ Pauli backpropagation to express the QCNN measurement as a weighted sum of Pauli-string expectation values to be evaluated directly on input states, and study how truncation parameters control the trade-off between approximation accuracy and the size of the resulting Pauli expansion. Robust convergence is achieved for the Heisenberg model under aggressive truncation, whereas the Fermi-Hubbard model requires substantially looser thresholds, resulting in a sharp growth in retained Pauli strings and evaluation cost. Our results contribute to charting where hybrid quantum-classical training is viable for learning strongly correlated quantum states, and provide practical guidance for choosing truncation regimes in Pauli backpropagation-based surrogates.

title: Modeling and Analysis of Cooling Induced Isotropic Nematic Transitions in Pharmaceutical Liquid Crystals
abstract: This paper studies the phase transition from an isotropic to a nematic liquid crystal driven by controlled cooling, motivated by the manufacturing of next-generation pharmaceutical drugs. Using the non-isothermal Ericksen model for liquid crystals with a variable degree of orientation, we formulate the problem as a stiff, quasilinear system of parabolic partial differential equations. We establish a consistent thermodynamic framework, prove the well-posedness of the system, and conduct a rigorous asymptotic and numerical scaling analysis of the moving phase boundary in a cylindrical cell subjected to bottom-wall convective cooling. Our analysis identifies a critical sample thickness that separates two distinct physical regimes. Below this threshold, the transition follows the cooling dynamics and the material remains quasi-isothermal. Above the thickness threshold, bulk thermal diffusion governs the dynamics, imposing a dominant thermal delay characterized by a concave quadratic propagation front. These results demonstrate that scaling from laboratory characterization to industrial production fundamentally alters the spatial thermal history of the material, providing a predictive mathematical framework to optimize cooling protocols for kinetic arrest.

title: Quantifying Local and Global Fidelity of Nonlinear Embeddings
abstract: Dimension reduction methods are chosen by a common claim: t-SNE and UMAP preserve local structure, and PCA preserves global structure. Checking it on given data takes local and global scores on one scale and a test that compares two maps. Both scores come from one curve. The locality profile is the chance-corrected share of each point's k nearest neighbors that a map keeps, over all neighborhood sizes. Its value at k = 10 is the local fidelity L, and its mean over 30 to 50 percent of the data is the global fidelity G. We prove that at the midpoint the profile is the agreement on which half of the data is near each point, a rank correlation of the distances. Because L and G are one statistic, two maps can be tested against each other. The LG reversal test applies to any two dimension reduction methods. It decides, with a block-jackknife p-value, whether one map is more local and the other more global, and returns the scale at which to change maps. On 156 maps of twelve datasets with up to 1.38 million points, G agrees with established global scores at 0.89 and 0.96, and 2,000 points estimate it. The test confirms the usual claim on seven datasets. On both retail datasets and both rolled-up manifolds, it finds the neighbor embeddings more global. In an agent memory of one million passages, the two maps cross at 150,000 passages (p = 2.6e-5). Applications span pathology, single cells, supply chains and AI agent memory.

title: When AI Agents Act on Our Behalf: A Taxonomy of Human-Agent Interaction Failure
abstract: AI agents write and execute code, manipulate user interfaces, and transact on their users' behalf. We ask what forms failure takes in human-agent interaction, and how those forms change as agents act with greater autonomy. From 695 documented incidents in two public repositories, we developed 12 failure modes bottom-up within three interaction stages adapted from Amershi et al.'s guidelines, coding the autonomy at which each arose. What a person can do when an agent fails depends on how much the agent completes between points of user involvement--a property fixed at deployment. Therefore, the same model on the same task can fail differently under different configurations. All 12 modes appear at both low and high autonomy, and rising autonomy changes the form each failure takes. Users need controls between full delegation and full manual work, and neither incident records nor agent benchmarks reach the interaction where these failures occur.

title: Seeing the Unseen: Unified Visible--Invisible Motion for Physically Consistent Video Generation
abstract: Recent advances in video generation have achieved impressive visual quality, yet they often fail to produce physically consistent dynamics due to the lack of explicit modeling of underlying physical processes. Existing approaches either rely on simulators with strong assumptions or use coarse semantic guidance, and further struggle to effectively inject physical priors into generation models. In this work, we propose Seeing the Unseen, a unified framework for physics-grounded video generation. Our approach decomposes the problem into two stages: learning physical dynamics and injecting them into video synthesis. First, we introduce a lightweight Particle-based Graph Dynamics Simulator (PGDS) that learns generalizable physical interactions from data and predicts plausible 3D motion trajectories. Second, we propose a Visible--Invisible Motion Field (VIMF) that captures both motion observable in the input frame and motion that emerges over time due to object dynamics. This representation enables more complete and structured motion guidance compared to conventional physical signals. By integrating these trajectories into a diffusion-based generator, our method produces videos that are both visually coherent and physically consistent. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved motion accuracy, interaction consistency, and reduced physical artifacts compared to strong baselines.

title: The Agentic AI Kerr Lab: LLM Agents for Kerr Microscopy Experiments with Magnetic Skyrmions
abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are topological spin textures that can be observed directly by magnetic microscopy and driven by fields and currents, which makes them a model system for fundamental physics and candidates for spintronic devices. Magneto-optical Kerr microscopy is a method to image them in real time; however, most experiments use an inefficient cycle of consecutive imaging, analysis and excitation in which every step requires the judgement of the experimentalist operating the setup. Here we present the Agentic AI Kerr Lab (AgentKerr), in which an agent based on a large language model operates this cycle automatically and efficiently on a Kerr microscope. Rather than relying on pattern detection by a language model, a convolutional neural network trained on Kerr images turns live images into skyrmion observables such as position, size and shape, on which the agent bases its decisions. The architecture lets agents operate the instruments safely, as every hardware action is checked deterministically against an action policy, independently of the agent that issues it. With no procedure given, the agent determines by itself how to create, tune and move skyrmions, and writes its own analyses. The approach can be transferred to other spin textures and points towards magnetic imaging experiments in which the researcher poses the question and the agent finds the way to realize the experiments that yield the answer.

title: Recurrence in Sequence Space: How Epistasis Mimics Shared Ancestry
abstract: Sequences in a protein family do not explore the sequence space freely: folding, packing, and binding couple residues, so the set of viable sequences is irreducibly correlated, a phenomenon referred to as epistasis. We show that such correlations lower the \emph{intrinsic dimension} $d_{\rm IN}$ of sequence space, counteracting the concentration of measure and broadening the distribution of pairwise distances. Consequentially, they make it likely that independently evolving lineages \emph{recur}, approaching one another by chance long after they last shared an ancestor. Using Kac's lemma we show that the logarithmic mean recurrence time grows linearly with the intrinsic dimension, $\log τ_{\rm rec} \propto {d_{\rm IN}}$ for typical sequences, so strongly constrained (low-dimensional) families recur often and generate sequence similarity that carries no genealogical signal. We establish this first in a solvable Ising-like model with tunable correlation, then in a real protein family using Potts models and Markov chain Monte Carlo, where $d_{\rm IN}$ remains predictive of recurrence even in multi-basins landscapes. Because recurrence is a property of the evolutionary process rather than of any estimator, it bounds the recoverability of deep history for distance-based and likelihood methods alike.

title: Agent Stack for ML Training Lifecycle: Generation, Validation, and Optimization
abstract: Production model development requires repeated architecture design, platform integration, debugging, training, and evaluation. We present an agent stack deployed at LinkedIn with two independently usable agent loops: AutoTorch for model generation and migration, and AutoResearch for model optimization. AutoTorch generates PyTorch models and training pipelines for TensorFlow migration, XGBoost replacement, and new-model development. Executable validation hooks check platform API compliance, trainability, and conversion fidelity on sampled data, guiding iterative repair before engineer review and full-scale distributed training. AutoResearch explores architecture and training-configuration changes through expert-steered or autonomous experimentation. An external orchestrator manages parallel trials, experiment history, candidate selection, and wall-clock budgets across agent sessions. A shared runtime preserves execution state independently of agent reasoning and allocates GPUs separately from agent execution. Across ranking, content understanding, and recommendation workloads, AutoTorch completed generation and full-scale training in 92 of 115 workflow runs (80%). Of these, 77 (83.7%) produced models meeting post-training quality requirements. In a separate cohort, AutoResearch improved the primary task metric on held-out data for 28 of 100 production pipelines. Engineering teams estimate that the stack reduced elapsed end-to-end migration time from approximately eight weeks to two weeks, a 4x speedup.

title: Dependence-Aware Risk Assessment and Optimal Design of AI-Agent Safeguard Systems
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on safeguards to prevent unauthorized actions while preserving legitimate service. However, existing risk assessments often focus on individual safeguard performance while overlooking dependence among safeguard decisions. This paper develops a dependence-aware framework for risk assessment and optimal design of multi-component AI safeguard systems, jointly selecting configurations and operating policies for sequential layered screening and selective verification. We establish stochastic comparisons of layered-screening error probabilities and invocation costs under lower-orthant ordering. For selective verification, we characterize exactly which policies have error probabilities and review costs that respond monotonically to stronger dependence under supermodular ordering. For a fixed first stage and reviewer, we show that the optimal routing map is a two-threshold rule in the first-stage likelihood ratio. An accompanying open-source software package, Dependence-Aware Policy Optimization Algorithms (DAPOA), facilitates the practical implementation of the proposed framework. Numerical experiments show that ignoring dependence can lead to inaccurate risk assessments and infeasible safeguard designs, with independence-based selections violating security requirements in six of eight scenarios. An empirical study using four LLM safeguards on benchmark-derived agent actions further demonstrates the practical implications of dependence modeling. Under the principal operating setting, dependence-aware selection lowers held-out total cost by 39.6% relative to independence-based selection.

title: Helical Magnetic Nature of $β$-Mn Structured CoZn Thin-Films Determined by a Bayesian Approach to Modeling Polarized Neutron Reflectivity Data
abstract: Chiral magnetic materials can host skyrmions and hence are of interest for numerous spintronic applications including low-power storage. To reach this goal, room temperature operation and a thin film form are needed. We have studied the chiral magnetism in a $β$-Mn structured CoZn sputtered film, with a Curie temperature of $\approx 130$ °C, by means of polarized neutron reflectometry (PNR) in order to reveal its magnetic field-temperature phase diagram. In bulk this material has a helimagnetic ground state. Here we use PNR data to show that the helimagnetism survives in a CoZn film only 100 nm thick, roughly half a helical period. Given the subtlety of differentiating the helical state from a uniform state with reduced interfacial magnetism, we have developed and employed a Bayesian approach that uses model selection to analyze our PNR data and to map out the field-temperature phase diagram of our thin film.

title: BEEF: A Hybrid Integrated Photonic Simulation Framework
abstract: A Python framework is presented that retains first-principles electromagnetic modeling while extending simulation to devices whose length and geometric complexity place them beyond the practical reach of either method alone. The Bridged Engine for eigenmode expansion (EME) and finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) (BEEF) partitions a device into sections which are simulated using either EME or FDTD independently developed Maxwell solvers depending on what best suits each section's geometry, and cascades the resulting responses. BEEF calibrates the EME propagation constants against FDTD-measured phase accumulation, providing a mode identity verification diagnostic across solver interfaces. For a 2x2 multimode-interference splitter, the hybrid result agrees with full-device FDTD to within 0.59% (bar) and 0.76% (cross) across the C-band; a tapered variant agrees to within 0.87% and 2.01%, respectively. For a directional coupler, effective-index calibration reduces cut-position dependence 167-fold. A circuit-level cascade reproduces the measured Fabry-Perot resonance lineshape and free spectral range while exploring the coupler-length and arm-length design plane through post-processing of four cached simulations. Finally, we use BEEF to simulate a 167.3 um-long 4x4 MMI-based 90-degree optical hybrid that is computationally impractical for full-device FDTD, with a reduced-length variant confirming close agreement in transmission and relative phase.

title: TAP-Out: Tracking Any Point in 360° via Outpainting
abstract: Tracking points that leave the camera's field of view (FoV) requires reasoning about unobserved scene dynamics, a fundamentally different problem from tracking visible correspondences. We present TAP-Out, an offline method that makes this out-of-view (OOV) reasoning explicit by leveraging generative video outpainting as a world-model prior. Given a narrow-FoV input video, TAP-Out outpaints a complete 360° equirectangular video, locates target objects within the panoramic scene via video object segmentation, and synthesises object-centred perspective crops on which standard in-frame trackers operate. This decoupled design composes off-the-shelf foundation models without requiring task-specific architectural modifications. On the TAPVid360 benchmark, TAP-Out achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving OOV tracking accuracy by approximately 3x over the best prior method. We demonstrate its flexibility on out-of-frame object segmentation and detection and we provide detailed diagnostic analyses across motion regimes, static versus dynamic content, and hallucination quality, characterising when and why the approach succeeds or fails.

title: Nonconformal Distortion and Local Orientation Reversal in the Fourier Circuit of a Modular-Addition Transformer
abstract: We study the local differential geometry of a Fourier-based modular-addition circuit in a one-layer transformer whose algorithm has previously been reverse-engineered. For each of the five key Fourier frequencies, we restrict the model's multilayer perceptron (MLP) contribution to a corresponding Fourier input plane and readout, and measure its directional Beltrami coefficient under continuous input perturbations. Whereas nondegenerate restrictions of ideal complex multiplication are conformal, the trained maps exhibit nonconformal distortion (median $|μ|=0.304$--$0.446$), spatial organization in the Beltrami argument, and regions of local orientation reversal. The median across frequencies decreases from $0.939$ at initialization to $0.390$ after training. The key-frequency planes also show lower median distortion than most random-plane controls, although their distributions overlap and the coordinate frames differ in conditioning. Across 500 checkpoints in one training run, most of the aggregate reduction in Beltrami magnitude occurs before the principal increase in the measured Fourier-circuit formation. At the individual-input level, Beltrami magnitude shows negligible association with the correct-logit margin ($|ρ|\leq0.026$). Late-checkpoint measurements across six runs show comparable distortion for most selected frequencies. These results provide a quantitative characterization of local deformation in a frequency-projected component of an identified neural circuit, complementary to its algorithmic reconstruction.

title: Residual error modelling for process-based flood frequency analysis
abstract: Flood frequency analysis (FFA) is essential for flood risk management and infrastructure design, yet estimates of flood quantiles remain strongly influenced by the length and representativeness of available streamflow record. We introduce UQ-flood, a process-based flood-frequency framework that integrates a stochastic weather generator, a process-based hydrologic model, and a residual error model developed at the annual-maximum scale. The framework explicitly addresses the presence of errors in simulated annual flood peaks generated by models calibrated to continuous streamflow data. We apply UQ-flood to three Canadian watersheds with contrasting hydroclimatic conditions using 30 years of meteorological and streamflow observations. Long-record empirical annual-maximum estimates provide the primary benchmark, while Bayesian Generalized Extreme Value estimates based on short and long records provide secondary statistical benchmarks for the central flood-quantile estimates. Across the three watersheds, the central UQ-flood estimates remained within the confidence intervals for the long-record discharge quantiles, although their relative proximity to the empirical estimates varied by watershed and return period. Process-based simulations without residual-error correction systematically underestimated flood magnitudes, whereas applying the residual error model shifted the estimated flood-frequency curves toward the long-record observational benchmarks. The framework also propagates residual predictive variability directly at the annual-maximum scale. These results demonstrate that annual-maximum residual error modelling can correct for systematic discrepancies in process-based flood estimates and support central flood-quantile estimation even at sites with short data records.

title: Application of Blockchain Technology in Agricultural Product Traceability
abstract: In today's world, people's living standards have been gradually improving, and their health awareness has been constantly increasing; consumers need better quality and experience when shopping. The process of selling agricultural products needs to be further developed with digital transformation. The construction of an agricultural product traceability system based on blockchain technology enables full process tracking of the agricultural product supply chain for the integrity and transparency of traceability information; furthermore, because of its decentralized feature and immutability of transaction records, it provides a novel way for transforming and upgrading traditional agricultural product retail processes. In order to make clear the direction of this field, we attempt to summarize and review the existing domestic and international literature within the scope of blockchain technology and agricultural product sales: analyze the current research status, theoretical foundation of blockchain tech, case study and analysis as well as policy support, identify the shortcoming in current academic research (sample, method, depth, scenario).In doing so, it aims to clarify the research context and development status of the field, organize mainstream research perspectives, key technologies, and typical applications, analyze existing deficiencies and controversial issues, and thereby provide a forecast for future research directions. This offers theoretical references and insights for subsequent studies, promoting further deepening and improvement of related research.
journal: Frontiers in Computing and Intelligent Systems

title: Research on the Synergistic Model of Pasture and Photovoltaic Complementarity and Ecological Restoration Technology in the Cold Highland Pastoral Areas of the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau
abstract: Driven by the goal of ' double carbon ', the large-scale wind power photovoltaic base in Shagehuang accelerates the layout. The alpine pastoral area of the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau bears the triple pressure of clean energy development, grassland ecological restoration and animal husbandry efficiency. However, the alpine region is ecologically fragile, the recovery period is long, and the grass-livestock balance constraints are strong. The existing results are scattered and out of line with engineering needs. This paper systematically reviews the system mechanism, application mode, key technology, ecological zoning evaluation and engineering practice progress of photovoltaic-pastoral complementary. The results showed that array shading, precipitation redistribution and wind field weakened the inter-plate-under-plate-edge microhabitat, and the vegetation-soil response was non-linearly differentiated along the drought gradient. The heat island effect was significant in the extremely arid area and the ecological positive feedback in the semi-arid area. The four models of natural grassland light grazing, artificial pasture mixed sowing, ecological restoration gradual and compound industry integration have their own applicable boundaries; array adaptation, grass species configuration, grazing control and water and fertilizer regulation constitute the key technical system. The two-dimensional zoning method based on ecological sensitivity and construction suitability tends to be mature, and the local-regional-global multi-scale effect framework is initially established. Aiming at the problem of disconnection between static results and engineering requirements, it is proposed to establish a long-term positioning monitoring network, clarify the multi-factor coupling threshold, develop a mechanism-data hybrid evaluation method, and formulate lightweight technical standards, so as to provide scientific reference for the large-scale development of plateau photovoltaic-pastoral complementary.
journal: Academic Journal of Science and Technology

title: Plant Disease Detection Using Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Plant diseases cause substantial crop losses, and timely diagnosis is difficult for growers without access to pathologists. This paper presents an image-based system that classifies 38 plant-disease and healthy-leaf categories across 14 crop species using transfer learning. A MobileNetV2 network pretrained on ImageNet is adapted in two phases: a new classification head is first trained on the frozen convolutional base, and the last 30 base layers are then fine-tuned at a lower learning rate with batch-normalization layers kept frozen. Training uses the PlantVillage dataset (54,305 images) with a stratified 70/15/15 split. On the held-out test set of 8,162 images the model achieves 97.35% accuracy and a macro-averaged F1-score of 96.27%, against 96.13% and 94.85% for a compact custom CNN baseline. Per-class analysis shows that errors concentrate in visually similar tomato diseases and in under-represented classes. The trained model is served through a Streamlit web application that returns the predicted class, a confidence score and the top three predictions. Because PlantVillage contains laboratory images and the split was made per image, the results are in-distribution estimates that require field validation. Key Words: plant disease detection, convolutional neural network, transfer learning, MobileNetV2, PlantVillage, precision agriculture.
journal: International Scientific Journal of Engineering and Management

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN THE CONTEXT OF TECHNOLOGICAL AND FOOD SECURITY: DRONES IN THE INDUSTRIAL ECONOMICS
abstract: The relevance of this study is caused by the need for close attention to strengthening Russia's food security, import substitution under sanctions pressure, and government-set goals to achieve technological sovereignty and the active digital transformation of the economy. Digitalization of logistics in the agricultural sector and food production is one of the most significant tools for increasing the efficiency and sustainability of business processes by minimizing raw material losses and ensuring the stability of raw material chains, especially in strategically important areas of economic activity, such as agro-industrial complexes. The study was conducted using the example of the implementation of Russian irrigation drones as an element of the digital transformation of agricultural business processes, facilitating import substitution. An analysis of the volume of hop defects on Russian plantations revealed signif-icant shortcomings in the system for monitoring and operational control of crop condition, as well as ineffective agricultural risk management. To resolve the identified problems, the authors proposed the introduction of specialized drone assistants that com-bine the functions of remote crop monitoring (shooting with multispectral sensors) and targeted irrigation systems. This solution will minimize crop losses caused by crop drying out and increase their productivity. The proposed digital solution will reduce the per-centage of defective products, ensure cost savings, and enhance the competitiveness of domestic hops by increasing the yield of suitable raw materials and reducing domestic enterprises' dependence on imported supplies.

title: Petani Muda di Era AI: Kesiapan Human Capital 5.0 dalam Transformasi Digital Pertanian Nusa Tenggara Barat
abstract: Digital transformation and the development of artificial intelligence (AI) are changing the competency needs of agricultural entrepreneurs. Within the framework of Human Capital 5.0, technology is positioned to enhance human capacity, making the readiness of human resources an important part of agricultural transformation. This study aims to analyze the readiness of young farmers in West Nusa Tenggara Province (NTB) in facing digital transformation by reviewing farmer regeneration, education, technology use, the structure of smallholder farmers, and agricultural economic performance. This research employs a descriptive quantitative approach with secondary data analysis. Secondary data is obtained from the 2023 Agricultural Census (ST2023). Analysis is conducted descriptively and uses Spearman correlation. The results indicate a moderately positive and statistically insignificant relationship between the proportion of young farmers and the RLS with technology use, with correlation coefficients of 0.503 and 0.406, respectively. Furthermore, the relationship between technology use and agricultural GDP per UTP has a correlation coefficient of 0.539, indicating a strong positive relationship, although it is not statistically significant. Meanwhile, the proportion of smallholder farmers has a very strong negative and significant relationship with agricultural GDP per UTP, with a correlation coefficient of -0.927.
journal: Prosiding Seminar Nasional Lembaga Penelitian Dan Pendidikan (LPP) Mandala

title: National‑Scale Soil Erosion Risk Mapping in Zambia Using the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE)
abstract: Soil erosion poses a significant threat to agriculture and land sustainability across sub-Saharan Africa. In this study, we assess the extent and spatial distribution of soil erosion in Zambia using the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) model. This model incorporates environmental parameters, including rainfall erosivity (R), soil erodibility (K), slope length and steepness (LS), cover-management (C), and support practices (P) to estimate average annual soil loss across the landscape. To achieve this, we integrated a Digital Elevation Model (DEM), satellite-based precipitation data, global soil databases, and land cover maps within a GIS environment. Furthermore, high-resolution orthoimages were used to identify and digitize existing conservation practices (e.g., contour farming, terracing), to accurately assess the P-factor. Results showed that the majority of the country is characterized by very low erosion susceptibility. However, critical erosion hotspots were identified in areas lacking conservation measures, exceeding tolerable soil loss thresholds. The study results confirmed that areas implementing erosion control exhibited significantly reduced soil loss, highlighting the effectiveness of these land management strategies. The derived spatial erosion patterns provide valuable insights for prioritizing conservation measures and sustainable land use planning in Zambia.
journal: IAEG 2026: Engineering Geology in a Rapidly Changing World - XV IAEG World Congress

title: Are Earthquake Early Warning and Prediction Systems effective, useful, and applicable for Risk Management in Costa Rica?
abstract: Increased attention to earthquake prediction and early warning systems aims to reduce disasters. However, several issues affect their transparency and reliability; many efforts have yielded inconclusive and unreliable results. We recommend more adaptive multi-modal cohesive information sharing systems that require integrated observation, surveillance, warning, alarm, and response instruments. Communications should be expedient, clear, and trustworthy to enable society to enhance preparedness, act effectively in emergencies, reduce vulnerability, and promote resilient recovery. The approach requires integrated protocols, community involvement, technological efficiency, and precise scientific and communication skills to avoid confusion and ensure effective risk management. Anticipation, prediction, prognosis, and forecast need to be clearly defined. Since frequent and intense seismicity has occurred for tens of millions of years and will not stop in the future, Costa Rica should prioritize proactive risk management, considering the unresolved limitations of precise and available data in its complex tectonic settings. Past and recent failed prediction efforts have caused false alarms, public fear, and economic harm. Advanced technologies like AI show promise but are still nascent and should support, not replace, preparedness. Early warning systems offer limited reaction time, are costly, often fail in rural or near-source areas, become overdependent on high-tech solutions, and create false senses of security. Worse, they undermine essential measures like building codes, public education, and hazard-based land use planning. The priority should be on communication, long-term resilience, and reducing vulnerability. The key to saving lives and economic loss lies in risk management, not in unreliable earthquake predictions and warnings.

title: Cassava Leaf Disease Detection using VGG16 Transfer Learning Based on Digital Images
abstract: Cassava leaf diseases reduce crop productivity, and farmers still diagnose them mainly by visual inspection, which is error-prone because the symptoms of different diseases look alike. This study develops an automated system for detecting cassava leaf diseases from digital images using transfer learning with the VGG16 convolutional neural network. A balanced subset of 1,000 images from the Cassava Leaf Disease Classification dataset, covering five classes (cassava bacterial blight, cassava brown streak disease, cassava green mottle, cassava mosaic disease, and healthy leaves), was divided into 70% training, 15% validation, and 15% test data. The images were resized to 224 × 224 pixels, normalized, and augmented. A VGG16 network pre-trained on ImageNet was fine-tuned with its first 14 layers frozen, a dropout rate of 0.5, and the Adam optimizer. The best model reached a validation accuracy of 94.37% and a test accuracy of 93.66%, with macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1-score of 94.38%, 93.88%, and 93.97%, respectively. These results show that VGG16 transfer learning can classify cassava leaf diseases accurately even with a limited dataset. A Flask-based web interface was also designed to present the predictions to users.
journal: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Engineering Applications (JAIEA)

title: Analysis of the Effects of Batch Size and Epoch Variations on MobileNetV2 for Mango Leaf Disease Classification
abstract: Mango (Mangifera indica L.) is one of the most widely cultivated horticultural crops due to its high economic value. However, leaf diseases remain one of the primary factors affecting crop productivity. Manual disease identification has several limitations, as it is time-consuming, highly dependent on the expertise of the observer, and inefficient for large-scale cultivation areas. This study aims to analyze the effects of epoch and batch size variations on the performance of the MobileNetV2 model for mango leaf disease classification using a transfer learning approach. The dataset consisted of 4,000 images representing eight classes: Healthy, Anthracnose, Bacterial Canker, Cutting Weevil, Die Back, Gall Midge, Powdery Mildew, and Sooty Mould. The dataset was divided into training, validation, and testing sets using an 80:10:10 ratio. Four training scenarios were then conducted using different combinations of batch sizes (16 and 32) and epochs (25 and 50 The experimental results demonstrated that the configuration with a batch size of 32 and 50 epochs achieved the best performance, obtaining an accuracy of 99.75%, while the precision, recall, and F1-score each reached 100%. These findings indicate that variations in batch size and number of epochs significantly influence the performance of the MobileNetV2 model, with the combination of a batch size of 32 and 50 epochs providing the most optimal classification performance for the mango leaf disease dataset.
journal: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Engineering Applications (JAIEA)

title: From Intelligent Systems to Trustworthy Agents: a Comprehensive Survey of Agentic Ai in Smart Healthcare
Procedimientos para evaluar el efecto de aplicación de bioestimulantes en germinación y desarrollo vegetativo de hortalizas
abstract: This study presents methodological procedures for evaluating the effect of biostimulants on the germination and vegetative development of vegetable crops, focusing on cucumber and pepper cultivation in Ecuador. Addressing the challenges of climate change and the need to diversify agricultural production beyond traditional monoculture, the study highlights the potential of biostimulants to enhance nutrient uptake, abiotic stress tolerance, and early vigor. The proposed methodology was implemented in two key phases: the germination phase, which evaluates variables such as final germination percentage, hypocotyl and radicle length (via digital analysis using ImageJ), dry biomass accumulation, and seedling vigor indices (SVI-I and SVI-II); and the vegetative development phase, which involves the periodic foliar application of solutions (at 15, 30, and 45 days) and the recording of plant height, stem diameter, number of active leaves, and root volume via water displacement. Overall, establishing these standardized protocols enables the collection of precise technical data to optimize the efficient use of biostimulants in specific horticultural systems.

title: RISING DEMAND FOR ANIMAL PRODUCTS AND FEED IN INDIA: PROSPECTS FOR PRODUCTION, TRADE, AND TECHNOLOGICAL ADVANCEMENT
abstract: India's livestock sector plays a major role in food security, rural livelihoods, agricultural diversification, and the supply of nutritious animal-source foods. Population growth, rising household incomes, urbanization, changing consumption preferences, and the expansion of food-processing industries are expected to increase demand for milk, meat, eggs, and other animal products over the coming decades. Meeting this demand will require simultaneous improvements in livestock productivity, feed availability, animal health, supply-chain efficiency, and technological innovation. Feed resources are particularly important because livestock production depends on the availability, nutritional quality, affordability, and year-round accessibility of feed and fodder. Competition for agricultural land, seasonal fodder shortages, climate variability, and fluctuations in oilseed meal and grain markets may constrain future expansion. The USDA Economic Research Service's 2025 assessment indicates that Indian demand for animal products may grow faster than supply under historical productivity trends and that additional feed imports may become necessary. This review examines the major drivers of animal-product demand, the present production outlook, feed-resource constraints, trade opportunities, and emerging technologies relevant to India's livestock economy. Potential interventions include precision feeding, improved fodder varieties, crop-residue treatment, silage production, alternative feed ingredients, genetic improvement, digital livestock management, disease surveillance, and climate-smart farming. The review argues that an integrated strategy combining productivity growth, efficient resource use, appropriate trade policies, and inclusive technology adoption is essential for a resilient livestock sector. Particular attention should be given to smallholder farmers, feed affordability, food safety, environmental sustainability, and the development of domestic feed supply chains.
journal: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology

title: ENSURING GLOBAL FOOD SAFETY: A COMMERCE AND AGRIBUSINESS PERSPECTIVE ON SUPPLY CHAIN RESILIENCE, REGULATORY HARMONIZATION, AND TRADE COMPLIANCE
abstract: Ensuring global food safety has emerged as a fundamental determinant of sustainable international commerce, cross-border agricultural trade, and macroeconomic stability. In an interconnected world characterized by elongated and highly fragmented agri-food supply chains, food safety is no longer merely a public health imperative; it represents a strategic commercial necessity governing market access, non-tariff trade barriers, transaction costs, and firm competitiveness. This research paper examines the multi-dimensional commercial dynamics of global food safety governance, focusing on the interface between Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) compliance, cold-chain logistics investment, private quality certification standards (such as GlobalG.A.P., BRCGS, and ISO 22000), and institutional trade facilitation. Grounded in New Institutional Economics and Transaction Cost Theory, the study investigates the structural, financial, and operational barriers encountered by agricultural producers, exporters, and agribusiness micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in developing economies, with specific empirical context drawn from Indian agricultural exports. Employing an explanatory, mixed-method analytical approach utilizing secondary macro-level trade datasets from UN Comtrade, the World Trade Organization (WTO), the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), APEDA, and interviews with export trade intermediaries, the study evaluates the incidence and economic ramifications of border rejection notifications, import alerts, and SPS-related non-tariff measures. The quantitative and thematic results indicate that compliance asymmetries, stringent maximum residue limits (MRLs), high certification recurring costs, and infrastructural bottlenecks in cold-chain integrity disproportionately penalize smallholder agricultural supply chains, creating substantial export revenue volatility. Furthermore, the findings reveal that while private food safety standards elevate transaction costs in the short run, institutionalized compliance mechanisms yield significant long-term commercial dividends by mitigating product recall risks, securing premium pricing in regulated global markets, and fostering supply chain traceability via emerging digital architectures such as blockchain-enabled provenance. The paper provides actionable commercial and policy recommendations, advocating for harmonized multilateral regulatory frameworks, cluster-level food safety infrastructure development, credit-linked financial subsidies for MSME certification, and capacity-building initiatives to integrate smallholders into sustainable, compliant global agri-food value chains.
journal: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology

title: A NOVEL HYBRID CLUSTERING AND ENSEMBLE LEARNING FRAMEWORK FOR AGRICULTURAL CROP RECOMMENDATION
abstract: Selecting a suitable crop for a given soil and climatic condition is an important decision-support task in precision agriculture. This paper investigates a hybrid data-mining framework that combines unsupervised clustering with ensemble classification for crop recommendation. The dataset contains 2,200 records, seven numerical attributes—nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), temperature, relative humidity, soil pH, and rainfall—and 22 crop labels. After stratified train-test partitioning, K-means clustering was fitted on standardized training features and its cluster assignment was appended as a one-hot encoded feature. A soft-voting ensemble comprising Random Forest, Extra Trees, and Histogram-based Gradient Boosting was then trained to predict the crop class. The proposed cluster-aware ensemble achieved 99.09% accuracy and a weighted F1-score of 99.09% on the 440-record test set. Extra Trees, used as a benchmark, achieved 99.55% accuracy, indicating that clustering augmentation did not outperform every individual model on this dataset. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the hybrid approach but also highlight the need for repeated cross-validation, external validation, and agronomic testing before deployment. The study contributes a reproducible hybrid pipeline and an evaluation protocol rather than claiming that the approach is universally superior.

title: Women at the Core of Climate-Smart Agriculture: Advancing Equity and Food Security through Empowerment
abstract: Climate volatility threatens global food security, particularly in developing nations where female farmers face severe resource barriers. This narrative review synthesizes empirical research published between 2010 and 2026 to evaluate women’s empowerment, climate-smart agricultural adoption, and household food security. Applying structured narrative frameworks, 44 academic studies and policy reports were synthesized across four major academic databases. The selected literature was analyzed using Feminist Political Ecology and the Women’s Empowerment in Agriculture Index conceptual frameworks. Findings reveal that conventional technical adaptation programs often fail by ignoring local power dynamics and increasing female unpaid care burdens. In contrast, gender-responsive interventions addressing land tenure, credit constraints, and information gaps generate strong economic benefits. Securing equal access to essential productive assets directly increases agricultural yields for female farmers. This productivity gain expands household dietary diversity, reduces child stunting, and strengthens climate shock absorption. Labor-saving equipment and solar micro-irrigation reduce drudgery while improving seasonal farm earnings. However, national climate policies often ignore gender metrics, lack gender-disaggregated data, and risk male control over profitable practices. Achieving sustainable food security requires moving from gender-neutral programs toward gender-transformative governance models. National frameworks must mandate joint land titling and protect female property rights. Public agencies and financial institutions should offer flexible credit programs, direct mobile digital advisories, and inclusive participatory technology design. Evidence confirms that targeted investment in female agricultural producers is essential for building efficient, fair, and productive agrifood systems across vulnerable communities.
journal: Journal of Agricultural Policy and Transformation

title: Optimizing Classification-Based Machine Learning Models for Bacterial Spot Disease Detection in Tomato Plants
abstract: Plant pests and diseases destroy up to 40% of global crop production each year, causing more than US$220 billion in losses [4]. Tomatoes are among the most widely consumed crops, with approximately 160 million tons consumed each year [13]. In Florida, bacterial spot, caused mainly by Xanthomonas perforans [9, 11] and favored by hot, humid, rainy weather, cost tomato growers almost $900,000 in the 2007–2008 season [2]. We hypothesized that infected tomato leaves differ measurably from healthy leaves in color and texture, and tested whether machine learning could detect these differences. Using 3,769 PlantVillage leaf images, we compared Logistic Regression, Ridge Classifier, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Support Vector Classifier (SVC) models with a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN). The tuned SVC performed best among the classical models (99.34% accuracy, 99.44% F1, ROC-AUC 1.00) and matched the CNN (McNemar’s test, p = 1.00). However, its accuracy fell sharply on rotated or brightened images, so field performance is likely lower. Machine learning shows promise for early detection of bacterial spot, but it must be validated on field images before practical use.
journal: International Journal of Secondary Computing and Applications Research

title: Advancing Sustainable Farming Systems Using AI: Evaluating Impact and Implementation Challenges
abstract: This study investigated the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) among farmers in North Karnataka, India, in the context of sustainable farming, covering perceived advantages, barriers to adoption, and farmer readiness. Drawing on the Attention, Interest, Desire, and Action (AIDA) model and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), a quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted. A structured questionnaire with five-point Likert items was administered to 100 farmers, and the data were analyzed with descriptive statistics, regression analysis, and moderation analysis. Farmers' awareness of AI was positively associated with the perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use of AI systems, though these effects were not significant at the 5% level and should be interpreted with caution. The strongest association was between readiness to adopt AI and behavioral intention to adopt. Perceived usefulness and government support were positively related to adoption intention, but government support did not significantly moderate the relationship between perceived usefulness and adoption intention. The findings suggest that affordable digital agricultural technologies, training, support services, and targeted policy are needed to increase AI adoption among farmers.

title: Peningkatan Kapasitas Lumbung Mataraman Melalui Digitalisasi Berbasis Augmented Reality (AR) di Kalurahan Gulurejo, Lendah, Kulon Progo
abstract: Lumbung Mataraman Gulurejo has the potential to be developed as an agriculture- and education-based tourism destination. This tourism concept integrates food production, food consumption, the natural environment, and social interaction as part of a tourism experience that supports the well-being of both managers and tourists. Observations indicate that the management of Lumbung Mataraman Gulurejo currently lacks digital promotional tools capable of reaching all segments of tourists, and that the harvest times for longan and grapes are unpredictable. Objectives of the community service project: (i) Strengthening human resources to increase grape and longan production in an effort to enhance marketing and green tourism at Lumbung Mataraman Gulurejo, Kulon Progo, DIY; (ii) To design an application using Augmented Reality (AR) technology capable of showcasing green tourism potential to enhance tourist services by providing real-time information on conditions at Lumbung Mataraman Gulurejo, Kulon Progo, DIY. The community service methodology included the following stages: socialization, implementation of AR technology and cultivation practices, mentoring, and ensuring the sustainability of the activities. The results of this community service project indicate that Lumbung Mataraman Gulurejo does not yet have a digital platform for promotional purposes; therefore, an AR-based application was developed as a means of transforming promotional efforts for managers, tourists, and potential visitors. Furthermore, the cultivation patterns for longan and grapes tend to be unpredictable and season-dependent, making it possible to implement alternative cultivation techniques such as off-season flowering and pruning. On the other hand, the need to develop marketing systems and innovations in longan and grape processing is a strategic effort to attract tourists and potential tourists to visit. Recommendations from the community service project include the need for a sustainability strategy to increase longan and grape production capacity, as well as the structured use of AR-based applications as a promotional tool for Lumbung Mataraman. Regarding marketing systems and innovation, it is essential to stay abreast of current trends to effectively reach consumers from all walks of life.

title: Uncertainty, Volatility, and Renewable Energy Stock Returns: Evidence From Regime‐Dependent and Machine‐Learning Forecasting Models
abstract: This study examines the predictability of renewable energy stock returns under economic, financial, and policy uncertainty within a real‐time forecasting framework. Using monthly data from May 2007 to May 2025, we compare conventional econometric models, shrinkage estimators, machine‐learning algorithms, and regime‐dependent forecasting models using a recursive expanding‐window design. Forecast performance is evaluated using statistical accuracy measures, robustness analyses, and an economic portfolio evaluation. The results show that nonlinear forecasting methods consistently outperform conventional linear benchmarks. Gradient boosting achieves the lowest forecast errors, while principal component regression provides stable performance across alternative evaluation designs. Regime‐dependent forecasting models improve directional prediction during periods of heightened financial uncertainty but generate more modest gains in forecast accuracy. Predictor‐importance analysis identifies financial‐market volatility as the dominant source of forecasting information, followed by oil‐market volatility and broader policy uncertainty. Overall, the findings demonstrate that combining multiple sources of uncertainty with flexible forecasting methods improves both statistical forecasting performance and the economic value of investment decisions. title: Hydrocalumite-Like Material Induces Early Osteogenic Priming and ECM Remodeling Without Effective Mineralization in Preosteoblasts.
abstract: Hydrocalumite-like phases, belonging to the layered double hydroxide family, are potential biomaterials for bone repair; however, their cellular effects remain incompletely understood. Here, we evaluated a hydrocalumite-like material of composition [Ca2Al(OH)₆]Cl·nH2O (abbreviated Ca2Al-Cl) in preosteoblastic MC3T3-E1 cells, assessing viability, adhesion/signaling, osteogenic differentiation, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, and cytokine profiles. Across a 0.002-0.2 mg mL-1 range of Ca2Al-Cl, preserved cell viability and membrane integrity were observed, with the highest concentration (0.2 mg mL-1) eliciting the largest increase in metabolic activity (~270% of control), with a progressive reduction at lower concentrations; quantitative Crystal Violet staining showed increased total attachment at 0.2 and 0.02 mg mL-1, while early adhesion transcripts (Integrin-β1, FAK, Src, PP2A, Cofilin) decreased. Cell-cycle readouts revealed increased p21 and decreased CDK6, with CDK2/4 levels remaining unchanged. During 14-day differentiation, Osteocalcin increased, and ALP staining revealed more foci, yet Alpl, Runx2, and Osterix/Sp7 decreased, and Alizarin Red showed no visible mineral increase; OPG/RANKL were not modulated, thus the regulatory axis of bone resorption was not altered. The collagen content, as determined by Picrosirius staining, matched that of the Control, whereas the osteogenic medium was lower. Gelatin zymography indicated relatively higher MMP-2 (pro/intermediate/active) and lower MMP-9 under Ca2Al-Cl. Cytokine profiling revealed increased levels of IL-6 and IL-33, accompanied by reduced IL-1/IL-1β and IL-10, and unchanged TNF. Collectively, Ca2Al-Cl induces an ECM-centric, early osteogenic priming phenotype characterized by selective remodeling (MMP-2-biased) and cytokine modulation without late mineral accrual under these conditions. These findings position Ca2Al-Cl as a potential modulator of the early bone regenerative microenvironment, a property that could be harnessed for applications where controlled matrix organization is prioritized over rapid mineralization. However, further studies quantifying ion release dynamics and utilizing 3D/co-culture models are essential to elucidate the causal mechanisms and translate this priming effect into a functional regenerative outcome.
journal: Journal of biomedical materials research. Part A

title: Development of conditional cores via supersaturated designs for genetic diversity-based prediction models.
abstract: Genetic diversity is fundamental to sustainable crop improvement. This study uses 1755 soybean [Glycine max (L.) Merr.] recombinant inbred lines from the soybean nested association mapping population, phenotyped for yield across nine environments to optimize the composition of the training set for a given testing set. Using supersaturated designs, we generated conditionally optimized training sets by iteratively selecting candidate genotypes according to a metric that quantifies diversity as the trace of the cross‐product of the genomic matrix containing both a candidate training set and the fixed testing set. Two strategies were considered: (i) maximizing and (ii) minimizing genetic distances to the testing set. Our results show that maximizing genetic distance relative to the testing set improves prediction accuracy over random training sets under standard genomic best linear unbiased prediction. However, this advantage disappeared when models incorporated family structure or genotype‐by‐environment interactions, which consistently yielded superior overall accuracy regardless of training set selection. This result highlights the complexity of considering multi‐omics integration for interpretability: determining whether an increase in accuracy comes from a better model specification or from capturing confounding factors. Finally, we also found that maximizing the genetic diversity of the training set with respect to the testing set preserves at least one individual from as many different families as possible. In contrast, minimizing diversity either excludes or overrepresents families. Further studies should consider a completely unbalanced dataset that mimics the real‐life scenarios breeders face in their programs.

title: Ultrasonography (IOTA-ADNEX) vs magnetic resonance imaging (ADNEX MR) for diagnosing ovarian cancer in high-risk patients: a prospective study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES To systematically validate and compare ultrasonography, using the ultrasound-based International Ovarian Tumor Analysis - Assessment of Different NEoplasias in the adneXa (IOTA-ADNEX) model, with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), using the MRI-based ADNEX MR scoring system, as second-line imaging modalities for estimating the risk of adnexal malignancy in patients identified as being at risk of malignancy on first-line ultrasound examination. METHODS This was a prospective, single-center diagnostic accuracy study designed as a head-to-head comparison. All patients referred to a tertiary referral center at Aarhus University Hospital, Aarhus, Denmark, for suspected adnexal malignancy on first-line imaging between May 2021 and December 2022 were offered second-line diagnostic testing. This comprised both a systematic expert ultrasound examination, including IOTA-ADNEX risk estimation, and a systematic MRI scan with ADNEX MR scores assigned by expert radiologists. The imaging assessments were performed prospectively, with ultrasound examiners and radiologists blinded to the results of other imaging modalities and to the reference standard (tumor outcome). The reference standard was a histopathological diagnosis of the primary adnexal mass or, in a small number of cases, clinical follow-up. Borderline tumors, invasive adnexal malignancy and metastases to the adnexa were grouped as malignancies. Diagnostic performance of the IOTA-ADNEX model, ADNEX MR scoring system and CA 125 for predicting malignancy was evaluated using the area under the receiver-operating-characteristics curve (AUC), and AUCs were compared using DeLong's test. Diagnostic metrics were estimated at clinically relevant cut-offs and scores. Agreement between modalities was assessed for the identification of morphological features and overall risk estimation using Cohen's kappa statistics, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Bland-Altman plots. For the IOTA-ADNEX model, calibration and the ability to discriminate between tumor subtypes were evaluated. RESULTS The included cohort comprised 342 patients (342 lesions analyzed). In the final cohort, 78.1% of patients were postmenopausal and the overall prevalence of malignancy was 58.8%. The AUC for distinguishing patients with benign tumors from those with malignant tumors was 0.96 (95% CI, 0.94-0.98) for the IOTA-ADNEX model (with or without CA 125) compared with an AUC of 0.93 (95% CI, 0.91-0.96) for ADNEX MR. Agreement between ultrasound and MRI ranged from moderate to substantial for key morphological features (κ = 0.46-0.75) and from good to excellent for lesion-size measurements (ICC = 0.78-0.92). The IOTA-ADNEX model performed similarly to the ADNEX MR scoring system regardless of lesion morphology or size. The IOTA-ADNEX model had good calibration. Furthermore, its multinomial discriminative ability between tumor subtypes was generally high, although performance was reduced when distinguishing borderline tumors from Stage-I invasive malignancy (AUC, 0.71 (95% CI, 0.56-0.82)). CONCLUSIONS The IOTA-ADNEX model and ADNEX MR scoring system demonstrated comparable diagnostic accuracy for differentiating benign from malignant adnexal masses in this study. Results appeared to be consistent when stratified by lesion morphology. Both modalities may be used for second-line assessment of masses deemed at risk of malignancy in the first-line ultrasound examination, depending on resources in specific centers. © 2026 The Author(s). Evaluating seasonal forecasts in Austria using agrometeorological indicators
abstract: Farmers rely on weather information to guide crop management; however, outcomes often remain uncertain until harvest. This pilot study evaluated downscaled medium- to seasonal-range forecasts for Austria (2018–2022), focusing on air temperature, precipitation, and six crop-independent agrometeorological indicators (stress and suitability metrics). Spatial downscaling enhanced temperature forecast performance, whereas gains for precipitation were limited. Agrometeorological indicators generally showed higher forecast accuracy at shorter lead times, although the magnitude of this effect varied among indicators. Warm springs in 2018–2019 led to temperature underestimation and reduced springtime accuracy, while Frost Stress Days were affected by a systematic cold bias during the study period. Indicators based on moderate temperature thresholds showed more robust performance than extreme-based ones. Sum of Effective Growing Temperature performed best, particularly for June-start forecasts, whereas Heat Wave Days showed limited operational suitability because of high false-alarm rates. Regional differences in forecast errors were significant for several indicators, with their magnitude and direction varying across climate regions. Site-level MAE was also significantly associated with altitude, mean temperature, and precipitation for several indicator-forecast combinations. For potential water balance, forecasts underestimated available water, consistent with combined temperature and precipitation biases. To enhance agricultural applicability, future studies should improve the accuracy of extreme-weather forecasts, calibrate models regionally, and integrate seasonal forecasts into user-friendly decision support systems. Given the short verification period (2018–2022), the results provide preliminary evidence of forecasting skill under the climatic conditions represented in the study period rather than robust long-term predictability estimates. Preprint available at https://zenodo.org/records/18890040.

title: Climate-based suitability scenario models for high-protein crop cultivation in Europe
abstract: Despite several concurrent environmental and nutritional benefits, protein crop production in the EU remains low, and imports remain high. Therefore, a knowledge gap exists in relation to the suitability of different protein crops in Europe and how this may change under future climates. In this research, we aimed to identify areas conducive to cultivating human-grade, high-protein crops. To achieve this, we used species distribution modelling, combining locations for eight economically important protein crops with 1-km geospatial data on climate, topography and soil to project current and future distributions across three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways. We identified large areas of agricultural lands suitable for crop-specific expansion, with all species showing sensitivity to future conditions, diversifying across and within projections and timescales. For example, faba increases in suitability across Spain, Turkey, and Greece, while oat shifts its suitability northwards towards Norway and Sweden. In general, faba, lupins and peas substantially increase in suitability under future scenarios, while quinoa and perennial ryegrass decline, soy and oats remain stable. Importantly, all areas (i.e. every individual pixel in the model) retain a suitability above a minimum threshold, meaning there should always be an optimal protein crop for that area, at that time, regardless of the climate scenario. By identifying the agricultural areal extent of suitability for each European country across the different crops, we provide targeted figures to inform decision-making and support European-specific targets such as the EU protein strategy and the current Common Agricultural Policy aiming to increase native, high-protein crop production by 2050.

title: Learning safe behaviour via justified human preferences and hypothetical queries
abstract: Although reinforcement learning is a powerful paradigm for agent sequential decision-making, it cannot be used in its traditional form in most safety-critical environments. Human feedback can enable an agent to learn a good policy while avoiding unsafe states, but at the cost of human time. We present JPAL-HA, a model for safe learning in safety-critical environments that is grounded on two novel ideas: (i) human preferences over a choice of actions are augmented with justifications such as one action is preferred because the other is unsafe; and (ii) we use these justifications to guide the generation of future queries over hypothetical actions to enable the agent to more effectively map out unsafe regions. We evaluate JPAL-HA using modified configurations of the Island Navigation environment from the AI Safety Gridworlds. We empirically show that it significantly improves safety compared to existing approaches for safe learning from human preferences and outperforms other safe human-in-the-loop algorithms in terms of sample efficiency. We also include an analysis of safety/human burden trade-off. Additionally, we evaluate our method with people training a mobile robot, demonstrating that a diverse group of people can complete training in only a few minutes and that hypothetical actions not only further improve safety, but also slightly decrease the training time and keep it to admissible levels.

title: DynFreqRec: A frequency-aware training–inference synergistic enhancement framework for sequential recommendation
Using shortwave infrared spectral indices to monitor short-term water stress dynamics in peach orchards
abstract: Purpose Capturing rapid changes in water status is key to optimizing deficit irrigation in Mediterranean orchards, but thermal remote sensing is constrained by the availability of high-spatial-resolution data. This study assesses the ability of visible, near-infrared, and shortwave infrared (VNIR/SWIR) indices to detect short-term water stress in peach orchards. Methods An experiment was conducted in two commercial orchards in south-eastern Spain, where mild water stress was induced by withholding irrigation for four days. High-resolution hyperspectral and thermal imagery were acquired concurrently with stem water potential measurements (ψ stem ). Structural, pigment-related, and water-sensitive indices were evaluated at several spatial resolutions, from high (20–50 cm) to medium (30 m), to analyze the effects of pixel size on stress detection. The Crop Water Stress Index (CWSI), derived from thermal imagery, served as a reference indicator. Results Those optical indices based on SWIR reflectance at 1240 nm, the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI₁₂₄₀) and the Simple Ratio Water Index (SRWI), showed the strongest sensitivity to ψ stem variability (R 2 = 0.63, p < 0.001), comparable to the thermal CWSI (R 2 = 0.67, p < 0.001). The analyzed SWIR indices proved more robust under spatial aggregation than other classical VNIR indices, preserving sensitivity when soil/shadow effects were included. Radiative transfer simulations (PROSPECT/3D FLIGHT model) confirmed the NDWI₁₂₄₀ response to variations in leaf water content and leaf angle under short-term stress. Conclusion The results demonstrate the potential of SWIR-based indices, especially in the 1200–1300 nm range, to detect early water stress in Mediterranean woody crops and support their applicability for large-scale monitoring with current and upcoming satellite sensors, though further validation using operational satellite data is required.

title: Persistent free radicals on biochar surfaces redirect straw-derived carbon toward mineral-associated organic matter
abstract: Returning crop residues to soil is a central strategy for increasing soil organic carbon (SOC), yet whether biochar-associated persistent free radicals (PFRs) actively regulate the stabilization of residue-derived carbon remains unresolved. Here, graded PFR activities were generated by selective radical quenching while maintaining similar biochar physicochemical properties, and 13C-labeled straw was used to trace residue-derived carbon dynamics in two contrasting agricultural soils. Biochar PFRs enhanced hydroxyl radical (·OH) production in a dose-dependent manner, with the highest-PFR treatment generating 6.1- and 18.1-fold higher ·OH levels than the straw-only control in black soil and fluvo-aquic soil, respectively. This abiotic oxidation accelerated early-stage (0–14 d) straw carbon mineralization without increasing net carbon loss. Instead, it redirected straw-derived carbon toward aromatic intermediates that preferentially accumulated as mineral-associated organic matter (MAOM), increasing the proportion of MAOM carbon derived from straw from 59.4% to 64.2% in black soil and from 53.8% to 60.0% in fluvo-aquic soil. Structural equation modeling further demonstrated that PFRs promoted MAOM formation primarily through ·OH-driven chemical transformation, whereas microbial communities acted mainly as secondary responders. These findings demonstrate that biochar-derived PFRs redirect, rather than simply accelerate, straw-derived carbon turnover by coupling abiotic oxidation with microbial processing. This study establishes a mechanistic link between biochar surface redox chemistry and soil carbon persistence, providing a mechanistic basis for designing biochars with enhanced carbon sequestration potential. Biochar persistent free radicals initiate abiotic oxidation of straw-derived carbon. PFR-driven chemical transformation redirects residue carbon into mineral-associated pools. Coupled abiotic–biotic pathways explain biochar-induced straw carbon stabilization. Biochar persistent free radicals initiate abiotic oxidation of straw-derived carbon.
