title: Predicting Seasonal Activity of Blunt-nosed Leafhoppers Using Degree-day Models in Cranberry
abstract: Accurate prediction of pest and crop phenology is essential for optimizing integrated pest management (IPM) in cranberry production systems. Degree-day models are widely used to forecast insect development and crop phenology; however, few have been developed for cranberry insect pests. We developed and validated degree-day–based models for the blunt-nosed leafhopper, Limotettix vaccinii (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae), in relation to cranberry bloom phenology in New Jersey, USA. Multiyear field data collected from commercial cranberry beds between 2022 and 2024 were used to develop and optimize the models, whereas independent datasets collected from 289 beds over a 5-year period (2021–25) were used for validation. Phenological progression of both pest and crop was modeled using logistic functions driven by growing degree-day (GDDpest and GDDcrop, respectively), with optimized base temperatures and biofix dates. The optimal L. vaccinii model used a base temperature of 10 °C and a biofix corresponding to floodwater drawdown [day of year (DOY) 112], whereas the cranberry bloom model converged on a base temperature of 4.44 °C and a DOY 94 biofix. Developmental trajectories showed consistent biological patterns, with nymphal activity preceding bloom and adult emergence overlapping the later stages of bloom. Model integration revealed that 10% bloom occurred, on average, at 716 GDDcrop (DOY 160), by which time ∼70% of nymphal development had already been completed. Based on these dynamics, the optimal insecticide application window was identified between 195 GDDpest (DOY 144; 25% nymphal progression) and peak nymph abundance at 266 GDDpest (DOY 153; 50% progression), maximizing nymph suppression while minimizing pollinator exposure. These results demonstrate that empirically optimized degree-day models can effectively synchronize L. vaccinii management with cranberry crop phenology. This framework provides a practical decision support tool for cranberry IPM and highlights the importance of regional calibration of phenology models to local climatic conditions and management practices.

title: Mathematical Modeling and Simulation of Eimeria spp. Transmission Dynamics Between Poultry Manure and Vegetable Crops in Integrated Farming Systems
Forecasting financial support for government institutions using artificial intelligence: The case study of museums
abstract: Subject. Forecasting the financial support of public institutions based on regional panel data of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation. Objectives. To develop and test a methodology for forecasting the financial support of museums using artificial intelligence methods. Methods. A panel dataset of 85 constituent entities of the Russian Federation for 2018–2024 was compiled. Machine learning methods were applied, including gradient boosting, regularized linear models, and their ensembles. Hyperparameter tuning was carried out using an artificial intelligence agent (AI agent) based on the Qwen3.5‑27B language model. Thirty‑two computational experiments were conducted. Forecast accuracy was assessed using the median absolute percentage error (MdAPE); rolling validation was applied over four test years (2021–2024). Results. The gradient boosting model achieves an MdAPE of 8.1% across regions, outperforming the best naive forecast by 1.9 percentage points and the previous‑year forecast by 4.6 percentage points. The average MdAPE under rolling validation was 12%. For 64% of the regions, the forecast error does not exceed 15%. Infrastructure‑related characteristics of institutions (28.6%) and personnel‑related characteristics (22%) demonstrate the highest predictive power. A systematic tendency to underestimate forecasts for large regions was identified; this is driven by discretionary budgetary decisions that cannot be predicted based on operational indicators. Conclusions and Relevance. Artificial intelligence methods demonstrate an advantage over traditional econometric approaches in the context of nonlinear relationships and interregional heterogeneity. The proposed methodology is applicable to forecasting financial indicators of public institutions in other sectors, provided that similar operational data at the regional level are available. The results can be used by public authorities in budget expenditure planning and in preliminary assessments of expected levels of financial support.

title: Accounting and control support for settlements with certain categories of employees: Issues and solutions
abstract: Subject. This article addresses theoretical and practical aspects of accounting for and internal control over settlements with personnel in agricultural organizations operating under seasonal production conditions. Objectives. Based on assessing the current state of accounting practice and designing innovative forms of internal reporting, as well as identifying the specific features of managing settlements with seasonal personnel, the article aims to develop scientifically grounded recommendations for improving the accounting and control framework for settlements with seasonal workers. Methods. For the study, we used the general scientific methods, statistical analysis, and digital modeling. Results. The article proposes and substantiates areas for improving the accounting and control framework for settlements with seasonal workers involving the implementation of an integrated digital profile of a seasonal worker and an operational register of seasonal operations, which enables real-time monitoring of performance against planned targets and supports timely managerial decision-making. Conclusions and Relevance. The digital transformation of accounting through the implementation of an employee's digital profile and an operational register of seasonal works incorporating predictive analytics ensures end-to-end traceability of labor input and the timely detection of deviations from planned targets. The proposed approach contributes to greater reliability of accounting data, more effective internal control and the mitigation of tax and labor risks. The proposed internal reporting forms and digital tools are designed for agricultural organizations characterized by pronounced production seasonality. Accounting and economic departments may apply these solutions to enhance the reliability of accounting for settlements with personnel, strengthen internal control and mitigate the risks of non-compliance with labor and tax legislation. The findings are also applicable to organizations in other industries.

title: Geoclimatic changes, industry structure and external energy dependence as factors of economic dynamics
abstract: Subject. The impact of geoclimatic shifts – temperature anomalies and extreme hydrometeorological events – on the economic development of national economies. Objectives. Construction and econometric verification of a panel model that makes it possible to assess the direction and impact of geoclimatic factors on the logarithm of per capita GDP for a sample of 54 countries for 2000–2024. Methods. The study is based on a synthesis of theoretical analysis of the climate-economic literature and an empirical assessment using panel data. Results. An increase in the average annual temperature by 1°C relative to the climatic norm of 1961–1990 reduces per capita GDP by an average of 1.8%, and each additional extreme event (drought, flood, storm) – by 2.6%. The share of agriculture in GDP and energy dependence significantly increase climate vulnerability, while increased grain yields and trade openness act as compensating mechanisms. The model explains 80.7% of the intra-country variation in per capita GDP. Conclusions. Taking into account the combined effects of temperature anomalies, extreme events, and structural characteristics of the economy allows for more accurate estimates of climate damage compared to traditional approaches that consider these factors in isolation. The high share of agriculture and energy dependence create a "structural trap" that increases vulnerability, while technological modernization of the agricultural sector and diversification of foreign trade can partially compensate for losses. The results obtained substantiate the need to integrate climate risks into macroeconomic forecasting and budget planning.

title: Digital maturity of agroecosystems in the global economy: Theoretical and methodological approach to assessment and forecasting
abstract: Subject. This article focuses on the digital ecosystems of the agro-industrial complex of different countries. Objectives. The study aims to develop a theoretical and methodological approach to assessing the maturity of digital agroecosystems in the global economy and to identify the conditions for the transition from fragmented digitalization to a sustainable digital agro-industrial ecosystem. Methods. For the study, we used methods of content analysis, comparative and institutional analyses, systematization of scientific literature and regulatory methods, expert grouping of indicators. Results. The article proposes a stage-based model of digital agroecosystem formation in different countries. It also substantiates the need for a comprehensive methodology to assess the depth of digital ecosystems, and identifies the main barriers to the transition from fragmented digitalization to an ecosystem. Conclusions. The choice of financial and credit mechanisms for small and medium-sized agricultural producers in global and Russian practice will depend on the level of digital agroecosystems maturity. The research results can support the development of agricultural digitalization roadmaps, digital ecosystem architecture design, and the analysis of digitalization projects by maturity level.

title: The role of digitalization in creating agro-industrial clusters: Regional aspects and economic efficiency
abstract: Subject. Economic efficiency of agriculture, development of digitalization processes in the economy at the regional level. Objectives. Assessment of the economic effects of implementing digital technologies in agricultural enterprises. Methods. Systematic, comparative analysis. Results. Digital platforms and modeling tools make it possible to optimize the process of creating agro-industrial clusters. By using digital tools, costs for fertilizers, fuel, and other components are reduced. However, the level of digital maturity in Russian agro-industrial companies is still low. Conclusions. An important task for Russia is creating a unified state policy aimed at actively developing the agro-industrial complex in the regions.

title: Conceptual aspects of strategic planning of a large metallurgical company
abstract: Subject. The conceptual foundations of strategic planning of large metallurgical companies and the possibilities of their practical application in modern conditions of industry development. Objectives. Development of conceptual provisions for strategic planning of large metallurgical companies based on the differentiation of the concepts of strategic planning and strategic management, the formation of an adaptive cyclical model for the preparation, implementation and adjustment of strategic decisions, as well as an assessment of its practical applicability. Methods. The research is based on systematic and comparative approaches, methods of analysis, synthesis and generalization, as well as a comparative analysis of industry statistics and corporate strategies of the largest metallurgical companies. Results. A conceptual model of strategic planning of a large metallurgical company has been developed based on the cyclical interaction of the stages of diagnosis, goal setting, implementation, adaptation and strategic monitoring. The proposed model provides continuous feedback and the ability to adjust strategic decisions based on changes in the external and internal environment. Conclusions. An analysis of the industry dynamics and strategies of the largest Russian metallurgical companies has confirmed the relevance of an adaptive approach to strategic planning and the need to integrate its key elements into a single system.

title: Digital Transformation of Agricultural Libraries for Supporting Smart Agriculture: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Prospects
abstract: Digital transformation has created new opportunities for agricultural libraries to support smart agriculture through improved access to digital resources, information dissemination, and technology-enabled services. The present study examines the opportunities, challenges, and factors influencing digital transformation in agricultural libraries in Nagpur City. A quantitative and descriptive research design was adopted, and data were collected from 44 agricultural library professionals using purposive sampling through a structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Cronbach’s Alpha, and multiple linear regression were applied. The factor analysis identified seven factors explaining 74.377% of the total variance, with reliability coefficients ranging from 0.856 to 0.919. Regression analysis showed that the identified factors did not significantly predict technology adoption (R² = 0.064; F(7,36) = 0.355; p = 0.922). Therefore, the null hypothesis was not rejected, indicating no statistically significant influence of the identified factors on technology adoption in the present sample. The findings highlight the need for stronger financial and institutional support, improved digital infrastructure, staff training, and user-oriented digital services to strengthen agricultural libraries for smart agriculture.

title: ТЕОРЕТИКО-МЕТОДОЛОГІЧНІ ЗАСАДИ УПРАВЛІННЯ ФІНАНСОВО-ЕКОНОМІЧНИМ ЗАБЕЗПЕЧЕННЯМ РОЗВИТКУ МАТЕРІАЛЬНО-ТЕХНІЧНОЇ БАЗИ АГРАРНИХ ПІДПРИЄМСТВ
abstract: The article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of managing the financial and economic support for the development of the material and technical base of agricultural enterprises under current macroeconomic challenges, instability, and martial law. The strategic importance of the material and technical base for ensuring the efficiency of production and economic activities, the competitiveness of agricultural enterprises, and the sustainable development of rural areas is substantiated. The specific features of the formation and reproduction of the material and technical base are revealed, taking into account the seasonality of production, dependence on natural and climatic conditions, the territorial dispersion of resources, the need for maintenance services, and the impact of scientific and technological progress. The main sources of financial and economic support for its development are systematized, and the need for their diversification is substantiated. Conceptual principles for managing the development of the material and technical base are proposed, including innovative modernization, digitalization of production processes, resource conservation, development of processing capacities, optimization of logistics flows, improvement of maintenance services, and strengthening the role of the intellectual and human-resource component. Strategic, tactical, and operational objectives of managing the financial and economic support of the material and technical base of agricultural enterprises are identified. Criteria for the effectiveness of such management are substantiated, including the completeness of financial support, timeliness of decision-making, balance of funding sources, economic justification of expenditures, resource conservation, adaptability, transparency, and flexibility of the management system.
journal: Herald of Khmelnytskyi National University. Economic sciences

title: ЦИФРОВІЗАЦІЯ УПРАВЛІННЯ ВИРОБНИЧИМИ ПРОЦЕСАМИ СІЛЬСЬКОГОСПОДАРСЬКИХ ПІДПРИЄМСТВ В УМОВАХ СУЧАСНИХ ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЙ
abstract: The article analyzes the relevance and essence of digitalizing production process management in agricultural enterprises, that is a topic of particular importance in the current business environment, especially taking into consideration martial law. It notes that the evolution and development of agricultural technologies necessitate managerial transformations, with digitalization serving as a key tool in this process. The article outlines the primary tools and capabilities associated with digitalizing the management of agricultural enterprises, citing examples such as cloud technologies, artificial intelligence, analytics platforms, the Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain technology, precision farming systems, and digital accounting systems. Special attention is paid to blockchain technology, which is currently gaining traction and enhancing corporate transparency and efficiency by enabling process monitoring, data collection, execution of smart contracts, and fraud prevention. Blockchain technology plays a vital role in providing the information necessary for enterprise operations – a factor that is currently crucial for the effective management of modern agricultural businesses under the conditions of uncertainty and transformation. The study concludes that digitalizing production process management offers significant advantages to Ukrainian agricultural enterprises, bolstering their resilience and competitiveness. These benefits are realized through faster managerial decision-making supported by analytics tools and software, more efficient resource allocation in production, and the use of systems for monitoring and tracking logistics processes. All of this contributes to increased efficiency and labor productivity, improved product quality, responsiveness to changes in consumer demand and preferences, the mitigation of climate change, and the addressing of other threats. Thus, the digitalization of management processes in agricultural enterprises has a significant, positive, long-term impact on the operations of domestic agricultural businesses.
journal: Herald of Khmelnytskyi National University. Economic sciences

title: ІННОВАЦІЙНО-ТЕХНОЛОГІЧНА ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЯ АГРАРНИХ ПІДПРИЄМСТВ УКРАЇНИ: ВІД ВОЄННОЇ АДАПТАЦІЇ ДО ЦИФРОВІЗАЦІЇ ТА ТОЧНОГО ЗЕМЛЕРОБСТВА
abstract: The article presents a comprehensive theoretical and empirical diagnosis of the current state, dynamics, and structure of innovative activity among Ukrainian agricultural enterprises amidst geopolitical, macroeconomic, and war-induced shocks. It is evident that innovation adoption has shifted from a tool for maximizing profits to a fundamental prerequisite for operational survival and long-term business resilience. The study examines Ukraine's positions in global innovation benchmarks (European Innovation Scoreboard, Global Innovation Index). It analyzes the financial structure of R&D expenditures, revealing an over-reliance on internal firm funds against the backdrop of stagnant R&D intensity below 0.38% of GDP. The catastrophic damage to the sector's capital stock is estimated at over $12.1 billion in direct agricultural losses and the destruction of over 130,000 machinery units. The structural aging of the machinery fleet is detailed—with 42–67% of combine harvesters and tractors exceeding 12 years of age—leading to disproportionate repair costs and a 20–28% drop in seasonal operational output. The study categorizes digital technology adoption across four maturity levels (RTK satellite navigation, NDVI satellite monitoring, Variable Rate Technology (VRT), and Farm Management Information Systems (FMIS)). The economic returns of drone-based land auditing and resource optimization are quantified, highlighting the prevalence of "patchwork digitalization." Key operational bottlenecks include declining EBITDA, GPS suppression via Electronic Warfare (EW), field contamination from unexploded ordnance, and severe shortages of skilled human capital. Finally, institutional and economic policy recommendations are formulated: promoting the Precision Agriculture as a Service (PAaaS) model, reorienting the "5-7-9%" preferential credit scheme toward technological modernization, unifying digital registries via open APIs, and establishing public-private educational-innovation clusters.
journal: Herald of Khmelnytskyi National University. Economic sciences

title: ІНТЕГРАЦІЙНІ МЕХАНІЗМИ УПРАВЛІННЯ «ЗЕЛЕНОЮ» КОНКУРЕНТОСПРОМОЖНІСТЮ В СИСТЕМІ НАЦІОНАЛЬНОЇ ЕКОНОМІЧНОЇ ПОЛІТИКИ УКРАЇНИ
abstract: This article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations for developing and integrating mechanisms to manage "green" competitiveness amidst the transformation of Ukraine’s national economic policy. Given contemporary global challenges and the country’s European integration objectives, the article argues that traditional approaches to securing competitive advantages require a synergistic combination of fundamental instruments. The author proposes an architecture for how institutional, organizational-managerial, economic, and innovation-technological mechanisms interact, with an information-digital framework serving as an overarching "superstructure" to ensure transparency, monitoring, and adaptable management decisions. Ukraine's key strategic priorities for economic policy are systematized in the context of the transition toward a climate-neutral economy, circularity, and the "greening" of the agricultural sector. A hierarchical system of integration principles is proposed—ranging from the foundational alignment of goals to the achievement of an overall synergistic effect. Particular attention is paid to the need to align national regulatory norms with European standards, particularly the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). The text emphasizes the importance of decentralizing environmental initiatives and engaging regional stakeholders in implementing climate projects. The availability of critical raw materials, combined with a post-war reconstruction approach of "building back better," provides a strong foundation for integrating Ukrainian industry into European value chains. Furthermore, the success of environmental transformations depends directly on developing human capital, upskilling the workforce, and increasing investment in clean technologies (clean-tech). These factors provide a solid basis for the national economy's long-term competitiveness in the global market. The authors conclude that comprehensive implementation of the proposed concept will not only ensure effective economic growth but also guarantee a high level of environmental security and sustainable development for the nation in the future.
journal: Herald of Khmelnytskyi National University. Economic sciences

title: The “Third Place”: Anatomy of Poltava State Agrarian University’s Library
abstract: The purpose of the work is to investigate the complex role of the modern university library as a “third place” phenomenon in the context of intensive digitalisation and current social challenges. The study aims to analyse the transformation of the library from a traditional book repository into a sociocultural hub that provides mental recovery and social integration for the student community. Particular attention is paid to studying the ability of the library space to compensate for digital isolation and burnout through the implementation of hybrid spaces and services. The research methodology of the work is based on the application of an interdisciplinary approach that combines Ray Oldenburg’s sociological concept of the “third place” with empirical research methods. The article analyses annual reports of the Poltava State Agricultural University (PSAU) library for 2023 and 2024, as well as the results of the author's students’ survey regarding their perception of the library environment. Comparative analysis methods were used to trace the evolution of library services from crisis response to strategic management. The scientific novelty of the research consists in the rethinking of the university library as a wellness infrastructure that combines academic functions with tools for mental health. It is proven that the combination of rare book collections, international partnerships (specifically with the University of Leicester), and inclusive practices for internally displaced people (IDPs) creates a unique type of library that is impossible in only a digital format. The conclusions confirm that the present-day university library has successfully adapted to the conditions of digital saturation, shifting the focus from the management of information to the management of human experience and well-being. The analysis of the PSAU library’s activities demonstrates that in an era of social change, the most valuable resource of a higher education institution becomes the physical space itself, which provides a sense of security, belonging to a community, and emotional relief.
journal: Scientific journal “Library Science. Record Studies. Informology”

title: The role of climate information in enhancing household food security in rural northern Ghana
abstract: Smallholder climate resilience in sub-Saharan Africa is limited by low uptake of adaptation technologies due to poor access to climate forecast information services (CFIS). Cross-sectional data from 2,934 farming households in northern Ghana are used to explore econometric drivers of CFIS access and its causal mediation on household food security. Probit marginal effects show that access to agricultural extension, formal literacy, radio ownership, and perceptions of climate stress strongly increase the likelihood of CFIS adoption. However, peripheral upper west and northeast households face severe access deficits due to infrastructure dead zones and ethno-linguistic barriers, respectively. Two-stage causal mediation and generalized structural equation modeling (GSEM) indicate that CFIS access significantly increases dietary diversity by 0.210 units and significantly reduces food insecurity access anxiety by 0.103 units. Agricultural yield is a strong and significant partial mediator, but only 7.8–14.6% of total food security gains are mediated by it. That is, direct risk-buffering channels dominate (about 85.4 to 92.2%); hence, CFIS is primarily an adaptive safety net for off-farm labor reallocation, asset preservation, and consumption smoothing. Policymakers need to move beyond narrow agronomic advice to integrated climate risk management by bundling CFIS with weather-index insurance, local-language interactive voice response platforms, and decentralized extension networks.

title: Geoinformatics-oriented concept-guided segmentation of Earth observation imagery using text-driven foundation models
abstract: Earth observation image segmentation is a central geoinformatics task, enabling precise land cover mapping, infrastructure monitoring, and environmental change detection from satellite and aerial imagery. However, existing remote sensing segmentation models are typically trained for fixed class taxonomies, lack cross-sensor generalizability, and require extensive manual annotation for every new geographic scene or sensor configuration. To overcome these limitations, we propose ConceptSeg, a concept-driven open-vocabulary segmentation framework tailored for geoinformatics-oriented Earth observation analysis, which we evaluate on optical satellite (Sentinel-2, Gaofen-2, and WorldView-3), aerial, and UAV imagery. ConceptSeg fine-tunes a decoder built on top of a frozen Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3)-style Promptable Concept Segmentation (PCS) backbone on a large curated corpus of remote sensing images paired with rich geospatial concept labels, comprising 285,100 image patches drawn from seven publicly available benchmarks. Users can target arbitrary land cover types, buildings, agricultural features, and disaster damage via open-vocabulary text descriptions such as “regulated river channel,” “white residential house,” or “terraced farmland,” without being restricted to predefined class sets or geometric prompts. The framework addresses fundamental domain gaps between natural and overhead imagery—differences in viewing geometry (nadir vs. oblique), spatial resolution (0.3–10 m GSD), spectral rendering, and geospatial terminology—through three purpose-built components: a multiscale image encoder with geospatially aware positional encoding, a concept encoder that projects textual descriptions into geospatial semantic embeddings, and a cross-attention decoder that fuses prompt features with multiscale image representations. Because prompted segmentation methods can receive different amounts of test-time information, we evaluate ConceptSeg under three explicitly separated input regimes: (i) conventional closed-set automatic segmentation, (ii) fully automatic open-vocabulary text-only segmentation, and (iii) interactive segmentation guided jointly by text and a spatial bounding box. Comprehensive experiments on seven remote sensing benchmarks demonstrate that, within each regime, ConceptSeg is competitive with or outperforms specialist CNN/transformer models and SAM-based adaptations evaluated under the same input regime. Under the interactive text-plus-box regime, ConceptSeg T + I achieves 0.929 mIoU on building extraction (WHU Building), 0.579 mIoU on multiclass land cover segmentation (LoveDA), 0.896 mIoU on dense urban buildings (Inria), 0.723 mIoU on agricultural anomaly detection (Agriculture-Vision), and 0.771 mIoU on disaster damage assessment (xView2), each 1.7–3.3 percentage points above the strongest baseline evaluated under the same box-conditioned regime, and stable across three independent training runs (paired-bootstrap test, p < 0.05 ; full mean ± s.d. and per-class statistics in Section 4.5). Under the fully automatic, text-only regime, ConceptSeg T attains only 0.21–0.46 mIoU, confirming that text alone does not reproduce the box-conditioned numbers above and that spatial priors remain important for top-tier accuracy; the framework additionally exhibits open-vocabulary generalization on withheld concept phrases (avg. 0.594 mIoU across LoveDA and Gaofen Image Dataset novel phrases, +15.6 points over the strongest training-free baseline) and cross-sensor transfer from Sentinel-2 to Gaofen-2 and aerial RGB composites (0.712 and 0.685 mIoU with oracle boxes, retaining 92%–94% of this performance when boxes are instead produced by an off-the-shelf detector, Section 4.6). These findings indicate that grounding remote sensing segmentation in semantic language embeddings, combined with spatial priors, improves domain generalization relative to pixel-space baselines, whereas fully automatic text-only segmentation remains comparatively weaker and is an important direction for future work. Code, configuration files, data splits, and trained checkpoints will be released at https://github.com/ConceptSeg/ConceptSeg upon publication.

title: Spatio-temporal coupling of satellite and reanalysis hydro-meteorological signals for cocoa market volatility
abstract: Climate extremes increasingly disrupt the supply of agricultural commodities grown in concentrated geographic regions. Cocoa ( Theobroma cacao ) plants are particularly vulnerable, since Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana grow about 60% of the world’s supply. Climate precursors of agricultural price shocks are typically reported at country scales, while recent Earth observation (EO) products provide high-resolution cocoa classification maps at plantation scales. The latter provide an opportunity to sample hydro-meteorological variables over the cocoa growing area to investigate potential association with future market changes. During 2024, cocoa futures rose above US$12,000 per metric ton after 2 decades below US$3,800. Here we analyze weekly records of satellite and reanalysis precipitation, soil moisture and 2 m temperature and cocoa futures prices from 2000 to 2025. We identify change points with the Pettitt test and a block bootstrap that allows for autocorrelation, and we monitor an energy index from a lag-embedded principal component analysis fitted only on 2000 to 2017. The mapped footprint contracted by 3,757 km 2 (2.5%) between 2020 and 2024. Soil moisture shifted downward in December 2023, and temperature upward in July 2023, although the temperature shift loses significance once the warming trend is removed. The price entered a high-price regime in March 2024, and both climate shifts preceded it in 87% of bootstrap replicates. The energy index entered its most intense alert episode on 19 November 2023, 16 weeks before the high-price regime. It had raised three earlier episodes without a comparable price rise, and removing the warming trend of the calibration period shortened the lead to 5 weeks. Beyond the cocoa-masked overland area, the soil moisture shift was 26% smaller and the index alerted only after the high-price regime began. The findings indicate that climate records sampled over plantation-scale cocoa maps can provide physically grounded indicators of excessive heat and soil drying that may precede supply shocks. The methodology is reproducible and transferable to other geographically concentrated crop types and EO products.

title: DRAMM-Pest: Direct Multi-Horizon Forecasting of Rice Leaf Roller Activity from Light-Trap and Field-Survey Records
abstract: Multi-horizon forecasts of rice leaf roller activity support advance surveillance planning. Routine light-trap and field-survey records differ in measurement meaning and availability, complicating their complementary use across future monitoring periods. We developed DRAMM-Pest, a mask-aware dual-measurement model in which available field histories condition temporal states derived from light-trap history before horizon-specific aggregation. The model jointly predicts positive-catch probability and light-trap rate over six successive monitoring periods, with observed field-survey targets providing auxiliary supervision during training. On a public 24-year rice leaf roller dataset covering 11 sites, chronological testing on 2020–2023 yielded a light-trap-rate RMSLE of 0.837±0.029 and a Brier score of 0.084±0.004. The corresponding absolute reductions relative to XGBoost were 0.25023 and 0.00859, respectively. Removing all field information or retaining only its binary availability indicator increased mean light-trap-rate MAE by 3.12 and 2.74, respectively. The findings support using complementary monitoring records as historical context and training targets within a horizon-specific forecasting framework for pest-surveillance planning.

title: A Multi-Level Distributed Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Method Based on Knowledge Transfer
abstract: Conventional independently trained models for distributed photovoltaic (DPV) power forecasting at the feeder, main-transformer, and regional-grid levels do not explicitly reuse spatiotemporal representations across the distribution-network hierarchy. This paper proposes a knowledge-transfer-based multilevel method for short-term DPV power forecasting. First, a T-GCN encoding block integrating a temporal convolutional network and an adaptive graph convolutional network is developed at the distribution-transformer-area–feeder level to capture multiscale temporal dependencies and implicit spatial correlations. Second, the pretrained feeder-level encoder is transferred to the main-transformer task and frozen, while a Transformer-based cross-feeder aggregation network and a decoder are trained for the target task. At the grid level, a meteorology-driven weighting network fuses the representations of individual main transformers. In a regional case study using real-world operating data, the proposed method achieves equal-weighted mean relative reductions of approximately 20.0% in NRMSE and 17.5% in NMAE over an independently trained T-GCN baseline across the three forecasting levels. Identical-architecture comparisons at the main-transformer level further show that fine-tuning a pretrained encoder improves forecasting accuracy relative to training from random initialization, while freezing the pretrained encoder yields additional error reductions. These findings support the proposed pretraining-and-freezing strategy under the evaluated conditions.

title: Compute-Constrained Adaptive Electricity Load Forecasting via Offline Policy Learning
abstract: Background: Electricity load forecasting services must allocate inference across models with different accuracy and compute costs under a shared daily budget. Methods: We evaluate offline policies using only pre-call information, complete-day rolling folds, outcome-time embargoes, and a reservation rule that preserves minimum service for later origins. Four public datasets are tested at four horizons and three budgets, comparing contextual allocation with fitted Q iteration (FQI), double FQI, and neural FQI against a feasible static forecaster. Results: All 960 formal policy evaluations satisfy the budget. The mean gains in mean absolute error (MAE) are 9.22%, 7.37%, 7.77%, and 3.83% for the four methods, respectively. The contextual gains are positive on Steel, Tetouan, and Open Power System Data (OPSD) but negative on UCI ElectricityLoadDiagrams (UCI–ECL). A disjoint deployment gate yields a 10.63% aggregate gain at 51.7% coverage with six harmful activations and 61 missed beneficial cases; this empirical risk-control filter is not a safety guarantee. The lightweight multilayer perceptron (MLP) extension and sequential audits find no uniform benefit from a larger action pool or deeper Bellman backups; FQI improves over contextual allocation only at the smallest tested switching penalty in the cache-state experiment. Conclusions: Offline policy learning can support budget-feasible adaptive forecasting, but its benefit depends on dataset and runtime conditions. Chronological validation, explicit feasibility checks, and static fallback are needed; the results do not establish the universal superiority of sequential reinforcement learning.

title: Cross-Task Latent Feature Distillation Learning for Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection
abstract: Hyperspectral anomaly detection (HAD) aims to identify Earth’s surface anomalies without prior knowledge. However, most existing unsupervised HAD methods rely on training data roughly partitioned into background and anomalies, suffering from severe class imbalance and yielding feature representations heavily tied to scene-specific distributions. In contrast, supervised hyperspectral classification networks can extract well-organized spectral–spatial representations from diverse land-cover types; yet, this valuable knowledge remains underutilized in HAD due to the absence of labeled anomaly samples. To circumvent this limitation, this paper proposes a novel knowledge transfer paradigm from classification tasks to anomaly detection. The proposed framework employs a pretrained convolutional enhanced Transformer (CET) classification network as the teacher model, transferring its rich spectral–spatial context encodings via feature-level distillation. Concurrently, by synergizing latent feature alignment, Gaussian mixture model (GMM) priors, and reconstruction objectives, the student network is equipped with compact background modeling and highly discriminative representation abilities, which provide robust support for feature-space anomaly detection. Extensive experiments on spaceborne and airborne hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that our method substantially improves detection accuracy against complex terrestrial backgrounds with fast inference, while exhibiting superior cross-scene generalization.

title: Multisource Remote Sensing Assessment of Ocean Responses and Rainfall-Related Flood Hazards During Severe Tropical Storm Maysak
abstract: This study examines ocean conditions and rainfall-related flood candidates during Severe Tropical Storm Maysak using multisource observations in the northwestern South China Sea and Guangxi, China. Satellite products, atmospheric data, operational ocean products, published gauge summaries and official impact reports were analyzed with explicit observation windows and sensor provenance. Regional daily mean wind speed, significant wave height and mixed-layer depth peaked around 4 July 2026. Daily mean sea surface temperature (SST) on 5 July was 1.12 °C below the maximum during the study period. A daily first frontal analysis south of Hainan showed reductions of 15.3% in mean SST gradient and 25.6% in the mean daily strong front area between paired 15-day windows. Gradient decreases persisted across the tested windows and smoothing settings. Photosynthetically available radiation decreased by 24.1%, and diffuse attenuation at 490 nm increased by 7.9% across their respective windows. The merged chlorophyll-a retrievals increased descriptively by approximately 5.0%; sensor differences and limited common observations prevent interpreting this estimate as a bio-optical response independently corroborated across sensors. Integrated Multisatellite Retrievals for the Global Precipitation Measurement mission (IMERG) indicated a maximum accumulation of approximately 702 mm over the prolonged 2–16 July rainfall episode, including subsequent weather systems. Water-change masks identified 126.5 km2 of potential new inundation candidates, including 1.5 km2 of same-pixel multisensor overlap. The analysis documents marine changes, prolonged rainfall and regional water-change candidates within their stated observation windows.

title: Towards Noisy-Reference Paragraph Change Captioning: A Weakly Supervised Detection-Guided Historical-Cascaded Network for Remote-Sensing Images
abstract: Remote-sensing image change captioning (RSICC) generally assumes correctly paired bitemporal images and focuses on isolated sentence descriptions, limiting applicability to archives where the correct temporal counterpart may be unknown. We introduce the Noisy-Reference Paragraph-Level Change-Captioning (NRP-CC) task, which requires retrieving the post-change observation from a noisy candidate pool before generating a coherent multi-statement paragraph. We construct the SECOND-ParCap dataset with image-level semantic annotations and paragraph-level change descriptions, and propose a Weakly Supervised Detection-Guided Historical-Cascaded Network (WSDHC-Net). WSDHC-Net leverages Dual Similarity Matching (DS-Matching) for retrieval from noisy candidate pools and employs weakly supervised detection to mine semantic cues for the Historical-Cascaded Paragraph Refinement Change-Captioning (HCPR-CC) module, which generates multi-statement paragraphs describing scene changes. We further introduce SA-ROUGE to evaluate sentence-level correspondence across the generated statements. On SECOND-ParCap, WSDHC-Net achieves Acc@1 scores of 99.53%, 99.29%, and 98.52% under appearance-hard retrieval with 5, 10, and 20 candidates, respectively. In a separate captioning benchmark using identical frozen retrieved inputs across all compared methods, WSDHC-Net attains ROUGE-L and SA-ROUGE scores of 0.5017 and 0.5016, respectively, under reference-assisted sentence-level evaluation; the corresponding paragraph-level scores are 0.2749 and 1.9305. These results support the feasibility of integrating temporal-correspondence retrieval with paragraph-level change description in NRP-CC.

title: Synergistic Multi-Source Remote Sensing and Machine Learning for Regional-Scale Soil Salinity Retrieval in the Hyper-Arid Tarim River Basin
abstract: Saline–alkali land is known colloquially as the “ringworm of the Earth” because of its wide distribution, difficulty of management, and the serious threat it poses to agricultural production and ecological security in arid regions. The Tarim River Basin is the primary distribution area of saline–alkali land in the arid region of northwest China. Therefore, accurate assessment of its distribution and degree of saline–alkali development is important for the comprehensive management and maintenance of regional ecological security in this region. However, the distribution and characteristics of regional saline–alkali land are unclear because of the limitations of traditional land survey methods. To address this, a field campaign was conducted across the Tarim River Basin, yielding 147 topsoil specimens subsequently subjected to electrical conductivity determinations, and it used a retrieval model for saline–alkali soils by integrating remote sensing techniques and machine learning algorithms. The results show that a Random Forest (RF) model integrating all multi-source features was optimal for soil salinity retrieval, achieving the highest accuracy (R2 = 0.73, RMSE = 3.58 dS m−1, MAE = 1.89 dS m−1), with superior robustness and extreme value prediction, while Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) complemented saline vs. non-saline boundary extraction. Macro-climatic variables (MAT, MAP) dominated with a 33.2% combined contribution, consistent with the dominant climatic control on soil salinity in hyper-arid regions. Multi-source synergies including optical indices, Sentinel-1 SAR (12.0%), and environmental covariates enhanced physical interpretability. Spatially, soil salinity exhibited strong heterogeneity (CV = 113.04%), being concentrated in the middle–lower plains and irrigation districts affected by anthropogenic activities, contrasting with low-salinity upper mountainous regions. Our results demonstrate that incorporating land survey, remote sensing, and machine learning supports screening-level retrieval of the extent of saline–alkali land in the hyper-arid Tarim River Basin, providing a foundation for its systematic improvement.

title: A Data-Driven Latent Digital Twin Framework for Sustainable Agroecosystem Management
abstract: In recent years, digital twins have been increasingly used in agroecosystem management. However, integrating heterogeneous satellite observations into a unified framework remains challenging. This study developed a latent-state Digital Twin framework using Sentinel-2, MODIS, and SMAP observations from 23 agricultural fields at the North Kazakhstan Agricultural Experimental Station (NKAES) LLP during 2020–2025. These observations were combined with NASA POWER meteorological data. A three-dimensional multilayer perceptron autoencoder (MLP-AE-3D) was used to represent vegetation, thermal, and soil moisture conditions in a unified latent space. The model achieved a test R2 of 0.9654. To model temporal dynamics, MLP, GRU, and TSN architectures with different hidden dimensions were evaluated. GRU-512 was selected as the temporal prediction model, achieving a test R2 of 0.7962 and an RMSE of 0.0749. A Kalman-based Latent Assimilation Unit (LAU) was used to update predicted latent states while accounting for uncertainty. The adaptive J-RA-LAU configuration further reduced the RMSE to 0.0701. Controlled climate-stress scenarios were used to assess latent-state and vegetation responses to heat, drought, and compound environmental stressors. The proposed framework provides a unified dynamic representation to support field-level monitoring, climate-stress assessment, and sustainable agroecosystem management.

title: Digital Transformation and Energy Poverty Alleviation: Heterogeneous Transmission of Sub Dimensions of Urban-Rural Integration
abstract: Energy poverty has become a major issue that impedes social equity, exacerbates the wealth gap, and constrains China’s modernization process. The rapid development of the digital economy and urban–rural integration has provided new pathways to address this challenge. This study adopts urban–rural integration as its research perspective, utilizes panel data from various provinces in China spanning from 2013 to 2023, and employs a mediation and moderation effect model to systematically examine the impact of the digital economy on energy poverty, its underlying mechanisms, and its heterogeneous characteristics. The research findings indicate that the digital economy can significantly alleviate energy poverty. The mediation mechanism of urban–rural integration reveals that spatial integration and non-agricultural employment serve as the primary transmission channels through which the digital economy mitigates energy poverty, whereas industrial integration may instead exacerbate energy poverty by reducing energy consumption levels. Heterogeneity analysis demonstrates that the energy poverty alleviation effects of the digital economy are stronger in low-income provinces, provinces with high energy intensity, and resource-based provinces. This study contributes to scientifically clarifying the causal relationships among the digital economy, urban–rural integration, and energy poverty, thereby providing a reference framework for developing countries of similar types to address structural contradictions arising from urban–rural dual structures and energy poverty governance.

title: Provincial Data-Factor Capability and Individual Employment in China: A Multilevel Socio-Technical Systems Perspective
abstract: Employment adjustment under digital transformation is a multilevel outcome that depends not only on regional technical capability but also on the structural configuration and worker response conditions in which that capability is embedded. This study examines the relationship between provincial data-factor capability and individual employment in China by matching China Family Panel Studies data for 2012–2022 with a provincial DataIndex. Binary Logit models with province and year fixed effects reveal an age gradient: the employment association of DataIndex is positive for younger workers, weakens around midlife, and becomes negative at older ages. Province-year regressions further show that stronger data-factor capability is associated with industrial structure upgrading and greater regional innovation activity, while interaction tests indicate less favorable employment associations among agricultural-hukou and rural residents. These findings show that improvements in regional digital capability do not translate uniformly into employment gains. Instead, their labor-market consequences depend on worker adaptability and institutional and spatial conditions. The study therefore highlights the need to evaluate digital transformation not only through technological and structural progress, but also through the inclusiveness of its employment outcomes.

title: Artificial Intelligence: Competencies for design in emerging creative environments
abstract: The study, titled From Artificial Intelligence: Competencies for Design in Emerging Creative Environments, aims to determine the competencies linked to the use of Artificial Intelligence in the training of designers, as well as to examine its impact on the professional environment. The advancement of AI has reconfigured not only the tools for design practice, but also the essential dynamics of the creative process. In emerging human-AI collaboration [HAIC] scenarios, these systems operate as cooperative agents and not merely as support tools. However, even though design students are progressively incorporating these technologies into their practice, a gap persists in the development of fundamental competencies for establishing effective interaction with these systems. Therefore, the need to strengthen disciplinary training through competencies that integrate critical interpretation, collaborative interaction, ethical and metacognitive reflection, in addition to specialized technical mastery is recognized. Based on the above, this research is structured around a comprehensive review of scientific literature, analysing studies retrieved from specialized databases in both design and higher education. The methodology will adopt the PRISMA [2021] systematic review protocol, which will ensure a rigorous process for the identification, selection, and synthesis of emerging competencies. The findings will be presented through graphic visualizations, and the discussion will incorporate relevant case studies. Ultimately, the study aims to offer an in-depth theoretical and methodological framework for future lines of research, highlighting the strategic role of AI competencies in the academic achievement and professional development of designers. These competencies are essential for overcoming limitations related to the originality, quality, and coherence of creative proposals, indispensable elements for competitive performance in educational and professional contexts.

title: Effects of physiologically relevant alcohol concentrations on early retinal development: A microfluidic retinal organoid chip analysis.
abstract: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorder can lead to aberrant retinal development. However, traditional culture systems fail to avoid alcohol volatilization, leaving the pathogenic mechanisms underlying low-concentration alcohol-induced retinal developmental abnormalities at physiological levels still unclear. In this study, we established a long-term low-concentration (0.03% and 0.1% for 3 weeks) and short-term intoxicating-concentration (0.2% for 24 hours) alcohol exposure model based on microfluidic human retinal organoid chip. We found that long-term 0.1% alcohol exposure leads to reduced proliferation, elevated apoptosis, and severe disruption of the structural organization of the neural retina in human retinal organoids. Using single nuclear RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), we identified a population of abnormal neurons as HuC/D+/Brn-3A- neurons. SnRNA-seq combined with experimental validation revealed a significant increase in this population following alcohol treatment. Furthermore, we identified that impaired energy metabolism in retinal progenitor cells represents the primary mechanism underlying this aberrant differentiation. Alcohol exposure (0.03%) caused a milder phenotype. Additionally, we observed that short-term exposure to intoxication concentrations of alcohol induced developmental delay in human retinal organoids. Notably, Microelectrode Array recordings further demonstrated that alcohol treatment significantly impaired the functional maturation of human retinal organoids. This study identifies impaired energy metabolism as a key driver of alcohol-induced aberrant neurogenesis in human retinal development, providing a mechanistic basis for exploring therapeutic interventions for fetal alcohol spectrum disorder-associated retinal lesions. It also confirms that the microfluidic retinal organoid chip serves as a reliable platform for the toxicological investigation of volatile substances represented by alcohol.

title: Navigating the Digital Peso: The Influence of Social Media Marketing and Technology on E-wallet Adoption for Business Owners in San Jose, Batangas
abstract: The Philippines is undergoing a significant digital transformation, with electronic transactions accounting for over 57% of total retail payment volume in 2024, a trend driven by national policy and a tech-savvy population. While this indicates a national shift towards a cashless society, a significant paradox exists at the micro-enterprise level, where a majority of small business owners express a reluctance to adopt e-wallets, citing ingrained habits and a perception that the technology may not significantly improve their business performance. This study addresses this gap by investigating the phenomenon of e-wallet adoption in the unique local context of San Jose, Batangas, a municipality characterized by its dominant agricultural economy as the "Egg Basket of the Philippines" and its contrasting digitally-advanced local government. The study examines the dual influence of social media marketing and technological factors on the behavioral intention of business owners to use e-wallets. The study seeks to determine how social influence and technological attributes like perceived ease of use and security can overcome documented resistance to change. The study reveals that e-wallet adoption in San Jose, Batangas, is driven by a powerful synergy of social influence, technical utility, and structural support, with social media marketing acting as the primary catalyst for shaping a positive digital mindset. Regression analysis confirms that while performance expectancy is the strongest motivator, the presence of reliable facilitating conditions is critical for translating intention into actual business practice. It is recommended that e-wallet providers shift toward community-centric strategies using local "social anchors," while the local government should institutionalize digital norms through infrastructure improvements and business incentives like permit discounts for cashless-ready stalls.

title: An Explainable Software-Based Framework for Pre-Symptomatic Grape Disease Risk Assessment Using MobileNetV2, Grad-CAM, and Weather Data
abstract: Viticulture faces severe yield losses from major fungal diseases such as Downy Mildew, Powdery Mildew, and Black Rot. Existing deep learning classification models predominantly rely on visible symptomatic lesions on leaves or fruit clusters. However, waiting for visual symptoms to manifest often delays chemical mitigation beyond the optimal therapeutic window, resulting in irreversible crop degradation. This paper proposes a software-based, explainable framework for pre-symptomatic grape disease risk assessment. The architecture combines finegrained leaf image feature extraction using MobileNetV2 with micro-climate weather telemetry (temperature, relative humidity, leaf wetness duration, and rainfall forecast). To ensure clinical transparency for agronomists and farmers, Explainable AI (XAI) is integrated via Gradientweighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM), generating visual saliency heatmaps that highlight sub-visual cellular stress indicators and necrotic margins. A dynamic Epidemiological Micro-Climate Risk Index (EMRI) fuses deep learning probabilities with real-time weather analytics. Evaluated on multi-source datasets including PlantVillage and field-captured vineyard imagery, MobileNetV2 achieves a classification accuracy of 97.84%. Based on a comprehensive literature review, a critical research gap is identified: current agricultural systems treat image classification and micro-climate forecasting as disjoint workflows without explainable decision support. The proposed framework fills this gap through an integrated web and mobile platform featuring automated risk alerts and actionable advisory generation

title: TerraSense AI: Soil Quality Classification Using Image Processing, Deep Learning and an AI-Based Soil Advisory System
abstract: Knowing the soil type of a field is one of the first steps in agricultural planning, yet judging it by eye is subjective and laboratory analysis is slow. This paper presents TerraSense AI, a web-based prototype that sorts soil photographs into seven classes (Alluvial, Arid, Black, Laterite, Mountain, Red and Yellow) using a convolutional neural network (CNN) built with TensorFlow and Keras and served through Flask. The CyAUG-Dataset held 5,097 images before we audited it for exact duplicates, which turned up 54 duplicate groups and 55 extra files. We split the data only after handling the duplicates and resized every image to 224 × 224 RGB. On the held-out test split the model reached 93.42% accuracy, 92.89% weighted F1 and 83.07% macro F1, with Arid and Mountain soils noticeably weaker than the other classes. Around the classifier, the prototype adds a provisional, dataset-relative NPK rating drawn from a 257-row measurement table, a SQLite prediction history with analytics, and an AI Soil Advisor that is still under development. The CNN predicts soil type from an image; it does not measure fertility, nutrient concentration, crop suitability or overall soil health, and the NPK ratings are not validated agronomic thresholds. All results come from one dataset, so performance on other data remains untested. The contribution of this work is an integrated, transparent prototype together with an honest account of what its evaluation does and does not show
