title: Leakage-Free Evaluation of Capsule Network Heads for Brain Tumor MRI Classification
abstract: Background: Deep learning studies using the widely used Brain Tumor MRI Dataset routinely report accuracies above 95%. However, the dataset combines overlapping public collections, and capsule networks are often promoted for such data without controlled comparisons. Objective: This study quantified duplicate-induced data leakage in the dataset and investigated whether capsule heads improve classification under leakage-free evaluation. Methods: Exact and near-duplicate slices were identified using file hashing and correlation analysis of head-cropped thumbnails, with the correlation threshold calibrated against label-conflict rates. Ten models using three backbones were trained under a unified protocol with five random seeds on a consumer-grade GPU. Capsule, dense, and pooling heads were compared. The models were also evaluated using the original, potentially leaky split, and their rotation robustness and inference costs were assessed. Results: Near-duplicates linked 1,707 of 5,712 training images (29.9%) to images in the test set, and data leakage inflated test accuracy by 3.22–6.33 percentage points through both memorization and the larger effective training set. With a lightweight backbone trained from scratch, the capsule head improved macro-F1 by 7.16 percentage points over the dense head while using 91.3% fewer parameters, and by 6.63 percentage points over the pooling head. These improvements were consistent across all five random seeds. However, the capsule head provided no improvement with ImageNet-pretrained backbones and did not consistently reduce the loss in accuracy under rotation. Conclusion: Capsule heads appear to offer the greatest benefit when features are learned from limited data. Leakage-free evaluation across multiple random seeds is essential for credible brain tumor MRI benchmarks. These conclusions apply to the tested public dataset and experimental protocol and do not constitute clinical validation.

title: Explainable Industry-Aware Social Media Virality Prediction Using Temporal and Categorical Features
abstract: This study proposes an explainable, industry-aware machine learning framework to predict social media post virality using pre-publication metadata. Utilizing 528 observations (January 2025–February 2026) from Instagram and TikTok across the IT, F&B, and manufacturing sectors, virality was defined using a leakage-free 75th-percentile engagement threshold. Several classifiers, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, XGBoost, and CatBoost, were evaluated using five-fold stratified cross-validation and time-based testing. Model interpretability was addressed using SHAP analysis, and optimal posting times were simulated via a marginal approach.During cross-validation, the categorical-only XGBoost achieved an F1-score of 0.4158 and ROC-AUC of 0.6046, while the operational simulation model (combined_main_no_client) yielded a lower F1-score of 0.3581. In chronological final-test evaluation (January–February 2026), the model suffered severe performance decay due to temporal covariate shift, dropping to an F1-score, Recall, and Precision of 0.2917, while missing 70.83% of actual viral cases. SHAP analysis identified month index and IT industry affiliation as the strongest predictive features. These findings highlight the challenges of pre-publication virality forecasting and emphasize the vulnerability of static classifiers to temporal shifts in low-sample environments.
journal: International Journal of Advances in Data and Information Systems

title: Decorrelation and Deformation: Sentinel-1 InSAR Analysis of the March 2025 Earthquake in Central Myanmar and along the Sagaing Fault
abstract: A moment magnitude (Mw) 7.7 earthquake, as reported by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), struck central Myanmar on 28 March 2025. Its epicenter was situated near the Sagaing Fault, a major right-lateral strike-slip fault system that accommodates the relative motion between the Indian and Sunda plates. As one of Southeast Asia’s most active tectonic structures, the Sagaing Fault has a history of producing destructive earthquakes, and this event caused significant ground displacement and surface rupture particularly across the Mandalay and Sagaing regions, which lie directly along its central segment. Using Sentinel-1 satellite imagery and advanced Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) techniques, the co-seismic deformation was mapped and quantified with high precision, revealing clear patterns of displacement. Interferometric phase analysis indicated a reported maximum line-of-sight (LOS) pixel displacement of 52.0 cm, which requires coherence and phase-unwrapping validation before it can be interpreted as ground displacement concentrated near the fault trace while coherence analysis showed localized areas of signal decorrelation corresponding to intense ground disturbance. To refine rupture mapping, the Normalized Coherence Change Index (NCCI) was applied for the identification of severely damaged zones. Spatial analysis further indicates that as the distance from the epicenter increases, the deformation amplitude gradually decreases, which is consistent with the typical elastic strain release of strike-slip faults. Quantitative assessments were conducted by dividing the affected area into multiple zones for the evaluation of displacement gradients and rupture extent. The results provide new insights into the mechanics of active fault systems in central Myanmar and reveal the spatial patterns of ground movement associated with large-magnitude seismic events. These findings identify regions of high seismic vulnerability and highlight the importance of remote sensing combined with ground-based observations for hazard assessment, infrastructure resilience planning and earthquake preparedness.
journal: Journal of Island and Marine Studies

title: Mapping soil salinization in the Shirvan plain based on Sentinel-2 data
abstract: In this study, we used topographic indices derived from digital elevation model (DEM), SAR and vegetation indices generated by Sentinel-2 to map soil salinization in the Kurdamir, located in the central and northern Shirvan plain of Azerbaijan Republic, and evaluated the potential of multi-source sensors to predict soil salinity. This paper reflects the results of assessing the degree of salinity of Kurdamir soils based on remote sensing technologies. Classification of soils by salinity degree was performed using indices calculated from data in Sentinel-2 spectral channels. Based on a comparative analysis of machine learning and remote sensing methods, it was found that they provide similar results for soil salinity assessment, when the study area does not cover a large area of land. Using the soil electrical conductivity (EC) values of soil sampling sites as the target variable, and the optimal environmental factors as the predictive variable, we constructed three soil salinity inversion models based on classification and regression tree (CART), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). This work has important implications for understanding soil salinity dynamics, and could be used in further research on land and agricultural management at the regional level.

title: LoGA: Loop-Carried Graph Attention Based Looped Vision Transformers for Fine-Grained Plant Disease Classification
abstract: Fine-grained plant disease classification requires separating classes of the same crop that often differ only in small, sparse lesion patterns. Looped Vision Transformers (LoopViTs) obtain depth by applying a small stack of weight-tied blocks repeatedly, yet each block rebuilds its attention graph from scratch at every iteration, although the same block has just computed a graph over the same tokens. We propose LoGA, a looped vision transformer with Loop-Carried Graph Attention, in which the attention graph of each block at iteration $t$ is biased by the graph the same block produced at iteration $t-1$, used as a tempered prior. In its log-prob form the update $A_t \propto \exp(QK^\top/\sqrt{d})\odot A_{t-1}^{\gamma}$ is, when the floor is inactive, equivalent to attending with a geometrically discounted sum of past query-key logits; a flash-compatible qk variant carries one step of raw logits. LoGA adds 24 scalars to a 9.91\,M-parameter model and reduces exactly to vanilla LoopViT at initialisation. We also study a parameter-free graph-stability signal $\Delta_t$ and show that, under label smoothing, predictive entropy stays near 0.671 nats, so a common entropy-exit threshold is never reached. Trained from scratch, LoGA-logprob reaches 99.78%, 94.2%, 98.6% and 99.53% top-1 accuracy on the held-out splits of PlantVillage, PlantDoc, Cassava and Plant Pathology 2020, versus 98.11%, 88.3%, 84.4% and 91.7% for vanilla LoopViT. On PlantVillage, the CLS-attention graph contracts across iterations and accuracy is maintained at twice the training depth. We regard these results as encouraging first evidence and discuss their limitations.
journal: ICCK Transactions on Emerging Topics in Artificial Intelligence

title: Explaining Organizational Decoupling through Informal Governance: A Latent Mediation Model of Academic Discipline
abstract: This study examines how Informal governance is associated with Organizational decoupling among Chinese university students, with Academic discipline proposed as an explanatory mechanism. Drawing on self-determination and self-regulated learning perspectives, a conditional process model was specified and evaluated using a synthetic dataset of 486 cases. The simulated measurement model demonstrated acceptable reliability (composite reliability = 0.84) and fit (CFI = 0.95, TLI = 0.94, RMSEA = 0.049, SRMR = 0.046). Structural estimates suggested that Informal governance was positively associated with Academic discipline (β = 0.35, p < .001) and with Organizational decoupling (β = 0.25, p < .001). The standardized indirect effect through Academic discipline was 0.15, with a synthetic 95% bootstrap interval excluding zero. Together, the modeled predictors explained 42% of the variance in Organizational decoupling. The paper contributes a concise mechanism-based account of adaptive learning and demonstrates an empirical structure aligned with The Journal of Interactive Social Sciences. Because all results are simulated, the findings are illustrative and require validation with ethically collected data.
journal: The Journal of Interactive Social Sciences

title: A multispecies foundation model for genome function prediction, gene annotation and sequence design
abstract: Comparative genomics and synthetic biology require models that can interpret, annotate, and design DNA sequences across species, yet genomic models have not combined these capabilities beyond a few well-characterized organisms. Here we introduce Nucleotide Transformer v3 (NTv3), a long-context cross-kingdom foundation model that provides a common backbone for functional prediction, gene annotation and controllable sequence generation across phylogenetically diverse species. NTv3 is pretrained on more than 128,000 genomes using sequences up to 1 Mb and post-trained on 16,262 functional tracks across 15 animal and plant genomes. NTv3 performs comparably to AlphaGenome on matched human assays and matches or exceeds evaluated published models for functional-track prediction across 19 species spanning mammals, birds, fish, plants, fungi and protists. Ablation experiments show that both genome pre-training and expanding functional supervision from human and mouse to 15 species improve track prediction. Leveraging these learned functional representations, NTv3 outperforms leading ab initio gene predictors across mammals, plants and insects, with fewer spurious gene models and improved recovery and reduced fragmentation of long genes. Finally, the same representations can be used with discrete diffusion to design regulatory DNA sequences with specific activity levels. We demonstrate this in plant and fly promoters and enhancers, and experimentally validate the activity and promoter selectivity of the generated fly enhancers. Together, NTv3 unifies genome interpretation, gene annotation and regulatory sequence design across the animal and plant kingdoms, with direct relevance to agriculture, biodiversity research and biotechnology.

title: An Agentic AI Pipeline for an Evidence-Grounded Environmental Health Public Information System: Development and Evaluation
abstract: Background: Existing environmental and health information systems typically provide isolated data streams, requiring users to interpret heterogeneous information sources without personalized guidance. Residents and health providers of urban regions with complex environmental conditions, such as the Salt Lake Valley, frequently seek timely, location-specific information about weather, air quality, and their associated health impacts, but may find it difficult to integrate this information in their decision-making, precluding the effective translation of valuable environmental health information into action. Objective: This study aimed to develop and evaluate an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) pipeline that delivers evidence-grounded, neighborhood-scale responses to health-related environmental questions raised lay persons by dynamically orchestrating authoritative weather, neighborhood-scale environmental observations, air quality, and health-evidence resources. Methods: We developed an agentic AI pipeline using LangGraph and OpenAI large language models to interpret natural language queries, select and invoke relevant external tools, retrieve real-time environmental data and evidence-based health guidance, and synthesize responses. The pipeline integrates multiple authoritative resources, including weather forecasts, air-quality observations, geospatial services, and a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) module built from asthma-related clinical guidance. The system incorporates fallback mechanisms to improve robustness when external services are unavailable. We evaluated the pipeline using a curated benchmark of representative user questions, assessing tool-needed recognition, correct tool selection, avoidance of irrelevant tools, parameter mapping, analytic pathway selection, and incorporation of tool outputs into the final response. Results: The developed system successfully integrated heterogeneous environmental and health information sources into a unified conversational interface that produces evidence-grounded, neighborhood-scale responses for the Salt Lake Valley. Evaluation demonstrated generally strong tool recognition, parameter mapping, and incorporation of retrieved information across diverse question types, supporting the pipeline's ability to retrieve and integrate authoritative environmental and health information consumable by lay persons and providing an important step for the T3 and T4 phases of the translational pipeline of exposure health informatics. Conclusions: By combining existing environmental health knowledge with local sensor observations and neighborhood-scale environmental measurements, and authoritative state and national weather and air quality resources, the system delivers more localized and context-aware guidance than approaches that rely on authoritative regional or state-level information. Rather than depending on the internal knowledge of a large language model, the pipeline dynamically retrieves, synthesizes, and attributes evidence from authoritative sources. The modular architecture enables seamless integration of additional environmental data streams, health knowledge sources, and geographic regions, providing a scalable foundation for future translational pipelines, completing the T3 to T4 path for environmental health.

title: DiaBench: A Benchmarking Framework to Evaluate the Performance of LLMs in T2D Patient Education
abstract: Background Effective type 2 diabetes (T2D) education improves patient outcomes, but clinician time constraints limit what can be covered during encounters. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable way to answer patient questions, yet their accuracy and reliability in T2D education across health literacy levels remain poorly characterized. Methods We developed DiaBench, a standardized benchmarking framework built from 96 question-and-answer pairs collected by clinicians from representative real-world patient encounters. GPT-5 transformed each pair into multiple-choice questions (MCQs) under three configurations (1-3) simulating different question formats and levels of user background. A five-member panel of certified diabetes care and education specialists (CDCESs), medical doctors (MDs), and endocrinologists validated the transformations, rating question rephrasing, answer rephrasing, and answer correctness. We then evaluated seven LLMs (GPT-51, Gemini-2.5-Flash2, Cohere Command3, Llama-44, DeepSeek-R15, Perplexity Sonar6, Mistral-Large-2.07) for accuracy and self-consistency across three runs. Results (i) Expert validation showed a consensus over MCQ transformation. For configuration 1, 98.1% (SD 0.01) of rephrased answers were appropriate, 98.1% (SD 0.01) of MCQ answers were correct, and 95.0% (SD 0.05) of rephrased questions were appropriate; corresponding values for configuration 2 were 96.3% (SD 0.05), 97.5% (SD 0.02), and 89.8% (SD 0.14). (ii) across benchmarking for configurations 1 and 2, most models achieved high accuracy ([≥]95%), but Mistral-Large-2.0, Llama 4, and Perplexity Sonar showed substantially lower self-consistency (60.4%-91.7%) than other models ([≥]95%). All models degraded in both accuracy and self-consistency on configuration 3. Conclusions DiaBench quantitatively differentiates LLM capability in T2D patient education, with Gemini, GPT-5, and DeepSeek-R1 performing strongly and other models suboptimally. DiaBench provides a transferable platform for evaluating existing and newly developed LLMs, addressing the need for standardized benchmarking before clinical deployment of LLM-based systems in patient education.

title: PedDx: An End-to-End Deep Learning Framework for Pediatric Posterior Fossa Tumor Diagnosis with Agentic AI-Enabled Independent External Evaluation
abstract: Reliable clinical translation of diagnostic artificial intelligence (AI) requires evaluation beyond classification accuracy. We developed PedDx, a segmentation-free framework for pediatric posterior fossa tumor diagnosis using T2-weighted MRI, pretrained 3DINO representations, calibrated predictions, and confidence-based abstention. Evaluation included 492 discovery, 114 replication, 129 external validation, and 40 independently tested cases, alongside 236 out-of-distribution (OOD) cases and controlled imaging perturbations. Classification accuracy was 79.8% in replication and 81.4% in external validation, increasing to 90.5% and 88.7%, respectively, among non-abstained cases. OOD analyses revealed performance degradation and confidently incorrect predictions, while perturbation analyses identified acquisition and alignment vulnerabilities. An external institution independently executed the complete agentic workflow, successfully generating predictions and structured quality-control reports for all 40 cases, with classification accuracy of 92.5%, increasing to 97.3% among non-abstained cases. PedDx demonstrates how uncertainty assessment, failure-mode characterization, external validation, and independently reproducible, traceable reporting can collectively inform the reliability and limitations of diagnostic AI systems.

title: Linguistic Exchange as Foreign Policy: The Brazil–Nigeria Case
abstract: Foreign policy has traditionally been conducted by central government bodies, but universities, research institutions and civil society increasingly contribute to a country’s international engagement. This article argues that linguistic exchange should be understood as an instrument of foreign policy, using Brazil and Nigeria as a case. The two countries are the most populous in their regions and share deep historical, cultural and diaspora ties, from the Agudá returnee communities of the Bight of Benin to contemporary trade, yet language remains a barrier: Portuguese in Brazil, English in Nigeria. Many Brazilians lack affordable access to quality English instruction, while Portuguese is little known in Nigerian society. The article proposes a reciprocal Brazil–Nigeria linguistic exchange programme, connecting universities and federal institutes in both countries with the support of Brazil’s Instituto Guimarães Rosa, Ministry of Education/CAPES and the International Institute of the Portuguese Language. It would offer Portuguese and English instruction at all levels, use existing digital platforms, and follow a horizontal model in which participants teach their own language in exchange for learning the partner’s. The proposal is set against planned large-scale cooperation such as the Green Imperative agricultural programme, which would require linguistic infrastructure. It is illustrated by the NIDOA Brazil Language Academy in São Paulo, a community-based example of low-cost reciprocal language learning. The article concludes that linguistic exchange can strengthen public, cultural and science diplomacy, expand educational opportunity, and consolidate South–South cooperation between Brazil and Nigeria.
journal: International Journal of Social Work and Development Studies

title: QORAQALPOG‘ISTON QISHLOQ XO‘JALIGINI RAQAMLI BOSHQARISHNING IQTISODIY SAMARADORLIGI
abstract: The article analyzes the economic efficiency of digital agricultural management under water scarcity. The study uses official data from Karakalpakstan and research findings on digital agricultural technologies. Water-saving technologies, Smart Water, remote monitoring, and digital irrigation management are examined. The results demonstrate the role of digital tools in improving water resource management and farm-level decisions. Technical maintenance and data transmission problems are also identified.

title: SUV TANQISLIGI SHAROITIDA QISHLOQ XO‘JALIGI INVESTITSIYA SIYOSATI
abstract: The article analyzes investment policy and investment efficiency in agriculture of the Republic of Karakalpakstan under water scarcity. The study considers water-saving technologies, irrigation infrastructure, digital technologies, and public-private partnerships.

title: Hybrid Machine Learning Optimization for Production Scheduling and Resource Al location in Smart Manufacturing Systems: A Review
abstract: Efficient resource allocation and production scheduling directly dictate manufacturing productivity, cost efficiency, and energy utilization. However, intensifying sustainability mandates, operational uncertainty, and demand volatility have exposed the limits of traditional, deterministic optimization methods. Consequently, contemporary research has pivoted toward integrating mathematical programming with Machine Learning (ML) to enhance decision-making under uncertainty. This review synthesizes literature from 2020 to 2026 across standalone classical optimization, ML approaches, and hybrid ML-optimization frameworks, critically evaluating their performance outcomes, archi tectural trends, and robustness across diverse manufacturing systems. The findings indicate that while mathematical models ensure solution transparency and strict constraint enforcement, ML components maximize adaptability to dynamic conditions and demand forecasting precision. While hybrid frameworks generally yield superior makespan reduction and schedule robustness, their efficacy is bounded by distinct computational latency and data-density trade-offs. Additionally, multi-tiered sensitivity and scenario analyses are established as vital diagnostics for validat ing model stability against stochastic shopfloor noise and macro-systemic shocks. Despite these analytical advances, significant deployment barriers persist regarding computational complexity, interpretability, real-time scalability, and data quality. To bridge these gaps, this review maps emerging frontiers in Industry 5.0 human-centric optimiza tion, reinforcement learning, and digital twins, providing a structured foundation for deploying resilient, scalable, and sustainable production planning systems.
journal: Global journal of Engineering Innovation and Applications

title: Comparing Random Forest and SHAP Feature Selection for LSTM-Based Stock Price Prediction
abstract: Feature selection is often used in stock price prediction, but its results remain mixed. This study analyzes the effect of feature selection based on Random Forest native feature importance (RF Importance) and SHAP on LSTM performance in predicting ADRO, ASII, and TLKM stock prices. Daily data from May 2021 to May 2026 were processed into 20 relative features from price, volume, technical indicators, and the Jakarta Composite Index (JCI), with return as the target. Both methods used the same Random Forest model and a mean-score threshold, while the LSTM was evaluated with five seeds and compared with a naive model. Feature selection reduced the input from 20 to 9 - 12 features (40% to 55%) and the LSTM parameters from 125,761 to 120,129 - 121,665 (3.3% to 4.5%). The MAPE of all schemes ranged from 1.76% to 1.90%, close to the naive model (1.72% to 1.87%), with differences between schemes of no more than 0.07 percentage points. Only for ADRO did the all-features scheme perform clearly better. Both methods retained the volume and JCI features and removed redundant trend indicators, with SHAP selecting fewer features. Therefore, the main benefit of feature selection was a simpler model input, not better prediction accuracy.

title: Technological Innovation and Green Process Innovation: A Serial Mediation Model of Information Quality and Green Work Engagement
abstract: Growing environmental concerns and increasing sustainability expectations have encouraged manufacturing organizations to adopt technological innovations that support environmentally responsible production processes. However, the mechanisms through which technological innovation enhances green process innovation remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the direct effect of technological innovation on green process innovation and examines the serial mediating roles of information quality and green work engagement in Malaysian manufacturing organizations. Drawing upon the Resource-Based View (RBV) and the Ability–Motivation–Opportunity (AMO) framework, a conceptual model was developed and empirically tested. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among employees of manufacturing organizations in Malaysia, and 391 responses were collected using a convenience sampling technique. The collected data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The findings indicate that technological innovation positively influences information quality and green process innovation. Information quality significantly enhances both green work engagement and green process innovation, while green work engagement positively contributes to green process innovation. Furthermore, the results support the mediating role of information quality and the serial mediating effects of information quality and green work engagement in the relationship between technological innovation and green process innovation. These findings highlight the importance of integrating technological capabilities with high-quality organizational information and employees' environmental engagement to achieve sustainable manufacturing practices.

title: Digital RMB 2.0 and the Transformation of the Real Economy: A Case Study of Agricultural Bank of China
abstract: The digital RMB has upgraded from “Digital Cash 1.0” to “Digital Deposit Currency 2.0,” fundamentally resolving the issue of insufficient incentives for both users and banks. Taking the Agricultural Bank of China as a case study, this paper analyzes the mechanisms and effectiveness of its role in empowering the transformation of the real economy across six dimensions: payment efficiency, smart contracts, supply chain synergy, the expansion of inclusive finance, consumer-facing (C-end) consumption, and cross-border payments. Research has found that payment and settlement allow funds to reach the payee directly in seconds, greatly improving transaction efficiency. Smart contracts are the core, and programmable currency can effectively reduce contract fulfillment costs and prevent fund misappropriation. Funds penetrate multiple levels of the industrial chain to achieve “transaction is settlement, settlement is confirmation of rights.” Agricultural Bank of China relies on its full coverage of county-level outlets and products such as Huinong e-loans to form a differentiated path to inclusive finance. C-side consumption is transmitted to the real economy through interest calculation mechanism and scenario expansion. Agricultural Bank of China relies on the multilateral central bank digital currency bridge to implement interest calculation functions and cross-border coupling effects in multiple branches. This study could provide empirical evidence on the role of Digital RMB 2.0 in the transformation of the real economy.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Plant Breeding: Data-driven Frameworks for Genomic Prediction, High-throughput Phenotyping and Accelerated Cultivar Development
abstract: Plant breeding is increasingly a data-intensive science. Modern programmes generate genome-wide marker data, multi-environment trial records, remote-sensing and sensor streams, and high-resolution images at a scale that exceeds the capacity of conventional statistical workflows. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer a set of tools for extracting predictive signal from such data. This review surveys the application of ML and deep learning across the breeding cycle, beginning with the foundations of the main algorithm families and moving to genomic selection, where linear mixed models remain the benchmark against which random forests, support vector machines, neural networks and convolutional architectures are measured. It then considers image-based high-throughput phenotyping and disease detection, modelling of genotype-by-environment interaction and integration with crop growth models, yield prediction, optimisation of training populations and trial design, and the coupling of predictive models with genome editing. Deep learning is most firmly established for image- and sensor-based phenotyping, although generalisation across sites remains a recognised weakness, whereas the advantage of ML over well-specified linear models for genomic prediction of complex traits is modest and context dependent. Key obstacles include small sample sizes relative to the number of predictors, limited model interpretability, data heterogeneity, and unequal access to computing and expertise.
journal: Journal of Advances in Biology & Biotechnology

title: Wireless Electrical Stimulation via a Conductive Hydrogel Scaffold Synergizes With Stem Cell Transplantation Therapy to Promote Traumatic Brain Injury Repair.
abstract: Electrical stimulation (ES) offers a robust approach to boost the efficacy of stem cell transplantation therapy for the treatment of neurological disorders. Notably, wireless technology blends convenience with the elimination of infection risk posed by wired connections, but the challenge lies in the integration of wireless-enabled stimulation materials and stem cell carriers. Here, we describe a flexible annular conductive dopamine-modified hyaluronic acid (HAD)/polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/carbon nanotube‌ (CNT) hydrogel that acts as a secondary coil to realize wireless ES via electromagnetic induction, while also serving as a three-dimensional (3D) scaffold carrier for endogenous neural stem cells (NSCs). Established on the annular HAD/PVA/CNT hydrogel with high conductivity and good biocompatibility, wireless ES significantly enhances neuronal differentiation of NSCs. Furthermore, transplantation of the NSC-laden annular hydrogel into a traumatic brain injury (TBI) rat model modulates the behaviors of both exogenous and endogenous neural cells. The combined therapy of wireless ES and NSC transplantation promotes neuronal differentiation in both the injury zone and hippocampus in association with the PI3K-Akt pathway, reduces post-traumatic inflammatory responses, and effectively restores motor and memory functions in TBI rats. This study offers a promising therapeutic strategy of integrating wireless ES with stem cell transplantation therapy for brain injury repair.

title: DUSP26 Regulated by YY1 Lactylation Couples Osteogenesis and Angiogenesis by Dephosphorylating PMPCB at Y141 and Activating Mitophagy in BMSCs
abstract: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) support bone formation through osteogenic differentiation and pro‐angiogenic paracrine activity, but the mechanisms coordinating these functions remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified dual‐specificity phosphatase 26 (DUSP26) as a regulator of BMSC osteogenesis and mitochondrial homeostasis. DUSP26 expression increased during osteogenic differentiation and was reduced in osteoporotic femoral tissues. p300 gain‐ and loss‐of‐function experiments, together with analysis of the Yin Yang1(YY1) K183R mutant, supported the conclusion that p300‐regulated YY1 lactylation contributes to DUSP26 transcriptional activation. DUSP26 interacted with the mitochondrial processing peptidase subunit beta(PMPCB) and reduced its tyrosine phosphorylation, with mass spectrometry and mutational analyses implicating Y141 as involved in this regulation. Functional assays supported a model in which DUSP26 limits mitochondrial processing peptidase (MPP)‐mediated PTEN‐induced kinase 1 (PINK1) processing and promotes PINK1‐dependent mitophagy, thereby supporting mitochondrial homeostasis. DUSP26 enhanced osteogenic differentiation and the pro‐angiogenic activity of BMSC‐conditioned medium(CM), whereas its knockdown impaired bone formation and reduced type H vessels in vivo. Furthermore, BMSC‐derived exosomes carrying a runt‐related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2) promoter‐driven DUSP26 plasmid produced preferential transgene expression in osteogenic‐lineage cells and attenuated ovariectomy‐induced bone loss in mice. These findings link lactylation‐associated transcriptional regulation to mitochondrial protein processing and support further preclinical evaluation of DUSP26‐directed approaches for osteoporosis.

title: Single‐Nucleus RNA Sequencing Identifies CREM as a Brake on Myofiber Hypertrophy in Chickens
abstract: Myofiber hypertrophy is central to economically important agricultural traits and vertebrate development, yet the underlying cellular and molecular programs remain elusive. Chickens have undergone substantial divergence in muscle growth following decades of artificial selection, making them a unique model for dissecting these mechanisms at single‐cell resolution. Here, we performed singlenucleus RNA sequencing on 91 144 nuclei from postnatal chicken pectoralis major. Eight major conserved cell populations were resolved, with temporal dynamics exhibiting divergence between fast‐growing broilers and slow‐growing layers. A novel terminally differentiated myocyte subpopulation (AK1 + myocytes) was markedly enriched in slow‐growing birds. Analysis revealed that accelerated myoblast expansion and delayed terminal differentiation are primary drivers of myofiber hypertrophy, supported by a pro‐growth niche involving IGF‐signaling FAPs and macrophage‐myogenic crosstalk. Further comprehensive analyses identified CREM as a master repressor of myofiber hypertrophy. Mechanistically, CREM directly binds and transcriptionally activates the JUN promoter, and both factors cooperatively sustain the expression of growth inhibitors MSTN, FBXO32, and TRIM63. In vivo and in vitro functional validation confirmed that CREM deletion promotes myofiber hypertrophy, increasing pectoralis major weight and percent by 29.96% and 20.50%, respectively. This study uncovers CREM as a novel brake on myofiber hypertrophy, offering fundamental insights into vertebrate skeletal muscle development.

title: Parallelized multi‐stimuli bioreactor for combined, physiologically relevant fluid shear stress and intermittent hydrostatic pressure in 3D bone tissue models
abstract: Regeneration of bone tissue is tightly regulated by its complex mechanical microenvironment, in which intraosseous hydrostatic pressure (HP) and interstitial fluid flow‐induced shear stress (FSS) represent key mechanical cues. While the individual effects of these stimuli have been extensively investigated, their combined influence within physiologically relevant three‐dimensional (3D) bone tissue models remains largely unexplored due to the lack of suitable experimental platforms. In this study, we present an automated, parallelized multi‐stimuli bioreactor designed to deliver tunable combinations of FSS and intermittent HP to 3D bone tissue models. The platform integrates a direct perfusion bioreactor with a custom‐designed, modular intermittent HP unit based on a solenoid pinch valve, enabling independent and combined control of flow rate and pressure waveforms. Bioreactor performance was characterized using two biomimetic polylactic acid (PLA) scaffold types, demonstrating the ability of the system to reproduce physiologically relevant ranges of HP (1.81–30.59 kPa) and FSS (0.48–683.26 mPa). Biological experiments using bone marrow‐derived mesenchymal stem cells (BM‐MSCs) suspended in a collagen matrix and seeded into PLA scaffolds, cultured for 7 days, showed that dynamic culture conditions significantly enhanced cell viability compared with static culture. Moreover, the combination of FSS and intermittent HP stimulation within daily activity‐related ranges accelerated early osteogenic differentiation compared to direct perfusion alone. Overall, the proposed platform provides a versatile and robust investigation tool for advancing bone mechanobiology and tissue engineering research.

title: Maize Anthocyanins: Biosynthesis, Regulatory Networks, and Breeding for Crop Improvement
abstract: Maize ( Zea mays L.) is an important model for studying flavonoid biosynthesis and enhancing cereal nutritional value. Its diverse anthocyanin pigmentation across kernels, vegetative, and reproductive tissues makes it especially valuable. This review summarizes anthocyanin chemistry, genetic regulation, environmental influences, breeding strategies, and opportunities to develop anthocyanin‐enriched maize. Maize anthocyanins occur predominantly as glycosides of cyanidin, pelargonidin, and peonidin, with their biosynthesis regulated through coordinated interactions between structural and regulatory genes. The MYB–bHLH–WD40 (MBW) transcriptional complex plays a central role, where MYB transcription factors ( c1 and pl1 ) and bHLH regulators ( r1/b1 family) control tissue‐specific and developmental anthocyanin accumulation. The pr1 locus, encoding flavonoid 3′‐hydroxylase, directs pigment composition by determining cyanidin‐derived purple or pelargonidin‐derived red anthocyanins. Environmental factors, including light, temperature, and nutrient availability, further influence anthocyanin biosynthesis through gene expression. Recent advances in molecular breeding and marker‐assisted selection have enabled the identification and incorporation of favorable alleles, facilitating the development of anthocyanin‐rich maize with improved nutritional value and genetic stability. Coordinated genetic regulation via the MBW complex and the pr1 metabolic switch, together with environmental modulation, governs anthocyanin diversity in maize. Marker‐assisted breeding enables efficient introgression of favorable anthocyanin traits into elite germplasm, overcoming historical linkage drag and enhancing biofortification. This review highlights the potential for developing anthocyanin‐enriched maize as a functional food and a sustainable alternative source of natural colorants.

title: vibe-qc: An Open-Source, General-Purpose Electronic-Structure Code for Molecules and Solids Developed With Generative AI.
abstract: We present vibe‐qc, a general‐purpose open‐source electronic‐structure code for molecules and solids, developed almost entirely with agentic AI under expert human direction. The code is released under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 (MPLv2). The implementation comprises a C++17 numerical core and Python calculation drivers. Molecular methods include Hartree–Fock, Kohn–Sham DFT, Møller–Plesset theory and double hybrids, coupled cluster, active‐space methods, and excited states. Dispersion corrections, continuum solvation, and effective core potentials are also available. Periodic calculations use Gaussian‐basis HF and DFT with Brillouin‐zone sampling. Molecular and periodic method coverage differs; the feature matrices specify analytic and numerical derivatives and distinguish validated and experimental implementations. The validation set is a key contribution of this work. It combines independent program comparisons, published benchmarks, and internal consistency tests. Molecular mean‐field energies agree at the nanohartree scale, and conventional CCSD(T) energies agree within 3.3×10−7Eh for the tested systems. Local‐correlation and periodic limitations are reported with the comparisons. Numerical results, calculation metadata, and analysis scripts are supplied as machine‐readable Supporting Information. The independently maintained vibe‐view viewer, vibe‐queue scheduler, and qvf toolkit support visualization and job management; trexio provides wavefunction interchange.

title: Radiomic Signatures From Conventional MRI Predict Recovery in Obstetric Brachial Plexus Palsy: A Machine Learning Approach in Infants.
abstract: PURPOSE Obstetric brachial plexus palsy (OBPP) causes variable neurological outcomes, but early prognostic biomarkers remain limited. This study evaluated whether radiomic features extracted from routine T2-STIR MRI can predict functional recovery in infants with OBPP, and whether combining these features with routinely available clinical predictors improves prognostic performance. METHODS In this prospective single-center study, 39 infants with OBPP (mean age 12.5 ± 5.7 weeks) underwent 3 T MRI during physiological sleep. Postganglionic lesions were semi-automatically segmented on coronal T2-STIR images, and 111 radiomic features were extracted per patient. After a minimum two-year clinical follow-up (mean 25.5 ± 2.0 months; range 24-32 months), patients were classified as having complete (n = 17) or partial recovery (n = 22). Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm. Five supervised machine learning models were trained and internally optimized on the training set (n = 28) using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV), and their performance was subsequently evaluated on an independent holdout test set (n = 11). A clinical model (Narakas classification, birth weight, pseudomeningocele) and a combined clinical-radiomic model, summarized as a nomogram, were additionally developed. RESULTS Eight radiomic features, including shape, first-order, and texture metrics, differentiated recovery groups. Among the radiomics-only models, SVM-RBF performed best (training AUC = 0.929, F1-score = 0.889; test AUC = 0.867, F1-score = 0.750), followed by random forest (training AUC = 0.952; test AUC = 0.783); test-set specificity was low for several classifiers. The combined clinical-radiomic model outperformed the radiomics-only model (training AUC = 1.000; test AUC = 0.933, accuracy = 0.818), and the bias-corrected calibration curve of the nomogram showed good agreement with observed outcomes (mean absolute error = 0.07). CONCLUSION Radiomic analysis of routine T2-STIR MRI shows promise for predicting recovery in OBPP, and its combination with simple clinical predictors further improves discrimination. Given the small sample size and the performance drop between training and test sets, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and hypothesis-generating, and require validation in larger, multicenter cohorts before clinical use.

title: Productivity, Stability, and Adaptability of Onion Genotypes Using Additive Main Effects and Multiplicative Interaction and Mixed‐Model Analysis
abstract: Onion ( Allium cepa L.) is a vegetable crop of both nutritional and medicinal importance. Bulb development is strongly dependent on the interaction between photoperiod and temperature, which drives the adaptation of genotypes to specific growing conditions. The objective of this study was to assess the agronomic performance of different onion genotypes across diverse environments, focusing on stability and adaptability through the Additive Main effects and Multiplicative Interaction (AMMI) analysis and mixed‐model (REML‐BLUP) methods using the harmonic mean of relative performance of genotypic values (MHPRVG). Six genotypes were tested in a randomized complete block design across three growing seasons: one in Barra do Rio Azul–RS and two in Florianopolis–SC. Evaluated traits included bulb production (classified by transverse diameter), total yield, percentage of commercial bulbs, and resistance to Botrytis squamosa . High commercial quality was noted, with 85.3% commercial bulbs for genotype PO‐39 achieving 28.26 t ha −1 total yield, confirming the importance of balancing yield and quality in cultivar selection. The AMMI model proved effective in identifying onion genotypes with high yield potential and wide adaptability, consistent with the MHPRVG mixed‐model results. These findings offer guidance for future research and breeding strategies, ensuring that new onion varieties meet market demands and are economically viable for producers.
journal: New Zealand Journal of Crop and Horticultural Science

title: Effectiveness of model-based decision tools for disease control in wheat, potato and grapevine: a multilevel meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND A multilevel meta-analysis was conducted to provide further evidence on the benefits of decision tools (DTs) in crop protection for grapevines, potato, and wheat. Published data on disease severity, the Treatment Frequency Index (TFI; an index combining the number and dose of fungicide sprays), and crop yield (for potato and wheat only) in standard farmer- (ST) and DT-based fungicide scheduling, compared with untreated controls (UTC), were collected through a systematic literature review. Experience-based (EX) interventions were also included for grapevines, with treatments scheduled according to monitoring or crop phenology. The data set (516 comparisons) comprised substantial among-study variability in disease severity. RESULT In grapevine, DT and ST showed similar disease control, with >75% efficacy compared with UTC; DT significantly reduced TFI by 40% in both organic and integrated pest management systems compared with ST. Despite reduced TFI, EX provided significantly lower disease control than both ST and DT. In potato, ST showed significantly lower disease severity than DT (9.2% and 10.2% severity, respectively), corresponding to 52.4% and 45.8% efficacy. DT reduced TFI by 31% compared with ST, while maintaining a similar yield. In wheat, ST provided a slightly lower but significant disease severity than DT (18.0% and 19.8%, respectively), corresponding to 64.2% and 51.8% efficacy, respectively, compared with UTC. DT reduced TFI by 42% and yield by 3%. CONCLUSION Our results showed that DTs can contribute to reducing fungicide dependence, although their performance can vary among crops. Farmers should be supported in the appropriate use of DTs to achieve more sustainable crop protection. © 2026 The Author(s). Pest Management Science published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Synaptic Molecules Expression in the Hippocampus After Reinstatement of Methamphetamine Conditioned Place Preference.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Drug addiction treatment remains a significant challenge in addiction relapse, which is associated with brain regions including the hippocampus (Hip). The Hip is part of the limbic system and linked to memory and learning processes closely associated with relapse. Drugs alter glutamate neurotransmission and molecules such as presynaptic and postsynaptic membrane proteins and synaptic modulators. Methamphetamine (METH) is a psychostimulant and induces addictive behaviors. METH has high addiction potential. However, the specific synaptic molecules in the Hip under METH relapse conditions are unclear. METHODS In the study, mice were given 2.5 mg/kg METH for 7 days, followed by extinction and reinstatement with 1.0 mg/kg METH. Western blot analysis was used to examine the expression of glutamatergic receptors, synapse-related proteins, and other molecules. RESULTS 1.0 mg/kg METH induced the reinstatement of conditioned place preference (CPP) in mice. The expression of Dopamine D1 receptor (D1R), Vesicular glutamate transporter 1 (VGLUT1), VGLUT2, N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor 2B (NR2B), α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR), synaptophysin (Syn), postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD-95), and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) was increased. The expression of Cerebellin 1 precursor (Cbln1), complement component 1q subcomponent (C1q), and Homeobox A5 (Hoxa5) was upregulated; the expression of Cbln3, neurogranin (Ng), and neurogenic differentiation 2 (NeuroD2) was decreased. DISCUSSION The results suggest that synaptic molecules in the Hip are involved in METH relapse. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT Using a METH‑induced conditioned place preference reinstatement model in male C57BL/6 mice, this study systematically examined expression levels of multiple synaptic‑related proteins in the hippocampus. Our findings provide experimental evidence that may contribute to understanding the synaptic molecules underlying METH relapse. However, given the exclusive use of male animals and the whole‑hippocampus homogenate approach, these results should be interpreted with caution given these limitations. Further studies incorporating female subjects and region‑specific analyses are essential to determine the generalizability and spatial specificity of these molecular alterations, and to evaluate whether hippocampal synaptic molecules could serve as viable targets for intervention in METH addiction.

title: Information integrity and the justice of agri-food transitions

Migrant Labor and Regional Economic Performance: Spatial Associations by Skill Level and Industrial Structure
abstract: This study investigates how skill-specific migrant labor is associated with regional economic performance, with a focus on industrial structure and spatial interdependence. Using a balanced panel of 16 metropolitan cities and provinces in Korea over the period 2012–2023, we estimate spatial panel models and adopt the Spatial Durbin Model as the main specification because the diagnostics indicate spatial dependence and the research question requires decomposition into direct, indirect, and total effects. The results indicate that a higher share of low-skilled migrant labor is positively associated with regional GRDP per capita, both within regions and through indirect spatial associations across neighboring regions. In contrast, the association for high-skilled migrant labor is more contingent on regional production structures. Although the baseline estimates suggest a negative average association, this relationship varies systematically by industrial composition. The association becomes more favorable in manufacturing-oriented regions, although this manufacturing-related pattern is less robust to the inclusion of additional native labor-market controls. In service-oriented regions, the within-region association is less favorable, but positive indirect associations make the overall spatial-system association more favorable. Taken together, the findings show that the economic role of migrant labor is shaped by both industrial heterogeneity and spatial interconnectedness. These findings imply that migrant labor policy should be spatially and industrially differentiated, with attention to skill-specific matching and cross-regional indirect spatial associations rather than uniform national allocation.

title: Nanoformulations of Asiatic Acid and Asiatic Acid-enriched Fraction of Centella asiatica Preserve Mitochondrial and Dopaminergic Integrity in Cellular and MPTP-induced Mouse Models of Parkinson’s Disease
Agricultural systems modelling in a changing world: virtual issue on the Agricultural Production Systems SIMulator (APSIM)
Landscape connectivity and climatic drivers shaping Noctuidae communities in a Brazilian seasonally dryland fruit-producing region
abstract: Drylands are highly sensitive to climatic shifts, affecting insect population dynamics and multi-trophic interactions. This study evaluated Noctuidae diversity and temporal distribution in the São Francisco Valley, a semi-arid, irrigated, fruit-producing region in Northeast Brazil, in relation to local environmental factors. We conducted monitoring over two consecutive years using Pennsylvania light traps deployed across two agricultural landscapes integrated with native Caatinga dry forest: an experimental multi-crop station and a commercial table grape farm. We captured 12,407 Noctuidae moths; raw richness favored the grapevine site, but diversity did not differ, and per-individual richness favored the multi-crop site once sampling effort was considered. Four Noctuinae species dominated the assemblage (94.04% of total captures): Spodoptera frugiperda (Smith) (39.53%), Elaphria agrotina (Guenée) (36.89%), Spodoptera cosmioides (Walker) (9.21%), and Spodoptera albula (Walker) (8.40%). Immediate captures of S. frugiperda and S. albula rose with lower wind speed and higher precipitation; previous-month captures showed the same patterns for S. frugiperda and S. albula, but E. agrotina responded to temperature and S. cosmioides to site and precipitation instead. Circular statistics indicated a stark temporal segregation between S. frugiperda and S. cosmioides. These findings suggest Caatinga connectivity elevates vineyard abundance, whereas the multi-crop mosaic’s heterogeneity yields higher per-individual richness. Specialized crop management practices, such as continuous vineyard pruning, generate stable niches that favor detritivorous species like E. agrotina. Local multi-year calibrations are essential for accurate pest forecasting and integrated management across agricultural-forest interfaces in semi-arid zones.

title: SPEI-based drought forecasting using decomposition-coupled LSTM models: a case study of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea
Prioritizing Circular Supply Chain Strategies in Construction: A Hybrid Delphi–AHP–DEMATEL–TOPSIS Framework
abstract: The construction industry is a major contributor to economic development in the United Arab Emirates (UAE); however, it simultaneously places considerable pressure on natural resources, energy systems, and construction and demolition waste management infrastructure. Despite national sustainability initiatives such as the Circular Economy Policy 2031 and Net Zero 2050, the implementation of circular supply chain (CSC) practices within the UAE construction sector remains fragmented and operationally inconsistent. Existing studies provide limited empirically grounded and context-specific decision-support approaches capable of prioritizing circular strategies while accounting for multidimensional sustainability trade-offs and interdependencies among influencing factors. To address this gap, this study develops and validates an integrated multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework for evaluating and prioritizing CSC strategies in the UAE construction sector. The framework integrates Delphi, Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL), and Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). Delphi established expert consensus on evaluation dimensions, AHP quantified hierarchical importance, DEMATEL identified causal relationships among sustainability criteria, and TOPSIS prioritized alternative CSC strategies. Expanded robustness and sensitivity analyses were further conducted to evaluate ranking stability under multiple weighting and alternative-removal scenarios. The findings indicate that environmental criteria received the highest hierarchical importance, while DEMATEL identified environmental and technological dimensions as dominant causal drivers within the CSC system. At the strategy level, Modular Prefabrication and Off-site Manufacturing (A2) emerged as the most preferred strategy with the highest TOPSIS closeness coefficient (CC = 0.841649), followed by BIM/IoT-enabled Material Traceability (A4) (CC = 0.581554), Construction and Demolition (C&D) Waste Recycling (A1) (CC = 0.36718), Green Procurement and Local Sourcing (A3) (CC = 0.349074) and Reverse Logistics and Take-back Systems (A5) (CC = 0.213104). Expanded sensitivity and alternative-removal analyses further demonstrated that the prioritization of A2 and A4 remained stable across multiple perturbation scenarios, confirming the robustness of the proposed decision-making framework. The study also fulfills its theoretical contribution by empirically differentiating between importance and causality-based appraisals in circular supply chain decision-making and by showing the usefulness of thoroughly integrated hybrid MCDM models in sparse and scarce data situations. In practice, the findings can be inferred to actionable recommendations for construction companies, supply chain management, and policy makers to align high-leverage circular drivers with strategic investments. Altogether, the suggested framework will provide a clear, high-quality, and context-sensitive decision-support tool to speed up the circular supply chain change in the UAE construction industry and similar emerging economies.

title: Explainable multi-agent AI systems for intelligent software engineering and business automation
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) are revolutionizing software programming and enterprise business automation in the 4th industrial revolution era. Current multi-agent systems, however, are constrained in being able to collaborate, in understanding how to reach consensus, in their knowledge sharing and, in their ability, to adapt to changes and therefore are not suitable for certain industrial critical applications. To address the above challenges, this paper introduces a cognitive swarm-based multi-agent framework with collaborative reasoning, collective cognitive memory, explainable decision intelligence, digital twin simulation and autonomous governance, which are integrated into an explainable cognitive swarm control framework XCognitive SwarmNet. Proposed framework mathematically models agent collaboration, trust, explainability, Knowledge sharing and Optimization of the flow of business tasks to support the complete Software Development Lifecycle and Intelligent Business process Automation. By using the powerful and representative software engineering and business process datasets, some experimental assessments are performed and the proposed mechanism is compared to six state-of-the-art multi-agent approaches. The proposed framework completes the task with 98.1% accuracy, reduces resource consumption by 22.8% relative to the selected baseline/reference configuration, achieves 97.5% in explainability fidelity, optimizes the workflow by 95.9% and optimizes the efficiency of agent collaboration by 94.7% with a 27.4% reduction in execution time. Overall, the results indicate that XCognitive SwarmNet provides a promising framework for transparent, adaptive, and trustworthy AI-assisted software engineering and business automation, while further industrial validation is required before claims of deployment in safety-critical or operational Industry 4.0 environments can be established.

title: Monitoring enabled livestock decarbonization through MRV digital technologies and governance in sustainable production systems
abstract: Livestock production systems are vital to global food security, rural livelihoods, and agricultural economies, yet they remain a major source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, particularly methane (CH₄), nitrous oxide (N₂O), and carbon dioxide (CO₂). Although significant progress has been made in developing mitigation strategies, measurement tools, and monitoring technologies, the widespread adoption of climate-smart approaches within sustainable production systems is constrained by persistent and interconnected barriers. This review critically synthesizes these constraints, emphasizing the role of monitoring and sensing technologies in enabling mitigation and sustainable livestock production, and categorizing constraints across four domains: technical, economic, data-management, and socio-political. Technical limitations include uncertainties in emission factors, sensor accuracy, and the integration of advanced tools into farm operations. Economic constraints arise from high upfront costs, limited financial incentives, and market inequities that disproportionately affect smallholder producers. Data-related constraints involve fragmented datasets, inadequate monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) frameworks, and poor interoperability across production scales. Policy and governance constraints reflect institutional fragmentation, regulatory misalignment, and inequitable policy structures that hinder alignment with sustainable production objectives. Recognizing these constraints as deeply interdependent, the review highlights key solution pathways, including advances in sensing and AI-driven technologies, improved emission metrics, strengthened MRV frameworks, policy reforms, and global collaboration mechanisms. By linking uncertainty reduction in emission quantification with MRV credibility, economic incentives, governance systems, and value-chain accountability, this review positions emission monitoring as foundational infrastructure for scalable and sustainable livestock decarbonization aligned with long-term climate-neutrality objectives.

title: Imidazole derivative-regulated Cu-MOF nanozyme sensor array integrating machine learning for flavonoids detection and soy milk traceability.
abstract: Flavonoids are important natural bioactive compounds with remarkable health benefits, requiring rapid and accurate detection for food nutrition assessment and quality control. However, it remains challenging to simultaneously discriminate multiple flavonoids in complex matrices. Taking inspiration from the tunable structures of MOF-based nanozymes and the ability of sensor arrays to simultaneously detect multiple substances, we herein propose an innovative four-channel colorimetric sensor array for flavonoid identification. Four copper-based MOF nanozymes (Cu-ImC2N, Cu-ImC2, Cu-ImCl2, Cu-ImPh) were synthesized with different imidazole derivatives as ligands, showing significant differences in their peroxidase-like activities. Exploiting their specific catalytic activity variations at pH 6.0 and 6.5, the two most active nanozymes (Cu-ImC2N and Cu-ImC2) were strategically selected to construct the array. Upon processing the array data with linear discriminant analysis (LDA), the array achieved 100% accurate discrimination and quantitative detection of seven flavonoids, with limits of detection (LODs) ranging from 0.039 to 0.982 μM. Furthermore, comparisons of concentration-independent models built with multiple machine learning algorithms showed that the K-nearest neighbors (KNN) method outperformed LDA, effectively reducing interference from concentration variations. The sensor array was successfully applied to the analysis of commercial soy milk, reliably differentiating products from different brands and bean sources (e.g., soybean and mung bean). This strategy surpasses traditional single-analyte methods and holds substantial practical potential for the rapid on-site detection of complex food systems.

title: HyGage: Solving the hysteresis puzzle with a new streamflow monitoring method
abstract: 11 The questionable reliability of discharges obtained using the traditional stage–discharge 12 method under gradually varied flow conditions continues to motivate the search for 13 improved monitoring approaches that support water resources management, streamflow 14 forecasting, and multipurpose scientific investigations related to the water cycle. This 15 paper introduces HyGage, a new physically based monitoring method grounded in the 16 governing equations of spatiotemporal, gradually varied, shallow open channel flow. The 17 methodology integrates measurement elements commonly employed in the index velocity 18 and slope area methods within a unified analytical framework, enabling real time discharge 19 estimation in both steady and gradually varied flows without relying on the semi empirical 20 techniques of the past. The performance of HyGage is evaluated by comparing its discharge 21 estimates with those obtained from established methods. Unlike conventional approaches, 22 HyGage is not built around any specific instrument; instead, it can flexibly incorporate 23 combinations of immersed, close range, and remote sensing measurements through 24 seamless integration. 25

Impact of S-metolachlor, atrazine and their metabolites on the morphological, structural and functional properties of the intestinal barrier.
abstract: S-metolachlor (MTC) and atrazine (ATZ) are herbicides commonly applied to corn and soybean crops. Their persistence in water and soil has led to frequent detection of these compounds and their metabolites in the environment, supporting the need to better understand their potential impact on organisms. Contaminated water and food represent important routes of human exposure to MTC and ATZ through ingestion, bringing these compounds into direct contact with intestinal epithelial cells. Such exposure may affect intestinal epithelial function and compromise barrier integrity. We used Caco-2 cells as an in vitro model to assess the effects of exposure to MTC, ATZ and their metabolites on the morphological, structural, and functional properties of the intestinal barrier. Despite the absence of functional or morphological effects following exposure to ATZ and its metabolites, ATZ fully crossed the epithelial barrier, indicating a potential route to systemic exposure and warranting further investigation of its effects beyond the intestinal compartment. After prolonged exposure, MTC induced an epithelial hypertrophic response characterized by increased cell and nuclear size and reduced proliferation, without overt disruption of intercellular junctions or barrier integrity. In contrast, its metabolites did not induce the hypertrophic phenotype observed with MTC but displayed distinct molecular effects, highlighting the need to consider both parent compounds and their metabolites in toxicological assessments. The biological significance of this hypertrophic response and the consequences of repeated or chronic exposure remain to be determined.

Transformation of aflatoxins by a thermostable and mediator-independent laccase from Thermincola ferriacetica.
abstract: Aflatoxin, a potent carcinogenic mycotoxin, commonly contaminates crops and poses a serious threat to global food and feed security. In recent years, enzymatic degradation of aflatoxins (AFs) has attracted considerable attention, with microbial laccases being the most extensively investigated. Here, we identified a thermostable laccase from Thermincola ferriacetica (Thfe-Lac) that is capable of transforming AFB1 in the absence of mediators. Under mediator-free condition, Thfe-Lac removed over 95% of 20 μg/mL AFB1 within 12 h. The optimal pH of Thfe-Lac against ABTS and AFB1 were pH 4.0 and pH 8.0, indicating distinct oxidation mechanisms for these two substrates. Thfe-Lac exhibited its optimal temperature at 70 °C and retained over 60% of residual activity after 2 h of incubation at 70-80 °C. The addition of the natural mediator acetosyringone (AS) further enhanced the AFB1-transforming ability of Thfe-Lac. In the presence of AS, Thfe-Lac was also able to transform other mycotoxins, including zearalenone (ZEN) and deoxynivalenol (DON). Moreover, several key residues within the substrate-binding pocket were identified through molecular docking. Further quantum mechanics calculations on residue-substrate interaction models revealed that dispersion interactions played an important role in AFs binding. Notably, elimination of unfavored π-π interaction and steric hindrance significantly improved the activity of the F232A mutant. Meanwhile, the enlarged substrate binding pocket facilitate AFB1 entry and promotes closer positioning toward the His500-Cys501-His502 motif. Finally, Thfe-Lac and its mutant F232A represent efficient mediator-free laccase for decontamination of AFB1 in food and feed systems.

title: Biosurfactants in the food chain: Perspectives and challenges.
abstract: Biosurfactants (BS) of microbial origin combine inherent surface activity with unique functional properties and natural status, enabling the development of innovative clean-label products and more sustainable processing strategies. This article synthesizes recent advances in the application of BS throughout the food chain, from farm to table with particular emphasis on studies reported during the last five years and validated in food-relevant models. The review highlights BS applications in crop protection, animal health, food processing and formulation, waste valorization, and nanotechnology, while critically discussing current limitations and emerging opportunities. The multifunctional nature of BS supports their use as antimicrobial agents, functional ingredients, sanitizers, postbiotics for animal health, and components of smart and active packaging systems. Furthermore, the valorization of food residues and agro-industrial waste streams as substrates for BS production contributes to circular bioeconomy approaches and more sustainable food systems. However, despite promising laboratory-scale results, the translation of BS applications into industrial practice remains constrained by limited validation in complex food systems, production and purification costs, safety assessment requirements, and regulatory challenges. Future research should prioritize application-oriented studies, safety and regulatory frameworks to facilitate the broader adoption of BS across the food chain.

title: From SCA cupping to Coffee Value Assessment: non-interchangeable scores, multidimensional sensory profiling and sensory-volatile links in Brazilian Federal District coffees.
abstract: The Specialty Coffee Association (SCA) replaced its former cupping protocol with the Coffee Value Assessment (CVA), which separates affective quality judgments from descriptive sensory characterization. Coffees from 14 producers in the Brazilian Federal District were evaluated in 2024 and 2025. Former SCA cupping was conducted by certified Q Graders, whereas CVA was applied by a coffee-experienced, semi-trained panel. SCA and CVA affective scores were not numerically interchangeable, and their final-score configurations were not significantly aligned. Assessor-blocked models detected producer differentiation under both protocol-panel conditions. SCA showed stronger adjusted differentiation and greater sensitivity to the markedly defective coffee in each harvest; removing these samples substantially reduced SCA effect sizes, while CVA effects changed little. Among non-defective coffees, SCA scores were comparatively compact. CVA affective ratings spanned a wider range but showed greater within-sample variability and did not produce stronger score-based differentiation. CVA descriptive intensities, structured check-all-that-apply (CATA) descriptors and free notes provided complementary sensory information and revealed harvest-specific patterns not captured by final scores alone. Fisher-selected volatile features added an exploratory chemical dimension, but whole-configuration sensory-volatile alignment was low to moderate and nonsignificant. Overall, former SCA cupping yielded a more compact and defect-sensitive score representation, while CVA contributed a broader multidimensional sensory record. Because different assessor panels applied the two frameworks, the observed contrasts reflect both protocol and panel composition.

title: PdO-T nanozyme-based three-channel colorimetric sensor array coupled with machine learning for accurate differentiation and quantitative detection of aflatoxins in U.S. pecan.
abstract: Aflatoxins (AFs) represent a class of highly toxic food contaminants, yet existing detection approaches still suffer from several critical limitations. Herein, three PdO nanoenzymes (denoted as PdO-160, PdO-200, and PdO-240) were synthesized by regulating the hydrothermal temperature. All three nanozymes display robust and stable peroxidase-like activity via the generation of •OH and 1O₂. By exploiting the distinct inhibitory effects of AFB1, AFB2, AFG1, and AFG2 toward these nanoenzymes, a three-channel colorimetric sensor array was rationally constructed. Combined with a random forest (RF) model, the proposed array enables accurate discrimination of all four AFs independent of concentration. Further quantitative prediction was conducted using RF regression and artificial neural network (ANN) models, and the RF regression delivers optimal fitting performance with the maximum determination coefficient R2 up to 0.971 for the four target analytes. In real-sample analysis, the array obtains favorable classification performance for mixed aflatoxins, with an accuracy of 95.65% for concentration-independent identification, and all R2 values above 0.956 in quantitative analysis. The nanoenzymes also exhibit excellent batch-to-batch reproducibility and long-term storage stability. This study offers a promising colorimetric sensing strategy for the screening of aflatoxins in food matrices.

title: Multi-label classification model of the five tastes based on molecular structure and natural language processing techniques
A data-driven approach to evaluating the use of the periodisation of skill training framework for classifying training in a team-sport context.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the application of the PoST framework in a team sport context and compare two data-driven classification methods to objectively assess the skill training outcomes. Training drills were assessed for information complexity and game-representativeness using variables describing the training environment and athlete performance. Coach classifications of drills were analysed using repeated-measures MANOVAs, while k-means and Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) clustering objectively grouped drills based on information complexity, and compared with PoST stages. Coach classifications varied, with training intentions not always clearly distinguished, and similar game-representativeness observed across classifications, despite PoST emphasising this as a key differentiator. Both clustering methods identified three distinct training types, aligning with PoST's 'Complex Training', 'Team-based Training' and 'Performance Training' stages. However, the probabilistic overlap of the GMM better captured drills transitioning between stages. Neither method identified drills reflecting PoST's Coordination stage, suggesting misalignment between coach intent and the framework's definition. Coaches should consider both training complexity and representativeness to better align drills with game demands and desired outcomes. A modified framework designed for team-level skill development may support this, while objective classification methods may be used to enhance training design and evaluation.

title: Structures and therapeutic mechanisms in ZNF384-r B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
abstract: ZNF384 gene rearrangement (ZNF384-r) is one of the major genetic lesion in 4% B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) patients. However, the exact pathogenic mechanism leading to the leukemia outbreak remains elusive. Here, we determined the crystal structure of the ZNF384 zinc finger (ZF) domains 3-4 (2.0 Å). This helped to obtain the model ZNF384-DNA complex by AlphaFold 3, SAXS and X-ray crystallography. Site directed mutagenesis identified key residues Q68 in ZF3 and Q98 in ZF4 that were essential for transcriptional activity. Clinical characteristics of 10 new cases of ZNF384-r B-ALL were reported and integrated multi-omics profiling identified ID2 as a ZNF384-r-dependent target gene that was frequently associated with poor prognosis. Abnormal ID2 expression delineated a clinically adverse subgroup characterized by more severe differentiation arrest and immunosuppressive signature. Supportively, targeting ID2 in ZNF384-r cells induced mitochondrial apoptosis and effectively suppressed leukemia progression in patient derived xenograft (PDX) mice. Altogether, this study not only revealed the DNA engagement mechanism in oncogenic ZNF384-r fusion, but also highlighted ID2 as a promising therapeutic target in B-ALL.
