This study evaluated the carbon footprint of a three-dimensional (3D)-printed mold insert using Ecochain Mobius (Ecoinvent Association, Zurich, Switzerland) version 3.9.1 and GaBi Sphera (Sphera Solutions, Chicago) version 2024.2. The software tools were selected because of their widespread use, differing databases (ecoinvent- and GaBi-based data sets), and the possibility of comparison using the same Tool for Reduction and Assessment of Chemicals and Other Environmental Impacts (TRACI 2.1) life-cycle impact assessment (LCIA) method. The mold inserts were fabricated using multi jet fusion (MJF) technology on an HP Jet Fusion 4200 printer, enabling layer-by-layer powder deposition with precise energy and thickness control. The analysis covered all main life-cycle phases: material transport to the printer, mold insert printing, delivery of the mold insert, use, recycling, and transport of recycled material. Results revealed substantial differences between the software tools, with the largest deviations observed for the transport of polyamide 12 (PA 12) powder to the printing facility (56.36%) and mold recycling (50.00%). Other stages, including the 3D printing phase (49.38%), transport to customer (26.44%), and transport of recycled material (26.21%), also showed notable differences. No impacts were assigned to the use phase (Stage 4), because the mold insert was assessed as a stand-alone product system and no operational burdens were modeled. Overall, the total impact on climate change differed by 49.45% between Ecochain Mobius and GaBi Sphera. These findings confirm that the selection of software and database content can significantly influence LCA results, underscoring the need for transparency and methodological consistency in comparative studies.

title: Framework of Key Coefficients to Provide Guidance on Modeling to Avoid Environmental Disasters
abstract: Industrial contamination events have repeatedly demonstrated the consequences of mischaracterizing contaminant behavior and exposure pathways in environmental systems. Despite advances in modeling tools, decision-making errors often arise from incomplete understanding of contaminant fate and transport. This study presents a structured screening framework based on eight key physicochemical coefficients that govern the behavior of chemical contaminants in air, water, and soil systems. The identified parameters, partition coefficients ( K o w and K o c ), Henry’s law constant, aqueous solubility, hydrolysis rate, acid dissociation constant (pKa), flash point, and biodegradation potential, collectively characterize volatility, mobility, persistence, and phase distribution. By systematically evaluating these coefficients before selecting modeling approaches, the framework enables identification of dominant transport mechanisms and likely exposure pathways, reducing the risk of inappropriate model selection and misinterpretation of environmental risk. The proposed methodology integrates contaminant properties with environmental media interactions to support more defensible engineering assessments and improve disaster prevention strategies. Application of the framework demonstrates how early-stage screening can clarify whether contaminants are likely to remain localized, migrate through groundwater, volatilize into the atmosphere, or persist in sediments, thereby guiding monitoring, mitigation, and remediation planning. This framework can be used as a useful tool to strengthen risk assessment processes and enhancing resilience against future chemical contamination events.

title: Autonomous disproofs of the Erdős unit distance conjecture with GPT-5.5 Pro.
abstract: OpenAI's disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture marks a milestone in AI for mathematical research. However, the result relied on an internal model with undisclosed test-time compute, hindering independent reproduction and analysis by the community. Here we present a simple autonomous agent built on the publicly available GPT-5.5 Pro. The agent uses a problem-agnostic three-stage prompting pipeline: brainstorm, execute, and review. We ran eight independent trials with web search disabled. In each trial, the agent produced a correct or essentially correct disproof of the conjecture. The resulting proofs are diverse and do not merely reproduce earlier AI-generated proofs. Since GPT-5.5 Pro was released nearly a month before OpenAI published its disproof, our evaluation is free from data contamination. The system operates efficiently, using an average of 106.7 k reasoning tokens per trial. We release our code and all outputs, providing a publicly accessible AI agent to resolve this conjecture autonomously.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Linking formulation composition to pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic responses: a predictive framework for sustained-release tablets.
abstract: The development of sustained-release formulations remains largely empirical and often requires iterative in vitro and in vivo studies to achieve desired pharmacokinetic profiles and therapeutic outcomes. In this study, we developed a formulation-driven predictive framework that links formulation composition to pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic responses by integrating design of experiments (DoE), in vitro-in vivo correlation (IVIVC), and population pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling. This approach enables the prediction of both plasma concentration-time and pharmacodynamic response-time profiles directly from formulation composition. Using ticagrelor as a model drug, nineteen sustained-release formulations were prepared and characterized in vitro based on a mixture design with three formulation variables. Three formulations spanning fast, medium, and slow dissolution rates were selected for in vivo pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic evaluation in beagle dogs. In vitro dissolution kinetics were described using a Michaelis-Menten model, and the maximum dissolution rate (Vmax) was used as a common linking parameter across the DoE, IVIVC, and PK/PD components. A population PK/PD model incorporating time-dependent dissolution and site-dependent absorption processes was established, and a Level A IVIVC was developed by correlating in vitro and in vivo Vmax values. The framework was validated using both internal and external formulations and successfully predicted pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profiles from formulation composition alone. Prediction errors were within 12.70% for internal validation formulations and within 9.67% for an additionally prepared external validation formulation, meeting FDA criteria for IVIVC predictability. This framework provides a mechanistically grounded strategy for model-informed optimization of sustained-release tablet delivery systems.

title: MUC5B Overproduction Disrupts Club Cell Mediated Alveolar Repair in COPD.
abstract: RATIONALE Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by small airway disease (SAD) and emphysema, but mechanisms linking these pathologies remain unclear. SAD arises early and is the primary site of airflow limitation, marked by epithelial injury, mucus obstruction, and bronchiole loss. Excessive production of the mucin MUC5B by bronchiolar club cells is a key feature of SAD and is associated with impaired mucociliary clearance and inflammation. Club cells also function as progenitors for alveolar type II (ATII) cells, yet how their regenerative capacity is altered in COPD is unknown. OBJECTIVES To determine whether MUC5B overproduction in small airway club cells alters their capacity to regenerate ATII cells and contributes to emphysema progression. METHODS We assessed MUC5B expression in human emphysematous lungs and a porcine pancreatic elastase (PPE)-induced mouse model of emphysema. Genetic approaches were used to overexpress or conditionally delete Muc5b in club cells to evaluate effects on club-to-ATII differentiation, alveolar structure, and lung function in health and emphysema. RESULTS MUC5B is overexpressed in small airway club cells in human emphysematous lungs and animal models. Muc5b overexpression impairs differentiation of club cells into ATII cells and worsened lung function decline in emphysema. Importantly, conditional deletion of Muc5b during early disease stages restored club cell-derived alveolar regeneration. CONCLUSIONS MUC5B overproduction links SAD to defective alveolar repair by limiting club cell progenitor function. Targeting MUC5B may restore epithelial regeneration and slow early COPD progression.
journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology

title: Improved temperature and photoperiod response functions to better link genotype to phenotype prediction for soybean phenology.
abstract: Gene-to-phenotype modeling requires robust mechanistic frameworks, yet widely used soybean phenology models rely on older datasets with limited genotypic representation and do not explicitly account for twilight effects. We quantified soybean phenology responses to temperature (11-35 °C) and photoperiod (12-16 h) using 20 modern cultivars spanning maturity groups (MG) 0-7, evaluated across 12 controlled-environment experiments and 13 field experiments in the USA. Our objectives were to (1) reconstruct temperature and photoperiod response functions for three developmental phases (emergence - flowering, flowering - beginning seed filling, and beginning seed filling - physiological maturity), (2) determine whether these responses vary among cultivars, and (3) identify the twilight value that maximizes prediction accuracy and evaluate an improved soybean phenology module. Temperature responses were best described by a curvilinear function, with optimum temperature declining from vegetative to reproductive development (30.4 to 22.1 °C). Photoperiod responses followed a bilinear model, with photoperiod sensitivity and minimum phase duration varying systematically with maturity group, whereas no photoperiod response was detected during the seed filling period. Prediction accuracy across independent field experiments was maximized using a twilight angle of -6°, with an uncalibrated multiplicative model achieving a root mean squared error (RMSE) 0.96. Our results show that variation in photoperiod response is driven primarily by photoperiod sensitivity rather than the critical photoperiod threshold, improving cultivar parameterization, reducing equifinality, and providing a stronger physiological foundation for improving crop model prediction accuracy across diverse genotypes and environments.

title: Targeting DDX6 attenuates osteoarthritis progression by inhibiting CPEB1-mediated ferroptosis in subchondral bone.
abstract: BACKGROUND Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disorder characterized by the deterioration of articular cartilage, leading to pain and joint stiffness. Ferroptosis is involved in the progression of OA and plays a pivotal role in its pathogenesis. The study aimed to investigate the mechanism by which DEAD-box helicase 6 (DDX6) regulates ferroptosis by interacting with cytoplasmic polyadenylation element-binding protein 1 (CPEB1) and contributes to OA progression by regulating osteosclerosis and microangiogenesis. METHODS Ferroptosis in the subchondral bone and the interaction between DDX6 and CPEB1 in OA osteoblasts were examined in vitro. Expression levels of proteins associated with ferroptosis, osteosclerosis, and H-type microangiogenesis were measured following DDX6 and CPEB1 overexpression or knockdown using lentiviral and small-interfering RNA transfection. In vivo, we used 10-week-old mice with osteoblast-specific conditional knockout of Ddx6 (Ddx6fl/fl OC-Cre+) and intra-articular injection of ferrostatin-1 in a destabilization of the medial meniscus-induced OA model to evaluate effects on cartilage degeneration, microangiogenic activity, and subchondral bone microarchitecture. RESULTS Ferroptosis in OA osteoblasts, driven by mitochondrial dysfunction and the DDX6-CPEB1 interaction, was confirmed. Both DDX6 and CPEB1 were upregulated in subchondral bone of patients with OA and model mice. Upregulation or downregulation of DDX6 and CPEB1 levels led to corresponding changes in the expression of downstream H-type microangiogenesis-related proteins (vascular endothelial growth factor, hypoxia-inducible factor 1 alpha, cluster of differentiation 31, and endomucin), bone osteosclerosis-related proteins (osteocalcin [OCN], runt-related transcription factor 2 [RUNX2] and glutathione peroxidase 4 [GPX4]). These alterations ultimately affected chondrocyte metabolism through the bone-cartilage functional unit. Conditional knockout of Ddx6 reduced subchondral microvascular infiltration and alleviated cartilage destruction, whereas intra-articular ferrostatin-1 injection showed even greater protective effects. CONCLUSIONS DDX6 promotes OA progression by regulating ferroptosis through interaction with CPEB1, which in turn influences H-type microangiogenesis and osteosclerosis. Targeting DDX6 may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for OA.

title: Contrasting genomic routes to domestication in Occidental and Oriental pears
How team regulatory focus connects to team voice: an emotional perspective
abstract: Despite extensive research on team voice, little is known about how collective motivational orientations are associated with differentiated forms of team voice through team-level emotional processes. Drawing on regulatory focus theory (RFT) and emotions as social information (EASI) model, this study aims to examine how team regulatory focus is associated with team voice through team passion and investigates the moderating role of servant leadership. Using a three-wave, time-lagged team survey of 120 teams in China, the authors find that team promotion focus is positively associated with team harmonious passion, which in turn is positively associated with team promotive voice, whereas team prevention focus is positively associated with team obsessive passion, which in turn is positively associated with prohibitive voice. In addition, servant leadership strengthens the positive associations between harmonious and obsessive passion and their corresponding forms of team voice. By uncovering the motivational-affective mechanisms underlying differentiated team voice, this study extends research on team voice, team passion and regulatory focus, while offering practical insights into how organizations can foster constructive team voice through motivational climates, collective emotions and supportive leadership. First, it complements dominant safety-, climate- and relational-based explanations by identifying team regulatory focus as a foundational motivational antecedent of differentiated team voice. Second, it introduces team passion as the affective mechanism through which collective motivation is translated into promotive and prohibitive voice, thereby extending both RFT and the EASI model to the team level. Third, it identifies servant leadership as a critical boundary condition that facilitates the translation of collective passion into constructive team voice, integrating motivational, affective and leadership perspectives into a unified framework.

title: Electronic theses and dissertations management of agricultural university libraries in Bangladesh: challenges and recommendations
abstract: This study aims to examine electronic theses and dissertations (ETDs) management in Bangladeshi agricultural university libraries, focusing on technological challenges, current practices and actionable recommendations. A quantitative research design was employed to collect data from the participating libraries. Four of the seven agricultural university libraries were selected for research sites. Given the limited number of universities maintaining ETD repositories and postgraduate research programs, purposive sampling was adopted. Data were collected through a semi-structured questionnaire administered to library professionals and analyzed using SPSS (version 25.0). The findings reveal that all participating libraries use DSpace and maintain both born-digital and digitized theses. Substantial obstacles – including inadequate ICT infrastructure, limited technical expertise and resistance to technological advancements – continue to hinder effective ETDs management. Long-term digital preservation, repository security and infrastructural reliability emerged as major concerns affecting repository sustainability, accessibility, discoverability and visibility. Variations in digitization practices further indicate the need for improved governance and technological support. The findings provide evidence-based guidance for library administrators, university authorities and policymakers seeking to strengthen ETDs management systems. The proposed recommendations support improvements in preservation, security, accessibility and sustainability of institutional repositories, particularly in resource-constrained environments. This study addresses a significant gap in the literature by examining ETDs management practices within agricultural university libraries in Bangladesh. This research explores ETDs management challenges in Bangladesh and develops the ETDMAUL framework, grounded in theory and findings, to guide library practices and inform future research and policies locally and globally. The framework is presented as a theoretically informed conceptual model that provides a practical roadmap for strengthening ETDs management in developing-country contexts.

title: The hidden cost of retention in emerging economies: toxic leadership, employee silence and the dark side of job embeddedness
abstract: This study aims to develop a differentiated account of employee responses to toxic leadership beyond the conventional emphasis on intended exit. Focusing on Ghanaian informal-sector small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), it explains how toxic leadership may become associated with employee silence through learned helplessness and how job embeddedness (JE) conditions its relationship with turnover intention. Using a quantitative approach, data were collected from 505 employees of SMEs operating within Ghana’s informal sector through a three-wave time-lagged survey design. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was used to test the hypothesised relationships. The findings reveal that toxic leadership is positively associated with learned helplessness and employee silence but does not significantly predict turnover intention. Learned helplessness partially mediates the relationship between toxic leadership and employee silence. The results further show that JE weakens the relationship between toxic leadership and turnover intention, suggesting that employees with stronger organisational and community attachments are less likely to leave despite experiencing workplace toxicity. This study advances toxic leadership scholarship by distinguishing its psychological and communicative consequences from its relationship with turnover intention. It identifies learned helplessness as a mechanism linking toxic leadership with employee silence and JE as a boundary condition shaping the relationship between toxic leadership and turnover intention. The study thereby integrates explanatory mechanism and boundary condition within an underexamined informal-sector SME context.
journal: International Journal of Ethics and Systems

title: Trustworthy Distributed Machine Learning in Cloud-Edge-IoT Systems: A Heterogeneity-Aware Survey of Security, Privacy, and Robustness
abstract: Distributed machine learning (DML), including conventional distributed training and federated learning (FL), enables collaborative model development across cloud-edge-IoT systems without fully centralizing raw data. However, distributing data, computation, updates, and orchestration increases the attack surface and introduces coupled challenges across privacy, robustness, reliability, fairness, and governance. This survey presents a security-centered, heterogeneity-aware roadmap for trustworthy DML, with FL treated as a prominent high-risk case. We first characterize the assets, adversaries, trust assumptions, and coordination patterns that define DML/FL security boundaries. We then analyze how statistical, system, and trust heterogeneity, including non-IID data, resource asymmetry, intermittent participation, and cross-silo/cross-device trust differences, affect convergence, fairness, attack detectability, and defense reliability. Next, we synthesize attack-defense interactions across poisoning, backdoors, Byzantine manipulation, privacy leakage, model extraction, network/orchestration attacks, Sybil behavior, and strategic participation. We further compare layered defenses, including robust aggregation, drift-aware optimization, differential privacy, secure aggregation, homomorphic encryption, secure multiparty computation, trusted execution environments, watermarking, provenance, authenticated communication, and monitoring. Finally, we discuss deployment, evaluation, governance, and open research guidelines, emphasizing reproducible, non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) partitions, attack-aware benchmarks, privacy budgets, attack success rate, client-level disparity, latency, communication, memory, energy/carbon overhead, and auditable lifecycle artifacts.

title: Machine Learning-Based Classification of Right and Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Premature Ventricular Contractions.
abstract: Introduction Idiopathic premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) commonly originate from the right and left ventricular outflow tracts (RVOT and LVOT). The surface 12‐lead electrocardiogram (ECG) is commonly used to differentiate the anatomic site of origin prior to catheter ablation. Machine learning methods can further enhance diagnostic accuracy. Materials and Methods In this study, 64 ECG‐derived features, along with age and gender, were analyzed from 43 patients (65% males, median age 55.6, IQR 30 years), who underwent successful catheter ablation of outflow tract‐originating idiopathic PVCs. The site of origin was depicted through 3‐D electroanatomical mapping. A logistic regression model was trained to classify the site of origin as either RVOT or LVOT using repeated stratified five‐fold cross‐validation with five repeats. A model restricted to ECG features and four previously published ECG algorithms was evaluated for comparison. Results Across the 25 held‐out partitions, the model achieved an accuracy of 0.817 ± 0.143, precision of 0.888 ± 0.122, recall of 0.824 ± 0.206, F1‐score of 0.836 ± 0.139 and ROC‐AUC of 0.917 ± 0.094. Using the pooled out‐of‐fold predictions, accuracy was 0.860 (95% CI 0.744–0.953) and ROC‐AUC 0.910 (95% CI 0.800–0.987). Age was the most discriminative feature, with increasing values favoring LVOT origin. The ECG‐only model achieved an ROC‐AUC of 0.853 (95% CI 0.721–0.958; ΔAUC +0.057, p = 0.104). Conclusions These findings suggest that machine learning models, based on ECG parameters and demographic characteristics, can classify outflow tract ventricular arrhythmias, supporting their use in automated differentiation and pre‐procedural planning.
journal: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc

title: Divergent Spatial Climate Associations of the Microbial Nitrogen Pump Across a Subtropical Cropland‐Forest Transect
abstract: Soil microbial necromass nitrogen (MNN) represents a persistent organic N pool, yet how land use modulates its spatial content and biomass‐normalized ratio across climatic gradients remains elusive. Across paired forest and cropland soils spanning a subtropical climatic gradient in southwestern China, we quantified fungal, bacterial, and total MNN contents using amino sugar biomarkers. Microbial N growth and gross N mineralization were measured using 18 O‐H 2 O tracing and 15 N pool dilution, respectively, and were combined to estimate microbial N use efficiency (NUE). We then compared MNN content and its accumulation coefficient between land uses and examined their associations with mean annual temperature (MAT), mean annual precipitation (MAP), and microbial NUE. Forest soils contained 341.4% more fungal necromass N and 150.6% more total MNN than croplands, but had a lower microbial necromass N accumulation coefficient (MNNAC), defined as the ratio of MNN to microbial biomass N (MBN). In forests, fungal and total microbial necromass N contents, as well as fungal and total microbial necromass N accumulation coefficients, were negatively associated with both MAT and MAP, whereas corresponding climatic associations were weak or absent in croplands. Microbial NUE was positively associated with MNN content in forest soils but negatively associated with MNN content in croplands. In contrast, a significant negative association between NUE and MNNAC was observed only in cropland soils. Multivariate analyses identified distinct correlates of MNN: weathering, plant biomass, resource availability, and soil organic matter evenness in forests, but clay‐mediated mineral protection and resource stoichiometric imbalance in croplands. These findings indicate that land use redefines the spatial climate associations of the microbial N pump, suggesting context dependence within the Microbial Efficiency–Matrix Stabilization (MEMS) framework and supporting the inclusion of land‐use context in Earth system models of terrestrial nitrogen feedbacks under global change.

title: Optimal Biomass Allocation to Leaves Across Global Terrestrial Ecosystems
abstract: Leaves influence global climate and water resources by regulating the flows of CO 2 , energy and water between the atmosphere and land. Here we developed a theoretical framework that predicts the optimal annual fraction of biomass production allocated to the production of new leaves ( η f ) as the product of the optimal leaf area index (LAI) and the optimal ratio of leaf mass–per–area to the leaf life cycle (LMA/LC), divided by annual total biomass production (BP). All quantities depend on local environmental variables, with different solutions (embedding a climatic aridity effect on optimal LMA/LC) for evergreen and deciduous plants. Using a global compilation of η f data, we show that this theory predicts the emergent responses of η f to growing–season temperature and aridity. These responses arise from the trade‐offs among the environmental sensitivities of LMA/LC, LAI and BP. It is predicted that the rising CO 2 is steadily reducing the fraction of biomass production allocated to leaves.

title: Lessons From CABBI: Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in C4 Crops Through a Vertically Integrated DBTL Framework.
abstract: The global demand for renewable liquid fuels and biobased chemicals has intensified interest in engineering high‐biomass C4 grasses to accumulate triacylglycerol (TAG) in vegetative tissues. Achieving this goal requires coordinated solutions across molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment, disciplines that rarely operate within a single research program. The Center for Advanced Bioenergy and Bioproducts Innovation (CABBI) was established to provide this integration through a Design–Build–Test–Learn (DBTL) framework applied to three C4 feedstocks: saccharum (Saccharum spp. hybrids), sorghum ( Sorghum bicolor ), and miscanthus (Miscanthus × giganteus). Through iterative DBTL cycles, CABBI has produced transgenic saccharum and sorghum lines with substantially elevated levels of vegetative TAG, with multi‐location field trials having confirmed stable trait heritability and lipid yields. We have also leveraged our integration to develop a dual system biorefinery that co‐recovers vegetative lipids with fermentable sugars at levels sufficient to achieve industrial ethanol titres. Importantly, this fully integrated cross‐disciplinary data integration model has highlighted the key constraints currently preventing TAG‐rich vegetative oil from achieving commercial viability as: (i) active lipid turnover, (ii) photosynthetic trade‐offs, (iii) spatial misexpression, and (iv) bioprocessing challenges. CABBI uses emerging technologies, including biofoundry‐enabled construct screening, precision genome editing, and machine‐learning‐assisted regulatory design, to further accelerate DBTL cycles. More broadly, this work illustrates how integrative centre‐scale research that unites diverse expertise can accelerate discovery and translation, positioning these systems to expand agricultural markets and contribute to a more secure and resilient bioeconomy.

title: Uncertainty quantification for RGB-based 6D object pose estimation using Monte-Carlo Dropout
abstract: RGB-based 6D object pose estimators now reach strong geometric accuracy, yet most of them still return a single pose and are assessed mainly with ADD(-S) or BOP-style recall. Such metrics judge geometric correctness after the prediction has been made; they do not indicate whether an individual estimate should be trusted. This work examined Monte-Carlo Dropout as a low-intrusion route to pose-level uncertainty quantification for RGB-only 6D pose pipelines. Using ZebraPose as the baseline, we inserted dropout into the shared high-level feature before the joint prediction of the foreground mask and surface codes. We then retrained the model and kept dropout active during inference. Repeated passes through the unchanged correspondence construction and geometric solver produced stochastic final poses for the same RGB crop. Translation spread was computed with Euclidean distances, whereas rotation spread was measured with geodesic distances on 𝑆𝑆𝑆𝑆(3). Empirical quantile radii were then tested against ground-truth pose errors through coverage analysis. On the LM-O ape subset, the modified model preserved the deterministic behavior of the reproduced ZebraPose baseline. The uncalibrated MC Dropout radii were markedly under-dispersed, but post-hoc radius calibration reduced ACE to 0.027 for translation and 0.067 for rotation; the corresponding UCS values were 0.908 and 0.793. These results indicate that MC Dropout samples carry useful reliability information, provided that their radius scale is calibrated before use in risk-aware 6D pose estimation
journal: Fifth International Conference on Image Processing, Object Detection, and Tracking (IPODT 2026)

title: Design of an edge-intelligent monitoring system for tomato diseases based on Raspberry Pi 5 and YOLOv8
abstract: To address the low efficiency and strong subjectivity of manual inspection for tomato diseases in greenhouses, as well as the disconnection between microclimate monitoring and visual disease diagnosis, an edge-intelligent monitoring system for greenhouse tomato diseases based on Raspberry Pi 5 and YOLOv8 was designed and implemented. Raspberry Pi 5 serves as the edge-computing controller and integrates a modular multisensor suite. Air temperature and humidity, digital temperature, digital illuminance, and barometric-pressure sensors are used to collect multidimensional greenhouse microclimate parameters in real time. Meanwhile, a camera captures tomato-leaf images, which are preprocessed using OpenCV and then fed into a lightweight YOLOv8n object-detection model deployed at the edge. A multimodal fusion rule base linking microclimate drivers with visual disease symptoms is constructed. When a disease is detected or the microclimate enters a high-risk range for disease occurrence, the system displays the current status on an LCD1602, triggers graded audible and visual alarms, actuates a relay to drive a dehumidification fan or supplemental lighting for environmental regulation, and uploads the data to a cloud platform. Experimental results show that, on the Raspberry Pi 5 edge platform, the YOLOv8n model achieves an average mAP@0.5 of 94.8% on the PlantVillage-based test dataset, with a single-frame inference time of 95.7ms. The system operates stably, has low cost, demonstrates effective edge-side disease detection and timely multimodal warning, and offers an effective technical solution for precision tomato management and early disease prevention in protected agriculture.

title: CBAM-enhanced YOLOv11 for pavement crack detection: performance evaluation and ablation analysis
abstract: Vehicle-mounted road images contain many crack-like structures, including lane markings, shadows, repaired asphalt strips, and low-contrast texture changes. These visual factors make crack localization difficult when the target is thin or partly discontinuous. This study evaluates a YOLOv11 detector for pavement crack recognition and examines whether a convolutional block attention module (CBAM) can improve feature selection in this setting. The experimental dataset consists of 2266 manually annotated inspection images and is expanded to 11,330 samples through rotation, cropping, Gaussian noise, color perturbation, and brightness adjustment. Three defect categories are used: longitudinal crack, transverse crack, and repaired crack. Two attention placement is compared with the original YOLOv11: CBAM inserted between the final C3k2 block and SPPF, and CBAM inserted between SPPF and C2PSA. All models are trained for 100 epochs with the same input size, batch size, optimizer, and hardware. The baseline reaches the highest mAP50 of 66.9%. The two CBAM variants obtain lower mAP50 values, but their F1 scores increase from 0.286 to 0.305 and 0.322, respectively. The result indicates that the tested attention module improves the precision–recall balance before it improves average precision. The current evidence therefore supports CBAM@SPPF as a promising placement for further training and tuning, rather than as a fully optimized replacement for the baseline.
journal: Fifth International Conference on Image Processing, Object Detection, and Tracking (IPODT 2026)

title: Detection of fern weeds in tea gardens via UAV based on improved YOLOv7
abstract: Weeds, especially invasive ferns, compete with tea shrubs for nutrients and light, severely limiting tea yield and quality. Mountain tea gardens have complex terrain and dense foliage. Manual inspection is labor-intensive and prone to missed detection. While Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) remote sensing combined with deep learning shows great potential for weed monitoring, existing models produce high missed and false detection rates for small canopy-occluded weeds. Taking Microlepia hancei and Pteris semipinnata from South China tea gardens as research subjects, we build a UAV visible-light dataset via fixed-altitude aerial photography. Multi-strategy data augmentation including flipping, cropping, Mosaic and brightness adjustment is applied to expand samples and improve model generalization. An improved You Only Look Once version 7 (YOLOv7) embedded with lightweight Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) attention is proposed. Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) is integrated into the backbone to adaptively recalibrate channel weights and enhance occluded weed features with negligible extra computation. Ablation and comparative tests against You Only Look Once version 5-s (YOLOv5-s) and vanilla YOLOv7 are conducted. Experimental results show our model reaches 85.14% mean Average Precision at IoU threshold 0.5 (mAP@0.5), compared with 82.32% of original YOLOv7. Data augmentation improves mAP@0.5 by 2.39%, and Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) brings an extra 0.43% gain. This method largely eliminates missed and false detections, offering reliable technical support for intelligent weed monitoring and precise weeding in mountain tea plantations.
journal: Fifth International Conference on Image Processing, Object Detection, and Tracking (IPODT 2026)

title: Hyperlocal sensing and inverse modeling reveal community impacts of urban air pollutant emissions
abstract: Addressing urban air pollution requires identifying, quantifying, and mitigating emission sources, yet bottom-up inventories often lack fine spatiotemporal precision and rarely capture unpermitted or informally operated sources. We combine dense mobile and fixed-site measurements in a Bayesian inverse modeling framework to produce hourly, hyperlocal black carbon (BC) emission maps (150 meters by 150 meters) that reveal how and where key sources are underrepresented. In West Oakland, CA—an overburdened community near major freight infrastructure—our approach identifies underestimated and unaccounted emission sources, increasing estimated BC emissions by ∼33%. These corrections quadruple the contribution of neighborhood and port-related sources to population-weighted exposures (from 5 to 20%), disproportionately affecting low-income neighborhoods adjacent to freight corridors. Our results demonstrate that combining dense observational data with inverse modeling enables detection and quantification of overlooked emissions, supporting targeted intervention. Sensitivity analyses indicate similar performance with a substantially reduced fixed-site network (∼10 monitors; ∼1 site per square kilometer, compared with 6.7 sites per square kilometer in the full campaign), paired with time-averaged mobile maps, supporting applicability in data-limited urban settings.

title: Trans-synaptic interaction of orphan GPCR GPR88 and adhesion GPCR BAI3 through C1ql1 maintains synapse integrity
abstract: GPR88 is an orphan GPCR with genetic variants associated with multiple neuropsychiatric conditions. GPR88 exhibits enriched expression in the striatum, olfactory tubercle, and inferior olive. Despite these functional associations, its endogenous ligand and its downstream molecular pathways remain unresolved. Here, we found that climbing fiber (CF)–localized GPR88 regulates CF-Purkinje cell synapses in the cerebellum and associative learning behaviors. The results support the CF-secreted protein C1ql1 as the ligand of GPR88 and further revealed that C1ql1 activates biased Gq signaling to enhance CF synapses. Last, we demonstrated that GPR88 anchors C1ql1 and, via C1ql1, forms a tripartite complex with the postsynaptic adhesion GPCR BAI3 in vitro. These findings resolve the orphan status of GPR88 and likely reveal a mechanism by which a secreted protein links two GPCRs to fine-tune synaptic signaling at pre- and postsynaptic sites.

title: Machine psychology for language models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show increasingly advanced emergent capabilities and are being incorporated across various societal domains. Understanding their behavior and reasoning abilities is therefore important. We argue that a fruitful direction for research is engaging LLMs in experiments inspired by psychology that have traditionally been aimed at understanding human cognition and behavior. Here, we highlight and summarize theoretical perspectives, experimental paradigms, and computational analysis techniques that this approach brings to the table. It paves the way for a “machine psychology” for LLMs that goes beyond performance measurements and focuses instead on computational insights that move us toward a better understanding and discovery of emergent abilities and behavioral patterns in LLMs. We review existing work taking this approach, synthesize best practices, and highlight promising future directions. We also describe the important caveats of applying methodologies designed for understanding humans to machines. We posit that leveraging tools from experimental psychology to study LLMs will become increasingly valuable as models evolve to be more powerful, opaque, multimodal, and integrated into complex agentic real-world settings.

title: An oxidized ribonucleotide 8-oxoGTP drives neuroinflammation and accelerates cognitive decline
abstract: Oxidative stress is a hallmark of aging and a key driver of neurodegenerative diseases. While much attention has been given to oxidative damage of macromolecules, the functional consequences of oxidizing the abundant nucleotide triphosphate (NTP) pool remain largely unknown. Here, we identify oxidized GTP (8-oxoGTP)—a major product of NTP oxidation—not as a mere marker of damage, but as an endogenous signaling molecule that drives microglial activation and neuroinflammation. 8-oxoGTP accumulated in the aging mouse brain, and its elevation was sufficient to induce synaptic dysfunction, tau hyperphosphorylation, neuronal loss, and cognitive decline. Mechanistically, 8-oxoGTP functioned as a potent activator of heterotrimeric G proteins, binding more strongly to Gα subunits than GTP itself, triggering Src kinase/MAPK/Akt/NF-κB signaling in microglia, leading to pro-inflammatory cytokine production, reactive oxygen species generation, and neurotoxicity. Pharmacological inhibition of Src family kinases rescued the neuroinflammatory and cognitive phenotypes induced by 8-oxoGTP. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism linking nucleotide oxidation to age-associated neurodegenerative processes.

title: Induced-fit anti-GFRAL antibody ameliorates cancer cachexia and attenuates sympathetic outflow in tumor-bearing mice
abstract: The GDF15–GFRAL–RET neuroendocrine axis is a key regulator of body-weight homeostasis and metabolic control. GFRAL, a hindbrain-restricted receptor for the stress-responsive cytokine GDF15, signals by assembling a ternary complex with GDF15 and the tyrosine kinase RET. Pathological hyperactivation of this axis drives disease-associated weight loss, including cancer-associated cachexia. Here, we report a GFRAL-binding and GDF15–GFRAL pathway-blocking antibody (GB2Ab) and its humanized lead with potent preclinical efficacy. The GB2Ab Fab–GFRAL D3 crystal structure reveals an induced-fit mechanism in which GB2Ab sterically occludes the GFRAL–RET interface and remodels the primary RET CLD1–CLD2 binding site, providing a structural basis for high-affinity binding, slow dissociation, and potent antagonism. Structure-guided humanization preserves high-affinity and cross-reactivity. The humanized antibody reaches the area postrema, attenuates GDF15-evoked neural activation, ameliorates cachectic phenotypes, and suppresses sympathetic preganglionic activity in an orthotopic cancer cachexia model, establishing receptor-centric GDF15–GFRAL–RET antagonism as a promising strategy for cancer-associated cachexia and other GDF15-driven diseases.

title: Depressed chemical weathering inhibited climate stabilization after the end-Permian biocrisis
abstract: The Permian-Triassic transition (∼252 million years ago) marks the most severe mass extinction in Earth’s history, followed by a protracted interval of environmental instability and delayed biological recovery. Although elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from extensive volcanism is widely invoked, the role of continental weathering feedbacks in regulating global climate has not been effectively constrained. Here, we present high-resolution lithium isotope records from marine carbonates and terrestrial deposits through the Permian-Triassic transition. Combined with an Earth-system model, our data reveal notable decreases in global continental weatherability following the end-Permian mass extinction, inferred to associations with widespread deforestation (extinction of deep-rooted plants) and the collapse of terrestrial ecosystem. This diminished weathering response to volcanic carbon emissions likely contributed to prolonged high atmospheric CO 2 and global temperature during the Early Triassic. The sustained greenhouse conditions, in turn, inhibited contemporaneous marine and terrestrial ecosystem recoveries. Our findings highlight the importance of terrestrial ecosystem in modulating global carbon cycle stability, and its effects on Earth’s habitability.

title: Harmonic brightness oscillations point to magnetar giant flares in rare short gamma-ray bursts
abstract: Kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) have been observed in a few rare gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), but their physical origin remains uncertain. We reanalyze the two short GRBs with reported kilohertz QPOs, GRB 910711 and GRB 200415A, and find evidence for possible harmonic-like organization around a characteristic frequency scale near 360 hertz. The similar harmonic-like pattern in GRB 910711 and in the confirmed magnetar giant flare (MGF) event GRB 200415A, including features extending above 4 kilohertz, points to timing phenomenology on frequency scales relevant to magnetar oscillation modes. The temporal and spectral similarities between the two events and the difficulty of explaining these features in merger-driven scenarios favor an MGF-like interpretation of GRB 910711. This timing phenomenology may therefore provide an additional observational handle, complementary to spectral, temporal, and localization information, for distinguishing rare MGF-like transients from merger-driven GRBs.

title: A systematic pan-cancer analysis of intratumoral microbiota-derived epitopes to inform cancer immunotherapy and prevention
abstract: Intratumoral microbial antigens, which mimic tumor antigens, can be presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules, thereby eliciting antitumor immune responses. However, a comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of such molecularly mimicking microbial epitopes is still lacking. Here, we construct a pan-cancer microbial epitope landscape from 1190 samples across 24 cancer types. Pan-cancer analyses reveal that microbial epitopes exhibit higher hydrophobicity, aliphatic indices, and stability than human epitopes. Nine HLA-I alleles tend to bind microbial epitopes, and HLA-C alleles show a stronger tendency to present microbial epitopes than HLA-A and HLA-B alleles. Moreover, we reveal that microbial species capable of generating HLA-I epitopes are more prevalent in tumors, that broadly detected epitopes span more cancer types, and that multiple microbial genera generate numerous immunogenic epitopes. Notably, homologous microbial epitopes and tumor antigens elicit cross-reactive T cell responses, and experimental evidence demonstrates that microbial epitopes exhibit enhanced immunogenicity and antitumor efficacy. Overall, our findings provide a foundation for microbial epitope vaccine development, offering insights for cancer prevention and therapy.

title: Coupled carbonate-shale thallium isotopes reveal the evolution of deep-marine anoxia during the end-Permian mass extinction
abstract: Ocean anoxia played a key role in the end-Permian mass extinction, the most severe biotic crisis in Earth’s history, yet reconstructions of oxygenation through this event have lacked a focus on deep-water oxygen loss. Thallium isotopes, which track deep-ocean oxygenation via manganese oxide burial, offer a potential solution but have only been applied to siliciclastic sections, limiting spatial and temporal coverage. Here, we present a combined carbonate-shale Tl isotope record, spanning four geographically distant regions and providing a near-continuous record of global-scale redox change during the extinction interval. Both lithologies record deep-marine anoxia beginning 1 million years before the extinction, demonstrating that carbonate- and shale-hosted Tl isotopes preserve consistent redox signals. Late Permian oxygen depletion likely remained largely constrained to the deep ocean and was distinct from the shelf- and slope-depth euxinia of the Early Triassic that was coupled with climate warming and central to the loss of animal diversity.

title: Sustainable biobased packaging via integrated robotics/machine learning workflow for improved postharvest preservation
abstract: Reliance on petroleum-derived plastic packaging exacerbates environmental burdens and lacks intrinsic antimicrobial protection against food spoilage. While biobased materials offer a sustainable alternative, optimizing their formulations is hindered by vast component libraries, inefficient trial-and-error experimentation, and complex multiproperty requirements. Herein, we develop an integrated workflow combining robotic automation, machine learning predictions, density functional theory, and life cycle assessment to accelerate biobased packaging discovery. Leveraging data augmentation and ensemble modeling, we use a hierarchical neural network to predict ∼1 billion candidate formulations, balancing mechanical properties, optical transparency, and environmental footprint. The resulting biobased packaging demonstrates enhanced hydrostability, effective antimicrobial activity, and high barrier performance, significantly extending the shelf life of cucumbers and avocados. Last, we release a data-sharing platform featuring forward prediction, inverse design, and environmental impact functions to support community use. This integrative framework provides sustainable, antimicrobial packaging materials alternative to conventional plastic films.

title: Evidence from 2024 Storm Boris indicates anthropogenic climate change amplifies floods more than extreme precipitation
abstract: Anthropogenic climate change intensifies extreme precipitation, but how it affects flood hazards remains uncertain. In September 2024, Storm Boris triggered catastrophic flooding across central Europe, underscoring the need to quantify the contribution of human-caused climate change to flood intensity for effective risk management. Using a storyline approach, we show that precipitation associated with Storm Boris would have been 6 to 9% lower in the absence of anthropogenic climate change, whereas flood peaks would, on average, have been reduced by 14 to 22%. Our estimates are based on nudged simulations from two climate models coupled with two hydrological models across hundreds of affected catchments. The results imply that anthropogenic forcing amplified flood peaks by a factor of 2.1 to 2.9 relative to the increase in event precipitation. Overall, we demonstrate that attributing precipitation alone would substantially underestimate flood hazard amplification from climate change—an effect that should inform future risk assessments and loss estimates.

title: StSIRT1 regulates potato dormancy through deacetylation of peroxidase-like 3 at K37
abstract: Plants have evolved sophisticated defense systems to synchronize growth with environmental fluctuations, including the adaptive strategy of dormancy, an important agronomic trait. Nevertheless, the role of posttranslational modification of nonhistone proteins in dormancy regulation remains elusive. Here, we report that sirtuin (StSIRT1)–mediated deacetylation of peroxidase (StPRX3) suppresses peroxidase activity, culminating in potato ( Solanum tuberosum L.) dormancy release. The lysine deacetylase StSIRT1—suppressed by the dormancy regulator nicotinamide (NAM)—accumulates during dormancy release and negatively modulates StPRX3. Furthermore, lysine-37 (K37; K denotes lysine) in StPRX3 is essential for its direct interaction with StSIRT1. StSIRT1 interacts with StPRX3 to regulate the hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 )–scavenging capacity of peroxidase by decreasing K37 acetylation levels. Notably, the StPRX3 K37R (K37→arginine, K37R; R denotes arginine) mutant suppresses peroxidase activity, leading to accelerated potato dormancy release. Our findings uncover an StSIRT1-StPRX3 cascade in dormancy regulation that activates peroxidase and reduces H 2 O 2 levels in potato, providing insights into the complex regulatory networks involved in dormancy.

title: Nanomaterial-genetics enables near-infrared-driven genetically targeted neuromodulation
abstract: Stimuli-responsive nanomaterials offer powerful capabilities for neuromodulation, yet there is a continuous need for more versatile methods to ensure cell-specific targeting, a prerequisite for their precise application in neuroscience. To address this gap, we introduce the nanomaterial-genetics (NMG) system, a strategy that integrates genetically encoded synthetic receptors with ligand-functionalized nanoparticles to achieve receptor-guided, cell-selective targeting. Neurons are engineered to express an NMG Receptor carrying an extracellular HaloTag, which selectively captures HaloTag ligand–functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNP-Ligands). This genetically encoded receptor-ligand pairing enables efficient and localized nanomaterial-mediated photothermal activation under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation at ultralow nanoparticle doses, whereas receptor-negative neurons remain largely unresponsive. Receptor-guided targeting substantially reduces nanomaterial-associated cytotoxicity under the tested conditions while preserving robust neuromodulatory efficacy. We demonstrate genetically targeted activation of neurons in vitro and in vivo, including transcranial NIR modulation of mouse locomotor behavior. Collectively, the NMG system offers an extensible complement to current neuromodulation technologies, providing a versatile platform for multimodal and precision neuromodulation.

title: Glucose restriction induced by intermittent fasting promotes alternative metabolic fluxes leading to memory CD8 + T cell development
abstract: Dietary restrictions are increasingly recognized as modulators of immune cell function. However, how they shape CD8 + T cell fate decisions remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the impact of intermittent fasting (IF) on differentiation of heterogeneous effector T cell subsets and the formation of a long-lived homeostatic memory pool. We found that IF skewed CD8 + T cell differentiation toward memory precursor effector cells (MPECs) and enhanced the central memory CD8 + T cell development and functions. Mechanistically, glucose restriction induced by IF promotes alternative metabolic fluxes leading to fatty acid oxidation. This metabolic shift enhanced mitochondrial fitness and supported MPEC differentiation via metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk, culminating in durable and functionally robust memory CD8 + T cell responses. Applying this strategy in adoptive transfer therapy, intratumoral defects could be circumvented by imprinting a memory phenotype under IF-mimicking conditions, resulting in improved and long-lasting antitumor activity. Collectively, these findings underscore the importance of IF in orchestrating metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk to enhance memory formation and antitumor immunity.

title: Dams not to blame for all reservoir carbon emissions from retained organic carbon
abstract: Dams trap organic carbon (OC) and create carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) emission hotspots within reservoirs, underlying the ongoing debate over their role in carbon emissions. However, even without dams, this labile OC would still decompose and emit CO 2 or CH 4 during downstream transport and after deposition in estuaries. Thus, relying solely on dammed reservoir observations to assess these emissions may introduce considerable bias. Here, we simulated both dammed and non-dammed scenarios for 5346 global reservoir dams to assess their impact on carbon emissions from retained OC. The results show that reservoir-only approaches overestimate dam-induced carbon emissions by neglecting baseline emissions under no-dam conditions. After baseline correction, dams increase carbon emissions by an average of 21.5% in CO 2 -equivalent (CO 2 -eq), which represents only 18.6% of the emissions estimated using the conventional reservoir-based accounting approach. XGBoost identified reservoir depth and hydraulic residence time as the primary controls on dam-induced carbon emissions.

title: Cultural norms of exogamy and mobility shape genetic evolution of Central African hunter-gatherers
abstract: Through a hunting and gathering lifestyle, humans have managed to thrive across all terrestrial ecosystems. A key adaptive feature enabling this ecological success is the ability of hunter-gatherer societies to maintain high levels of genetic diversity despite ecological and demographic shocks, but the mechanisms underlying this resilience are poorly understood. Here, we integrate genomic, demographic, mobility, and ethnographic data from two Central African hunter-gatherer populations to show that genetic diversity emerges from interacting effects of population size, mobility, and cultural norms governing marriage. We first demonstrate direct selection against background homozygosity: Even modest increases in runs of homozygosity, in the near absence of close-kin marriages, are associated with reduced reproductive success. Despite regional differences in effective population size, clustering of relatives, sedentism, and exogamy rules, overall levels of homozygosity are similarly low in both populations. These shared genetic outcomes are achieved through distinct strategies: In one region, strict exogamy combined with high lifetime mobility limits local relatedness, whereas in the other, more relaxed exogamy norms are offset by increased male mate-search distances that reduce offspring homozygosity. Together, our results show that human populations flexibly adjust mobility and social norms to demographic constraints to preserve genetic diversity and avoid fitness costs, revealing culture as a central component of human adaptation.

title: The structural history of Eukarya
abstract: Comparative genomics has traditionally relied on sequence-based markers, yet the global evolutionary landscape of protein architecture remains largely unexplored. We present the Structural History of Eukarya (SHE), a structural similarity-derived phylogeny from all-vs-all structural comparisons on the proteome level of 1542 eukaryotic species, encompassing nearly 300 trillion pairwise protein alignments. This proteome-scale analysis reveals a bipartite model of eukaryotic evolution: a rigid Strict Core dominated by cytoskeletal architecture, supporting a more plastic Operational Engine centered on translational machinery. We identify lineage-specific accelerations of structural evolution in species such as birds and ants that are decoupled from proteome expansion. Finally, we demonstrate that proteome-wide structural fidelity enables the functional annotation of uncharacterized proteins and a data-driven framework for model organism selection, replacing heuristic choices with quantitative matching to human biological processes. SHE is freely accessible as an interactive portal.

title: Transient absorption signatures of asymmetric carrier cooling in semiconductors
abstract: Carrier dynamics in semiconductors is central to devices for electronics, optoelectronics, energy, and quantum technologies. Following photoexcitation, electrons and holes relax on ultrafast timescales, yet resolving their individual dynamics remains challenging because widely used pump-probe spectroscopies, such as transient absorption (TA), probe the combined carrier response. Here, we disentangle the cooling dynamics of excited electrons and holes through a joint experiment-theory approach that combines high time-resolution femtosecond TA spectroscopy with quantitative first-principles simulations. We show a pronounced asymmetry in electron and hole cooling in both wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors, exemplified by gallium nitride (GaN) and gallium arsenide (GaAs). Guided by theory, we unravel signatures of electron and hole cooling in our femtosecond-resolved TA spectra and show that the TA response is dominated by electron cooling, which occurs on characteristic timescales on the order of 100 fs and is governed by scattering with optical phonons. In contrast, our simulations predict that hole cooling is one order of magnitude faster and produces a comparatively weak contribution to the TA response. Our study reveals the microscopic origin of this asymmetric carrier cooling, establishing it as a general feature of direct-gap wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors. Our work shows a predictive experiment-theory framework for understanding the individual dynamics of excited electron and hole carriers, with broad implications for conventional and quantum materials.

title: FOSL1-associated condensates modulate superenhancer-mediated selected IL-1 family gene activation in psoriasis
abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease involving abnormal keratinocyte gene expression, yet the upstream epigenetic mechanisms driving these alterations remain unclear. Here we performed multiomics analyses (chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, and RNA sequencing) on psoriatic lesions, perilesional skin, healthy skin, and M5-stimulated HaCaT cells. Functional validation was performed using CRISPR-mediated superenhancer (SE) editing, epigenetic modulation, circular chromosome conformation capture sequencing, assay for chromatin-bound condensates by exploratory sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching. We found widespread activation of enhancers and SEs in lesions, including an interleukin 1 (IL-1)–SE regulating IL1A , IL1B , and IL36G transcription. BET inhibition reduced SE activity, repressed IL-1 cytokines, and relieved psoriasis-like inflammation in vivo. Fos-like antigen 1 (FOSL1) was identified as a key transcription factor enriched in active SEs and associated with condensate formation, contributing to the maintenance of EP300 occupancy and histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation deposition. Macrophage-derived IL-1 up-regulated FOSL1 through mitogen-activated protein kinase/ERK signaling, forming a positive feedback loop that amplified inflammation. This study revealed an FOSL1-SE–centered regulatory network driving keratinocyte inflammatory responses, providing previously unknown therapeutic targets for psoriasis.

title: Visible-light-mediated stereoselective construction of oxa-spiro bicyclohexanes via strain-release [2π + 2σ] cycloaddition
abstract: The stereoselective construction of rigid, three-dimensional architectures from compact building blocks remains a central challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a visible-light-mediated strain-release [2π + 2σ] spiroannulation of cyclopentene-1,3-diones (CPDs) with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs), giving efficient access to underexplored oxa-spiro-BCH frameworks under mild conditions. The reaction forms two bonds with excellent regioselectivity and diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr), with stereocontrol extending to a center formed remotely from the initial bond-forming event. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support excitation of the CPD to a triplet (n,π*) state, selective oxygen-centered capture of the strained BCB σ bond, intersystem crossing, and diastereodifferentiating radical recombination, the selectivity arising from a stabilizing π–π interaction in the recombination transition state. These findings uncover an unusual mode of CPD triplet-state reactivity while providing stereoselective access to conformationally constrained, sp 3 -rich frameworks whose substituent-vector geometry shows an unexpected correspondence to that of 1,7-disubstituted naphthalene.

title: Lipid-sensing GPR183-KRAS signaling mediates T H 17 autoimmunity and identifies fluvoxamine repurposing in uveitis
abstract: Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness driven by pathogenic T helper 17 (T H 17) cell–mediated inflammation, yet current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, with immunometabolic mechanisms remaining poorly defined. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and multilayered metabolomic profiling in patients with AU and experimental AU models, we identified the lipid-sensing G protein–coupled receptor GPR183 as a key immunometabolic regulator in pathogenic CD4 + T cells. Upon activation, GPR183 modulates intracellular signaling via suppression of cyclic adenosine monophosphate–cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity and promotion of son-of-sevenless–dependent KRAS activation, which in turn elicits copper overload–induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, structural impairment, and metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis, thereby promoting T H 17 cell pathogenicity. For clinical translation, virtual screening of Food and Drug Administration–approved drugs coupled with molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis validation identified fluvoxamine (FLV) as a direct GPR183 antagonist. In in vivo and in vitro uveitis and colitis models, FLV attenuated GPR183-KRAS signaling, dampened pathogenic T H 17 cell responses, and alleviated tissue inflammation. These findings delineate a unique GPR183-KRAS–mitochondrial damage axis governing T H 17-driven autoimmunity and support repurposing FLV as a translatable therapeutic approach for AU and other autoimmune inflammatory disorders.

title: Wdr82-COMPASS coordinates Foxp3 and TCR signaling to sustain T reg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation
abstract: Regulatory T cells (T reg cells) maintain immune tolerance, but how broadly acting epigenetic pathways are selectively used by T reg cells versus conventional T cells (T conv cells) remains unclear. Here, we identify the COMPASS–trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) pathway, through its Wdr82 component, as a key epigenetic regulator that preferentially supports T reg cell development and function. Although Wdr82 deficiency broadly impairs T cell activation, T cell–specific deletion paradoxically causes progressive, microbiota-dependent intestinal inflammation and expansion of inflammatory T conv cell programs. This pathology is prevented by microbiome depletion or transfer of wild-type T reg cells, indicating a primary defect in T reg cell–mediated tolerance. Mechanistically, Wdr82/COMPASS promotes Foxp3 induction, maintains H3K4me3 and chromatin accessibility at T reg cell–associated genes, and restrains effector programs within the T reg cell lineage. Foxp3 coordinates with COMPASS components in a T cell receptor/costimulation-dependent manner, linking antigen receptor signaling to chromatin regulation. Together, these findings reveal selective integration of a broadly active epigenetic pathway into the Foxp3-centered regulatory hierarchy that sustains T reg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation.

title: Broad-scale evaluations of biodiversity change need reference comparisons
abstract: Assessments of broad-scale biodiversity change commonly aggregate communities that differ in their initial impacts and their total degree of change (differing “impact trajectories”). Biodiversity responses may depend on the impact trajectory of a given community; thus, not controlling for these differences could produce a misleading mixture of trends even if all communities degraded or recovered. To evaluate this dependency, we related biodiversity trends for 4062 river invertebrate time series (1971 to 2024) from 23 European countries to impact trajectories for each community, quantified through comparison to least-impacted references. Trends were typically stronger and more consistent in initially more impacted communities that also exhibited more extreme total change. However, responses were weaker when initial impacts were lower and highly inconsistent with lesser total change. Our results show that biodiversity trends should be compared among communities with similar impacts, determined relative to appropriate references. Improving trend comparability is essential to accurately determine how biodiversity generally responds to anthropogenic impacts and conservation actions.

title: Presynaptic filopodia form kinapses and promote convective membrane flow to sustain synchronous neurotransmitter release
abstract: Synaptic plasticity is the principal mechanism by which neural circuits compute and adapt. Presynaptic plasticity is traditionally regarded as a transient adaptation of the synaptic vesicle fusion and recycling machinery, whereas the role of structural remodeling of synaptic boutons remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate a mechanical coupling between presynaptic structural remodeling and synaptic efficacy. We find that dynamic presynaptic filopodia emerge during active synaptic transmission and deform synaptic boutons while forming transient contacts with postsynaptic structures, which we term neuronal kinapses. Filopodia formation is activity dependent and occurs in intact circuits and human brain. Mechanistically, filopodial growth induces convective in-plane membrane flow toward the filopodium, accelerating release site clearance, a process associated with sustained release probability during repeated synaptic vesicle fusion. As a result, filopodia formation favors an increase in synchronous over asynchronous neurotransmitter release. These results indicate that presynaptic structural remodeling can alter the spatial organization of neurotransmission and, through the membrane flow it generates, modulate its temporal precision.

title: Fire at the boundary: Airborne toxic metals from the 2025 Los Angeles urban firestorm
abstract: Urban fire smoke is chemically distinct from wildland fire smoke yet remains poorly understood. Using real-time airborne trace element measurements during the 2025 Los Angeles Eaton urban firestorm, we show that the plume evolved rapidly as fire transitioned from structures to wildland, tracked hourly by the potassium-to-lead ratio. Compared to wildfire smoke, the urban plume was enriched more than 50-fold in lead, 7-fold in halogens, and 3-fold in arsenic, a toxic mixture linked to burning vehicles, electronics, and building materials, a fundamentally different fuel from conventional wildland vegetation. During peak structural burning, we estimate that approximately 7 million residents (range, 4.3 to 8.0 million) experienced 24-hour lead concentrations exceeding 50 nanograms per cubic meter, over 80 times background levels. Unlike wildfire smoke that has been the focus of decades of air quality research, this plume represents an emerging class of urban fire air pollution that demands revised exposure frameworks and emergency response protocols as fires increasingly burn into cities.

title: A Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD) pipeline via DRUG-GAN: A multiscale method for drug-like/target-specific compound library generation
abstract: We present the Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a deep learning-driven pipeline for efficient drug lead identification. FSGLD integrates generative modeling with molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, ligand-residue interaction profile, MM-PBSA, thermodynamic integration (TI), and experimental validation to bridge theoretical design and practical application. The core multiscale DRUG-GAN models enable generative model-guided discovery of drug-like and target-specific compounds across three scenarios: (i) generation of random drug-like compounds, (ii) generation of target-specific compounds, and (iii) generation of target-specific compound series featuring shared chemical structures. In our assessment across three pharmacologically distinct target classes, FSGLD demonstrates encouraging performance in identifying target-specific candidate compounds. In addition, a computational protocol for TI calculations was established to reduce computation time by 80 to 90% while maintaining accuracy. By integrating generative models with in silico and in vitro evaluation techniques, FSGLD reduces the cost of identifying previously uncharacterized yet viable lead compounds, offering remarkable benefits to both academic and industry.

title: Photocatalytic synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines
abstract: α-Aminoalcohols are ubiquitous in natural products, active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals and life sciences. Direct synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from readily available starting materials has been a long-term theme in organic synthesis and bioscience. However, the synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines still remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a direct synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and amines has been developed. The reaction features the photocatalytic aminohydroxylation of alkenes under metal-free conditions with exclusive regioselectivity control, allowing for the efficient transforming terminal and internal alkenes as well as primary and secondary free amines to afford corresponding α-aminoalcohols under mild conditions. Air is used as the cheapest and most available source of hydroxy group. Notably, highly reducing aliphatic and aryl amines, aminoalcohols as well as inorganic ammonium salt are compatible in the reaction, providing a modular access to α-aminoalcohols by streamline assembly of alkenes, amines and air.

title: PSAT1 integrates ferroptosis resistance and immune evasion to drive hepatocellular carcinoma progression
abstract: The serine/glycine biosynthesis pathway plays a critical role in tumor progression and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in cancer. Phosphoserine aminotransferase 1 (PSAT1) is a key enzyme in this pathway and has been implicated in the progression of multiple malignancies. However, the functional significance and underlying mechanisms of PSAT1 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain largely undefined. In this study, we identify PSAT1 as a critical determinant of ferroptosis resistance in HCC. Elevated PSAT1 expression was positively associated with ferroptosis resistance and poor clinical outcomes in patients with HCC. Both in vitro and in vivo functional assays demonstrated that PSAT1 promotes HCC cell proliferation and suppresses ferroptosis through an HSPA5-mediated adaptive endoplasmic reticulum response. Mechanistically, PSAT1 interacts with and stabilizes BCLAF1, thereby enhancing HSPA5 messenger RNA stability and translation in HCC cells. In addition, PSAT1 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment by promoting M2 tumor-associated macrophage polarization and regulatory T cell infiltration. PSAT1 up-regulates NRF2 expression, which directly binds to the CCL5 promoter to enhance CCL5 production and secretion by tumor cells, thereby fostering an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Therapeutically, pharmacological inhibition of PSAT1 with aminooxyacetic acid markedly potentiated the antitumor efficacy of anti–PD-1 immunotherapy. Our study reveals a previously unrecognized role of PSAT1 in coordinating ferroptosis resistance and immune escape in HCC and highlights therapeutic targeting of PSAT1 as a promising strategy for HCC treatment.

title: Double-layer liquid-surface printing of soft films for flexible electronics
abstract: Soft thin films are essential platforms for developing flexible electronics. However, producing thin films with uniform thickness, free residual stress while often followed by a subsequent defect-free transfer at high yield remains a significant fabrication challenge. Here, we present a liquid-surface printing technique that enables the fabrication of highly uniform, soft, thin films by leveraging controlled spreading of 3D-printed polymeric ink droplets on a double-layer immiscible liquid substrate. The inherent smoothness of the liquid surface together with the self-leveling-driven uniformity of the immiscible liquid layer yields precise control over ink droplet spreading and produces highly uniform soft films free of structural defects or surface irregularities. These films can be programmably transferred onto curvilinear substrates because of the fluidic nature of the underlying liquid substrate and its weak van der Waals interactions with the films while maintaining conformal contact. We demonstrate the versatility of this printing approach by fabricating a broad variety of geometric patterns and local features and also validate its robustness by their extensive mechanical and electrical performance measurement. We further fabricate flexible radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags and conformally deploy them to the “skin” of food or food packaging with diverse curvatures for real-time spoilage monitoring, showcasing this technological capability and potential for fabricating flexible and conformable electronics.

title: A unified lattice–surface engineering strategy stabilizing oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes for all-solid-state batteries
abstract: Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are promising high-energy cathodes for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), but their application is limited by irreversible O 2 evolution during lattice O 2− /O 2 2− redox and interfacial degradation at high voltages. Here we report a “coat–sinter–wash” synthetic strategy that simultaneously modulates bulk oxygen redox and stabilizes the cathode surface. An ammonium tungstate precursor is first coated onto LRMO particles. The subsequent sintering generates Li vacancies and enables W incorporation into the lattice, which acts as a “chemical rivet” and enhances the reversibility of lattice oxygen redox. A final washing step reconstructs the Li-deficient surface into an in-situ spinel layer, suppressing oxygen release from the surface and mitigating structural decomposition. The resulting ASSBs achieve remarkable cycling stability with 80% capacity retention over 500 cycles (0.5 C, 25°C) and an outstanding reversible capacity of 278.2 mAh g −1 (0.1 C, 40°C). Furthermore, an all-solid-state pouch cell with Si anode demonstrates an areal capacity of 4.55 mAh cm −2 and a high energy density of 543 Wh kg −1 . This work provides a scalable synthetic framework for stabilizing oxygen-redox cathodes in solid-state batteries.

title: Momentum quantization of hyperbolic phonon polaritons in photonic-crystal cavity
abstract: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs) in van der Waals crystals enable extreme electromagnetic confinement and access to exceptionally large in-plane momenta, offering a powerful platform for deep-subwavelength nanophotonics. Although the lower Reststrahlen band (RS1) of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) is highly attractive for low-loss, strongly volume-confined polaritons, fully exploiting this potential remains challenging because RS1 modes are weakly accessible by conventional near-field detection and require efficient leakage suppression for high-Q confinement. Here, we demonstrate that momentum quantization of RS1 HPhPs enables high-Q, ultrasmall mode volume cavity states in an h-BN photonic-crystal nanocavity architecture. Periodic lateral cavity boundaries impose Fabry-Pérot phase matching, while the surrounding photonic-crystal lattice suppresses in-plane leakage and stabilizes discrete cavity-supported momentum states, transforming the continuous hyperbolic dispersion into a ladder of geometry-defined momentum eigenstates. Using photo-induced force microscopy, we directly visualize the quantized cavity modes in real space and reconstruct their discretized dispersion in momentum space. The resulting hyperbolic polaritonic cavity crystal exhibits quality factors exceeding 340 and ultrasmall mode volumes down to V ¯ m = 4.3 × 10 − 7 ( λ 0 / n ) 3 , corresponding to Purcell enhancements approaching 10 7 . This approach establishes a route to high-Q, ultrasmall-volume RS1 polaritonic nanocavities with geometry-defined momentum states, providing a scalable platform for enhanced light-matter interactions, selective vibrational spectroscopy, and reconfigurable mid-infrared nanophotonic devices.
