title: Small-statured tomato plants for automating greenhouse production: opportunities, constraints, and research priorities
abstract: Systems based on small-statured plants could contribute to the future of automated tomato production, but require an integrated approach of cultivation, crop management, plant physiology, breeding, robotics, and modelling. Greenhouse tomatoes are typically grown according to a high-wire system, where plant stems reach 10 m or more in length during one cycle of production. This system has served the industry for about 50 years, and allows for near-continuous year-round production, high yield, and good fruit quality. However, it is labor intensive, requiring manual fruit harvest, pruning of side shoots and leaves, as well as training the stem around the support string. The viability of high-wire cultivation is now challenged by high labor costs and shortage of workers. In this perspective paper, we propose two alternative tomato production systems: dwarf tomato and limited-truss tomato (LTT). They both produce small-statured tomato plants with short cultivation cycles, which may improve compatibility with automated production. We evaluate and compare the two production systems based on yield, light use efficiency, fruit quality, and labor requirement. Future directions for both research and industry for innovative tomato production are presented as well.

title: Integrating a soil temperature module into AquaCrop improves simulation of crop growth and yield under straw mulching
abstract: Straw mulching is a core practice in conservation agriculture, improving the soil hydrothermal environment, enhancing water-use efficiency, and increasing crop yield, and is widely regarded as an environmentally friendly and sustainable mulching technique. However, most existing crop models simplify or neglect mulch-induced regulation of soil temperature and water processes, thereby limiting their capacity for system-level assessment of crop growth and water dynamics under mulched conditions. This study aims to enhance the adaptability of AquaCrop to mulched environments and to evaluate the interactive effects of straw mulching on soil water–heat processes and crop growth. Based on the AquaCrop framework, a soil temperature submodule (ST) incorporating key surface-cover environmental factors was developed to extend the model’s capability to simulate soil temperature dynamics. Early-season crop development was driven by cumulative thermal time in the topsoil rather than air-temperature growing degree days, yielding a coupled model, AquaCrop–ST. A maize conservation-agriculture field experiment was conducted in Northeast China using locally prevalent mulching practices, with four treatments: straw crushing mulch, straw strip mulch, whole-straw mulch, and a no-mulch control. The coupled model was evaluated against observations. Straw mulching significantly moderated topsoil temperature dynamics, lowering soil temperature by 1.77–4.46 °C during warm periods and reducing early-season thermal accumulation by 10–24%. The improved model reproduced topsoil temperature dynamics under mulching well, with R 2 values of 0.92–0.95, RMSE values of 0.93–1.06 °C, and NSE values of 0.88–0.94, and also captured the seasonal patterns of deeper soil temperature. Compared with the original model, canopy development simulations were substantially improved, with RMSE decreasing from 33.49–33.73% to 3.13–8.13%. The improved model also successfully captured mulch-induced phenological delay and improved the simulation of soil water dynamics and evapotranspiration.

title: A real-time deep learning method for detection and localization of non-emerged cabbage seedlings
abstract: Real-time detection and localization of non-emerged seedlings play a pivotal role in effective vegetable crop management. Traditionally, checking the non-emergence of crop seedlings relies on labor-intensive and time-consuming manual inspections. To address this issue, this paper introduces a precise, rapid, and real-time method for detecting and locating non-emerged seedlings using an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). The proposed Enhanced YOLOv8n detector improves upon the base model through a more efficient backbone and a bidirectional feature-fusion neck, achieving a mAP50–95 of 81.4%, an 8% improvement over the base model, while preserving real-time inference capability. Furthermore, integrating the Enhanced YOLOv8n, the YOLO tracking algorithm, and image processing algorithms enabled the development of a robust real-time detection and localization method for non-emerged seedlings. The recognition accuracy for non-emerged cabbage seedlings reached 96.9%. Notably, this method can distinguish the quantity of consecutive non-emerged seedlings, demanding only one-fifth of the manual effort, demonstrating substantial potential for practical applications. In summary, the UAV-deployed real-time detection and localization method exhibits excellent capability in detecting and locating non-emerged cabbage seedlings, thus significantly reducing the manpower needed for crop management.

title: ACCM-Net: an adaptive CLAHE-CBAM-MobileNet architecture for wheat leaf disease classification
abstract: Wheat disease classification is critical for early detection and crop management, but manual identification is challenging due to visually similar symptoms in early infection stages. Existing deep learning approaches are not adept at addressing class imbalance, complex lesion patterns, and non-uniform field conditions, and thus, practical use is obstructed. To address this, this paper presents ACCM-Net, a fusion architecture founded on a frozen MobileNetV2 backbone and Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) for enhanced feature refinement, combined with adaptive CLAHE and Sobel-based preprocessing to emphasize disease-discriminative regions. The model incorporates dynamic learning rate scheduling for stable training and enhanced generalization. Evaluated on a Kaggle-sourced dataset of 407 wheat leaf images, ACCM-Net attained an overall accuracy of 97.56%, F1-score of 97.60%, sensitivity of 98.41%, and specificity of 98.92%, beating baseline CNN and five other pre-trained models. The results show that ACCM-Net's combination of contrast enhancement, attention mechanisms, and adaptive learning techniques significantly enhances classification accuracy and interpretability and, thus, is a promising practical tool for agricultural diagnostics. Future work will extend the model to other disease classes and explore transformer-based enhancements to further contextual understanding.

title: DMSP special sensor H (SSH) data rescue and assimilation in reanalysis
abstract: The accuracy of climate reanalyses is limited by observation availability, especially satellite soundings prior to 1979, when operational polar-orbiting satellites become more prevalent. This paper reports on successful efforts to locate the data record collected by the pioneering instrument Special Sensor H (SSH) mounted on four Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) block-5D1 satellites (F-1 to F-4) from 1976 to 1980. This data record was unavailable in recent decades, until the present investigations. The SSH instrument features 8 Thermal InfraRed (TIR) channels, one sensitive to ozone and the others primarily sensitive to atmospheric temperature and the surface, and 8 Far InfraRed (FIR) water-vapor-sensitive channels. The FIR region of the electromagnetic spectrum, which has not been much monitored since SSH, is under renewed interest with the recent PREFIRE and upcoming ESA FORUM missions. The SSH data record that could be rescued, from March 1977 to February 1980, covers an important time period in the global climate record, coinciding with the acceleration of ozone layer depletion. The paper presents the methodology used to recover the observations from the original tapes, and the derivation of a fast radiative transfer model capable of supporting data assimilation. The observations are assessed using radiance simulations and comparisons to the contemporary instrument High-resolution Infrared Radiation Sounder on NOAA satellites. An Observing System Experiment is conducted, using an early and lower-resolution version of the upcoming ERA6 reanalysis data assimilation system. Several configuration trials are made, to separate the impact of FIR channels from other channels. The results indicate that the assimilation of all available channels sensitive to temperature, ozone, and water vapor, including those in the FIR, yields the largest impact to improve the analyses and forecasts. Radiance simulations of the hyperspectral sounder SI-1 mounted on Soviet satellite Meteor-29 in 1979 demonstrate that DMSP SSH observations’ assimilation leads to a better representation of the SI-1 measurements, confirming the positive impact of SSH to improve reanalysis quality.

title: Feedstock quality gradients and net energy constraints in sustainable aviation fuel: a biophysical economic assessment of the HEFA pathway
abstract: Despite extensive policy support and climate commitments, Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) remains more expensive than conventional jet fuel. Hydroprocessed esters and fatty acids (HEFA) are currently the dominant commercial SAF pathway. This paper evaluates a narrower proposition: whether differences in lipid-feedstock quality create a biophysical mechanism that could contribute to persistent production-cost differences as HEFA deployment expands. The analysis is structural and comparative rather than a time-series or causal model of observed prices. Using a biophysical-economics framework, this study compares the external energy required to acquire, prepare, and convert used cooking oil (UCO), conventional crop oils, and purpose-grown oil crops. Under midpoint assumptions for external input and liquid-energy recovery, external-energy EROI is approximately 4.06:1 for UCO, 1.55:1 for conventional crop oils, and 1.82:1 for purpose-grown oil crops. The corresponding full-combination envelopes are 3.0–5.9, 0.99–3.2, and 1.3–3.2, respectively; these envelopes combine favorable or unfavorable parameter endpoints and are not probability distributions. The UCO baseline applies a cut-off attribution convention: no original agricultural-production burden is assigned after the oil has completed its first use, although collection, transport, pretreatment, hydrogen, and conversion energy are included. This convention is not a claim that UCO is physically burden-free. Reassigning 25%, 50%, and 100% of a representative 0.29 MJ/MJ original crop-oil burden lowers the UCO EROI to approximately 3.05, 2.44, and 1.74, respectively; adding 0.50 MJ/MJ lowers it to approximately 1.23. Thus, UCO's absolute advantage is allocation-sensitive, whereas the physical energy required for collection and HEFA conversion is unchanged. The results identify a step from low-attributed-burden waste lipids to an overlapping band of deliberately cultivated oils. Eliminating the modeled midpoint conversion-stage energy would offset only about 15.6% of the representative external-input difference between UCO and conventional crop oil. This static comparison supports a plausible offsetting mechanism between conversion learning and marginal-feedstock quality, but it does not locate a deployment level or date at which one effect overtakes the other. Tallow remains volumetrically important but energetically unresolved, and a numerical petroleum comparison is withheld pending a boundary-harmonized well-to-gate calculation.

title: Design and validation of a measurement scale for digital transformation capabilities in agricultural settings
abstract: Digital transformation is essential for strengthening agri-food systems in emerging economies. However, there is a lack of validated tools to assess both the capabilities and levels of digital maturity in agricultural production units. This research validates an instrument to measure Digital Transformation (DT) capabilities and levels of digital maturity in agricultural production units (APU) in an emerging economy. The instrument encompasses six dimensions: sensing, seizing and transforming capabilities, along with the stages of digital maturity, digitization, digitalization, and digital transformation. The validation process was developed in five stages, including theoretical foundation, item development, expert review, and exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, applied to a sample of 68 potato farmers from south-central Chile. The final instrument consists of 32 items with promising psychometric properties; reliability and validity indicators met recommended thresholds across most dimensions, with a small number of exceptions discussed in the study. The results reveal that farmers widely recognize the value of digital technology and demonstrate a willingness to invest, despite being in early stages of digitalization, with widespread use of basic tools such as smartphones and messaging applications, but with limited adoption of more advanced technologies such as precision agriculture. This gap between perceived value and actual implementation highlights the role of structural barriers in rural contexts. This instrument offers researchers and policymakers a promising, albeit preliminary, tool to assess dynamic capabilities and digital maturity at the individual farmer level, representing an initial step toward diagnostic tools for digital transformation processes in this context.

title: Beyond risk mitigation: agricultural insurance enhances crop carbon absorption and delivers environmental co-benefits
abstract: Agricultural insurance is widely recognized as an economic instrument for dispersing production risk, yet whether it yields environmental co-benefits remains underexplored. This study shifts the focus beyond risk mitigation by examining how agricultural insurance shapes crop carbon absorption. Drawing on a 14-year panel of 333 prefecture-level cities in China, we combine a two-way fixed effects model augmented with province-by-year interaction effects, an instrumental variable approach, and a robust heterogeneous Difference-in-Differences approach to establish causality. The results show that agricultural insurance significantly enhances crop carbon absorption. Mechanism analyses trace this effect to the reshaping of farmers’ production decisions: structural adjustment toward staple crop cultivation and scale expansion through a higher multiple cropping index. Heterogeneity analyses corroborate these channels, revealing stronger effects in major grain-producing areas and regions with larger per capita arable land. The carbon benefits are also more pronounced in economically underdeveloped areas and regions where non-agricultural industries are less developed. Beyond risk mitigation, agricultural insurance thus serves as a policy lever translating micro-level farmer behavior into macro-level ecological gains, and the resulting carbon absorption co-benefit deserves greater weight in future insurance design.

title: Is County-Level Urban–Rural Integration Associated with Farmers’ Green Production Capabilities? Evidence from 506 Vegetable Growers in Shandong and Zhejiang, China
abstract: This study examined the association between county-level urban–rural integration and farmers’ green production capabilities, conceptualizing the county context as a local opportunity structure. It also examined whether this association differed by farm scale. Data were collected from 506 farmers in Shandong and Zhejiang between late 2024 and early 2025; 282 were primarily engaged in vegetable production, while 224 cultivated vegetables alongside other crops. A county-level urban–rural integration index (CURI) was developed covering four dimensions: economic, social, spatial, and ecological and agricultural production integration. The hypotheses were evaluated using ordered logit and city random-intercept models. The baseline CURI was positively associated with self-rated green production capabilities. A one-sample-standard-deviation increase in CURI corresponded to a 6.50 percentage point higher average predicted probability of attaining high green production capability, and the association was stronger among small-scale farmers. The analysis also showed a stable negative association between CURI and pesticide expenditure, while green production capability was positively associated with direct sales to urban end markets. Fertilizer expenditure and order- or contract-based sales showed no stable relationship. Overall, county-level urban–rural integration was a contextual correlate of green production capacity. The findings may inform the design and evaluation of future efforts to improve access to green-production services and market linkages, particularly for small-scale farmers.

title: How Much Temporal Information Is Needed? Optimizing Sentinel-2 Time Series for Operational Rice Crop Mapping
abstract: Rice crop mapping is essential for precision agriculture, irrigation management, yield forecasting, and assessment of the environmental impacts of rice cultivation. This information is particularly relevant in Mediterranean rice-growing wetlands, such as L’Albufera Natural Park (Valencia, Spain), where crop development is closely linked to seasonal flooding and water-management practices. Although multitemporal Sentinel-2 imagery is widely used for crop classification, the temporal information required to achieve accurate early-season mapping remains insufficiently investigated. This study evaluates the optimal temporal window and spectral variables for operational rice mapping in L’Albufera using Sentinel-2 imagery acquired during the 2023 and 2024 growing seasons. Monthly reflectance composites from visible and near-infrared bands (B2, B3, B4, and B8) and vegetation indices (NDVI, NDWI, EVI, and RVI) were analyzed through temporal profiling, statistical analysis, principal component analysis, and supervised machine-learning classification. Within the classifiers evaluated, performance gains were associated more closely with temporal and spectral feature selection than with classifier family. The strongest performance was achieved using the NDVI, EVI, B3, and B8 from April through June (on the 2023 holdout set, overall accuracy [OA] = 83.8% and rice F1 score = 0.90; in the 2024 cross-year evaluation, OA = 76.5% and rice F1 score = 0.86). Model-agnostic permutation importance and Shapley values were used to identify the most influential predictors, yielding a compact six-predictor set comprising the NDVI from April to June, B8 from May to June, and B3 in June. This reduced six-predictor model retained similar performance in the 2023 holdout set (OA = 82.4%; rice F1 score = 0.89) and in the 2024 cross-year evaluation (OA = 75.4%; rice F1 score = 0.85). These results show that rice fields can be mapped before crop maturity within the study area while reducing temporal and predictor requirements.

title: NWP-Conditioned Dynamic Simplicial Neural Networks for Joint Day-Ahead Forecasting of Regional Wind Farm Clusters
abstract: Regional day-ahead wind power forecasting (WPF) requires spatial dependence to adapt to forecast weather. Many existing graph models mainly capture pairwise relations derived from static geography or historical correlations, limiting their representation of multi-farm responses under changing wind fields. This paper proposes AeroSimp-Lite, an NWP-conditioned dynamic simplicial neural network that represents farms, pairwise relations, and three-farm interactions as nodes, edges, and triangles. A fixed sparse complex preserves simplicial closure, while forecast wind vectors dynamically condition interactions at each lead time. Hodge-inspired filtering integrates multi-order information, and a temporal residual decoder corrects a local NWP-based power prior. Regional-consistency and ramp losses constrain aggregate production and rapid changes. Experiments on onshore and offshore clusters demonstrate improved site-level and regional accuracy with moderate computational cost. In the model-order comparison, dynamic edges reduce regional nMAE by 7.1% onshore and 12.0% offshore relative to the node-only model, while adding triangle interactions yields further reductions of 3.8% and 4.5%, respectively, relative to Dynamic-GNN. Ablation results show that dynamic edges provide the main gain, while triangles offer smaller, metric-dependent improvements. However, the lower offshore ramp F1 shows that average accuracy gains do not extend to every objective. AeroSimp-Lite provides a practical approach to modeling weather-dependent higher-order spatial interactions without claiming atmospheric causality.

title: Hormone-Mediated Signaling of Reactive Oxygen Species Under Abiotic Stress
abstract: Abiotic stresses trigger the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in various subcellular compartments of plant cells, where they perform a dual function: acting as cytotoxic agents during acute stress and as highly specific signaling modulators under mild or chronic stress. However, the fundamental question of how the cell distinguishes between toxic and signaling ROS pools—and how phytohormones coordinate this distinction—remains unresolved. This review re-examines the molecular logic of the hormone-redox interface, focusing on the post-translational modifications of NADPH oxidases (RBOHs) and antioxidant enzymes as a key mechanism for the rapid tuning of signals. Moving beyond traditional linear cascade models, we propose the concept of a “dynamic hormonal code,” in which abscisic acid acts as the primary initiator of apoplastic ROS bursts via SnRK2-dependent phosphorylation, while salicylates and jasmonates modulate the duration and amplitude of these bursts, thereby determining the outcome—ranging from programmed cell death to systemic resistance. Known mechanisms of the hormonal code have been established (e.g., ABA → SnRK2 → RBOH; SA/JA antagonism mediated by NPR1; and the redox relay involving PRXIIB/GPX3 → ABI2). This review goes beyond simple hormone combinatorics by proposing a conceptual framework: the hormonal code encodes ROS signals through parameters of time, amplitude, and cellular compartment. Particular attention is paid to recent discoveries regarding the roles of auxin and brassinosteroids in reconfiguring chloroplast redox homeostasis during flooding and heat shock. Generalizing these data, we propose an integrated model of spatiotemporal regulation that explains how feedback loops involving ROS, Ca2+ waves, and hormone receptors facilitate systemic acclimation. Thus, targeting key crosstalk nodes—specifically SnRK2 and TOR kinase complexes—offers new strategies for engineering stress-resilient crops in the face of climate change.

title: Effects of Serine Acetyltransferase 2 (sat2) Haplotypes and Multiple Environmental Factors on Grain Protein Content and Yield-Related Traits in Bread Winter Wheat
abstract: Serine acetyltransferase 2 (sat2), rate-limiting for cysteine biosynthesis, is a candidate gene for grain protein content in durum wheat. We tested whether its intragenic variants are associated with protein content in bread winter wheat and how the effect depends on year, crop management, cultivar origin and other loci. Sixty-five cultivars were genotyped by Kompetitive Allele-Specific PCR for TDsat2.e9.1 (G>A, Gly325Ser) and TDsat2.i1.1 (G>T, intron 1). The variants were completely linked: only Hap1 (G; T; 32 cultivars) and Hap2 (A; G; 33 cultivars; the Chinese Spring reference haplotype) occurred. The 5913 observations (2021–2025; 16 year × management environments at one site) were analysed with a linear mixed model, the cultivar being the unit of replication. Hap1 exceeded Hap2 in protein content by 0.58% (95% CI 0.22–0.93; p = 0.0017; q = 0.014); the effect persisted with grain yield as a covariate and after adjustment for Glu-A1, Glu-D1 and 1BL.1RS, and haplotype frequencies were unrelated to cultivar origin and Rht-B1. Independently measured traits, including grain yield, did not differ. The effect kept its sign in all years but varied in size (p = 0.0013); no interaction with crop management was detected. The association requires confirmation in other collections.

title: Projected Crop-Calendar Shifts and Burning-Window Ventilation in Mainland Southeast Asia by Mid-Century: Implications for Residue Collection and Burning Management
abstract: Crop-residue burning in mainland Southeast Asia wastes a bioresource and coincides with the region’s worst air quality. We asked how projected crop-calendar shifts change the overlap between residue burning and stagnant weather by mid-century (2041–2060). Burning windows from harvest to the next planting, validated against satellite cropland fire detections, were projected with 15 bias-corrected CMIP6 models under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 and combined with two stagnation indices: calm days and poorly ventilated afternoons. Rice harvests advance by 6–9 days, but the calendar shift changes the share of residue burning on stagnant days by less than 0.5 percentage points in the ensemble mean, whether burning follows the harvest or the next planting, because burning peaks in late February and March, when the frequency of stagnant days changes little from week to week. The shift instead removes one to two dry days from the first month after the rice harvest, when straw is collected. The change in the ventilation climate is larger but uncertain, because models disagree on near-surface wind, and it differs between and within countries. Crop-calendar shifts are therefore unlikely to increase the exposure of residue burning to stagnant conditions.

title: Multimodal Classification of Urban Trees into Remote-Sensing-Derived Taxonomic Groups Across the United States
abstract: Urban trees provide important ecosystem services; however, municipal inventories used to characterize urban-forest composition remain incomplete and inconsistent among cities. We developed a multimodal deep-learning framework that combined municipal inventories with tree-centered National Agriculture Imagery Program aerial imagery, airborne LiDAR canopy height, Sentinel-2 time series and phenology, Google Satellite Embeddings, and daily weather. Beginning with 5.43 million records from 60 U.S. cities, quality-control and data-availability screening retained 1.85 million records representing 579 taxa across 36 cities. Because many species and genera had overlapping remote-sensing signatures, a supervised discrimination model identified 11 intermediate groups that were subsequently collapsed into six remote-sensing-derived taxonomic groups. On an independent test set of 161,508 records, the final pruned ensemble achieved 0.793 accuracy, 0.772 macro-F1, and 0.792 weighted-F1. Group-specific F1 ranged from 0.705 to 0.867 among trees with LiDAR-derived vegetation height ≥ 2 m. Gate weights emphasized high-resolution NAIP-based inputs, whereas ablation and single-modality analyses showed that Sentinel-2 and weather time series supplied important complementary temporal information. Mean accuracy and macro-F1 declined to 0.685 and 0.478 when target cities were withheld but remained substantially higher than for models trained using individual cities. This framework supports scalable classification of individual urban trees into broader remotely distinguishable groups, not species-level identifications or ecological functional types. Sentinel-2 measurements provide contextual information at 10 m resolution rather than individual-crown observations.

title: Co-Fusion: Advancing 3D Object Detection with Collaborative Fusion
abstract: LiDAR–camera fusion for 3D object detection combines the metric geometry of LiDAR measurements with the semantic information in images. However, projected LiDAR depth is sparse and provides incomplete geometric guidance to the image branch, while the modality-specific branches follow different learning dynamics during multimodal training. We present Co-Fusion, a LiDAR-dominant collaborative fusion framework that extends the previously published Co-Fix3D detector. Co-Fusion introduces a LiDAR-depth guidance pipeline that standardizes projected LiDAR depth using dataset-level statistics and encodes the sparse measurements into features aligned with the image branch. A gated fusion network applies multiplicative modulation to the joint image–depth representation to produce depth-aware camera features. A three-stage parameter-transfer training schedule selectively transfers parameters from the LiDAR branch to initialize the camera and fusion branches. Experiments on the nuScenes 3D detection benchmark show that Co-Fusion reaches 74.1% mAP and 75.3% NDS in the single-frame multimodal setting without test-time augmentation.

title: Terrain-Modulated Multi-Polarimetric Fusion for Efficient Volumetric Radar Nowcasting
abstract: Volumetric radar nowcasting requires models to represent storm evolution across time and altitude without incurring prohibitive computational cost. Conventional two-dimensional approaches omit explicit vertical structure, whereas many three-dimensional models rely on computationally expensive volumetric operators. Reflectivity-only forecasting further fails to exploit complementary information from auxiliary radar variables and terrain. We therefore propose TerraCast3D, an end-to-end framework for deterministic gridded volumetric radar nowcasting conditioned on three polarimetric variables, namely differential reflectivity ZDR, specific differential phase KDP, and copolar correlation coefficient ρHV, together with Doppler spectrum width σV and terrain. TerraCast3D combines source-specific altitude-grouped encoding, terrain-modulated gated fusion, terrain-conditioned modulation of low-altitude reconstruction features, and lightweight spatiotemporal modeling to predict future reflectivity volumes while limiting the use of dense 3D operations. Experiments using GridRad-Severe volumetric radar data from 2019 to 2023 show that TerraCast3D achieves the highest CSI and HSS among the evaluated 3D models at all examined reflectivity thresholds while requiring substantially fewer FLOPs. At 40 dBZ, its full-volume CSI and HSS reach 0.3044 and 0.4501, respectively. Ablation experiments show that auxiliary radar variables mainly improve full-volume continuous-field accuracy and categorical skill at 20 and 30 dBZ, whereas joint auxiliary radar and terrain conditioning yields the highest 40 dBZ and threshold-averaged categorical scores. These findings show that altitude-aware representation and adaptive multi-source conditioning can strengthen intense-echo prediction while maintaining low arithmetic complexity in volumetric radar nowcasting.

title: Robust Crop Classification Model Based on Asynchronous SAR and Optical Temporal Feature Fusion
abstract: In-season crop identification requires accurate, timely, and reliable predictions from asynchronous SAR and optical observations that accumulate progressively during early and middle calendar checkpoints. This study proposes a progressive SAR–optical fusion framework with selective risk control for parcel-level crop monitoring. A Gated Cross-Attention Temporal Network (GCAT) integrates complementary Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 time-series information, while random-prefix training and real day-of-year encoding accommodate asynchronous and unequal-length observations. Probability calibration and a sequential ACCEPT/DEFER strategy further allow uncertain predictions to be deferred until a predefined acceptance criterion is satisfied. Experiments on PASTIS-R show that GCAT achieves a full-season Macro-F1 of 80.57 ± 0.83% across five official folds, outperforming unimodal and multimodal fusion baselines. In the primary Fold-2 evaluation, GCAT provides larger gains than the Sentinel-2-only model at early- and mid-season operational checkpoints, reaches acceptance 7.55 days earlier on average among jointly accepted parcels, and increases accepted coverage. Cross-year evaluation on Brandenburg shows that the classification and earliness advantages of multimodal fusion are partially retained, whereas the confidence–risk relationship degrades markedly. These results highlight the value of SAR–optical fusion for earlier in-season decisions while emphasizing the need for renewed calibration and reliability assessment across years.

title: Evaluating Protected Area Effectiveness: A Remote Sensing Review
abstract: Protected Areas (PAs) are essential for global biodiversity conservation, yet assessing their management and conservation effectiveness remains a formidable challenge. While remote sensing (RS) enables synoptic, large-scale monitoring, existing reviews are often fragmented—either decoupled from PA governance contexts or confined to isolated threat mappings. To bridge this gap, this review proposes a dual-dimensional analytical framework integrating management effectiveness and conservation effectiveness. Based on the literature retrieved via a systematic Boolean search in the Web of Science, we first establish a multi-source RS technology stack covering space-borne optical, radar, nighttime-light, LiDAR and cloud-computing platforms. We then review RS applications within the two dimensions. For management effectiveness, we trace the progression from single-disturbance tracking to integrated pressure assessments using counterfactual matching designs. For conservation effectiveness, we synthesize advances in biodiversity dynamics, ecosystem pattern integrity, quality evaluation, and ecosystem service quantification. Our review demonstrates that RS has become a major component of large-scale PA evaluation, revealing measurable successes while highlighting the risk of overestimating conservation outcomes when relying solely on greenness-based proxies. Persistent challenges include the lack of standardized, biome-specific assessment frameworks and the disconnect between biophysical monitoring and socio-ecological drivers. Addressing these gaps requires unified evaluation systems aligned with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, AI-driven multi-sensor fusion, and the operationalization of RS into routine PA governance to support the “30 × 30” target and ecological product value realization.

title: Dual-Gaussian Distribution Location Loss for Real Oriented Object Detection in Remote Sensing Image
abstract: In general object detection tasks, accurate responses to the boundaries and classifications of potential objects are required of detectors. Given the diverse shapes of objects, these bounding boxes are typically represented as horizontal rectangles. However, in aerial imagery scenarios, horizontal bounding boxes can easily miss valid detections when objects are densely distributed. In recent years, oriented object detection algorithms have achieved considerable success. However, they focus on the boundaries of the object without taking into account its head–tail attributes and true orientation. Getting the true orientation of objects serves as the long-term aim of remote sensing object detection task. To resolve these issues, we decompose the single Gaussian distribution probability loss into a sequential dual-probability distribution, thereby establishing a one-to-one collaborative loss mechanism. This enables the model to learn the real orientation relationship from the dual distribution loss, achieving the acquisition of objects’ true orientation information. To more accurately reflect the preference of detectors, we design a new evaluation metric based on the cosine function and average precision. We conduct a series of experiments on the DOTA dataset, HRSC dataset, and FAIR1M dataset, achieving satisfactory results that validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Climate Change and the Sustainability of Rainfed Common Bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) Production in Latin America: A Scoping Review
abstract: Climate change poses one of the greatest threats to the sustainability of rainfed agriculture in Latin America, where common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) production is particularly vulnerable because of its high sensitivity to fluctuations in temperature and precipitation, as well as to extreme climatic events. This scoping review aimed to examine the evolution of scientific research on the impacts of climate change on the sustainability of rainfed common bean production in Latin America by identifying geographic and temporal research trends, methodological approaches, major scientific advances, knowledge gaps, and future research priorities. The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodological framework and the PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines and included 154 peer-reviewed studies published in indexed journals. The evidence was synthesized by country, publication period, and methodological approach, encompassing field experiments, agroclimatic assessments, crop-simulation models, Geographic Information Systems (GISs), remote sensing, review articles, meta-analyses, and farmer surveys. The results revealed that scientific production was concentrated primarily in Mexico and Brazil, whereas research in the remaining Latin American countries remained limited and geographically fragmented. Over time, the field evolved from studies focused primarily on crop physiology and genetic improvement toward multidisciplinary approaches integrating climatic, agronomic, environmental, and socioeconomic perspectives. Despite these advances, important knowledge gaps remain, particularly the limited availability of long-term field experiments and the insufficient integration of environmental, economic, and social dimensions into climate adaptation research. This review provides a comprehensive regional synthesis of the available scientific evidence on climate change and rainfed common bean production in Latin America, offering a solid evidence base to guide future research, inform climate adaptation strategies, and strengthen the resilience and sustainability of rainfed common bean production systems.

title: Agricultural and Rural Big Data Policy and Agribusiness Supply Chain Resilience: Implications for Sustainable Agriculture in China
abstract: Supply chain resilience supports sustainable agriculture by helping firms maintain operations and food supply during disruptions. This study examines whether agricultural digital public infrastructure strengthens agribusiness supply chain resilience, using China’s 2016 Agricultural and Rural Big Data Pilot Program as a quasi-natural experiment within a difference-in-differences design. The estimates indicate that the program significantly improves supply chain resilience. Exploratory channel analyses provide evidence consistent with bank-credit and corporate digital-transformation channels. The estimated gains are greater among state-owned enterprises, firms with digitally experienced executives, and firms in regions with higher internet penetration. Component analyses show positive estimates for agricultural data sharing, market-based investment and operational mechanisms, and big-data applications, whereas commodity-specific database development has no statistically detectable effect. These findings contribute to sustainability research by linking digital public infrastructure to the capacity of agribusinesses to withstand and recover from disruptions, an important foundation for the economic sustainability of agricultural supply chains. They also suggest that coordinated investment in data infrastructure, financing access, and digital capabilities may support more reliable agricultural supply and sustainable agricultural development, particularly in economies with fragmented production and limited information sharing.

title: Proposal for a Multidimensional Local Development Index for Rural Communities in the Amazonas Region of Peru
abstract: Rural areas in the Peruvian Amazon exhibit profound structural gaps, yet traditional development measurements often rely on linear, compensatory approaches that mask simultaneous deprivations. Achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in these territories requires comprehensive diagnostic tools adapted to complex local realities. This study proposes the Multidimensional Local Development Index (MLDI) for 63 rural communities in the Amazonas region in Peru. Utilizing data from the 2024 National Agricultural Survey and fieldwork, an initial set of 29 candidate indicators across six dimensions (Population, Social Welfare, Economy, Environment, Technology, and Production) was identified and validated via the Delphi method. Following a variance-based proportional weighting, the 8 most statistically discriminant indicators were retained and aggregated using a geometric mean to explicitly prevent compensatory biases. The MLDI revealed a generalized scenario of “Low” to “Very Low” development (scores ranging from 0.11 to 0.37), with no communities achieving medium or high levels. The non-compensatory aggregation exposed a critical territorial dynamic: the “illusion of productivity”. While some settlements showed advances in agricultural output or internet access, severe structural bottlenecks prevented these from translating into economic well-being. The study identified significant transmission friction between productive volume and household income. The results suggest that sectoral interventions focused solely on increasing agricultural yield or digital connectivity are insufficient to reduce rural poverty. To achieve sustainable development, public policies must shift toward integrated territorial management, ensuring that productivity gains are strictly paired with infrastructure, market access, and institutional capacity.

title: Nonlinear Effects of Digital Empowerment on Agricultural Green Total Factor Productivity in China
abstract: Achieving sustainable agricultural development requires both technological progress and well-designed public institutions. This paper examines whether regional digital development improves agricultural green total factor productivity (AGTFP) in China—an integrated measure of productivity, resource conservation, and environmental performance—and whether government fiscal intervention conditions that relationship. A city-level digital empowerment index is constructed from digital infrastructure, digital applications, and digital human capital, and AGTFP is measured with a Super-SBM model that incorporates undesirable outputs such as agricultural carbon emissions and excess fertilizer input. Using panel data for 226 prefecture-level cities over 2011–2020, two-way fixed-effects estimates show that digital empowerment is positively and significantly associated with AGTFP: a one-standard-deviation increase in digital empowerment corresponds to roughly 0.03 standard deviations of AGTFP, suggesting that digitalization can advance resource-saving and low-carbon agricultural production. Crucially, this sustainability dividend is not automatic. The positive association weakens as fiscal intervention intensifies, and threshold estimates identify a structural break at a fiscal-intervention ratio of about 0.29, above which the association turns negative—a pattern consistent with fiscal crowding out of market-led digital investment. These findings imply that digital dividends for sustainable agriculture depend on how public spending is allocated, not merely on how much is spent. This paper contributes city-level evidence on the boundary conditions of digital empowerment in agriculture and shows why linear, quadratic, and threshold specifications should be interpreted as distinct forms of nonlinearity rather than as a single policy optimum.

title: Beyond Rainfall: A Conceptual Framework for Multi-Hazard Weather-Based Insurance Adoption Among Small-Scale Tobacco Farmers in Zimbabwe
abstract: Smallholder tobacco farmers in Mashonaland West Province, Zimbabwe, face increasing exposure to multihazard climate catastrophes, including drought, excessive rainfall, hail, and windstorms. Although weather-based crop insurance is promoted as a climate risk-financing tool, most products rely on single rainfall indices that poorly capture localized perils, creating basis risk and low renewal rates. This conceptual paper develops an integrated adoption framework that moves beyond rainfall. Combining Protection Motivation Theory [PMT] and Diffusion of Innovations Theory [DOI], the paper explains adoption intention as a function of threat appraisal, coping appraisal, innovation attributes, affordability, and institutional trust. To bridge the gap between adoption and actual resilience, the paper proposes the original Climate Catastrophe Agricultural Insurance and Resilience [CCAIR] Model with six pillars: Catastrophe intelligence, Contract matching, Affordable financing, Information integrity, Rapid recovery, and Resilience learning. The model specifies hazardspecific product design, inclusive premium financing, and measurable post-event recovery outcomes. A sequential mixedmethods validation protocol is outlined for Mashonaland West, comprising documentary review, farmer surveys, key informant interviews, and historical index-loss back-testing. The paper does not report primary data; all relationships are propositional and await empirical testing.
journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology

title: Smart Vehicle Identification and Tracking Using YOLO-Based License Plate Recognition
abstract: Manual verification of vehicle registration plates can be time consuming and error-prone. This paper details a functional prototype which enables license plate detection, reading and results presentation. Once images or videos have been uploaded the system uses Python to detect license plates within them, and then extracts and displays the plate information through a simple web interface. Detection is done by training a YOLO model using the Ultralytics library. The license plate is cropped using OpenCV, and then the characters are read using EasyOCR. If a video is used, ByteTrack will link detections between frames using temporary tracking IDs. The system has been made using Gradio to create a dashboard for the user. A detection section allows users to upload an image and detect license plates. There is also a video tracking section, detection history section and CSV export. On one example test image the detection had an accuracy of around 90.1%. The OCR stage found the plate text "DL1CA6207 IND" with an accuracy of around 99.43%. These are only for one example and do not give an indication of the overall accuracy. This project contributes by providing a functional, open source solution to license plate detection, recognition, tracking and recording. The limitations are well discussed and include OCR errors, additional printing on the plates, temporary tracking IDs and there needs to be more testing on a larger scale. A clear plan is provided to properly evaluate the project
