title: Development and Pilot Evaluation of a Standardized and Accessible Rubric (OMNI) for Assessing Generative AI in Health Care Contexts: Four-Stage Mixed Methods Study.
abstract: Background The rapid adoption of generative AI in the community and health care necessitates reliable, human-led evaluation. Objective This study aimed to develop a standardized rubric to support health care professionals, administrators, and researchers in evaluating generative AI outputs in health contexts. Methods A rubric was developed through a 4-stage mixed methods study: literature synthesis, expert refinement, pilot application, and post-pilot feedback. The rubric was informed by 69 publications and refined through iterative feedback from a multidisciplinary expert panel (n=23). The pilot rubric was applied to 4 health care scenarios: responses to health-related Reddit questions, generation of health-related images and videos, responses to health professional continuing education questions, and automated physician-to-physician clinical documentation generation. Via these scenarios, 15 clinicians (medical practitioners, pharmacists, and medical oncologists) evaluated 250 input-output pairs using domain-level ratings and qualitative comments. The evaluated outputs included 200 AI-generated responses across the 4 health care scenarios and 50 physician-tagged replies in the health-related Reddit questions scenario. Results The final rubric, OMNI, comprised 10 evaluation domains (Accuracy, Safety, Recognizes Uncertainty, Completeness, Communicates Clearly, Empathetic, Context Aware, Referencing, Follows Instructions, and Avoids Coerciveness) assessed on 4-point Likert scales, supported by detailed instructional and example materials. Via the 4 pilot scenarios, assessors generated 9600 domain-level ratings and 4010 qualitative comments. The mean pairwise agreement for the 4-point Likert groups ranged from 30.8% to 53.4%, increasing to 59.3% to 79.6% when collapsed into broad agreement categories; Gwet’s AC2 ranged from 0.49 to 0.80. OMNI differentiated strengths and weaknesses between models within scenarios, while recurrent limitations in Referencing, Recognizes Uncertainty, Completeness, Empathetic, and Accuracy were identified across scenarios. Multimodal image and video outputs had the highest occurrence of negative rating domains. Assessors reported OMNI was usable and indicated they would reuse it. Conclusions OMNI is a standardized, accessible rubric for expert-led evaluation of generative AI outputs in health contexts. Pilot application demonstrated that OMNI could differentiate AI performance across models and domains while generating structured feedback. Further work is needed to assess its applicability to purpose-built health AI tools, agentic systems, and organizational evaluation settings.

title: AI Digital Twin for Cloud Cyber Security
abstract: The key advantage of cloud computing is scalability and flexibility of infrastructure, however, the growing complexity of cloud environments has led to numerous security issues. Current security systems are largely reactive, which means that any detected attacks have already taken place. This paper suggests the use of the AI-based Digital Twin technology for cybersecurity in cloud environments, providing the possibility of creating a virtual copy of the cloud environment that can be used for continuous monitoring, attack simulation, and security testing. The proposed framework uses AI/ML algorithms for anomaly detection, attacks' classification, and risk assessment in conjunction with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) in order to achieve collaboration and adaptability of security response. The system includes cloud resource monitoring, attacks simulation, security logging, alert generation, access control by roles, and security analysis dashboard. The development of the system takes place using MERN stack architecture with Digital Twin synchronization of virtual cloud resources and their metrics. With the combination of Digital Twin technology, AI-based threat detection and multi-agent decision making, the proposed framework can provide enhanced proactivity,adaptiveness, and real-time performance of cybersecurity in cloud environments.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Smart AI-Based Agriculture Decision Support System (AgriSens)
abstract: Traditional farming relies heavily on empirical guesswork and legacy ancestral knowledge, frequently leaving crops vulnerable to uncalibrated chemical fertilizer application, unpredictable micro-climates, and delayed foliar disease detection. This paper introduces AgriSens, a comprehensive, full-stack smart farming platform developed to empower farmers with datadriven precision agriculture. The system integrates a multi-parameter crop recommendation engine using a mathematical Gaussian-decay environmental fitness model alongside a multimodal leaf disease diagnostic system powered by Google Gemini 3.7 Flash computer vision to identify foliar pathogens from smartphone imagery. Furthermore, the architecture deploys a soiltexture-aware fertilizer optimization engine that calculates precise N-P-K (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium) nutrient deficits, a real-time agro-meteorological forecasting stream driven by the Open-Meteo API for chemical spray safety alerts, and a closedloop automated IoT irrigation telemetry simulator. To eliminate structural literacy barriers within rural farming communities, the platform features native voice synthesis and a 7-language localized translation module. Simulation benchmarks demonstrate that the platform achieves rapid visual diagnostic latencies under 2.5 seconds and optimizes water conservation by 25% to 35% compared to baseline scheduled flooding methods
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Secure Multi-Agent Collaboration Using Large Language Models
abstract: As Large Language Models have emerged and become increasingly significant, the way to develop smart multi-agent systems has been transformed, enabling them to communicate, collaborate and decision more efficiently. These systems rely on agents working independently which need to effectively and safely coordinate their actions, to maintain reliability in messy realworld environments. However, bringing LLMs into the mix introduces new risks like data leaks, trickery from bad actors, and trust issues. This paper breaks down a full plan for keeping multi-agent teamwork secure when using LLMs. We look at everything from how they are built and the rules they use to communicate to the safety tools used to stop attacks. We also talk about where this is being used now, the hurdles we still face, and where the tech is headed for building secure AI ecosystems
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: AI Powered Smart Personalized Study Planner with Intelligent Reminder
abstract: In the contemporary academic paradigm, tertiary and secondary students consistently encounter significant cognitive overhead and temporal fragmentation, largely attributable to suboptimal scheduling methodologies, procrastination, and lack of individualized pedagogical pacing. Conventional digital calendars and static scheduling instruments fail to account for fluid academic priorities, cognitive fatigue thresholds, or behavioral non-compliance. To address these systemic inefficiencies, this paper introduces an AI-Powered Smart Study Planner with Intelligent Reminders, a pervasive Android-based architectural framework engineered to synthesize automated, context-aware study trajectories and foster disciplined academic behaviors. Developed natively utilizing Java and XML with persistent cloud synchronization facilitated by Firebase Realtime Database, the proposed architecture provides dynamic schedule synthesis parameterized by examination schedules, subject difficulty profiles, available temporal bandwidth, and granular academic milestones. A principal contribution of this system lies in its dual integration of predictive behavioural modeling and state-of-the-art conversational artificial intelligence. The framework incorporates a novel Snooze Risk Prediction module that systematically evaluates telemetry data—encompassing chronological snooze frequency, missed learning intervals, and temporal inertia—to compute probabilistic risk factors associated with task avoidance, thereby dynamically recalibrating dispatch heuristics for targeted interventions. Simultaneously, the platform integrates Natural Language Processing (NLP) pipelines and Generative Artificial Intelligence primitives to deliver on-demand cognitive scaffolding. These automated pedagogical tools encompass dynamic notes summarization, programmatic multi-tier quiz synthesis, automated contextual disambiguation of complex academic topics, and real-time conversational agent mediation
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: AI Agent-Driven Datacenter Optimizer: A Guardrailed, Explainable LLM Orchestrator for Cloud Platform Management
abstract: Modern datacenters must balance three objectives that often conflict: keeping hardware within safe thermal limits, meeting latency expectations for high-priority work, and reducing the cost and carbon footprint of electricity. Traditional controllers handle these with fixed rules or heavily engineered optimization pipelines. This paper presents Grid Control, an autonomous datacenter orchestration system in which a large language model (LLM) acts as the decision-making agent. A simulated multi-region datacenter (5 regions, 15 servers, 60 chipsets) streams telemetry every second. Every decision interval the agent receives a frozen telemetry window and selects exactly one action from a small, closed vocabulary: shift_within_server, shift_within_region, migrate_region, or pass. A prioritized policy ranks overheating first, latency and load balance second, and cost and carbon third. Safety is enforced outside the model by a guardrail layer that routes high-criticality or administratorprohibited actions to a human approval queue. A feedback loop returns measured outcomes of past actions to the prompt as incontext learning signal, and a scope-restricted explainability module answers operator questions about the agent's behavior. Over 20 paired simulation runs, a deterministic stand-in for the agent's policy reduced time spent above the 68 °C threshold by about 24% and carbon-weighted load by about 9% relative to a no-agent baseline, with about 3% lower electricity cost. LLM-inthe-loop evaluation is left to future work. The contribution is an architecture and a reproducible testbed for studying safe, explainable, LLM-driven infrastructure control.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: DeepGuard: A Robust Multimodal Framework for Automated Deepfake Screening and Triage
abstract: Deepfakes are synthetic images, videos, and voice recordings produced by deep generative models, and their realism now exceeds what human observers can reliably judge. Most existing detectors address a single medium, which leaves them blind to forgeries that live in motion or in sound. This paper presents DeepGuard, a unified multimodal framework that accepts an image, a video, or an audio file through one web interface and returns a Real or Deepfake verdict together with a confidence percentage. Uploaded media are normalized and, for video, separated into frames and an audio track. YOLOv8-Face localizes and crops the facial region, a ResNet-50 convolutional network extracts spatial forgery cues such as texture irregularities and blending artifacts, a bidirectional long short-term memory network models frame-to-frame inconsistencies, and a Wav2Vec2 model examines the speech signal for synthetic or cloned voices. A Bayesian weighted fusion stage combines whichever modality predictions are available into one deepfake probability, which is thresholded and stored with its metadata in a history database. The system is implemented with a Flask backend, OpenCV, and NumPy. The paper details the design rationale, the algorithm of each module, the fusion rule, and a leakage-free evaluation protocol based on accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and a confusion matrix. Quantitative results are intentionally not reported here; they will be added after experiments on benchmark datasets.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Agility as a Driver of Audit Mission Effectiveness: A Theoretical Framework and Case Study of Deloitte Morocco
abstract: Objective: This article examines the extent to which integrating agile practices (Scrum, Kanban), framed by the COSO model and the Takeuchi and Nonaka agile framework, can improve the effectiveness of audit engagements compared with the traditional approach. Methods: An exploratory qualitative study was conducted through a semi-structured interview, organized in five parts, with the head of an audit engagement at Deloitte Morocco. Results: The findings show that Deloitte Morocco, like the other Big Four firms present in Morocco, still relies on a traditional audit process and has not yet integrated agile practices; the interview nonetheless reveals the firm's openness to future integration, which does not allow the four proposed hypotheses (H1-H4) to be empirically confirmed or refuted. Conclusion: This exploratory study highlights the gap between the theoretical potential of agile auditing and its actual adoption in Morocco and paves the way for future research based on a larger sample allowing statistical testing of the proposed hypotheses.

title: Convolutional Neural Network Based on Transfer Learning for Pest Classification in Chili Plant
abstract: Pest infestation is a major cause of productivity loss in chili cultivation, requiring accurate and automated pest identification systems to support precision agriculture. This study proposes a lightweight MobileNetV2-based transfer learning model for multi-species chili pest classification using a validated Indonesian digital image dataset. The dataset consists of 2,450 images representing seven major chili pest species, collected from publicly available web sources and complemented with field images acquired under natural conditions. All images underwent manual curation, quality control, taxonomic verification, and annotation validation by experts to ensure dataset reliability. The dataset was divided into training and testing in a ratio of 80:20, and data augmentation techniques were applied to improve model generalization. MobileNetV2 was compared with ResNet50 and EfficientNetB0. All models were trained for 50 epochs using the Adam optimizer and the categorical cross-entropy loss function. Model performance was evalu-ated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. Experimental results show that MobileNetV2 achieved the highest accuracy (98.29%), outperforming ResNet50 (97.84%) and EfficientNetB0 (97.56%) while maintaining low computational complexity suitable for resource-constrained environments. This study contributes (1) a validated Indonesian multi-species chili pest dataset, (2) an optimized MobileNetV2 transfer learning model for accurate pest classification, and (3) a practical Streamlit-based pest monitoring system for precision agriculture.
journal: Jurnal Teknik Pertanian Lampung (Journal of Agricultural Engineering)

title: Effects of Binary and Ternary Biomass Blending on Updraft Gasification Performance, Syngas Composition, and Flame Characteristics
abstract: The increasing global energy demand and environmental concerns associated with fossil fuels have intensified interest in renewable energy, particularly biomass. Agricultural residues such as rice husk (RH), corn cob (CC), and reed biomass (RB) are abundant resources that can be converted into energy through gasification. This study aimed to compare the gasification performance and flame characteristics of these feedstocks and their binary and ternary blends and to identify conditions for improved performance. Experiments were conducted using a fixed-bed updraft gasifier with a constant feedstock mass of 1 kg per run. RH was used in its raw form, whereas CC and RB were ground to 10–30 mm. Airflow rates ranged from 1.8 to 2.8 m³/h by adjusting blower speed. Flame characteristics were analyzed from digital images using ImageJ. CC showed the highest gasification efficiency (72.8%) and gas yield (2.65 Nm³/kg), whereas RH showed the lowest values (61.4% and 2.10 Nm³/kg), attributed to its high ash content. Blending improved performance, with the RH+CC+RB mixture achieving the highest efficiency (74.8%) and gas yield (2.80 Nm³/kg). The ternary blend also produced higher CO (24.9%) and H₂ (21.7%) and lower CO₂ (11.3%), with a strong blue flame, maximum blue flame intensity of 82.6%, and flame temperature of 980 °C. These findings demonstrate that feedstock blending can enhance biomass gasification and syngas combustion performance.
journal: Jurnal Teknik Pertanian Lampung (Journal of Agricultural Engineering)

title: Patient-Specific Dosimetry for [131I]NaI Therapy in End-Stage Renal Disease: Segmented Time-Activity Analysis, Hemodialysis Clearance, and Radiation Safety.
abstract: [131I]NaI therapy in patients with end-stage renal disease undergoing hemodialysis is challenging because renal clearance is markedly reduced, systemic retention is prolonged, and hemodialysis produces abrupt changes in activity. Patient-specific dosimetry may support individualized treatment planning and radiation-safety management. Methods: This prospective case series included 5 hemodialysis-dependent patients with end-stage renal disease and differentiated thyroid carcinoma treated with [131I]NaI under a standardized protocol combining scheduled hemodialysis with serial whole-body and blood measurements with family-dose and occupational radiation assessments. Whole-body activity was analyzed using a measurement-constrained segmented time-activity representation that explicitly accounted for dialysis-associated activity reductions. Blood activity concentration was integrated using trapezoidal integration with terminal monoexponential extrapolation. Whole-body and blood time-integrated activities, residence times, blood absorbed dose, red marrow absorbed dose, the modeled activity corresponding to a 2-Gy blood absorbed dose, postdischarge total effective dose equivalent, and occupational exposure were assessed. Results: Whole-body residence time ranged from 16.45 to 37.85 h, demonstrating substantial interpatient variability. Blood absorbed dose ranged from 0.054 to 0.452 Gy, and modeled red marrow absorbed dose ranged from 0.056 to 0.363 Gy. The modeled activities corresponding to a 2-Gy blood absorbed dose exceeded the administered activities but were not interpreted as evidence of activity escalation. Central postdischarge total effective dose equivalent estimates ranged from 0.13 to 2.47 mSv. All were below the 5-mSv constraint for comforters and caregivers, whereas cases 2 and 3 exceeded the 1-mSv constraint for other family members and had broad propagated uncertainties. Occupational exposure ranged from 5 to 158 μSv per hemodialysis session. Conclusion: In this 5-patient series, hemodialysis-adapted patient-specific dosimetry was feasible, and modeled blood and red marrow doses remained below the selected dosimetric constraint under the administered activities. The dosimetric workflow provides a practical framework for coordinating dosimetry, hemodialysis, and radiation safety but requires validation in larger multicenter prospective studies.

title: Few-shot semantic segmentation of UAV imagery for plant conservation: A systematic comparison of foundation models for Euphorbia resinifera mapping
abstract: Deep learning has transformed vegetation mapping from UAV imagery, yet state-of-the-art segmentation models require hundreds to thousands of expertly annotated images, creating prohibitive labor costs for conservation applications targeting endangered flora. This study addresses this bottleneck by systematically comparing three foundation models namely: DINOv2 (self-supervised), SegGPT (supervised), and SAM (promptable), for binary segmentation of Euphorbia resinifera, an endemic Moroccan succulent of conservation concern, using patches extracted from a single annotated UAV orthomosaic. A single-image training framework is presented where spatial diversity within one high-resolution orthomosaic substitutes for diversity across multiple images, combined with sliding window inference with vote-based fusion for full-resolution deployment. SegGPT achieved 83.74±2.55% mean IoU across 20 spatially independent test images spanning a 10.5-fold vegetation density gradient (2.01 to 21.11% coverage), outperforming DINOv2 (78.09±6.63%) and SAM (47.03±20.64%). The observed collapse in SAM’s performance, despite billion-mask pretraining, can be attributed to its architectural constraints. SAM’s fixed 1024×1024 input reduced training patches by 76.2%, and its frozen encoder limited trainable parameters to 0.1M versus SegGPT’s 316M. These findings establish that fine-tuned encoders substantially outperform frozen-encoder architectures for specialized vegetation (Euphorbia resinifera) segmentation, and that single-image foundation model training offers a viable paradigm for conservation deployment, reducing annotation costs from tens of thousands to hundreds of dollars. While demonstrated for a morphologically distinctive species, these principles may inform broader conservation remote sensing applications pending validation across diverse plant forms.

title: A Study on the Collaborative Approach of Tailored Policies and Technology Empowerment for Plateau Specialty Agriculture Bases in Yuxi City
abstract: Grade-based and category-specific management of agricultural bases, combined with tech empowerment, are two main approaches to improving the quality and efficiency of plateau agriculture. However, in practice, these two have long operated independently according to their own logics. The classification standards focus more on static conditions, and tech support often lacks scenario adaptation, leading to a structural mismatch between “recognized bases” and “empowered bases.” This paper develops an analysis framework of “classification identification—technology matching—collaborative governance,” using the provincial, municipal, and county-level base recognition system in Yuxi City along with tech support in facility agriculture, seed industry, technology commissioners, and digital agriculture as case studies. It examines how classification-based measures and tech empowerment are coupled. The study finds that Yuxi has established a classification system with “ten standards” for quantitative recognition and three-tier dynamic management, while tech support covers facilities and equipment, seed breeding, promotion services, digital platforms, and processing/cold chains, with some bases already showing a preliminary coupling of “high facilities—high output—high drive”. However, the recognition standards fall short in identifying the need for tech upgrades, there’s a mismatch between tech supply and base types, county-level bases have weak capacity to utilize tech, and tech penetration in farmer linkages is insufficient, creating four main obstacles to coordinated progress. Based on this, the paper proposes solutions like tiered precise empowerment, type-specific technology routes, joint review and conduction by dispatched teams, linking tech indicators to rewards instead of subsidies, and dynamic monitoring via digital platforms, providing a reference for turning highland agricultural bases from just “recognized” to “technologically empowered”.

title: Automated Textile Quality Control Using Deep Learning: Multi-Class Classification of Fabric Surface Defects
abstract: Fabric defects directly influence the surface appearance and overall quality of textile products, which makes their reliable detection and classification an essential component of quality control in the textile industry. This study applies deep learning, specifically transfer learning with a pretrained convolutional neural network, to automatically recognize six fabric image categories: vertical defects, defect-free fabric, holes, horizontal defects, lines, and stains. A dataset of 2,739 fabric images was divided into 1,369 images for training and 1,370 images for validation. Prior to model input, all images were converted to three-channel colour format, resized, centre-cropped to 224 × 224 pixels, and normalized. An 18-layer residual neural network (ResNet18), pretrained on a large image corpus, was fine-tuned for five epochs using the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 0.001 and a batch size of 32. Performance was evaluated on the validation partition, which was also reused for final testing, yielding an overall accuracy of 91.17%, a macro-averaged F1 score of 81.10%, and a support-weighted F1 score of 91.12%. Classification results differed noticeably across defect categories: defect-free images and stains achieved F1 scores of 98.12% and 92.27%, respectively, whereas holes proved more difficult to recognize, reaching an F1 score of 68.31% and a recall of 60.58%. These outcomes demonstrate that a fine-tuned deep learning model can effectively distinguish multiple categories of fabric surface condition within the evaluated dataset, while also exposing uneven recognition performance for certain defect types, particularly those with subtle or irregular visual patterns. By linking established textile defect categories with quantitative deep learning evaluation metrics, this work offers a preliminary baseline for automated, CNN-driven fabric quality assessment. The approach is relevant to textile manufacturing organizations, including those in Russia, seeking to integrate intelligent visual inspection systems into their production and quality assurance workflows.
journal: Journal of Computer Science and Technology Studies

title: Digital Financial Inclusion, Climate Resilience and Food Security in East Africa: Does Inequality Shape the Digital Finance–Agriculture Nexus?
abstract: Food insecurity is a long-standing development problem in East Africa, where farming systems are becoming more and more exposed to climate change and access to financial resources and socioeconomic inequalities. Meanwhile, the rapid expansion of digital financial services offers new opportunities for households and agricultural actors to access payments, savings, credit and risk-management services. It is, however, not yet well understood whether digital financial inclusion and climate resilience enhance food security, and whether inequality conditions the effect. This study explores how digital financial inclusion and climate resilience influence East African food security and the moderating effect of income inequality. The study is based on secondary panel data for East African countries and the two-step System Generalized Method of Moments (SGMM) estimator is used to deal with dynamic persistence, unobserved country heterogeneity and endogeneity. The findings suggest that digital financial inclusion, climate resilience are statistically significant and have a positive impact on food security, while income inequality is statistically significant and has a negative impact. Next, the relationship between digital financial inclusion and income inequality is negative and statistically significant, meaning that increasing inequality reduces the effect of digital financial inclusion on food security. The results suggest that simply increasing digital financial services might not be enough to enhance food security when there are financial barriers to entry for vulnerable groups. The study thus calls for policies to address inequalities and constraints in access to digital financial services and to build climate resilient agriculture to achieve inclusive digital financial services for improving food security in East Africa.

title: Mosca’s inequality revisited: a systematic review of quantum risk-timing models after the 2025–2026 reductions in quantum resource estimates
abstract: Estimates of the quantum resources required to break public-key cryptography fell sharply across 2025 and 2026, by enough to disturb the assumptions underlying the timing models organizations use to plan cryptographic migration. This review synthesizes published estimates for breaking RSA-2048, an integer-factoring target, and 256-bit elliptic-curve cryptography, a discrete-logarithm target, and examines what the revised figures do and do not imply for Mosca’s inequality, the standard risk-timing framework. Following a protocol adapted from PRISMA 2020 conventions for a technical corpus, and after a search conducted in two rounds, 84 sources were included from preprint servers, standards repositories, and peer-reviewed venues, with 13 core studies charted in a structured extraction matrix of twelve fields that records the assumption set behind every physical-qubit figure. The headline physical-qubit estimate for factoring RSA-2048 fell from about one billion in 2012 to 20 million in 2019, to roughly 900,000 in 2025, and to figures between about 11,000 and 471,000 in 2026 depending on the operating point selected. Estimates for 256-bit elliptic-curve keys followed a comparable path. The reductions are attributable to arithmetic and circuit innovations, magic-state techniques, higher-rate quantum error-correcting codes, and changed architectural and hardware assumptions, and these contributions are decomposed separately here instead of being reported as a single trend. A synthesis restricted to peer-reviewed sources alone yields the same direction of travel but a materially weaker magnitude, and this is reported explicitly. A reduction in required qubits compresses a resource threshold, not a calendar. Because the relationship between a resource requirement and the date a machine meeting it is built depends on fabrication yield, achieved error rates, connectivity, decoder throughput, control systems, and sustained-runtime engineering, this review presents the consequences for Mosca’s inequality as conditional implications and supports them with scenario analysis across plausible confidentiality lifetimes, migration times, and threat horizons in place of a point forecast. The evidence reduces one barrier to feasibility and widens the uncertainty around the threat horizon; on a risk-management basis, not an evidentiary one, that combination favors prioritized migration of long-lived confidential data.

title: Perceived regional economic benefits of smart agriculture: a dynamic capability and leadership perspective on AI adoption
abstract: Firms and regions increasingly adopt artificial intelligence (AI) in agriculture, yet the mechanisms through which AI adoption translates into broader economic outcomes remain underexplored. Drawing on dynamic capability theory, this study examines how AI adoption and transformational leadership are associated with perceived regional economic benefits through smart agriculture, while investigating the moderating role of workforce digital skills. A time-lagged survey was conducted over eight months in China, collecting data from 452 respondents working in agricultural and agri-food organizations. The proposed relationships were examined using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and necessary condition analysis (NCA). The findings indicate that AI adoption and transformational leadership are positively associated with smart agriculture and perceived regional economic benefits. Smart agriculture partially mediates the relationships between AI adoption, transformational leadership, and perceived regional economic benefits. Furthermore, workforce digital skills significantly strengthen the relationship between AI adoption and smart agriculture. The necessity analysis identifies AI adoption and transformational leadership as key bottleneck conditions for achieving higher levels of perceived regional economic benefits. This study advances the literature on agricultural digitalization by conceptualizing smart agriculture as an organizational digital-agriculture capability and integrating technological adoption, transformational leadership, and workforce digital skills into a unified theoretical framework. The findings provide practical insights for agricultural organizations and policymakers seeking to strengthen smart agricultural transformation and promote perceived regional economic benefits in China.

title: Sensor-Based Monitoring and Control of Precision Seed Metering Systems in Digital Agriculture
abstract: Precision seed metering has evolved from mechanically optimized devices to sensor-based, digitally connected systems. However, research remains fragmented across metering mechanisms, sensing, data processing, communication, and control. This review examined monitoring and closed-loop control throughout the seed-delivery process, from pickup and release to tube passage, furrow placement, and crop emergence. This structured review synthesized 49 primary studies identified through Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection, with supplementary searching using Google Scholar and literature coverage through 1 September 2026. Optical and photoelectric sensors provide the most direct evidence for seed-passage detection, whereas encoders, pressure, vacuum, motor-current, and vibration measurements primarily indicate machine or actuator conditions. Machine vision provides spatial information and can support independent reference measurements, but requires suitable imaging conditions and computational resources. Capacitive, acoustic, impact-based, and hybrid approaches remain less extensively validated. Reported performance cannot be directly compared across studies due to differences in seed characteristics, mechanisms, operating speeds, event definitions, disturbances, and reference methods. Most studies demonstrate monitoring, alarms, or open-loop optimization rather than complete sensor-to-actuator correction. An engineering framework is therefore proposed to connect measurement targets, evidence maturity, latency, actuator authority, and independent verification. Future research should prioritize standardized testing, disturbance robustness, synchronized multi-row field validation, and measured end-to-end delay. Transparent reporting of correction accuracy, stability, cost, power demand, and interoperability is also required to support deployment and defensible assessment of closed-loop seeding systems.

title: Dynamic Prediction of Drought and Flood Catastrophes Under Climate Change: A Coupled GM(1,1)–Weibull–Bootstrap Model for Zhengzhou, China (1951–2024)
abstract: Drought and flood catastrophes threaten water security in the Yellow River Basin, yet prediction is hampered by sparse extreme event records. This study couples catastrophe series extraction via GM(1,1), Weibull extreme value modeling, and bootstrap uncertainty quantification, applying it to 74 years (1951–2024) of annual precipitation in Zhengzhou, China. Percentile thresholds of 410 mm (drought) and 864.6 mm (extreme precipitation) yield five drought and seven extreme precipitation catastrophe years. Both Weibull fits pass three goodness-of-fit tests, whereas the GM(1,1) benchmark fails for the flood series (mean error 21.5% vs. 3.31% for drought). The 0.9 quantile recurrence times (17.8 and 22.9 years) project the next drought catastrophe around 2031 (90% bootstrap window 2025–2033) and the next extreme precipitation catastrophe around 2044 (2034–2047); conditional residual life forecasts shift these by only 1–2 years (to 2033 and 2045, respectively). Two truncated record hindcasts (2013 drought; 2003 flood) fell within the predicted windows, and threshold perturbation and alternative distribution analyses support their robustness. Divergent shape parameters (k = 2.47 vs. 1.29) reveal accelerating drought but decelerating extreme precipitation hazard, providing probabilistic lead times for disaster risk management in data-scarce regions.

title: Scenario-Contextualized Short-Horizon Electricity Demand Forecasting for Istanbul: A Multi-Model Assessment for Emergency Power-System Planning
abstract: Major earthquakes can simultaneously interrupt routine electricity use and concentrate emergency-service requirements. This study reports a 22-method retrospective comparison of short-horizon hourly electricity-demand forecasting for Istanbul in a hypothetical Mw 7.5 disaster-information context. The Istanbul hourly electricity-demand series was obtained from EPİAŞ for the period 1 January 2020–1 January 2025 and is retained in the author-supplied workbook, which contains 43,968 records, including 96 repeated timestamps. The historical demand observations were used directly; no national-to-Istanbul scaling by 0.15 was applied. No earthquake-induced load reduction or critical-load increment is independently documented in the target. For the 24 h of 1 January 2025, the archival LSTM predictions yield MAE 79.89 MWh, RMSE 104.01 MWh, R2 approximately 0.97 and MAPE 1.65%. A separate information-removal experiment has a full-feature reference MAE of 666.2882 MWh; its RMSE–R2 relationship is compatible with an 8794 h historical holdout rather than the 24 h local comparison. Nine California/CAISO forecast series were reconciled on 24 common target observations; Random Forest had the lowest error (MAE 661.89 MWh; R2 0.7220), whereas the TensorFlow neural additive method was less accurate. An independently developed chronology-controlled demand-only study is also reported separately. The analyses quantify forecast errors, not observed earthquake effects, network adequacy, or validated operational restoration.

title: Wind Power Forecasting Architectures in Complex Terrain and Coastal Environments: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Comparative Performance
abstract: Wind forecasting in complex coastal terrain, such as the Colombian Caribbean, is hindered by air–sea heat fluxes and nonlinear atmospheric dynamics. This pre-registered systematic review and meta-analysis tests whether advanced architectures (artificial intelligence, hybrid, ensemble) outperform classical ones (physical, statistical). Scopus and Web of Science (last query: 22 September 2026) yielded 100 studies with extractable effect sizes; 76 compared a proposed model with an explicit comparator (primary analysis). Hedges’ g (negative values favor the proposed model) was pooled with REML random effects and Knapp–Hartung inference. The pooled effect was g=−1.07 (95% CI [−1.38,−0.75]; 95% prediction interval [−2.77,0.64]; I2=69.5%), robust to the estimator and to influential studies, although 59 comparisons were against a baseline of the same family. The estimates favored advanced over classical architectures, but not significantly (β=−0.30, 95% CI [−0.99,0.38]); only 10 studies compared them directly, and 9 favored the advanced model (g=−0.78, 95% CI [−1.93,0.36]). Only AI (g=−1.08, k=48) and physical (g=−0.93, k=19) models had intervals excluding zero. Egger and Begg tests indicated funnel-plot asymmetry, but the Pustejovsky–Rodgers test, robust to the dependence of the standard error on the effect, did not. Proposed models outperform their baselines; the superiority of any architectural class is not established.

title: Geophysical Surveys of Southern Pacific Northwest Coast Plankhouses
abstract: Geophysical and remote sensing surveys of Pacific Northwest Coast plankhouses, sweathouses, and other architectural features have been a growing component of Pacific Northwest Coast archaeological studies. Most of these studies have focused on coastal plankhouses with associated shell middens, especially in British Columbia. Limited geophysical examples exist of Pacific Northwest Coast architectural features from the southern region, including northern California and Oregon, especially in riverine settings. In this study, we integrate ground-penetrating radar and magnetic gradiometry to document subsurface features in collaboration with the Tsnungwe Council. Our findings, based on our interpretations of the observed data but not ground-truthed at this time, document subsurface features ranging from ~2 m wide pits to large rectangular plankhouses ~6 m wide and 12 m long. These houses include central subterranean pits, which contain a hearth, that are ~5 m wide. Our findings support the interpretation of a large multicomponent village site with several plankhouses present, providing a unique example of southern Pacific Northwest Coast Indigenous architecture. Future ground-truthing efforts may confirm and/or revise these interpretations.

title: An Interpretable and Transferable Allometric Model for Remote Sensing-Based Estimation of Forest Aboveground Biomass
abstract: Remote sensing provides an effective means of estimating forest aboveground biomass (AGB) over large areas. However, empirical models calibrated in a specific region may lose predictive accuracy when transferred elsewhere because predictor–AGB relationships can vary with forest structure and environmental conditions. In addition, the complex nonlinear relationships learned by many machine learning models are not explicitly linked to ecological processes, limiting their ecological interpretability. To address these challenges, we developed a height-based allometric framework that incorporates the kernel normalized difference vegetation index (kNDVI) derived from Sentinel-2 imagery and leaf area index (LAI) indirectly estimated from UAV-LiDAR point clouds into the scaling relationship between mean stand height and AGB. By allowing the scaling exponent to vary with canopy spectral and structural conditions, the proposed framework was designed to account for spatial variation in the height–biomass relationship while retaining an explicit allometric structure. Its performance was compared with four commonly used machine learning methods: k-nearest neighbors (kNN), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and Bayesian Regularized Neural Network (BRNN). Within the calibration region, the proposed allometric model achieved an R2 of 0.67, an RMSE of 17.74 Mg ha−1, and an rRMSE of 15.17%, closely approaching the performance of RF, which was the most accurate machine learning model (R2 = 0.69, RMSE = 17.20 Mg ha−1, and rRMSE = 14.71%). More pronounced differences emerged when the models were evaluated using independent samples located outside the calibration area. Under this spatial transfer test, the allometric model retained an R2 of 0.48, with an RMSE of 22.31 Mg ha−1 and an rRMSE of 20.83%. In comparison, BRNN was the best-performing machine learning method in the same external validation but achieved an R2 of 0.32, an RMSE of 25.44 Mg ha−1, and an rRMSE of 23.75%. Introducing either LAI or kNDVI into the scaling exponent provided greater explanatory value than using a fixed exponent, while the kNDVI-based formulation (R2 = 0.41, RMSE = 23.60 Mg ha−1, and rRMSE = 22.03%) exhibited stronger spatial transferability than its LAI-based counterpart (R2 = 0.37, RMSE = 24.42 Mg ha−1, and rRMSE = 22.80%). Although all evaluated models experienced accuracy losses outside the calibration region, the reduction was substantially greater for the machine learning approaches. The proposed framework therefore provides predictive accuracy comparable to that of machine learning models within the calibration area while offering greater ecological interpretability and stronger performance under spatial transfer. This approach provides a basis for large-area forest AGB estimation by integrating optical observations with canopy structure information and could potentially be extended to applications combining optical imagery with structural information derived from satellite LiDAR. Future research could incorporate spatial autocorrelation and spatial heterogeneity into the proposed framework to further reduce uncertainty in forest AGB estimation.

title: Two-Level Spectral Adaptation and Multilevel Spectral Evidence Diagnostics for Hyperspectral Remote Sensing Salient Object Detection with a Wavelength-Conditioned Foundation Model
abstract: Wavelength-conditioned remote sensing foundation models accept flexible spectral configurations, but compatibility does not ensure effective spectral utilization. We investigate this issue for hyperspectral remote sensing salient object detection and propose SpecAudit, an offline framework diagnosing input discriminability, entry-kernel geometry, and layer-wise spectral readability, together with Two-Level Spectral Adaptation (TLSA). On the 32-band hyperspectral remote sensing salient object detection dataset (HRSSD), expanding a Dynamic One-For-All (DOFA)-based pipeline from 3 to 32 bands yields no stable saliency gain. A ground-truth-assisted image-specific diagnostic readout, fitted and evaluated on spatially separated regions of each test image, yields ΔSα=+0.0418, indicating substantial image-specific spectral discriminability despite the absence of a stable direct prediction gain. TLSA combines task-shared Band Amplitude Calibration, using one learnable gain per band before the frozen entry, with Self-Guided Spectral Refinement, which fits an image-specific spectral discriminant from the coarse prediction at inference. Across five training seeds and paired image-level tests, both adaptation levels provide positive incremental improvements. TLSA increases mean Sα from 0.6472 to 0.6613, yields a positive paired improvement over the three-band reference, and exceeds the highest mean Sα among nine retrained published methods by 3.5%. These results indicate that hyperspectral gains depend on how spectral evidence is exposed and used, not only on available band count. The complete TLSA implementation and SpecAudit diagnostic code will be publicly released upon publication.

title: A Decision-Support Model for Sustainable Management of Raw Material Flows in Hard Coal Preparation Plants
abstract: This paper presents an integrated decision-support model for the sustainable management of raw material flows in hard coal preparation plants, aimed at optimizing technological processes and supporting circular economy principles. Developed within the DynGOSP project, the framework combines a stationary process model with an automated UAV–GIS workflow for stockpile inventory. The computational component, designated as the “Forecast” module, incorporates empirical classification and partition-curve models to evaluate separation performance, product recovery, and quality under varying feed characteristics. The predictive accuracy of the beneficiation module was verified using laboratory and industrial reference data, yielding absolute relative errors ranging from 0.89% to 7.51% for concentrate yield and 0.73% to 3.37% for concentrate ash content. To extend the management concept beyond plant operations, the system integrates photogrammetry, QGIS spatial data processing, and GRASS GIS tools to generate Digital Surface Models (DSMs) for continuous volumetric monitoring of external coal stockpiles and waste dumps. The proposed solution constitutes a comprehensive Industry 4.0 framework that bridges process evaluation with spatial inventory, providing a scalable tool for resource efficiency, waste reduction, and supply chain optimization in the mining sector.

title: Dynamic Electric-Vehicle Adoption in India: A Genuinely Coupled Bass–Agent-Based Simulation Framework with Dynamic PESTL Integration
abstract: Electric-vehicle (EV) diffusion in large, heterogeneous, and price-sensitive markets such as India cannot be adequately represented by either aggregate diffusion curves or agent-based models (ABMs) in isolation: the former cannot express heterogeneous buyers or shifting policy, and the latter are rarely anchored to a calibrated national diffusion trajectory. This paper develops a dynamic mathematical model of EV adoption among Indian passenger-car buyers that couples a Bass diffusion model at the macro level with an ABM of heterogeneous consumers at the micro level, with both layers driven by a time-varying PESTL (political, economic, social, technological, legal/environmental) representation of the market environment. Unlike earlier hybrid proposals in which the two layers are described together but solved independently, this framework implements a genuine two-way coupling: in every simulated year, 5000 agents positioned on a small-world social network make discrete vehicle-choice decisions based on deterministic utility; the resulting peer-adoption share and the normalised PESTL drivers jointly determine the time-varying innovation coefficient p(t) and imitation coefficient q(t); a bounded Bass equation with a time-varying saturation ceiling then advances the national EV share of new-car sales; and that macro share re-enters the agents’ social-influence term in the following period, closing the loop. The model is anchored on current Indian parameters—a passenger-car EV penetration of approximately 4% in 2025, volumetric battery-pack cost near US$108/kWh, and around 29,000 public charging points—and run under baseline, aggressive-support, and stalled-support scenarios to 2050, together with a 3 × 3 scenario matrix cross-combining three PESTL environments with three agent-population profiles. For the illustrative calibration, the baseline scenario yields approximately 29.5% EV sales share by 2030—narrowly below the Government of India’s 30% target for passenger cars—and approximately 30.4% under the aggressive-support scenario. A formal two-way ANOVA-based variance decomposition, with 10 independent random-seed replications per scenario cell (90 observations in total), indicates that heterogeneous agent characteristics account for 81.3% of the variance in 2030 outcomes, substantially exceeding the 16.8% attributable to the PESTL policy environment, with the remaining 1.9% reflecting interaction and stochastic noise. One-at-a-time sensitivity analysis identifies the peer-influence weight as the parameter with the largest overall effect on 2030 penetration, with the purchase-subsidy multiplier remaining the most effective lever among instruments directly controllable by policy. The emergent Bass coefficients fall within established meta-analytical ranges, providing internal plausibility validation. The framework is offered as a transparent decision-support and scenario-analysis tool for policymakers and industry planners, not as a point forecast of future EV sales.

title: Digital Literacy, Institutional Support, and Agricultural Mechanization Adoption: Pathways to Sustainable Rice Farming in Indonesia
abstract: Sustainable rice production in Indonesia requires digital skills, machinery, and institutional services. Serdang Bedagai, North Sumatra, provides a major rice-producing setting with land development programs and varied machinery service arrangements. A cross-sectional survey of 340 farmers in seven subdistricts was analyzed using ordinary partial least squares structural equation modeling with 5000 bootstrap resamples. Agricultural mechanization adoption (AMA) and self-reported sustainable rice farming practices (SRF) were composites. Digital literacy (DL) was associated with AMA (β = 0.374, p < 0.001); DL, institutional support (IS), and AMA were associated with SRF (β = 0.234, 0.243, and 0.149). The IS–AMA association was non-significant (β = 0.056, p = 0.386). Removing two digital SRF indicators retained the DL–SRF association (β = 0.240, 95% CI (0.107, 0.377)) and DL → AMA → SRF indirect association (β = 0.063, 95% CI (0.024, 0.113)). The indirect association was non-significant with routine stage count and trial or routine count AMA measures. An exploratory membership comparison for Usaha Pelayanan Jasa Alat dan Mesin Pertanian (UPJA) found a stronger IS–SRF association among members (difference = 0.408, permutation p = 0.006); AMA non-invariance limits interpretation. Digital literacy development, machinery services, and institutional coordination merit integrated attention. Longitudinal evidence and objective measurements are needed to establish sustainability gains.

title: Automated Multi-Class Classification of Plant Seedling Species Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Timely and accurate identification of plant seedlings is important for precision agriculture, particularly for early crop monitoring and weed management. Manual seedling identification is often time-consuming, subjective, and prone to error, especially when plant species exhibit similar visual characteristics at early growth stages. This study presents an application-oriented deep learning framework based on a compact four-layer custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for multi-class classification of plant seedling images. The publicly available Kaggle Plant Seedlings Classification dataset, consisting of 12 seedling species, was used for model development and evaluation. To improve model generalization and reduce overfitting, systematic image preprocessing and data augmentation techniques were applied during training. The proposed CNN achieved an overall classification accuracy of 90%, a validation loss of 0.3837, and a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.89. The use of data augmentation improved validation accuracy from 78% to 90%, demonstrating its positive effect on classification performance. Class-wise evaluation using precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrix analysis showed strong performance for visually distinctive species such as Charlock, Common Chickweed, and Sugar Beet, while most misclassifications occurred among morphologically similar classes. The main contribution of this study lies in developing and empirically evaluating a simple, reproducible, and computationally efficient CNN-based pipeline for plant seedling classification. The results indicate that a compact CNN combined with appropriate preprocessing and augmentation can provide practical performance for automated plant monitoring applications, while also highlighting the need for more advanced feature extraction methods to improve classification of visually similar species.

title: Random Forest–Based Integrated Crop Recommendation and NPK-Driven Fertilizer Decision Support System for Precision Agriculture
abstract: Precision agriculture calls for data-driven methods to determine the optimal choice of crops and fertilizers depending on soil conditions and climate. In this paper, an integrated decision support system is presented, which is based on Random Forest crop classification and NPK-based fertilizer recommendation system. The proposed system works with seven agronomic features, including nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, temperature, humidity, soil pH, and rainfall, from crop recommendation dataset with 2,200 entries and 22 classes of crops. After processing data and separating them into training set (80%) and testing set (20%), a Random Forest classifier with 100 decision trees was built to classify the crops. The classified crop is matched with the nutrient knowledge base, and the current soil NPK content is compared to the nutrient needs of the crop. Finally, the rules-based decision engine finds out nutrient deficiencies and makes fertilizer recommendations. The performance of the classifier on the test dataset was 97.6% accuracy, 97.1% precision, 96.8% recall, and 96.9% F1-score.

title: Técnicas de visión artificial aplicadas a tecnologías asistivas para personas con discapacidad visual: una revisión sistemática de la literatura
abstract: Visual impairment constitutes one of the primary barriers to social inclusion, affecting over 285 million individuals experiencing low vision or blindness, while assistive devices are frequently costly or lack accessibility. Consequently, the present study conducted a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) with the main objective of identifying the most efficient artificial intelligence models in the domain of text, color, and object recognition—specifically concerning items such as fruits, banknotes, and facial expressions. This research encompasses articles published between 2020 and 2026, exploring prominent indexed scientific databases including Redalyc, the ACM Digital Library, Consensus, IEEE Xplore, Springer Nature Link, and Google Scholar. Throughout the search process, 46 articles were identified and analyzed, revealing that architectures based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and deep learning models are the most effective for processing visual information through images or real-time video without demanding substantial computational resources.

title: Analisis Perencanaan dan Pengendalian Persediaan Material Filter Menggunakan Metode Forecasting di PT ABC
abstract: Effective inventory management is a crucial aspect in ensuring the continuity of production processes and fulfilling customer demand optimally, especially in a dynamic and fluctuating market environment. PT ABC, as a manufacturing company producing filter components, faces challenges related to demand fluctuations and additional Purchase Orders (PO) from customers, which impact material availability. This study aims to analyze the planning and control of filter inventory by applying forecasting methods, specifically Moving Average and Linear Regression methods. Historical demand data were used to forecast the requirements for filters with diameters Ø50 mm and Ø72 mm. The results indicate that Linear Regression produces lower forecasting errors compared to Moving Average for both filter sizes. For the Ø50 mm filter, Linear Regression yields an MSE of 3,524,583.3, MAD of 1,576, and MAPE of 0.4121, all of which are lower than the values produced by the Moving Average method. A similar pattern is observed for the Ø72 mm filter, where Linear Regression results in an MSE of 1,182,480.374, MAD of 817, and MAPE of 0.2667, which are also lower than those generated by Moving Average. Therefore, this study concludes that Linear Regression is the recommended forecasting method for planning filter requirements at PT ABC. Keywords: Filter, Forecasting, Linier Regression, Material, Moving Average

title: Association of Pre-Chemotherapy Serum Alkaline Phosphatase Levels and p53 Protein Expression with Huvos Tumor Necrosis Grading in High-Grade Osteosarcoma: An Indonesian Tertiary Referral Center Experience
abstract: Background: High-grade osteosarcoma shows unpredictable chemosensitivity. Whether pre-chemotherapy serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and immunohistochemical p53 expression forecast post-neoadjuvant histopathological tumor necrosis remains contested in resource-constrained settings. Methods: In a hospital-based nested cohort, 14 consecutive patients with primary high-grade extremity osteosarcoma (Palembang, 2023–2025) received three cycles of standardized neoadjuvant chemotherapy before wide resection. Pre-chemotherapy serum ALP and immunohistochemical nuclear p53 were related to Huvos response, dichotomized as poor ( 104 U/L) occurred in 92.9%, and p53 immunoreactivity was positive in 78.6%. Baseline serum ALP was not significantly associated with Huvos response (76.9% poor in elevated vs. 100.0% in normal; Fisher’s exact p = 1.000; RR = 0.769, 95% CI: 0.571–1.036), nor was p53 (81.8% poor in p53-positive vs. 66.7% in p53-negative; p = 1.000; OR = 2.250, 95% CI: 0.130–38.811; RR = 1.227, 95% CI: 0.526–2.864). ROC analysis for serum ALP yielded an AUC of 0.515 (95% CI: 0.205–0.825, p = 0.938), equivalent to random classification. An empirical cutoff of 176.5 U/L showed 100.0% specificity but only 36.4% sensitivity. Conclusion: Pre-chemotherapy serum ALP and immunohistochemical p53 expression fail to predict post-neoadjuvant histopathological tumor necrosis in osteosarcoma, and cannot substitute for microscopic Huvos grading in guiding adjuvant treatment.
journal: Bioscientia Medicina : Journal of Biomedicine and Translational Research

title: A detailed anatomical characterisation of 17 Satureja species (Lamiaceae) from Türkiye
abstract: Satureja species, commonly known as savory herbs, are a diverse group of plants belonging to the family Lamiaceae and are widely distributed throughout Türkiye. These aromatic herbs play an important role in both culinary and medicinal practices, contributing to local traditions and customs. Understanding their anatomy is essential for identifying species variations, ecological adaptations, and potential uses in agriculture and pharmacology. This study provides comprehensive details of the anatomical characteristics of different Satureja species found in Türkiye. The anatomical characteristics of 17 Satureja species, including their leaf structure, stem, and roots, provided important insights into their identification and classification. For the taxa studied, the root and stem cross-sectional structure, such as the vascular bundles, collenchyma type, and presence and density of the sclerenchyma, was important. In particular, the leaf, trichome type density, and mesophyll characteristics also provided more reliable tools for identifying the taxa. Understanding these anatomical characteristics will not only aid in the classification of Satureja species but also enhance our knowledge of their ecological roles and their potential applications in improving crop resilience and medicinal applications.

title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning
abstract: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.

title: Sociotechnical Imaginaries of Inclusion in Digital Agri-extension Services in the Philippines
abstract: This research aims to assess the Philippine policy and institutional landscape for digital agriextension services and the underlying mechanisms that support or constrain the digital inclusion of Filipino smallholder farmers. Using a two-phase documentary and policy analysis of academic literature, government policies, institutional reports, and related sources, the study examines both the institutional foundations and broader state narratives underpinning agricultural digitalization in the Philippines. Grounded in this political-institutional landscape, the study then articulates state-led imaginaries of inclusive agricultural digitalization using Jasanoff and Kim’s (2009) notion of sociotechnical imaginaries(STI). The assessment presents a mixed picture of agricultural digitalization: multisectoral representation in governance supports a whole-of-society approach to service delivery, while existing policies—despite their fragmentation and limitations—demonstrate continuing policy attention to digital inclusion. Similarly, the decision-making by the Philippine state and its stated program priorities have linked imaginaries of inclusive digital agriculture to notions of economic development, modernization, and globalization. Efforts to provide equal access to agricultural innovation, however, remain uneven and constrained by persistent institutional and structural barriers. The study thus calls for the institutionalization of a national policy ondigital agriculture.
journal: Asian Journal of Agriculture and Development

title: An Inverted Organoid-Derived Intestinal Epithelial Monolayer Model for Studying Immune Cell-Epithelial Interactions.
abstract: Human intestinal organoids provide a powerful model system to study epithelial biology by preserving key characteristics of intestinal tissue organization, cellular differentiation, and function. However, their three-dimensional architecture limits direct experimental access to the apical surface, which is enclosed within the organoid lumen. This restricted accessibility complicates studies requiring controlled stimulation of epithelial compartments, barrier analysis, and investigation of interactions between epithelial and immune cells. This protocol describes the generation of an inverted organoid-derived intestinal epithelial model designed to improve accessibility to both the apical and basal compartments while maintaining essential epithelial properties. In this approach, organoid-derived single cells are seeded onto an inverted permeable support, where they establish a polarized epithelial monolayer that retains important features of intestinal differentiation and organization. The open configuration enables direct use of epithelial compartments and facilitates functional applications, including compartment-specific stimulation and immune-epithelial interaction studies. Furthermore, the model allows the integration of immune cell co-culture approaches to investigate cellular communication and migration processes. This platform provides a practical and adaptable experimental system that bridges conventional three-dimensional organoid cultures and accessible epithelial monolayer models. It offers a valuable approach for studying intestinal barrier function, inflammatory responses, immune interactions, and disease-associated mechanisms under controlled experimental conditions.

title: Foundation Models in Gastroenterology: Emerging Applications and Future Directions
abstract: Foundation models are being investigated in gastroenterology because the specialty already generates multimodal data, including endoscopy videos, pathology slides, abdominal images, laboratory results, molecular profiles, and longitudinal clinical notes. This review examines where these models may be useful in emerging applications, where evidence remains limited, and what is required before wider clinical deployment. Large language models (LLMs) can support document organization, report generation, guideline retrieval, and patient communication, but fluent output can conceal errors. Endoscopic models are beginning to move beyond single-task polyp detection towards reusable visual pretraining across gastrointestinal sites and procedures. Pathology and radiology foundation models may assist with biomarker prediction, image segmentation, and tumor detection, although performance remains sensitive to staining, scanners, acquisition protocols, and case mix. The immediate goal is not to build a single model that covers the entire specialty. Rather, gastroenterology needs systems that are locally validated, auditable, privacy-aware, uncertainty-calibrated, and sufficiently focused to remain within clinical responsibility.

title: Road Blockage Estimation Using Remote Sensing Terrain Data from Disaster Areas
journal: Journal of the Japan society of photogrammetry and remote sensing

title: Comparative Analysis and Adaptation Strategies of Vision Foundation Models in Dermoscopic Image Segmentation
abstract: Accurate segmentation of skin lesions is of critical clinical importance for early melanoma diagnosis; however, the direct application of large foundation models like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to medical images characterized by low contrast and fuzzy boundaries remains insufficient due to substantial domain gaps. In current study, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy is presented by integrating lightweight adapter modules into a frozen Vision Transformer backbone. The proposed SAM-Adapter approach was comparatively evaluated against the original SAM and MedSAM models on the publicly available ISIC2018 and HAM10000 dermoscopic datasets. Optimized with AdamW, the model achieved the highest Dice (0.9603) and IoU (0.9241) scores along with the lowest HD95 (22.57) value on the HAM10000 dataset. Validated as statistically significant via the Wilcoxon test, this approach minimized computational overhead while demonstrating superior accuracy in boundary delineation. This adapter-based framework is planned for integration into clinical decision-support systems and other medical imaging modalities.
