title: 3Dtrees.earth: community research infrastructure for tree and forest analysis using close-range LiDAR data
abstract: From individual trees to forest stands, three-dimensional structure shapes carbon, water, and energy flows, habitat conditions, and resource availability. Yet tree and forest structural attributes remain difficult to assess consistently across space and time. Close-range LiDAR (light detection and ranging) records detailed 3D structure from branches and trees to forest plots, including trees outside forests. However, broader reuse is constrained when data, acquisition context, processing, computation, and access conditions are maintained separately. We present 3Dtrees.earth, an operational community research infrastructure that brings close-range LiDAR datasets, analysis tools, and computing resources together while linking original observations to their metadata and processing outputs. As of 23 October 2026, the platform comprised 2,760 datasets, including 2,481 publicly visible datasets. These point cloud datasets span 46 countries on all six inhabited continents and include terrestrial, mobile, and uncrewed aerial laser scanning. Users can contribute and discover datasets, run standardized processing workflows on shared computing infrastructure, inspect point clouds and model predictions in the browser, and access data and processing outputs together with citation information. Workflows combine rule-based and machine-learning methods, with tools updated as methods advance. Outputs include raster products, individual-tree and semantic segmentation, and tree- and stand-level metrics. Original point clouds and processing records are retained, enabling reprocessing with improved tools while preserving provenance. With broader coverage, curation, and validation, this shared resource could extend individual surveys into a basis for model evaluation and benchmarking, cross-site synthesis, calibration and validation of larger-scale Earth observation products, and macroecological analysis.

authors.name: Domingos Fortunato P. F. da Silva
Wouter A. J. Van den Broeck

title: Responsible Quantum Machine Learning for Medical Imaging: A Fairness Audit Across Sensitive Subgroups
abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) is increasingly explored for medical classification, yet its behaviour under subgroup-aware fairness criteria remains understudied. We present an empirical fairness audit of classical and quantum classifiers for medical imaging, assuming QML is not inherently fair. Two scenarios are evaluated: dermatological lesions on DDI (sensitive attribute: Fitzpatrick skin type) and chest X-rays on CheXpert-derived data (sensitive attribute: age group). Using ResNet-18 embeddings, we train SVM, MLP, QSVM and QCNN under a baseline and three mitigation settings: differentiable Equalized Odds (EO) regularisation, Gradient Reversal Learning (GRL), and both combined. Foundation models (PanDerm, EVA-X) serve as external references. Quantum classifiers may achieve competitive aggregate performance while still exhibiting subgroup disparities. Since a smaller subgroup AUC gap may stem from degrading the best group rather than improving the worst, each mitigation is also tested against a pre-specified non-inferiority margin relative to its baseline. Under this criterion, several configurations with the smallest disparity, notably QCNN with GRL on DDI, are not clinically acceptable due to loss of global discrimination. On DDI, QSVM with GRL+EO performed best and approached PanDerm in the performance/fairness trade-off; on CheXpert, QCNN with GRL achieved the highest aggregate performance but increased disparity, and EVA-X remained stronger. Fairness effects are model- and dataset-dependent, so QML requires empirical subgroup-aware evaluation. All quantum models run in classical simulation; we claim no quantum advantage.

title: Learning Lotteries with Minimal Stakeholder Violations from Membership Queries
abstract: An AI developer often has several candidate versions of a system and can deploy a mixture of them, sending each request to a randomly chosen version, as in A/B testing. Each stakeholder (e.g., a safety team, a regulator, or a customer with private test data) accepts a mixture exactly when its expected performance (e.g., its rate of harmful replies) meets the stakeholder's own standard, which the developer can learn only by asking whether a proposed mixture is acceptable. We model this as choosing a lottery over $m$ alternatives for $n$ agents, each of whom accepts exactly the lotteries in an unknown halfspace and answers such binary membership queries. While Choo et al. (ICML 2026) sought a lottery that every agent accepts, none may exist when, say, safety and helpfulness requirements conflict, so we minimize the number of rejecting agents. We show that this problem is APX-hard even when all halfspaces are known and all utilities are $0$ or $1$. We then give exact algorithms that run in polynomial time when $m$ is constant, and in quasi-polynomial time when, for a constant $\eta$, some optimal lottery has no accepting agent within $\eta$ of its threshold. When only some agents can be queried, optimizing over a uniform sample of agents gives additive and relative guarantees for the whole population, with a sample size that does not depend on $n$, and a linear program gives a polynomial-time method for any $m$. On the other hand, for $m\ge 3$, a deterministic algorithm that queries only $K$ distinct agents cannot guarantee fewer than $n-K$ extra rejections, and this is achievable; in other words, it can guarantee nothing for the agents it does not ask. Small synthetic experiments indicate that our worst-case bounds are conservative on random instances.

title: Measuring Where Intent Gets Lost in Agentic Smart Contract Synthesis
abstract: AI agents can now write software from a plain-English description, but code that runs is not the same as code that does what was asked. This gap matters most for smart contracts, the programs behind Web3 applications that move money on a blockchain and cannot be fixed once deployed. We ask how to check whether an AI-written contract behaves as it should, and where the requested behavior gets lost. We design an evaluation built on execution rather than opinion. We replay the same transactions on an AI-written contract and on the original it should reproduce and measure how often they agree. We test every grading tool on planted mistakes, compare against an answer key written without the description, and audit our own scorer until known wrong answers cannot pass. Common methods, such as AI judges and standard analysis tools, miss obvious mistakes, and scoring choices matter too. Checking only the functions every system includes hid about half the difference between pipelines. We then propose an elicitation-first architecture. Before writing code, the agent asks the client a short checklist of questions, checks the contract against an independently written executable answer key, and returns disagreements to the client instead of silently rewriting code. Asking first matters far more than reviewing or patching afterwards, across three AI models, while automated security fixes often break requested behavior. A few well-chosen questions recover much of what a short description omits, and their value can be estimated without the original contract. To our knowledge, this is the first study in smart contract synthesis to gather missing requirements before generation and check the result against an independently written executable model. The lessons extend to any setting where AI agents turn requests into programs. We release our tools, 600 tasks and all results.

title: Model Criticism via Stochastic Optimization
abstract: Many generative models are specified by how data are simulated. An observation is a deterministic transform $Y=G(θ,X)$ of a draw $X$ from an assumed noise law, indexed by a structural parameter $θ$. Such models cover discrete, continuous and functional data, as well as i.i.d. replicates of stochastic processes, but their likelihoods are often unavailable. We propose a simulation-based procedure that tests whether such a model fits the data and, when it does not, locates where it fails, without choosing a test statistic. The procedure splits the data in two and is formulated as a two-stage stochastic program. In the estimation stage, $θ$ is fitted on the first block by minimizing a Wasserstein distance between the data and simulations from the model. In the recourse stage, $θ$ is frozen at the fitted $\tildeθ$, and a finite set of representative noise values $\{\bar x_j\}$ is pushed through the fitted mechanism to give model atoms $G(\tildeθ,\bar x_j)$. The held-out block optimizes weights $\textbf{w}$ on the model atoms to best match its own distribution. The optimized weights are then compared with theoretical weights under correct specification. Since each model atom is the image of known noise values, the disagreement between optimal and theoretical weights points to the part of the noise law that is wrong. The split makes the scaled weights conditionally multinomial, yielding a calibrated Pearson test. We prove strong consistency of both stages under checkable assumptions and illustrate the procedure on a Gaussian location--scale family, the number of segregating sites under Kingman's coalescent, a Yule process, and an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck diffusion.

title: Detecting Covert Collusion between AI Agents through Partner-Outsider Positive Listening
abstract: AI agents that share a secret convention can coordinate through messages that look innocent, so a monitor that reads only the messages can miss them. We propose a behavioural test: a partner that uses a code reacts to the exact wording of a message, whereas an uninvolved agent placed in its seat does not. Partner--Outsider Positive Listening (PoPLi) is the difference between the two agents in how much their action changes when the message is reworded with its meaning kept, and it is computed after the fact by replaying logged prompts. In a simulated market with five conditions (no collusion, a joint reward with neutral messages, the same with an openly stated intention, a covert first-letter code, and the code with a stated intention), PoPLi is between 0.48 and 0.59 whenever the code is present (95% intervals all above 0.29) and between -0.10 and -0.01 without it. Message-only monitors did not separate the conditions: one reading the speaker's messages answered "no" in all 50 markets, and one reading every seller's messages flagged 9 of 10 markets with no collusion. PoPLi detects the use of a private channel, not collusion as such, and it cannot detect collusion through incentives alone or codes carried by meaning.

title: Evaluating and improving AI agents for sequencing protocol understanding
abstract: Existing scientific-agent benchmarks rarely evaluate whether agents can reconstruct the exact molecular structures and generation workflows specified by sequencing protocols, a capability critical for analyzing customized sequencing assays. We introduce LibStructBench, a document-grounded benchmark for reconstructing sequencing-library structures and molecular workflows. Our experiments show that frontier agents often produce approximately correct reconstructions but remain unreliable at exact reconstruction, particularly in molecular-state representation and workflow connectivity. Switching the underlying language model produced larger average performance differences than switching agent harnesses, with a statistically significant difference only for molecular-state reconstruction. Additional knowledge improved oligo-family recovery in a small pilot without improving mean molecular-workflow scores. Autonomous accumulation of procedural rules and cross-protocol examples showed non-monotonic validation performance and no mean held-out molecular-workflow improvement in the tested trajectory. These findings highlight the need for more controlled and verifiable approaches to scientific reasoning about molecular processes in complex experimental protocols.

title: Advisor, Co-pilot, or Guardian? AI Role Framing and Human Decision Behavior in Automated Vehicle Takeovers
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technology has gradually been integrated into automated vehicles. However, how this technology could systematically support takeover transitions in SAE Level 3 automated vehicles remains unknown, even though this level may remain a major form of driving automation in the near future. To address this, we implemented the three AI roles proposed by the triadic Human-AI collaboration framework (Advisor, Co-pilot, and Guardian) as potential authority-ability configurations for AI agents within an automated system. We then examined their interactions with explanation type (why and action) and directional semantics (ipsilateral and contralateral) in an automated driving simulator study with 24 participants. Results showed that, across the three AI roles, Advisor had the shortest decision-making time, followed by Guardian and Co-pilot. Advisor and Guardian were associated with higher decision-making accuracy and higher satisfaction ratings than Co-pilot. Guardian was associated with the lowest workload, followed by Advisor and Co-pilot. The effect of explanation type on decision-making time depended on AI role. Action explanations were faster under Advisor, whereas why explanations were faster under Co-pilot. For directional semantics, ipsilateral semantics were associated with shorter decision-making time than contralateral semantics. Overall, these findings provide preliminary guidance for designing AI-role authority-ability configurations and their associated speech-based takeover messages.

title: The MARTINI platform II. Tracing r-process nucleosynthesis in neutron star mergers with long-lived remnants
abstract: Binary neutron star (BNS) mergers are among the primary sites of the rapid neutron-capture (r-)process. In mergers with long-lived remnants, sustained neutrino irradiation raises the electron fraction of the disc wind ejecta, modifying the resulting nucleosynthesis pattern. Yields from numerical-relativity simulations with accurate neutrino transport are needed to quantify the contribution of BNS mergers to the Galactic production of heavy elements and to interpret kilonova spectra. We present and publicly release tracer trajectories and nucleosynthesis yields for eight BNS mergers forming long-lived neutron star remnants, obtained from general-relativistic simulations with M1 neutrino transport, spanning two equations of state (DD2 and SFHo), and a range of total masses and mass ratios. Passive tracer particles following the dynamical and wind ejecta were post-processed with the nuclear reaction network WinNet up to 1 Gyr. The yields and tracer trajectories are available on the MARTINI platform. At 1 day, the production of light and first-peak elements (He, Ni, Sr, and Y) is similar across models and is primarily enhanced by the neutrino-irradiated disc wind. The yields of heavy nuclei vary by more than one order of magnitude, with unequal-mass binaries producing the largest amounts owing to their more neutron-rich ejecta. Our He yields, particularly in the wind, exceed those of recent studies based on an M0 neutrino scheme, consistent with the stronger neutrino irradiation resulting from an M1 scheme. At 1 Gyr, all models reproduce the second and third solar r-process peaks, but differ in the first peak, the lanthanide region, the mass range between the first and second peaks, and the trans-lead region, reflecting the electron fraction distribution of the ejecta and the dynamical and wind contributions. Two equal-mass models provide a close match to the solar pattern.

title: What Is the Role for Humans in Creative Writing? Creativity and Diversity in Human-AI Collaboration
abstract: As AI agents increasingly participate in creative teamwork, writing emerges from hybrid human-AI teams. Although AI can improve the creativity of individual outputs, these gains may come at the cost of homogenization. What is the best role for human intervention? We introduce a transmission-chain paradigm inspired by cognitive models of writing, with four stages: Plan, Write, Review, and Revise. Each stage receives the previous output and passes its own forward. Using data from 333 participants across 427 stories, we compared creativity, diversity, and enjoyment across human, AI, and hybrid chains. Consistent with prior work, all-AI chains produced more creative but less diverse stories than all-human chains. Introducing a single human into an otherwise all-AI chain increased diversity depending on role. Human planning provided the best balance: it preserved AI-level creativity, increased diversity that persisted through downstream AI stages, and maintained enjoyment. We discuss implications for designing human-in-the-loop creative pipelines.

title: VerifiedLab: Harnessing Knowns for Unknowns
abstract: Across human history, knowledge has undergone several transitions, from orality to writing and then to digital archives. At each transition, humans established new conventions to preserve knowledge for the new era. Nowadays, as research agents are increasingly deployed for laboratory experiments, knowledge is crossing another boundary: from records written for humans to those for machines. In this work, we introduce VerifiedLab, a multi-agent harness framework for this human-to-machine transition of knowledge. VerifiedLab transforms research output from passive artifacts into active systems that accelerate downstream use, adoption and prediction of future trends. In VerifiedLab, a team of AI scientists with distinct roles reasons over records verified field by field: a principal investigator plans, a librarian computes the evidence directly from the records, specialists draft, and a gate and a critic check each claim against the measured reliability of its data before the harness decides whether to release or withhold it. We demonstrate the efficacy of VerifiedLab through extensive experiments on perovskite solar cells: VerifiedLab recovers known physical trends, anticipates devices reported a year later, and lets AI scientists inherit the literature together with a measure of how far it can be trusted. By scaling the inference-time verification compute, VerifiedLab introduces a new pathway for knowledge dissemination and machine harness for AI co-scientists.

title: Doppler-Shannon Association in Vehicular Networks: A Stochastic Geometry Analysis
abstract: Historically, in cellular networks, the user equipment (UE) association with a base station (BS) has been largely confined to nearest BS association strategies. Unlike cellular networks wherein the BSs are static, vehicular networks are prone to high mobility, resulting in the UE experiencing a Doppler shift. The Doppler shift further results in the fading channel exhibiting high temporal variability. In this work, we present a novel stochastic geometry framework, modeling the effects of the Doppler shift on the physical layer network performance through the coherence time. First, the statistics of the Doppler shift are studied in a two- and three-dimensional Poisson point process (PPP) setting. The distribution and the geometric factors influencing the Doppler shift are analyzed. Next, we propose Doppler shift aware utilities, modeling the Doppler shift induced Shannon rate achievable in time-selective fading links. Through these utilities, we analytically study the outage and coverage probabilities for a UE to achieve a given quality of service. These probabilities are computed based on the optimal BS association in vehicular networks, which goes beyond the closest Euclidean distance. In the UE-BS line of sight, the novel BS association policies factor the BS direction of motion and the fading gain, in addition to the Euclidean distance. We show that the nearest BS is no longer the optimal BS association, resulting in non-convex coverage tessellations associated with the BSs. Our analytical and simulation results illustrate the need for a Doppler shift correction, complementing the ideal SNR based Shannon performance. The network performance achieved through the proposed Doppler-Shannon based association is proved, analytically as well as through simulations, to be superior to the classical Shannon based association.

title: Agentic AI for QCD perturbation theory or: how I learned to stop worrying and love the bot
abstract: AI coding agents are extremely effective at performing calculations that can be broken down into modular steps, each with verifiable checks of correctness. Perturbative QCD calculations satisfy both of these properties and we find that they are well-suited to solution by agentic AI systems. We discuss our methods for instructing and verifying the work of agents in one- and two-loop perturbative calculations, with a focus on pre-empting common mistakes. We find that once an agent has successfully completed one perturbative calculation, its instructions transfer very well to other similar calculations which can then be completed and verified in a matter of hours with little effort from the user.

title: Probabilistic Stellar Mass and Radius Estimation with Bayesian Hierarchical Stacking
abstract: Accurate stellar parameters are essential for the characterisation of exoplanets, yet most host stars lack direct measurements of mass and radius. We aim to predict stellar masses and radii from commonly available observables and to quantify uncertainties and systematic effects in a way that is consistent with stellar observations. By not relying on a single model, we aim to obtain more robust predictive distributions and reduce sensitivity to model misspecification and outliers. We develop a Bayesian machine-learning framework that combines three probabilistic models through Bayesian hierarchical stacking (BHS): a Bayesian additive regression tree model, a two-process heteroscedastic sparse Gaussian process, and a hierarchical Bayesian neural network. The method propagates measurement uncertainties, accounts for correlations among inputs, and aggregates model variance into final predictive distributions. On a held-out test set the method attains a mean absolute relative difference (MARD) of 3.5% for mass and 2.1% for radius, improving on empirical-relation-based methods and standard machine-learning baselines. For 44 Kepler LEGACY stars, the BHS masses differ from estimates obtained with the BAyesian STellar Algorithm (BASTA) by a MARD of 4.8%, compared with 8.5% between the empirical relations and BASTA. Applied to about 2400 exoplanet host stars, the predictions differ from literature values by a MARD of 2.7% in both mass and radius. Residual analysis reveals mild underestimation for cool dwarfs, consistent with sparse training coverage, and positive offsets near the main-sequence turn-off that may reflect priors in isochrone-based catalogues. Internal consistency with g = GM/R^2 is greater for the BHS predictions, with a scatter in Delta log g lower by a factor of three than that of the literature values.

title: Efficient Deep Gaussian Process Surrogates via Mini-Batch Latent MAP Estimation
abstract: Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) are flexible surrogate models for computer experiments with nonstationary response surfaces, but inference over their latent representations remains computationally challenging. Existing methods typically rely on variational inference or Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), which impose variational-family assumptions or require costly posterior sampling. We propose the latent maximum-a-posteriori deep Gaussian process (LaMP-DGP), which uses gradient-based optimization to obtain MAP estimates of the latent representations and enables efficient probabilistic prediction through linked-GP calculations. To scale LaMP-DGP to large datasets, we develop a mini-batch optimization algorithm and, under a polynomial mini-batch bias-decay condition, establish a stationarity bound for latent-state optimization that motivates a growing batch-size schedule. Across numerical experiments and real-data analyses, LaMP-DGP provides consistently competitive predictive performance relative to doubly stochastic variational inference, stochastic gradient Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, and fully Bayesian Vecchia DGP inference. Computationally, LaMP-DGP is substantially faster than the Vecchia MCMC approach while remaining broadly competitive with the stochastic-gradient alternatives. These results position LaMP-DGP as a competitive and computationally efficient alternative for DGP inference. An R package, "LaMPDGP", is available for implementing the proposed method.

title: State-Dependent Delay Modeling of Wind-Farm Wake Dynamics
abstract: Turbines convert wind to electrical power. In the wake of a turbine, wind speed is reduced in proportion to the amount of power extracted. In a wind farm, downstream turbines may be located in wake of an upstream turbine, requiring coordination to yield maximum power generation. This paper creates a state-dependent delay model for a two turbine wind farm. The upstream turbine creates a wake that diminishes the wind speed at the downstream turbine. Changing the upstream turbine operation will affect the downstream turbine after a delay that depends on the wind-propagation time between them. This delay depends on the upstream power extraction and it can destabilize the combined dynamics. Conventional models of this effect rely on nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs). Control design and analysis with such models is difficult with established methods. We first show that the PDE model can be represented by an Abel-type state-dependent delay differential equation. The equation has an implicit solution. To obtain an explicit representation, we then introduce a simplified state-dependent delay model. Both models predict destabilizing interactions between the two turbines. Numerical examples illustrate delay-induced oscillations using the simplified model and verify their effectiveness in simulation.

title: A Differentiable, GPU-Accelerated Finite-Element Formulation in JAX for Large-Deformation Shells with Contact: Application to Patient-Specific Aortic Valve Simulation
abstract: Patient-specific aortic-valve models can help assess how tissue properties and geometry influence leaflet deformation and coaptation, with potential to inform intervention planning. Large deformations, near-incompressibility, and evolving contact make these simulations computationally demanding and can challenge nonlinear convergence. Differentiable, GPU-accelerated methods offer efficient derivative evaluation and parallel computation, but their matrix-free application to soft-tissue shells with contact remains less established. We developed a forward solver using tatva's energy-based finite-element framework in JAX. The solver combines finite-strain extensible-director shells, hyperelastic constitutive models, and a finite-range repulsive contact energy. Nonlinear equilibrium is solved using a regularized, matrix-free Newton-Krylov method with two-level preconditioning. Automatic differentiation evaluates tangent-vector products without forming or storing the primary tangent matrix, while GPU execution parallelizes element and quadrature-point computations. Constitutive, shell, contact, and self-contact responses were assessed against analytical, semi-analytical, and published benchmarks. At a contact-free plate equilibrium, implicit sensitivities of the converged apex displacement to constitutive parameters, thickness, and pressure agreed with finite differences from independent nonlinear simulations. Simulations of three patient-specific aortic-valve models (two tricuspid and one bicuspid) achieved final relative equilibrium residuals below 10^-4. Median GPU runtimes were approximately 15-25 minutes, with 5.3-6.5-fold speedups relative to corresponding CPU runs on the tested hardware. These results provide component-level verification and demonstrate GPU-accelerated forward valve simulation in the tested cases, supporting future gradient-based inverse studies.

title: Цифрова трансформація аграрного сектору як чинник соціально-економічної стійкості сільських територій: досвід ЄС та імплікації для України
abstract: The war has turned the resilience of Ukraine’s rural areas into a question of their survival: demographic losses are estimated at about 10 million people, and over 4 million rural residents lack quality fixed internet access. In Ukraine, the digital transformation of the agricultural sector is implemented mainly as an instrument of production efficiency. In EU policy, by contrast, it has been institutionalised as a factor of rural community resilience – with dedicated programmes, targeted funding and practical mechanisms. This asymmetry determines the relevance of the study: the social potential of agricultural digitalisation in Ukraine remains untapped precisely when the need for it is most acute. The purpose of the study is to substantiate the role of agricultural digital transformation as a factor of socio-economic resilience of rural areas and to develop practical measures for strengthening it based on the EU experience. The methodological basis comprises the systems approach, content analysis of EU and FAO strategic documents, comparative analysis, scientific modelling and systematisation. A three-component model of resilience is proposed, distinguishing the production-economic, social and institutional dimensions of the impact of agricultural digital transformation. It is substantiated that under war conditions the social and institutional dimensions acquire priority, as they determine the capacity of communities to retain population and recover. A matrix of practical measures is developed across the three dimensions, specifying responsible actors, time horizons and differentiated funding sources, together with a roadmap for implementation at the wartime, recovery and integration stages. The practical significance lies in the applicability of the proposed measures for shaping state policy for the recovery of rural areas. The scientific contribution lies in adapting a multidimensional approach to rural resilience to the conditions of wartime disruption by substantiating the priority of the social and institutional dimensions of agricultural digital transformation and translating the resulting policy priorities into a matrix of measures and a phased recovery roadmap. Article type: theoretical and applied.
journal: Bulletin of the Academy of Labor, Social Relations and Tourism. Series: Economics, Psychology and Management

title: Industry Dynamics and Strategic Business Analysis: An Applied Case Study of Data Bridge Market Research
abstract: Market research supports strategic decision-making by helping organizations interpret customer needs, competitive conditions, regulatory developments, technological change, and emerging sources of risk. Yet the availability of information does not automatically produce reliable market intelligence. Researchers must define the market precisely, assess the credibility and comparability of evidence, and connect observations to the business question being examined. This paper presents an applied case study of secondary market research and strategic analysis conducted in the professional research environment of Data Bridge Market Research Private Limited (DBMR), Pune. The analysis is based on a documented research project undertaken between 12 May and 11 August 2026 and uses a descriptive, single-organization case-study design. It covers healthcare, packaging, advanced materials, chemicals, food and agriculture, and technology and services. Eight markets received detailed attention: global sleep apnea devices, European aesthetic dermatology, global paper and paperboard packaging, Brazilian corrugated board packaging, global soft magnetic materials, European vegetable oil-based esters, global custom pulses, and U.K. restaurant point-of-sale systems. Approximately 30–40 market report descriptions were also prepared, according to the project record. The analytical process drew on PESTEL analysis, Porter’s Five Forces, company and competitor research, supply-chain and value-chain analysis, regulatory review, tariff research, and technology-trend assessment. Across the markets examined, the documented observations point to the importance of evaluating demand alongside cost, regulation, supply availability, sustainability, technological capability, and customer adoption. Healthcare-related markets required attention to awareness, diagnosis, treatment access, and regulation; packaging markets highlighted material performance and sustainability; advanced materials were connected to industrial and technological applications; and restaurant POS systems raised issues of digital adoption and integration. A recurring methodological challenge was that public sources differed in definitions, geographic coverage, reporting periods, and measurement approaches. The paper therefore argues for systematic source validation and industry-specific interpretation rather than relying on isolated market figures or applying one analytical template mechanically to every sector. The findings are descriptive, based on the documented project record, and do not establish causal effects on client decisions or company performance. Keywords: market research, market intelligence, industry analysis, competitive intelligence, secondary research, PESTEL, Porter’s Five Forces
journal: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management

title: Unraveling Plant–Soil Interaction Networks: A Multi-Analytical Framework Linking Elemental Composition, Microbial Abundance, and Ecosystem Function Across Land-Use Gradients
abstract: The intricate networks governing plant-soil interactions constitute the biochemical foundation of terrestrial ecosystem function. Despite their ecological significance, the application of complex network theory to integrate physicochemical, elemental, and microbial parameters remains underexplored. This study employs an interdisciplinary framework combining X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and standard plate count methodology to characterize four distinct land-use soil systems: grassland (S-1), canal-margin (S-2), forest (S-3), and agricultural (S-4). Total microbial counts ranged from 12,910 cfu (S-1) to 20,170 cfu (S-4), following the gradient of anthropogenic disturbance intensity. XRF analysis revealed SiO₂ dominance (66.30–76.50%) with significant inter-site variation in Fe₂O₃, Al₂O₃, and P₂O₅ fractions. FTIR spectra identified distinct functional group signatures, including silicate frameworks (985–1001 cm⁻¹), hydroxyl stretching (3359–3383 cm⁻¹), and aromatic C=C vibrations (1627–1629 cm⁻¹). Correlation analysis and network topology modeling demonstrated that soil moisture (r = 0.91, p < 0.05) and Fe₂O₃ content (r = 0.85, p < 0.05) were the strongest predictors of microbial abundance, while pH and electrical conductivity exhibited moderate positive associations. Network centrality metrics identified total microbial count (TMC) and nutrient uptake as the most influential hub nodes within the plant-soil interaction network. These findings underscore that ecosystem function emerges from non-linear, multi-scale interactions among abiotic matrices, microbial communities, and plant-mediated feedback loops. The study provides a replicable methodological template for integrating spectroscopic and microbiological data into network-based ecological models, offering actionable insights for sustainable land management and soil health monitoring.
journal: International Journal of Science, Strategic Management and Technology

title: Satellite Image Based Agricultural Monitoring Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
abstract: Approaches for agriculture monitoring should consistently assess vegetation conditions throughout farm fields and limit the need for manual surveys. Satellite-derived information offers one source of spatially-explicit data that can be used to monitor crops using their spectral reflectance properties. Thresholding vegetation indices to classify vegetation conditions may be difficult to interpret across cropland with variable canopy structure, phenology, and reflectance. Here, we introduce a crop monitoring framework which integrates Sentinel-2 multitemporal data, vegetation indices, machine learning, outlier detection, and explainable AI. Sentinel-2 multispectral (MS) and RGB data streams are handled with separate processing components. Vegetation indices including Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index (SAVI), Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI), and Excess Green Index (ExG) are computed from spectral bands when applicable. Crop condition class labels are predicted with a Random Forest classification model. Thresholding on crop-specific NDVI values is included for comparison as a rules-based method. An Isolation Forest algorithm detects anomalous vegetation conditions. Finally, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are used to interpret ML model predictions. Six crop types are included in the framework: cotton, sugarcane, paddy, carrot, wheat, and barley. An initial test of the framework is done using a single Sentinel-2 MS image and five historical records yielded a NDVI value of 0.75 for the satellite image along with a classification of Healthy, 99% model certainty, and 0.0% of pixels identified as stressed vegetation.
journal: International Journal of Innovative Research in Computer Science and Technology

title: Vitamin C and Methylprednisolone Modulate Apoptotic and Transcript Responses in a B-35 Scratch Screening Model.
abstract: In vitro mechanical injury platforms using proliferative neuronal cell lines provide accessible systems for preliminary pharmacological screening before progression to differentiated, primary, or in vivo models. We investigated the effects of vitamin C and methylprednisolone, alone or in combination, on cell viability, Annexin V/PI-defined apoptotic cell death, scratch-gap closure, and selected transcript responses in the B-35 rat neuroblastoma cell line. Mechanical injury was induced in confluent B-35 monolayers using a standardized scratch method. Vitamin C, methylprednisolone, or their combination was applied either immediately after injury (0 h) or after a 24 h delay. Scratch-gap closure was quantified by image-based analysis, and IL-4, IL-10, and TUBB3 expression was evaluated by quantitative real-time PCR. Early combined exposure to vitamin C and methylprednisolone was associated with low apoptotic cell fractions, faster scratch-gap closure, and higher IL-4, IL-10, and TUBB3 mRNA levels than either single treatment, whereas delayed treatment showed attenuated responses. These findings describe treatment-associated changes in a simplified B-35 cell-line screening model. They should not be interpreted as evidence of regeneration, pharmacological synergy, neuroprotection, or spinal cord injury therapy. Protein-level validation, proliferation control, and confirmation in differentiated neuronal cultures, primary neuronglia co-cultures, organoid or slice models, and in vivo injury systems are required before mechanistic or translational conclusions can be drawn.

title: Biografías históricas, inclusión y autoestima: Modelo BIO-INCLUYE para la educación secundaria
abstract: History education has formative potential beyond the acquisition of knowledge about events, processes, and temporalities, as it offers opportunities to understand diverse human experiences and establish reflective connections between past and present. This article aims to provide the theoretical foundations for a didactic model based on the inclusive and humanized use of historical biographies to foster historical empathy, participation, and the potential strengthening of self-esteem among secondary school students, with particular attention to learners who experience mobility-related barriers and require specific educational support. A qualitative theoretical-documentary study was conducted through a critical and integrative review of literature on inclusive education, historical empathy, self-esteem, Universal Design for Learning, and history education. As a result, the BIO-INCLUYE Model is proposed, structured around five components: biographical humanization, historical contextualization, historical empathy, reflective identification, and inclusive participation. The proposal is aligned with Universal Design for Learning principles and includes multiple means of engagement, representation, action, and expression. A coherence matrix and a content-validation protocol involving five expert judges are also incorporated. It is concluded that historical biographies have the potential to support more inclusive history education when idealized heroism is avoided and diversity, barriers, support, decision-making, and differentiated forms of participation are recognized. The relationship with self-esteem is presented as a pedagogical hypothesis requiring empirical validation.

title: Interface management in relationships between systems
abstract: Modeling of complex systems is based on established theories and concepts, but also on innovative constructions that harmonize the system with the requirements foreseen for its operating life. The problems of system interaction are concentrated at each coupling interface between them, where the harmonization of inputs and outputs of matter, energy and information, the management of coupling variables, the mutual compatibility of systems, the harmonization of error handling procedures, data processing protocols and reliability are achieved. The refinement of current and future systems, especially in the context of advanced integration of artificial intelligence and the human factor, requires new approaches, theories and tools of mutual interaction, involving even the quantum level of human consciousness and awareness. The inter-, trans- and multi-disciplinary characteristics of system coupling interfaces must be considered, covering a wide range of phenomena, from deterministic to probabilistic, even to quantum subtleties. Therefore, interface management must become a strategic solution in the optimal functioning of networked systems.
journal: Journal of Engineering Sciences and Innovation

title: How Does Digital Literacy Drive the Low-Carbon Production Behavior of Farmers?—An Empirical Analysis Based on an Integrated TAM-TPB Framework
abstract: Digital literacy serves as a core capability that enables farmers to integrate low-carbon technologies into their production practices. Clarifying the pathways through which digital literacy influences agricultural production is therefore crucial for promoting the green transformation of agriculture. Based on micro-survey data from 451 farmers in Sichuan Province, this study employed partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) within an integrated and expanded Technology Acceptance Model-Theory of Planned Behavior (TAM-TPB) theoretical framework to analyze the internal mechanisms through which digital information literacy affects the low-carbon production behavior of farmers. The results show three key features of this system. (1) Digital information literacy has a significant positive impact on farmers' perception of digital technology functions, low-carbon agricultural cognition, willingness to adopt digital technologies, and willingness to improve their digital literacy. Through these factors, it further exerts a positive influence on their low-carbon production behavior. (2) The results of the chain mediation tests for the “digital literacy→cognition/perception→willingness” and “cognition/perception→willingness→behavior” pathways show that low-carbon agricultural cognition partially mediates the effect of digital information literacy on willingness to improve digital literacy, while the perception of digital technology functions also plays a significant mediating role in the pathway from digital information literacy to willingness to adopt digital technologies. (3) When willingness variables serve as mediators, willingness to adopt digital technologies plays a significant mediating role in the pathway from the perception of digital technology functions to low-carbon production behavior, thereby further strengthening the driving effect of functional perception on behavioral transformation. In contrast, the mediating effect of willingness to improve digital literacy in the pathway from low-carbon agricultural cognition to low-carbon production behavior is not significant, suggesting that the transition from cognition to action relies more on external technological empowerment than on self-directed literacy improvement. This study reveals the dynamic pathway through which digital literacy influences low-carbon production behavior via a synergistic mechanism of “cognitive iteration, functional perception, and technology embedding,” thereby providing a theoretical basis for policymakers to develop digital literacy cultivation systems and optimize low-carbon technology promotion strategies.

title: Edge AI Based Real-Time Arecanut Plant Disease Detection Using Deep Learning and Smartphone Deployment
abstract: Arecanut (Areca catechu) is an important plantation crop in India, and identifying diseases at an early stage can be difficult in the field. This paper presents an Android application for preliminary arecanut disease detection using deep learning and on-device inference. A MobileNetV2 model converted to TensorFlow Lite classifies accepted arecanut images using meaningful class names such as Bud borer, Healthy Leaf, Stem bleeding, and Yellow leaf disease rather than displaying numeric class indices. A separate input gate checks whether an image is related to arecanut before disease classification. The application displays the predicted class, confidence score, symptoms, possible causes, remedies, and pesticide-related information. It also includes an offline Farmer Assistant that answers a limited set of predefined farming questions, such as what causes a detected disease, its symptoms, and basic management guidance, without requiring an internet connection or an online AI service. The reported evaluation includes 2,032 test images after exact duplicate images were excluded. The Keras model achieved 99.31% accuracy, while standard TFLite and Float16 TFLite achieved 98.97% and 99.21%, respectively. The Float16 model reduced the reported model size from 8.50 MB to 4.28 MB. Functional testing recorded 11 successful cases out of 14 for the existing detection workflow; the offline Farmer Assistant is described as a limited, rule-based guidance feature and its performance is not included in these model accuracy figures. Further field testing is required.
journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Engineering & Technology

title: Smart Farmers Equipment Rental and Pest Classification System: an Integrated Web Platform Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning
abstract: Small and marginal farmers face three recurring problems: the high cost of owning agricultural machinery, delayed or inaccurate identification of crop pests, and limited direct access to buyers for their produce. This paper presents the Smart Farmers Equipment Rental and Pest Classification System, an integrated web application that addresses these problems on a single platform. The system is developed using Python Flask, HTML, CSS and JavaScript with an SQLite3 database. It provides(i) an equipment rental module supported by a machine learning regression model that predicts rental price from equipment type, condition, usage duration and market demand; (ii) a pest classification module in which a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) built with TensorFlow/Keras classifies uploaded crop images as harmful or non-harmful and returns precautions and preventive measures; and (iii) an agricultural marketplace that lets farmers list fruits and vegetables and lets registered companies browse and purchase them. Role-based access is provided for farmers, equipment owners, company/buyers and administrators. The paper describes the system architecture, UML and data flow design, module implementation, and testing strategy, with a target CNN test accuracy of at least 90%. The modular design allows the platform to be extended with additional crops, pest categories, equipment types, weather information and a mobile application
journal: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology

title: Potato Leaf Disease Classification using a Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Sustainable Agriculture
abstract: Leaf diseases of potato are significant factors responsible for losses in productivity in potato crops worldwide and for food shortages. Prompt and precise diagnosis of diseases is critical for minimizing yield losses and optimizing agricultural sustainability. The conventional testing process where ad-vanced farmers physically examine the disease is laborious, costly and not possible in remote areas. Engineered based on deep learning, the plant disease detection system can detect plant diseases automatically from images. This study is a weighted ensemble deep learning system that consists of two models: VGG19 and ResNet50V2 for potato leaf disease classification. The proposed framework is based on transfer learning, which is based on a pre-trained network on ImageNet, and fine-tuning the network on potato leaf disease dataset with three classes: Potato Early Blight, Potato Late Blight and Healthy leaves. Before training, the image pre-processing and augmentation techniques including resizing, normalization, rotation, shifting, shearing, zooming and horizontal flipping were applied to improve the ability of the models to generalize data. They were individually trained and the prediction probabilities of each model were combined by a weighted averaging ensemble strategy, where the weight is the performance of each model. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the ensemble model to leverage both the architecture-based feature representations, which is beneficial for classification compared to using each model’s feature representation alone. The solution is reliable, easily scalable and has good potential to be integrated in precision agriculture systems for potato disease diagnosis, management and crop productivity.
journal: European Journal of Applied Science, Engineering and Technology

title: Rancang Bangun Sistem Informasi Manajemen Surat Masuk Dan Surat Keluar Berbasis Web Menggunakan Framework Laravel Pada Bagian Tata Usaha Dan Kepegawaian Sekretariat DPRD Provinsi Jambi
abstract: Sekretariat DPRD Provinsi Jambi masih menggunakan sistem manual dalam pengelolaan surat masuk dan surat keluar sehingga proses pencatatan, pencarian, dan penyusunan laporan kurang efisien. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang Sistem Informasi Manajemen Surat Berbasis Web menggunakan metode pengembangan Waterfall. Perancangan sistem dilakukan menggunakan Unified Modeling Language (UML), sedangkan implementasi sistem menggunakan Framework Laravel. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sistem yang dirancang mampu mendukung pengelolaan surat masuk dan keluar, pengarsipan dokumen, pencarian data, serta penyajian laporan secara lebih cepat, efektif, dan akurat. The Secretariat of DPRD Jambi Province still uses a manual system for managing incoming and outgoing mail, resulting in inefficient recording, retrieval, and reporting processes. This study aims to design a web-based mail management information system using the Waterfall software development method. The system was designed using Unified Modeling Language (UML) and implemented using the Laravel Framework. System design employed Unified Modeling Language (UML), while implementation was carried out using the Laravel Framework. The results show that the proposed system supports mail management, document archiving, data retrieval, and report generation more quickly, effectively, and accurately.

title: Perancangan Sistem Monitoring Dan Pengelolaan Barang Masuk Berbasis Web Menggunakan Metode Waterfall Pada Dinas Komunikasi Dan Informatika Provinsi Jambi
abstract: Dinas Komunikasi dan Informatika Provinsi Jambi masih melaksanakan proses pencatatan dan monitoring barang masuk secara manual menggunakan dokumen administrasi dan aplikasi perkantoran sederhana, sehingga menimbulkan kendala berupa kesalahan pencatatan, keterlambatan pencarian data, dan kesulitan penyusunan laporan. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang Sistem Monitoring dan Pengelolaan Barang Masuk Berbasis Web untuk membantu proses pencatatan, monitoring, pencarian, dan pelaporan data barang masuk secara lebih efektif. Metode pengembangan yang digunakan adalah Waterfall, meliputi analisis kebutuhan, perancangan, implementasi, pengujian, dan pemeliharaan, dengan pemodelan menggunakan UML serta basis data MySQL. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sistem yang dibangun mampu mempermudah proses pencatatan barang, mempercepat pencarian data, meningkatkan akurasi penyimpanan data, serta menyederhanakan penyusunan laporan secara otomatis. The Communication and Informatics Office of Jambi Province still records and monitors incoming goods manually using administrative documents and basic office applications, resulting in recording errors, delayed data retrieval, and difficulties in report preparation. This study aims to design a Web-Based Monitoring and Management System for Incoming Goods to support recording, monitoring, searching, and reporting processes more effectively. The system was developed using the Waterfall method, covering requirements analysis, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance, modeled with UML and a MySQL database. The results show that the developed system simplifies the recording of goods, accelerates data search, improves data storage accuracy, and streamlines automatic report generation.

title: Rural E-Commerce Development in Huarong County, Hunan Province, China: A Policy and Infrastructure Case Study
abstract: Rural e-commerce has become an important policy instrument for connecting agricultural producers, county-level enterprises, and urban consumers in China. This article examines Huarong County in Hunan Province, purposively selected as an analytically informative example of a government-led, agriculturally oriented county with explicit e-commerce support and accessible administrative records. Drawing on policy documents issued between 2015 and 2024, official statistical communiques, and secondary county-level administrative data, the study applies an institutional-theory lens and directed qualitative content analysis across five dimensions: policy environment, infrastructure, production scale, production effects, and development models. The findings indicate that local incentives and interorganizational coordination created entry conditions for rural e-commerce, while digital infrastructure, logistics integration, practitioner capability, and market governance shaped whether those institutional inputs translated into durable participation and market outcomes. By 2020, Huarong reported 1,200 e-commerce practitioners, RMB 790 million in transaction value, and 12.36 million completed orders. These figures are administrative self-reports and are interpreted as reported scale indicators rather than independently audited effects. The case therefore suggests an institutional enablement mechanism: government coordination can reduce early-stage coordination costs, but sustainable upgrading requires complementary implementation capacity, performance-based support, supply-chain traceability, professional training, and stronger platform governance.

title: Forecasting Apple Stock Prices Using LSTM, GRU, and Transformer Models: A Deep Learning Approach to Digital Market Prediction
abstract: The rapid growth and volatility of digital financial markets have increased the demand for accurate, data-driven forecasting methods capable of handling complex temporal and nonlinear relationships. This study investigates the predictive performance of three deep learning architectures Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Transformer Encoder in forecasting Apple Inc.’s stock prices. Using historical data spanning 1980 to 2025, each model was trained on 60-day sequences to predict the next trading day’s closing price. The dataset was normalized using the MinMaxScaler and divided into 80 percent for training and 20 percent for testing. All models were trained for 20 epochs with a batch size of 32, employing the Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss function and the Adam optimizer. The results show that the GRU model achieved the best predictive accuracy, with an RMSE of 4.8281 and an MAE of 3.5578, followed by the LSTM model with an RMSE of 8.8865 and an MAE of 6.0122. The Transformer model performed less effectively, indicating its reliance on larger and more complex datasets to optimize its self-attention mechanism. Overall, the findings demonstrate that recurrent neural network-based models remain highly effective for stock price forecasting in digital financial environments. The study concludes that deep learning, particularly the GRU architecture, provides a powerful and computationally efficient framework for real-time prediction and decision-making in digital market analysis and algorithmic trading applications.

title: From Adoption to Impact: A Life-Cycle Monitoring Framework for Scalable and Meaningful Digital Agriculture in India

authors.name: Pranjal Cholke
authors.affiliation: MAEER'S MIT Art's Commerce and Science College, Alandi, Pune

abstract: India's pursuit of Viksit Bharat@2047 has placed digital agriculture at the centre of agricultural policy through initiatives such as the Digital Agriculture Mission, AgriStack, the Soil Health Card scheme, the electronic National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) and a rapidly growing agri-tech start-up ecosystem. Yet the success of digital programmes is still reported largely through enrolment and adoption counts: farmers registered, devices distributed or applications downloaded. Such figures reveal little about whether a technology remains in use, why farmers discontinue it, or whether it delivers measurable benefit on the farm. In a country where most operational holdings are small and marginal, this gap between adoption and outcome is a central implementation risk. This chapter proposes the Agri-Tech Lifecycle Monitor (ALCM), a conceptual and design-oriented framework that follows an agricultural technology from introduction through adoption, usage, continued usage, actual benefit and impact. A parallel recovery pathway, comprising abandonment, reason identification, problem analysis, corrective action and re-tracking, treats discontinuation as diagnostic information rather than as failure. The framework defines stage-wise indicators, including the continuation rate, abandonment rate, recovery rate and a proposed Meaningful Digital Transformation Conversion (MDTC) ratio, which expresses the share of adopters who reach a defined measurable-impact stage. A multilingual farmer interface (Marathi, Hindi and English) and a stakeholder dashboard for extension officers, Krishi Vigyan Kendras, farmer producer organisations, technology providers and policymakers form the operational layer. Using an illustrative smart-irrigation scenario, the chapter shows how lifecycle monitoring exposes attrition and unrealised benefit that adoption statistics conceal. It then derives policy lessons and implementation pathways for embedding lifecycle monitoring in programme design, extension systems and digital public infrastructure. The chapter argues that scalable digital agriculture should be judged not by how many farmers adopt a technology, but by how many continue to use it and gain from it.

title: Explaining Institutional Resilience through Educational Governance: A Latent Mediation Model of Strategic Management
abstract: This study examines how Educational governance is associated with institutional resilience among Chinese university students, with strategic management proposed as an explanatory mechanism. Drawing on self-determination and self-regulated learning perspectives, a conditional process model was specified and evaluated using a synthetic dataset of 486 cases. The simulated measurement model demonstrated acceptable reliability (composite reliability = 0.88) and fit (CFI = 0.93, TLI = 0.92, RMSEA = 0.051, SRMR = 0.038). Structural estimates suggested that Educational governance was positively associated with strategic management (β = 0.41, p .002) and with institutional resilience (β = 0.31, p .002). The standardized indirect effect through strategic management was 0.18, with a synthetic 95% bootstrap interval excluding zero. Together, the modeled predictors explained 48% of the variance in institutional resilience. The paper contributes a concise mechanism-based account of adaptive learning and demonstrates an empirical structure aligned with the Journal of Adaptive Learning and Psychological Growth. Because all results are simulated, the findings are illustrative and require validation with ethically collected data.
journal: The Journal of Interactive Social Sciences

title: Psi-programmes of the Human Psyche: Key Aspects
abstract: The aim of the study was to provide a theoretical substantiation and conceptualisation of the notion of a “psi-programme” in order to explain the mechanisms by which stimuli are transformed into controllable mental processes. The methodology combined theoretical modelling based on fundamental psychological works with a secondary analysis of contemporary statistical reports on the state of mental health in the United States, Germany and Ukraine. The main result was the definition of a psi-programme as a dynamic informational-energetic structure that operates through four successive stages: the catalysis of a fixed set, the search for a strategy, the formation of an algorithm, and implementation. Comparative analysis revealed unique national patterns of dominant psi-programmes. In the United States, where 23.4% of adults have a diagnosed mental disorder, programmes of personal success and social anxiety were identified. In Germany, where only 25% of the population is in a state of psychological flourishing, programmes of stability and perfectionism are characteristic. In Ukraine, where 83% of the population experiences a high level of stress due to the war and overall satisfaction with psychological well-being has fallen to 36%, programmes of collective resilience and individual trauma were identified. Three levels for the practical modification of maladaptive psi-programmes were also defined: individual (psychotherapy), educational-media (high-quality content), and socio-institutional (supportive policies). The conclusions indicate that the psi-programme model is a valid tool for analysing mental activity. It was established that the sociocultural context is a key factor in the formation of dominant mental patterns that determine the psychological state of both the individual and society. The practical significance lies in the possibility of developing comprehensive, multi-level strategies for correcting maladaptive programmes and strengthening mental health.

title: A Novel MPSI Weighting and Proximity Indexed Value Framework for Multi-Criteria Selection of Marketplace Logistics Partners
abstract: In facing the increasingly intense competition in the logistics industry, companies are often confronted with challenges in selecting the most appropriate logistics partner due to the many performance criteria that must be considered simultaneously. This study aims to evaluate and determine the best logistics partner using a Multi-Criteria Decision-Making approach through the integration of the MPSI method for criteria weighting and PIV for the alternative ranking process. The criteria used include Transit Time, On-Time Delivery, First-Attempt Success, Attempt Rate, and Package Volume, which are analyzed based on the performance data of each alternative. The weighting results indicate that Package Volume and Transit Time are the most dominant factors in the evaluation process. Based on the PIV method calculations, the ranking results were obtained, with NJ Logistics Partner occupying the first rank with a score of 0.46408, followed by TK Logistics Partner in second place with a score of 0.44014, and JT Logistics Partner in third place with a score of 0.39282. Sensitivity tests through various weight change scenarios showed that the ranking structure remained consistent, indicating that the model has a high level of stability and resilience to parameter variations. Overall, the proposed approach is able to produce decisions that are objective, measurable, and reliable as a basis for supporting strategic logistics partner selection.
journal: Journal of Decision Support Systems and Multi-Criteria Decision Making
