title: Drum-Buffer-Rope and rolling horizon MILP for shifting bottleneck synchronization in sugar beet logistics
abstract: Objectives: This study develops and validates a cyber-physical mathematical framework for synchronizing stochastic agricultural harvesting with deterministic industrial processing in regional sugar beet logistics. The framework addresses real-time coordination conflicts between distributed field supply nodes, limited transport capacity, dynamic field accessibility, and continuous factory demand. Prior work: Traditional static logistics models treat agro-industrial cargo as inert mass and primarily optimize spatial distance. Such approaches are poorly suited to environments characterized by high-frequency schedule nervousness, weather-driven field accessibility changes, shifting bottlenecks, and non-linear raw material degradation during temporary field storage. Approach: The proposed Digital Twin architecture combines dynamic Drum-Buffer-Rope (DBR) pull logic for shifting bottlenecks with rolling Model Predictive Control (MPC) and a multi-phase Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) heuristic. Spatial transport work is handled during seasonal stratification, feasible route assignment, and topological filtering; within the active rolling MILP core it is treated as a quasi-invariant structural term. This allows the optimization layer to focus on time-sensitive trade-offs between sucrose preservation, factory starvation avoidance, and logistical feasibility. Results: Empirical validation using an 11- year industrial dataset comprising more than 180,000 unique transactional cycles shows that the multi-phase heuristic achieves sub-second solver response times in the tested industrial scenarios, with the active MILP core converging within 0.45 seconds. Operational deployment is associated with compression of factory reception-yard turnaround time from 24.6 to 13.8 minutes and a 41% reduction in active fleet dispersion. Implications: The adaptive sigmoid switching mechanism dynamically shifts objective priorities between quality preservation and plant starvation avoidance during environmental shocks. For practitioners, the framework provides a real-time execution tool for synchronizing harvesting, loading, transportation, and factory reception under stochastic disturbances. For researchers, it demonstrates a scalable approach to time- based buffer management in temporal agro-industrial networks. Value: The scientific novelty lies in integrating adaptive DBR pull constraints, rolling MILP optimization, graph-based topological filtering, and physics- informed quality inputs into a unified cyber-physical synchronization framework. The proposed architecture transforms agricultural logistics from a rigid cost center into a resilience-oriented decision system without compromising grower equity or systemic transparency.
journal: Smart Cities and Regional Development (SCRD) Journal

title: Creation of information services for automated database upgrading of agricultural machinery
abstract: This article presents the results of a methodological approach to developing information services for automated replenishment of a digital catalog of agricultural machinery database, designed to optimize agricultural production processes. An algorithm for creating and updating a digital resource is considered to reduce the time required to prepare analytical samples, improve the reliability of agricultural machinery data, and reduce the labor intensity of information and analytical support for the digital service by eliminating manual data entry. Particular attention is paid to the use of a DAG-oriented ETL pipeline, which allows the database update process to be decomposed into sequential and manageable tasks. The stages of source identification, identifier extraction, equipment card loading, intermediate storage, validation, reclassification, writing to PostgreSQL, and data transfer via an API to the user interface are presented.
journal: JOURNAL OF MONETARY ECONOMICS AND MANAGEMENT

title: Decentralized Autonomous Organizations in the Russian Agricultural Sector: Challenges and Prospects for Assimilation and Development
abstract: The paper’s subject focuses on the steps taken to implement decentralized autonomous organizations (DAO) to guarantee the resilience of agri-food systems. This study aims to explore the possibilities of using DAO in farm produce production and marketing, concentrating on increasing transparency, lowering operational costs, and enhancing resistance to external disruptions. The study assesses the practicality of implementing DAO in Russia’s farming sector by examining factors like cryptocurrency adoption, economic and logistical resilience, and supply chain pressures amid sanctions and market limitations. It outlines the possibility of increasing domestic farm competitiveness and building a transparent, verifiable technological foundation using DAO in Russia’s agri-food industry. The authors developed a potential DAO architecture model for the Russian Federation. This study’s scientific innovation stems from its detailed analysis of the potential effects of decentralized management and coordination mechanisms on key operational parameters in farming. The research highlights that in the face of increasing external uncertainty, the digital transformation of the agricultural economy, and the pressing need to systematize and automate the distribution and oversight of state agricultural subsidies while building greater trust in these procedures. The authors conclude that DAO significantly lower coordination hurdles and transaction expenses, and help mitigate information asymmetry within the producer-to-consumer supply chain. The statement stresses that achieving the complete economic and social benefits of DAO necessitates developing a customized regulatory framework alongside a phased, pilotdriven adoption of the technology within regional agri-food systems, mindful of their institutional and digital maturity.

title: A TIERED LIFECYCLE GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORK FOR AGENTIC ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN FINANCIAL SERVICES
abstract: The rapid emergence of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) presents significant governance challenges for financial services, where autonomous systems increasingly support high-impact financial activities. Existing regulatory approaches remain fragmented and continue to rely primarily on non-binding supervisory guidance, leaving important gaps in lifecycle oversight, accountability, and systemic risk management. This paper proposes the Tiered Lifecycle Governance (TLG) Framework, a strategic governance model that integrates lifecycle-based AI oversight with responsive, risk-based regulation. The framework combines three transaction-risk tiers with four AI lifecycle stages to establish proportionate oversight obligations that balance innovation, regulatory accountability, and financial stability. Drawing on technological, economic, legal, and institutional perspectives, the framework is applied to the 2026 U.S. interagency review of model risk management guidance (SR 26-2) to demonstrate how lifecycle governance can strengthen oversight of agentic AI in financial services. The analysis shows that the TLG Framework provides a structured alternative to the existing guidance-versus-rulemaking approach by aligning regulatory obligations with transaction risk rather than institutional size or technology labels. The paper concludes that binding, lifecycle-based oversight offers a practical pathway for improving resilience, transparency, and accountability in financial AI governance while providing a transferable governance model for other emerging AI policy domains.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: IMAGE CLASSIFICATION OF POTATO LEAF DISEASES USING K-NEAREST NEIGHBOR WITH ADDITIONAL CHLOROSIS AND NECROSIS FEATURES
abstract: This study aims to improve the accuracy of potato leaf disease classification by addressing the limitations of existing models that rely solely on general features such as shape, texture, and color. Potato leaf diseases such as early blight and late blight can significantly reduce crop yields if not detected early and accurately. However, many current models overlook critical biological symptoms like chlorosis and necrosis, which impacts detection performance. To overcome this issue, this study proposes a classification approach using the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) algorithm, integrating chlorosis and necrosis features alongside conventional features. The dataset consists of three classes Potato Early blight, Potato Late blight, and Potato healthy, sourced from Kaggle. Feature extraction is conducted using color histograms, shape descriptors, texture analysis, and binary masks for chlorosis and necrosis regions. The model is evaluated using an 80:20 train-test split and assessed using a confusion matrix, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The results show that the addition of chlorosis and necrosis features significantly enhances classification performance, with the best accuracy reaching 90%. This demonstrates that the proposed method effectively improves the KNN algorithm’s ability to distinguish between disease types and healthy leaves, thereby addressing the initial problem of limited classification accuracy.
journal: JOURNAL OF SCIENCE AND APPLIED ENGINEERING

title: CLASSIFICATION OF MALAKA WOVEN CLOTH TITLES BASED ON DIGITAL IMAGES USING THE CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORK (CNN) METHOD
abstract: Malaka woven cloth is one of the cultural heritages of Malaka Regency, East Nusa Tenggara, which has various distinctive motifs such as Marobo, K'nun Rua, and Sorat Los. Unfortunately, public understanding of these motifs is still limited, so a technology-based approach is needed to document and introduce them more widely. This study aims to classify the types of Malaka woven cloth based on digital images using the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) method. Two CNN architectures used in this study are VGG-19 and ResNet-50. The data used are 900 images for training and 300 images for testing, which have gone through pre-processing stages such as cropping, augmentation, and normalization. The test results show that the VGG-19 architecture provides the highest accuracy reaching 99% with very low classification errors, while ResNet-50 is only able to achieve a maximum accuracy of 86% and shows difficulty in distinguishing certain motifs, especially K'nun Rua. Thus, the CNN method, especially the VGG-19 architecture, has proven effective in classifying Malaka woven fabrics, and has the potential to support efforts to preserve and digitize local culture through image processing technology.
journal: JOURNAL OF SCIENCE AND APPLIED ENGINEERING

title: Sustainable nutrition: integrating food systems, environmental science, and diet to advance public and planetary health
abstract: Nutrition science has traditionally focused on dietary intake, nutrient metabolism, physiology, and health outcomes. Although these domains remain fundamental, advancing public health increasingly requires understanding nutrition within the broader systems that shape food production, processing, access, consumption, and environmental sustainability. This Perspective proposes sustainable nutrition as a unifying concept: maintaining nutritional status that supports growth, development, and health across the lifespan while accounting for population needs, context, and the capacity and resilience of food systems. We describe a Nutritional Ecology framework that conceptualizes nutrition as the product of dynamic, reciprocal interactions among human biology, dietary patterns, food systems, and environmental conditions. Agricultural practices affect food quantity, quality, nutrient composition, biodiversity, water resources, greenhouse gas emissions, and ecosystem resilience, while environmental change influences crop productivity, nutrient density, food safety, and nutrition security. Dietary patterns simultaneously affect chronic disease risk and the environmental footprint of food systems. These interdependencies argue against evaluating human health and environmental sustainability in isolation. We therefore call for a transformation toward integrated, systems-based nutrition research that incorporates biological variability, environmental drivers, and system-level interactions. Multidisciplinary collaborations spanning nutrition, food, agricultural, environmental, epidemiologic, computational, systems, and implementation sciences will be essential. Emerging approaches, including systems mapping, network analysis, computational modeling, artificial intelligence, and multiscale data integration, can identify trade-offs and leverage points for intervention. Integrating nutrition, food systems, and environmental science is a scientific necessity for generating evidence across diverse population contexts that supports resilient food systems, effective dietary guidance, improved clinical care, healthier people, and a healthier planet.

title: Computational drug screening for drug-resistant tuberculosis: advances, challenges, and future perspectives
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis , remains a major global health challenge, further exacerbated by the rapid emergence of drug-resistant strains. Despite continuous efforts, the discovery of novel anti-TB agents has lagged behind the evolution of resistance, largely due to the limitations of conventional experimental pipelines and the growing biological complexity of the pathogen. In recent years, computational drug discovery approaches—including virtual screening, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven modeling, and hybrid computational frameworks—have substantially expanded the chemical space accessible for early-stage anti-TB research. However, their translational success remains limited. This discrepancy reflects a fundamental mismatch between target-centric computational paradigms and the multi-scale biological constraints of Mtb , including permeability barriers, efflux mechanisms, metabolic state heterogeneity, lesion-level pharmacokinetics, and regimen-dependent therapeutic effects. This review critically evaluates current computational strategies for anti-TB drug screening, with particular emphasis on their performance under TB-specific biological and resistance constraints. We further explore computational approaches designed to address drug-resistant Mtb , including resistance-aware compound design, host-directed therapy, and combination regimen modeling. Finally, we explore key limitations in current computational pipelines, including challenges in data quality, biological integration, and regimen-level modeling, and propose a shift toward biologically grounded, regimen-aware, and systems-level frameworks. Bridging the gap between in silico prediction and clinical efficacy will require integrating multi-scale biological realism into computational pipelines, enabling more reliable translation of computational advances into effective anti-TB therapeutics.

title: Engineering aptamer-based therapeutics for precision cancer immunotherapy: from molecular targeting to clinical applications
abstract: Although cancer immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer therapy, the clinical efficacy of this approach is restricted due to tumor heterogeneity, immune escape, therapeutic resistance, poor tumor penetration, and toxic side effects. Short single-stranded DNA or RNA oligonucleotides, termed aptamers, have high affinity for a given target, low immunogenicity, and high chemical programmability and are emerging as promising agents for precision cancer therapies and immuno-oncology. This review aims to provide a comprehensive, integrated overview of the development of aptamer-based cancer therapeutics, from molecular engineering and pharmacology to clinical applications and translational potential. The discovery and optimization of tumor and immune-specific aptamers have been enhanced by the development of conventional SELEX, Cell-SELEX, in vivo SELEX, high-throughput sequencing, microfluidic selection, and AI-assisted selection. To enhance nuclease resistance, circulation time, biodistribution, and tumor accumulation, chemical modifications such as PEGylation, 2′-fluoro, 2′-O-methyl, LNAs, phosphorothioate linkages, circularization, and lipid/albumin binding have been developed. Aptamers can directly regulate oncogenic and immune signaling pathways or be used as targeted delivery vehicles for chemotherapeutic drugs, siRNAs, miRNAs, proteins, peptides, and CRISPR-based systems. Moreover, aptamers targeting tumor-associated biomarkers, cancer stem cells, the tumor vasculature, stromal components, and immune regulatory pathways have the potential to selectively remodel the tumor microenvironment. In addition, they are well-suited to other immunotherapy strategies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, photodynamic or photothermal therapy, oncolytic viruses, and cancer vaccines, thereby further supporting a multifunctional, personalized treatment approach. Although there has been significant progress in pre-clinical research, several issues remain regarding pharmacokinetics, tumor penetration, off-target effects, manufacturing, long-term safety, regulatory approval, and clinical validation. Additional advancements in aptamer engineering, nanotechnology, computational design, and biomarker-directed therapy could potentially enable the development of these platforms into successful next-generation precision cancer immunotherapies.

title: Integrating UAV-based multispectral imagery and machine learning to classify glyphosate-resistant palmer amaranth and assess herbicide program efficacy in soybean
abstract: Palmer amaranth is one of the most troublesome and economically important weeds in soybean production, with widespread occurrence of glyphosate-resistant (GR) populations. This study aimed to map and classify GR Palmer amaranth using UAV-based multispectral imagery and evaluate the effects of herbicide programs [preemergence (PRE) only, postemergence (POST) only, and PRE followed by (fb) POST] on Palmer amaranth coverage (early- and late-season) in soybean field in central Louisiana in 2025. A multispectral drone was used to map GR Palmer amaranth, and images were processed into orthomosaic using Pix4DFields and georeferenced in ArcGIS Pro. Weed classification was performed using pixel-based and object-based approaches implemented in ENVI and Orfeo Toolbox (OTB) within QGIS, employing Random Forest (RF), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithms. Both classification methods exhibited high performance, with RF achieving the highest overall accuracy (99%). UAV-based assessments provided a spatiotemporally efficient method for early-season Palmer amaranth mapping and late-season evaluation of residual weed activity following herbicide applications. UAV-derived Palmer amaranth coverage showed moderate positive correlation with the ground-truth weed density. Herbicide programs significantly reduced UAV-derived Palmer amaranth coverage during early-season (P = 0.0004) and late-season (P = 0.0223) assessments. Among the evaluated programs, PRE fb POST resulted in the greatest reduction in weed coverage (4.3%), compared with PRE only (9.2%) and POST-only (8.8%) programs. In conclusion, integrating UAV-based multispectral imagery with machine learning algorithms, particularly RF, offers a promising, automated approach for classification of GR Palmer amaranth and evaluating herbicide program effectiveness across different crop growth stages.

title: LDblockR: a cross-platform R toolkit for multi-format linkage disequilibrium analysis and integrated regional genomics visualization
abstract: Linkage disequilibrium (LD) analysis is central to candidate-gene refinement, haplotype characterization, marker selection, and the interpretation of genome-wide association studies. However, commonly used LD programs often require format conversion, platform-specific binaries, or separate tools for LD calculation, block detection, regional annotation, subgroup comparison, and publication-quality visualization. We developed LDblockR, a pure-R, cross-platform toolkit that unifies regional LD analysis from VCF/VCF.GZ, HapMap, PLINK BED/BIM/FAM or PED/MAP files, and numeric 0/1/2 genotype matrices. LDblockR calculates dosage- or phased-haplotype-based r² and Lewontin’s D′, estimates haplotype frequencies for unphased diploid genotypes using an expectation-maximization procedure, and supports multiple block definitions, tag-SNP selection, LD-neighbor searches, LD decay, haplotype frequencies, population-group comparisons, and batch regional analysis. Its principal contribution is workflow integration and interoperability rather than a new LD estimator: a single R-native object model links heterogeneous genotype inputs, established LD statistics, regional annotation, and publication-ready visualization. In the bundled phased benchmark of 60 diploid samples and 42 variants (861 unique pairs), LDblockR agreed with LDBlockShow 1.41 to the three-decimal precision reported by LDBlockShow, with all r² and D′ values within 0.00051. We additionally analyze the official TASSEL/rTASSEL maize HapMap tutorial dataset, comprising 281 maize inbred lines and 3,093 genome-wide markers. After allele-consistency, missingness, and MAF filtering, 2,526 markers remain, including 428 SNPs on chromosome 1. Chromosome-wide dosage r² analysis covers 91,378 pairs; a highlighted 1-Mb interval contains 16 SNPs and 120 pairs. Independent pairwise calculations match the archived regional reference table to a maximum absolute difference of 5.01 × 10 −13 . This real-data example demonstrates regional LD analysis on crop genotypes with observed missing calls and allele-metadata conflicts. LDblockR therefore provides a transparent bridge between genotype input, regional LD analysis, and post-GWAS interpretation for plant association genetics and breeding.

title: Can the policy-based agricultural credit guarantee influence farmers’ adoption of straw-returning technology?
abstract: Promoting straw-returning technology is an important way to shift agricultural production from extensive, energy-intensive practices to green, sustainable development. This paper uses the fractional probit model to empirically analyze the impact of policy-based agricultural credit guarantee (PACG) on farmers’ adoption of straw-returning technology. The study found that: (1) PACG has a significant role in promoting farmers’ adoption of straw-returning technology, and a consistent conclusion can be drawn after using instrumental variables to address endogeneity problems. (2) PACG promotes farmers’ application of straw-returning technology by promoting their purchase of agricultural social services and matching between the green credit term and the green production cycle. (3) The impact of PACG on farmers’ adoption of straw-returning technology varies among different farmers, and it has a more significant impact on farmers with a lack of formal social capital and a high level of digital literacy, and in agricultural green development pioneer areas.

title: Estimation of agricultural carbon abatement costs using a marginal-productivity-based production-input model: evidence from Fujian Province, China
abstract: The shadow price of agricultural carbon emissions serves as a key indicator for quantifying the cost of carbon reduction in agriculture and for reflecting the associated opportunity costs. It has substantial theoretical and practical relevance for the green development and low-carbon transformation of agriculture under the dual-carbon goals. It holds significant theoretical and practical value for advancing green development and low-carbon transformation in agriculture under the dual-carbon goals. Drawing on marginal productivity theory, this study classifies agricultural carbon emissions as a production factor, builds a translog production function model, and employs ridge regression to address multicollinearity. Using panel data from nine prefecture-level cities in Fujian Province (2010–2023), we measure the shadow prices of agricultural carbon emissions across cities and conduct robustness tests via stochastic frontier analysis (SFA), exploring spatiotemporal evolutionary patterns and the drivers of regional disparities. The key findings are as follows: (1) Fujian’s agricultural carbon emission shadow prices show an overall sustained upward trend, with the economic opportunity cost of per-unit carbon reduction rising consistently across cities. (2) Significant regional disparities exist—the average shadow prices in eastern and northern Fujian remain among the highest in the province, while southern Fujian remains at a lower level, forming a “southeastern coastal–northwestern inland” dual spatial pattern. (3) The shadow price of agricultural carbon emissions varies significantly across regions, with Zhangzhou, Fuzhou, and Nanping having the highest emission reduction costs and Xiamen having the lowest. By quantifying the spatiotemporal characteristics of the costs of agricultural carbon emission reduction in Fujian, this study provides an economic basis for formulating differentiated carbon reduction policies while identifying limitations such as the restricted scope of carbon source accounting and clarifying directions for future research.

title: Digital infrastructure and local food supply diversity: evidence from 257 Chinese prefecture-level cities
abstract: As food system governance increasingly emphasizes supply diversity, nutrition sensitivity, and sustainability, understanding the role of digital infrastructure in diversifying local food supplies has become important. This study examines whether digital infrastructure is associated with greater diversity across nutritionally relevant food categories in China. We construct a Nutritional Food Supply Diversity (NFSD) index and analyze panel data from 257 Chinese prefecture-level cities over 2011 -2023. The analysis examines the association between digital infrastructure and NFSD, potential mechanisms, and heterogeneity across regional development levels, agricultural resource endowments, and urbanization levels. We also address potential endogeneity and conduct robustness checks. Digital infrastructure development is significantly and positively associated with NFSD. A one-standard-deviation increase in the digital infrastructure index is associated with an average increase of approximately 0.0664 index points in NFSD. This association remains robust after addressing potential endogeneity and conducting robustness checks. Mechanism analyses suggest three potential pathways: encouraging the entry of relevant businesses and service providers, thereby expanding producers’ channels of market participation; improving the matching of digital agricultural services; and strengthening feedback on food demand. The association varies with regional development, agricultural resource endowments, and urbanization. The findings suggest that assessments of the food system effects of digital infrastructure should consider both food quantities and the diversity of local supplies across nutritionally relevant categories. These effects appear to depend on the physical agricultural base, market conditions, and stages of urban development. This study provides an empirical framework for coordinating digital infrastructure development, adjustments to agricultural production structures, and policies promoting the diversity of the local food-supply base.

title: How to overcome the productivity pains of digital transformation? The U‑shaped TFP trajectory of Chinese agricultural firms, fixed‑asset constraints and subsidy threshold effects
abstract: Digital transformation has profoundly reshaped agricultural production systems, yet its productivity effects remain insufficiently explored. Using panel data of Chinese listed agricultural firms from 2010 to 2022, this paper examines the effects, mechanisms, moderation, and heterogeneity of digital transformation on total factor productivity (TFP). First, digital transformation exerts a significant U-shaped nonlinear effect on TFP: the linear coefficient is −0.154 ( p < 0.01), and the squared coefficient is 0.036 ( p < 0.01), indicating that early-stage fixed asset accumulation, organizational restructuring, and system adaptation frictions drag down TFP, while after crossing the critical threshold, network synergy and factor allocation optimization drive sustained TFP growth. Second, the fixed asset-to-revenue ratio serves as a key transmission channel, forming a nonlinear mediation path of “digitalization → fixed asset-to-sales ratio → TFP.” Bootstrap tests show that the indirect effect turns from negative to positive as digitalization increases and is significant only at high levels. Third, government subsidies significantly moderate the U-shaped relationship, shifting the turning point leftward and increasing curvature, reflecting a “turning point forward shift and dividend amplification” mechanism. Fourth, the U-shaped relationship is more pronounced for non-state-owned, small-scale, and livestock enterprises. Theoretically, this paper constructs a nonlinear mediation framework of “digitalization–asset structure–TFP,” reveals the inverted U-shaped transmission of the fixed asset-to-revenue ratio, identifies the nonlinear moderating role of government subsidies, and enriches research on digital transformation and agricultural TFP. Practically, it suggests establishing a “pain period” tolerance mechanism, shifting subsidies toward soft support, and precisely supporting non-state-owned, small-scale, and livestock enterprises to release productivity dividends.

title: Early-Winter Thermal Responses of East–West and North–South Tomato Ridge Layouts in a Chinese Solar Greenhouse
abstract: This exploratory study compared early-winter thermal conditions in east–west (E-W) and north–south (N-S) tomato ridge blocks within one Chinese solar greenhouse from 22 November to 3 December 2025. A thin-film partition separated the blocks. We measured canopy-air, soil-surface, plastic-film, north-wall, and rear-slope temperatures and used transient computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to interpret spatial patterns. Mean canopy-air temperatures were 15.34 °C (E-W) and 15.22 °C (N-S), whereas mean soil-surface temperatures were 14.43 and 13.31 °C, respectively. On a representative cloudy day, daytime soil-surface temperature was 2.48 °C lower in the N-S block. The CFD model reproduced broad surface-temperature cycles on both representative days; canopy-air comparison was restricted to the sunny day from 12:30 to 21:00. Under the tested operating conditions, layout-related contrasts were more evident at the soil surface than in mean canopy air. Because the comparison involved two unreplicated blocks within one greenhouse and did not include crop-response measurements, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory thermal associations rather than evidence of a general causal or agronomic advantage of either ridge orientation.

title: A Flexible Chemiresistive Sensor Combining Halogen Bonding and Swelling-Mediated Permeation for Field Detection of Plant Stress VOCs
abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) act as vital early indicators of biotic or abiotic stress in plants, and their accurate, timely detection is significant for early crop health warning. To address the need for field-deployable sensors with high selectivity, operational stability, and practical usability, we developed a resistive VOC sensor with a sensing layer of 4-fluorothiophenol (FTP)-functionalized silver nanowires embedded in a poly(vinyl alcohol)/poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)-poly(styrenesulfonate) matrix. Reversible halogen bonding between FTP ligands and aldehyde/ketone groups enables analytes to induce swelling of the PVA matrix, producing significant signal amplification by altering resistance, while aldehydes and ketones are differentiated by polarity and steric hindrance, with optimal responsiveness to aldehydes. The sensor achieves a linear response to aldehydes over 25–200 ppm (R2 = 0.99), an estimated detection limit of 11.6 ppb, and response and recovery times of ~30 s, with reliable resistance to humidity and temperature variations. Combining stomatal observation with real-time sensor recordings of mechanical damage and pre-symptomatic early blight, we monitored plant stress multidimensionally, detecting disease signals three days before visible symptoms. Principal component analysis establishes stress-type fingerprints, and long short-term memory forecasts VOC emission trends, providing diagnostic classification and predictive intelligence for early intervention and a low-cost, non-destructive pathway for plant health monitoring.

title: Uncertainty- and Age-Aware UWB Fleet Scheduling with an Admitted-Cycle Energy Proxy
abstract: Industrial ultra-wideband (UWB) tags can share a limited ranging-update budget through gateway-side admission control. We evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted priority rule that combines predictive uncertainty, nonlinear age of information (AoI), and a cold-start indicator, using dimensionally explicit coefficients. The dataset contains 166,142 cleaned range events from seven tags and eight anchors. Forecasting is evaluated on sessions held out in chronological order within each device. Replay draws 16 paired synthetic fleets of 100 virtual tags from 598 overlapping 80 s windows of three test sessions of one physical tag. Two state-update assumptions are compared. Under causal state updates using only recorded observations, the proposed priority rule does not outperform periodic scheduling at any evaluated budget from 5% to 40%; at a 20% evaluation budget, its mean absolute raw-range reconstruction error is 10.23% higher. At the same budget, retrospective replay with linearly interpolated state updates yields lower error (0.361 m versus 0.366 m) and an estimated matched-quality reduction of 2.49% in admitted evaluation cycles (95% paired-replay interval: 1.58–3.46%). This reduction is conditional on the interpolated retrospective replay assumptions, which use subsequent observations to reconstruct controller state non-causally. Admitted-cycle count serves only as a proxy for relative tag energy under an equal per-cycle cost assumption; electrical energy consumption was not directly measured. The replay evidence is limited to three physical sessions from a single device, so these findings do not establish generalizability to independent devices, environments, or simultaneous physical fleets.

title: Diversity of Rhopalosiphum padi L. Collected in Different Geographic Zones of Russia in Relation to the Type of Development
abstract: The bird cherry-oat aphid (Rhopalosiphum padi L.) is a major pest of cereal crops, characterized by significant variability in reproductive strategies and population-genetic structure. However, the nuclear-genetic and clonal structure of R. padi populations in Russia remain insufficiently studied. We investigated the genetic diversity and clonal structure of 71 R. padi clones collected in the northwestern and southern regions of European Russia and analyzed their association with life-cycle types. Reproductive strategies were determined experimentally based on traits such as autumn remigration, production of sexual morphs, and overwintering ability. Genetic variation was assessed using seven microsatellite loci; genetic relationships were analyzed via multilocus genotypes, analysis of molecular variance, Neighbor-Joining and UPGMA clustering methods, and principal coordinate analysis. A total of 116 alleles were identified. Northwestern populations exhibited complete multilocus diversity (each clone represented a unique multilocus genotype), whereas repeated genotypes were found in southern populations (G/N = 0.83). Genetic differentiation between regions was significant based on allele frequencies (FST = 0.092; p = 0.001) but not based on allele size variation (RST = 0.019; p = 0.085). Northwestern populations were holocyclic, while southern populations were predominantly anholocyclic, although in-between life-cycle types were found in both geographic regions. Three microsatellite alleles (R5.29b_170, R2.73_286, and S17b_161) showed an association with the life cycle type; based on these, a “life cycle index” (LCI) was developed, enabling the classification of analyzed clones in accordance with experimental phenotyping results. The data indicate significant genetic diversity and incomplete geographic differentiation among Russian R. padi populations and also suggest candidate molecular markers for further study of the genetic basis of reproductive strategies.

title: Regional Water-Erosion Screening in Northeastern Algeria Using RUSLE and Machine-Learning Classification
abstract: Water erosion poses a persistent challenge for agricultural soils and catchment management in Mediterranean landscapes. We examined Skikda Province, northeastern Algeria, using a revised RUSLE screening framework that combines a CHIRPS-based rainfall-erosivity estimate for 2000–2024, the soil-erodibility dataset, terrain-derived LS, land-cover-based C and P = 1. The reference map covers 26,821,605 valid output cells (3798.21 km2); Model A has a median of 6.05 and a mean of 137.36 in nominal t ha−1 yr−1, with a strongly skewed upper tail. A matched, spatially buffered evaluation of Random Forest, LightGBM, XGBoost and CatBoost used 60,599 complete samples. LightGBM achieved macro-F1 = 0.942 with all 12 predictors but only 0.469 when the four factors defining the RUSLE target were excluded. This contrast underscores that the classifiers mainly reproduce model-derived erosion classes. An external field comparison was possible at 77 of 100 georeferenced sites; at an exploratory threshold of 20 t ha−1 yr−1, site-level accuracy was 87.0%, sensitivity 58.8% and specificity 95.0%. Field observations indicate visible erosion features rather than measured annual soil loss. Uncertainty in empirically estimated erosivity, crop-specific C values and terrain-derived LS limits the quantitative interpretation of absolute erosion rates.

title: OBB-PBD: Extending Parallel Box Decoding to Oriented Bounding Boxes for Referring Expression Grounding in Aerial Imagery
abstract: Referring expression grounding in overhead imagery requires oriented bounding boxes rather than horizontal ones, since aerial objects appear at arbitrary orientations. Most grounding models emit box coordinates sequentially; Parallel Box Decoding (PBD) instead predicts all geometry slots in one forward pass, but only for four-coordinate horizontal boxes. We extend this block-aligned interface to a six-slot oriented representation using a double-angle parameterization. Rather than assuming correctness from a decreasing loss curve, we verify the extension with image/prompt-shuffle controls and visibility/leakage probes, which show that the corrected model depends on both the image and the prompt rather than on prompt statistics alone. On the aerial vehicle visual grounding (AVVG) benchmark, whose targets are genuinely oriented, the extended model improves rotated intersection over union (rotIoU) from 0.1253 for the zero-shot baseline to 0.303 +/- 0.012 (mean +/- standard deviation over three training seeds) across the complete 6139-record test split spanning all 120 images. Learning oriented boxes rather than their axis-aligned envelopes adds 0.055 +/- 0.008 rotIoU beyond a matched control (per-seed 95% confidence intervals all excluding zero), whereas block expansion alone yields no rotIoU gain distinguishable from zero.

title: Rotation-Equivariant Feature Learning and Dual-Head Decoupling for Oriented Remote Sensing Object Detection
abstract: Oriented remote sensing object detection (ORSOD) remains challenging because objects usually appear at arbitrary rotations, with large aspect-ratio variations and dense spatial layouts. Although recent detectors have achieved notable progress, most still rely on standard convolutional backbones, whose limited inherent rotation equivariance weakens robustness to rotated targets and reduces localization reliability. To address these issues, this paper proposes RedhDet, an ORSOD framework based on rotation-equivariant feature learning and dual-head decoupling. Specifically, a Ladder-Structured Implicitly Equivariant Network (LSIEN) is developed as the backbone to extract rotation-equivariant features in a soft manner, without relying on strictly constrained kernels or equivariant pre-trained weights. In addition, a decoupled dual-head architecture is introduced, in which a fully connected branch is used for classification and a convolutional branch is used for bounding box regression, thereby better matching the distinct requirements of semantic recognition and precise localization. Experimental results on the DOTA-1.0 and HRSC2016 datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. On the DOTA-1.0 test set, RedhDet improves mAP50 by 2.09% and mAP75 by 14.84% over the baseline. On HRSC2016, gains of 14.12% and 51.85% are achieved for mAP50 and mAP75, respectively. With multi-scale training and testing, the proposed method achieves 80.40% mAP on DOTA-1.0, indicating its effectiveness and competitiveness for ORSOD.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Agriculture for Smallholder Farming: An Africa-Centred Scoping Review of Global South Evidence
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied in agriculture, but evidence concerning its relevance to smallholder farming remains heterogeneous and geographically uneven. This scoping review mapped evidence on AI and related digital agricultural technologies, their applications, adoption conditions, and equity and governance implications for smallholder farming in Africa-centred Global South contexts. This review was reported using PRISMA-ScR guidance. Across Google Scholar, Web of Science and Scopus, 150 potentially relevant records were retained for the documented screening process, and 42 sources were included. Sources were classified as AI-specific evidence, AI-enabled systems or contextual digital-agriculture evidence and synthesised thematically. The literature addressed crop monitoring, yield prediction, irrigation, climate-risk management and digital advisory services. However, it was dominated by African evidence and included empirical studies, technical demonstrations, reviews, policy analyses and conceptual papers. The mapped sources more often described technological feasibility and adoption conditions than sustained effects on productivity, income, resilience or farmer welfare. Recurring constraints included cost, connectivity, digital literacy, language, trust and institutional capacity. Equity and governance concerns included data rights, gender inclusion, algorithmic bias and unequal benefit distribution, although many were conceptually rather than empirically documented. The findings support context-sensitive, farmer-centred implementation while highlighting the need for longitudinal and geographically broader research.

title: Penerapan Peramalan Tingkat Penghunian Kamar sebagai Dasar Pengambilan Keputusan Manajerial di Sadara Resort Tanjung Benoa, Bali
abstract: Room Occupancy Rate (ROR) is an important indicator of hotel performance and serves as a basis for operational planning and managerial decision-making. Fluctuations in ROR influenced by trend and seasonal patterns require hotels to use accurate forecasting methods to anticipate changes in demand. This study aims to analyze the characteristics of Room Occupancy Rate (ROR) data, generate ROR forecasts using the Holt-Winters Additive method, analyze the accuracy and feasibility of the forecasting model, and examine the implications of the forecasting results for managerial decision-making at Sadara Resort Tanjung Benoa, Bali. This study employs a quantitative approach using a time series method. The data consist of monthly ROR data from Sadara Resort for the period of January 2023 to June 2026, comprising 42 observations. The Holt-Winters Additive method was selected because the data demonstrate trend and seasonal patterns. Model accuracy and feasibility were evaluated using MAPE, MAE, RMSE, Stationary R-squared, R-squared, and the Ljung-Box Q test. The research results indicate that the Room Occupancy Rate (TPK) data exhibits fluctuation and seasonal patterns that recur annually. The Additive Holt-Winters model yielded a MAPE of 6.242%, an MAE of 4.806, and an RMSE of 7.073. The MAPE value was calculated based on model-building data from January 2023 to June 2026 and falls into the "highly accurate" category according to Lewis's (1982) criteria. The Ljung-Box Q test result showed a significance value of 0.487 (> 0.05); thus, the residuals do not exhibit significant autocorrelation, and the model is deemed suitable for generating future forecasts. Forecasting results for the period of July 2026 to December 2027 indicate that the highest projected TPK is 96.80% in August 2027, while the lowest is 64.70% in March 2027. Based on this evaluation, the Additive Holt-Winters model demonstrates an excellent fit with the model-building data and is suitable for estimating future TPK. Sadara Resort can utilize these forecasting results to formulate revenue management, operational, budgetary, and marketing strategies aligned with demand conditions for each period.
journal: Ranah Research : Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Development

title: Soil and water bioengineering between knowledge and governance: practitioners' conceptual positioning, improvement priorities, and innovation pathways
abstract: Soil and Water Bioengineering (SWB) is an established discipline increasingly reframed within emerging policy concepts such as Nature-Based Solutions (NBS) and Green and Blue Infrastructure (GBI). However, it remains unclear how this conceptual repositioning translates into professional practice, and whether governance and institutional frameworks keep pace with practitioners’ needs. This study investigates the science-policy interface of SWB in Italy by examining how practitioners position the discipline conceptually, what barriers they encounter, and which improvement priorities and innovation pathways they identify. Data were collected through a questionnaire administered in 2024, yielding 1,428 responses classified into specialists (professionally involved in SWB, 26.54%), familiar (aware but not practicing, 50.49%), and unfamiliar respondents (no prior SWB knowledge, 22.97%). Results reveal a specialist core rooted in agriculture/forestry and geology, with familiar respondents recognizing SWB functions and expressing interest in training. While practitioners broadly situate SWB within the NBS framework – treating NBS and GBI as umbrella concepts - this conceptual alignment does not correspond to coherent intervention classification, exposing significant ambiguity at the science-practice interface. Practitioners identify improvement needs more clearly than innovation pathways: training, institutional awareness, regulatory clarity, monitoring, and vegetation management rank as priorities, whereas innovation is primarily conceived through a techno-scientific lens, encompassing materials, plant-based components, and digital tools. These findings suggest that SWB development is constrained less by technical gaps than by governance deficits, weak standardization, and insufficient long-term monitoring frameworks. The study offers actionable insights for policy actors seeking to embed nature-based practices more effectively within regulatory and institutional structures.

title: Fabric: An Agentic AI Workspace for Natural-Language Data Analysis and Multi-Tool Task Execution
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence systems combine language-model interaction with tools that perform operations beyond text generation. In data analytics, an integrated workspace must support dataset handling, analytical computation, visualization, and controlled tool execution while making the limits of each capability clear. This paper presents Fabric, a software project intended to bring conversational model access and data-oriented workflows into a common workspace. The paper documents its architecture and a preliminary local evaluation on Windows 11 using Node.js v24.15.0. JavaScript syntax validation passed, and a targeted evaluation suite reported seven passing tests. A synthetic local benchmark processed 10,000 rows and verified a sum of 505,000. The broader test suite reported 415 passing tests and four failures, including a Windows filesystem-permission verification failure and spreadsheet-processing failures. These observations support only narrow claims about selected components. They do not establish end-to-end model accuracy, secure execution isolation, production readiness, or performance under real-world workloads. The paper reports the methodology, results, limitations, and further validation required for a rigorous assessment of Fabric as an AI-assisted data-analysis workspace.

title: SlowLab: Benchmarking Autonomous AI Agents on a Year of Experiments They Cannot Undo
abstract: AI agents are increasingly proposed as autonomous experimenters, yet the benchmarks that test them mostly offer cheap experiments that answer at once. Experiments in physical facilities are different: they take months, occupy scarce equipment and cannot be undone. We present SlowLab, a benchmark in which an agent runs a one-year campaign in four simulated greenhouse compartments on a site whose crop, facility and prices are hidden. The agent decides when to plant which climate policy, whether to stop a crop and which measurements to read while crops grow, and at the end recommends one policy, which a private evaluator scores in weather the agent never saw. In a preregistered study on 48 unseen sites, three low-cost language-model agents ended near a standard grower setting and clearly below a Bayesian-optimisation baseline that starts from that setting. They ran the facility as two synchronous batches, so measurements taken during the season never changed what they planted, and these measurements improved no method's result. Letting other methods re-read the evidence a campaign had collected did not yield significantly better recommendations, which points to where the models start and which experiments they try. Code is released under the MIT license.

title: Regional prediction of hematoma expansion from non-contrast computed tomography in spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage patients
abstract: Background The combination of hematoma location, expansion and final volume influence neurological outcome. The aim of this study was to derive and validate a quantitative and interpretable region-based NCCT image feature model for predicting hematoma expansion. Methods The Ethnic/Racial Variations of Intracerebral Hemorrhage(ERICH) study was used for derivation and the Virtual International Trials in Stroke Archive(VISTA) was used for validation. NCCT images at presentation and 24+/-6hours were pre-processed, segmented and categorized into lobar, basal ganglia or thalamic regions. Hematoma expansion was defined by region and according to its effect on clinical outcome. Transport-based morphometry (TBM) produced a unique transport-based representation from each NCCT hematoma image. Linear classifiers applied to transport representations were used to derive a predictive model. The regional TBM model's performance was compared to alternate methods using AUROC analyses. Results The derivation dataset included 574 patients, comprising 162 lobar, 257 basal ganglia and 155 thalamic hematomas. The validation dataset included 196 patients, comprising 31 lobar, 119 basal ganglia and 46 thalamic hematomas. A combined regional model predicted hematoma expansion in the validation dataset with an AUROC of 0.787. The principal image features which varied by location were size, heterogeneity, eccentricity and density distribution towards the hematoma periphery. The regional TBM model outperformed alternative clinician based and machine-learning methods. Conclusions TBM discriminated and visualized regional features of hematoma expansion from presentation NCCT scans. This provides preliminary evidence for regional radiographic features of hematoma expansion. It has the potential to improve hematoma expansion prediction and understanding of hematoma expansion pathophysiology.

title: Exploring perceptual straightness in learned visual representations
abstract: Humans have been shown to use a "straightened" encoding to represent the natural visual world as it evolves in time (Hénaff et al. 2019). In the context of discrete video sequences, "straightened" means that changes between frames follow a more linear path in representation space at progressively deeper levels of processing. While deep convolutional networks are often proposed as models of human visual processing, many do not straighten natural videos. In this paper, we explore the relationship between network architecture, differing types of robustness, biologically-inspired filtering mechanisms, and representational straightness in response to time-varying input; we identify strengths and limitations of straightness as a useful way of evaluating neural network representations. We find that (1) adversarial training leads to straighter representations in both CNN and transformer-based architectures but (2) this effect is task-dependent, not generalizing to tasks such as segmentation and frame-prediction, where straight representations are not favorable for predictions; and nor to other types of robustness. In addition, (3) straighter representations impart temporal stability to class predictions, even for out-of-distribution data. Finally, (4) biologically-inspired elements increase straightness in the early stages of a network, but do not guarantee increased straightness in downstream layers of CNNs. We show that straightness is an easily computed measure of representational robustness and stability, as well as a hallmark of human representations with benefits for computer vision models.

title: Machine Learning Applications in the Solar Interior and Atmosphere
abstract: The solar interior and atmosphere constitute a strongly coupled, multiscale dynamical system defined by continuous temporal evolution. Predicting the state of this system requires modeling physical interactions that span disparate spatial and temporal scales, constrained by heterogeneous and sparse data. This chapter formalizes the Sun within the mathematical framework of dynamical systems theory, defining a global state vector ($\vec{S}$) governed by thermodynamical, kinetic, and magnetic properties. Because solar observations represent projected, multi-modal, and partially observable measurements ($\vec{O}[\vec{S}]$) of this hidden state, pure physics-based deduction is fundamentally constrained. We present a unifying thesis: the primary role of machine learning in heliophysics is to act as a structured family of mathematical operators---specifically Inference ($\mathcal{I}$), Emulation ($\mathcal{E}$), Propagation ($\mathcal{P}$), and Control ($\mathcal{C}$)---that reconstruct, simulate, and couple this global state vector across disparate physical layers. By framing the vast, multi-disciplinary literature within this unified state-space taxonomy, we demonstrate how data-driven techniques bridge observational gaps to resolve hidden multiscale couplings and dramatically accelerate the simulation of non-linear processes, establishing a rigorous pathway to predict the global evolution of the Sun.

title: SearchHorizonBench: A Benchmark for Search Value in AI Agents
abstract: AI agents must decide when another search is worth its cost. Answer-success probabilities capture question difficulty, while this decision requires estimating the additional benefit of search. We introduce SearchHorizonBench, a benchmark for learning and evaluating search value from execution experience. Paired continuations and repeated executions separate expected search gain from generation noise and connect prediction quality to decision utility. The resource contains 45,632 executions across 3,168 questions. On 1,632 held-out questions, historical calibration reduces Brier error by 16.2%, with the improvement concentrated in success-level information. Search gains have a standard deviation of 21.4 percentage points, and tested historical estimators explain less than 2% of this variance in point estimates. Matched-configuration learning curves probe this distinction across training scales. At the reference token price, free selection observations yield a 2.49-point utility opportunity over the best constant action, driven primarily by gain information. Reusable histories, frozen splits, strong baselines and scoring tools provide a common foundation for developing and evaluating value-aware search agents.

title: iPrefBench: A User-Centric Benchmark for Personalized Mobile Use Agents
abstract: An agent that truly knows and acts on behalf of its user has been a long-standing promise of AI assistants. Computer-use agents bring this promise within reach by capably executing fully specified tasks across apps. However, real-world user requests are often underspecified. To act correctly for the particular user, an agent must infer some missing information from the user's activity history and ask for other information that only the user can provide, without making unsupported assumptions or burdening the user with unnecessary questions. We present iPrefBench, a benchmark for evaluating the infer and ask capabilities of personal mobile-use agents in an executable iOS environment with an interactive simulated user. Grounded in a coherent persona with 3,051 past activity events, iPrefBench comprises 130 underspecified user tasks across 26 apps. Each omitted user-dependent requirement is, by construction, either history-inferable or ask-only. iPrefBench evaluates personalized mobile agents on both whether agents complete tasks correctly for the user (i.e., personalized task completion) and whether they seek user input when necessary (i.e., user-agent interaction). Evaluation of 7 frontier agents reveals a substantial gap between execution and personalization. Agents achieve high action completion scores (up to 91.6%) but low full task success (up to 47.7%) because personalization lags behind. They especially struggle with ask-only information, failing to request enough necessary information. Our findings highlight a challenge for personalized agents in knowing what to infer and when to ask. We hope that iPrefBench can serve as a valuable testbed for building agents that know their user and work with them.

title: From Sentinel-2 to 1-m Imagery: Real-World $\times 10$ Cross-Sensor Super-Resolution via Visual Autoregressive Modeling
abstract: Reconstructing 1-m imagery from Sentinel-2 combines two difficulties. The input and the reference are observed by different satellites, which differ in spatial resolution, spectral response, radiometry, acquisition time, and local geometry, so no synthetic degradation operator links them. The required magnification of ten in each spatial dimension also far exceeds the factors of two to four at which remote sensing super-resolution is usually developed. We study this real-world $\times 10$ problem using YREB-SR, which pairs 2022 Sentinel-2 RGB composites with 2022 Jilin-1 RGB references resampled to a 1-m grid over the Yangtze River Economic Belt. The benchmark contains 11,559 geographically matched scene pairs, with 6,409, 2,135, and 3,015 assigned to training, validation, and testing, respectively. We develop CrossVAR, a visual autoregressive model that predicts the 1-m latent as a nine-scale hierarchy conditioned on the Sentinel-2 input and estimates the remaining quantization residual with a diffusion refiner run without injected noise. Complete 1600 $\times$ 1600 scenes are reconstructed in overlapping windows that start on the Sentinel-2 pixel grid, as every training patch does, and every window is decoded at the size on which the decoder was trained before the windows are blended with Gaussian weights. On all 3,015 test scenes, CrossVAR achieves 27.60 dB PSNR, 0.7725 SSIM, 0.1451 LPIPS, and 7.15 FID, the best value of each metric among the compared methods. These results establish a strong autoregressive baseline for large-scale cross-sensor reconstruction. To facilitate reproducibility, the source code and implementation are publicly available at https://github.com/SHANOAL/RSSR.

title: SceneAgent: An Agentic Pipeline from 3D and 4D Captures to Simulation Environments
abstract: Visual captures provide detailed scene appearance, but converting them into interactive simulation environments requires object reconstruction, physical modeling, and correction of intermediate errors. We present SceneAgent, an agentic pipeline that coordinates these steps through simulator-based visual inspection and repair. The pipeline processes 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), photogrammetry, LiDAR captures, AI-generated 3DGS scenes, and 4D videos of dynamic scenes, and combines object segmentation, physical parameter estimation, part decomposition, articulation, and deformable simulation. To support policy learning, SceneAgent generates diverse object variants ("digital sisters") and scripted demonstrations. On a cluttered bin scene from GraspClutter6D, SceneAgent raises F1 at 1 cm for every coding agent with scorable outputs both with and without its skills, and its reconstructions are better than SimFoundry: all agent configurations exceed SimFoundry's F1 score, with a best of 60.75% versus 6.9%. On three dynamic scenes from 4DCodeBench, SceneAgent raises the mean dynamic IoU of Gemini 4 Argon from 0.86% to 99.09%. We further demonstrate diverse simulated interactions and preliminary policy transfer to a real robot.

title: Babysitting AI Agents: A User-Centered Taxonomy and Study of Agentic Delegation Failures
abstract: Users are increasingly delegating tasks to AI agents, allowing agents to perform long-running, multi-step workflows on their behalf. However, agents may perform these tasks in ways that depart from users' expectations for how they should be carried out, leading to what we call agentic delegation failures. We leverage a large corpus of 163,487 Reddit posts, describing AI agent use, to develop MANDATE: a taxonomy of 23 failure categories organized into seven groups. A follow-up study with 73 AI agent users examined the relationship between prevalence and perceptions of severity and noticeability, finding that failures rated as more severe are considered harder to notice, and that prior experience with a failure is associated with greater noticeability. Finally, we assess the maturity of research on each failure and identify commonly encountered failures that have received little attention (e.g., agents running without making progress). Our findings inform opportunities to make delegation easier for users to oversee and better studied by the research community.

title: Adaptive Probe Design for Auditing AI Agents
abstract: How can we audit an AI agent before it is safe and practical to deploy? A central task is to estimate its performance under the intended deployment policy (the target policy). However, historical observations may provide insufficient coverage of relevant states and actions, limiting evaluation reliability. We propose CAD (Flow-Constrained Audit Design), a framework that combines historical logs with a limited budget of targeted audit trials (probes). The key idea is to design probes that minimize the mismatch between the combined state-action visitation distribution (occupancy) of the logs and probes and that of the target policy. We formulate this design as a constrained convex optimization problem, directing probes toward regions important to the target policy but underrepresented in historical logs. We develop an adaptive algorithm that iteratively estimates environment dynamics and occupancies to update the probe policy. We link occupancy mismatch to bounds on mean squared error and asymptotic variance, and establish error bounds for CAD's adaptive estimator in finite and continuous state spaces. Experiments in Gridworld, LunarLander, and autonomous driving using real-world logs from the Waymo Open Motion Dataset show improved estimation accuracy over alternative data collection and probe designs.

title: The Physical Cost of Context: Quality-Constrained Resource Accounting for Coding Agents
abstract: Coding agents resend a growing context on every model call, and context policies are usually judged by the prompt tokens they save. Executed work also depends on call count and prefix reuse: a caching runtime prefills only the tokens after the longest cached prefix. A shorter prompt can therefore cost more if it rewrites cached history. Our quality-gated protocol splits executed prefill into logical prompt minus reused prefix and measures KV residency, time, and energy. On 450 localization cases derived from SWE-rebench V2, preloading ten retrieved blocks (Eager) and adding anchored history compaction (Compact) both pass a five-point non-inferiority gate. In a separate 900-cell study, Eager cuts model calls by 35.7% and the GPU-energy proxy by 33.2% against on-demand search (Grep); Compact saves nothing further. Enabling prefix caching leaves Eager's prompt volume similar (+8.3%; its 95% CI spans zero) but cuts its uncached prefill by 67.7%. Deleting history can turn a token saving into extra work. With mini-SWE-agent on 100 SWE-bench Verified instances, keeping only the last five observations (Mask-5) cuts Eager's prompt volume by 33.3% but loses 135.9k reusable tokens per task. Uncached prefill rises by 608.5%, the energy proxy by 125.6%, and the policy misses the quality gate. Policies thus save physical work by shortening the trajectory and can multiply it by editing reusable history.

title: From AI-assisted to AI-native Industrial Control: Architecture, Agent Design, and Challenges
abstract: The integration of AI and industrial control is rapidly transforming industrial automation. However, current approaches remain predominantly AI-assisted, where AI functions are incorporated as auxiliary components without fundamentally altering the underlying architecture of industrial control systems. Consequently, the potential of AI to enable higher levels of autonomy, adaptability, and continuous evolution remains underutilized. This paper proposes an AI-native industrial control paradigm, which reconceptualizes industrial control systems by positioning AI as the intrinsic core rather than an external enhancement. The proposed paradigm is built upon an AI-native infrastructure and a collection of collaborative agentic AIs, each encapsulating a set of advanced skills. Among them, the industrial control agent plays a central role in orchestrating the system lifecycle. Through this paradigm, industrial control shifts from a closed, capability-oriented, human-driven, and passive engineering process to an open, task-oriented, intent-driven, and autonomous solution delivery mechanism. The paper further analyzes the key challenges of the AI-native paradigm from both AI and industrial control perspectives, including issues related to AI model reliability, formal verification, real-time assurance, and heterogeneous resource orchestration. Overall, this work outlines a forward-looking vision for industrial control in the AI era and identifies critical research directions toward autonomous, evolvable, and adaptive control systems in complex and dynamic industrial environments.

title: ToDoPro: Faster and Better Reference-Based Generation: Early Token Reduction via Downsampled Self-Probing
abstract: Recent generic reference-based image generation models natively support multiple conditions by concatenating all reference image and text tokens into a joint sequence processed by a single Diffusion Transformer (DiT). However, this versatile paradigm comes at an efficiency cost: accommodating multiple references leads to a token explosion, incurring massive $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ computational complexity. Most acceleration methods operate inside the DiT, showing limited capability in reducing spatial redundancy and failing to alleviate peak VRAM. While some pre-model token reduction alternatives exist, they inevitably introduce external models. This raises a question: Is it possible to achieve acceleration and memory savings while preserving compatibility with in-model techniques and requiring no additional parameters? In this work, we realize this goal by proposing the early Token reduction via Downsampled self-Probing (ToDoPro). By executing a few denoising steps on spatially $2\times$ downsampled reference images, this cheap probing stage utilizes the DiT model itself to effectively and efficiently extract reference token importance. Using the probed importance, we apply a hierarchical reduction before the main denoising stage: we completely discard low-importance tokens, substitute mid-importance tokens with their downsampled counterparts to cheaply preserve global context, and keep high-importance tokens. Experiments across three base models and two benchmarks demonstrate that our early reduction accelerates inference significantly and mitigates peak GPU memory. Furthermore, we can improve generation quality by safely filtering out noisy, uninformative reference tokens, enabling the model to concentrate its limited attention capacity on genuinely useful tokens. The code will be released at https://github.com/scy639/ToDoPro

title: Towards Spatio-Temporal Intelligence Systems in Urban Space: A Twin-Agent Perspective
abstract: Cities must coordinate domains like infrastructure, mobility, environmental management, emergency response, and public services as conditions evolve. An urban Spatio-Temporal Intelligence (STI) system helps the city monitor citywide states, analyze problems, plan and execute interventions, and adapt through feedback, making urban governance more timely, effective, and transparent. Recent urban twinning and agentic AI techniques provide foundations for such systems. From a twin-agent perspective, this survey takes a system-level view of how these disparate techniques can be coherently integrated into an urban STI system. Specifically, we review how the twin reconstructs and represents a persistent, information-enriched urban environment, and how the agent understands the twin via interfaces, reasons over it, acts reliably, and continuously evolves with the city. Built upon this synthesis, we summarize a two-loop blueprint, where an inner agent loop for grounding, reasoning, and verification, and an outer system loop linking data, twin, agentic action, feedback, and update. We then use this to structure an STI research agenda and show how a shared prototype supports diverse urban domains.

title: Interpretable Brain Age Prediction Using White Matter Fiber Orientation Distributions with Rotation-Equivariant Deep Learning
abstract: Diffusion MRI (dMRI) provides information about white matter microstructure that can support brain age prediction. However, many existing prediction models use diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) scalar metrics that omit orientation information. Deep learning is increasingly used for brain age prediction, but conventional CNNs do not explicitly respect the geometric structure of orientation-dependent features. We present an interpretable brain age prediction framework that combines white matter fiber orientation distributions (WM-FODs) with an SE(3) (Special Euclidean group in 3 dimensions) equivariant CNN. The network operates directly on spherical harmonic (SH) coefficients of the FOD, preserving their transformation properties under rotation. Evaluation in 692 participants aged 36-90 years from the Human Connectome Project Aging dataset showed that the combined framework outperformed the evaluated DTI-based models and conventional CNNs. Averaging predictions from five cross-validation models yielded a mean absolute error of 3.54 years and Pearson's correlation of 0.958. Our results indicated that the performance advantage depended on combining WM-FODs with equivariant processing. Prediction accuracy was highest at a maximum SH order of Lmax = 2 and declined at higher orders. Tract-level occlusion, where each segmented tract was masked in turn, revealed age-dependent patterns of model sensitivity, with importance peaks in frontal projection pathways at 36-44 years, the fornix at 45-54 years, the callosal isthmus at 55-64 years, the middle cerebellar peduncle at 65-74 years, and the callosal genu at 75-90 years. These findings support rotation-equivariant processing of WM-FODs for accurate brain age prediction with anatomically interpretable model sensitivity.

title: Transporting Quantiles to Codebook: Scalable Vector Quantization without Codebook Collapse
abstract: Effective discrete representation learning with VQ-VAE serves as a fundamental component of modern autoregressive generative models. However, it is widely known to suffer from codebook collapse and inefficient code utilization. To address this issue, we propose FlowVQ, a simple yet effective alternative to standard vector quantization by formulating neural quantization as a joint modeling and clustering process. Specifically, we learn the latent space using a lightweight flow matching model alongside training, corresponding to a probability flow ODE that transports an often fixed well-behaved source distribution while preserving probability mass. Based on this, we define the codebook C_1 by transporting even-quantile partitioned prior codes C_0 from the source space through the learned flow, and obtaining the Voronoi centroids under the induced distribution, leading to a structured discretization. We evaluated on image tokenization and generation, as well as on two tasks requiring high-precision tokenization, demonstrating scalability and improved expressivity of the codebook with full utilization.

title: Ethics by Configuration: AI Ethics Principles in Coding Agent Instructions
abstract: As AI coding agents become integral to software development, projects increasingly utilise configuration files, such as context files and skills, to govern agent behaviour. While AI ethics principles are widely used in research and policy, little is known about whether and how they are reflected when developers configure coding agents. We studied ethics principles in 40,079 configuration files across 8,893 GitHub repositories. Using a validated large language model (LLM) classification, we measured the prevalence of ethics-related statements, and qualitatively analysed 702 stratified samples across 679 files to uncover the ethical considerations reflected in these files and the parties they concern. Ethics-related statements appeared in 39.4% of files and 61.5% of repositories; concentrated on accountability, transparency, privacy protection, and reliability; and occurred more often in task-specific files such as skills than in project-wide context files. Our qualitative analysis identified 30 categories of ethical considerations, which take the form of concrete rules for the agent. Accountability appeared mainly as requirements for human approval, transparency as explain and honestly report the agent's work, and fairness as accessibility and localisation. These considerations reveal a difference in focus. Whereas public ethics frameworks aim to protect society and end users, configuration files mainly concern developers, maintainers, and community members in the development workflow. Ethics-related content appeared mainly in prose-based files, and whether agents follow these instructions remains untested. We discuss the implications for practitioners, researchers, and policymakers.

title: DecoyCount: Evaluating Visual-Reasoning Misalignment in Counting
abstract: Visual counting benchmarks report whether vision-language models produce the correct number, but not whether errors arise from perception or reasoning. We introduce DecoyCount, a benchmark built from 1,660 real-world images with designed decoys across seven mechanisms, along with paired prompts: a neutral question, a matched alignment cue, and a novel multi-hop, multi-image question that situates the same counting problem in a realistic scenario. Using this design, we find that counting failures are induced partly by visual misalignment: models can execute the intended counting process when cue-guided but fail to select it unaided, and we term this difference in accuracy the reasoning-alignment gap. Despite being highly capable on general reasoning, frontier models remain below 50\% accuracy on our benchmark, while alignment gaps range from 11.8-22.1 percentage points; strikingly, we observe that more capable models, greater thinking budgets, and agentic processes often induce larger gaps. Because humans may bring context that models lack, we test whether textual underspecification contributes to misalignment using a scenario-based multi-hop condition without explicit hinting, but this added context does not improve aggregate performance. Our analysis concludes that stronger general reasoning does not by itself generalize to aligned visual reasoning, leaving misalignment with human visual expectations as a substantial component of the remaining deficit.

title: Semantic Atoms for Scalable Text Analysis in Data Analytics in the Era of LLM-Based Agents
abstract: Much of the information needed for data analysis is buried in text columns: an analyst may infer customer frustration from complaint text and use it to explain resolution time. We call workloads in which processing text columns is central to subsequent data analysis TADA (\emph{Text Analysis in Data Analytics}). In an agentic setting, the user's query dynamically specifies this processing, and answering it interleaves LLM-based semantic steps with exact SQL or Python operations. This mixed execution raises two design questions: which work should be neural and which symbolic, and which semantic outputs later steps can reuse. We address them for agent-planned TADA workflows with two complementary, query-driven semantic atoms. Each atom takes a sequence of text items and a natural-language query specifying the semantic task: \textbf{Tagging} returns one string per input item, while \textbf{Categorization} returns $M$ category objects over $N$ input items. Tagging results are materialized as a row-aligned column and Categorization results as a category table; SQL or Python then performs exact computation over this exposed state. We realize this interface in TADA-Agent, whose atoms run inside generated Python programs and internally handle inputs beyond a reliable context window. We evaluate TADA-Agent on TABench, a benchmark of 40 complete analysis requests over spreadsheet tables spanning workflow composition, input--output structure, and literature-grounded analytical scenarios.
