title: Penerapan Rule-Based Keyword Matching dan OCR Tesseract untuk Validasi Dokumen Persyaratan pada Sistem Permohonan Pengujian ALSINTAN Berbasis Web
abstract: This study develops an automatic document validation feature for a web-based testing application used by UPTD BMSPP, West Sumatra, to process agricultural machinery testing applications. Previously, the system checked uploaded files only by format and size, not by content, so staff inspected every document manually and mismatched documents were detected only after processing. Here, “validation” means checking whether a document’s text matches its expected document type, it does not verify authenticity or legal validity. The study builds a model combining Optical Character Recognition (OCR) using the Tesseract engine with rule-based keyword matching for five document types. The model runs as a separate Python Flask microservice: it extracts text from digital PDFs using pdfplumber, applies Tesseract OCR to scanned documents and images, then compares the text with per-type keyword lists to return a real-time status. The system was developed using the Waterfall method and tested with black-box testing on six scenarios. Five of the six scenarios (83%) produced the expected results, this shows scenario conformity, not OCR recognition accuracy or classification accuracy on a broad document population. One scenario returned an error message that did not match the expected response for an unsupported file format, marking an area for improvement.
journal: Saturnus: Jurnal Teknologi dan Sistem Informasi

title: Developing a community of practice in health professions education: reflections from the Africa HPE ECHO project
abstract: This paper discusses key themes that emerged from the Africa Health Professions Education Extension for Community Healthcare Outcomes (Africa HPE ECHO) online discussion sessions and provides recommendations for development of the community of practice and integration of the identified themes into health professions education. A qualitative study was employed to identify themes that emerged from transcripts of reflective discussion sessions. Non-probability purposive sampling was used to recruit health educators through the authors’ personal networks and by snowballing. Between 2024 and 2025, 36 60-minute sessions were held, with on average 24 participants attending each session. FS, IC and JC inductively extracted key themes from the transcripts of each recorded session, while PB provided overall review of those. Participants valued having a safe, supportive space in which to explore the issues they face, and appreciated that many of their challenges were shared or commonly experienced among the group. They reflected on the absence of any such learning and practice communities in their institutions, and on the importance of the support offered by the Africa HPE ECHO discussion sessions. Scenarios presented during the sessions addressed a wide range of topics that coalesced around five themes: caring; fit-for-purpose professionals; growth mindset; leading; and swimming upstream. The rift between theory and practice, and what transformation is required in both education and health care were cross-cutting issues across all themes. The sessions enabled in-depth exploration of ideas, responses, and practices aimed at facilitating the development of educators as change agents within the healthcare system. There is a need for a community of practice where healthcare educators and other stakeholders in this field can engage in discussions to explore potential solutions to the challenges of training caring, fit-for-purpose healthcare professionals and leaders, in a rapidly changing world of AI and environmental uncertainty.

title: Career Management and Succession in The Agricultural Sector: Exploring Motivation, Vocational Identity and Digital Skills
abstract: Indonesia's farm workforce is aging faster than it is being replaced: in the 2023 Agricultural Census, only 1.24% of individual farm operators were aged 15–24. This study explores how career motivation, vocational identity and digital skills take shape among agricultural vocational students, how they differ between early- and final-semester students, and what this implies for career management and succession. Eight students of the Plantation Crop Production Technology Study Program, Politeknik Negeri Sriwijaya, were selected by purposive sampling stratified by semester (four in semester 2, four in semester 8), interviewed in semi-structured format, and their accounts analyzed with Reflexive Thematic Analysis. On career motivation, participants came to see agriculture as a knowledge-based field, and all of them ranked job stability above income. On vocational identity, confidence in their career choice sat at 7–8 out of 10 and grew through practice and internships. Final-semester students held more realistic and specific career images, one participant moved toward laboratory research rather than field work, and obstacles were handled with strategies participants worked out on their own. On digital skills, social media changed how participants saw the sector, yet few had used agricultural technology themselves, mostly because neither campus nor internship sites had the equipment. For career management and succession, the findings point to structured experiential learning, hands-on digital training, and open communication of the full range of agricultural career paths.
journal: Equivalent : Journal of Economic, Accounting and Management

title: Advances in Plant Electrical Signals for Plant Health Monitoring and Smart Agriculture
abstract: Plant electrical signals are fast electrophysiological responses to environmental stimuli, physiological regulation and stress. Because they often change before visible symptoms appear, they are attractive indicators for early plant-health monitoring and for sensing in precision agriculture. Research in this area has moved from recording single action potentials to analyzing the plant electrome, and now draws on flexible wearable electrodes, implantable and electrochemical sensors, machine learning, multi-source data fusion and edge-cloud computing. This review follows the technical chain from mechanism to application. We first summarize the physiological basis of the main signal types and how they relate to biotic and abiotic stress. We then compare acquisition technologies, including conventional electrodes, flexible wearable devices, microneedles and electrochemical sensors for biochemical markers. Next, we discuss preprocessing, multi-scale feature extraction, and recognition with conventional machine learning, deep learning and multi-source fusion. Finally, we examine applications in environmental sensing and stress identification and outline the remaining obstacles to field use. Most published results still come from laboratory or greenhouse studies with small datasets and non-standard protocols. Progress toward field deployment will depend on standardized acquisition and reporting, long-term sensor stability, cross-species and cross-site validation, open datasets, interpretable models and low-power edge inference. With these elements in place, plant electrical signals could serve as one component of decision-support systems for early warning and crop management.

title: GenFedEdgeAgri: Diffusion-Enhanced Federated Edge AIoT for Climate-Resilient Precision Agriculture
abstract: Modern precision agriculture is undermined by data scarcity, privacy concerns, and high latency in remote areas, and centralized AI models struggle to forecast rare, climate-induced crop stresses given insufficiently diverse datasets and stakeholders' reluctance to share sensitive data. To address these obstacles, this study presents GenFedEdgeAgri, a framework aimed at improving climate-resilient crop monitoring, soil intelligence, and intelligent irrigation, and it examines how synthetic, data-driven augmentation-achieved by incorporating Generative Diffusion Models (GDMs) into a Federated Edge AIoT architecture-can enhance model robustness while preserving strong localized privacy. Methodologically, we propose a decentralized architecture in which Edge AIoT gateways employ lightweight Latent Diffusion Models to produce high-fidelity synthetic samples of nutrient depletion and extreme-weather stress; these samples harden local models before Federated Learning (FL) weight aggregation, thereby mitigating the effects of non-IID data distribution. We specify a pre-registered evaluation protocol-with defined datasets, baselines and metrics-under which the framework is compared against standard FL frameworks on multi-modal data in terms of accuracy, decision latency, and communication cost. The framework is evaluated against a pre-specified protocol; the projected gains-a 14.2% improvement in crop-disease detection accuracy, a 19% relative reduction in soil-moisture forecasting RMSE, and up to a 43% reduction in communication rounds-are stated as pre-registered hypotheses to be empirically confirmed, not as validated results. If confirmed, GenFedEdgeAgri would offer a scalable, privacy-preserving path to sustainable smart infrastructure, advancing autonomous, water-efficient agriculture through on-device intelligence that anticipates climate variability.

title: Extracting Agricultural Experts' Experiential Knowledge from Non-Standardized Text with Quantity and Operation Scope Constraints
abstract: Expert advice on crop management is often written informally, and in such text a number can easily be assigned the wrong role or attached to the wrong operation, material, or measurement basis. We propose QS-IE, a knowledge extraction method constrained by quantity and operation scope. Its unit of extraction is a complete quantitative fact. Given a shared set of numeric candidates and a single base model, QS-IE selects complete candidates from several prompting strategies, verifies them against the source text, and applies scope constraints, so that every extracted quantity stays linked to its source evidence. We built a corpus of 4006 texts on tomato cultivation. Two researchers with agronomy backgrounds jointly annotated and reviewed 1000 of them; the other 3006 were annotated with large language model assistance and then reviewed by hand. The corpus was split into 3206 development texts and 800 independent test texts. On the 1152 reference facts of the test set, QS-IE reached a precision of 84.02%, a recall of 86.72%, and a micro-averaged F1 of 85.35%, which is 3.91 percentage points higher than the strongest baseline, a multi-strategy in-context learning ensemble. Removing the operation scope constraints lowered test F1 by 8.24 percentage points. In a sampled human audit of the test set, 82.00% of the outputs for texts containing target facts were judged usable, and all six engineering checks on storage and evidence traceability were passed. The results indicate that explicit association constraints make quantitative facts extracted from tomato cultivation texts more complete and easier to review, which supports the structured, traceable storage of experiential knowledge that experts express in non-standardized text.

title: Interpreting Short Tandem Repeat Variations with Plant Genomic Foundation Models in Olive
abstract: Short tandem repeats (STRs) are highly mutable, multiallelic variants with distinctive mutation dynamics and have been associated with phenotypic variation across diverse species. However, genome-wide STR variation remains poorly characterized in olive, and the large number of naturally occurring alleles creates a challenge for variant interpretation. Genomic language models offer a potential way to assess how STR length changes alter learned sequence representations, but their responses to natural multiallelic STR series have not been systematically evaluated. Here, we identified 117,119 polymorphic STRs across 212 Iranian and Mediterranean olive accessions. STRs recovered the major SNP-defined ancestry axes while resolving additional geographically structured subcomponents. We then quantified STR-induced embedding perturbation using three plant genomic language models: AgroNT, PlantCAD2, and GPN. Across all three models, embedding distance generally increased with repeat-length difference from the reference allele, and 7,417 loci were embedding-sensitive in all three models. These signals were robust to fixed-length input construction and exceeded those of matched nonrepetitive indels at most tested loci. Integration with oil-composition associations prioritized four exploratory loci supported by all three models. Overall, we provide a genome-wide olive STR resource and show that plant genomic language models capture reproducible responses to natural STR length variation. Combining cross-model embedding evidence with phenotype association provides a potential framework for prioritizing candidate STRs for further investigation.

title: Prediction transfer does not imply reliability transfer in single-cell foundation models
abstract: Single-cell foundation models are increasingly transferred across tissues, diseases, perturbation screens, and experimental platforms. Although substantial effort has focused on prediction transfer, it remains unclear whether a model's assessment of its own reliability transfers similarly across biological contexts. Here we define reliability transfer as the ability to transfer an accurate assessment of when model predictions are likely to be correct or incorrect and investigate its behavior across ten perturbation-prediction systems spanning multiple datasets, models, and evaluation settings. We find that reliability transfer varies substantially across source-target pairs and cannot be inferred from predictive performance alone, indicating that prediction transfer and reliability transfer constitute distinct forms of generalization. Analyses of biological annotations, network connectivity, target exposure, and contextual factors reveal that prediction reliability is associated with both shared and context-dependent signals, with their relative importance differing across systems. To characterize this variability, we introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints, context-level signatures derived from strictly cross-fitted SHAP explanations that summarize how reliability estimators combine biological and contextual information when assigning confidence. Across systems, contexts with similar attribution-magnitude fingerprints tended to transfer reliability more successfully, and fingerprint similarity identified transfer sources achieving higher reliability-transfer performance within the observed candidate set. However, these relationships weakened under stricter cross-family transfer settings, indicating that transferable reliability structure remains partly dependent on shared contextual information. Finally, transferred reliability estimators produced different perturbation rankings despite identical perturbation predictions, illustrating a practical consequence of reliability transfer for downstream prioritization. Together, these results establish reliability transfer as a distinct aspect of foundation-model generalization and introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints as a framework for characterizing transferable reliability structure across biological contexts.

title: Using Diffusion Similarity Networks to Identify, Track, and Predict Movement Disorders
Economic Empowerment of Women Through the Processing of Household Waste into Marketable Products
abstract: Household waste is usually framed as an environmental burden, yet a growing body of community-based initiatives treats it as a raw material through which women can earn income and gain voice. This article examines how the processing of household and domestic waste into marketable products contributes to women's economic empowerment, and what conditions separate short-lived training projects from durable livelihoods. Using a systematic literature review, records were retrieved from the Consensus academic database, deduplicated, and screened against inclusion criteria covering publication between 2021 and 2026, an active DOI, a focus on women, and an explicit link between waste processing and economic value. Twenty studies met the criteria and were synthesised thematically, supported by five recent conceptual and empirical sources. The review identifies five value pathways: organic and biological conversion, plastic and packaging upcycling, textile and agricultural residue crafts, mixed household recyclables, and collective collection services. Across these pathways, empowerment advances through four mechanisms: skill acquisition, product diversification, market and digital access, and collective organisation. However, most evidence comes from short community-service programmes that report outputs rather than measured income or agency. The article proposes a Household Waste-to-Value Empowerment framework and argues that market linkage and collective institutions, not technical training alone, determine whether waste becomes a sustained source of women's economic power
journal: Archipel: Journal of Indonesian Interdisciplinary Studies

title: Predictive Ability of Psychological Alienation in Futsal Players
abstract: The present study sought to uncover the extent of psychological alienation and sporting ambition among futsal athletes, while also determining the relationship between these two variables and constructing a predictive model through a regression equation to forecast sporting ambition based on the facets of psychological alienation. The investigator employed a descriptive methodology incorporating both relational and predictive techniques to align with the research aims. The study population comprised futsal club athletes during the sports season, and the foundational sample was randomly chosen from 56 individuals. The investigator employed two validated psychological scales (honesty and consistency) to gather data: the first scale measured psychological alienation with 20 items across two dimensions, while the second assessed sports ambition level with 36 items across four domains. The statistical analyses were conducted utilising the Social Sciences Statistical Package (SPSS v27), employing: arithmetic means, standard deviations, t-tests for two independent samples and one sample, Pearson correlation coefficient, and Stepwise Multiple Regression analysis. The findings additionally indicated a statistically significant negative association between the two variables. The regression analysis yielded the development of a statistically significant prediction model, wherein the facets of psychological alienation accounted for 65.9% of the total variance in mathematical ambition (R^2 = 0.659). The aspect of handicap and the erosion of mathematical comprehension had the most significant adverse effect on forecasting aspiration, succeeded by the factors of isolation and psychological irregularity. Given the findings, a linear predictive model was developed to assess ambition levels concerning alienation, and the researcher advocated for the implementation of psychological sports counselling and the utilization of the predictive model by technical organizations as a preventative diagnostic instrument to safeguard players' motivational frameworks.

title: Ai Agents in Game Development Using an Engine or Specialized Libraries
Artificial Intelligence Applications in Fruit Production, Harvesting and Postharvest Quality: A Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored as a tool for improving decision-making across fruit production and postharvest management. However, evidence regarding its applications, reported performance, and practical limitations remains distributed across different fruit crops, sensing technologies, and computational approaches. This review systematically examines the applications of machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, robotics, the Internet of Things (IoT), and remote sensing in fruit science. Relevant publications were identified through searches of [databases used] covering the period from [start year] to [end year], using predefined search terms and eligibility criteria. Of the [number] records identified, [number] studies were included in the final synthesis. The selected literature was categorised into precision orchard management, pest and disease detection, fruit detection and yield estimation, robotic harvesting, non-destructive quality assessment, and postharvest handling. The synthesis compares the reported performance of AI models, their application across fruit crops, the sensing technologies employed, and the principal limitations affecting field implementation. Particular attention is given to quantitative outcomes reported for detection accuracy, prediction performance, harvesting efficiency, resource use, and fruit quality assessment. The review also evaluates challenges associated with dataset availability, model generalization, computational requirements, sensor integration, and deployment under variable orchard conditions. Emerging approaches, including edge AI, multimodal data fusion, explainable AI, and autonomous orchard systems, are discussed in relation to the limitations identified in existing studies. By connecting reported experimental outcomes with implementation constraints, this review identifies evidence-based research priorities for developing reliable and scalable AI applications in fruit production and postharvest management.
journal: Journal of Advances in Biology & Biotechnology

title: Rice and Wheat Straw for Biofuel and Bioenergy Production: Implementation Evidence, Environmental Sustainability, and Scale-Up Gaps in Selected Countries
abstract: Aim: To evaluate rice- and wheat-residue biofuel pathways through documented implementation cases in India, China, Italy, Denmark, the United States, and Canada, with emphasis on evidence maturity, environmental trade-offs, and scale-up constraints. Approach: A structured comparative narrative review integrated peer-reviewed conversion and life-cycle studies with dated government, laboratory, and facility records. Each numerical observation was classified as measured operation, anticipated process performance, nameplate capacity, historical use, or modelled outcome. Mixed-feedstock attribution and variation in life-cycle assessment boundaries were considered explicitly. Findings: The Panipat plant in India was announced with a design basis of approximately 200,000 tonnes of rice straw and 30 million litres of ethanol per year; the associated 300,000 tonnes of CO₂-equivalent annual avoidance remains a government projection. In Qingpu, China, documented 2020 co-digestion of 2,125 tonnes of dry rice straw and 142 tonnes of fresh manure yielded 442,015 m³ biogas and 662,475 kWh electricity. The historical Tianguan demonstration had a reported capacity, rather than verified annual output, of 3,000 tonnes ethanol per year. Industrial lignocellulosic processing capacity was documented at Crescentino, Italy, whereas Denmark reported an expected ethanol yield exceeding 198 litres per dry tonne of wheat straw in earlier demonstration work. American and Canadian examples show why commissioning, government-fleet use, and later commercial continuity must be evaluated separately. Conclusions: Rice and wheat residues can support renewable fuels and integrated biorefineries, but crop-residue production is not equivalent to a sustainably harvestable supply. Climate and economic outcomes depend on the management baseline, soil-carbon and nutrient requirements, feedstock logistics, process inputs, coproduct treatment, and verifiable operating continuity. The six cases illustrate heterogeneous pathways rather than national or global adoption rates.
journal: Journal of Geography, Environment and Earth Science International

title: Finite Element-Based Stress Analysis of the Main Frame of a Battery-Operated Lathyrus Harvester
abstract: Lathyrus (Lathyrus sativus L.) is a climate-resilient pulse grown mainly as a relay crop in rice fallows, but it is still harvested by hand, a slow, labour-intensive and physically demanding process. A battery-operated lathyrus harvester was therefore developed, and this study evaluated the structural safety of its main frame, the principal load-bearing component, using finite element analysis (FEA). A three-dimensional model of the frame was analysed in ANSYS Workbench 2024 R1 under static loads representing field operation, namely the weight of the battery, motor and transmission, the cutting resistance of lathyrus stems and the inertial force of the reciprocating knife. Structural steel properties were assigned, and support reactions, equivalent elastic strain, directional deformation and von Mises stress were evaluated. The maximum von Mises stress was 223.92 MPa, confined to a critical joint region and below the 250 MPa yield strength of the material, giving a minimum factor of safety of 1.12. The maximum equivalent elastic strain was 0.0011939 m/m and was limited to local stress-concentration zones, while most of the frame showed negligible strain. The frame deflected like a cantilever, with a maximum upward displacement of 11.995 mm at the free end and a maximum downward displacement of 8.913 mm near the restrained region. The frame is therefore safe against yielding under static field loads, but the narrow safety margin and the free-end deflection show that local reinforcement is needed to resist dynamic loads and keep the cutter bar aligned. The study demonstrates that FEA is an effective, low-cost tool for designing lightweight battery-operated harvesters for small farms.
journal: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports

title: Growth, Trend and Decomposition Analysis of Garlic in Rajasthan State, India (2005–06 to 2024–25)
abstract: This study examines changes in garlic cultivation in Rajasthan from 2005–06 to 2024–25, with emphasis on cultivated area, production, productivity and the factors contributing to production growth. Secondary time-series data were analysed using absolute and relative changes, coefficients of variation, linear growth rates and a decomposition model that separates area, yield and interaction effects. The analysis covers 20 agricultural years and focuses on the aggregate indicators reported for Rajasthan rather than district-level variation. The reported area increased from 22,392 to 69,471, representing a relative increase of approximately 210%. Production rose from 113,980 to 423,012, equivalent to approximately 271% growth. Reported productivity increased from 5.09 to 6.08, an increase of approximately 19.45%. Variation was greatest for production (60.53%), followed by area (50.50%) and productivity (14.58%). The estimated linear growth rates were 1.57% for area, 2.63% for production and 2.52% for productivity, with the manuscript reporting statistical significance at the 5% level for all three indicators. Decomposition attributed 77.54% of the total production change to area expansion, 15.22% to the interaction between area and yield, and 7.24% to the yield effect. These findings indicate that cultivated-area expansion accounted for most of the increase in garlic production, although improvements in productivity also contributed. The results suggest that measures aimed at improving crop yield warrant attention alongside continued assessment of production trends in Rajasthan.
journal: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports

title: Probiotic Extracellular Vesicles Enable Oral Alendronate Therapy for Glucocorticoid-Induced Osteoporosis.
abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) involves impaired bone remodeling, intestinal dysbiosis, and immune imbalance, which together limit the long-term benefit of conventional oral bisphosphonate therapy. Here, we report LpEVs@ALN, a probiotic extracellular vesicle-based oral nanoplatform constructed by loading alendronate (ALN) into Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-derived extracellular vesicles. LpEVs@ALN maintains vesicle integrity and epithelial compatibility, improves ALN retention under acidic exposure, and enables sustained ALN release at intestinal pH conditions. In dexamethasone-suppressed BMSCs, LpEVs@ALN enhances osteogenic differentiation, as evidenced by increased ALP activity and matrix mineralization. In zebrafish GIOP models, LpEVs@ALN improves cranial mineralization, new bone formation, scale regeneration, and locomotor/shoaling performance; accompanied by reduced inflammatory tone, improved ALP/RANKL-associated bone turnover readouts, and rebalanced oxidative-stress indices. Microbiome profiling shows recovery of richness/diversity and reduced Proteobacteria dominance, while scale RNA-seq reveals broad reversal of glucocorticoid-driven dysregulation toward pro-osteogenic and anti-inflammatory programs. Integrated correlation analysis further linked microbial remodeling with systemic and skeletal responses, suggesting involvement of the gut-immune-bone axis. Collectively, LpEVs@ALN alleviates GIOP by combining ALN-mediated bone protection with probiotic extracellular vesicle-associated regulation of intestinal and systemic homeostasis, highlighting its potential as an oral therapeutic strategy for GIOP.

title: In Situ Reconstructed Pt-CeO2 Nanozymes With Rich Interfacial Oxygen Vacancies for Kinetic Fingerprint-Based Clinical Thiol Discrimination.
abstract: Deciphering structurally similar thiol analogues is vital for disease diagnosis, yet conventional one-to-one sensing strategies are intrinsically bottlenecked by signal cross-interference. Herein, we report an in situ reconstructed interfacial oxygen vacancies engineering strategy to prepare vacancy-rich Pt-CeO2 nanozymes for intelligent thiol differentiation. By combining incipient wetness impregnation with subsequent H2 reduction, isolated Pt single atoms were transformed into uniformly dispersed Pt clusters on CeO2 nanorods, simultaneously inducing abundant oxygen vacancies and dynamically coupled Pt-CeO2 interfaces. The optimized nanozyme exhibited significantly enhanced peroxidase-like catalytic activity over its single-atom state or directly deposited cluster counterparts. Crucially, the boosted catalytic kinetics significantly amplified the subtle response discrepancies among different thiols, yielding highly resolved time-dependent fingerprints. By integrating these distinct kinetic profiles with multivariate statistical analysis and predictive machine learning models, accurate differentiation of thiol species, complex multicomponent mixtures and clinical serum samples was achieved. This work not only provides insights into reconstruction-induced interfacial defect engineering but also establishes an effective framework for intelligent kinetic sensing in early disease screening.

title: Lithium-Doped Hydroxyapatite Nanowires Rejuvenate Senescent Macrophages Via the Lysosome-Dependent Ferroptosis Axis to Promote Aged Bone Regeneration.
abstract: Senescent bone repair remains a formidable clinical challenge without an entirely satisfactory strategy. Emerging evidence has identified macrophage senescence as a critical determinant of impaired bone healing in the aged skeleton, and precisely reversing macrophage senescence has therefore emerged as a highly promising therapeutic approach. In this study, guided by multi-omics features of senescent macrophages, we develop lithium-doped hydroxyapatite nanowires (Li-nHAP) and demonstrate that Li-nHAP effectively alleviates macrophage senescence and subsequently enhances the osteogenic differentiation of aged bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. Mechanistically, we identify the lysosome-dependent ferroptosis axis as a previously unrecognized target mediating the anti-senescent effects of Li-nHAP in bone marrow-derived macrophages. Specifically, Li-nHAP re-establishes lysosomal homeostasis, including restoring acidity, preserving membrane integrity, maintaining iron storage, and enhancing hydrolytic activity, thereby suppressing ferroptosis and ultimately reversing macrophage senescence. In vivo studies further validate that Li-nHAP significantly alleviates macrophage ferroptosis and senescence, reduces local iron accumulation, and accelerates bone regeneration in an aged mandibular defect model. Collectively, these findings establish Li-nHAP as a novel osteo-immunomodulatory biomaterial that offers a promising strategy for the repair of age-related bone defects.

title: Generative artificial intelligence in medical oncology: A clinically focused narrative review of large language, vision-language, and agentic artificial intelligence systems.
abstract: Rapid advances in cancer genetics and genomics, pathophysiology, diagnostics, and therapeutics have substantially increased the complexity of clinical oncology. Integrating large and diverse data streams into timely, patient-specific decisions provides a compelling rationale for incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) into cancer care. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) encompasses several classes of models capable of generating new content. This clinically focused review concentrates on GenAI applications based primarily on large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), as well as emerging agentic systems that use these models to perform coordinated, multistep tasks. LLMs demonstrate substantial medical knowledge, strong performance on oncology-related assessments, and emerging capabilities in clinical reasoning. Guideline- and retrieval-augmented systems can improve concordance with expert recommendations and interpretation of complex treatment algorithms. LLMs and VLMs have been applied to documentation, patient communication, information extraction and summarization, clinical decision support, and multimodal data synthesis. However, performance varies substantially across tasks and clinical domains, with important limitations including incomplete or outdated information, training-data bias, automation bias, and confabulation. Agentic AI represents an emerging extension of these technologies in which LLMs or VLMs are incorporated into systems capable of multistep planning, external information retrieval, specialized tool use, and iterative evaluation and refinement. Early oncology applications include evidence synthesis, multimodal clinical decision support, radiology, pathology, surgery, and individualized treatment planning. With rigorous validation, transparent implementation, continual updating, and appropriate expert oversight, GenAI may augment oncologists' judgment, improve patient understanding and experience, streamline cancer care delivery, and advance personalized oncology.

title: A Projection‐Based ARIMA Framework for Nonlinear Dynamics in Macroeconomic and Financial Time Series: Closed‐Form Estimation and Fast Rolling Forecasting
abstract: We develop Galerkin–ARIMA, a projection‐based forecasting framework that expands observation‐ and innovation‐lag states with finite basis functions while nesting classical multiplicative SARIMA as a restricted linear specification. The model is estimated using preliminary residual proxies followed by a joint least‐squares or ridge regression, which supports efficient rolling refitting. For the fixed‐dimensional unpenalized estimator, we establish asymptotic normality while accounting explicitly for generated regressors. Across 10 US macroeconomic and financial series, Galerkin–ARIMA has competitive one‐step‐ahead forecast accuracy, with nonlinear gains varying across series and the linear specification providing the most stable performance. In pre‐specified runtime experiments on Real GDP, the S&P 500, and the Unemployment Rate, Ridge Galerkin–ARIMA is substantially faster than likelihood/state‐space SARIMA under fixed, initially tuned, and repeatedly retuned rolling specifications. The results suggest that the main value of the framework is flexible lag‐state modeling and computationally efficient forecasting. Nonlinear enrichment does not produce uniform accuracy gains.

title: Effects of Scallop Mantle Toxin on the Male Mouse Reproductive System.
abstract: The mantle of Yesso scallops contains a novel 18-/29-kDa protein toxin. Previous studies have confirmed that this toxin induces subacute toxicity without a clear dose-effect relationship. However, its effects on the male reproductive system remain unclear. This study aimed to explore the toxic effects of scallop mantle toxin (SMT) on the reproductive organs of male mice. Male Kunming mice were fed diets supplemented with 2% scallop mantle for 5 consecutive weeks, with the dosage determined based on previous studies from our research group. Instead of using purified toxin extracts, this study directly adopted raw scallop mantle tissue as the toxin source. Mouse growth status was monitored, with analyses performed on testicular and epididymal histology, sperm morphology, sperm DNA integrity, sperm nucleoprotein maturation, and the expression of spermatogenesis-related genes. The results showed that SMT induces significant reproductive toxicity in male mice by impairing spermatogenesis, as evidenced by structural disruption of seminiferous tubules, reduced spermatogenic cell layers, decreased counts of mature elongated spermatozoa, elevated sperm malformation and DNA damage, and disrupted histone-to-protamine transition. Furthermore, SMT significantly downregulated the expression of TSSK6, a postmeiotic differentiation marker, indicating that SMT primarily targets the late stages of spermatogenesis. Taken together, SMT damages the structural integrity of male reproductive organs and compromises sperm quantity and quality in mice, and may interfere with postmeiotic sperm formation and maturation. These findings provide an important theoretical basis for establishing scallop mantle-related reproductive toxicity models and evaluating shellfish food safety risks.

title: Porcupine Detection and Mitigation in Kashmir Valley Orchards Using Edge Computing
abstract: Roughly 20% to 28% of the GDP of the Kashmiri agricultural sector are based on high‐value crops, such as apples, walnuts, saffron, and apricots. These face significant economic challenges due to crop damage caused by the Indian crested porcupine (Hystrix indica). This research aims to study and develop an effective real‐time management solution for wildlife intrusion in orchards, overcoming the limitations of traditional deterrence methods. Methods : We propose a multilayered edge‐IoT architecture that combines motion, acoustic, and visual sensing with edge‐based machine learning and automated wildlife monitoring. The system leverages lightweight YOLOv8n models running on edge devices, secure communication frameworks, and intelligent monitoring with a user‐facing application for alerts and analytics. A comprehensive wildlife detection dataset was developed by integrating multiple public datasets and converting segmentation annotations into object‐detection bounding boxes. The final dataset contains 1758 images with 2249 annotated instances across three classes: porcupine, hedgehog, and others. Object detection is performed using YOLOv8n on resource‐constrained edge devices for efficient real‐time inference. Experimental results show that YOLOv8n achieves 93.9% mAP@0.5 and 86.4% mAP@0.5:0.95 with 84.0% precision and 89.9% recall on the test dataset. The porcupine class specifically achieves 99.5% mAP@0.5 and 95.4% mAP@0.5:0.95, demonstrating highly reliable porcupine detection performance. The lightweight YOLOv8n architecture achieves approximately 4.9 ms inference time per image on the validation host, and 81 ms per frame on a Jetson Nano edge node, enabling efficient edge deployment for real‐time orchard monitoring. All reported figures are obtained from real image data combined with simulated multi‐sensor confidence modeling; no result derives from a deployed orchard installation, and the scope of validation is stated explicitly. Furthermore, the proposed framework establishes a foundation for future privacy‐preserving and Agentic AI‐enabled intelligent wildlife monitoring systems capable of adaptive decision‐making, autonomous monitoring, and collaborative edge intelligence under dynamic environmental conditions

title: A predictive approach to genome design for multi-trait improvement and environmental adaptability via machine learning
Exploratory donor-aware analysis of developmental transcriptomic trajectories in 15q13.3-deletion cortical organoids
Automated classification of non-functional requirements twenty years later: why this isn’t a solved problem
abstract: This paper revisits “Automated Classification of Non-Functional Requirements”, published in the Requirements Engineering Journal in 2007, and reflects on how the underlying problem has evolved over two decades. The original work addressed the central challenge in requirements engineering that quality concerns are difficult to identify because they are distributed across heterogeneous artifacts and only partially documented. It introduced one of the earliest machine-learning approaches for NFR classification and produced the NFR PROMISE dataset, which became a widely used benchmark in this area. To understand the paper’s long-term impact, we conducted a citation review of 55 papers and replicated representative NFR classification approaches spanning two decades. The results show substantial advances in automated classification, culminating in modern LLM and agent-based techniques that outperform earlier approaches on PROMISE. However, improved accuracy has not solved the underlying problem. Contemporary AI-assisted development increasingly blurs the boundaries between Requirements Engineering, architectural design, and implementation. Quality concerns continue to emerge throughout development, but now appear as conversational fragments, implementation discussions, and architectural tradeoffs rather than explicit requirements statements. We argue that the next generation of requirements engineering tools must move beyond classifying documents toward identifying, surfacing, and preserving architecturally significant quality concerns as they emerge throughout development. We then outline a research agenda centered on detecting emerging and missing quality concerns, selective intervention, living documentation of quality decisions, and evaluation beyond classification accuracy. Finally we take a retrospective look at two decades of sharing and reusing the dataset, including the importance of dataset lineage, experimental comparability, and benchmark evolution.

title: Sustainable career in the age of artificial intelligence: an agent-based simulation from a complex adaptive systems perspective
Data-driven segmentation of solar filaments based on ground-based instrument data
abstract: The dynamic behavior of solar prominences and filaments is a precursor to coronal mass ejections (CMEs), which can disrupt Earth's magnetosphere and affect satellite communications. Systematic ground-based solar observations, conducted with high temporal resolution, are instrumental in monitoring these structures. Analysis of the morphological changes and destabilization processes of filaments and prominences captured in datasets can help identify early warning signs of potential eruptions. This capability is vital for developing reliable space weather forecasting systems, thereby mitigating the adverse effects of solar disturbances on Earth's technological infrastructure. Previously, we introduced hybrid algorithmic-data driven method which performance was shown on a set of Solar Dynamic Observatory (SDO) Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) instrument data performing segmentation of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) and shock waves. In this work, we extend certain aspects of this approach to image segmentation of solar features -- filaments and prominences using H-alpha Kanzelhohe Observatory data. We describe a leakage-aware, sparse multi-year sampling strategy. We present image segmentation models pre-trained on synoptic and normalized image data, followed by a discussion of how model performance depends on training-set engineering, data preprocessing techniques, and the choice of loss metrics. We perform a limited study, both analytically and numerically, of the effect of external, fixed normalization versus native input for compact U-Net-based segmentation of solar H-alpha filaments, also contributing to ongoing research on normalization in deep networks in general and compact models in particular.
