From AI boyfriends to AI shopping agents? The emerging convergence of relational AI and AI-assisted commerce
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is becoming both relational and agentic. AI boyfriends are treated as a visible romantic exemplar within the broader theoretical and empirical domain of relational AI. This paper examines whether relational AI, including AI boyfriends, is emerging alongside AI-assisted commerce, and whether functional integration keeps pace with attention and market growth. Study 1 analyzes Google Trends data (2020–2026, six markets): relational-AI attention rises significantly in five countries, AI-commerce attention rises in all six, with substantial but non-invariant temporal co-movement in attention. Study 2 examines 44 AI-companion apps on Google Play: the category shows substantial downloads and spending, romantic positioning (e.g., AI boyfriends) shows no observable adoption penalty, in-app purchasing is universal, yet no app positions shopping as a core feature. Study 3 analyzes 181,226 Reddit posts from relational-AI communities: design-weighted coding estimates 9.1% of corpus posts contain commercial discourse, but only 0.3% involve the companion itself in consumer or purchasing decisions. We conceptualize this as an attention-market-integration gap, where attention and market realization outpace functional commerce integration. The study equips managers and researchers with guidance for engaging with the emerging AI boyfriend trend.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: AP2/ERF transcription factors in plant stress adaptation: evolutionary expansion, functional diversification and hormone crosstalk.
abstract: APETALA2/ethylene response factor (AP2/ERF) transcription factors constitute a plant-specific regulatory family that coordinates plant development, environmental stress responses, and hormone signaling. However, the contribution of AP2/ERF family expansion and functional diversification to environmental adaptation has not been fully integrated across evolutionary and mechanistic scales. This review synthesizes classical findings and representative advances from the past five years in structural classification, duplication-driven expansion, functional diversification, stress adaptation, and hormone crosstalk, with particular emphasis on how post-duplication divergence shapes regulatory function. Across these studies, AP2/ERF proteins emerge as context-dependent nodes that connect environmental or hormonal signals with direct target genes and downstream physiological responses. This perspective distinguishes family expansion from demonstrated adaptive function and helps explain why closely related AP2/ERFs can produce contrasting outcomes in different biological contexts. We further discuss priorities for functional validation in non-model species, multi-stress experiments, multi-omics integration, field phenotyping, and gene-editing-based breeding, highlighting AP2/ERF regulators with potential for engineering stress-resilient crops.

title: Cone-beam computed tomography radiomics for differentiating clinicoradiologic labels of osteosclerosis, cemento-osseous dysplasia and odontoma: an internal model-development study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES To develop and internally validate cone-beam computed tomography radiomics for recorded clinicoradiologic classification of osteosclerosis, cemento-osseous dysplasia and odontoma, with secondary same-case three-dimensional convolutional neural-network benchmarking. METHODS This retrospective single-centre study included 126 lesions from 126 patients. From manual three-dimensional segmentations, 107 original radiomics features were extracted. A class-weighted least absolute shrinkage and selection operator one-vs-rest logistic-regression model was evaluated using 100 repeats of stratified five-fold held-out resampling. No independent histopathology report was retrievable in the retained study archive. A secondary strict 124-lesion three-dimensional analysis used 0.30-mm isotropic variable-size lesion-centred inputs, at least 5 mm of physical context and nested architecture/epoch selection; locked radiomics was evaluated on the same cases and outer folds. RESULTS Primary radiomics achieved accuracy 0.825, balanced accuracy 0.842, macro F1-score 0.834 and macro area under the curve 0.932. In the matched 124-lesion analysis, macro area under the curve was 0.935 (95% bias-corrected and accelerated confidence interval 0.889-0.963) for radiomics and 0.601 (0.516-0.682) for the nested three-dimensional network. The network showed marked odontoma-class collapse (sensitivity 1/22, 0.045). CONCLUSIONS Radiomics showed promising internal discrimination of the recorded labels, whereas the secondary three-dimensional benchmark was unstable for odontoma in this small cohort. These findings do not establish diagnostic accuracy against histopathology or general algorithmic superiority; external validation, standardised imaging and stronger reference standards are required. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE This study extends cone-beam computed tomography radiomics to radiopaque/mineralised jaw-lesion recorded labels and reports a same-case nested three-dimensional benchmark with explicit disclosure of class-specific failure.

title: On the number of species required to detect stabilizing selection in gene expression evolution.
abstract: Differentiating between genes that evolve under neutral drift versus stabilizing selection is one of the first explorations in comparative phylogenomic studies. Neutral drift and stabilizing selection of gene expression levels across a phylogeny are modelled using a Brownian motion and an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, respectively. Most empirical gene expression datasets contain only a few species, raising concerns about statistical power for model selection and parameter estimation. Furthermore, gene expression datasets often contain multiple samples per species, contrary to common macroevolutionary analyses of trait evolution. Here, we designed a targeted simulation study to evaluate the power to identify stabilizing selection, emphasizing the impact of the number of species, strength of selection and within-species variances. Our results show that the accuracy of selection strength estimation improves with increasing phylogeny size. Distinguishing weak selection, i.e., lower selection strength, from neutral drift is challenging, whereas varying levels of within-species variance have only minor effects on parameter estimation and model selection. Overall, our results suggest that we can have sufficient power to detect stabilizing selection with approximately 17 species, if the underlying strength of selection is sufficiently strong and if a relatively relaxed statistical significance threshold is adopted.

title: Time-dependent mortality and reduced population growth potential in Tetranychus urticae (Acari: Tetranychidae) following exposure to graphene oxide-treated leaves.
abstract: Graphene oxide (GO) is increasingly investigated for crop protection, but its direct effects on the twospotted spider mite, Tetranychus urticae Koch (Acari: Tetranychidae), remain poorly defined. Because short-term mortality alone may not reveal effects on population performance, we combined an acute leaf-dip bioassay with age-stage, two-sex life-table analysis under laboratory conditions. Adult females were exposed to kidney bean leaves treated with GO suspensions at nominal concentrations of 0.05 to 0.80 mg/mL. Mortality increased with concentration and exposure time, reaching 22.2% after 24 h and 87.8% after 48 h at 0.80 mg/mL, while control mortality remained 1.1%. The 24-h response did not reach 50% mortality within the tested range; the model-estimated 48-h LC10, LC50, and LC90 values were 0.15, 0.46, and 0.91 mg/mL, respectively, with LC90 extrapolated beyond the highest tested concentration. A 0.10 mg/mL GO suspension, selected from the adult acute-response data, was subsequently evaluated under continuous life-cycle exposure. Preadult survival remained high in both treatments, but GO-treated leaves reduced adult female longevity from 30.0 to 23.6 d and fecundity from 81.6 to 65.1 eggs per female. Net reproductive rate, intrinsic rate of increase, and finite rate of increase declined from 56.6 to 38.6 offspring per individual, 0.141 to 0.127 d-1, and 1.152 to 1.135 d-1, respectively. These findings show time-dependent adult mortality and reduced reproductive and population growth potential under laboratory conditions, supporting further evaluation of GO-treated leaves under crop-based conditions and with relevant non-target organisms.

title: β-Hydroxybutyrate in Cancer: From Alternative Fuel to a Context-Dependent Metabolic Signal.
abstract: β-Hydroxybutyrate (BHB) is the primary circulating ketone body generated during fasting, prolonged exercise, carbohydrate restriction, and ketogenic diets. Beyond functioning as an alternative oxidative substrate, BHB engages in HCAR2-mediated signaling, HDAC-related regulation, redox coupling, and lysine β-hydroxybutyrylation, thus influencing tumor cell metabolism, chromatin state, and the tumor immune microenvironment. The biological effects of BHB in cancer exhibit high context dependency. In certain models, BHB inhibits inflammation, angiogenesis, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, or tumor growth, while in others, it promotes metabolic adaptation, survival, metastasis, or treatment resistance. These seemingly contradictory outcomes can be elucidated through two major mechanistic switch points. The first involves tumor cell ketolytic competence: cells exhibiting effective BHB uptake, functional BDH1-OXCT1-dependent ketolysis, and preserved mitochondrial respiration may utilize BHB as an adaptive substrate under nutrient or therapeutic stress. The second concerns cellular allocation within the tumor microenvironment, determining whether BHB preferentially supports malignant cells, antitumor lymphocytes, or other immune and stromal populations. Furthermore, BHB source and treatment context further modulate these responses. Notably, ketogenic diet, direct BHB supplementation, and tumor-intrinsic ketogenesis represent biologically distinct experimental states and should not be interpreted interchangeably. This review integrates current evidence into a source-access-interpretation framework that differentiates tumor-adaptive, signaling-dominant, and immune-supportive BHB states, emphasizing priorities for causal, cell-resolved, and biomarker-guided investigation.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

title: Geodesic-SVDD Latent Mixup for One-Shot Distributed Tabular Learning
abstract: Distributed Learning on structured data is a key and widely adopted approach in privacy-sensitive sectors, ranging from financial fraud prevention to federated healthcare diagnostics. While Gradient Boosted Decision Trees are widely used in centralized settings due to their efficiency, they are incompatible with standard gradient-based federated learning protocols because of their non-differentiability. Conversely, standard deep classifiers that are amenable to federated optimization often suffer from catastrophic forgetting under label distribution skew. In this work, to address these gaps we propose Geodesic-SVDD, a framework for Distributed Spherical Prototype Learning that recasts each client's task as one-class density estimation on the hypersphere, so that local models can be aggregated as probabilistic manifolds in a single round. Specifically, for each client, we employ a Residual Spherical Encoder and Geodesic Latent Mixup that enforces strict hyperspherical constraints ($\|φ(x)\| \equiv 1$), preventing the manifold collapse observed in linear approximations. Furthermore, leveraging this insight, we propose a novel One-Shot "Product of Experts" protocol that enables privacy-preserving aggregation without iterative synchronization. Finally, we mechanistically analyze the trade-off between interpolation strategies, demonstrating that while linear mixup offers an enticing computational shortcut, it destabilizes optimization gradients by orders of magnitude ($10^9\times$). Across five tabular benchmarks and four levels of label skew, Geodesic-SVDD attains the highest mean AUROC among seven federated methods, outperforms federated tree ensembles by up to 21 AUROC points on Covertype, and its One-Shot variant matches centralized Deep SVDD under IID and mild skew with a single communication round.

title: Conservative Spruce Outperforms Acquisitive Larch Under Warming and CO 2
abstract: Predicting boreal forest growth is hindered by limited experimental tests on the compounding effects of climate change and atmospheric CO 2 . We integrated regional tree‐ring data with a peatland warming and CO 2 manipulation experiment, including 45 trait measurements, to assess growth responses of two widespread boreal conifers, Larix laricina and Picea mariana , to temperature, vapor pressure deficit (VPD), soil moisture, and elevated CO 2 . L. laricina growth was consistently more climate‐sensitive than P. mariana , increasing strongly with soil moisture and declining slightly with VPD at the regional scale, but responding positively to VPD and temperature—not soil moisture or CO 2 —at the experimental peatland. L. laricina 's acquisitive strategy enhanced water and nutrient uptake, sustaining growth but reducing hydraulic safety. By contrast, P. mariana 's conservative strategy maintained water‐use efficiency and hydraulic resilience without compromising growth. Our results challenge projections of widespread CO 2 fertilization in boreal forests and highlight conservative conifers as potential winners under warming and drying, sustaining growth while maintaining low mortality risk. This dynamic could reshape projections of the boreal carbon sink and its role in global climate feedback.

title: Biodegradable and Non‐Biodegradable Microplastics Drive Divergent Microbial Carbon and Nitrogen Metabolism Regimes in Soil–Plant Systems
abstract: The accumulation of microplastics (MPs) in soils worldwide has raised concerns about their potential impacts on microbially mediated carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) cycling. However, whether biodegradable and non‐biodegradable MPs differently affect microbial C and N metabolism and coupling, and whether these responses are modulated by co‐occurring plant identity remain uncertain. We combined a meta‐analysis with a controlled pot experiment comparing soil responses under two congeneric plant species exposed to two biodegradable and two non‐biodegradable MPs at doses ranging from 0% to 2% (w/w). In the meta‐analysis, MPs generally increased CO 2 emission and microbial biomass N (MBN), but had no significant overall effect on microbial biomass C (MBC). In the pot experiment, MPs likewise increased CO 2 emission, whereas overall effect sizes of MBC and MBN were nonsignificant. Nevertheless, these overall responses did not capture the distinct patterns of microbial C–N metabolic coordination between MP types. Under biodegradable MPs, tighter MBC–MBN coupling with a dose‐dependent shift toward greater respiratory C loss relative to MBC collectively indicated a maintenance‐associated metabolic pattern. In contrast, MBC–MBN decoupling and stronger MBC–CO 2 coupling under non‐biodegradable MPs indicated a biomass‐linked metabolic pattern. In addition, plant identity modulated these microbial metabolisms in an MP‐type manner, particularly in N‐related processes. These metabolic responses were accompanied with changes in soil property conditions and substrate availability, weakened DOC–DON coupling, and shifts in microbial community structure and life history strategy. RDA‐based hierarchical and variation partitioning and SEM further indicated that modeled soil property pathways were more prominent under non‐biodegradable MPs, while substrate‐related pathways were prominent under biodegradable MPs. Together, the meta‐analysis reveals the general microbial metabolic patterns under MP type, and the pot experiment further reveals how MP type and plant identity jointly influence microbial C–N metabolism through contrasting associations with soil substrates and property conditions.

title: "Dump my brain so it remembers for me": An AI-Augmented External Autobiographical Memory for Aphantasia and SDAM
abstract: I have aphantasia (no voluntary mental imagery) and severely deficient autobiographical memory (SDAM): I cannot relive my past or picture it. The deficit falls less on daily survival than on knowledge work — holding a project’s history, knowing what a colleague last said and cares about, assembling the context to send a message. Conventional memory aids fail this profile: built around images I cannot form (and, rarely photographed, do not capture), assuming a user who returns to review their own store. I report a one-month autoethnographic deployment of a memory prosthesis I do not operate: an AI agent over a continuously and automatically ingested personal knowledge base. I supply intent; the agent owns the rest of the memory loop — it gathers across my tools, connects scattered sources into the context an action needs, organizes and indexes the store, and surfaces proactively because I will not pull. I introduce AI-augmented external autobiographical memory as a cognitive prosthetic for this overlooked, non-clinical profile, derive design principles from daily use, and argue that the function the prosthesis must own is connection — reconnecting dispersed context across sources and time — which for this profile is not merely effortful but structurally unsupported. This works for someone with an unusually high digital footprint; capturing a low-footprint life remains open.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computers and Accessibility

title: Auxel: A Multi-Agent Conversational Data-Analysis Assistant for Blind and Low-Vision Users
abstract: Blind and low-vision (BLV) users increasingly have access to AI-powered data analysis tools such as Excel Copilot, ChatGPT Advanced Data Analysis, Claude for Excel, and Gemini in Sheets. While these systems can successfully analyze tabular data, they largely assume a sighted interaction model in which users inspect visual tables, charts, and formatted outputs. As a result, the final presentation of results—and the interaction required to explore them—remains a significant accessibility barrier. To address this, we developed Auxel, a web-based conversational data assistant that enables BLV users to interact with spreadsheet data via natural-language speech or text, while a multi-agent pipeline performs ambiguity resolution, intent classification, code generation, and response synthesis. Rather than simply returning visual outputs, Auxel generates multimodal, screen-reader-optimized responses, including concise spoken summaries, accessible tables, and interactive grid views designed for efficient exploration with assistive technologies. This demo presents Auxel running live in a web browser with both JAWS and VoiceOver. We also discuss implementation insights gained while engineering a highly interactive web interface for screen-reader users, including undocumented differences in JAWS and VoiceOver behavior, practical limitations of current WAI-ARIA guidance for complex data interfaces, and the design trade-offs required to support consistent accessible interactions across assistive technologies.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computers and Accessibility

title: Voice Over Persona: Dialogue Modality Drives Player Engagement and Immersion in LLM-Driven AI Agents in Games
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled Non-Player Characters (NPCs) in video games to generate context-aware, real-time dialogue, opening new possibilities for designing richer and more immersive player experiences [14]. However, the effects of specific NPC design variables on player experience remain empirically underexplored. This paper presents a work-in-progress study examining how NPC persona (Empathic/Supportive vs. Low-Empathy/Task-focused) and dialogue modality (Text vs. Voice) influence player emotional response, engagement, and immersion in an AI-driven game environment. A Unity-based first-person detective game prototype was developed, in which an AI-driven NPC mentor guides players through a fictional investigation. Using a 2 × 2 within-subjects factorial design, 23 adult university students each completed four gameplay scenarios representing all combinations of persona and modality. Player experience was measured after each scenario using the Self-Assessment Manikin (SAM), the User Engagement Scale Short Form (UES-SF), and two subscales of the Immersive Experience Questionnaire (IEQ). Results indicated that dialogue modality had a consistent and significant effect on player experience, with voice-based interaction producing significantly higher scores on IEQ Emotional Involvement and UES Focused Attention compared to text-based interaction, and marginal trends in the same direction across all remaining measures. NPC persona did not produce significant differences in any measure; a result interpreted as reflecting the brief scenario duration and inherent variability of real-time LLM-generated dialogue rather than the absence of any persona effect. No significant interaction between persona and modality was found. These findings suggest that the modality through which players communicate with an AI-driven NPC is a more immediate impactful design decision, offering practical guidance for developers designing LLM-driven NPC systems in narrative games. Future work will include studies to investigate how specific NPC communication styles impact player experience in prolonged multiple round game levels.
journal: Companion Proceedings of the Annual Symposium on Computer-Human Interaction in Play

title: Serving the Player or Shaping Them? Game-Embedded AI Companions and the Rewiring of Well-being
abstract: AI companions are increasingly embedded in games. Prior work highlights the benefits of companions in games for improved mental-health; however, these systems raise concerns around dependency, safety, and ethical responsibility. In this provocation, we argue game-embedded AI companions must be critically reframed as neuropsychologically adaptive agents capable of shaping players’ cognitive and emotional processes over time, often in ways that may be opaque to players or difficult to meaningfully consent to. Drawing on psychology, cognitive neuroscience, ethics, HCI, and game design, we call for a shift from short-term outcomes toward understanding how AI companions may actively rewire well-being through play.
journal: Companion Proceedings of the Annual Symposium on Computer-Human Interaction in Play

title: Adapting DNNs to Embrace Voltage Scaling Induced Errors via Accumulation-Aware Quantization
abstract: The pervasive deployment of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) across the computing spectrum has brought growing attention to energy efficiency, alongside raw performance. While voltage scaling is a potent knob for power reduction, its application in next-generation nodes is hampered by severe throughput degradation and susceptibility to process variation. This work aims to address these energy-reliability trade-offs by introducing a hardware-software co-design methodology, based on the observation that timing-robust bit ranges within the accumulator of a systolic array vary significantly across different voltage-frequency operating points. At the software level, we propose an Accumulation-Aware Training approach that incorporates this information as a first-order optimization constraint during training. By integrating mixed-precision quantization with unstructured pruning, we effectively constrain the model's weight distribution to avoid activating the hardware's sensitized high-rank carry chains. At the architectural level, we complement this with selective MSB-masking and fine-grained clock-gating to minimize unnecessary dynamic switching activity. Furthermore, we employ a layer-wise Dynamic Frequency Scaling strategy to further adapt to the accumulator's reduced dynamic range, based on the numerical sensitivity of each layer. We experimentally evaluate the proposed solution on a deep scaled 2nm technology node and demonstrate that, when operating at a low-voltage frontier, our co-optimized post-layout architecture delivers substantial energy and energy-delay product gains of 39% and 23% respectively, relative to the nominal voltage implementation, while maintaining accuracy degradation within 1%.

title: Knowing When to Trust Cheap Retrieval: A Calibration and Cost-Aware Decision Layer for Open-Vocabulary Temporal Change Retrieval
abstract: Multimodal information retrieval in remote sensing increasingly poses free-text questions about time: given co-registered image pairs (T1, T2) of one location at two acquisition times, the task is to retrieve the pairs in which a described change — for example, “low vegetation became bare ground” — has occurred. The efficient way to serve this is to keep a large vision–language model frozen, embed each pair once, cache the result, and answer queries by vector arithmetic. We study what such a cheap, training-free pipeline can and cannot deliver, and contribute the decision machinery that makes it deployable. Under a pre-registered protocol on a public bi-temporal benchmark, with queries posed as templated transitions over six land-cover classes, a frozen encoder carries genuine ranking signal: 18 of 22 supported change transitions are forward-reliable at a false-discovery rate of q ≤ 0.05. As a per-item decision, however, it only ties a base-rate predictor on a coverage-fair selective-risk metric. Across three frozen encoders it never beats that predictor: it ties on two and is significantly worse on the third — the one whose ranking map is the strongest — so ranking quality does not purchase per-item decision quality. Re-pricing the same decisions under asymmetric misclassification costs recovers an operating envelope in which acting on the cheap signal is cheaper than following prevalence, and this advantage appears only where the ranking signal is genuine. The contribution is a near-zero-compute calibration-and-cost decision layer, evaluated jointly for effectiveness and serving cost, that tells an operator when a frozen, cache-once retriever is worth trusting, rather than a new backbone or a leaderboard number.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 The 2nd EReL@MIR Workshop on Efficient Representation Learning for Multimodal Information Retrieval

title: Cryptic diversity in groundwater amphipods of Iran: insights from morphological and molecular approaches
abstract: Groundwater ecosystems host a diverse yet poorly understood fauna, largely due to their inaccessibility and the prevalence of cryptic species. These organisms often exhibit convergent adaptations (troglomorphy), such as loss of pigmentation and eyes, which can mask true phylogenetic relationships and impede species delimitation based solely on morphology. This study investigates the diversity of three populations of the stygobiont amphipod genus Niphargus from springs in Iran using an integrative taxonomic approach, combining molecular data (mitochondrial COI and nuclear 28S rRNA genes) with traditional morphological analysis. Phylogenetic reconstructions placed all three populations within the N. alisadri subclade. Despite minimal differentiation in the 28S marker and only subtle morphological divergence, species delimitation analyses (ASAP and bPTP) of COI sequences and genetic distance calculations identified the populations as comprising two putative new species. We describe these as N. hamedanensis sp. nov. and N. arakensis sp. nov. The small but significant genetic and inferred functional differences between these species and N. alisadri suggest a recent evolutionary divergence, potentially driven by allopatric isolation in higher altitude refugia. This discovery of cryptic diversity highlights the necessity of molecular methods for uncovering groundwater biodiversity and presents a model system for studying the initial stages of speciation in subterranean environments.

title: Research on the Pricing of Green Asset Securitization: A case Study of “Yingfeng 2024-1 ABS”
abstract: To address global environmental challenges, green finance has embraced green asset securitization (Green ABS) as an innovative tool, reducing corporate financing costs and meeting investors’ risk diversification needs. However, current Green ABS pricing largely relies on traditional securitization frameworks, failing to fully leverage green attributes and undermining product competitiveness. Using the “Yingfeng 2024-1 Asset-Backed Securities” as an empirical case, this paper analyzes Green ABS pricing models, summarizes existing research, identifies systemic deficiencies, and proposes a comprehensive pricing structure. Integrating the CIR model, option-adjusted spread, and Monte Carlo simulation for interest rate forecasting, coupled with multiple linear regression for issuing spread assessment, the model derives discount rates and theoretical valuations. Analysis of the “Yingfeng 2024” project—covering asset composition, cash flow projections, and rate simulations—yields a theoretical value of 2.095 billion yuan, marginally higher than the actual issuance price. Finally, measures to optimize information disclosure, standardize third-party certification, and promote green investment are proposed to support stable market growth and rational pricing for issuers and investors.

title: SUSTAINABLE E-LEADERSHIP AND ORGANIZATIONAL TRANSFORMATION: THE ROLES OF FLEXIBILITY, DIGITALIZATION, AND CULTURE IN ENHANCING OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY
abstract: The given paper analyzes the contribution of sustainable e-leadership (SEL) to the efficiency of operations with the help of the mediating variables, such as organizational flexibility (OF) and digitalization (DIG), and the moderating role of digital organizational culture (DOC). Based on the Resource-Based View (RBV), the conceptual framework of the study is sustainable eleadership that is a crucial intangible asset that helps organizations transform flexible structures and digitalized operational processes to effective and reliable performance results in dynamic and highly regulated environments. Data were collected from 300 senior and middle managers across 15 Jordanian commercial banks—a highly regulated sector undergoing intensive digital pressure in an emerging-economy context—using an online survey. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) provided by SmartPLS 4.0 was imposed on the proposed research model. The results indicate that sustainable e-leadership affects both flexibility and digitalization of organizations significantly in a positive manner that leads to improvement in operational efficiency. Besides, organizational flexibility and digitalization can work as independent and sequential mediators exposing a multistage process of capability development in which leadership initiatives are transformed into effective everyday operations. The findings show as well that digital organizational culture reinforces the effect of sustainable e-leadership on flexibility and digitalization, which determines the degree to which digital initiatives are institutionalized into consistent operating patterns, instead of being a solitary technological endeavor. Focusing on the organizational change as the process of increasing efficiency in operations under the leadership, flexibility, digitalization and cultural fit, this research adds the RBV knowledge to the operational segment of digital leadership. The paper makes theoretical contributions by explaining how e-leadership-facilitating capabilities contribute to efficiency-oriented change and offers practical implications to the banking managers looking to increase flexibility, instill digitalization in their operations, and promote a culture that encourages sustainable operational excellence.

title: DETERMINANTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION STRATEGIES AMONG RICE (ORYZA SATIVA L.) FARMING HOUSEHOLDS IN BENUE STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: The study examined the determinants of climate change adaptation strategies among rice (Oryza sativa L.) farmers in Benue State, Nigeria. Multistage sampling technique was used to select 498 rice farmers across 24 rice farming communities, 6 Local Government Areas and 3 Agricultural Zones. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and analysed using descriptive statistics and multinomial logit model. Results showed that fertilizer application (85.94%), multiple plots (69.28%) and improved rice varieties (68.27%) were the major climate change adaptation strategies used. Age negatively influenced the tendency of using multiple plots (-0.030, P<0.05) and education positively influenced the probability of using improved rice varieties (0.119, P<0.01). Also, climate change experience positively influenced the probability of using multiple plots (0.166), crop diversification (0.166), multiple planting dates (0.150), irrigation (0.207), trees planting (0.319) at P<0.01 and improved rice varieties (0.146) at P<0.05. The study concluded that rice farmers in Benue State are actively engaged in adapting to climate change which is driven by experience and influenced by a spectrum of socio-economic factors (sex, age, education, experience, credit access, extension, cooperative membership) that influence the choice of specific climate change adaptation strategies among rice farmers. The study recommended that farmers should be encouraged and supported by government through extension services to scale up the adoption of climate change adaptation strategies. Also, government and relevant organisations should establish user-friendly climate information service systems that provide timely, accurate and context-specific climate forecasts, advisories and early warning signs.
journal: FUDMA Journal of Agriculture and Agricultural Technology

title: Mechanical Interactions Between Agricultural Machinery and Soil and Crop-Derived Media: Mechanisms, Modeling, and Engineering Applications
abstract: This review focuses on the basic mechanisms, media responses, modeling methods, and engineering applications of agricultural machinery–media interactions, and presents an integrated framework linking mechanical interaction mechanisms to equipment design and operational regulation. This review analyzes the transmission and dissipation mechanisms of mechanical loads in agricultural media. Typical responses in soil–machinery and crop–machinery interactions are summarized, with soil emphasis on cutting, disturbance, compaction, and residue coupling, and crop emphasis on cutting, bending, compression, impact, threshing, and grasping-induced damage. Subsequently, experimental characterization, discrete element method (DEM), multibody dynamics, and coupled modeling methods such as DEM–FEM and DEM–CFD are reviewed. On this basis, this review further discusses pathways for translating mechanical insights into engineering applications, including geometric structure optimization, material and surface engineering, operating parameter matching, low-damage equipment design, and adaptive machinery–media interactions. The above analysis indicates that existing research has increasingly linked material properties and interfacial interactions with numerical simulation and parameter calibration to equipment optimization and intelligent control. However, the cross-material and cross-condition transferability of models under complex field conditions, the computational efficiency of coupled models, and the cross-scale correlation between microdamage evolution and macroscopic agronomic effects remain the main challenges. Future work should integrate mechanism models, data-driven approaches and digital twins, and link machinery mechanical response with soil, crop and energy consumption indicators to support the design of low-disturbance, low-damage agricultural machinery.

title: Effects of Residue Burial Depth and Rate on Soil Fertility and Pineapple Yield in Tropical Cultivation Systems
abstract: Pineapple is widely cultivated in tropical regions, but intensive management and improper residue disposal can accelerate soil degradation and yield decline. To evaluate under-ridge residue burial (URRB) as a soil improvement practice, parallel field experiments were conducted from 2023 to 2024 at two sites in tropical southern China. A two-factor randomized complete block design was used, with two burial rates (half- and full-rate, i.e., 10 and 20 t ha−1) and three burial depths (10, 20, and 30 cm), plus a residue removal control (CK). Compared with CK, URRB generally increased soil pH and the stocks of soil organic carbon and available nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K), accompanied by higher leaf area index (LAI), total root surface area (TRSA), photosynthetic pigment contents, fruit vitamin C content, and plant N, P, and K accumulation. Increasing burial rate significantly enhanced plant P and K accumulation and fruit yield, while burial at 30 cm produced greater improvements in soil pH, soil organic carbon (SOC), and available N, P, and K stocks than burial at 10 cm and 20 cm. Compared with other treatments, full-rate residue burial at 30 cm depth under the ridge (FD30) most effectively promoted canopy growth, root development, fruit yield, and chlorophyll a content. On average across the two sites, FD30 increased LAI and TRSA by 20.9% and 34.0%, respectively, compared with CK, with significant increases of 20.1% in fruit yield and 25.3% in fruit vitamin C content. Partial least squares path modeling identified positive indirect associations of soil pH and nutrient availability with yield. Although pineapple yield did not differ significantly between FD30 and FD10, SOC, available N, P, and K stocks were significantly greater under FD30 than under FD10. Thus, FD30 is a more promising strategy for improving both soil fertility and pineapple production under the present experimental conditions. This study also provides new insights into crop residue management in tropical cultivation systems.

title: Machine Learning Assisted Optimization of Climate-Resilient Smart Greenhouse Microgrids
abstract: Modern greenhouse horticulture under the Agriculture 4.0 paradigm relies heavily on smart, automated, and energy-intensive climate control, making a reliable and sustainable power supply a core operational requirement. This study presents a data-driven, machine learning (ML)-assisted framework to optimize a smart hybrid microgrid—combining photovoltaic (PV), wind, battery energy storage, and limited backup generation with demand-side load flexibility—for a 5-hectare greenhouse cooperative in Çanakkale, Türkiye. To capture meteorological variability and smart farming load dynamics, five statistically independent hourly realizations (43,800 operating hours) were generated from published climate statistics and coupled with a weather-responsive electricity demand model. Using a 1505-point experimental design (comprising 1500 Latin hypercube samples augmented with 5 benchmark configurations) and chronological dispatch simulations, three surrogate algorithms (random forest, extremely randomized trees, and histogram gradient boosting) were evaluated to predict key socio-economic and environmental metrics: levelized cost of electricity (LCOE), life-cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) intensity, loss-of-power-supply probability (LPSP), and renewable fraction. Multi-objective Pareto screening and subsequent full chronological verification identified an optimal compromise configuration comprising 1040 kW PV, 50 kW wind, 2000 kWh/540 kW battery storage, 105 kW diesel reserve, and 19.9% flexible load capacity. The optimized smart microgrid achieved an LCOE of 0.208 USD/kWh, a GHG intensity of 0.074 kg CO2e/kWh, a worst-realization LPSP of 0.042%, and a mean renewable fraction of 99.3%. Compared to traditional fossil-fuel energy supply, the proposed system reduced energy costs by 65.9%, carbon footprint by 94.7%, and diesel reliance by 99.4%. The findings demonstrate that integrating ML surrogates with smart demand scheduling offers a scalable and transferable digital pathway toward energy-autonomous, decarbonized, and resilient Agriculture 4.0 greenhouse operations.

title: β-Sitosterol–Naringenin Co-Loaded Nanophytosomes: Encapsulation, Compound-Specific Release Kinetics, Machine Learning-Assisted Release Prediction, and Cell-Dependent Anticancer Activity
abstract: β-Sitosterol and naringenin have anticancer potential but poor biopharmaceutical properties, while their behavior when co-encapsulated remains poorly defined. This study examined whether co-loading alters encapsulation efficiency, compound-specific release behavior, predictability, and cell-dependent activity. Single- and co-loaded nanophytosomes were characterized for encapsulation and release. Release profiles underwent comparative kinetic modelling, uncertainty-aware augmentation, early-to-late ridge-regression forecasting, Weibull-parameter reconstruction, and exploratory reconstructed-replicate holdout assessment. Cytotoxicity was assessed in A549 (ATCC CCL-185), HCT116 (ATCC CCL-247), and HEK293 (ATCC CRL-1573) cells, with docking against MEK1, COX-2, and PI3Kα. Co-loading increased β-sitosterol encapsulation from 5.92% to 66.61% but reduced naringenin encapsulation from 89.76% to 40.40% (p = 0.02), the co-loaded formulation also exhibited the smallest vesicles (132.7 ± 3.2 nm). At 48 h, release reached 87.30% and 73.24%, respectively; Weibull best described β-sitosterol and Higuchi naringenin, revealing asynchronous release and a time-dependent delivery ratio. Across 1200 augmented profiles, first-4-h measurements predicted 6–48-h release with R2 = 0.976–0.996, while parameter-based reconstruction reproduced compound-specific trajectories. Exploratory reconstructed-replicate assessment yielded a pooled R2 of 0.938 (mean absolute error (MAE) = 3.32%; root-mean-square error (RMSE) = 4.78%). The co-loaded formulation showed its strongest relative activity in A549 cells and better preserved HEK293 viability than the free combination, whereas the free combination was more active in HCT116 cells. Naringenin docked across all targets (7.58 to −8.40 kcal/mol), whereas β-sitosterol showed weaker binding and no COX-2 pose. Co-loading was associated with opposing encapsulation trends, while the resulting formulation exhibited compound-specific release kinetics and cell-dependent responses rather than uniformly enhanced activity. Integrating physicochemical characterization, kinetic discrimination, predictive modelling, docking, and cell testing provides a multidimensional framework for dual-bioactive nanophytosomes.

title: Sustainable Freight Modal Allocation Using an Integrated Modelling and CRITIC–SREM Framework
abstract: Freight modal allocation requires balancing economic efficiency, operational performance, environmental impacts, reliability, and infrastructure capacity. This study develops an integrated ANN–CRITIC–SREM framework for evaluating alternative freight allocations among road, rail, and inland waterway transport. The framework is demonstrated through a case study of the Prahovo–Šabac corridor in Serbia. Latin hypercube sampling was used to generate representative system states for training and validating a multi-output feed-forward artificial neural network employed as a surrogate model for simultaneously estimating six decision criteria. The CRITIC method was used to determine objective criterion weights, while SREM was applied to rank the alternatives. The ANN showed close agreement with engineering-generated reference values on an independent testing subset within the defined parameter ranges. Under the adopted baseline assumptions, the alternative comprising 60% road and 40% rail transport achieved the highest overall score. Sensitivity analysis showed that this alternative remained preferred for most analysed values of the SREM balancing coefficient, whereas urgent-delivery, environmental-priority, and capacity-priority scenarios favoured different modal structures. The results indicate that the integrated framework provides a transparent and flexible decision-support basis for evaluating freight modal allocation under changing economic, operational, environmental, and capacity-related priorities.

title: CA-Mamba: A Change-Aware Mamba Decoding Framework for Remote Sensing Binary Change Detection
abstract: Remote sensing binary change detection aims to identify real changes in bi-temporal images while suppressing pseudo-change responses induced by complex backgrounds and temporal variations in otherwise unchanged regions. Although existing state-space-based methods incorporate cross-temporal interaction, integrating explicit difference priors into state-space parameter generation and subsequent boundary-aware decoding remains an important design problem. To address this problem, CA-Mamba, a change-aware Mamba decoding framework, is proposed. An Asymmetric Change-Aware State-Space Mixer (ACSSM) is introduced to condition state-space parameter generation on bi-temporal difference priors and to modulate the two temporal branches asymmetrically. The Cascaded Difference Prior Module (CDPM), the Change Boundary Enhancement (CBE) module, and the Change Representation Constructor (CRC) are further integrated into a unified pipeline for difference-prior generation and propagation, change-aware mixing, boundary enhancement, and region–boundary collaborative representation construction. Experiments on four public datasets, namely, LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, CDD, and CLCD, show competitive detection performance. Ablation results support the use of signed-difference pathways and the overall CRC design under the evaluated settings. The efficiency analysis characterizes the trade-offs among detection accuracy, reported computational cost, inference latency, and parameter storage.

title: WRA-FPN: Weak-Response-Aware Feature Pyramid Network for Tiny Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images
abstract: Tiny object detection remains challenging because tiny instances often occupy only a few pixels, yielding weak, sparse, and easily degraded feature responses. Feature Pyramid Networks (FPNs) are widely used to construct multi-scale feature representations, but they still face two key limitations in tiny object detection. First, conventional FPNs do not explicitly enhance weak target responses. Although existing methods leverage frequency-domain information to strengthen structural details, high-frequency responses can originate from both target boundaries and complex background textures, making indiscriminate enhancement vulnerable to background interference. Second, sparse evidence from tiny objects is highly sensitive to minor spatial deviations during cross-scale propagation and can be diluted by background-dominated feature aggregation. To address these challenges, we propose a Weak-Response-Aware Feature Pyramid Network (WRA-FPN) comprising two complementary components. The Selective Wavelet Enhancement (SWE) module uses scale-adaptive Mexican-hat wavelets to extract localized high-frequency responses and fuses them with input features and high-level semantic features to generate spatial selection weights that enhance target-relevant cues while suppressing background interference. A target–background response constraint further improves feature discriminability. The Adaptive Local–Global Alignment (ALGA) module combines continuous local cross-scale interactions with region-level global dependencies to improve spatial correspondence and preserve weak target evidence, while adaptively fusing local and global information. Extensive experiments on AI-TOD, VisDrone2019, and MS COCO 2017, using multiple representative baseline detectors including RetinaNet, Faster R-CNN, Cascade R-CNN, and DetectoRS, demonstrate improved detection performance of WRA-FPN. On AI-TOD, WRA-FPN improves AP by 4.4% and 2.4% over the corresponding RetinaNet and DetectoRS baselines, respectively.

title: UniRS-Seg: Shared Sparse–Dense Query Decoding for Joint Semantic and Referring Remote Sensing Segmentation
abstract: Remote sensing semantic and referring segmentation share mask geometry but differ in whether a category vocabulary or a natural-language expression selects the output. UniRS-Seg bridges these interfaces through a shared sparse–dense query compiler and a hierarchical mask decoder, jointly trained on independently annotated datasets. Class names and referring expressions are projected from SigLIP 2 into the same decoder space; dense image–query activations supply spatial support, and sparse query tokens specify the requested region. An adapted SAM ViT-B pathway and parallel convolutional features recover local geometry, while learnable soft mask cross-attention refines both tasks and class-balanced mask-guided self-attention supports semantic parsing. UniRS-Seg achieves 57.30%, 85.31%, and 88.24% mIoU on LoveDA, Vaihingen, and Potsdam, and 78.18% and 70.88% gIoU on RefSegRS and RRSIS-D. These scores exceed the strongest listed baseline means by 0.68, 0.99, 1.18, 0.79, and 1.71 percentage points, respectively. Against separately trained semantic-only and referring-only versions of the shared architecture, joint training improves the four evaluated datasets by 0.45, 0.89, 1.40, and 0.97 points. An additional supervised RISBench evaluation achieves 72.91% gIoU and 74.85% cIoU, with the highest gIoU among the listed methods. On RefSegRS, adding learnable mask cross-attention to combined sparse and dense prompts increases gIoU by 0.86 points. The results support supervised dual-task transfer through a common query-conditioned decoder; the comparison uses published baseline results and does not establish unseen-domain or zero-shot generalization.

title: Local-to-Global Shape-Consistent Learning for Boundary-Reliable Agricultural Object Extraction from High-Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: Accurate agricultural object extraction from high-resolution remote sensing imagery requires not only high regional segmentation accuracy but also reliable object geometry. Yet most semantic segmentation frameworks are optimized primarily for pixel- or region-level agreement, so high overlap scores can coexist with boundary discontinuities, object merging, and structurally inconsistent predictions. To address this mismatch, we propose Attention-enhanced DeepLab V3+ with Local-to-Global Shape Consistency (ADLSC), a local-to-global framework that coordinates semantic discrimination, adaptive boundary representation, and complete-object geometric consistency. Target-aware multiscale context strengthens target–background discrimination, contour-adaptive representation adjusts sampling to local boundary variation while preserving narrow inter-object separation, and a staged hierarchical objective extends optimization from regional agreement to curvature- and shape-related consistency. On cropland parcel and greenhouse facility datasets, ADLSC improves IoU by 8.28 and 15.92 percentage points and matching rate by 24.32 and 42.88 percentage points, respectively, relative to DeepLab V3+, while reducing curvature and shape errors. The larger gains in object matching than in regional overlap show that explicitly coupling local contour adaptation with object-level geometric constraints improves aspects of segmentation quality that pixel-oriented objectives alone do not capture, supporting more reliable object-based agricultural mapping and spatial analysis.

title: Poor-Laying Hen Identification by Integrating HVI Color-Space Transformation and Differentiable Histogram
abstract: Identifying poor-laying hens is important for reducing feed waste, but visual screening is labor-intensive. Motivated by the relationship between laying status and pigmentation, we propose CHIC (Color-Histogram Integrated Classifier), a lightweight model combining HVI (Horizontal, Vertical, Intensity) transformation with differentiable histogram encoding of learned feature activations and global-average-pooled features. Evaluation used a four-class head-and-leg patch dataset collected from 20 hens in six cages at a single facility, with cage-level laying-status labels. Across ten training runs with different development-data folds and a fixed frame-level test set, CHIC achieved mean binary F1-scores of 92.21% for head patches and 96.06% for leg patches, exceeding the MobileNetV4-S baselines. With 2.69 million parameters, the classifier had a mean forward-pass latency of 21.87 ms per patch on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super. Component comparisons showed configuration-dependent effects; histogram integration also benefited grayscale inputs, while mean–standard-deviation pooling with HVI inputs achieved similar mean performance to CHIC. The classification advantage was maintained when predictions from detected head and leg regions were aggregated into hen-level decisions. However, performance declined substantially on unseen cages. These findings support CHIC as a candidate for automated poor-laying hen screening, with further validation required across independent hens and farms.

title: KrishiTech: A Multilingual Smart Farming Assistance Platform
abstract: Farmers frequently need to consult separate sources for weather information, crop selection, crop health guidance, market prices, government support, and equipment access. KrishiTech is a web-based farming assistance platform designed to bring these services together in a single interface. It is implemented using the MERN stack: MongoDB, Express.js, React.js, and Node.js. The application includes weather information, rule-based crop recommendations, image-based crop disease screening through an external Plant.id service, agricultural market-price comparison, a farm-profit calculator, fertilizer guidance, government-scheme information, equipment rental and booking, and a seeds-and-fertilizers marketplace. English, Kannada, and Telugu interface options are provided, alongside a multilingual chatbot and browser-based voice navigation. Farmer and administrator functions are separated through role-based access control; account passwords are hashed using bcryptjs, and protected requests use JSON Web Tokens (JWT). This paper presents the platform’s requirements, architecture, modules, data model, implementation approach, and preliminary functional observations. The current evidence describes implemented features rather than measured agricultural outcomes. No controlled farmer study, diagnostic benchmark, or yield-impact experiment is claimed. Formal usability evaluation, independent validation of disease predictions, and verification of the timeliness and accuracy of market data remain important next steps
journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

title: Agent-to-Agent Synthetic Social Engineering on the Web
abstract: An AI agent can prepare an accurate report and still request an action its user has not authorized. Cooperation across Web services therefore requires separate judgments about identity, evidentiary support, and permission. We define synthetic social engineering (SSE) as deliberately deceptive or misleading influence intended to exploit AI recipients' responses to credibility, authority, or obligation cues and redirect behavior away from authorized objectives. We focus on separately tasked sender agents that produce or adapt misleading communication. Drawing on cybersecurity, social engineering, and persuasion research, we develop an operational framework connecting actors, deceptive representations, candidate influence routes, evidence or permission boundaries, responses, and consequences. The framework distinguishes attempts from successful redirection, without assuming human psychological processes. We implement it in the Agent Service Exchange and Evidence Commons (ASE-EC), a reproducible testbed with independently specified records and authorization scopes. Across 1,260 research episodes using Qwen3-4B in two fictional briefing tasks, matched comparisons test authority and commitment appeals, while defense comparisons assess protection alongside authorized task completion. Invoking a limited prior agreement increased unauthorized requests from 43.3% to 96.7%, although recipients retained supported decisions and permissions remained unchanged. These controlled findings identify action selection as a distinct security concern, even when evidence handling succeeds, and they provide a reusable basis for evaluating safeguards that preserve useful cooperation across Web services.

title: Freezing Mechanism and Topology Dependence of Information Flow Structure in Small-Scale Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: The neighborhood topology of particle swarm optimization (PSO) determines information propagation and regulates the exploration-exploitation balance. However, existing evaluation methods based on fitness and spatial diversity fail to characterize the dynamic evolution internal interaction structure of the population. To address this gap, this paper focuses on small-scale PSO (20-50 particles) with regular topologies and models the iterative process as a dynamic weighted influence graph. We construct a multi-scale information-flow evaluation framework covering micro-, meso-, and macro-level metrics, and propose a freeze-point detection method based on effective nodes, a macro-level distributional metric. Experiments on CEC2017 benchmark functions show that the information flow structure freezes early in the search (3 percent - 22 percent for representative configurations and 15 percent-49 percent for global medians) and remains unchanged thereafter. The freeze time follows the order Gbest$<$ Von Neumann $<$Ring, consistent across standard, LDIW, and TVAC variants. Parameter-adaptive variants delay freezing without altering the topological order, and the freeze point is significantly negatively correlated with final solution quality. Intervention experiments under Gbest show that weakening hub nodes delays freezing and improves performance on multimodal functions, while strengthening hubs produces no additional deterioration due to saturation, revealing a decoupling between structural and performance effects. Among the three metric levels, only macro-level distributional metrics effectively capture freezing under regular topologies, because micro- and meso-level structures are predetermined by the topology. These findings reveal the freezing mechanism of information flow in small-scale PSO and provide structural prior signals for adaptive topology control.

title: Optimization-based Cell Average Limiters as Metric Projections: Constrained Evolution and Convergence Analysis for Convection-diffusion Equations
abstract: The optimization-based cell average limiter enforces global conservation and bounds, and has been successfully applied to discontinuous Galerkin (DG) discretizations of a wide range of nonlinear systems, from phase-field models to the compressible Navier-Stokes equations. In this paper, taking the heat and convection-diffusion equations as prototypes, we analyze the convergence of the scheme resulting from cell average limiting. Encoding conservation and admissibility in a differential inclusion identifies the limiter as a backward Euler proximal step in a Lie splitting of the constrained evolution. This proximal step is the metric projection onto the convex admissible set, and we prove that it is nonexpansive and stable in the $L^2$ norm, and that it does not increase the total variation of the cell averages. Combined with the standard error analysis, nonexpansiveness yields an $O(τ+h^{k+1})$ estimate for implicit Euler time stepping with DG discretization of polynomial degree $k$ under a reverse CFL condition, together with an unconditional $O(τ+h^{k})$ estimate. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates and the enforcement of the bounds.

title: Cross-Bond Panel Learning for Next-Day Price Forecasting of Chinese Convertible Bonds: A Reality Check
abstract: Recent advances in financial machine learning have prompted growing interest in applying deep neural networks to convertible bond valuation and forecasting. However, existing studies often focus on in-sample valuation fit or cross-sectional return rankings, leaving out-of-sample next-day price forecasting insufficiently benchmarked against persistence. This paper provides a comprehensive empirical reality check on cross-bond panel learning for Chinese convertible bonds. Using a daily panel of 73,806 observations across 100 A-share convertible bonds from 2022 to 2025, we evaluate whether cross-bond neural architectures reliably outperform the random walk under strict temporal splitting, boundary purging, fold-specific preprocessing, and dependence-aware inference. On the 29,514-observation holdout, the random walk achieves an RMSE of 2.3577 CNY. Five-seed ensembles of small and large price-change MLPs yield RMSEs of 2.3619 and 2.3645 CNY, with negative out-of-sample R^2 values (-0.0035 and -0.0057) and target-date clustered HAC p-values of 0.453 and 0.248. Ten-day circular block-bootstrap intervals span zero, while direct price-level training degrades performance substantially. Although cross-bond pooling provides a variance-stabilizing shrinkage effect over single-bond estimation (lowering test RMSE for 79 of 90 individual bonds), it fails to produce an aggregate forecast advantage over persistence. Error decomposition reveals that failure is not uniform: five highly volatile, clause-sensitive bonds account for 74.4% of the model's total excess squared error. Without contemporaneous equity market information or explicit contractual event conditioning, deep panel architectures do not deliver incremental next-day predictability over persistence.

title: Semantic-First: Temporal Scheduling in Flow Matching for Reliable Emotional Image Generation
abstract: Affect-controlled image generation should change how a scene feels while preserving what the prompt specifies. We study the temporal allocation of stochastic exploration and policy optimization in flow-matching models as a means of controlling this balance. During RL training, our semantic-first schedule uses deterministic ordinary differential equation (ODE) sampling during the high-noise phase and confines stochastic differential equation (SDE) exploration and group relative policy optimization (GRPO) to a late window. Controlled experiments separate exploration location, optimization location, and terminal-step sampling, showing distinct semantic benefits from late exploration and late updates. On FLUX.1-dev, semantic-first improves prompt faithfulness, independently evaluated affect accuracy, and human-rated semantic preservation and overall preference. The expanded semantic audit records 2.7% subject drift, while GRPO training time decreases by 41.1% relative to original full-path Flow-GRPO. Window-width experiments characterize the affect-semantic and computational trade-offs, and replication on SD3.5-Medium reproduces the scheduling advantage. These results establish denoising time as a practical control dimension for reliable emotional image generation.

title: LegoSR: A Unified Framework for Self-improving Agent-Guided Scientific Discovery
abstract: Equation discovery solvers often use different data interfaces, equation representations and evaluation criteria, making their results difficult to compare. We present LegoSR, a unified framework for algebraic symbolic regression and differential equation discovery. LegoSR integrates seven solvers through a common equation representation and evaluation process, and supports searches constrained by partially known equations. Researchers can run solvers directly or use LegoSR Agent, which selects solvers and adapts searches based on solver knowledge, intermediate results and lessons from earlier tasks. On noisy ordinary and partial differential equation benchmarks, LegoSR Agent recovers nearly as many equations as the union of seven expert-tuned solvers and outperforms a generic agent with the same model, tools and budget by up to 29 percentage points. Three examples demonstrate basic use, adaptive solver selection and discovery guided by partial physical knowledge.

title: ReSight: Task-Driven Self-Improving Memory for Embodied Agents
abstract: Robots can use historical observations to answer spatiotemporal queries in familiar environments, but the presence of relevant evidence does not imply that existing tools support the operations a task requires. We introduce ReSight, a task-driven self-improving memory system for embodied agents that expands the capabilities for processing and accessing historical observations as task demands arise. ReSight retains keyframes and their spatiotemporal associations, separating observation evidence from extensible derived fields so that stored observations can be reprocessed for new needs. An execution agent and a coding agent share this memory through different interfaces: the former calls registered tools within a bounded online budget, while the latter uses a programmable workspace and a larger exploration budget to inspect evidence, write programs, and acquire models as needed. To realize capability expansion in ReSight, we develop Explore-Distill-Mount (EDM), which identifies capability gaps from execution and exploration records without task reference answers and converts exploration-derived solutions into reusable memory builders, query tools, and skills, extending memory representations and access capabilities as needed. Experiments on three public benchmarks demonstrate effective base memory access and capability expansion. With the execution model and online budget held fixed within each benchmark, EDM reduces mean position error on OC-NaVQA from 33.10 m to 24.72 m and improves high-level success on FindingDory from 38.3% to 63.8%. With the tools and skill frozen, success still improves by 28.3 percentage points on FindingDory episodes excluded from exploration and distillation. Experiments on real robot patrol memories further demonstrate reuse of these capabilities for subsequent queries and new memories, with fewer online tool calls on average.

title: Component Pooling Trained Across Orientations for Few-Shot Remote Sensing Scene Classification
abstract: Few-shot remote sensing scene classification (FSRSSC) aims to recognize novel scene categories from only a few labeled images. Most FSRSSC methods summarize the feature map of an image by global average pooling, which treats the few objects that define an aerial scene and the large background around them alike, and they rarely consider that aerial images have no canonical orientation. To address these issues, we propose RoCoP, a parameter-free component pooling network trained across orientations. RoCoP consists of a feature extractor, a non-negative decomposition module (NDM) and a component scoring module (CSM). NDM factorizes the local descriptors of each image into a few additive components with a deterministic initialization and a single multiplicative update, so that the positions of one object are grouped together. CSM weights each component by its activation magnitude and converts the weights into a soft mask for pooling. Because both modules are invariant to permutations of feature positions, the only rotation-sensitive part of the pipeline is the backbone, which we train to classify randomly rotated views of every image. Experiments on NWPU-RESISC45, AID and UC Merced show that component pooling and rotated-view training are complementary: together they improve a strong transfer-learning baseline by about 2.5 points in 5-way 1-shot accuracy on NWPU-RESISC45 and AID, without adding parameters at inference. Under an identical protocol, RoCoP outperforms re-implemented metric-based and task-adaptive methods, and NDM and CSM also improve existing methods when plugged into them. We further identify the regime in which the method does not apply, namely very small base sets.

title: Optimizing Physical Neural Networks through Device Variable Selection
abstract: Physical neural networks (PNNs) leverage device physics in electronics, optics, and related domains to enable energy-efficient neural networks. Broken-isomorphism PNNs replace linear operations with multivariate physical transformations, modifying how input signals are mapped to device variables. We exploit network architectures emerging from these mappings by treating the routing between signals and input variables of physical devices as trainable parameters. This approach expands device-level tunability of the physical transformations while, at the system level, demonstrating improved expressivity of PNNs with negligible additional inference overhead. This discrete routing is optimized by training a categorical distribution using Gumbel-Softmax reparametrization. We evaluate this approach using experimentally calibrated differentiable models of multivariate electronic RNPUs for MNIST and CIFAR-10 classification. Using variable selection, we improve the MNIST classification accuracy for a small CNN model from 94.5% to 96.9% and the accuracy of CIFAR-10 from 62.8% to 68.0%. Our method uniquely leverages the induced biases of broken-isomorphism PNN architectures, paving the way towards more efficient physics-based neural network inference.

title: Large spin large deviations for interacting particle systems
abstract: We propose a novel framework for analyzing the sample-path large deviations of interacting particle systems directly on a lattice by considering a large-spin limit ($s \to \infty$). Through an appropriate scaling of variables, the process concentrates around its deterministic trajectory, governed by the lattice diffusion equation. We quantify the exponential cost of observing atypical trajectories by explicitly computing the path-space large deviation rate function from the scaled microscopic generator, based on a theory due to Feng and Kurtz. The rate function is described in terms of a Hamiltonian on a lattice in terms of classical spin variables. Notably, for our main model, the symmetric harmonic process, the corresponding Hamiltonian is identified with the classical integrable non-compact Ishimori spin chain. Furthermore, we show that our large spin large deviation theory is fully consistent with traditional Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (MFT), smoothly recovering the standard MFT Hamiltonian in the spatial continuous limit. We also perform a Poisson-noise Martin--Siggia--Rose (MSR) computation to derive the non-linear lattice Hamiltonian directly from microscopic dynamics, use a relative entropy argument to obtain the density-current action, and establish the lattice fluctuation theorem alongside its symmetry origin. Overall, our framework provides a naturally regularized, lattice analogue of MFT that circumvents spatial ultraviolet singularities and possible continuous density blow-ups. We also apply our new scheme to partial symmetric exclusion process, symmetric inclusion processes, Brownian energy process and integrable heat conduction model, showing how their large-deviation Hamiltonians relate to classical compact and non-compact spin chains.

title: Path space large deviation on a lattice for interacting particle systems
abstract: We investigate the path space large deviation principle (LDP) for a class of interacting particle systems on a fixed finite discrete torus. As an illustrative example, we use the partial exclusion process with maximal occupation of $s$ particles. We first verify the standard Kurtz-type law of large numbers for the original and tilted processes, thereby identifying the deterministic flows around which the large deviations are formulated. We then establish the path space LDP, with speed $s$, and identify the associated rate function in variational form as the Legendre transform of a nonlinear Hamiltonian. The proof relies on martingale techniques, exponential tightness, and a change-of-measure argument based on exponential tilting, which renders atypical trajectories typical under a modified dynamics. We also explain how the same strategy extends to further interacting particle systems. The inclusion process illustrates the conservative non-compact finite-jump case. The harmonic process is qualitatively different: a single transition may move a variable number of particles, and the limiting Hamiltonian is logarithmic with a non-trivial domain. This places the harmonic process outside the usual finite-reaction framework for density-dependent Markov jump processes. Finally, we discuss continuous-state energy-exchange models, such as the Brownian energy process and an integrable heat-conduction model, to indicate how the same Hamiltonian large-deviation formalism appears beyond discrete-state particle systems.

title: Cross-Scale Sparse Attention for Referring Segmentation in Remote Sensing
abstract: High-resolution remote sensing (RS) imagery provides fine spatial detail over large areas, making it essential for fine-grained scene understanding. Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation (RRSIS) aims to segment regions described by natural language, yet many existing methods rely on sequential alignment--fusion pipelines with limited joint modeling of cross-scale visual hierarchies and linguistic dependencies. Moreover, dense attention mechanisms struggle with the sparsity and wide spatial dispersion of RS targets, while current datasets offer limited structured evaluation of multi-target references, multi-hop relational reasoning, and multi-granularity descriptions, limiting both model development and evaluation. To address these challenges, we propose a Cross-Scale Sparse Attention Model (CSSAM), which aligns multiscale visual features with complex referring expressions through two key modules. The Cross-scale Modality-aligned Fusion Module (CMFM) performs unified cross-scale cross-modal fusion, while the Dynamic Multimodal Sparse Hybrid Attention (DMSHA) selectively attends to informative visual--textual tokens, reducing dense visual interactions. Furthermore, we introduce M$^{3}$RRSIS-D, a RRSIS dataset explicitly designed around three core reasoning dimensions: multi-target (M$^{1}$), reference-dependent multi-hop (M$^{2}$), and multi-granularity (M$^{3}$) expressions. Extensive experiments on M$^{3}$RRSIS-D and two public RRSIS benchmarks demonstrate that CSSAM achieves competitive performance across accuracy, fine-grained reasoning, and high-IoU localization metrics, validating its effectiveness for complex semantic reasoning in realistic RS scenarios. Code, dataset, and model weights will be released upon acceptance.

title: Accelerating high-fidelity gyrokinetic fusion simulations with iGENE
abstract: We present the latest version of iGENE, a differentiable implementation of the local (flux-tube) gyrokinetic code GENE, now fully rewritten in JAX. iGENE features a multispecies, collisional, fully electromagnetic nonlinear gyrokinetic model while preserving end-to-end differentiability. The code is verified against GENE for linear ITG, TEM and KBM physics and for nonlinear turbulent fluxes with adiabatic and kinetic electrons. Forward-mode derivatives of the linear growth rate agree with finite differences for all five parameters tested, resolving the 30--50\% discrepancy in $\hat{s}$ and $\epsilon$ reported for the earlier TensorFlow version. All collectives are native JAX operations, and the code strong-scales from 2 to 32 H100 GPUs with 86\% parallel efficiency. We then assess three routes to a shorter time to solution. Custom CUDA FFT kernels operating in bfloat16 are up to $3.97\times$ faster than fp32 cuFFT on the transforms, and on a single H100 iGENE is $2.63\times$ faster per time step than single-precision GENE. Multi-rate sub-cycling of the parallel dynamics yields a further $1.89\times$ speedup with kinetic electrons. Finally, a Hermite-Laguerre velocity-space representation is implemented, offering tunable fidelity.

title: Developers as Managers of AI Agents: A Workplace Shadowing Study
abstract: As AI coding agents become more autonomous, developers increasingly direct, coordinate, and check their work. Yet little is known about these practices in everyday professional development. We shadowed 11 professional developers across approximately 15 hours of work, coded their activities and task transitions, analyzed 255 submitted prompts, and conducted 4.6 hours of follow-up interviews. Developers spent an average of 33.4% of observed time formulating prompts or checking AI responses, with task-switching rates ranging from 0 to 101.6 switches per hour. Beyond producing artifacts, prompts supported understanding, requirements clarification, agent configuration, and coordination. We identified three recurring patterns: \textit{Supervisor}, involving direct artifact inspection; \textit{Delegator}, involving dialogue-based coordination and delegated implementation and checking; and \textit{Learner}, involving agents primarily to build understanding. Developers sought technical information from agents and organizational context, authority, and alignment from colleagues. Our findings suggest future studies of how developers manage attention across concurrent agent tasks and tools that support verification, coordination, and learning.

title: Auditing evaluation artifacts and data leakage in large language model systems for rare disease diagnosis
abstract: Augmented large language model (LLM) systems have reported high benchmark accuracies in rare disease diagnosis, yet their real-world clinical utility remains unproven. A recent meta-analysis flagged augmented LLM diagnostic evaluations as having a high risk of bias due to suspected data leakage; however, the precise impact of these vulnerabilities on model inference has yet to be fully quantified. In this study, we present a comprehensive empirical audit to quantify evaluation artifacts across prevailing AI paradigms, using a repository of over 60,000 cases from diverse public and independent clinical cohorts. By reconstructing a state-of-the-art agentic framework, we demonstrate that candidate-space contamination artificially inflates performance: enforcing strict cross-dataset isolation resulted in a marked performance decline, with the cross-dataset mean Recall@1 decreasing from 54.3% (under conventional one-vs-rest evaluation) to 40.3% (Hedges' g = 0.94). Similar spatial overfitting in supervised classifiers caused diagnostic accuracy to drop from an internal mean of 42.9% to 16.7% across external cohorts (Cohen's d = 2.01). Furthermore, we quantify how LLMs infer diagnoses by exploiting retrospective therapeutic cues in clinical narratives, and how temporal misalignment in foundational knowledge bases leads to performance fluctuations. We conclude that prevailing evaluation protocols for augmented LLM systems inadvertently reflect data leakage rather than genuine medical reasoning.
