title: Thermodynamic origin of the phonon Hall effect in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
abstract: The underlying mechanism of the thermal Hall effect generated by phonons in a variety of insulators is yet to be identified. In this work, we report on a sizable thermal Hall conductivity in nickel phosphorus trisulfide (NiPS 3 ), a van der Waals stack of honeycomb layers with a zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The longitudinal (κ aa ) and the transverse (κ ab ) thermal conductivities peak at the same temperature, and the thermal Hall angle, at this peak, respects a previously identified bound. The amplitude of κ ab is extremely sensitive to the amplitude of magnetization along the b axis but is not correlated with the phonon mean free path, which points to an intrinsic origin.

title: Electronic bound states in the continuum in a two-dimensional metal
abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are quantum states that remain localized despite lying within a continuum of extended, delocalized states. Whereas optical BICs have been realized in photonic systems, achieving electronic bound states embedded in a metallic background remains an ongoing challenge. In this study, we used scanning tunneling microscopy to identify two defect-induced electronic states that remain localized within the metallic continuum of Pd 5 AlI 2 , a two-dimensional van der Waals metal. Our calculations suggest that electron-hopping interference on the decorated checkerboard lattice of Pd 5 AlI 2 gives rise to a (quasi) flat band built from spatially localized eigenstates that are orthogonal to the dispersive continuum. Atomic defects within this frustrated lattice shift the associated flat-band localized states into the metallic continuum, forming robust, symmetry-protected BICs.

title: Wireless electrocatalytic closed-loop system for drug-free management of diabesity
abstract: Lifestyle-related type 2 diabetes and associated obesity (diabesity) affect >2.5 billion people worldwide and impose nearly $3 trillion in annual health care costs. We developed an implantable, wirelessly powered electrocatalytic closed-loop health optimization (ECHO) device containing platinum-decorated gold nanoclusters embedded in graphite felt that enabled selective, electrically tunable oxidation of blood glucose to renally cleared gluconate. In type 2 diabetic mice, wireless, low-power activation (0.75 volts, 10 milliamperes) restored glucose homeostasis within 1 hour, shifted metabolism from glucose to lipid utilization, reduced body weight and triglycerides, and increased circulating free fatty acids and ketone bodies without detectable hypoglycemia or adverse physiological, inflammatory, or behavioral effects during 6 weeks of treatment. Coupling this ECHO device to a commercial continuous glucose monitoring system enabled autonomous, smartphone-controlled, drug-free closed-loop management of experimental diabesity.

title: BAK and BAX form a multiprotein complex to drive mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death
abstract: The apoptotic regulators BAX and BAK, once activated, form homo-oligomers to trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP), activating the apoptosome and caspases. Activation of BAX-BAK without apoptosome activation triggers sustained efflux of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and caspase-independent cell death. However, the molecular basis of mtDNA efflux remains unclear. We purified a macromolecular complex comprising BAK, BAX, activator BH3-only molecules, voltage-dependent anion channels 1 and 2 (VDAC1 and VDAC2), and prohibitins that released mtDNA from mitoplasts. BAX-BAK activation resulted in VDAC closure, mitochondrial calcium influx, and mtDNA efflux. Loss of VDAC1, VDAC2, or prohibitins prevented BAX-BAK activation–induced mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death without affecting MOMP or mitochondrial inner membrane herniation. These findings support differential regulation of cytochrome c and mtDNA efflux by distinct BAX-BAK complexes.

title: Intron retention regulates STAT2 function and associates with immunotherapy response in lung cancer
abstract: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the STAT2 gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti–programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in STAT2 as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.

title: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet
abstract: During interglaciations, the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS), which is the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, retreats to Arctic Canada, where it achieves a minimum configuration. The reexpansion of the LIS following this minimum marks the start of the next glaciation. Here, we show that the last remaining remnant of the most recent LIS, Barnes Ice Cap (Baffin Island, Canada), achieved its minimum interglacial dimensions after ~3.6 thousand years ago, before reexpanding ~2000 years ago, marking the onset of the next glaciation. The new LIS reached maximum dimensions in ~1960 CE, after which anthropogenic summer warming resulted in a negative mass balance, ice margin recession, and the termination of the next glaciation. The demise of the next glaciation, despite the ongoing decline in summer insolation, illustrates the influence of anomalous greenhouse gas forcing on climate.

title: Ultrarapid decision-making in an avian brain
abstract: Perceptual decision-making is well studied in mammals, but its operation in other vertebrates remains unclear. We show that carrion crows ( Corvus corone ) make deliberate decisions in a classic visual motion discrimination task with unprecedented speed, reporting choices in approximately 235 milliseconds on average, which is roughly twice as fast as has been observed in monkeys or humans and without sacrificing accuracy. Recordings from the pallial endbrain reveal that direction-selective neurons encode the upcoming choice as early as about 70 milliseconds after stimulus onset and about 170 milliseconds before the response, with ramping activity scaling with sensory evidence and converging at response onset. These findings highlight the extraordinary efficiency of avian decision-making circuitry, possibly shaped by evolutionary pressures for rapid visuomotor control.

title: Dynamic functionality–enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.

title: Imaging electron-hole asymmetry in the quantum melting of generalized Wigner crystals
abstract: Two-dimensional moiré materials provide a versatile platform to explore phase transitions in strongly correlated systems. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we imaged the density-driven melting of generalized Wigner crystals (GWCs) and Mott insulators (MIs) in electron-doped, near-60°–twisted molybdenum diselenide bilayers featuring a triangular moiré superlattice. We observed notable electron-hole asymmetry in GWC melting: Hole-doped GWCs yielded interaction-driven disordered states, whereas electron-doped GWCs melted into delocalized liquid-like states. This asymmetry arose from the broken particle-hole symmetry of the moiré superlattice, which produced electron and hole Fermi pockets with different momentum geometries upon GWC condensation. MI states melted without such asymmetry, consistent with the absence of a symmetry-breaking density modulation. This work provides direct visualization of the emergent phases that appear as GWCs undergo quantum melting transitions.

title: Visualizing symmetry-broken Chern insulators and their quantum melting
abstract: In the presence of a magnetic field, electronic states of moiré quantum materials develop a Hofstadter spectrum that provides a distinctive setting for studying the interplay between band topology and strong electron-electron interaction. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we studied Hofstadter’s states in bilayer graphene aligned with hexagonal boron nitride and directly visualized the formation of interaction-driven symmetry breaking Chern insulators. Our measurements revealed the formation of phases that double, triple, or quadruple the moiré unit cell at fractional filling of the Hofstadter bands as well as states with complex intra–unit cell wave functions. We visualized two distinct quantum phenomena in different Chern states, including quantum melting driven by the appearance and proliferation of topological defects and a quantum transition co-occurring with phase competition and separation.

title: Decoupled self-assembled monolayer and perovskite deposition for efficient flexible solar modules
abstract: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability of flexible perovskite solar modules (PSMs) are less than those of their rigid devices because surface hydroxyls desorption on flexible substrates, which disrupts self-assembled monolayer (SAM) anchoring and perovskite crystallization. We developed a decoupled SAM-perovskite codeposition strategy that accelerates SAM anchoring by reducing the SAM-perovskite interaction and ameliorates perovskite crystallization. The certified PCE with phenethylammonium iodide as the passivation molecule was 20.2% on PSMs with device areas of 750 cm 2 . With 1,3-diaminopropane dihydroiodide as the passivator, the PCE of 22.0% for a device area of 14.55 cm 2 decreased by 8% after 1044 hours under maximum power point tracking at 85°C and 65% relative humidity. The devices pass all sequences of an international commercialization assessment standard for flexible portable PSMs.

title: Natural product biosynthesis by guanidine prenyltransferases in plants and bacteria
abstract: Guanidine exists almost exclusively as a resonance-stabilized cation, making its direct enzymatic functionalization challenging. We identified the cyanobacterial enzyme NosH, which catalyzes direct prenyl transfer to free guanidine. Structural and mechanistic analyses revealed guanidine activation by a two-aspartate clamp coupled to prenyl-donor binding through a distinct catalytic architecture. Guided by these features, we identified a large family of guanidine prenyltransferases across bacteria and plants. Plant enzymes produced guanidine alkaloids such as galegine in vitro and heterologous expression of a plant ortholog in Nicotiana benthamiana produced galegine in planta, providing a direct enzymatic link to plant-specialized metabolism.

title: Sequential diagnosis with language models
abstract: We explored the capabilities of frontier language models in sequential diagnosis, a diagnostic paradigm that captures the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Given a brief clinical presentation, clinicians selectively acquired information to reach a diagnosis, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy and workup cost. We developed an interactive benchmark and an artificial intelligence (AI) system that simulates a panel of physicians, continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests. Using this benchmark, the system achieved 83.2% accuracy on New England Journal of Medicine clinicopathological conference cases and 80.3% on MIMIC-IV-ED emergency department admissions, outperforming generalist physicians (36.1 and 46.8%, respectively). Although these findings were obtained in a controlled benchmark setting, they highlight the promise of language models for supporting more accurate, lower-cost diagnoses.

title: Generalized continuous nowhere differentiable function families
abstract: The existence of continuous nowhere-differentiable functions is a fundamental phenomenon in real analysis, challenging the classical intuition that continuity generally implies differentiability. Once regarded as pathological constructions, such functions are now recognized as abundant in the space of continuous functions, both in the sense of Baire category and through notions of prevalence. In this paper, we develop a general framework for constructing continuous nowhere differentiable functions represented by trigonometric series with decaying amplitudes and rapidly increasing frequencies. We establish a sufficient condition for nowhere differentiability that applies to a broad class of Fourier-type series, thereby providing a unified criterion that encompasses several classical constructions, including the Weierstrass function and related examples. The proposed approach also yields new families of continuous nowhere differentiable functions under flexible conditions on the amplitudes and frequencies. These results contribute to a systematic understanding of the mechanisms underlying the breakdown of differentiability and further illustrate the richness and ubiquity of nowhere-differentiable behavior within the class of continuous functions.

title: Exploring the Dark Tetrad in Human–GenAI Relationships: A Multi-Source Evaluation of GenAI Abuse
abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) companions become increasingly integrated into users’ social lives, concerns have arisen regarding the potential for abuse of these artificial agents. Some scholars have further suggested that such abusive behaviors toward GenAI may eventually spill over into human interpersonal contexts. Guided by the Realistic Accuracy Model (RAM), this study investigated how Machiavellianism, narcissism, psychopathy, and sadism predict emotionally abusive behavior toward GenAI companions. A dyadic design was employed, collecting parallel reports from both human users (self-reports) and their GenAI companions (GenAI assessments) among 1041 participants (632 females; average age = 25.10 years) recruited from an online human–GenAI relationship community. Results demonstrated that psychopathy and sadism were consistent predictors of GenAI abuse across both reporting perspectives, whereas narcissism exhibited a stable negative association with abuse. In contrast, Machiavellianism predicted GenAI abuse only through GenAI assessments, but not self-reports. Theoretically, our findings extend RAM to human–AI relationships, demonstrating that personality traits vary in how accurately they can be judged in GenAI contexts. Practically, the results highlight that individuals high in certain Dark Tetrad traits—specifically psychopathy and sadism—represent personality-driven high-risk groups, providing insights for practitioners in education and technology to develop interventions or safeguards aimed at mitigating abusive behavior toward GenAI companions.

title: Factors Associated with Adverse Effects of Postoperative TSH-Directed Levothyroxine Therapy in Adults with Differentiated Thyroid Cancer: A Scoping Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND Postoperative thyrotropin (TSH)-directed levothyroxine is used to reduce recurrence risk in selected patients with differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), but treatment-related adverse effects may vary based on patient susceptibility and treatment exposure. Contemporary guidelines increasingly require balancing anticipated oncologic benefit against potential harm. This scoping review synthesizes patient-, treatment-, and disease-related factors associated with adverse effects of postoperative TSH-directed levothyroxine therapy in adults with DTC. METHODS This scoping review was reported following PRISMA-ScR guidelines and prospectively registered on the Open Science Framework. MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from January 1, 2011, to February 24, 2026. Eligible studies reported associations between patient-, treatment-, or disease-related factors and adverse effects among adults with DTC receiving postoperative TSH-directed levothyroxine therapy. Data were summarized descriptively and synthesized narratively, with stratification according to TSH exposure definition. RESULTS Of 7361 records screened, 35 studies including 11,819 patients were included. Skeletal outcomes were most frequently reported (51.4%), followed by cardiometabolic (40.0%), neuropsychological (11.4%), reproductive (2.9%), and muscular outcomes (2.9%). TSH exposure definitions varied substantially: 18 studies evaluated subnormal TSH, 2 low-normal TSH, 8 mixed categories spanning subnormal and low-normal TSH, 4 continuous biochemical/treatment measures, and 3 unclear exposures. Greater suppression intensity was the most consistently reported treatment-related factor associated with adverse skeletal outcomes, particularly in studies evaluating subnormal TSH. Longer treatment duration was associated with skeletal harm in selected studies. Postmenopausal status emerged as a relatively consistent patient-level factor, whereas associations with age and body mass index were variable. Evidence for cardiometabolic, neuropsychological, reproductive, and muscular outcomes was less extensive and less consistent, and disease-related factors were infrequently examined. Only two studies conducted prediction/discrimination analyses, both involving skeletal outcomes. CONCLUSIONS Evidence on adverse effects associated with TSH-directed levothyroxine therapy in DTC is most consistent for skeletal outcomes and predominantly derives from studies evaluating subnormal TSH exposure. The available literature provides limited evidence for clinically applicable prediction of toxicity or cumulative treatment burden. Future longitudinal studies should better characterize the intensity and persistence of biochemical exposure and develop outcome-specific prediction models integrating baseline susceptibility, organ vulnerability, and longitudinal treatment exposure to support individualized TSH management.

title: The sociopolitical dimension of attachment: differences in attachment anxiety and attachment avoidance between East and West Germans
abstract: Attachment is a universal, cross-cultural basic need, which, however, is defined, satisfied and shaped differently in each socio-cultural context. Germany with its history of two divided states and their different sociopolitical environments offers an unique opportunity to study their impact on attachment behavior. Attachment behavior was assessed in a representative sample (N = 2,328) using the dimensions of attachment anxiety and attachment avoidance in couple relationships of the Experiences in Close Relationships questionnaire (ECR-RD 12). Differences between East and West Germans were examined in a univariate analysis of variance, differentiated by age cohorts and sex. Socioeconomic variables were included in the model as control variables. Significant East-West differences were found for attachment anxiety (p = .01), but not for attachment avoidance. The analysis differentiated by age cohorts revealed on average a lower level of attachment anxiety for East Germans born between 1921 and 1989 compared to West Germans. These differences were not found for the post-reunification generation (born after 1989), although this comparison included only 28 East German participants and should be interpreted with caution. Gender-related effects were only found in relation with age cohorts. Adults who grew up in the former German Democratic Republic (GDR) report lower attachment anxiety than their West German counterparts. Although effect sizes were small, the findings suggest that the sociopolitical environment is a relevant factor for attachment behavior in close relationships, particularly attachment anxiety.

title: Expression of Concern: The agricultural carbon reduction effect of digital rural construction under the dual carbon target
Protein lactylation in atherosclerosis - Mechanisms and therapeutic potential: A narrative review.
abstract: Protein lactylation, which links cellular metabolism to gene regulation and protein function, may influence atherosclerosis. This narrative review explores its cellular mechanisms and therapeutic potential. We searched PubMed from inception to September 30, 2026, for English-language studies and reviews. The synthesis differentiated lactylation from lactate signaling and distinguished direct evidence in atherosclerosis from findings in other disease models. Predominantly preclinical evidence suggests that both histone and non-histone lactylation are involved in endothelial inflammation, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, macrophage polarization and ferroptosis, and vascular smooth muscle cell senescence, phenotypic remodeling, and calcification. Depending on the cellular context, modification site, and downstream targets, lactylation can either promote vascular injury or support anti-inflammatory responses and plaque stabilization. Candidate interventions target lactate production, transport, and lactylation-related enzymes, but their effects often lack specificity for lactylation. Much of the therapeutic evidence originates from non-atherosclerotic models, and clinical validation is currently absent. Therefore, therapeutic development should consider cell type, disease stage, and modification site, with validation of causal mechanisms, selectivity, and safety in atherosclerosis models prior to clinical translation.

title: A multivariate analysis of the influence of soil conditions on wheat yields
abstract: Rapid global population growth has led to food demand out-pacing supply, increasing food insecurity. In light of this, the United Nations declared ending hunger as its Second Sustainable Development Goal in 2015. Environmental changes from pollution and climate change further threaten food security. In this study, machine learning regression models were employed to analyze the impact of fertilizer use, soil organic carbon displacement due to erosion, surface water conductivity, soil pH, and organic carbon content on wheat yields. Permutation feature importance scores were used to evaluate the importance of each variable. Through the application of a ridgeCV stacking regression model, we identified that soil pH was the most influential variable in determining wheat yields. In the regressions tested, all p-values were below 0.005, so the null hypothesis could be rejected. The study’s results suggest that regular pH monitoring, building organic carbon-boosting infrastructure, using drainage systems, and employing sustainable agricultural practices are necessary to maximize agricultural production efficiency. Soil pH could further be protected through directed future policymaking. To expand upon the research conducted in this study, investigating the effects of climate change on properties affecting soil quality could yield valuable information on strategies to promote sustainable agriculture. Furthermore, analyzing crops other than wheat would extend the study’s results to different agricultural practices, such as tropical agriculture.

title: Managing the Training Process in Rhythmic Gymnastics as a Reflection of the State Sports Policy of the Russian Federation: From Strategic Guidelines to a Management Model for Sports Reserve Development in the Context of Latent Risks Associated with Managerial Decisions
abstract: Based on a retrospective and comparative analysis, the article examines the evolution of the training process management system in rhythmic gymnastics in the Russian Federation as a projection of the priorities of state sports policy. The relevance of the study is due to the identified latent risks associated with a fundamental change in the rules of the International Gymnastics Federation in 2024-2026, aimed at leveling the advantages of a domestic school, as well as with domestic management challenges, including gaps between the current federal standard and the real requirements of coordination, subject and plastic training. The purpose of the work is to substantiate the need to modernize the management model of sports reserve training, taking into account exogenous and endogenous factors. The methodological basis consisted of a systematic analysis of the current regulatory framework, economic and mathematical modeling (a cluster approach to segmentation of female athletes as "investment assets") and a generalization of data from the All-Russian competitions in 2024-2025. As a result, critical shortcomings of the federal standard of sports training in terms of coordination control, load differentiation and judicial regulations have been identified. Practical recommendations on changing the rules of a sport and methodological support for the stages of training (from initial to sports improvement) are formulated.

title: ANALISIS PERBANDINGAN KINERJA REGRESI LINEAR DAN K-NEAREST NEIGHBORS (KNN) DALAM PEMBUATAN MODEL PREDIKSI HASIL PANEN TANAMAN TEBU
abstract: Sugarcane yield prediction is an important aspect in agricultural planning and decision-making. This study aims to compare the performance of Linear Regression and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) methods in predicting sugarcane yields in Gondanglegi Village, Malang Regency. The dataset used consists of historical yield data from 2020 to 2024, including land area and rainfall as independent variables and crop yield as the dependent variable. The research stages include data preprocessing, normalization, data splitting with three ratios (80:20, 70:30, and 90:10), model training, and evaluation using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and the coefficient of determination (R²). The results indicate that Linear Regression consistently achieves higher R² values compared to KNN, indicating a better ability to explain yield variability. Although KNN shows competitive error values in certain ratios, it is more sensitive to data structure and parameter selection. Therefore, Linear Regression is considered more suitable for sugarcane yield prediction based on the dataset used in this study.

title: General-Purpose Vision Models to Dermatology-Specific Foundation Models: Comparative Evaluation for Facial Skin Disease Classification
abstract: Skin diseases represent a major global health burden, while access to dermatological expertise remains limited in many rural and resource-constrained settings. These disparities have increased interest in scalable digital tools for dermatological assessment and patient education. However, trustworthy clinical AI requires reproducible evaluation, standardized benchmarking, transparent reporting of failure patterns, and assessment of model robustness across different representations and classification strategies. This study presents a systematic transfer-learning framework for six-class facial skin disease classification, comparing seven pretrained visual representations comprising ResNet50, MobileNetV3-Large, ViT-B/16, Swin-T, DINOv2, DermLIP and Derm Foundation, under a common downstream classification framework. XGBoost was used as the primary downstream classifier, while an RBF-kernel support vector machine (SVM) was additionally evaluated as an ablation analysis to investigate the dependence of classification performance on downstream classifier selection. Performance was assessed using accuracy, macro-F1, macro-AUROC, per-class recall, confusion matrices, and bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals, with paired McNemar testing and Holm correction used to compare classifier. Derm Foundation achieved the highest performance among the evaluated feature representations when combined with XGBoost, obtaining 88.17% accuracy, 88.05% macro-F1, and 98.58% macro-AUROC on the testing set. At the class level, recall was 94.5% for acne, 87.0% for atopic dermatitis, 100.0% for normal skin, 90.5% for psoriasis, 84.0% for rosacea, and 73.0% for seborrheic dermatitis. Classifier comparisons showed that the relative performance of XGBoost and RBF-SVM depended on the underlying feature representation. The principal residual classification difficulty involved seborrheic dermatitis, particularly its reciprocal confusion with rosacea. To demonstrate technical feasibility, the classification framework was integrated into a prototype Django-based web application architecture featuring an exploratory LLM module for automated patient-education content translation. Preliminary, descriptive specialist feedback was gathered to identify future engineering optimization constraints, such as inference latency and communication mechanics. These findings are limited to the evaluated testing dataset and do not establish external generalizability or clinical efficacy.

title: Machine Learning-Based Yield and Water Efficiency Prediction for Deficit-Irrigated Maize in Semi-Arid Ethiopia
abstract: Water scarcity constrains maize production in semi-arid Ethiopia, requiring irrigation strategies that improve water productivity while maintaining grain yield. This study integrated machine learning with water-balance-based deficit irrigation to predict maize grain yield and water use efficiency (WUE). Field experiments evaluated five irrigation treatments (100%, 85%, 70%, 55%, and 40% ETc) in a randomized complete block design. Plant height, leaf length, and biomass were measured as growth parameters, while cob length, cob diameter, number of grains per cob, and grain yield were evaluated as yield-related parameters, together with irrigation water applied. Random Forest, XGBoost, Linear Regression, and Ridge Regression models were evaluated. XGBoost provided the highest test-set accuracy for grain yield prediction (R² = 0.8912, RMSE = 183.01 kg ha⁻¹, MAE = 155.05 kg ha⁻¹), whereas Ridge Regression performed best for WUE prediction (R² = 0.6540, RMSE = 0.210 kg m⁻³, MAE = 0.171 kg m⁻³). Under the experimental conditions, 70% ETc provided a balance between grain yield and water saving, producing 6,621 kg ha⁻¹ with a WUE of 2.10 kg m⁻³ and saving 1,350 m³ ha⁻¹ (30%) relative to full irrigation. Given the small dataset, the ML results are exploratory and require validation using larger multi-season and multi-location datasets.

title: The Reliability Gap: Repeated-Trial Consistency and the Deployable Autonomy Horizon of Frontier AI Agents
abstract: Capability evaluations of AI agents increasingly summarise progress as a time horizon: the length of task, measured in human expert time, that an agent completes with 50% probability. Deployment decisions, however, depend on whether an agent succeeds every time a task recurs, not on whether it succeeds on average. This article estimates reliability-adjusted time horizons for frontier AI agents and asks how far they lag behind capability horizons. Using the public run-level records of the METR time-horizon evaluations (60,417 attempts by 30 and 20 models released between 2023 and 2026, on 170 and 228 tasks in two benchmark versions), it combines the unbiased pass^k estimator with per-model fractional logistic curves on log task duration, and quantifies uncertainty with a task-family cluster bootstrap (1,000 replicates). Four hypotheses were specified before estimation. For every model, the horizon at which all four attempts succeed with 50% probability is shorter than the capability horizon (geometric-mean ratio 2.39, 95% CI 2.07–2.84, in the newer benchmark; 2.33, 1.98–2.81, in the older one). The gap narrows by about 17% per year in point estimate, but the trend is not statistically distinguishable from zero, and the reliability horizon doubles at a rate indistinguishable from the capability horizon. Contrary to a pre-specified hypothesis, the 80% horizon does not double more slowly than the 50% horizon. Outcome inconsistency peaks for tasks just below each model's capability horizon. A further, unanticipated result is that repeated attempts are strongly correlated within tasks (intraclass correlation 0.68–0.87): observed reliability horizons are 1.6 to 8.0 times longer than independent attempts would imply. Agent failures are therefore mostly task-determined rather than stochastic. The article discusses, as an implication rather than a finding, why capability disclosures for autonomous agents should report reliability-adjusted horizons alongside average-success horizons.

title: Geoinformation methods and models for spatial data registration and access within geoportal systems
abstract: The purpose of this article is to summarize the experience of developing, implementing, and practical use of the “Geospatial Data Provider Cabinet” (a web workspace for data providers) subsystem within municipal geographic information systems and urban planning cadastre GIS. Particular attention is paid to geoinformation methods and technical frameworks that support the registration, description, generation, access configuration, maintenance, and further use of geospatial datasets within territorial communities. The research methodology is based on a systems analysis of geospatial data creation and maintenance processes in municipal GIS, a structural and functional analysis of the “Geospatial Data Provider Cabinet” subsystem, and a synthesis of practical implementation experience. The study analyzes scenarios for organizing access to the subsystem, the dataset lifecycle, the technological implementation of automated schema generation, and real-world operational results. Practical effectiveness is assessed through subsystem deployments within the GIS of the Kryvyi Rih City Council, the Lutsk Urban Territorial Community, and the Lviv Urban Territorial Community. Additionally, the study examines quantitative indicators of information resource development, including the dynamics of application-based dataset formation and thematic diversity. Results. The findings indicate that the “Geospatial Data Provider Cabinet” subsystem supports the complete lifecycle of geospatial datasets, spanning from initial application submission and registration to database table and map layer creation, access control configuration, initial data population, public or internal utilization, subsequent maintenance, and updating. The subsystem's technological architecture allows users to generate new thematic datasets directly via a web interface, eliminating the need for manual database interventions or writing custom software for each new layer. Practical deployments confirm the subsystem’s operational efficiency: within the GIS of the Kryvyi Rih City Council, 216 datasets were generated from processed requests from 2024 to 24 June 2026. Concurrently, the GIS of Lutsk Urban Territorial Community produced 20 datasets, while the GIS of Lviv Urban Territorial Community generated 22 datasets. The thematic composition of the datasets shows that the subsystem can be used not only for urban planning but also for the digitalization of a wide range of municipal governance areas, including public amenities, social infrastructure, civil protection, transport, environmental management, entrepreneurship, municipal property, open data, and related fields. Scientific novelty and practical significance. The scientific novelty of the study lies in the theoretical substantiation and formalization of a technological framework for a subsystem dedicated to the registration, creation, access control, and maintenance of geospatial datasets within geoportal configurations and municipal GIS. Unlike traditional approaches that focus mainly on publishing pre-prepared geospatial data, the proposed model encompasses the entire dataset lifecycle: from application initiation to automated database table creation, layer configuration, access rights assignment, data population, and public or internal utilization. Furthermore, the study generalizes a conceptual model where an application serves not merely as an administrative document but as a direct source of input parameters for automated dataset generation. This approach successfully integrates the organizational procedures of data maintenance within a territorial community with the technical mechanisms of spatial resource provisioning in GIS. The practical significance of the study lies in confirming the feasibility of deploying the “Geospatial Data Provider Cabinet” subsystem in real-world municipal GIS and urban planning cadastre GIS. The proposed approach enables local governments to create new thematic datasets via a web interface, thereby reducing their dependence on manual database operations, direct developer involvement, or custom software modifications for each new layer. The subsystem provides centralized registration for applications and datasets, streamlines the identification of responsible personnel and organizational units, simplifies access and visualization configurations, and facilitates the involvement of specialized departments in idata updates. These findings can be directly applied to the design, modernization, and strategic development of municipal geographic information systems, community geoportals, and local-level urban planning cadastre GIS.

title: ChemEidos: Synthesis-Aware Multimodal Foundation Models for Domain-Specific Generative Design
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence models for de novo drug discovery often suffer synthetic tractability issues and lack fidelity in underrepresented chemical domains. This white paper highlights ChemEidos, a novel multimodal generative design platform that utilizes the underlying patterns, forms, and organizing principles of chemical space (eidos) by incorporating expert domain knowledge in focused training sets and at inference time.

title: Effect of UAV Flight Altitude on Wheat Field Classification Accuracy and Operational Efficiency
abstract: Flight altitude ties the quality of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery to the cost of acquiring it, yet operational guidance on selecting it for crop mapping remains largely qualitative. This study quantifies the trade-off using a repeat-altitude survey of one winter wheat field in Kayseri, Türkiye. A 20 MP RGB camera on a fixed-nadir gimbal acquired 300 frames over the same ground at six altitudes between 10 m and 120 m (0.227–2.725 cm/pixel). After removing 25 frames whose gimbal yaw deviated from the flight heading, imagery was resampled onto a common 5 m × 5 m ground cell grid so that every altitude represents identical ground at an identical input size, making ground sampling distance (GSD) the only variable. A total of 183 colour, colour index and texture features were extracted from 11 251 cell tiles and classified with Random Forest under five-fold spatial block cross-validation with a 10 m buffer; the cell (n = 654) rather than the tile was the statistical unit. For three-class land cover over a 2× GSD range (60–120 m, n = 654), overall accuracy declined monotonically from 0.804 to 0.734 (McNemar p < 0.0001 for 60 m versus both coarser altitudes). For binary wheat extent mapping over a 6× GSD range (20–120 m, n = 186), accuracy was statistically flat from 20 m to 90 m (0.903, 0.909, 0.914; McNemar p = 0.75–1.00) and fell only at 120 m (0.866; p = 0.039 and 0.049); because the 20 m mission itself carried motion blur, this plateau compares effective resolution and not nominal GSD. Under a fixed 75 %/65 % overlap plan, 90 m required 17× fewer images, 19× less storage and 4–17× less flight time than 20 m for equal accuracy, identifying 90 m as the operational optimum for this task and sensor. Processing time did not decrease with altitude, because it scales with ground area and not with image count; a pipeline that classifies each ground cell once instead of once per overlapping frame ran 6–12× faster. A 40 m mission flown two hours later in weaker light required a 1/41 s exposure, which introduced approximately 12 pixels of motion blur and reduced effective sharpness to 34 % of the 60 m mission despite a finer nominal GSD, showing that nominal GSD is not effective resolution.

title: Unidirectional and bidirectional long short-term memory for multiple seasonal time series data: A systematic review
abstract: This systematic review examines developments from January 2023 to November 2025 in unidirectional and bidirectional long short-term memory (LSTM and BiLSTM) models for forecasting multiple seasonal time series, a task complicated by overlapping cycles, nonlinear behaviors, and spatiotemporal variability across real-world datasets. While deep learning has become a dominant approach for handling complex seasonal structures, the rapid expansion of architecture variations, hybrid designs, and domain-specific implementations presents fragmentation and uncertainty regarding the most effective modeling strategies. To address this gap, the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) protocol was applied using two major databases, Web of Science and Scopus. From an initial pool of records, 45 published primary studies met all the inclusion criteria, offering a focused and contemporary evidence base. The selected studies were synthesized into three thematic clusters: (1) Renewable and power systems forecasting, where studies showed that seasonal–spatiotemporal learning with BiLSTM, decomposition techniques, and attention mechanisms improved the prediction of wind, solar, load, and hybrid energy systems; (2) Environmental quality and hydroclimate forecasting, where hybrid, feature selection, and spatial weighting enhanced the modeling of air pollution, streamflow, rainfall, evapotranspiration, and carbon-related emissions; and (3) Mobility, demand, and market forecasting, where multistage decomposition and hybrid recurrent networks outperformed traditional baselines in traffic flow, tourism demand, commodity prices, and agricultural yield prediction. Numerical evidence across themes demonstrated frequent reductions in forecasting error and improved long-range stability when BiLSTM or hybrid architectures were used. Hence, the review concludes that integrating decomposition, attention, feature engineering, and bidirectional recurrent structures offers a strong and adaptable foundation for multiseasonal forecasting while also highlighting remaining challenges in interpretability, generalizability, and computational efficiency.

title: Comparative analysis of bioethanol production in Ghana and West Africa: capabilities, challenges, and transferable practices—a systematic review
abstract: Ghana’s bioethanol industry holds significant renewable energy potential in West Africa; it is characterized by abundant agricultural resources but constrained by structural and policy challenges. This systematic review examines Ghana’s bioethanol production capabilities relative to eight regional countries (Nigeria, Mali, Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, and South Africa), analyzing feedstock availability, policy frameworks, technological adoption, and socioeconomic impacts through a defined literature search and screening strategy, comparative policy analysis, and thematic synthesis (see Methodology). Ghana demonstrates diversified feedstock potential with cassava yields of 22–38 tons/hectare and ethanol production potential of 280–320 L/ton from cassava peels. Agricultural residues could theoretically produce 200 million liters annually, sufficient for five million households. However, only 5% of this potential is currently utilized due to collection and processing constraints. Policy analysis reveals that while Ghana established a 10% biofuel integration target by 2020 (extended to 20% by 2030), implementation lacks enforcement mechanisms, unlike successful regional models such as Malawi’s E10 blending mandate, which has been in place since 1982. Ghana possesses exceptional feedstock diversification potential, particularly through non-competitive food crops like sweet sorghum and agricultural residues, positioning it favorably for sustainable bioethanol production. Region-specific comparison shows that no single country offers a complete template: success requires adapting Ethiopia’s blending-mandate consistency, Mali’s community engagement model, Kenya’s marginal-land feedstock strategy, and Mozambique’s residue-based, export-oriented model to Ghana’s own institutional and agroecological context.

title: Early growth vigor monitoring and salt tolerance assessment of cotton based on SDI-YOLO11-seg
abstract: By precisely quantifying the growth changes of seed radicles and cotyledons over continuous time periods, the impact of saline stress environments on early crop growth can be assessed. However, traditional manual measurements struggle to accurately quantify these indicators continuously. Therefore, we developed a Full-Time Series Crop Growth Vigor Monitoring System. This system captured images of the hydroponic germination process and the soil-based seedling growth process of Xinjiang cotton seeds. We constructed a labeled dataset for identifying the germination process and calculating cotyledon growth. Using the SDI-YOLO11-seg model, we achieved the extraction and quantification of germination rate, emergence rate, radicle length, and cotyledon area over continuous time, validating the feasibility of a rapid, batch-assessment method for early cotton seed growth vigor based on the full-time series monitoring system and deep learning. Building on this, we conducted experiments involving four Xinjiang cotton varieties under hydroponic (germination stage) and soil-based (seedling stage) conditions with six different concentrations of NaCl solution stress. Germination rate, emergence rate, radicle length, and cotyledon area for each variety were measured continuously over time. The results show that the proposed SDI-YOLO11-seg model achieved a mean average precision for bounding boxes at IoU 0.5 (mAPbox50) of 0.961 and for masks (mAPmask50) of 0.937, representing improvements of 0.9% and 6.0% over the baseline YOLO11-seg, respectively. Validation against manual ImageJ measurements yielded coefficients of determination (R²) of 0.970 for radicle length and 0.993 for cotyledon area, confirming high measurement accuracy. Under salt stress concentrations ranging from 0 to 250 mmol/L, Jinken 1565 exhibited the fastest germination rate, the highest final germination rate, and the longest average radicle length, indicating strong salt tolerance during the bud stage. In contrast, Jinken 1775 demonstrated a higher seedling emergence rate, the fastest cotyledon growth rate, and the largest cotyledon area, suggesting excellent salt tolerance during the seedling stage. The Tahe 2 variety exhibited weaker salt tolerance during both the bud and seedling stages compared to the other three varieties. Coefficient of variation analysis further revealed that Jinken 1565 exhibited the most uniform radicle growth under high salt stress during the germination stage, while Jinken 1775 and Xinluzao 64 demonstrated superior uniformity in seedling growth, complementing the mean-based vigor assessment.

title: Does the rural digital economy enhance green total factor productivity of agriculture? An empirical approach using double machine learning
abstract: Introduction In the context of the green transformation of agriculture, the digital economy offers a novel pathway to mitigate environmental externalities and operational inefficiencies. Recognizing that agricultural digitalisation relies heavily on the spillover of macro-level digital resources, this study constructs a multidimensional rural digital economy (RDE) framework. Methods Employing a double machine learning (DML) model on a panel dataset of 30 Chinese provinces from 2011 to 2022, we empirically investigate the impact of the RDE on agricultural green total factor productivity (GTFP). Results We find that: (1) The RDE exerts a positive effect on GTFP. Dimensional analysis strictly confirms that digital industry development and industrial digital transformation have positive linkages with this productivity growth, whereas basic infrastructure alone is insufficient. (2) Mechanism analyses demonstrate that the RDE empowers green agriculture by optimizing inter-sectoral factor allocation and significantly reducing agricultural polluting energy intensity; however, the mediating role of government digital policy attention is not statistically established. (3) To accurately capture asymmetric effects, group-based heterogeneity tests reveal that the empowerment effect of the RDE is significantly stronger in provinces with larger cultivated scales. Discussion These findings indicate that the RDE currently empowers green agriculture primarily through structural factor reallocation and precision energy management rather than immediate technological leaps. To overcome hardware-software structural lags and mitigate scale disadvantages faced by smallholders, policymakers should pivot toward enhancing farmers’ digital literacy, expanding shared digital socialized services, and implementing market-based environmental governance.

title: The impact of digital transformation on agricultural green total factor productivity: moderating and threshold effects of farmland scale operation
abstract: Drawing on the perspective of farmland scale operation, this paper investigates how digital transformation affects agricultural green total factor productivity (AGTFP). Using Chinese provincial panel data from 2011 to 2023, we measure the level of agricultural digital transformation via the entropy method and compute AGTFP using the GML index based on the super-efficiency EBM distance function. Empirically, we employ two-way fixed effects models, moderating effect models, and panel threshold models. The results show that agricultural digital transformation significantly improves AGTFP, a finding that remains robust after addressing endogeneity and conducting a series of robustness checks. This positive effect is heterogeneous across regions, being more pronounced in eastern regions and major grain-producing areas. Furthermore, farmland scale operation positively moderates the relationship between digital transformation and AGTFP. Notably, this moderating effect exhibits a single-threshold nonlinear pattern with increasing marginal effects, suggesting a structural turning point in the enabling role of digital transformation under different levels of farmland scale operation. Overall, this paper provides new empirical evidence on the linkages among agricultural digital transformation, scale operation, and green agricultural transition, with important policy implications for promoting sustainable agriculture and optimizing the integration of digital technologies with scale operation policies.

title: New path for agricultural carbon governance: the emission reduction effect and mechanism of green finance
abstract: Reducing agricultural carbon emissions is central to China’s carbon-neutrality goals, yet the effectiveness and operating mechanisms of green finance in supporting low-carbon agricultural production remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the effects, mechanisms, regional heterogeneity, and spatial spillovers of green finance on agricultural carbon emissions. Using provincial panel data for China from 2007 to 2024, we estimated two-way fixed-effects and spatial Durbin models within the technology–organization–environment framework. We used mechanism, moderating-effect, robustness, and instrumental-variable analyses to examine transmission channels, contextual conditions, model sensitivity, and endogeneity. A one-unit increase in the green finance index corresponded to an approximately 19% reduction in agricultural carbon emissions. Green finance reduced emissions by promoting agricultural green technological innovation and strengthening agricultural socialized services, while digital infrastructure enhanced its carbon-reduction effect. The effect was stronger in major grain-producing regions and areas exposed to higher agricultural natural risks. Agricultural carbon emissions exhibited positive spatial dependence. Green finance produced a statistically significant local direct effect, but we found no robust evidence of cross-regional spillovers. Green finance supports agricultural decarbonization through locally embedded technological and organizational capacities. Policies should align green financial instruments with regional production functions and natural-risk conditions, strengthen digital infrastructure and agricultural service systems, and improve cross-regional coordination.

title: Agroecological transition in olive based farming systems among smallholder farms in northwestern Tunisia
abstract: Agricultural intensification has increased production and economic growth but has also generated significant environmental and social challenges that threaten long-term sustainability, highlighting the need for more sustainable farming models. Agroecology offers a promising pathway to enhance resilience and support inclusive rural development. In this context, Tunisia’s olive sector provides a relevant case for examining agroecological transitions in semi-arid smallholder systems. This study evaluates the degree of agroecological transition among smallholder olive farms in the Elles region of northwestern Tunisia using the FAO Tool for Agroecology Performance Evaluation (TAPE). Based on a sample of 60 farms, the analysis applies the Characterization of Agroecological Transition (CAET) index, grounded in the 10 Elements of Agroecology, to compare four production systems: (i) olive monoculture, (ii) diversified cropping, (iii) olive–livestock integration, and (iv) integrated olive–crop–livestock systems. Economic, social, environmental and institutional performance were explored using the TAPE Core Criteria of Performance (Step 2) and examined in relation to CAET scores. Results reveal a clear agroecological gradient, with diversified and integrated systems achieving markedly higher CAET scores (up to 52%) compared to monoculture systems (31%). Spearman correlations show strong associations between CAET and key dimensions, including synergy (ρ = 0.79), human and social values (ρ = 0.78), and diversity (ρ = 0.71). Several TAPE economic performance indicators, including monthly income, which ranged from approximately 1,349 TND in monoculture systems to 4,892 TND in diversified olive–crop–livestock systems, were positively associated with higher CAET scores, suggesting that agroecological transition may not necessarily imply a trade-off between productivity and sustainability. However, limited collective action, weak market integration, and insufficient extension services constrain broader adoption. These findings highlight the potential of diversification as a key lever for agroecological transition and underscore the importance of targeted policy support.

title: Sustainable service scenes: formation mechanism of consumers’ premium purchase of specialty agricultural and livestock products in short-video live streaming
abstract: Advancing the market realization of premium pricing for high-quality agricultural and livestock products is essential to facilitating the transition of traditional agriculture toward a sustainable, resource-efficient, and quality-driven development paradigm. However, Information asymmetry in the agricultural and livestock products market gives rise to the “lemons problem,” impeding the sustainable consumption of high-quality, differentiated products and undermining their ability to command premium pricing. With the development of the digital economy, short-video live streaming has emerged as a new driver for promoting the sustainable consumption of such products at premium prices. Drawing on servicescape theory, this study uses Inner Mongolia mutton as a representative case and constructs a structural equation model based on 402 valid questionnaires to examine the formation mechanism of consumers’ premium purchase intentions for specialty agricultural and livestock products in short-video live streaming. In addition, multi-group analysis is conducted to examine whether these mechanisms differ across consumers with different demographic characteristics. The results indicate that short-video live streaming effectively encourages consumers to purchase specialty agricultural and livestock products at premium prices through the dual pathways of “scene reconstruction–value upgrading” and “scene reconstruction–trust establishment.” Further, multi-group analysis reveals significant differences in consumers’ psychological responses and purchase intentions across demographic groups. This study provides a theoretical basis and practical insights for promoting the sustainable consumption of specialty agricultural and livestock products at premium prices, and thereby contribute to the long-term sustainability of the agricultural sector.

title: Digital Twins in Irrigation Optimization: Advantages, Opportunities, and Challenges
abstract: Efficient irrigation management is important to increase agriculture water use efficiency and achieve sustainable crop production under increasing water scarcity and climatic variability. Based on advanced devices and artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms, the irrigation system can be digitalized and transformed from experience-driven decision-making toward data-driven, predictive, and adaptive control. Digital Twins (DTs) enable smart irrigation management through continuous bi-directional data flows, dynamic model updating, intelligent prediction, and closed-loop execution. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the applications of DTs in irrigation management and optimization, covering Internet of Things (IoT), Remote Sensing (RS), and advanced simulation-inspired irrigation systems. Furthermore, we discuss the opportunities and challenges in DTs for irrigation optimization with the development of new techniques, and identify the major technological trends, existing bottlenecks, and future research directions for DT-enabled irrigation.

title: Soil Quality Shapes Yield Gains from Improved Management in China’s Cereal Systems
abstract: Recovering unrealized crop production through improved field management is important for sustainable agriculture, but the benefits may depend on soil conditions. We aimed to determine how soil quality modifies the yield benefits of management improvement in China’s maize, wheat and rice systems. We test two hypotheses: (1) that higher soil quality is associated with smaller relative yield shortfalls, and (2) that the gains associated with improved technical efficiency (TE) depend on soil quality. Using field observations across China, we quantified the difference between cultivar-specific attainable and actual field yields and combined stochastic frontier estimation, random forest modeling and scenario analysis. The relative shortfall was 8.4 percentage points (pp) lower in maize, 11.0 pp lower in wheat and 11.8 pp lower in rice on high- than low-quality soils. However, its sensitivity to TE improvement declined with soil quality in maize and wheat but increased in rice. Better soils therefore partly compensated for inefficient management in maize and wheat, whereas they enabled greater returns to management improvement in rice. Soil organic matter and available phosphorus were the principal soil attributes associated with lower shortfalls in maize and wheat, whereas available potassium and pH were more influential in rice. Scenarios analyses showed that combined soil and TE improvement reduced predicted relative shortfall by 8.7 pp in maize, 8.9 pp in wheat and 15.1 pp in rice. Spatial prioritization further identified where soil-focused, management-focused or integrated interventions offered the greatest potential. These findings identify crop-specific associations between soil conditions and TE-related yield-shortfall reduction and provide model-based priorities for evaluating soil and management interventions through field testing.

title: Comparative Performance Evaluation of Low-Cost, Continuous, Field-Deployable Trail Cameras for Agricultural Field Monitoring
abstract: Monitoring plant traits such as chlorophyll content and stress response is essential for agricultural research and crop management. However, traditional phenotyping methods are often destructive, labor-intensive, and lack temporal resolution. Continuous imaging using digital cameras offers a non-invasive approach to tracking plant development over time. This study evaluated trail cameras commonly used in ecological research for their effectiveness in continuous, nondestructive plant monitoring in an agricultural setting. Eight cameras were deployed at canopy height in a cranberry field to capture images and temperature data at 30 min intervals over a 15-day period. Based on operational reliability and data quality, four cameras were shortlisted for detailed analysis. Key performance parameters included image quality (blur, color cast, and noise), temperature measurement accuracy, and battery longevity. Temperature readings were compared with data from a canopy-level probe sensor and a dike-level weather station. Cameras 3, 5, and 7 each demonstrated strengths across different performance metrics, with Camera 3 excelling in battery longevity (maintaining 100% capacity over 15 days) and temperature correlation (R2 up to 0.983), Camera 5 showing superior color accuracy (lowest color cast score: 9.679 ± 0.06), and Camera 7 achieving the lowest noise levels (0.906 ± 0.002) along with highly consistent imaging performance. These models also demonstrated reliable temperature measurement accuracy, with coefficients of determination (R2) ranging from 0.935 to 0.983 when compared with canopy-level probe data. Overall, the results indicate that each camera offers distinct advantages depending on the specific monitoring requirements, such as image clarity, color accuracy, noise reduction, or continuous field deployment. The results highlight trail cameras as affordable and reliable tools for remote, non-destructive, and continuous plant monitoring, offering valuable guidance for researchers in plant phenotyping and crop management.

title: Spectroscopic Sensing for Hydroponic Crop Monitoring: From Analytical Validation to Closed-Loop Management
abstract: Hydroponic production enables precise control of nutrient supply, irrigation, lighting and root-zone conditions, creating a need for rapid, reliable and biologically meaningful monitoring. Optical and spectroscopic approaches can non-destructively assess nutrient solutions, roots, plant physiology and crop quality. This review critically evaluates VIS–NIR and NIR spectroscopy, multispectral and hyperspectral imaging, chlorophyll fluorescence, Raman spectroscopy, FTIR/MIR spectroscopy, laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) and optical sensing of nutrient solutions. Rather than ranking technologies by predictive accuracy, we classify them by the information they provide: direct or near-direct measurement, calibrated quantitative prediction, physiological proxy sensing, and classification or anomaly detection. Despite substantial proof-of-concept progress, evidence remains constrained by homogeneous datasets, information leakage, limited external validation, calibration transfer barriers and scarce commercial evaluation. Reliable deployment requires representative calibration, validated reference methods, biologically independent validation, uncertainty assessment and continuous quality assurance. Progress will depend less on increasingly sophisticated algorithms than on stronger analytical and biological foundations and integration of complementary solution, environmental and physiological measurements. Spectroscopic sensing should therefore progress from isolated sensor-to-trait models towards validated decision support systems linking measurement, state estimation, diagnosis, intervention and outcome verification, evaluated for analytical validity, transferability, biological interpretability, deployment readiness and demonstrated management value.

title: A Review on Multi-Process Movement of Water and Nutrients in Low-Pressure Sprinkler Irrigation and Related Crop Regulation Mechanisms
abstract: Low-pressure sprinkler irrigation combined with fertigation is a promising approach for sustainable agriculture. However, reducing operating pressure changes sprinkler hydraulic performance, droplet characteristics, and irrigation uniformity, which in turn affect droplet evaporation and drift, canopy interception, soil infiltration, and field microclimate, ultimately influencing crop growth and resource use efficiency. A systematic synthesis of these interconnected processes is currently missing. This review synthesizes current knowledge on low-pressure sprinkler irrigation by integrating findings from hydraulic engineering, soil physics, micro-meteorology, and crop physiology. It covers sprinkler hydraulic performance, water and nutrient transport, and crop response mechanisms. It also identifies priority directions for future research. Based on a critical evaluation of existing studies, several key findings emerge. For hydraulic performance, non-circular nozzles and flow dispersion devices can improve jet breakup and uniformity under low pressure. In particular, non-circular nozzles enhance jet instability and air entrainment via axis-switching, while water-dispersing needles and off-axis plate motion effectively improve near-sprinkler water distribution. For water and nutrient transport, low pressure increases droplet size and kinetic energy, reducing evaporation and drift losses. Canopy modifies throughfall droplets, affecting soil structure, infiltration and erosion. A notable finding is that soil water redistribution compensates for low irrigation uniformity, making root-zone soil water more uniform, whereas soil nitrogen uniformity remains close to the sprinkler irrigation uniformity. For crop responses, sprinkler irrigation improves microclimate (cooling and humidifying), enhances crop photosynthesis and reduces transpiration, thus increasing yield and water use efficiency. Importantly, reduced irrigation uniformity did not significantly reduce yield under the specific conditions reported in existing studies, benefit by lower losses and soil compensation. However, most existing microclimate studies are based on medium- and high-pressure systems; the response mechanisms under low-pressure conditions remain unclear. Future research should prioritize four areas, including long-term performance and economic feasibility of low-pressure sprinklers, coupled multi-process modelling of water and fertilizer transport and environmental risk assessment, field microclimate responses and crop physiological mechanisms under low pressure, and system regulation strategies tailored to different crops and regions. This review provides a holistic basis for optimizing water, energy, and fertilizer synergies in sprinkler irrigation.

title: Silent Modality Collapse and the Measurement of Fusion Gains: A Nationwide Out-of-Time Test of Earth Observation for Agricultural Default Forecasting
abstract: Satellite Earth observation (EO) is widely proposed as alternative data for agricultural credit risk, yet reported fusion gains are rarely tested against the protocol producing them. We specify three inexpensive instruments—matched alert volumes instead of a fixed threshold, neutralization of a modality inside a fitted model, and diagnostics of whether a fused branch is used—and apply them to ST-CRAAN, a dual-branch forecaster combining an eleven-channel monthly EO tensor with borrower financial covariates, on 1,496,721 Thai rice-cultivating borrowers with the 2022 crop year withheld. The diagnostics detect silent modality collapse: weight decay drove the recurrent input kernel from 0.0750 at initialization to 7.0 × 10−8 (about 10−6 of its initial value), and replacing the EO tensor by its population mean changed test AUC by 0.00000. An ablation traces the collapse to gradient starvation of the branch, which weight decay completes rather than causes. With the branch in use, a factorial of five model families by eight feature sets, refitted under several seeds, finds that EO lowers test AUC in every fit of the three tabular families when it joins financial and spatial covariates, and gives the two neural families no reliable gain. Added to sub-district repayment history alone, it lowers test AUC in every fit of all five families. Ranking borrowers by the realized default rate of their sub-district–year cell bounds any predictor constant within such a cell at AUC 0.67721; every family stays below it, by 0.029 to 0.031. On this panel and across this year boundary, areal EO does not improve borrower-level default forecasting for a lender holding its own records: the binding constraint is resolution, not architecture.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning of Hydrogen Production from Reactive Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Polyethylene Oxidative Gasification
abstract: Reactive molecular dynamics (ReaxFF MD) simulations of polyethylene (PE) oxidative gasification generate large trajectory datasets suited to machine learning (ML). We recast H2 production monitoring as a leakage-free forecasting task: given the simulated thermochemical state at time t, predict the time-weighted cumulative H2 production cumH2(t+h) a fixed horizon h=25 ps ahead. Data from 48 trajectories spanning six O2 loadings (1–900 molecules per 50 PE chains) and eight temperatures (1500–2900 K) yield 72,117 forecast pairs (45 simulations; three truncated trajectories excluded). Eight tabular regression models are benchmarked against persistence and physics-informed baselines under simulation-grouped nested cross-validation, a held-out test partition, temperature- and loading-holdout stress tests, and a paired ablation removing all H2-derived inputs. With the H2 history available, the best test model (random forest) attains R2=0.9999 at RMSE 121.8 molecules·ps, a 93.0% RMSE reduction relative to persistence, robust to unseen O2 loadings and largely robust to unseen temperatures. Without it, no model beats persistence in any evaluation: the best ML model (an artificial neural network) is 26.0% worse, and accuracy decreases substantially under temperature extrapolation. The ablation attributes 93.3–98.3% of the tree and kernel models’ RMSE reduction to the H2-derived features, quantifying how much forecasting skill derives from the target history rather than instantaneous observables.

title: HallucinationNerd: A Framework and Tool to Detect Hallucinations and Unsupported Claims
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic systems, and human authors produce text with inline citations, but the cited sources do not always support the claims attributed to them. We present HallucinationNerd, a modular citation-verification engine that decomposes text into atomic claims, retrieves relevant passages from each cited source, and determines whether the source supports the claim. In addition, HallucinationNerd identifies claims that carry no citation and searches user-approved databases to find or refute supporting evidence for them. The system handles five common citation formats, operates on PDFs, web pages, and plain text, and produces per-claim verdicts with evidence pointers. The underlying algorithm mixes parsing (to identify claim–citation pairs), overlapped chunking, stopword elimination, and AI-based semantic comparison. In head-to-head comparison on the same data, HallucinationNerd substantially outperforms (by about 20% in F1 score) state-of-the-art systems on accuracy and precision on a benchmark built from research papers. HallucinationNerd can also be used to verify the output of other AI systems. For example, we audited a set of outputs of Scholar GPT, a publicly available scholarly research agent. In that sample at least, its citations were faithful to the cited sources.

title: Deficit Irrigation Strategies in Almond Orchards: A Review of the Effects on Yield, Physiology, Nut Quality, Economics, and Remote Sensing
abstract: Sustainable water use is a major challenge in irrigated agriculture, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions where water availability strongly influences crop productivity and quality. Almond (Prunus dulcis (Mill.) D.A. Webb) is an important nut crop cultivated extensively in such environments, making efficient irrigation management essential for sustainable production. A total of 63 studies were included in the review, comprising 62 field studies and one pot experiment, some of which incorporated modelling, remote sensing, physiological monitoring, or sensor-based irrigation-management approaches, to evaluate deficit irrigation (DI) in almond, with particular emphasis on regulated deficit irrigation (RDI), sustained deficit irrigation (SDI), low-frequency deficit irrigation (LFDI), and partial root-zone drying (PRD). The review examines how irrigation strategy, deficit intensity, timing and duration of water restriction, cultivar, tree age, and environmental conditions affect irrigation water savings, yield, kernel quality, water productivity, water-use efficiency, and physiological responses. In addition, the economic implications of DI and recent applications of remote sensing (RS) for detecting water stress and supporting irrigation scheduling are evaluated. Overall, the evidence indicates that DI can substantially reduce irrigation water use while maintaining acceptable yields and, under specific conditions, improving kernel quality. However, responses vary considerably among studies, reflecting interactions among deficit characteristics, environmental conditions, cultivar, and tree age and limiting the development of universally applicable management recommendations. The review further indicates that integrating DI with RS-based monitoring has potential to support site-specific and adaptive irrigation management by improving water allocation, detecting emerging water stress, and enhancing water-use efficiency. Such integrated approaches may become increasingly important in regions experiencing greater drought frequency and competition for water resources. Future research should prioritize multi-environment and multi-cultivar validation of integrated DI–RS approaches, the development of practical decision-support tools and economic thresholds, and the assessment of their transferability from experimental conditions to commercial orchards. Combining physiological indicators, RS technologies, and crop-specific irrigation strategies could contribute to more resilient and sustainable almond production under increasing water scarcity and climate variability.

title: Application of Multi-Temporal LiDAR for Gully Erosion Monitoring in Mediterranean Intensive Olive Groves
abstract: Monitoring the dynamics of gullies in Mediterranean agrosystems is critical but severely limited by agricultural practices that generate continuous machinery compaction and tillage of the soil, camouflaging topographic features and disturbing erosion analyses. This study discusses strategies to quantify erosion by distinguishing natural erosion from agricultural disturbance, integrating multitemporal LiDAR data (2014, 2020, 2024) with gully inventories using orthophoto maps (2011–2022). The volumetric changes were assessed using DoD for the periods 2014–2020 and 2020–2024, and the morphometric performance of the TNO index was further validated using ROC curves in R. Both approaches performed consistently higher in detecting permanent gullies. The TNO index has proven its usefulness for semi-automated delimitation in large or low-data areas. By intersecting DoD surfaces with the gully inventory, localized erosion processes were successfully isolated from the surrounding agricultural landscape matrix. The quantified rate of erosion in the gullies refers strictly to their internal dynamics, which have been close to the natural threshold for soil formation, indicating a risk of soil degradation.

title: PRIWCD: Prototype, Relation, and Instance Guidance for Weakly Supervised Remote Sensing Change Detection
abstract: Weakly supervised remote sensing change detection reduces annotation costs but suffers from incomplete class activation maps, unreliable pseudo-label propagation, and insufficient discrimination between adjacent change regions. To address these limitations, we propose PRIWCD, a weakly supervised framework for remote sensing change detection. PRIWCD introduces a dynamic prototype comparison module to enhance high-level differential features by modeling unchanged regions and diverse change patterns with multiple dynamic prototypes. A dual relationship propagation guidance module further refines class activation maps by jointly exploiting changes in bi-temporal attention relationships and feature similarity. In addition, instance separation regularization improves feature compactness within pseudo-instances and enhances the separation between changed regions and the background. Experiments on WHU-CD, CLCD, and DSIFN demonstrate the effectiveness of PRIWCD. The proposed method achieves the best mean F1 scores of 79.10%, 62.33%, and 62.68%, respectively, outperforming the compared weakly supervised methods. The results demonstrate that PRIWCD effectively improves pseudo-label quality and provides robust change detection under image-level supervision.
